They are: the causes and conditions for the arising of world-oceans; the basis upon which world-oceans rest; the shapes of world-oceans; the essential nature of world-oceans; the adornments of world-oceans; the purification of world-oceans; the appearance of Buddhas in world-oceans; the duration of kalpas in world-oceans; the distinctions in the transformations of kalpas in world-oceans; and the gates of non-differentiation in world-oceans.
Sons of the Buddha!
Briefly stated, there are these ten matters concerning the oceans of worlds;
if explained in detail, they are as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, and have been taught, are being taught, and will be taught by all Buddhas of the past, present, and future.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Briefly stated, by means of ten kinds of causes and conditions, all world-oceans have been formed, are being formed, and will be formed. What are these ten?

That is to say: it is due to the spiritual power of the Tathāgatas; because the nature of phenomena is thus; because of the karmic actions of all sentient beings; because of what is attained by all Bodhisattvas upon achieving all-knowledge; because of the shared accumulation of roots of goodness by all sentient beings and Bodhisattvas; because of the power of the vows of all Bodhisattvas to adorn and purify buddha-lands; because of the accomplishment of non-retrogressive practices and vows by all Bodhisattvas; because of the sovereign power of the pure resolute understandings of all Bodhisattvas; because of the outflow from the roots of goodness of all Tathāgatas and the sovereign power of all Buddhas at the time of their attainment of enlightenment; and because of the sovereign power of the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
O Sons of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of causes and conditions explained in brief;
if explained in detail, they are as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
“The boundless oceans of lands you have described Are all completely adorned and purified by Vairocana.
The realm of the World-Honored One is inconceivable; Such is the power of his wisdom and spiritual penetrations.”
The Bodhisattva practices an ocean of vows, universally following the desires of the minds of sentient beings;
as the mental activities of sentient beings are vast and boundless, so too do the Bodhisattva’s lands pervade the ten directions.
The Bodhisattva proceeds toward all-knowledge, Diligently cultivating various powers of mastery;
From an immeasurable ocean of vows, they universally arise, And vast buddha-lands are all brought to fulfillment.
Cultivating boundless oceans of all practices, Entering the Buddha’s realm is likewise immeasurable;
To purify all lands throughout the ten directions, They spend immeasurable eons in each and every land.
Sentient beings are turbid, agitated by afflictions; They differentiate desires and pleasures in manifold ways.
Inconceivably, they create karma according to their minds, And thus all oceans of lands are established.
The Buddha-sons' ocean of lands, a treasury of adornments, Is formed of stainless, radiant jewels;
This arises from a mind of vast faith and understanding, And all that dwells throughout the ten directions is likewise so.
The Bodhisattva is able to cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra, Traveling through the paths of atoms within the Dharma-realm;
Within every atom, he manifests infinite lands, Pure and vast as space itself.
Manifesting supernatural powers throughout the realm of empty space, they all proceed to the sites of enlightenment where the Buddhas dwell;
upon lotus thrones they display various forms, each individual body encompassing all lands.
In a single thought-moment, one universally manifests throughout the three periods of time;
all oceans of lands are established therein, and the Buddha enters them all through skillful means—this is that which Vairocana has adorned and purified.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Each ocean of worlds has as many bases of support as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds."

That is to say: some dwell relying on all manner of adornments; some dwell relying on space; some dwell relying on the radiance of all jewels; some dwell relying on the radiance of all Buddhas; some dwell relying on the radiance of the colors of all jewels; some dwell relying on the voices of all Buddhas; some dwell relying on the form of the powerful Asura Vajrapāṇi, born from karma that is like an illusion; some dwell relying on the bodies of all world-protectors; some dwell relying on the bodies of all Bodhisattvas; and some dwell relying on the ocean of all various adornments produced by the vows of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
"Sons of the Buddha!
The oceans of worlds have such abodes as these, numbering as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"Pervading the entirety of the space-realm in the ten directions, All lands that exist therein,
Through the empowerment of the Tathāgata’s spiritual power, Are manifested everywhere and may be seen by all."
There are various kinds of lands, all of which are composed of stainless jewels;
they are most exquisite with pure maṇi-gems, brilliantly manifesting a vast ocean of light.
There are pure and luminous lands that abide supported by the realm of empty space;
some rest within oceans of mani-jewels, while others dwell securely within treasuries of light.
The Tathāgata dwells within this ocean-like assembly, Expounding the Wheel of Dharma with exquisite skill;
The realm of all Buddhas is vast and boundless, And those sentient beings who behold it rejoice in their hearts.
Some are adorned with mani-jewels, arranged extensively like flower-lamps;
their fragrant flames and clouds of light blaze with color, covered by nets of radiant, wondrous jewels.
There are buddha-fields without limit, Abiding in deep, vast oceans of lotuses;
Vast, pure, and extraordinary compared to the world, Because they are adorned with the wondrous goodness of all Buddhas.
Some oceans of lands revolve with the wheel, yet abide securely through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power;
within them dwell hosts of bodhisattvas everywhere, constantly beholding infinite and vast jewels.
Some abide in the body of Vajrapāṇi, and others abide in the body of the Lord of Devas;
the unsurpassed Honored One, Vairocana, constantly turns the wheel of Dharma in this very place.
Some rest evenly upon jewel trees, and it is likewise so within clouds of fragrant flames;
some rest amidst the great waters, while others dwell upon the firm adamantine ocean.
Some rely upon the Vajradhvaja, while others dwell within oceans of flowers;
there is nothing the vast and great supernormal powers do not pervade—all this Vairocana is able to manifest.
Whether long or short, they are of immeasurable kinds; their circular formations are likewise not uniform.
This wondrous treasury of adornment is distinct from the world, and can only be seen through pure cultivation and refinement.
Thus, these various distinct differences all abide within the ocean of vows;
some lands are eternally in space, filled everywhere by Buddhas like clouds.
Some dwell suspended and inverted in space; sometimes they exist, and sometimes they do not.
There are lands that are utterly pure, abiding within the jeweled crowns of Bodhisattvas.
The great supernormal powers of the Buddhas of the ten directions are all seen within this;
the voices of all Buddhas pervade everywhere—this is brought about by the transformative power of karma.
There are lands that pervade the entire Dharma-realm, Pure and free from defilement, arising from the mind;
Like shadows and like illusions, vast and boundless, Each distinct like the net of Indra.
Some manifest various treasuries of adornments, established by relying upon empty space;
the spheres of their various karmas are inconceivable, yet through the Buddha’s power, they are all revealed for all to see.
Within every single atom of every land, In every thought-moment, he manifests all Buddha-fields;
Their number is infinite, equal to the number of sentient beings— Such is the constant activity of Samantabhadra.
Desiring to bring sentient beings to maturity, they practice herein through oceans of eons;
their vast and great spiritual transformations arise without exception, pervading the entire realm of phenomena.
Within every single atom of the lands of the Dharma-realm, All oceans of great buddha-fields abide;
Clouds of Buddhas pervade them all equally, Filling every single place.
Just as there is sovereign mastery within a single atom, so it is likewise within all atoms;
the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, Vairocana is able to manifest them all.
All vast and extensive lands are like shadows, like illusions, and like mirages;
in the ten directions they are seen to have no place of origin, nor do they have any place from which they come or to which they go.
Destruction and formation, arising and ceasing, revolve in mutual succession; within the void of space, there is not even a moment’s rest.
None of these fail to arise from pure vows, sustained by the power of vast karma.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
The oceans of worlds possess various distinct forms and characteristics."
That is to say:
some are circular, some are square, some are neither circular nor square, with infinite variations;

some are shaped like whirlpools, some are shaped like mountain flames, some are shaped like trees, some are shaped like flowers, some are shaped like palaces, some are shaped like sentient beings, and some are shaped like Buddhas...
"Such as these, there are as many world-oceans as there are atoms.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The oceans of lands are variously distinct, With various adornments and various dwellings; ... (the rest of the verses follow)"
Diverse forms, all beautiful, pervade the ten directions; you all should observe them together.
Their shapes may be circular or square, or perhaps triangular or octagonal;
like mani-jewel wheels or lotuses—all these differ according to the power of karma.
Some are adorned with pure flames, interspersed with refined gold in many exquisite ways;
their gates and portals open in competition without obstruction—this results from vast karma and an undistracted mind.
The boundless treasury of distinctions within the ocean of lands is like clouds spread across the void;
with jeweled wheels arrayed upon the ground in wondrous adornment, all is illuminated by the radiance of the Buddhas.
All lands are mental constructions, Manifesting various kinds of radiant light;
Within such oceans of buddha-fields, The Buddha displays his supernormal powers in each and every one.

Whether there be defilement or purity, and whether one experiences suffering or joy with their respective distinctions—all this arises from the inconceivable ocean of karma; such is the constant nature of all phenomena in saṃsāra.
Within a single pore are inconceivable lands, Abiding in various ways as numerous as atoms;
In each one dwells the All-Illuminating Honored One, Proclaiming the wondrous Dharma amidst the great assemblies.
Within a single atom are lands, great and small, Diverse in their various distinctions as numerous as atoms;
Whether level or high and low, each being different, The Buddha goes to them all and turns the wheel of Dharma.
All the lands manifested within every atom, Are all produced by the power of original vows and spiritual penetrations;
According to the various inclinations of beings' minds, They are all able to be created within the void of space.
Within every single atom of all lands, the Buddha enters;
for the sake of all sentient beings, he manifests spiritual transformations—such is the Dharma of Vairocana.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
You should know that the oceans of worlds possess various kinds of essences."
That is to say:
some have as their essence the adornment of all jewels; some have as their essence the various adornments of a single jewel;
some have as their essence the radiance of all jewels; and some have as their essence the radiance of various colors.
Some have as their essence the light of all adornments; some have as their essence indestructible vajra;
some have as their essence the sustaining power of the Buddha; some have as their essence the marks of exquisite jewels;
some have as their essence the transformations of the Buddha; some have as their essence the solar maṇi-wheel; and some have as their essence the most subtle atoms.
It has jewels as its substance, or it has all jewel-flames as its substance, or it has various fragrances as its substance,
or it has all jewel-flower crowns as its substance, or it has all jewel-reflections as its substance,
or it has all manifested adornments as its substance, or it universally manifests within a single thought-moment.
Its substance consists of manifested realms; or it consists of jewels in the form of bodhisattvas; or it consists of the filaments of jewel flowers;
or it consists of the vocal sounds of the Buddha.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"There are some oceans of lands, Composed of exquisite jewels, Solid and indestructible, Resting upon precious lotus flowers."
Or it may be pure radiance, its origin unknowable;
adorned by all lights, it abides supported by space.
Or it may have pure light as its essence, further abiding supported by radiance.
Adorned with clouds of light, these are the places where Bodhisattvas dwell together.
There are some oceans of lands that arise from the power of vows;
they abide like reflections, such that neither their grasping nor their description can be found.
Some are formed of mani-jewels, universally radiating the light of the sun-treasury;
their ground is adorned with spheres of pearls, and bodhisattvas completely fill them.
There are lands formed of jewel-flames, with clouds of flames covering them above.
The radiance of the various jewels is most exquisite, all obtained through the power of karma.
Some arise from wondrous forms, adorning the ground with manifold marks;
like a crown worn together upon the head, these arise from the Buddha’s transformative power.
Some arise from the ocean of the mind, abiding according to what the mind understands;
like illusions, they have no fixed location—all are but conceptual constructions.
Others take the light of the Buddha or the radiance of mani-jewels as their essence.
Within this, all Buddhas appear, each manifesting supernatural powers.
Some are the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, who manifests oceans of lands adorned by the power of his vows; all of these are extraordinary and sublime.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
You should know that the oceans of worlds possess various kinds of adornments."

That is to say: some are adorned by the emergence of clouds of supreme excellence from all ornaments; some are adorned by the proclamation of all the virtues of bodhisattvas; some are adorned by the proclamation of the karmic retributions of all sentient beings; some are adorned by the manifestation of the ocean of vows of all bodhisattvas; some are adorned by the representation of the images of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; some are adorned by the manifestation in a single thought-moment of the supernatural realms of boundless eons; some are adorned by the appearance of the bodies of all Buddhas; some are adorned by the appearance of clouds of all precious incenses; some are adorned by the radiant illumination of all exquisite treasures within all sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*); and some are adorned by the manifestation of all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra...
"Such as these, there are as many world-oceans as there are atoms.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The vast oceans of lands are boundless, All accomplished through pure karma; The Tathāgatas appear therein, Their forms as infinite as the sea."
Adorned in various ways and dwelling in various places, they pervade all the ten directions.
Clouds of jewel-flames with boundless forms and colors, vast adornments of many kinds,
constantly appear throughout the oceans of lands in the ten directions, universally proclaiming the Dharma with sublime sounds.
The Bodhisattvas’ boundless ocean of merit, adorned by various great vows,
simultaneously emits wondrous sounds from this land, universally shaking the networks of all lands throughout the ten directions.
The ocean of sentient beings' karma is vast and immeasurable; according to their respective retributions, they differ from one another.
Amidst the adornments of all places, it is the Buddhas who are able to expound them all.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time universally manifest their supernormal powers throughout oceans of lands;
within each and every phenomenon, all Buddhas are present—observe such pure adornments as these.
Throughout the kalpas of the past, future, and present, And within all lands of the ten directions—
Whatever great adornments exist therein, Each and every one is seen within this single realm.
In all matters, immeasurable Buddhas, equal in number to sentient beings, pervade the world;
to bring them to subdual, they manifest spiritual powers, thereby adorning the ocean of lands.
All manner of adornments emit wondrous clouds: clouds of various flowers, clouds of fragrant flames, and clouds of mani-jewels constantly appear; by these, the ocean of lands is adorned.
All places throughout the ten directions where enlightenment is attained, With every kind of adornment fully perfected,
Emitting radiant light that spreads afar like colored clouds— May all these be seen within this ocean of lands.
Buddha-sons who practice the vows and deeds of Samantabhadra, Diligently cultivate them for as many eons as there are sentient beings;
They adorn boundless lands, Appearing clearly in every place.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
You should know that within the oceans of worlds, there are oceans of pure skillful means as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds."

That is to say: because all Bodhisattvas draw near to all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) to share in the same roots of goodness; because they increase and expand clouds of vast merit that pervade the Dharma-realm; because they purely cultivate vast and supreme resolute beliefs (*adhimukti*); because they observe all Bodhisattva realms and dwell therein; because they cultivate and purify all the perfections (*pāramitā*) until they are entirely fulfilled; because they observe all the stages (*bhūmi*) of Bodhisattvas and enter and abide in them; because they give birth to the ocean of all pure vows; because they practice all essential paths of transcendence; because they enter the ocean of all adornments; and because they accomplish the power of pure skillful means (*upāya*)...
"Such as these, there are as many worlds as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The various adornments of all oceans of lands Are born from the power of vows and countless skillful means."
All oceans of lands are eternally radiant, Arising from the power of immeasurable pure karma.
Having long approached spiritual friends, They have cultivated wholesome deeds together until all are pure;
With vast compassion pervading all sentient beings, They adorn all these oceans of lands with this.
All dharma-gates, samādhis, and the like, The stages of meditative concentration, liberation, and skillful means—
Having thoroughly purified these in the presence of all Buddhas, One thereby brings forth oceans of all buddha-lands.
Generating immeasurable resolute understandings, they realize that the Tathāgatas are equal and without distinction;
having cultivated the ocean of patience through skillful means, they are thus able to adorn and purify boundless lands.
Cultivating sublime practices for the benefit of sentient beings, their vast merit constantly increases;
like clouds spreading to equal the expanse of space, they bring all oceans of lands to fulfillment.
The various perfections, as immeasurable as the atoms of all lands, have all been practiced until they are fully perfected;
may these perfections never be exhausted, so that oceans of pure lands may arise from them.
Purifying all peerless dharmas, Arising boundless practices of transcendence,
Transforming all living beings through various skillful means— Thus they adorn the oceans of buddha-lands.
Cultivating the ground of skillful means as adornment, Entering the ocean of the Buddha’s gates of dharma and merit,
Universally causing all sentient beings to exhaust the source of suffering, And bringing to fulfillment vast and pure buddha-lands.
The ocean of power is vast and beyond compare, universally causing all sentient beings to plant roots of goodness;
making offerings to all Tathāgatas, the boundless lands are entirely purified.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
You should know that in each and every world-ocean, there are as many distinct appearances of Buddhas as there are atoms within a world-ocean."

That is to say: sometimes manifesting a small body, or manifesting a large body; sometimes manifesting a short lifespan, or manifesting a long lifespan; sometimes solely adorning and purifying a single Buddha-land, or adorning and purifying immeasurable Buddha-lands; sometimes solely revealing the Dharma-wheel of the One Vehicle, or revealing the inconceivable Dharma-wheels of the various vehicles; or manifesting the subduing of a limited number of sentient beings, or demonstrating the subduing of boundless sentient beings...
"In this manner, there are as many such [worlds] as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The various skillful means of all Buddhas Bring forth all oceans of lands; ... (as many as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds)..."
All according to what sentient beings' minds delight in—this is the Tathāgata’s skillful power.

The Dharma-body of all Buddhas is inconceivable; it has no color, no form, and no image, yet it can manifest various marks for the sake of sentient beings, causing them all to see according to their mental inclinations.
Sometimes manifesting short lifespans for the sake of sentient beings, Or manifesting a lifespan that abides for immeasurable kalpas;
The Dharma-body appears universally throughout the ten directions, Appearing in the world according to what is appropriate.
Some adorn and purify inconceivable oceans of all lands throughout the ten directions;
others adorn and purify only a single land, manifesting it in its entirety without exception.
In accordance with the inclinations of sentient beings' minds, he manifests inconceivable varieties of vehicles;
sometimes he proclaims only the Dharma of the One Vehicle, yet within that One, through skillful means, he manifests the infinite.
Some spontaneously attain perfect enlightenment, causing a small number of sentient beings to abide in the Way;
others, within a single thought-moment, awaken countless deluded beings.
Or from a single pore he emits clouds of emanations, manifesting immeasurable and boundless Buddhas;
all worlds behold them as they appear, employing various skillful means to deliver all living beings.
There are voices that pervade everywhere, preaching the Dharma according to the inclinations of beings' minds;
throughout inconceivable great eons, they tame an ocean of immeasurable sentient beings.
There are lands of infinite adornment, where assemblies sit pure and solemn;
Buddhas are spread therein like clouds, filling every ocean of lands throughout the ten directions.
The skillful means of all Buddhas are inconceivable; Appearing before all according to the minds of sentient beings, They dwell universally in various adorned lands, Pervading every single realm.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
You should know that the oceans of worlds have durations of abiding for as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds."

That is to say: there are those who abide for incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas; some abide for immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) kalpas; some abide for boundless (*ananta*) kalpas; some abide for incomparable (*asama*) kalpas; some abide for uncountable (*agaṇeya*) kalpas; some abide for ineffable (*atulya*) kalpas; some abide for inconceivable (*acintya*) kalpas; some abide for unfathomable (*ameya*) kalpas; and some abide for unspeakable (*anabhilāpya*) kalpas...
"Such as these, there are as many worlds as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The various eons within the oceans of worlds Are adorned with vast and great skillful means."
All the lands of the ten directions are clearly perceived, And their numerical distinctions are fully understood.
I behold the oceans of worlds in the ten directions, With kalpas as infinite as the number of sentient beings—
Whether long, short, or boundless— I now proclaim them all By means of the Buddha’s voice.

I behold the oceans of lands in the ten directions; some abide for as many eons as there are atoms in a land, while others remain for a single eon or for countless ones, each differing according to their various vows.
Some are purely pure, some are purely defiled, and others are a mixture of both defilement and purity;
the oceans of vows are established in various distinct ways, abiding within the thoughts and minds of sentient beings.
Having practiced in the past for eons as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, He attained a vast and pure ocean of worlds;
The realms of all Buddhas are fully adorned, Abiding forever through infinite and expansive eons.
There is one named Various Jewel Radiance, or named Equal Sound Flame-Eye Treasury;
there is Radiance Free from Dust and the Worthy Eon—this Pure Eon encompasses them all.
In some pure kalpas, a single Buddha appears; in others, immeasurable Buddhas manifest within a single kalpa.
Through the power of inexhaustible skillful means and great vows, they enter into all various kinds of kalpas.
Sometimes immeasurable eons enter into a single eon, and sometimes a single eon enters into many eons;
within all the various gateways of the ocean of eons, the lands of the ten directions appear clearly.
Or the adornments of all kalpas, one perceives them all manifested within a single kalpa;
or the adornments within a single kalpa, one universally enters into all infinite kalpas.
Beginning from a single thought and ending with the formation of eons, all arise in dependence upon the mental conceptions of sentient beings;
though the oceans of lands and eons are boundless, they are all purified through a single skillful means.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
You should know that within the oceans of worlds, there are as many distinct transformations of kalpas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds."
That is to say:
because the nature of phenomena is thus, the oceans of worlds undergo transformation through immeasurable kalpas of formation and destruction;
because defiled sentient beings dwell therein, the oceans of worlds undergo transformation through kalpas of defilement.
Because sentient beings dwell in the cultivation of vast merit, the world-oceans undergo transformation through kalpas of both defilement and purity;
because Bodhisattvas dwell in resolute belief and understanding, the world-oceans undergo transformation through kalpas of both defilement and purity;
and because immeasurable sentient beings resolve their minds toward Bodhi, the world-oceans undergo transformation through kalpas of absolute purity.
Because the various bodhisattvas each travel through the various worlds, the world-oceans undergo transformation during the kalpas of boundless adornment;
because the clouds of bodhisattvas from all world-oceans in the ten directions assemble together, the world-oceans undergo transformation during the kalpas of immeasurable great adornment;
and because the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, enter parinirvāṇa, the world-oceans undergo transformation during the kalpas of the cessation of adornment.
Because the Buddhas appear in the world, the vast and pure kalpas of all world-oceans undergo transformation;
because of the Tathāgatas’ supernatural powers and transformations, the world-oceans undergo transformation through the universally pure kalpas...
"Such as these, there are worlds as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"All lands and realms Are born according to the power of karma."
You all should observe that the nature of transformation is thus:
sentient beings are defiled, entangled by karma and afflictions, and are truly terrifying;
their minds cause the entire ocean of lands to become thoroughly defiled.
If there are those with pure minds who cultivate various meritorious deeds,
their minds cause the oceans of lands to become either defiled or purified.
Bodhisattvas who possess faith and understanding are born within those eons.
According to the states of their minds, they perceive various defilements and purities.
Immeasurable sentient beings all resolve upon bodhicitta;
by that mind, the oceans of lands remain eternally pure throughout the kalpas.
Immeasurable billions of bodhisattvas travel to the ten directions;
their adornments are without distinction, yet they appear differently within each eon.
Within every single atom, there are Buddha-fields as numerous as those atoms.
The Bodhisattvas gathered like clouds, and all lands were pure.
When the World-Honored One entered nirvana, the adornments of those lands vanished;
sentient beings became unfit vessels for the Dharma, and the world became defiled.
If a Buddha appears in the world, all things become precious and excellent;
according to the purity of their minds, they are fully adorned.
Through the supernatural powers of the Buddhas, inconceivable manifestations are displayed.
At that time, all oceans of lands were universally and completely purified.
Then, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
“O Children of the Buddha!
One should know that there are as many undifferentiated world-oceans as there are atoms within a world-ocean.
That is to say:
within each individual world-ocean, there are as many undifferentiated worlds as there are atoms within a world-ocean;
Within each and every ocean of worlds, there is no difference in the majestic power manifested by all Buddhas;
within each and every ocean of worlds, there is no difference in all the sites of enlightenment pervading the ten directions of the Dharma-realm;
within each and every ocean of worlds, there is no difference in the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
In each and every ocean of worlds, the light of all Buddhas pervades the dharma-realm without distinction;
in each and every ocean of worlds, the names of the emanations of all Buddhas are without distinction;
in each and every ocean of worlds, the voices of all Buddhas pervade the oceans of worlds and abide for boundless eons without distinction.
In each ocean of world-systems, there is no difference in the skillful means of turning the wheel of Dharma;
in each ocean of world-systems, all oceans of worlds universally enter into a single atom without distinction;
in each ocean of world-systems, within every single atom, the vast realms of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the three periods of time are manifested therein without distinction.
O Sons of the Buddha!
The oceans of worlds are without distinction; this is a brief explanation.
If explained in detail, they are as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Within a single mote of dust are many oceans of lands, Each location distinct, all perfectly pure;
Thus, these infinite realms enter into one, Yet each remains distinct, without confusion or overlap.”
Within each and every atom are inconceivable Buddhas, Who appear universally before the minds of sentient beings;
There is no ocean of lands they do not pervade, Yet such skillful means are without distinction.
Within each and every atom are kings of trees, Adorned with all manner of ornaments hanging down;
They appear identically throughout the lands of the ten directions, And all such things are without distinction.
Within each and every atom, hosts of beings as numerous as atoms all surround the Lord of Men;
surpassing all, they pervade the world, yet there is no crowding or confusion.
Within each and every atom are immeasurable lights, Pervading all lands throughout the ten directions;
They manifest the bodhisattva practices of all Buddhas, Throughout the entire ocean of realms without distinction.
Within each and every atom are infinite bodies, Manifesting like clouds, pervading everywhere;
Guiding all classes of beings through the Buddha’s spiritual powers, The lands of the ten directions are likewise without distinction.
Within each and every atom, he expounds all dharmas; those dharmas are pure like the turning of a wheel.
Through various gates of skillful means and mastery, he proclaims them all without distinction.
Within a single mote of dust, the voices of all Buddhas are universally proclaimed, filling all sentient beings who are vessels of the Dharma;
throughout the ocean of lands for infinite eons, these sounds remain ever the same.
The infinite, wondrous adornments of the oceans of lands all enter into a single atom;
such supernatural powers of the Buddhas arise entirely from the nature of karma.
Within each and every atom are the Buddhas of the three times; according to their inclinations, all are made to see them.
Their essential nature neither comes nor goes, yet by the power of their vows, they pervade the world.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Seven;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Five: The Flower Treasury World System.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!

This Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean was purified by the great vows, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, which the Tathāgata Vairocana cultivated while practicing the bodhisattva path for as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds; in each and every eon, he attended upon Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, and at the site of each and every Buddha, he purified those great vows as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
O Sons of the Buddha!
This Flower Bank Adorned World-Ocean is supported by wind-circles as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru.
The lowest of these wind-circles is named:
The wind-circle of Equal Abiding can support all the blazing jewel-flames and adornments above it.
Above that is the wind-circle named Producing Various Jewel Adornments, which can support the king of mani-jewel banners illuminated by pure light above it.
Above that wind-circle is one named Jewel Splendor,
which can support all the jewel bells above it.
Above that wind-circle is one named...
The Equal Flame wind-wheel can support the sun-light-marked maṇi-king wheel above it.
Above that is the wind-wheel named Various Universal Adornments, which can support the light-wheel flower above it.
Above that wind-circle is one named Universal Purity,
which can support all the flower-flame lion-thrones above it.
Above that wind-circle is one named:
The sound pervades the ten directions, and it can support all the banners of jewel-kings above it.
Above that wind-circle is one named All-Jewel Radiance,
which can support all the flowers of the mani-king trees above it.
Above that wind-circle is one named Swift Universal Support, which can sustain all the fragrant maṇi Sumeru clouds above it.
Above that wind-circle is one named:
They travel through various palaces, able to sustain all the clouds of jewel-colored fragrance terraces above them.
O Sons of the Buddha!
Among those wind-circles, as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, the one at the very top is named:
The ocean of fragrant water named Repository of Supreme Majestic Radiance is adorned with mani-jewels that emit universal light;
within this ocean of fragrant water is a great lotus flower named Banner of Fragrance with Multicolored Radiant Filaments.
The Flower Treasury Adorned Ocean of Worlds dwells therein, level and even on all four sides, pure and firm;
it is encircled by the Diamond Rim Mountains,
while the lands, seas, and various trees each have their own distinct characteristics.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
“In the past, throughout all realms of existence, The World-Honored One cultivated pure deeds at the abodes of countless Buddhas;
Therefore, he attained various jewel-lights, And the Flower Treasury Adorned Ocean of Worlds.”

The vast clouds of compassion pervade all things; having sacrificed bodies as numerous as the atoms of immeasurable lands, through the power of practice throughout oceans of past eons, this world is now free from all defilement.
Emitting great radiance that pervades all space, Supported by the power of the wind, it remains unshakable;
Adorned everywhere with the maṇi-jewels of the Buddha-treasury, It is rendered pure through the power of the Tathāgata’s vows.
Flowers from the wondrous treasury of mani-jewels are scattered everywhere; by the power of past vows, they abide in the air.
Various oceans of firm and solid adornments, with clouds of light streaming down, fill the ten directions.
Clouds of Bodhisattvas from within various mani-jewels travel everywhere throughout the ten directions with blazing radiance;
their flames form wheels adorned with exquisite flowers, circulating through the entire dharma realm without exception.

From within all jewels, pure light is emitted; that light shines universally upon the ocean of sentient beings, pervading the lands of the ten directions, causing all to emerge from suffering and turn toward Bodhi.

Within the jewels are Buddhas as numerous as sentient beings; from their pores they emit transformation bodies—such as Brahmā, Śakra, and universal monarchs—as well as all sentient beings and all Buddhas.
He manifests light equal to the Dharma-realm; within that light, he proclaims the names of all Buddhas.
Through various skillful means, he demonstrates subduing, universally responding to the minds of all beings without exception.
Within every single atom of all the worlds in the Flower Treasury, The entire Dharma-realm is seen within each and every atom;
Precious lights manifest Buddhas gathered like clouds— This is the Tathāgata’s mastery over his buddha-field.
The vast clouds of vows pervade the Dharma-realm, transforming all sentient beings throughout every eon;
having fully accomplished the practices of Samantabhadra’s ground of wisdom, all manner of adornments emerge from them.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!

This Great Cakravāḍa Mountain of the Flower Bank Array World-Ocean rests upon a lotus flower of the Sun-Jewel King. It has sandalwood-maṇi for its body, majestic virtue-jewel kings for its peaks, and exquisite fragrance-maṇi for its rims; it is established by the confluence of flame-treasury vajras, and all fragrant waters flow through its midst."

Forests of various jewels abound, with exquisite flowers in full bloom; fragrant herbs carpet the ground, interspersed with the adornment of bright pearls; all manner of incense and flowers fill every place;
nets of *maṇi* gems hang down and cover it on all sides.
"In this manner, there are various wonderful adornments as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The great oceans of worlds are boundless, With pure jewel wheels of manifold colors; ... (the rest of the verses follow)"
All these adornments are utterly wondrous, arisen through the supernatural power of the Tathāgata.
Wheels of maṇi jewels, wheels of exquisite incense, and wheels of pearl lamp-flames—
all adorned with various wonderful gems— rest securely within the pure Cakravāḍa mountains.
With solid mani-jewels as its core, adorned with Jāmbūnada gold, it radiates light and emits flames throughout the ten directions; transparent both inside and out, it is entirely pure.
Accumulated from vajra-maṇis, they further rain down various wonderful maṇi jewels;
these treasures are exquisite and manifold, emitting pure radiance that is universally magnificent and beautiful.
The streams of fragrant water flow in immeasurable colors, scattering various flowers, jewels, and sandalwood;
multitudes of lotuses bloom in competition like spread-out garments, and rare grasses grow in profusion, all exquisitely fragrant.
Immeasurable jewel trees provide universal adornment; Their blossoms open and their filaments emerge in blazing colors.
Various kinds of famous garments are within them, And clouds of light shine everywhere, ever perfectly full.
Immeasurable and boundless great bodhisattvas, holding canopies and burning incense that fill the Dharma-realm,
all produce every kind of wondrous sound, universally turning the Tathāgata’s true wheel of Dharma.
All the mani-trees are formed from precious powder; each grain of precious powder manifests radiant light, wherein the pure body of Vairocana enters entirely, allowing all to see him everywhere.
Within all manner of adornments, the Buddha’s body appears, With boundless forms and infinite varieties;
It reaches everywhere throughout the ten directions, And the sentient beings it transforms are likewise limitless.
All adornments emit wondrous sounds, proclaiming the wheel of the Tathāgata’s original vows;
throughout all the oceans of pure lands in the ten directions, the Buddha’s sovereign power causes them to pervade entirely.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
All the great earth within this world-ocean’s Great Cakravāḍa Mountains is composed entirely of vajra; it is firm, majestic, and indestructible."
It is pure and level, without high or low;
its wheels are made of mani-jewels, and its storehouses consist of various treasures;
all sentient beings possess their manifold forms and appearances.
Various maṇi jewels were interspersed as inlays;
powdered fragments of many precious gems were scattered about, and lotus flowers were spread across the ground;
maṇis from the Fragrant Treasury were placed at intervals throughout.
All manner of ornaments filled the space like clouds, adorning and embellishing all the Buddha-lands of the three periods of time;
nets of exquisite maṇi jewels manifested everywhere the realms of the Tathāgatas, arrayed therein like the net of Indra.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
This ground of the world-ocean possesses such adornments as these, numbering as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The ground is level and utterly pure, Abiding firmly and indestructible;
It is adorned everywhere with mani-jewels, With various precious gems interspersed therein."
The ground of vajra is most delightful, adorned with jewel wheels and jeweled nets;
lotus flowers are spread upon it in perfect fullness, and exquisite garments cover it everywhere.
The jeweled necklaces and celestial crowns of the bodhisattvas are all spread upon the ground as a magnificent adornment;
sandalwood and mani-jewels are scattered throughout, all radiating pure and wondrous light.
Precious flowers emit flames that radiate wondrous light; these radiant flames, like clouds, illuminate all things.
These exquisite flowers and various jewels are scattered, universally covering the earth as a magnificent adornment.
Dense clouds arise and spread, filling the ten directions; Vast and magnificent light is without end.
Reaching everywhere throughout all lands of the ten directions, They proclaim the Tathāgata’s nectar-like Dharma.
Within the wish-fulfilling jewel of all Buddhas’ vows, The infinite and vast eons are universally manifested;
Whatever was practiced by the Supreme Wise Ones in the past, None of it fails to appear within this jewel.
All the mani jewels within that land receive the entry of all buddha-fields;
within every single atom of those buddha-fields, all lands likewise enter.

In the Flower Treasury World adorned with exquisite jewels, Bodhisattvas travel throughout the ten directions, proclaiming the great vows of these Mahasattvas; this is the power of mastery within the site of enlightenment.
The ground is adorned with exquisite mani jewels, Radiating pure light and arrayed with every ornament;
Pervading the Dharma-realm as vast as space— Such manifestations appear spontaneously through the Buddha’s power.
Those great sages who have cultivated the vows of Samantabhadra and entered the realm of the Buddhas can know all such miraculous transformations within this ocean of lands.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!

Within the great earth of this world-ocean, there are incalculable numbers of fragrant water oceans, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields. Their bottoms are adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels; their shores are adorned with exquisite fragrance-maṇis; and they have nets made of Vairocana-maṇi jewel-kings."
Fragrant waters, clear and translucent, possessing the colors of various jewels, fill its interior;
diverse jewel-flowers swirl and spread across its surface;
and fine sandalwood powder settles as a sediment beneath.
They emanated the melodic voices of the Buddhas and radiated precious light;
boundless bodhisattvas held various canopies and manifested supernatural powers.
All the adornments existing throughout every world appeared therein.
Stairways made of the ten precious substances were arranged in rows;
railings made of the ten precious substances surrounded them on all sides;
and *pundarīka* flowers, adorned with every kind of jewel as numerous as the atoms within the four continents, bloomed vibrantly amidst the waters.

There were hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of banners of the ten kinds of precious *śīla*, banners of nets of bells made of all kinds of jewels as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, pavilions of jewel flowers with boundless colors and forms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of cities of ten kinds of precious lotuses, and groves of trees made of various jewels as numerous as the atoms in the four continents—networked with *ratnajvālā-maṇi* jewels—and sandalwood incense as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, *maṇi* jewels emitting the light-flames of the speech and sounds of all Buddhas, and walls made of various jewels as numerous as unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas, all surrounding and universally adorning [the assembly].
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
Upon the great earth within this world, Is an ocean of fragrant water adorned with mani-jewels;
Pure and wondrous treasures are spread across its bottom, Resting securely upon indestructible vajra.
The banks are formed by heaps of *maṇi* jewels from the treasury of fragrances; wheels of sun-flame pearls are spread like clouds.
With exquisite lotus jewels as their necklaces, they are adorned everywhere, pure and stainless.
Fragrant waters are clear and still, possessing manifold colors; Precious flowers are arrayed in spirals, radiating brilliant light.
Resounding voices shake everywhere, heard both far and near, As the Buddha’s majestic power expounds the wondrous Dharma.
The steps and terraces are adorned with various jewels, further embellished with mani-gems as interspersed ornaments;
the surrounding railings are entirely made of precious gems, and lotus-flower pearl nets are spread like clouds.
Rows of mani-jewel trees stand in formation, their blossoms and filaments flourishing with brilliant, radiant light;
various musical sounds are constantly played in competition, all brought about by the Buddha’s power of supernatural transformations.
Various exquisite jewels and white lotuses are spread out, adorning the fragrant water seas;
the radiance of fragrant flames never ceases, vast and perfect, pervading everywhere.
Luminous jewel banners blaze perpetually, Exquisite robes hang down as adornments;
Nets of mani-bells proclaim the sound of Dharma, Causing all who hear them to advance toward Buddha-wisdom.
Wondrous jewel lotuses form the city walls, Adorned and polished by mani-gems of myriad colors;
Cloud-like shadows of pearls spread across the four quarters— Such is the adornment of the fragrant water ocean.
Walls and fences encircle it on all sides, with multi-storied pavilions rising one after another atop them;
immeasurable light burns ever brightly, a sea of various pure adornments.
In the past, Vairocana purified all manner of oceans of lands;
such vastness, without limit or end, is entirely the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!

Within each and every ocean of fragrant water, there are as many rivers of fragrant water as there are atoms in four continents, circling to the right. All of them have banks made of vajra, adorned with mani-jewels of pure light, constantly manifesting clouds of jewel-colored light from all Buddhas, as well as the voices and sounds of all sentient beings."
In all the places where that river has eddies and whirlpools, the various forms of the causal practices cultivated by all Buddhas emerge from within;
nets of *maṇi* jewels and clusters of precious bells manifest therein all the adornments of the oceans of worlds;

clouds of *maṇi* jewels cover its surface, and these clouds universally manifest the Flower Treasury World (*Kusumatalagarbha*), Vairocana, the transformation Buddhas of the ten directions, and the miraculous deeds of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, it emits wondrous sounds, extolling the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time;
from within that fragrant water, clouds of light-flames of all kinds of jewels constantly emerge, continuing without interruption.
"If explained in detail, each and every river possesses adornments as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to reiterate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"Pure fragrant streams fill the great rivers, With adamantine, wondrous jewels forming their banks."
Jeweled powder forms wheels spread across the ground; all manner of adornments are exquisitely fine.
Rows of jeweled stairways are wondrously decorated, and the surrounding railings are entirely magnificent.
Pearls serve as the foundation for various floral ornaments, while diverse necklaces and garlands hang down together.
The precious light of fragrant waters is pure in color, constantly emitting mani-jewels that flow forth in rapid competition;
as various flowers sway with the waves, they all play musical sounds proclaiming the wondrous Dharma.
Fine powdered sandalwood forms the mud and silt, while all manner of exquisite jewels swirl together in eddies;
clouds of fragrance from the treasury of perfumes spread within, emitting flames and flowing scents that pervade everywhere.
Within the river, various wondrous jewels are born, all emitting radiant light of blazing colors;
these lights spread their shadows to form pedestals and seats, complete with flower canopies and pearl necklaces.
Within the mani-jewel king, the Buddha-body appears; its radiance universally illumines the lands of the ten directions.
Taking this as a wheel to adorn the ground, the fragrant waters reflect with clarity and are ever full.
With nets of mani-jewels and bells of gold, they cover the fragrant rivers and proclaim the Buddha’s voice;
they fully declare all paths to enlightenment, as well as the wondrous practices of Samantabhadra.
The mani-jewel of the Jewel Shore is utterly pure, Constantly emitting the sounds of the Tathāgata’s original vows;
All that the Buddhas of the past have practiced, Those sounds proclaim everywhere, causing all to see it.
From every place where whirlpools form in that river, Bodhisattvas constantly emerge like clouds;
they travel to all vast buddha-fields, filling them entirely until the very limits of the Dharma-realm.
Kings of pure jewels spread like clouds, completely covering all fragrant rivers;
these jewels, equal to the mark between a Buddha’s eyebrows, brilliantly manifest the images of all Buddhas.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
The lands between these various rivers of fragrant water are all adorned with various kinds of exquisite jewels; each one has as many [adornments] as there are atoms in the dust of four continents."
Lotus flowers of white lilies, adorned with various jewels, completely filled the surroundings, each numbering as many as the atoms within the four continents;

rows of jewel-trees stood in orderly succession, from each tree constantly emerging clouds of all manner of adornments, while sovereign mani-jewels shone amidst them, and various floral fragrances filled every place.
Furthermore, those trees produced subtle and wondrous sounds, proclaiming the great vows cultivated by all Tathāgatas throughout all kalpas.
Furthermore, various kinds of sovereign maṇi-jewel kings were scattered, filling the ground. They were as follows: the sovereign maṇi-jewel king of lotus wheels;

the sovereign maṇi-jewel king of fragrant flame-light clouds; the sovereign maṇi-jewel king of various adornments; the sovereign maṇi-jewel king that manifests inconceivable colors of adornment; the sovereign maṇi-jewel king of the sun-bright garment treasury; the sovereign maṇi-jewel king of light-net clouds that universally hang down throughout the ten directions; the sovereign maṇi-jewel king that manifests the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas; the sovereign maṇi-jewel king that manifests the ocean of karmic retributions of all sentient beings... such as these, numbering as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
"Between those rivers of fragrant water, every single spot of ground is fully endowed with such adornments.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The ground is level and utterly pure, Adorned with both true gold and mani-jewels."
Rows of trees shade the area within, their towering trunks and drooping branches bearing flowers like clouds.
Their branches are adorned with exquisite jewels, and the flaming blossoms form wheels of light that shine in the four directions.
Jeweled mani fruits are spread out like clouds, allowing them to be constantly seen throughout the ten directions.
The ground is entirely covered with mani-jewels, adorned together with various flowers and precious powders;
furthermore, palaces are fashioned from mani-jewels, all manifesting the reflections of sentient beings.
The maṇi-kings, images of all Buddhas, are scattered everywhere across the ground without exception;
thus they blaze forth throughout the ten directions, and within every single atom, a Buddha is seen.
Exquisitely adorned with jewels, beautifully arranged, Interspersed with networks of pearl lamps;
Everywhere there are mani wheels, Each manifesting the supernatural powers of the Buddha.

Adorned with myriad jewels, they radiate great light; within that light, emanated Buddhas appear everywhere, each traveling in circuit to reach all places without exception, extensively expounding the Dharma through the ten powers.
The exquisite maṇi-jewels and white lotuses fill every body of water;
their various flowers, each distinct from the others, all manifest light that never ceases.
All the adornments existing throughout the three periods of time Are all manifested within the mani fruit;
Their essential nature is unborn and ungraspable— This is the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
Within all the adornments of this land, The vast body of the Tathāgata appears in its entirety;
Yet he neither comes nor goes— All is made visible through the power of the Buddha’s past vows.
Within every single atom of this ground, all the sons of the Buddha practice the Way;
each perceives the lands they are destined to attain in the future, which are entirely pure according to their own inclinations.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
The oceans of worlds of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are adorned with inconceivable magnificence."
Why is this? O Sons of the Buddha!
Every single realm within this Flower Bank Array World-Ocean is adorned with pure merits as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to reiterate this meaning, receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"In every place within this ocean of lands, All are adorned with various jewels;
Blazing flames rise into the sky like clouds, Their light penetrating and constantly pervading all."
Maṇi-jewels emit clouds without end, within which the reflections of the Buddhas of the ten directions appear;
their supernatural transformations never cease for a moment, and all Bodhisattvas have gathered there.
All mani-jewels emanate the Buddha’s voice; That voice is exquisite and inconceivable.
The deeds performed by Vairocana in the past Are constantly heard and seen within these jewels.
The Honored One of Pure Radiant Pervasive Illumination manifests his reflections within every ornament;
surrounded by a multitude of transformed emanations, he pervades all oceans of lands.
All emanated Buddhas are like illusions; their place of origin cannot be found.
Through the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha-realm, they appear thus within all lands.
The Tathāgata’s sovereign deeds of supernatural power pervade all lands throughout the ten directions;
through this pure adornment of the ocean of worlds, everything is seen within the jewels.
All the various transformations throughout the ten directions Are entirely like images within a mirror;
They arise solely through the supernatural powers and the power of vows Practiced by the Tathāgata in the past.
If there are those who can cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra, Entering the ocean of the Bodhisattvas' supreme wisdom,
They are able, within every single atom, To universally manifest their bodies and purify all lands.
Throughout inconceivable billions of great eons, they have attended upon all Tathāgatas;
whatever those Buddhas practiced, they can manifest it all within a single kṣaṇa.
The lands of all Buddhas are like space—ineffable, unborn, and without marks;
yet, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, they universally adorn and purify them, dwelling therein by the power of their original vows.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
What kinds of worlds abide herein?"
I shall now speak.
O Sons of the Buddha!
Within these seas of fragrant water, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, there abide world-systems as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
Within each world-system, there are furthermore worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
O Sons of the Buddha!

Those world-systems within the ocean of worlds each have their own basis of support, each their own shape, each their own essential nature, each their own location, each their own mode of entry, each their own adornment, each their own boundaries, each their own arrangement, each their own non-differentiation, and each their own empowerment by power.

"O Sons of the Buddha! This world-system may rest upon a great lotus-flower ocean; or it may rest upon an ocean of jewel-flowers of boundless colors; or it may rest upon an ocean of precious necklaces from all pearl-treasuries; or it may rest upon an ocean of fragrant water; or it may rest upon an ocean of all flowers; or it may rest upon an ocean of mani-jewel nets; or it may rest upon an ocean of swirling radiant light; or it may rest upon an ocean of bodhisattvas’ precious crowns of adornment; or it may rest upon an ocean of the bodies of various sentient beings; or it may rest upon an ocean of mani-jewels of the voices of all Buddhas... "
If these were explained in detail, they would be as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
"O Children of the Buddha!

All those world-systems may have the shape of Mount Sumeru, or the shape of rivers, or the shape of whirlpools, or the shape of eddies, or the shape of wheel-rims, or the shape of sacrificial altars, or the shape of groves of trees, or the shape of multi-storied pavilions, or the shape of mountain banners, or the shape of universal squares, or the shape of embryonic wombs, or the shape of lotus flowers, or the shape of *kharaka* (seats), or the shape of the bodies of sentient beings, or the shape of clouds, or the shape of the primary and secondary marks of all Buddhas, or the shape of perfect radiance, or the shape of various nets of jewels, or the shape of all manner of gates and portals, or the shape of various ornaments...
If these were explained in detail, they would number as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Those various world-systems have, some, the clouds of mani-jewels from the ten directions as their substance; others..."
They have various colored flames as their essence; some have various radiances as their essence;
some have jewel-incense flames as their essence; some have *tārā* flowers adorned with all kinds of jewels as their essence;
some have the images of bodhisattvas as their essence; or some have the radiances of the Buddhas as their essence. Or...
Some take the physical marks of a Buddha as their essence; some take the light of a single jewel as their essence;
some take the light of many jewels as their essence; some take the sounds of the ocean of merit of all sentient beings as their essence;
some take the sounds of the ocean of karmic actions of all sentient beings as their essence; or some take a single... [as their essence].
It has as its essence the pure sounds of the realm of all Buddhas; or it has as its essence the sounds of the ocean of great vows of all Bodhisattvas;
or it has as its essence the sounds of the skillful means of all Buddhas;
or it has as its essence the sounds of the formation and disintegration of the adornments of all lands; or it has as its essence the infinite...
The essence of the Buddha’s voice consists of the sounds of the Buddhas; or it may consist of the transformative voices of all Buddhas;
or it may consist of the virtuous voices of all sentient beings; or it may consist of the pure voices from the ocean of merits of all Buddhas...
"If these were to be explained in detail, they would be as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The world-systems are firm and wonderfully adorned, Vast, pure treasuries of radiant light."
Some abide resting upon oceans of lotus jewels, while others dwell upon seas of fragrance and the like;
shaped like Mount Sumeru, cities, trees, or sacrificial altars, all these world-systems pervade the ten directions.
With various ornaments and distinct forms, each is arrayed and established in its own place.
Some have as their substance pure radiance, Or are flower-treasuries and jewel-clouds;
Some world-systems are formed from flames, Abiding in indestructible maṇi treasuries.
Lamp-clouds, flame-paintings, and radiant light, Various and boundless pure colors,
Or some whose essence consists of speech and sound— These are the inconceivable manifestations expounded by the Buddha.
Or these sounds may emerge from the power of vows, having the nature of miraculous transformations;
the sounds of the great meritorious deeds of all sentient beings, and the sounds of the Buddha’s virtues, are likewise so.
Each distinct gate of the world-systems is inconceivable and inexhaustible;
thus they pervade all ten directions, manifesting their divine power through vast adornments.
All the vast lands throughout the ten directions Come entirely into this world-system;
Though one sees them all entering therein, In truth, there is neither coming nor entering.
A single world-system enters into all, and all enter into one without exception;
their essence and characteristics remain as they were, without distinction—unequaled and immeasurable, they pervade everywhere.
Within every atom of all lands, the Tathāgata is universally seen;
with a sea of vows and a voice like the roll of thunder, he brings all sentient beings to complete subdual.
The Buddha’s body pervades all lands, And countless bodhisattvas likewise fill them.
The Tathāgata is sovereign and peerless, Universally transforming all sentient beings.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
These incalculable oceans of fragrant water, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many buddha-fields, abide within the Flower Bank Adorned World-Ocean, distributed like the net of Indra."
O Sons of the Buddha!
This central sea of fragrant water is named Boundless Light of Wondrous Flowers;
its floor consists of mani-jewel king banners that manifest the forms of all bodhisattvas.
A great lotus emerges, named Adorned by All Fragrant Maṇi Kings;
upon it rests a world-system named:

The blazing jewel-light universally illumines the ten directions; it has all manner of ornaments as its substance, within which are arrayed worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
At its very bottom is a world named Supreme Light Pervading All, bounded by a radiant wheel adorned with all kinds of vajras, resting upon a bed of various jewel-maṇi flowers;

its shape is like that of a maṇi gem, completely covered above by clouds of adornments of all precious flowers, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, each abiding in various ways and adorned in various ways; the Buddha’s name is:
Pure Eye, Lamp Free from Defilement:
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Various Fragrant Lotus Wondrous Adornments;
it has all manner of ornaments as its boundary and rests upon a network of precious lotuses.

Its form was like a lion throne, completely covered above by clouds of jeweled canopies in the colors of all precious gems; it was surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within two buddha-fields, and the Buddha’s name was Lion Light Supreme Illumination.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Universal Illumination Adorned with All Jewels, bounded by wheels of fragrant wind and resting upon various jewel-flower necklaces;

it is octagonal in shape, covered above by clouds of sun-discs of exquisite light and the sun-like face of Maṇicūḍa, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in three buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:
Pure Light Wisdom Supreme Banner.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field,
there is a world named Adorned with Various Radiant Flowers, bounded by all kinds of jewel kings and resting upon an ocean of multicolored vajra-śīla banners.
Its form is like a mani-lotus, covered above by clouds of light from vajra-maṇi jewels, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within four buddha-fields;
it is purely and entirely pure, and the Buddha’s name is Vajraprabhāpramāṇavīryasudarsana.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Universally Radiating Sublime Flower Light, bounded by a network adorned with all kinds of precious bells, resting upon an ocean of jewel-wheel networks adorned with all manner of forests;

its shape is generally square with many corners, covered above by clouds of Brahma-sound mani-kings, and surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in five buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:
Beyond this ocean of the power of joy from fragrant light, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field,
there is a world named Pure and Wondrous Radiance, bounded by banners adorned with jewel-kings and resting upon an ocean of diamond palaces.
Its shape is square, covered above by clouds of mani-jewel wheel-topknot canopies, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in six buddha-fields;
the Buddha’s name is Universal Light Sovereign Banner.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, there is a world named Adorned with the Flames of Various Flowers, which has various flower adornments for its boundaries and rests upon an ocean of flames of all jewel colors;

its shape is like that of a multi-storied pavilion, covered above by clouds of railings made of pearls and garments of all jewel colors, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in seven Buddha-fields, being purely and entirely serene. The Buddha’s name is:
Joyful Ocean of Merit Renowned Sovereign Light.
Above this, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field,

there is a world named Ground of Manifesting Majestic Power, which has a boundary adorned with all-sound-producing mani-kings and rests upon an ocean of space supported by lotus seats of various jewel colors;
Its form was like Indra’s net, covered above by clouds of flower-nets of infinite colors, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within eight buddha-fields;
the Buddha’s name was Vast Renown Wisdom-Ocean Banner.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Producing Exquisite Sounds.
It is bounded by a wheel adorned with mind-king *maṇi* jewels and rests upon an ocean of *maṇi* jewel kings adorned with clouds that constantly emit all exquisite sounds.

Its shape is like the body of Brahmā, covered above by clouds of lion thrones adorned with immeasurable jewels, and it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in nine buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:
The mark of the pure moonlight is invincible. Above this,
past worlds as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, there is a world named Vajradhvaja,
bounded by pearl-treasury jewel necklaces of infinite adornment, resting upon a sea of maṇi-jewels that serve as lion-thrones of all-encompassing adornment.

Its form was perfectly circular, covered above by clouds of *sumeru*-like fragrant *maṇi* flowers as numerous as the atoms in ten *sumeru* mountains; it was surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, being purely and entirely serene.
The Buddha’s name was Supreme King of the Ocean of All Dharmas.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Constantly Manifesting Sapphire Radiance, which has a boundary adorned with indestructible, most firm diamond and rests upon an ocean of various extraordinary flowers;

its shape is like that of a half-moon, covered above by clouds of celestial jewel canopies, and surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in eleven buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:
Infinite Meritorious Qualities. Beyond this,
past worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, there is a world named Radiant Illumination,
bounded by Universal Light Adornments and resting upon a sea of fragrant water called Flower-Swirl.
It is shaped like a swirling flower, covered above by clouds of various garments, and surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in twelve buddha-fields;
the Buddha’s name is Transcending Śakra and Brahmā.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, one reaches this world named Sahā.
It has a boundary adorned with vajras and rests upon a lotus net supported by wind-circles of various colors;

its form is like space, covered above by clouds of celestial palaces that adorn the void with universal perfection, and it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within thirteen buddha-fields. Its Buddha is the World-Honored One, Vairocana Tathāgata.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Tranquil Light Free from Dust, bounded by all manner of jewel adornments and resting upon an ocean of various precious garments;

its shape is like that of Vajrapāṇi, covered above by diamond clouds of boundless colors, and surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in fourteen buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:
Universal Sound of the Dharma Realm.
Above this, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field,
there is a world named Lamp of All Wondrous Radiance, which has canopies of every kind of adornment as its boundary and rests upon a sea of pure flower-nets.
Its shape is like that of a svastika, covered above by clouds of mani-tree fragrant water seas, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in fifteen buddha-fields;
it is purely and entirely pure, and the Buddha’s name is Indestructible Power Universally Shining Banner.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Pure Light Shining Everywhere, bounded by inexhaustible jewel-cloud maṇi-kings and resting upon a sea of various fragrant-flame lotuses;

its shape is like that of a tortoise shell, covered above by a cloud of round-light maṇi-wheels and sandalwood, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in sixteen buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:
Pure Sun of Meritorious Eyes: Above this,
past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Jewel Adornment Treasury,
which has mani-kings in the forms of all sentient beings as its boundaries and rests upon an ocean of light-treasury mani-kings.

Its shape is octagonal, covered above by a network of jewel-adorned flowering trees from all the Cakravāḍa mountains; it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in seventeen buddha-fields.
The Buddha’s name is Unobstructed Wisdom Light Shining Throughout the Ten Directions.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Free from Dust, which has all manner of exquisite marks as its boundary and rests upon an ocean of lion thrones made of various wonderful flowers;

it is shaped like a pearl necklace and is covered above by clouds of radiant halos from all kinds of precious fragrant mani-kings, surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in eighteen buddha-fields, being purely and entirely serene. The Buddha’s name is:
Above this world-system of the Supreme Banner of Immeasurable Expedient Means, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field,

there is a world named Pure Light Shining Everywhere, bounded by mani-kings that produce inexhaustible clouds of jewels, and resting upon a Mount Sumeru ocean of mountains with infinite colors, fragrances, and flames.

Its form is like precious flowers arranged in spirals, covered above by a canopy of infinite-colored radiant *maṇi* kings and sapphire clouds; it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in nineteen buddha-fields.
The Buddha’s name is Universal Illumination of the Dharma Realm and Space Light.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Wondrous Jewel Flame.
It has the jewel of the sun and moon of universal radiance as its boundary and rests upon an ocean of *maṇi* jewels in the forms of all the devas.

Its shape is like a precious ornament, covered above by clouds of banners of all kinds of jewel-garments and by nets of *maṇi*-lamp treasuries; it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in twenty buddha-fields, being purely and entirely serene. The Buddha’s name is:
The Radiance of the Marks of Merit.
