In this world-system called Blazing Jewel Radiance Illuminating the Ten Directions, there are as many vast worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, each with its own basis of support, its own shape, its own essential nature, its own orientation, its own mode of entry, its own adornment, its own boundaries, its own arrangement, its own lack of distinction, and its own power of sustaining grace, all surrounding it on every side."
That is to say:
worlds shaped like ten buddha-field-microdust atoms of revolving forms; worlds shaped like ten buddha-field-microdust atoms of rivers;
worlds shaped like ten buddha-field-microdust atoms of whirlpools; worlds shaped like ten buddha-field-microdust atoms... [and so forth].
Worlds shaped like wheel-rims as numerous as the atoms in a mote of dust; worlds shaped like ritual altars as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds shaped like groves of trees as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds shaped like multi-storied pavilions as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds shaped like banners of ethical discipline (*śīla*) as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; and worlds [shaped like... as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
Worlds shaped like universal squares, as numerous as atoms; worlds shaped like wombs, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds shaped like lotuses, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds shaped like *kharaka* (a type of vessel), as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
and worlds shaped like various sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
Worlds shaped like the physical forms of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds shaped like circular halos as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds shaped like clouds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds shaped like nets as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds shaped like gateways as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields...
Such as these, they are as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
Each of these worlds is surrounded on all sides by ten times the number of vast worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field.
In each of these worlds, there are further world-systems, as numerous as the atoms described above, serving as their retinues.
All these aforementioned worlds are situated within this Boundless Exquisite Flower Light Sea of Fragrant Water, as well as within the rivers of fragrant water that surround this sea.

its shape is like the svastika, it rests upon an ocean of jewel-cloth banners, it is completely covered by clouds of canopies adorned with all kinds of flowers, and it is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in nine buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:

its shape is like the svastika, it rests upon a sea of jewel-kings in the form of Śakra, it is completely covered by clouds of sun-bright lotus flowers, and it is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in eleven buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:

its shape is like that of an asura body, it rests upon a sea of vajra lotuses, and it is completely covered above by clouds of light and shadow from jeweled crowns. It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in fifteen buddha-fields, and the Buddha’s name is:

past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Candanacandra;

its shape is like a swirling eddy of fragrant water, resting upon an ocean of boundless colored jewel-lights, covered above by clouds of exquisite fragrance and radiance, surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in seventeen buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is:

The Buddha’s name is Lamp Universally Illuminating Space.

it has as its essence the sounds of the ocean of all Buddhas' virtues.

the Buddha’s name is Ocean of Merit of the Radiance of Impartial Wisdom.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Banner of Inexhaustible Light Adornments;

it is shaped like a lotus and rests upon an ocean of all-jeweled nets, with a net of lotus-light mani jewels covering its surface. It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in twenty buddha-fields and is purely and entirely serene. The Buddha’s name is:
The Pure Radiance of the Dharma Realm.

Within these seas of fragrant water, as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, there are world-systems as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields. All of them rest upon lotuses adorned with mani-jewel king banners that manifest the forms of all bodhisattvas; each has its own uninterrupted boundaries of adornment, each emits light of jewel-like colors, each is covered by clouds of light, each possesses its own array of ornaments, each has its own distinct eon, each has its own appearance of a buddha, each has its own ocean of Dharma being expounded, each is filled everywhere with sentient beings, each is universally entered from the ten directions, and each is sustained by the spiritual power of all buddhas."
Within each of these world-systems, all worlds rest upon various adornments and are joined together in succession to form a world-net;
these are established throughout the Flower Bank Adornment World-Ocean in all their diverse distinctions.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power and spoke in verse:
“The Flower Treasury World-Ocean, Equal to the Dharma-realm and without distinction,
Its adornments are supremely pure, Abiding peacefully within space.”
Within this ocean of world-systems, the arrays of lands are inconceivable;
each is sovereign and individually distinct, without any confusion.
In the Flower Treasury Ocean of World-Systems, the arrays of lands are perfectly and beautifully disposed.
With diverse forms and various adornments, their myriad characteristics differ.
The transformative voices of all Buddhas take on various essences;
according to the power of karma, one perceives the wondrously adorned arrays of the world-systems.
The net-like city of Mount Sumeru, circular in shape like a swirling wheel of water,
with vast lotuses in full bloom, each surrounding the other;
shaped like mountain banners and pavilions, and revolving in the form of vajras.
Thus are these inconceivable and vast clusters of lands;
The ocean-like pearls and flames, And the inconceivable nets of light—
All such clusters of lands Reside within the lotus.
In each and every world-system, nets of light are beyond description;
within those lights, myriad lands appear, pervading the oceans of the ten directions.
All the ornaments possessed by every world-system—
All lands enter therein, universally seen without end;
The inconceivable clusters of realms, the boundless worlds,
Adorned with various wondrous beauties— all arise through the power of the Great Sage.
Within all the systems of world-systems, the worlds are inconceivable:
some are forming, some are disintegrating, and some have already perished.
Just as with the leaves in a forest, there is both growth and falling.
Within such world-systems, worlds undergo formation and destruction.
Just as there are various distinctions among fruits depending on a forest,
so too do various sentient beings dwell depending upon these world-systems.
Just as seeds differ, The fruits they produce are each distinct;
Because of the differences in the power of karma, The lands of sentient beings are not the same.
Just as with the wish-fulfilling jewel, the mind-king, Various forms appear according to the mind.
Because the minds of sentient beings are pure, They are able to see pure lands.
Just as a great dragon king Raises clouds that pervade the void,
So too, by the power of the Buddha's vows, Are all these lands brought forth.
Just as a magician’s spells can manifest all manner of things, so too,
through the power of the karma of sentient beings, lands are inconceivable.
They are like various painted images, created by a master painter.
All such lands are created by the mind as their painter.
The bodies of sentient beings differ from one another, arising according to the mind’s conceptualizations.
These various kinds of lands are all without exception produced by karma.
Just as one sees a guide manifesting various distinct forms according to the mental activities of sentient beings, so too does one see all lands.
At the boundaries of all these lands, nets of lotuses are spread everywhere.
With various and diverse characteristics, their adornments are all pure.
Those nets of lotuses are the locus where the networks of lands abide;
they possess various kinds of adornments and are the dwellings of various kinds of sentient beings.
In some buddha-fields, there are rugged terrains that are treacherous and uneven;
due to the afflictions of sentient beings, they perceive them in such a way.
There are immeasurable varieties of fields, both defiled and pure.
Arising in accordance with the minds of sentient beings, sustained by the power of the Bodhisattvas;
in some lands there is defilement and in others purity—
these arise through the power of karma, yet they are the transformations of the Bodhisattvas.
There are lands that emit radiance, Composed of stainless jewels and adorned with various wonders, Which all Buddhas cause to be purified.
Within each and every seed of a land, The kalpa-conflagrations are inconceivable.
Though what appears may be ruined or evil, its locus is always firm and solid.
Through the karmic power of sentient beings, many buddha-fields are produced;
they rest upon the wind-circle and abide supported by the water-circle.
Such is the nature of the world: various views differ, yet in reality there is no arising, nor is there any destruction.
Within each and every thought-moment, immeasurable lands are produced.
By the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, all are seen as pure and stainless.
There are lands formed of clay, their substance extremely hard and rigid;
they are shrouded in darkness without light, the dwelling place of those who perform evil deeds.
There are lands formed of vajra, defiled by great sorrow and fear;
where suffering abounds and joy is scarce, they are the dwelling places of those with meager merit.
Some are made of iron, or fashioned from red copper.
The rocky mountains are perilous and fearsome, filled with those who have committed evil deeds.
Within this world-system are hells, where sentient beings suffer without rescue;
they dwell perpetually in darkness, scorched by the blazing ocean of flames.
Or there are animals with various hideous forms;
due to their own evil karma, they constantly undergo all manner of suffering and affliction.
Or one sees the realm of Yama, tormented and oppressed by hunger and thirst.
Ascending great volcanic mountains, they undergo various most grievous sufferings.
Yet there are some lands composed of the seven treasures, with various kinds of palaces; these are obtained through pure karma.
You should observe the world, wherein humans and devas,
having accomplished the fruits of pure karma, experience happiness according to the season.
Within each and every pore, there are inconceivable billions of lands.
Adorned with various marks, it is never cramped or narrow.
According to the individual karma of sentient beings, worlds are of infinite kinds;
therein they give rise to grasping and attachment, experiencing different forms of suffering and joy.
There are lands formed of various jewels, constantly emitting boundless light;
adorned with wondrous diamond lotuses, they are pure and stainless.
There are lands whose very substance is light, abiding supported by circles of radiance.
Golden sandalwood incense, with clouds of flames illuminating everywhere;
there are lands formed like lunar discs, where fragrant robes are spread all around,
and within each lotus flower, bodhisattvas completely fill it.
There are lands formed of myriad jewels, Their forms and colors free from all defilement;
Like the net of the Lord of Devas, Their radiance shines forever.
There are lands whose substance is fragrance, Or perhaps they consist of diamond flowers.
The forms of mani-jewel light and shadow are observed with extreme purity.
There are inconceivable lands, accomplished through revolving flowers,
filled entirely with transformation buddhas and bodhisattvas of universal radiance.
There are some pure lands where all are trees of various flowers;
their wondrous branches spread across the site of enlightenment, shaded by clouds of mani-jewels.
There are lands illuminated by pure light, formed from vajra-flowers.
There is this emanated voice of the Buddha, Forming an infinite web of sounds.
Some lands are like Bodhisattvas, Or like crowns of exquisite maṇi jewels;
Others have the shape of thrones, All emerging from emanated radiance.
Or perhaps from sandalwood powder, or from the light between the eyebrows,
or from sounds within the Buddha’s radiance, this wondrous land was formed.
Some see a pure land adorned with a single ray of light.
Some see many adornments, all of them wondrous and marvelous;
some use the exquisite objects of ten lands as ornaments,
while others use everything within a thousand lands for their decoration.
Or using the substances of billions of lands to adorn a single realm,
with various features that differ from one another, all appearing like reflections;
or using the substances of unspeakably many lands to adorn a single land.
Each emits its own radiance, arising through the power of the Tathāgata’s vows.
There are some lands that have been purified by the power of his vows;
within all these adornments, one universally beholds oceans of myriad realms.
All those who cultivate the vows of Samantabhadra Attain pure buddha-lands;
The adornments of the lands of the three periods of time Are all manifested therein.
O Son of the Buddha, you should observe The majestic spiritual power of these world-systems.
All future lands, as numerous as dreams, he causes them all to see;
The worlds of the ten directions and the oceans of past lands,
All appear within a single moment, like manifested illusions.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time, And all their lands,
Are entirely seen within a single world-system;
Through the spiritual power of all Buddhas, Multitudes of lands appear within a single atom.
All these various forms are clearly seen, Like shadows, they lack true reality.
There may be many lands, Shaped like the great ocean,
Or like Mount Sumeru— Worlds that are inconceivable.
There are lands well-established, their forms like Indra’s net,
or shaped like groves of trees, filled with Buddhas;
some take the form of jewel wheels, while others have the appearance of lotuses.
The eight corners are adorned with various ornaments, all of them utterly pure.
Some have the shape of a seat, others are triangular;
some resemble a *kharaka*, others the city walls or the body of Brahmā.
Some are like the crest of the Lord of Devas; some are like a half-moon;
some are like Mount Maṇi; some have the shape of the solar disc.
Some have the form of a world-system, resembling the swirling of a fragrant ocean.
Some take the form of circles of light, as those formerly purified by the Buddhas;
some have the shape of rims, some the shape of altars;
some resemble the *ūrṇā* hair-tuft, the *uṣṇīṣa*, or the broad, long eyes.
Some are like the hand of a Buddha, some like a vajra, or like the shape of a mountain of flames; Bodhisattvas pervade them all.
Some are like the form of a lion, or like the shape of a sea oyster.
Infinite varieties of forms and appearances, Each with its own distinct essential nature;
Within a single world-system, The shapes of worlds are inexhaustible.
All arise through the power of the Buddha’s vows, And by his protective mindfulness, they abide in peace.
There are lands that endure for one kalpa, Or endure for ten kalpas,
even exceeding A hundred thousand kalpas, as numerous as the atoms of a realm.
Within a single kalpa, One may see a land undergo formation and destruction.
Some are immeasurable and innumerable, even unto the inconceivable.
Some lands have Buddhas, some lands have no Buddhas;
some have but a single Buddha, while others have immeasurable Buddhas.
If there is no Buddha in this land, a Buddha from another world-system will manifest through transformation to perform all the wondrous deeds:
descending from heaven, entering the womb, and being born.
Having subdued Māra and attained perfect enlightenment, you turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma.
According to the inclinations and joys of sentient beings' minds, you manifest various forms;
in order to turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, you respond to all their faculties and desires.
In each and every buddha-field, a single Buddha appears in the world and,
for billions of years, expounds the unsurpassed Dharma.
Yet sentient beings who are not vessels for the Dharma are unable to see these Buddhas.
If there are those with a joyful mind, they shall see [the Buddhas] in all places.
Within each and every land, a Buddha arises in the world;
in all these lands, the number of Buddhas is incalculable, beyond thought.
Within this, each and every Buddha manifests immeasurable miraculous transformations,
pervading the entire dharma-realm to tame the ocean of sentient beings.
There are lands without light, shrouded in darkness and filled with many terrors.
The touch of suffering is like swords and blades; those who behold it are naturally pained by its venom.
There are the lights of various devas, the lights of palaces, or the radiance of the sun and moon—the net of worlds is inconceivable.
There are lands with self-radiance, or where trees emit pure light;
there is never any suffering or affliction, due to the power of the merit of sentient beings.
There are some with the radiance of mountains, and others with the light of mani-jewels.
Some are illuminated by the light of lamps, all through the power of the karma of sentient beings;
some possess the radiance of a Buddha, with Bodhisattvas filling their midst;
some have the light of lotus flowers, the color of their flames most majestic and beautiful.
Some lands are illuminated by the light of flowers, some by the light of fragrant waters;
they are illuminated by ointments and incense, all through the power of pure vows.
Some are illuminated by the light of clouds, and some by the light of mani-jewel oysters.
The Buddha’s supernormal power illuminates with light, able to proclaim sounds that gladden the mind.
Sometimes it shines with the light of jewels, or sometimes with the flames of vajra;
this pure sound can resound afar, and wherever it reaches, there is no suffering.
Some emit the light of mani-jewels, some the light of ornaments,
and others the radiance of the site of enlightenment, illuminating the midst of the assembly.
The Buddha emits a great light, within which transformation Buddhas fill the space.
That light shines universally, pervading the entire dharma-realm.
There are lands most terrifying, where there are sounds of wailing and great suffering;
those sounds are so piercingly agonizing that all who hear them give rise to loathing and fear.
In the realms of hell and animals, And in the abode of Yama,
This turbid and evil world Constantly produces sounds of sorrow and suffering.
Yet in some lands, There are always sounds of delight that emerge.
Delightful and compliant with his teachings— this is obtained through pure karma.
In some lands, one constantly hears the voice of Śakra,
or the voice of Brahmā, or the voices of all the lords of the world.
In some buddha-fields, wondrous sounds emerge from the clouds;
jeweled oceans, mani trees, and the resonance of music fill them all.
Within the circular halos of the Buddhas, emanated voices flow on without end.
And the wondrous voices of Bodhisattvas, heard throughout the lands of the ten directions;
the sound of the universal turning of the Wheel of Dharma in inconceivable realms;
the sounds emerging from the ocean of vows; and the sounds of the wondrous voices of spiritual practice.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time, Arising in all worlds,
Are fully endowed with their names, And their voices are inexhaustible.
In some lands, one hears The sounds of the power of all Buddhas.
The stages, the perfections, and the immeasurables—such dharmas as these are all proclaimed.
By the power of Samantabhadra’s vows, a wondrous sound is uttered across billions of lands;
like the roar of thunder, that sound continues without end throughout the kalpas.
In a pure land, the Buddha manifests the voice of mastery;
throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions, there is nothing that does not hear it.
—From the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Ten.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Scroll Eleven, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Six: Vairocana. Chapter Six: Vairocana.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!
In the distant past, beyond world-microdust numbers of kalpas, and even twice that number, there was an ocean of worlds named:
Universal Gate Pure Radiance.

Within this ocean of worlds, there is a world named Supreme Sound, which rests upon an ocean of mani-flower nets and has as its retinue as many worlds as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru. Its shape is perfectly circular, and its ground possesses infinite adornments. It is surrounded by three hundred tiers of wheels of jewel-trees and Ringing Mountains, all covered above by clouds of every kind of treasure. Pure and stainless, it shines with brilliant light; its cities and palaces are like Mount Sumeru, and clothing and food arrive according to one's thoughts. The eon is named:
Various Adornments.
"O Children of the Buddha!
In that world of Supreme Sound, there is a sea of fragrant water named:
Pure and radiant,
within that ocean there appeared a great Flower Sumeru Mountain named Banner of Universal Adornment with Flower Flames, surrounded on all sides by railings made of ten kinds of jewels.
Upon that mountain, there was a great forest named Maṇipuṣpabhañjīcakra;
immeasurable flowered pavilions and immeasurable jeweled terraces were arrayed all around it.
Infinite banners of exquisite fragrance and infinite banners of jewel-mountains were most exquisitely adorned;
infinite jewel *pundarīka* flowers bloomed in profusion everywhere;
and infinite nets of fragrant *maṇi* lotuses hung down and spread all around.
The sounds of music were harmonious and pleasing, and clouds of fragrance shone brilliantly; each was immeasurable in number, beyond all reckoning.
There were hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of cities surrounding it on all sides, where various kinds of sentient beings dwelt.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
To the east of this grove is a great city named Flaming Radiance,
the capital of a human king, surrounded on all sides by a hundred trillion nayutas of cities;
It was established from pure and wondrous jewels, measuring seven thousand yojanas in both length and breadth;
its courtyards were made of the seven treasures, with watchtowers and battlements all most magnificent and beautiful;
there were seven tiers of jewel moats, filled to the brim with fragrant water.
Utpala flowers, padma flowers, kumuda flowers, and puṇḍarīka flowers—all made of various jewels—are distributed everywhere as adornments;
jeweled tārā trees surround it in seven tiers;
and the palaces and towers are all magnificently adorned with jewels.
Various exquisite nets were spread over it;
scented ointments and scattered flowers rendered its interior fragrant and radiant;
there were hundreds of billions of nayutas of gates, all adorned with jewels.
Before each gate, there were forty-nine jeweled śīla-banners arranged in successive rows.
Furthermore, a hundred trillion gardens and groves surrounded them on all sides;
within them were various kinds of blended incenses and the fragrance of maṇi-trees, which circulated and permeated everywhere.
The various birds warbled in harmony, bringing joy to those who heard them.

All the inhabitants of this great city had fully perfected the supernormal power of karmic fruition; they traveled through the air like the gods, and whatever their hearts desired arrived instantly upon their thought.
To the south of that city, there is a celestial city named Tree-Flower Adornment;
turning clockwise from there, there is a great dragon city named:
Beyond that is a yakṣa city named Vajra-Excellently Sublime Banner;
Next there is a city of gandharvas named Wondrous Palace;
next there is a city of asuras named:
Jewel Wheel;
next there is a garuḍa city named Exquisite Jewel Adornment;
Next there is the city of the kiṃnaras, named Playful Joy;
next there is the city of the mahoragas, named:
Vajradhvaja; next there is the city of the Brahma King named Various Exquisite Adornments...
There were as many as hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of such cities.
Each of these cities was surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of multi-storied pavilions, each of which possessed immeasurable adornments.
"O Sons of the Buddha! Within this Great Forest of Jewel Flower Branch Wheels, there is a site of enlightenment named Jewel Flower Universal Illumination.

It is adorned with the distribution of various great jewels; wheels of mani flowers are everywhere in full bloom; incense lamps are lit; clouds of flames in the colors of all kinds of jewels completely cover it; nets of light shine everywhere; various ornaments constantly produce exquisite jewels; among all the musical instruments, elegant sounds are perpetually played; the king of mani jewels manifests the body of a bodhisattva; and various wonderful flowers pervade the ten directions."
Before his site of enlightenment, there was a great ocean named Fragrant Maṇi-Vajra;
from it emerged a great lotus flower named:

The calyxes and flames of these lotuses form wheels; each flower is vast, measuring ten billion *yojanas* in breadth. Their stalks, leaves, filaments, and pedestals are all composed of wondrous jewels. Ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of lotuses surround them, constantly emitting radiance and perpetually producing sublime sounds that pervade the ten directions.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
In that world of Supreme Sound, during its first eon, there appeared in the world as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in ten Mount Sumerus."
The first Buddha was named Sarvaguṇaparvata-sumeru-jaya-megha.
O Sons of the Buddha!
It should be known that when that Buddha was about to appear, one hundred years prior, this great forest of Maṇi-flower branches and wheels was entirely adorned and pervasively pure.
That is to say:
they emit clouds of inconceivable jewel-flames, uttering sounds that praise the Buddha’s merits and manifesting the vocal tones of countless Buddhas;
they extend light and spread nets, completely covering the ten directions.
The palaces and towers illuminated one another;
the radiance of precious flowers rose and gathered into clouds.

Furthermore, they emitted sublime sounds, proclaiming the vast roots of goodness cultivated by all sentient beings in their past lives, reciting the names of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, expounding the ultimate path of the vows and practices cultivated by all Bodhisattvas, and articulating the various words used by all Tathāgatas as they turn the wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
By manifesting such signs of adornment, he revealed that the Tathāgata was about to appear in the world.
Because all the kings within that world beheld these signs, their roots of goodness ripened, and they all desired to see the Buddha, coming thus to the site of enlightenment.
At that time, the Buddha Supreme Cloud of Mount Sumeru of All Merits suddenly appeared within a great lotus flower at his site of enlightenment.
His body was all-pervasive, equal to the true Dharma-realm; he manifested birth in all buddha-fields and proceeded to every site of enlightenment.
He possessed boundless wondrous colors and was perfectly pure.
Throughout all worlds, none can outshine or surpass him;
endowed with the marks of myriad jewels, each distinct and luminous, the images of all palaces appear within them.
All sentient beings behold with their own eyes boundless transformation Buddhas emerging from his body, as various colored lights fill the world.

Just as he manifested his body and sat upon a seat atop Mount Sumeru, adorned with banners of flower-flames, within the Great Forest of Mani Flower Branches in this Pure Luminous Fragrant Water Ocean;
so too did he manifest his body and sit upon all sixty-eight thousand billion peaks of Mount Sumeru throughout that World of Supreme Sound.
At that time, that Buddha immediately emitted a great light from between his eyebrows;

this light was named "Sound that Arouses All Roots of Goodness," with as many subsidiary lights as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields accompanying it, filling all lands throughout the ten directions.

If there are sentient beings who should be tamed, when they are touched by this light, they immediately awaken of their own accord; they extinguish the heat of all delusions, tear asunder the net of all hindrances, shatter the mountains of all obstructions, purify all turbid defilements, give rise to great faith and understanding, and produce supreme roots of goodness. They forever leave behind all hardships and terrors, eliminate all physical and mental suffering and affliction, give birth to the mind that beholds the Buddha, and advance toward omniscience.

At that time, the lords of all worlds, together with their retinues numbering in the hundreds of thousands, having been awakened by the light of the Buddha, all went to where the Buddha was and prostrated themselves at his feet.
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Within that great city of Blazing Radiance, there is a king named Joyful Vision and Good Wisdom (Priyadarśana-suvijña), who governs a million billion nayutas of cities. He has thirty-seven thousand wives and court ladies, with Auspicious Fortune (Puṇya-śrī) as their chief."
According to a separate version, there were five hundred princes—though another text says twenty-five thousand—with Mahātejas as their leader;
Prince Mahātejas had ten thousand consorts, with Sudarśanā as their leader.
At that time, having beheld the Buddha’s radiance, Prince Mahātejas, by the power of the roots of goodness he had previously cultivated, immediately realized ten kinds of Dharma-gates.

What are these ten? They are: attaining the samādhi of the wheel of all Buddhas' merits; attaining the universal gateway dhāraṇī of all Buddha-dharmas; attaining the Prajñāpāramitā of the vast treasury of skillful means; attaining the great adornment of great compassion that subdues all sentient beings; attaining the great compassion of the universal cloud-sound; attaining the supreme mind of great joy that gives rise to boundless merit; attaining the great equanimity that awakens to all phenomena as they truly are; attaining the great supernatural power of the treasury of equality through vast skillful means; attaining the great vow that increases the power of faith and understanding; and attaining the gate of eloquence of the light of universal wisdom.
At that time, having attained such illumination of the Dharma, Prince Mahātejas, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the great assembly and spoke in verse:
“The World-Honored One sits at the site of enlightenment, A pure and great radiance, Like a thousand suns rising, Universally illuminating the realm of space.”
After immeasurable billions of kalpas, a Guide appears only at rare intervals;
now the Buddha has emerged into the world, to be venerated by all.
Behold the Buddha’s radiance and his inconceivable emanated Buddhas.
Within all the palaces, they dwell in tranquil meditative absorption.
Behold the Buddha’s supernormal powers: from his pores emerge clouds of flames that illuminate the world, their radiance never-ending.
You should contemplate the Buddha’s body: its net of light is utterly pure, manifesting forms equal in number to all things, pervading the ten directions.
Its wondrous voice fills the world; all who hear it rejoice.
In accordance with the speech of all sentient beings, they praise the virtues of the Buddha.
Wherever the World-Honored One’s light shines, all sentient beings find peace and happiness;
their sufferings are entirely extinguished, and their hearts give rise to great joy.
Beholding the assembly of bodhisattvas, who have gathered from the ten directions, all emitting clouds of mani-jewels, they stand before the Buddha and offer praise.
From the site of enlightenment, wondrous sounds emerge; these sounds are exceedingly profound and far-reaching.
Able to extinguish the suffering of sentient beings—this is the Buddha’s spiritual power.
All pay him reverence with hearts full of great joy;
together before the World-Honored One, they gaze up at the Dharma King.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
When Prince Mahātejas uttered these verses, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, their sound pervaded the world-system of Jyotirghoṣa."
At that time, King Priyadarśana-Buddhi, having heard these verses, was filled with great joy. He surveyed his retinue and spoke in verse:
“You should quickly assemble The entire multitude of kings, The princes and the great ministers, And the governors of the cities and provinces.”
Proclaim throughout all the cities: "Quickly beat the great drums;
Gather all people together, And go as one to see the Buddha.
At every crossroads, All should ring the precious bells.
Together with his wife and retinue, he went forth to behold the Tathāgata.
All the city walls and moats should be made completely pure;
everywhere erect supreme and wondrous banners, adorned with mani jewels.
Jeweled canopies spread with myriad nets, and celestial music like clouds are arrayed in the void, filling every place.
The roads are all adorned and purified, as wondrous garments rain down everywhere.
Girding yourselves and mounting your precious vehicles, come with me to behold the Buddha.
Each according to their own power, let them rain down ornaments everywhere;
like clouds spreading forth, may they fill the entirety of space.
Auspicious flaming lotus canopies, half-moons, precious necklaces,
and countless exquisite robes— you all should rain these down.
Sumeru mountains, seas of fragrant water, and supreme mani-jewel wheels.
And pure sandalwood, all should rain down to fill the sky.
With various precious flower-garlands, adorned, pure, and stainless,
as well as mani-lamps, let them all abide in the air.
"Everyone shall turn toward the Buddha, their hearts giving rise to great joy;
together with their wives, children, and retinues, they shall go to see the World-Honored One.
At that time, King Priyadarśana-Buddhila, accompanied by thirty-seven thousand queens and court ladies—with Puṇyamaṅgala at their head—[set out].
Five hundred princes were together with him, Mahātejas as their leader;
sixty thousand ministers were together with him, Prajñābala as their leader...
Thus, surrounded before and behind by a multitude of seven hundred and seventy trillion nayutas, they departed from the great city of Jvālāmukha.
By the power of the king, the entire great assembly ascended into the air and proceeded there; all manner of offerings filled the void of space.
Upon reaching the Buddha’s presence, they prostrated at his feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
Furthermore, there was the celestial king Subhūṣitaketu from the city of Supuṣpa, together with ten billion nayutas of retinues;
furthermore, there was the nāga king Viśuddhaprabha from the city of Paramārtha, together with twenty-five billion retinues;
furthermore, there was the yakṣa king Vikramavīra from the city of Vajravijayadhvaja, together with seven hundred and seventy million retinues.
Furthermore, there was the Gandharva King Delightful Vision from the City of Stainless, together with a retinue of nine billion seven hundred million;
furthermore, there was the Asura King Pure-Form Contemplation from the City of Wondrous Wheels, together with a retinue of five billion eight hundred million;
furthermore, there was the Garuḍa King Ten-Power Practice from the City of Wondrous Adornments, together with a retinue of ninety-nine thousand.
Furthermore, there was the Kinnara King Vajraśrī from the city of Līlāsukha, accompanied by eighteen billion followers;
furthermore, there was the Mahoraga King Ratnakīrtidhvaja from the city of Vajradhvaja, accompanied by three hundred thousand nayutas of followers;
furthermore, there was the Brahma King Paramavijaya from the city of Viśuddhasupratimaṇḍita, accompanied by eighteen billion followers...

In this manner, all the kings and their retinues within these hundreds of billions of nayutas of great cities went together to the presence of the Tathāgata Sarvaguṇasumeruśrīmegha, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.

At that time, in order to discipline and transform all sentient beings, that Tathāgata, within the ocean-like assembly of the place of enlightenment, preached the *Sūtra on the Universal Collection of the Sovereign Dharmas of All Buddhas of the Three Times*, with as many *sūtras* as there are atoms in a world serving as its retinue, causing all sentient beings to obtain benefit according to their respective minds.
At that time, having heard this Dharma, the Bodhisattva Mahāteja immediately attained the light of the ocean of Dharma accumulated over past lives by the Buddha Sarvaguṇasumeru-jaya-megha.
That is to say:
the light of wisdom of the samādhi of equality regarding the collection of all dharmas;
the light of wisdom in which all dharmas enter and abide within the initial mind of bodhicitta; and the pure eye of the universal light treasury of the dharma-realm in the ten directions.
The light of wisdom that observes the ocean of great vows of all Buddha-dharmas; the light of wisdom of pure conduct that enters the ocean of boundless merit;
the light of wisdom of the treasury of great power and swiftness that proceeds toward non-retrogression;
the light of wisdom of the wheel of emergence through the power of immeasurable transformations within the dharma-realm; the determination...

The light of wisdom that enters the ocean of the perfection of immeasurable merit; the light of wisdom that understands the ocean of the accomplishment of the adornments of the definitive understanding of all Buddhas;
the light of wisdom that understands the ocean of supernatural powers manifested before all assemblies by the infinite Buddhas of the dharma-realm;
and the light of wisdom that understands the powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas.
The Radiance of Dharma-Knowledge.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahātejaḥprabha, having attained such immeasurable radiance of wisdom, spoke these verses by the Buddha’s majestic power:
“I have heard the Buddha’s wondrous Dharma, And thereby attained the radiance of wisdom.”
By means of this, I behold the World-Honored One’s deeds performed in the past;
in every place of birth, his various names and physical forms,
as well as his making offerings to the Buddhas— all these I see entirely.
In the presence of all Buddhas of the past, They served them all;
through practice for immeasurable eons, They purified oceans of buddha-fields.
They gave away their own bodies, Vast and boundless in extent.
Cultivating the most supreme practices, they adorn and purify the oceans of all lands.
Giving away their ears, noses, heads, hands, feet,
and even their various palaces in measureless quantities, they adorn and purify the oceans of all lands.
In each and every land, throughout inconceivable billions of eons,
they cultivate the practices of enlightenment and adorn the oceans of all lands.
By the power of Samantabhadra’s great vows, within the ocean of all Buddhas,
Practicing immeasurable deeds, I adorn and purify the oceans of all lands.
Just as by the light of the sun one beholds the solar disk itself, so too,
through the light of the Buddha’s wisdom, I behold the path traversed by the Buddhas.
I contemplate the oceans of Buddha-fields, Pure, of great radiance, and tranquil, having realized Bodhi; They pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
May I, like the World-Honored One, Thoroughly purify all these oceans of fields.
"By the Buddha's majestic spiritual power, I shall cultivate the practices for awakening.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahātejaḥprabha, having beheld the Buddha Sarvaguṇaparvatameruśikharābhyudgataśrīmegha..."
Through serving and making offerings, they attained realization of the mind in the presence of the Tathāgata;
for the sake of all worlds, they revealed the ocean of the Tathāgata’s past conduct, revealed the skillful means of the Bodhisattva’s past practices,
revealed the ocean of all Buddhas’ merits, and revealed the universal entry into the purity of the entire Dharma-realm.
Wisdom displays the sovereign power of attaining Buddhahood within all sites of enlightenment;
it displays the Buddha’s powers and fearlessnesses, as well as non-discriminative wisdom; it displays the universal manifestation of the Tathāgata’s body;
it displays inconceivable buddha-miracles; it displays the adornment of immeasurable, pure buddha-lands; it displays universality...
May all the practices and vows of the worthy Bodhisattva cause sentient beings as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru to resolve upon Bodhicitta,
and sentient beings as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field to achieve the pure lands of the Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Buddha Meruśikharadhvaja-sarvaguṇa-gandhottama-cloud spoke these verses for the Bodhisattva Mahātejaḥprabha:
“Excellent, Mahātejaḥprabha, Treasury of merit with far-reaching renown!
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, You have set out upon the path to enlightenment.”
You have attained the light of wisdom, which completely pervades the entire dharma realm;
with both merit and wisdom fully expanded, you shall attain the ocean of profound knowledge.
Practicing within a single buddha-field for as many eons as there are atoms in that field, you shall realize this.
As you have seen me, so shall you attain such wisdom.
Those of inferior practice cannot understand this skillful means;
only by attaining the power of great diligence can one purify the ocean of buddha-fields.
Within each and every atom, practicing for immeasurable eons,
that person is then able to attain the adornment of all Buddha-fields.
For the sake of each and every sentient being, they undergo the cycle of rebirth throughout oceans of kalpas.
With a mind free from weariness or indolence, one shall become a Teacher of the World.
Making offerings to each and every Buddha until the very end of the future,
with a heart never for a moment weary or disheartened, one shall attain the Unsurpassed Way.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time shall together fulfill your vow;
within all the assemblies of the Buddhas, your body shall dwell therein.
All Tathāgatas possess vows that are without limit.
Those who possess great wisdom and thorough penetration can understand this skillful means.
Having made offerings to me with great radiance, they have thereby attained great majestic power,
enabling them to bring beings as numerous as motes of dust to maturity and direct them toward Bodhi.

After that Buddha passed into parinirvāṇa,
another Buddha appeared in the world named Pāramitā-sunetra-alaṃkāra-rāja, who likewise attained perfect enlightenment within that same Great Forest of Mani Flower Branches.
At that time, the youth Great Radiance, seeing that Tathāgata having attained equal and perfect enlightenment and manifested supernatural powers,
immediately attained the Buddha-remembrance samādhi called "The Door of the Boundless Ocean-Treasury," and immediately attained a dhāraṇī called:
The ocean of the Dharma of great wisdom-power;

Unimpeded light appears universally everywhere;

In this manner, he thoroughly mastered ten thousand such Dharma-gates.
At that time, the youth Great Radiance, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic authority, spoke these verses for his retinue:
“Throughout inconceivable billions of eons, A guiding world-teacher is difficult to encounter once.
The sentient beings of this land possess abundant roots of goodness; Now they have beheld a second Buddha.”
The Buddha’s body universally radiates great light, Its forms and marks are boundless and utterly pure;
Like clouds, they fill all lands, Praising the Buddha’s virtues everywhere.
All who are illumined by this radiance rejoice; The sufferings of sentient beings are entirely extinguished.
Each is led to give rise to a compassionate heart through reverence; This is the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
They emit clouds of inconceivable transformations and radiate nets of light in immeasurable colors;
filling all lands throughout the ten directions—this is what is manifested by the Buddha’s supernormal powers.
From each and every pore, clouds of light appear, pervading the void and emitting great sounds;
there is no darkness that they do not illuminate, causing all the sufferings of the hells to be extinguished.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous voice pervades the ten directions, Fully expounding every possible sound and speech;
According to the power of the past roots of goodness of all sentient beings— This is the Great Teacher’s miraculous display of supernormal power.
Within an immeasurable and boundless ocean of the great assembly, the Buddha appears in every part;
he universally turns the inexhaustible, wondrous wheel of Dharma, taming all sentient beings.
The Buddha’s power of spiritual transformations is boundless, appearing within all buddha-fields;
the Sugata possesses such unimpeded wisdom that he attains perfect enlightenment for the benefit of all beings.
"You all should give rise to a heart of joy, leaping with delight and profound reverence;
I shall go there together with you, so that you may behold the Tathāgata and the extinction of all suffering."
Generating the mind and dedicating merit toward enlightenment, With compassionate thoughts for all sentient beings,
May they all abide in the vast vows of Samantabhadra, And like the Dharma King, attain sovereign mastery.
“Sons of the Buddha!

When the youth Mahāteja spoke these verses, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, his voice was unimpeded and was heard throughout all worlds, and immeasurable sentient beings resolved their minds upon Bodhicitta.”

At that time, Prince Great Majestic Light, together with his parents, his retinue, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings surrounding him before and behind, with jeweled canopies like clouds covering the entirety of space, proceeded together to the presence of the Tathāgata King Adorned with the Good Eye of Perfection.
That Buddha preached for them the Sūtra on the Purity and Adornment of the Essential Nature of the Dharma-realm, with as many auxiliary sūtras as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
When that great assembly had heard this sutra, they attained pure wisdom named "Entry into All Pure Expedient Means" and attained the stage named:
Stainless Radiance;
attaining the wheel of the pāramitās, named:
Manifesting the Adornments Beloved by All Worlds;

Vast Radiance of the Ocean of All Dharmas.

attaining the ocean of wisdom through consecration is called:
Through effortless cultivation, one attains the most sublime vision;
one obtains the manifestation of great radiance,
named "The Universal Illumination of the Reflected Light of the Marks of the Ocean of Tathāgata Virtues."
He attained the pure wisdom of the power of birth from vows,
named the Treasury of Resolute Belief in Immeasurable Vow-Power.
At that time, that Buddha spoke these verses for the Bodhisattva Great Majestic Light:
“Excellent! O ocean of merit and wisdom, you have resolved your mind toward great enlightenment.
You shall attain the inconceivable state of Buddhahood and serve as a refuge for all sentient beings.”
You have already given birth to the great ocean of wisdom, And are fully able to comprehend all phenomena;
With inconceivable and wondrous skillful means, You shall enter the inexhaustible realm of the Buddha’s practice.
Having beheld the clouds of merit of all Buddhas, And having entered the ground of inexhaustible wisdom,
The one of great renown shall fulfill the ocean of skillful means of the pāramitās.
Having attained the gate of skillful dhāraṇīs and the gate of inexhaustible eloquence,
they cultivate all manner of practices and vows, and shall thereby achieve great, unequaled wisdom.
You have already given birth to the ocean of all vows; you have already entered the ocean of samādhis.
You shall possess various great supernormal powers and the inconceivable qualities of all Buddhas.

The ultimate dharma-realm is inconceivable; With a vast and profound mind already purified, They universally behold all Buddhas of the ten directions, Adorned with stainless arrays throughout the oceans of lands.
You have already entered my bodhisattva conduct; the ocean of skillful means from your past lives, such as those purified through my own practice, you have awakened to in all these sublime deeds.
In each and every one of my infinite lands, I have made various offerings to oceans of Buddhas;
the fruits obtained through such practice—I now manifest as these adornments for you all to behold.
Throughout vast oceans of kalpas without end, Cultivating pure conduct within all lands,
With firm vows that are inconceivable, One shall attain such spiritual power as this of the Tathāgata.
Making offerings to all Buddhas without exception, purifying all lands with their adornments,
and cultivating sublime practices throughout all kalpas— you shall attain the great merit of Buddhahood.
"O Sons of the Buddha!

After the Tathāgata King Adorned with the Fine Eye of the Perfections had entered parinirvāṇa, King Joyful Vision and Good Wisdom also passed away, and the youth Great Majestic Radiance inherited the position of the Universal Monarch."
In that Great Forest of Mani Flower Branches, the third Tathāgata appeared in the world, named Most Victorious Ocean of Merit.

At that time, the Universal Monarch Mahātejaḥprabha, beholding the signs of that Tathāgata’s attainment of Buddhahood, went together with his retinue, the fourfold army, all the people of the cities and villages, and carrying the seven treasures, to the place where the Buddha was; there he offered to the Buddha a great multi-storied pavilion adorned with all kinds of fragrant mani-jewels.
At that time, within that forest, that Tathāgata preached the *Sūtra on the Practice of the Universal Eye Radiance*, with as many *sūtras* as there are atoms in a world-system serving as its retinue.
At that time, having heard this Dharma, the Bodhisattva Great Majestic Light attained a samādhi named "Great Merit and Universal Radiance.
Because he had attained this samādhi, he was able to fully comprehend the oceans of merit and demerit of all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings throughout the past, present, and future.
At that time, that Buddha spoke these verses for the Bodhisattva Great Majestic Light:

“Excellent, O Great Majestic Light of Merit! That you have now come to my presence, Out of compassion for the ocean of all sentient beings, And have resolved upon the supreme mind of great bodhicitta vows.”
For the sake of all sentient beings suffering, you have given rise to great compassion to bring them liberation;
you shall become the refuge for the deluded masses—this is called the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means.
If there is a bodhisattva who is able to remain steadfast, cultivating all supreme practices without weariness or indolence,
they shall attain such wondrous wisdom— the most excellent, most sublime, and unimpeded analytical knowledge.
O Light of Merit, Banner of Merit, Abode of Merit, Ocean of Merit—
The vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Into these you, Great Light, are able to enter.
By means of this vast vow, you are able to enter the inconceivable oceans of all Buddhas;
the boundless oceans of the Buddhas' merit you perceive through your wondrous understanding.
Within the lands of the ten directions, you see all the infinite and boundless Buddhas;
the oceans of all those Buddhas' past practices—you see them all in their entirety.
If one dwells in this ocean of skillful means, One will surely enter the stage of wisdom;
This is the study that accords with all Buddhas, And one shall certainly attain omniscience.
Throughout oceans of all buddha-fields, you have cultivated various practices for oceans of eons as minute as atoms;
having mastered the oceans of practices of all Tathāgatas, you shall attain buddhahood.
Just as you see within the ten directions, All oceans of lands are most pure and adorned;
Your own land’s purity shall likewise be so, As that which is attained by those of boundless vows.
Now this ocean-like assembly at this site of enlightenment, having heard your vow, has given rise to joy;
they all enter the vast vehicle of Samantabhadra, resolve their minds upon it, and turn toward Bodhi.
Within each and every one of the boundless lands, they enter and practice throughout oceans of kalpas;
by the power of their vows, they are able to bring to perfection all the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Within that Great Forest of Mani Flower Branch-Wheels, there is another Buddha who has appeared,
named Lotus-Eye Banner of Universal Renown."
At that time, Mahātejas passed away there and was reborn in the celestial city of the Śānta-ratna-palace atop Mount Sumeru as a great heavenly king named Vimalapuṇyaketu.
Together with the hosts of devas, he went to the place where the Buddha was and rained down clouds of precious flowers as an offering.

At that time, that Tathāgata preached for them the *Sūtra of the Universal Gate’s Illumination through Vast Expedient Means*, with as many *sūtras* as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds serving as its retinue.

By the power of this samādhi, they were able to enter the ocean of the true mark of all phenomena.
Having obtained these benefits, they emerge from the site of enlightenment and return to their original abodes.

Chapter Seven: The Names and Titles of the Tathāgata At that time, the World-Honored One was in the country of Magadha, at the site of enlightenment in the forest retreat (araṇya-dharma-bodhimaṇḍa), having just attained perfect awakening. He sat upon the Lotus-Treasury Lion Throne in the Hall of Universal Radiance; his wondrous realization was fully perfected, and the two types of conduct were forever severed.
They have realized the dharma of signlessness and abide in the abode of the Buddhas;
they have attained the equality of the Buddhas and reached the state of non-obstruction;
their dharmas are irreversible, and their conduct is unimpeded.
Established in the inconceivable, they universally perceive the three periods of time.

Together with bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields—none of whom were not in their final birth before enlightenment—they had all gathered from other directions. They were universally skilled in observing the realms of sentient beings, the dharma-realm, the world-realm, and the nirvana-realm; the retributions of various karmas; the successive sequences of mental activities; and all literary meanings regarding the mundane and supramundane, the conditioned and unconditioned, and the past, present, and future.
At that time, the bodhisattvas reflected thus:

"If the World-Honored One would take pity on us, we pray that he will, according to our wishes, reveal the Buddha-fields, the Buddha-abodes, the adornments of the Buddha-fields, the nature of the Buddha-dharma, the purity of the Buddha-fields, the teachings spoken by the Buddha, the essential nature of the Buddha-fields, the majestic power of the Buddha, the accomplishment of the Buddha-fields, and the Great Bodhi of the Buddha."
Just as all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all worlds throughout the ten directions, for the sake of bringing all bodhisattvas to fulfillment,
so that the lineage of the Tathāgatas shall not be interrupted, to rescue and protect all sentient beings,
to cause all sentient beings to forever leave behind all afflictions, and to fully comprehend all conditioned phenomena, proclaim [the Dharma]...
Because all phenomena are thus, because all defilements are purified and removed, because the net of all doubts is forever severed,
because all expectations are uprooted, and because all bases of attachment are destroyed,
[the Buddha] spoke of the ten abodes, ten practices, ten transferences, ten treasuries, ten stages, and ten... of the bodhisattvas.
The vows, the ten concentrations, the ten supernormal powers, and the ten summits; as well as the exposition of the stage of the Tathāgata,
the realm of the Tathāgata, the spiritual power of the Tathāgata, the conduct of the Tathāgata, the powers of the Tathāgata,
the fearlessnesses of the Tathāgata, the samādhis of the Tathāgata, the superknowledges of the Tathāgata, the masteries of the Tathāgata, and the unimpededness of the Tathāgata.
The Tathāgata’s eye, the Tathāgata’s ear, the Tathāgata’s nose, the Tathāgata’s tongue,
the Tathāgata’s body, the Tathāgata’s mind, the Tathāgata’s eloquence, the Tathāgata’s wisdom, and the Tathāgata’s supreme excellence.

The Path of Union is also named Constant Immovability,
or named the Meaning of Excellence.
O Sons of the Buddha!
In the world-system Viniścitaghoṣa, the Four Noble Truths are taught under four hundred billion times ten thousand such names;
according to the minds of sentient beings, they cause all to be tamed.
“O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as in this Sahā world there are four hundred billion ten-thousand names for the Four Noble Truths,

so too, in the east— in hundreds of thousands of billions of worlds that are innumerable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, and unfathomable, throughout the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of space— within each and every one of those worlds, the Four Noble Truths are likewise taught by four hundred billion ten-thousand names.”
According to the minds of sentient beings, they cause all to be tamed and subdued.
As it is in the east, so it is in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as it is in the Sahā world as described above, so it is in all those worlds throughout the ten directions; each of them is likewise.

In the worlds of the ten directions, within each and every world, there are hundreds of billions of millions of names for the Noble Truth of Suffering; likewise, there are hundreds of billions of millions of names for the Noble Truth of Origination, the Noble Truth of Cessation, and the Noble Truth of the Path.
These all accord with what sentient beings delight in their hearts, thereby bringing them to subdual.
