A heart of loving-kindness is all-pervasive, equal to space, Yet it makes no discrimination toward sentient beings; Thus pure, one wanders through the world.
All sentient beings of the ten directions are fully comforted; all that they do is truly real.
Always with a pure mind and no divergent speech, they are constantly protected by the Buddhas together.
Recalling all that has passed in the past, Discerning all that lies in the future,
They enter universally into the worlds of the ten directions, To deliver sentient beings and bring them forth from suffering.
The Bodhisattva, endowed with the light of wondrous wisdom, thoroughly understands causes and conditions without doubt;
having severed all delusions, they thus traverse the Dharma-realm.
The palaces of the Māra kings are utterly destroyed, And the cataracts of sentient beings are all eliminated.
Free from all conceptual discrimination, the mind remains unmoving, Thoroughly understanding the realm of the Tathāgata.
The net of doubt regarding the three periods of time has been entirely removed;
having given rise to pure faith toward the Tathāgata, one attains immovable wisdom through that faith; because wisdom is purified, one understands reality.
To enable sentient beings to attain liberation, He universally benefits them until the end of time;
With long-term diligent effort and a tireless mind, He accepts even the sufferings of hell.
Endowed with immeasurable merit and wisdom, he fully understands the faculties and desires of all sentient beings;
seeing no action or conduct that remains unseen, he preaches the Dharma according to their inclinations.
Fully realizing that all things are empty and selfless, They never abandon their compassionate regard for sentient beings;
With a single, subtle voice of great compassion, They enter the world everywhere to proclaim the Dharma.
They emit great light of various colors, universally illuminating sentient beings to dispel darkness;
within the light, Bodhisattvas sit upon lotus flowers, expounding the pure Dharma for the sake of the multitudes.
Upon a single hair-tip appear myriad lands, Filled entirely with great Bodhisattvas;
The wisdom of those in the assembly differs for each, Yet all are able to clearly understand the minds of sentient beings.
The worlds of the ten directions are unspeakably many, yet in a single thought-moment they traverse them all without exception;
benefiting sentient beings and making offerings to the Buddhas, they inquire about the profound meaning in the presence of each Buddha.
Regarding all Tathāgatas as one's father, they cultivate the practices of awakening for the benefit of sentient beings;
with skillful wisdom, they penetrate the treasury of the Dharma and enter the realm of profound knowledge without attachment.
Contemplating in accordance with the Dharma-realm while preaching the Dharma, it cannot be exhausted even throughout immeasurable eons;
though their wisdom skillfully enters it, there is no location, and they remain without weariness or attachment.
Born into the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, They realize the wondrous Dharma-body of the Tathāgata;
Universally manifesting myriad forms for the sake of all living beings, Just as a magician can produce anything at all.
Sometimes they manifest the initial cultivation of sublime practices; sometimes they manifest birth and renunciation;
sometimes they manifest the attainment of enlightenment beneath the tree; and sometimes they manifest nirvana for the sake of sentient beings.
The marvelous dharmas in which the Bodhisattvas dwell are the realm of the Buddhas alone, not that of the two vehicles;
having eliminated all thought of body, speech, and mind, they are able to manifest in various ways according to what is appropriate.
The various Buddha-dharmas attained by Bodhisattvas would cause sentient beings to go mad with mere thought;
yet their wisdom enters the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) without obstruction, universally manifesting the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
In this world there is none equal to him, let alone one who further increases his sublime practice;
though he has not yet perfected all-knowledge, he has already attained the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
Having already abided in the ultimate path of the One Vehicle, Deeply entered the subtle and supreme Dharma,
And skillfully knowing the proper and improper times for sentient beings, He manifests supernatural powers for their benefit.
Emanating bodies that pervade all lands, They radiate pure light to dispel the darkness of the world;
Just as a dragon king raises great clouds, Raining down wondrous rain everywhere until all are fully saturated.
Observing that sentient beings are like illusions and dreams, constantly transmigrating due to the power of karma,
he feels great compassion and pities them, rescuing them all and preaching for them the unconditioned nature of pure reality.
The power of the Buddha is likewise immeasurable; like space, it has no bounds.
To bring sentient beings to liberation, he practices diligently for billions of eons without weariness.
Contemplating various sublime merits, skillfully cultivating the unsurpassed, foremost deeds,
never abandoning these supreme practices, they focus their minds solely on generating all-encompassing wisdom.
Manifesting a single body as infinite bodies, pervading all worlds entirely;
with a mind pure and free from discrimination—such is the inconceivable power of a single thought-moment.
Making no distinctions among the various worlds, Free from conceptual construction regarding all phenomena, Though observing all dharmas, they do not grasp them;
They constantly rescue sentient beings, yet there is nothing to be delivered.
All worlds are merely conceptual constructs, wherein various distinctions arise;
knowing that the realm of concepts is perilous and deep, he manifests supernatural powers to rescue and liberate beings.
Just as a master illusionist possesses sovereign power, so too are the miraculous transformations of the Bodhisattva;
their bodies pervade the Dharma-realm and all of space, appearing to sentient beings wherever their minds turn.
Free from both subject and object of conceptualization, With neither grasping at defilement nor purity,
And having forgotten all wisdom regarding bondage or liberation— I only pray that you may universally bestow happiness upon all sentient beings.
The entire world exists only through the power of conceptualization; Entering it with wisdom, the mind is free from fear.
Contemplating all phenomena in this same way, One seeks them throughout the three times and finds they cannot be obtained.
They can enter the past, reaching its ultimate limit; they can enter the future, reaching its ultimate limit;
they can enter all places in the present, constantly and diligently observing that nothing exists.
Conforming to the dharma of nirvāṇa and quiescence, dwelling in non-contention and without dependence,
with a mind equal to the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), one is single-mindedly directed toward bodhi, never regressing.
Cultivating all supreme practices without retreat or fear, Abiding securely in Bodhi, unshakable;
The Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas, and the world— All are clearly understood throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm.
If you wish to attain the most supreme and foremost path, To become a king of omniscience and liberation,
You should swiftly resolve upon bodhicitta, To forever exhaust all outflows and benefit all living beings.
The mind directed toward enlightenment is pure, its merit vast and beyond description;
for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, I shall now proclaim it—listen well, all you worthy ones.

Immeasurable worlds are reduced entirely to dust; within each particle of dust are immeasurable lands, and the Buddhas therein are all immeasurable—yet one can clearly perceive them all without grasping at anything.
Skillfully knowing that sentient beings have no notion of birth, skillfully knowing that speech has no notion of speaking;
with a mind unimpeded throughout all worlds, they thoroughly understand all things without attachment.
His mind is as vast as space; he clearly understands all matters of the three periods of time.
All doubts and delusions are extinguished, and through right contemplation of the Buddha-dharma, he grasps at nothing.
To the infinite lands of the ten directions, they travel in a single thought-moment with a mind free from attachment;
having thoroughly realized the various phenomena of suffering in the world, they all abide in the true reality of non-arising.
To the abodes of immeasurable and inconceivable Buddhas, he goes to all those assemblies to pay his respects;
ever acting as their leader, he questions the Tathāgatas regarding the various vows and practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas.
The mind constantly recollects the Buddhas of the ten directions, Without dependence and without grasping;
It always exhorts sentient beings to plant roots of goodness, Adorning the buddha-lands to make them pure.
With unimpeded eyes, they observe all sentient beings throughout the three realms of existence;
their habitual tendencies, faculties, and understandings—immeasurable and boundless—they clearly perceive them all.
He fully understands the inclinations and joys of the minds of sentient beings, and thus preaches the Dharma according to their needs;
he penetrates all that is defiled and pure, causing them to cultivate and refine themselves so as to enter the Path.
In a single thought-moment, the Bodhisattva can enter immeasurable and innumerable samādhis;
therein, they thoroughly understand and attain mastery over conceptualization, wisdom, and their respective objects.
When Bodhisattvas attain this vast wisdom, they swiftly advance toward enlightenment without hindrance;
desiring to benefit all living beings, they proclaim the Dharma of the Great Man everywhere.
Skillfully knowing the long and short kalpas of the world, The months, half-months, and days and nights,
And that the distinct natures of various lands are equal, They constantly observe with diligence and never slacken.
They travel everywhere to all worlds throughout the ten directions, yet they grasp at no location therein;
they purify all lands without exception, yet they never give rise to pure conceptual distinctions.
Regarding the proper and improper courses for sentient beings, And the distinctions in the retributions of their various karmas—
By contemplating these in accordance with reality, they enter the powers of a Buddha, And come to fully understand all of this.
The various natures of all worlds, the diverse modes of conduct by which beings dwell within the three realms of existence,
and those of sharp, medium, and inferior faculties— all such things he observes with complete clarity.
He clearly perceives all various understandings of the pure and the impure, as well as the superior, inferior, and middling;
he can explain the conduct of all sentient beings wherever they go, and how they continue through the three realms of existence.

The meditative concentrations, liberations, and various samādhis, Arise from different causes of defilement and purity, As well as the distinctions between past suffering and joy; Through the power of the Buddha’s pure cultivation, all these can be seen.
The karma and delusions of sentient beings continue through the various realms of existence; by severing these realms, one attains quiescence.
All manner of outflowing phenomena never arise again, as both their active manifestations and their latent seeds are fully understood.
The Tathāgata has eradicated all afflictions, And the light of his great wisdom illuminates the world;
Regarding the Buddha’s ten powers, Though the Bodhisattva has not yet realized them, he harbors no doubt.
Within a single pore, the Bodhisattva universally manifests infinite lands throughout the ten directions;
whether they are defiled or pure, he fully comprehends all the various karmic actions performed therein.
Within a single atom are infinite lands, With infinite Buddhas and their sons;
Each land is distinct without confusion, All clearly seen as if they were one.
Within a single pore one sees the ten directions, all the worlds throughout the entirety of space;
there is not a single place empty of Buddhas, for all such Buddha-fields are utterly pure.
Within a single pore, one beholds Buddha-fields, And likewise sees all sentient beings;
The three periods of time and the six realms of existence are each distinct, Bound by day or night, month or season, yet liberated.
Such Bodhisattvas of great wisdom, single-mindedly aspiring toward the rank of the Dharma King,
contemplate in accordance with the Buddha’s dwelling and attain boundless, great joy.
The Bodhisattva manifests countless billions of emanations, Making offerings to all Tathāgatas;
His supernormal transformations are peerlessly supreme, Able to abide in every place where Buddhas travel.
They have gazed up with reverence at immeasurable Buddhas and savored all their treasuries of Dharma;
having seen the Buddhas and heard the Dharma, they practice with diligence, their hearts filled with joy like those drinking ambrosia.
Having already attained the supreme samādhi of the Tathāgata, They skillfully enter all dharmas and their wisdom increases;
Their faith is immovable like Mount Sumeru, Universally serving as a treasury of merit for all living beings.
With a vast and great heart of loving-kindness pervading all sentient beings, may they all swiftly attain omniscience;
yet remaining forever unattached and without dependence, may they be free from all afflictions and attain mastery.
With vast wisdom that compassionates sentient beings, you universally embrace all as if they were yourself;
knowing emptiness, signlessness, and the lack of true reality, you act with a mind that never falters or retreats.
The measure of the merit of a bodhisattva’s resolve cannot be exhausted even by praising it for billions of eons;
for it brings forth all Tathāgatas and provides peace and happiness to pratyekabuddhas and śrāvakas.
If one were to bestow peace upon all sentient beings in the lands of the ten directions for immeasurable eons,
exhorting them to uphold the five precepts and the ten wholesome paths, and further providing them with the bliss of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables,
and various meditative states for many more eons, thereby causing them to sever all delusions and become arhats;
Though those accumulations of merit are immeasurable, they cannot compare to the virtue of generating the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, even if one were to teach billions of beings to become pratyekabuddhas, attaining the subtle path of non-contention (*araṇā*),
when compared to the bodhicitta, no calculation or analogy can reach it.
In a single thought-moment, one can traverse lands as numerous as atoms;
though such travel continues for immeasurable eons, the number of those lands might still be measured, yet the merit of generating the mind of enlightenment remains unknowable.
The kalpas of the past, future, and present, though their number is boundless, may still be known;
yet the merit of generating the bodhicitta can never be measured.
With the bodhicitta pervading the ten directions, there is no conceptual distinction they do not know;
in a single thought-moment, they clearly comprehend the three periods of time, for the sake of benefiting immeasurable sentient beings.
The sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions, their intentions, their skillful means, and their conduct—
even if the limits of space could be measured, the merit of their resolve for enlightenment is difficult to fathom.
The Bodhisattva’s vows are equal to the ten directions, And their compassionate heart universally moistens all living beings.
Causing them all to cultivate and achieve the merit of Buddhahood, Therefore, their power is without limit or bound.

The desires, understandings, and inclinations of sentient beings, And their various faculties, expedient means, and practices— All are fully known within a single thought-moment; The mind of omniscience is equal toward all.
The afflictions and karmas of all sentient beings, through which the three realms of existence continue without even a moment’s interruption—
the limits of these may yet be known, but the merit of generating the bodhicitta is inconceivable.

The arousal of the mind can leave behind karma and afflictions; by making offerings to all Tathāgatas, one leaves behind karma and delusions so that the continuity of existence is severed, attaining liberation throughout the three periods of time.
In a single thought-moment, one makes offerings to boundless Buddhas, And likewise offers to countless sentient beings.
With incense, flowers, and exquisite garlands, With jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, and fine robes,
With delicious food, precious seats, and places for walking meditation, And with various palaces, all most magnificently adorned.
The *vairocana* jewel of wondrous gems, the wish-fulfilling *maṇi* radiating brilliance—
If one were to hold and offer such [a jewel] in every thought-moment for unspeakable eons of immeasurable kalpas,
though the mass of that person’s merit would be vast, it would not equal the greatness of the merit of generating the resolve [for enlightenment].
The various analogies that have been taught can never equal the bodhicitta;
for all those Honored Ones among men of the three periods of time were born from the arousal of this mind.
The arousal of the mind is unimpeded and without limit; One seeks its measure, yet it cannot be found.
I vow that the wisdom of all-knowledge shall surely be accomplished, And that all sentient beings shall forever be delivered.
The resolve they have made is as vast as space, The merits they produce are equal to the Dharma-realm;
Their conduct is universal and without distinction, Forever free from all attachments, they are equal to the Buddhas.
There is no gateway to the Dharma they do not enter; They are able to travel to all lands;
They fully penetrate the realm of all-knowledge; And they accomplish all meritorious virtues.
Always able to relinquish everything in constant succession, purifying all categories of precepts without attachment,
fully endowed with unsurpassed great merit, they are ever diligent and never regress.
Entering deep meditative concentration and constantly reflecting, In perfect accord with vast wisdom—
this is the supreme stage of the Bodhisattva, From which all paths of Samantabhadra arise.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, Without exception, protect and mind those who have first resolved for enlightenment;
With all their samādhis and dhāraṇīs, And with supernatural powers and transformations, they adorn them together.
Sentient beings in the ten directions are immeasurable, And the worlds and empty space are likewise so;
The resolve to attain enlightenment is more immeasurable than they, And thus it is able to give birth to all Buddhas.
The bodhicitta is the root of the ten powers, And likewise the root of the four analytical knowledges and fearlessnesses;
So it is with the eighteen unique qualities as well— There is nothing that is not attained through the arousal of this mind.
The physical bodies of all Buddhas, adorned with marks and signs, as well as their equal and wondrous Dharma-bodies,
and their wisdom that is unattached and worthy of offerings— all these are obtained through the initial resolve for enlightenment.
All Pratyekabuddhas and those of the Śrāvaka vehicle, The bliss of the various dhyānas and samādhis of the form realm,
And all the samādhis of the formless realm— All take the arousal of the bodhicitta as their foundation.
All the sovereign joys of humans and devas, And the various pleasures of the different realms of existence,
As well as the manifold delights of vigor, concentration, faculties, and powers— None of these fail to arise from the initial resolve for enlightenment.
By giving rise to the vast mind through these causes, one is able to practice the six perfections;
by exhorting all sentient beings to practice right conduct, they shall experience peace and happiness within the three realms.
Abiding in the Buddha’s unimpeded wisdom of ultimate reality, you fully expound all sublime deeds;
you enable immeasurable sentient beings to sever their afflictions and karma, and turn toward Nirvana.
The light of wisdom is like the pure sun; All practices are complete like the full moon;
Virtues are ever-filling like the vast ocean; Stainless and unimpeded, identical to space.
Universally issuing boundless vows of merit, Bestowing happiness upon all sentient beings,
Following these vows and practices throughout the bounds of the future, Constantly and diligently cultivating the means to deliver all beings.
Immeasurable great vows, inconceivable, Vow to cause all sentient beings to be entirely pure;
Though empty, signless, and wishless, with no place of reliance, By the power of these vows, all are made manifest.
Having realized that the intrinsic nature of phenomena is like space, All are quiescent and entirely equal;
Though the gateways of Dharma are innumerable and ineffable, One teaches them to sentient beings without attachment.
The Tathāgatas of the worlds in the ten directions all join in praising the first arousal of the mind;
this mind is adorned with immeasurable virtues and can reach the other shore, equal to the Buddhas.
Even if one were to speak for as many eons as there are sentient beings, their merits could not be fully exhausted;
for they dwell in the vast and great abode of the Tathāgata, where no phenomena within the three realms can provide an analogy.
If you wish to know all the dharmas of the Buddhas, you should swiftly resolve to attain bodhicitta;
this mind is the most supreme among all merits, and one will surely obtain the unimpeded wisdom of the Tathāgata.
The mental activities of sentient beings may be counted and known, And likewise the atoms within all lands;
Even the limits of empty space might be measured, But the merit of generating the bodhicitta is beyond all measure.
Giving birth to all Buddhas of the three periods of time, Accomplishing all happiness in the world,
Increasing all supreme merits, And forever severing all doubts and delusions.
Revealing all sublime realms, Completely eliminating all obstacles,
Accomplishing all pure lands, And giving birth to the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
Desiring to see all Buddhas of the ten directions, Desiring to bestow the inexhaustible treasury of merit,
And desiring to extinguish all the sufferings and afflictions of sentient beings, One should swiftly resolve to attain Bodhicitta.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Seventeen;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Eighteen.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
18. Chapter on Elucidating the Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vīryamati addressed the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!..."

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva first resolves to seek all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), they accomplish such immeasurable merit, become endowed with great adornment, ascend the vehicle of all-knowledge, enter the stage of certainty for Bodhisattvas, abandon all worldly dharmas, and attain the supramundane dharmas of a Buddha. They are taken into the care of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, and are certain to reach the ultimate state of unsurpassed enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).

How do those bodhisattvas practice within the Buddha’s teaching so that all Tathāgatas are filled with joy, they enter the abodes where bodhisattvas dwell, all their great practices become purified, all their great vows are fully satisfied, they obtain the vast treasury of the bodhisattvas, they constantly preach the Dharma according to those to be transformed, they never abandon the practice of the pāramitās, they cause all sentient beings they have in mind to attain liberation, they succeed to the lineage of the Triple Gem so that it is never severed, and their roots of goodness and skillful means are all rendered non-empty?
"O Son of the Buddha!
By what skillful means can those bodhisattvas cause this Dharma to be brought to full perfection?
We pray that you will look upon us with compassion and explain it for our sake."
"In this great assembly, there is none who does not delight in hearing this!

Furthermore, as all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly and diligently practice, they eliminate all the darkness of ignorance, subdue Māra and his enemies, and restrain all non-Buddhists; they forever wash away all defilements of the mind and afflictions;
they are fully able to accomplish all roots of goodness, forever emerge from all evil destinies and difficulties, and purify the realm of all great wisdom."

They have accomplished all the stages of the bodhisattvas, the pāramitās, dhāraṇīs, samādhis, the six supernormal powers, the three clarities, and the four fearlessnesses—these pure merits; they have adorned all buddha-fields and fully perfected the marks and signs of excellence, as well as the conduct of body, speech, and mind. They skillfully know the spheres of activity of the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique buddha-qualities of all tathāgatas, as well as the sphere of omniscient wisdom.
Desiring to bring all sentient beings to maturity, they take up buddha-fields according to their inclinations and preach the Dharma appropriately according to their faculties and the times.

All manner of immeasurable and vast Buddha-activities, as well as other immeasurable dharmas of merit, practices, paths, and spheres, will all be fully perfected; one will swiftly attain equality with the merits of a Tathāgata.

One will be able to protect, reveal, and expound the treasury of Dharma accumulated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas over hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kalpas during their cultivation of bodhisattva practices; no Māras or non-Buddhists will be able to obstruct or destroy it, and one will uphold the True Dharma without end.

When he expounds the Dharma in all worlds, the kings of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, human kings, Brahmā kings, and the Tathāgata, the King of Dharma, all provide protection;
all the world honors and makes offerings to him;
they all consecrate his crown, and he is constantly protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas and cherished and respected by all bodhisattvas.
Having attained the power of the roots of goodness and increased the white dharmas, you expound the Tathāgata’s profound treasury of Dharma and adorn yourself by upholding the True Dharma.
We pray that you will fully explain the successive stages of practice for all bodhisattvas!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vīramatī, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"The one of great renown is well able to expound The dharmas of merit accomplished by Bodhisattvas;
Deeply entering boundless and vast practices, They are fully endowed with pure, teacherless wisdom."
If there be a bodhisattva who first resolves their mind, Accomplishing the vehicle of merit and wisdom,
Entering the stage of certainty and transcending the world, They will universally attain the dharma of perfect enlightenment.
Furthermore, how can one within the Buddha’s teaching Firmly and diligently practice so as to increase in excellence,
Causing all Tathāgatas to be fully delighted, And swiftly enter the stage where the Buddhas abide?

Their conduct is pure and their vows are all fulfilled; having attained the vast treasury of wisdom, they are constantly able to preach the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, while their minds remain without dependence or attachment.
The Bodhisattva perfectly practices all the pāramitās without deficiency;
they deliver all sentient beings they think of, constantly upholding the lineage of the Buddhas so that it never ceases.
What is performed is firm and not in vain; all accomplishments lead to liberation.
Just as the Victors have practiced, may you proclaim that path of purity!
Forever shattering all the darkness of ignorance, Subduing all demons and heterodox teachers,
Completely washing away every defilement, One draws near to the Great Wisdom of the Tathāgata.
Forever free from the perilous hardships of the evil realms, Thoroughly purifying the sublime sphere of great wisdom,
Attaining the power of the wondrous path to dwell near the Supreme Honored One, All merits and virtues are fully accomplished.
Having realized the Tathāgata’s most supreme wisdom, Abiding in immeasurable buddha-fields,
He teaches the Dharma according to the minds of sentient beings And performs vast and manifold buddha-activities.
How does one attain all the wondrous paths, Expound the Tathāgata’s treasury of the True Dharma,
And always be able to receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas, Such that none can surpass them and none can equal them?
How is it that you are fearless like a lion, and your conduct is as pure as the full moon?
How do you cultivate the virtues of a Buddha, remaining unstained like a lotus in water?
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharmamati addressed the Bodhisattva Vīryamati, saying: "Excellent,
Son of the Buddha!

It is because you now desire to bring great benefit, great peace and happiness, and great welfare to many, out of compassion for the gods and humans of the world, that you ask about such pure conduct practiced by bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
You abide in the true Dharma, have aroused great vigor, increased it without regression, and have already attained liberation;
that you are able to ask such a question is equal to the Tathāgata.
Listen attentively!
Listen attentively!
Reflect upon it well!
Now, relying on the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, I shall explain a small portion of it for you.
"O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who has already resolved upon the mind of omniscience should distance themselves from the darkness of delusion, diligently guarding it so as not to become negligent."
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in ten dharmas,
it is called "heedfulness."
What are the ten? First, upholding all the precepts;
second, distancing oneself from ignorance and purifying the bodhicitta.
Third, their minds delight in sincerity and straightforwardness, remaining free from all flattery and deception;
fourth, they diligently cultivate roots of goodness without ever regressing;
fifth, they constantly engage in skillful reflection upon the resolve they have themselves generated.
Sixth, not delighting in associating with any ordinary persons, whether lay or ordained;
seventh, cultivating all virtuous deeds without seeking worldly retribution;
eighth, forever departing from the two vehicles and practicing the bodhisattva path.
Ninth, they delight in cultivating all manner of wholesome deeds so that they are never interrupted;
tenth, they constantly and skillfully observe the power of their own mental continuum.
O Son of the Buddha!
If bodhisattvas practice these ten dharmas, they are said to abide in heedfulness.
"Sons of the Buddha!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in heedfulness, they attain ten kinds of purity."
What are these ten? First, acting according to what one says;
second, the accomplishment of mindfulness and wisdom;
Third, dwelling in profound meditative concentration, neither sinking nor becoming agitated;
fourth, joyfully seeking the Buddha-dharma without weariness or rest;
fifth, observing the Dharma as it has been heard according to principle, thereby fully giving rise to skillful wisdom.
Sixth, they enter deep meditative concentration and attain the supernormal powers of a Buddha;
seventh, their minds are impartial, without distinction of high or low;
eighth, toward all sentient beings—whether superior, middling, or inferior—their minds are free from obstruction, benefiting them equally just as the great earth does.
Ninth, if one sees even a single sentient being who has resolved to attain bodhicitta, one should honor and serve them as if they were one's own preceptor (upādhyāya).

Tenth, toward the preceptor who confers the precepts, the ācārya, all bodhisattvas, spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), and Dharma masters, one should always give rise to respect, serving and making offerings to them.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are called the ten kinds of purity for a bodhisattva dwelling in heedfulness.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in heedfulness and exert great diligence;
they give rise to right mindfulness and produce superior aspiration, never ceasing their practice;
regarding all phenomena, their minds have no place of dependence.
They are able to diligently cultivate the profound Dharma;
they enter the gate of non-contention and increase their vast mind;
they are able to accord with and understand the boundless Buddha-Dharma, causing all Tathāgatas to be entirely delighted.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, there are ten dharmas by which a bodhisattva mahāsattva can cause all Buddhas to rejoice. What are these ten?
First, to be diligent and never retreat;
second, to not begrudge one's body or life;
third, to have no longing for gain or offerings.
Fourth, knowing that all phenomena are like empty space;
fifth, being skillfully able to observe and universally enter the dharma-realm;
sixth, knowing the seals of all phenomena, with a mind free from dependence or attachment.
Seventh, they constantly make great vows;
eighth, they achieve the light of pure patience and wisdom;
ninth, they contemplate their own wholesome dharmas with a mind free from increase or decrease.
Tenth, by relying on the gate of non-action, they cultivate all pure practices.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten dharmas in which a bodhisattva abides, enabling them to bring joy to all Tathāgatas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, there are ten dharmas that can cause all Buddhas to rejoice. What are these ten?
That is to say:
abiding in heedfulness;
abiding in the patience of non-arising;
Abiding in great loving-kindness;
abiding in great compassion;
abiding in the fulfillment of all perfections.
Abiding in all practices;
abiding in great vows;
abiding in skillful means.
They abide in the power of valor;
they abide in wisdom, observing that all phenomena have no place of abiding, being like empty space.
O Son of the Buddha!
If bodhisattvas abide in these ten dharmas, they can cause all Buddhas to rejoice.
"O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of dharmas that enable bodhisattvas to swiftly enter the various stages."
What are the ten? First, skillfully perfecting the two practices of merit and wisdom;
second, being able to greatly adorn the path of the pāramitās.
Third, their wisdom is clear and penetrating, such that they do not follow the words of others;
fourth, they serve virtuous friends, never abandoning them;
fifth, they constantly practice diligence, remaining free from indolence.
Sixth, they are well able to dwell securely in the spiritual power of the Tathāgata;
seventh, they cultivate all roots of goodness without giving rise to weariness;
eighth, with a profound mind and sharp wisdom, they adorn themselves with the Mahāyāna Dharma.
Ninth, regarding the dharma-gates of each stage, the mind dwells nowhere;
tenth, one’s roots of goodness and skillful means are of the same essential nature as those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
O Son of the Buddha!
These ten kinds of dharmas enable all bodhisattvas to swiftly enter the various stages.
"Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!"
When Bodhisattvas first dwell in the stages, they should skillfully observe:

they should skillfully observe all the Dharma-gates they possess, their profound wisdom as it exists, the causes they cultivate, the fruits they attain, their spheres of activity, their functional powers, their manifestations, their discernments, and all that they have realized.
Knowing that all phenomena are solely one's own mind, one remains without attachment;
having known this, one enters the bodhisattva stages and is able to dwell therein with perfect stability.
O Son of the Buddha! Those bodhisattvas reflect thus:
"We ought to enter the various stages (bhūmis) with speed."
Why is this? Because if we abide in each of these stages, we shall accomplish such vast merit;
having fulfilled these merits, we shall gradually enter the stage of a Buddha.
Having dwelled in the stage of Buddhahood, one is able to perform boundless and vast Buddha-activities.
Therefore, one should constantly and diligently practice without rest or weariness, adorning oneself with great merit and entering the stages of a Bodhisattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of dharmas that cause the conduct of all bodhisattvas to be pure. What are these ten?
First, they completely relinquish all wealth and property to fulfill the wishes of sentient beings;
second, they maintain pure precepts without any transgression;
third, they possess gentle patience that is inexhaustible.
Fourth, they diligently cultivate all practices and never regress;
fifth, through the power of right mindfulness, their minds are free from confusion;
sixth, they discern and thoroughly understand immeasurable dharmas.
Seventh, they cultivate all practices without attachment;
eighth, their minds are unshakable, like the king of mountains;
ninth, they extensively deliver sentient beings, like a bridge.
Tenth, knowing that all sentient beings and all Tathāgatas share the same single essence.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten dharmas that cause the conduct of all Bodhisattvas to be pure.
“Once a bodhisattva has attained the purity of practice, they further acquire ten kinds of superior dharmas. What are these ten?
First, all Buddhas of the other directions will protect and keep them in mind.”
Second, their roots of goodness increase and excel, surpassing all their peers;
third, they are well able to receive the power of the Buddha's empowerment;
fourth, they constantly find virtuous people to serve as their refuge.
Fifth, they abide securely in diligence and are ever free from negligence;
sixth, they know that all phenomena are equal and without distinction;
seventh, their minds constantly abide in unsurpassed great compassion.
Eighth, they contemplate phenomena as they truly are, giving rise to sublime wisdom;
ninth, they are able to skillfully practice expedient means;
tenth, they are able to know the power of the Tathāgata’s expedient means.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of superior dharmas of the bodhisattvas.
"O Son of the Buddha!"
Bodhisattvas have ten kinds of pure vows. What are these ten?
The first vow is to bring sentient beings to maturity without ever becoming weary.
The second vow is to practice all manner of goodness and purify all worlds;
the third vow is to serve the Tathāgatas, always generating reverence;
the fourth vow is to uphold the True Dharma, not sparing even one's own body or life.
The fifth vow is to enter all Buddha-lands by observing them with wisdom;
the sixth vow is to share the same essential nature as all bodhisattvas;
the seventh vow is to enter the gateway of the Tathāgata and comprehend all dharmas.
The eighth vow: that all who see me shall give rise to faith and none fail to obtain benefit;
the ninth vow: that by my spiritual power I shall abide in the world until the end of future kalpas;
the tenth vow: that I shall fulfill the practices of Samantabhadra and purify the gateway to all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvajñatā*).
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of pure vows of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!"
When Bodhisattvas abide in ten dharmas, they cause all their great vows to be fully perfected. What are these ten?
First, their minds are free from weariness and fatigue.
Second, they are fully endowed with great adornments;
third, they keep in mind the sublime power of the vows of all bodhisattvas;
fourth, upon hearing of all buddha-fields, they vow to be reborn in them all.
Fifth, their profound resolve endures for a long time, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future;
sixth, they vow to fully accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings;
seventh, they abide through all kalpas without regarding it as wearisome.
Eighth, to undergo all sufferings without giving rise to weariness or aversion;
ninth, to have no mind of greedy attachment toward any pleasures;
tenth, to constantly and diligently protect the unsurpassed Dharma-gate.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva fulfills such vows, they immediately attain ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries. What are these ten?

They are: the inexhaustible treasury of universally beholding all Buddhas; the inexhaustible treasury of *dhāraṇī* that never forgets; the inexhaustible treasury of definitively understanding all phenomena; the inexhaustible treasury of great compassion that provides rescue and protection; the inexhaustible treasury of various *samādhis*; the inexhaustible treasury of vast merit that fulfills the hearts of sentient beings; the inexhaustible treasury of profound wisdom that expounds all phenomena; the inexhaustible treasury of supernormal powers obtained as retribution; the inexhaustible treasury of abiding for immeasurable eons; and the inexhaustible treasury of entering boundless worlds.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten inexhaustible treasuries of the bodhisattva.
Once a bodhisattva has attained these ten kinds of treasuries, their merit will be fully perfected and their wisdom will be pure.
To all sentient beings, he preaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate for each.
O Son of the Buddha!
How does a bodhisattva preach the Dharma to all sentient beings according to what is appropriate for each?
That is to say:
knowing their actions, knowing their causes and conditions, knowing their mental activities, and knowing their inclinations.
For those with an abundance of desire, he teaches the meditation on impurity.
To those with an abundance of hatred, he teaches great loving-kindness;
to those with an abundance of delusion, he instructs them to diligently engage in contemplation;
and to those in whom the three poisons are equal, he teaches the Dharma-gate for accomplishing supreme wisdom.
For those who delight in birth and death, he preaches the three kinds of suffering;
for those attached to places, he preaches the emptiness and stillness of places;
for those whose minds are indolent, he preaches great diligence.
For those who harbor pride, they preach the equality of all dharmas;
for those who are full of flattery and deception, they preach the Bodhisattva path so that their minds may become upright and sincere;
and for those who delight in tranquility, they extensively preach the Dharma to bring them to fulfillment.
The Bodhisattva thus preaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate for each.
When preaching the Dharma, the phrasing is coherent and the meaning is free from error;
he contemplates the sequence of the teachings and distinguishes them with wisdom.
This is definitively established and does not contradict the seal of the Dharma;
it sequentially establishes boundless gateways of practice to cause all sentient beings to sever all doubts,
and skillfully knows the various faculties [of beings] so that they may enter the teaching of the Tathāgata.
Realizing the limit of reality, they know the equality of all phenomena;
severing all craving for dharmas, they eliminate every attachment;
constantly mindful of all Buddhas, their minds never abandon them for even a moment.
They thoroughly understand that the nature of sound is equal in essence;
regarding all speech, their minds remain unattached;
they skillfully employ parables without contradiction, causing all beings to realize the equal wisdom-body of all Buddhas, which manifests universally according to the needs of others.

"When a bodhisattva thus expounds the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, they personally cultivate and increase their own benefit and profit; they do not abandon the various perfections and fully complete the path of the adorned pāramitās."

At that time, in order to bring satisfaction to the minds of sentient beings, the Bodhisattva relinquishes both internal and external things without attachment; this is how one can purify the dāna-pāramitā.
To uphold all the precepts without attachment and to be forever free from the conceit of "I" is to be able to purify the *śīla-pāramitā*.

To be able to endure all evils and to maintain a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings, unshakable like the great earth which supports everything, is to be able to purify the *kṣānti-pāramitā*.

Universally initiating all deeds, one constantly practices without indolence; in all that is undertaken, one never regresses; with courageous power that cannot be subdued, one neither grasps nor rejects any merits, yet is able to fulfill all gates of omniscience—this is the purification of the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*).

Having no attachment to the objects of the five desires, they are able to fully accomplish all the successive meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*). Constantly engaging in right reflection, they neither remain within nor depart from them, yet are able to extinguish all afflictions (*kleśa*).

They give birth to immeasurable gateways of samādhi and achieve boundless great supernormal powers (*ṛddhibala*). Entering various samādhis in both direct and reverse order, they enter infinite samādhi-gateways through a single one; they thoroughly know the spheres of all samādhis and do not contradict the seals of wisdom (*jñānamudrā*) regarding all samādhis and *samāpattis*. Being able to swiftly enter the stage of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*), this is the purification of the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*).
They hear and uphold the Dharma from all Buddhas; they attend upon spiritual friends with tireless service;
they always delight in hearing the Dharma, their minds never reaching satiety;
and according to what they have heard and received, they reflect upon it in accordance with reality.
Entering true samādhi, one leaves behind all deviant views;
skillfully observing all phenomena, one attains the seal of the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇamudrā*) and thoroughly understands the Tathāgata’s path of effortlessness.

Riding upon the wisdom of the universal gate, one enters the gateway of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), attaining eternal rest; this is how one can purify the *prajñāpāramitā*.
They manifest all worldly activities to teach and transform sentient beings without weariness, appearing in bodily forms according to their inclinations;
all their actions are free from defilement and attachment, whether they manifest the conduct of ordinary beings or the conduct of sages, or manifest birth and death, or manifest nirvana;

they skillfully observe all that is done, manifesting all manner of adornments without craving or clinging, and entering all realms of existence to deliver sentient beings—this is the purification of the perfection of skillful means (*upāya-pāramitā*).

To fully accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings, to fully adorn all worlds, to fully make offerings to all Buddhas, to fully penetrate the unobstructed Dharma, to fully practice conduct that pervades the entire Dharma-realm, to have one’s body constantly abide throughout all future kalpas, to have wisdom that fully knows all mental activities, to fully awaken to the cycle of birth-and-death and its cessation, to fully manifest in all lands, and to fully realize the wisdom of the Tathāgata—this is the perfection of the vow of purification.
They possess the power of profound resolve, because they are free from all defilement;
they possess the power of deep faith, because nothing can overcome or subdue them;
they possess the power of great compassion, because they never give rise to weariness or fatigue.
They possess the power of great compassion, because their conduct is impartial;
they possess the power of dhāraṇī, because they are able to maintain all meanings through skillful means;
they possess the power of eloquence, because they cause all sentient beings to rejoice and be satisfied.
They possess the power of the pāramitās, because they adorn the Mahāyāna;
they possess the power of great vows, because they are never interrupted;
they possess the power of supernormal knowledges, because they give rise to the immeasurable.
Possessing the power of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), they cause others to believe, understand, and receive [the teaching]; this is the power that purifies the perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*).

Knowing those who act out of desire, knowing those who act out of hatred, knowing those who act out of delusion, knowing those whose temperaments are equal [in these three], knowing those who practice on the stages of training (*śaikṣabhūmi*), and within a single thought-moment knowing the conduct of infinite sentient beings, knowing the minds of infinite sentient beings, knowing the reality of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-tattva*), and knowing the powers of all Tathāgatas—thus universally awakening to the gates of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*)—this is the power that purifies the perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*).
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva thus purifies the various pāramitās, fulfills the various pāramitās, and does not abandon the various pāramitās, they abide within the Greatly Adorned Bodhisattva Vehicle.”
According to their respective thoughts, he preaches the Dharma to all sentient beings, causing them to increase their pure karma and attain liberation.
To those fallen into the evil realms, he teaches them to resolve their minds [on enlightenment];
to those in distress, he causes them to apply themselves with diligent vigor.
For sentient beings with excessive greed, he demonstrates the dharma of non-greed;
for sentient beings with excessive anger, he causes them to practice equanimity;
for sentient beings attached to views, he explains dependent origination.
For sentient beings of the desire realm, he teaches them to abandon desire, ill will, and unwholesome states;
for sentient beings of the form realm, he proclaims *vipaśyanā* (insight) for them;
and for sentient beings of the formless realm, he proclaims subtle and wondrous wisdom for them.
For those of the two vehicles, he teaches the practice of tranquility;
for those who delight in the Mahāyāna, he expounds the vast adornment of the ten powers.
Just as in the past when he first resolved his mind [on enlightenment], seeing immeasurable sentient beings fallen into the various evil realms, he let out a great lion’s roar and spoke these words:
"I shall deliver them through various Dharma-gates according to what is appropriate for each!
Possessing such wisdom, the Bodhisattva is able extensively to deliver and liberate all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva is endowed with such wisdom, they cause the lineage of the Three Jewels to never be severed. Why is this?
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva teaches all sentient beings to resolve upon bodhicitta; therefore, he is able to ensure that the lineage of the Buddhas is never severed.
He constantly expounds the treasury of the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings; therefore, he is able to ensure that the lineage of the Dharma is never severed.
He skillfully upholds the teachings of the Dharma without any contradiction; therefore, he is able to ensure that the lineage of the Sangha is never severed.
Furthermore, because they are able to fully praise all great vows, they can cause the lineage of the Buddhas to remain unbroken;
because they analytically expound the gateway of causes and conditions, they can cause the lineage of the Dharma to remain unbroken;
and because they constantly and diligently practice the six dharmas of harmonious respect, they can cause the lineage of the Saṃgha to remain unbroken.
Furthermore, by sowing the seeds of the Buddha within the field of sentient beings, one ensures that the lineage of the Buddha remains unbroken;
by upholding the True Dharma without regard for body or life, one ensures that the lineage of the Dharma remains unbroken;
and by presiding over the great assembly without weariness, one ensures that the lineage of the Sangha remains unbroken.

Furthermore, regarding the Dharma taught and the precepts established by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, one upholds them all completely and does not abandon them in mind; therefore, one is able to ensure that the lineages of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha are never severed.

In this way, the bodhisattva upholds and causes the Three Jewels to flourish; all their actions are free from fault, and whatever they do is dedicated toward the gateway of omniscience. Therefore, their three karmas are entirely without blemish.

Because they are free from blemish, all the various good deeds they perform and the practices they carry out to transform sentient beings—teaching the Dharma according to their needs—even for a single thought-moment, are without error. All are in accord with skillful means and wisdom, and are entirely directed toward the knowledge of all modes; none of them pass away in vain.
"When a bodhisattva thus cultivates wholesome dharmas, in every thought-moment they are fully endowed with ten kinds of adornments.
What are these ten? They are as follows:"
Adornment of body, because one manifests in accordance with the needs of sentient beings to be disciplined;
adornment of speech, because one cuts off all doubts and causes all to rejoice;
adornment of mind, because one enters all samādhis within a single thought-moment.
The adornment of the Buddha-field is all-pure, because it is free from all afflictions;
the adornment of light is the radiance of boundless beams that universally illumine sentient beings;
the adornment of the assembly is the universal gathering of the multitude, causing them all to rejoice.
The adornment of supernormal powers, because they are manifested with sovereign mastery according to the minds of sentient beings;
the adornment of the true teaching, because it is able to gather in all intelligent people;
and the adornment of the stage of nirvana, because although one attains enlightenment in a single location, it pervades the ten directions without exception.
They are skillfully adorned with eloquence, for they preach the Dharma according to the place, the time, and the faculties of sentient beings.
Having achieved such adornments, in every thought-moment, their physical, verbal, and mental actions never go to waste, as they dedicate them all toward the gateway of omniscience.
If there are sentient beings who see this bodhisattva, you should know that none of them will have done so in vain, for they shall certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Whether they hear his name, make offerings to him, dwell together with him, recollect him, follow him into the homeless life, hear his preaching of the Dharma, rejoice in his roots of goodness, or even from afar give rise to reverence—up to the point of extolling and praising his name—they shall all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like a medicine named "Good Vision," which,
when seen by sentient beings, eliminates all poisons.
When Bodhisattvas have thus accomplished these dharmas, if sentient beings see them, all the poisons of their afflictions are extinguished and wholesome dharmas increase.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this Dharma and practice it with diligent effort, they extinguish all darkness of delusion through the light of wisdom;
they crush and subdue the armies of Māra through the power of compassion;
and they restrain all non-Buddhist paths through the power of great wisdom and merit.
By means of the adamantine concentration, they eliminate all mental impurities and afflictions;
by the power of diligence, they gather all roots of goodness;
and by the power of the roots of goodness for purifying Buddha-fields, they remain far removed from all difficulties of the evil realms.
By the power of non-attachment, they purify the realm of wisdom;

by the power of skillful means and wisdom, they bring forth all the bodhisattva stages, the pāramitās, as well as all samādhis, the six superknowledges, the three clarities, and the four fearlessnesses, causing them all to be completely pure;
by the power of all wholesome dharmas, they fully accomplish all the pure lands of the Buddhas, with boundless marks and signs, and their bodies, speech, and minds are fully adorned.
By the power of observation through mastery of wisdom, they know that all the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma) of all Tathāgatas are entirely equal;
by the power of vast wisdom, they fully comprehend the realm of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna);

and by the power of their past vows, they manifest Buddha-lands according to those who are to be transformed, turning the great wheel of Dharma and delivering immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas diligently cultivate this Dharma, they successively accomplish all the practices of Bodhisattvas, until they attain equality with all Buddhas. They become great Dharma masters within boundless worlds, protecting and upholding the True Dharma;
they are protected and remembered by all Buddhas, guarding and maintaining the vast treasury of the Dharma.”
Having attained unimpeded eloquence, they enter deeply into the Dharma-gates;

amidst the great assemblies in boundless worlds, they universally manifest their bodies according to the diverse types of beings, endowed with perfect physical marks, most excellent and peerless. With unimpeded eloquence, they skillfully expound the profound Dharma;
because their voices are perfect and skillfully distributed, they enable those who hear them to enter the gate of inexhaustible wisdom.

Knowing the mental activities and afflictions of all sentient beings, he preaches the Dharma for them; because the sounds he utters are perfectly pure, his single voice can eloquently expound the teachings and cause everyone to feel joy.
Because his body is upright and possesses great majestic power, no one can surpass him when he is amidst the assembly.
Because he skillfully knows the minds of the multitude, he is able to manifest his body everywhere.
Because he skillfully expounds the Dharma, his voice is unimpeded;
because he has attained mastery over the mind, he skillfully expounds the Great Dharma, such that none can obstruct or destroy him;
and because he has attained fearlessness, his mind is free from timidity.
Because he possesses mastery over all phenomena, none can surpass him;
because he possesses mastery over wisdom, none can excel him;
and because he possesses mastery over the *prajñāpāramitā*, the characteristics of the dharmas he teaches do not contradict one another.
Because of mastery over eloquence (*pratibhāna-vaśitā*), they preach the Dharma according to their inclination in an uninterrupted succession;
because of mastery over dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇī-vaśitā*), they definitively reveal the true nature (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*) of all phenomena;
and because of mastery over eloquence, whatever they expound, they are able to open various doors of parables.
Because of mastery over great compassion, he diligently instructs sentient beings with a mind that never tires;
because of mastery over great kindness, he emits nets of light to gladden the hearts of all.
Thus, the Bodhisattva, seated upon a high and vast lion throne, expounds the Great Dharma.

With the exception of the Tathāgata and those great Bodhisattvas of supreme vows and wisdom, no other sentient beings are able to surpass him, none can behold the crown of his head, and none can outshine him;
it is impossible for anyone to cause him to retreat or yield by means of difficult questions.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Once a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has attained such sovereign power, suppose there were a great site of enlightenment as vast as unspeakably many worlds, filled with sentient beings, each of whom possessed the majestic virtue and physical appearance of a lord of a trichiliocosm.

When the Bodhisattva merely manifests his body here, he is able to completely outshine this entire assembly; with great compassion, he soothes those who are timid and weak; with profound wisdom, he examines their inclinations and desires; and with fearless eloquence, he preaches the Dharma for them, enabling all to give rise to joy.
Why is this? Sons of the Buddha!
Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the wheel of immeasurable wisdom, they have accomplished immeasurable skillful analysis.
Because they are distinct, they have achieved the power of vast and correct mindfulness; they have achieved inexhaustible skillful wisdom;
they have achieved the *dhāraṇī* that definitively realizes the true mark of all phenomena; they have achieved the boundless bodhicitta;
they have achieved unerring and wondrous eloquence; and they have achieved the attainment of all Buddhas.

Because they have attained profound faith and understanding through empowerment; because they have accomplished the power of wisdom that universally enters the assembly grounds of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
because they have accomplished the pure mind that knows the single identical nature of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
and because they have accomplished the wisdom of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time and the great vow-wisdom of all Bodhisattvas, which is capable of performing great [deeds].
“Because the Dharma Master elucidates the treasury of the True Dharma of all Buddhas and protects and upholds it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharma Wisdom, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power and spoke in verse:
“The mind abides in Bodhi and gathers manifold blessings; Always being heedful, one plants firm wisdom.”
Maintaining right mindfulness, their intent is never forgotten; all Buddhas of the ten directions rejoice.
Their aspiration is firm and they exert themselves with diligence; having no reliance in the world, they are free from retreat or fear.
Entering the profound Dharma through conduct free from contention, all Buddhas of the ten directions rejoice.
Having rejoiced, the Buddha firmly applied himself with diligence, practicing the dharmas that aid the path through merit and wisdom;
he entered the various stages, purified all his conduct, and fulfilled the vows spoken by the Tathāgata.
Thus practicing, one attains the sublime Dharma; having attained the Dharma, one bestows it upon all living beings.
According to their inclinations and their faculties, one expounds it for them in a manner that is entirely appropriate.
The Bodhisattva expounds the Dharma for others, Without abandoning his own practice of the various perfections;
Having already perfected the path of the pāramitās, He constantly rescues all sentient beings from the ocean of existence.
Diligently practicing day and night without weariness, they ensure that the lineage of the Triple Gem is never severed;
all the pure and white dharmas they practice are entirely dedicated toward the stage of the Tathāgata.
The myriad virtuous deeds cultivated by the Bodhisattvas are universally for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to fulfillment;
they cause them to shatter darkness and extinguish afflictions, subduing the armies of Māra and attaining perfect enlightenment.
Practicing in this way, one attains the Buddha’s wisdom, Entering deeply into the Tathāgata’s treasury of the True Dharma;
Acting as a great Dharma teacher to expound the wondrous Dharma, Just like nectar that is sprinkled everywhere.
Compassion and pity pervade all things; you know the mental activities of sentient beings without exception.
According to their inclinations, you reveal and expound the infinite and boundless teachings of the Buddhas.
His movements are calm and slow like those of an elephant king; he is courageous and fearless like a lion.
Immovable as a mountain, his wisdom is like the ocean, and he is like a great rain that dispels all heat.
When the Bodhisattva Dharmamati had spoken these verses, the Tathāgata rejoiced, and the great assembly practiced them accordingly.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle Eighteen.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle Nineteen.

Chapter Nineteen: Ascending to the Palace of the Yāma Heaven.

At that time, through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata, in every world throughout the ten directions—in each of the four continents, specifically in Jambudvīpa to the south, as well as upon the summit of Mount Sumeru—the Tathāgata was seen dwelling amidst the assemblies.
All those bodhisattvas, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, expounded the Dharma, each of whom considered themselves to be constantly in the presence of the Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One, without departing from beneath all the Bodhi trees or from the summit of Mount Sumeru, proceeded toward the Jewel-Adorned Hall in the Palace of the Yāma Heaven.

At that time, the King of the Yāma Heaven, seeing the Buddha approaching from afar, immediately used his supernormal powers to manifest within his palace a lion throne of precious lotus-womb. It was adorned with a million tiers, interlaced with a million golden nets, and covered above by a million flower canopies, a million garland canopies, a million incense canopies, and a million jewel canopies. A million flower parasols, a million garland parasols, a million incense parasols, and a million jewel parasols were likewise arranged all around, while a million rays of light shone forth in brilliance.
A million kings of the Yāma Heaven paid him respectful homage;
a million Brahmā kings leaped for joy;
and a million bodhisattvas extolled and praised him.
A million celestial musical instruments each played a million kinds of Dharma sounds, continuing without interruption;
a million kinds of flower clouds, a million kinds of garland clouds, a million kinds of clouds of ornaments, and a million kinds of robe clouds completely covered the surroundings;
and a million kinds of mani-jewel clouds shone with brilliant light.

Born from ten million kinds of roots of goodness, sustained by the protection of ten million Buddhas, increased by ten million kinds of merit, purified by ten million kinds of profound resolve and ten million kinds of vows, arising from ten million kinds of practices, established by ten million kinds of dharmas, and manifested through ten million kinds of supernormal powers, it constantly emits ten million kinds of sounds and voices to reveal all phenomena.
Then, having prepared the seat, that Heavenly King bowed his body with palms joined toward the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and addressed him with reverence and respect, saying:
"Welcome, World-Honored One!"
Welcome, Sugata! Welcome, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!
We pray that you will have compassion for us and dwell in this palace.
Then, the Buddha accepted the invitation and immediately ascended the jeweled palace;
this occurred in the same manner throughout all the ten directions.
At that time, the Heavenly King recalled the roots of goodness he had planted in the presence of past Buddhas, and, sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, spoke these verses:
“The Tathāgata Yaśas is heard throughout the ten directions; Among all auspicious things, he is supreme.
He once entered this maṇi palace; Therefore, this place is most auspicious.”
The Tathāgata Jewel King, the Lamp of the World, is the most unsurpassed among all that is auspicious;
he once entered this pure palace, and therefore this place is most auspicious.
The Tathāgata Priyanetra sees without obstruction; he is the most supreme among all auspicious things.
He once entered this adorned palace; therefore, this place is most auspicious.
The Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara illuminates the world; among all auspicious things, he is supreme.
He once entered this most excellent palace; therefore, this place is the most auspicious of all.
The Tathāgata Ārādhana benefits the world; among all auspicious things, he is supreme.
He once entered this stainless palace; therefore, this place is most auspicious.
The Tathāgata Sugata has no teacher; he is the most supreme among all that is auspicious.
He once entered this Hall of Precious Incense, and for this reason, this place is most auspicious.
The Tathāgata Jitendriya, the lamp of the world, the most supreme among all that is auspicious—
once he entered this Hall of Wondrous Fragrance, therefore this place is most auspicious.
The Tathāgata Amoghadarśin, the hero among debaters and the supreme among all that is auspicious, once entered this Hall of the Universal Eye; therefore, this place is most auspicious.
The Tathāgata Anabhibhū, endowed with all virtues, is the most supreme among all that is auspicious;
he once entered this well-adorned palace, and therefore this place is most auspicious.
The Tathāgata Duṣkaracaryā benefits the world; among all auspicious things, he is supreme.
He once entered this Hall of Universal Adornment; therefore, this place is most auspicious.
Thus, in this world-system, the King of the Yāma Heaven, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, recalled the merits of the Buddhas of the past and extolled them;
likewise, the Kings of the Yāma Heavens in all worlds of the ten directions did the same, praising the merits of the Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Maṇi-Adorned Hall and sat cross-legged upon a lion throne within a treasury of precious lotuses.
Suddenly, this hall became vast and spacious, just like the dwellings of the various celestial hosts;
and so it was throughout all the worlds of the ten directions.

Chapter Twenty: Verses of Praise in the Palace of Yāma. At that time, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, there came from worlds beyond as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in a hundred thousand buddha-fields one great bodhisattva from each of the ten directions, each accompanied by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field. Their names were:

Bodhisattva Forest of Merit, Bodhisattva Forest of Wisdom, Bodhisattva Forest of Victory, Bodhisattva Forest of Fearlessness, Bodhisattva Forest of Shame and Remorse, Bodhisattva Forest of Diligence, Bodhisattva Forest of Power, Bodhisattva Forest of Practice, Bodhisattva Forest of Awakening, and Bodhisattva Forest of Knowledge.
The lands from which these bodhisattvas have come are as follows:

the world of Kindred Wisdom, the world of Banner Wisdom, the world of Jewel Wisdom, the world of Supreme Wisdom, the world of Lamp Wisdom, the world of Vajra Wisdom, the world of Blissful Wisdom, the world of Sun Wisdom, the world of Pure Wisdom, and the world of Brahma Wisdom.
These bodhisattvas each cultivated the pure conduct of brahmacarya under various Buddhas, namely:

the Buddha Ever-Abiding Eye, the Buddha Unconquerable Eye, the Buddha Non-Abiding Eye, the Buddha Immovable Eye, the Buddha Celestial Eye, the Buddha Liberation Eye, the Buddha Discerning Eye, the Buddha Radiant Mark Eye, the Buddha Supreme Eye, and the Buddha Azure Eye.

When these bodhisattvas had arrived at the Buddha’s abode, they prostrated at his feet; then, according to the direction from which each had come, they each magically manifested a lion throne made of a treasury of mani jewels, upon which they sat cross-legged.
In this world-system, bodhisattvas have gathered from the Yāma Heaven;
it is likewise in all worlds, for the names of those bodhisattvas, the worlds, and the Tathāgatas are all identical and without distinction.
At that time, the World-Honored One emitted hundreds of thousands of billions of rays of wondrously colored light from his two feet, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions;
within the Yāma Heaven palace, the Buddha and the great assembly were all clearly manifested.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Forest of Merit, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The Buddha emits a great radiance, Universally illuminating the ten directions;
One clearly beholds the Honored One of Gods and Humans, Whose penetration is free from all obstruction.”
The Buddha sat in the palace of Yāma, pervading the realms of the ten directions;
this matter is most extraordinary, something rare in the world.
The King of the Suyāma Heaven praised the ten Tathāgatas with verses.
Just as we have seen in this assembly, it is so in all places.
Those multitudes of bodhisattvas there all bear names identical to our own;
throughout the ten directions, they everywhere proclaim the unsurpassed Dharma.
The worlds from which they come have names that are likewise without distinction;
each, in the presence of their respective Buddhas, has purely cultivated the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
Those Tathāgatas as well are identical in name.
The lands are all prosperous and joyful, and his spiritual powers are entirely sovereign.
In every place throughout the ten directions, all say that the Buddha is here;
some see him among humans, while others see him dwelling in celestial palaces.
The Tathāgata dwells universally throughout all lands;
we now see the Buddha residing here in this celestial palace.
Having long ago made the vow for bodhicitta, it has reached throughout the realms of the ten directions.
Therefore, by the Buddha’s majestic power, which is all-pervading and inconceivable,
he remains far removed from worldly attachments and is fully endowed with boundless virtues;
thus he attains supernormal powers, such that there are no sentient beings who do not behold him.
Wandering through the realms of the ten directions, like space, they encounter no obstruction;
their single body is infinite bodies, yet their characteristics cannot be apprehended.
The Buddha’s merit is boundless—how could it ever be measured or known?
"Neither abiding nor departing, universally entering the Dharma-realm.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Forest of Wisdom, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The Great Teacher of the world, The Stainless, Unsurpassed Honored One,"
In inconceivable kalpas, it is difficult to encounter [a Buddha].
The Buddha emits a great radiance, such that there is none in the world who does not see it;
for the sake of the multitude, he extensively expounds the Dharma, bringing benefit to all living beings.
The Tathāgata has appeared in the world to dispel the darkness of ignorance for the sake of the world;
such a lamp of the world is rare and difficult to behold.
Having already cultivated generosity, ethical discipline, and patience, as well as diligence and meditative concentration.
The Prajñāpāramitā illuminates the world with this;
the Tathāgata has no equal, and none can be found to compare with him.
Those who do not understand the reality of dharmas are unable to perceive him.
The Buddha’s body and his supernormal powers are sovereign and inconceivable;
Without going and without coming, he preaches the Dharma to deliver sentient beings.
If there are those who see or hear him—the pure Teacher of Gods and Humans—
Forever departing from all evil realms, One abandons all suffering.
Even if one practices the conduct of enlightenment For immeasurable and incalculable eons,
If one cannot understand this meaning, One shall not attain Buddhahood.
If one can understand this meaning, their merit shall surpass that of one who, for inconceivable eons, made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas;
or one who filled immeasurable lands with precious jewels and offered them all to the Buddhas.
"Unable to understand this meaning, one will ultimately not achieve bodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śubhakānti, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Just as in the first month of summer, the sky is pure and free from the obscuration of clouds,"
The brilliant sun raises its radiant light, filling the ten directions without exception.
Its radiance is limitless and boundless; none are able to fathom or know it.
If this is so even for those with eyes, how much more so for those who are blind and in darkness?
The Buddhas are likewise thus: their merit is boundless;
throughout inconceivable eons, none can discern or know it.
All phenomena have no place of origin, nor is there any creator.
There is nothing from which they arise, and they cannot be differentiated.
All phenomena have no coming; therefore, there is no arising.
Since arising does not exist, cessation likewise cannot be found.
All phenomena are without birth, and likewise they are without cessation;
if one can understand them in this way, such a person sees the Tathāgata.
Because all phenomena are without birth, their intrinsic nature is non-existent.
One who discerns in this way understands the profound meaning.
Because phenomena lack intrinsic nature, there is nothing that can be fully known.
To understand phenomena in this manner is to ultimately have nothing to understand.
Regarding that which is said to have birth, they manifest all lands;
being able to know the nature of these lands, their minds are not deluded.
They observe the nature of the worlds and lands exactly as it truly is.
"If one can know this, one will skillfully explain all meanings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Fearless Forest, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The Tathāgata’s vast body is ultimately coextensive with the Dharma-realm."
Without leaving this seat, one pervades all places.
If one hears such a Dharma and reverently believes and delights in it,
they will forever leave behind the three evil realms and all sufferings and hardships.
Even if one were to travel to worlds beyond measure and beyond count,
with a single-minded desire to hear the sovereign power of the Tathāgata—
such are the teachings of all Buddhas, which constitute unsurpassed bodhi.
Even if one wished to hear it for but a moment, there would be no one capable of obtaining it.
If there were anyone in the past who believed in such a Buddha-dharma,
they have already become a Honored One among two-legged beings and act as a lamp for the world.
If there are those who shall hear of the Tathāgata’s power of mastery,
and having heard it, are able to give rise to faith, they too shall attain Buddhahood.
If there are those in the present who can believe in this Buddha-dharma, [they too shall attain Buddhahood].
They too shall attain perfect enlightenment and preach the Dharma without fear.
Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, this Dharma is extremely difficult to encounter;
those who are able to hear it should know that this is due to the power of their original vows.
If there be one who can receive and uphold these teachings of the Buddhas,
and having upheld them, proclaims them widely, this person shall attain Buddhahood.
How much more so for one who applies themselves with diligent vigor, with a firm mind that never abandons [the practice].
"You should know that such a person will certainly attain enlightenment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Forest of Shame and Remorse, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"If a person hears this rare and sovereign Dharma,..."
Able to give rise to a joyful heart, Swiftly clearing away the web of doubt and confusion.
