Far removed from all worldly faults and afflictions, Universally bestowing peace and happiness upon all sentient beings,
Capable of acting as an unequaled Great Teacher— Those of supreme virtue travel this path.
Constantly bestowing the gift of fearlessness upon sentient beings, causing all to rejoice universally;
with a mind pure and free from defilement, that peerless one practices this path.
With mental karma purified and perfectly disciplined, free from all conceptual proliferation and verbal faults,
their majestic radiance complete and revered by all— those most excellent ones practice this path.
Entering the true meaning and reaching the further shore, Abiding in the realm of merit with a mind forever tranquil,
Constantly protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas— Those who would extinguish existence travel this path.
Distant from self and free from affliction, they constantly proclaim the True Dharma with a great voice;
throughout the lands of the ten directions there is nowhere it does not reach—those who transcend all analogies practice this path.

The perfection of giving has been fully accomplished; adorned with the marks and signs of a hundred merits, all sentient beings who see him rejoice—such is the path traveled by that one of supreme wisdom.
The stage of wisdom is profoundly deep and difficult to enter;
those who can dwell well therein with sublime insight, their minds ultimately unshakable, practice this path with steadfast conduct.
They are able to enter all that exists within the dharma-realm; wherever they enter, they reach ultimate perfection.
Their supernormal powers are sovereign and all-encompassing; such is the path traversed by the light of those dharmas.
The Great Munis, unequaled among all, diligently cultivate samādhi free from dualistic marks;
their minds are ever in meditative concentration, delighting in tranquility—those who see universally practice this path.
Subtle and vast lands, each distinct yet mutually interpenetrating—
knowing them all exactly as they are within their own realms, the King of Wisdom Mountains traverses this path.

The mind is ever luminous and pure, free from all defilements; Without attachment within the three realms, one maintains the various precepts to reach the other shore— It is those with such a pure mind who practice this path.
Wisdom is boundless and ineffable, pervading the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space;
skillfully training and dwelling therein, those of adamantine wisdom traverse this path.
The realm of all Buddhas of the three periods of time— With wisdom they enter it skillfully and pervasively;
Never for a moment do they give rise to weariness or fatigue; Those most excellent ones practice this path.
Skillfully able to discern the dharmas of the ten powers, Thoroughly knowing all paths leading to every destination,
With unimpeded physical action attaining mastery— That body of merit practices this path.
Throughout the infinite and boundless realms of the ten directions, I shall protect and never abandon all sentient beings; those who are fearless practice this path.
Diligently practicing all the Buddha-dharmas, With a mind always energetic and never weary,
Purifying all the worlds— Such is the path traversed by that Great Dragon King.

Knowing that the faculties of sentient beings differ, and that their inclinations and understandings are immeasurably diverse, they clearly comprehend all various realms; those who enter universally practice this path.
To the immeasurable lands throughout the worlds of the ten directions, they go to take birth in them all without number;
never for a single thought-moment do they give rise to weariness—those who rejoice practice this path.
Universally emitting immeasurable nets of light, They illuminate all worlds;
That light shines so as to enter the nature of phenomena— This is the path traversed by those of excellent wisdom.

They cause the lands of the ten directions—countless billions of nayutas—to tremble, yet they do not allow sentient beings to feel any alarm or fear; this is the path traversed by those who benefit the world.
Skillfully understanding all methods of language, they exhaustively master questioning and responding;
possessing sagacity and eloquent wisdom such that there is nothing they do not know—this is the path traversed by those who are fearless.
Skillfully understanding all lands, whether inverted or upright, Discerning and contemplating them until reaching the ultimate,
Causing all to dwell upon the stage of inexhaustibility— This is the path traversed by those of supreme wisdom.
Immeasurable *nayuta*s of merit, all cultivated for the sake of seeking the Buddha-way;
having reached the further shore in all of these, this is the path traversed by inexhaustible conduct.
A great master who transcends the world, A lion’s roar of supreme eloquence,
Who leads all living beings to the further shore— This is the path traversed by those of pure mind.

The foremost dharma of the Buddhas’ empowerment—having already received this dharma upon their crowns, their minds dwell ever peacefully in the gateway of the True Dharma; with such a vast mind, they practice this path.
All sentient beings are immeasurably diverse; He thoroughly understands their minds in their entirety.
Resolutely upholding the treasury of the Buddha-dharma, He practices this path like Mount Sumeru.

Within each and every single word, they universally manifest immeasurable sounds, causing those sentient beings to understand according to their own kind; this is the unimpeded vision that practices this path.
Regarding all dharmas of written characters and speech, wisdom enters them skillfully without discrimination;
abiding within the realm of reality—this is the path traveled by those who have realized the nature of seeing.
Abiding securely in the profound ocean of the Great Dharma, Skillfully able to seal and determine all phenomena,
Thoroughly understanding the true gateway of the signlessness of phenomena— This is the path traversed by those who see reality.
They travel to each and every buddha-field, exhausting immeasurable and boundless eons;
observing and contemplating without a moment’s pause—this is the path traversed by those who are untiring.
Immeasurable and innumerable Tathāgatas, Each with various and distinct names, Are all clearly seen upon a single hair-tip; This is the path traversed by those of pure merit.
Upon the tip of a single hair, one sees Buddhas, Their number being immeasurable and beyond description;
It is likewise throughout the entire dharma-realm— Such is the path traversed by those sons of the Buddha.
Immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable eons, Are all clearly seen within a single thought-instant;
Knowing that their duration has no fixed characteristic— This is the path traversed by those practicing this liberation.
They cause those who behold them not to pass in vain, so that all may plant the seeds of causes and conditions within the Buddha-dharma;
yet their minds remain unattached to what they do— this is the path traversed by those Most Excellent Ones.
For nayutas of eons they constantly meet the Buddhas, never for a single thought-moment giving rise to weariness;
their hearts grow ever more joyful—this is the path traversed by Akṣayamati.
Throughout immeasurable and boundless eons, observing the realms of all sentient beings,
I have never seen a single being who follows the path traveled by this steadfast one.
Cultivating the boundless treasury of merit and wisdom, universally creating a cooling pool of merit,
benefiting all living beings— such is the path traversed by those of the foremost rank.
All the various categories within the dharma-realm, Pervading space in measureless abundance, Are understood to abide solely through verbal expression; This is the path traversed by this lion’s roar.
Able to enter, within each and every samādhi, Countless other samādhis in their entirety,
Reaching the profound and subtle depths of all dharma-gates— The Moon-Debater practices this path.
Diligently cultivating the power of patience to reach the further shore, Able to endure the most supreme dharma of quiescence,
With a mind that is equanimous and unshakable— This is the path traversed by those of boundless wisdom.
In a single world, at a single seat, his body remains unmoving and eternally tranquil;
yet he manifests his form everywhere throughout all realms—this is the path traversed by that one of boundless body.
Immeasurable and boundless lands, all are made to enter together into a single atom;
universally contained without obstruction—those of boundless thought and practice follow this path.
Thoroughly comprehending what is possible and what is impossible, they are able to enter universally into all the bases of power;
having accomplished the supreme powers of the Tathāgata, this is the path traversed by those of foremost power.
Throughout the past, future, and present worlds, they fully comprehend with wisdom all immeasurable and boundless karmic retributions;
this is the path traversed by those who possess thorough understanding.
Thoroughly understanding the proper and improper times in the world, they discipline all sentient beings as is appropriate;
never failing to act in accordance with what is suitable—this is the path traveled by those who possess excellent discernment.
Well-guarding the actions of body, speech, and mind, Always causing one to practice in accordance with the Dharma,
Free from all attachments and subduing the hosts of Māras— This is the path traveled by those whose minds possess wisdom.
Attaining skillfulness regarding all phenomena, One is able to enter the state of the equality of suchness;
With inexhaustible eloquence, one proclaims the teachings— This is the path traveled by those who practice the Buddha-way.
Having perfected the gateways of dhāraṇī, they are skillfully established in the treasury of non-obstruction;
having attained complete penetration into all dharma-realms, this is the path traveled by those who have entered deeply.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely equal in mind and identical in wisdom;
they are of one nature and one characteristic without distinction—this is the path traversed by those of unimpeded lineage.
Having pierced through the film of all ignorance, They have entered deeply into the vast ocean of wisdom;
Universally bestowing the pure eye upon all sentient beings— This is the path traveled by those who possess eyes.

Having perfected all the qualities of the Guides, possessing impartial supernormal powers and non-dual conduct, they have attained the sovereign power of the Tathāgatas; this is the path traveled by those who practice well.
Wandering through all worlds in every direction, Universally raining down the boundless rain of the sublime Dharma,
Causing all to attain definitive understanding of its meaning— This is the path traversed by those in the Cloud of Dharma.
One who can give rise to profound, pure faith in the Buddha’s wisdom and liberation, never regressing,
and through that faith produce the root of wisdom— this is the path traveled by those who learn well.
In a single thought-moment, they fully comprehend all sentient beings without exception;
having realized the intrinsic nature of those beings' minds, they have attained the path traveled by those who realize the absence of intrinsic nature.
Throughout all lands in the entire Dharma-realm, they are able to manifest and travel there in infinite numbers;
their bodies are most wondrous and peerless—this is the path traversed by those of incomparable conduct.
Buddha-fields are boundless and beyond numbering; within them dwell immeasurable Buddhas.
Therein, Bodhisattvas appear before them all, drawing near to serve and honor them with reverence.
The Bodhisattva is able, with but a single body, To enter into samādhi and remain in tranquil concentration;
Causing his bodies to appear as infinite in number, Each and every one arising from within that samādhi.
The dwelling of the Bodhisattva is most profound and wondrous; their conduct and deeds transcend all conceptual proliferation.
Their minds are pure and ever joyful, able to bring all sentient beings to complete delight.
The various faculties and their diverse applications, he is able to perceive them all clearly with wisdom;
yet he realizes that these faculties have no basis, for this is the path traveled by those who tame the untamable.
Able to skillfully discern through expedient means, they attain mastery over all phenomena;
though the worlds of the ten directions are each different, they perform buddha-work within them all.
Their faculties are subtle and their conduct likewise; they are able to expound the Dharma extensively for the sake of sentient beings.
Who among those who hear it would not rejoice? Such is the path traversed within space.
The eye of wisdom is pure and peerless, clearly seeing all phenomena;
such skillful discernment through wisdom is the path traveled by those who are unequaled.
All inexhaustible and vast merit, May all practices be brought to ultimate completion;
May all sentient beings be rendered entirely pure— This is the path traversed by the Peerless One.
Universally exhorting them to cultivate the dharmas that aid the Path, Causing all to dwell securely on the stage of skillful means;
Delivering and liberating countless sentient beings, Yet never for a moment giving rise to the notion of "sentient beings."
Observing all capacities and conditions, first protecting their minds so that they remain free from strife,
and universally showing sentient beings the place of peace and security— this is the path traversed by those of skillful means.

Having accomplished the supreme, foremost wisdom, And being fully endowed with immeasurable, boundless wisdom, He is fearless among the fourfold assembly; This is the path traversed by the wisdom of skillful means.
They are able to enter all worlds and all phenomena, attaining mastery therein;
they also enter into all assemblies, liberating countless sentient beings.
Throughout all lands in the ten directions, you beat the great Dharma drum to awaken all sentient beings;
as the supreme and unsurpassed master of the gift of Dharma, this is the path traversed by the Immortal One.

Sitting upright in the full lotus posture with a single body, they fill immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions without their bodies becoming cramped; this is the path traversed by those of the Dharma-body.
Able to expound immeasurable and boundless teachings from within a single meaning and a single phrase,
yet with no limit to be found— this is the path traversed by those of boundless wisdom.
Having well practiced the liberation of the Buddha, They attain the unobstructed wisdom of the Buddha;
Accomplishing fearlessness as heroes of the world— This is the path traversed by those of skillful means.
They thoroughly know the oceans of worlds in the ten directions, And they also know the oceans of all Buddha-fields;
Fully understanding the ocean of wisdom and the ocean of Dharma, All sentient beings who behold them rejoice.

Sometimes manifesting entry into the womb and initial birth, Or manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening— Thus causing all in the world to behold them; This is the path traversed by those who are boundless.
Within immeasurable billions of lands, he manifests his body entering nirvana;
yet in truth, he does not abandon his vows to return to quiescence—this is the path traversed by this heroic debater.
The firm, subtle, and wondrous single body is equal to the Buddha, without distinction;
yet according to the various perceptions of sentient beings, it appears differently—this is the path traversed by the One True Body.
The Dharma-realm is equal and without distinction, Possessing infinite and boundless meanings;
Delighting in contemplating its single characteristic with an unwavering mind— This is the path traversed by the wise of the three periods of time.
Regarding all sentient beings and the Buddha-dharma, they establish and empower them to ultimate perfection;
possessing the power of retention equal to that of a Buddha, these supreme holders traverse this path.
With unimpeded supernormal powers like those of a Buddha, with unimpeded divine eye most pure,
and with unimpeded faculty of hearing that hears well— this is the path traversed by one of unimpeded mind.
All supernormal powers are fully possessed; According to their wisdom, all are accomplished.
They skillfully know all things without peer; This is the path traversed by these wise and virtuous ones.
His mind is in right concentration, unshakable; his wisdom is vast and without limit.
He clearly penetrates all spheres of experience—the path traversed by all who see.
Having reached the shore of all merit, they are able to deliver sentient beings in successive order;
their minds are ultimately never weary or satisfied—this is the path traveled by those who are ever-diligent.
All the Buddha-dharmas existing throughout the three periods of time, they know and see them all;
born from the lineage of the Tathāgatas, those sons of the Buddhas traverse this path.
Having perfected speech that is compliant and harmonious, they skillfully subdue discordant discourse;
always able to advance toward the Bodhi of the Buddha, this is the path traveled by those of boundless wisdom.
A single light shines forth, touching all without limit, Pervading every land throughout the ten directions;
It causes the entire world to attain great illumination— This is the path traveled by the Destroyer of Darkness.
According to those who should see him and those who should make offerings, he manifests the pure body of a Tathāgata;
he teaches and transforms hundreds of thousands of billions of sentient beings, and likewise adorns the Buddha-fields.
To cause sentient beings to transcend the world, All sublime practices are cultivated;
These practices are vast and boundless— How could anyone be able to know them?
Even if one were to manifest unspeakably many emanations, equal in number to the dharma-realm and empty space,
and all together extol his merits, they could not exhaust them even in hundreds of thousands of millions of eons.
The merits of the Bodhisattva are boundless; All practices are fully perfected.
Even if immeasurable and infinite Buddhas Were to speak for immeasurable eons, they could not exhaust them.
How much less could the gods and humans of the world, or all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
ever reach a final conclusion by praising and extolling [it] throughout immeasurable and boundless kalpas?
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty, and Volume Twenty-one,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Command.
22. The Chapter on the Ten Inexhaustible Treasuries, the Twenty-second.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Guṇakanda addressed the assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of treasuries, which all Buddhas of the past, future, and present have taught, will teach, and are now teaching.
What are the ten? They are:

the treasury of faith, the treasury of ethical discipline, the treasury of self-respect, the treasury of moral dread, the treasury of learning, the treasury of generosity, the treasury of wisdom, the treasury of mindfulness, the treasury of retention, and the treasury of eloquence; these are the ten.
“O Son of the Buddha! What is the treasury of faith of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

This bodhisattva has faith that all phenomena are empty; faith that all phenomena are signless; faith that all phenomena are wishless; faith that all phenomena are unconditioned; faith that all phenomena are non-discriminative; faith that all phenomena have no basis; faith that all phenomena are immeasurable; faith that all phenomena are unsurpassed; faith that all phenomena are difficult to transcend; and faith that all phenomena are unborn.”
If a bodhisattva can thus accord with all dharmas and, having given rise to pure faith, hears that the teachings of all Buddhas are inconceivable and their mind does not become timid;
hears that all Buddhas are inconceivable and their mind does not become timid;
hears that the realm of sentient beings is inconceivable and their mind does not become timid;
Hearing that the dharma-realm is inconceivable, their minds do not become timid or weak;
hearing that the realm of empty space is inconceivable, their minds do not become timid or weak;
hearing that the realm of nirvana is inconceivable, their minds do not become timid or weak.
Hearing that the past world is inconceivable, their minds are not cowed;
hearing that the future world is inconceivable, their minds are not cowed;
hearing that the present world is inconceivable, their minds are not cowed.
Hearing that one enters all inconceivable eons, the mind does not become timid or weak. Why is this?
Because this bodhisattva possesses single-minded, firm faith in all Buddhas, knowing that the wisdom of the Buddhas is boundless and inexhaustible.

In the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions, there are respectively immeasurable Buddhas who have attained, are attaining, or will attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; who have appeared in the world, are appearing in the world, or will appear in the world; and who have entered *nirvāṇa*, are entering *nirvāṇa*, or will enter *nirvāṇa*. The wisdom of those Buddhas neither increases nor decreases, is neither born nor extinguished, neither advances nor recedes, is neither near nor far, and is without knowing or abandoning.
This bodhisattva enters the wisdom of the Buddhas and accomplishes boundless, inexhaustible faith;

having attained this faith, their mind does not regress, their mind is not distracted, it is indestructible, free from defilement, and always possesses its fundamental basis. They accord with the sages, dwell in the family of the Tathāgatas, protect and uphold the lineage of all Buddhas, increase the faith and understanding of all bodhisattvas, accord with the roots of goodness of all Tathāgatas, and give rise to the skillful means of all Buddhas.
This is called the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s treasury of faith.
When a Bodhisattva dwells in this treasury of faith, they are able to hear and retain all Buddha-dharmas, and explain them to sentient beings, causing them all to attain awakening.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the treasury of precepts of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

This bodhisattva accomplishes the precept of universal benefit, the precept of non-acceptance, the precept of non-abiding, the precept of freedom from regret, the precept of freedom from contention, the precept of non-affliction, the precept of freedom from impurity, the precept of freedom from craving, the precept of freedom from fault, and the precept of freedom from transgression.”
What is the precept of universal benefit?
This bodhisattva upholds the pure precepts fundamentally for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.
What is meant by "not receiving the precepts"?

This bodhisattva does not undertake any of the precepts of the non-Buddhists; rather, being naturally diligent by nature, they uphold the equal and pure precepts of all the Tathāgatas, the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
What is meant by "non-abiding precepts"?
When this bodhisattva upholds the precepts, the mind does not abide in the desire realm, does not abide in the form realm, and does not abide in the formless realm.
Why is this? Because one upholds the precepts without seeking birth in those realms.
What is the precept of being without regret?
This bodhisattva always dwells securely in a mind free from regret.
Why is this? Because he commits no grave offenses, practices neither flattery nor deceit, and does not violate the pure precepts.
What is the precept of non-contention?
This bodhisattva does not disparage what was previously established, nor does he innovate new rules;
his mind always remains in conformity, directed toward the precepts of nirvāṇa, fully receiving and upholding them without any transgression.
One does not maintain the precepts by causing distress to other sentient beings or making them suffer; rather, one maintains the precepts with the aspiration that all hearts may always be joyful.
What is meant by the precept of non-affliction and non-harming?

This bodhisattva does not, for the sake of the precepts, study various incantations or arts, or prepare medicinal prescriptions to harm sentient beings; rather, they uphold the precepts solely for the purpose of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings.
What is the unadulterated precept?
This bodhisattva does not cling to extreme views and does not maintain adulterated precepts; rather, observing dependent origination, they maintain the precept of renunciation.
What is the precept free from greedy seeking?
This bodhisattva does not manifest extraordinary signs to display their own virtue, but maintains the precepts solely for the sake of fulfilling the dharma of renunciation.
What is meant by "precepts free from fault"?
This bodhisattva does not become conceited, saying, "I uphold the precepts";
nor does he look down upon or disparage those who break the precepts, causing them shame;
rather, he maintains the precepts with a single-minded focus.
What is meant by being without transgressions of the precepts?

This bodhisattva permanently abandons killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, divisive speech, harsh speech, and idle chatter, as well as covetousness, malice, and wrong views, fully upholding the ten types of wholesome karma.
When a bodhisattva maintains these precepts without transgression, they reflect thus:
"All sentient beings who violate the pure precepts do so because of their perverted views;
only the Buddha, the World-Honored One, can know by what causes and conditions sentient beings give rise to such perversions and violate the pure precepts."
"I shall achieve unsurpassed bodhi and extensively expound the true Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, causing them to leave behind all perversions.
This is called the second treasury of precepts of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the treasury of shame of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
This bodhisattva recollects the various evils committed in the past and thereby gives rise to shame.”
That Bodhisattva reflects within his own mind:

"Since beginningless time, I and all sentient beings have alternately served as fathers, mothers, brothers, sisters, sons, and daughters to one another. Because we were possessed of greed, hatred, delusion, pride, flattery, deceit, and all other afflictions, we have harmed and injured one another, vying with one another for gain, committing adultery, and killing;

there is no evil we have not done. All sentient beings are likewise; because they fully commit various evils through their afflictions, each fails to revere, respect, obey, humble themselves before, instruct, or protect the others, instead harming one another and acting as mutual enemies."
Reflecting upon myself and all sentient beings—past, future, and present—who have practiced shameless conduct, there are none of the Buddhas of the three periods of time who do not know and see this.
If I do not now sever this conduct of shamelessness, the Buddhas of the three periods of time will likewise behold me.
How could I continue to act without ceasing?
This would be utterly improper.

"Therefore, I should single-mindedly eliminate [these afflictions], realize unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and extensively preach the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.
This is called the third treasury of shame (hrī-kośa) of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the treasury of shame of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

This bodhisattva feels personal shame for having, from the past until now, engaged in various kinds of greedy seeking amidst the five desires without ever reaching satiety, thereby increasing all afflictions such as greed, anger, and delusion.
"I should not engage in such conduct again. He further thought: "Sentient beings lack wisdom;
they give rise to various afflictions, fully practice unwholesome dharmas, do not respect one another, do not honor one another, and even go so far as to treat each other as enemies."

Such evils as these they have committed without exception; having committed them, they rejoice, pursue them, and praise them. Blind and devoid of the eye of wisdom, they possess neither knowledge nor insight.
Entering the womb of a woman, one undergoes birth and forms a defiled body, ultimately reaching the state where the hair turns white and the face becomes wrinkled.
One with wisdom observes that this is merely an impure phenomenon arising from sexual desire, as all Buddhas of the three periods have known and seen.
If I were still to engage in such deeds now, I would be deceiving the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Therefore, I shall practice a sense of shame and quickly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, so as to extensively preach the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.
This is called the fourth treasury of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: the treasury of shame.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s treasury of hearing?
This Bodhisattva knows that because this exists, that exists; because this does not exist, that does not exist;
because this arises, that arises; and because this ceases, that ceases.
These are mundane phenomena; these are supramundane phenomena;
these are conditioned phenomena; these are unconditioned phenomena;
these are determinate phenomena; these are indeterminate phenomena.
What is meant by "because this exists, that exists"?
It means:
because ignorance exists, volitional formations exist.
What is meant by "because this thing does not exist, that thing does not exist"?
It means:
because consciousness does not exist, name-and-form do not exist.
What is meant by "because this arises, that arises"? It means:
because craving arises, suffering arises.
What is meant by "because this thing ceases, that thing ceases"?
It means:
because existence ceases, birth ceases.
What are the worldly dharmas? They are:
form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
What are the supramundane dharmas? They are:
ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
What are conditioned phenomena? They are:
the realm of desire, the realm of form, the realm of formlessness, and the realm of sentient beings.
What are the unconditioned dharmas?
They are: space, nirvāṇa, cessation through deliberation, cessation not through deliberation, and the abiding nature of dependent origination.
What are the dharmas that are determinately taught? They are:

the four noble truths, the four fruits of śrāmaṇya, the four analytical knowledges, the four fearlessnesses, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
What are the indeterminate dharmas? They are as follows:
the world is finite, the world is infinite, the world is both finite and infinite, and the world is neither finite nor infinite.
The world is eternal; the world is non-eternal; the world is both eternal and non-eternal; the world is neither eternal nor non-eternal.

After the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, he exists; after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, he does not exist; after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, he both exists and does not exist; after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, he neither exists nor does not exist.
The self and sentient beings exist; the self and sentient beings do not exist; the self and sentient beings both exist and do not exist; the self and sentient beings neither exist nor do not exist.
In the past, how many Tathāgatas entered parinirvāṇa?
How many śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas entered parinirvāṇa?
In the future, how many Tathāgatas will there be?
How many śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are there?
How many sentient beings?
And how many Buddhas currently abide?
How many śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas abide?
How many sentient beings abide?
Which Tathāgata appeared first?
Which śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas appear first?
Which sentient beings appear first?
And which Tathāgatas appear last?
Which śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas emerge last?
Which sentient beings emerge last?
Which dharma is foremost at the beginning?
Which phenomenon is the very last?
From where does the world come, and to what place does it go?
How many worlds are formed?
How many world-systems are destroyed?
From where do world-systems come, and to what place do they go?
What constitutes the initial limit of birth and death?
What constitutes the final limit of birth and death?
This is called an indeterminate (avyākṛta) phenomenon.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
"All sentient beings within the cycle of birth and death lack extensive learning and are thus unable to fully comprehend all these dharmas.
I shall now resolve my mind to uphold the treasury of extensive learning, realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and preach the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings."
This is called the fifth treasury of learning of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the treasury of giving of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
This bodhisattva practices ten kinds of giving, namely:

giving by apportioning, exhaustive giving, internal giving, external giving, internal-and-external giving, all-encompassing giving, giving of the past, giving of the future, giving of the present, and ultimate giving.
O Son of the Buddha!
What is the bodhisattva’s practice of partial giving?
This bodhisattva is by nature compassionate and kind, and delights in practicing generosity.
If one obtains delicious food, one does not consume it exclusively for oneself, but must first share it with sentient beings before eating;
all things received are treated in this same manner.
When eating, one should reflect thus:
"Within my body dwell eighty thousand families of worms who depend upon me for their existence. When my body is satisfied with pleasure, they too are satisfied with pleasure;
when my body suffers from hunger, they too suffer from hunger."
"As I now receive all this food and drink, may all sentient beings everywhere obtain full satisfaction.
Thinking thus, he eats it for the sake of giving to others, without craving its flavor.
He further reflects:
"For a long night, I have been attached to this body, desiring to satisfy it by partaking of food and drink.
Now, by giving this food as a gift to sentient beings, I vow that I shall forever sever my greedy attachment to the body."
This is called "the gift of apportionment.
What is the bodhisattva’s "gift of total exhaustion"?
O Son of the Buddha!

This bodhisattva obtains various kinds of superior food and drink, incense, flowers, clothing, and articles of livelihood. If he were to enjoy these for himself, he would live in peace and comfort with a long life; yet if he were to withhold them from himself and give them to others, he would fall into poverty and suffer an early death.
At that time, suppose someone were to come and say:
"Whatever you currently possess, you must give it all to me.
The Bodhisattva reflects to himself:
"Since beginningless time, I have lost my body countless times due to hunger, yet I have never obtained even so much as a hair's breadth of benefit for sentient beings or gained any wholesome merit."

Now I, too, shall likewise relinquish my life as in the past; therefore, for the benefit of sentient beings, I should give up everything I possess, even unto the end of my life, without any stinginess.
This is called the "exhaustive giving.
What is the bodhisattva’s internal giving?
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva is in the prime of youth, handsome and beautiful, his body adorned with fragrant flowers and garments;
having just received the consecration, he holds the rank of a Wheel-Turning King, possessing the seven treasures and ruling over the four quarters of the world.
At that time, a certain person came and addressed the king, saying:
"Great King, you should know!
I am now old and decrepit, afflicted by a grave illness; solitary and emaciated, my death will not be long in coming."
If I may obtain the hands, feet, blood, flesh, head, eyes, marrow, and bones of the King’s body, my own life shall surely find hope for survival.
I only pray that Your Majesty will not further deliberate or harbor any hesitation;
simply look upon me with compassion and grant them to me as a gift!
At that time, the Bodhisattva thought to himself:
"This body of mine will certainly die in the end, yielding not a single benefit;
it is fitting that I should quickly abandon it now to rescue sentient beings."
Having reflected thus, he gives it away with a mind free from regret.
This is called internal giving.
What is the external giving of a bodhisattva?
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva is in the prime of youth, possesses a beautiful complexion, and is endowed with all the marks of excellence; he adorns his body with famous flowers and superior garments.
Having first received the consecration and ascended to the rank of a Wheel-Turning King, he was endowed with the seven treasures and reigned over the four quarters of the world.
At that time, someone might come and say to the king:
"I am now impoverished and destitute, oppressed by manifold sufferings."
"I only pray that you, out of your benevolence, will take special pity on me and relinquish this royal throne for my sake;
I shall govern it and enjoy the king's blessings and happiness!
At that time, the Bodhisattva thought to himself:
"All that is flourishing and prosperous must inevitably decline; once it has declined, one can no longer further benefit sentient beings.
I should now fulfill their request and satisfy their wishes."
Having formed this thought, he immediately gave it away without any regret.
This is called external giving.
What is the bodhisattva’s internal and external giving?
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva, as previously described, occupies the station of a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*), is endowed with the seven treasures, and rules over the four continents.
At that time, someone might come and say:
"Your Majesty has long occupied this position of a Wheel-Turning King, yet I have never attained it.
I only pray that Your Majesty will relinquish it to me, and that you, along with your person, become my servant!"
At that time, the Bodhisattva thought to himself:
"My body, my wealth and treasures, and even my royal throne—all these are impermanent and subject to decay."
"I am now in the prime of my youth and possess the wealth of the world;
since a beggar stands before me, I should use that which is not firm to seek the Dharma of the firm.
Having formed this thought, he immediately gave it away, even performing labor with his own body with diligent devotion, his mind free from any regret.
This is called internal and external giving.
What is the bodhisattva’s all-encompassing giving?
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva is also as described above: he occupies the rank of a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*), possesses the seven treasures in full, and rules over the four continents.
At that time, immeasurable impoverished people come before him and speak these words:
"Great King, your fame resounds throughout the ten directions; we have come here out of admiration for your reputation.
We each now have our own requests; we pray that you will universally bestow your compassion and cause them to be fulfilled!"

At that time, those poor people begged from the great king for his kingdom, or for his wife and children, or for his hands and feet, his blood and flesh, his heart and lungs, his head, eyes, marrow, and brain.
At that time, the Bodhisattva thought to himself:
"All those gathered through affection must inevitably part; yet, this [wealth] brings no benefit to sentient beings.
Now, desiring to forever abandon craving and attachment, I shall fulfill the wishes of sentient beings with all these things that are destined to be dispersed."
Having formed this thought, he gives everything away with a heart free from regret, and does not give rise to feelings of aversion or contempt toward sentient beings.
This is called "universal giving."
What is the past giving of a bodhisattva?

This bodhisattva hears of all the merits of the buddhas and bodhisattvas of the past; having heard them, they do not become attached, but realizes they are non-existent, gives rise to no discrimination, does not crave or savor them, nor seeks to acquire them, remaining without any dependence.
They see phenomena as like dreams, lacking any solidity.
Regarding all roots of goodness, they do not give rise to the notion of existence, nor do they rely upon anything;
rather, for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings who are attached to grasping, and in order to bring the Buddha-dharma to maturity, they expound it;
furthermore, they observe as follows:
"Past dharmas, when sought throughout the ten directions, are entirely unobtainable.
Having formed this thought, one ultimately relinquishes all past dharmas.
This is called past giving.
What is the future giving of a bodhisattva?

When this bodhisattva hears of the practices cultivated by all future Buddhas, they realize them to be non-existent; they do not grasp at their signs, nor do they specifically desire to be reborn in the lands of those Buddhas. They neither savor nor cling to them, yet they do not give rise to aversion.
They do not dedicate their roots of goodness toward those realms, nor do they allow their roots of goodness to regress because of them. They constantly and diligently practice, never abandoning them;
they do so only because they wish to gather in sentient beings through those very realms, preaching the truth for them and causing them to mature in the Buddha-dharma.
However, this Dharma has no location, nor is it without a location; it is neither internal nor external, neither near nor far.
Furthermore, one should reflect:
"If a phenomenon does not exist, it cannot be that it is not to be relinquished."
This is called future giving.
What is the present giving of a bodhisattva?

This bodhisattva hears of the assemblies of the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmā Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmakāyika-parṣadya Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābhā Heaven, the Apramāṇābhā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubha Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Vṛhatphala Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Vṛhatphala Heaven, the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; and even hears of the complete merits of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Having heard this, their minds are neither deluded nor submerged; they do not contract nor disperse, but simply contemplate all conditioned phenomena as being like dreams and unreal, free from any craving or attachment.

For the sake of causing sentient beings to abandon the evil realms, they cultivate the bodhisattva path with a mind free of discrimination, and they expound [the Dharma] to bring about the fulfillment of the Buddha-dharma.
This is called present giving.
What is the ultimate giving of a bodhisattva?
O Son of the Buddha!
Suppose there were immeasurable sentient beings—some lacking eyes, some lacking ears, or others lacking noses, tongues, hands, or feet—who came to the Bodhisattva’s presence and said to him:
"Our bodies are of meager fortune, our faculties being incomplete."
“I only pray that you, out of your benevolence, will employ skillful means to relinquish what you possess so that I may be made complete.
Upon hearing this, the Bodhisattva immediately bestowed it upon him;
even if, because of this, his sense faculties were rendered incomplete for incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*), he would not give rise to a single thought of regret or stinginess.

One should simply observe one's own body: from its initial entry into the womb as an impure and minute form, through the fetal stages and the development of the sense organs, until birth, old age, sickness, and death.

Furthermore, one observes that this body has no reality; it possesses neither shame nor remorse; it is not the property of the noble ones; it is foul, filthy, and unclean; it is a framework of bones held together by joints, smeared with blood and flesh; it constantly flows from nine apertures; and it is something loathed and despised by others.
Having made this contemplation, they do not give rise to even a single thought of attachment or craving.
They further reflect:
"This body is precarious and fragile; it possesses no solidity."
How could I now give rise to attachment?
I ought to bestow these upon him to fulfill his wish.
Acting as I have done, I shall thereby guide all sentient beings, causing them not to produce craving for body or mind, so that they may all achieve the pure body of wisdom.
This is called ultimate giving.
This constitutes the sixth treasury of giving for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the treasury of wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
This bodhisattva knows form as it truly is; knows the arising of form as it truly is; knows the cessation of form as it truly is; and knows the path leading to the cessation of form as it truly is.

He knows feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as they truly are; he knows the arising of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as it truly is; he knows the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as it truly is; he knows the path leading to the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as it truly is.

He knows ignorance as it truly is; he knows the arising of ignorance as it truly is; he knows the cessation of ignorance as it truly is; he knows the path leading to the cessation of ignorance as it truly is.

He knows craving as it truly is; he knows the arising of craving as it truly is; he knows the cessation of craving as it truly is; he knows the path leading to the cessation of craving as it truly is.

He knows the śrāvakas as they truly are; he knows the dharmas of the śrāvakas as they truly are; he knows the origin of the śrāvakas as it truly is; he knows the nirvāṇa of the śrāvakas as it truly is. He knows the pratyekabuddhas as they truly are;

he knows the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas as they truly are; he knows the origin of the pratyekabuddhas as it truly is; he knows the nirvāṇa of the pratyekabuddhas as it truly is. He knows the bodhisattvas as they truly are;
he knows the dharmas of the bodhisattvas as they truly are; he knows the origin of the bodhisattvas as it truly is; he knows the nirvāṇa of the bodhisattvas as it truly is.
How is this known?

It is known that all things are produced from the causes and conditions of karmic retribution and volitional formations (*saṃskāra*); they are entirely false, empty, and devoid of reality; they are neither self nor solid; and there is not even the slightest phenomenon (*dharma*) that can be established as existing.
Desiring to cause sentient beings to know their true nature, he extensively proclaims it for them.
What does he proclaim?
He proclaims that all phenomena are indestructible.
What dharmas are indestructible? Form is indestructible;

feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are indestructible; ignorance is indestructible; and the dharmas of the śrāvakas, the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, and the dharmas of the bodhisattvas are indestructible.

Why is this? Because all phenomena are without action, without an agent, without verbal expression, without location, unarisen, unoriginated, neither given nor taken, without movement, and without functional activity.

When Bodhisattvas have accomplished such immeasurable treasuries of wisdom, they comprehend all phenomena through slight means; they attain spontaneous and clear penetration, awakening without depending on others.
This treasury of wisdom is inexhaustible because it possesses ten kinds of inexhaustibility; therefore, it is called "inexhaustible.
What are these ten? They are as follows:

Because the skillfulness of extensive learning is inexhaustible; because the proximity to spiritual friends is inexhaustible; because the skillful discernment of words and meanings is inexhaustible; because the entry into the profound realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is inexhaustible; because the adornment with the wisdom of a single flavor is inexhaustible; because the accumulation of all merit with a tireless mind is inexhaustible; because the entry into all *dhāraṇī* gates is inexhaustible; because the ability to discern the languages and sounds of all sentient beings is inexhaustible; because the ability to sever the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings is inexhaustible; and because the manifestation of the spiritual powers of all Buddhas for all sentient beings to teach, transform, and subdue them so that their practice never ceases is inexhaustible—these are the ten.
This is the seventh treasury of wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
One who dwells in this treasury attains inexhaustible wisdom and is universally able to awaken all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha! What is the treasury of mindfulness of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas?

This Bodhisattva abandons delusion and confusion, attaining perfect mindfulness. He recollects one birth, two births, and even ten births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of births; eons of formation, eons of destruction, eons of both formation and destruction; not just a single eon of formation, a single eon of destruction, or a single eon of both formation and destruction; but hundreds of eons, thousands of eons, hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas*, and even up to incalculable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, uncountable, inexpressible, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and unspeakably unspeakable eons.”
To recollect the name of one Buddha, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;
to recollect one Buddha appearing in the world to bestow predictions of enlightenment, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas appearing in the world to bestow predictions of enlightenment;
to recollect one Buddha appearing in the world to preach a sutra, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas appearing in the world to preach sutras.
As it is with the *sūtra*, so it is with the *geya*, *vyākaraṇa*, *gāthā*, *nidāna*, *udāna*, *itivṛttaka*, *jātaka*, *vaipulya*, *adbhutadharma*, *avadāna*, and *upadeśa*;
likewise, one recollects a single assembly, up to an unspeakably unspeakable number of assemblies;
and one recollects the exposition of a single teaching, up to the exposition of an unspeakably unspeakable number of teachings.
He contemplates the various natures of a single faculty, up to the various natures of faculties that are unspeakably unspeakable;
he contemplates the immeasurable various natures of a single faculty, up to the immeasurable various natures of faculties that are unspeakably unspeakable;
he contemplates the various natures of a single affliction, up to the various natures of afflictions that are unspeakably unspeakable.
One contemplates the various natures of one samādhi, up to the various natures of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of samādhis.
This mindfulness has ten aspects, namely:

tranquil mindfulness, pure mindfulness, unclouded mindfulness, lucid mindfulness, dust-free mindfulness, mindfulness free from various kinds of dust, stainless mindfulness, radiant mindfulness, delightful mindfulness, and unobstructed mindfulness.

When a bodhisattva dwells in this mindfulness, nothing in all the worlds can disturb them; no heterodox doctrines can cause them to waver; their roots of goodness from past lives become entirely purified; they remain unstained by worldly dharmas; they cannot be destroyed by any māras or non-Buddhists; and they experience no loss of memory when taking rebirth in future bodies.
Throughout the past, present, and future, their preaching of the Dharma is inexhaustible;
and as they dwell together with sentient beings in all worlds, they are never at fault.
Entering the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas without obstruction, and being able to draw near to the presence of every Buddha—
this is called the eighth treasury of mindfulness of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s treasury of retention?
This Bodhisattva retains the sūtras spoken by all Buddhas, including their phrases, sentences, and underlying principles, without any forgetfulness or loss."
Maintaining [the name] for one lifetime, up to unspeakably unspeakable lifetimes;
maintaining the name of one Buddha, up to unspeakably unspeakable Buddhas;
maintaining it for the duration of one eon, up to unspeakably unspeakable eons.
They uphold the prediction of enlightenment of one Buddha, up to the prediction of enlightenment of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;
they uphold one sūtra, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sūtras;
they uphold one assembly, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of assemblies.
They maintain and expound a single teaching, even unto the expounding of unspeakably unspeakable teachings;
they maintain the immeasurable variety of natures of a single faculty, even unto the immeasurable variety of natures of unspeakably unspeakable faculties;
they maintain the various natures of a single affliction, even unto the various natures of unspeakably unspeakable afflictions.
They maintain the various natures of one samādhi, up to the various natures of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of samādhis.
O Son of the Buddha!

This Treasury of Sustenance is boundless and difficult to fill; it is difficult to reach its bottom, difficult to approach, and cannot be overcome. It is immeasurable and inexhaustible, possessing great majestic power; it is the realm of the Buddhas, which only a Buddha can fully comprehend.
This is called the ninth treasury-retention of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s treasury of eloquence?

This bodhisattva possesses profound wisdom and thoroughly understands the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). He extensively expounds all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings, never contradicting the sūtras of any Buddha;
he may preach a single chapter of the Dharma, or even an unspeakably unspeakable number of chapters of the Dharma.
To speak the name of one Buddha, up to the names of unspeakably unspeakable Buddhas;

likewise, to speak of one world, to speak of the prediction of enlightenment for one Buddha, to speak of one sūtra, to speak of one assembly, to speak of the exposition of one Dharma, to speak of the immeasurable and various natures of a single faculty, to speak of the immeasurable and various natures of a single affliction, to speak of the immeasurable and various natures of a single samādhi, and even to speak of the immeasurable and various natures of unspeakably unspeakable samādhis.

It may be taught for one day, or for half a month or one month; it may be taught for a hundred years, a thousand years, or a hundred thousand years; it may be taught for one kalpa, a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, or a hundred thousand kalpas; it may be taught for hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas; or it may be taught for incalculable, immeasurable, even up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas.
The number of kalpas may come to an end, but the meaning and principles of a single word or a single phrase are difficult to exhaust. Why is this?
Because these bodhisattvas have accomplished ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries.
Having accomplished this treasury, the dhāraṇī-door that encompasses all phenomena manifests before them, with a retinue of ten million asaṃkhyeya dhāraṇīs;
having attained these dhāraṇīs, they extensively expound the Dharma for sentient beings through the light of the Dharma.
When he preaches the Dharma, he emits wondrous sounds with his broad and long tongue, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions;
according to their faculties and natures, he causes them all to be fully satisfied, their minds to attain joy, and all the entanglements and defilements of affliction to be extinguished.

They skillfully enter into all sounds, languages, letters, and eloquence, ensuring that the seed of the Buddha is never severed for all sentient beings and that their pure minds continue in succession; furthermore, they expound the Dharma through the light of the Dharma without end, never giving rise to weariness.
Why is this? Because these bodhisattvas have accomplished boundless bodies that exhaust space and pervade the Dharma-realm.
This is the tenth treasury of eloquence of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

This treasury is inexhaustible, undivided, uninterrupted, unceasing, immutable, unobstructed, and non-retrogressive; it is profoundly deep and bottomless, difficult to enter, yet universally enters the gateway of all Buddha-dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
These ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries possess ten kinds of inexhaustible dharmas, which cause all bodhisattvas to ultimately achieve unexcelled enlightenment.”

What are these ten? They are: because of benefiting all sentient beings; because of skillfully dedicating through original vows; because of being uninterrupted throughout all kalpas; because of awakening the infinite mind throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space; because of dedicating toward the conditioned without attachment; because of the inexhaustibility of all phenomena within the scope of a single thought-moment; because of the unchanging nature of the great vow-mind; because of skillfully grasping all dhāraṇīs; because of being protected and remembered by all Buddhas; and because of understanding that all phenomena are like illusions.
These are the ten kinds of inexhaustible dharmas, which enable all that is done in every world to attain the ultimate, inexhaustible great treasury.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Twenty-one;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Twenty-two.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Twenty-three: Ascending to the Tuṣita Heaven Palace.

At that time, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, throughout all worlds in the ten directions, within each of the Jambudvīpa continents under the four heavens, everyone beheld the Tathāgata sitting beneath a tree; in each place, there were bodhisattvas who, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual strength, expounded the Dharma, such that none failed to think for themselves that they were always in the presence of the Buddha.

At that time, by means of his supernatural power, the World-Honored One, without departing from beneath this Bodhi tree, nor from the summit of Mount Sumeru, nor from the palace of the Yāma Heaven, proceeded to the Palace Adorned with All Wondrous Jewels in the Tuṣita Heaven.
At that time, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, seeing the Buddha approaching from afar, immediately prepared a lion throne of the maṇi-treasury within his palace.

This lion throne was composed of all manner of celestial, exquisite jewels; it was obtained through the roots of goodness cultivated in the past, manifested by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, born from immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas of roots of goodness, and arisen from the pure dharmas of all Tathāgatas. It was adorned and polished by the power of boundless merit;
its retribution of pure karma was indestructible.
Those who behold it rejoice, never wearying of the sight;
this is a supramundane dharma, untainted by the world;
all sentient beings come to observe it, yet none are able to exhaustively fathom its wondrous excellence.
There were hundreds of billions of tiers surrounding it on all sides;

hundreds of billions of golden nets, hundreds of billions of flower canopies, hundreds of billions of jewel canopies, hundreds of billions of garland canopies, and hundreds of billions of incense canopies were spread above it;
flower garlands hung down, and their fragrance perfumed everywhere.
A hundred trillion flower canopies, a hundred trillion garland canopies, and a hundred trillion jewel canopies were held aloft by the devas, arranged in rows on all four sides;
a hundred trillion precious garments were spread upon them;
and a hundred trillion multi-storied pavilions were magnificently adorned and resplendent.
A hundred trillion nets of mani-jewels and a hundred trillion nets of precious gems covered it from above;
a hundred trillion nets of precious necklaces hung down on all four sides;
and a hundred trillion nets of ornaments, a hundred trillion nets of parasols, a hundred trillion nets of garments, and a hundred trillion nets of precious canopies were spread over its top.
A hundred trillion jeweled lotus nets were in full bloom with radiant glory;
a hundred trillion jeweled incense nets emitted exquisite fragrances that delighted the hearts of all beings;
and a hundred trillion jeweled bell canopies had their bells move ever so slightly, producing harmonious and elegant sounds.
There were a hundred trillion precious canopies of sandalwood, their fragrance wafting everywhere;
a hundred trillion canopies of precious flowers, with blossoms in full bloom;
and a hundred trillion canopies of robes of myriad exquisite colors, rare in the world.

A hundred trillion bodhisattva canopies, a hundred trillion multicolored canopies, a hundred trillion canopies of pure gold, a hundred trillion canopies of lapis lazuli, and a hundred trillion canopies of various jewels were all spread above;
a hundred trillion canopies of every kind of jewel were adorned with great maṇi gems;
and a hundred trillion exquisite jewel flowers surrounded and embellished them.
A hundred trillion *bimba* canopies of exquisite variety were interspersed;
a hundred trillion jewel garlands and a hundred trillion incense garlands hung down on all four sides;
and a hundred trillion celestial, solid fragrances pervaded everywhere with their scent.

A hundred trillion celestial ornaments and necklaces, a hundred trillion jewel-flower necklaces, a hundred trillion supreme treasury jewel necklaces, a hundred trillion maṇi-jewel necklaces, and a hundred trillion ocean-maṇi jewel necklaces adorned the body of the seat;
a hundred trillion exquisite jewel silks served as hanging ribbons;
and a hundred trillion Indra-vajra jewels, a hundred trillion sovereign maṇi jewels, and a hundred trillion treasuries of exquisite-colored pure gold served as interspersed decorations.
A hundred trillion Vairocana mani jewels and a hundred trillion Indra mani jewels radiated brilliant light;
a hundred trillion celestial *sāra* (firm) mani jewels served as windows and casements;
and a hundred trillion *viśuddha-guṇa* (pure merit) mani jewels displayed exquisite colors.
A hundred trillion pure and wondrous treasure-treasuries formed its gates and portals;
it was interspersed and adorned with a hundred trillion half-moon jewels, the most supreme in the world; a hundred trillion stainless-treasury maṇi jewels; a hundred trillion lion-faced maṇi jewels;
and a hundred trillion mind-sovereign maṇi jewels that grant all desires as wished.
A hundred trillion Jambūnada-maṇi jewels, a hundred trillion pure-treasury maṇi jewels, and a hundred trillion imperial-banner maṇi jewels all emitted radiance that completely covered it above;
a hundred trillion white-silver-treasury maṇi jewels and a hundred trillion Sumeru-banner maṇi jewels adorned its interior.

A hundred trillion pearl necklaces, a hundred trillion lapis lazuli necklaces, a hundred trillion red jewel necklaces, a hundred trillion maṇi necklaces, a hundred trillion jewel-light necklaces, a hundred trillion necklaces of various treasury maṇis, a hundred trillion extremely delightful red pearl necklaces, a hundred trillion necklaces of maṇi jewels from treasuries of infinite colors and forms, a hundred trillion incomparably pure jewel necklaces, and a hundred trillion necklaces of supreme light maṇi jewels hung all around as adornments;
there were also a hundred trillion maṇi bodies, exquisitely and wonderfully decorated.

A hundred trillion jewels of Indra’s exquisite colors; a hundred trillion black sandalwood incenses; a hundred trillion incenses of inconceivable realms; a hundred trillion exquisite incenses of the ten directions; a hundred trillion most supreme incenses; and a hundred trillion most delightful incenses—all emitting fragrant scents that universally permeate the ten directions;
a hundred trillion *bimbara* incenses, scattered throughout the ten directions;
and a hundred trillion pure-light incenses, universally perfuming all sentient beings.
A hundred trillion boundless varieties of colors and fragrances universally permeate all buddha-lands, never ceasing;
a hundred trillion ointment incenses, a hundred trillion powdered incenses, and a hundred trillion burning incenses, their scents wafting forth and pervading everywhere;
and a hundred trillion lotus-treasury aloeswood incenses emit great sounds.
There are a hundred trillion *vīṇā* perfumes that can transform the minds of the multitude;
a hundred trillion *aruṇa* perfumes whose fragrance permeates everywhere and whose flavor is sweet and delicious;
and a hundred trillion perfumes capable of awakening, which pervade all things and cause the faculties of those who smell them to become tranquil.
Furthermore, there were a hundred trillion incomparable kings of fragrances, adorned in various ways.

There rained down clouds of a hundred trillion celestial flowers, clouds of a hundred trillion celestial incenses, clouds of a hundred trillion celestial powdered incenses, and clouds of a hundred trillion celestial *kusuma* flowers. There rained down a hundred trillion...
There were clouds of celestial padma flowers, raining down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial utpala flowers,
clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial kumuda flowers, clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial puṇḍarīka flowers,
clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial māndārava flowers, and clouds of all kinds of celestial flowers, each numbering in the hundreds of billions.
They rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial garments; they rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of mani-jewel clouds;

they rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial parasols; they rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial banners; they rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial crowns;
they rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial ornaments; they rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial jewel garlands.
They rained down clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial jewel necklaces, clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial sandalwood incense,
and clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial aloeswood incense.

They erected a hundred trillion jeweled banners, suspended a hundred trillion jeweled pennants, draped a hundred trillion jeweled silk streamers, lit a hundred trillion incense burners, spread a hundred trillion jeweled garlands, held a hundred trillion jeweled fans, and grasped a hundred trillion jeweled whisks.
A net of hundreds of billions of precious bells was suspended, which, stirred by a gentle breeze, produced wondrous sounds;
it was surrounded on all sides by hundreds of billions of precious railings,
with hundreds of billions of precious tala trees arranged in successive rows.
A hundred trillion windows and casements of exquisite jewels were magnificent and ornate;
a hundred trillion jewel trees provided shade all around;
and a hundred trillion jewel pavilions extended far and wide, exquisitely adorned.
A hundred trillion jeweled gates hung with draped necklaces;
a hundred trillion golden bells emitted wondrous sounds;
and a hundred trillion auspicious-marked necklaces hung down, pure and majestic.
There were a hundred trillion *siddhika* jewels capable of eliminating all evils;
a hundred trillion golden treasuries woven with golden threads;
and a hundred trillion jeweled canopies with poles made of various precious gems, held aloft in orderly rows.
A hundred trillion nets of all kinds of jewel ornaments were interspersed as adornments;
a hundred trillion luminous jewels emitted various rays of light;
and a hundred trillion beams of light shone everywhere in all directions.
There were a hundred trillion sun-treasury wheels and a hundred trillion moon-treasury wheels, all composed of jewels of immeasurable colors;
there were a hundred trillion fragrant flames, their radiance clear and penetrating;
and there were a hundred trillion lotus-treasuries, blooming with fresh and vibrant splendor.
A hundred trillion jeweled nets, a hundred trillion flower nets, and a hundred trillion incense nets completely covered it from above;

there were a hundred trillion celestial jewel robes, a hundred trillion celestial blue robes, a hundred trillion celestial yellow robes, a hundred trillion celestial red robes, a hundred trillion celestial robes of wondrous colors, a hundred trillion celestial robes of various wonderful jewels, a hundred trillion robes perfumed with various fragrances, a hundred trillion robes made of every kind of jewel, and a hundred trillion pure white robes, all beautifully spread out, bringing joy to those who saw them.
There were hundreds of billions of celestial bell-banners and hundreds of billions of golden net-banners, emitting subtle and wondrous sounds;
there were hundreds of billions of celestial silk banners, complete with every variety of color;
and there were hundreds of billions of incense banners, draped with hanging nets of fragrant incense.
A hundred trillion flower-banners rained down all kinds of flowers;
a hundred trillion celestial robe-banners hung and spread exquisite garments;
a hundred trillion celestial maṇi-jewel banners were adorned with various precious gems.
There were a hundred trillion celestial banners of ornamental jewels, adorned with every kind of accessory;
a hundred trillion celestial garland banners, with various flower garlands arrayed on all four sides;
and a hundred trillion celestial parasol banners, with precious bells chiming in harmony, bringing joy to all who heard them.
A hundred trillion celestial conch shells produced wondrous sounds;
a hundred trillion celestial drums produced great sounds;
and a hundred trillion celestial harps produced exquisite melodies.
A hundred trillion celestial *mudrā* instruments produced sublime and wondrous sounds;
a hundred trillion celestial various musical ensembles played in unison;
and a hundred trillion celestial instruments of sovereign joy emitted exquisite tones, their sound pervading all Buddha-fields.
There were a hundred trillion celestial musical instruments of transformation and delight, their sounds like echoes, universally responding to all;
a hundred trillion celestial drums produced wondrous tones through being struck;
and a hundred trillion celestial *cintāmaṇi* lutes spontaneously emitted sounds, their rhythms and notes harmonizing with one another.
A hundred trillion celestial musical instruments produced wondrous sounds that extinguish all afflictions;
a hundred trillion pleasing voices offered praise and worship;
and a hundred trillion vast sounds extolled their service.
A hundred trillion profound sounds praised the practice of cultivation;
a hundred trillion myriad exquisite sounds extolled the karmic fruits of the Buddha’s deeds;
a hundred trillion subtle sounds lauded the principle of reality as it is.
A hundred trillion sounds of unobstructed true reality praised the Buddha’s past conduct;
a hundred trillion pure sounds extolled his offerings to the Buddhas of the past;
and a hundred trillion sounds of Dharma-gates praised the Buddhas’ supreme fearlessness.
A hundred trillion sounds of immeasurable resonance extolled the inexhaustible merits of all bodhisattvas;
a hundred trillion sounds of the bodhisattva stages praised and revealed the practices corresponding to all the bodhisattva stages;
a hundred trillion uninterrupted sounds extolled the unceasing merits of the Buddhas.
A hundred trillion voices in accordance with sound praised and extolled the conduct of beholding the Buddha;
a hundred trillion profound sounds of Dharma praised the principle corresponding to the unimpeded wisdom regarding all phenomena;
and a hundred trillion vast sounds, whose resonance filled all buddha-fields.
There were a hundred trillion sounds of unimpeded purity that caused all beings to rejoice according to their inclinations;
a hundred trillion sounds of non-abiding in the three realms that caused those who heard them to penetrate deeply into the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*);
and a hundred trillion sounds of joy that caused those who heard them to have no mental obstructions and to develop deep faith and reverence.
There are the sounds of the spheres of a hundred trillion Buddhas, which, according to the voices they produce, are all able to reveal and demonstrate the meaning of all dharmas;
there are the sounds of a hundred trillion dharanis, which skillfully proclaim the distinctions among all dharma-words and definitively resolve the secret treasury of the Tathagatas;
there are the sounds of a hundred trillion all-dharmas, whose tones are harmonious and flowing, perfectly blending with all music.
There were hundreds of billions of bodhisattvas who had first resolved their minds on enlightenment; upon merely seeing this seat, their resolve for omniscience increased all the more.
There were hundreds of billions of bodhisattvas in the stage of "preparing the ground," whose minds became pure and filled with joy.
There were hundreds of billions of bodhisattvas in the stage of "cultivation," who attained clear understanding and purity.
One hundred trillion Bodhisattvas of Noble Birth abide in superior resolve and joy;
one hundred trillion Bodhisattvas Perfect in Skillful Means initiate the practices of the Mahāyāna;
and one hundred trillion Bodhisattvas Abiding in the Right Mind diligently cultivate all bodhisattva paths.
A hundred trillion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas have purely cultivated all the bodhisattva stages;
a hundred trillion youthful bodhisattvas have attained the light of all bodhisattva samādhis;
and a hundred trillion prince-of-the-dharma bodhisattvas have entered the inconceivable realms of all Buddhas.
One hundred trillion bodhisattvas who have received the consecration are able to manifest the ten powers of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas have attained sovereign supernormal powers;
and one hundred trillion bodhisattvas have given rise to pure understanding.
A hundred trillion bodhisattvas gave rise to a heart of joyful affection;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas possessed indestructible, profound faith;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas possessed vast and great power.
A hundred trillion bodhisattvas increase in renown;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas expound the meaning of the Dharma, causing wisdom to become decisive;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas maintain right mindfulness without distraction.
A hundred trillion bodhisattvas gave rise to decisive wisdom;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the power of hearing and retaining, upholding all Buddha-dharmas;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas produced immeasurable and vast awakening and understanding.
A hundred trillion bodhisattvas dwell securely in the faculty of faith;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas have attained the dāna-pāramitā and are able to practice universal giving;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas have attained the śīla-pāramitā and fully maintain all the precepts.
One hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), their minds remaining unshakable as they were able to endure all Buddha-dharmas;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*), capable of practicing immeasurable diligence for transcendence;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the perfection of meditation (*dhyāna-pāramitā*), fully endowed with the immeasurable radiance of meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
A hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the prajñāpāramitā, their light of wisdom able to illuminate everywhere;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas fulfilled their great vows, all of which were utterly pure;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas obtained the lamp of wisdom, its brilliance illuminating the Dharma gates.
A hundred trillion bodhisattvas were illuminated by the Dharma-light of the Buddhas of the ten directions;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas pervaded the ten directions, expounding the Dharma that transcends delusion;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas universally entered all Buddha-fields.
One hundred trillion bodhisattvas, through their dharma-bodies, reach all buddha-fields;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attain the voice of the Buddha and are able to bring about vast awakening;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attain the skillful means for generating all-knowledge.
One hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the accomplishment of all dharma-gates;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas accomplished the wisdom of dharmas, like precious banners, able to universally manifest all Buddha-dharmas;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas were able to fully manifest the realm of the Tathāgata.
A hundred trillion celestial kings paid him respectful homage;
a hundred trillion dragon kings gazed upon him with tireless devotion;
and a hundred trillion yakṣa kings joined their palms above their heads.
A hundred trillion gandharva kings gave rise to pure faith;
a hundred trillion asura kings severed their arrogant minds;
and a hundred trillion garuḍa kings held silk ribbons in their beaks.
A hundred trillion kinnara kings leaped for joy;
a hundred trillion mahoraga kings gazed upon him with delight;
and a hundred trillion lords of the world bowed their heads in prostration.
A hundred trillion kings of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven gazed upon him with unblinking eyes;
a hundred trillion kings of the Yāma Heaven rejoiced and offered praise;
a hundred trillion kings of the Tuṣita Heaven prostrated themselves, stretching out their bodies in worship.
One hundred trillion kings of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet;
one hundred trillion kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven joined their palms in reverence;
and one hundred trillion Brahmā kings observed him with single-minded attention.
A hundred trillion Mahesvara Heavenly Kings paid respectful homage and made offerings;
a hundred trillion bodhisattvas raised their voices in praise;
and a hundred trillion celestial maidens offered worship with single-minded devotion.
One hundred trillion devas with shared aspirations leaped for joy;
