When the Bodhisattva undergoes such suffering and poison in this way, he becomes even more diligent; he does not abandon, avoid, startle, fear, retreat, or cower, nor does he experience weariness or fatigue.
Why is this? Because, in accordance with their vows, they resolutely desire to shoulder the burden of all sentient beings in order to bring them to liberation.
At that time, the bodhisattva forms this thought:

"All sentient beings dwell in the midst of the various sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death, wandering according to their karma, possessed of false views and lacking wisdom, and having lost all wholesome dharmas; I should rescue them and cause them to attain liberation."

Furthermore, all sentient beings are entangled in the net of craving and shrouded by the veil of ignorance; they are stained by and attached to the various realms of existence, pursuing them without relinquishing them. They enter the cage of suffering and perform the deeds of Māra; their merit and wisdom are utterly exhausted, and they constantly harbor doubts. Seeing no place of peace and knowing no path of deliverance, they revolve incessantly within the cycle of birth and death, perpetually submerged in the mire of all sufferings.

Having seen this, the Bodhisattva gives rise to a mind of great compassion and a mind of great benefit, desiring to bring all sentient beings to complete liberation. He dedicates all roots of goodness with a vast mind, dedicating in the manner practiced by the Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time and as described in the *Mahāpariṇāmanā-sūtra*, vowing that all sentient beings may universally attain purity and ultimately achieve all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Again, he reflects thus:

"The practice I cultivate is intended to cause all sentient beings to fully attain the sovereignty of unsurpassed wisdom; it is not for my own sake that I seek liberation, but solely to rescue and protect all sentient beings, so that they may all attain the mind of omniscience, cross the stream of birth and death, and be liberated from all suffering."
He further thought:
"I shall universally undergo all manner of sufferings on behalf of all sentient beings, so that they may emerge from the great abyss of immeasurable suffering within birth and death."

I shall universally act for the sake of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and within all evil realms, enduring every form of suffering until the end of future kalpas, while constantly and diligently cultivating roots of goodness for the sake of sentient beings.
Why is this? I would rather alone undergo such manifold sufferings than allow sentient beings to fall into hell.

I shall, in those perilous places such as the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of King Yama, offer my own body as collateral to ransom all sentient beings of the evil paths, causing them to attain liberation.
He further thought:
"I vow to protect all sentient beings and never abandon them; what I have spoken is truthful and free from falsehood."

Why is this? I have resolved upon bodhicitta for the sake of rescuing and delivering all sentient beings; I do not seek the unsurpassed path for my own sake, nor do I cultivate the practices of enlightenment for the sake of seeking the realms of the five desires or the various pleasures within the three realms of existence.
Why is this? All worldly pleasures are nothing but suffering.
They are the realm of the various Māras, craved by the ignorant, and censured by all Buddhas; all manner of suffering and affliction arise because of them.
In the hells, among the hungry ghosts and animals, and in the realm of King Yama, there is anger, strife, litigation, and mutual insults and humiliation.
All such evils are caused by attachment to the five desires.
"Attached to the five desires, they distance themselves from all Buddhas and obstruct their birth in the heavens; how much more so regarding the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*!

Thus observing that those in the world who crave the taste of minor desires undergo immeasurable suffering, the Bodhisattva never seeks unsurpassed enlightenment or practices the Bodhisattva path for the sake of those pleasures of the five desires.

Rather, it is solely for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings that he resolves his mind to practice, fulfills his great vows, and severs the snares of suffering for all beings, causing them to attain liberation.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:

‘I shall dedicate my roots of goodness in such a way that all sentient beings may attain ultimate happiness, beneficial happiness, the happiness of non-reception, the happiness of tranquility, the happiness of non-reliance, the happiness of immovability, immeasurable happiness, the happiness of neither abandoning nor retreating, the happiness of non-extinction, and the happiness of omniscience.’”
Again, he formed this thought:

"I shall act as the tamer and guide for all sentient beings; I shall serve as their general and minister, holding aloft the great torch of wisdom to reveal the path of peace and security, leading them away from perilous difficulties. Through skillful means, I shall cause them to realize the true meaning;
furthermore, within the ocean of birth and death, I shall act as a master mariner of omniscience and skillfulness, ferrying all sentient beings across to the other shore."
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way, namely:

'May I rescue and protect all sentient beings according to their needs, causing them to emerge from birth and death; may I serve and make offerings to all Buddhas, attaining the unobstructed wisdom of omniscience; may I abandon all demons and stay far away from evil associates, while drawing near to all Bodhisattvas who are virtuous friends; may I extinguish all transgressions and sins, accomplish pure karma, and fulfill the vast practices and vows of a Bodhisattva, as well as immeasurable roots of goodness.'"
“O Son of the Buddha!
Having correctly dedicated all roots of goodness, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:
‘It is not because the sentient beings of the four continents are numerous that many suns appear;’”
Yet, when the sun rises, it is able to universally illuminate all sentient beings.
Furthermore, it is not by means of their own bodily radiance that sentient beings know day and night, travel about and observe, or engage in the performance of various karmic deeds;
all these matters are accomplished solely through the emergence of the Sun Deva-son. Nevertheless, that solar orb is but one and not two.
In the same way, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva cultivates and accumulates roots of goodness and dedicates them, he reflects thus:
"Those sentient beings are unable to save themselves; how could they possibly save others?"
I alone, with a solitary resolve and without companion, cultivate and gather roots of goodness and dedicate them in this way:

namely, for the sake of extensively delivering all sentient beings; for the sake of universally illuminating all sentient beings; for the sake of showing guidance to all sentient beings; for the sake of awakening all sentient beings; for the sake of caring for and protecting all sentient beings; for the sake of gathering in all sentient beings; for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to fulfillment; for the sake of causing all sentient beings to rejoice; for the sake of causing all sentient beings to find delight; and for the sake of causing all sentient beings to sever their doubts.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:
'I should be like the sun, universally illuminating all things, without seeking any reward for my kindness.'"
When sentient beings commit evil, one is able to accept it all, never abandoning one's vow on this account;
nor does one abandon all sentient beings because of the evil of a single sentient being.
One should simply diligently cultivate roots of goodness and dedicate them so that all sentient beings may universally attain peace and happiness;
though the roots of goodness may be few, one should universally embrace all sentient beings by dedicating them with a vast and joyful mind.
If one possesses roots of goodness but does not wish to benefit all sentient beings, it is not called dedication;
only when one takes every single root of goodness as a universal object of focus for all sentient beings is it called dedication.

The dedication that establishes sentient beings in the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) which is free from attachment; the dedication that perceives the self-nature of sentient beings as unmoving and unchanging;
the dedication that is without dependence or grasping regarding dedication; the dedication that does not grasp at the marks of roots of goodness;
the dedication that does not discriminate the essential nature of karmic retribution; and the dedication that is not attached to the five aggregates.
Dedication that does not destroy the characteristics of the five aggregates; dedication that does not grasp at karma; dedication that does not seek retribution;
dedication that is not stained by causes and conditions; dedication that does not differentiate what arises from causes and conditions;
dedication that does not cling to names; dedication that does not cling to locations; dedication that does not cling to the false.
The dedication of Dharma: dedicating without attachment to the mark of sentient beings, the mark of worlds, or the mark of mind and thought;
dedicating without giving rise to inversion of mind, inversion of perception, or inversion of view; dedicating without attachment to the path of language;
dedicating by contemplating the true nature of all phenomena; and contemplating the equality of all sentient beings.

They dedicate with the dedication of equal characteristics; they dedicate by sealing all roots of goodness with the seal of the dharma-realm; they dedicate by contemplating that all phenomena are free from desire.
Understanding that all phenomena are non-existent, they plant roots of goodness in the same way.
One contemplates all phenomena as non-dual, unarisen, and unceasing; dedication is likewise so.
By dedicating roots of goodness in this manner, one practices the pure methods of counteraction, such that all roots of goodness accord with supramundane dharmas.

One does not create dualistic marks; one does not realize all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) by means of karma itself, nor does one turn toward all-knowledge apart from karma. All-knowledge is not identical to karma, yet one does not attain all-knowledge apart from karma.
Because karma is pure like a reflection of light and shadow, its retribution is also pure like a reflection of light and shadow;
because retribution is pure like a reflection of light and shadow, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is also pure like a reflection of light and shadow.

"Free from all disturbances of thought and discrimination regarding 'self' and 'what belongs to self,' one understands thus and dedicates [the merit] through the skillful means of all roots of goodness.
When a bodhisattva dedicates in this manner, they liberate sentient beings constantly without rest, yet do not dwell in the marks of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*);

although they know that all phenomena are without karma and without retribution, they are well able to produce all karmic retributions without contradiction. In such a way, they skillfully cultivate dedication through these skillful means.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate in this manner, they are free from all faults and are praised by all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the first dedication of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva: "The Dedication to Protecting All Sentient Beings while Remaining Free from the Notion of Sentient Beings."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja surveyed all the assemblies throughout the ten directions, extending to the entire Dharma-realm. He entered into the profound meanings of the words, cultivated supreme practices with immeasurable minds, and universally covered all sentient beings with great compassion. He ensured that the lineage of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time would not be severed, entered the treasury of the meritorious dharmas of all Buddhas, and gave birth to the Dharma-bodies of all Buddhas. Being well able to discern the minds of all sentient beings, he knew when their planted roots of goodness had reached maturity; thus, while abiding in the Dharma-body, he manifested a pure form-body. Empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual strength, he spoke these verses:

“Having practiced the Way through inconceivable eons, With firm diligence and an unobstructed mind, He has perfected his conduct through countless kalpas, And now manifests this body for the sake of all beings.”
Desiring to benefit the multitudes of living beings, they constantly seek the meritorious dharmas of all Buddhas.
These peerless guides of the world cultivate their minds until they are exceedingly bright and pure;
resolving to universally save all sentient beings, they are able to skillfully enter the treasury of dedication.
Endowed with the power of courageous diligence, With wisdom that is penetrating and a pure mind,
Universally rescuing all living beings, Their minds are patient and unshakable.
The mind dwells well-established and peerless; the intellect is ever pure and greatly joyful.
Thus one diligently practices for the sake of beings, just as the great earth universally receives all.
Seeking no happiness for oneself, but desiring only to rescue and protect all sentient beings—
one who thus gives rise to the mind of great compassion will swiftly enter the stage of non-obstruction.
All sentient beings throughout all worlds in the ten directions are gathered and sustained;
for the sake of rescuing them, one abides well in the mind, thus training in these various dedications.
Practicing generosity with great joy, Upholding pure precepts without transgression,
With courageous diligence and an unshakable mind, Dedicating all toward the Tathāgata’s omniscience.
Their minds are vast and boundless, Abiding securely in the power of patience, unshakable;
Their meditative concentration is profoundly deep and ever-illuminating, And their wisdom is subtle and wondrous, beyond conception.
Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, I fully cultivate and purify these practices;
I dedicate all such merit and virtue for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
The Great Being diligently cultivates all virtuous deeds, Immeasurable, boundless, and beyond counting;
Thus he benefits all sentient beings, Causing them to abide in inconceivable, unsurpassed wisdom.
For the sake of all sentient beings everywhere, They remain in the hells for inconceivable eons;
Thus, they never harbor a heart of weariness or retreat, But with courageous resolve, they always dedicate [their merit].
Seeking neither form, sound, fragrance, nor taste, Nor aspiring for any exquisite tactile sensations,
But solely for the sake of delivering all living beings, One constantly seeks the unsurpassed, most supreme wisdom.
With wisdom as pure as space, they cultivate the boundless practices of a Mahāsattva;
in accordance with all the dharmas of practice performed by the Buddhas, such persons constantly train and study in this way.
The Great Being wanders through all worlds, Able to bring peace and security to all living beings;
He causes everyone everywhere to rejoice, Cultivating the bodhisattva practices without weariness.
Eliminating all poisons of the mind, one contemplates and cultivates supreme wisdom;
not seeking peace and happiness for oneself, one only wishes that sentient beings may be freed from suffering.
This person attains ultimate fulfillment through dedication; their mind is ever pure and free from all poisons.
Entrusted by the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, they dwell in the city of the unsurpassed Great Dharma.
Never stained by attachment to any form, and likewise regarding sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;
with a mind forever transcending the three realms of existence, all accumulated merit is dedicated toward enlightenment.
The Buddha perceives and knows all sentient beings, Gathering them all in without exception;
Vowing to bring them all to liberation, He practices for their sake with great joy.
Their minds dwell constantly and peacefully in every thought-moment; their wisdom is vast and beyond compare.
Free from delusion, they remain ever tranquil through right mindfulness, and all their karmic actions are completely purified.
Those bodhisattvas dwelling in the world do not cling to any internal or external phenomena;
like the wind moving unimpeded through space, so too is the mental application of these Great Beings.
All bodily actions are completely pure, And all speech is free from fault;
With a mind always directed toward the Tathāgata, They are able to bring joy to all Buddhas.
To all the infinite lands throughout the ten directions, I go to every place where a Buddha resides;
Therein I behold the Honored One of Great Compassion, Whom I do not fail to revere and serve with devotion.

The mind is ever pure, free from all faults; universally entering the world without fear, you abide in the unsurpassed path of the Tathāgata, and further serve as a great dharma-pool for the three realms of existence.
Diligently observing all phenomena, Contemplating them as either existent or non-existent,
Thus proceeding toward the principle of reality, One enters the profound state free from contention.
By this, one cultivates and perfects the firm path, which no sentient being can destroy;
skillfully and thoroughly understanding the nature of all phenomena, one remains universally unattached throughout the three periods of time.
Thus dedicating [merit] to reach the other shore, may all sentient beings be freed from every defilement;
forever detached from all points of reliance, may they enter the ultimate state of non-reliance.
The paths of speech of all sentient beings differ according to their respective kinds;
the Bodhisattva is able to explain them all with discernment, yet his mind remains unattached and unimpeded.
When a bodhisattva practices dedication in this way, The merit and skillful means are beyond description;
They cause all the Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions To offer them their praise.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Vast and Profound, Scroll Twenty-Three;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Vast and Profound, Scroll Twenty-Four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Decree.
The Twenty-Fifth Chapter on Dedication, Part Two:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
What is the indestructible dedication of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?"
“O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains indestructible faith in all Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present, because they are able to serve all Buddhas;

and they attain indestructible faith in all Bodhisattvas—even those who have first resolved their minds for a single thought-moment seeking omniscience—because they vow to cultivate all Bodhisattva roots of goodness without weariness.”
They attain indestructible faith in all Buddha-dharmas because they have given rise to profound aspiration and joy;
they attain indestructible faith in all Buddha-teachings because they protect, maintain, and uphold them;
they attain indestructible faith in all sentient beings because they regard them with eyes of universal compassion, dedicate their roots of goodness, and bring benefit to all.
They attain indestructible faith in all pure and white dharmas, because they universally gather boundless roots of goodness;
they attain indestructible faith in the path of dedication of all bodhisattvas, because they fulfill all sublime aspirations and inclinations;
they attain indestructible faith in all bodhisattva Dharma-teachers, because they conceive the thought of the Buddha toward all bodhisattvas.
They attain indestructible faith in the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas, because they have deep faith in the inconceivability of all Buddhas;
they attain indestructible faith in the skillful means and practices of all Bodhisattvas, because they embrace the various, immeasurable, and innumerable spheres of practice.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva thus abides in indestructible faith, regarding the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, as well as the teachings of all Buddhas and all sentient beings—within these various spheres—they plant roots of goodness that are immeasurable and boundless, causing the bodhicitta to increase further and further;
their compassion becomes vast, they observe with equanimity, they practice in accordance with the deeds of all Buddhas, and they gather in all pure roots of goodness.”
Entering into the true meaning, accumulating practices of merit, practicing great giving, cultivating all virtues, and viewing the three periods of time with equanimity,
the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness and merits toward omniscience,
making this vow: "May I always see all Buddhas, draw near to virtuous friends, and dwell together with all bodhisattvas."
They maintain mindfulness of omniscience, never relinquishing it for even a moment;
they receive and uphold the Buddha’s teachings, diligently protecting and guarding them;
they teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity, constantly dedicating their minds toward the supramundane path; and they make offerings to and attend upon all Dharma masters.
"Having understood all phenomena, they remember and uphold them without forgetting;
they practice their great vows and bring them all to fulfillment.

In this way, the bodhisattva accumulates roots of goodness, accomplishes roots of goodness, increases roots of goodness, contemplates roots of goodness, fixes mindfulness upon roots of goodness, discriminates roots of goodness, delights in roots of goodness, cultivates roots of goodness, and dwells securely in roots of goodness.

“Once the bodhisattva-mahāsattva has thus accumulated all these roots of goodness, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices based on the resultant fruits obtained from those roots of goodness; in every thought-moment, they see immeasurable Buddhas and serve and make offerings to them as is appropriate.”
With incalculable jewels, incalculable flowers, incalculable garlands, incalculable garments,
incalculable parasols, incalculable banners, incalculable pennants, incalculable ornaments,
incalculable attendants, incalculable ground-sprinklings, and incalculable ointments...
incense, incense in incalculable quantities, blended incense in incalculable quantities,
burning incense in incalculable quantities, incalculable deep faith, incalculable affection and joy, incalculable pure mind,
incalculable reverence, incalculable praise, incalculable prostration, and incalculable jewels.
Seats: incalculable flower seats, incalculable incense seats, incalculable garland seats,
incalculable sandalwood seats, incalculable cloth seats, incalculable vajra seats, incalculable maṇi seats,
incalculable precious silk seats, and incalculable precious-colored seats.
...immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jeweled walkways, immeasurable flower walkways,
immeasurable incense walkways, immeasurable garland walkways, immeasurable robe walkways,
immeasurable walkways inlaid with various jewels, and immeasurable walkways of all kinds of precious silken fabrics...
The walkways, the walkways covered by incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel *tāla* trees,
the walkways with incalculable railings made of all kinds of jewels, the walkways completely draped with incalculable nets of all kinds of jeweled bells,
and the incalculable palaces made of all kinds of jewels and the incalculable palaces made of all kinds of flowers.
Immeasurable palaces of all kinds of incense, immeasurable palaces of all kinds of garlands,
immeasurable palaces of all kinds of sandalwood, immeasurable palaces of all kinds of solid and wondrous fragrant treasuries,
immeasurable palaces of all kinds of vajra, and immeasurable palaces of all kinds of maṇi jewels.
All were exquisite and surpassed those of the devas;

there were incalculable [asaṃkhyeya] trees of various jewels, incalculable trees of diverse fragrances, incalculable trees of precious garments, incalculable trees of musical instruments, incalculable trees of precious ornaments, incalculable trees of wondrous sounds, incalculable inexhaustible jewel-trees, incalculable trees of precious silken streamers, and incalculable trees of precious earrings. There were also incalculable trees adorned with all manner of flowers, perfumes, banners, pennants, garlands, and canopies. Such trees as these, with their spreading branches and dense foliage, provided shade and reflected light, adorning the palaces.

Those palaces were further adorned with incalculable railings, incalculable windows, and incalculable gateways; they were adorned with incalculable multi-storied pavilions, incalculable crescent-shaped ornaments, and incalculable canopies. Incalculable golden nets covered them from above, incalculable fragrances perfumed them on all sides, and incalculable garments were spread upon their floors.
“O Son of the Buddha!

With such offerings as these, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, throughout immeasurable, incalculable, unspeakably unspeakable kalpas, honors, reveres, and makes offerings to all Buddhas with a pure mind, never regressing and without rest;
likewise, after each and every Tathāgata has entered parinirvāṇa, he likewise reverently makes offerings to all their relics.”

In order to cause all sentient beings to give rise to pure faith; to cause all sentient beings to gather roots of goodness; to cause all sentient beings to be free from all suffering; to cause all sentient beings to attain vast understanding; to cause all sentient beings to be adorned with great adornments and adorned with immeasurable adornments; so that all their undertakings may reach ultimate fulfillment; to know that the appearance of the Buddhas is difficult to encounter; to fulfill the immeasurable power of the Tathāgatas; to adorn and make offerings to the stupas and shrines of the Buddhas; and to uphold all the teachings of the Buddhas—one thus makes offerings to the present Buddhas as well as to all their relics after they have entered parinirvāṇa.
These various offerings could not be fully described even in incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
Thus, they cultivate and accumulate immeasurable merit solely for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity; they never regress, never rest, and never grow weary;
they are free from attachment and have transcended all conceptual thoughts.
Without dependence, forever severing all bases for reliance;
far removed from the self and what belongs to the self;
the seal of the Dharma as it truly is, sealing all gateways of karma.
Attaining the non-arising of dharmas, they abide where the Buddhas abide; contemplating the nature of non-arising, they seal all realms.

They dedicate their resolve with the protection and mindfulness of all Buddhas; they dedicate in accordance with the nature of all dharmas; they dedicate by entering the unconditioned to accomplish skillful means; they dedicate through the skillful means of relinquishing all conceptual attachments to things; they dedicate by abiding in immeasurable skillfulness; they dedicate to forever transcend all states of existence; they dedicate with the skillfulness of practicing all deeds without dwelling on signs; they dedicate by universally gathering all roots of goodness; they dedicate with the vastness of universally purifying all Bodhisattva practices; they dedicate by generating the mind of unsurpassed bodhicitta; they dedicate by dwelling together with all roots of goodness; and they dedicate by fulfilling the mind of supreme faith and understanding.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner, although they follow the cycle of birth and death, they do not undergo change; they seek all-knowledge without ever regressing; they remain amidst the various realms of existence without mental agitation; they are able to deliver and liberate all sentient beings; they are unstained by conditioned phenomena; and they do not lose their unimpeded wisdom.”
In the stages of a bodhisattva’s practice, causes and conditions are inexhaustible;
the various phenomena of the world cannot cause any change or disturbance;
having fully perfected all the pure pāramitās, they are able to accomplish all powers of wisdom.
Thus, the bodhisattva leaves behind all the darkness of delusion, accomplishes the bodhicitta, reveals the light, increases pure dharmas, dedicates them toward the supreme path,
and fulfills all practices; with a purified mind, they are well able to discern,
understanding that all phenomena appear entirely in accordance with the mind.
They know that karma is like an illusion, the retribution of karma is like a reflected image, and all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are like magical transformations;
that dharmas born of causes and conditions are entirely like echoes;
and that all the practices of Bodhisattvas are like shadows.
They give birth to the pure Dharma-eye that is free from attachment, seeing the vast realm of the unconditioned;
they realize the nature of cessation and comprehend the non-duality of all phenomena;
they attain the true mark of dharmas and fulfill the practices of a bodhisattva.
They are entirely unattached to any signs;
they are skillfully able to practice the various activities of "sameness of purpose" (sābhoga-karma); they never abandon or neglect pure dharmas;
they are free from all attachments and abide in the practice of non-attachment.

When a bodhisattva thus skillfully contemplates, they are free from delusion, do not contradict the nature of all phenomena, do not destroy the causes of karma, clearly perceive reality, and are skilled in dedication (*pariṇāmanā*).
Knowing the intrinsic nature of phenomena, they accomplish karmic retribution through the power of skillful means and reach the further shore.
With wisdom they observe all phenomena, thereby attaining the knowledge of supernormal powers and the roots of goodness of all actions.
Acting without fabrication, they exercise mastery over their minds.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate all roots of goodness in this manner because they desire to deliver all sentient beings, to ensure that the lineage of the Buddhas is never severed, and to remain forever free from the works of Māra. They perceive the omniscience of all-knowledge as being without limit; they believe in and delight in it, yet do not abandon the worldly realm, while severing all defilements.

Furthermore, they vow that sentient beings shall attain pure wisdom, enter into profound skillful means, transcend the laws of birth and death, and obtain the roots of goodness of the Buddhas. They vow to forever sever all demonic activities, to universally seal all karmas with the seal of equality, to resolve to enter into all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), and to accomplish all supramundane dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the second indestructible dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this dedication, they are able to see all the countless Buddhas, accomplish immeasurable pure and wondrous Dharmas, attain a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings, and remain free from doubt regarding all phenomena.”
Empowered by the spiritual authority of all Buddhas, they subdue all Māras and forever leave behind their karmic activities;
they achieve noble birth and fulfill the bodhicitta;
they attain unimpeded wisdom that does not depend on the explanations of others, and are skillfully able to expound the meanings of all dharmas.
By the power of their mental conceptions, they are able to enter all buddha-fields, universally illuminating sentient beings and causing them all to become pure.
Through this power of indestructible dedication, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas gather all roots of goodness and dedicate them in this manner.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja surveyed the ten directions and, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, spoke these verses:
“The Bodhisattva has already attained an indestructible mind, And practices all manner of wholesome deeds;
Therefore, they are able to bring joy to the Buddhas— The wise dedicate [their merit] in this way.”
Making offerings to immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, practicing generosity and upholding the precepts to subdue the sense faculties,
he acts for the benefit of all sentient beings, universally causing them all to attain purity.
With all manner of supreme and exquisite incenses and flowers, Immeasurable varieties of excellent garments,
Precious parasols and ornamental regalia, I make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
Thus making offerings to all Buddhas for immeasurable, countless, and inconceivable eons, they remained respectful,
reverent, and ever joyful, never for a single thought-moment giving rise to weariness or fatigue.
With single-minded devotion, one should bring to mind all Buddhas, the great luminous lamps of all worlds;
all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions will appear before one as clearly as if seen with one's own eyes.
Throughout inconceivable and immeasurable kalpas, his mind never grew weary of various acts of giving;
throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, he cultivated all manner of wholesome dharmas in this very same way.
After those Tathāgatas have entered parinirvāṇa, one makes offerings to their relics without weariness;
with all manner of exquisite adornments, one establishes inconceivable numbers of stupas and temples.
They fashioned peerless and most excellent forms, adorned with pure gold from the treasure-trove;
towering and vast like the king of mountains, their number reached immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions.
Having purified the mind and made offerings with reverence, one further gives rise to a joyful intent for the benefit [of others],
remaining in the world for inconceivable eons to rescue and protect sentient beings, bringing them to liberation.
Knowing that all sentient beings are but conceptual constructions, they remain free from discrimination toward them all;
yet, being able to skillfully discern the faculties of sentient beings, they universally bring benefit to the masses.
The Bodhisattva cultivates and accumulates all merits, vast and supreme beyond compare;
realizing that their essential nature is entirely non-existent, he thus resolutely dedicates them all.
Observing all phenomena with the most supreme wisdom, one finds that not a single phenomenon therein arises;
by practicing dedication through such skillful means, one's merit becomes immeasurable and inexhaustible.
By these skillful means, one purifies the mind, becoming entirely equal to all Tathāgatas;
since the power of these skillful means is inexhaustible, the resulting merit and reward are likewise without end.
Having resolved upon the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment, Without depending on anything in all the worlds,
They reach everywhere throughout the realms of the ten directions, And remain unimpeded by anything at all.
All Tathāgatas appear in the world Desiring to guide the minds of sentient beings;
Yet when they observe according to the nature of the mind, Ultimately, it cannot be found through investigation.
All phenomena without exception enter entirely into suchness, which is devoid of intrinsic nature;
dedicating with these pure eyes, may they open the prison of birth and death for the world.
Although they cause all realms of existence to be completely purified, they do not discriminate among those realms;
knowing that the nature of all realms is non-existent, they cause beings to rejoice and their minds to be pure.
Without dependence on a single buddha-field, all buddha-fields are likewise so;
they are not stained by conditioned phenomena, for they know that the nature of those phenomena has no place of reliance.
By this one cultivates and accomplishes all-knowledge; by this one is adorned with unsurpassed wisdom;
by this all Buddhas rejoice—this is the bodhisattva’s work of dedication.
The Bodhisattva focuses the mind on all Buddhas, Their unsurpassed wisdom and skillful means;
Just as the Buddhas rely on nothing at all, May I cultivate and perfect these merits.
Dedicating oneself to the rescue and protection of all, causing them to remain far removed from all evil karma;
thus benefiting all living beings, one maintains mindfulness and reflection without ever abandoning it.
Abiding on the stage of wisdom and guarding the Dharma, They do not seek nirvana through other vehicles;
Wishing only to attain the Buddha’s unsurpassed path— Thus do Bodhisattvas skillfully dedicate their merit.
They do not grasp at the words spoken by sentient beings, nor at any conditioned phenomena which are false;
though they do not rely on the path of verbal expression, they likewise do not cling to the absence of speech.
All Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions, Thoroughly comprehend all phenomena without exception;
Though they know all things are empty and quiescent, They do not give rise to mental conceptions regarding emptiness.
Adorning all things with a single adornment, yet not giving rise to conceptual discrimination regarding phenomena—
thus awakening all sentient beings, [one realizes] that all things lack intrinsic nature and are without anything to be observed.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas that is equal to that of all Buddhas?
O Son of the Buddha!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva follows and trains in the path of dedication of the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present.
When training in this path of dedication in such a manner, whether encountering any form or even any tactile object—whether beautiful or ugly—they give rise to neither attachment nor aversion;
their mind attains mastery, is free from all faults, and is vast and pure.
They are filled with joy and delight, free from all sorrow and affliction;
their minds are supple and their faculties are cool and serene.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains such peace and happiness, they further resolve their mind toward dedication to all Buddhas, forming this thought:
"May the roots of goodness I have now planted cause the bliss of all Buddhas to increase even more excellently—namely:

the inconceivable bliss of the Buddhas' dwelling; the peerless bliss of the Buddhas' samādhi; the immeasurable bliss of great compassion; the bliss of liberation of all Buddhas; the boundless bliss of great supernormal powers; the most supreme and honorable bliss of great mastery; the vast and ultimate bliss of immeasurable power; the tranquil bliss of being free from all sensory perceptions; the bliss of abiding in the unobstructed state of constant right concentration; and the bliss of practicing the non-dual path without change."
“O Son of the Buddha!
Having dedicated all roots of goodness to the Buddhas, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further dedicates these roots of goodness to other Bodhisattvas, saying:

‘May those whose vows are not yet fulfilled attain fulfillment; may those whose minds are not yet pure attain purity; and may those who have not yet perfected the various pāramitās attain their perfection.’”

Abiding in the adamantine bodhicitta, one attains non-retrogression regarding all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), does not abandon great diligence, and guards all roots of goodness that constitute the gateway to enlightenment;
one enables sentient beings to relinquish pride, to resolve upon bodhicitta, and to fulfill their aspirations;
abiding in the dwelling of all bodhisattvas, one acquires the sharp and keen faculties of a bodhisattva, cultivates roots of goodness, and realizes omniscience (*sarvajña*).
"O Son of the Buddha!
After the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has dedicated all roots of goodness in this way to other Bodhisattvas, he further dedicates them to all sentient beings, saying:

'May all sentient beings, by virtue of all their roots of goodness—even for as little as the duration of a single snap of the fingers—behold the Buddhas, hear the Dharma, and revere the Noble Sangha.'"

All those roots of goodness are free from obstacles; they mindfully contemplate the perfection of the Buddha, the skillful means of the Dharma, and the venerability of the Saṃgha. They never depart from beholding the Buddha, their minds attain purity, they obtain all Buddha-dharmas, they accumulate immeasurable virtues, they purify all supernormal powers, they abandon doubts regarding the Dharma, and they abide in accordance with the teachings.
"Just as one dedicates [merit] for the sake of sentient beings in this way, so too does one dedicate it for the sake of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Furthermore, may all sentient beings forever leave behind the hells, the hungry ghosts, the animals, and all evil realms such as those of King Yama; may they increase their aspiration for unsurpassed bodhicitta, single-mindedly and diligently seek all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), never slander the true Dharma of the Buddhas, attain the peace and bliss of the Buddhas, purify body and mind, and realize all-encompassing wisdom."
“O Son of the Buddha!

All the roots of goodness possessed by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are initiated and correctly initiated, accumulated and correctly accumulated, increased and correctly increased by means of great vows, so that they all become vast, complete, and fully perfected.”
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells within his home together with his wife and children, he never for a moment abandons the mind of bodhi. With right mindfulness, he contemplates the realm of sarvajñā (all-knowledge), delivering himself and others to bring them to ultimate attainment.
By means of skillful expedients, he transforms his own kin and retinue, causing them to enter the wisdom of a Bodhisattva and bringing them to maturity and liberation.”

Although he dwells together with them, his mind is free from attachment; out of his fundamental great compassion, he remains within the household life, and through his heart of loving-kindness, he accords with his wife and children, remaining unimpeded on the pure path of a bodhisattva.
Although a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells at home and engages in various worldly activities, they never for a moment abandon the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñā-citta*).
That is to say:

whether putting on clothes, eating flavorful food, taking medicinal decoctions, washing, rinsing, or anointing the body; whether turning around, looking about, walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; whether in the actions of body, speech, or mind; or whether asleep or awake.

In all such activities they undertake, their minds are constantly dedicated to the path of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge); they maintain focused mindfulness and reflection, never abandoning it for a moment.
Desiring to benefit all sentient beings, they dwell securely in the immeasurable great vows of bodhi, gathering countless vast roots of goodness;

they diligently cultivate all virtues to universally rescue all beings, forever remaining free from pride and negligence, resolutely proceeding toward the ground of omniscience, never giving rise to the intention to follow any other path.

Constantly contemplating the bodhi of all buddhas, forever abandoning all defiled phenomena, and practicing all that is studied by bodhisattvas, they encounter no obstacles on the path to omniscience;

abiding in the ground of wisdom, they delight in recitation and study, accumulating all roots of goodness through immeasurable knowledge; their minds harbor no attachment to any worldly realm, nor do they become stained by the practices they perform, as they single-mindedly uphold the Buddha’s teachings.
"In this way, a bodhisattva dwelling in the household life universally gathers roots of goodness and causes them to increase, dedicating them toward the unexcelled enlightenment of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
At that time, even when giving a single morsel or a single grain of food to an animal, the bodhisattva makes this vow: "May these beings abandon the animal realm;

may they obtain benefit and peace, attain ultimate liberation, forever cross the ocean of suffering, forever extinguish painful sensations, forever eliminate the aggregates of suffering, and forever sever the perception of suffering, the accumulation of suffering, the practice of suffering, the cause of suffering, the root of suffering, and all states of suffering;
may those sentient beings all achieve such renunciation."
"In this way, the Bodhisattva focuses his mind and fixes his attention upon all sentient beings; taking those roots of goodness as the foremost, he dedicates them toward omniscience."

When a bodhisattva first resolves upon the mind of enlightenment, they universally gather in all sentient beings and dedicate all cultivated roots of goodness toward this end: desiring to cause them forever to leave behind the wilderness of birth and death, to attain the unimpeded bliss of all Tathāgatas, to emerge from the ocean of afflictions, and to cultivate the path of the Buddha-dharma;
with a heart of universal loving-kindness and vast power of compassion, they cause all beings everywhere to obtain pure happiness;
they guard their roots of goodness and draw near to the Buddha-dharma.
They emerge from the realm of Māra and enter the realm of the Buddha;
they sever the seeds of the world and plant the seeds of the Tathāgata, dwelling within the dharma of the equality of the three periods of time.
All such roots of goodness—those already accumulated, those yet to be accumulated, and those currently being accumulated by the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas—are entirely dedicated through this dedication.
Again, he formed this thought:

"Just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past practiced—reverently making offerings to all Buddhas, delivering all sentient beings so they might forever transcend [suffering], and diligently cultivating all roots of goodness, dedicating them all while remaining free from attachment—I shall do likewise."
That is to say:
not relying on form, not clinging to sensation, having no inverted perception, not performing mental formations, not grasping at consciousness, and relinquishing the six sense bases;
not dwelling in worldly dharmas, but delighting in the supramundane.
They know that all dharmas are like space: they come from nowhere, neither arising nor ceasing, devoid of reality, and free from attachment;
they are far removed from all discriminative views, unmoving and unchanging, indestructible and imperishable;
they abide in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), signless and beyond signs, being in essence but a single mark.
Thus, having deeply penetrated the nature of all phenomena, they constantly delight in practicing the roots of goodness of the universal gate and perceive the assemblies of all Buddhas.
Just as all Tathāgatas of the past dedicated their roots of goodness, I likewise dedicate mine;
understanding this Dharma, realizing this Dharma, and relying upon this Dharma, they resolve to cultivate practice without contravening the characteristics of phenomena.

One knows that the practice undertaken is like an illusion, like a shadow, like the moon in water, and like a reflection in a mirror—manifested through the conjunction of causes and conditions, extending even to the ultimate stage of the Tathāgata.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:
'Just as the Buddhas of the past, when they were practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva, dedicated their various roots of goodness in this manner;'"
The same applies to those of the future and the present.
I, too, should now, like those Buddhas, resolve my mind in this way and dedicate all roots of goodness through these dedications:

the foremost dedication, the superior dedication, the most excellent dedication, the highest dedication, the unsurpassed dedication, the unequaled dedication, the dedication equal to the unequaled, the incomparable dedication, the peerless dedication, the venerable dedication, the sublime dedication, the impartial dedication, the upright dedication, the dedication of great merit, the vast dedication, the virtuous dedication, the pure dedication, the dedication free from evil, and the dedication that does not follow evil.
Having thus correctly dedicated all roots of goodness, the Bodhisattva accomplishes pure actions of body, speech, and mind; abiding in the Bodhisattva-dwelling, they are free from all faults;
they cultivate wholesome deeds, remain aloof from physical and verbal evils, and their minds are without blemish;
they cultivate omniscience, abide in a vast mind, and know that all phenomena are devoid of anything to be performed.
Abiding in supramundane dharmas, they are undefiled by worldly dharmas;
they discern and understand immeasurable karmas, accomplish the skillful means of dedication and transference, and forever uproot the foundation of all grasping and attachment.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the third dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, which is equal to that of all Buddhas.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this dedication, they enter deeply into the activities of all Tathāgatas and proceed toward the supreme and wondrous merits of the Tathāgatas.”
They enter the realm of profound and pure wisdom, never departing from the activities of all bodhisattvas, and are skillfully able to discern subtle and wondrous expedient means;
they enter the profound dharma-realm and well know the sequential stages of bodhisattva practice;
they enter the buddha-lineage and, through skillful expedient means, discern and understand all infinite and boundless dharmas.
"Although they manifest their bodies within the world, their minds have no attachment to worldly dharmas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"These Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas Cultivate the method of dedication practiced by the Buddhas of the past."
They also study the conduct of all Teachers throughout the future and present ages.
Having attained peace and bliss within all spheres of experience, they are praised by all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
With vast radiance and pure vision, they dedicate it all toward great wisdom.
The bodhisattva’s body-faculty experiences manifold pleasures, and so too do the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue;
all such immeasurable and supreme delights are dedicated to the Most Victorious Ones.
All the various wholesome dharmas in all worlds, And those accomplished by all the Tathāgatas—
I fully embrace them all without exception, And rejoice in them entirely for the benefit of sentient beings.
The world rejoices in immeasurable ways; now this dedication is for the sake of sentient beings.
May all the happiness possessed by the Lions among Men be fully perfected for the multitudes of living creatures.
May all the various joys known and seen by the Tathāgatas of all lands be attained by all sentient beings,
so that they may become great, brilliant lamps illuminating the world.
The supreme and wondrous bliss attained by the Bodhisattva is entirely dedicated to all living beings;
though he dedicates it for the sake of all beings, he remains unattached to that dedication.
As Bodhisattvas practice this dedication, Arousing immeasurable great compassion,
May I likewise fulfill all the virtues of dedication As practiced by the Buddhas.
Just as the Most Victorious Ones have accomplished, The subtle and wondrous bliss of the vehicle of omniscience,
And the practices I have undertaken while in the world, The immeasurable bliss of the bodhisattva deeds,
The bliss of showing entry into all realms for the sake of peace and security, And the constant guarding of the sense faculties in the bliss of tranquility—
Dedicating it all to all living beings, may they everywhere cultivate and perfect supreme wisdom.
It is not that body, speech, and mind are themselves karma, nor is there anything else apart from them;
yet by means of skillful expedients to extinguish the darkness of ignorance, one thus cultivates and perfects supreme wisdom.

The various deeds practiced by Bodhisattvas, Accumulating immeasurable, supreme merit, They accord with the Tathāgata and are born into the Buddha-family; Tranquil and undisturbed, they rightly dedicate [their merit].
All sentient beings throughout all worlds in the ten directions are gathered and sustained;
I dedicate all my roots of goodness to them, wishing that they may be fully endowed with peace, security, and happiness.
Seeking no benefit for oneself, desiring that all beings be entirely at peace,
never for a moment giving rise to a mind of conceptual proliferation, one contemplates only that all phenomena are empty and selfless.
To all the Supreme Victors throughout the ten directions, And to every true son of the Buddha whom they behold,
I dedicate all my roots of goodness to them, Vowing that they may swiftly attain unsurpassed enlightenment.
All sentient beings throughout the world, without exception, I embrace with an impartial mind;
by means of all the virtuous deeds I have performed, may those beings swiftly attain Buddhahood.
The immeasurable and boundless great vows proclaimed by the Unsurpassed Teacher—
may all the Buddha-sons become pure, and may they fulfill them all according to their hearts' desires.
Universally observing all worlds in the ten directions, He bestows his merits upon them all;
Vowing that they may all possess sublime adornments— In this way, the Bodhisattva trains in dedication.
The mind does not weigh or measure dualistic phenomena, but always realizes that all dharmas are non-dual;
whether dharmas are dual or non-dual, within them there is ultimately no attachment whatsoever.
All worlds throughout the ten directions are entirely the conceptual discriminations of sentient beings;
since neither concept nor non-concept can be apprehended, one thus thoroughly understands all such concepts.
Once those bodhisattvas have purified their bodies, their minds will likewise be pure and free from defilement;
once their verbal karma is purified and free from faults, you should know that their minds are pure and without attachment.
With single-minded right mindfulness, one recollects the Buddhas of the past, And likewise remembers all the Teachers of the future,
As well as the Honored One among gods and humans in the present, Learning thoroughly from the Dharma they have taught.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, With wisdom clear and penetrating and minds unimpeded,
Desiring to benefit all sentient beings, Dedicate their merits toward Bodhi and accumulate all virtuous deeds.
That foremost wisdom, vast wisdom, non-erroneous wisdom, unerring wisdom,
impartial and true wisdom, and pure wisdom— thus speaks the one of supreme wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the dedication of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva that reaches all places?
O Son of the Buddha!”
When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates all roots of goodness, he forms this thought:
"May the power of the merit of these roots of goodness reach all places."

For example, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) reaches nowhere it does not reach: it reaches all things, all worlds, all sentient beings, all lands, all phenomena, all space, all three periods of time, all conditioned and unconditioned states, and all speech and sounds.
May these roots of goodness likewise reach all the Tathāgatas, making offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time;

may the vows of all past Buddhas be fully fulfilled, may all future Buddhas be endowed with complete adornments, and may all present Buddhas, along with their lands, bodhimaṇḍas, and assemblies, pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.

By the great power of faith and understanding, by the unobstructed nature of vast wisdom, and by the dedication of all roots of goodness, may these offerings—consisting of all the various articles of worship used by the devas—be presented as offerings that fill immeasurable and boundless worlds.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:
'The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, pervade the entirety of the dharma-realm of all space.'"

Arising from various karmic actions, throughout all unspeakable world-systems in the ten directions—unspeakable varieties of Buddha-lands and Buddha-realms, immeasurable worlds, boundless worlds, inverted worlds, horizontal worlds, upright worlds, and overturned worlds—in all such worlds as these, he manifests his presence through the span of his life, displaying various supernatural powers and transformations.

Therein, there are bodhisattvas who, by the power of their resolute conviction, for the sake of those sentient beings capable of being transformed, manifest as Tathāgatas appearing in the world within all those various worlds, reaching the wisdom of all places.
They universally reveal the immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata; the Dharma-body goes everywhere without distinction, entering all dharma-realms with equality.

Because the Tathāgata-treasury body is neither born nor extinguished, it skillfully manifests throughout the world; because it realizes the true nature of phenomena which transcends all things; because it has attained the non-regressive power of non-obstruction; and because it is born within the lineage of the Tathāgata’s unobstructed vision and vast majesty.
“O Son of the Buddha!

By means of the vows regarding all the roots of goodness they have planted, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas make offerings at the abodes of such Tathāgatas with various exquisite flowers, various exquisite incenses, garlands, canopies, banners, pennants, robes, lamps, and all other kinds of ornamental requisites;
they do the same for the images of the Buddhas and the stupas and temples of the Buddhas.”
With these roots of goodness, one dedicates them in this way:

namely, with undisturbed dedication, single-minded dedication, dedication according to one's own intention, respectful dedication, unshakable dedication, non-abiding dedication, non-reliant dedication, dedication free from the mind of a sentient being, dedication free from a restless and competitive mind, and dedication with a tranquil mind.
Again, he formed this thought:

"Throughout all kalpas of the past, future, and present, across the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, all Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, having attained all-knowledge and realized the path of Bodhi, possess infinite names each distinct from the others; appearing at various times to manifest perfect enlightenment, they all abide with a lifespan reaching to the end of the future. Each one adorns their body with the adornments of the Dharma-realm, and their assemblies at the sites of enlightenment pervade the entire Dharma-realm; in all lands, they appear according to the time to perform the work of a Buddha."

I universally dedicate all these roots of goodness to all such Buddhas and Tathāgatas, wishing that there may be countless incense canopies, countless incense banners, countless incense flags, countless incense curtains, countless incense nets, countless incense images, countless incense lights, countless incense flames, countless incense clouds, countless incense seats, countless incense walking paths, countless incense abodes, countless incense worlds, countless incense mountains, countless incense seas, countless incense rivers, countless incense trees, countless incense garments, countless incense lotuses, and countless incense palaces; as well as immeasurable flower canopies, and so forth, up to immeasurable flower palaces.
Canopies of Boundless Garlands, explained at length up to palaces of Boundless Garlands;
Canopies of Peerless Unguents, explained at length up to palaces of Peerless Unguents;
Canopies of Innumerable Incense Powders, explained at length up to palaces of Innumerable Incense Powders.
Inconceivable canopies of robes, and so forth, up to inconceivable palaces of robes;
inconceivable canopies of jewels, and so forth, up to inconceivable palaces of jewels;
immeasurable canopies of lamp-light, and so forth, up to immeasurable palaces of lamp-light.
There are unspeakably many canopies of ornaments, and so forth, up to unspeakably many palaces of ornaments;

there are unspeakably many unspeakable numbers of mani-jewel canopies, unspeakably many unspeakable numbers of mani-jewel banners, as well as mani-jewel pennants, mani-jewel curtains, mani-jewel nets, mani-jewel images, mani-jewel radiance, mani-jewel flames, mani-jewel clouds, mani-jewel thrones, mani-jewel walking paths, mani-jewel abodes, mani-jewel lands, mani-jewel mountains, mani-jewel oceans, mani-jewel rivers, mani-jewel trees, mani-jewel garments, mani-jewel lotuses, and mani-jewel palaces—all of which are unspeakably many, unspeakably many.

In this way, within each and every one of these realms, there were countless railings, countless palaces, countless towers, countless gates, countless half-moons, countless defensive parapets, countless windows, countless pure jewels, and countless ornaments; with such articles of offering, they reverently made offerings to the aforementioned Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
May all worlds be rendered pure; may all sentient beings attain liberation, abide on the ground of the Ten Powers, and obtain unimpeded illumination of the Dharma regarding all phenomena.

May all sentient beings be endowed with roots of goodness and be fully tamed; may their minds be immeasurable, equal to the realm of empty space; may they travel to all lands without going anywhere; may they enter all realms to bestow various wholesome dharmas; may they always behold the Buddhas, plant all roots of goodness, and accomplish the Great Vehicle; may they remain unattached to all phenomena, be replete with manifold virtues, and establish immeasurable practices; may they universally enter the boundless entire dharma-realm, achieve the supernormal powers of all Buddhas, and attain the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes of being.
Just as non-self universally encompasses all phenomena, so too are my roots of goodness: they universally encompass all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, because I make offerings to them all without exception;
they universally encompass all infinite phenomena, because I am able to penetrate them all without obstruction.
They universally encompass all the assemblies of bodhisattvas, because they ultimately share the same roots of goodness;
they universally encompass all the practices of bodhisattvas, because they have brought them all to fulfillment through the power of their original vows;
they universally encompass the illumination of all bodhisattva teachings, because they have attained unimpeded penetration of all phenomena.
Because they universally encompass the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas to accomplish immeasurable roots of goodness;
because they universally encompass the powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas to give rise to immeasurable minds that fulfill all things;
and because they universally encompass the gates of bodhisattva samādhis, eloquence, and dhāraṇīs, being well able to illuminate and realize the non-dual Dharma.
It universally encompasses the skillful means of all Buddhas, because it manifests the great supernormal powers of the Tathāgatas;

it universally encompasses all Buddhas of the three periods of time—descending from Tuṣita, attaining enlightenment, turning the wheel of the true Dharma, taming sentient beings, and entering parinirvāṇa—because it fully and universally honors and makes offerings to them all;
and it universally encompasses all worlds in the ten directions, because it brings the purification of Buddha-lands to ultimate completion.
Because they universally encompass all vast eons, manifesting therein the uninterrupted cultivation of bodhisattva practices;
because they universally encompass all realms of existence, manifesting birth within them all;
and because they universally encompass all realms of sentient beings, fully perfecting the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Because they universally encompass all habitual tendencies of affliction, purifying them entirely through skillful means;
because they universally encompass the faculties of all sentient beings, fully understanding their infinite distinctions;
and because they universally encompass the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings, causing them to leave behind defilement and attain purity.
It universally encompasses all practices for transforming sentient beings, because it manifests bodies according to what is appropriate for them;
it universally encompasses all paths for responding to sentient beings, because it enters entirely into all realms of sentient beings;
and it universally encompasses the nature of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, because it protects and upholds the teachings of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner, they employ non-apprehension as their skillful means; they do not discriminate between karma and its retribution, nor do they discriminate between retribution and karma.

While remaining free from discrimination, they universally enter the Dharma-realm; while performing no action, they constantly abide in roots of goodness; and while originating nothing, they diligently cultivate the supreme Dharma."

Without believing in any phenomena, one is able to penetrate deeply; without existing within phenomena, one fully knows and perceives them, such that neither what is created nor what is uncreated can be apprehended.

One knows that the nature of all phenomena is eternally non-autonomous; thus, although one perceives all phenomena, there is nothing perceived, and while universally knowing all things, there is nothing known.

When a bodhisattva thus thoroughly understands the realm of experience, they know that all phenomena have causes and conditions as their basis; they perceive the *dharmakāya* of all Buddhas and reach the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) where all phenomena are free from defilement. They comprehend that the world is entirely like a magical transformation, clearly realizing that sentient beings are but a single dharma and possess no dual nature, yet they do not abandon the skillful means of the objective sphere of karma.
Within the realm of the conditioned (*saṃskṛtadhātu*), they manifest the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛtadharma*) without destroying the characteristics of the conditioned;
within the realm of the unconditioned, they manifest the conditioned without discriminating the characteristics of the unconditioned.

The Bodhisattva thus contemplates all phenomena as ultimately quiescent; having perfected all pure roots of goodness, they give rise to a mind that seeks to rescue and protect sentient beings. With wisdom that clearly penetrates the ocean of all phenomena, they constantly delight in practicing the dharma that transcends ignorance. Having already fully accomplished supramundane merit, they no longer train in mundane dharmas; having attained the eye of pure wisdom free from the cataracts of delusion, they cultivate the path of dedication through skillful means.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner, they accord with the hearts of all Buddhas; they adorn and purify all Buddha-lands; they teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity; and they fully uphold all Buddha-dharmas.
They become the supreme field of merit for all sentient beings, the wise guides for all merchants, and the pure sun-disks for all worlds.”
Each and every root of goodness pervades the Dharma-realm; it is able to rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing them all to be pure and fully endowed with merit. "O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate in this manner, they are able to protect and uphold all Buddha-seeds, mature all sentient beings, adorn and purify all buddha-fields, ensure that all karmic actions are not destroyed, fully comprehend all dharmas, equally contemplate all dharmas as non-dual, travel everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions, realize the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) free from desire, achieve pure faith and understanding, and perfect the sharpness and clarity of their faculties.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s fourth dedication, ‘Reaching All Places.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in this dedication, they attain the physical activity that reaches all places, because they are able to universally manifest throughout all worlds.”
They attain speech-action that reaches all places, because they expound the Dharma throughout all worlds;
they attain mental-action that reaches all places, because they receive and uphold all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas;
they attain the supernormal power of the bases of mastery that reaches all places, because they go everywhere in accordance with the minds of sentient beings to respond to them.
They attain the wisdom that realizes all places, because they are able to universally comprehend all phenomena;
they attain the dhāraṇīs and eloquence that reach all places, because they cause all sentient beings to rejoice according to their inclinations;
they attain entry into the dharma-realm at all places, because they universally enter all worlds within a single pore.
One attains the body that enters everywhere, because one universally enters the bodies of all sentient beings within the body of a single sentient being;
one attains the universal vision of all kalpas everywhere, because one constantly beholds all Tathāgatas within each and every kalpa;
one attains the universal vision of all thoughts everywhere, because all Buddhas manifest before one within each and every thought.
"O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains the dedication that reaches all places, and is thus able to dedicate roots of goodness in this manner.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“In all worlds, both internal and external, the Bodhisattva is entirely without attachment;
yet he does not abandon the work of benefiting sentient beings—such is the wisdom practiced by the Great Being.”
All the lands throughout the ten directions Are entirely without support and have no place of abiding;
One does not grasp at various dharmas such as livelihood, Nor does one falsely give rise to any conceptual discriminations.
Universally encompassing all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions without exception,
one contemplates that their essential nature is non-existent, and thus skillfully dedicates [merit] to reaching all places.
Universally encompassing all conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, one does not give rise to deluded thoughts therein;
as it is with worldly phenomena, so too is the illumination of the Lamp of the World—thus one awakens.
The various karmic practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas, distinguished into superior, middling, and inferior grades,
they dedicate all these roots of goodness to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
The Bodhisattva dedicates merit to reach the other shore, Fully accomplishing all that is learned from the Tathāgata;
Constantly employing sublime wisdom in skillful reflection, They are endowed with the most excellent Dharma among men.
Pure roots of goodness are universally dedicated, Benefiting all deluded beings without ever forsaking them;
May all sentient beings without exception Attain the state of the Unsurpassed Lamp that Illumines the World.
Never discriminatingly grasping at sentient beings, nor falsely conceptualizing any phenomena,
though they remain unstained by the world, they likewise do not abandon any conscious beings.
The Bodhisattva always delights in the dharma of quiescence, Following it until reaching the realm of nirvāṇa;
Yet they do not abandon the path of sentient beings, Attaining such subtle and wondrous wisdom as this.
The Bodhisattva never discriminates among karmas, nor does he grasp at or cling to any of their fruits;
all worlds arise from conditions, and he perceives all phenomena as inseparable from causes and conditions.
Deeply entering such realms as these, they do not give rise to conceptual discrimination therein;
as teachers who discipline all sentient beings, they clearly understand and skillfully dedicate [their merit] within this state.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Four;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Five.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
Chapter Twenty-Five, Part Three: The Dedication of the Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the dedication of the inexhaustible treasury of merit of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?"
“O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva [dedicates] the roots of goodness arising from the confession and removal of all heavy karmic obstructions;
and the roots of goodness arising from prostrating in reverence to all Buddhas of the three periods of time;”
The roots of goodness arising from exhorting all Buddhas to preach the Dharma;
the roots of goodness arising from hearing the Buddhas preach the Dharma and practicing with diligent application to realize the inconceivable and vast realm;
and the roots of goodness arising from giving rise to sympathetic joy for all the roots of goodness of all Buddhas and all sentient beings of the past, future, and present.
The inexhaustible roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present; the roots of goodness obtained by the assembly of Bodhisattvas through diligent cultivation;

the roots of goodness produced by the Bodhisattvas’ generation of sympathetic joy upon knowing that the Buddhas of the three periods of time attain equal and perfect enlightenment, turn the wheel of the true Dharma, and subdue sentient beings;

and the roots of goodness produced by their sympathetic joy regarding all matters from the initial aspiration of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, through their cultivation of Bodhisattva practices, their attainment of supreme perfect enlightenment, and even the manifestation of their entry into parinirvāṇa, as well as the duration of the True Dharma remaining in the world after their parinirvāṇa until its final extinction—all such roots of goodness they rejoice in.

The Bodhisattva thus contemplates the unspeakable realms of all Buddhas as well as their own realm, up to the unobstructed realm of enlightenment. All such vast and immeasurable varieties of roots of goodness—whatever has been accumulated, whatever has been believed and understood, whatever has been rejoiced in, whatever has been perfected, whatever has been accomplished, whatever has been practiced, whatever has been obtained, whatever has been realized, whatever has been sustained, and whatever has been increased—they dedicate them all toward adorning all Buddha-lands, just as in the boundless eons of the past, throughout all worlds and all places where Tathāgatas have practiced.
That is to say:
the immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-world systems, known by the wisdom of Buddhas, recognized by Bodhisattvas, and received by those of great resolve;
the adornment of Buddha-fields, the pure practices of karma, and that which flows forth and is drawn out, arising in response to sentient beings.

That which is manifested through the spiritual power of the Tathāgatas is accomplished by the pure karma of the Buddhas appearing in the world and arises from the sublime practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
therein all Buddhas attain enlightenment and manifest various sovereign spiritual powers.

Throughout the limits of the future, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who dwell pervading the Dharma-realm shall attain the Buddha-way and shall obtain all pure and adorned merit-filled Buddha-lands.

Throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—boundless, limitless, uninterrupted, and inexhaustible—all are born from the wisdom of the Tathāgata and adorned with immeasurable, wondrous jewels.
That is to say:

the adornment of all fragrances, the adornment of all flowers, the adornment of all garments, the adornment of the treasury of all merits, the adornment of the powers of all Buddhas, and the adornment of all Buddha-lands.
The capital city of the Tathāgata is inconceivable; there dwell various pure assemblies who share his past karmic conditions and will attain perfect enlightenment in future ages.
This is that which is accomplished by all Buddhas and is not seen by the world; only the pure eyes of Bodhisattvas can perceive it.

These Bodhisattvas possess great majestic virtue and have planted roots of goodness in past lives. Knowing that all phenomena are like illusions and transformations, they universally practice the various pure deeds of Bodhisattvas. Having entered the inconceivable and sovereign samādhi, they employ skillful means to perform the work of Buddhas, emitting the light of the Buddha that shines universally upon the world without limit or end.
All the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the present are likewise so.

They adorn their worlds with immeasurable forms and appearances, and immeasurable light and colors—all of which are accomplished through merit: immeasurable fragrances, immeasurable jewels, immeasurable trees, innumerable adornments, innumerable palaces, and innumerable sounds.
In accordance with past affinities, various spiritual friends manifest all manner of adornments of merit without end.
That is to say:

Adorned with all kinds of fragrances, adorned with all kinds of garlands, adorned with all kinds of powdered incense, adorned with all kinds of jewels, adorned with all kinds of banners, adorned with all kinds of precious silk streamers, adorned with all kinds of precious railings, adorned with incalculable nets of gold, adorned with incalculable rivers, adorned with incalculable clouds and rains, and accompanied by the playing of incalculable musical instruments producing subtle and wondrous sounds—by means of such infinite and innumerable articles of adornment, they adorn everything throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, including all worlds of infinite variety arising from the karma of the ten directions, as known and proclaimed by the Buddhas; that is, all the Buddha-lands contained therein.
That is to say:
