Adorned Buddha-lands, pure Buddha-lands, equal Buddha-lands, exquisite Buddha-lands, majestic Buddha-lands, vast Buddha-lands, blissful Buddha-lands, indestructible Buddha-lands, inexhaustible Buddha-lands, immeasurable Buddha-lands, immovable Buddha-lands, fearless Buddha-lands, luminous Buddha-lands, non-opposing Buddha-lands, delightful Buddha-lands, universally illuminating Buddha-lands, magnificent Buddha-lands, refined and beautiful Buddha-lands, skillfully crafted Buddha-lands, foremost Buddha-lands, superior Buddha-lands, distinguished Buddha-lands, most excellent Buddha-lands, supremely excellent Buddha-lands, sublime Buddha-lands, unsurpassed Buddha-lands, peerless Buddha-lands, incomparable Buddha-lands, and Buddha-lands beyond analogy.
In this way, regarding all the adornments of every buddha-field of the past, future, and present, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates their own roots of goodness with this resolve:

"May all the pure adornments of the lands of all buddhas of the past, future, and present adorn a single world; may all the adornments found in those various buddha-fields be fully accomplished, fully purified, fully gathered, fully manifested, fully perfected, and fully sustained."

As it is with one world, so it is throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space; all worlds are likewise, such that all Buddha-lands of the three periods of time are fully endowed with every kind of adornment.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all the Buddha-fields that I cultivate be completely filled with great Bodhisattvas.’”

These bodhisattvas possess a truly real nature; their wisdom is penetrating, and they are skillfully able to discern all world-realms and realms of sentient beings. They enter deeply into the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, having abandoned delusion.

They achieve mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma as truly inconceivable, and mindfulness of the Sangha as immeasurable and universally pervasive, while also maintaining mindfulness of relinquishment.
With the sun of Dharma full and the light of wisdom shining everywhere, they see all things without obstruction.

From non-attainment arises the birth of all Buddha-dharmas; they become the sovereign lords of the most excellent roots of goodness for the multitudes, giving rise to the unsurpassed mind of bodhicitta;

abiding in the powers of the Tathāgata, they proceed toward sarvajñā (omniscience), destroy all demonic activities, purify the realms of sentient beings, penetrate deeply into the nature of dharmas, forever depart from perversion, and ensure that their roots of goodness and great vows are entirely not in vain.
In this way, bodhisattvas fill that land; born in such a place, possessing such virtues, they constantly perform the work of Buddhas and attain the pure radiance of a Buddha’s bodhi.
They are endowed with the wisdom of the dharma-realm and manifest supernatural powers, a single body filling the entire dharma-realm.
Having attained great wisdom, they enter the sphere traversed by all-knowledge and are skillfully able to discern the infinite and boundless phrases and meanings of the dharma-realm.
They are entirely unattached to any buddha-field, yet they can manifest universally in all buddha-lands;
their minds are like space, having no point of reliance, yet they can discern the entire dharma-realm and skillfully enter and emerge from inconceivable, profound samādhis;
they advance toward omniscience (*sarvajñā*), dwell in the lands of all buddhas, attain the powers of the buddhas, and fearlessly reveal and expound incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) teachings.

They accord with the roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; they universally illumine the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas and are fully able to receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas;
they know the linguistic methods of incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) varieties and are skillfully able to produce inconceivable and differentiated sounds;
they enter the unexcelled stage of the Buddhas' own sovereignty and travel everywhere through all worlds in the ten directions without obstruction.
They practice in accordance with non-contention and the absence of any basis for reliance, remaining free from discrimination;
they cultivate and expand the bodhicitta, attain skillful wisdom, and are well-versed in the meaning of words and phrases, able to reveal and expound them in their proper sequence.

May such great bodhisattvas adorn that land, filling it and being distributed throughout it, dwelling in accordance with the Dharma, practicing cultivation and supreme cultivation, being pure and supremely pure, and remaining tranquil and serene.

In a single buddha-field, in every direction and location, there are pervasively filled with such countless, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and unspeakably unspeakable numbers of great bodhisattvas.
As it is in one direction, so it is in all directions;
as it is in one Buddha-field, so it is in all Buddha-fields throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm.

“O Son of the Buddha! By means of all their roots of goodness, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas skillfully dedicate them to all Buddha-lands; they skillfully dedicate them to all Bodhisattvas; they skillfully dedicate them to all Tathāgatas; they skillfully dedicate them to the Bodhi of all Buddhas; they skillfully dedicate them to all vast vows; they skillfully dedicate them to all paths of definitive liberation; they skillfully dedicate them to purifying the realms of all sentient beings; they skillfully dedicate them to always seeing the appearance of all Buddhas in the world throughout all worlds; they skillfully dedicate them to always seeing the immeasurable lifespan of the Tathāgatas; and they skillfully dedicate them to always seeing all Buddhas pervading the entire Dharma-realm, turning the unobstructed and non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma.”
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner, because they universally enter all buddha-lands, all buddha-fields become entirely pure;
because they universally reach all realms of sentient beings, all bodhisattvas become entirely pure.
Because all Buddha-lands universally aspire for the appearance of Buddhas, the bodies of all Tathāgatas transcendently manifest throughout the entire Dharma-realm and all Buddha-fields.
O Son of the Buddha!

By means of such incomparable dedications, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva proceeds toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). His mind is vast, like space, without limit or measure; he enters the inconceivable and knows that all karma and its retributions are entirely quiescent.
His mind is ever-equal, without boundary, and is able to universally penetrate the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they do not discriminate between self and what belongs to self; they do not discriminate between the Buddha and the Buddha-dharma; they do not discriminate between buddha-fields and their adornments; they do not discriminate between sentient beings and their transformation; they do not discriminate between karma and the retribution of karma; they do not cling to volition or that which arises from volition;
they do not destroy causes, they do not destroy effects, they do not grasp at things, and they do not grasp at dharmas.
One does not conceive of birth and death as having distinctions; one does not conceive of nirvana as eternally quiescent; one does not conceive of the Tathāgata as realizing a Buddha-realm;
there is not the slightest dharma that co-exists with dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they universally bestow all roots of goodness upon sentient beings, bringing them to certain maturity and teaching them with equanimity;
it is signless, objectless, immeasurable, and without falsehood, remaining far removed from all conceptual discrimination and attachment.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva has dedicated in this manner, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
That is to say:
because they mindfully recollect all Buddhas of the three periods of time, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
Because they keep all bodhisattvas in mind, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
because they purify all buddha-fields, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
because they purify the realms of all sentient beings, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
Because they have deeply entered the Dharma-realm, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
because they cultivate immeasurable minds equal to the realm of empty space, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
because they profoundly understand the spheres of all Buddhas, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
Because they diligently cultivate the deeds of a bodhisattva, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
because they thoroughly comprehend the three periods of time, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate all roots of goodness in this manner, they realize that within the realm of all sentient beings there are no sentient beings; they understand that all phenomena have no life-span; they know that all phenomena have no agent; they awaken to the fact that all phenomena have no *pudgala*; they realize that all phenomena are free from anger and contention; they contemplate that all phenomena arise from conditions and have no place of abiding; they know that all things have nothing upon which they rely; they realize that all lands have no fixed location; they contemplate that all bodhisattva practices likewise have no locus; and they see that all objective realms are entirely non-existent.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates merit in this way, his eyes never behold impure buddha-fields, nor does he perceive sentient beings with divergent characteristics. There is not the slightest phenomenon that enters into his wisdom, nor is there the slightest wisdom that enters into phenomena.

He understands that the body of the Tathāgata is not like empty space, for it is perfected by all merits and immeasurable sublime dharmas, and because it causes all sentient beings in all places to fully accumulate roots of goodness.
“O Son of the Buddha!

In every thought-moment, these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attain unspeakably unspeakable stages of the Ten Powers; they are fully endowed with all merit, have perfected pure roots of goodness, and serve as fields of merit for all sentient beings.”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished the treasury of merit of the wish-fulfilling jewel; for whatever necessities may arise, all articles of enjoyment are obtained.

Wherever they travel, they are able to adorn and purify all lands; and wherever they go, they cause unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings to become entirely pure, as they gather merit and cultivate all practices.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva thus dedicates [merit], they cultivate all bodhisattva practices; their merit is preeminent and their physical marks are peerless.
Their majestic power and radiance surpass all worlds, such that neither Māra nor his followers can gaze upon them.
Fully endowed with roots of goodness, they have accomplished their great vows;
their minds are ever more expansive, equaling all-knowledge;
and within a single thought-moment, they are able to pervade immeasurable Buddha-fields.
His power of wisdom is immeasurable; he thoroughly understands the realms of all Buddhas and attains profound faith and understanding in all Buddhas.
He abides in the power of the bodhicitta of boundless wisdom, as vast as the dharma-realm and ultimate as space.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the fifth inexhaustible treasury of merit dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in this dedication, they attain ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries.”
What are the ten? They are:
attaining the inexhaustible treasury of seeing Buddhas, because one sees incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Buddhas appearing in the world within a single pore;
They attain the inexhaustible treasury of entering the Dharma, because they observe with the power of the Buddha's wisdom that all phenomena entirely enter into a single phenomenon;
they attain the inexhaustible treasury of recollection and retention, because they receive and uphold all the teachings spoken by the Buddhas without forgetting or losing them;
they attain the inexhaustible treasury of definitive wisdom, because they skillfully know the secret expedient means of all the teachings spoken by the Buddhas.
They attain the inexhaustible treasury of understanding meanings and intentions, because they skillfully know the principles, patterns, and limits of all phenomena;
they attain the inexhaustible treasury of boundless awakening and comprehension, because they penetrate all phenomena of the three periods of time with wisdom that is like space;
they attain the inexhaustible treasury of merit, because it fulfills the minds of all sentient beings without end.
They attain the inexhaustible treasury of courageous wisdom and awakening, because they are able to completely eliminate the cataracts of ignorance in all sentient beings;
they attain the inexhaustible treasury of definitive eloquence, because they expound the impartial Dharma of all Buddhas so that all sentient beings may fully understand it;

and they attain the inexhaustible treasury of the ten powers and fearlessnesses, because they fulfill all the practices of Bodhisattvas, bind their crowns with the silk ribbon free from defilement, and reach the unobstructed state of omniscience.
These are the ten.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate all roots of goodness, they attain these ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The Bodhisattva accomplishes the power of profound resolve, Attaining mastery over all phenomena;
By means of the merit of exhortation and sympathetic joy, He skillfully dedicates it through unimpeded expedient means.”
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, Whose adorned and pure Buddha-fields pervade the world,
Possessing every merit in its entirety— I dedicate [my merits] toward a pure field in the same way.
All the Buddha-dharmas of the three periods of time, the Bodhisattvas contemplate them all with perfect clarity;
grasping them with their minds without exception, they thus adorn the buddha-fields.
Even if one were to spend all the kalpas throughout the three periods of time praising the various merits of a single Buddha-field,
those kalpas of the three periods might come to an end, but the merits of the Buddha-field would never be exhausted.
All such Buddha-fields as these, the Bodhisattva perceives without exception;
he unifies them all to adorn a single Buddha-land, and all Buddha-lands are likewise so.
There are sons of the Buddha whose minds are pure, All born through transformation from the Tathāgata’s Dharma;
With minds adorned by all merits, They fill every buddha-field.
Those bodhisattvas are all fully endowed with bodies adorned by immeasurable marks and signs;
their eloquence in expounding the Dharma pervades the world, like the great ocean that is inexhaustible.
The Bodhisattva dwells securely in all samādhis, Fully accomplishing every practice;
His mind is pure and peerless, Its radiance universally illuminating the worlds of the ten directions.
In this way, all Buddha-fields without exception are filled with these bodhisattvas;
they have never even thought of the vehicle of the śrāvakas, nor do they seek the path of the pratyekabuddhas.
With such purity of mind, the Bodhisattva dedicates their roots of goodness to all living beings,
desiring that they all may achieve the Perfect Path and fully realize the teachings of all Buddhas.
All the māras and adversaries throughout the ten directions are utterly crushed by the bodhisattva’s majestic power;
with courageous wisdom that none can surpass, he resolutely practices the ultimate Dharma.
By the power of these great vows, the Bodhisattva’s every dedication is free from obstruction;
entering the inexhaustible treasury of merit, it remains forever undiminished throughout the past, future, and present.
The Bodhisattva skillfully contemplates all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), thoroughly understanding that their nature is not independent;
having realized that the nature of all phenomena is thus, they do not falsely grasp at karma or its retribution.
There are no dharmas with form and no dharmas without form; there is neither perception nor non-perception.
Both existent dharmas and non-existent dharmas are entirely absent; one thoroughly understands that all things are unattainable.
All phenomena arise from causes and conditions; their essential nature is neither existent nor non-existent.
Yet, regarding those causes and conditions and that which is produced from them, there is ultimately no grasping or attachment therein.
In the realm of the speech of all sentient beings, Ultimately nothing at all can be apprehended therein;
One thoroughly understands that names and forms are all mere conceptual constructions, And clearly realizes that all phenomena are entirely without self.
Just as the nature of sentient beings is fundamentally quiescent, so too does one understand all phenomena:
everything subsumed within the three times without exception, including lands and all karmic actions, is entirely equal.
Dedicating with such wisdom, merit arises according to one's realization;
since these various marks of merit are also like that realization, how could anything be obtained therein?
Thus, the mind of dedication is stainless; it never attempts to measure the nature of all phenomena.
Having realized that their nature is in fact no-nature, it neither dwells in the world nor departs from it.
All the various wholesome deeds performed, Are entirely dedicated to all living beings;
May they all realize and penetrate their true nature, And cause all conceptual discriminations to be dispelled.
All false views whatsoever are entirely abandoned without remainder;
free from all feverish afflictions, they remain ever cool, dwelling in the unimpeded stage of liberation.
The Bodhisattva does not destroy any phenomena, nor does he annihilate the nature of phenomena;
understanding that all phenomena are like echoes, he remains entirely unattached to anything whatsoever.
He thoroughly understands that all sentient beings of the three periods of time arise entirely from the conjunction of causes and conditions;
he likewise knows their mental inclinations and habitual tendencies, yet never destroys or annihilates any phenomena.
Thoroughly understanding that the nature of karma is not karma itself, yet not contradicting the characteristics of all phenomena,
nor destroying the retribution of karmic results, one explains that the nature of all phenomena arises from conditions.
Knowing that sentient beings have no arising, And that there are no sentient beings who transmigrate, There is no real sentient being to be described;
It is only in accordance with worldly convention that they are provisionally taught.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s dedication that accords with all firm roots of goodness?
O Son of the Buddha!”

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva may become a sovereign ruler presiding over a great kingdom; his majestic virtue spreads far and wide, and his fame resounds throughout the world. All enemies submit without exception, and every proclamation and edict accords with the True Dharma (*saddharma*). Holding a single parasol that provides universal shade for the ten thousand regions, he travels throughout the land without obstruction wherever he turns. With a stainless silk cloth bound upon his crown, he possesses mastery over the Dharma; all who behold him are humbled, submitting through the influence of his virtue without the need for execution or punishment.
He gathers all sentient beings through the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*) and becomes a Wheel-Turning King (*cakravartin*), providing for all without exception.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in such sovereign merits, they possess a great retinue that cannot be broken or destroyed; they are free from all faults, and those who behold them never tire of the sight. Adorned with merit and virtue, their primary marks and secondary signs are perfected, and their physical form and limbs are well-proportioned and complete.
They attain the firm body of Nārāyaṇa, achieving great power that none can subdue;
they acquire pure karma and remain free from all karmic obstructions.

They fully practice all forms of giving: they give food and drink as well as various exquisite flavors; they give vehicles; they give clothing; they give flower garlands, blended incenses, ointments, couches, seats, houses, and dwellings; they give superior and wonderful lamps and candles, medicinal decoctions for the sick, precious vessels, precious chariots, and well-trained elephants and horses—all beautifully adorned—and they give with joy.

If there were those who came to beg for the throne upon which the king sat, or for canopies, umbrellas, banners, pennants, precious objects, or various ornaments; or even for the jeweled crown upon his head, the bright pearl within his topknot, or even the royal throne itself—he would not be stingy with any of these.
If he sees sentient beings within prisons, he relinquishes all wealth, treasures, wives, children, and kinsmen, even using his own body to rescue them so they may be liberated.
If he sees a prisoner about to be executed, he immediately sacrifices his own body to take their life in its place.
Or, seeing someone come to beg for his skin, scalp, and hair, he joyfully gives them away without any stinginess.

His eyes, ears, nose, and tongue, as well as his teeth, head, hands, feet, flesh, blood, marrow, heart, kidneys, liver, lungs, large intestine, small intestine, thick skin, thin skin, the various fingers of his hands and feet, and even his fingernails and toenails with their flesh—all these he gives away entirely with a joyful mind.
Some, seeking to request unprecedented dharmas, cast themselves down into deep pits of blazing fire;
some, to protect and uphold the True Dharma of the Tathāgata, endure all manner of suffering and poison with their own bodies;
and some, seeking even a single word of the Dharma, are able to completely relinquish everything they possess within the four seas.
He constantly transforms and guides sentient beings through the True Dharma, causing them to cultivate wholesome deeds and abandon all evils.
If he sees sentient beings harming or disfiguring the bodies of others, he rescues them with a compassionate heart, leading them to relinquish their sinful karma.
If they see the Tathāgata attain supreme perfect enlightenment, they shall praise and extol him so that all may hear and know.
Or they shall give land to construct monasteries, dwellings, and halls as places of residence;
and they shall give servants to attend to and perform labor for them.
They may give their own bodies to those who come begging, or they may give them to the Buddha;
for the sake of seeking the Dharma, they rejoice with leaping exultation,
and for the sake of sentient beings, they serve and make offerings.
Or they may relinquish their royal rank, cities, towns, villages, palaces, gardens, wives, children, and retinues; whatever is requested, they fulfill all such wishes.
Or they may relinquish all their means of livelihood and universally establish a great, unrestricted assembly of charity (*amogha-mahā-dāna*).

Within this assembly, there are various fields of merit among sentient beings—whether coming from afar or from near, whether wise or foolish, whether handsome or ugly, whether male or female, human or non-human—with diverse mental dispositions and differing requests; to all of them they give equally, causing everyone to be fully satisfied.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices giving in this manner, they generate a well-governed mind and dedicate it all.
That is to say:
Skillfully gathering form, they accord with and strengthen all roots of goodness;
skillfully gathering feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, they accord with and strengthen all roots of goodness;
skillfully gathering royal sovereignty, they accord with and strengthen all roots of goodness.
They skillfully gather their retinues, thereby conforming to and strengthening all roots of goodness;
they skillfully gather the necessities of life, thereby conforming to and strengthening all roots of goodness;
they skillfully gather acts of giving, thereby conforming to and strengthening all roots of goodness.
"O Son of the Buddha!
To whatever extent the objects given by a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva are immeasurable and boundless, they dedicate those roots of goodness in this way:

'When giving superior and exquisite food to sentient beings, my mind is pure; regarding the object given, I am without greed, without attachment, and without any sense of regret or stinginess, thus fulfilling the practice of giving. "

May all sentient beings obtain the food of wisdom, their minds free from hindrance; may they thoroughly understand the nature of food and be without attachment to it, but instead delight in the food of the joy of Dharma and renunciation.
May they be filled with wisdom, abide firmly in the Dharma, and gather roots of goodness, so that they may travel with the purity of the Dharma-body and Wisdom-body.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, acting as a field of merit for them, they manifest the acceptance of solid food.
"This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives food.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives drink, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way, namely: "
"May all sentient beings drink the water of the flavor of the Dharma, diligently practice and cultivate it, and fulfill the bodhisattva path;
may they sever worldly thirst and craving, constantly seek the Buddha-wisdom, leave behind the realm of desire, and attain the joy and bliss of the Dharma."
Their bodies are born from pure dharmas; they constantly discipline and harmonize their minds through samādhi;
they enter the ocean of wisdom, raise great clouds of Dharma, and pour down the great rain of Dharma.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives drinks.
"O Son of the Buddha!
A bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives various kinds of pure, superior flavors."
That is to say:
pungent, sour, salty, bland, as well as sweet and bitter.

These various flavors are fully moistening and complete, able to bring the four great elements into a state of peace and harmony, making the body full and robust, and causing the mind to be pure and constantly joyful.
When swallowing and chewing, one does not cough or feel constricted;
the faculties are clear and sharp, and the internal organs are full and robust;
poisons cannot invade, and diseases cannot harm.
From beginning to end, they shall be free from affliction and forever attain peace and happiness.
With these roots of goodness, one should dedicate them in this way:
"May all sentient beings obtain the most supreme flavors, filled with ambrosia;..."
May all sentient beings attain the flavor of the knowledge of phenomena, thoroughly understanding the functions and effects of all flavors;
may all sentient beings attain immeasurable flavors of the Dharma, fully comprehend the Dharma-realm, and dwell securely within the great city of the ultimate reality;
may all sentient beings become great clouds of the Dharma, raining down the rain of Dharma everywhere throughout the Dharma-realm to teach, transform, and subdue all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings attain the flavor of supreme wisdom, their bodies and minds filled with the unsurpassed joy of the Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain freedom from craving for any superior flavors, remain unstained by any worldly tastes, and constantly and diligently cultivate all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain the flavor of the single Dharma, realizing that all Buddha-dharmas are entirely without distinction.
May all sentient beings attain the most supreme flavor, riding upon omniscience until the end without ever regressing;
may all sentient beings enter the undifferentiated flavor of the Dharma of all Buddhas, and be fully able to discern all faculties;
may the flavor of the Dharma increase for all sentient beings, so that they always attain fulfillment in the unimpeded Buddha-dharma.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives the flavor [of food];
it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to diligently cultivate merit and virtue, so that they may all be fully endowed with the body of unobstructed wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give gifts of vehicles, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:

‘May all sentient beings fully attain the vehicle of omniscience; may they ride upon the Great Vehicle, the indestructible vehicle, the most excellent vehicle, the supreme vehicle, the swift vehicle, the vehicle of great power, the vehicle endowed with merit, the supramundane vehicle, and the vehicle that gives birth to the infinite Bodhisattvas.’”
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives vehicles.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives clothing, they dedicate the various roots of goodness in this way, namely:

"May all sentient beings obtain the garment of shame and modesty to cover their bodies, abandon the evil practices of heretical paths and nakedness, possess lustrous complexions and supple skin, achieve the supreme bliss of all Buddhas, and attain the most pure knowledge of all modes."
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives clothing.
"O Son of the Buddha!
A bodhisattva-mahāsattva constantly gives various kinds of named flowers, namely:

Subtle and exquisite fragrant flowers, flowers of various colors, immeasurable and wondrous flowers, well-seen flowers, delightful flowers, flowers that bloom in all seasons, celestial flowers, human flowers, flowers cherished and loved by the world, and exceedingly fragrant, pleasing flowers.

With such immeasurable and wondrous flowers as these, they make offerings to all Buddhas currently living, as well as to all stupas and temples after the Buddhas have passed into parinirvāṇa; or they offer them to those who preach the Dharma, or to the Sangha of bhikṣus, to all bodhisattvas, spiritual friends, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, parents, and kinsmen, down to themselves and all others who are poor, destitute, and without refuge.
When practicing giving, one dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain the flowers of the samādhis of all Buddhas, and be able to cause all dharmas to bloom;
may all sentient beings become like the Buddhas, such that all who see them rejoice and their hearts never tire of beholding them."
May all sentient beings encounter what is harmonious and pleasing, their minds free from agitation;
may all sentient beings fully practice vast and pure deeds;
may all sentient beings constantly mind their virtuous friends, their hearts remaining unchanging.
May all sentient beings be like the agada medicine, able to eliminate the manifold poisons of all afflictions;
may all sentient beings fulfill their great vows and all become supreme kings of wisdom;
may the sun of wisdom of all sentient beings shatter the darkness of ignorance.
May the pure moon of bodhi of all sentient beings increase and reach fulfillment;
may all sentient beings enter the great jewel-island, behold spiritual friends, and fully accomplish all roots of goodness.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives flowers, in order to cause all sentient beings to attain pure and unobstructed wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha! When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give garlands, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:

‘May all sentient beings be pleasing to behold; may those who see them praise them with admiration; may those who see them regard them with intimacy and kindness; may those who see them love and delight in them; may those who see them yearn for them with longing; may those who see them have their sorrows dispelled; may those who see them give rise to joy; may those who see them leave behind evil; may those who see them always attain close proximity to the Buddhas; and may those who see them become pure and obtain all-knowledge.’”
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives flower garlands.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives incense, they dedicate their various roots of goodness in this way:

"May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the fragrance of precepts, attaining the precepts that are unbroken, unmixed, unstained, free from regret, detached from entanglements, without feverish affliction, without transgression, boundless, supramundane, and the bodhisattva pāramitā-precepts;
may all sentient beings, by virtue of these precepts, all achieve the body of precepts of all Buddhas."
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives incense, performed in order to cause all sentient beings to fully attain the aggregate of unimpeded ethical discipline.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows fragrant ointments, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the gift of fragrance, and may they all be able to generously relinquish everything they possess;’”
May all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of precepts and attain the ultimate pure precepts of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of patience and be free from all treacherous and harmful intentions;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of diligence and constantly don the armor of Mahāyāna diligence.
May all sentient beings be universally suffused with the fragrance of concentration, dwelling securely in the samādhi of the presence of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings be universally suffused with the fragrance of wisdom, attaining supreme sovereignty of knowledge in a single thought-moment;
may all sentient beings be universally suffused with the fragrance of the Dharma, attaining fearlessness regarding the unsurpassed Dharma.
May all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of virtue, accomplishing all great merit and wisdom;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of Bodhi, attaining the ten powers of a Buddha and reaching the other shore;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the sublime fragrance of pure, white dharmas, forever extinguishing all unwholesome states.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives fragrant ointments.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives couches and seats, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings obtain the seats of the devas and realize great wisdom;
may all sentient beings obtain the seats of the worthy and noble ones, abandon the mind of an ordinary person, and abide in the bodhicitta;
may all sentient beings obtain the seats of peace and bliss, forever departing from all the sufferings and afflictions of birth and death."
May all sentient beings obtain the ultimate seat and behold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain the seat of equanimity and constantly and universally cultivate all wholesome dharmas;
may all sentient beings obtain the most supreme seat, possessing pure karma such that none in the world can equal them.
May all sentient beings obtain peaceful and secure seats, realize the true Dharma, and be fully perfected;
may all sentient beings obtain pure seats, cultivate the realm of the Tathāgata’s pure wisdom;
may all sentient beings obtain seats of firm abiding, and be constantly followed and protected by spiritual friends.
"May all sentient beings obtain lion thrones and always lie on their right sides, just as the Tathāgata does.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives beds and seats, for the purpose of causing sentient beings to practice right mindfulness and to skillfully guard their sense faculties.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give dwellings, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all sentient beings attain abiding in pure Buddha-fields and diligently cultivate all meritorious virtues;’”
Abiding in the realm of profound samādhi, they relinquish all attachment to dwelling places;
realizing that all dwelling places are non-existent, they leave behind all worldly realms and abide in omniscience;
they embrace the abodes of all Buddhas and dwell in the blissful state of the ultimate path.
"Abiding forever in the foremost pure roots of goodness, one shall never abandon the Buddha’s unsurpassed dwelling.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives dwellings;
it is for the purpose of benefiting all sentient beings, contemplating their rescue and protection according to what is appropriate for each.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives dwellings, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all sentient beings constantly obtain wholesome benefits, and may their minds be peaceful and happy;’”

May all sentient beings abide by relying upon the Tathāgata, abide by relying upon great wisdom, abide by relying upon spiritual friends, abide by relying upon the sublime and victorious, abide by relying upon wholesome conduct, abide by relying upon great loving-kindness, abide by relying upon great compassion, abide by relying upon the six pāramitās, abide by relying upon the great bodhicitta, and abide by relying upon the path of all bodhisattvas.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives a dwelling place, for the sake of purifying all merit; for ultimate purity; for the purity of wisdom; for the purity of the path; for the purity of the Dharma; for the purity of ethical discipline; for the purity of aspiration and inclination; for the purity of faith and understanding; for the purity of vows; and for the purity of all supernatural powers and merits.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bestow various lamps, they are as follows:
ghee lamps, oil lamps, jewel lamps, maṇi lamps, lacquer lamps, fire lamps, aloeswood lamps, sandalwood lamps, lamps of all kinds of incense, and lamps of immeasurable colored light.”
When giving such immeasurable lamps, it is for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings and for the sake of gathering in all sentient beings; one dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain immeasurable light that universally illumines the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain pure light that perceives even the most subtle forms in the world."
May all sentient beings attain the light free from obscuration and realize that the realm of sentient beings is empty and non-existent;
may all sentient beings attain boundless light, with bodies emitting wondrous radiance that universally illumines all;
may all sentient beings attain the light of universal illumination, so that their minds never regress from the teachings of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain the pure light of the Buddhas, manifesting throughout all lands;
may all sentient beings attain unimpeded light, with each ray illuminating the entire dharma-realm;
may all sentient beings attain uninterrupted light, its radiance shining continuously across all Buddha-lands.
May all sentient beings attain the light of the wisdom-banner, universally illuminating the world;
may all sentient beings attain light of immeasurable colors, illuminating all lands and manifesting spiritual powers.

When the Bodhisattva thus gives lamps, it is for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings. By means of these roots of goodness, he follows after sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, he gathers in sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, he distributes them [to others]; by means of these roots of goodness, he feels compassion for sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, he nurtures sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, he rescues and protects sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, he fulfills sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, he contemplates sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, he benefits sentient beings equally; and by means of these roots of goodness, he observes sentient beings.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives lamps; dedicating in this way is free from all obstacles, universally causing all sentient beings to abide within roots of goodness.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bestow medicinal decoctions, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all sentient beings ultimately emerge from all hindrances and entanglements;’”
May all sentient beings forever leave behind diseased bodies and attain the body of a Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings become great efficacious medicines to eliminate all diseases of unwholesomeness;
may all sentient beings become agada medicines and abide securely on the stage of non-retrogression of Bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings become like the medicine of the Tathāgata, able to extract the poisonous arrows of all afflictions;
may all sentient beings draw near to the worthy and holy ones, extinguish all afflictions, and cultivate pure conduct;
may all sentient beings become great kings of medicine, forever eliminating all illnesses so that they do not recur.
May all sentient beings become indestructible medicinal trees, capable of healing and saving all sentient beings;
may all sentient beings attain the light of omniscience to extract the arrows of all maladies;
may all sentient beings skillfully understand the methods of worldly medicine and pharmaceuticals to provide relief and healing for all illnesses.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give medicinal decoctions, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way: for the sake of causing all sentient beings to forever be free from all illnesses; for the sake of ultimate peace and security; for the sake of ultimate purity; so that they may be like the Buddha, free from disease; for the sake of extracting the arrows of all ailments; for the sake of attaining an inexhaustible and solid body; for the sake of attaining a body indestructible by the Diamond Ring Mountains; for the sake of attaining firm and perfect strength; for the sake of attaining the perfect and irremovable bliss of a Buddha; and for the sake of attaining the sovereign and solid body of all Buddhas. They dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are fully capable of bestowing all manner of vessels and utensils.
That is to say:

Golden vessels were filled with various jewels; silver vessels were filled with many exquisite treasures; lapis lazuli vessels were filled with diverse gems; crystal vessels were filled with immeasurable ornaments of precious adornments; mother-of-pearl vessels were filled with red pearls; agate vessels were filled with coral and maṇi-jewels; white jade vessels were filled with various delicious foods; sandalwood vessels were filled with celestial garments; and diamond vessels were filled with many wonderful fragrances.

There were immeasurable and innumerable vessels made of various jewels, filled with immeasurable and innumerable varieties of precious gems; some were offered to the Buddhas out of faith in the inconceivable field of merit that is the Buddha;
some were offered to the Bodhisattvas because of the knowledge that spiritual friends are difficult to encounter;
and some were offered to the noble Saṅgha for the sake of causing the Buddha-dharma to abide long in the world.
Or one may give to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, out of pure faith toward the noble ones;
or one may give to one's parents, out of respect for them;
or one may give to teachers and elders, because they constantly provide guidance and instruction, leading one to cultivate merit in accordance with the holy teachings.
Or they give to those who are inferior, poor, and destitute, because they regard all sentient beings with eyes of great kindness and great compassion;
because they single-mindedly fulfill the *dānapāramitā* of all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present;
and because they universally bestow all things upon all, never wearying of or abandoning sentient beings.
When giving in this manner, one is entirely without attachment to either the objects given or the recipients.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives by filling various precious vessels with immeasurable treasures, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:

"May all sentient beings become boundless treasuries like space, possessing vast power of mindfulness, such that they are able to receive and uphold all worldly and world-transcending scriptures without ever forgetting them."
May all sentient beings become pure vessels, able to awaken to the profound and true Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings become unsurpassed jewel-vessels, fully able to receive and uphold the Buddha-Dharmas of the three periods of time;
may all sentient beings achieve the vast Dharma-vessels of the Tathāgatas, embracing the Bodhi-Dharmas of the Buddhas of the three periods of time with indestructible faith.
May all sentient beings achieve the vessel of supreme jewel-adornment and abide in the bodhicitta of great majestic power;
may all sentient beings achieve the vessel that is the locus of reliance for merit, giving rise to pure faith and understanding toward the immeasurable wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings achieve the vessel that enters into omniscience, ultimately attaining the unimpeded liberation of the Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings attain the vessel of bodhisattva practice that extends through all future kalpas, enabling them to cause all beings to dwell securely in the power of omniscience;

may all sentient beings achieve the supreme vessel of the lineage and merit of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, able to receive and uphold all that is spoken by the sublime voices of all Buddhas;

may all sentient beings achieve the vessel capable of containing the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas throughout the entire dharma-realm, the realm of space, and all worlds, becoming foremost among great beings in proclaiming the teachings and exhorting all Buddhas to turn the wheel of the true Dharma.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives vessels, for the purpose of universally causing all sentient beings to fully attain the vessel of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-five;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
The Twenty-fifth Chapter on Dedication, Part Four:
“O Sons of the Buddha!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas take various chariots, adorned with all kinds of jewels, and offer them as gifts to the Buddhas and bodhisattvas, teachers, virtuous friends, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas—thus to immeasurable varieties of fields of merit—and even to those who are poor and destitute.”

These multitudes of people have come either from afar or from nearby; some have come because they heard the fame of the Bodhisattva’s name, some have come due to their karmic connection with the Bodhisattva, some have come because they heard of the vows of generosity the Bodhisattva made in the past, and some have been invited by the Bodhisattva’s own mental vow.
At that time, the Bodhisattva would sometimes give precious chariots or golden chariots, all exquisitely adorned with nets of bells draped over them and jeweled ribbons hanging down;
or he would give superior lapis lazuli chariots, decorated with immeasurable rare treasures;
or again, he would give silver chariots covered with golden nets and drawn by swift horses.
Or again, he may give chariots adorned with immeasurable varieties of jewels, covered with jeweled nets and yoked to fragrant elephants;

or again, he may give sandalwood chariots with wheels of exquisite gems and canopies of various jewels, upon which well-arranged and magnificent lion-thrones of precious materials are placed, where hundreds of thousands of court ladies sit in rows, while a hundred thousand men lead and drive them along;

or again, he may give crystal chariots decorated with many kinds of wonderful jewels, filled with beautiful women, with jeweled curtains covering them above and banners and streamers attending at their sides.

Or again, he may give a chariot made of agate, adorned with various jewels, perfumed with diverse incenses, and decorated with the scattering of many kinds of exquisite flowers; it is driven by hundreds of thousands of maidens holding precious necklaces, well-trained and harmonious in its movement, able to travel securely even over perilous terrain.

Or again, he may give a sturdy incense-chariot with wheels made of various jewels, magnificent and grand in its adornment; a jeweled canopy covers it above and a jeweled net hangs down from it, while various precious garments are spread within. Pure and fine incense flows forth with its fragrance penetrating to the outside; its scent is so exquisite that it delights the hearts of men, and it is escorted by immeasurable devas as they travel, carrying various treasures to provide for others according to their needs.

Or again, they may give away a chariot of radiant jewels, its various precious gems reflecting brilliant colors, covered above by nets of exquisite jewels, with necklaces of diverse gems hanging down all around; it is strewn with powdered incense, fragrant and pure within and without, and their beloved sons and daughters are all seated upon it.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas offer such various and wondrous jeweled chariots to the Buddhas, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
'May all sentient beings fully understand how to make offerings to the supreme field of merit; may they have deep faith in giving to the Buddhas and thereby obtain immeasurable retribution;'"
May all sentient beings turn their minds single-mindedly toward the Buddha and always encounter immeasurable, pure fields of merit;
may all sentient beings have no stinginess toward the Tathāgatas and fully accomplish the mind of great relinquishment;

may all sentient beings, practicing acts of giving in the presence of the Buddhas, leave behind the aspirations of the two vehicles and attain the Tathāgata’s unimpeded liberation and the wisdom of all-knowledge.
May all sentient beings practice inexhaustible giving in the presence of all Buddhas and enter the immeasurable merit and wisdom of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings enter the supreme wisdom of the Buddhas and attain the status of a pure, unsurpassed King of Wisdom;
may all sentient beings obtain the Buddhas' all-pervading and unimpeded supernormal powers, so that wherever they wish to go, they are never without mastery.
May all sentient beings enter deeply into the Mahāyāna, attain immeasurable wisdom, and abide therein immovably;
may all sentient beings be able to give birth to the dharmas of omniscience and become the supreme field of merit for all devas and humans;
may all sentient beings harbor no feelings of resentment toward the Buddhas, diligently plant roots of goodness, and joyfully seek the wisdom of the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings be able to travel spontaneously to all Buddha-fields, pervading the entire Dharma-realm in a single kṣaṇa without weariness;
may all sentient beings attain the sovereign supernormal powers of Bodhisattvas, manifesting bodies that fill the entirety of space to approach and make offerings at all the abodes of Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain incomparable bodies, traveling throughout the ten directions without ever feeling weary.
May all sentient beings attain vast bodies that travel with swift flight, proceeding wherever they wish without ever experiencing weariness or retreat;

may all sentient beings attain the ultimate sovereign power of the Buddhas, manifesting within a single kṣaṇa throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space all the supernatural transformations and miracles of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings cultivate the practice of peaceful bliss and accord with all the paths of the Bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings attain swift movement, ultimately perfecting the ten powers, wisdom, and spiritual penetrations;
may all sentient beings universally enter the dharmadhātu and the lands of the ten directions, reaching their very limits without any distinction;
may all sentient beings practice the conduct of Samantabhadra without regression, reaching the other shore and attaining all-knowledge.
"May all sentient beings ascend the vehicle of incomparable wisdom and, in accordance with the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), perceive reality as it truly is.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when offering precious chariots to all present Buddhas and to all stūpas and temples after the Buddhas have passed into extinction, for the sake of enabling sentient beings to attain the Tathāgata’s ultimate, unobstructed vehicle of liberation.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give precious chariots to spiritual friends such as other Bodhisattvas, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all sentient beings always remember and uphold the instructions of spiritual friends, diligently guarding them so that they are never forgotten or lost;’”
May all sentient beings share the same purpose and benefit as their spiritual friends, universally gathering and sharing all roots of goodness with them;
may all sentient beings draw near to spiritual friends, honoring and making offerings to them, relinquishing all they possess, and acting in accordance with their wishes;
may all sentient beings attain virtuous aspirations, following after good companions without ever abandoning them.
May all sentient beings always encounter virtuous friends, serving them with single-minded devotion and never contravening their instructions;
may all sentient beings delight in virtuous friends, never abandoning them, remaining constant and pure without interval or distraction, and free from error;
may all sentient beings be able to offer their very bodies to virtuous friends, following their teachings and commands without any opposition.
May all sentient beings be embraced by spiritual friends, cultivate great loving-kindness, and remain far removed from all evils;
may all sentient beings follow spiritual friends to hear the true Dharma taught by all Buddhas;

may all sentient beings share the same roots of goodness and the pure fruits of karma as their spiritual friends, and attain the ultimate ten powers through the same practices and vows as all Bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings be able to receive and uphold the teachings of spiritual friends, attaining the wisdom and supernormal powers of all samādhi-realms;
may all sentient beings be able to receive and uphold all true dharmas, cultivating all practices to reach the other shore;
may all sentient beings ride upon the Great Vehicle without obstruction, ultimately accomplishing the path of omniscience.
May all sentient beings fully ascend the vehicle of omniscience and reach the state of peace and security without ever regressing;
may all sentient beings know the practice of reality as it is, such that according to whatever Buddha-dharma they hear, they shall all attain its ultimate realization and never again forget it;
may all sentient beings be universally embraced by all Buddhas, attain unimpeded wisdom, and bring all phenomena to their final consummation.
May all sentient beings attain sovereign supernormal powers that are never lost, reaching whatever place they wish to go in a single thought-moment;
may all sentient beings travel with mastery, extensively practicing transformation and guidance to establish others in the Mahāyāna;
may the deeds of all sentient beings not be in vain, as they ride upon the vehicle of wisdom to reach the ultimate stage.
"May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded vehicle, reaching all places through unimpeded wisdom.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives various chariots to spiritual friends, in order to cause sentient beings to become fully endowed with merit, equal and no different from Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives precious chariots as an offering to the Saṃgha, they give rise to the mind that learns all forms of giving, the mind of wise discernment, the mind of pure merit, the mind of compliant relinquishment, the mind that the Jewel of the Saṃgha is difficult to encounter, the mind of deep faith in the Jewel of the Saṃgha, and the mind that upholds the true teaching. Abiding in superior aspiration and joy, they attain what has never been attained before; they organize a great assembly of giving, producing immeasurable and vast merit, and they have deep faith that the Buddha’s teaching cannot be destroyed.
They dedicate these roots of goodness in this way, namely:”
"May all sentient beings universally enter the Buddha-dharma and remember it without forgetting;
may all sentient beings leave behind the dharmas of the ordinary and ignorant, entering the station of the worthy and noble;
may all sentient beings swiftly enter the ranks of the sages, and be able to guide and inspire others through the successive stages of the Buddha-dharma."
May all sentient beings be honored and revered by the whole world, their words always trusted and believed;
may all sentient beings skillfully enter into the equality of all phenomena, thoroughly understanding that the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm is non-dual;
may all sentient beings be born from the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, surrounded by those who are well-disciplined and harmonious.
May all sentient beings abide in the dharma free from defilement and extinguish all the dust and grime of afflictions;
may all sentient beings fully accomplish the unsurpassed Sangha-jewel, leave the stage of ordinary beings, and enter the assembly of noble sages;
may all sentient beings diligently cultivate wholesome dharmas, attain unimpeded wisdom, and be endowed with the merits of the holy ones.
May all sentient beings attain the mind of wisdom, remaining unattached to the three periods of time and acting with sovereign mastery like kings among all assemblies;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of wisdom and turn the wheel of the true Dharma;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with supernatural powers, able to travel in a single thought-moment to unspeakably unspeakable worlds.
May all sentient beings mount the body of space and possess unimpeded wisdom regarding all worlds;
may all sentient beings universally enter the assemblies of all Buddhas throughout the entire dharma-realm of space and accomplish the foremost practice of the pāramitās;
may all sentient beings attain the supreme wisdom of the buoyant body and be able to pervasively enter all buddha-fields.
May all sentient beings attain boundless and skillful spiritual powers (*ṛddhi*), manifesting their bodies universally in all lands;
may all sentient beings obtain a body that is entirely non-reliant, appearing everywhere like a shadow through the power of spiritual transformations;
may all sentient beings attain inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers, appearing before those who can be transformed according to their needs to teach, transform, and subdue them.
"May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded skillful means to enter the Dharma-realm, traversing the lands of the ten directions in a single thought-moment.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives chariots as a gift to the Sangha;
it is for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to universally mount the pure, unsurpassed vehicle of wisdom, so that they may turn the wheel of unimpeded dharma-wisdom throughout all worlds.
“O Son of the Buddha! When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas give precious chariots as alms to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, they give rise to such thoughts as these:

the thought of a field of merit; the thought of reverence; the thought of an ocean of merit; the thought capable of producing merit and wisdom; the thought born from the power of the Tathāgata’s merits; the thought cultivated over hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas; the thought capable of practicing the bodhisattva path for unspeakable numbers of kalpas; the thought that liberates one from all the fetters of Māra; the thought that destroys all the hosts of Māra’s armies; and the thought whose light of wisdom clearly illuminates the unsurpassed Dharma.”
With all the roots of goodness from this gift of a chariot, he dedicates them in this way:
"May all sentient beings become the foremost field of merit trusted by the world, fully perfecting the unsurpassed *dānapāramitā*;
may all sentient beings leave behind useless speech, always delight in dwelling alone, and have no dualistic thoughts in their minds."
May all sentient beings become the foremost, most pure field of merit, gathering in all beings and causing them to cultivate meritorious deeds;
may all sentient beings become an abyss of wisdom, able to bestow upon sentient beings the immeasurable and innumerable fruits and rewards of roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings abide in unimpeded conduct, fulfilling the pure and supreme field of merit.
May all sentient beings abide in the dharma of non-contention, realizing that all phenomena are without activity and have non-substantiality as their very nature;
may all sentient beings always be able to draw near to the supreme field of merit, fully cultivating and perfecting immeasurable blessings and virtues;
may all sentient beings be able to manifest immeasurable sovereign supernormal powers, gathering in all conscious beings through the pure field of merit.
May all sentient beings be endowed with inexhaustible merit and fields of blessings, able to bestow upon sentient beings the fruit of the supreme vehicle—the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings become true fields of blessings capable of producing such fruits, attaining all-knowledge and an inexhaustible accumulation of merit;
may all sentient beings obtain the dharma for extinguishing transgressions, and be fully able to receive and uphold the meanings of the phrases of the Buddha-dharma never heard before.
May all sentient beings always diligently listen to and receive all Buddha-dharmas, understanding and awakening to them upon hearing them, so that none pass by in vain;
may all sentient beings hear the Buddha-dharma and penetrate it to its ultimate depth, expounding it in accordance with what they have heard;
may all sentient beings believe, understand, and practice the teachings of the Tathāgata, abandoning all ninety-six kinds of heterodox and false views.
May all sentient beings constantly behold the worthy and noble ones, and cause all supreme roots of goodness to increase;
may all sentient beings always have hearts that trust and delight in those who practice wisdom, dwelling together with and rejoicing alongside all the sages and philosophers;
may all sentient beings never find it in vain to hear the names of the Buddhas, and according to what they hear, may they all obtain direct vision of them.
May all sentient beings skillfully discern and understand the true teachings of all Buddhas, and be able to protect and uphold those who maintain the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings always delight in hearing all Buddha-dharmas, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, explaining, and clearly realizing them;
may all sentient beings believe in and understand the true merits of the Buddha's teachings, relinquishing all they possess to offer respectful worship and offerings.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives various chariots to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas;

it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to achieve pure, supreme wisdom and supernormal powers, to practice with diligence and without indolence, and to attain all-knowledge, the powers, and the fearlessnesses.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give various precious chariots to fields of merit, including the poor, the destitute, and the solitary, they relinquish everything requested by them, giving rise to joy in their hearts without weariness or fatigue. Furthermore, they address those people, saying:
‘I should have gone to you to provide offerings and support; I ought not to trouble you by coming such a distance, causing you exhaustion.’”
Having spoken thus, he prostrated himself and inquired after [the king’s] well-being; whatever was required, he gave it all away.
At times he bestowed upon him a mani-jewel chariot filled with the foremost woman-treasure of Jambudvīpa;
at other times he bestowed a gold-adorned chariot filled with the woman-treasures of the human world.
Or again, they may give away exquisite lapis lazuli chariots, filled with the ladies of the inner palace;
or they may give various kinds of wondrous precious chariots, filled with young maidens like the celestial nymphs;
or they may give countless chariots adorned with jewels, filled with precious women who are gentle, intelligent, eloquent, and wise.

Some give away exquisite sandalwood chariots as gifts, or again, they give away precious crystal chariots, all of which are filled with precious women whose countenances are upright and whose physical features are peerless; they are adorned in magnificent garments, bringing joy to all who see them.
Or again, they give away carnelian chariots, upon which consecrated princes sit;
or at times, they give away chariots of solid fragrance, in which all their sons and daughters are seated.
Or they may give chariots adorned with all kinds of jewels, carrying their beloved and virtuous kinsmen and retinues—things difficult to relinquish.
"O Son of the Buddha!
By means of such immeasurable jeweled chariots, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva respectfully bestows them according to what is requested, causing all to fulfill their wishes and be joyful and satisfied."
They dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings mount the vast vehicle of the non-retrogressive, unobstructed wheel and proceed to the inconceivable foot of the Bodhi tree;
may all sentient beings mount the Great Vehicle of Dharma-Wisdom, the pure cause, and throughout all future kalpas, cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva never to regress."
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the non-existence of all phenomena, forever leaving behind all conceptualization and attachment, while constantly cultivating the path to omniscience;
may all sentient beings mount the honest and upright vehicle free from flattery and deception, traveling to the buddha-fields with sovereign ease and without hindrance;
may all sentient beings accord with and dwell securely in the vehicle of omniscience, finding mutual delight in the teachings of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of the pure conduct of bodhisattvas, becoming fully endowed with the ten paths of renunciation and the bliss of samādhi;

may all sentient beings ride upon the four-wheeled vehicle—namely, dwelling in a favorable land, relying on virtuous friends, accumulating supreme merit, and making great vows—thereby fulfilling all the pure brahmacarya of bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings obtain the vehicle of the light of Dharma that universally illumines the ten directions, and cultivate and learn the power of wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings ride the vehicle of the Buddha-dharma and reach the ultimate further shore of all dharmas;
may all sentient beings carry the inconceivable vehicle of manifold blessings and virtues, universally demonstrating the secure and correct path throughout the ten directions;
may all sentient beings ride the vehicle of great giving and abandon the defilement of stinginess.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of pure precepts and uphold boundless pure precepts equal to the dharma-realm;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of patience and always remain free from the turbid mind of anger toward other beings;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of great diligence and non-retrogression, steadfastly cultivate supreme practices, and proceed upon the path to bodhi.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of meditative concentration, swiftly reach the site of enlightenment, and realize the wisdom of Bodhi;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of wisdom and skillful means, manifesting transformation bodies that fill all dharma realms and the spheres of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the Dharma King, achieve fearlessness, and constantly and universally bestow the Dharma of omniscience upon all.
May all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of non-attached wisdom, able to enter everywhere throughout the ten directions without wavering from the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*);
may all sentient beings ride upon the Buddha-vehicle of all Buddhas, manifesting births throughout the lands of the ten directions without ever losing or destroying the path of the Great Vehicle;
may all sentient beings ride upon the supreme jewel-vehicle of omniscience, fulfilling the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva without weariness.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when they give various precious chariots as offerings to fields of merit, even down to the poor, the destitute, and the orphaned;
it is for the purpose of causing sentient beings to possess immeasurable wisdom, to leap for joy, and ultimately to all attain the vehicle of omniscience.

“O Son of the Buddha! When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away the treasure of an elephant, it is of a nature that is well-tamed and obedient; its seven limbs are complete, its age is in full vigor, and its six tusks are pure. The color of its mouth is crimson-red like a lotus flower, and its body is as bright white as the Snowy Mountains. It is adorned with golden banners and covered with jeweled nets; its trunk is embellished with various exquisite gems. Those who see it find delight in gazing upon it, never wearying of it; it can stride ten thousand *li* without ever becoming fatigued.”

Or again, he may give away the treasure of a well-trained horse, endowed with all auspicious marks like a celestial steed, adorned with the light of a wondrous jewel moon-disc, covered above by a net of pure gold bells, walking with steady and upright gait so that the rider is secure and at ease; it travels swiftly as the wind wherever it desires, roaming through the four continents with sovereign freedom and without hindrance.

With these precious elephants and precious horses, the Bodhisattva may support their parents and spiritual friends, or provide for the poor and suffering sentient beings; his mind remains vast and open, giving rise to neither regret nor stinginess, but instead redoubled joy and celebration, increasing his compassion as he cultivates Bodhisattva virtues and purifies the Bodhisattva mind.
He dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings abide in the vehicle of harmony and discipline, and may they increase all Bodhisattva merits."
May all sentient beings attain the skillful vehicle, able to give rise to all Buddha-dharmas accordingly;
may all sentient beings attain the vehicle of faith and understanding, universally illuminating the Tathāgata’s power of unimpeded wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain the vehicle of setting forth, able to universally arouse and bring forth all great vows.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the vehicle of the perfection of equanimity and bring to fulfillment all roots of goodness that are impartial;
may all sentient beings achieve the jewel-vehicle and give birth to the unsurpassed jewel of wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings achieve the vehicle adorned by the practices of Bodhisattvas and cause the flowers of all Bodhisattva samādhis to bloom.
May all sentient beings attain the boundless and swift vehicle, purifying the bodhisattva mind throughout incalculable eons, diligently contemplating and thoroughly penetrating all phenomena;
may all sentient beings accomplish the most supreme and well-tamed Great Vehicle, fully perfecting the bodhisattva stages through skillful means;
may all sentient beings achieve the highest, most expansive, and firm Great Vehicle, universally able to transport all beings so that they all reach the stage of omniscience.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives elephants and horses;
it is for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to mount the vehicle of unimpeded wisdom and to fulfill and reach the ultimate Buddha-vehicle.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives seats as a gift, they may give a lion throne in their own dwelling.
These thrones are high, vast, extraordinary, and exquisitely beautiful; they have feet made of lapis lazuli, are wrought with gold filigree, and are spread with soft, supple garments upon them.”
It was erected with precious banners and perfumed with various exquisite incenses; it was adorned with countless ornaments of diverse jewels;
a golden lattice covered its summit, and as jeweled bells swayed in the wind, they produced sublime sounds;
tens of thousands of rare treasures were arrayed all around for decoration, such that all subjects and citizens gazed upon it with reverence.
The consecrated Great King dwells alone at its summit, proclaiming the transformation of the Dharma, which all the myriad states revere and uphold.
Furthermore, that king adorns his body with exquisite jewels, namely:

The Universal Radiance Jewel, the Sapphire, the Great Sapphire, and the Victorious Treasury Maṇi Jewel were as bright and pure as the sun and as cool as the moon; they were spread out in profusion all around like the multitude of stars, a supreme and peerless adornment.

The Ocean’s Extraordinary Wondrous Jewel and the Ocean’s Firm Banner Jewel possessed marvelous patterns and extraordinary appearances, adorned in various ways, being the most honored and most excellent among the great assembly.
With a crown of Jāmbūnada gold and stainless precious silk upon his head, he received the position of consecration and ruled over Jambudvīpa, possessing immeasurable and great majestic power;
with compassion as his primary principle, he subdued all enemies and adversaries, such that none failed to obey his commands and instructions.

At that time, the Wheel-Turning King took such immeasurable, innumerable, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of seats adorned with jewels and offered them as gifts to the Tathāgata—the foremost field of merit—as well as to all Bodhisattvas, true spiritual friends, the Sangha of noble sages, teachers of the Dharma, parents, kinsmen, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and those who have set out upon the Bodhisattva vehicle;
he also gave them to the stūpas of the Tathāgata, and even to all who were poor and destitute, providing for each according to their needs, giving everything to them.
With these roots of goodness, one dedicates them in this way:
"May all sentient beings sit upon the seat of enlightenment and be able to fully awaken to the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings occupy the seat of mastery, attain mastery over the Dharma, be indestructible by any mountain of adamant, and be able to utterly subdue all demonic armies."
May all sentient beings attain the lion throne of the Buddha’s sovereignty, to be gazed upon by all living beings;
may all sentient beings attain various exquisite jewel-adorned thrones, ineffable beyond description, and through mastery over the Dharma, transform and guide all beings;
may all sentient beings attain the most supreme throne among the three worlds, adorned with vast roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings obtain seats that pervade unspeakably unspeakable worlds, which could not be exhausted even after praising them for incalculable eons;
may all sentient beings obtain the seat of great, profound, and secret merit, their bodies filling the entire Dharma-realm;
may all sentient beings obtain inconceivable seats of various jewels, and according to the sentient beings they have kept in mind through their original vows, extensively provide the gift of Dharma.
May all sentient beings obtain excellent and wondrous seats, manifesting the ineffable supernatural powers of all Buddhas;

may all sentient beings obtain seats made of every kind of jewel, every kind of incense, every kind of flower, every kind of garment, every kind of garland, every kind of mani-jewel, and every kind of inconceivable variety of precious materials such as lapis lazuli; may they obtain seats of immeasurable and ineffable worlds, seats pure with the adornments of all worlds, and adamantine seats, manifesting the majestic power and sovereign mastery of the Tathāgatas and attaining supreme perfect enlightenment.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives precious thrones;
it is for the purpose of causing sentient beings to attain the great seat of awakening that transcends the world, so that they may spontaneously awaken to all Buddha-dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows various precious canopies.

These canopies are extraordinary and fit for the use of the noble; they are adorned with various great jewels and are the foremost among hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of most excellent canopies.

With various jewels for its poles and exquisite nets covering it above, jeweled cords with golden bells hang down all around; mani-garlands are suspended in succession, and as they are stirred by a gentle breeze, their wondrous sounds harmonize perfectly.

It is filled with various treasuries of pearls and jade, adorned with every kind of rare and marvelous treasure; the sublime fragrances of sandalwood and aloeswood permeate everywhere, and the light of Jāmbūnada gold is pure and radiant.
