Thus, with an utterly pure mind, they offered for the Buddha’s sake, as well as for all his stūpas and shrines after his parinirvāṇa, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas of various exquisite jewels and articles for complete adornment. Or, for the sake of the Dharma, they gave to bodhisattvas, spiritual friends, and renowned Dharma masters; or they gave to their parents; or they gave to the Jewel of the Saṅgha; or they offered it to all the Buddhas’ teachings; or they gave to various fields of merit among sentient beings; or they gave to preceptors, teachers, and venerable elders;
or they gave to those who had first resolved upon bodhicitta, even down to all who were poor and destitute. To whoever came seeking, they gave everything.
With these roots of goodness, one dedicates them in this way:
"May all sentient beings diligently cultivate roots of goodness to cover their bodies, and may they always be sheltered by all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings take merit and wisdom as their canopy, forever remaining free from all afflictions of the world."
May all sentient beings be covered by wholesome dharmas, so that they may eliminate the dust, defilements, and feverish afflictions of the world;
may all sentient beings attain the treasury of wisdom, becoming a joy for all to behold, such that no one ever tires of seeing them;
may all sentient beings shelter themselves with the serene white dharmas, and may they all attain the ultimate, indestructible Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings well-shroud their bodies, ultimately attaining the pure Dharma-body of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings become universal canopies, with the wisdom of the ten powers pervading the world;
may all sentient beings attain wondrous wisdom, transcending the three periods of time without any attachment.
May all sentient beings obtain the parasol of being worthy of offerings, become supreme fields of merit, and receive all offerings;
may all sentient beings obtain the most excellent parasol, attain unsurpassed wisdom, and awaken spontaneously.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives the canopy:
so that all sentient beings may obtain the canopy of mastery, being able to uphold all wholesome dharmas;

and so that all sentient beings may, with a single canopy, universally cover all lands within the dharma-realm of empty space, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas without regression.
To cause all sentient beings to be able to adorn all worlds in the ten directions with a single canopy as an offering to the Buddhas;
to cause all sentient beings to offer exquisite banners, pennants, and various precious canopies to all Tathāgatas;
and to cause all sentient beings to obtain universally adorned canopies that cover all Buddha-lands exhaustively without exception.
To cause all sentient beings to obtain the vast canopy and universally cover all beings, so that they may all give rise to faith and understanding toward the Buddha;
to cause all sentient beings to offer unspeakably many wonderful jewel canopies to a single Buddha, doing likewise before each and every unspeakable number of Buddhas;
and to cause all sentient beings to obtain the high and broad canopy of the Buddha’s Bodhi, universally covering all Tathāgatas.

It is to cause all sentient beings to obtain canopies adorned with all kinds of maṇi jewels, canopies adorned with all kinds of precious necklaces, canopies adorned with all kinds of solid fragrances, canopies of various pure jewels, canopies of immeasurable pure jewels, and canopies of vast pure jewels; to have jeweled nets spread over them, with jeweled bells hanging down that sway with the wind and produce subtle, wondrous sounds, universally covering the bodies of all Buddhas throughout the Dharma-realm, the space-realm, and all worlds;
to cause all sentient beings to obtain canopies adorned with unobstructed and unhindered wisdom, universally covering all Tathāgatas;
and furthermore, to desire that all sentient beings attain the foremost wisdom.
Furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the adornments of the Buddha's merits;
furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to give rise to a pure desire and aspiration for the Buddha's merits;
and furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the jewel of a mind of infinite and boundless sovereignty.
Furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to fulfill the sovereign wisdom of all dharmas;
furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to universally cover all things with their roots of goodness;
and furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to achieve the canopy of supreme wisdom.
Furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to achieve the universal canopy of the ten powers;
furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to be able to cover all Buddha-fields throughout the Dharma-realm with a single canopy;
and furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to be sovereign over the Dharma and become Kings of the Dharma.
Furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain a mind of great majesty and sovereign mastery;
furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain vast wisdom that is ever-continuous and never-ending;
and furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain immeasurable merit that universally covers all things and reaches ultimate fulfillment.
Furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to cover their minds with various merits;
furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to cover other sentient beings with a mind of equanimity;
and furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the great wisdom of the canopy of equanimity.
Furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to be endowed with the skillful means of great dedication;
furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to obtain the pure mind of supreme desire and joy;
and furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the pure intention of wholesome desire and joy.
Furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the great dedication that universally covers all sentient beings.
"O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva may give various kinds of sublime banners and streamers."
With various jewels for its shafts, precious silks for its banners, and diverse colored fabrics for its streamers;
with jeweled nets draped overhead, their radiant colors filling all space;
and with precious bells gently swaying, their tones harmonizing in rhythmic accord.
Exquisite and wondrous jewels, shaped like half-moons and with a Jāmbūnada-golden luster surpassing the brilliance of the sun, were all placed atop the banners;
these were further adorned with various wonderful objects manifested according to the karmic fruits of the respective worlds.

In this manner, countless thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of exquisite banners and streamers joined their shadows and linked their splendors, alternating and radiating light; their brilliant, pure majesty pervaded the great earth and filled the ten directions, the void, the Dharma-realm, and all Buddha-fields.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, with a pure mind and resolute faith, uses such immeasurable banners and pennants to make offerings either to all Buddhas currently present and to all stūpas and temples after their parinirvāṇa, or to the Jewel of the Dharma, or to the Jewel of the Saṅgha, or to Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends, or to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, or to the great assemblies, or to individuals;
to all who come seeking, he gives universally to each.
They dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings be able to establish the banners and streamers of all roots of goodness and merit so that they cannot be destroyed;
may all sentient beings establish the banners and streamers of mastery over all dharmas, honoring and delighting in them, and diligently guarding them."
May all sentient beings always transcribe the True Dharma with precious silks, and protect and uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings erect lofty and prominent banners, lighting the lamp of wisdom to universally illuminate the world;
may all sentient beings establish firm and solid banners, fully able to destroy and eliminate all demonic activities.
May all sentient beings establish the banner of the power of wisdom, which cannot be destroyed by any demons;
may all sentient beings attain the Nārāyaṇa banner of great wisdom, crushing and destroying all banners of pride in the world;
may all sentient beings attain the great radiance banner of the sun of wisdom, universally illuminating the dharma-realm with the light of wisdom.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the banner of immeasurable jewel adornments, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions to make offerings to all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain the banner of the Tathāgata, destroying all ninety-six kinds of heterodox views of external paths.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives banners and streamers, for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to attain the pure path of the banner of the profound, lofty, and vast bodhisattva practices, as well as the banner of the supernormal powers of all bodhisattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva opens the treasuries of all kinds of jewels and bestows hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of exquisite treasures upon all infinite sentient beings, giving them according to their wishes without a single thought of stinginess;
he dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, namely:”
"May all sentient beings always behold the Buddha-jewel, abandon ignorance, and practice right mindfulness;
may all sentient beings fully attain the radiance of the Dharma-jewel and protect and uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings be able to fully embrace the Sangha-jewel, providing for and making offerings to them everywhere, never feeling weary or satisfied."
May all sentient beings attain the jewel of the supreme mind of omniscience, purifying their bodhicitta so that it never regresses;
may all sentient beings attain the jewel of wisdom, universally entering into all phenomena with minds free from doubt;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the jewels of all the bodhisattva’s merits, revealing and expounding immeasurable wisdom.
May all sentient beings obtain the jewels of immeasurable, wondrous merit and cultivate the wisdom of the ten powers of perfect enlightenment;
may all sentient beings obtain the jewels of wondrous samādhi and the sixteen kinds of knowledge, ultimately fulfilling vast wisdom;
may all sentient beings achieve the jewel of the foremost field of merit and awaken to the unsurpassed wisdom of the Tathāgata.
"May all sentient beings attain the status of the foremost, unsurpassed lords of jewels, expounding all dharmas with inexhaustible eloquence.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows various jewels, performed so that all sentient beings may fully realize the jewel of supreme wisdom and the jewel of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded, pure eye.
“O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva may practice giving by means of various exquisite ornaments.
That is to say:”
All ornaments that adorn the body render it pure and exquisite, such that nothing is unsuitable.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas regard all sentient beings in the world as their only child, desiring that they all attain the pure adornment of the body, achieve the supreme worldly peace and happiness as well as the bliss of Buddha-wisdom, abide securely in the Buddha-dharma, and benefit all sentient beings.
With hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of such various, exquisite, and wonderful jewel ornaments, they diligently practice giving.
When practicing giving, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings achieve unsurpassed, sublime ornaments, and may humans and devas be adorned with all pure merits and wisdom."
May all sentient beings attain the marks of pure adornment, adorning their bodies with pure merit;
may all sentient beings attain the marks of supreme and exquisite adornment, adorning their bodies with the marks of a hundred blessings;
may all sentient beings attain the marks of unconfused adornment, adorning their bodies with all marks.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through pure and excellent speech, being endowed with various kinds of inexhaustible eloquence;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through the sound of all merits, their voices being so pure that all who hear them rejoice;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through the delightful speech of all Buddhas, causing all beings to rejoice upon hearing the Dharma and to cultivate pure conduct.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of the adornment of the mind, entering deep meditative concentration and universally beholding all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of the adornment of dhāraṇī, illuminating the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of the adornment of wisdom, adorning their minds with the wisdom of the Buddhas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows all kinds of ornaments;

it is for the purpose of causing sentient beings to be fully endowed with all immeasurable Buddha-dharmas, to be perfectly adorned with merit and wisdom, and to forever leave behind all arrogance and negligence.
“O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows upon all sentient beings the crown-jewel of the sovereign king’s consecration and the pearl from his topknot, without any thought of stinginess in his heart. Constantly and diligently practicing, he acts as a great donor, training in the wisdom of giving, increasing the faculty of relinquishment, and becoming skillful in wisdom. His mind is vast as he provides for all, dedicating those roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all sentient beings receive the consecration of all Buddha-dharmas and attain all-knowledge;’”
May all sentient beings be endowed with the uṣṇīṣa, attain supreme wisdom, and reach the other shore;
may all sentient beings universally gather in all beings with the jewel of wondrous wisdom, causing them all to reach the ultimate summit of merit;
may all sentient beings achieve the crest-jewel of wisdom, becoming worthy of the world’s veneration and respect.
May all sentient beings adorn their heads with the crown of wisdom, becoming sovereign kings who have mastery over all dharmas;
may all sentient beings have the bright pearl of wisdom bound upon their crowns, such that no one in any world can see it;
may all sentient beings be worthy of receiving the prostrations of the world, achieving the summit of wisdom and illuminating the Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings wear the crown adorned with the ten powers, their ocean of wisdom-jewels pure and complete;
may all sentient beings reach the summit of the great earth, attain all-knowledge, perfect the ten powers, and shatter the hosts of Māras at the peak of the desire realm;
may all sentient beings become the foremost, unsurpassed sovereign of the summit, attaining the summit of the light of all-knowledge that can never be eclipsed.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives a jeweled crown, in order that sentient beings may obtain the crown of the wondrous maṇi-jewel of wisdom—the foremost knowledge and the most pure state.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees sentient beings dwelling in dark prisons, their bodies bound by handcuffs, fetters, and shackles; restless in rising or sitting; with various sufferings converging upon them; having no relatives or acquaintances; having no refuge and no protector; naked, hungry, and emaciated; and enduring such intense agony that it is difficult to bear—[he acts as follows].”

Having seen this, the Bodhisattva relinquishes all his wealth and treasures, his wife, children, and retinue, as well as his own person, to rescue those sentient beings from prison—just like the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika and the Bodhisattva King Subhacakṣu.
Once they have been delivered, he provides them with whatever they require, universally bestowing it upon them to eliminate their suffering and afflictions and to bring them peace and security.

Thereafter, he grants them the unsurpassed treasure of the Dharma, causing them to abandon negligence, to dwell securely in the roots of goodness, and to remain with minds that never regress within the Buddha’s teaching.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas rescue sentient beings from within prisons, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings ultimately be liberated from the fetters of craving and attachment;..."
May all sentient beings sever the stream of birth and death and ascend to the shore of wisdom;
may all sentient beings eliminate ignorance and cultivate wisdom, attaining liberation from the entanglements of all afflictions;
may all sentient beings extinguish the bonds of the triple world, attain all-knowledge, and achieve ultimate transcendence.
May all sentient beings forever sever all fetters of affliction and reach the further shore of wisdom—the ground free from affliction and free from obstruction;
may all sentient beings be detached from all stirring thoughts, deliberations, and discriminations, and enter the ground of equanimous, immovable wisdom;
may all sentient beings be liberated from the bonds of desire, forever depart from all worldly greed and lust, and remain unstained by attachment within the triple world.
May all sentient beings attain superior aspiration and joy, and may they always receive the teaching of the Dharma-gates from all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain liberation that is without attachment or bondage, with minds as vast as the Dharma-realm and ultimate as space;
may all sentient beings attain the spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas, taming sentient beings in all worlds, causing them to leave the mundane world behind and dwell in the Mahāyāna.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when rescuing sentient beings suffering in prisons, performed in order to cause all sentient beings to universally enter the ground of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees a prisoner bound at five points, undergoing various agonizing torments;

guarded and driven forward, he is being led to his place of execution where his life is about to be severed. He has abandoned all the pleasures of Jambudvīpa, and must bid eternal farewell to his relatives and friends. He is placed upon a high block and butchered with knives, or impaled through his body on wooden stakes, or wrapped in cloth soaked in oil and set ablaze—thus subjected to such diverse and oppressive sufferings.”
Having seen this, the Bodhisattva relinquished his own body to undergo it in their stead;

just as the Bodhisattva Ajita, the Bodhisattva King of Supreme Conduct, and countless other great Bodhisattvas, for the sake of sentient beings, have relinquished their own bodies and lives to endure all manner of suffering and poison.
At that time, the Bodhisattva said to the official:
"I vow to give up my own body to take his life; you may inflict such sufferings upon me as you wish.
Treat this man as you please, and do whatever you intend."
Even if I must undergo suffering many times greater than that, countless as *asaṃkhyeya*, I shall endure it so that they may be liberated.
If, upon seeing them about to be slaughtered, I do not sacrifice my own body and life to ransom them from their suffering, then I cannot be said to abide in the bodhisattva mind.
"Why is this? It is because I have resolved to attain the bodhicitta of omniscience in order to rescue and protect all sentient beings.
"O Son of the Buddha!"
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sacrifices their own body and life to save sentient beings, they dedicate all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain ultimate body and life that is never severed or exhausted, forever free from all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions;
may all sentient beings dwell in reliance upon all Buddhas, receive all-knowledge, and be endowed with the ten powers and the prophecy of enlightenment."
May all sentient beings universally rescue all conscious beings, causing them to be free from fear and forever emerge from the evil realms;
may all sentient beings attain all life and enter the realm of deathless wisdom;
may all sentient beings be forever parted from enemies and adversaries, be free from all calamities and hardships, and always be sustained by the Buddhas and virtuous friends.
May all sentient beings abandon all swords, blades, weapons, and various instruments of evil suffering, and cultivate diverse kinds of pure and wholesome karma;
may all sentient beings be free from all fears and subdue the armies of Māra beneath the Bodhi tree;
may all sentient beings be free from the fear of the great assembly, possess a pure mind regarding the unsurpassed Dharma without dread, and be able to let forth the supreme lion’s roar.
May all sentient beings attain the unobstructed lion-like wisdom and practice right action within all worlds;
may all sentient beings reach the state of fearlessness and constantly remember to rescue and protect those suffering beings.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a bodhisattva-mahāsattva when he personally sacrifices his own life to save those prisoners facing execution;
it is for the purpose of causing sentient beings to leave behind the suffering of birth and death and to attain the supreme, wondrous bliss of the Tathāgata.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-Six;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
The Twenty-fifth Chapter on the Dedication of Merit, Part Five:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
There are Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who give their begging alms-seekers even their skin and topknots, such as the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhin, the Bodhisattva Varabodhi, and countless other Bodhisattvas."
At that time, when the Bodhisattva saw the beggar approaching, his heart was filled with joy, and he said to him:
"If you now require my topknot together with its skin, you may take it from me."
"This uṣṇīṣa of mine is the foremost in Jambudvīpa.

When he spoke these words, his mind was undisturbed; he did not think of other activities, but renounced the world, seeking tranquility, ultimate purity, diligent integrity, and directed himself toward all-knowledge.
He then took a sharp blade and cut off the uṣṇīṣa upon his head, including the skin, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and gave it away with single-minded devotion.
Maintaining right mindfulness of the practices of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time, he gives rise to great joy and increases his superior aspiration.

His mind becomes well-illuminated and liberated regarding all phenomena; he does not grasp at suffering, but understands that painful sensations are signless and unarisen, and that all sensations arise in mutual succession without any permanence.

He thinks: "Therefore, I should practice great relinquishment just as all Bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present do, giving rise to deep faith and joy, seeking omniscience without ever turning back, through the power of spiritual friends rather than by the teaching of others."
When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices such giving, he dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings obtain the invisible crown of the head and achieve the usnīsa of a Bodhisattva, which is like a stūpa;
may all sentient beings obtain hair that is deep blue-black, hair as firm as a vajra, and hair that is fine and soft, capable of extinguishing all the afflictions of sentient beings."
May all sentient beings obtain hair that is lustrous, hair that is dense, and hair that does not encroach upon the temples or forehead;
may all sentient beings obtain hair that is soft, with hair growing completely from the temples and forehead;
may all sentient beings obtain hair marked with the svastika and hair with right-turning spiral curls.
May all sentient beings obtain hair with the marks of a Buddha, forever free from all afflictions, fetters, and habitual tendencies;
may all sentient beings obtain radiant hair, whose light universally illumines the worlds of the ten directions;
may all sentient beings obtain unconfused hair, like that of the Tathāgata, pure, wondrous, and without admixture.
May all sentient beings attain hair that constitutes a reliquary stūpa worthy of offerings, such that those who see it perceive it as the hair of a Buddha;
may all sentient beings obtain the unstained hair of a Tathāgata, forever free from all obscurations, dust, and defilement.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away his topknot along with its skin;

it is for the purpose of causing sentient beings to have tranquil minds, so that they may all attain the perfection of all dhāraṇīs and ultimately realize the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes and the ten powers.
“O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives his eyes as alms to those who come to beg, just as the Bodhisattva Pramudita-caryā, the Bodhisattva Candraprabha-rāja, and other immeasurable Bodhisattvas have practiced in their acts of giving.”

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away their eyes, they give rise to a mind of pure giving of eyes; they give rise to a mind of the pure eye of wisdom; they give rise to a mind that relies upon the light of the Dharma; they give rise to a mind that realizes the unsurpassed path of the Buddha; they resolve upon a mind of vast wisdom for the sake of dedication (pariṇāmanā); they resolve upon a mind of impartial relinquishment equal to that of the bodhisattvas of the three periods of time; they resolve upon a mind of indestructible pure faith arising from the unimpeded eye; and they give rise to a mind of joyful acceptance toward those who beg.

They generate such a mind for the sake of perfecting all supernormal powers, for the sake of producing the Buddha-eye, for the sake of increasing the vast bodhicitta, for the sake of cultivating great compassion, and for the sake of subduing the six sense faculties. Thus they direct their mind toward these dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives his eyes, he generates a mind of love and joy toward the beggar; he establishes assemblies for giving, thereby increasing the power of the Dharma;
he abandons worldly attachment, views, and negligence; he severs the bonds of desire, and cultivates bodhi.
According to their requests, with a mind peaceful and unmoving, he does not oppose their intentions but fulfills them all, while constantly practicing non-dual equanimity in accordance with them.
He dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, saying:
"May all sentient beings obtain the most supreme eye and guide all beings."
May all sentient beings attain the unobstructed eye, opening wide the treasury of wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain the pure fleshly eye, its radiance penetrating so clearly that nothing can obscure it;
may all sentient beings attain the pure celestial eye, seeing entirely the karmic fruits of birth and death for all beings.
May all sentient beings attain the pure Dharma-eye, able to accord with and enter the realm of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings attain the wisdom-eye, abandoning all conceptual discrimination and attachment;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the Buddha-eye, able to awaken to all dharmas.
May all sentient beings achieve the universal eye, reaching the limits of all realms without obstruction;
may all sentient beings achieve the pure eye free from the cataracts of delusion, realizing that the realm of sentient beings is empty and non-existent;
may all sentient beings be endowed with the pure, unobstructed eye, and all attain the ultimate ten powers of the Tathāgata.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives his eyes, for the purpose of enabling sentient beings to attain the pure eye of omniscience.
“O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva can give their ears and noses to those who beg for them, just as did the Bodhisattva King of Supreme Conduct, the Bodhisattva Invincible, and countless other Bodhisattvas.”
At the time of giving, they draw close to those who beg, single-mindedly cultivating all the practices of a bodhisattva;

possessing the lineage of the Buddhas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas, and they mindfully recollect the acts of giving practiced by all bodhisattvas. They constantly and diligently give rise to the bodhi of all Buddhas, purifying their faculties, merits, and wisdom;
and they observe that within the three realms of existence, not a single thing is solid or permanent.
May I always behold all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and may I mindfully recollect all Buddha-dharmas in accordance with them;
may I know that the body is illusory, empty, and non-existent, and have no greed or attachment toward it.
When a bodhisattva gives away their ears and nose in this manner, their mind remains constantly tranquil and they subdue all the sense faculties;
they rescue sentient beings from perilous and evil calamities, cause all wisdom and merit to grow, enter the great ocean of giving,
thoroughly comprehend the meaning of the Dharma, and fully cultivate all paths.
Practicing in reliance upon wisdom, they attain mastery over the Dharma and exchange their non-solid bodies for solid bodies.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away their ears, they dedicate all roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings attain unobstructed ears, universally hearing the sounds of all teachings;
may all sentient beings attain unimpeded ears, being able to fully understand and comprehend all voices;
may all sentient beings attain the ears of a Tathāgata, being all-pervasive in their discernment without any obstruction."
May all sentient beings attain pure ears, such that they do not give rise to discriminatory thoughts based on the sense-base of the ear;
may all sentient beings attain ears free from deafness, causing deluded consciousness never to arise again;
may all sentient beings attain ears that pervade the Dharma-realm, fully knowing the Dharma-sounds of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain unimpeded ears, awakening to all dharmas without obstruction;
may all sentient beings attain indestructible ears, skillfully knowing all treatises such that none can defeat them;
may all sentient beings attain universally hearing ears, vast and pure, becoming kings among all ears.
"May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the divine ear and the Buddha-ear.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives away their ears, performed so that all sentient beings may attain the pure ear.
O Son of the Buddha! When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away their nose, they dedicate the merit in this way:

"May all sentient beings obtain a prominent and straight nose; obtain a nose of the secondary marks (anuvyañjana); obtain a nose of excellent characteristics; obtain a nose that is lovely and delightful; obtain a pure and wondrous nose; obtain a harmonious nose; obtain a lofty and distinguished nose; obtain a nose that subdues enemies; obtain a nose of good vision; and obtain a nose like that of the Tathāgata."

May all sentient beings attain a face free from anger; attain a face of all dharmas; attain an unobstructed face; attain a face of excellent vision; attain a face of conformity; attain a pure face; attain a face free from faults; attain a perfect face like that of a Tathāgata; attain a face that pervades all places; and attain an immeasurably beautiful face.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives their nose,
for the sake of causing sentient beings to ultimately enter into all Buddha-dharmas, for the sake of causing sentient beings to ultimately embrace all Buddha-dharmas,
for the sake of causing sentient beings to ultimately understand all Buddha-dharmas, and for the sake of causing sentient beings—
In order to ultimately uphold all Buddha-dharmas; in order to cause sentient beings to ultimately and constantly behold all Tathāgatas;
in order to cause sentient beings to fully realize and attain the gates of the Buddha-dharmas;

in order to cause sentient beings to ultimately achieve an indestructible mind; and in order to cause sentient beings to be able to clearly illuminate and understand the true [teachings] of all Buddhas...
Because of the Dharma, it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to universally adorn and purify all Buddha-lands,
and for the sake of causing all sentient beings to attain the body of great majestic power of the Tathāgata.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give their ears and noses.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in the stage of firm and stable sovereignty, they are able to give their teeth to all sentient beings, just as in the past the Bodhisattva King Flower-tooth, the Bodhisattva Six-tusked Elephant King, and countless other Bodhisattvas did."
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his teeth as a gift, his mind is pure, rare and difficult to encounter like the udumbara flower.

That is to say: he gives with an inexhaustible mind; he gives with a mind of great faith; he gives with a mind that accomplishes immeasurable renunciation at every step; he gives with a mind that subdues all the sense faculties; he gives with a mind that relinquishes everything; he gives with a mind that aspires for omniscience; he gives with a mind that brings peace and happiness to sentient beings; he gives with a great gift, an ultimate gift, a superior gift, a most excellent gift, and a gift from which he does not harbor resentment even when withholding what is essential to his own body.
At that time, the bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings obtain sharp and white teeth, becoming supreme reliquaries to receive the offerings of devas and humans;
may all sentient beings obtain even and level teeth, like the marks and signs of a Buddha, without gaps or deficiencies."
May all sentient beings attain a subdued mind and skillfully enter the bodhisattva practices of the pāramitās;
may all sentient beings have mouths that are thoroughly pure, with teeth that are bright white and clearly manifest;
may all sentient beings obtain well-remembered and adorned teeth, their mouths being pure and free from any unpleasant appearance.
May all sentient beings achieve and possess forty perfect teeth, constantly emitting various kinds of rare and wondrous fragrances;
may all sentient beings have their minds well-tamed, with teeth as fresh and pure as white lotuses, and the *svastika* pattern of their dental ridges fully perfected;
may all sentient beings have lips that are fresh and clean, and teeth that are pure white, radiating immeasurable light that shines everywhere.

May all sentient beings have teeth that are firm and sharp, such that they consume food without leaving a single grain intact and remain free from attachment to flavors, thereby becoming supreme fields of merit;
may all sentient beings constantly emit radiance from between their teeth, bestowing the foremost prediction of enlightenment upon all bodhisattvas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives his teeth;
it is for the sake of causing sentient beings to possess all-knowledge and to have pure wisdom regarding all phenomena.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When someone comes to beg for the tongue of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, he should address that beggar with a mind of loving-kindness and compassion, using gentle and affectionate speech, just as in the past the Bodhisattva King of Upright Face, the Bodhisattva Non-Retrogression, and countless other Bodhisattvas did.”
O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas take birth within the various realms of existence, there come to them for alms immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings seeking their tongues.

At that time, the Bodhisattva places the person upon a lion throne and, with a mind free from anger, a mind free from malice, a mind free from resentment, a mind of great majesty, a mind born of the lineage of the Buddha, a mind abiding in the dwelling of Bodhisattvas, a mind that is ever unpolluted and undisturbed, a mind abiding in great power, a mind unattached to the body, and a mind unattached to speech, touches both knees to the ground, opens his mouth and extends his tongue to show it to the beggar;
then, with a compassionate heart and gentle words, he addresses him, saying:
"This body of mine now belongs entirely to you."
"You may take my tongue and use it as you please;
let all your aspirations be fully satisfied.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicated his roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings attain a universal tongue, able to proclaim and reveal all modes of speech;
may all sentient beings attain a tongue that covers the face, such that their words are non-dual and entirely true;
may all sentient beings attain a tongue that universally covers all Buddha-lands, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas."
May all sentient beings obtain soft and supple tongues, constantly experiencing exquisite, pure, and superior flavors;
may all sentient beings obtain tongues of eloquence, able to sever the net of doubts of all the world;
may all sentient beings obtain tongues of radiance, able to emit countless billions of rays of light.
May all sentient beings attain the tongue of certainty, expounding all dharmas without exhaustion;
may all sentient beings attain the tongue of universal subduing, skillfully revealing all secret essentials and causing all their speech to be received with faith;
may all sentient beings attain the tongue of universal penetration, skillfully entering the great ocean of all languages.
"May all sentient beings obtain tongues that skillfully expound all dharma-gates, reaching the further shore of all knowledge regarding speech.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his tongue, so that all sentient beings may attain perfect and unimpeded wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his head as an offering to those who come to beg, just as the Bodhisattva Most Supreme Wisdom (Jñānavara), the Great Man King of Kāśi, and other such great Bodhisattvas practiced in their acts of giving.”

It is for the sake of accomplishing the head of supreme wisdom that enters into all phenomena; for the sake of accomplishing the head that realizes great enlightenment to rescue sentient beings; for the sake of fulfilling the foremost head that perceives all phenomena; for the sake of attaining the head of pure wisdom of right view; for the sake of accomplishing the head of non-obstruction; for the sake of realizing the head of the first stage (*bhūmi*); for the sake of seeking the head of the most supreme wisdom in the world; for the sake of becoming the head of pure wisdom whose crown cannot be seen by anyone in the three realms; for the sake of attaining the head of the King of Wisdom who manifests universal reach throughout the ten directions; and for the sake of fulfilling the head of sovereignty over all phenomena that cannot be destroyed.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells securely in these dharmas and practices them with diligent effort, they have already entered the lineage of all Buddhas and learn the Buddhas' practice of giving;
they give rise to pure faith toward all Buddhas and increase their roots of goodness.
Causing all beggars to attain joy and contentment;
their minds becoming pure, they experience immeasurable celebration and delight;
with hearts of pure faith and understanding, they illuminate the Buddha-dharma.
They give rise to the aspiration for awakening and abide in a mind of equanimity;
their faculties are joyful and their merits increase;
they generate wholesome desires and always delight in practicing vast and extensive deeds of giving.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings obtain the head of a Tathāgata and attain the invisible crown;
may they be such that no one can eclipse them anywhere, and may they be the most preeminent leaders within all Buddha-fields."
His hair curls to the right, radiant, pure, and lustrous, adorned with the svastika—a rarity in the world;

he possesses the head of a Buddha, has achieved the head of wisdom, and is the foremost head among all worlds; it is a complete head, a pure head, and the head of perfected wisdom seated at the site of enlightenment.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives away their head;
it is for the sake of causing sentient beings to attain the most supreme dharma and to achieve unsurpassed, great wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give their hands and feet to sentient beings, just as the Bodhisattva Constantly Diligent, the Bodhisattva King Without Sorrow, and countless other bodhisattvas did.”
Among the various realms of existence and diverse places of birth, they give their hands and feet; taking faith as their hand, they initiate acts of benefit.
Moving to and fro and circulating through all states, they diligently cultivate the True Dharma, vowing to obtain the "Precious Hand" to practice giving with that hand.
Their actions are never in vain as they fulfill the Bodhisattva path, always extending their hands to provide vast and universal kindness.
Walking with steady steps, they are courageous and fearless; through the power of pure faith, they possess diligent practice, eliminate the evil realms, and achieve bodhi.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give in this manner, they do so with an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind, opening the gateway to the pure Dharma and entering the ocean of all Buddhas;
they perfect the hand of giving to provide for all throughout the ten directions;
and by the power of their vows, they sustain the path to omniscience, abiding in a mind that is ultimately free from defilement.
The Dharma-body and Wisdom-body are uninterrupted and indestructible; no demonic activities can shake them.
Relying upon spiritual friends to fortify their resolve, they practice the perfection of generosity together with all bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas seek all-knowledge for the sake of all sentient beings and give their hands and feet, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings be endowed with supernormal powers and all obtain precious hands;..."
Having obtained these jewel-hands, they each came to revere one another, perceiving them as fields of merit, and offered various kinds of jewels to one another;

furthermore, they made offerings of many jewels to all Buddhas, raising clouds of exquisite gems that pervaded all Buddha-lands, causing all sentient beings to give rise to mutual compassion and refrain from harming one another;
they traveled through all Buddha-fields, dwelling securely in fearlessness, naturally becoming fully endowed with ultimate supernatural powers.

Furthermore, may they all obtain the jewel-hand, the flower-hand, the incense-hand, the robe-hand, the parasol-hand, the garland-hand, the powdered-incense-hand, the ornament-hand, the boundless-hand, the immeasurable-hand, and the universal-hand;

having obtained these hands, may they constantly and diligently travel to all Buddha-lands through their supernormal powers, able to stroke all Buddha-worlds with a single hand, hold all sentient beings with their sovereign hands, obtain exquisite palms that emit immeasurable light, and be able to universally cover all sentient beings with a single hand, thereby perfecting the Tathāgata’s marks of webbed fingers and copper-colored nails.
At that time, the Bodhisattva, with his hand of great vows, universally covered all sentient beings, saying:

"May all sentient beings always aspire to seek unsurpassed bodhi with joy; may they give birth to the great ocean of all merits; may they feel unflagging joy upon seeing those who come to beg; and may they enter the ocean of the Buddha-dharma and share in the Buddha's roots of goodness."
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give their hands and feet.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas destroy their bodies and draw blood to give as alms to sentient beings, such as the Bodhisattva Dharmākara, the Bodhisattva Rājasuta, and countless other Bodhisattvas."

When giving his own body and blood amidst the various realms of existence, he gives rise to the mind that accomplishes all-knowledge; he gives rise to the mind that yearns for and reveres great enlightenment; he gives rise to the mind that delights in practicing the bodhisattva path; he gives rise to the mind that does not grasp at painful sensations; he gives rise to the mind that delights in seeing beggars; he gives rise to the mind that does not disdain those who come to beg; he gives rise to the mind that advances toward all bodhisattva paths; he gives rise to the mind that guards all bodhisattva renunciation; he gives rise to the mind that increases and expands the bodhisattva’s virtuous giving; and he gives rise to the non-retrogressive mind, the tireless mind, and the mind free from attachment to self.
He dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, saying: "May all sentient beings fully accomplish the dharma-body and the wisdom-body."
May all sentient beings attain bodies free from weariness and fatigue, as indestructible as vajra;
may all sentient beings attain unbreakable bodies that cannot be harmed;
may all sentient beings attain transformation-bodies that appear universally throughout the world without end.
May all sentient beings attain a body that is lovely and delightful, pure, wondrous, and firm;
may all sentient beings attain a body born of the dharma-realm, identical to that of the Tathāgata in being without dependence;
may all sentient beings attain a body like the radiance of exquisite jewels, which no person in the world can outshine or obscure.
May all sentient beings attain the body of the treasury of wisdom, obtaining mastery within the realm of immortality;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the ocean of jewels, such that all who see them receive benefit and none pass by in vain;
may all sentient beings attain the body of empty space, remaining undefiled by the afflictions and sufferings of the world.

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when giving his own blood, dedicates the roots of goodness with a Mahāyāna mind, a pure mind, a vast mind, a joyful mind, a celebratory mind, a glad mind, a superior mind, a peaceful mind, and an untroubled mind.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone begging for the marrow and flesh of his body, he speaks with joyful and gentle words, saying to the beggar:
‘The marrow and flesh of my body are yours to take and use as you wish.’”
"Like the Bodhisattva Ānāthapiṇḍada, the Bodhisattva Sarvadarśin-rāja, and other immeasurable bodhisattvas,
when they give their marrow and flesh to beggars within the various realms of existence and diverse places of birth, their joy is vast and their resolve to give increases;
they cultivate roots of goodness together with all bodhisattvas, leave behind worldly dust and defilement, and attain profound aspiration and delight."
They universally bestow their own bodies with minds that never exhaust;
they are fully endowed with immeasurable and vast roots of goodness, gathering all the jewels of sublime merit, practicing according to the Bodhisattva Dharma without weariness;
their hearts always delight in the merit of giving, providing for all without exception, their minds free from any regret.
Thoroughly observing that all phenomena lack intrinsic substance because they arise from conditions, one does not crave the act of giving nor its karmic retribution;
rather, one gives impartially according to whatever circumstances are encountered.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives in this manner, all Buddhas appear before them, for they perceive them as fathers and receive their protective mindfulness;
all sentient beings appear before them, so that they may universally cause them to abide securely in the pure Dharma;
and all worlds appear before them, so that they may adorn and purify all Buddha-lands.
All sentient beings appear before them, because they universally rescue and protect them with a heart of great compassion;
all Buddha-ways appear before them, because they joyfully contemplate the ten powers of the Tathāgata;
and all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present appear before them, because they together fulfill all roots of goodness.
All fearlessnesses are fully manifested, for they are able to let out the supreme lion’s roar;
all three periods of time are fully manifested, for they attain the wisdom of equality and universally observe them;
all worlds are fully manifested, for they give rise to vast vows to cultivate bodhi throughout all future kalpas.
All the tireless practices of all bodhisattvas manifest before them, because they have given rise to an immeasurable and vast mind.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives their marrow and flesh, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings attain a vajra-body that cannot be destroyed;
may all sentient beings attain a firm and dense body that is forever without deficiency or diminution;
may all sentient beings attain a mind-born body, like the body of a Buddha, adorned and pure."
May all sentient beings attain bodies adorned with the marks of a hundred merits, graced by the thirty-two primary characteristics;
may all sentient beings attain bodies beautifully adorned with the eighty secondary signs, endowed with the ten powers, and indestructible;
may all sentient beings attain the body of a Tathāgata, ultimately pure and immeasurable.
May all sentient beings attain a firm and solid body, indestructible by any maras or adversaries;
may all sentient beings attain a body of one mark, sharing the same physical characteristics as the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
may all sentient beings attain an unobstructed body, pervading the realm of empty space with the pure Dharma-body.
"May all sentient beings attain the body of the treasury of bodhi, which is universally capable of containing all worlds.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva seeks to give his marrow and flesh for the sake of attaining all-knowledge, in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the ultimately pure and immeasurable body of a Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives with the mind to those who come as supplicants, just like the Bodhisattva Arhatyāna, the Bodhisattva Anāvaraṇarāja, and other immeasurable great Bodhisattvas.”

When giving from one’s own mind to a beggar, one trains in the mind of sovereign giving, cultivates the mind of universal giving, practices the mind of the *dānapāramitā*, and accomplishes the mind of the *dānapāramitā*. One trains in the mind of the generosity of all bodhisattvas, the inexhaustible mind of relinquishing everything, the mind habituated to giving everything, the mind that bears the burden of the practice of giving of all bodhisattvas, the mind of right mindfulness with all Buddhas appearing before one, and the uninterrupted mind of making offerings to all who come as beggars.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice giving in this manner, their minds are pure. For the sake of liberating all sentient beings; for the sake of attaining the state of enlightenment endowed with the ten powers; for the sake of practicing in reliance upon their great vows; for the sake of dwelling securely in the Bodhisattva path; for the sake of accomplishing omniscience; and so as not to abandon their original vows, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain the Vajra-treasury mind, which cannot be destroyed by any of the Vajra-rimmed mountains or similar obstacles;
may all sentient beings attain the Vajra-realm mind adorned with the svastika mark, which is unshakable."
He attained a mind that is beyond fear; he attained a mind that constantly benefits the world without ever being exhausted;
he attained a mind that is a treasury of wisdom, a banner of great valor; he attained a mind as firm and solid as the banner of Nārāyaṇa;
he attained a mind as inexhaustible as the ocean of sentient beings; he attained a mind that is an indestructible treasury of Nārāyaṇa.
They extinguish all demonic activities and the minds of the hosts of māra armies;
they attain a mind free from fear, a mind of great majestic power, a mind of constant diligence, a mind of great valor,
a mind free from alarm or dread, a mind clad in the adamantine armor, the supreme mind of all bodhisattvas, and the attainment of buddhahood.

The mind of the light of the Dharma-bodhi attains the mind that sits beneath the Bodhi tree, abides securely in the true Dharma of all Buddhas, is free from all delusions, and accomplishes all-knowledge; it attains the mind that achieves the ten powers.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the mind of giving;
it is for the purpose of causing sentient beings not to be defiled by the world, so that they may fully possess the mind of the Tathāgata’s ten powers.
“O Son of the Buddha!

If there are those who beg for the intestines, kidneys, liver, or lungs, a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives them all away, just as the Bodhisattva Sudatta, the Bodhisattva Mārajit-viśeṣarāja, and countless other great Bodhisattvas did.”
When practicing this giving, upon seeing a beggar approach, his heart rejoices and he gazes upon them with eyes of affection;
seeking enlightenment, he bestows everything according to their needs, without any regret arising in his mind.
One contemplates this body as lacking any solidity, thinking:
"I should give this to others in order to obtain a solid body.
Furthermore, one reflects that this body will soon perish and decay, causing revulsion in those who see it, and being devoured by foxes, wolves, and hungry dogs.
This body is impermanent; it must eventually be abandoned and consumed by others, devoid of any sensation or cognition.
Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva contemplates in this way, he knows that the body is impermanent and the ultimate in defilement. He attains great joy through his realization of the Dharma and gazes with reverence upon the beggar who approaches, regarding him as a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) come to protect him. Whatever is requested, he bestows it all without exception, exchanging this non-solid body for a solid one.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives in this manner, he dedicates all his roots of goodness, saying:
"May all sentient beings attain the body of the treasury of wisdom, pure both internally and externally;..."
May all sentient beings attain a body that is a treasury of merit, capable of universally upholding all vows for omniscience;
may all sentient beings attain a most sublime body, inwardly imbued with wondrous fragrance and outwardly radiating light;
may all sentient beings attain a body whose abdomen is not prominent, being straight from top to bottom with limbs and joints in perfect proportion.
May all sentient beings attain a body of wisdom, nourished and sustained by the flavor of the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings attain an inexhaustible body, practicing and dwelling securely in the profound nature of phenomena;
may all sentient beings attain a body that is a pure treasury of dhāraṇīs, manifesting all dharmas through sublime eloquence.
May all sentient beings attain a pure body, such that both body and mind are purified within and without;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the Tathāgata’s wisdom of profound contemplation, filled with wisdom and raining down the great rain of Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain a body of inner tranquility, acting externally as kings of the banner of wisdom for all beings, emitting great radiance that universally illumines everything.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving their intestines, kidneys, liver, and lungs;
it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to become pure both internally and externally, so that they may all dwell securely in unimpeded wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who give their limbs, joints, and bones to beggars, such as Dharmagarbha Bodhisattva, Prabhāsarāja Bodhisattva, and countless other great Bodhisattvas.”

When giving his own body parts, limbs, joints, and bones, upon seeing a beggar approach, he gives rise to a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of joy, a mind of pure faith, a mind of peace and happiness, a mind of valor, a mind of compassion, a mind free from obstruction, a mind of purity, and a mind intent on granting whatever is requested.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives their own bones, they dedicate the roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain a body like a transformation-body (nirmāṇakāya), never again receiving a body of bone, flesh, and blood;
may all sentient beings attain a vajra-body that is indestructible and invincible."
May all sentient beings attain the perfectly fulfilled Dharma-body of omniscience, born within the realm that is unbound, unattached, and unconditioned;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the power of wisdom, with all faculties perfected, uninterrupted and indestructible;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the power of the Dharma, possessing mastery over the power of wisdom and reaching the further shore.
May all sentient beings attain a firm and solid body, which is steadfast and real, never subject to decay or destruction;
may all sentient beings attain an adaptable body, teaching and transforming all sentient beings according to their needs;
may all sentient beings attain a body perfumed by wisdom, endowed with the great strength of Nārāyaṇa’s limbs and joints.
May all sentient beings attain a body of firm continuity that is never severed, forever free from all exhaustion and fatigue;
may all sentient beings attain a body of great power that dwells securely, fully endowed with the great strength of diligence;
may all sentient beings attain the universal, equal Dharma-body of the world, abiding in the realm of immeasurable, supreme wisdom.
May all sentient beings attain bodies of merit and power, benefiting all who behold them and remaining far removed from all evils;
may all sentient beings attain bodies that dwell nowhere, fully endowed with the wisdom of non-reliance and non-attachment;
may all sentient beings attain bodies embraced by the Buddhas, constantly sustained by the protective empowerment of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain bodies that universally benefit all beings, and may they be able to enter all realms of existence;
may all sentient beings attain bodies that manifest everywhere, universally illuminating and manifesting all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain bodies endowed with perfect diligence, single-mindedly and assiduously cultivating the wisdom-practices of the Mahāyāna.
May all sentient beings attain a pure body free from pride, arrogance, and conceit, with wisdom ever-abiding and undisturbed;
may all sentient beings attain a body of firm practice, accomplishing the deeds of universal wisdom of the Mahāyāna;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the Buddha-family, forever departing from all birth and death in the world.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives his own bones, performed for the sake of causing sentient beings to attain all-knowledge and achieve eternal purity.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone approach, holding a sharp blade in their hand and begging for the skin of their body, they give rise to joy and their faculties become delighted, as if someone had bestowed upon them a profound kindness. They welcome and receive the person, spread out a seat and invite them to sit, bowing with reverence and forming this thought:”
"Those who come as beggars are very difficult to encounter; they have come to seek from me for the sake of fulfilling my vow for all-knowledge and to bring me benefit.
With a joyful and serene countenance, he spoke to them, saying:
"I now relinquish this body entirely; whatever skin you require, take and use it as you please."
It was just like in the past, when the Bodhisattva Viśuddhagarbha, the Bodhisattva Mṛgarājakaṇṭhapāla, and countless other great Bodhisattvas were exactly the same, without any difference.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings obtain subtle skin, as pure in appearance as that of the Tathāgata, such that those who see it never tire;
may all sentient beings obtain indestructible skin, like adamant, such that nothing can destroy it."
May all sentient beings obtain golden skin, as pure, bright, and immaculate as the most exquisite Jāmbūnada gold;
may all sentient beings obtain skin of immeasurable colors, manifesting pure hues according to their mental inclinations;
may all sentient beings obtain skin of pure and wondrous color, fully endowed with the excellent, gentle, and pure physical marks of a Tathāgata.
May all sentient beings obtain the foremost skin of color, naturally pure, with a physical appearance beyond compare;
may all sentient beings achieve the pure skin of color of a Tathāgata, adorning themselves with the various marks and signs of excellence;
may all sentient beings obtain a wondrous skin of color that emits great radiance, universally illuminating all things.
May all sentient beings obtain skin like a net of light, like a lofty banner in the world, emitting ineffably perfect radiance;
may all sentient beings obtain lustrous skin, such that all physical forms are entirely pure.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives his own skin;
it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to attain all adorned and purified buddha-fields and to be fully endowed with the great merits of the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give their fingers and toes to those who beg for them, just as the Bodhisattva Firm Diligence, the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Jambudvīpa, and countless other great bodhisattvas have done.”

At that time, the bodhisattva’s countenance was serene and joyful, his mind peaceful and virtuous, free from all inversion. Riding upon the Mahāyāna, he sought neither beautiful desires nor the pursuit of fame; he gave rise solely to the vast resolve of a bodhisattva, remained far removed from all defilements such as stinginess and envy, and directed himself exclusively toward the unsurpassed, wondrous Dharma of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice giving in this manner, they gather all roots of goodness and dedicate them entirely, saying:
"May all sentient beings obtain long, slender fingers, no different from those of the Buddhas;..."
May all sentient beings obtain fingers that are plump and rounded, with the upper and lower parts in perfect proportion;
may all sentient beings obtain fingers with nails of red copper, their nails swelling upward, pure and translucent;
may all sentient beings obtain the fingers of the supreme Great Being of All-Knowledge, capable of grasping and upholding all dharmas.
May all sentient beings obtain fingers with the secondary marks, fully endowed with the ten powers;
may all sentient beings obtain the fingers of a Great Man, slender, rounded, and perfectly even;
may all sentient beings obtain fingers with the wheel-mark, with joints that are complete and lines that swirl to the right.
May all sentient beings attain fingers that curl in a clockwise swastika like a lotus flower, adorned with the marks and signs resulting from the karma of the ten powers;
may all sentient beings attain fingers that are treasuries of light, emitting great radiance that illuminates unspeakably many Buddha-worlds;
may all sentient beings attain well-arranged fingers, skillfully distributed and complete with webbed membranes.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives his fingers, performed so that all sentient beings may attain purity of mind.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva requests the Dharma, if someone should say:
‘If you can give me your fingernails along with the flesh attached to them, I shall give you the Dharma.’”
The Bodhisattva replied:
"Simply give me the Dharma;
as for my flesh and nails, you may take and use them as you please."

Just as the Bodhisattva Dharmaviśeṣarāja, the Bodhisattva Akṣaya, and countless other great Bodhisattvas, for the sake of seeking the Dharma, desiring to reveal, demonstrate, and expound the True Dharma to benefit sentient beings and cause them all to attain fulfillment, gave their flesh-and-nail-clad hands and feet to those who begged for them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings obtain the copper-colored nails of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain glossy nails, adorned with the secondary marks of excellence."
May all sentient beings obtain radiant and pure nails, supreme in their penetrating clarity;
may all sentient beings obtain the nails of omniscience, endowed with the marks of a great man;
may all sentient beings obtain incomparable nails, remaining unstained by and unattached to any world.
May all sentient beings obtain wonderfully adorned nails, whose radiance universally illumines all worlds;
may all sentient beings obtain indestructible nails, pure and without flaw;
may all sentient beings obtain nails with the characteristics of skillful means for entering all Buddha-dharmas, such that their vast wisdom is entirely purified.
May all sentient beings obtain well-formed nails, for the fruits of the Bodhisattva’s karma are entirely pure and sublime;
may all sentient beings obtain the nails of the Great Teacher of All-Knowledge, which emit a treasury of wondrous light in immeasurable colors.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away his flesh and fingernails for the sake of seeking the Dharma, in order to cause sentient beings to be fully endowed with the unimpeded power of the fingernails of all-knowledge of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva seeks the treasury of the Buddha-dharma, they revere and respect it, conceiving the thought that it is difficult to encounter.
If someone capable of explaining it comes and says to them:”
"If you can cast yourself into a fire-pit seven fathoms deep, I shall bestow the Dharma upon you.
Upon hearing this, the Bodhisattva leaped for joy and reflected:

"For the sake of the Dharma, I should endure immeasurable suffering even while dwelling for a long time in all the evil realms, such as the Avīci Hell; how much more so when I can hear the Dharma simply by entering a fire-pit in the human world?"
"How marvelous!
The True Dharma is so easy to encounter that one need not undergo the immeasurable agonies of the hells; it is sufficient merely to enter the fire-pit to hear it.
Just speak for me, and I shall enter the fire-pit."
"Just as the Bodhisattva Dharmarājaparyeṣin and the Bodhisattva Vajracintin entered a pit of fire for the sake of seeking the Dharma,
so too at that time the Bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
'May all sentient beings abide in the Dharma of omniscience wherein the Buddhas abide, and never regress from unexcelled bodhi.'"
May all sentient beings be free from all perils and hardships, and receive the peace and happiness of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain a mind of fearlessness and be free from all terrors;
may all sentient beings always joyfully seek the Dharma, be fully endowed with bliss, and be adorned by all dharmas.
May all sentient beings be free from all evil realms and extinguish the blazing fires of the three poisons;
may all sentient beings always attain peace and happiness, being fully endowed with the supreme and wondrous joys of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings attain the bodhisattva mind and forever leave behind the fires of greed, anger, and ignorance.
May all sentient beings fully attain the bliss of all bodhisattva samādhis, universally behold all Buddhas, and have their hearts filled with great joy;
may all sentient beings skillfully expound the True Dharma, reach its ultimate realization, and never forget it;
may all sentient beings be endowed with the wondrous bliss of bodhisattva supernormal powers and ultimately abide in the knowledge of all modes.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva throws himself into a pit of fire for the sake of seeking the true Dharma;
it is done so that sentient beings may be freed from obstructive karma and all attain the fire of perfect wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!

In order to seek the True Dharma, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas analyze and expound it, opening the path of the Bodhisattva, showing the way to Bodhi, and proceeding toward unexcelled wisdom. They diligently cultivate the ten powers, broaden the mind of omniscience, and attain the dharma of unimpeded wisdom, causing sentient beings to dwell in purity within the realm of the Bodhisattva.”

When diligently cultivating great wisdom to protect the Buddha’s bodhi, one undergoes immeasurable suffering and affliction with the body, just as did the Bodhisattva Seeking the Good Dharma, the Bodhisattva Valiant King, and countless other great bodhisattvas.

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, they undergo immeasurable suffering, even taking upon themselves all the afflictions that such extremely wicked people— who slander the true Dharma, are shrouded by evil karma,
and are possessed by the works of Māra— must endure, all for the purpose of seeking the Dharma.
They dedicate these roots of goodness in this way, saying:
"May all sentient beings forever be free from the oppression of all suffering and affliction, and may they achieve peace, happiness, mastery, and supernormal powers;
may all sentient beings forever be free from all forms of suffering and attain all forms of happiness."
May all sentient beings forever extinguish the aggregate of suffering and attain illumination of their present bodies, constantly experiencing peace and happiness;
may all sentient beings transcend the prison of suffering and accomplish wise conduct;
may all sentient beings behold the path of tranquility and leave behind all evil destinies.
May all sentient beings attain the joy of the Dharma and forever sever all suffering;
may all sentient beings eternally uproot all suffering, cherish one another with loving-kindness, and harbor no intent to harm;
may all sentient beings attain the bliss of all Buddhas and depart from the suffering of birth and death.
May all sentient beings achieve pure and incomparable peace and happiness, such that no suffering or affliction can cause them harm;
may all sentient beings attain all supreme joys, ultimately becoming fully endowed with the unimpeded bliss of the Buddhas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva undergoes various sufferings for the sake of seeking the Dharma;
it is because they desire to rescue and protect all sentient beings, enabling them to leave behind perilous difficulties and dwell in the state of omniscience, which is unobstructed liberation.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva occupies the throne of a king and seeks the True Dharma, they conceive the thought that even a single phrase, a single word, a single sentence, or a single meaning is difficult to obtain. Consequently, they are able to completely relinquish everything within the realm—whether near or far—including kingdoms, cities, towns, the populace, treasuries, gardens, ponds, houses, groves, flowers, and fruits; even all rare and wondrous objects, palaces, towers, wives, children, retinues, and the royal throne itself—they are able to give them all away.

Seeking the firm dharma within that which is not firm, they diligently pursue the path of the Buddhas' unimpeded liberation and ultimate purity of all-knowledge for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, just as did the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Bodhisattva Jayottararāja, and countless other great Bodhisattvas.
Diligently seeking the True Dharma, even to the smallest extent, one prostrates with the five limbs upon the ground for the sake of a single word;
with right mindfulness of all the Buddha-dharmas of the three periods of time, one delights in their cultivation;
never craving fame or gain, one renounces all worldly positions of sovereign kingship to seek the state of a Buddha, the Sovereign Dharma-King.
Their minds have no attachment to worldly pleasures, nourishing their hearts instead with supramundane dharmas;
they are forever free from all worldly conceptual proliferation, abiding in the non-proliferated dharma of all Buddhas.
At that time, the bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings always delight in giving and relinquish everything;
may all sentient beings be able to give away all they possess without any regret in their hearts."
May all sentient beings always seek the true Dharma, not begrudging their bodies, lives, or the necessities of life;
may all sentient beings fully obtain the benefits of the Dharma and be able to sever all doubts and delusions of all sentient beings;
may all sentient beings attain the aspiration for wholesome dharmas and their minds always rejoice in the true Dharma of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings, for the sake of seeking the Buddha-dharma, be able to relinquish their bodies, lives, and royal thrones, and with a great mind cultivate unexcelled bodhi;
may all sentient beings honor the True Dharma, always deeply loving and delighting in it, and not begrudging their bodies or lives;
may all sentient beings protect and uphold the extremely rare Dharma of all Buddhas, and constantly and diligently practice it.
May all sentient beings attain the light of the Bodhi of all Buddhas, accomplish the practices of Bodhi, and awaken through their own power rather than depending on others;
may all sentient beings always be able to contemplate all Buddha-dharmas, extract the arrows of doubt, and attain peace and stability of mind.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes kingdoms and cities in search of the true Dharma;
it is for the sake of enabling sentient beings to perfect their knowledge and vision, so that they may always abide in the path of peace and security.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva acts as a great king, he attains mastery over the Dharma and universally issues commands, causing the cessation of the karma of killing;
he causes all slaughter within the cities, towns, and villages of Jambudvīpa to be strictly prohibited and forbidden.”

Toward those without feet, those with two feet, those with four feet, and those with many feet—among all such diverse classes of beings—he universally bestows fearlessness with a heart free from deceit or plunder. He extensively cultivates all the practices of a bodhisattva, overseeing all things with benevolence and never inflicting harm or affliction. Having generated the wondrous jewel-like mind, he brings peace and security to sentient beings;
he establishes deep resolve and joy in the presence of all Buddhas, constantly abiding himself in the three types of pure precepts, and likewise causes all sentient beings to abide therein.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva establishes all sentient beings in the five precepts so that they forever sever the karma of killing;
he dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings resolve to attain the bodhicitta, be fully endowed with wisdom, and eternally preserve their life-span without end."
May all sentient beings abide for immeasurable kalpas, making offerings to all Buddhas, reverently and diligently practicing, and further increasing their lifespans;
may all sentient beings fully cultivate their practice, transcend the laws of old age and death, and remain unhindered in life by any calamities or poisons;
may all sentient beings fully achieve a body free from illness and affliction, attain mastery over their lifespan, and be able to dwell therein according to their will.
May all sentient beings attain inexhaustible life, abiding in the bodhisattva practices throughout the exhaustion of future kalpas to teach, transform, and subdue all sentient beings;
may all sentient beings become gateways for longevity, wherein the roots of goodness of the ten powers increase;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with roots of goodness, attain inexhaustible life, and bring their great vows to fulfillment.
May all sentient beings behold all Buddhas, making offerings and serving them, dwelling in inexhaustible lifespans, and cultivating and accumulating roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings, under the Tathāgatas, skillfully train in what is to be learned, attaining the joy of the noble Dharma and inexhaustible life;
may all sentient beings attain freedom from aging and illness, abide eternally in the life-faculty, and with courageous diligence enter the wisdom of the Buddha.

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, abiding in the three clusters of pure precepts, permanently severs the roots of unwholesome karma such as killing and dedicates [the merit] so that sentient beings may attain the perfect wisdom of the ten powers of a Buddha.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees sentient beings harboring cruelty in their hearts, who mutilate the male organs of humans and livestock, causing their bodies to be deficient and making them undergo various agonizing torments;
having seen these things, he gives rise to great compassion and pities and rescues them, causing all the people of Jambudvīpa to abandon such karma.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva said to that person:
"For what purpose have you committed such evil karma?
I possess treasuries numbering hundreds of thousands of millions of billions, filled with every kind of object of enjoyment; whatever you require, I shall provide it all to you."
