From what you have done, various sins arise; I now exhort you not to do such a thing.
Your actions are contrary to the Way; even if you were to obtain something from them, what use would it be?
"To harm others for one’s own benefit—such a thing can never happen.
Such evil conduct and all unwholesome dharmas are not praised by any Tathāgata.
Having spoken these words, he immediately gave away all his articles of pleasure and enjoyment as alms.
Furthermore, with kind speech, he expounded the sublime Dharma to them to bring them joy.
That is to say:

he showed them the Dharma of tranquility so that they might believe and accept it; he caused them to eliminate unwholesome states and cultivate pure deeds; and he inspired them to give rise to mutual compassion and refrain from harming one another.
Having heard this, that person forever abandons evil deeds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings possess the form of a great man and achieve the Tathāgata’s mark of the horse's organ being concealed within a sheath."
May all sentient beings possess the form of a man, and with courageous resolve, cultivate all pure conduct (*brahmacarya*);
may all sentient beings possess heroic power, always acting as leaders, abiding in unimpeded wisdom, and never regressing;
may all sentient beings fully attain the body of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa*), forever leave behind lustful thoughts, and remain free from all defilement and attachment.
May all sentient beings fully accomplish the qualities of a true son of noble family, with wisdom increasing and praised by all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings universally possess the power of a Great Being, always able to cultivate the roots of goodness of the Ten Powers;
may all sentient beings never lose their male form, constantly cultivating the unprecedented dharmas of merit and wisdom.

May all sentient beings be without attachment or bondage amidst the five desires, attain liberation of mind, grow weary of and depart from the three realms of existence, and abide in the bodhisattva practice;
may all sentient beings achieve the status of the foremost wise man, be universally honored and trusted, and submit to their transformative influence;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the wisdom of the bodhisattva-man and before long accomplish the state of the Unsurpassed Great Hero.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas prohibit and eliminate all that destroys the male form;

it is for the sake of causing sentient beings to possess the male form, so that they may all be able to protect themselves as virtuous men, be born into the families of sages and saints, be fully endowed with wisdom, and constantly and diligently practice the superior conduct of men. Possessing the utility of men, they are skillfully able to manifest the seven paths of men, and are fully endowed with the lineage of the Buddhas’ virtuous men, the correct teaching of men, the valor of men, the diligence of men, the wisdom of men, and the purity of men, universally causing all sentient beings to ultimately attain these in their entirety.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Seven;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
The Sixth Part of the Twenty-fifth Chapter on the Dedication of Merit:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sees a Tathāgata appear in the world and proclaim the True Dharma, [he hears] that [the Buddha], with a great voice, universally proclaims to all:..."
“Tathāgata has appeared in the world!
Tathāgata has appeared in the world!
By causing all sentient beings to hear the name of the Buddha, they shall abandon all conceit and frivolous proliferation.

Furthermore, he exhorted them again, causing them to see the Buddha quickly, to bring the Buddha to mind, to turn toward the Buddha, to take the Buddha as their object of focus, to contemplate the Buddha, and to praise the Buddha;
he further explained to them extensively that a Buddha is difficult to encounter, appearing only once in ten million billion kalpas.
By means of this, sentient beings are able to see the Buddha, giving rise to pure faith, leaping with joy and delight, and honoring him with offerings;
furthermore, hearing the names of various Buddhas in the presence of the Buddha, they encounter yet more countless Buddhas, planting roots of goodness and cultivating them to growth.
At that time, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of sentient beings, by virtue of seeing the Buddha, all attained pure and ultimate subduing.
Those sentient beings conceived the thought of the Bodhisattva as the supreme spiritual friend;
through the Bodhisattva, they accomplished the Buddha-dharma and, with the roots of goodness planted over countless eons, universally performed the work of a Buddha throughout the world.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas reveal themselves to sentient beings so that they may see the Buddhas, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings, without waiting for exhortation or inducement, go of their own accord to see the Buddhas, serve and make offerings to them, and cause them all to rejoice;..."
May all sentient beings always delight in seeing the Buddha, never abandoning this aspiration;
may all sentient beings constantly and diligently cultivate vast wisdom, upholding the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings awaken to the Buddha-dharma upon hearing any sound, and practice the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons.
May all sentient beings abide in right mindfulness, constantly beholding the appearance of Buddhas with the eye of wisdom;
may all sentient beings not dwell on other activities, but always remember seeing the Buddha and diligently cultivate the ten powers;
may all sentient beings see all Buddhas in all places, thoroughly understanding that the Tathāgata pervades the realm of empty space.
May all sentient beings fully attain the sovereign body of a Buddha, universally realizing enlightenment and preaching the Dharma throughout the ten directions;
may all sentient beings encounter spiritual friends, constantly hear the Buddha-dharma, and attain indestructible faith in all Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings be able to praise the appearance of all Buddhas, causing all who behold them to attain universal purity.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when praising the appearance of Buddhas in the world;
it is for the sake of causing sentient beings to see all Buddhas, to make offerings to them, and to serve them, so that they may attain ultimate purity in the unsurpassed Dharma.
“O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva relinquishes the great earth, either giving it to the Buddhas to construct monasteries,
or giving it to Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends to use as they please;”
They may give to the Saṃgha to provide them with dwellings;

they may give to their parents, or to other individuals, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and various fields of merit; or they may give to all who are poor, destitute, and unprotected, as well as to the other four assemblies, providing for them according to their needs so that they lack nothing;
or they may give to construct and establish stūpas and temples for the Tathāgata.
Within all such places, he provides them with every necessity and utensil for their livelihood, allowing them to use them as they please without any fear.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows land in any location, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the ground of pure omniscience and reach the further shore of all the practices of Samantabhadra."
May all sentient beings attain the stage of dhāraṇī, correctly receiving and upholding all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings abide in the power of maintenance, always able to protect all the teachings of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain a mind like the earth, maintaining constant purity of intention toward all beings, free from any evil thoughts.
May all sentient beings uphold the seeds of all Buddhas and achieve the successive stages of the bodhisattva grounds without interruption;
may all sentient beings universally serve as a place of peace and security for all, bringing them all to subdual and causing them to abide in the path of purity;
may all sentient beings, like all Tathāgatas, benefit the world and cause all to diligently cultivate and dwell securely in the power of the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings be universally beloved by the world, and may they all be established in the unsurpassed bliss of the Buddha;
may all sentient beings attain skillful means and abide within the various powers and fearlessnesses of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain earth-like wisdom and practice all Buddha-dharmas with sovereign mastery.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows the great earth, for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to attain the ultimate, pure ground of all Tathāgatas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives servants as gifts to make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and true spiritual friends; or he gives them to the Jewel of the Sangha, or presents them to his parents as supreme fields of merit;
or again, he bestows them upon sentient beings suffering from illness, so that they may lack for nothing and thus preserve their lives.”
Furthermore, they may give to the poor, the orphaned, the destitute, and all others who have no one to care for them;

or, for the sake of protecting the stūpas and temples of the Tathāgata, or for the purpose of copying and upholding the true Dharma of the Buddhas, they provide hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of servants at all times.

All those servants and attendants were intelligent and skillful; by nature they were self-disciplined and compliant, always diligent and energetic, free from indolence. They possessed a mind of integrity, a mind of peace and happiness, a mind of benefit, a mind of benevolence, a mind of reverence, a mind free from resentment, and a mind free from enmity. They were able to act for the benefit of others according to what was appropriate for the customs and regions of those who received them;

furthermore, all were produced through the power of the Bodhisattva’s pure karma, being thoroughly proficient in talents, arts, crafts, and mathematics, and well able to serve and please their hearts.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain a mind of harmony and discipline, cultivating roots of goodness in the presence of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings accord with and make offerings to all Buddhas, and be able to hear and receive all that the Buddhas teach."
May all sentient beings be taken into the care of the Buddhas, constantly contemplating the Tathāgata with no other thoughts;
may all sentient beings never sever the lineage of the Buddhas, diligently cultivating all roots of goodness that accord with the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings always and diligently make offerings to all Buddhas, never letting a single moment pass in vain.
May all sentient beings uphold the wondrous meanings of all Buddhas, possess pure speech, and wander with fearlessness;
may all sentient beings always delight in seeing the Buddhas, never feeling satiated, and not begrudging their own bodies or lives for the sake of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings behold the Buddhas with minds free from attachment, transcending worldly dependencies.
May all sentient beings take refuge solely in the Buddha, forever departing from all false objects of refuge;
may all sentient beings follow the path of the Buddha, their minds always joyfully contemplating the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives servants and attendants;
it is for the purpose of causing sentient beings to distance themselves from dust and defilement, to purify the stage of a Buddha, and to be able to manifest the sovereign body of a Tathāgata.

“O Son of the Buddha! When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives his own body to those who come to beg, at the time of giving, he generates a mind of humility; he generates a mind like the earth; he generates a mind that endures all sufferings without wavering; he generates a mind that serves sentient beings without weariness; he generates a mind that dedicates all roots of goodness to all sentient beings, just as a compassionate mother does; and he generates a mind of universal forgiveness toward all kinds of injuries and oppressions from foolish, treacherous, and extremely wicked sentient beings. Thus, abiding in roots of goodness, he diligently attends to their needs.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way, saying:

"May all sentient beings never lack anything according to their needs; may they cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva without interruption; may they not abandon any of the benefits and purposes of a Bodhisattva; may they dwell well on the path practiced by Bodhisattvas; may they thoroughly understand the equal nature of phenomena (dharmatā) of Bodhisattvas; may they be numbered among the lineage of the Tathāgatas; may they abide in truthful speech and maintain the conduct of a Bodhisattva; may they cause all worlds to attain the pure Buddha-dharma, gaining deep faith and understanding, and realizing the ultimate state of the Dharma;
and may they cause all sentient beings to give birth to pure and superior roots of goodness, to dwell in great merit, and to be endowed with all-knowledge."

Furthermore, by means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always be able to make offerings to all Buddhas, understand all dharmas, and receive, uphold, read, and recite them without forgetting, losing, destroying, or dispersing them; may their minds be well-tamed, taming those that are untamed, and train them through the dharma of tranquility.
May those sentient beings abide in such matters before all Buddhas.
Furthermore, by means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings become the foremost stūpas, worthy of receiving various offerings from the world;
may all sentient beings become the supreme field of merit, attain the wisdom of the Buddha, and bring enlightenment to all.
May all sentient beings become supreme recipients, universally able to benefit all living beings;
may all sentient beings achieve the highest welfare and benefit, enabling them to be fully endowed with all roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings become the foremost field of merit for giving, enabling them to obtain immeasurable rewards of fortune.
May all sentient beings attain liberation from within the triple world;
may all sentient beings become supreme guides, able to show the world the path of reality as it is;
may all sentient beings attain sublime dhāraṇī, fully upholding the true Dharma of all Buddhas.
"May all sentient beings realize the immeasurable, supreme Dharma-realm and be fully endowed with the unimpeded right path that is like space.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving their own bodies, in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the body of immeasurable wisdom worthy of offerings.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas hear the Dharma, they rejoice with gladness and give rise to pure faith. They are able to make offerings to all Buddhas with their very bodies; they delight in and believe in the unsurpassed jewel of the Dharma; they conceive the thought of their parents toward all Buddhas;

and they read, recite, receive, and uphold the unobstructed path of the Dharma, universally entering into countless nayutas of dharmas, the jewel of great wisdom, and the gates of all roots of goodness.”
Their minds constantly recollect immeasurable Buddhas, entering the realm of the Buddhas and deeply penetrating their profound principles;
they are able, with the subtle and secret Brahma-voice of the Tathāgata, to raise the clouds of the Buddha-dharma and rain down the rain of the Buddha-dharma with courageous mastery;

they are able to analytically explain the foremost ground of those possessing all-knowledge (sarvajña), fully accomplishing the vehicle of omniscience (sarvajñatā-yāna), and perfecting all faculties through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of great dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas hear such a Dharma from the presence of the Buddhas, they experience immeasurable joy and dwell securely in the True Dharma;
they sever their own doubts and delusions, and likewise cause others to sever theirs.
The mind is perpetually serene and expansive, with merit brought to full completion;
endowed with perfected roots of goodness, the intention flows in constant succession;
benefiting sentient beings, the mind is never exhausted.
Attaining supreme wisdom, they become Vajragarbha;
drawing near to all Buddhas, they purify all Buddha-fields, and constantly and diligently make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates their roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings attain the most supreme body, fully perfected and embraced by all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings always remain near the Buddhas, dwelling in reliance upon them, constantly beholding and revering them, never being separated;
may all sentient beings attain a pure and indestructible body, endowed with all merits and wisdom."
May all sentient beings constantly and diligently make offerings to all Buddhas, practicing the ultimate Brahma-conduct of non-apprehension;
may all sentient beings attain a selfless body, free from "I" and "mine";
may all sentient beings be able to manifest bodies throughout the lands of the ten directions, appearing like reflections without coming or going.
May all sentient beings attain bodies of mastery, traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions without self or grasping;
may all sentient beings be born from the body of the Buddha, dwelling in the unsurpassed household of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the power of Dharma, possessing the great strength of forbearance that none can destroy.
May all sentient beings attain the incomparable body and accomplish the pure Dharma-body of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings accomplish the body of supramundane merit and be born into the pure Dharma-realm of non-apprehension.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a bodhisattva mahāsattva through offering his own body to the Buddhas, in order to cause sentient beings to dwell forever in the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
“O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives his own body as a gift to all sentient beings, desiring to cause them universally to accomplish and recollect roots of goodness. The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva vows that his own body shall be a great bright lamp, able to illuminate all sentient beings everywhere;
he becomes a source of all articles of enjoyment, able to universally sustain all sentient beings.”
They are a treasury of the sublime Dharma, universally able to sustain all sentient beings;
they are pure radiance, universally able to enlighten and awaken all sentient beings;
they are the light and shadow of the world, universally causing all sentient beings to always behold them.
Acting as the causal condition for roots of goodness, may they cause all sentient beings to always encounter them;
acting as true spiritual friends, may they cause all sentient beings to receive their instruction and guidance;
acting as a level path, may they cause all sentient beings to be able to tread upon it.
To be unsurpassed and fully endowed with peace and happiness, causing all sentient beings to leave suffering behind and attain purity;
to be a bright and pure sun, universally bringing equal benefit to the world.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings always draw near to the Buddhas and enter the ground of the Buddha's wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain conforming wisdom and abide in unsurpassed enlightenment."
May all sentient beings always dwell in the assemblies of the Buddhas, their minds well-tamed;
may all sentient beings act according to the rules, possessing the majestic deportment of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings fully attain nirvana and deeply understand the meaning of the Dharma.
May all sentient beings possess the practice of contentment and be born into the family of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings abandon the desires of ignorance and abide in the aspiration and joy of the Buddha;
may all sentient beings give birth to supreme roots of goodness and sit beneath the Bodhi tree.
"May all sentient beings slay the thieves of affliction and be free from thoughts of enmity and harm;
may all sentient beings fully possess and uphold all Buddha-dharmas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives his own body as a gift to all sentient beings.
"Because they desire to benefit all sentient beings and cause them to attain the unsurpassed state of peace and security.
'O Son of the Buddha!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas personally serve the Buddhas with their own bodies; in the presence of these Buddhas, they contemplate repaying their profound kindness as they would think of their own parents, and they give rise to deep faith and joy toward the Tathāgatas."
With a pure mind, they protect the Bodhi of the Buddhas and abide in all Buddha-dharmas;
free from worldly conceptions, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas;
following in the footsteps of all Buddhas, they leave the realm of Māra behind.
Thoroughly comprehending all that the Buddhas practice and becoming a vessel for all the Buddha-dharmas,
the bodhisattva at that time dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain a pure mind and adorn themselves with the jewel of omniscience;..."
May all sentient beings abide in sublime self-mastery and remain far removed from all unwholesome karma;
may all sentient beings obtain indestructible and steadfast retinues, and be universally able to uphold the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings become disciples of the Buddha and reach the stage of Bodhisattva consecration.
May all sentient beings always be sustained by the Buddhas and forever leave behind all unwholesome dharmas;
may all sentient beings accord with the Buddhas and practice the most supreme dharmas of the Bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings enter the realm of the Buddhas and all receive the prediction of omniscience.
May all sentient beings be entirely equal to all Tathāgatas, possessing sovereign mastery over all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings be gathered and sustained by all Buddhas, always able to practice deeds free from grasping and attachment;
may all sentient beings always serve as the foremost attendants of all Buddhas, cultivating the practices of wisdom in the presence of every Buddha.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas serve and attend upon all Buddhas:

desiring to realize the bodhi of all Buddhas; desiring to rescue and protect all sentient beings; desiring to transcend all three realms; desiring to achieve a mind free from harm and affliction; desiring to attain immeasurable and vast bodhi; desiring to achieve the wisdom that illuminates the Buddha-dharma; desiring to be constantly sustained by the grace of all Buddhas; desiring to receive the protection and support of all Buddhas; desiring to have faith and understanding in all Buddha-dharmas; desiring to achieve roots of goodness equal to those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time; and desiring to fulfill a mind free of regret in order to realize all the dharmas of the Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away all things within his realm, even including his royal throne;
regarding all worldly affairs, his mind attains mastery, being unattached, unfettered, and free from any lingering attachment.”
They distance themselves from evil karma and bring benefit to sentient beings;
they do not cling to the fruits of karma, take no pleasure in worldly dharmas, and no longer crave or become defiled by any place of birth.
Although they dwell in the world, they are not born from within it.
The mind does not cling to the phenomena of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases; the mind has no dependence or dwelling upon internal or external phenomena;
it never forgets the various practices of bodhisattvas and is never separated from spiritual friends;
it upholds the vast vows and practices of bodhisattvas and always delights in serving all virtuous companions.
At that time, the bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings become great Dharma Kings, attaining mastery over the Dharma and reaching the other shore;
may all sentient beings become Buddhas, Kings of Dharma, who utterly destroy all enemies that are the afflictions."
May all sentient beings abide in the royal seat of the Buddha, attain the wisdom of the Tathāgata, and expound the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings abide in the realm of the Buddha and be able to turn the unsurpassed, sovereign wheel of Dharma;
may all sentient beings be born into the family of the Tathāgata, attain mastery over the Dharma, protect and uphold the lineage of the Buddhas, and ensure it never ceases.
May all sentient beings reveal and teach the true Dharma of the immeasurable Dharma Kings, and may they bring to fruition the state of infinite great Bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings abide in the pure Dharma-realm, become great Dharma Kings, and manifest the appearance of Buddhas in succession without interruption;
may all sentient beings act as kings of wisdom throughout all worlds, guiding and transforming all living beings without ever ceasing for even a moment.
May all sentient beings universally act as donors of the Dharma for all sentient beings throughout the realms of the Dharma and the realm of empty space, enabling them all to abide in the Mahāyāna;
may all sentient beings become sovereigns perfected in all virtues, equal to the roots of goodness of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when giving away a royal throne;
it is for the purpose of causing all those sentient beings to ultimately abide in a state of peace and security.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for the royal capital, magnificent great cities, or all the customs duties collected at the passes and fortifications, they give them all away without any sense of stinginess;
they focus solely on Bodhi, making great vows, abiding in great loving-kindness, practicing great compassion, and with a joyful mind, they benefit all sentient beings.”
With vast wisdom they understand the profound Dharma and abide in the equal dharmatā of all Buddhas;

they practice giving for the sake of seeking all-knowledge, because they give rise to deep delight in the dharma of mastery, because they seek to realize sovereign wisdom, because they purely cultivate all merits, because they dwell in firm and vast wisdom, because they extensively gather all roots of goodness, because they practice the vows of all Buddha-dharmas, because they naturally awaken to the dharma of great wisdom, because they abide in the bodhicitta without regression, and because they cultivate all bodhisattva practices and vows to reach the ultimate limit of all-knowledge.
They dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings be able to adorn and purify immeasurable buddha-lands, offering them to the Buddhas as their dwelling places;
may all sentient beings always delight in residing in araṇya hermitages, remaining tranquil and unmoving."
May all sentient beings never rely upon royal capitals or villages, but delight in tranquility and forever attain ultimate realization;
may all sentient beings never take pleasure in or become attached to any worldly realm, always delighting in remaining far removed from worldly discourse;
may all sentient beings be free from a greedy mind, giving away all they possess without any regret in their hearts.
May all sentient beings attain the mind of renunciation and abandon all worldly household affairs;
may all sentient beings attain a mind free from stinginess and constantly practice generous giving;
may all sentient beings attain a mind free from attachment and leave behind the ways of domestic life.
May all sentient beings be free from all suffering, and may all calamities, misfortunes, and fears be eliminated;
may all sentient beings adorn and purify all worlds throughout the ten directions and offer them to all Buddhas.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when giving away a royal capital, performed for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to fully adorn and purify all buddha-fields.
“O Son of the Buddha!

All the members of the inner palace retinue and the assembly of female attendants belonging to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva are of upright countenance and fully endowed with talent; their speech, laughter, song, and dance are all exquisite and skillful. Adorned with various garments and diverse flowers and perfumes, those who behold them rejoice, never wearying of the sight.”

Thus, there were hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of such precious women, all born from the virtuous karma of the Bodhisattva; they acted with sovereign ease according to his will, showing respectful compliance without fail.

He gave them all in charity to those who came to beg, yet within this he harbored no heart of affection, no heart of longing, no heart of attachment, no heart of bondage, no heart of grasping, no heart of greedy defilement, no heart of discrimination, no heart of pursuit, no heart of seizing signs, and no heart of desire.

At that time, the Bodhisattva contemplates all roots of goodness and dedicates them so that all sentient beings may attain liberation; he dedicates them to attaining the joy of the Buddha-dharma; he dedicates them to attaining firmness within what is not firm; he dedicates them to attaining the indestructible mind of adamantine wisdom; he dedicates them to entering the Buddha’s place of enlightenment; he dedicates them to reaching the other shore; he dedicates them to attaining the unsurpassed bodhicitta; he dedicates them to being able to penetrate and understand all phenomena through wisdom; he dedicates them to giving birth to all roots of goodness; and he dedicates them to entering the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in such dharmas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas;
they increase the pure and supreme causes of all Buddhas, and give birth to the most excellent path to omniscience.
They enter deeply into the vast wisdom-activities of bodhisattvas, extinguishing all worldly defilements and afflictions, and are always able to make offerings to the field of merit.

For the sake of all sentient beings, they proclaim the sublime Dharma, skillfully establishing them so that they may practice all pure deeds, while constantly and diligently gathering all roots of goodness.
At that time, the bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings always attain the retinue of immeasurable samādhis, with the supreme concentrations of bodhisattvas continuing without interruption;
may all sentient beings always delight in seeing the Buddhas and fully enter the samādhi of the adornments of all Buddhas."
May all sentient beings achieve the inconceivable samādhis of bodhisattvas and sport with mastery in immeasurable supernormal powers;
may all sentient beings enter the samādhi of suchness and attain an indestructible mind;
may all sentient beings fully obtain the profound samādhis of bodhisattvas and attain mastery over all meditative concentrations.
May all sentient beings attain a mind of liberation and accomplish the retinue of all samādhis;
may all sentient beings become skillful in all various samādhis and be able to fully grasp the characteristics of all samādhis;
may all sentient beings attain the samādhi of supreme wisdom and be universally able to study all gateways of samādhi.
May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded samādhi, entering deep meditative concentration never to fall back;
may all sentient beings attain the non-attached samādhi, their minds always in right reception, grasping neither of the two dharmas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away all members of their inner palace and retinue;
it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to attain indestructible and pure retinues,
and for the sake of causing all sentient beings to attain the retinues of bodhisattvas.
It is because they wish to cause all sentient beings to fully attain the fulfillment of the Buddha-dharma;
it is because they wish to cause all sentient beings to fulfill the power of all-knowledge;
it is because they wish to cause all sentient beings to realize unsurpassed wisdom.
It is because he desires to cause all sentient beings to obtain compliant retinues;
it is because he desires to cause all sentient beings to dwell together with fellow practitioners of the same resolve;
and it is because he desires to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with all merit and wisdom.
It is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to accomplish pure roots of goodness;
it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to obtain a harmonious retinue;
it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to accomplish the pure Dharma-body of the Tathāgata.
It is because they desire to cause all sentient beings to achieve sequential and rational eloquence, so as to skillfully expound the inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas;
it is because they desire to cause all sentient beings to forever abandon all mundane roots of goodness and collectively cultivate supramundane, pure roots of goodness;
it is because they desire to cause all sentient beings to fulfill their pure karma and accomplish all pure dharmas.
It is because they desire to cause all Buddha-dharmas to manifest before all sentient beings, universally adorning and purifying them with the light of the Dharma.
"O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to give away their beloved wife and children, just as did Prince Sudāna, the Bodhisattva King Pradyota, and countless other Bodhisattvas in the past."
At that time, the bodhisattva, mounting the mind of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), practices all forms of giving and purely cultivates the bodhisattva’s path of generosity.
With a pure mind and without any regret, he relinquishes all that is cherished in order to seek omniscience;

he causes all sentient beings to purify their deep aspirations and resolve, to accomplish the practices for enlightenment, to contemplate the bodhisattva path, to recollect the enlightenment of the Buddha, and to abide in the lineage of the Buddhas.
Once the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has accomplished such a mind of giving, they resolutely seek the body of a Tathāgata;
they observe their own body as being dependent upon all others and lacking autonomy,
and they universally embrace all sentient beings with that body, just as a jewel island provides for all, bringing those who are unsatisfied to fulfillment.
In this way, the Bodhisattva protects and attends to sentient beings, desiring to make his own person the foremost stupa so that all may universally give rise to joy;
desiring to give birth to a mind of equanimity toward the world;
and desiring to act as a pool of coolness for sentient beings.
They desire to bestow all peace and happiness upon sentient beings;
they desire to act as great benefactors for sentient beings;
possessing mastery of wisdom, they thoroughly understand the practices performed by Bodhisattvas and are thus able to adorn themselves with such great vows.
Advancing toward omniscience, may they vow to become unsurpassed fields of merit for wisdom;
universally mindful of sentient beings, may they constantly follow and protect them while being able to accomplish their own benefit;
may the light of their wisdom shine universally throughout the world, as they always diligently recollect the bodhisattva’s mind of giving and ever delight in observing the realm of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give away their wives and children with a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they dedicate the roots of goodness thus gathered in this way:
"May all sentient beings abide in the Bodhi of the Buddhas, manifest transformation bodies, pervade the entire Dharma-realm, and turn the wheel of non-retrogression."
May all sentient beings attain an unattached body, traversing all Buddha-fields through the power of their vows;
may all sentient beings abandon hearts of love and hatred, severing the fetters of greed and anger;
may all sentient beings become children of the Buddhas, following the conduct of the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings, in the presence of all Buddhas, give rise to a mind as their own that cannot be thwarted or destroyed;
may all sentient beings always be children of the Buddha, born through transformation from the Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain the ultimate state and achieve the sovereign wisdom of the Tathāgata.
May all sentient beings realize the Bodhi of the Buddhas and be forever free from afflictions;
may all sentient beings be able to fully expound the path to the Bodhi of the Buddhas and always delight in practicing the unsurpassed gift of Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain a mind of right concentration, unshakable by any conditions.

"May all sentient beings sit beneath the Bodhi tree, attain supreme perfect enlightenment, and reveal and teach the immeasurable sons and daughters of noble family who are born through transformation from the Dharma.

This is the dedication of the roots of goodness from a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s giving away of wife and children, performed so that all sentient beings may fully realize unimpeded liberation and non-attached wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva adorns his residence and all his requisites, and whenever there is one who begs, he gives everything away, practicing the dharma of giving;

he has no attachment to his home, remains far removed from all domestic thoughts and reflections, feels aversion toward household affairs and the means of livelihood, is neither greedy nor savoring of them, and his mind is free from fetters and attachments.”
Knowing that the household life is easily ruined, his mind is constantly weary of it and seeks to renounce it; he finds no delight whatsoever within it.

Desiring only to leave the home-life to cultivate the bodhisattva practices and adorn himself with the teachings of all Buddhas, he relinquishes everything without any regret in his heart, and is always praised by all Buddhas.
Regarding their dwellings and wealth, whatever they possessed at any given place, they bestowed as gifts entirely, with no lingering attachment in their hearts;
upon seeing those who came to beg, their minds were filled with joy and celebration.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings abandon wives and children and achieve the supreme bliss of renunciation;
may all sentient beings be liberated from the bonds of the household, enter the homeless state, and practice the holy life within the teachings of all Buddhas."
May all sentient beings abandon the defilement of stinginess, delight in all forms of giving, and have minds that never regress;
may all sentient beings forever leave behind the ways of householders, possess few desires and be content, and refrain from hoarding or accumulating;
may all sentient beings depart from the mundane home and dwell in the family of the Tathāgata.
May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded Dharma and extinguish all paths of obstruction;
may all sentient beings be free from attachment to family and kin, so that though they appear to live at home, their minds remain without clinging;
may all sentient beings be skillful in transformation and guidance, not departing from the ways of the household while expounding the wisdom of the Buddha.
May all sentient beings, while physically remaining in the household life, always abide with their minds in accord with the Buddha’s wisdom;
may all sentient beings, while on the ground of householders, dwell upon the ground of the Buddhas, universally causing immeasurable and boundless sentient beings to give rise to a heart of joy.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away their home and dwelling, performed in order to cause sentient beings to accomplish the various practices, vows, supernormal powers, and wisdom of a bodhisattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives various gardens, terraces, pavilions, and places of play, joy, and adornment, he forms this thought:
‘I shall create excellent gardens for all sentient beings; I shall [create them] for all sentient beings.’”
I shall manifest the joy of the Dharma; I shall bestow upon all sentient beings a mind of gladness;
I shall demonstrate to all sentient beings boundless bliss and joy; I shall open the gateway to the pure Dharma for all sentient beings;
I shall cause all sentient beings to give rise to a heart of jubilation; I shall cause all sentient beings...
Upon attaining the Bodhi of a Buddha, I shall cause all sentient beings to fulfill their great vows;
I shall be like a compassionate father to all sentient beings; I shall cause all sentient beings to observe with wisdom;
I shall bestow upon all sentient beings the necessities of life; and I shall [act] toward all sentient beings...
"Just like a compassionate mother, they nurture and grow all roots of goodness and great vows.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this way regarding all roots of goodness, they do not give rise to weariness or aversion toward evil sentient beings, nor do they mistakenly develop a mind of abandonment."

Even if all sentient beings throughout the world were entirely ungrateful, the Bodhisattva would harbor no resentment toward them from the outset, nor would they give rise to even a single thought of seeking recompense; they desire only to extinguish their immeasurable suffering and affliction.
Toward all worlds, their mind is like empty space, free from any defilement or attachment, as they universally contemplate the true mark of all phenomena.
They give rise to great vows to extinguish the suffering of sentient beings, never wearying of or abandoning their Mahāyāna aspiration.
They extinguish all views and cultivate the impartial practices and vows of all bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
Having observed in this way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva gathers all roots of goodness and dedicates them entirely, as follows:
"May all sentient beings, in every thought-moment, give rise to immeasurable wholesome dharmas and achieve the mind that is like a supreme garden;
may all sentient beings attain the unshakable dharma and see all Buddhas, causing them all to rejoice;
may all sentient beings delight in the garden of the Dharma and obtain the wondrous bliss of the gardens of all Buddha-fields."
May all sentient beings attain a pure and wondrous mind, always beholding the gardens of the Tathāgata’s supernatural powers;
may all sentient beings attain the playful joy of the Buddhas, always skillfully sporting within the realm of wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain the joy of playful sport, universally proceeding to the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment in all Buddha-fields.
May all sentient beings achieve the playful liberation of Bodhisattvas, performing the practices of a Bodhisattva throughout all future eons with minds free from weariness;
may all sentient beings see all Buddhas filling the Dharma-realm, giving rise to the vast mind and dwelling in the groves of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings be able to travel everywhere to all Buddha-fields, making offerings to all Buddhas within each and every field.
"May all sentient beings attain a mind of wholesome aspiration, purifying and adorning all Buddha-fields.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness from a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s gift of all gardens, groves, terraces, and pavilions;
it is for the purpose of enabling sentient beings to behold all Buddhas and to sport within all the Buddha-gardens.
“O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva performs hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of immeasurable and innumerable vast assemblies of giving; all are pure and approved by all Buddhas, never causing harm or affliction to even a single sentient being;
they cause all beings everywhere to remain far removed from all evils, purify the three paths of action, and achieve wisdom.”

They open and establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeyas of pure realms; they accumulate immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeyas of excellent articles for sustaining life; they give rise to the bodhicitta, which is most difficult to attain, and practice boundless giving, causing all sentient beings to abide in the path of purity, which is good in the beginning, middle, and end, so that they may produce pure faith and understanding.

According to the inclinations of the hearts of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of sentient beings, they cause them all to rejoice; with great compassion, they rescue and protect all, serving and making offerings to the Buddhas of the three periods of time;

desiring to bring to fulfillment the seed of all Buddhas, they practice giving with a mind free from regret in the midst of it, increasing the root of faith, perfecting supreme conduct, and advancing in the *dānapāramitā* with every thought.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings resolve upon the Great Vehicle and fully accomplish the giving of the Mahāyāna;

may all sentient beings be able to practice the great assembly giving, exhaustive giving, virtuous giving, most excellent giving, unsurpassed giving, most unsurpassed giving, unequaled giving, giving that transcends all worlds, and the giving praised by all Buddhas."

May all sentient beings become the foremost donors, rescuing and liberating beings from all evil realms, causing them all to enter the path of unimpeded wisdom; may they cultivate impartial vows and roots of goodness according to reality, attaining non-discriminative realization of the wisdom of their own sphere;

may all sentient beings dwell securely in the wisdom of tranquil meditative concentrations, enter the path of immortality, perfect all supernatural powers and wisdom, and with courageous diligence, fulfill the stages, adorn the Buddha-dharma, reach the other shore, and never regress;

may all sentient beings establish great assemblies of giving, never becoming weary, providing for and saving sentient beings without rest, until they ultimately attain the unsurpassed knowledge of all modes.
May all sentient beings constantly and diligently plant all roots of goodness, reaching the other shore of immeasurable merit;

may all sentient beings always be praised by all Buddhas, universally acting as great donors for the world, their merits complete, filling the Dharma-realm, illuminating the ten directions, and bestowing unsurpassed bliss;
may all sentient beings establish great assemblies of giving, extensively gather roots of goodness, equally embrace all beings, and reach the other shore.
May all sentient beings become supreme givers, universally establishing all beings in the foremost vehicle;
may all sentient beings practice timely giving, forever remaining free from untimely giving, and bring great giving to ultimate completion;
may all sentient beings achieve virtuous giving and reach the far shore of the great giving of the Buddha, the Great Man.
May all sentient beings ultimately and constantly practice the great adornment of giving, taking all Buddhas as their teachers, drawing near to them all, and offering great worship;
may all sentient beings abide in pure giving, accumulate immeasurable merit equal to the Dharma-realm, and reach the other shore;
may all sentient beings become great donors within all worlds, vowing to deliver all classes of beings, and dwell in the stage of the Tathāgata.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when establishing great assemblies of giving; it is for the sake of causing sentient beings to practice the unsurpassed giving, the ultimate giving of a Buddha, the perfected giving, the indestructible giving, the giving that makes offerings to all Buddhas, the giving free from anger and resentment, the giving that rescues sentient beings, the giving that accomplishes all-knowledge, the giving that constantly beholds all Buddhas, the giving of excellent diligence, and the vast giving that accomplishes all bodhisattva merits and the wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give away all things necessary for life, their minds are free from greed or attachment, and they do not seek karmic retribution;
they harbor no expectations for worldly wealth or pleasure, remain free from deluded thoughts, and skillfully contemplate the Dharma.”
Desiring to benefit all sentient beings, they thoroughly contemplate the true nature of all phenomena;

according to the various differences among sentient beings and their respective needs and aspirations, they provide immeasurable requisites for life, all of which are exquisitely adorned and of superior quality;
they practice boundless giving, universal giving, and the giving of both internal and external things.
When practicing this giving, one increases the power of aspiration and joy, attains great merit, and accomplishes the jewel of the mind;
one is constantly able to protect all sentient beings, causing them all to give rise to sublime vows, never once harboring a thought of seeking recompense;
and all roots of goodness are made equal to those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, thereby perfecting all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*).
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness from this giving to sentient beings, saying:
'May all sentient beings be pure and well-tamed;'"
May all sentient beings extinguish their afflictions and adorn and purify all Buddha-fields;
may all sentient beings, with a pure mind, pervade the entire Dharma-realm in a single thought-moment;
may all sentient beings be filled with wisdom as vast as space and the Dharma-realm.

May all sentient beings attain all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), universally enter the three periods of time to discipline sentient beings, and at all times constantly turn the pure, non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma;
may all sentient beings be endowed with all-knowledge, skillfully manifesting supernatural powers and expedient means to benefit sentient beings;

may all sentient beings be able to awaken to and enter the Bodhi of all Buddhas, and throughout all future eons, constantly proclaim the True Dharma within the worlds of the ten directions without ever ceasing, so that all sentient beings may universally hear and know it.
May all sentient beings cultivate the bodhisattva practices throughout immeasurable eons and attain their complete perfection;

may all sentient beings, in all worlds—whether defiled or pure, small or large, coarse or subtle, inverted or upright, whether adorned in a single way or with manifold adornments—as they are described, and throughout as many worlds as there are worlds, cultivate the bodhisattva practices without exception;
may all sentient beings, in every thought-moment, constantly perform all the buddha-works of the three periods of time, teaching and transforming sentient beings toward omniscience.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas provide all that sentient beings require according to their needs, bestowing such incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) things as these;
they do so to ensure that the Buddha-dharma continues without interruption and to universally rescue all sentient beings through great compassion.”
Abiding in great compassion, they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva;
they never transgress the teachings of the Buddha, and through skillful means, they practice all manner of virtues, ensuring that the lineage of all Buddhas is never interrupted.

Granting whatever is requested without weariness or fatigue, they relinquish everything without ever regretting it in their hearts, constantly and diligently dedicating their merit toward the path of omniscience.

At that time, beings of various forms and types, from various realms of rebirth and various fields of merit throughout the lands of the ten directions, all gathered together and came to where the Bodhisattva was, seeking and requesting various things.
Having seen them, the bodhisattva universally embraces them all;
his heart gives rise to joy as if seeing a virtuous friend;
with great compassion and pity, he contemplates fulfilling their aspirations.
The mind of renunciation increases without ceasing, and one never grows weary;
according to whatever they seek, one causes them all to be fully satisfied, freeing them from the suffering of poverty.

At that time, all the beggars were filled with great joy and celebration; they spread the word further and further, praising his virtue, until his excellent reputation reached afar and everyone came to seek refuge in him.
Having seen this, the Bodhisattva experienced immeasurable joy;

even if one were to experience the pleasures of Śakra for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas, the pleasures of the Yāma Heaven for incalculable kalpas, the pleasures of the Tuṣita Heaven for immeasurable kalpas, the pleasures of the Sunirmita Heaven for boundless kalpas, the pleasures of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven for incomparable kalpas, the pleasures of a Brahmā King for uncountable kalpas, the pleasures of a Cakravartin King ruling over the three thousandfold world-system for ineffable kalpas, the pleasures of the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven for inconceivable kalpas, or the pleasures of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven for unspeakable kalpas, none of these could equal it.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees a beggar approaching, he feels joy, love, and delight; he exults with leaping gladness, his faith increases, his aspiration becomes pure, his faculties are harmonized and compliant, his faith and understanding reach fulfillment, and he even advances toward the Bodhi of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
By means of these roots of goodness, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates them for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings;
he dedicates them for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings; he dedicates them so that all sentient beings...
They dedicate [merit] because they have attained great benefit; they dedicate it so that all sentient beings may attain complete purity;
they dedicate it so that all sentient beings may all seek awakening; they dedicate it so that all sentient beings may all attain equanimity;
they dedicate it so that all sentient beings may all become virtuous and excellent.
One dedicates with the mind; one dedicates in order to cause all sentient beings to enter the Mahāyāna;
one dedicates in order to cause all sentient beings to fully attain noble and virtuous wisdom;

one dedicates in order to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, to fulfill the vehicle of the ten powers, and to manifest perfect enlightenment.
[The Buddha] said: "O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this manner, the actions of body, speech, and mind are entirely liberated. They are without attachment and without bondage; there is no perception of a sentient being (*sattva*), no perception of a life-principle (*jīva*), no perception of a person (*pudgala*), no perception of a human (*manuja*), no perception of a youth (*māṇava*), no perception of a born one (*jantu*), no perception of an agent (*kāraka*), no perception of an experiencer (*vedaka*), no perception of existence, no perception of non-existence, no perception of this world or the next world, no perception of dying here and being born there, no perception of permanence, no perception of impermanence, no perception of the three realms of existence (*trai-dhātuka*), no perception of the absence of the three realms of existence, and neither perception nor non-perception."
In this way, it is neither a bound dedication nor a liberated dedication;
neither a dedication of karma nor a dedication of karmic retribution;
neither a conceptual dedication nor a non-conceptual dedication.
It is not a dedication through thought, nor is it a dedication after having thought;
it is not a dedication through the mind, nor is it a dedication without the mind.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they do not cling to the internal, nor do they cling to the external;
they do not cling to the subject that perceives, nor do they cling to the object perceived;
they do not cling to causes, nor do they cling to effects.
He does not cling to dharmas, nor does he cling to non-dharmas;
he does not cling to thought, nor does he cling to non-thought;
he does not cling to form, nor does he cling to the arising of form, nor does he cling to the cessation of form.

One does not cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; one does not cling to the arising of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; nor does one cling to the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
O Son of the Buddha!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain unattached to these dharmas, then they are not bound by form, nor bound by the arising of form, nor bound by the cessation of form;

they are not bound by feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor bound by the arising of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor bound by the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
If one is not bound to these phenomena, then one is likewise not liberated from them.
Why is this? Because there is not even the slightest phenomenon that is presently arising, has already arisen, or will arise.
There is no dharma that can be grasped, and no dharma that can be clung to.

The intrinsic characteristics of all dharmas are thus: they possess no self-nature; they are devoid of self-nature; they are neither one nor two, neither many nor immeasurable, neither small nor large, neither narrow nor broad, neither deep nor shallow, neither quiescent nor conceptual proliferation; they are neither a locus nor a non-locus, neither dharma nor non-dharma, neither essence nor non-essence, and neither existent nor non-existent.
When a bodhisattva observes all phenomena in this way, they are seen as non-dharmas;
yet within the realm of language, following worldly convention, they establish what is not dharma as dharma.
They do not sever the paths of karma, nor do they abandon the bodhisattva practices, seeking omniscience until the end without ever turning back.

They understand that all karmic conditions are like dreams, sounds are like echoes, sentient beings are like shadows, and all phenomena are like illusions; yet they do not destroy the power of causes, conditions, and karma.

They understand that the function of all karmas is vast and extensive, and they comprehend that all dharmas are without agency; thus, they practice the path of non-action without ever ceasing for even a moment.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, abiding in omniscience, universally dedicates both the appropriate and the inappropriate toward the nature of omniscience;
in all places, they dedicate everything without ever turning back.”
For what reason is it called "dedication" (*pariṇāmanā*)?
Because it forever carries one across the world to the other shore, it is called dedication;
because it forever leads one out of the aggregates (*skandha*) to the other shore, it is called dedication.
It is called dedication because it crosses beyond the path of language to reach the other shore;
it is called dedication because it leaves behind all manifold perceptions to reach the other shore;
it is called dedication because it forever severs the view of a self-identity to reach the other shore.
Because one eternally leaves behind all bases of dependence and reaches the further shore, it is called dedication;
because one eternally severs all conditioned activity and reaches the further shore, it is called dedication;
because one eternally emerges from all states of existence and reaches the further shore, it is called dedication.
Because one forever abandons all grasping and reaches the other shore, it is called dedication;
because one forever transcends worldly dharmas and reaches the other shore, it is called dedication.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they are then in accord with the dwelling of the Buddha, in accord with the dwelling of the Dharma, in accord with the dwelling of wisdom, in accord with the dwelling of enlightenment, in accord with the dwelling of meaning, in accord with the dwelling of dedication, in accord with the dwelling of the objective sphere, in accord with the dwelling of practice, in accord with the dwelling of reality, and in accord with the dwelling of purity.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate in this manner, they thoroughly comprehend all dharmas and serve all Buddhas;
there is not a single Buddha whom they do not serve, and there is not a single dharma that they do not offer.
There is not a single dharma that can be destroyed, nor is there a single dharma that can be contradicted;
there is not a single thing to which one may become attached, nor is there a single dharma from which one may feel aversion;
one does not perceive any internal or external phenomena as having even the slightest destruction or as contradicting the way of dependent origination.
"Endowed with the power of the Dharma, they never cease.
'O Son of the Buddha!
This is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s sixth dedication, which accords with all firm roots of goodness.'"

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this dedication, they are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas; they remain firm and non-regressive, entering the profound nature of phenomena (dharmatā) and cultivating omniscience (sarvajñā).
They accord with the meaning of the Dharma, accord with the nature of phenomena, accord with all firm roots of goodness, and accord with all perfected great vows.
Being fully endowed with the quality of acceding to what is firm, they cannot be destroyed by any diamond-like [obstacles], and they attain mastery over all phenomena.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja surveyed the ten directions, surveyed the assembly, and surveyed the Dharma-realm. Having entered into the profound meaning of words and phrases, he cultivated an immeasurable and vast mind, universally covering the world with a heart of great compassion. He extended the lineage of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, entered into the merits of all Buddhas, and accomplished the body of the sovereign power of all Buddhas. Observing the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings and according to the roots of goodness they were ready to mature, he manifested a form-body from his Dharma-nature body and, sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, spoke these verses:
“The Bodhisattva manifests as a king, Peerless among all worldly positions;”
The majesty and radiance of his merit surpass all; he universally brings forth benefit for all living beings.
With a mind pure and free from attachment, he is sovereign in the world and universally honored;
proclaiming the True Dharma to instruct all people, he causes all sentient beings everywhere to attain peace and security.
In this life, he rises from noble birth to the royal throne; Constantly relying on the True Teaching, he turns the Wheel of Dharma.
By nature compassionate, free from cruelty and tyranny, He is revered by the ten directions, and all follow his transformation.
With wisdom that discerns all with constant clarity, Possessing every physical mark and talent in full measure,
He governs the entire realm such that none do not obey, Subduing the armies of Māra until they are utterly destroyed.
Firmly upholding the pure precepts without transgression, Resolutely enduring all with unshakable resolve,
Forever vowing to eliminate the mind of anger and resentment, Always delighting in the practice of all Buddha-dharmas.
Food, drink, incense, garlands, and clothing, Carriages, horses, beds, mats, seats, and lamps—
The Bodhisattva provides all these to aid and relieve people, Along with countless other varieties.
Giving for the sake of benefiting others causes them to develop a vast and expansive mind;
toward the most exalted ones and all others alike, their minds become pure and they give rise to joy.
The Bodhisattva provides for all without exception, being able to relinquish everything both internal and external;
he ensures that his mind remains forever pure, never allowing even a moment of narrowness or inferiority to arise.
Whether giving away his head or his eyes, Or giving away his hands or his feet,
His skin, flesh, marrow, bones, and all other things— He relinquishes everything with a heart free from stinginess.

The Bodhisattva, though occupying the rank of a great king, Of noble lineage and honored among men, Extends his tongue from his open mouth as a gift to all living beings; His heart is joyful, free from sorrow or attachment.
By means of all the merits from that gift of the tongue, I dedicate them to all sentient beings;
may they all, by virtue of these excellent causes and conditions, universally attain the broad and long tongue of the Tathāgata.

Whether giving away their wives and children or even their royal throne, or offering their own bodies as servants, their minds remain pure and ever-joyful; thus, in all such acts, they are free from sorrow or regret.
Whatever they seek according to their desire, he bestows it all; He provides relief at the proper time without weariness or fatigue.
He can relinquish everything he possesses, Fully satisfying all who come to him in search of aid.
For the sake of hearing the Dharma, he gave up his own body; practicing various ascetic austerities, he sought bodhi.
Furthermore, for the sake of sentient beings, he relinquished everything, seeking supreme wisdom without ever regressing.
Having heard the True Dharma from the Buddha, they offered their own bodies as attendants;
desiring to universally save all living beings, they gave rise to immeasurable hearts of joy.
Seeing the World-Honored One, the Great Guide, who is able to bring vast benefit through a heart of loving-kindness,
he then leaped for joy and gave rise to great delight, as he listened to and received the profound flavor of the Tathāgata’s Dharma.
All the roots of goodness possessed by Bodhisattvas, they dedicate entirely to all sentient beings;
universally rescuing and protecting them without exception, forever causing them to attain liberation and eternal peace and happiness.
All the retinues belonging to the Bodhisattvas possess physical forms that are upright and majestic, and they are endowed with eloquence and wisdom;
with flower garlands, garments, and ointments, they are fully equipped with every kind of adornment.
These retinues are most rare and extraordinary; the Bodhisattva is able to give them all away.
Solely seeking perfect enlightenment to deliver all living beings, such a mind he never abandons for even a moment.
When a bodhisattva reflects with such discernment, they fully carry out various vast deeds and dedicate them all to all sentient beings,
yet without giving rise to a mind of grasping or attachment.
The Bodhisattva relinquished that great royal throne, as well as the kingdom and its various cities, palaces, towers, and gardens;
he was without stinginess regarding even his servants and attendants.
Throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kalpas, he traveled everywhere bestowing gifts;
by means of this, he instructed all living beings, causing them all to transcend and ascend to the shore beyond.
Infinite varieties, each distinct, have gathered from the worlds of the ten directions;
having seen them, the Bodhisattva rejoices in his heart and satisfies them according to their lack.
Just as the Buddhas of the three periods have dedicated their merit, so too do Bodhisattvas cultivate such deeds;
following all that the Honored One, the Tamer of Men, has practiced, they learn accordingly and reach the other shore.
The Bodhisattva contemplates all phenomena: who is it that can enter these phenomena?
How does one enter, and what is it that is entered?
Thus, the mind of giving abides nowhere.
The Bodhisattva dedicates with skillful wisdom; The Bodhisattva dedicates through the methods of expedient means;
The Bodhisattva dedicates toward the ultimate reality, Remaining unattached within those dharmas.
The mind does not discriminate among any karmas, nor is it stained by or attached to the fruits of karma;
knowing that the nature of bodhi arises from conditions, one enters the profound dharma-realm without opposition.
Karma does not exist within the body, nor does it abide depending upon the mind;
through wisdom one realizes the nature of karmalessness, yet karma is never lost due to the power of causes and conditions.
The mind does not falsely grasp at past phenomena, nor does it crave or cling to future events;
it does not dwell upon the present, for it thoroughly understands that the three periods of time are entirely empty and quiescent.
The Bodhisattva has already reached the further shore of form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise so.
Having transcended the worldly stream of birth and death, his mind is humble and ever pure.
Contemplate thoroughly the five aggregates, the eighteen elements, The twelve bases, and your own body;
Seeking enlightenment within each of these, Their essential nature is ultimately unattainable.
One does not grasp at the mark of the permanence of all phenomena, nor does one cling to the mark of annihilation;
the nature of dharmas is neither existent nor non-existent, yet the sequence of karmic principles is ultimately inexhaustible.
Not dwelling upon any phenomena, one perceives neither sentient beings nor bodhi;
throughout the lands of the ten directions and the three periods of time, one ultimately finds nothing that can be obtained.
If one can contemplate all phenomena in this way, it will be as the Buddhas have realized:
though one seeks their intrinsic nature, it cannot be found, yet the practice of the Bodhisattva is not in vain.
The Bodhisattva realizes that all phenomena arise from conditions;
He does not contravene any of the paths practiced, Revealing and explaining the traces of all karmic actions, Desiring to bring all sentient beings to complete purity.
This is the path traveled by the wise, as taught by all Tathāgatas;
by contemplating it in accordance with reality, one enters the true principle and spontaneously awakens to attain Bodhi.
All phenomena are neither born nor extinguished, Neither coming nor going;
Without dying here to be born there— Such a person understands the Buddha-dharma.
Thoroughly comprehending the true nature of all phenomena, yet making no conceptual distinctions regarding that dharmatā;
knowing that phenomena lack intrinsic nature and are non-conceptual—such a person skillfully enters the wisdom of all Buddhas.

The nature of phenomena pervades all places; all sentient beings and lands throughout the three periods of time are entirely contained within it without exception, yet it possesses no form or characteristic that can be apprehended.
That which all Buddhas have fully awakened to is entirely encompassed without exception;
though they speak of all phenomena throughout the three periods of time, such phenomena as these do not exist at all.
Just as the nature of all phenomena pervades everything, so too is the bodhisattva’s dedication;
dedicating in this way to all sentient beings, they never regress from the world.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Eight;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
Chapter Twenty-five, Part Seven: The Dedication of the Seventy [Verses].
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the dedication of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas that accords with all sentient beings?
“O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva, according to all the roots of goodness they have accumulated—namely:
small roots of goodness, great roots of goodness, extensive roots of goodness, manifold roots of goodness, and immeasurable roots of goodness—”
various roots of goodness; roots of goodness as numerous as motes of dust; incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) roots of goodness;
boundless roots of goodness; inconceivable roots of goodness; immeasurable roots of goodness; roots of goodness within the realm of the Buddha;
roots of goodness within the realm of the Dharma; roots of goodness within the realm of the Saṅgha; and roots of goodness within the realm of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
The roots of goodness regarding the faculties; the roots of goodness regarding the sphere of all sentient beings; the roots of goodness regarding the sphere of skillful means;
the roots of goodness regarding the cultivation of various virtuous minds; the roots of goodness regarding the internal sphere; the roots of goodness regarding the external sphere;
the roots of goodness regarding the sphere of the boundless factors of enlightenment; and the establishment of the roots of goodness through the diligent practice of all forms of relinquishment.
The roots of goodness of maintaining pure precepts with ultimate superior resolve; the roots of goodness of enduring all forms of renunciation without exception;
the roots of goodness of constant vigor with a mind that never regresses; the roots of goodness of entering immeasurable samādhis through great skillful means;
the roots of goodness of skillfully observing with wisdom; and the knowledge of the differences in the mental activities of all sentient beings.
The roots of goodness; the roots of goodness that accumulate boundless merit; the roots of goodness that diligently cultivate the practices and deeds of a bodhisattva;
and the roots of goodness that universally cover and nurture all worlds.
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice and abide in these roots of goodness, they enter into them, embrace them, accumulate and prepare them, and attain pure understanding through their minds;
when they manifest and give rise to them, they obtain a mind of endurance and close the gates to the evil realms.
They have well-restrained their sense faculties and are fully endowed with dignified deportment; they are far removed from perversions and perfect in right practice;
they are worthy vessels for all the Buddhas' teachings and serve as excellent fields of merit for sentient beings;

they are held in the Buddhas' mindfulness, grow the roots of goodness of the Buddhas, abide in the vows of the Buddhas, and perform the deeds of the Buddhas; their minds attain mastery, equaling those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
They proceed to the Buddha’s place of enlightenment and enter the power of the Tathāgata; they are endowed with the physical marks of a Buddha and transcend all worlds;
they take no pleasure in rebirth in the heavens, do not crave wealth or enjoyment, and do not cling to conditioned phenomena;
they dedicate all roots of goodness to become a treasury of merit for all sentient beings.

Abiding in the ultimate path, they universally cover all things; from within the path of falsehood, they extract sentient beings and cause them to dwell securely in all wholesome dharmas, pervading all realms without interruption or exhaustion;
they open the gate of the bodhi of omniscience, erect the banner of wisdom, and adorn and purify the Great Way;

they are able to manifest throughout all worlds, causing the removal of defilements, bringing about the excellent taming of the mind, birth into the family of the Tathāgata, and the purification of the Buddha-lineage.
Fully endowed with merit, they act as great fields of blessings and serve as a reliance for the world;
they establish all sentient beings in purity and constantly and diligently cultivate all roots of goodness.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva cultivates various roots of goodness through the power of the mind of pure aspiration for enlightenment, they form this thought:

‘These roots of goodness are that which has been accumulated by the mind of enlightenment; they are that which has been contemplated by the mind of enlightenment; they are that which has been initiated by the mind of enlightenment; they are that which has been delighted in by the mind of enlightenment; they are that which has been increased by the mind of enlightenment.’”
"All this is for the sake of compassion for all sentient beings, for the sake of seeking all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), and for the sake of accomplishing the ten powers (daśabala) of a Tathāgata.
When one forms such a thought, one's roots of goodness increase and one never regresses.
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further reflects:

‘May I, by the fruit and retribution of these roots of goodness, cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all future kalpas, bestowing them entirely upon all sentient beings and dedicating them entirely to all sentient beings, universally and without exception.’”

May incalculable worlds be filled with precious jewels; may incalculable worlds be filled with garments; may incalculable worlds be filled with exquisite fragrances; may incalculable worlds be filled with ornaments; may incalculable worlds be filled with immeasurable maṇi gems; may incalculable worlds be filled with wonderful flowers; may incalculable worlds be filled with the finest flavors; may incalculable worlds be filled with wealth and goods; and may incalculable worlds be filled with couches and seats—canopied with jeweled curtains and spread with exquisite fabrics—and may incalculable worlds be filled with various kinds of adorned crowns.
Suppose there were a single person who, throughout all future kalpas, constantly came to seek these things, and one bestowed them as gifts upon him without ever becoming weary or ceasing.
