"As it is toward one person, so it is toward all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives in this manner, they have no heart of hypocrisy, no heart of expectation, no heart seeking renown, no heart of regret, and no heart of feverish distress; rather, they give rise only to the mind that single-mindedly seeks the path of omniscience, the mind of total renunciation, the mind of compassion for sentient beings, the mind of teaching and maturing them, and the mind that causes all to dwell securely in the wisdom of omniscience.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner, constantly practicing generosity throughout all future eons.
O Son of the Buddha!"
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further reflects:

"For the sake of even a single sentient being, I desire to cause the *asaṃkhyeya* worlds to be filled with precious elephants, complete with their seven limbs, of an extremely well-trained nature, with golden banners standing upon them, covered by golden nets, and adorned with various exquisite jewels, which I shall employ as gifts;
I vow to cause the *asaṃkhyeya* worlds to be filled with precious horses, like the king of dragon-horses, adorned with various ornaments of many jewels, which I shall hold forth as gifts."
May I cause countless worlds (*asaṃkhyeya-loka*) to be filled with courtesans, all capable of performing various exquisite melodies, which I shall offer as a gift;
may I cause countless worlds to be filled with men and women, which I shall offer as a gift;
may I cause countless worlds to be filled with my own bodies, generating the bodhicitta and offering them as a gift.
May I cause my own heads to fill incalculable worlds and give them as alms with a mind of non-negligence;
may I cause my own eyes to fill incalculable worlds and give them as alms;
may I cause my own body’s flesh, blood, and even marrow to fill incalculable worlds, giving them away without any lingering attachment.
May I cause the sovereign thrones of incalculable worlds to fill them completely, and offer them as a gift;
may I cause the servants and laborers of incalculable worlds to fill them completely, and offer them as a gift.
"Thus, with such various things as these, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, dwelling in a vast mind of universal giving throughout all future eons, gives to a single sentient being;
and as he does for one sentient being, he gives in this same manner to every single sentient being throughout the entire realm of sentient beings."
“O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, throughout all future kalpas in a single world-system, cultivates the bodhisattva practices and bestows such things as these upon a single sentient being; doing so for all sentient beings, he brings them all to fulfillment.

As it is in one world-system, so it is in all world-systems throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm. His great compassion universally covers all, never ceasing for an instant; he universally extends his pity, providing and making offerings according to their needs, ensuring that his practice does not falter when encountering circumstances, nor does he give rise to a mind of weariness even for the duration of a finger-snap.”
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas practice giving in this manner, they give rise to these thoughts, namely:

the unattached mind, the unbound mind, the liberated mind, the mind of great power, the profound mind, the well-restrained mind, the non-clinging mind, the mind free from the notion of a life-span, the well-tamed mind, the undistracted mind, the non-conceptualizing mind, the mind endowed with various precious natures, the mind that seeks no karmic reward, the mind that thoroughly comprehends all dharmas, the mind abiding in great dedication, the mind that skillfully resolves all meanings, the mind that causes all sentient beings to abide in supreme wisdom, the mind that gives birth to the light of the Great Dharma, and the mind that enters the wisdom of omniscience.
“O Son of the Buddha!
With the roots of goodness thus accumulated, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates them in every thought-moment as follows:
‘May all sentient beings have abundant wealth and treasures, lacking nothing at all;’”
May all sentient beings achieve the inexhaustible treasury of great merit;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with every form of peace and happiness;
may all sentient beings increase the karma of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
May all sentient beings fully accomplish the immeasurable, supreme, and foremost Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain non-retrogression in the vehicle of omniscience;
may all sentient beings universally behold all Buddhas of the ten directions.
May all sentient beings forever be free from the defilements and dust of worldly delusions;
may all sentient beings attain a pure and equanimous mind;
may all sentient beings leave behind all places of hardship and realize all-encompassing wisdom.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates in this way, they give rise to a heart of joy;
for the sake of causing all sentient beings to obtain benefit and peace and happiness."
In order to cause all sentient beings to attain a mind of equanimity;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind capable of relinquishment;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of universal giving.
In order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of joyful giving;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving that is forever free from poverty;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving all material wealth and treasures.
In order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the mind of giving away countless treasures;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the mind of universal giving, immeasurable giving, and all-encompassing giving;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the mind of uninterrupted giving throughout all future kalpas.
In order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving characterized by total renunciation, free from regret and affliction;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving that relinquishes all requisites for life;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving that is compliant with the Dharma;
In order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the mind of gathering through giving;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the mind of vast giving;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the mind of giving by relinquishing immeasurable ornaments as offerings;
In order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of unattached giving;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of impartial giving;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving with the supreme power of a vajra;
In order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving that is like the radiance of the sun;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in a mind of giving that gathers the wisdom of the Tathāgata;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the retinue of their roots of goodness.
In order to cause the roots of goodness and wisdom of all sentient beings to be ever present before them;
in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the perfection of an indestructible pure mind;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to accomplish the most supreme and pure roots of goodness.
In order to cause all sentient beings to awaken from the slumber of afflictions;
in order to cause all sentient beings to eliminate all doubts and delusions;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the pure merit of impartial wisdom.
In order to cause all sentient beings to perfect their merit so that it cannot be destroyed;
in order to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the pure and immovable samādhi;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the indestructible wisdom of omniscience.
In order to cause all sentient beings to fully accomplish the immeasurable, pure, and supernatural powers of bodhisattvas;
in order to cause all sentient beings to cultivate and accumulate roots of goodness free from attachment;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to purify their minds by recollecting all Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
In order to cause all sentient beings to give birth to pure and supreme roots of goodness;
in order to cause all sentient beings to eliminate all obstacles to the Path created by the works of Māra;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the dharmas of unimpeded, pure, and impartial merit.
To cause all sentient beings to constantly mindfully recollect all Buddhas with a vast mind, never becoming weary or negligent;
to cause all sentient beings to always draw near to all Buddhas and diligently make offerings to them;
and to cause all sentient beings to widely open the gates of all roots of goodness and universally be able to fulfill all pure and white dharmas.
In order to cause the immeasurable mind, the vast mind, and the most supreme mind of all sentient beings to be completely purified;
in order to cause all sentient beings to achieve a mind of pure and equal giving;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to uphold the Śīla-pāramitā and other perfections of all Buddhas so that they are pure; [he manifests this].
In order to cause all sentient beings to attain the great perfection of patience;
in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in the perfection of diligence and remain forever free from indolence;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in immeasurable concentrations and be able to give rise to various supernormal powers and wisdom;
In order to cause all sentient beings to know the Prajñāpāramitā that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature;
in order to cause all sentient beings to fulfill the boundless pure realm of reality (dharmadhātu);
and in order to cause all sentient beings to fully accomplish all pure roots of goodness and supernormal powers (abhijñā).
To cause all sentient beings to abide in impartial conduct so that their accumulation of wholesome dharmas may be fully perfected;
to cause all sentient beings to skillfully enter the realms of all Buddhas so that they may pervade them entirely;
and to cause the physical, verbal, and mental actions of all sentient beings to be universally purified.
In order to cause the karmic fruits of all sentient beings' wholesome deeds to be universally pure;
in order to cause all sentient beings to thoroughly comprehend all phenomena so that they are universally pure;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to thoroughly comprehend the true meaning so that it is universally pure.
In order to cause all sentient beings to cultivate all supreme practices for universal purity;
in order to cause all sentient beings to fulfill all great vows of bodhisattvas for universal purity;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to realize all merit and wisdom for universal purity.
To cause all sentient beings to accomplish all roots of goodness of the same essence, dedicating them toward the universal fulfillment of the vehicle of omniscience;
to cause all sentient beings to adorn and purify all Buddha-lands, achieving universal fulfillment;
and to cause all sentient beings to behold all Buddhas without attachment, achieving universal fulfillment.
In order to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the primary and secondary marks, so that their merit and adornments may be universally perfected;

in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the sixty kinds of vocal tones, so that their speech is truthful and sincere, worthy of being believed and accepted by all, and adorned with hundreds of thousands of dharmas, thereby perfecting the Tathāgata’s unimpeded merit and wondrous voice;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to achieve the ten powers, adorned with an unimpeded and equanimous mind.
In order to cause all sentient beings to attain the inexhaustible light of the Dharma of all Buddhas and to universally perfect all eloquence;
in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the supreme, fearless lion’s roar of the Hero among Men;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to attain all-knowledge and turn the irreversible, inexhaustible wheel of Dharma.
In order to cause all sentient beings to fully comprehend all phenomena by means of revealing, teaching, and expounding them universally and perfectly;
in order to cause all sentient beings to cultivate pure wholesome dharmas at the appropriate times, achieving universal perfection;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to accomplish the purity of the unsurpassed Dharma-treasure of the Teacher and other such qualities;
In order to cause all sentient beings to universally fulfill the single adornment, the immeasurable adornment, the great adornment, and the adornments of all Buddhas;
in order to cause all sentient beings to equally enter and pervade all realms throughout the three periods of time;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to be able to travel to all Buddha-fields to hear and receive the true Dharma without exception.
In order to cause all sentient beings to possess the benefit of wisdom and be honored by the world as equals to the Buddhas;
in order to cause all sentient beings to know all phenomena through omniscience, thereby attaining universal perfection;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to perform unshakable karma and attain the fruit of non-obstruction, thereby attaining universal perfection.
To cause all sentient beings to attain supernatural powers in all their faculties, so that they may know the faculties of all sentient beings;
to cause all sentient beings to attain non-discriminative, equalizing wisdom, which is universally pure within the dharma of a single characteristic;
and to cause all sentient beings to never contradict principle, so that all roots of goodness are fully perfected.
In order to cause all sentient beings to fully comprehend and master all the sovereign spiritual powers of all bodhisattvas;
in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the inexhaustible merits of all buddhas, such that their merit and wisdom are entirely equal;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to resolve upon bodhicitta, understanding that all phenomena are of one equal mark without exception or deficiency.
To cause all sentient beings to thoroughly understand the True Dharma, so that they may become the most supreme field of merit for the world;
to cause all sentient beings to achieve impartial and pure great compassion, so that they may become a field of great power for all donors;
and to cause all sentient beings to be firm and foremost, such that they cannot be thwarted or destroyed by any.
It is to ensure that all sentient beings who behold [this] will inevitably receive benefit and be invincible;
it is to ensure that all sentient beings fully perfect the most supreme mind of equanimity;
and it is to ensure that all sentient beings skillfully comprehend all phenomena and attain great fearlessness.
It is to cause all sentient beings to emit a single ray of light that universally illumines all worlds throughout the ten directions;
it is to cause all sentient beings to universally cultivate all the diligent practices of bodhisattvas without weariness or retreat;
it is to cause all sentient beings to universally fulfill all vows of practice through a single vow of practice.
In order to cause all sentient beings to universally hear with a single sublime voice and thereby attain understanding;
in order to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the pure minds of all bodhisattvas;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to universally encounter all spiritual friends and receive their guidance;
To cause all sentient beings to cultivate the bodhisattva practices and to subdue sentient beings without rest;
to cause all sentient beings to possess all sounds through wondrous eloquence, extensively expounding the Dharma according to their capacities without interruption or exhaustion;
and to cause all sentient beings to be able to know all minds with a single mind, dedicating all roots of goodness equally.
To cause all sentient beings to always delight in accumulating all roots of goodness and to establish them in pure wisdom;
to cause all sentient beings to attain omniscience, merit, wisdom, and a pure body;
and to cause all sentient beings to skillfully know the roots of goodness of all other sentient beings, observing and dedicating them so that they may be universally accomplished.
To cause all sentient beings to attain all-knowledge and achieve the universal perfection of equal and right enlightenment;
to cause all sentient beings to attain the wisdom of perfected spiritual powers, so that by manifesting in a single place, they manifest in all places;
and to cause all sentient beings to attain the wisdom of universal adornment, so that by adorning and purifying a single assembly, they adorn and purify all assemblies.
In order to cause all sentient beings to universally see all Buddha-lands within a single Buddha-land;
in order to cause all sentient beings to universally and pervasively adorn all Buddha-lands with every kind of ornament, unspeakable ornaments, immeasurable ornaments, and inexhaustible ornaments;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to be able to fully comprehend the profound meaning of all dharmas.
To cause all sentient beings to attain the supreme and foremost sovereign supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas;
to cause all sentient beings to attain the sovereign supernormal powers of all merits, which are neither identical nor different;
and to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with all impartial roots of goodness, so that they may universally receive the consecration upon their crowns from all Buddhas.
It is to cause all sentient beings to fully attain and perfect the body of pure wisdom, so that they may be the most honored and supreme among all states of existence.
"O Son of the Buddha!

Thus do Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, out of compassion, benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, causing them all to be purified; they cause them to remain far removed from stinginess and envy, to receive superior and wondrous births, to possess great majestic virtue, to give rise to great faith and understanding, and to forever leave behind anger as well as all obscurations and turbidities."

Their minds are pure, upright, and supple, free from flattery, crookedness, delusion, and ignorance. They practice the path of renunciation; their firm and indestructible mind of equanimity never regresses. They are fully accomplished in the power of pure dharmas, free from affliction or loss, and skillful in dedication.
They constantly cultivate right conduct to subdue sentient beings, extinguishing all unwholesome karma and practicing asceticism for the sake of all roots of goodness.

Furthermore, they exhort sentient beings to engage in such cultivation, universally undergoing all sufferings on behalf of conscious beings. With the eye of great wisdom, they observe that all roots of goodness have wisdom as their nature, and through skillful means, they dedicate them to all sentient beings.
In order to cause all sentient beings to dwell securely in all states of pure merit;
in order to cause all sentient beings to be able to embrace all roots of goodness and to know the nature and meaning of all meritorious qualities;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to universally purify all their roots of goodness.
It is to cause all sentient beings to plant various wholesome dharmas within the field of merit without regret;
it is to cause all sentient beings to be universally able to embrace all other sentient beings, leading each and every one toward omniscience;
and it is to cause all sentient beings to universally gather all roots of goodness, ensuring that each and every one is in accord with impartial dedication.
Furthermore, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way: "May all sentient beings attain ultimate peace;

may all sentient beings attain ultimate purity; may all sentient beings attain ultimate bliss; may all sentient beings attain ultimate liberation; may all sentient beings attain ultimate equality; may all sentient beings attain ultimate realization; may all sentient beings dwell ultimately in all pure and white dharmas; may all sentient beings obtain unimpeded eyes; may all sentient beings skillfully discipline their minds; and may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the ten powers to subdue and transform sentient beings."
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they do not cling to karma, do not cling to its retribution, do not cling to the body, do not cling to objects, do not cling to lands, do not cling to directions, do not cling to sentient beings, do not cling to the absence of sentient beings, do not cling to all phenomena, and do not cling to the absence of all phenomena.”
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they universally bestow these roots of goodness upon the world, saying:

"May all sentient beings fulfill the wisdom of a Buddha, attain a pure mind, possess clear and lucid wisdom, have inner tranquility, remain unmoved by external conditions, and increase and perfect the seed of the Buddhas of the three periods of time."
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice such dedication, they transcend all things, and none can surpass them; all the verbal expressions of every world together praising them could never exhaust their merit.
They universally cultivate all the practices of Bodhisattvas, are able to travel to all Buddha-lands, and behold all Buddhas without any obstruction.”

Furthermore, they are able to universally behold the practices of all Bodhisattvas throughout all worlds; through skillful means, they analyze the profound words and meanings of all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings; having attained *dhāraṇī*, they expound the sublime Dharma without interruption until the end of future kalpas;
for the sake of sentient beings, in every thought-moment, they universally manifest their bodies like reflections throughout unspeakably unspeakable worlds to make offerings to all Buddhas;

and in every thought-moment, they adorn and purify unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-lands, pervading them all, practicing the wisdom that adorns and purifies Buddha-fields without ever feeling weary or satisfied.
In every thought-moment, they cause unspeakably unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings to attain purity and accomplishment, achieving equal fulfillment;
within all those various lands, they diligently cultivate all the pāramitās, gathering in sentient beings and accomplishing pure karma;

they attain unimpeded ears, and throughout unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-worlds, they hear, receive, and uphold the turning of the wheel of Dharma by each and every Tathāgata, practicing with diligent effort without giving rise to a single thought of abandonment.

Abiding in the bodhisattva’s supernormal powers—which are non-apprehensible, without dependence, unconditioned, and unattached—in a single kṣaṇa, the snap of a finger, they manifest bodies that travel everywhere to unspeakably many Buddha-worlds, sharing the same vision as all those bodhisattvas.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas cultivate the bodhisattva practices in this manner, they are already able to fulfill immeasurable, unspeakably unspeakable pure merits that cannot be fully exhausted even by recollection or praise; how much more so when they attain unsurpassed bodhi, wherein all Buddha-fields are equally pure, all sentient beings are equally pure, all bodies are equally pure, all faculties are equally pure, all karmic fruits are equally pure, all assemblies and sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) are equally pure, all perfected practices are equally pure, the wisdom of skillful means regarding all dharmas is equally pure, the vows and dedications of all Tathāgatas are equally pure, and the spheres of supernormal power of all Buddhas are equally pure.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they attain the Dharma-gate of pure joy in all merits, which is adorned by the perfection of immeasurable virtues.”
When dedicating in this manner, sentient beings do not conflict with all lands, and lands do not conflict with all sentient beings;
lands and sentient beings do not conflict with karma, and karma does not conflict with lands and sentient beings;
thought does not conflict with the mind, and the mind does not conflict with thought.
Volition does not conflict with the mental object, nor does the mental object conflict with volition;
karma does not conflict with its retribution, nor does retribution conflict with karma;
karma does not conflict with the path of action, nor does the path of action conflict with karma.
The nature of phenomena does not contradict their characteristics, and characteristics do not contradict the nature;
the arising of phenomena does not contradict the nature, and the nature does not contradict arising;
the equality of lands does not contradict the equality of sentient beings, and the equality of sentient beings does not contradict the equality of lands.
The equality of all sentient beings does not contradict the equality of all phenomena; the equality of all phenomena does not contradict the equality of all sentient beings.

The equality of the limit of detachment does not contradict the equality in which all sentient beings abide; the equality in which all sentient beings abide does not contradict the equality of the limit of detachment.
The past does not contradict the future, and the future does not contradict the past.
The past and future do not contradict the present, and the present does not contradict the past and future;
the equality of the world does not contradict the equality of the Buddha, and the equality of the Buddha does not contradict the equality of the world;
the bodhisattva practice does not contradict all-knowledge, and all-knowledge does not contradict the bodhisattva practice.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they attain equality of karma, equality of retribution, equality of body, equality of skillful means, equality of vows, equality with all sentient beings, equality with all lands, equality with all practices, equality with all-knowledge, and equality with the Buddhas of the three periods of time.”

One attains the opportunity to serve all Buddhas; one attains the opportunity to make offerings to all Bodhisattvas; one attains the opportunity to plant all roots of goodness; one attains the opportunity to fulfill all great vows; one attains the opportunity to teach and transform all sentient beings; one attains the opportunity to thoroughly understand all karma; one attains the opportunity to serve and make offerings to all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra); one attains the opportunity to enter all pure assemblies and sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa); one attains the opportunity to penetrate all correct teachings; and one attains the opportunity to bring all pure dharmas (śukladharma) to full completion.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the seventh dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, which is equal and in accord with all sentient beings.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes this dedication, they are able to destroy all demonic adversaries, pull out the thorns of desire, attain the bliss of liberation, abide in non-dual nature, possess great majestic power, rescue and protect sentient beings, and become a king of merit.”
With unimpeded supernormal power (*ṛddhipāda*), they travel to all lands and enter the state of quiescent extinction;

possessing all bodies, they accomplish the practices of bodhisattvas, attaining mastery of mind over all conduct and vows; they discern and understand all phenomena, being able to manifest universally in all buddha-fields;
having attained unimpeded hearing, they hear all sounds within every land.
Having attained the pure eye of wisdom, they never for a moment cease beholding all Buddhas;
regarding all objective realms, they bring forth roots of goodness with a mind free from high or low;
and regarding all dharmas, they attain the state of non-attainment.
"Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with all their roots of goodness, accord with and conform to all sentient beings; in this way they dedicate [their merit].
At that time, Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The various merits performed by bodhisattvas Are subtle, vast, profound, and far-reaching."
Even practicing for but a single thought-moment, they are able to dedicate it all toward the boundless.
All the requisites for life possessed by these Bodhisattvas are of every variety, abundant and beyond measure— hundreds of millions in number—
with fragrant elephants and precious horses yoked to their chariots, and garments and treasures all exquisite and wonderful.
Whether with head, eyes, hands, or feet, or holding their own flesh and marrow,
they reach throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions, universally bestowing them all so that they may be fully satisfied.
All the merits cultivated throughout immeasurable eons are entirely dedicated, for the sake of delivering all living beings; their resolve never regresses.
For the sake of delivering sentient beings, the Bodhisattva constantly cultivates the most supreme practice of dedication;
may all throughout the three realms attain peace and happiness, and may they all fully realize the unsurpassed fruit.
The Bodhisattva universally gives rise to impartial vows; according to the pure karma they have accumulated, they bestow it all as a dedication to all living beings, never forsaking such a great vow.
The Bodhisattva’s power of aspiration is infinite and unimpeded, embracing all worlds;
thus dedicating [merit] to all living beings, they never for a moment give rise to a discriminating mind.
May all sentient beings possess clear and lucid wisdom; May their generosity and observance of precepts be entirely pure;
May they practice with diligence, never wearying or ceasing; May such great vows continue without rest.
The Bodhisattva dedicates merit to reach the other shore, universally opening the pure and wondrous Dharma-gate;
with wisdom equal to that of the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings, they discern the true meaning and attain the ultimate.
The Bodhisattva has already attained mastery of speech, and likewise possesses all kinds of wisdom;
he expounds the Dharma according to principle without obstruction, yet his mind remains unattached therein.
One should always not conceive of duality among all phenomena, nor yet conceive of non-duality;
being free from both duality and non-duality, one knows them all to be merely the path of verbal expression.
Knowing that all worlds are entirely equal, There is nothing that is not the karma of mind and speech;
Sentient beings are like illusions and transformations, lacking any reality, Yet all karmic retributions arise from this.
Whatever exists within all the worlds, The various fruits of retribution, each distinct— None are not brought to completion by the power of karma; If karma is extinguished, they all come to an end.
The Bodhisattva observes all worlds, With the actions of body, speech, and mind entirely equal;
He also causes sentient beings to abide in equality, Just like the peerless, Great Holy Honored One.
The Bodhisattva dedicates all wholesome karma, universally causing the physical forms of sentient beings to be pure;
with merit and skillful means fully perfected, they become equal to the Unsurpassed Tamer of Men.
The Bodhisattva benefits all sentient beings, dedicating the entirety of his ocean of merit;
may his majestic radiance transcend the world, and may he attain a body of heroic, fierce, and great power.
May all the merits I have cultivated through practice cause the world to be universally pure;
as the Buddhas are pure and peerless, so too shall sentient beings be pure.
The Bodhisattva attains skillfulness in meaning and is able to know the most supreme Dharma of all Buddhas;
by dedicating all such virtuous deeds equally, they vow that all beings may become identical with the Tathāgata.
The Bodhisattva thoroughly understands that all phenomena are empty;
In all worlds there is nothing at all, Neither creation nor a creator exists, Yet the karmic retribution of sentient beings is never lost.

All phenomena are quiescent, yet not quiescent; one who is far removed from these two dualistic conceptualizations knows that such discrimination is a worldly view, and enters the state of right determination where discrimination is exhausted.
Such true sons of the Buddhas, born through transformation from the Dharma of the Tathāgata,
are able to perform such skillful dedication, whereby all doubts and delusions in the world are utterly extinguished.
The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Nine;
The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Thirty.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Decree.
The Twenty-fifth Chapter on the Dedication, Part Eight:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
What is the dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva characterized by suchness?"
“O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva possesses clear and lucid right mindfulness; his mind is firmly established and free from delusion;
he practices with single-minded devotion, and his profound resolve remains unshakable.”
They accomplish indestructible karma and proceed toward omniscience, never regressing;
they aspire to the Mahāyāna with courageous fearlessness;
they plant the roots of all virtues and bring universal peace to the world.
They give birth to supreme roots of goodness and cultivate pure, white dharmas;
their great compassion increases and the jewel of their mind is perfected;
they constantly mindfulness of all Buddhas and protect and uphold the True Dharma.
With firm faith and joy in the bodhisattva path, they accomplish immeasurable, pure, and wondrous roots of goodness;
they diligently cultivate all merits and wisdom, acting as guides and teachers who give rise to all wholesome dharmas, dedicating them through the skillful means of wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattva, with the eye of wisdom, universally observes all roots of goodness, which are immeasurable and boundless.

When these various roots of goodness were being cultivated and accumulated—whether in seeking conditions, or in preparation, or in purification, or in entry, or in diligent exertion, or in the arousal of practice, or in clear realization, or in meticulous scrutiny, or in exposition—all such things involve various gates, various objects, various characteristics, various matters, various divisions, various practices, various names, various distinctions, various origins, and various cultivations. Among them, every single root of goodness is established by a mind directed toward the vehicle of the Ten Powers; they are all dedicated to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), being one and non-dual.
They dedicate all roots of goodness in this way, saying:
"May I attain perfect and unimpeded physical action to cultivate the bodhisattva practice;
may I attain pure and unimpeded verbal action to cultivate the bodhisattva practice."
May I achieve unimpeded mental action and dwell securely in the Mahāyāna;
may I perfect the unobstructed mind and purely cultivate all bodhisattva practices;
may I give rise to an immeasurable and vast spirit of giving, providing for all infinite sentient beings without exception.
May I attain mastery of mind over all phenomena and manifest the great light of Dharma, which nothing can obscure;
may I attain clear penetration into the realm of all-knowledge, give rise to the bodhicitta, and universally illuminate the world;
may I always maintain right mindfulness of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, contemplating the Tathāgata as ever present before me.
May they dwell in the fulfillment of their superior resolve and aspiration, remaining far removed from all māras and adversaries;
may they attain stable abiding in the wisdom of the Buddha’s ten powers, universally gathering in sentient beings without ceasing;
may they attain samādhi to travel through all worlds, yet remain unstained by the mundane world.
May I dwell in all worlds without weariness, teaching and transforming sentient beings without ever ceasing;
may I give rise to immeasurable wisdom born of reflection and skillful means to accomplish the inconceivable path of a bodhisattva;
may I attain the wisdom that is not deluded regarding all directions, being able to discern all worlds in their entirety.
May I attain the power of sovereign spiritual penetrations and wisdom, such that in a single thought-moment I am able to completely adorn and purify all lands;
may I attain universal entry into the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, seeing all worlds as entirely pure;
may I attain the arising of non-discriminative wisdom, entering all lands within a single land.
May I manifest all matters of the adornments of every buddha-field to transform and guide immeasurable and boundless sentient beings;
may I manifest the infinite dharma-realm within a single buddha-field, and likewise in all buddha-fields;
may I attain the wisdom of sovereign great supernormal powers to travel universally to all buddha-lands.
“O Son of the Buddha!
By means of all his roots of goodness, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva vows to adorn all Buddha-lands, vows to pervade all worlds, and vows to achieve the observation of wisdom.”
Just as one dedicates for oneself, so too does one dedicate for the sake of all sentient beings, saying:
"May all sentient beings forever leave behind all realms of hell-beings, animals, and the Lord of Death;
may all sentient beings eliminate all karmic obstacles."
May all sentient beings attain a universal mind and impartial wisdom;
may all sentient beings embrace both enemies and kin with equanimity, bringing them all peace and happiness, and may their wisdom be pure;
may all sentient beings achieve the perfection of wisdom, with pure light shining everywhere.
May all sentient beings perfect their wisdom born of reflection and realize the true meaning;
may all sentient beings, through pure aspiration and joy, seek enlightenment and attain immeasurable wisdom;
may all sentient beings be able to universally manifest the abode of peace and security.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva constantly dedicates with a virtuous mind in this way: to cause all sentient beings to encounter the cool clouds and pour down the rain of Dharma;
and to cause all sentient beings to always meet with fields of merit and supreme realms."
In order to cause all sentient beings to be able to skillfully enter the treasury of the bodhicitta and thereby protect and uphold it themselves;
in order to cause all sentient beings to be free from all hindrances and entanglements and to dwell securely therein;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to attain unimpeded supernormal powers and wisdom;
To cause all sentient beings to attain bodies of mastery by universally manifesting them;
to cause all sentient beings to achieve the most supreme knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) so that their universal exertion of benefit is never in vain;
and to cause all sentient beings to universally gather all categories of beings and bring them to purity.
It is for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to ultimately attain all-knowledge;
it is for the sake of causing the minds of all sentient beings to be unshakable and free from hindrance.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees delightful lands, gardens, groves, grasses, trees, flowers, fruits, famous incenses, exquisite garments, rare jewels, wealth, and various ornaments; or sees pleasant villages, towns, and settlements; or sees the majestic power and sovereignty of kings; or sees dwellings free from all clamor and distraction—”

Having seen these things, they diligently cultivate through the wisdom of skillful means, giving rise to immeasurable, supreme, and wondrous merits. For the sake of all sentient beings, they earnestly seek wholesome dharmas with a mind free from laxity, extensively gathering all manner of goodness.

Like the great ocean, they universally cover all with inexhaustible goodness, serving as the locus upon which all wholesome dharmas rely. Through the skillful dedication of various roots of goodness, they remain free from discrimination;

they reveal immeasurable varieties of roots of goodness, and their wisdom constantly observes all sentient beings. Their minds perpetually keep in mind the realm of roots of goodness, dedicating these roots—which are equal to True Suchness—to all sentient beings without ceasing.
At that time, the bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings obtain the delightful sight of all Tathāgatas; may they see the true nature of phenomena as perfectly equal and free from attachment, becoming fully pure;
may all sentient beings behold the most delightful sight of all Tathāgatas and perform perfect offerings."
May all sentient beings be reborn in all pure Buddha-fields that are free from afflictions and most delightful;
may all sentient beings behold the delightful Dharma of all Buddhas;
and may all sentient beings always delight in protecting and upholding all the delightful practices of Bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings obtain the eye of delightful and lovable spiritual friends, seeing without obstruction;
may all sentient beings always see all delightful and lovable things, never encountering opposition;
may all sentient beings realize and attain all delightful and lovable dharmas, and diligently protect and uphold them.
May all sentient beings attain pure radiance within the delightful dharmas of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings cultivate the bodhisattva’s mind capable of relinquishing all that is dear and cherished;
may all sentient beings attain fearlessness and be able to expound all delightful dharmas.
May all sentient beings attain the most delightful and profound samādhis of all bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings attain the most delightful dhāraṇī-gates of all bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings attain the most delightful wisdom of skillful observation of all bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings be able to manifest the most delightful and sovereign spiritual powers of a bodhisattva;
may all sentient beings be able to proclaim the most delightful, profound, and wondrous Dharma within the great assemblies of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings be able to skillfully reveal and expound upon the most delightful distinctions of its phrases.
May all sentient beings always be able to give rise to the most deeply cherished and joyful impartial great compassion;
may all sentient beings, in every thought-moment, give rise to the most deeply cherished and joyful mind of great enlightenment, constantly causing their faculties to be joyful and delighted;
may all sentient beings be able to enter the most deeply cherished and joyful families of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings attain the practice of delightful subduing, subduing sentient beings without ceasing;
may all sentient beings attain the most delightful and inexhaustible eloquence of the Bodhisattvas to expound all dharmas;
may all sentient beings, throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons, abide in all delightful worlds to transform and teach sentient beings with minds free from weariness.
May all sentient beings, through immeasurable skillful means, be able to universally awaken to and enter the most delightful Dharma-gates of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain delightful and unimpeded skillful means, knowing that all phenomena have no fundamental root;
may all sentient beings attain the delightful limit of freedom from desire, knowing that all phenomena are ultimately non-dual, and severing all hindrances.
May all sentient beings attain the delightful limit of freedom from craving and know the equal and true reality of all phenomena;
may all sentient beings fully perfect all the most delightful and non-conceptual dharmas of the bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings attain the diamond-treasury mind of diligence and accomplish the delightful path to omniscience.
May all sentient beings possess delightful and unimpeded roots of goodness, subduing all enemies that are the afflictions;
may all sentient beings attain the delightful gateway to omniscience and universally manifest perfect enlightenment throughout the world.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas cultivate these various roots of goodness, they attain the light of wisdom and are taken into the care of spiritual friends. The sun of the Tathāgata’s wisdom shines brightly upon their minds, forever extinguishing the darkness of ignorance;

they diligently practice the True Dharma, enter into all intellectual activities, skillfully study the stages of wisdom, and distribute their roots of goodness throughout the Dharma-realm, dedicating them through wisdom."

They exhaust the very source and bottom of all bodhisattvas' roots of goodness, and through wisdom they enter deeply into the ocean of great skillful means, accomplishing immeasurable and vast roots of goodness.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"I shall not be attached to the world, nor shall I grasp at sentient beings;
my mind shall be pure, without any point of dependence."
Maintaining right mindfulness of all phenomena, they are free from discriminatory views;
they do not abandon the sovereign wisdom of all Buddhas, nor do they contravene the gate of right dedication of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
they accord with all impartial and true Dharma, do not destroy the true marks of the Tathāgata, and contemplate the three periods of time as equal, being devoid of the mark of a sentient being.

They skillfully follow the Buddha-way and skillfully expound the Dharma; they deeply comprehend its meaning and enter the most supreme stage; they awaken to the true Dharma, their wisdom is perfected, and their faith and delight are firm and steadfast;

though they skillfully cultivate right action, they know the nature of karma is empty; they understand that all phenomena are like illusions and transformations, knowing that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature;
they contemplate all meanings and various practices, conforming to worldly conventions of speech without any attachment.

They eliminate all causes and conditions for attachment and know the principle of reality as it is; they contemplate that the nature of all phenomena is entirely quiescent and understand that all dharmas share a single true mark, knowing that the characteristics of all phenomena do not contradict one another.
They dwell together with all bodhisattvas, practicing their path and skillfully gathering in sentient beings, entering the gates of dedication of all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present.
Their minds have no fear toward any Buddha-dharma, and through immeasurable minds, they cause all sentient beings to universally attain purity.

In the worlds of the ten directions, they do not give rise to the mind that grasps at "self" or "what belongs to self," nor do they engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any worldly phenomena.
They do not produce defiled attachment toward any sense objects, but diligently cultivate all supramundane dharmas.

Having neither grasping nor reliance toward any worldly realms, their right view regarding the profound and wondrous path is firm; they are free from all false views and have realized the true Dharma.
Just as true suchness pervades all places without limit or boundary, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it pervades all places without limit or boundary.
For example, just as true thusness has reality as its nature, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it understands that all phenomena have reality as their nature.
For example, just as true thusness constantly maintains its original nature without change, [so too is the dedication of roots of goodness].
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus: it maintains its original nature, remaining unchanged from beginning to end.
Just as True Suchness takes the absence of intrinsic nature in all phenomena as its own nature, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it realizes that the absence of intrinsic nature in all phenomena constitutes its own nature.

For example, just as true thusness (tathatā) has "signlessness" as its characteristic, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it understands all phenomena to have signlessness as their characteristic.
For example, just as if there were one who attained true thusness, they would never regress; so it is with this dedication.
The dedication of roots of goodness is also like this: whoever attains it shall never regress from the teachings of all Buddhas.
Just as True Suchness is the sphere of activity for all Buddhas, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness the sphere of activity for all Tathāgatas.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) transcends the characteristics of objects yet serves as their object;
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā), which transcends the characteristics of objects yet serves as the perfected sphere of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
For example, just as true thusness (tathatā) is able to establish all things,
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā), which is able to establish all sentient beings.
For example, just as true thusness is by nature ever-conforming;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus: throughout all future eons, it continues uninterrupted in accordance with reality.
Just as True Suchness cannot be measured, so too the dedication of roots of goodness is equal to the realm of empty space and the minds of all sentient beings, such that no one can measure it.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) pervades all things, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: in a single instant, it universally encompasses the entire dharma-realm (dharmadhātu).
Just as true thusness is eternally abiding and inexhaustible;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus, ultimately inexhaustible.
Just as true suchness has no counterpart, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it is universally able to fulfill all Buddha-dharmas, having no counterpart.

Just as the nature of true suchness (tathatā) is firm and solid, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā); its nature is firm and solid, and it cannot be thwarted by any afflictions or delusions.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is indestructible,
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā), which no sentient being can destroy.
Just as true thusness has illumination as its essence;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus, having universal illumination as its nature.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is omnipresent, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it is entirely present in all places.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) pervades all times,
so too does the dedication of roots of goodness pervade all times.
Just as true thusness is by nature eternally pure;
The dedication of roots of goodness is also like this: while abiding in the world, its essence remains pure.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is unimpeded regarding all phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it circulates through all things without any obstruction.
For example, just as true thusness (tathatā) serves as the eye for all phenomena,
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā), which can serve as the eye for all sentient beings.
For example, just as true thusness is by nature free from weariness;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise so: one practices all the various deeds of a bodhisattva without ever experiencing weariness or fatigue.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is profound in its essential nature, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness profound in its nature.

For example, just as true thusness (tathatā) has not a single thing within it, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā): one understands its nature to have not a single thing within it.
For example, just as the nature of true thusness is not something that appears;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus: its essence is subtle and difficult to perceive.
Just as true suchness is free from all defilements and obscurations, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; with the eye of wisdom purified, it is free from all veils of ignorance.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) is by nature without equal, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā): it accomplishes all bodhisattva practices in a manner that is supreme and peerless.
For example, just as the essence of true thusness (tathatā) is quiescent, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it is well able to accord with the dharma of quiescence.
For example, just as true thusness has no root;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus: it is able to enter all phenomena that are without foundation.
Just as the essence of true suchness (*tathatā*) is boundless, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it purifies sentient beings, the number of whom is boundless.
Just as the nature of true thusness (tathatā) is free from attachment,
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā), being ultimately detached from all attachments.
Just as true thusness is without obstruction;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise: it eliminates all worldly obstacles.
Just as true suchness is not within the sphere of worldly activity, so too the dedication of roots of goodness is not something that can be practiced by any in the world.
For example, just as the essence of true thusness (tathatā) has no abiding;
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā), for all of birth and death is not a place of abiding.
For example, just as the nature of true thusness performs no action; [so too is the dedication of roots of goodness].
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise so: all that has been done is entirely relinquished.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) abides in its essential nature, so too does the dedication of roots of goodness abide in reality.
Just as true thusness is universally associated with all phenomena,
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness universally associated with the hearing and cultivation practiced by all bodhisattvas.
Just as true thusness is by nature eternally equal among all phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it cultivates the practice of equality toward all worlds.
Just as true thusness is not separate from all phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it does not abandon the world until the end of the future.
Just as true thusness is ultimately inexhaustible among all phenomena;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus: it is inexhaustible in its dedication toward all sentient beings.
Just as True Suchness (tathatā) is not in conflict with any phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness not in conflict with any of the Buddha-dharmas of the three periods of time.
Just as true thusness universally encompasses all phenomena,
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness, for it fully encompasses the roots of goodness of all sentient beings.
Just as true thusness shares the same essential nature as all phenomena;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise so: it shares the same single essence as the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is never separate from all phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it encompasses and sustains all mundane and supramundane dharmas.
Just as true thusness cannot be eclipsed, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; nothing in all the worlds can eclipse it.
Just as true thusness is unshakable, so too is this dedication.
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus: no demonic activities whatsoever can shake it.

Just as the nature of true suchness (*tathatā*) is free from defilement and turbidity, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: in practicing the bodhisattva path, there is no defilement or turbidity.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) is without change or alteration, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā); out of compassion for sentient beings, the mind remains without change or alteration.
Just as true thusness is inexhaustible;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus; it cannot be exhausted by any worldly phenomena.
Just as true suchness is by nature eternally awakened, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness, for it is universally able to awaken to all dharmas.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) cannot be lost or destroyed, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā): having generated supreme aspirations for all sentient beings, they are never lost or destroyed.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) can provide great illumination, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā): it illuminates all worlds with the light of great wisdom.
Just as true thusness is ineffable;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus, beyond what can be expressed by any words.
Just as True Suchness sustains all worlds,
so too does the dedication of roots of goodness sustain all the practices of Bodhisattvas.
Just as true thusness conforms to worldly discourse,
so too does the dedication of roots of goodness conform to all discourse of wisdom.
Just as true thusness pervades all phenomena;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise thus: it manifests great supernormal powers and achieves equal and perfect enlightenment throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions.
Just as true suchness is without discrimination, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; within all worlds, it is free from any discrimination.
Just as true thusness pervades all bodies,
so too does the dedication of roots of goodness pervade the infinite bodies within the lands of the ten directions.
Just as the essential nature of true thusness is unborn;
The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise so: through skillful means it manifests birth, yet there is nothing born.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is omnipresent, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness;
throughout the Buddha-fields of the ten directions and the three periods of time, it universally manifests spiritual powers, being everywhere present.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is omnipresent throughout the night, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; throughout every night, it radiates great light and performs the work of a Buddha.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) pervades all days, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:

it causes all sentient beings throughout the day to behold the Buddha’s spiritual transformations, hear him expound the wheel of non-retrogression, and become free from defilement and pure, so that none pass their time in vain.
Just as true suchness pervades both the half-month and the full month, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
through skillful means, it attains mastery over all temporal sequences in the world, knowing every moment within a single thought-instant.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) pervades all years, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it abides through immeasurable eons, becoming clearly manifest and matured, causing all faculties to be brought to full perfection.

Just as true suchness pervades the kalpas of formation and destruction, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it abides through all kalpas, pure and untainted, teaching and transforming sentient beings until they are all rendered pure.

Just as true suchness extends to the end of the future, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: extending to the end of the future, one cultivates all the pure and wondrous practices of a bodhisattva, fulfilling great vows without ever turning back.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) pervasively abides throughout the three periods of time, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it causes all sentient beings to see the Buddhas of the three periods of time in a single instant, never for even a single thought-moment being separated from them.
Just as true thusness pervades all places, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it transcends the triple world, circulates everywhere, and attains complete mastery.

Just as true thusness abides in both existence and non-existence, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it thoroughly realizes that all phenomena of existence and non-existence are ultimately pure.

Just as the essence of true suchness (*tathatā*) is pure by nature, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; through skillful means, it can gather the factors conducive to enlightenment and purify all bodhisattva practices.
Just as the nature of true thusness (tathatā) is luminously pure, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it causes all bodhisattvas to attain a mind of luminous purity through samādhi.

Just as the essence of true suchness (*tathatā*) is by nature stainless, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā*): it remains far removed from all defilements and fulfills all pure intentions.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) is devoid of self and what belongs to a self, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; with a mind purified of self and what belongs to a self, it fills the buddha-lands of the ten directions.

Just as the nature of true suchness (*tathatā*) is equal in its essence, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it attains the equality of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), illuminating all phenomena and departing from the cataracts of ignorance.
Just as true thusness transcends all measure and number, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:

it dwells together with the great power of the Dharma-treasury of the vehicle of omniscience that transcends measure and number, giving rise to vast clouds of Dharma throughout all worlds in the ten directions.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) dwells in equanimity, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā): it gives rise to all bodhisattva practices and dwells with equality upon the path to omniscience (sarvajñatā).
Just as true thusness (tathatā) pervades and dwells within the realms of all sentient beings, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it fulfills unimpeded omniscience (sarvākārajñatā), manifesting before all beings throughout the realms of sentient beings.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is without discrimination and universally abides within the wisdom of all sounds, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it is fully endowed with the wisdom of all speech and sounds, able to universally manifest various types of speech and sound to instruct and reveal them to sentient beings.
Just as true thusness is eternally detached from the world,
so too is the dedication of roots of goodness, universally causing all sentient beings to transcend the world forever.
Just as true thusness is vast in its essential nature;

The dedication of roots of goodness is likewise: it is able to receive and uphold the vast Buddha-dharma of the past, future, and present, never forgetting or losing it, while diligently cultivating all the practices of a bodhisattva.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) is without interruption or cessation, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; desiring to establish all sentient beings upon the ground of great wisdom, one practices the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout all eons without interruption or cessation.

Just as true suchness (*tathatā*) is vast in its essential nature and pervades all phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā*); it is pure mindfulness without obstruction, universally encompassing all vast Dharma-gates.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) universally encompasses all categories of phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it realizes immeasurable varieties of wisdom and cultivates the authentic, sublime practices of all bodhisattvas.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) is free from all grasping and attachment, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it involves no grasping at any phenomena whatsoever, extinguishing all worldly attachments and causing universal purity.
Just as the essence of true suchness is immovable, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: abiding securely in the perfect conduct and vows of Samantabhadra, it is ultimately unshakable.
Just as true thusness is the realm of the Buddhas, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it causes all sentient beings to fulfill the realm of all-encompassing great wisdom and extinguishes the realm of afflictions, rendering it entirely pure.
Just as true thusness cannot be overcome, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it cannot be overcome by any of the activities of Māras or the heterodox arguments of outside paths.
For example, true thusness (tathatā) is neither something that can be cultivated nor something that cannot be cultivated;
the dedication of roots of goodness is likewise: having abandoned all conceptual constructions and attachments, one makes no distinction between cultivation and non-cultivation.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) never regresses or abandons anything, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: one constantly beholds all Buddhas, gives rise to the bodhicitta, and is adorned by great vows, never regressing or abandoning them.
Just as true thusness universally encompasses all worldly speech and sounds, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it enables one to attain the supernatural wisdom of all distinct forms of speech and sound, and to universally produce all manner of diverse expressions.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) has no longing for any phenomena, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it causes all sentient beings to mount the vehicle of Samantabhadra and attain liberation, such that they have no craving or seeking for any phenomena.

Just as true thusness abides in all stages, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: it causes all sentient beings to abandon the stages of the world and abide in the stage of wisdom, adorning themselves with the practices of Samantabhadra.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) is without interruption, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; having attained fearlessness regarding all phenomena, one preaches everywhere in accordance with the various sounds of beings, without interruption.
Just as true suchness is free from all outflows, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it causes all sentient beings to achieve the wisdom of dharmas, to thoroughly comprehend all phenomena, and to fulfill the untainted merits of bodhi.

Just as true thusness cannot be corrupted or disturbed by even the slightest phenomenon such that it would cease to be awakening in the slightest degree, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it universally causes all phenomena to be awakened to, its mind being immeasurable and pervading the entire dharma-realm.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) has no beginning in the past, no end in the future, and no variation in the present;

so too is the dedication of roots of goodness: for the sake of all sentient beings, one constantly gives rise anew to the bodhicitta vow, universally purifying them so that they may forever leave birth and death behind.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) is without discrimination throughout the three periods of time, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā): in the present, every thought-moment is constantly awakened, while the past and future are entirely pure.

Just as true thusness (tathatā) brings all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to fulfillment, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness (kuśalamūla-pariṇāmanā): it gives rise to all the skillful means of great vows and brings to fulfillment the vast wisdom of all Buddhas.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is ultimately pure and does not coexist with any afflictions, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness:
it can extinguish the afflictions of all sentient beings and bring to fulfillment all pure wisdom.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas dedicate in this manner, they attain equality with all Buddha-fields, because they universally adorn and purify all worlds;
they attain equality with all sentient beings, because they universally turn the unobstructed wheel of Dharma for them."
They attain the equality of all bodhisattvas, because they universally give rise to the vows for omniscience;
they attain the equality of all buddhas, because they observe that the essence of all buddhas is non-dual;
they attain the equality of all phenomena, because they universally know that the nature of all phenomena is unchanging.
They attain equality with all worlds, because they skillfully understand all paths of language through the wisdom of expedient means;
they attain equality with all bodhisattva practices, because they dedicate all roots of goodness they plant toward enlightenment;
they attain equality across all times, because they diligently cultivate the Buddha-work without interruption at any time.
They attain equality regarding the fruits of all karma, for they are entirely free from attachment to any mundane or supramundane roots of goodness;
they attain equality regarding the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas, for they manifest the deeds of a Buddha in accordance with the world.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the eighth dedication, the Dedication of the Mark of True Suchness.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this dedication, they realize immeasurable gates of pure Dharma and are able to let out the great lion’s roar of the Tathāgata, sovereign and fearless.”
Through skillful means, they teach and bring to maturity immeasurable bodhisattvas, never resting at any time;
they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect body, with a single body pervading all worlds;
they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect voice, with a single sound awakening all sentient beings.
They attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect power, which can universally contain all lands within a single pore;
they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect spiritual penetrations, placing all sentient beings within a single atom;
they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect liberation, manifesting the realms of all Buddhas and attaining equal and perfect enlightenment within the body of a single sentient being.
They attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect samādhis, wherein within a single samādhi they can universally manifest all samādhis;

they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect eloquence, such that by speaking a single phrase of Dharma, it remains inexhaustible until the end of the future, completely removing the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings;

they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable and perfect mastery over sentient beings, possessing the ten powers of a Buddha, and manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment throughout the entire realm of sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is how a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness in accordance with the mark of True Suchness.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The Bodhisattva’s aspiration is ever-abiding; with firm right mindfulness, he is free from delusion.
His mind is supple and always cool, as he accumulates boundless meritorious deeds.”
The Bodhisattva is humble and compliant, never acting in opposition; all his aspirations are entirely pure.
Having attained the great radiance of wisdom, he is well able to illuminate and understand all karmic actions.
The Bodhisattva contemplates the vastness of karma, Its manifold distinctions most rare and wondrous;
Resolutely practicing without regression, He thereby brings benefit to all living beings.

The various distinctions of karma are immeasurable in kind; the Bodhisattva diligently cultivates them all, acting in accordance with sentient beings without contradicting their inclinations, universally causing their minds to become pure and giving rise to joy.
Having ascended the stage of the Honored One, the Tamer of Men, Free from all feverish afflictions and with an unimpeded mind,
Fully proficient in both the Dharma and its meaning, He applies himself with even greater diligence for the benefit of all living beings.
The various virtuous practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas, Infinite, innumerable, and of manifold distinctions—
Knowing them all through analytical wisdom, They dedicate them for the benefit of all living beings.
Constantly observing with sublime wisdom, one realizes the ultimate, vast, and true principle;
severing all states of existence without exception, one skillfully dedicates [merit] in accordance with that suchness.
Just as true suchness pervades all things, so too does it universally encompass all worlds;
with this mind, the bodhisattva dedicates merit, causing all sentient beings to be free from attachment.
The Bodhisattva’s power of aspiration pervades all things, Just as True Suchness is nowhere absent;
Whether seen or unseen, mindfulness is omnipresent, All of which is dedicated through merit.

Abiding through the night, one also abides through the day; Abiding for half a month or a full month, and likewise for years or eons— Such is the nature of True Suchness (tathatā), and such too is its activity.
All that exists in the three times and all buddha-fields, All sentient beings and all phenomena—
Abiding within them yet dwelling nowhere, I dedicate through such practice.
Just as the true nature (*tathatā*) is the primordial self-nature, so does the bodhisattva generate the great mind;
wherever true nature resides, there is nowhere it is not present—by means of such practice, one dedicates [merit].
Just as the true nature (*tathatā*) is the primordial self-nature, wherein not a single dharma has ever existed,
and this very lack of self-nature is the true nature— thus one dedicates through such karma.
As is the characteristic of *tathatā*, so too is karma; as is the nature of *tathatā*, so too is karma.
Just as the nature of *tathatā* is fundamentally real, karma is likewise identical to *tathatā*.
Just as true thusness (tathatā) is without limit, so too karma is without limit;
yet within it there is no binding attachment, and for this reason, this karma attains purity.
Such wise and true sons of the Buddha, firm in their vows and unshakable,
through the power of their wisdom skillfully attain thorough penetration and enter the treasury of the expedient means of all Buddhas.
The Dharma King has awakened to the true Dharma; therein he is neither attached nor bound.
Thus, with a sovereign mind free from obstruction, he has never seen a single dharma arise.
The deeds performed by the Tathāgata’s Dharma-body appear to all in the world according to their respective forms;
yet he teaches that the characteristics of all phenomena are signless—to know such characteristics is to know the Dharma.
The Bodhisattva abides in this inconceivable state; within it, thought cannot be exhausted.
Entering this realm of the inconceivable, both thought and non-thought are utterly stilled.
Contemplating the nature of all phenomena in this way, One thoroughly understands the distinctions among all karmas;
All grasping at a self is extinguished, And one abides in merit, immovable.
All karmic fruits and retributions of the Bodhisattva are sealed by inexhaustible wisdom;
thus, their inexhaustible self-nature is exhausted, and therefore they cease through inexhaustible skillful means.
The Bodhisattva contemplates that the mind does not exist externally, nor can it be found within;
knowing that the nature of the mind is non-existent, he realizes that both self and dharmas are forever extinguished and detached.
Those sons of the Buddhas know thus: the nature of all phenomena is eternally empty and quiescent;
there is not a single phenomenon that can be created, for they have awakened to non-self just like the Buddhas.
Fully understanding that all worlds are entirely equal in nature to True Suchness (tathatā), one perceives this inconceivable characteristic;
such a person is then able to know the dharma of signlessness (animitta).
If one can abide in this profound Dharma, Constantly delighting in the practice of the bodhisattva path,
Desiring to benefit all living beings, Adorned with great vows, one shall never retreat.
Thus they transcend the world, Not giving rise to the deluded discriminations of birth and death;
Thoroughly understanding that the mind is like an illusion, They diligently cultivate all practices to deliver all sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva observes the world with right mindfulness: All things arise from the conditions of karma;
Desiring to deliver them, he cultivates all practices, Universally gathering those in the three realms without exception.
Knowing that the various differences among sentient beings are all discriminations of perception and mental formations,
one observes them with complete clarity, yet does not destroy the nature of all phenomena.
The wise one understands all Buddha-dharmas And dedicates through such practice;
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, They cause them to correctly contemplate the true Dharma.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty, and Volume Thirty-One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Twenty-five, Part Nine: The Dedication of the Ninety [Verses], "The Unattached, Unbound, and Liberated Dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the unattached, unbound, and liberated dedication of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?"
“O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to a mind of deep respect toward all roots of goodness.
That is to say:”
One gives rise to a mind of reverence for transcending birth and death;
one gives rise to a mind of reverence for gathering all roots of goodness;
one gives rise to a mind of reverence for aspiring toward all roots of goodness.
One gives rise to a mind of reverence toward the repentance of all transgressions and karmic deeds;
one gives rise to a mind of reverence toward the sympathetic rejoicing in roots of goodness;
one gives rise to a mind of reverence toward the prostration and veneration of all Buddhas.
