They give rise to a mind of reverence when joining their palms in respectful salutation;
they give rise to a mind of reverence when prostrating before stupas and temples;
they give rise to a mind of reverence when exhorting the Buddha to preach the Dharma.
Regarding these various roots of goodness, they give rise to respect for all of them, and accord with them through patient acceptance.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give rise to respect for those roots of goodness and accord with them through patient acceptance, they experience ultimate joy and possess firm faith and understanding."
Abiding in peace for oneself and establishing others in peace;
diligently cultivating non-attachment and freely accumulating merit;
achieving supreme aspiration and delight, and dwelling within the realm of the Tathāgata.
Their power increases, and they attain full knowledge and vision.
They dedicate all roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, may I accomplish the physical karma of Samantabhadra."
With a mind free from attachment, bondage, and liberation, one purifies the verbal karma of Samantabhadra.
With a mind free from attachment, bondage, and liberation, one perfects the mental karma of Samantabhadra.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they initiate the vast and great diligence of Samantabhadra.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they are fully endowed with the *dhāraṇī* gate of the unobstructed voice of Samantabhadra; its sound is vast and pervasive throughout the ten directions.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they are fully endowed with the Samantabhadra-dhāraṇī-door of seeing all Buddhas, and constantly behold all Buddhas of the ten directions.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they achieve the dhāraṇī-door of comprehending all sounds, and in harmony with all voices, they preach immeasurable teachings.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the *dhāraṇī* gate of Samantabhadra’s abiding throughout all eons, universally cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva throughout the ten directions.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they achieve the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; within the body of a single sentient being, they manifest the cultivation of all bodhisattva practices, continuing without interruption throughout all future eons.
As it is with the body of one sentient being, so it is with the bodies of all sentient beings.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; they universally enter all assemblies of bodhimandas and universally appear before all Buddhas to cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra Buddha and manifest it within a single gateway for unspeakably unspeakable eons without exhaustion, causing all sentient beings to attain awakening and entry.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra Buddha, manifesting through various gateways for unspeakably unspeakable eons without end, causing all sentient beings to attain awakening and entry, while their bodies appear universally before all Buddhas.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; in every thought-moment, they cause unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings to abide in the wisdom of the ten powers, their minds never wearying.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; within the bodies of all sentient beings, they manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas, causing all sentient beings to abide in the conduct of Samantabhadra.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; within the speech of each and every sentient being, they produce the speech of all sentient beings, causing every single sentient being to abide in the stage of omniscience.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; within the body of each and every sentient being, they universally accommodate the bodies of all sentient beings, causing them all to perceive themselves as having accomplished the Buddha-body.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one accomplishes the sovereign power of Samantabhadra, such that one can adorn all worlds throughout the ten directions with a single flower.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; they emit a great sound that pervades the entire Dharma-realm, reaching all Buddha-lands, and thereby gather in and subdue all sentient beings.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; throughout all unspeakably unspeakable eons until the end of the future, in every moment of thought, they are able to universally enter all worlds, adorning them according to their thoughts through the spiritual power of the Buddhas.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra; throughout all kalpas remaining until the end of the future, they are constantly able to enter all worlds and manifest the attainment of Buddhahood and appearance in the world.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the conduct of Samantabhadra; with a single light, they universally illumine all worlds throughout the entirety of space.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the conduct of Samantabhadra, attain immeasurable wisdom, possess all supernatural powers, and proclaim various teachings.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the conduct of Samantabhadra and enter the immeasurable supernatural wisdom of the Tathāgatas, which exhausts all kalpas.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the conduct of Samantabhadra and abide in the presence of all Tathāgatas throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
by the spiritual power of the Buddhas, they cultivate all practices of Bodhisattvas, never experiencing weariness or fatigue in their physical, verbal, or mental actions.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one accomplishes the conduct of Samantabhadra; not contradicting the ultimate meaning and not violating the Dharma, one’s speech is pure and one delights in inexhaustible eloquence;
one teaches and tames all sentient beings, causing them to attain the unsurpassed bodhi of all Buddhas.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra; upon entering a single dharma-gate, one emits immeasurable light, illuminating all inconceivable dharma-gates.
Just as with this one dharma-gate, so too does one penetrate all dharma-gates without obstruction, ultimately attaining the stage of omniscience.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they abide in the conduct of Bodhisattvas and attain mastery over all phenomena, reaching the further shore of Samantabhadra’s adornments;
in each and every realm, they observe and penetrate them with omniscience, yet omniscience itself is never exhausted.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, beginning from this life until the end of the future, they abide in the conduct of Samantabhadra, never ceasing, attaining all-knowledge, awakening to the ineffably ineffable true Dharma, reaching the ultimate in all phenomena, and remaining free from delusion.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the deeds of Samantabhadra; possessing mastery in skillful means, they attain the radiance of the Dharma and clearly perceive, without obstruction, all the practices performed by Bodhisattvas.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra and attain all-knowledge of skillful means, knowing all skillful means, namely:

immeasurable skillful means; inconceivable skillful means; the skillful means of bodhisattvas; the skillful means of omniscience; the skillful means for the discipline and conversion of all bodhisattvas; the skillful means for turning the immeasurable wheel of Dharma; the skillful means regarding ineffable times; the skillful means for expounding various teachings; the skillful means of the boundless treasury of fearlessness; and the skillful means for expounding all dharmas without exception.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they abide in the conduct of Samantabhadra and accomplish physical karma, causing all sentient beings who see them to rejoice and never give rise to slander;
they resolve upon bodhicitta, never regressing, and reach ultimate purity.

With a mind free from attachment, bondage, and liberation, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and attain the pure wisdom of the languages of all sentient beings; their every utterance is fully adorned, responding universally to sentient beings and causing them all to rejoice.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they abide in the conduct of Samantabhadra, establish supreme resolve, and possess a pure mind; having attained vast supernormal powers and vast wisdom, they go everywhere to all vast worlds, vast lands, and vast assemblies of sentient beings, to proclaim the unspeakably vast Dharma of all Tathāgatas—the treasury of vast adornments and perfect fulfillment.

With a mind free from attachment, bondage, and liberation, they fulfill the practices and vows of Samantabhadra’s dedication; they attain the pure body, pure mind, and pure understanding of all Buddhas, encompassing the merits of the Buddhas and abiding in the realm of the Buddhas. With the seal of wisdom shining universally, they manifest the pure karma of Bodhisattvas, skillfully entering all differentiated phrases and meanings, and displaying the vast sovereignty of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, manifesting perfect enlightenment for the sake of all sentient beings.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they diligently cultivate the practices and vows of Samantabhadra’s faculties, thereby attaining: the faculty of keen intelligence; the faculty of disciplined compliance; the faculty of mastery over all dharmas; the inexhaustible faculty; the faculty of diligent cultivation of all roots of goodness; the faculty of equality regarding the spheres of all Buddhas; the faculty of great vigor for receiving the prediction of non-retrogression from all Bodhisattvas; the faculty of the adamantine realm of all Buddha-dharmas; the faculty of the adamantine flame of the light of wisdom of all Tathāgatas; the faculty of sovereign discernment of all faculties; the faculty of establishing immeasurable sentient beings in omniscience; the boundlessly vast faculty; the faculty of total perfection; and the pure, unimpeded faculty.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and attain the spiritual powers of all Bodhisattvas, namely:

the power of immeasurable and vast strength; the power of immeasurable sovereign wisdom; the power to manifest universally in all Buddha-fields without moving their bodies; the power of unimpeded, uninterrupted sovereignty; the power to gather all Buddha-fields and place them within a single location; the power of a single body pervading all Buddha-fields; the power of the playful sport of unimpeded liberation; the power of sovereign mastery in a single thought-moment without action; the power of abiding in the natureless and the non-reliant; and the power to sequentially establish unspeakable worlds within a single pore, traveling throughout the Dharma-realm to the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas and manifesting to all sentient beings so that they may all enter the gate of great wisdom.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they enter the gateway of Samantabhadra and give rise to the practices of a bodhisattva. With sovereign wisdom, in a single thought-moment, they universally enter immeasurable buddha-lands; a single body accommodates immeasurable buddha-fields, and they attain the wisdom capable of adorning and purifying buddha-lands. Constantly observing and beholding boundless buddha-lands with wisdom, they never again give rise to the mind of the two vehicles.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the skillful practices of Samantabhadra, enter the realm of wisdom, and are born into the family of the Tathāgatas. Abiding in the path of the bodhisattvas, they are endowed with unspeakably unspeakable, immeasurable, inconceivable, and supreme minds; they carry out immeasurable vows without ever resting, and fully comprehend all dharma-realms throughout the three periods of time.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the pure dharma-gate of Samantabhadra; within a space the size of a single hair-tip, they fully contain all unspeakably unspeakable lands throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm, causing them all to be clearly seen;
as it is with the space of one hair-tip, so it is for every single hair-tip throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of space.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the profound mind and skillful means of Samantabhadra; within a single thought-moment, they manifest the thoughts of a single sentient being throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons, and in this manner, they manifest the thoughts of all sentient beings throughout as many eons as there are.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they enter the dedication of Samantabhadra and practice the stage of skillful means; within a single body, they are able to fully contain as many bodies as are unspeakably unspeakable throughout the entire Dharma-realm, yet the realm of sentient beings neither increases nor decreases.
As it is with one body, so it is with all bodies throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the skillful means of Samantabhadra’s great vows; they abandon all inversions of perception, mind, and view, and universally enter the realm of all Buddhas.
They constantly behold the Buddhas’ pure Dharma-bodies, equal to the realm of space, adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, and possessing sovereign spiritual powers.

They constantly use wondrous voices to reveal and expound the teachings without obstruction or interruption, causing those who hear them to receive and uphold them as taught, while realizing that within the Tathāgata’s body there is nothing to be grasped.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and abide in the stages of a bodhisattva.

In a single thought-moment, they enter all worlds—namely: worlds turned upward, worlds turned downward, and unspeakably unspeakable worlds throughout the entire vast net of the ten directions. By means of the skillful methods of Indra’s net, they universally discern the entire dharma-realm; they enter a single world by means of various worlds; they enter a single world by means of unspeakably unspeakable and immeasurable worlds; they enter a single world by means of the immeasurable worlds established within the entire dharma-realm; and they enter a single world by means of the immeasurable worlds established throughout the entire realm of empty space, yet without destroying the characteristics of their established forms, causing them all to be clearly seen.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; they receive the empowerment of the Buddhas and, within a single thought-moment, enter the stage of skillful means, fully accomplishing and abiding in the jewel of wisdom of all practices;
they are able to thoroughly understand all conceptualizations, namely:

the conceptualization of sentient beings, the conceptualization of phenomena, the conceptualization of lands, the conceptualization of directions, the conceptualization of Buddhas, the conceptualization of worlds, and the conceptualization of karma.
The perception of thought, the perception of mental formations, the perception of elements, the perception of liberation, the perception of faculties, the perception of time,

the perception of sustenance, the perception of affliction, the perception of purification, the perception of maturation, the perception of seeing the Buddha, the perception of turning the wheel of Dharma,
the perception of understanding the Dharma upon hearing it, the perception of discipline, the perception of the immeasurable, the perception of renunciation, and the perception of the lineage.

The perception of the earth, the perception of the immeasurable earth, the perception of the Bodhisattva’s thorough knowledge, the perception of the Bodhisattva’s cultivation, the perception of the Bodhisattva’s samādhi,
the perception of the Bodhisattva’s emergence from samādhi, the perception of the Bodhisattva’s formation, the perception of the Bodhisattva’s destruction,
the perception of the Bodhisattva’s disappearance, the perception of the Bodhisattva’s birth, and the perception of the Bodhisattva’s liberation.
The bodhisattva’s perception of mastery, the perception of sustaining, the perception of the bodhisattva’s sphere of activity, the perception of the formation and destruction of kalpas,
the perception of light, the perception of darkness, the perception of day, the perception of night, the perception of the variations of half-months, months, seasons, and years,
the perception of going, the perception of coming, the perception of staying, the perception of sitting, and the perception of sleeping.
Perceptions and conceptualizations— such perceptions as these— one can fully comprehend within a single thought-moment,
yet remains free from all perceptions and without discrimination;
having severed all hindrances, one is without any attachment.

The wisdom of all Buddhas fills their minds; the roots of goodness for all Buddha-dharmas grow within them; they share the same body as all Tathāgatas; they are embraced by all Buddhas; they are stainless and pure; and they follow the cultivation and study of all Buddha-dharmas to reach the further shore.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra for the sake of all sentient beings, giving birth to the jewel of great wisdom. Within each and every thought, they know infinite minds; according to their bases, their discriminations, their dispositions, their actions, their karmic functions, their appearances, and their reflections, they clearly perceive all their various differences without exception.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they accomplish the jewel of wisdom of Samantabhadra’s great vows; within a single location, they know immeasurable and ineffable locations;
as it is with one location, so it is with all locations.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the stages of wisdom and the practices of Samantabhadra; within a single action, they are able to know immeasurable, unspeakably unspeakable actions, clearly perceiving and seeing how each such action is produced by various conditions;
as it is with one action, so it is with all actions.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one cultivates the wisdom of Samantabhadra that knows all phenomena; within a single phenomenon, one knows the ineffable and unspeakable phenomena, and within all phenomena, one knows the single phenomenon.
Thus, these various phenomena are each distinct, yet without obstruction, without contradiction, and without attachment.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they abide in the conduct of a bodhisattva and attain the unhindered ear-faculty of Samantabhadra; within a single utterance, they know the unspeakably unspeakable varieties of infinite and boundless sounds without any attachment;
as it is with one utterance, so it is with all utterances.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the wisdom of Samantabhadra, initiate the conduct of Samantabhadra, and abide in the stage of Samantabhadra; within each and every dharma, they expound unspeakably unspeakable dharmas.
These dharmas are vast, with various distinctions for teaching and gathering beings, corresponding to inconceivable skillful means.

Throughout immeasurable time and at all times, according to the inclinations and understandings of all sentient beings, and in accordance with their faculties and the timing, they preach the Dharma using the voice of a Buddha.

With a single sublime voice, they cause all the immeasurable sentient beings in the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment throughout the unspeakable paths to rejoice; in each and every Tathāgata’s realm, immeasurable Bodhisattvas fill the Dharma-realm.

Establishing supreme resolve and generating vast vision, they thoroughly comprehend all conditioned activities, abide in the stage of Samantabhadra, and according to the teachings they proclaim, are able to realize and enter them in every thought-moment. Within a single kṣaṇa, they increase immeasurable, unspeakably unspeakable masses of great wisdom.
Thus they continue to expound for as many eons as lie in the future, cultivating and perfecting vast practices equal to space in all lands.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the gates of practice for all the faculties of Samantabhadra, becoming great kings of conduct who are able, within each and every faculty, to fully know immeasurable faculties, immeasurable mental inclinations, and the wondrous practices arising from inconceivable realms.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, abiding in the great heart of dedication to the practices of Samantabhadra, they attain extremely subtle knowledge of form, extremely subtle knowledge of the body, extremely subtle knowledge of lands, extremely subtle knowledge of eons, extremely subtle knowledge of worlds, extremely subtle knowledge of directions, extremely subtle knowledge of time, extremely subtle knowledge of numbers, extremely subtle knowledge of karmic retribution, and extremely subtle knowledge of purity—all such things that are extremely subtle they are able to fully comprehend within a single thought-moment; yet their minds are not terrified, not deluded, not distracted, not scattered, not turbid, and not inferior.
Their minds are focused on a single object, well-settled in tranquil concentration, well-discriminating, and well-established.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they abide in the wisdom of bodhisattvas and cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra without weariness or fatigue. They are able to know all the subtle movements of sentient beings: the extreme subtlety of their death, the extreme subtlety of their birth, the extreme subtlety of their dwelling, the extreme subtlety of their abodes, the extreme subtlety of their categories, the extreme subtlety of their realms, the extreme subtlety of their conduct, the extreme subtlety of their grasping, and the extreme subtlety of their focal objects—all such extreme subtleties they are able to fully comprehend within a single thought-moment.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, establishing profound aspiration and joy,

one cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra and is able to know all the extremely subtle aspects of how Bodhisattvas, from their first resolve, cultivate Bodhisattva practices for the sake of all sentient beings—
the extreme subtlety of the Bodhisattva’s dwelling places, the extreme subtlety of the Bodhisattva’s supernormal powers, and the Bodhisattva’s...
The subtle wandering through immeasurable Buddha-fields; the subtle light of the Dharma of Bodhisattvas;
the subtle pure eye of Bodhisattvas; the subtle accomplishment of the supreme mind of Bodhisattvas;
the subtle visiting of the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas; and the dhāraṇī of Bodhisattvas.
The wisdom of the gates is extremely subtle; the exposition of the treasury of all eloquence from the bodhisattva’s immeasurable stages of fearlessness is extremely subtle;

the characteristics of the bodhisattva’s immeasurable samādhis are extremely subtle; the wisdom of the samādhi through which the bodhisattva beholds all Buddhas is extremely subtle; the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s profound samādhis is extremely subtle. The bodhisattva—
The wisdom of the samādhi of the great adornment of the bodhisattva is extremely subtle; the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s dharma-realm samādhi is extremely subtle;
the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s samādhi of great sovereign supernormal powers is extremely subtle;

the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s samādhi of maintaining vast conduct throughout the limits of the future is extremely subtle; and the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s production of the immeasurable... is extremely subtle.

The extremely subtle wisdom of the samādhi of differentiation; the extremely subtle wisdom of the samādhi through which Bodhisattvas are born before all Buddhas, diligently practicing offerings and never abandoning them;
the extremely subtle wisdom of the samādhi through which Bodhisattvas cultivate all that is profoundly deep, vast, and unobstructed; and the ultimate [wisdom] of all Bodhisattvas.
The stage of wisdom, the stage of sustaining practice, the stage of great spiritual powers, the stage of definitive meaning,
and the wisdom of the *vimala* (cloudless) samādhi— extremely subtle as these and all such [stages] are, he is able to fully comprehend them all.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra,
fully knowing the extreme subtlety of all bodhisattvas’ established wisdom, the extreme subtlety of the bodhisattva stages, the extreme subtlety of the bodhisattvas’ immeasurable practices,
the extreme subtlety of the bodhisattvas’ generation of resolve and dedication of merit, and the bodhisattvas’ attainment of the treasury of all Buddhas.
Exceedingly subtle is the bodhisattva’s wisdom of observation; exceedingly subtle is the bodhisattva’s power of supernatural faculties and vows;
exceedingly subtle is the bodhisattva’s samādhi of eloquent exposition; exceedingly subtle is the bodhisattva’s skillful means of mastery;
exceedingly subtle is the bodhisattva’s seal; and exceedingly subtle is the bodhisattva’s state of being in their final birth before enlightenment.
The Bodhisattva’s birth in the Tuṣita Heaven is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s dwelling in the celestial palace is extremely subtle;
the Bodhisattva’s purification of the Buddha-land is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s observation of the human realm is extremely subtle;
the Bodhisattva’s emission of great radiance is extremely subtle; and the Bodhisattva’s excellence of lineage is extremely subtle.
The assembly at the bodhisattva’s site of enlightenment is extremely subtle; the bodhisattva’s taking birth throughout all worlds is extremely subtle;
the bodhisattva’s manifesting the death of all bodies within a single body is extremely subtle;
the bodhisattva’s entering the mother’s womb is extremely subtle; the bodhisattva’s abiding in the mother’s womb is extremely subtle; the bodhisattva’s being...
The subtle manifestation by the Bodhisattva within the mother’s womb of the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment throughout the entire dharma-realm;
the subtle manifestation by the Bodhisattva within the mother’s womb of all the spiritual powers of all Buddhas;
the subtle manifestation by the Bodhisattva of the event of his birth; and the subtle wisdom of the Bodhisattva’s seven steps as he strides like a lion.

The Bodhisattva’s skillful means in manifesting residence within a royal palace is extremely subtle; his renunciation of the world and cultivation of practices for self-discipline is extremely subtle;
his sitting beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment is extremely subtle;
and his defeat of the hosts of Māra and attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is extremely subtle—just as [it is].
The arrival at and sitting upon the Bodhi-seat, emitting great radiance that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, is extremely subtle;
the Tathāgata’s manifestation of immeasurable supernatural transformations is extremely subtle; the Tathāgata’s lion’s roar of Great Nirvāṇa is extremely subtle;
the Tathāgata’s subduing of all sentient beings without any obstruction is extremely subtle; the Tathāgata’s... [is] not... [extremely subtle].
The power of mastery over thought is as subtle as the vajra-like bodhicitta;
the Tathāgata’s universal mindfulness and protection of all worldly realms is extremely subtle;

the Tathāgata’s universal performance of buddha-works in all worlds throughout all future kalpas without cessation is extremely subtle; and the Tathāgata’s unimpeded spiritual power is [extremely subtle].

The subtle subtlety of pervading the entire dharma-realm; the subtle subtlety of the Tathāgata universally manifesting as a Buddha in all worlds throughout the entirety of space to tame sentient beings;
the subtle subtlety of the Tathāgata manifesting immeasurable Buddha-bodies from within a single Buddha-body;
and the subtle subtlety of the Tathāgata abiding at the site of enlightenment throughout the three periods of past, future, and present.
Their wisdom is exceedingly subtle—they are able to fully comprehend all such subtleties;
they have attained purity and can universally manifest throughout all worlds;
in every thought-moment, their wisdom increases, becoming perfect and non-regressive.
Skillfully employing expedient means, they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva without ceasing;

they achieve the stage of Samantabhadra’s dedication, are endowed with all the merits of the Tathāgatas, and never weary of or abandon the conduct of a bodhisattva; they give rise to the manifest realm of a bodhisattva;
their immeasurable expedients are entirely pure, as they universally desire to bring peace and security to all sentient beings.

Cultivating the bodhisattva practices, they achieve the stages of great majestic power of the bodhisattvas; they attain the aspirations and desires of the minds of all bodhisattvas and obtain the gate of the adamantine banner dedication; they give birth to the treasuries of all merits within the dharma-realm and are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas;

they enter the profound and wondrous dharma-gates of the bodhisattvas and expound the meaning of all that is true; they possess skillful mastery of the Dharma without error or loss, and they give rise to great vows never to abandon sentient beings;
within a single thought-moment, they fully know the treasury of all minds and the realms beyond the mind, manifesting the arising of the mind from that which is not mind.

Distant from all verbal expression and dwelling securely in wisdom, they practice the same conduct as all bodhisattvas; through the power of mastery, they manifest the attainment of the Buddha-way, remaining constantly without rest until the end of the future.

Throughout the kalpas of all sentient beings in every world, which are established by the conceptual speech of deluded thoughts, they are able to manifest everything through their supernormal powers and the force of their vows.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and attain the most subtle wisdom regarding the realm of all sentient beings, which is as follows:

The extremely subtle wisdom that discerns the realm of sentient beings; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the verbal expressions concerning the realm of sentient beings; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding attachments within the realm of sentient beings; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the diverse categories within the realm of sentient beings; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the homogeneous types within the realm of sentient beings; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the immeasurable destinies within the realm of sentient beings; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the inconceivable various conceptualizations and actions within the realm of sentient beings; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the immeasurable defilements within the realm of sentient beings; and the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the immeasurable purities within the realm of sentient beings—such as all these extremely subtle spheres of the realm of sentient beings, he is able, within a single thought-moment, to know them all truly and as they are through his wisdom.
He extensively gathers sentient beings and preaches the Dharma for them, revealing various gates of pure dharmas and causing them to cultivate the vast wisdom of a bodhisattva;

manifesting immeasurable transformation bodies that bring joy to all who see them, he uses the sunlight of wisdom to illumine the minds of bodhisattvas, enabling them to attain awakening and mastery over wisdom.

With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra for all sentient beings in all worlds, attaining the most subtle wisdom regarding the entirety of the realm of empty space,
the dharma-realm, and all worlds— namely: the most subtle wisdom regarding small worlds, the most subtle wisdom regarding large worlds,
the most subtle wisdom regarding defiled worlds, the most subtle wisdom regarding pure worlds, and the most subtle wisdom regarding incomparable worlds...
Subtle wisdom; subtle wisdom regarding the various worlds; subtle wisdom regarding vast worlds; subtle wisdom regarding narrow worlds;
subtle wisdom regarding worlds adorned without obstruction; subtle wisdom regarding the appearance of Buddhas throughout all worlds;
and subtle wisdom regarding the preaching of the True Dharma throughout all worlds.
The extremely subtle wisdom; the extremely subtle wisdom of universally manifesting bodies throughout all worlds;
the extremely subtle wisdom of emitting great light throughout all worlds; the extremely subtle wisdom of manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas throughout all worlds;
and the [extremely subtle wisdom] of manifesting with a single voice throughout all worlds...
The extremely subtle wisdom that perceives all sounds; the extremely subtle wisdom that enters the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment in all worlds and all Buddha-fields;
the extremely subtle wisdom that makes all dharma-realms and Buddha-fields into a single Buddha-field;
the extremely subtle wisdom that makes a single Buddha-field into all dharma-realms and Buddha-fields; and the knowledge of one...
The subtle wisdom that knows all worlds are like dreams; the subtle wisdom that knows all worlds are like reflections;
the subtle wisdom that knows all worlds are like illusions;

thus understanding, they give rise to the path of all bodhisattvas, enter the wisdom and spiritual powers of Samantabhadra’s conduct, possess the contemplation of Samantabhadra, and cultivate the bodhisattva practices without ever ceasing.

They attain the sovereign spiritual transformations of all Buddhas, possess unimpeded bodies, and abide in non-reliant wisdom. They have no grasping or attachment toward any wholesome dharmas, and in the movements of their minds, they find nothing to be apprehended.

In all places, they give rise to the perception of detachment; in the bodhisattva practices, they give rise to the perception of pure cultivation; and regarding omniscience, they maintain a perception free from grasping. They adorn themselves with various samādhis, and their wisdom accords with the entire dharma realm.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they enter the gateway of the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
attaining the extremely subtle wisdom of the infinite Dharma-realm, the wisdom that expounds all the extremely subtle aspects of the Dharma-realm,
the wisdom that enters the extremely subtle aspects of the vast Dharma-realm, and the wisdom that discerns the inconceivable Dharma-realm.
The extremely subtle wisdom that discriminates all dharma-realms; the extremely subtle wisdom that pervades all dharma-realms in a single thought-moment;
the extremely subtle wisdom that universally enters all dharma-realms; the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all dharma-realms are unattainable;
and the extremely subtle wisdom that contemplates all dharma-realms as being without obstruction.
The extremely subtle knowledge that knows all dharma-realms to be without arising;
the extremely subtle knowledge that manifests spiritual transformations within all dharma-realms— such as these, which are all extremely subtle within the dharma-realms,
they know all as they truly are through vast wisdom.
Attaining mastery over all phenomena, they manifest the conduct of Samantabhadra, causing all sentient beings to reach complete fulfillment;
without abandoning the ultimate meaning and without clinging to phenomena, they give rise to impartial and unobstructed wisdom;

knowing the root of non-obstruction, they do not dwell in any phenomena nor destroy the nature of phenomena; being as truly unstained as space, they conform to the world by giving rise to verbal expression.

They open up the meaning of ultimate reality and demonstrate the nature of quiescent extinction; regarding all objects, they are without dependence, without dwelling, and without conceptual differentiation.
Clearly perceiving the dharma-realm, they establish it in its vast expanse, realizing that all worlds and all phenomena are equal and non-dual, free from all attachments.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra and gives rise to the extremely subtle wisdom regarding all kalpas, which is as follows:

With the extremely subtle wisdom that takes unspeakable eons as a single thought-moment; with the extremely subtle wisdom that takes a single thought-moment as unspeakable eons; with the extremely subtle wisdom that enters one eon within incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*); with the extremely subtle wisdom that enters incalculable eons within one eon; with the extremely subtle wisdom that enters long eons into short eons; with the extremely subtle wisdom that enters short eons into long eons; with the extremely subtle wisdom that enters eons with Buddhas and eons without Buddhas; with the extremely subtle wisdom that knows the number of all eons; with the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all eons as non-eons; and with the extremely subtle wisdom that perceives all eons of the three periods of time within a single thought-moment—such all eons, however subtle they may be, the Tathāgata’s wisdom knows them all as they truly are within a single thought-moment.

They attain the mind that is the sovereign of the perfect conduct of all bodhisattvas; the mind that enters the conduct of Samantabhadra; the mind that is free from all conceptual discrimination, divergent paths, and frivolous proliferation; the mind that gives rise to great vows without weariness or rest; the mind that universally perceives the infinite network of worlds filled with infinite Buddhas; the mind capable of hearing and retaining the roots of goodness of all Buddhas and the practices of all bodhisattvas; the mind that, having heard of the vast conduct for comforting all sentient beings, never forgets it; the mind capable of manifesting the appearance of Buddhas in the world throughout all kalpas; the mind that, in each and every world, performs the immovable practice without cessation until the end of the future; and the mind that fills the bodies and minds of bodhisattvas in all worlds with the physical actions of the Tathāgata.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra, achieve non-retrogression, and attain the most subtle wisdom regarding all phenomena, namely:

The subtle wisdom regarding the profound Dharma; the subtle wisdom regarding the vast Dharma; the subtle wisdom regarding diverse dharmas; the subtle wisdom regarding the adorned Dharma; the subtle wisdom regarding the immeasurable nature of all dharmas; the subtle wisdom regarding all dharmas entering into one dharma; the subtle wisdom regarding one dharma entering into all dharmas; the subtle wisdom regarding all dharmas entering into non-dharmas; the subtle wisdom regarding the establishment of all dharmas within the absence of dharmas without contradiction; and the subtle wisdom regarding the entry into the skillful means of all Buddha-dharmas without exception—such subtle wisdoms as these, pertaining to all the dharmas established through all the verbal expressions in all worlds, he possesses in equal measure; his wisdom is unimpeded, and he knows them all as they truly are.
They attain the mind that enters the boundless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), dwelling with firm resolve within each and every realm of phenomena and accomplishing unimpeded conduct;

they fill all their faculties with omniscience (*sarvajñā*) and enter the wisdom of all Buddhas; through right mindfulness and skillful means (*upāya*), they accomplish the vast merits of all Buddhas;

pervading the entire realm of phenomena, they universally enter the bodies of all Tathāgatas, manifesting all the physical actions (*kāyakarman*) of Bodhisattvas, and in accordance with the languages of all worlds, they expound the Dharma.

They attain the mental karma of wisdom empowered by the spiritual power of all Buddhas, which gives rise to the omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) that discriminates all phenomena through immeasurable skillful means.
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one cultivates the conduct of Samantabhadra, giving rise to all most subtle wisdoms, namely:

The wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of all lands; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of all sentient beings; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of the retribution of all phenomena; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of the minds of all sentient beings; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of all times of preaching the Dharma; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of the entire dharma-realm; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of the three periods of time throughout the entirety of space; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of all paths of speech; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of all worldly practices; the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of all world-transcending practices; and even the wisdom that knows the extreme subtlety of the path of all Tathāgatas, the path of all Bodhisattvas, and the path of all sentient beings.
Cultivating the bodhisattva practices and abiding in the path of Samantabhadra, they know both the letter and the meaning as they truly are;

they give rise to the wisdom that all is like a shadow, the wisdom that all is like a dream, the wisdom that all is like an illusion, the wisdom that all is like an echo, the wisdom that all is like a transformation, the wisdom that all is like space, the wisdom of cessation, the wisdom of the entire dharma-realm, the wisdom of non-reliance, and the wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas.

“O Son of the Buddha! The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates with a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated. He does not discriminate between the world and worldly phenomena; he does not discriminate between bodhi and the bodhisattva; he does not discriminate between the bodhisattva practices and the path of transcendence; he does not discriminate between the Buddha and all Buddha-dharmas; he does not discriminate between those who are to be tamed and those who are not to be tamed; he does not discriminate between roots of goodness and dedication; he does not discriminate between self and other; he does not discriminate between the gift and the recipient of the gift; he does not discriminate between bodhisattva practice and perfect enlightenment; and he does not discriminate between dharmas and wisdom.”
“O Son of the Buddha! The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates those roots of goodness in this way:

namely, ‘May there be liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of the mind; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of the body; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of speech; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of karma; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of retribution; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of the world; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of Buddha-fields; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of sentient beings; liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of phenomena; and liberation through non-attachment and non-binding of wisdom.’”
"When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they practice dedication as the Buddhas of the three periods practiced dedication when they were themselves Bodhisattvas;
they learn the dedication of past Buddhas, accomplish the dedication of future Buddhas, and abide in the dedication of present Buddhas;
they dwell securely in the path of dedication of past Buddhas, do not abandon the path of dedication of future Buddhas, and accord with the path of dedication of present Buddhas."
Diligently practicing the teachings of all past Buddhas, accomplishing the teachings of all future Buddhas, and fully understanding the teachings of all present Buddhas;
fulfilling the equanimity of all past Buddhas, accomplishing the equanimity of all future Buddhas, and abiding in the equanimity of all present Buddhas;
traversing the realm of all past Buddhas, dwelling in the realm of all future Buddhas, and equalizing the realm of all present Buddhas.

They attain the roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, possess the lineage of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, abide in the conduct of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, and accord with the realm of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the ninth dedication of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva: the unattached, unbound, liberated mind.

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in this dedication, they cannot be destroyed by any of the Vajra-circled mountain ranges; among all sentient beings, their physical form is foremost and unsurpassed; they are able to utterly shatter all the evil deeds of Māras and manifest universally throughout all worlds in the ten directions."
Cultivating the bodhisattva practices, they seek to awaken all sentient beings by teaching the Buddha-dharma through skillful means;
attaining great wisdom, their minds are free from delusion regarding the Buddha-dharma. In every place of birth, whether moving or staying, they always encounter an indestructible retinue;

they are able to receive and uphold all the true Dharma taught by the Buddhas of the three periods of time through pure mindfulness, cultivating the bodhisattva practices throughout all future eons without ever resting, remaining free from all attachment.
"The practices and vows of Samantabhadra increase and become fully perfected; one attains all-knowledge and performs the Buddha-work, accomplishing the sovereign spiritual powers of a bodhisattva.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"To the peerless Honored Ones throughout the ten directions, I have never once given rise to a mind of contempt."
In accordance with the meritorious deeds they have cultivated, they likewise show reverence and respect.
All the various merits they have cultivated are not for themselves or for others;
rather, with a mind of supreme faith and understanding, they dedicate them for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.
Never for a moment did they give rise to a mind of pride, nor did they ever conceive a sense of inferiority;
regarding all the physical and other actions of the Tathāgata, they inquired about them all and applied themselves diligently to their practice.
All the various roots of goodness that have been cultivated are entirely for the benefit of all sentient beings;
abiding in a profound mind and vast understanding, they are dedicated toward the state of merit of the Honored One among Men.
All the infinite varieties in the world, The various skillful and marvelous matters—
Whether coarse or subtle, vast or profound— There is none he does not practice or fully comprehend.
All the various bodies that exist in the world, He enters into them with the equality of his own body;
By practicing here, he attains realization, And achieves the gateway of wisdom without ever regressing.
The worlds and lands of the universe are of infinite kinds—subtle or vast, upright or inverted;
yet by means of the gateways of wisdom, a Bodhisattva can see them all within a single pore.
The mental activities of sentient beings are immeasurable; They can cause them all to enter equally into the one mind.
Through the gateway of wisdom, they are fully awakened, And never regress from their practice.
The faculties and inclinations of sentient beings—whether superior, middling, or inferior—are each distinct;
though all are profoundly deep and difficult to know, he can fully comprehend them according to their inherent natures.
The various karmas of all sentient beings, Distinguished by their superior, middling, and inferior grades—
The Bodhisattva enters deeply into the power of the Tathāgata, And perceives them all clearly through the gateway of wisdom.
Inconceivable and immeasurable eons can be made to enter equally into a single thought-moment;
having seen thus throughout the ten directions, one cultivates all pure deeds.
Regarding the past, future, and present, one thoroughly understands that their characteristics are each distinct, yet does not contradict the principle of equality;
this is the practice of the great-minded and luminous penetration.
The practices of sentient beings in the world differ; whether manifest or hidden, they are of immeasurable kinds.
The Bodhisattva fully knows their distinct characteristics, yet he also knows that these characteristics are all without characteristic.
The sovereign power of spiritual transformations manifested by all Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions is vast and inconceivable;
yet the Bodhisattva is able to discern and know them all.
In all the Tuṣita heavens throughout every world, The Lion among Men awakens spontaneously;
His merit is vast, pure, and peerless, And he is able to see it exactly as its true nature and form appear.
Sometimes manifesting the descent of the spirit into a mother’s womb, with immeasurable and sovereign great miraculous transformations;
attaining Buddhahood, preaching the Dharma, and demonstrating parinirvāṇa—pervading the world without a moment’s rest.
When the Lion among Men was first born, all those of supreme wisdom offered him their service;
none among the celestial lords, Śakras, and Brahmās failed to gaze upon him with reverence and attend to him.
Throughout all ten directions without exception, within the immeasurable and boundless realm of phenomena—
without beginning or end, and without distance— the Tathāgata manifests his sovereign power.
Once the Honored Guide among Men has manifested his birth, he walks seven paces in each direction;
wishing to awaken all living beings through the sublime Dharma, the Tathāgata gazes everywhere.
Seeing all sentient beings submerged in the ocean of desire, Enveloped by blindness, darkness, and ignorance,
The Sovereign among Men manifests a smile, Mindful that he shall rescue them from the suffering of the three realms of existence.
The Great Lion’s Roar emits a wondrous sound: "I am the foremost honored one in the world;
I shall kindle the bright and pure lamp of wisdom to extinguish the darkness of ignorance within birth and death."
When the Lion among Men, the King, appears in the world, he universally radiates immeasurable great light,
causing all evil realms to come to rest and forever extinguishing the manifold sufferings and hardships of the world.
At times he manifests dwelling in royal palaces, and at times he manifests leaving home to practice the Way;
for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, he displays such sovereign power.
When the Tathāgata first sat upon the site of enlightenment, the entire great earth shook;
all worlds in the ten directions were bathed in light, and sentient beings of the six realms were all freed from suffering.
Shaking all the palaces of Māra, awakening the minds of sentient beings throughout the ten directions—
those who were previously transformed by his teachings and those who have practiced— he causes them all to realize the true meaning.
All the lands throughout the ten directions, without exception, enter into a single pore;
within those infinite lands of every pore, he universally manifests his supernormal powers.
They awaken to all the immeasurable skillful means expounded by all Buddhas;
even that which the Tathāgatas have not spoken, they are able to comprehend and diligently practice.
Pervading the entire trichiliocosm, all the hosts of Māras may raise up strife and commit immeasurable varieties of evil deeds;
yet the gateway of unimpeded wisdom can utterly extinguish them all.
Whether the Tathāgata is in various Buddha-fields, Or manifests his presence in the palaces of the devas,
Or appears in the Brahma-heavens, The Bodhisattvas see them all without obstruction.
The Buddha manifests infinite and diverse bodies, Turning the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma;
Even throughout all kalpas of the three periods of time, One cannot find its limit or end.
The precious throne is high and vast, peerless and supreme, Pervading the immeasurable realms throughout the ten directions;
Adorned with various wondrous marks, The Buddha sits upon it, inconceivable.
Surrounded by the assembly of all Buddha-sons, Pervading the entire realm of phenomena without exception,
They reveal the immeasurable practices of Bodhi, The path through which all the Most Victorious Ones have come.
The deeds performed by all Buddhas according to their suitability are immeasurable, boundless, and equal to the Dharma-realm;
yet the wise, by means of a single skillful method, can comprehend them all completely and without exception.
By the sovereign power of the Buddhas' supernormal knowledges, they manifest all manner of diverse bodies;
sometimes they appear as infinite births within the various realms of existence, and sometimes they appear surrounded by a retinue of court ladies.
In immeasurable worlds, they manifest leaving the household life and attaining the path of Buddhahood,
even unto their final parinirvāṇa, distributing their remains to erect stupas and temples.
Such various and boundless practices as these, which the Guide has proclaimed as the abodes of the Buddhas—
may I exhaustively practice all the great virtues possessed by the World-Honored One through my vows.
When dedicating those roots of goodness, abiding in such skillful means and thus practicing the conduct of enlightenment, their minds never become weary or indolent.
All the great supernormal powers possessed by the Tathāgata, as well as his boundless and supreme merits,
and even all the various modes of wisdom and conduct in the world— he knows them all completely, without exception.
Thus all these lords of men, according to their respective spheres of experience,
realize them all within a single thought-moment, yet they do not abandon the practice of bodhi.
All the subtle activities of the Buddhas, And the various phenomena of all lands—
He is able to know them all in accordance with reality, Ultimately dedicating them to reach the other shore.
All kalpas, whether finite or infinite, the Bodhisattva understands to be a single thought-moment;
thus skillfully entering the practice of enlightenment, they constantly and diligently cultivate it without ever regressing.
All the infinite lands throughout the ten directions, whether defiled or pure,
as well as all the Tathāgatas therein— the Bodhisattva is able to discern and know them all.
In every thought-moment, they clearly perceive inconceivable and immeasurable eons;
thus, throughout the three periods of time without exception, they fully cultivate and purify the bodhisattva practices.
They enter with equanimity into all minds, and they likewise enter all phenomena with equanimity;
even throughout the entirety of the Buddha-fields of space it is thus—they fully comprehend those most excellent practices.
The birth of sentient beings and all phenomena, And all the various kinds of wisdom— The spiritual power of Bodhisattvas is likewise so; All such things are inexhaustible.
The various subtle wisdoms, each distinct and different, the Bodhisattva gathers them all without exception;
thoroughly knowing both their common and specific characteristics, they thus practice the vast conduct.
Throughout the infinite Buddha-fields of the ten directions, The sentient beings therein are each immeasurable;
Their modes of rebirth and various species differ, Yet he knows them all through his mastery of abiding and practice.
In the past, future, and present worlds, all those who are the Guides—
if a person knows this and dedicates [their merit] accordingly, they will be equal in conduct to those Buddhas.
If a person can practice this dedication, they are training in the path traversed by the Buddhas;
they shall attain all the merits of the Buddhas, as well as all the wisdom of the Buddhas.
Nothing in all the worlds can destroy them; All that they study is fully accomplished.
They are always able to keep all Buddhas in mind, And constantly behold the lamps of all the worlds.
The sublime practices of the Bodhisattvas are immeasurable, And all their qualities and dharmas are likewise so;
Having already abided in the unsurpassed conduct of the Tathāgatas, They fully know the sovereign powers of all Buddhas.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Volume Thirty-one;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Volume Thirty-two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
The Tenth of the Twenty-fifth Chapter on the Tenfold Dedication:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
What is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s dedication that is equal to the infinite realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*)?"
“O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has a stainless silk ribbon bound upon his crown; he abides in the rank of a Dharma Master, extensively practices the gift of Dharma, gives rise to great compassion to establish sentient beings, and constantly acts for their benefit within the bodhicitta without ceasing;
he nurtures roots of goodness through the bodhicitta, serves as a teacher and guide for all sentient beings, and reveals to them the path to omniscience.”
For the sake of all sentient beings, they act as the sun of the Dharma-treasury, the radiance of their roots of goodness universally illuminating all;
their minds are impartial toward all sentient beings, and they cultivate various virtuous deeds without rest;
their minds are pure and untainted, their wisdom is sovereign, and they never abandon any path of practice rooted in virtue.
He acts as a great wise leader for all sentient beings, causing them universally to enter the secure and correct path;
he serves as a guide for all sentient beings, leading them to cultivate all roots of goodness and dharmic practices;
he acts as an indestructible and steadfast virtuous friend for all sentient beings, causing their roots of goodness to increase and reach fulfillment.
“O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva takes the gift of Dharma as primary, giving rise to all pure and white dharmas (*śukla-dharma*). He embraces the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and his supreme power of aspiration is ultimately firm and solid.

Having achieved increase and possessing great majestic virtue, he relies upon spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), is free from flattery and deception in heart, and contemplates and observes the boundless realms of the gates of omniscience.”
With these roots of goodness, one should dedicate them in this way:
"May I cultivate, accomplish, and increase the vast and unobstructed state of all realms;
may I, within the true teaching of the Buddha, hear even a single phrase or a single verse, and receive, uphold, and expound it."

May I attain the power of recollection regarding all Buddhas of the past, future, and present in all infinite and boundless worlds, equal in extent to the Dharma-realm; having attained such recollection, may I cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva.

Furthermore, I vow that by means of these roots of goodness from recollecting the Buddha, I shall practice the bodhisattva path for the sake of a single sentient being in a single world throughout all future kalpas;
as I do in one world, so shall I do in all worlds throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space;
and as I do for one sentient being, so shall I do for all sentient beings.

By means of skillful expedients, each and every one of these is adorned with great vows to endure through all kalpas until the end of the future; they never harbor the thought of being separated from the Buddhas, their spiritual friends, and they constantly see all Buddhas appearing before them, such that there is not a single Buddha arising in the world whom they do not have the opportunity to approach and serve.
They vow to fully perfect the pure brahmacarya praised and taught by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, namely:

unbroken brahmacarya, flawless brahmacarya, unmixed brahmacarya, stainless brahmacarya, unfailing brahmacarya, unobscured brahmacarya, brahmacarya praised by the Buddhas, independent brahmacarya, non-apprehending brahmacarya, the increasing pure brahmacarya of Bodhisattvas, the brahmacarya practiced by the Buddhas of the three periods of time, unimpeded brahmacarya, unattached brahmacarya, non-contentious brahmacarya, non-extinguishing brahmacarya, securely established brahmacarya, incomparable brahmacarya, immovable brahmacarya, undisturbed brahmacarya, and non-angry brahmacarya.
"O Son of the Buddha!
If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva can practice such pure Brahma-conduct for their own sake, they will then be able to do so universally for the sake of all sentient beings,
causing all sentient beings to dwell securely and causing all sentient beings to attain clear understanding."
May all sentient beings achieve full accomplishment;
may all sentient beings attain purity; may all sentient beings become stainless.
May all sentient beings attain illumination;
may all sentient beings be free from the defilement of dust;
may all sentient beings be without any obstructions or veils.
May all sentient beings be freed from all feverish afflictions;
may all sentient beings be freed from all fetters and bonds;
may all sentient beings forever be free from all evils.
They cause all sentient beings to be free from all afflictions and harms, becoming ultimately pure. Why is this?
Because if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cannot themselves purify their own holy life (*brahmacarya*), they cannot cause others to attain purity.
Having themselves regressed from the holy life, they cannot cause others to be free from regression;
having themselves failed and ruined the holy life, they cannot cause others to be free from failure and ruin;
having themselves become estranged from the holy life, they cannot cause others to remain forever unestranged.
If one is indolent regarding the holy life oneself, one cannot cause others to be free from indolence;
if one does not personally give rise to faith and understanding regarding the holy life, one cannot cause others' minds to give rise to faith and understanding;
if one does not personally abide securely in the holy life, one cannot cause others to attain secure abiding.
Not having personally realized entry into the holy life, one cannot cause others' minds to realize entry;
having personally abandoned the holy life, one cannot cause others to never abandon it;
and being personally distracted and agitated regarding the holy life, one cannot cause others' minds not to be distracted and agitated.

Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in non-erroneous practice and teach the non-erroneous Dharma; their words are truthful, and they practice according to what they have taught. They purify body, speech, and mind, remain free from all defilements, abide in unimpeded conduct, and extinguish all obstacles.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains a pure mind for himself and expounds the Dharma of the pure mind to others;
he personally cultivates harmony and patience, subduing his own mind with all roots of goodness, and causes others to practice harmony and patience, subduing their minds with all roots of goodness;
he personally leaves behind doubt and regret, and likewise causes others to forever leave behind doubt and regret.
Having attained pure faith for oneself, one also causes others to attain indestructible pure faith;
dwelling in the True Dharma oneself, one also causes sentient beings to abide securely in the True Dharma.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness arising from this Dharma-giving in this way:

"May I attain all the inexhaustible Dharma-gates of all Buddhas, and universally analyze and explain them for all sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice and their minds to be fully satisfied, while crushing and destroying all the heterodox arguments of external paths."

May I be able to expound for all sentient beings the ocean of dharmas of the Buddhas of the three periods of time; regarding each and every dharma’s arising, each and every dharma’s principle, each and every dharma’s name and terminology, each and every dharma’s establishment, each and every dharma’s explanation, each and every dharma’s manifestation, each and every dharma’s gateway, each and every dharma’s entry, each and every dharma’s observation, and each and every dharma’s stage—may I fully attain the boundless and inexhaustible treasury of dharmas therein, obtain fearlessness, and possess the four types of eloquence, so as to analyze and explain them extensively for sentient beings without end until the limits of the future.
In order to cause all sentient beings to establish supreme aspirations and give rise to unimpeded and infallible eloquence;

in order to cause all sentient beings to experience joy; in order to cause all sentient beings to accomplish the radiance of all pure dharmas and to expound them without interruption according to their respective languages;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to have deep faith and joy, abide in omniscience, discern all dharmas, and be free from confusion—one forms this thought:

I shall, throughout all worlds, diligently practice for the sake of all sentient beings, so as to attain an infinite body of sovereign mastery pervading the entire dharma-realm; to attain an infinite, vast, and expansive mind pervading the entire dharma-realm; to possess infinite pure voices equal to the dharma-realm; to manifest infinite assemblies and sites of enlightenment equal to the dharma-realm; to cultivate infinite bodhisattva deeds equal to the dharma-realm; to attain infinite bodhisattva abodes equal to the dharma-realm; to realize infinite bodhisattva equanimity equal to the dharma-realm; to study infinite bodhisattva dharmas equal to the dharma-realm; to dwell in infinite bodhisattva practices equal to the dharma-realm; and to enter infinite bodhisattva dedications equal to the dharma-realm.
This is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness, in order that all sentient beings may fully achieve omniscience.
“O Son of the Buddha! Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness in this way, namely: ‘In order to behold infinite Buddhas equal to the Dharma-realm;

to discipline infinite sentient beings equal to the Dharma-realm; to sustain infinite Buddha-lands equal to the Dharma-realm; to realize the infinite wisdom of Bodhisattvas equal to the Dharma-realm; to attain the infinite fearlessnesses of Bodhisattvas equal to the Dharma-realm; to accomplish the infinite dhāraṇīs of Bodhisattvas equal to the Dharma-realm; to obtain the infinite inconceivable abodes of Bodhisattvas equal to the Dharma-realm; to be endowed with infinite merits equal to the Dharma-realm; and to fulfill the infinite roots of goodness for benefiting sentient beings equal to the Dharma-realm.’”

Furthermore, by virtue of these roots of goodness, may I attain equality in merit, equality in wisdom, equality in power, equality in fearlessness, equality in purity, equality in mastery, equality in perfect enlightenment, equality in preaching the Dharma, equality in meaning, equality in certainty, and equality in all supernormal powers; may such dharmas as these be entirely perfected.
"May all sentient beings also attain exactly what I have attained, being no different from me.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further dedicates their roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"As the dharma-realm is immeasurable, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; the wisdom thereby attained shall never be limited.
As the dharma-realm is boundless, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; in beholding all Buddhas, there shall be no limit.
As the dharma-realm is infinite, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; in visiting all Buddha-fields, there shall be no restriction."
Just as the dharma-realm is boundless, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; one cultivates the bodhisattva practice in all worlds without limit.
Just as the dharma-realm is uninterrupted, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; abiding in omniscience, it is forever unceasing.
Just as the dharma-realm is of a single nature, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it shares the same nature of wisdom with all sentient beings.
Just as the nature of the dharma-realm is intrinsically pure, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness, causing all sentient beings to attain ultimate purity;
just as the dharma-realm is compliant, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness, causing all sentient beings to fully comply with the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra;
just as the dharma-realm is adorned, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness, causing all sentient beings to be adorned by the conduct of Samantabhadra.
Just as the dharma-realm cannot be lost or destroyed, so too is the dedication of roots of goodness; it causes all bodhisattvas to never lose or destroy their pure practices.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, saying:
'May I, by means of these roots of goodness, serve all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and cause them all to rejoice;'"
By these roots of goodness, may I swiftly attain entry into the nature of omniscience;
by these roots of goodness, may I cultivate omniscience in all places;
by these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always be able to go and behold all Buddhas.
By this root of goodness, may all sentient beings always behold the Buddhas and be able to perform the work of a Buddha;
by this root of goodness, may all sentient beings constantly obtain the sight of the Buddhas and never give rise to a mind of indolence regarding the work of a Buddha;
by this root of goodness, may all sentient beings always obtain the sight of the Buddhas, their minds joyful and pure, without any regression.
By means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always behold the Buddha and attain excellent understanding;
by means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always behold the Buddha and give rise to no attachment;
by means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always behold the Buddha and realize unimpeded penetration.
By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always behold the Buddhas and accomplish the conduct of Samantabhadra;
by these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always see the various Buddhas appearing before them, never forsaking them for even a moment;
by these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always see the various Buddhas and give birth to the immeasurable powers of a Bodhisattva.
“By this root of goodness, may all sentient beings always behold the Buddhas and never forget or lose any of the dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this manner, namely: dedicating them as the non-arising nature of the dharma-realm;

dedicating them as the fundamental nature of the dharma-realm; dedicating them as the self-nature of the dharma-realm; dedicating them as the non-reliant nature of the dharma-realm; dedicating them as the non-forgetful nature of the dharma-realm; dedicating them as the empty and non-existent nature of the dharma-realm; dedicating them as the quiescent nature of the dharma-realm; dedicating them as the locationless nature of the dharma-realm; dedicating them as the immutable nature of the dharma-realm; and dedicating them as the undifferentiated nature of the dharma-realm.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness arising from the proclamation, the awakening, and the teaching of the Dharma through this gift of Dharma as follows:
‘May all sentient beings become Bodhisattva Dharma-teachers, always being protected and remembered by all Buddhas;’”
May all sentient beings become unsurpassed Dharma teachers, skillfully establishing all sentient beings in omniscience;
may all sentient beings become invincible Dharma teachers, such that no interrogations or challenges can exhaust them;
may all sentient beings become unimpeded Dharma teachers, attaining the unhindered light of all dharmas.
May all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers who are treasuries of wisdom, able to skillfully expound all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers with the sovereign mastery of all Tathāgatas, well able to discern the wisdom of the Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers who are like eyes, preaching the Dharma as it truly is, without depending on the instruction of others.
May all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who uphold all Buddha-dharmas, expounding them according to principle without contradicting the words or their meanings;
may all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who practice the signless path, adorning themselves with all sublime marks, emitting immeasurable light, and skillfully entering into all dharmas;
may all sentient beings become Dharma teachers of the Great Body, whose bodies pervade all lands, raising great clouds of Dharma and raining down all Buddha-dharmas.

May all sentient beings become Dharma-preachers who protect the treasury of the Dharma, erecting the banner of invincibility, guarding all Buddha-dharmas, and ensuring that the ocean of the True Dharma suffers no deficiency;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-preachers who are suns for all dharmas, attaining the eloquence of the Buddhas and skillfully expounding all phenomena;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-preachers of wondrous voice and skillful means, excellently explaining the treasury of the boundless realm of reality.
May all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers who have reached the further shore of the Dharma, opening the treasury of the True Dharma through wisdom and supernormal powers;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers who dwell securely in the True Dharma, expounding the ultimate wisdom of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers who thoroughly understand all phenomena, able to proclaim immeasurable and inexhaustible merits.
May all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who do not deceive the world, able to lead others into the limit of reality through skillful means;
may all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who shatter the hosts of Māras, skillfully awakening to and recognizing all demonic activities;
may all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who are sustained by all Buddhas, free from the grasping mind of "I" and "mine."
"May all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who bring peace and security to all worlds, and may they fulfill the bodhisattva’s vow-power for preaching the Dharma.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, namely:"

"One does not dedicate with attachment to karma; one does not dedicate with attachment to retribution; one does not dedicate with attachment to the mind; one does not dedicate with attachment to dharmas; one does not dedicate with attachment to phenomena; one does not dedicate with attachment to causes; one does not dedicate with attachment to words, sounds, or voices; one does not dedicate with attachment to names, phrases, or syllables; one does not dedicate with attachment to dedication itself; and one does not dedicate with attachment to benefiting sentient beings."
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, ‘I do not dedicate them for the sake of attachment to the realm of forms; I do not dedicate them for the sake of attachment to sounds, fragrances, ...’”
They dedicate [their merit] for the sake of the objects of taste, touch, and mental phenomena;
they do not dedicate it for the sake of seeking birth in the heavens, nor for the sake of seeking sensual pleasures,
nor for the sake of attachment to the realm of desire, nor for the sake of seeking a retinue, nor for the sake of seeking sovereignty, nor for the sake of seeking...

One dedicates for the sake of the happiness of birth and death, but does not dedicate out of attachment to birth and death; one does not dedicate for the sake of delighting in the various realms of existence (*bhava*);
one does not dedicate for the sake of seeking the pleasure of union; one does not dedicate for the sake of seeking a place of delightful attachment;
one does not dedicate with a mind harboring malice; and one does not allow the roots of goodness to be destroyed.
Therefore, one dedicates by not relying on the three realms; one dedicates by not clinging to the various dhyānas, liberations, and samādhis;
and one dedicates by not dwelling in the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
They dedicate solely for the purpose of teaching and taming all sentient beings;
they dedicate solely for the purpose of fulfilling the knowledge of all modes;
they dedicate solely for the purpose of attaining unimpeded wisdom.
One dedicates solely for the sake of attaining unobstructed, pure roots of goodness;
