one dedicates solely for the sake of causing all sentient beings to transcend birth and death and realize great wisdom;
one dedicates solely for the sake of making the mind of great bodhi as indestructible as a vajra.
They dedicate solely for the sake of accomplishing the ultimate dharma of deathlessness;
they dedicate solely for the sake of adorning the lineage of the Buddhas with immeasurable adornments and manifesting mastery over all-knowledge;
they dedicate solely for the sake of seeking the great supernormal knowledge and wisdom that illuminates all dharmas of the bodhisattvas.

I dedicate solely for the sake of practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra in all Buddha-fields throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, attaining perfection without regression; wearing the armor of firm great vows, I dedicate so that all sentient beings may be established upon the stage of Samantabhadra.

I dedicate solely for the sake of liberating sentient beings throughout all future eons without ever resting, and to manifest the unimpeded light of the stage of omniscience in constant, uninterrupted succession.
“O Son of the Buddha! When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate those roots of goodness, they do so with such a mind as this:

namely, they dedicate with a mind of equality regarding intrinsic nature; they dedicate with a mind of equality regarding the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); they dedicate with a mind of immeasurable equality regarding all sentient beings; they dedicate with a mind of equality free from contention; they dedicate with a mind of equality wherein no self-nature arises; they dedicate with a mind that knows all phenomena without confusion; they dedicate with a mind that enters into the equality of the three periods of time; they dedicate with a mind that gives birth to the lineage of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; they dedicate with a mind that attains non-retrogressive supernormal powers (*abhijñā*); and they dedicate with a mind that brings to fulfillment the practices of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).”
Furthermore, one dedicates [merit] so that all sentient beings may forever be free from all hells;
one dedicates so that all sentient beings may not enter the realm of animals;
one dedicates so that all sentient beings may not go to the abode of King Yama.
They dedicate [their merit] in order to cause all sentient beings to eliminate all factors that obstruct the Path;
they dedicate it in order to cause all sentient beings to fulfill all roots of goodness;
they dedicate it in order to cause all sentient beings to be able to turn the Wheel of Dharma at the appropriate time, bringing joy to all.
I dedicate this so that all sentient beings may enter the wheel of the ten powers;
I dedicate this so that all sentient beings may fulfill their boundless, pure Dharma-vows as bodhisattvas;
and I dedicate this so that all sentient beings may follow the instructions of all spiritual friends and bring the vessel of the bodhicitta to fulfillment.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may uphold and practice the profound Buddha-dharma and attain the light of the wisdom of all Buddhas;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may cultivate the unobstructed practices of Bodhisattvas so that they are constantly manifest before them;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may always see all Buddhas appearing before them.
They dedicate [their merit] so that the light of the pure Dharma may constantly manifest before all sentient beings;
they dedicate it so that the fearless great bodhicitta may constantly manifest before all sentient beings;
and they dedicate it so that the inconceivable wisdom of the bodhisattvas may constantly manifest before all sentient beings.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may universally rescue and protect other beings, and so that their pure mind of great compassion may be constantly manifest;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may adorn all Buddha-lands with unspeakably unspeakable numbers of supreme and wondrous ornaments;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may destroy and eliminate the nets of karma consisting of all demons and conflicts.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may practice the bodhisattva path without any dependence upon any buddha-field;
and I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may give rise to the mind of omniscience and enter the vast gateway of all Buddha-dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness through pure right mindfulness;
he dedicates them with decisive wisdom;
They dedicate with the aim of fully knowing all the skillful means of the Buddha-dharma;
they dedicate for the sake of accomplishing immeasurable and unimpeded wisdom;
and they dedicate because they desire to fulfill the pure and sublime mind.
One dedicates for the sake of all sentient beings abiding in great loving-kindness;
one dedicates for the sake of all sentient beings abiding in great compassion;
one dedicates for the sake of all sentient beings abiding in great sympathetic joy.
They dedicate for the sake of abiding in great equanimity for the benefit of all sentient beings;
they dedicate for the sake of dwelling in supreme roots of goodness that are forever free from the two attachments;
and they dedicate for the sake of contemplating, examining, discerning, and expounding all dharmas of dependent origination.
They dedicate for the sake of establishing the mind of great heroic banners;
they dedicate for the sake of establishing the treasury of invincible banners;
and they dedicate for the sake of destroying all hosts of Māras.
They dedicate for the sake of attaining a mind that is pure and unimpeded regarding all phenomena;
they dedicate for the sake of practicing all bodhisattva deeds without falling back;
they dedicate for the sake of attaining a mind that joyfully seeks the supreme, most excellent Dharma.
They dedicate for the sake of attaining the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), which seeks all meritorious dharmas and is sovereignly pure;

they dedicate for the sake of fulfilling all vows, eliminating all disputes, and attaining the unimpeded, pure dharmas of a Buddha’s sovereignty, so as to turn the non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings;

they dedicate for the sake of attaining the sun of wisdom of the Tathāgata’s most supreme and distinguished dharmas, adorned with hundreds of thousands of rays of light, which universally illumines all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).

I dedicate [these roots of goodness] because I desire to subdue all sentient beings, constantly satisfying them according to their inclinations; because I do not abandon my original vows, but until the end of the future, shall cause them to hear the true Dharma, cultivate great practices, attain pure wisdom and stainless radiance, sever all pride, extinguish all afflictions, tear the net of craving and desire, shatter the darkness of ignorance, and become fully endowed with the stainless and unobstructed Dharma;

and because for the sake of all sentient beings, throughout incalculable eons, I shall constantly and diligently cultivate all practices for omniscience without ever regressing, causing each and every one of them to attain unimpeded, wondrous wisdom, and manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas without rest.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner, they should not be greedily attached to the three realms of existence or the objects of the five desires.”

Why is this? A bodhisattva mahāsattva should dedicate with roots of goodness free from greed; should dedicate with roots of goodness free from anger; should dedicate with roots of goodness free from delusion; should dedicate with roots of goodness free from harmfulness; should dedicate with roots of goodness free from pride; should dedicate with roots of goodness free from flattery; should dedicate with roots of goodness that are upright; should dedicate with roots of goodness characterized by diligence; and should dedicate with roots of goodness cultivated through practice.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they attain pure faith; they joyfully accept and endure the bodhisattva practices, cultivating the pure path of the great bodhisattvas;
they possess the buddha-lineage and attain the wisdom of the buddhas.
Abandoning all evil, one distances oneself from the deeds of Māra;
drawing near to virtuous friends, one fulfills one's own great vows;
and inviting all sentient beings, one establishes a great assembly for giving.
“O Son of the Buddha! Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness arising from this gift of Dharma in this way:

‘May all sentient beings obtain pure and wondrous voices; obtain soft and supple voices; obtain the voice of the celestial drum; obtain immeasurable, incalculable, and inconceivable voices; obtain voices that are delightful and pleasing; obtain pure voices; obtain voices that pervade all Buddha-fields; obtain voices adorned with hundreds of thousands of nayutas of unspeakable merits; obtain lofty and far-reaching voices; obtain vast and expansive voices; obtain voices that extinguish all distraction; obtain voices that fill the entire Dharma-realm; and obtain voices that encompass the languages of all sentient beings.’”

They attain the wisdom of the boundless voices of all sentient beings; they attain the wisdom of all pure linguistic sounds; they attain the wisdom of immeasurable linguistic sounds; they attain the wisdom of the most sovereign voice that enters into all sounds;
they attain all pure and adorned sounds; they attain all worldly sounds that never weary;
they attain sounds that are ultimately unattached to any world; they attain the sound of joy; and they attain the purity of the Buddhas.
He attains the voice of speech and sound that proclaims all Buddha-dharmas and is free from the cataracts of delusion, with its renown heard everywhere;
he attains the voice adorned by the *dhāraṇīs* of all dharmas, enabling all sentient beings to obtain them; he attains the voice that expounds all immeasurable kinds of dharmas;
and he attains the voice that reaches everywhere throughout the dharma-realm to the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of immeasurable multitudes.
They attain the sound of the vajra-phrase that universally upholds inconceivable dharmas; they attain the sound that reveals the voice of all dharmas;
they attain the sound of the treasury of wisdom that can explain the distinctions between expressible and inexpressible words and phrases;
they attain the sound that expounds all dharmas without attachment and without interruption; they attain the sound that illuminates all dharmas with radiance. They attain...
They are able to bring all worlds to ultimate purity, reaching the sound of omniscience;
they attain the sound that universally encompasses the phrases and meanings of all dharmas; they attain the sound of sovereign, unimpeded power protected by spiritual might;
and they attain the sound of wisdom that reaches the further shore of all worlds.

Furthermore, by means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain voices that are not inferior; attain voices free from fear; attain voices free from defiled attachment; attain voices that bring joy to all assemblies and sites of enlightenment; attain voices that are harmonious and exquisite; attain voices that skillfully expound all Buddha-dharmas; attain voices that sever the doubts of all sentient beings and cause them all to awaken; attain voices endowed with perfect eloquence; and attain voices that universally awaken all sentient beings from the long night of sleep.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
‘May all sentient beings attain the pure Dharma-body, free from all faults and evils; may all sentient beings...’”
Having attained by birth the pure and wondrous merit that is free from all faults and evils, may all sentient beings attain the pure and wondrous marks that are free from all faults and evils;
may all sentient beings attain the pure karmic fruits that are free from all faults and evils;
may all sentient beings attain the pure mind of omniscience that is free from all faults and evils; may one...
May all sentient beings attain the immeasurably pure bodhicitta that is free from all faults and evils;
may all sentient beings attain the skillful means for knowing the faculties that are pure and free from all faults and evils;
may all sentient beings attain pure faith and understanding free from all faults and evils; may all sentient beings be free from all faults and evils.
“Purify your diligent cultivation of unimpeded vows and conduct, and vow that all sentient beings may attain freedom from all faults and evils,
as well as pure right mindfulness, wisdom, and eloquence.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness for the sake of all sentient beings in this way:
"May I attain various kinds of pure and wondrous bodies, namely:

the body of radiance, the body free from turbidity, the unstained body, the pure body, the extremely pure body, the body free from dust, the extremely dust-free body, the stainless body, the delightful body, and the unobstructed body."
They manifest the images of all karmas in all worlds, the images of all speech in all mundane realms, and the images of all established dwellings in all palaces.

Like a pure, bright mirror in which various forms and images naturally appear, it reveals to all sentient beings the practice of great bodhi; it reveals to all sentient beings the profound and wondrous Dharma; it reveals to all sentient beings their various merits; it reveals to all sentient beings the path of cultivation; it reveals to all sentient beings the practices for accomplishment; it reveals to all sentient beings the vows and conduct of Bodhisattvas; it reveals to all sentient beings the appearance of Buddhas in one world and in all worlds; it reveals to all sentient beings the supernatural transformations of all Buddhas; it reveals to all sentient beings the inconceivable power of liberation of all Bodhisattvas; and it reveals to all sentient beings the nature of omniscience through the fulfillment of the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

By means of such subtle and pure bodies, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva employs skillful means to gather in all sentient beings, causing them all to achieve the body of omniscience (sarvajñatā-kāya) endowed with pure merit.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness produced by this Dharma-giving in this way:

‘May my body abide throughout all worlds to cultivate the Bodhisattva practices; may all sentient beings who see me not do so in vain, but resolve upon Bodhicitta so as never to regress, and accord with the meaning of reality so as to be unshakable.’”
Throughout all worlds, for as long as all future kalpas endure, they abide in the bodhisattva path without weariness;
their great compassion is impartial and universal, equal in measure to the dharma-realm;
knowing the faculties of sentient beings, they preach the Dharma according to the appropriate time, never ceasing.
Regarding spiritual friends, one maintains constant right mindfulness, never relinquishing it for even a single kṣaṇa;
all Buddhas are ever present before one, and one maintains constant right mindfulness without the slightest laxity, cultivating all roots of goodness without hypocrisy;
and one establishes all sentient beings in omniscience, causing them never to regress.
Possessing the radiance of all Buddha-dharmas, sustaining the great cloud of Dharma, and receiving the great rain of Dharma, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices;

they enter into all sentient beings, enter into all buddha-fields, enter into all dharmas, and enter into all three periods of time; they enter into the wisdom of the karmic retributions of all sentient beings, enter into the wisdom of the skillful means of all bodhisattvas, enter into the wisdom of the manifestations of all bodhisattvas, enter into the wisdom of the pure realms of all bodhisattvas, enter into the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas, and enter into the entire boundless dharma-realm; abiding therein, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Scroll Thirty-two;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Scroll Thirty-three.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
The Eleventh of the Twenty-Fifth Chapter, "The Dedication of Merit," Part Eleven:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness cultivated through the gift of Dharma in this way:"
"May all Buddha-fields be entirely pure, adorned with unspeakably unspeakable arrays of ornaments.
May each and every Buddha-field be vast in measure, equal to the Dharma-realm, purely virtuous and unimpeded, radiant and pure, wherein all Buddhas manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment."
Within the pure realm of a single buddha-field, one can manifest all buddha-fields;
as it is with one buddha-field, so it is with all buddha-fields.
Each and every world-system was adorned with ornaments of pure, wondrous jewels—equal in extent to the dharma-realm and immeasurable and boundless.
That is to say:
there were incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) pure jewel thrones, spread with robes of various jewels;
Incalculable jeweled canopies with jeweled nets draped and spread;
incalculable jeweled parasols, where all exquisite jewels reflect one another with perfect clarity;
and incalculable jeweled clouds, raining down a multitude of treasures everywhere.
Countless *asaṃkhyeya* jewel flowers were everywhere pure;
countless railings, balustrades, porticos, and balconies made of various jewels were pure and magnificently adorned;
and countless jewel bells constantly produced the subtle and wondrous voices of all Buddhas, circulating throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
There were incalculable jewel lotuses, blooming in various jewel-hued splendors;
incalculable jewel trees stood in rows all around, their flowers and fruits composed of immeasurable wonderful jewels;
there were incalculable jewel palaces where immeasurable bodhisattvas resided, and incalculable jewel towers and pavilions, vast and magnificent, extending far and wide.
There were incalculable jewel defensive walls, formed of great jewels and exquisitely adorned;
there were incalculable jewel gate-towers, draped all around with wonderful jewel necklaces;
and there were incalculable jewel windows, purely adorned with inconceivable jewels.
There were incalculable *tāla* trees made of jewels, shaped like half-moons and composed of various precious gems.

All such things were adorned with every kind of jewel; they were stainless and pure, inconceivable, and none arose except from the roots of goodness of the Tathāgata, being fully endowed with the adornments of countless treasuries of jewels.
Furthermore, there were incalculable jewel rivers, flowing forth all pure and wholesome dharmas;
incalculable jewel oceans, filled to the brim with the water of the Dharma;
and incalculable jewel puṇḍarīka flowers, constantly emitting the sublime sound of the puṇḍarīka of the Dharma.
There were incalculable Sumeru mountains of jewels, with the King of Mountains of Wisdom rising preeminent and pure;
there were incalculable exquisite eight-faceted jewels, strung together with jeweled cords, their adornment and purity being beyond compare;
there were incalculable jewels of pure radiance, constantly emitting the unimpeded light of great wisdom, universally illuminating the Dharma-realm.
Countless *asaṃkhyeya* jewel bells and chimes strike against one another, producing wondrous sounds;
countless pure jewels completely fill the various precious implements of the bodhisattvas;
and countless jeweled silks hang down everywhere, their colors and forms radiant and pure.
There were incalculable banners of exquisite jewels, adorned with jeweled crescents;
incalculable jeweled pennants, which could rain down immeasurable jeweled pennants everywhere;
and incalculable jeweled sashes, draped through the air in a most wonderful and sublime array.
There were incalculable precious carpets that could produce various subtle sensations of pleasure;
incalculable exquisite jewel-spirals that manifested the all-knowing eye of the bodhisattvas;
and incalculable precious necklaces, each of which was a supreme adornment for hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas.
There were incalculable jewel palaces, surpassing all others in their exquisite and peerless splendor;
there were incalculable jewel ornaments, adorned with diamond-maṇi gems;
and there were incalculable varieties of exquisite jewel ornaments, constantly manifesting all pure and wondrous colors.
There were incalculable pure jewels of extraordinary shapes and diverse colors, their radiance clear and penetrating;
there were incalculable jewel mountains forming walls that surrounded it on all sides, pure and unobstructed;
and there were incalculable precious fragrances, whose scent universally perfumed all worlds.
There are incalculable manifestations of jewels, each manifestation pervading the entire dharma-realm;
there are incalculable jewel-lights, each light manifesting all lights.
Furthermore, there were incalculable jewel lights, the radiance of pure wisdom that clearly illumines all phenomena.
Furthermore, there were incalculable unimpeded jewel lights, each individual light pervading the entire dharma-realm.
There are incalculable places of jewels, wherein all manner of jewels are fully present.
There are incalculable treasuries of jewels, which reveal the treasures of the treasury of all true dharmas.
There were incalculable jewel banners, with the marks of the Tathāgata’s banner rising loftily and preeminently.
There were incalculable jewel worthies, the forms of worthies of great wisdom, fully endowed with purity.
Immeasurable jewel gardens produce the blissful joy of the samādhis of all bodhisattvas.
Immeasurable jewel sounds—the wondrous voice of the Tathāgata—universally manifest throughout the world.
There were incalculable jewel forms, each of which emitted immeasurable rays of light of the wondrous Dharma.
There were incalculable jewel marks, each of which transcended all other marks.
There are incalculable jewel-like dignities, such that all who see them give rise to the joy and delight of bodhisattvas.
There are incalculable accumulations of jewels, such that all who see them give rise to the accumulation of the treasure of wisdom.
There were incalculable precious jewels that remained steadfast; all who beheld them gave rise to the jewel-mind of virtuous stability.
There were incalculable precious garments; those who wore them gave rise to the peerless samādhis of all bodhisattvas.

There are incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) precious *kāṣāya* robes; whoever wears them attains the *dhāraṇī* gate of "Good Vision" (*sudarśana*) at the very moment they first resolve their mind toward awakening.
There are incalculable precious objects of cultivation; whoever sees them knows that all jewels are the fruits of karma and are definitively pure.
There are incalculable treasures of unimpeded knowledge and vision; whoever beholds them attains the pure Dharma-eye that comprehends all things.
There are incalculable treasuries of precious light; whoever beholds them achieves the treasury of great wisdom.
There were incalculable jewel thrones, upon which the Buddhas sat and let out the great lion’s roar.
There were incalculable jewel lamps, constantly emitting the pure light of wisdom.
Countless *asaṃkhyeya* jewel *tāla* trees stand in successive rows, encircled by jeweled cords, pure and magnificent.
Each tree further possesses countless jewel trunks that rise upward from their bases, straight, round, and pristine;
they have countless jewel branches, densely adorned with various kinds of jewels, where inconceivable birds flock and gather, constantly emitting wondrous sounds to proclaim the True Dharma.
There were incalculable jewel leaves that radiated the light of great wisdom, pervading all places;
there were incalculable jewel flowers, upon each of which immeasurable bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, traveling throughout the entire dharma-realm;
there were incalculable jewel fruits, such that anyone who beheld them would attain the fruit of non-retrogression in the knowledge of all-knowledge.
There are incalculable jewel villages, where those who see them abandon the worldly ways of village life.
There are incalculable jewel cities, filled with unimpeded sentient beings.
Within incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewel palaces, the King dwells, fully endowed with the Nārāyaṇa body of a bodhisattva—valiant and firm, clad in the armor of the Dharma, his mind never regressing.
There are incalculable jewel mansions, entering which one can eliminate the mind that clings to dwellings.
There are incalculable jewel robes, wearing which one can bring about the realization of non-attachment.
There were incalculable jeweled palaces, filled with bodhisattvas who had left the household life;
there were incalculable precious ornaments and playthings, which all who beheld them conceived immeasurable joy.
Countless jewel wheels emit inconceivable light of wisdom and turn the wheel of non-retrogression;
countless jewel-pāṭala trees are adorned with the pure Indra-net.
There were incalculable jewel grounds, adorned with the interspersed array of inconceivable jewels.
There were incalculable jewel winds, their clear and resonant sounds filling the entire Dharma-realm.
There were incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) precious drums, their wondrous sounds harmonious and resonant, continuing without ceasing throughout kalpas.
There were incalculable precious sentient beings, all of whom were able to uphold the unsurpassed treasure of the Dharma.
There are incalculable jewel-bodies, fully endowed with the wondrous jewels of immeasurable merit.
There are incalculable jewel-mouths, constantly emanating the jewel-sounds of all sublime Dharmas.
The *asaṃkhyeya* jewel of the mind, possessing the jewel of the great wisdom-vow of a pure intention;
the *asaṃkhyeya* jewel of mindfulness, which severs all delusions and ignorance, and is ultimately firm as the jewel of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
With incalculable jewel-like brilliance, they recite and uphold the Dharma-jewels of all Buddhas;
with incalculable jewel-like wisdom, they resolve and comprehend the Dharma-treasuries of all Buddhas.
With incalculable jewels of wisdom, they attain the great perfection of the jewel of omniscience.
With incalculable jewels of eyes, they discern the jewels of the ten powers without any obstruction.
They possess incalculable jewel-ears, hearing immeasurable sounds throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm, pure and unimpeded.
They possess incalculable jewel-noses, constantly smelling the pure jewel-fragrances that accord with the Way.
With incalculable jewel-tongues, they are able to expound immeasurable methods of speech;
with incalculable jewel-bodies, they travel throughout the ten directions without obstruction.
With incalculable jewel-like intentions, they constantly and diligently cultivate the practices and vows of Samantabhadra.
With incalculable jewel-like voices, their pure and wondrous sounds pervade the worlds of the ten directions.
There are incalculable precious physical actions, all of which are preceded by wisdom.
There are incalculable precious verbal actions, which constantly proclaim the practice of the jewel of unimpeded knowledge.
“With incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) precious mental actions, they attain the precious wisdom that is unobstructed, vast, and ultimately perfected.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Within all those buddha-fields, in a single buddha-field, in one direction, in one location, even within the measure of a single hair-tip, there are immeasurable, boundless, and unspeakably numerous great bodhisattvas, all of whom have fully accomplished pure wisdom and dwell therein filling it completely.”

Just as it is for one buddha-field, one direction, one location, or the measure of a single hair-tip, so it is for every single buddha-field, every single direction, every single location, and every measure of a single hair-tip throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the dharma-realm; all are likewise.
This is how Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their various roots of goodness, universally aspiring that all Buddha-lands be fully adorned with every kind of exquisite jewel.
As with the adornment of jewels, so it is explained in detail;

likewise for the adornment of incense, the adornment of flowers, the adornment of garlands, the adornment of ointments, the adornment of burning incense, the adornment of powdered incense, the adornment of robes, the adornment of parasols, the adornment of banners, the adornment of streamers, and the adornment of maṇi-jewels—each in succession increasing a hundredfold beyond the former, all as extensively described as the adornment of jewels.
“O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness accumulated through the giving of Dharma and other practices for the sake of nurturing all roots of goodness;
they dedicate them for the sake of adorning and purifying all Buddha-fields.”
They dedicate for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to fulfillment;
they dedicate so that all sentient beings may have minds that are pure and unshakable;
they dedicate so that all sentient beings may enter the profound Buddha-dharma.
They dedicate [their merit] so that all sentient beings may attain the pure qualities that none can surpass;
they dedicate so that all sentient beings may attain the indestructible power of pure merit;
and they dedicate so that all sentient beings may attain inexhaustible power of wisdom, thereby delivering all beings and causing them to enter the Buddha-dharma.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may attain equal, immeasurable, and pure speech;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may attain equal, unobstructed eyes and achieve wisdom that is coextensive with empty space and pervades the Dharma-realm;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may attain pure mindfulness and know all worlds throughout past eons.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may attain unimpeded great wisdom and be able to decisively resolve all treasuries of the Dharma;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may attain immeasurable great Bodhi, pervading the entire Dharma-realm without obstruction;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may attain equal, non-discriminative, and identical roots of goodness.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may attain a body, speech, and mental karma that are fully adorned with all merits and are utterly pure;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may attain conduct identical to that of Samantabhadra;
and I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may enter all Buddha-fields of universal, identical essence and purity.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may fully observe all-knowledge and enter into its perfection;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may become entirely free from unequal roots of goodness;
I dedicate them so that all sentient beings may attain equality and non-differentiation, and through their profound resolve, gradually fulfill all-knowledge.
They dedicate [their merit] so that all sentient beings may dwell securely in all pure dharmas;
they dedicate it so that all sentient beings may, within a single thought-moment, realize all-knowledge and attain the ultimate;
they dedicate it so that all sentient beings may fully accomplish the pure path of all-knowledge.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Having dedicated all roots of goodness for the sake of all sentient beings in this manner, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further dedicates these roots of goodness with the desire to universally fulfill the power of expounding all pure practices;
and with the desire to achieve the majestic power of pure conduct and attain unspeakably unspeakable oceans of Dharma, they dedicate them.”
They dedicate their merit because they desire to fully possess the light of pure wisdom that is equal to the Dharma-realm within each and every ocean of dharmas;
because they desire to reveal and expound the distinct phrases and meanings of all dharmas;
and because they desire to accomplish the boundlessly vast samādhi of the light of all dharmas.
They dedicate [their merit] because they wish to accord with the eloquence of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
they dedicate because they wish to accomplish the sovereign bodies of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
and they dedicate out of reverence for the delightful and unobstructed Dharma of all Buddhas.
They dedicate their merit so as to fulfill the mind of great compassion, never retreating in the rescue and protection of all sentient beings;

they dedicate it because they desire to accomplish inconceivable and diverse dharmas, unobstructed wisdom, a mind free from defilement, and the purity of all faculties, thereby universally entering all assemblies and sites of enlightenment;

they dedicate it because they desire to constantly turn the equal and non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma in all such Buddha-lands—whether inverted or upright, coarse or subtle, vast or narrow, small or large, defiled or pure.
They dedicate their merit because they wish to attain, in every moment of thought, the various inexhaustible eloquences and the light of the wondrous Dharma to reveal and expound it;

they dedicate their merit because they seek all that is wholesome with joy, giving rise to the resolve to practice so that their faculties become increasingly superior, attaining the great supernormal knowledge of all dharmas, and being able to fully comprehend all phenomena;
they dedicate their merit because they wish to approach and make offerings at all assemblies and sites of enlightenment, expounding all dharmas for all sentient beings to cause them all to rejoice.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
namely, ‘by dedicating through abiding in the immeasurable abidings of the Dharma-realm, by dedicating through abiding in the immeasurable physical actions of the Dharma-realm...’”
Dedication by abiding in the immeasurable verbal karma of the dharma-realm; dedication by abiding in the immeasurable mental karma of the dharma-realm;
dedication by abiding in the equality of immeasurable form within the dharma-realm;
dedication by abiding in the equality of immeasurable feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness within the dharma-realm; dedication by abiding in the immeasurable... [of the dharma-realm].
Dedication through the equality of the aggregates; dedication through abiding in the equality of the infinite realms of the *dharmadhātu*;
dedication through abiding in the equality of the infinite locations of the *dharmadhātu*; dedication through abiding in the equality of the infinite internal [realms] of the *dharmadhātu*;
dedication through abiding in the equality of the infinite external [realms] of the *dharmadhātu*; dedication through abiding in the infinite... of the *dharmadhātu*.
They initiate equal dedications: through dedication with an immeasurable, profound mind abiding in the dharma-realm;
through dedication with immeasurable skillful means abiding in the dharma-realm; through dedication with immeasurable faith and understanding abiding in the dharma-realm;
through dedication with immeasurable faculties abiding in the dharma-realm; and so forth.
They dedicate with the equality of the infinite past, present, and future limits of the dharma-realm;
they dedicate by abiding in the equality of the infinite karmic retributions of the dharma-realm; they dedicate by abiding in the equality of the infinite defilement and purity of the dharma-realm;
they dedicate by abiding in the equality of the infinite sentient beings of the dharma-realm; they dedicate by abiding in the dharma-realm... [infinite]... [text continues].
They dedicate with the equality of all Buddha-fields; they dedicate by abiding in the equality of the infinite dharmas of the dharma-realm;
they dedicate by abiding in the equality of the infinite light of the world within the dharma-realm;

they dedicate by abiding in the equality of the infinite Buddhas and Bodhisattvas within the dharma-realm; and they dedicate by abiding in the infinite practices and vows of Bodhisattvas within the dharma-realm.
They perform equal dedication by means of the equal dedication of the emergence of immeasurable bodhisattvas abiding in the dharma-realm;
they perform equal dedication by means of the equal dedication of the teaching and disciplining of immeasurable bodhisattvas abiding in the dharma-realm;

they perform equal dedication by means of the equal dedication of the non-duality of immeasurable dharmadhātus abiding in the dharma-realm; and they perform equal dedication by means of immeasurable Tathāgatas abiding in the dharma-realm.

“...dedicating it equally toward the assemblies and the sites of enlightenment. “O Son of the Buddha! When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate in this way, they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure body of the Dharma-realm; they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure speech of the Dharma-realm; they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure mind of the Dharma-realm; they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure conduct and vows of all Bodhisattvas within the Dharma-realm; they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure assemblies and sites of enlightenment within the Dharma-realm; they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure wisdom that extensively expounds all dharmas for all Bodhisattvas within the Dharma-realm; they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure bodies capable of entering all worlds throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm within the Dharma-realm; and they abide in the infinite, equal, and pure fearlessness of the light of all dharmas within the Dharma-realm.”

They are able, with a single voice, to completely sever the net of doubts of all sentient beings; according to their faculties and inclinations, they cause them all to rejoice, abiding in the unsurpassed knowledge of all modes, the powers, the fearlessnesses, sovereign spiritual penetrations, vast merits, and the dharma of transcendence.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the tenth dwelling of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the immeasurable dedication equal to the Dharma-realm.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness, such as the gift of Dharma, in this manner, they fulfill the immeasurable and boundless bodhisattva practices and vows of Samantabhadra; they are able to adorn and purify all buddha-fields throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm, which is coextensive with space, and cause all sentient beings likewise to attain this, fully accomplishing boundless wisdom and comprehending all phenomena. In every thought-moment, they see all Buddhas appearing in the world, and in every thought-moment, they see the immeasurable and boundless sovereign powers of all Buddhas, namely:”
The sovereign power of vastness; the sovereign power of non-attachment; the sovereign power of non-obstruction; the sovereign power of the inconceivable;
the sovereign power of purifying all sentient beings; the sovereign power of establishing all worlds;
the sovereign power of manifesting ineffable speech; and the sovereign power of appearing in accordance with the times.

The power of mastery over the wisdom of non-regressive spiritual penetrations; the power of mastery in expounding all boundless realms of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) without exception; the power of mastery in generating the boundless eye of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
and the power of mastery in hearing, retaining, and upholding the true Dharma of immeasurable Buddhas with unimpeded auditory consciousness. One...

With his body seated in the full lotus posture, he possesses the power of sovereign mastery that is not cramped or restricted among all sentient beings throughout the infinite dharma-realms of the ten directions;
and he possesses the power of sovereign mastery over the infinite dharmas of the three periods of time through the entry of perfect wisdom.
Furthermore, they attain immeasurable purity, namely: the purity of all sentient beings;

the purity of all Buddha-fields; the purity of all phenomena; the purity of the wisdom that universally knows all places; the purity of boundless wisdom pervading the realm of empty space; the purity of attaining the wisdom of all distinct sounds and voices to universally respond to sentient beings through various modes of speech; the purity of emitting immeasurable, perfect light that universally illuminates all boundless worlds; the purity of generating the wisdom of the practices of all Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time; the purity of the wisdom that enters, in a single thought-moment, the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; and the purity of entering all boundless worlds to cause all sentient beings to perform what each ought to do.

All these [qualities] have been fully attained, all have been accomplished, all have been cultivated, all have been made equal, all have become manifest, all have been known and seen, all have been entered into, all have been observed, all have been purified, and they have reached the further shore.
At that time, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten million buddha-fields in each of the ten directions shook in six ways:

namely, they moved, moved everywhere, and moved equally everywhere; they rose, rose everywhere, and rose equally everywhere; they surged, surged everywhere, and surged equally everywhere; they quaked, quaked everywhere, and quaked equally everywhere; they roared, roared everywhere, and roared equally everywhere; they crashed, crashed everywhere, and crashed equally everywhere.

By the spiritual power of the Buddha and because such is the nature of the Dharma, there rained down celestial flowers, celestial garlands, celestial powdered incense, various celestial incenses, celestial garments, celestial jewels, celestial ornaments, celestial maṇi-gems, celestial aloeswood incense, celestial sandalwood incense, exquisite celestial parasols, various celestial banners, multicolored celestial pennants, and the bodies of incalculable devas.

There arose immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of unspeakably many celestial sounds of the sublime Dharma, inconceivable celestial voices praising the Buddha, and incalculable celestial cries of joy, all exclaiming, "Excellent!
Immeasurable incalculable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of devas paid respectful homage and prostrated themselves.
Innumerable sons of heaven constantly keep the Buddhas in mind, seeking the immeasurable merits of the Tathāgatas with a heart that never forsakes them;
innumerable sons of heaven perform various musical performances, singing hymns and offering praise to make offerings to the Tathāgata;

hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya devas emit great radiance, universally illuminating all Buddha-lands throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, manifesting the infinite, asaṃkhyeya realms of the Buddhas.

The emanation body of the Tathāgata transcends all devas; just as he has preached this Dharma here in the Tuṣita Heaven palace of this world, it is likewise throughout all the Tuṣita Heaven palaces in every world of the ten directions.

At that time, again, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, from beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten million buddha-fields in each of the ten directions, there came to this assembly bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten million buddha-fields, filling the ten directions, all of whom spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent!
O Son of the Buddha!
You are indeed able to speak of these great dedications.
O Son of the Buddha!
We are all of one and the same name: Vajradhvaja;
we have all come to this land from the presence of the Buddha Vajradhvaja in the world Vajraprabhā.

All those worlds, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, proclaim this Dharma; the assembly of followers, the phrasing, and the meaning of the words are all likewise, neither increasing nor decreasing.
We have all come from that land by the Buddha’s spiritual power to bear witness for you.

Just as we have come to this assembly to bear witness for you, so too have all the bodhisattvas from the Tuṣita Heavens throughout all worlds in the ten directions come to this precious Adorned Hall to bear witness.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed all the assemblies in the ten directions as far as the Dharma-realm. Having thoroughly understood the words and their meanings, he expanded his vast mind; with great compassion universally covering all sentient beings, he fixed his mind in abiding within the seed of the Buddhas of the three periods of time. Skillfully entering into all the dharmas of the Buddhas’ merits, he accomplished the sovereign bodies of all Buddhas. Observing the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings and discerning all the roots of goodness they had planted, he manifested a body of pure and wondrous form in accordance with the Dharma-body.
Thereupon, at that very moment, he spoke in verse: “The Bodhisattva accomplishes the wisdom of the Dharma, And awakens to and understands the boundless gates of the True Dharma.”
He is the Teacher and Guide who illuminates the Dharma, thoroughly understanding the unimpeded and true reality of all phenomena.
The Bodhisattva is a great guide for the Dharma, Revealing the profound and rare teachings;
Leading immeasurable multitudes throughout the ten directions, Causing them all to dwell securely within the True Dharma.
The Bodhisattva has already drunk from the ocean of the Buddha-dharma; From the clouds of Dharma, he rains universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
The sun of Dharma appears in the world, Proclaiming the wondrous Dharma to benefit all living beings.
Always a donor of the Dharma who is difficult to encounter, thoroughly understanding the skillful means for entering the Dharma;
with the pure light of the Dharma illuminating their mind, they always teach the Dharma in the world without fear.
Skillfully cultivating mastery over the mind of the Dharma, they are able to penetrate all gateways of the teachings;
having accomplished the ocean of profound and wondrous Dharmas, they everywhere beat the drum of the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.
He proclaims the profound and rare Dharma, Nurturing all virtues through the Dharma;
Possessing a mind of pure joy in the Dharma, He reveals the treasury of the Buddha's teachings to the world.
Consecrated by all Buddhas, the Kings of Dharma, they have perfected the body that is the treasury of the wisdom of dharmatā;
they fully comprehend the true nature of phenomena and abide securely in all wholesome dharmas.
The Bodhisattva practices the foremost generosity, which all Tathāgatas praise and rejoice in;
whatever they do is validated by the Buddhas, and through this, they achieve the state of the Honored One among Men.
The Bodhisattva has accomplished the wondrous Dharma-body, Personally born through transformation from the teachings of all Buddhas;
To benefit sentient beings, he acts as a lamp of Dharma, Expounding the immeasurable, most supreme teachings.
In accordance with the sublime Dharma-gift practiced, one likewise observes those roots of goodness;
whatever merits are performed for the sake of sentient beings, all are dedicated through wisdom.
All the meritorious dharmas of attaining Buddhahood, I dedicate them entirely to all living beings;
may they all be purified and reach the further shore of the Buddha’s adornments.
The Buddha-fields of the ten directions are immeasurable, Each fully endowed with immeasurable great adornments;
Such adornments are inconceivable, Yet all are used to adorn a single land.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the pure wisdom of the Tathāgata,
Just like Samantabhadra, the true son of the Buddha, Adorned by all merits of their own accord.
Having accomplished vast and great supernormal powers, they travel throughout all worlds without exception;
they cause every single sentient being to practice the path of the bodhisattva.
All sentient beings throughout the ten directions, Whom the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, have brought to awakening—
May they all become like Samantabhadra, Fully accomplishing the supreme practices.
The various and diverse merits accomplished by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas—such merits are boundless; may all sentient beings fully perfect them.
The Bodhisattva, endowed with the power of mastery, goes to study all the precepts that should be learned;
manifesting all great supernormal powers, he travels everywhere to the infinite lands of the ten directions.
In a single moment of thought, the Bodhisattva can behold countless Buddhas, equal in number to all sentient beings;
furthermore, within a single hair-tip, they encompass all phenomena and perceive them all with perfect clarity.
The sentient beings of the world are immeasurable, yet the Bodhisattva is able to discern and know them all;
the Buddhas are as immeasurable as these beings, and with a great mind, he makes offerings to them all until none remain.
With various kinds of named incenses and most excellent flowers, With robes of many jewels and banners and canopies,
Distributed throughout the entire Dharma-realm until it is completely filled, They resolve their minds to universally make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Within a single pore, one clearly perceives Buddhas of inconceivable and immeasurable number;
In every pore it is likewise, As one universally pays homage to all the Lamps of the World.
Bowing with reverence, body by body, in successive order, I likewise praise all these infinite,
most supreme ones with words, throughout every kalpa until the end of the future.
The articles of offering for a single Tathāgata are as infinite in number as all sentient beings;
with such offerings one makes worship to a single Tathāgata, and it is likewise for all Tathāgatas.
Making offerings and praising all Tathāgatas throughout every kalpa of that world—
though the number of kalpas in the world may come to an end, the Bodhisattva’s offerings never cease or grow weary.
Throughout all the various eons of every world, practicing all manner of deeds for that many eons,
one reverently makes offerings to a single Tathāgata, never becoming weary or satisfied throughout the exhaustion of all eons.
As one might make offerings to a single Buddha for immeasurable eons, so too should one offer to all Buddhas;
yet one does not discriminate regarding the number of these eons, nor does one give rise to weariness or distaste toward those to whom one offers.
The Dharma-realm is vast and without limit; the Bodhisattva observes it all with complete clarity.
Within it, he spreads great lotus flowers everywhere, bestowing immeasurable Buddhas equal in number to all sentient beings.
The precious flowers, fragrances, and colors are all perfect; pure and adorned, they are most subtle and wondrous.
Nothing in all the worlds can compare to them, as they are held to make offerings to the Honored One among Men.
In as many immeasurable lands as there are sentient beings, Filled with various exquisite jeweled canopies, One makes offerings to a single Tathāgata; To offer to all Buddhas is likewise so.
This unexcelled and most supreme fragrant ointment, never before seen in any world,
is offered to the Teacher of Gods and Humans for as many eons as there are sentient beings.
With powdered incense, burning incense, and most exquisite flowers, with robes of various jewels and ornaments—
thus making offerings to all the Most Victorious Ones, they serve them with joy, never wearying.
As many as there are sentient beings, so many lamps illuminating the world, each moment realizing great enlightenment;
with boundless verses they offer praise and make offerings to the Tamer of Men.

If Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as all sentient beings, were to practice supreme and wondrous offerings for as many immeasurable eons as there are sentient beings, even such praise would never come to an end.
When making such offerings to all Buddhas, through the Buddha’s spiritual power they pervade everywhere;
they see the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions, abiding securely in the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
All roots of goodness throughout the past, future, and present—
may they cause me to constantly practice the conduct of Samantabhadra and swiftly attain abiding in the stage of Samantabhadra.
May all the infinite sentient beings in the world, as known and seen by all Tathāgatas,
come to possess every quality like that of Samantabhadra, and be praised by those who are wise.
This is the practice of dedication cultivated together by the great beings of the ten directions;
the Tathāgatas have taught it to me—this practice of dedication is most unsurpassed.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions without exception, may all sentient beings therein be led to awakening,
so that they may always act in accordance with the conduct of Samantabhadra.
If one practices giving with such dedication, likewise maintains the prohibitive precepts firmly,
exerts diligence over a long period without retreat or fear, remains patient and gentle with an unshakable mind,
holds the heart in meditative concentration always on a single object, and through wisdom realizes that objects are identical to samādhi—
They thoroughly penetrate the past, future, and present; no one in the world can reach their limit.
The bodhisattva’s physical, mental, and verbal actions—all such deeds are utterly pure.
Without exception in all their practices, they are entirely equal to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Just as the dharma-realm is without discrimination, where conceptual proliferation and defiled attachment are forever exhausted;
and just as nirvana is without obstruction, so too is the mind always thus, free from all grasping.
The method of dedication possessed by the wise has already been revealed by all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas;
by dedicating all various roots of goodness, one is thus able to accomplish the path of a bodhisattva.

The Sons of the Buddha who skillfully train in this dedication, Fully accomplish immeasurable practices and vows, And encompass the entire Dharma-realm without exception; Therefore, they are able to achieve the power of the Sugatas.
If you wish to accomplish the vast and sublime practices taught by the Buddha, you should dwell well in this dedication; such a son of the Buddhas is named Samantabhadra.
All sentient beings may be counted, And the mental dimensions of the three periods of time may also be known;
Yet the limits of the merit of such sons of the Buddhas, Samantabhadra, Can never be measured.
One might measure the limits of space with a single hair, And one might count the number of atoms in all lands;
Yet for these great sages, the sons of the Buddhas, The conduct, dwellings, and vows they practice are immeasurable.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-three;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Order.
Chapter Twenty-Six: The Ten Stages, Part One.
At that time, the World-Honored One was in the Maṇi-jewel Treasury Hall within the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, together with a great assembly of Bodhisattvas.
All those bodhisattvas were non-retrogressive regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and had all come together from worlds in other directions;
they dwelt in the sphere where the wisdom of all bodhisattvas abides and entered the state where the wisdom of all Tathāgatas enters;
they practiced with tireless diligence, skillfully manifesting various supernatural powers and deeds, teaching and taming all sentient beings without missing the proper time.
To fulfill all the great vows of a bodhisattva, they diligently cultivate all practices throughout all worlds, all eons, and all lands, never ceasing for even a moment;
they are fully endowed with the bodhisattva’s accumulations of merit and wisdom that aid the path, universally benefiting sentient beings without ever becoming exhausted;
they reach the ultimate further shore of all bodhisattvas’ wisdom and skillful means, manifesting entry into both birth-and-death and nirvana without ever abandoning them.

Practicing the bodhisattva path, they skillfully enter all bodhisattva meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), samādhis, attainments (*samāpatti*), and the wisdom of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*); in all their activities, they attain mastery.

Having acquired the sovereign spiritual powers of all bodhisattvas, they are able, without any physical movement, to travel in a single thought-moment to the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Tathāgatas; there, acting as leaders of the assembly, they request the Buddhas to preach the Dharma and protect and uphold the wheel of the True Dharma of all Buddhas.
With a vast mind, they make offerings to and serve all Buddhas, constantly and diligently practicing all the deeds performed by bodhisattvas.

His body manifests universally throughout all worlds; his voice reaches everywhere across the dharma-realm of the ten directions; his mind and wisdom are unimpeded, seeing clearly through the three periods of time;
he has fully practiced and perfected all the merits of every bodhisattva, such that they could not be fully described even in unspeakable eons.
Their names were: Vajragarbha Bodhisattva, Ratnagarbha Bodhisattva, Padmagarbha Bodhisattva, Guṇagarbha Bodhisattva,
Padmaguṇagarbha Bodhisattva, Sūryagarbha Bodhisattva, and Sūryagarbha Bodhisattva.
...the Bodhisattva Vimalacandragarbha, the Bodhisattva Sarvabuddhakṣetrasamantavyūhagarbha,
the Bodhisattva Vairocanajñānagarbha, the Bodhisattva Guṇakūṭagarbha, the Bodhisattva Candanaguṇagarbha,
the Bodhisattva Puṣpavarṇagarbha, the Bodhisattva Kusumaguṇagarbha, and the Bodhisattva Utpalagarbha...
Bodhisattva Guṇagañja, Bodhisattva Devaguṇagañja, Bodhisattva Puṇyagañja, Bodhisattva Asaṅgapariśuddhajñānaguṇagañja, Bodhisattva Guṇagañja, Bodhisattva Nārāyaṇaguṇagañja,
Bodhisattva Vimalagañja, Bodhisattva Vigatamalaprabhāsagañja, and Bodhisattva Nānāpratibhānavicitravyūhagañja.
The Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva Great Radiance Net Treasury, the Bodhisattva Pure Splendor Radiance King Treasury,
the Bodhisattva Gold Adorned Great Merit Radiance King Treasury, the Bodhisattva All-Aspect Adorned Pure Virtue Treasury,
the Bodhisattva Vajra Flame Virtue Sign Adornment Treasury, and the Bodhisattva Radiant Flame Treasury.
The Bodhisattvas: Star-King Radiant Illumination Treasury Bodhisattva, Space Unobstructed Wisdom Treasury Bodhisattva,
Wondrous Sound Unobstructed Treasury Bodhisattva, Dharani Merit Sustainer of All Sentient Beings’ Vow Treasury Bodhisattva,
Ocean Adornment Treasury Bodhisattva, Sumeru Virtue Treasury Bodhisattva, and Pure One...
The Bodhisattva Sarvaguṇakośa, the Bodhisattva Tathāgatagarbha, the Bodhisattva Buddhaguṇakośa, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, and so forth—

this assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, which was incalculable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, uncountable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, and unspeakable, with Vajragarbha Bodhisattva as its leader.
At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, entered the bodhisattva samādhi called "Great Wisdom Radiance.

Having entered this samādhi, immediately there appeared before him, from beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields in each of the ten directions, ten billion buddhas—each as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields—all sharing the same name:
Vajragarbha. They spoke these words:
“Excellent, excellent, Vajragarbha!
You are indeed able to enter this Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Radiance of Great Wisdom.”

"Good son! This is because all the Buddhas of ten billion Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions are collectively empowering you, through the power of the original vows of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana, through his majestic spiritual power, and also through the power of your own supreme wisdom, desiring that you explain to all bodhisattvas the light of the inconceivable teachings of all Buddhas."

That is to say: because it causes entry into the stage of wisdom; because it gathers all roots of goodness; because it skillfully discriminates all Buddha-dharmas; because it extensively knows all phenomena; because it is well able to expound the Dharma; because non-conceptual wisdom is purified; because one is unsullied by any worldly dharmas; because supramundane roots of goodness are purified; because one attains the sphere of inconceivable wisdom; and because one attains the sphere of the wisdom of the Omniscient One.

Furthermore, it causes them to attain the beginning and end of the ten stages of a bodhisattva; to explain, as they truly are, the distinct characteristics of the ten bodhisattva stages; to bring to mind all Buddha-dharmas; to cultivate and differentiate the untainted dharmas (*anāsrava-dharma*); to skillfully adorn themselves with the light of great wisdom through excellent selection and observation; to skillfully enter the gateway of definitive knowledge (*niyata-jñāna*); to sequentially and fearlessly proclaim the teachings wherever they dwell; to attain the light of unimpeded eloquence (*asaṅga-pratibhāna*); to abide securely in the stage of great eloquence; to maintain mindfulness of the bodhisattva-mind without forgetfulness; to bring all realms of sentient beings to maturity; and to be able to reach all places to provide certain awakening.
"Noble son! You should skillfully explain the distinctions within this Dharma gate, namely:

By virtue of receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power and being empowered by the Tathāgata’s wisdom-light; by purifying one’s own roots of goodness; by universally purifying the Dharma-realm; by universally gathering in all sentient beings; by deeply entering the Dharma-body and the Wisdom-body; by receiving the empowerment of all Buddhas; by attaining the most exalted and sublime body among all worlds; by transcending all worldly paths; by purifying supramundane roots of goodness; and by fulfilling the knowledge of all-knowledge.

At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha a body that could not be eclipsed by others; they bestowed unimpeded eloquence for joyful exposition; they bestowed pure wisdom capable of excellent discernment; they bestowed the power of excellent recollection and non-forgetfulness; they bestowed clear and decisive wisdom; they bestowed the wisdom of awakening that reaches all places; they bestowed the sovereign power of attaining the Way; they bestowed the fearlessnesses of a Tathāgata; they bestowed the eloquence and wisdom of an omniscient one who observes and discerns the various Dharma-gates; and they bestowed the supreme adornments of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Why is this? It is because the nature of this samādhi-dharma is thus; because it arises from original vows; because of the thorough purity of the profound mind; because of the thorough purity of the wheel of wisdom; because of the thorough accumulation of the factors conducive to enlightenment; because of the thorough cultivation and refinement of what is to be done; because of mindfulness of immeasurable vessels for the Dharma; because of knowing their pure faith and understanding; because of attaining the dhāraṇī free from error; and because of being well-sealed by the seal of wisdom regarding the dharma-realm.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions each extended their right hands and stroked the crown of Vajragarbha Bodhisattva’s head.
Having stroked his head, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva arose from samādhi and addressed the entire assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
“O Sons of the Buddha!

The vows of all Bodhisattvas are well-determined, unadulterated, and invisible; they are as vast as the Dharma-realm and as ultimate as space. Reaching to the end of the future and pervading all Buddha-fields, they rescue and protect all sentient beings, are guarded by all Buddhas, and enter the ground of wisdom of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
O Son of the Buddha!
What is the stage of wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?
O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten stages of wisdom for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, which have been taught by the Buddhas of the past, will be taught by those of the future, and are being taught by those of the present;
I, too, teach them in this same way.
What are these ten? First is the Stage of Joy;

second, the Stage of Purity; third, the Stage of Radiance; fourth, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom; fifth, the Stage Difficult to Conquer; sixth, the Stage of Manifestation; seventh, the Stage of Far-Going; eighth, the Immovable Stage; ninth, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence; and tenth, the Stage of the Dharma Cloud.
O Son of the Buddha!

These ten stages of the bodhisattva have been taught by all Buddhas of the three periods of time—those who have taught them in the past, those who will teach them in the future, and those who are teaching them now.
O Son of the Buddha!
I do not see any buddha-fields wherein the Tathāgatas do not teach these ten stages.
Why is this? Because these are the supreme path toward enlightenment for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and they are also gateways to the light of the pure Dharma, namely:
He analytically expounds the various stages (*bhūmi*) of the bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
This matter is inconceivable, namely, the wisdom realized by each bodhisattva according to their own attainment.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha had spoken these names of the ten bodhisattva stages, he remained silent and ceased further analysis.
Then, the entire assembly of bodhisattvas, having heard the names of the ten bodhisattva stages but not hearing their explanation, all felt a sense of longing and thirst, and thought to themselves:
"For what cause and for what reason does the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha merely state the names of the ten bodhisattva stages without explaining them?"
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the great assembly, questioned the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha in verse:
"Why does the one of pure awakening, Endowed with mindfulness, wisdom, and merit,
Speak of these most excellent stages, Yet possess the power to explain them not?"
All are resolute and courageous, free from any timidity;
why then do you speak only of the names of the stages and not expound upon them?
The wondrous meaning and intent of these stages—this assembly all desires to hear.
Their minds are free from timidity; I pray you explain this for them!
This assembly is entirely pure, free from indolence and adorned with cleanliness;
they are steadfast and immovable, endowed with merit and wisdom.
They gazed at one another with mutual reverence; all were single-mindedly devoted and looked up to him, like bees longing for fine honey, or like the thirsty yearning for nectar.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, of great wisdom and fearlessness, having heard these words, spoke in verse for the sake of the sons of the Buddha, desiring to bring joy to the hearts of the assembled multitude:
"The deeds of the bodhisattva stages, the supreme foundation of all Buddhas—
To reveal, analyze, and explain them is the foremost rarity and difficulty.
Subtle and difficult to perceive, they transcend thought and surpass the sphere of the mind."
Born into the realm of the Buddhas, those who hear this are entirely bewildered.
Holding the mind like a vajra, with deep faith in the supreme wisdom of the Buddha,
and knowing that the ground of the mind is without self— one can hear this sublime Dharma.
Like a painted image in the sky, like the appearance of wind in the air, so is the wisdom of the Muni;
its distinctions are exceedingly difficult to perceive.
As I contemplate the Buddha’s wisdom, it is most supreme and inconceivable.
"No one in the world is able to receive [it], so they remain silent and do not speak.
At that time, having heard these words, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!..."

Now this assembly has all gathered together; they possess pure and profound resolve, pure and refined contemplation, and have well cultivated all practices. They have well accumulated the factors conducive to enlightenment, have been able to draw near hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddhas, and have accomplished immeasurable roots of merit and virtue. Having abandoned delusion and confusion, they are free from defilement; with deep resolve and faith-understanding, they do not follow the teachings of others regarding the Buddha-dharma.
Excellent, Son of the Buddha!
You should expound this by virtue of the Buddha’s spiritual power, for these bodhisattvas are all able to realize and know such profound matters as these.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse:
"May you explain the most secure and peaceful The supreme conduct of the bodhisattvas,
Distinguishing the various stages, And how through the purity of wisdom one attains perfect enlightenment."
"This assembly is free from all defilements; their resolve and understanding are entirely clear and pure.
Having served immeasurable Buddhas, they are able to know the meaning of this stage.
At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
“O Son of the Buddha!
Although this assembly has gathered with pure and virtuous reflection, having abandoned ignorance and doubt, and does not rely on the teachings of others regarding the profound Dharma;

yet there are other beings of inferior understanding who, upon hearing these profound and inconceivable matters, will give rise to much doubt and confusion, suffering various forms of decline and affliction throughout the long night.”
"I have compassion for these beings; therefore, I remain silent.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse:
"Though this assembly is pure and possesses vast wisdom, Profound, brilliant, and capable of discernment,"
Their minds are as immovable as the king of mountains, and like the great ocean, they cannot be overturned.
Yet, having practiced for but a short time and not yet attained liberation, they act according to consciousness rather than wisdom;
hearing this, they give rise to doubt and fall into evil realms. Out of compassion for such as these, I do not speak [of it].
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha once more, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!

We pray that you will, by virtue of the Buddha’s spiritual power, analyze and explain this inconceivable Dharma; these people shall receive the Tathāgata’s protective mindfulness and give rise to faith and acceptance."
Why is this? When the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) are taught, all bodhisattva dharmas should be thus: they receive the Buddha’s protective mindfulness (*buddhānugraha*).
Because they receive this protective mindfulness, they are able to give rise to heroic vigor (*vīrya*) within this stage of wisdom.
Why is this? Because this is the primary practice of a bodhisattva, for it brings to fulfillment all the qualities of a Buddha.
It is like letters and numerical calculations; everything takes the alphabet as its basis and culminates in the alphabet, and there is not the slightest thing that is separate from the alphabet.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddha-dharmas take the ten stages as their foundation; through the ultimate cultivation and accomplishment of these ten stages, one attains all-knowledge.
Therefore, O Son of the Buddha!
"Please expound this for us!
This person must surely be protected by the Tathāgata, so that they may believe and accept it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
“Excellent, Son of the Buddha! We pray that you will expound upon the practices of the stages for entering into Bodhi.
Among all the Sovereign Honored Ones of the ten directions, there is none who does not protect and mindfully regard this root of wisdom.”
This abiding wisdom is also ultimate; it is the source from which all Buddha-dharmas arise.
Just as all scripts and numbers are subsumed within the alphabet, so too do all Buddha-dharmas depend upon the stages (bhūmis).
At that time, the assembly of great bodhisattvas simultaneously raised their voices in unison and addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha with these verses:
“O you of supreme, stainless wisdom, With boundless analytical eloquence,
You proclaim profound and beautiful words That accord with the ultimate truth.”
Mindfully maintaining pure conduct, Accumulating merit through the ten powers,
And discerning meanings with eloquence, He speaks of this most supreme stage.
With concentration and precepts, he gathers a right mind, Free from conceit and false views.
This assembly is free from doubt; we only wish to hear your excellent discourse!
Like the thirsty longing for cool water, like the hungry thinking of delicious food, like the sick remembering a potent medicine, or like bees craving fine honey.
We too are likewise; we pray to hear the Dharma of the Deathless!
O you of excellent and vast wisdom, pray speak of the entry into the stages, the accomplishment of the ten powers and unimpededness, and all the practices of the Sugata!

At that time, the World-Honored One emitted from between his eyebrows a pure light named "Flame-Light of the Bodhisattva’s Power," with hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* lights as its retinue. It shone universally throughout all worlds in the ten directions, leaving no place unpenetrated, so that the sufferings of the three evil realms were all brought to rest;
furthermore, it illuminated the assemblies of all Tathāgatas, manifesting the inconceivable power of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, it illuminates the bodies of all Bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who have been empowered by all Buddhas to preach the Dharma;
having performed this deed, it abides in the space above as a great cloud-net terrace of radiant light.

At that time, all the Buddhas of the ten directions likewise emitted pure light from between their eyebrows; the names, retinues, and functions of these lights were identical to those here. Furthermore, they illuminated this Sahā world—the Buddha and the great assembly, as well as the body and lion throne of Vajragarbha Bodhisattva—and then, in the space above, formed a great cloud-net pavilion of radiant light.
At that time, from within the hall of light, through the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas, these verses were spoken:

"The Buddha is unequaled, like empty space; With ten powers and immeasurable, supreme merits, The most excellent among humans and highest in the world— May the Dharma of the Lion of the Śākyas be bestowed upon them."
O Son of the Buddha, you should, by the power of all Buddhas, open this most excellent treasury of the Dharma King—
its vast wisdom of the stages and its sublime practices— and explain them in detail through the majestic spiritual authority of the Buddha.
If one is empowered by the strength of the Sugata, One shall obtain the jewel of the Dharma and enter it into one's heart;
The stainless stages will be fulfilled in succession, And one will likewise possess the ten powers of a Tathāgata.
Though one may dwell amidst the waters of the ocean or within the fires at the end of an eon, if one is capable of receiving this Dharma, one will surely hear it;
yet those who harbor doubts and lack faith shall never hear such a teaching as this.
One should explain the path of supreme wisdom of the various stages, Which is practiced through successive entry, abiding, and progression;
From this, the knowledge of dharmas arises regarding the spheres of practice, For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha surveyed the ten directions and, wishing to increase the pure faith of the great assembly, spoke these verses:
“The path of the Tathāgata, the Great Sage, Is subtle and difficult to know;
It is beyond thought and free from all conceptualization, And though one seeks to see it, it cannot be found.”
Without arising and without ceasing, its nature is pure and eternally tranquil;
this is the sphere of activity for the wise who are free from defilement.
Its self-nature is fundamentally empty and still, non-dual and inexhaustible.
Liberated from all realms of existence, one abides in the equality of nirvāṇa.
Neither beginning, middle, nor end; it cannot be expressed by words;
transcending the three periods of time, its characteristic is like space.
The realm of the Buddhas is quiescent cessation; no words can reach it.
The practice of the stages is likewise: difficult to explain and difficult to receive.
The arising of wisdom is the Buddha’s domain; it is beyond thought and apart from the path of the mind.
It is not through the gates of the aggregates, elements, or sense-bases; it is known by wisdom, yet beyond the reach of the mind.
Like the track of a bird in the sky, difficult to describe and difficult to demonstrate, so too is the meaning of the ten stages, which the intellect and mind cannot comprehend.
Through compassion and the power of aspiration, one enters the stages of practice;
as the mind is perfected in successive order, the conduct of wisdom transcends the realm of deliberation.
This state is difficult to perceive; it may be known, yet it cannot be described.
Through the power of the Buddha, I shall expound this; you all should receive it with reverence.
Such entry into the practice of wisdom could not be fully told even in billions of eons;
I now speak only briefly, yet the true meaning is complete without remainder.
Wait with single-minded reverence as I, sustained by the Buddha’s power,
proclaim the subtle sounds of the supreme Dharma, expressed through parables and syllables.
The spiritual powers of immeasurable Buddhas all enter my body.
This place is difficult to proclaim; I shall now speak of but a small portion.
Regarding the first stage, the first stage: "O Son of the Buddha!..."
