Furthermore, by means of the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena (*dharmapratisaṃvid*), one knows the distinctions among present phenomena;
by means of the unimpeded knowledge of meaning (*arthapratisaṃvid*), one knows the distinctions among past and future phenomena;
and by means of the unimpeded knowledge of expression (*niruktipratisaṃvid*), one speaks of past, future, and present phenomena without error.
With the unimpeded knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid*), one clearly explains the boundless dharmas within each and every world-age.
Furthermore, by means of the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena (*dharma-pratisaṃvid*), one knows the distinctions between phenomena;
by means of the unimpeded knowledge of meaning (*artha-pratisaṃvid*), one knows the distinctions between meanings.
The unimpeded knowledge of expression (nirukti-pratisaṃvid) is to preach according to their speech and sounds;
the unimpeded knowledge of eloquence (pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid) is to preach according to what their minds delight in.
Furthermore, the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena (dharma-pratisaṃvid) is to know distinctions as non-different through the knowledge of phenomena (dharma-jñāna).
The unimpeded knowledge of meaning (*arthapratisaṃvid*) knows distinctions as they truly are through subsequent knowledge (*anvayajñāna*);
the unimpeded knowledge of expression (*niruktipratisaṃvid*) explains distinctions through conventional knowledge (*saṃvṛtijñāna*);
and the unimpeded knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhānapratisaṃvid*) explains with skill through the knowledge of the ultimate truth (*paramārthajñāna*).
Furthermore, the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena (*dharmapratisaṃvid*) knows that all phenomena possess a single, indestructible characteristic;

the unimpeded knowledge of meaning (*arthapratisaṃvid*) knows skillfulness regarding the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), sense bases (*āyatana*), truths (*satya*), and dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*);
the unimpeded knowledge of expression (*niruktipratisaṃvid*) explains using beautiful sounds and characters that are easily understood by all people in the world.
The unimpeded knowledge of eloquence is explained by means of the ever-increasing, boundless illumination of the Dharma.
Furthermore, the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena knows the equality of the One Vehicle;
the unimpeded knowledge of meaning knows the distinctiveness of the various vehicles.
With the unimpeded knowledge of expression (*nirukti-pratisaṃvid*), one explains all vehicles (*yāna*) without distinction;
with the unimpeded knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid*), one explains the boundless teachings of each individual vehicle.

Furthermore, with the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena (*dharma-pratisaṃvid*), one knows all bodhisattva practices, the practice of wisdom, and the practice of phenomena, realizing them in accordance with their nature.
The unimpeded knowledge of meaning (*arthapratisaṃvid*) knows the distinctions in the meanings of the stages and positions of the ten *bhūmis*;
the unimpeded knowledge of expression (*niruktipratisaṃvid*) explains the non-differentiated characteristics of the path and the stages;
and the unimpeded knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhānapratisaṃvid*) explains the boundless aspects of the practice of each individual stage.
Furthermore, the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena (*dharmapratisaṃvid*) knows that all Tathāgatas attain perfect enlightenment in a single thought-moment;
the unimpeded knowledge of meaning (*arthapratisaṃvid*) knows the various distinctions of different times and different places;
and the unimpeded knowledge of expression (*niruktipratisaṃvid*) explains the distinctions of attaining perfect enlightenment.
The unimpeded knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid*) is such that one could speak upon even a single phrase of the Dharma for immeasurable eons without exhausting it.

Furthermore, the unimpeded knowledge of phenomena (*dharma-pratisaṃvid*) knows the speech, powers, fearlessnesses, unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), great loving-kindness and great compassion, eloquence, skillful means, the turning of the wheel of Dharma, and the realization of all-knowledge of all Tathāgatas.

The unimpeded knowledge of meaning (*artha-pratisaṃvid*) knows how the Tathāgata accords with the eighty-four thousand differences in the minds, conducts, faculties, understandings, and vocal expressions of sentient beings.
The unimpeded knowledge of eloquence follows the conduct of all sentient beings, expounding through the various distinctions of the Tathāgata’s voice;
the unimpeded knowledge of joyful exposition follows the faith and understanding of sentient beings, expounding through the fulfillment of the pure practices of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva dwells in the ninth stage, they attain such skillful and unimpeded wisdom and obtain the Tathāgata’s treasury of the sublime Dharma, acting as a great Dharma teacher. They attain the dharani of meaning, the dharani of dharma, the dharani of wisdom, the dharani of light-illumination, the dharani of excellent intelligence, the dharani of manifold wealth, the dharani of majestic power, the dharani of the gate of non-obstruction, the dharani of the limitless, and the dharani of various meanings. Thus, they fully perfect one million asaṃkhyeya dharani-gates and expound the Dharma through one million asaṃkhyeya gates of skillful sounds and eloquence.”

Having attained these millions of asaṃkhyeya dharanī-gates, this bodhisattva, before each and every one of the immeasurable Buddhas, listens to the True Dharma by means of these same millions of asaṃkhyeya dharanī-gates; having heard it, he does not forget it, and he expounds it for others through immeasurable gates of differentiation.
When this bodhisattva first beholds the Buddha, he prostrates with his head at the Buddha's feet and immediately receives immeasurable Dharma-gates from him;
these Dharma-gates received could not be fully grasped even by those great śrāvakas who possess the power of hearing and retaining, throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
Having attained such dhāraṇīs and such unimpeded wisdom, this bodhisattva sits upon the Dharma-seat and expounds the Dharma;
for the sentient beings filling the great trichiliocosm, he teaches according to the differences in their inclinations.
With the exception of the Buddhas and those bodhisattvas who have received their consecration, none among the remaining assembly can compare to his majestic virtue and radiance.
When this Bodhisattva sits upon the Dharma-seat, if he wishes to cause the entire great assembly to understand through a single voice, they immediately attain understanding;
or at times, he wishes to cause the entire great assembly to achieve awakening through various sounds;
or at times, his mind desires to emit great radiance and expound the Dharma-gates.
At times, he may wish that from every single pore of his body, the sound of the Dharma should be proclaimed;
at times, he may wish that all things, whether with form or formless, throughout the entire trichiliocosm, should all produce the sublime sounds of the Dharma;
or at times, he may wish to utter a single word or sound that pervades the entire Dharma-realm, causing all beings to understand it completely.
At times, they may desire that all speech and sounds become the sound of the Dharma, abiding eternally without ceasing;
at times, they may desire that the flutes, pipes, bells, drums, and songs of all worlds, as well as all musical sounds, proclaim the sound of the Dharma;
at times, they may desire that within a single syllable, all the various distinctions of dharma-terms and vocal expressions be fully contained.

At times, his mind desires that within the great aggregates of earth, water, fire, and wind throughout unspeakably immeasurable worlds, all the atoms contained therein should each, from every single atom, produce and proclaim unspeakable Dharma-gates.
"Whatever they thus contemplate, all accords with their minds; there is nothing they do not attain.
'O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose all sentient beings within the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world were to come before this Bodhisattva, and each were to pose difficult questions using immeasurable voices and sounds, with each question being distinct from the others;'"

In a single thought-moment, the Bodhisattva is able to receive them all in their entirety, and yet explains them universally with a single voice, causing each person to rejoice according to their own inclinations.

In this way, even if all sentient beings throughout unspeakably many worlds were to pose questions and challenges using immeasurable voices and sounds, each question being distinct from every other, the Bodhisattva is able to receive them all within a single thought-moment;
he then provides explanations for them all with a single voice, according to the inclinations of each heart, causing them all to attain joy.

Even for as many sentient beings as fill unspeakably unspeakable worlds, the bodhisattva is able to preach the Dharma to them according to their inclinations, faculties, and understandings; empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, they extensively perform the work of a Buddha and universally serve as a refuge for all.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva further exerts himself with diligence and achieves the illumination of wisdom.

Suppose that upon a single hair-tip there are assemblies of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many worlds, and in each assembly there are sentient beings as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many worlds; and suppose each sentient being possesses dispositions and desires as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many worlds—those Buddhas, according to those respective dispositions and desires, bestow upon them various Dharma-gates.
Just as it is at the tip of a single hair, so it is at every location throughout the entire dharma-realm.
Thus, regarding these immeasurable Dharma-gates that have been explained, the Bodhisattva is able to receive and retain them all within a single thought-moment, without any forgetfulness or loss.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva dwells in this ninth stage, they apply themselves with single-minded diligence day and night, having no other thoughts. They enter the realm of the Buddhas and draw near to the Tathāgatas; they enter the profound liberations of all bodhisattvas, constantly abide in samādhi, and perpetually behold all Buddhas, never departing from them.”

In each and every eon, they behold immeasurable Buddhas, immeasurable hundreds of Buddhas, immeasurable thousands of Buddhas, and even immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas. They revere, honor, serve, and make offerings to them; they pose various questions and challenges before these Buddhas, thereby attaining the *dhāraṇī* of the Dharma-exposition, and all their roots of goodness become increasingly bright and pure.

For example, just as pure gold fashioned by a skilled goldsmith into a precious crown adorns the head of a universal monarch (cakravartin), such that no ornamental regalia belonging to any minor kings, ministers, or subjects within the four continents can equal it;
so too are the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva in this ninth stage, for which all the roots of goodness of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas of the lower stages cannot equal.
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as the Great Brahmā King, lord of the two-thousandfold world system, emits light from his body that is able to illuminate the most remote and dark places within those two thousand worlds, thereby dispelling all gloom;

so too are all the roots of goodness of the Bodhisattvas on this stage, for they are able to emit light that illuminates the minds of sentient beings, causing the darkness of their afflictions to be completely extinguished.
Among the ten pāramitās, this bodhisattva’s pāramitā of power (bala-pāramitā) is the most preeminent;
it is not that they do not practice the remaining pāramitās, but they do so according to their power and capacity.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the brief explanation of the ninth stage of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (Sādhumatī).”
If explained in detail, it could not be exhausted even in immeasurable eons.
Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas dwell in this stage, they frequently become Great Brahmā Kings, lords of two thousand worlds. They are skillful in governance and sovereign in bringing benefit; they are able to analyze and expound the practice of the pāramitās for all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas.
In accordance with the minds of sentient beings, there is no one who can defeat him in debate regarding any questions or difficulties he may encounter.

Whether it be through giving, kind speech, beneficial action, or cooperation—indeed, in all such deeds he performs—he never departs from mindfulness of the Buddha, nor does he ever depart from mindfulness of all aspects or the knowledge of all modes.
Again, he forms this thought:
"I shall become the foremost among all sentient beings, the most excellent, and even the one upon whom the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) relies."

If this bodhisattva exerts diligent effort, in a single moment of thought, they attain as many samādhis as there are atoms in a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* worlds, and even manifest as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* worlds as their retinue;

yet if they manifest through the sovereign power of the bodhisattva’s sublime vows, it exceeds these numbers, such that even in hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayuta* kalpas one could not count or know them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse:
"With immeasurable power of wisdom he observes well; Most supreme and subtle, difficult for the world to know.
Universally entering the secret realm of the Tathāgatas, He benefits sentient beings and enters the ninth stage."
Mastery over all dhāraṇīs and samādhis, Attaining great supernormal powers to enter myriad lands;
Possessing the powers, wisdoms, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities, Through the power of vows and compassion, they enter the ninth stage.

Abiding in this stage, one upholds the treasury of the Dharma; One thoroughly understands the wholesome, the unwholesome, and the indeterminate, The out-flowing and the out-flow-free, the mundane and the supramundane, And knows well both the conceivable and the inconceivable.
Whether phenomena are determinate or indeterminate, they observe all that is accomplished by the three vehicles;
discerning the distinctions between conditioned and unconditioned activities, they thus know how to enter the world.
If one wishes to know the minds of all sentient beings, one can then know them as they truly are through wisdom—
knowing their various rapid transformations, whether decaying or non-decaying, and their manifold characteristics such as being without substance or being boundless.
Afflictions are boundless and ever-present as companions; whether dormant or active, they share a single nature as they continue through the various realms of existence.
The natures of karma are manifold and distinct; one can thus fully comprehend how causes perish and fruits accumulate.
The various faculties— whether inferior, middling, or superior— and their immeasurable distinctions across the past and future limits,
as well as the nature of understanding, inclinations, and desires, he knows all eighty-four thousand without exception.
Sentient beings are constantly bound by deluded views; the dense forest of beginningless [afflictions] has not yet been cleared away.
These arise together with their intentions and are born simultaneously with the mind, perpetually binding one another without interruption.
These are merely false imaginings and not substantial entities; they do not exist apart from the mind and have no location.
Even when dispelled through the state of meditative concentration, they still regress; only upon the destruction of them by the Vajra Path are they finally and utterly eliminated.

Birth in the six realms of existence differs for each; with karma as the field, craving as the moisture, and ignorance as the covering, consciousness acts as the seed and name-and-form as the sprout, continuing perpetually through the three realms without beginning.
Delusion, karma, and mental habituation give rise to the various realms of existence; if one is free from these, one is no longer reborn.
All sentient beings are contained within the three categories: some are submerged in views, while others practice the path.
Abiding in this stage and observing well, according to their inclinations, faculties, and understandings,
they expound the various distinctions as appropriate, employing unimpeded and wondrous eloquence.
Seated upon the Dharma throne like a lion, Like a bull king, a jewel mountain king,
Or a dragon king spreading dense clouds, He pours down the rain of nectar to fill the great ocean.
Well-knowing the nature of phenomena and their profound meaning, he is able to expound them with skillful speech;
he possesses a hundred thousand asaṃkhyeyas of dhāraṇīs, just as the great ocean receives all the rains.
The dhāraṇīs and samādhis are all pure; In a single thought-moment, they can see many Buddhas.
At the abode of each Buddha, they hear the Dharma, And further expound it with wondrous sounds.
If one wishes to transform and guide all sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm,
like clouds spreading vast and wide reaching everywhere, may they cause all to rejoice according to their faculties and inclinations.
The assemblies of Buddhas upon the tips of hairs are beyond numbering, and the inclinations and joys of sentient beings' minds are likewise infinite;
one should accord with their minds by bestowing Dharma-gates, and all realms of reality are thus.
Through the power of diligent and vigorous effort, the Bodhisattva further attains merit that becomes ever more sublime;
they hear and retain all such Dharma-gates, just as the earth can support every kind of seed.
Infinite sentient beings from the ten directions all come to sit together in this assembly;
in a single thought, each asks difficult questions according to their own minds, and with a single voice, the Buddha answers them all, satisfying everyone completely.
Abiding in this stage as a Dharma King, he guides and exhorts others according to their capacities without weariness;
day and night he beholds the Buddhas never ceasing, entering into profound, tranquil extinction through wisdom and liberation.
The merit of making offerings to all Buddhas is brilliantly beneficial, like a wondrous jeweled crown upon a king’s head;
it further causes the afflictions of sentient beings to be extinguished, just as the light of the Brahma King shines everywhere.
Abiding here, one frequently becomes a Great Brahma King, Converting sentient beings through the Dharma of the Three Vehicles;
The wholesome karma thus performed brings universal benefit, Until one shall attain all-encompassing wisdom.
In a single thought-moment, they enter as many samādhis as there are atoms in incalculable lands;
they likewise see Buddhas preaching the Dharma, yet what is accomplished through the power of their vows exceeds even this.
This is the ninth stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, The domain traversed by Bodhisattvas of great wisdom;
Profound, subtle, and difficult to perceive, I have now proclaimed it for the sake of the Buddha’s sons.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-Eight;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-Nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Twenty-six, Part Six: The Stage of the Tenth Ground.

Ten billion assemblies of gods from the Pure Abodes, Hearing of the supreme practices within this ground, Leaped for joy in the air with hearts full of delight, And all together made offerings to the Buddha with utmost sincerity.
The inconceivable assembly of bodhisattvas, likewise rejoicing greatly in the air,
all together burned the most supreme and pleasing incense, which universally perfumed the assembly and rendered it pure.
The Sovereign Lord of Devas and his celestial hosts, numbering immeasurable billions, were in the void;
they scattered heavenly robes as offerings to the Buddha, raining down hundreds of thousands of varieties in profusion.
The celestial maidens were beyond measure, all of whom joyfully made offerings to the Buddha;
each played various kinds of exquisite music, and with these words they offered praise:
“The Buddha’s body sits peacefully in a single land, yet manifests its presence throughout all worlds.”
With physical marks as majestic and sublime as immeasurable billions, They completely fill the vast expanse of the Dharma-realm.
From a single pore they emit radiant light, Universally extinguishing the darkness of afflictions in the world.
The atoms within all lands may be counted, But the number of these rays of light is unfathomable.
Some see the Tathāgata endowed with all the marks, turning the unsurpassed wheel of the true Dharma;
some see him traveling through the various Buddha-fields; and some see him in profound stillness, peaceful and unmoving.
Sometimes he manifests dwelling in the Tuṣita heaven; sometimes he manifests descending to enter his mother’s womb;
sometimes he shows himself abiding in the womb or emerging from it, causing all to see him within immeasurable lands.
Sometimes manifesting as one who leaves home to practice worldly paths, Or manifesting at the site of enlightenment to achieve perfect awakening,
Or manifesting preaching the Dharma or entering nirvana, Universally causing all throughout the ten directions to behold them.
Just as a magician, knowing his art, performs many deeds before a great multitude;
so too is the wisdom of the Tathāgata, manifesting its body everywhere throughout the world.
The Buddha abides in the profound and true nature of phenomena, Quiescent and signless like empty space;
yet within the ultimate reality, He manifests all manner of activities.
All deeds performed for the benefit of sentient beings Are attained by relying upon the nature of phenomena (dharmatā);
Characteristics and the absence of characteristics are without distinction, For entry into the ultimate is entirely without characteristics.
If one wishes to attain the wisdom of the Tathāgata, One should abandon all false conceptualization;
Thoroughly penetrating both existence and non-existence as equal, One will swiftly become a great guide for humans and devas.

Immeasurable and boundless hosts of celestial maidens, having offered praise with various voices and sounds, their bodies and minds became tranquil as they dwelt together in peace; gazing up at the Tathāgata, they remained in silence.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, perceiving that the entire assembly was profoundly tranquil,
addressed Vajragarbha, saying:
"O Great Fearless One, true Son of the Buddha!
From the ninth stage entering the tenth, May the wise one proclaim for us all the qualities,
The characteristics of all practices, And the matters of supernormal powers and transformations!
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha addressed the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!

From the first stage through the ninth stage, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, having observed and realized with such immeasurable wisdom, practices through skillful reflection, perfectly fulfills the pure dharmas (*śukla-dharma*), gathers boundless factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣa-dharma*), increases great merit and wisdom, extensively practices great compassion, knows the distinctions of worlds, enters the dense forest of the realm of sentient beings, enters the sphere of the Tathāgata’s activity, accords with the Tathāgata’s practice of quiescence, and constantly contemplates the Tathāgata’s powers, fearlessnesses, and unique Buddha-dharmas; this is called: [The Stage of the Cloud of Dharma]"
One attains the station of receiving the empowerment of all modes and the wisdom of all-knowledge.
"O Son of the Buddha!

Once a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has entered the stage of receiving empowerment through such wisdom, they immediately attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement, the Samādhi of Entering the Differentiations of the Dharma Realm, the Samādhi of Adorning the Site of Enlightenment, the Samādhi of Flower-Light of All Modes, the Samādhi of the Ocean Treasury, the Samādhi of the Ocean Seal, the Samādhi of the Vastness of the Space Realm, the Samādhi of Contemplating the Self-Nature of All Dharmas, the Samādhi of Knowing the Mental Activities of All Sentient Beings, and the Samādhi of All Buddhas Appearing Before One. In this way, millions of asaṃkhyeyas of samādhis all manifest before them."

Regarding all these samādhis, the bodhisattva attains skillfulness in both entering and arising from them, and also thoroughly understands the distinctions among the functions performed by all these samādhis.
The final samādhi is named "Receiving the Supreme Position of All-Knowledge.
When this samādhi manifests before one, a great precious lotus flower suddenly appears.
The flower was vast and expansive, equal in measure to ten million trichiliocosms, adorned with an interlacing array of various exquisite jewels, surpassing all worldly realms.

It was produced from supramundane roots of goodness; it was known to be composed of the various practices of the illusory nature of all phenomena. It constantly emitted light that universally illumined the Dharma-realm, a state impossible for any celestial abode to possess.

A *vaiḍūrya* mani-jewel formed its stem, sandalwood king formed its calyx, agate formed its filaments, and Jāmbūnada gold formed its petals. This flower was perpetually possessed of immeasurable radiance, with a treasury of various jewels and covered by a net of gems; it had as its retinue lotus flowers as numerous as the atoms within thirteen thousand great trichiliocosms.
At that time, the Bodhisattva sat upon this flower-seat, his physical form and proportions perfectly proportioned;

immeasurable bodhisattvas served as his retinue, each sitting upon their respective lotus flowers, surrounding him on all sides, and each attaining one million samādhis, gazing up at the Great Bodhisattva with single-minded devotion.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When this Great Bodhisattva and his retinue sit upon their lotus thrones, all their radiance and the sounds of their voices pervade and fill the Dharma-realm of the ten directions. All worlds tremble; the evil realms are stilled; the lands become adorned and pure; and bodhisattvas of the same practice do not fail to assemble. The music of humans and devas resounds simultaneously, and all sentient beings attain peace and happiness. With inconceivable articles of offering, they make offerings to all Buddhas, and the assemblies of all Buddhas appear clearly before them.”
“O Son of the Buddha!

When this bodhisattva sits upon that great lotus throne, they emit ten million *asaṃkhyeya* rays of light from beneath both feet, universally illuminating all the great hells of the ten directions and extinguishing the suffering of sentient beings;
they emit ten million *asaṃkhyeya* rays of light from both kneecaps, universally illuminating all the animal realms of the ten directions and extinguishing the suffering of sentient beings.”

From his navel wheel, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illumined the realms of the King of Yama throughout the ten directions, extinguishing the suffering of sentient beings;

from his left and right flanks, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illumined all human destinies throughout the ten directions, extinguishing the suffering of sentient beings;
and from his two hands, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illumined all the palaces of the devas and asuras throughout the ten directions.
From his two shoulders, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, universally illuminating all śrāvakas throughout the ten directions;
from his neck and back, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, universally illuminating the bodies of pratyekabuddhas throughout the ten directions;

and from his face, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, universally illuminating the bodies of all bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions, from those who have first resolved their minds up to those on the ninth stage.

From between his two eyebrows, he emitted a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* rays of light, which universally illumined the Bodhisattvas receiving their offices throughout the ten directions, causing all the palaces of Māra to become invisible.

From the crown of his head, he emitted a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* rays of light, as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* triple-thousand great thousandfold world systems; these universally illumined the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas throughout the worlds of the ten directions. They circled them ten times to the right, stayed suspended in mid-air, and formed a network of light called "Blazing Radiance.

It initiated various kinds of offerings to worship the Buddha. If one were to compare all the offerings made by other Bodhisattvas from their first resolve up to the ninth stage (*bhūmi*) with this, they would not equal even a hundredth part, nor could they be reached by any calculation or analogy.

That net of light universally rained down various exquisite incenses, flower garlands, robes, banners, pennants, jeweled parasols, and various *maṇi* ornaments before the assemblies of each and every Tathāgata throughout the ten directions as an offering; all were born from supramundane roots of goodness and transcended all worldly realms.
If there are sentient beings who see and know this, they shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When this great radiance has finished performing such acts of offering, it again circles each and every assembly at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions; having completed ten circumambulations, it enters through the soles of the feet of all Tathāgatas."

At that time, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas know that in a certain world, a certain Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to practice such vast conduct as to reach the stage of receiving the position of consecration.
O Son of the Buddha!

At that time, the assemblies of bodhisattvas from the ten directions—immeasurable, boundless, and including those up to the ninth stage—all came to surround him, paying respectful offerings and observing him with single-minded attention.
While they were thus observing correctly, each of those bodhisattvas immediately attained ten thousand samādhis.

At that time, all the bodhisattvas who had received their consecration throughout the ten directions emitted great rays of light from the mark of excellence upon their chests, which were adorned with vajras;

these rays were named "Able to Destroy the Enmity of Māra," accompanied by a retinue of millions of asaṃkhyeyas of lights, universally illuminating the ten directions and manifesting immeasurable supernatural transformations.
Having performed these deeds, they enter into this mark of virtue—the adamantine-ornamented chest of this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
once their light has entered, it causes all the wisdom and power of this bodhisattva to increase by more than a hundred thousandfold.

At that time, from the space between the eyebrows of all Buddhas of the ten directions, there issued forth a pure light called "Augmenting All-Knowledge and Spiritual Powers," with countless rays of light as its retinue.

It universally illuminated all worlds throughout the ten directions, circled them ten times to the right, and manifested the vast sovereignty of the Tathāgatas. It awakened immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas, caused all Buddha-fields to tremble everywhere, extinguished the sufferings of all evil realms, eclipsed all the palaces of Māras, and displayed the majestic power and the adornments of the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment where all Buddhas attain Bodhi.

Having thus universally illumined all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, [the light] came to this assembly of Bodhisattvas, circumambulated it to the right, and manifested various kinds of magnificent adornments;
having manifested these things, it entered through the crown of the great Bodhisattva’s head, and the radiance of his retinue likewise entered the crowns of those respective Bodhisattvas.
At that time, this bodhisattva attained one million samādhis previously unattained, known as:
having already received the rank of consecration, entering the realm of the Buddha, being fully endowed with the ten powers, and falling within the number of the Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like the crown prince born to a Wheel-Turning Sage King, whose mother is the principal queen and who is endowed with all physical marks of excellence.

The Wheel-Turning King causes this prince to sit upon a magnificent golden throne atop a white elephant treasure; he spreads a great net-like canopy, erects great banners and streamers, burns incense, scatters flowers, and performs various musical offerings. He takes water from the four great oceans and places it within a golden pitcher; the King then holds this pitcher and pours the water over the prince’s head. At that moment, he is given the name:
Having received the royal position and being included among the number of consecrated Kṣatriya kings, he is immediately able to fully practice the ten paths of wholesome action,
and may also be called a Wheel-Turning Sage King (Cakravartin).
The consecration of a bodhisattva is likewise: because the waters of the wisdom of all Buddhas are poured upon their crown, it is called "receiving the office";
and because they are endowed with the ten powers of a Tathāgata, they are reckoned among the ranks of Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva’s reception of the office of great wisdom.

By virtue of this office of great wisdom, the bodhisattva is able to perform immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of difficult practices and increase immeasurable wisdom and merit;
this is called "Abiding in the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma."
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas dwell in this Dharma-Cloud Stage (Dharmameghā-bhūmi), they know, as it truly is, the accumulation of the desire realm, the accumulation of the form realm, the accumulation of the formless realm, the accumulation of the world-realm, the accumulation of the dharma-realm, the accumulation of the conditioned realm, the accumulation of the unconditioned realm, the accumulation of the sentient-being realm, the accumulation of the consciousness-realm, the accumulation of the space-realm, and the accumulation of the nirvana-realm.”

This bodhisattva knows, as they truly are, the accumulation of views, afflictions, and conduct; the accumulation of the formation and destruction of worlds; the accumulation of the practices of śrāvakas, the accumulation of the practices of pratyekabuddhas, the accumulation of the practices of bodhisattvas, and the accumulation of the powers, fearlessnesses, form-body, and dharma-body of the Tathāgata; the accumulation of all modes of omniscience; the accumulation of manifesting the attainment of enlightenment and turning the wheel of Dharma; and the accumulation of entering the wisdom that discerns and determines all phenomena.
To state the essentials: by means of all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), they know all accumulations.
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, through such supreme and transcendent wisdom of awakening, knows as they truly are the transformation of sentient beings’ karma, the transformation of afflictions, the transformation of views, the transformation of worlds, the transformation of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the transformation of śrāvakas, the transformation of pratyekabuddhas, the transformation of bodhisattvas, the transformation of Tathāgatas, and the transformations of all conceptualization and non-conceptualization; all such things he knows as they truly are.

Furthermore, one knows as they truly are the Buddha-retention, Dharma-retention, Saṃgha-retention, karma-retention, affliction-retention, time-retention, vow-retention, offering-retention, practice-retention, eon-retention, and wisdom-retention; all such things are known as they truly are.
Furthermore, they know as it truly is the subtle wisdom of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas entering into subtlety, namely:

the subtle wisdom of spiritual practice, the subtle wisdom of the end of life, the subtle wisdom of taking birth, the subtle wisdom of leaving the household life, the subtle wisdom of manifesting supernormal powers, the subtle wisdom of attaining perfect enlightenment, the subtle wisdom of turning the wheel of Dharma, the subtle wisdom of maintaining the lifespan, the subtle wisdom of entering parinirvāṇa, and the subtle wisdom of the endurance of the teachings; all such things they know as they truly are.
Furthermore, they enter the secret realms of the Tathāgata, namely:

the secret of body, the secret of speech, the secret of mind, the secret of discerning the proper and improper time, the secret of bestowing predictions upon bodhisattvas, the secret of gathering in sentient beings, the secret of the various vehicles, the secret of the differences in the faculties and practices of all sentient beings, the secret of the workings of karma, and the secret of the practice for attaining awakening; all such things they know as they truly are.
Furthermore, they know all the Buddhas' wisdom regarding the entry into eons (*kalpa*), namely:

one eon entering incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*); incalculable eons entering one eon; finite eons entering infinite eons; infinite eons entering finite eons; a single thought-moment (*ekakṣaṇa*) entering an eon; an eon entering a single thought-moment; an eon entering a non-eon; a non-eon entering an eon; an eon with a Buddha entering an eon without a Buddha; an eon without a Buddha entering an eon with a Buddha; past and future eons entering the present eon; the present eon entering past and future eons; past eons entering future eons; future eons entering past eons; long eons entering short eons; and short eons entering long eons. All such things they know as they truly are.
Furthermore, he knows the various wisdoms of entry possessed by the Tathāgata, namely: the wisdom of entering the path of a single hair; the wisdom of entering atoms;

the wisdom of entering the enlightenment of the body within a land; the wisdom of entering the enlightenment of the bodies of sentient beings; the wisdom of entering the minds of sentient beings; the wisdom of entering the conduct of sentient beings; the wisdom of entering the enlightenment that accords with all places; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of universal conduct; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of conduct in accordance [with the world]; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of conduct in opposition [to the world]; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of the knowable and unknowable conduct of the conceivable and inconceivable worlds; and the wisdom of entering the manifestation of the wisdom of śrāvakas, the wisdom of pratyekabuddhas, the conduct of bodhisattvas, and the conduct of tathāgatas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The wisdom possessed by all Buddhas is vast and immeasurable; Bodhisattvas at this stage are all able to enter it.
O Son of the Buddha!"

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this stage, they immediately attain the ten inconceivable liberations of a bodhisattva: the liberation of non-obstruction, the liberation of pure observation, the liberation of universal illumination, the liberation of the Tathāgatagarbha, the liberation of conforming to the unimpeded wheel, the liberation of penetrating the three periods of time, the liberation of the treasury of the dharma-realm, the liberation of the wheel of light, and the liberation of the realm without remainder.
With these ten as the foremost, there are immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya gates of liberation, all of which are attained within this tenth stage.

In this manner, they fully accomplish even immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya gateways of samādhi, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya gateways of dhāraṇī, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya gateways of supernormal powers.
“O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, having attained such wisdom and accorded with immeasurable enlightenment, achieves skillful power of mindfulness; in a single instant, he is able to settle, receive, gather, and uphold all the immeasurable great lights of Dharma, the great illuminations of Dharma, and the great rains of Dharma belonging to the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions.”
For example, when the Dragon King Sāgara pours down a great rain, except for the great ocean, no other place whatsoever can accommodate it, receive it, contain it, or sustain it.

The Tathāgata’s great dharma-illumination, great dharma-radiance, and great dharma-rain of the secret treasury are likewise; with the sole exception of bodhisattvas of the tenth stage, all other sentient beings, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and even bodhisattvas up to the ninth stage are unable to settle in them, unable to receive them, unable to encompass them, and unable to uphold them.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like the great ocean, which can settle, receive, gather, and sustain the great rain poured down by a single great dragon king;

even if two, three, or even immeasurable numbers of dragon kings were to pour down their rain all at once within a single thought-moment, it can likewise settle, receive, gather, and sustain them all.
Why is this? Because it is an immeasurable and vast vessel.

It is likewise with the Bodhisattva dwelling on the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā-bhūmi): they are able to settle, receive, gather, and sustain the illumination of the Buddha’s Dharma, the radiance of the Dharma, and the rain of the Dharma.
Whether two, three, or even immeasurable [teachings], they are all likewise expounded simultaneously in a single moment of thought;
therefore, this stage is named "Dharma Cloud."
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra said:
"O Son of the Buddha!

In a single thought-moment, how many Tathāgatas can a bodhisattva of this stage receive, uphold, and maintain from them the great light of Dharma, the great illumination of Dharma, and the great rain of Dharma?"
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
It cannot be known by means of calculation; I shall provide you with a simile."
O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose that in each of the ten directions there were worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields. Within those worlds, every single sentient being attained the dhāraṇī of hearing and retaining, served as an attendant to a Buddha, and was foremost in learning among the assembly of śrāvakas—just like the bhikṣu Mahāvinīteśvara in the presence of the Buddha Vajrapadmodbhava.
Yet, whatever dharma one sentient being had received, no other would receive again.
O Son of the Buddha! What do you think?
Is the Dharma received by these sentient beings finite?
"Are they immeasurable?
Bodhisattva Vimukticandra replied,
"Their number is exceedingly great— immeasurable and boundless."
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
I shall speak for you so that you may attain understanding."
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva on this Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, in a single thought-moment at the presence of a single Buddha, establishes, receives, gathers, and maintains the great illumination of the Dharma, the great radiance of the Dharma, the great rain of the Dharma, and the treasury of the Dharma of the three periods of time—the Dharma heard and maintained by all sentient beings in as many worlds as previously mentioned does not equal even one hundredth part of this; indeed, no analogy can reach it.

Just as it is at the site of one Buddha, so it is with all the Buddhas throughout the ten directions, numbering as many as the atoms within the worlds previously described, and even exceeding that number—immeasurable and boundless. At the site of each and every one of those Tathāgatas, he is able to settle, receive, gather, and uphold all the illumination of the Dharma, the radiance of the Dharma, the rain of the Dharma, and the treasury of the Dharma of the three periods of time. For this reason, this stage is named "Dharma Cloud" (Dharmameghā).
O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattvas of this stage, by the power of their own vows, raise clouds of great compassion and thunder the great Dharma. With the supernormal powers, clarities, and fearlessnesses as flashes of lightning, and merit and wisdom as dense clouds, they manifest various bodies and travel back and forth. In a single thought-moment, they pervade hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of worlds, as numerous as the atoms within those lands, expounding the Great Dharma and subduing the hosts of Māra and enmity.

Furthermore, exceeding these numbers, in lands as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of worlds, they rain down the nectar of immortality according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, extinguishing the dust and flames of all delusions.
For this reason, this stage is named:
Cloud of Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!

In this stage, the Bodhisattva manifests Buddha-activities within a single world—from descending from Tuṣita Heaven until entering Nirvāṇa—in accordance with the minds of sentient beings who are to be saved.

Whether it be two, three, or even as many worlds as there are atoms in the aforementioned lands, and further exceeding these, up to worlds as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of worlds, it is likewise in all such cases.
Therefore, this stage is named:
Cloud of Dharma.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattvas on this stage possess clear and penetrating wisdom and mastery over supernormal powers.
According to their mental inclinations, they can transform a narrow world into a vast world and a vast world into a narrow world;
they can transform a defiled world into a pure world and a pure world into a defiled world.
Chaos-dwelling, sequential-dwelling, inverted-dwelling, and upright-dwelling—thus they can mutually manifest all such immeasurable worlds.

Or, according to their mental resolve, they may place within a single atom all the mountains, rivers, and Mount Sumerus of a world; yet the appearance of the atom remains as it was, and the world is not diminished.

Or again, within a single minute atom, they may place two, three, or even unspeakably many worlds with their Mount Sumerus, mountains, and rivers; yet the substance and appearance of that minute atom remain as they were, while the worlds within it all become clearly manifest.
Or, according to their mental inclinations, they manifest the adornments of two worlds within a single world, up to the adornments of unspeakably many worlds;
or, within the adornments of a single world, they manifest two worlds, up to unspeakably many worlds.
Or, according to their mental inclinations, they may place the sentient beings of unspeakably many worlds into a single world;
or, according to their mental inclinations, they may place the sentient beings of a single world into unspeakably many worlds, yet without causing any harm or affliction to those beings.
Or, according to his mental resolve, he manifests within a single pore all the adorned phenomena of the realms of all Buddhas.

Or, according to his mental resolve, within a single thought-moment he manifests bodies as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many worlds; each body manifests hands as numerous as those atoms, and each hand holds flower vases, incense caskets, garlands, canopies, banners, and pennants as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, pervading the ten directions to make offerings to the Buddhas.

Each body further manifests heads as numerous as those atoms, and each head further manifests tongues as numerous as those atoms, which, in every thought-moment, pervade the ten directions to extol the virtues of the Buddhas.

Or, according to their mental inclinations, in a single thought-moment they manifest throughout the ten directions the attainment of perfect enlightenment up to parinirvāṇa, as well as the adornments of buddha-fields;

or they manifest their bodies pervading the three periods of time, within which appear immeasurable buddhas and the adornments of their buddha-fields, such that the formation and destruction of worlds are all revealed;
or from a single pore of their own body they emit all winds, yet without causing any affliction or harm to sentient beings.

Or, according to his mental resolve, he may transform boundless worlds into a single great ocean; within the waters of this ocean, a great lotus flower appears, resplendent and magnificent, completely covering immeasurable and boundless worlds, wherein he manifests the adornments of the great Bodhi tree, even unto the manifestation of the attainment of all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Or, he may manifest all the lights of the worlds of the ten directions upon his own body, such that the radiance of mani jewels, the sun, the moon, the stars, clouds, lightning, and so forth, is all made to appear.
Or, by exhaling a breath from his mouth, he can shake immeasurable worlds in the ten directions without causing sentient beings to have any thought of alarm or fear.
In some instances, they manifest the wind, fire, and water calamities of the ten directions;
in others, according to the inclinations of sentient beings' minds, they manifest physical bodies fully adorned with ornaments;
or they manifest the body of a Buddha within their own bodies, or manifest their own bodies within the body of a Buddha.
Sometimes they manifest their own lands within the body of a Buddha, and sometimes they manifest the body of a Buddha within their own lands.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattvas on this Stage of the Cloud of Dharma can manifest such powers as well as other immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sovereign spiritual powers.

At that time, the bodhisattvas in the assembly, as well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, the four world-protecting kings, Śakra Devānām Indra, Brahmā, the Śuddhāvāsa deities, Maheśvara, and all the sons of the gods, all had this thought:
"If the power of the supernatural knowledges and wisdom of a bodhisattva can be such as this, what then must the Buddha be like?"
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the assembled multitude, addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha in gold-colored speech:
"O Son of the Buddha!
Now this great assembly, having heard of the bodhisattva’s power of supernatural knowledge and wisdom, has fallen into a net of doubt.
Excellent, O Benevolent One!
To sever their doubts, you should briefly manifest the deeds of a bodhisattva’s adornment of supernatural power.
At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva entered the samādhi called "The Essential Nature of All Buddha-lands.

When he entered this samādhi, all the bodhisattvas and the entire great assembly saw themselves within the body of Vajragarbha Bodhisattva; therein they beheld all the various adornments of the trichiliocosm, which could not be fully described even in the course of a hundred million kalpas.

Furthermore, within that [realm], he saw a Bodhi tree whose circumference was equal to one hundred thousand trichiliocosms, its height being one million trichiliocosms, and the shade cast by its branches and leaves was likewise the same.
In proportion to the size of the tree, there was a lion throne, upon which sat a Buddha named King of All-Knowledge Penetration (*Sarvajñābhijñārāja*).

The entire great assembly saw that Buddha sitting beneath the Bodhi tree on the lion throne, adorned with all manner of marks and signs, such that even if one were to speak for a hundred million eons, they could not exhaustively describe them.
After the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha had manifested such great supernormal powers, he restored the assembly so that each member returned to their original place.

At that time, the great multitude experienced what they had never known before; struck with a sense of wonder, they remained silent and gazed single-mindedly toward Vajragarbha in reverent contemplation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, saying:
"Son of the Buddha!
This samādhi is most rare and possesses great power; what is its name?"
Vajragarbha said: "The name of this samādhi is:
'The Essential Nature of All Buddha-fields.'"
He asked again:
"What is the sphere of this samādhi? He replied:
“O Son of the Buddha!

If a bodhisattva cultivates this samādhi, according to what the mind contemplates, they can manifest within their own body as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in the sands of the Ganges River, and even more than that—immeasurable and boundless.”

“O Son of the Buddha! When a Bodhisattva dwells in the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), they attain hundreds of thousands of such immeasurable great samādhis. Therefore, this Bodhisattva’s body and bodily actions (*kāyakarma*) are unfathomable; likewise their speech and verbal actions (*vākkarma*), and mind and mental actions (*manaskarma*). With sovereign mastery over supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), they observe the realms of the samādhis and the realms of wisdom of the three periods of time. They sport within all doors of liberation (*vimokṣamukha*);

whether through transformations, the performance of spiritual powers, or the manifestation of light—even down to the mere lifting and lowering of a foot—all such activities are such that even Bodhisattvas who are sons of the Dharma and dwell in the Ground of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī bhūmi*) cannot know them.”
O Son of the Buddha!
Such is a brief description of the sphere of experience of Bodhisattvas on this Ground of the Cloud of Dharma;
were it to be explained in detail, even an immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kalpas would not suffice to exhaust it.
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
If the sphere of a bodhisattva’s supernormal powers is such as this, what then is the power of a Buddha’s supernormal powers like?"
Vajragarbha said: "O Son of the Buddha!
It is as if, for example, there were a person who took a single clod of earth from among the four continents and spoke these words:"
"Between the soil of the great earth of infinite worlds and this [present] soil, which is more?
My observation of your question is likewise so: the wisdom of the Tathāgata is boundless and peerless; how can it be compared by measure with that of a bodhisattva?
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!
Suppose one were to take a tiny amount of soil from the four continents, while the remainder is immeasurable;

even if one were to explain only a small fraction of the supernatural powers and wisdom of this Dharma-Cloud Stage for immeasurable eons, how much more so would this be for the stage of the Tathāgata!
O Son of the Buddha!
I shall now cite examples for you as proof, so that you may come to know the realm of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose that in the ten directions, each direction contained as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in boundless worlds, and each of those lands were filled with Bodhisattvas who had attained this stage—dense as a grove of sugarcane, bamboo, reeds, rice, or hemp. Even the wisdom produced by all those Bodhisattvas through practicing the Bodhisattva path for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas would not equal even one hundredth part of the range of a single Tathāgata’s wisdom; it would not approach even a fraction up to an *upaniṣad*.
“O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva, dwelling in such wisdom, does not differ from the bodily, verbal, and mental activities of the Tathāgata; nor does he relinquish the power of the various samādhis of a Bodhisattva. For incalculable eons, he serves and makes offerings to all Buddhas, providing every kind of offering requisite in each and every eon.”

Empowered by the spiritual authority of all Buddhas, his light of wisdom became even more exalted; he skillfully explained all difficult questions within the Dharma-realm, such that no one could defeat him throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like a goldsmith who fashions an ornament for the body out of the finest, most exquisite pure gold, inlaid with great maṇi jewels; when the Sovereign King of the Gods himself wears it, no other celestial ornaments can compare to it.
So too is it with the Bodhisattva on this stage: from the first stage up to the ninth, the wisdom and conduct of all other Bodhisattvas cannot equal theirs.
The light of wisdom of the bodhisattvas on this stage can cause sentient beings to enter even into the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna); no other light of wisdom is capable of doing so.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as the radiance of the celestial king Maheśvara can cause the bodies and minds of sentient beings to become cool and refreshing, such that no other light can equal it;

so too is the wisdom-light of the Bodhisattva on this stage. It enables all sentient beings to attain coolness and refreshment, even leading them to abide in the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), such that the wisdom-lights of all Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and even Bodhisattvas up to the ninth stage cannot equal it.
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has already been able to dwell securely in such wisdom; the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, further expound for him the wisdom of the three periods of time, the wisdom of the distinctions within the Dharma-realm, the wisdom that pervades all worlds, the wisdom that illuminates all worlds, and the wisdom of compassionate mindfulness toward all sentient beings. To state it in brief, they even expound for him the attainment of the wisdom of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
For this Bodhisattva, among the ten pāramitās, the pāramitā of wisdom (jñāna-pāramitā) is preeminent;
yet it is not that they do not practice the remaining pāramitās.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is called a brief explanation of the tenth stage of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the Cloud of Dharma;
were it to be explained in detail, even an immeasurable number of asaṃkhyeya kalpas would not suffice to exhaust it.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva dwells in this stage, they frequently become the celestial king Maheśvara. Possessing mastery over all dharmas, they are able to bestow upon sentient beings, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all bodhisattvas the practices of the pāramitās. Within the dharma-realm, there is no one who can defeat them in debate or challenge their positions.

Generosity, kind speech, beneficial action, and cooperation—all such deeds as these are never apart from mindfulness of the Buddha, and so on, up to being never apart from mindfulness of the possession of all modes and the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Again, he forms this thought:
"I shall become the foremost and the most excellent among all sentient beings, even unto becoming the one upon whom the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) relies."

If one applies diligent effort, in a single moment of thought, one attains as many samādhis as there are atoms in ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, and even manifests as many bodhisattvas as there are such atoms to serve as one’s retinue;
yet if one manifests through the sovereign power of a bodhisattva’s sublime vows, it exceeds these numbers—namely:

in terms of cultivation, adornment, faith and understanding, deeds, body, speech, radiance, faculties, spiritual transformations, voice, and spheres of activity—even for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas, one could not calculate or know them.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When these ten stages of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva manifest their characteristics in succession, one is then able to enter into the wisdom of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).

It is like the Lake Anavatapta, from which flow four great rivers; these rivers pour forth and spread throughout Jambudvīpa, neither exhausting nor diminishing, but rather increasing further until they enter the ocean and cause it to be filled."
O Son of the Buddha!

It is the same for the Bodhisattva: from the bodhicitta flows the water of roots of goodness and great vows, which fills sentient beings through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) without ever being exhausted; it further increases until it enters the ocean of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), causing it to be completely filled.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The ten stages of the Bodhisattva exist with distinctions because of the Buddha's wisdom, just as there are ten mountain kings upon the great earth.
What are these ten?..."

They are: the King of Mountains Himavat, the King of Mountains Gandhamādana, the King of Mountains Vidyutprabha, the King of Mountains Ṛṣigiri, the King of Mountains Yugandhara, the King of Mountains Aśvakarṇa, the King of Mountains Nimindhara, the King of Mountains Cakravāḍa, the King of Mountains Ketumanta, and the King of Mountains Sumeru.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as the King of Snowy Mountains contains all medicinal herbs within it, such that they can never be exhausted when gathered;
so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Joy (Pramuditā-bhūmi), wherein all worldly scriptures, arts, literary compositions, and incantations are contained, such that they can never be fully expounded.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Gandhamādana, the king of mountains, is where all fragrances gather and can never be exhausted, so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Freedom from Defilement;
within it are contained all the bodhisattva precepts, practices, and dignified conducts, which can never be fully described.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Vaidūrya, the king of mountains, is composed entirely of jewels, with all manner of precious gems contained within it that can never be exhausted;

so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Radiance (Prabhākārī-bhūmi), wherein all worldly meditative concentrations, supernormal powers, liberations, samādhis, and samāpattis are contained, which can never be fully described.
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as the King of Mountains, Śarādvatīputra, is composed entirely of jewels and is the dwelling place of immortals possessing the five supernatural powers, where they reside in inexhaustible numbers;
so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Blazing Wisdom (Arciṣmatī), wherein all the most excellent wisdoms among all paths are contained, and can never be fully described.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Yugandhara, the king of mountains, is composed entirely of precious jewels and inhabited by great yakṣas in inexhaustible numbers;
so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Difficult to Conquer (Duranjayā), wherein all sovereign and wish-fulfilling supernormal powers (abhijñā) dwell, and can never be fully described.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as the King of Mountains, Aśvakarṇa, is composed entirely of precious jewels and contains all manner of fruits that can never be exhausted by taking them;

so too is the bodhisattva’s dwelling in the stage of Presence (Abhimukhī), wherein the entry into the principle of dependent origination and the realization of the fruits of the śrāvakas are all contained within it, such that they can never be fully expounded.

Just as Mount Nimiṃdhara, the king of mountains, is composed entirely of precious jewels and is the dwelling place of powerful nāga deities in inexhaustible numbers, so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Far-reaching (Dūraṃgamā);
within it are contained skillful means, wisdom, and the realization of the fruits of solitary awakening, which can never be fully described.

Just as Mount Khadiraka, the king of mountains, is composed entirely of jewels and is the dwelling place of all the hosts of *vaśavartin* gods without end, so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Immovability (*acalā-bhūmi*);
within it, the various worlds of the diverse practices of mastery of all Bodhisattvas reside, and they can never be fully described.

Just as Mount Kailāsa, the king of mountains, is composed entirely of precious jewels and is the dwelling place of the great and powerful asura kings without end, so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of Excellent Intelligence (Sādhumatī):
the wisdom and practices regarding the arising and ceasing of all worlds are contained within it, and can never be fully described.
Just as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, is composed entirely of precious jewels and is the dwelling place of all the gods of great majesty and power without end;

so too is the Bodhisattva’s stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā-bhūmi). Within it reside the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities of a Tathāgata, as well as all Buddha-activities, which can never be exhausted through questions, answers, or proclamations.
“O Son of the Buddha!
These ten kings of jewel mountains all exist within the great ocean, yet they receive their names through their differences;
likewise, the ten stages of the Bodhisattva also exist within omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), yet they receive their names through their differences.”
O Son of the Buddha!
For example, the great ocean receives its name as such by virtue of ten characteristics that cannot be altered or taken away. What are these ten?
First, it becomes progressively deeper;
second, it does not accept corpses;
third, when other waters enter it, they all lose their original names.
Fourth, universal uniformity of flavor;
fifth, immeasurable precious treasures;
sixth, being unable to reach its bottom.
Seventh, it is vast and immeasurable;
eighth, it is the dwelling place of great-bodied beings;
ninth, its tides do not overstep their bounds.
10. Just as a great rain falls everywhere without overflowing, so too is the practice of a bodhisattva:
by virtue of ten characteristics, it is called the bodhisattva practice, which cannot be shifted or taken away.
What are these ten? They are:
the Ground of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), because it gives birth to great vows that gradually deepen;
and the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), because one does not accept any corpse of broken precepts.
The Radiant Ground (*Prabhākārī-bhūmi*), because it abandons worldly conventional designations;
the Ground of Blazing Wisdom (*Arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), because its qualities are of one flavor with those of the Buddha;
the Ground Difficult to Conquer (*Sudurjayā-bhūmi*), because it gives birth to immeasurable skillful means, supernormal powers, and the various treasures produced in the world.
The Ground of Presence (*Abhimukhī*), because it observes the profound principle of dependent origination;
the Ground of Far-Going (*Dūraṅgamā*), because it skillfully observes with vast awakening wisdom;
the Ground of Immovability (*Acalā*), because it manifests vast and magnificent adornments.
The Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*Sādhumatī-bhūmi*), because one attains profound liberation and acts within the world, knowing things as they truly are without transgressing the limit;
the Stage of the Dharma-Cloud (*Dharmameghā-bhūmi*), because one can receive the great rain of the Dharma-light from all Tathāgatas without ever being satiated.
O Son of the Buddha!
For example, there is a great maṇi jewel that possesses ten kinds of qualities by which it surpasses all other jewels. What are these ten?
First, it emerged from the great ocean;
second, it was fashioned and refined by a skilled craftsman;
third, it is complete and without flaw.
Fourth, it is pure and free from defilement;
fifth, it is transparent both internally and externally;
sixth, it is skillfully drilled and pierced.
Seventh, they are threaded with precious cords;
eighth, they are placed atop tall banners of lapis lazuli;
ninth, they universally radiate all manner of various lights.
Tenth, they are able to rain down various precious objects according to the king’s will, fulfilling the aspirations of sentient beings in accordance with their hearts.
O Son of the Buddha!
You should know that the Bodhisattva is likewise in this way, possessing ten things that surpass all other sages.
What are the ten? First, generating the mind of omniscience;
second, maintaining the dhūta precepts with upright conduct that is pure and luminous.
Third, the various dhyānas and samādhis are complete and without deficiency;
fourth, their practice of the Path is pure and white, free from all defilements;
fifth, their skillful means and supernormal powers are transparently clear both internally and externally.
Sixth is the wisdom of dependent origination, which is skillfully able to pierce through;
seventh is threading it with the threads of various kinds of skillful means wisdom;
eighth is placing it atop a high banner of sovereign mastery.
Ninth, observing the conduct of sentient beings, they emit the light of hearing and retaining;
tenth, receiving the office of Buddha-wisdom, they are reckoned among the Buddhas and are able to extensively perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This chapter on the Dharma-door of the Bodhisattva Practice for Accumulating All Kinds of Merit and All-Knowledge cannot be heard by sentient beings who have not planted roots of goodness.”
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra asked:
"Upon hearing this Dharma-gate, how much merit is obtained?
The Bodhisattva Vajragarbha replied:
"As is the merit accumulated by one who possesses all-knowledge, so too is the merit of hearing this Dharma-gate.

Why is this? It is not possible to believe, understand, receive, uphold, read, or recite this Dharma-gate of merit without having heard it; how much less so to apply oneself with diligence and practice according to the teaching!"

Therefore, you should know that it is only by hearing this Dharma-gate of the merit of gathering all-knowledge that one can then believe, understand, receive, uphold, and practice it, before finally reaching the stage of all-knowledge.

At that time, through the spiritual power of the Buddha and because such is the nature of the Dharma, worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten billion Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions shook in six ways and eighteen manners.

That is to say: it shook, shook everywhere, and shook equally everywhere; it rose, rose everywhere, and rose equally everywhere; it surged, surged everywhere, and surged equally everywhere; it quaked, quaked everywhere, and quaked equally everywhere; it roared, roared everywhere, and roared equally everywhere; it crashed, crashed everywhere, and crashed equally everywhere.
A rain of celestial flowers, celestial garlands, celestial robes, and various precious ornaments for adornment, as well as banners, flags, and silk canopies, fell from the heavens.
Celestial music was performed, its sounds harmonious and elegant, sounding forth all at once to praise all the merits inherent in the stage of omniscience.
Just as this Dharma was expounded in the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven in this world, so it was in all worlds throughout the ten directions.

At that time, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, from beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields in each of the ten directions, there came to this assembly bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields, who spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent!
Vajragarbha! Speak this Dharma well.
We are all likewise named as such:
Vajragarbha, the worlds in which they dwell each differ from one another,
yet all are named Vajraguṇa; the Buddhas therein are named Vajradhvaja.

We abide in our own worlds, yet all, sustained by the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata, proclaim this Dharma; the assemblies are entirely equal, and the words, phrases, and meanings are no different from what is spoken here—neither more nor less.
All have come to this assembly through the Buddha’s spiritual power to serve as witnesses for you.

"Just as we have now entered this world, so too shall we go to and bear witness in all worlds throughout the ten directions. At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva surveyed the entire assembly in the ten directions, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.

Desiring to praise and inspire the mind set upon the wisdom of omniscience; desiring to manifest the realm of the bodhisattvas; desiring to purify the power of the bodhisattva practices; desiring to explain the path that encompasses all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*); desiring to eliminate all the defilements of the world; desiring to bestow omniscience; desiring to manifest the adornment of inconceivable wisdom; desiring to reveal all the merits of the bodhisattvas; and desiring to further open up and clarify the meaning of these stages, he, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, spoke in verse:
“His mind is quiescent and ever-disciplined, Equal and unimpeded like space;
Free from all defilements, he abides in the Way— Listen now to this sublime practice.”
Having cultivated all manner of virtues for hundreds of billions of kalpas, Making offerings to immeasurable and boundless Buddhas,
And likewise to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, One generates the Great Mind for the benefit of sentient beings.
Diligently upholding the precepts, always gentle and patient, Fully endowed with shame, remorse, merit, and wisdom,
Aiming to seek the Buddha’s wisdom and cultivating vast insight, May they attain the Ten Powers and resolve upon the Great Mind.
Making offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time, Thoroughly purifying all lands,
And realizing that all phenomena are equal, One gives rise to the Great Mind for the benefit of sentient beings.
Abiding in the first stage, they give rise to this mind, Forever free from all evils and always joyful;
Through the power of their vows, they extensively cultivate all wholesome dharmas, And out of compassion, they enter the subsequent stages.
Fully endowed with precepts and learning, mindful of sentient beings, He washes away defilements until the mind is bright and pure;
Observing the fires of the three poisons within the world, The one of vast understanding proceeds to the third stage.
All that exists within the three realms is impermanent; Like an arrow piercing the body, it burns with intense suffering.
Disgusted with conditioned existence, one seeks the Buddha-dharma; The person of vast wisdom proceeds toward the stage of Blazing Fire (Arciṣmatī).

Endowed with mindfulness and wisdom, they attain the knowledge of the Path; having made offerings to hundreds of thousands of immeasurable Buddhas, they constantly contemplate the most supreme virtues—such persons enter the stage that is difficult to surpass.
Skillfully observing with wisdom and expedient means, they manifest in various ways to save sentient beings;
further making offerings to the Unsurpassed Honored One of Ten Powers, they enter the Ground of Presence, which is Non-arising.
That which is difficult for the world to know, yet he knows; He does not grasp at a self and is free from existence and non-existence.
The nature of phenomena is fundamentally quiescent, yet it turns according to conditions; Attaining this subtle and wondrous state, he advances toward the seventh stage.
With wisdom, skillful means, and a vast mind, Difficult to practice, difficult to subdue, and difficult to comprehend,
Though having realized quiescence, they diligently cultivate it, Able to proceed toward the immovable stage that is like space.
The Buddha exhorts him to arise from quiescence, To extensively cultivate various karmas of wisdom,
And, endowed with the ten masteries, contemplate the world, Thereby ascending to the Stage of Excellent Wisdom (Sādhumatī).
With subtle and wondrous wisdom, he observes sentient beings— the dense forest of their mental activities, karma, and afflictions— and,
desiring to transform them so they may enter the Path, he expounds the supreme treasury of the Buddhas' ultimate meaning.

Practicing the stages in succession, they perfect all virtues; Up to the ninth stage, they accumulate merit and wisdom, Constantly seeking the supreme Dharma of all Buddhas, And receiving the Buddha’s water of wisdom poured upon their crowns.
Having attained countless samādhis, and being well-versed in their respective functions,
the final samādhi is named "Receiving the Office," wherein one dwells in a vast sphere of reality, forever unmoving.
When the Bodhisattva attains this samādhi, a great precious lotus suddenly appears;
his body, commensurate with its scale, sits within it, surrounded by the sons of the Buddha who all gaze upon him together.
He emits hundreds of billions of great rays of light, Extinguishing the suffering of all sentient beings;
Again, from the crown of his head he emits light, Universally entering the assemblies of the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Abiding entirely within the sky, they form a net of light; Having made offerings to the Buddha, they enter through his feet.
At that moment, all Buddhas fully perceived that this Son of the Buddha had ascended to his office.
Bodhisattvas from the ten directions came to observe him, and the Great Being receiving the office extended light that shone forth;
the Buddhas also emitted light from between their eyebrows, which illuminated everywhere and entered through the crown of his head.
The worlds of the ten directions all tremble, and the sufferings of all hells are extinguished;
at that time, the Buddhas confer their offices upon him, just as the eldest son of a wheel-turning king receives his station.
If one is graced by the empowerment of all Buddhas, This is called ascending to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud;
Wisdom increases without limit, Awakening all worlds.
The realm of desire, the realm of form, and the formless realm; The realm of phenomena, the realm of worlds, and the realm of sentient beings;
The finite, the infinite, and empty space— All such things as these they thoroughly penetrate.
With great power in all transformative activities, and through the subtle wisdom empowered by all Buddhas,
they are able to observe, exactly as it is, the secret kalpas, the paths of the pores, and so forth.
Taking birth, renouncing the world, and attaining the Perfect Way; turning the sublime Wheel of Dharma and entering Nirvana;
even the dharma of ultimate quiescent liberation, as well as all that has not yet been spoken—you are able to comprehend it all.
