When Bodhisattvas dwell in this Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, they are fully endowed with the power of mindfulness to uphold the Buddha-dharma;
just as the great ocean receives the rain from the dragons, so too does this stage receive the Dharma.
The immeasurable sentient beings of the ten directions all attain the power of hearing and retaining the Buddha-dharma;
the Dharma they hear from a single Buddha exceeds that number by an immeasurable amount.
By the power of his past wisdom, vows, and majestic spiritual strength, he pervades the lands of the ten directions in a single thought-moment;
raining down the nectar of immortality to extinguish afflictions, for this reason the Buddha calls him the Cloud of Dharma.
The manifestations of supernormal powers pervade the ten directions, transcending the realms of humans, devas, and the mundane world;
even beyond these countless billions, the intellects of worldly sages would surely be bewildered and distressed when contemplating them.
The measure of the merit of wisdom gained from lifting a single foot cannot be known even by those on the ninth bhūmi,
let alone by all sentient beings, as well as by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
The Bodhisattvas of this stage make offerings to the Buddhas, pervading all lands throughout the ten directions;
they also make offerings to the assembly of all present holy ones, fully perfecting the majestic adornments of the Buddha’s merit.
Abiding in this stage, one further explains the unimpeded wisdom regarding the dharma-realm of the three periods of time;
that all sentient beings and lands are likewise so, as are all the merits of the Buddhas.
The light of wisdom of the Bodhisattvas on this stage Can show sentient beings the path of the True Dharma;
Just as the light of the Sovereign Heaven dispels the darkness of the world, So too does this light extinguish all obscurity.
Dwelling here, they mostly act as kings of the three realms, skillfully expounding the Dharma of the Three Vehicles;
they attain immeasurable samādhis in a single thought-moment, and the Buddhas they behold are likewise so.
I have now briefly explained these stages; were I to explain them in detail, they could not be exhausted.
Thus, within the Buddha’s wisdom, these stages stand as firm and majestic as the ten kings of mountains.
The arts and crafts of the first stage are inexhaustible, like the Snowy Mountains where all medicinal herbs gather;
the precepts and learning of the second stage are like the Gandhamādana Mountain;
the third is like the Vaidūrya mountain, from which wondrous flowers bloom.
The jewel of the Path of Blazing Wisdom is inexhaustible, Like the Sage Mountain where the benevolent dwell;
The supernormal powers of the fifth stage are like the Yugaṃdhara Mountains;
The sixth is like Aśvakarṇa, possessing all fruits.
On the seventh stage, great wisdom is like Nimiṃdhara;
on the eighth stage, mastery is like Cakravāḍa;
on the ninth, like Ketu, it gathers all things without obstruction.
Like Mount Sumeru, they possess all virtues:
the first stage is the preeminence of vows, the second is the upholding of morality;
the third is merit, and the fourth is single-mindedness.
The fifth stage is subtle and wondrous; the sixth is profound;
the seventh is vast wisdom; the eighth is adornment;
the ninth stage contemplates subtle meanings and transcends all worldly paths.
On the tenth stage, one upholds all the Buddha-dharmas; such an ocean of practice is inexhaustible. The ten practices transcend the world:
the first is the initial arousal of the mind; the second is maintaining the precepts, the third is dhyāna;
the fourth is the purity of conduct, the fifth is accomplishment; the sixth is dependent origination, and the seventh is penetration.
The eighth is established upon the Vajradhvaja; the ninth observes the dense forest of sentient beings;
the tenth is the consecration that accords with the King’s intent—thus do these precious virtues gradually become purified.
The lands of the ten directions may be ground into dust, and their number known in a single thought;
the space traversed by a hair-tip may be measured, yet speaking of this for billions of eons would never reach its end.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-nine;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Forty.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.

27. Chapter on the Ten Samādhis. At that time, the World-Honored One was in the country of Magadha, at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) in the forest retreat (āraṇya-dharma), having newly attained perfect awakening. In the Hall of Universal Radiance, he entered the "Samādhi of the Momentary Limits of All Buddhas. By means of his own supernormal powers of omniscience, he manifested the body of a Tathāgata—pure and unimpeded, without dependence and without objective grasping. Abiding in the supreme tranquility of śamatha, endowed with great majestic virtue and free from all defilement, he enabled all who saw him to attain awakening. He appeared according to what was appropriate without missing the proper time, ever abiding in a single mark, which is to say, the markless.

He was accompanied by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, all of whom had attained the stage of consecration (*abhiṣeka*), were fully endowed with the bodhisattva practices, and were equal to the dharma-realm in its immeasurability and boundlessness. They had attained the bodhisattva samādhi of universal vision, brought peace and security to all sentient beings through great compassion, and possessed sovereign supernormal powers. Their wisdom entered deeply into that which is identical to the Tathāgata’s; they expounded the true meaning, were endowed with omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and subdued all Māras. Although they entered the world, their minds remained eternally tranquil, as they dwelt in the bodhisattva liberation of non-abiding.
Their names were: Bodhisattva Vajramati, Bodhisattva Asamaprajñā, Bodhisattva Arthavāgmati, Bodhisattva Varaprajñā,
Bodhisattva Nityatyāgamati, Bodhisattva Nāgamati, and Bodhisattva Siddhamati.
...the Bodhisattva Sādhuhita, the Bodhisattva Vinītamati, the Bodhisattva Mahābalamati,
the Bodhisattva Acintyamati, the Bodhisattva Asaṅgamati, the Bodhisattva Adhimātramati, the Bodhisattva Samantapūjamati,
the Bodhisattva Yathārthamati, the Bodhisattva Kovidamati, the Bodhisattva Dharmeśvaramati, and the Bodhisattva Dharmamati...
...Sattva, Śāntamati Bodhisattva, Gaganamati Bodhisattva, Ekalakṣaṇamati Bodhisattva,
Sumati Bodhisattva, Māyopamamati Bodhisattva, Vipulamati Bodhisattva, Balamati Bodhisattva, Lokamati Bodhisattva, Buddhakṣetramati Bodhisattva, and Bhūtamati Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Jyeṣṭhamati, the Bodhisattva Jñānaprabhamati, the Bodhisattva Anantamati, the Bodhisattva Smṛtivyūha,
the Bodhisattva Gaganasamudgata, the Bodhisattva Prakṛtivyūha, the Bodhisattva Gambhīrārtha,
the Bodhisattva Sthānāsthānakauśalya, the Bodhisattva Mahāprabha, and the Bodhisattva Nityaprabha.
The Bodhisattva Jñānabuddhi, the Bodhisattva Bodhivṛkṣa, the Bodhisattva Cittarāja, the Bodhisattva Ekacaryā,
the Bodhisattva Nityarddhipradarśana, the Bodhisattva Prajñāṅkura, the Bodhisattva Guṇasthāna,
the Bodhisattva Dharmapradīpa, the Bodhisattva Lokapradyota, the Bodhisattva Lokadhara, the Bodhisattva Paramakṣema, and the Bodhisattva Para...
The Superior Bodhisattva, the Unsurpassed Bodhisattva, the Peerless Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva Who Transcends All Ranks,
the Bodhisattva of Unobstructed Conduct, the Bodhisattva of Radiant Flames, the Moonlight Bodhisattva, the Single Atom Bodhisattva,
the Bodhisattva of Firm Conduct, the Bodhisattva Who Showering the Rain of Dharma, the Bodhisattva of the Supreme Banner, and the Universal...
The Bodhisattva Adorned with Splendor, the Bodhisattva Eye of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Dharma-Eye,
the Bodhisattva Cloud of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva King of Dhāraṇīs, the Bodhisattva of Non-Abiding Vows, the Bodhisattva Treasury of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Mind-King,
the Bodhisattva Inner Awakened Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Abiding in Buddha-Wisdom, and the Bodhisattva Valiant Power of Dhāraṇī.
The Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva Earth-Holding Power, the Bodhisattva Wondrous Moon, the Bodhisattva Sumeru Peak, the Bodhisattva Jewel Peak,
the Bodhisattva Universal Radiance, the Bodhisattva Majestic Virtue King, the Bodhisattva Wisdom Wheel,
the Bodhisattva Great Majestic Virtue, the Bodhisattva Great Dragon Appearance, and the Bodhisattva Upright Conduct.
...the Bodhisattva Avinivartanīya (Non-regressive), the Bodhisattva Dharmadhvaja-dhara (Holder of the Dharma Banner), the Bodhisattva Asammoṣa (Unforgetting),

the Bodhisattva Sarvagati-saṃgrāhaka (Gatherer of All Destinies), the Bodhisattva Acintya-niścita-prajña (Inconceivable and Decisive Wisdom), the Bodhisattva Ananta-jñāna-vikrīḍita (Sporting in Boundless Wisdom),
the Bodhisattva Akṣaya-sudharma-kośa (Inexhaustible Treasury of Sublime Dharma), the Bodhisattva Jñānasūrya (Wisdom Sun), and the Bodhisattva Dharmasūrya (Dharma Sun).
Bodhisattva Jñānagarbha, Bodhisattva Jñānavatī, Bodhisattva Samantadarśin, Bodhisattva Amoghadarśin, Bodhisattva Vajrābhijña, Bodhisattva Vajrajñāna, Bodhisattva Vajrajvāla,
Bodhisattva Vajraprajñā, Bodhisattva Samantanetra, Bodhisattva Buddhasūrya, and Bodhisattva Dhṛtabuddhavajraguhya.
The Bodhisattva Guhyārtha, the Bodhisattva Samantacakṣurviṣayajñānālaṃkāra, and so forth—

ten times the number of atoms in a buddha-field of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, in the past, had all cultivated together with the Tathāgata Vairocana the various practices of the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Eye (Samantacakṣus), empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"I wish to ask something of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; I pray that you will graciously grant me permission.
The Buddha said, "Puyan!"
"Ask whatever you wish, and I shall explain it for you so that your heart may rejoice.
Universal Eye Bodhisattva said,
"World-Honored One!"

To what extent have Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and the assembly of bodhisattvas who abide in all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra accomplished samādhis and liberations, such that they enter, emerge from, or occasionally dwell in the great samādhis of bodhisattvas?

Because they have skillfully entered into and emerged from the inconceivable, vast samādhis of a bodhisattva, they are able to exercise mastery over all samādhis and miraculous transformations without ceasing.
The Buddha said, “Excellent,
Universal Eye!”
You have asked about this meaning for the benefit of all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present.
Universal Eye!
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is now present here; he has already accomplished inconceivable and sovereign supernormal powers, surpassing all other bodhisattvas, and is difficult to encounter.

Born from immeasurable bodhisattva practices, their great vows have all been completely purified; the deeds they perform are entirely without regression. They have fully attained immeasurable gates of pāramitās, gates of unimpeded dhāraṇīs, and gates of inexhaustible eloquence—all of which are pure and unobstructed. With great compassion, they benefit all sentient beings, and by the power of their original vows, they remain untiring until the end of the future.
"You should request him; he shall explain to you that samādhi of sovereign liberation.

At that time, the assembly of bodhisattvas, upon hearing the name of Samantabhadra, immediately attained inconceivable and immeasurable samādhis. Their minds were unimpeded, tranquil, and unmoving; their wisdom was vast and difficult to fathom; their realm was profoundly deep and beyond compare.

They beheld countless Buddhas appearing before them, attained the powers of a Tathāgata, and shared the same nature as a Tathāgata. They clearly illuminated all things of the past, future, and present; their merit and virtue were inexhaustible, and they were fully endowed with all supernatural faculties.

Those bodhisattvas conceived a heart of deep respect for Samantabhadra and, thirsting with longing to see him, surveyed the entire assembly everywhere, yet they did not see him at all, nor did they see the seat upon which he sat.
"This is sustained by the majestic power of the Tathāgata, and it is also brought about by the sovereign spiritual powers of Samantabhadra.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Universal Eye addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Where is Samantabhadra Bodhisattva now?
The Buddha said,
“Universal Eye!”
"The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is now present here in this assembly at the site of enlightenment, dwelling in close proximity to me, without ever having moved from his place.
At that time, Universal Eye and the other bodhisattvas again scrutinized the assembly at the site of enlightenment, searching everywhere, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"We have not yet been able to see the body and seat of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
The Buddha said, "So it is, good sons!"
"Why is it that you do not see it? Good son,
it is because the dwelling place of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is profoundly deep and ineffable."

The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra has attained the gate of boundless wisdom, entered the Lion’s Rush Samādhi, and acquired supreme sovereign power. Having entered the realm of pure non-obstruction and given rise to the ten powers of a Tathāgata, he takes the treasury of the Dharma-realm as his body; he is protected and mindful of by all Tathāgatas, and in a single thought-moment, he is able to realize and enter the non-differentiated wisdom of all Buddhas of the three periods of time. For this reason, you are unable to see him.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Universal Eye, having heard the Tathāgata speak of the pure merits of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, attained ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* samādhis.
By the power of these samādhis, he further observed everywhere, thirsting with longing to see the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, yet he was unable to behold him.
All the other assemblies of bodhisattvas likewise could not be seen.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Universal Eye arose from samādhi and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

I have entered ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* samādhis seeking to see Samantabhadra, yet I have not found him; I do not see his body or his bodily actions, nor his speech or his verbal actions, nor his mind or his mental actions, nor his seat or his dwelling place—I see none of these at all.
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is! Good son!"
You should know that this is all due to the power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s abiding in the inconceivable liberation.
Puyan! What do you think?
"Is there anyone who can describe the locations where the various illusory manifestations within the words of an illusionist reside? He replied, "No."
The Buddha said, “Universal Eye!

Even the illusory marks within an illusion cannot be described; how much less can the realm of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s secret body, the realm of his secret speech, and the realm of his secret mind be entered or perceived!”
Why is this? The realm of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is profoundly deep, inconceivable, immeasurable, and beyond measure.

To state the essentials: Samantabhadra Bodhisattva enters the Dharma-realm universally with adamantine wisdom; throughout all worlds, he has no place of action and no place of abiding. He knows that the bodies of all sentient beings are, in their very nature, non-bodies, neither going nor coming. Having attained unceasing and inexhaustible, undifferentiated, sovereign spiritual powers, he is without dependence or fabrication, without movement or change, reaching the ultimate limit of the Dharma-realm.

"Good son! If there are those who behold Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, or serve him, or hear his name, or contemplate him, or keep him in mind, or give rise to faith and understanding, or diligently observe him, or first set out toward him, or earnestly seek him, or arouse vows for him, continuing these practices without interruption, they shall all obtain benefit; none shall pass through this in vain."

At that time, Universal Eye and the entire assembly of bodhisattvas felt a deep yearning for the mind of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to behold him, and spoke these words: “Namo to all Buddhas!”
"Homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva!
Thus he recited this three times, prostrating with his head at the ground in reverent salutation.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Universal Eye and the entire assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!

You should further pay homage to Samantabhadra with earnest entreaty; you should also observe the ten directions with single-minded devotion and visualize the body of Samantabhadra appearing before you."

Reflecting thus, pervading the entire dharma-realm, with a profound mind of faith and understanding, he felt weary of and detached from all things, vowing to share the same conduct and vows as Samantabhadra:

to enter the non-dual reality of the Dharma, to manifest his body throughout all worlds, to fully know the differences among the faculties of sentient beings, and to gather the path of Samantabhadra in all places.
"If one can give rise to such a great vow, then one shall behold the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
At that time, Universal Eye, having heard these words of the Buddha, together with all the bodhisattvas, prostrated themselves simultaneously and entreated to behold the Great Being Samantabhadra.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, by means of the power of his liberation and supernormal faculties, manifested physical bodies as was appropriate for each, so that all those bodhisattvas saw Samantabhadra approaching the Tathāgata and sitting upon a lotus throne amidst this entire assembly of bodhisattvas.
They also saw him, in succession and continuity, coming from the presence of all Buddhas in all other worlds;

they also saw him, in the presence of all those Buddhas, expounding all bodhisattva practices, revealing the path of omniscient wisdom, elucidating all bodhisattva supernormal powers, distinguishing all bodhisattva majesties, and manifesting all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Universal Eye and the entire assembly of bodhisattvas, beholding this divine transformation, their hearts leaped with joy and they experienced great rapture; there was none who did not prostrate before the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, conceiving a sense of reverence as if they were seeing all the Buddhas of the ten directions.

At that time, by the great majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, the power of the faith and understanding of all the bodhisattvas, and the power of the original vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, ten thousand kinds of clouds spontaneously rained down.
That is to say:

clouds of various flowers, clouds of various garlands, clouds of various perfumes, clouds of various powdered incenses, clouds of various parasols, clouds of various garments, clouds of various ornaments, clouds of various precious jewels, clouds of various burning incenses, and clouds of various silken fabrics.
Inexpressible worlds shook in six ways;
celestial music was played, its sound heard as far as inexpressible worlds;

a great radiance was emitted, its light universally illuminating inexpressible worlds, causing the three evil realms to be entirely extinguished, purifying inexpressible worlds, causing inexpressible bodhisattvas to enter the conduct of Samantabhadra, causing inexpressible bodhisattvas to perfect the conduct of Samantabhadra, and causing inexpressible bodhisattvas to fully accomplish the vows of the conduct of Samantabhadra and attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Universal Eye addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One! The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is one who dwells in great majestic power; one who dwells in the peerless; one who dwells in the faultless; one who dwells in non-retrogression; one who dwells in equanimity; one who dwells in the indestructible; one who dwells in all differentiated dharmas; one who dwells in all undifferentiated dharmas; one who dwells in the skillful mental abodes of all sentient beings; and one who dwells in the samādhi of sovereign liberation regarding all dharmas.”
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is!
Universal Eye!"
As you have said, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva possesses incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) pure merits, namely:

the merit of peerless adornment, the merit of immeasurable jewels, the merit of the inconceivable ocean, the merit of immeasurable marks, the merit of boundless clouds, the merit of infinite and inexpressible praise, the merit of inexhaustible dharmas, the merit of the ineffable, the merit of all Buddhas, and the merit of praising and extolling that can never be exhausted.
At that time, the Tathāgata addressed Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, saying: “Samantabhadra!

You should explain thirteen samādhis for the sake of Universal Eye and the assembly of bodhisattvas here, so that they may enter them skillfully and fulfill all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra.”

Because these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have taught these ten great samādhis, they have caused the bodhisattvas of the past to attain liberation, the bodhisattvas of the present to attain liberation now, and the bodhisattvas of the future to attain liberation in the future.

What are these ten? First is the Great Samādhi of Universal Radiance; second is the Great Samādhi of Sublime Radiance; third is the Great Samādhi of Successively Traveling to All Buddha-lands; fourth is the Great Samādhi of the Practice of the Pure Deep Mind; fifth is the Great Samādhi of Knowing the Treasury of Adornments of the Past; sixth is the Great Samādhi of the Treasury of the Light of Wisdom; seventh is the Great Samādhi of Thoroughly Knowing the Buddha-adornments of All Worlds; eighth is the Great Samādhi of the Differentiated Bodies of Sentient Beings; ninth is the Great Samādhi of Sovereignty over the Dharma-realm; and tenth is the Great Samādhi of the Unobstructed Wheel.
These ten great samādhis can be skillfully entered by the great bodhisattvas; they have been taught, will be taught, and are currently being taught by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
If bodhisattvas cherish and revere [this practice], cultivating it without indolence, they will achieve accomplishment.

Such a person is called a Buddha, is called a Tathāgata, and is also called one who has attained the ten powers; they are called a Teacher, a Great Teacher, All-Knowing One, All-Seeing One, one who dwells in non-obstruction, one who has mastered all objects, and one who is sovereign over all dharmas.
This Bodhisattva universally enters all worlds, yet remains unattached to those worlds;
universally enters all realms of sentient beings, yet grasps nothing among sentient beings;
universally enters all bodies, yet encounters no obstruction within those bodies.
They universally enter all dharma-realms, yet know that the dharma-realm has no boundaries.

They draw near to all Buddhas of the three periods of time and clearly perceive the teachings of all Buddhas. They skillfully expound all written characters, thoroughly comprehend all provisional designations, accomplish the pure path of all bodhisattvas, and dwell securely in all the distinct practices of bodhisattvas.

In a single thought-moment, they universally attain all wisdom of the three periods of time; they universally know all phenomena of the three periods of time; they universally proclaim all the teachings of the Buddhas; they universally turn all non-retrogressive wheels; and in each of the past, future, and present periods, they universally realize all paths to enlightenment.
Within each of these enlightenments, they universally comprehend everything taught by all the Buddhas.

This is the gateway to the characteristics of all bodhisattvas; it is the gateway to the wisdom-awakening of all bodhisattvas; it is the gateway to the invincible banner of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*); it is the gateway to the various practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; it is the gateway to fierce and sharp supernormal powers and vows; it is the gateway to all dhāraṇīs and eloquence; it is the gateway to the distinctions among all phenomena of the three periods of time; it is the gateway to the manifestations of all Buddhas; it is the gateway to establishing all sentient beings in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); and it is the gateway to purifying all worlds through the spiritual power of the Buddha.
If a bodhisattva enters this samādhi, they attain the power of the dharma-realm which is inexhaustible, and they attain the practice of space which is without obstruction;
they attain the station of the Dharma King with immeasurable sovereignty, just like the worldly rite of consecration and investiture.
Attaining boundless wisdom, they achieve universal penetration;
attaining vast power, they fulfill the ten kinds of perfection;
accomplishing a mind free from contention, they enter the limit of quiescence.
With great compassion and fearlessness, he is like a lion;
as a man of wisdom, he kindles the bright lamp of the True Dharma;
his all-encompassing merits are beyond the power of words to exhaust, and cannot be conceived by śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Attaining the wisdom of the dharma-realm, they abide in the immovable limit while being able to expound various teachings in accordance with worldly conventions;
abiding in signlessness, they skillfully enter into the characteristics of phenomena;
attaining the treasury of self-nature purity, they are born into the pure family of the Tathāgatas.
They skillfully open various distinct Dharma gates, yet through wisdom they realize that nothing exists;
they skillfully know the proper timing, constantly practicing the gift of Dharma to awaken all beings, and are thus called wise ones;
they universally gather in sentient beings, causing them all to become pure.
By means of the wisdom of skillful means, they manifest the attainment of the Buddha-way, yet they constantly practice the conduct of a bodhisattva without interruption or exhaustion;
they enter the realm of the skillful means of all-knowledge and manifest various kinds of vast supernormal powers.
Therefore, Samantabhadra!
You should now analyze and expound in detail the ten great samādhis of all bodhisattvas; the entire assembly here now wishes to hear them.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, receiving the intent of the Tathāgata, surveyed the assembly of bodhisattvas such as Universal Eye and addressed them, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
What is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of Universal Radiance?
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva possesses ten kinds of inexhaustible dharmas.

What are these ten? They are: the inexhaustible wisdom of the appearance of all Buddhas; the inexhaustible wisdom of the transformation of sentient beings; the inexhaustible wisdom that worlds are like reflections; the inexhaustible wisdom of penetrating deeply into the dharma-realm; the inexhaustible wisdom of skillfully gathering in bodhisattvas; the inexhaustible wisdom of the non-retrogression of bodhisattvas; the inexhaustible wisdom of skillfully observing the meaning of all dharmas; the inexhaustible wisdom of the power of the mind to skillfully maintain [the teachings]; the inexhaustible wisdom of abiding in the vast mind of enlightenment; and the inexhaustible wisdom of the power of the vow for omniscience regarding all Buddha-dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are called the ten inexhaustible dharmas of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to ten kinds of boundless minds.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
They resolve upon the boundless mind to liberate all sentient beings;
they resolve upon the boundless mind to serve all Buddhas;
they resolve upon the boundless mind to make offerings to all Buddhas.
They give rise to the boundless mind that universally beholds all Buddhas;
they give rise to the boundless mind that receives and upholds all Buddha-dharmas without forgetfulness;
they give rise to the boundless mind that manifests the infinite spiritual transformations of all Buddhas.
They resolve upon an infinite mind that does not abandon any bodhisattva practice, for the sake of attaining the power of a Buddha;
they resolve upon an infinite mind that universally enters the subtle realm of all-knowledge and expounds all Buddha-dharmas;
they resolve upon an infinite mind that universally enters the inconceivable and vast realm of the Buddhas.
They give rise to an infinite mind that, through the eloquence of the Buddhas, engenders profound aspiration and joy, and receives the boundless teachings of all Buddhas;
they give rise to an infinite mind that manifests various bodies of sovereign mastery and enters the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
These are the ten.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva possesses ten kinds of wisdom regarding the distinctions of entering samādhi.

What are these ten? They are as follows: entering meditative absorption in the east and arising in the west; entering meditative absorption in the west and arising in the east; entering meditative absorption in the south and arising in the north; entering meditative absorption in the north and arising in the south; entering meditative absorption in the northeast and arising in the southwest; entering meditative absorption in the southwest and arising in the northeast; entering meditative absorption in the northwest and arising in the southeast; entering meditative absorption in the southeast and arising in the northwest; entering meditative absorption below and arising above; and entering meditative absorption above and arising below.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva possesses ten kinds of skillful wisdom for entering the great samādhis."

What are these ten? O Son of the Buddha! A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva takes a trichiliocosm as a single lotus flower. He manifests his body so that it pervades this lotus flower and sits cross-legged upon it. Within his body, he further manifests a trichiliocosm, which contains ten billion sets of four continents (*cāturdvīpaka*). In each set of four continents, he manifests ten billion bodies; each body enters ten billion times ten billion trichiliocosms. In every set of four continents within those worlds, he manifests ten billion times ten billion Bodhisattvas practicing the path. Each Bodhisattva’s practice gives rise to ten billion times ten billion resolute understandings (*niścaya-vijñapti*). Each resolute understanding causes ten billion times ten billion types of spiritual faculties (*indriya*) to become perfected. Each type of spiritual faculty accomplishes ten billion times ten billion non-retrogressive karmas of the Bodhisattva-dharma.
However, the bodies they manifest are neither one nor many, and there is no confusion between their entering and emerging from meditative concentration.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the asura king Rāhu, whose original body is seven hundred yojanas long, yet who manifests a transformation body sixteen thousand eight hundred yojanas long, which emerges halfway out of the great ocean and stands exactly level with Mount Sumeru.
O Son of the Buddha!

Although that Asura King transforms his body to a length of one hundred and sixty-eight thousand yojanas, he does not destroy the characteristics of his original body. All his aggregates (skandhas), elements (dhātus), and sense bases (āyatanas) remain exactly as they were; his mind is not confused, nor does he conceive of the transformation body as something other than himself, nor does he conceive of his original body as not being himself. His original birth-body constantly experiences various pleasures, while his transformation body perpetually manifests all manner of sovereign supernatural powers and majestic might.
O Son of the Buddha!
Even the asura kings—who possess greed, hatred, and delusion, and are fully possessed of pride—are still able to manifest their bodies in such a way;

how much more so for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who deeply understand that mental phenomena are like illusions, that all worlds are entirely like dreams, that the appearance of all Buddhas in the world is like reflected images, that all worlds are like transformations, and that all speech and sounds are like echoes? Seeing the Dharma of reality, they take the Dharma of reality as their own body; knowing that the fundamental nature of all dharmas is pure, they realize that body and mind have no substantial essence. Their bodies dwell universally in immeasurable realms, and by means of the vast and great light of the Buddha’s wisdom, they purely cultivate all practices of enlightenment!
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they transcend the world and remain far removed from it; nothing can delude or disturb them, and nothing can outshine or eclipse them.”
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as a bhikṣu observes his own internal body, dwelling in the contemplation of impurity and clearly seeing that his entire body is nothing but impure, so too does the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwell in this samādhi and observe the Dharma-body.

He sees all worlds universally entering into his body; therein he clearly perceives all worlds and all worldly phenomena, yet he remains entirely unattached to those worlds and those worldly phenomena.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the first skillful wisdom of the great samādhi of Universal Radiance belonging to Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of Sublime Radiance? O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to enter as many trichiliocosms as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm; in each and every world, they manifest as many bodies as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm; from each body, they emit as many rays of light as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm; from each ray of light, they manifest as many colors as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm; each color illuminates as many worlds as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm; and within each world, they discipline as many sentient beings as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm.
These various worlds are diverse and different, and the Bodhisattva knows them all; that is to say:
the defilement of worlds, the purity of worlds, the causes of worlds, the establishment of worlds, the coexistence of worlds, the radiance and color of worlds, and the coming and going within worlds.
All such things as these, the Bodhisattva knows completely and enters into them all.
All these worlds likewise enter entirely into the body of the bodhisattva; yet, there is no confusion among the worlds, nor is any of the various phenomena destroyed or extinguished.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the rising sun circling Mount Sumeru and illuminating the mountains of the seven treasures. On those mountains of the seven treasures and in the spaces between them, all shadows and light appear with distinct clarity. Every solar reflection upon the treasure mountains is manifested within the shadows in the mountain intervals, and every solar reflection in the intervals between the seven mountains is likewise fully manifested within the reflections upon the mountains.

Thus they are mutually reflected back and forth; some say the solar reflection emerges from the mountains of the seven treasures, some say it emerges from the intervals between the seven mountains, some say the solar reflection enters the mountains of the seven treasures, and some say it enters the intervals between the seven mountains.

Yet these shadows reflect and manifest one another without limit; their essential nature is neither existent nor non-existent. They do not abide in the mountain, yet they do not depart from the mountain; they do not abide in the water, yet they do not depart from the water.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is the same for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: dwelling in this wondrous, luminous, and vast samādhi, they do not destroy the established characteristics of the world, nor do they extinguish the intrinsic nature of the various phenomena of the world;
they do not abide within the world, nor do they abide outside the world.
They do not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any worlds, yet they do not destroy the characteristics of worlds;
they contemplate all phenomena as having a single characteristic—namely, being without characteristics—and yet they do not destroy the intrinsic nature of phenomena;
they abide in the nature of *tathatā* (suchness), never abandoning it.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is, for example, like a master illusionist who is well-versed in the arts of illusion. Standing at a crossroads, he performs various illusory feats; within a single day, or even in the brief span of a single *muhūrta*, he may manifest a full day, or manifest a full night, or further manifest seven days and nights, half a month, a month, a year, or a hundred years. According to his desire, he can manifest cities and villages, springs, streams, rivers, and oceans, the sun, moon, clouds, and rain, as well as palaces, halls, and dwellings—all such things appear without exception.
Yet, because he manifests these over the course of years, he does not destroy the fundamental basis of that single day or single moment.
Because the original time is not extremely brief, it does not destroy the days, months, and years that appear therein;
the illusory manifestations appear clearly, yet the original time is not extinguished.
It is the same for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: entering this wondrous, vast, and great samādhi, they manifest incalculable worlds within a single world.

In each and every one of those incalculable worlds, there were all fully present with their various adornments: earth, water, fire, and wind; great oceans, mountains, cities, towns, villages, gardens, dwellings, celestial palaces, dragon palaces, yakṣa palaces, gandharva palaces, asura palaces, garuḍa palaces, kiṃnara palaces, and mahoraga palaces.

The realm of desire, the realm of form, and the formless realm; the small thousandfold world system and the great trichiliocosm; the karmic actions and their retributions; and dying here and being born there.

All the temporal divisions of the world—moments, days and nights, half-months, months, years, centuries, eons of formation, and eons of destruction—as well as defiled lands, pure lands, vast lands, and narrow lands, wherein Buddhas appear in the world; wherein Buddha-fields are purified and surrounded by assemblies of Bodhisattvas, who possess sovereign supernormal powers and transform sentient beings.

In all those lands and regions, they were entirely filled with immeasurable multitudes of people; there were infinite, boundless, and inconceivable beings of various forms and diverse destinies, and through the power of their pure karma in the past, future, and present, they produced immeasurable, supreme, and wondrous treasures.
All such matters as these are manifested and entered into a single world-system.

The Bodhisattva perceives them all clearly, enters them universally, contemplates them universally, and comprehends them universally; through inexhaustible wisdom, they know them all as they truly are. Because those worlds are many, this one world is not destroyed; because this world is one, those many worlds are not destroyed.
Why is this? Because the bodhisattva knows that all phenomena are without self;
therefore, this is called "entering the dharma of no life-principle and no activity."
Because the bodhisattva diligently practices the dharma of non-contention within all worlds,
they are called one who dwells in the dharma of selflessness;
because the bodhisattva perceives all bodies as they truly are, arising from conditions, they are called:
One who dwells in the dharma of non-existent sentient beings;
because the Bodhisattva knows that all dharmas of arising and ceasing are born from causes, this is called:
dwelling in the dharma of non-existent *pudgala*.
Because the Bodhisattva knows that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is equal,
he is said to be one who dwells in the state where there is no mind-born being (*manomaya*) and no person (*pudgala*);
because the Bodhisattva knows that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is quiescent, he is said to be:
One who dwells in the dharma of tranquility;
because a bodhisattva knows that all dharmas have a single characteristic,
they are said to be one who dwells in the dharma of non-discrimination.
Because the Bodhisattva knows that the dharma-realm has no various distinctions among phenomena,
they are said to be "one who dwells in the inconceivable dharma";
because the Bodhisattva diligently cultivates all skillful means to skillfully tame and transform sentient beings, they are said to be:
Regarding those who abide in the Dharma of Great Compassion:
"O Son of the Buddha!

A bodhisattva is thus able to cause incalculable worlds to enter into a single world; they know the various distinctions among countless sentient beings; they see countless bodhisattvas each setting out toward enlightenment; and they observe countless Buddhas appearing everywhere."
The Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas is fully received by all those bodhisattvas, and they also see themselves practicing therein;
yet they do not abandon this place while seeing themselves there, nor do they abandon that place while seeing themselves here, for there is no distinction between that body and this body.
Because they have entered the Dharma-realm, they constantly and diligently observe it without rest, never abandoning wisdom and never regressing.

It is like a master illusionist who performs various illusions in a single location; he does not destroy the original ground because of the illusory ground, nor does he destroy the original day because of the illusory day.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: in lands where there are no lands, he manifests lands; in lands where there are lands, he manifests no lands.
Where there are sentient beings, he manifests no sentient beings; where there are no sentient beings, he manifests sentient beings.
Where there is no form, he manifests form; where there is form, he manifests no form.

The end does not disturb the beginning, and the beginning does not disturb the end. The Bodhisattva understands that all worldly phenomena are likewise thus, identical to illusions and transformations. Because he knows phenomena are illusory, he knows wisdom is illusory; because he knows wisdom is illusory, he knows the mind is illusory. Because he knows the mind is illusory, he knows the self is illusory. Because he knows the self is illusory, he knows all dharmas are illusory. Because he knows all dharmas are illusory, he knows all sentient beings are illusory. Because he knows all sentient beings are illusory, he knows all afflictions are illusory. Because he knows all afflictions are illusory, he knows all karmic actions are illusory. Because he knows all karmic actions are illusory, he knows all retributions are illusory. Because he knows all retributions are illusory, he knows all realms of existence are illusory. Because he knows all realms of existence are illusory, he knows all Buddhas are illusory. Because he knows all Buddhas are illusory, he knows all dharmas are illusory. Because he knows all dharmas are illusory, he knows all teachings are illusory. Because he knows all teachings are illusory, he knows all paths are illusory. Because he knows all paths are illusory, he knows all fruits are illusory. Because he knows all fruits are illusory, he knows all nirvāṇas are illusory. Because he knows all nirvāṇas are illusory, he knows all attainments are illusory. Because he knows all attainments are illusory, he knows all non-attainments are illusory. Because he knows all non-attainments are illusory, he knows all things are illusory. Because he knows all things are illusory, he knows all dharmas are ultimately illusory. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately illusory, he knows all dharmas are ultimately empty. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately empty, he knows all dharmas are ultimately quiescent. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately quiescent, he knows all dharmas are ultimately unconditioned. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately unconditioned, he knows all dharmas are ultimately signless. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately signless, he knows all dharmas are ultimately wishless. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately wishless, he knows all dharmas are ultimately unborn. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately unborn, he knows all dharmas are ultimately unceasing. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately unceasing, he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-arising. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-arising, he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-perishing. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-perishing, he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-dual. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-dual, he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-distinct. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-distinct, he knows all dharmas are ultimately equal. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately equal, he knows all dharmas are ultimately one taste. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately one taste, he knows all dharmas are ultimately inconceivable. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately inconceivable, he knows all dharmas are ultimately ineffable. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately ineffable, he knows all dharmas are ultimately ungraspable. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately ungraspable, he knows all dharmas are ultimately unobtainable. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately unobtainable, he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-existent. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately non-existent, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like space. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like space, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a dream. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a dream, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an illusion. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an illusion, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a mirage. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a mirage, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an echo. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an echo, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a reflection. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a reflection, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a city of gandharvas. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a city of gandharvas, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a phantom. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a phantom, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a transformation. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a transformation, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a lightning flash. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a lightning flash, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a cloud. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a cloud, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a bubble. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a bubble, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like foam. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like foam, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like dust motes. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like dust motes, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a flame. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a flame, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a wheel of fire. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a wheel of fire, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a mountain torrent. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a mountain torrent, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a falling leaf. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a falling leaf, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a withered tree. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a withered tree, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a decaying corpse. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a decaying corpse, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a rotting stump. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a rotting stump, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a severed head. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a severed head, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a broken vessel. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a broken vessel, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a scattered pile of bones. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a scattered pile of bones, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a painted image. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a painted image, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a borrowed object. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a borrowed object, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a guest house. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a guest house, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a traveler. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a traveler, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a caravan leader. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a caravan leader, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a ferryman. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a ferryman, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a bridge. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a bridge, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a raft. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a raft, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a boat. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a boat, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a stream. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a stream, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a whirlpool. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a whirlpool, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a mirage. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a mirage, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a dream. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a dream, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an illusion. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an illusion, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a shadow. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a shadow, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an echo. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like an echo, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a reflection. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a reflection, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a phantom. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a phantom, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a transformation. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a transformation, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a lightning flash. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a lightning flash, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a cloud. Because he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a cloud, he knows all dharmas are ultimately like a bubble. Because
Because one knows that cognition is illusory, one knows that karma is illusory.
Having known that both cognition and karma are illusory, one gives rise to illusory wisdom and contemplates all karma.
Just as a worldly illusionist does not manifest his illusions outside of a location, nor does he have a location outside of his illusions.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: he does not enter the world from outside of space, nor does he enter space from outside of the world. Why is this?
Because there is no distinction between space and the world, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells both in the world and in space.

Within space, they are able to perceive and cultivate all the various distinct and wondrously adorned activities of the world; in a single thought-moment, they can fully comprehend the formation and destruction of countless worlds, as well as the sequential succession of all kalpas.
They can manifest countless kalpas within a single thought-moment, yet they do not cause that single thought-moment to become vast.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the illusory wisdom of inconceivable liberation and reach the other shore;
abiding at the limit of illusion, they enter the illusory calculations of the world and contemplate that all phenomena are entirely like illusions.

Without contradicting the illusory world, they exhaust illusory wisdom and realize that the three periods of time are no different from illusion. They decisively penetrate this truth, and their minds have no boundaries.
Just as all Tathāgatas abide in illusion-like wisdom, their minds are equanimous;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who knows that all worlds are entirely like illusions, and thus remains unattached in all places, free from the notion of "mine."
Just as a magician performs various magical illusions and, though he does not dwell together with those illusions, remains undeluded regarding them;

so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: knowing that all phenomena have reached the other shore, his mind does not conceive of a self that can enter into phenomena, nor does he experience confusion regarding phenomena.
This is the second subtle light, the great samādhi of skillful wisdom of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha-Avatamsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 40;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha-Avatamsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 41.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree, Chapter Twenty-seven, Part Two: "The Twenty Samādhis.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s samādhi of supernatural power that proceeds sequentially to all buddha-lands?
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva passes beyond incalculable worlds to the east, and further passes beyond as many worlds as there are...
In worlds as numerous as the atoms within a realm, he enters this samādhi within all those worlds— entering it for a single kṣaṇa,
or for a brief moment, or in continuous succession; entering it during the first watch of the day,
or the middle watch, or the last watch, or during the first watch of the night.
They may enter at the middle watch of the night, or at the latter watch of the night; they may enter once a day,
or once every five days, or once every half-month, or once a month, or once a year,
or once a hundred years, or once a thousand years, or once a hundred thousand years, or once in ten million years.
Some enter for hundreds of thousands of billions of years; some enter for hundreds of thousands of nayutas of billions of years;
some enter for one kalpa; some enter for a hundred kalpas; some enter for a hundred thousand kalpas; some enter for hundreds of thousands of nayutas of billions of kalpas;
some enter for incalculable kalpas; some enter for immeasurable kalpas; or some enter for boundless kalpas.
They enter for a period equal to an *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa, or for an incalculable (*agaṇeya*) kalpa, or for an incomparable (*atulya*) kalpa,
or for an inconceivable (*acintya*) kalpa, or for an immeasurable (*aprameya*) kalpa, or for an ineffable (*anabhilāpya*) kalpa,
or for an ineffably ineffable (*anabhilāpyānabhilāpya*) kalpa— whether for a long duration or a short one.
The Dharma, at various times, manifests in diverse and differing ways.

The Bodhisattva does not give rise to discrimination regarding them; his mind is free from defiled attachment. He does not conceive of duality, nor non-duality; he does not conceive of universality, nor particularity. Although he is detached from such discriminations, through the skillful means of supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), he arises from samādhi and, without forgetting or losing anything regarding all dharmas, reaches the ultimate goal.
For example, the Sun Deity travels in a circuit, illuminating all without ceasing day or night;
the rising of the sun is called day, and its setting is called night, yet the day does not arise, nor does the night perish.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva enters the samādhi of supernormal powers within countless worlds; having entered this samādhi, he clearly perceives that those same countless worlds are likewise so.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the skillful wisdom of the great samādhi of supernormal powers through which a bodhisattva mahāsattva successively visits all buddha-lands for the third time.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the samādhi of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice of the pure profound mind?
O Son of the Buddha!

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that the number of the bodies of all Buddhas is equal to the number of sentient beings, and he beholds immeasurable Buddhas exceeding the number of atoms in incalculable worlds.
Before each and every one of those Tathāgatas, they made offerings with all kinds of exquisite incenses,
made offerings with all kinds of exquisite flowers, and made offerings with all kinds of canopies as vast as incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Buddha-fields, surpassing everything in all worlds.
They made offerings with supremely exquisite ornaments; they made offerings by scattering all kinds of various jewels;
they made offerings by adorning the walking paths with all kinds of various ornaments;
they made offerings with all the countless, supremely exquisite treasuries of *maṇi* jewels; by the power of the Buddha...
They flow forth superior food and drink surpassing those of all the heavens as offerings;
with their supernormal powers, they are able to universally gather all manner of sublime and exquisite offering implements from all Buddha-fields to present as offerings.

Before each and every one of those Tathāgatas, he paid homage with reverence and respect, prostrating himself with his head to the ground and casting his entire body upon the earth. He inquired about the Buddha-dharma, praised the equanimity of the Buddhas, and extolled the vast merits of all Buddhas. He entered into the great compassion attained by all Buddhas and acquired the unimpeded power of the Buddhas' equanimity.

In a single thought-moment, he diligently sought the sublime Dharma in the presence of all Buddhas; yet, regarding the appearance of these Buddhas in the world and their entry into parinirvāṇa, he perceived no such signs as being truly existent.
Just as a distracted mind cognizes its objects such that, when the mind arises, one does not know from what object it arises, and when the mind ceases, one does not know at what object it ceases;
so too is this bodhisattva mahāsattva, who ultimately never discriminates between the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world and the marks of his parinirvāṇa.

"O Son of the Buddha! It is like a mirage in the midday sun: it does not arise from clouds, nor does it arise from a pool; it does not abide on land, nor does it dwell in water. It is neither existent nor non-existent, neither good nor evil, neither clear nor turbid. It cannot be used for drinking or rinsing, yet it cannot be defiled. It has no substance, yet it is not without substance; it has no flavor, yet it is not without flavor. Due to causes and conditions, it manifests the appearance of water; it is perceived by consciousness, and when viewed from afar, it resembles water and gives rise to the thought of water. Yet upon approaching, it is not there, and the thought of water naturally vanishes.
In this same way, these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas do not perceive the appearance of a Tathāgata appearing in the world, nor the appearance of his parinirvāṇa."
Whether Buddhas possess marks or are markless, all such states are merely conceptual distinctions made by the mind of perception.
O Son of the Buddha!
This samādhi is named:
This is the practice of the pure, profound mind.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva has entered this samādhi and subsequently emerges from it, he does not lose what was attained upon emerging.

It is like a person who awakens from sleep and remembers the events of a dream; although the objective realm of the dream no longer exists at the time of waking, they are still able to recollect it and their mind does not forget it.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise thus: entering into samādhi, he sees the Buddhas and hears the Dharma; arising from concentration, he retains it in memory without forgetting. By means of this Dharma, he enlightens all assemblies at the sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), adorns all Buddha-lands, and fully attains clear penetration into immeasurable meanings and intentions. All dharma-gates are likewise purified; he kindles the great torch of wisdom, nurtures the seeds of all Buddhas, is endowed with fearlessness, possesses inexhaustible eloquence, and reveals and expounds the profound treasury of the Dharma.
This is the fourth skillful wisdom of the great samādhi of the pure, profound mental application of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s samādhi of knowing the treasury of adornments of the past?”
O Son of the Buddha! This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to know the appearance of all past Buddhas, namely:

the sequence of lands within the sequence of kalpas; the sequence of kalpas within the sequence of lands; the sequence of the appearance of Buddhas within the sequence of kalpas; the sequence of teaching the Dharma within the sequence of the Buddhas' appearances; the sequence of various inclinations within the sequence of teaching the Dharma; the sequence of faculties within the sequence of inclinations; the sequence of taming within the sequence of faculties; the sequence of the lifespans of Buddhas within the sequence of taming; and the sequence of knowing the numerical quantities of billions of nayutas of years within the sequence of lifespans.

O Son of the Buddha! Because these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have attained such boundless sequential wisdom, they know all the Buddhas of the past; they know all the lands of the past; they know all the Dharma-gates of the past; they know all the eons of the past; they know all the dharmas of the past; they know all the minds of the past; they know all the understandings of the past; they know all sentient beings of the past; they know all afflictions of the past; they know all formal practices of the past; and they know all purities of the past.
O Son of the Buddha!
This samādhi is named the "Pure Treasury of the Past.

Within a single thought-moment, it can enter into a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, a hundred thousand kalpas, a hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* kalpas; it can enter into incalculable kalpas, immeasurable kalpas, boundless kalpas, incomparable kalpas, uncountable kalpas, inexpressible kalpas, unthinkable kalpas, unfathomable kalpas, unspeakable kalpas, and unspeakably-unspeakable kalpas.
O Son of the Buddha!
When those Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas enter this samādhi, they do not extinguish the present, nor do they take the past as an object of cognition.
O Son of the Buddha!

When that bodhisattva mahāsattva arises from this samādhi, they receive, purify, accomplish, enter, realize, fulfill, and maintain ten kinds of inconceivable consecration-dharmas from the Tathāgata; they also thoroughly understand the purity of the three spheres with equanimity.

What are the ten? First, eloquence that does not contradict the meaning; second, inexhaustible preaching of the Dharma; third, flawless terminology; fourth, uninterrupted delight in speaking; fifth, a mind free from fear; sixth, speech that is invariably truthful; seventh, being a refuge for sentient beings; eighth, rescuing and liberating those within the three realms; ninth, the most supreme roots of goodness; and tenth, the sublime Dharma of training and subduing.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of consecration methods.
If a bodhisattva enters this samādhi, they will attain them immediately upon arising from that samādhi.
Just as when the kalala enters the womb, consciousness takes rebirth in a single moment;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: arising from this samādhi, in a single thought-moment before the Tathāgata, he attains these ten kinds of dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s fifth skillful wisdom of the Great Samādhi of the Treasury of Adornments of the Past.
O Son of the Buddha!”
What is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of the Treasury of the Radiance of Wisdom?
O Son of the Buddha!
When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they are able to know all Buddhas throughout all kalpas in all worlds of the future.
Whether already spoken or yet to be spoken, whether already prophesied or yet to be prophesied, there are various distinct names, namely:
innumerable names, immeasurable names, boundless names, incomparable names, incalculable names, ineffable names, inconceivable names, unquantifiable names, and unspeakable names;

[these refer to those who] shall appear in the world, shall benefit sentient beings, shall become Dharma-kings, shall perform Buddha-activities, shall proclaim blessings and benefits, shall praise the meaning of goodness, shall expound the meaning of the pure side, shall purify all evils, shall abide securely in merit, shall reveal the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), shall enter the stage of consecration (*abhiṣeka*), and shall attain omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).

Those Tathāgatas have cultivated perfect conduct, made perfect vows, entered perfect wisdom, possessed perfect assemblies, prepared perfect adornments, accumulated perfect merit, awakened to the perfect Dharma, attained the perfect fruit, were endowed with perfect marks, and achieved perfect enlightenment.

He fully understands all such things as the names, surnames, and lineages of those Tathāgatas, their skillful means, their supernormal transformations, their maturing of sentient beings, and their entry into parinirvāṇa.
In a single thought-moment, this bodhisattva is able to enter one eon, a hundred eons, a thousand eons, a hundred thousand eons, and a hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* eons;
they enter as many eons as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, as many eons as there are atoms in the four continents, and as many eons as there are atoms in a small thousand-world system. They enter...
Entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a medium chiliocosm; entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a great trichiliocosm;
entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field; entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand buddha-fields;
entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand billion nayutas of buddha-fields; entering eons as numerous as the atoms in innumerable buddha-fields.
They enter eons as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable Buddha-fields; they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in boundless Buddha-fields;
they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in incomparable Buddha-fields; they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields;
they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in ineffable Buddha-fields; they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in inconceivable Buddha-fields...
They enter eons as numerous as the atoms in a world-system; they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable Buddha-fields;
they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable Buddha-fields; they enter eons as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields.
In this way, one can, through wisdom, fully comprehend all the kalpas of all future worlds.
Because of this comprehension, the mind further enters ten kinds of sustaining gates (*dhāraṇīmukha*).
What are these ten? They are:
because of entering the Buddha’s upholding, one attains the protective mindfulness of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
By entering into the upholding of the Dharma, one attains ten kinds of dhāraṇī-lights and inexhaustible eloquence;
by entering into the upholding of practice, one gives rise to perfect and supreme vows;
by entering into the upholding of power, one cannot be eclipsed or overcome.
Because they have entered the sustaining power of wisdom, their practice of the Buddha-dharma is without obstruction;
because they have entered the sustaining power of great compassion, they turn the pure wheel of Dharma that never regresses;
because they have entered the sustaining power of skillful phrases of differentiation, they turn the wheel of all syllables and purify the stages of all dharma-gates.
By upholding the dharma of entering the lion’s birth, one opens the lock of the Dharma and emerges from the mire of desire;
by upholding the power of wisdom, one cultivates the bodhisattva practices without ever ceasing;
and by upholding the power of spiritual friends, one causes boundless sentient beings to attain universal purity.
By entering the sustaining power of non-abiding, they enter unspeakably unspeakable vast eons;
by entering the sustaining power of the Dharma, through the wisdom of unimpeded skillful means, they know that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Having dwelled in this samādhi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva skillfully dwells for unspeakably unspeakable kalpas,
skillfully dwells in unspeakably unspeakable lands, and skillfully knows the unspeakable...”
One may speak of various sentient beings who are skillfully able to know the distinct characteristics of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings;
who are skillfully able to know the karmic retributions of the similarities and differences of unspeakably unspeakable numbers [of actions];
and who are skillfully able to know the distinctions in the continuities of the various practices of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of energetic efforts, faculties, and habitual tendencies.
They skillfully know the inconceivable, ineffable, and immeasurable varieties of contemplation regarding defilement and purity;
they skillfully know the inconceivable, ineffable various meanings of dharmas, their immeasurable syllables, and the verbal expressions used to expound them;
and they skillfully know the inconceivable, ineffable varieties of the appearance of Buddhas, their lineages, and their times.

They skillfully know the gates of unspeakably unspeakable and boundless wisdom— manifesting signs, preaching the Dharma, performing buddha-works, and entering parinirvāṇa— and they skillfully know the unspeakably unspeakable and infinite transformations of all supernatural powers.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the rising of the sun: all things in the world—villages, camps, cities, towns, palaces, houses, mountains, marshes, birds, beasts, forests, flowers, and fruits—all such various objects are clearly seen by those who possess eyes.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as the sunlight is impartial and free from discrimination, yet enables the eyes to perceive various forms;

so too is this Great Samādhi: its essential nature is impartial and free from discrimination, yet it enables Bodhisattvas to know the hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable distinct characteristics.
O Son of the Buddha!
When this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva understands time in this way, he causes all sentient beings to attain ten kinds of non-futility. What are these ten?
First is non-empty seeing, which causes all sentient beings to give rise to roots of goodness;
second is non-empty hearing, which causes all sentient beings to attain maturity;
third is non-empty co-residence, which causes the minds of all sentient beings to be tamed.
Fourth is the non-emptiness of aspiration, which causes all sentient beings to act according to their words, because it brings about penetration into the meaning of all phenomena;
fifth is the non-emptiness of practice, which causes all boundless worlds to become pure;

sixth is the non-emptiness of proximity, whereby, in the presence of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Tathāgatas across unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields, one severs the doubts of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings.
Seventh is the non-emptiness of vows: because they cause all sentient beings whom they keep in mind to perform supreme offerings and thereby fulfill all their aspirations;
eighth is the non-emptiness of skillful means regarding the Dharma: because they cause all beings to abide in unimpeded liberation and pure wisdom;

ninth is the non-emptiness of raining down the rain of Dharma: because, among inconceivable and ineffable numbers of sentient beings with various faculties, they employ skillful means to reveal the practices of omniscience and cause them to abide in the Buddha-way.
Tenth is the manifestation of non-emptiness, appearing as infinite marks so that all sentient beings may receive its illumination. Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in this samādhi and attains these ten kinds of non-empty times, the hosts of celestial kings all come to prostrate at his crown; the hosts of dragon kings raise great clouds of incense; the yakṣa kings prostrate at his feet; the asura kings offer respectful worship; the garuḍa kings surround him before and behind; all the Brahmā kings come to exhort and entreat him; the kinnara kings and mahoraga kings all join in praising him; the gandharva kings constantly come to attend upon him; and the hosts of human kings serve and make offerings to him.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the sixth skillful wisdom of the Great Samādhi, the Treasury of the Light of Wisdom, of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s samādhi for thoroughly knowing the Buddha-adornments of all worlds?
Son of the Buddha!
For what reason is this samādhi named "Thoroughly Knowing the Buddha-adornments of All Worlds"?
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they are able to enter the worlds of the eastern direction in succession; they are able to enter the worlds of the southern direction in succession; and likewise for all worlds in the western, northern, four intermediate directions, and above and below—they are able to enter them all in succession.

They all saw the Buddhas appearing in the world; they also saw all the supernatural powers of those Buddhas, as well as all the playful manifestations of the Buddhas, the vast majesty of the Buddhas, the supreme sovereignty of the Buddhas, the great lion’s roar of the Buddhas, the various practices cultivated by the Buddhas, the manifold adornments of the Buddhas, and the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas’ spiritual feet. They also saw the assemblies of the Buddhas gathering like clouds—whether those assemblies were pure, vast, of a single characteristic, or of many characteristics; whether they were in their respective locations, where they resided, how they were brought to maturity, how they were disciplined, and what their majesty was. All such things they clearly perceived.

He also saw assemblies whose dimensions were equal to Jambudvīpa; he also saw assemblies equal to the four continents; he also saw assemblies equal to a small thousand-world system; he also saw assemblies equal to a medium thousand-world system; and he also saw assemblies whose measure was equal to a great trichiliocosm.
He also saw assemblies filling hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
he also saw assemblies filling incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) buddha-fields; he also saw assemblies filling as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in a hundred buddha-fields;
he also saw assemblies filling as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in a thousand buddha-fields; he also saw—
He saw assemblies filling buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
he also saw assemblies filling buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within countless buddha-fields;

he also saw assemblies filling buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable buddha-fields; and he also saw assemblies filling buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within boundless buddha-fields.
I also see assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field;
I also see assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields;
I also see assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in inexpressible Buddha-fields; I also see assemblies filling...
I see assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in an inconceivable number of Buddha-fields;

I also see assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in an immeasurable number of Buddha-fields; I also see assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in an unspeakable number of Buddha-fields;
and I also see assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in an unspeakably unspeakable number of Buddha-fields.
In Buddha-fields as numerous as atoms,

I also saw various Buddhas within their respective assemblies and places of enlightenment manifesting various signs, at various times, in various lands, with various transformations, various supernormal powers, various adornments, various masteries, various forms and dimensions, and various activities.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva also sees his own body going to those assemblies; he also sees his own body preaching the Dharma there;
he also sees his own body receiving and upholding the Buddha’s words; he also sees his own body thoroughly understanding dependent origination;
he also sees his own body dwelling in empty space; and he also sees his own body abiding in the dharma-body. Furthermore—

One personally perceives that the body does not give rise to defiled attachment; one also personally perceives that the body does not abide in conceptual discrimination; one also personally perceives that the body is free from weariness;
one also personally perceives that the body universally enters into all forms of wisdom; one also personally perceives that the body universally knows all meanings;
one also personally perceives that the body universally enters into all stages (bhūmis); one also personally perceives that the body universally enters into all...
Furthermore, they see their own bodies everywhere knowing skillful means; they see their own bodies everywhere abiding before the Buddhas;
they see their own bodies everywhere entering the various powers; they see their own bodies everywhere entering True Suchness;
they see their own bodies everywhere entering the state of non-contention; and they see their own bodies everywhere entering all dharmas.

When viewing in this manner, one does not discriminate between lands, does not discriminate between sentient beings, does not discriminate between Buddhas, and does not discriminate between dharmas; one does not cling to the body, does not cling to bodily action, does not cling to the mind, and does not cling to the mental faculty.
For example, all phenomena do not discriminate their own nature nor do they discriminate sounds, yet their nature is not abandoned and their names are not extinguished;
