so too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, who does not abandon practice and acts in accordance with worldly affairs, yet remains without attachment to these two.
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva beholds the Buddhas’ immeasurable radiance and colors, their immeasurable forms and marks, which are perfectly accomplished, equal, and pure;
each appears before him, clearly realized and understood.”

Some see the Buddha’s body emitting various kinds of light; some see the Buddha’s body with a halo one fathom wide; some see the Buddha’s body with the color of the blazing sun; some see the Buddha’s body with subtle and wondrous light-colors; some see the Buddha’s body manifesting a pure color; some see the Buddha’s body manifesting a golden-yellow color; some see the Buddha’s body manifesting the color of a vajra; some see the Buddha’s body manifesting a deep azure color; some see the Buddha’s body manifesting boundless colors; and some see the Buddha’s body manifesting the color of a great blue maṇi jewel.

Some see the Buddha’s body measuring seven cubits; some see the Buddha’s body measuring eight cubits; some see the Buddha’s body measuring nine cubits; some see the Buddha’s body measuring ten cubits; some see the Buddha’s body measuring twenty cubits; some see the Buddha’s body measuring thirty cubits; and so on, up to one hundred cubits and even one thousand cubits.
Some see the Buddha’s body as one *krośa* in measure; some see the Buddha’s body as half a *yojana* in measure;
some see the Buddha’s body as one *yojana* in measure; some see the Buddha’s body as ten *yojanas* in measure; some see the Buddha’s body as a hundred *yojanas* in measure;
some see the Buddha’s body as a thousand *yojanas* in measure; or some see the Buddha’s body as a hundred [thousand]...
They may see the Buddha’s body as measuring one thousand yojanas; or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of Jambudvīpa; or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of the four continents;
or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of a small chiliocosm; or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of a medium chiliocosm;
or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of a great trichiliocosm; or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of a hundred great trichiliocosms.
Some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a thousand great trichiliocosms; some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a hundred thousand great trichiliocosms;
some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* great trichiliocosms;
some see the Buddha’s body as the size of innumerable great trichiliocosms; or they see the Buddha’s body as the size of immeasurable great trichiliocosms.
As for the measure of the world, some see the Buddha’s body as having the measure of boundless great trichiliocosms;
some see the Buddha’s body as having the measure of incomparable great trichiliocosms; some see the Buddha’s body as having the measure of incalculable great trichiliocosms;
some see the Buddha’s body as having the measure of ineffable great trichiliocosms; or they see the Buddha’s body as having an immeasurable...
One may contemplate the magnitude of a trichiliocosm; or see the Buddha’s body as immeasurable, with a magnitude equal to a trichiliocosm;
or see the Buddha’s body as inexpressible, with a magnitude equal to a trichiliocosm; or see the Buddha’s body as inexpressibly inexpressible, with a magnitude equal to a trichiliocosm.
O Son of the Buddha!

Thus does a bodhisattva behold the Tathāgatas with their infinite physical marks, infinite forms, infinite manifestations, infinite radiances, and infinite networks of light. The extent of these lights is equal to the Dharma-realm, illuminating everything within that realm without exception, universally causing the arousal of unsurpassed wisdom.
Furthermore, they behold the Buddha’s body as being free from attachment, free from obstruction, and supremely pure.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva perceives the body of the Buddha in this way, the body of the Tathāgata neither increases nor decreases.
It is like space: it does not diminish within the hole of a mustard seed eaten by an insect, nor does it expand throughout countless worlds.
The bodies of those Buddhas are likewise thus: when seen as large, they do not increase; when seen as small, they do not decrease.
O Son of the Buddha!
For example, just as the people of Jambudvīpa see the lunar disk as small in form yet it does not diminish, while those dwelling within the moon see its form as large yet it does not increase;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who, abiding in this samādhi, perceives according to his mental inclinations the various transformed marks of the Buddhas’ bodies and their verbal expounding of the Dharma, receiving and retaining them without forgetting, yet the body of the Tathāgata neither increases nor decreases.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as when sentient beings, after the end of their lives and as they are about to take rebirth, perceive what is pure without departing from the mind;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who perceives what is pure without departing from this profound samādhi.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in this samādhi, they accomplish ten kinds of swift dharmas. What are these ten?

That is to say: to swiftly increase all practices and fulfill great vows; to swiftly illuminate the world with the light of the Dharma; to swiftly turn the wheel of Dharma through skillful means to deliver sentient beings; to swiftly manifest the pure lands of all Buddhas in accordance with the karma of sentient beings; to swiftly enter the ten powers through impartial wisdom; to swiftly dwell together with all Tathāgatas; to swiftly destroy the armies of Māra through the power of great compassion; to swiftly sever the doubts of sentient beings and cause them to give rise to joy; to swiftly manifest spiritual transformations in accordance with their superior inclinations; and to swiftly purify all worlds through various sublime Dharmas and modes of expression.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further attains ten kinds of Dharma-seals, which seal all phenomena. What are these ten?
First, they share the identical roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
second, they share with all Tathāgatas the attainment of the Dharma-body of boundless wisdom; third, they share with all Tathāgatas the abiding in the non-dual dharma;
fourth, they share with all Tathāgatas the observation that the infinite realms of the three periods of time are entirely equal.
...fifth, they are equal to all Tathāgatas in having attained the unimpeded realm of the Dharma-realm;
sixth, they are equal to all Tathāgatas in accomplishing the ten powers and acting without impediment;

seventh, they are equal to all Tathāgatas in forever severing the two modes of practice and abiding in the dharma of non-contention; eighth, they are equal to all Tathāgatas in teaching and transforming sentient beings, never ceasing...
Ninth, they are identical to all Tathāgatas in their skillful mastery of wisdom and skillful mastery of meaning, being able to observe them thoroughly;
tenth, they are identical to all Tathāgatas, being equal and non-dual with all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes this skillful means door of the great samādhi that understands the Buddha-adornments of all worlds, they are one who has no teacher, for by not relying on the instruction of others, they enter all Buddha-dharmas of their own accord;
they are a true man, for they are able to awaken all sentient beings.”
It is pure because it knows that the nature of the mind is fundamentally pure;
it is supreme because it is able to deliver all the world;
it is a consolation because it is able to enlighten and awaken all sentient beings.
This is abiding securely, because it causes those who have not yet entered the lineage of the Buddhas to enter;
this is true knowledge, because it enters the gateway of all-knowledge;
this is the absence of divergent thoughts, because what is spoken is non-dual.
These are those who dwell in the treasury of the Dharma, because they have vowed to fully comprehend all Buddha-dharmas;
these are those who can rain down the rain of Dharma, because they cause all sentient beings to be fully satisfied according to the inclinations of their minds.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like Śakra, who places a maṇi jewel within his topknot; by the power of that jewel, his majestic radiance becomes even more magnificent.
When the Heavenly King Śakra first obtains this jewel, he attains ten qualities that surpass all those of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

What are these ten? First, physical appearance; second, bodily form; third, manifestation; fourth, retinue; fifth, requisites; sixth, voice; seventh, supernormal powers; eighth, mastery; ninth, wisdom and understanding; tenth, the application of knowledge.
These ten kinds [of palaces] all surpass those of all the Trāyastriṃśa gods.
In the same way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva first attains this samādhi, they obtain ten kinds of vast treasuries of wisdom.

What are these ten? First, the wisdom that illuminates all buddha-fields; second, the wisdom that knows the births and rebirths of all sentient beings; third, the wisdom that universally manifests transformations throughout the three periods of time; fourth, the wisdom that universally enters the bodies of all Buddhas; fifth, the wisdom that penetrates all Buddha-dharmas; sixth, the wisdom that universally gathers all pure dharmas; seventh, the wisdom that causes all sentient beings to universally enter the Dharma-body; eighth, the wisdom of the pure universal eye that directly perceives all phenomena; ninth, the wisdom of universal mastery that reaches the further shore; and tenth, the wisdom that dwells securely in all vast dharmas, exhausting them all without exception.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they further attain ten kinds of most pure and majestic bodies. What are these ten?
First, in order to illuminate unspeakably unspeakable worlds, they emit unspeakably unspeakable wheels of light;
second, in order to cause all worlds to become completely pure, they emit unspeakably unspeakable wheels of light of immeasurable colors and forms;
third, in order to subdue sentient beings, they emit unspeakably unspeakable wheels of light.
Fourth, in order to draw near to all Buddhas, they manifest unspeakably unspeakable bodies;
fifth, in order to serve and make offerings to all Buddhas, they rain down unspeakably unspeakable clouds of various exquisite incenses and flowers;
sixth, in order to serve and make offerings to all Buddhas and to discipline all sentient beings, they manifest within each and every pore unspeakably unspeakable varieties of musical instruments.
Seventh, for the sake of maturing sentient beings, they manifest unspeakably unspeakable varieties of immeasurable sovereign spiritual transformations;
eighth, for the sake of inquiring about the Dharma at the abodes of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions who bear various names, they leap across unspeakably unspeakable worlds in a single step;

ninth, so that all sentient beings who see or hear them shall not do so in vain, they manifest unspeakably unspeakable varieties of immeasurable pure physical forms, the crowns of whose heads none can see.
Tenth, in order to reveal and teach immeasurable secret dharmas to sentient beings, they produce unspeakably unspeakable sounds and languages.
O Son of the Buddha!
Once Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have attained these ten kinds of most pure and majestic bodies, they are able to cause sentient beings to attain ten kinds of perfection. What are these ten?

First, it enables sentient beings to behold the Buddha; second, it enables sentient beings to have deep faith in the Buddha; third, it enables sentient beings to hear the Dharma; fourth, it enables sentient beings to know that there are Buddha-worlds; fifth, it enables sentient beings to see the Buddha’s spiritual transformations; sixth, it enables sentient beings to recollect the karma they have accumulated; seventh, it enables sentient beings to perfect their concentrated mind; eighth, it enables sentient beings to enter the purity of the Buddha; ninth, it enables sentient beings to resolve upon bodhicitta; and tenth, it enables sentient beings to perfect the wisdom of the Buddha.
O Son of the Buddha!
After causing sentient beings to attain ten kinds of perfection, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further performs ten kinds of Buddha-activities for them. What are these ten?
That is to say:
performing the work of a Buddha through sound in order to bring sentient beings to maturity;
performing the work of a Buddha through physical form in order to discipline sentient beings.
They perform the work of a Buddha by means of mindfulness, for the sake of purifying sentient beings;
they perform the work of a Buddha by means of shaking the worlds, for the sake of causing sentient beings to leave the evil realms;
they perform the work of a Buddha by means of awakening through skillful means, for the sake of causing sentient beings not to lose their mindfulness.
They perform buddha-work by manifesting signs within dreams, so as to cause sentient beings to maintain constant right mindfulness;
they perform buddha-work by emitting great radiance, so as to universally gather in all sentient beings;
they perform buddha-work by practicing the bodhisattva path, so as to cause sentient beings to abide in supreme vows.
They perform the Buddha-work by attaining perfect enlightenment, in order to cause sentient beings to know that all phenomena are illusory;
they perform the Buddha-work by turning the sublime wheel of Dharma, in order to preach the Dharma for the masses without missing the proper time;
they perform the Buddha-work by manifesting a dwelling life-span, in order to discipline and subdue all sentient beings.
They manifest parinirvāṇa as a buddha-activity because they know that sentient beings might otherwise become weary and discouraged.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the seventh skillful wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, the great samādhi of thoroughly knowing the buddha-adornments of all worlds.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty-one;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty-two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
Chapter Twenty-seven, Part Three: The Thirty Samādhis.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s samādhi of the diverse bodies of all sentient beings?"
O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this samādhi, they attain ten kinds of non-attachment. What are these ten?
That is to say:

non-attachment to all lands, non-attachment to all directions, non-attachment to all eons, non-attachment to all assemblies, non-attachment to all phenomena, non-attachment to all bodhisattvas, non-attachment to all bodhisattva vows, non-attachment to all samādhis, non-attachment to all buddhas, and non-attachment to all stages.
These are the ten.
“O Son of the Buddha!
How does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva enter this samādhi?”
How does it arise?
O Son of the Buddha!
Regarding this samādhi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva enters with the internal body and arises with the external body.
Entering through the external body, arising within the internal body;
entering through the same body, arising in a different body;
entering through a different body, arising in the same body.
Entering with the body of a human, one emerges with the body of a yakṣa;
entering with the body of a yakṣa, one emerges with the body of a nāga;
entering with the body of a nāga, one emerges with the body of an asura.
Entering with the body of an asura, one arises in the body of a deva;
entering with the body of a deva, one arises in the body of a Brahmā king;
entering with the body of a Brahmā king, one arises in the body of the desire realm.
Entering from among the devas, they arise in hell;
entering from hell, they arise among humans;
entering from among humans, they arise in other realms of existence.
A thousand bodies enter and one body emerges;
one body enters and a thousand bodies emerge;
ten billion bodies enter and one body emerges.
Entering with a single body, they emerge with ten billion bodies;
entering among the multitudes of sentient beings in Jambudvīpa, they emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in Aparagoyānī;
entering among the multitudes of sentient beings in Aparagoyānī, they emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in Uttarakuru.
They enter among the multitudes of beings in Uttarakuru and emerge among the multitudes of beings in Pūrvavideha;
they enter among the multitudes of beings in Pūrvavideha and emerge among the multitudes of beings in the three continents;
they enter among the multitudes of beings in the three continents and emerge among the multitudes of beings in the four continents.
They enter among the multitudes of sentient beings of the four continents and emerge from among the multitudes of sentient beings differentiated by all oceans;
they enter among the multitudes of sentient beings differentiated by all oceans and emerge from among the multitudes of all ocean deities;
they enter among the multitudes of all ocean deities and emerge from within the great waters of all oceans.
They enter into the water element of all oceans and emerge from the earth element of all oceans;
they enter into the earth element of all oceans and emerge from the fire element of all oceans;
they enter into the fire element of all oceans and emerge from the wind element of all oceans.
They enter into all winds and great elements, and arise from within all four great elements;
they enter into all four great elements, and arise from within the dharma of non-arising;
they enter into the dharma of non-arising, and arise from within Mount Sumeru.
Entering from within Mount Sumeru, they emerge from within mountains of the seven treasures;
entering from within mountains of the seven treasures, they emerge from within all the various crops, forests, and Black Mountains upon the earth;
entering from within all the various crops, forests, and Black Mountains upon the earth, they emerge from within the adornments of all exquisite fragrant flowers and jewels.
They enter into all adornments of exquisite fragrances, flowers, and jewels; they arise from among all sentient beings taking birth below and above throughout all four continents.
They enter into all sentient beings taking birth below and above throughout all four continents; they arise from among the multitudes of sentient beings in a small thousand-world system.
They enter into the multitudes of sentient beings in a small thousand-world system; they arise from among the multitudes of sentient beings in a medium thousand-world system.
They enter among the multitudes of sentient beings in a medium chiliocosm and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in a great trichiliocosm;
they enter among the multitudes of sentient beings in a great trichiliocosm and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of great trichiliocosms;
they enter among the multitudes of sentient beings in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of great trichiliocosms and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in incalculable worlds.
They enter into the assemblies of sentient beings in countless worlds and emerge from the assemblies of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds;
they enter into the assemblies of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds and emerge from the assemblies of sentient beings in boundless Buddha-fields;
they enter into the assemblies of sentient beings in boundless Buddha-fields and emerge from the assemblies of sentient beings in incomparable Buddha-fields.
They enter among the multitudes of sentient beings in peerless Buddha-fields and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in incalculable worlds;
they enter among the multitudes of sentient beings in incalculable worlds and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in inexpressible worlds;
they enter among the multitudes of sentient beings in inexpressible worlds and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in inconceivable worlds.
They enter into the assemblies of sentient beings in inconceivable worlds and emerge from the assemblies of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds;
they enter into the assemblies of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds and emerge from the assemblies of sentient beings in ineffable worlds;
they enter into the assemblies of sentient beings in ineffable worlds and emerge from the assemblies of sentient beings in ineffably ineffable worlds.
They enter into the multitudes of sentient beings in unspeakably unspeakable worlds and emerge from the multitudes of defiled sentient beings;
they enter into the multitudes of defiled sentient beings and emerge from the multitudes of pure sentient beings;
they enter into the multitudes of pure sentient beings and emerge from the multitudes of defiled sentient beings.
Entering through the eye-base, one arises in the ear-base;
entering through the ear-base, one arises in the eye-base;
entering through the nose-base, one arises in the tongue-base.
The tongue-base enters and the nose-base arises;
the body-base enters and the mind-base arises;
the mind-base enters and the body-base arises.
Entering from one’s own place and arising in another’s place;
entering from another’s place and arising in one’s own place;
entering into a single atom and arising within the atoms of countless worlds.
Entering into as many worlds as there are atoms, one arises from within a single atom;
entering as a śrāvaka, one arises as a pratyekabuddha;
entering as a pratyekabuddha, one arises as a śrāvaka.
Entering one's own body, the Buddha-body arises;
entering the Buddha-body, one's own body arises;
entering a single thought-moment, billions of eons arise.
Entering for billions of kalpas, awakening in a single thought;
entering with a single thought, awakening at a different time;
entering at a different time, awakening with a single thought.
Entering at the prior limit, arising at the posterior limit;
entering at the posterior limit, arising at the prior limit;
entering at the prior limit, arising at the middle limit.
Entry into the middle limit arises from the prior limit;
entry into the three periods of time arises in a single instant;
entry into a single instant arises throughout the three periods of time.
When true suchness enters, verbal expression arises;
when verbal expression enters, true suchness arises.
"O Son of the Buddha!
For example, suppose there is a person possessed by a spirit; their body trembles and they cannot find peace, yet the spirit does not manifest its own form to cause the other's body to do so.

It is the same for a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwelling in this samādhi: while his own body enters meditative absorption, another’s body arises from it; while another’s body enters meditative absorption, his own body arises from it.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like a corpse that, through the power of a mantra, is able to rise and move, accomplishing whatever task is undertaken; although the corpse and the mantra are distinct from one another, they can harmonize to accomplish that task.

So too it is for a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwelling in this samādhi: entering meditative absorption in one realm, he arises in another; entering meditative absorption in another realm, he arises in the same realm.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is, for example, as when a bhikṣu attains mastery over the mind, and can either manifest many bodies from one body, or manifest one body from many bodies; it is not that one body perishes to give rise to many bodies, nor that many bodies perish to give rise to one body.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, it is likewise: he may enter meditative absorption with one body and emerge with many bodies, or enter meditative absorption with many bodies and emerge with one body.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like the great earth, which has but a single taste, yet the crops it produces have various distinct tastes; though the earth itself makes no distinction, its flavors differ.

So too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwelling in this samādhi: there is no conceptual differentiation, yet there is entering into concentration in one way and arising from it in many ways, or entering into concentration in many ways and arising from it in one way.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this samādhi, they receive praise through ten kinds of praiseworthy qualities. What are these ten?
That is to say:
because he has entered into suchness, he is called the Tathāgata;
because he has awakened to all dharmas, he is called the Buddha.
Because he is praised by all the world, he is called a Dharma Teacher;
because he knows all dharmas, he is called the All-Knowing One;
because he is the refuge for all the world, he is called the Place of Reliance.
Because he has thoroughly mastered the skillful means of all dharmas, he is called a Guide;
because he leads all sentient beings into the path of sarvajñā (omniscience), he is called a Great Guide;
and because he serves as a lamp for all the world, he is called Radiance.

With his resolve perfected and his purpose accomplished, having fulfilled all that was to be done, he abides in unimpeded wisdom; because he discerns and understands all phenomena, he is called "Mastery of the Ten Powers.
Because he has thoroughly penetrated all wheels of Dharma, he is called "The All-Seeing One."
These are the ten.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they further attain ten kinds of radiant illumination.
What are these ten? They are:
attaining the light of all Buddhas, because of being equal to them;
They attain the light of all worlds, because they are universally able to adorn and purify them;
they attain the light of all sentient beings, because they go everywhere to tame and transform them;
they attain the light of immeasurable fearlessness, because they expound the Dharma with the realm of reality as their arena.
They attain the light of non-differentiation, because they know that all phenomena lack any manifold nature;
they attain the light of skillful means, because they enter into the limit of detachment from all phenomena;
they attain the light of reality, because their minds are equanimous regarding the limit of detachment from all phenomena.
They attain the light of spiritual transformations that pervades all worlds, for they are constantly sustained by the empowerment of the Buddhas;
they attain the light of skillful reflection, for they have reached the shore of mastery over all Buddhas;
they attain the light of the suchness of all phenomena, for they skillfully expound everything from within a single pore.
These are the ten.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they further attain ten kinds of non-action.

What are these ten? They are: non-action regarding physical activity; non-action regarding verbal activity; non-action regarding mental activity; non-action regarding supernormal powers; non-action regarding the realization that phenomena lack intrinsic nature; non-action regarding the knowledge that karma is indestructible; non-action regarding non-discriminative wisdom; non-action regarding the wisdom of non-arising; non-action regarding the knowledge that phenomena are without cessation; and non-action regarding following the letter without violating the meaning.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas abide in this samādhi, there are immeasurable realms with various distinctions."
That is to say:
entering as one and arising as many; entering as many and arising as one;
entering identically and arising differently; entering differently and arising identically.
The subtle enters and the coarse arises; the coarse enters and the subtle arises;
the large enters and the small arises; the small enters and the large arises;
the forward enters and the reverse arises; the reverse enters and the forward arises.
Entering from the bodiless, one arises with a body; entering from that which has a body, one arises bodiless.
Entering from the signless, one arises with signs; entering from that which has signs, one arises signless.
One enters within arising, and arises within entering.
All such things are the sovereign spheres of this samādhi.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like a master illusionist who, having perfected his incantations, can manifest all manner of diverse forms and appearances.

Mantras are distinct from illusions, yet they can produce illusions; mantras are merely sounds, yet they can magically manifest various forms known by the visual consciousness, various sounds known by the auditory consciousness, various fragrances known by the olfactory consciousness, various tastes known by the gustatory consciousness, various tangibles known by the tactile consciousness, and various objects known by the mental consciousness.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwelling in this samādhi is likewise: he enters meditative absorption within the same and emerges within the different; he enters meditative absorption within the different and emerges within the same.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like when the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven were engaged in battle with the asuras; the gods achieved victory and the asuras were routed and fled.

The body of the asura king was seven hundred yojanas tall, and he was surrounded by countless tens of millions of the fourfold army. By the power of his illusory arts, he led all his troops simultaneously into the hollow of a lotus fiber.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having already perfectly accomplished the stage of illusory wisdom (*māyājñāna-bhūmi*), illusory wisdom is itself the Bodhisattva, and the Bodhisattva is himself illusory wisdom. Therefore, he is able to enter meditative absorption within non-differentiated phenomena and emerge from it within differentiated phenomena; or enter meditative absorption within differentiated phenomena and emerge from it within non-differentiated phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is just as when a farmer sows seeds in a field: the seed remains below while the fruit emerges above.

So too it is for a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwelling in this samādhi: they enter meditative absorption within one [moment] and arise within many, or enter meditative absorption within many and arise within one.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like when the red and white elements of a man and woman unite, and a sentient being takes birth therein; at that time, it is called the stage of the *kalala*.
From this point on, it develops in succession while dwelling within the mother’s womb for a full ten months.
By the power of wholesome karma, all limbs and members are fully formed, the sense faculties are unimpaired, and the mind is clear and lucid;

although the *kalala* stage and those six sense faculties differ in their physical forms, through the power of karma they are able to be successively perfected, whereby one experiences various karmic fruits, both similar and dissimilar.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: from the stage of the *kalala* of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), they gradually increase through the power of faith, understanding, and aspiration;

their mind becomes vast, spontaneously and freely, entering meditative absorption within non-existence and arising within existence, or entering meditative absorption within existence and arising within non-existence.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like a dragon palace that stands supported by the earth and not by empty space; the dragon dwells within the palace and is not in the air, yet it can raise clouds that fill the sky.
When someone looks up and sees these palaces, you should know they are all merely cities of the gandharvas and are not actual dragon palaces.
O Son of the Buddha!
Although dragons dwell below, their clouds spread above.
It is the same for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abiding in this samādhi: from the signless they enter the signful and arise, and from the signful they enter the signless and arise.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is, for example, like the palace where the Great Brahma King Sublime Light dwells, named:
Treasury of Supreme Purity of All Worlds;

Within this great palace, one universally beholds all the celestial palaces, dragon palaces, yakṣa palaces, gandharva palaces, asura palaces, garuḍa palaces, kiṃnara palaces, and mahoraga palaces throughout the four continents of the trichiliocosm;

as well as human dwellings, the three evil realms, Mount Sumeru, and various other mountains, great oceans, rivers, streams, marshes, springs, cities, villages, forests, and multitudes of jewels—all such diverse adornments extending to the very limits of the Great Cakravāḍa mountains, even down to the finest motes of dust suspended in the air—none fail to appear within the Brahma palace, just as one sees the reflection of one’s face in a clear mirror.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this Great Samādhi of the Differentiated Bodies of All Sentient Beings, they know various lands, see various Buddhas, deliver various assemblies, realize various dharmas, accomplish various practices, fulfill various understandings, enter various samādhis, manifest various supernormal powers, attain various wisdoms, and dwell in various moments of time.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reaches the further shore of ten kinds of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). What are these ten?
That is to say:
reaching the shore of the spiritual powers that pervade all Buddhas throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm;

reaching the shore of the ultimate, non-differentiated, and sovereign spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas; and reaching the ability to initiate the vast practices and vows of Bodhisattvas and enter [into them].
They have reached the perfection of spiritual powers regarding the Buddha-work of the Tathāgata’s gate;
they have reached the perfection of spiritual powers that can shake all worlds and all realms, making them entirely pure;

they have reached the perfection of spiritual powers that can freely know the inconceivable karma and its fruits of all sentient beings, all of which are like illusions and transformations; they have reached the perfection of spiritual powers that can freely know all...
Having reached the perfection of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) through the distinctions of entering and emerging from the coarse and subtle states of samādhi,
they reach the perfection of supernormal powers by generating great vows within the realm of the Tathāgatas, which enables them to manifest emanations of Buddhas,
turn the wheel of Dharma, and subdue sentient beings, causing them to produce the seed of Buddhahood, enter the Buddha-vehicle, and swiftly attain accomplishment.
Having reached the further shore of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), they arrive at the ability to understand all ineffable secret phrases and turn the wheel of Dharma,
causing hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of ineffably ineffable Dharma-gates to attain the further shore of pure supernormal powers;
having reached this state, they are able, without depending on days, nights, months, years, or eons, to accomplish [all things] in a single thought-moment.
Manifesting the perfection of supernatural powers throughout the three periods of time—
this is the tenth.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s eighth skillful wisdom of the great samādhi of the diverse bodies of all sentient beings.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s samādhi of mastery over the dharma-realm?
O Son of the Buddha!
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva enters into samādhi within their own sense-base of the eye, up to and including the sense-base of the mind; this is named:
Mastery over the Dharma-realm:

Within each and every pore of his own body, the Bodhisattva enters this samādhi and naturally comes to know all worlds, knows the dharmas of all worlds, knows all world-systems, knows billions of nayutas of world-systems, knows incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) world-systems, and knows world-systems as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

he sees Buddhas appearing in all these worlds, with assemblies of Bodhisattvas filling them entirely, their radiance pure, their nature purely wholesome and unadulterated, and magnificently adorned with various kinds of precious jewels.

In that regard, the Bodhisattva practices the Bodhisattva conduct without ever resting for one eon, a hundred eons, a thousand eons, ten million eons, a hundred thousand ten-million nayuta eons, incalculable eons, immeasurable eons, boundless eons, incomparable eons, uncountable eons, inexpressible eons, unthinkable eons, unfathomable eons, unspeakable eons, or unspeakably-unspeakable eons equal to the number of atoms in unspeakably-unspeakable Buddha-fields.

Furthermore, throughout such immeasurable eons, they abide in this samādhi, entering it and emerging from it; they bring worlds to fulfillment and discipline sentient beings; they thoroughly pervade the dharma-realm and universally know the three periods of time; they expound all dharmas and manifest great supernormal powers, employing various skillful means without attachment or obstruction.

Because they have attained mastery over the dharma-realm, they skillfully distinguish the eye, skillfully distinguish the ear, skillfully distinguish the nose, skillfully distinguish the tongue, skillfully distinguish the body, and skillfully distinguish the mind; thus, regarding these various distinctions and differences, they skillfully distinguish them all to their ultimate limit.
Having thus skillfully known and seen, the bodhisattva is able to give rise to ten trillion dhāraṇī-dharma radiances,
accomplish ten trillion pure practices, obtain ten trillion faculties,
perfect ten trillion supernormal powers, enter ten trillion samādhis, and achieve ten trillion...
Through spiritual power, they nurture ten trillion powers, perfect ten trillion profound intentions,
exercise ten trillion supports of strength, manifest ten trillion divine transformations,
fulfill ten trillion bodhisattva non-obstructions, complete ten trillion bodhisattva aids to the path, and accumulate ten trillion...
The Bodhisattva-piṭaka illuminates ten trillion bodhisattva skillful means,
expounds ten trillion meanings, accomplishes ten trillion vows, gives rise to ten trillion dedications,
purifies ten trillion bodhisattva stages, clarifies ten trillion dharma-gates, and reveals ten trillion...
He expounds billions of teachings and cultivates the purity of ten thousand billion bodhisattvas.
"O Son of the Buddha!

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva further possesses innumerable merits, immeasurable merits, boundless merits, incomparable merits, incalculable merits, ineffable merits, inconceivable merits, unfathomable merits, unspeakable merits, and inexhaustible merits."
O Son of the Buddha!

Regarding these merits, this bodhisattva has already prepared them all, accumulated them all, adorned them all, purified them all, made them all translucent, embraced them all, brought them all forth, praised them all, rendered them all firm, and accomplished them all.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they are sustained by as many Buddhas as there are atoms in ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* Buddha-fields in the eastern direction, each with a distinct name; furthermore, for each individual name, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* Buddha-fields, each being distinct.
As it is in the east, so it is in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.”
All those Buddhas appeared before him, manifesting for him the pure lands of all Buddhas;
they spoke of the immeasurable bodies of all Buddhas; they spoke of the inconceivable eyes of all Buddhas; they spoke of the immeasurable ears of all Buddhas;
they spoke of the pure noses of all Buddhas; they spoke of the pure tongues of all Buddhas; they spoke of all Buddhas...
For those with minds that do not abide, he expounds the unsurpassed supernormal powers of the Tathāgata, causes them to cultivate the unsurpassed enlightenment of the Tathāgata,
enables them to attain the pure voice of the Tathāgata, reveals the non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma of the Tathāgata,
displays the boundless assemblies of the Tathāgata, leads them into the boundless secrets of the Tathāgata, and praises [them].
They cause all the Tathāgata’s roots of goodness to enter the Tathāgata’s impartial Dharma;
they proclaim the Tathāgata’s lineage throughout the three periods of time; they manifest the Tathāgata’s immeasurable physical forms; they expound the Tathāgata’s method of protective mindfulness;
they fully articulate the Tathāgata’s subtle and wondrous Dharma-sounds; and they clearly distinguish all the Buddha-worlds.
They proclaim the samādhis of all Buddhas, manifest the successive assemblies of all Buddhas, and protect and uphold the inconceivable dharmas of all Buddhas.
They teach that all phenomena are like illusions and transformations, clarifying that the nature of all phenomena is without movement or change.
They reveal and expound all unsurpassed wheels of Dharma and praise the Tathāgata’s [immeasurable]...
Measuring their merit, they cause them to enter all clouds of samādhis, and cause them to know that their minds are like illusions and transformations—
boundless and inexhaustible.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this Samādhi of Sovereignty over the Dharma Realm, there are as many Tathāgatas in each of the ten directions as there are atoms in ten thousand asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields. Within each of their names, there are simultaneously as many Buddhas as there are atoms in ten thousand asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields who protect and sustain this bodhisattva, causing this bodhisattva to attain an infinite body;
causing this bodhisattva to attain an unimpeded mind;
and causing this bodhisattva to attain non-forgetfulness regarding all dharmas.
May this bodhisattva attain definitive wisdom regarding all phenomena;
may this bodhisattva become even more acute and intelligent, such that they are able to receive and comprehend all phenomena;
may this bodhisattva be able to clearly understand all phenomena.
May this bodhisattva’s faculties be sharp and keen, attaining complete mastery in the dharmas of spiritual powers;
may this bodhisattva’s sphere of activity be unimpeded, constantly traversing the dharma-realm without rest;
and may this bodhisattva attain unobstructed wisdom, which is ultimately pure.
By means of their supernormal powers, these bodhisattvas manifest the attainment of buddhahood in all worlds.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they attain ten kinds of oceans."
What are these ten? They are:
attaining the oceans of all Buddhas, because one beholds them all;
They attain the ocean of sentient beings, because they thoroughly subdue them all;
they attain the ocean of all dharmas, because they are able to fully comprehend them all through wisdom;
they attain the ocean of all lands, because they travel to them all by means of non-substantial and effortless spiritual powers.
They attain an ocean of merit, because all their practices are fully perfected;
they attain an ocean of supernormal powers, because they can extensively manifest them to bring about awakening;
they attain an ocean of the faculties, because they thoroughly know all their various differences.
They attain the ocean of all minds, because they know the infinite and variously differentiated minds of all sentient beings;
they attain the ocean of all practices, because they are able to fulfill them all through the power of their vows;
they attain the ocean of all vows, because they cause them all to be accomplished and forever purified.
O Son of the Buddha!
Once the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has attained these ten kinds of oceans, they further attain ten kinds of excellence. What are these ten?

First, they are the foremost among all sentient beings; second, they are the most distinguished among all devas; third, they possess the highest sovereignty among all Brahma kings; fourth, they are unstained by and unattached to any worldly realm; fifth, none in any world can eclipse or obscure them; sixth, no māras can confuse or disturb them; seventh, they enter universally into all realms of existence without obstruction; eighth, though taking birth in various places, they know such births to be insubstantial; ninth, they attain mastery over all Buddha-dharmas; and tenth, they are able to manifest all supernatural powers (*abhijñā*).
O Son of the Buddha!
Having attained these ten kinds of excellence, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further attains ten kinds of power, whereby they cultivate all practices within the realm of sentient beings.
What are the ten? First is the power of valor, because it subdues the world;
second is the power of diligence, because it never regresses; third is the power of non-attachment, because it is free from all defilements.
The fourth is the power of tranquility, because there is no contention regarding any phenomena;
the fifth is the power of conformity and non-conformity, because the mind has mastery over all phenomena;
the sixth is the power of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), because one attains mastery over all meanings.
The seventh is the power of non-obstruction, because wisdom is vast;
the eighth is the power of fearlessness, because one is able to expound all dharmas;
the ninth is the power of eloquence, because one is able to maintain all dharmas.
The tenth is called the power of manifestation, because wisdom is boundless.
O Son of the Buddha!
These ten powers are the vast power, the most supreme power, and the power that cannot be overcome.
The power of self-assessment, the power of skillful accumulation, the power of immovability, the power of firmness, the power of wisdom,
the power of accomplishment, the power of supreme concentration, the power of purity, the power of extreme purity,
the power of the Dharma-body, the power of the light of the Dharma, the power of the lamp of the Dharma, the power of the Dharma-gates, the power of indestructibility, and the power of extreme valor.
The power of vigor; the power of a great man; the power of the cultivation of a virtuous man; the power of attaining perfect enlightenment; the power of roots of goodness accumulated in the past;
the power of abiding in immeasurable roots of goodness; the power of abiding in the powers of a Tathāgata;
the power of mental reflection; the power of increasing the joy of Bodhisattvas; and the power that gives birth to the purity of Bodhisattvas.
The power of faith; the power of a bodhisattva’s valor; the power born of the bodhicitta; the power of a bodhisattva’s pure and profound resolve;
the power of a bodhisattva’s superior and profound resolve; the power of the cultivation of a bodhisattva’s roots of goodness;
the power of the ultimate dharmas; the power of the unobstructed body; and the entry into the dharma of skillful means.
The power of the gateway; the power of the pure and sublime Dharma; the power of abiding in great majesty such that all worlds cannot shake it;
and the power that no sentient being can eclipse.
O Son of the Buddha!

Regarding these immeasurable dharmas of merit, this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able to produce them, accomplish them, fulfill them, illuminate them, perfect them, universally perfect them, expand them, stabilize them, increase them, purify them, and universally purify them.

No one is able to describe the limits of this bodhisattva’s merit, the limits of his wisdom, the limits of his practice, the limits of his dharma-gates, the limits of his mastery, the limits of his asceticism, the limits of his accomplishment, the limits of his purity, the limits of his renunciation, or the limits of his sovereignty over the Dharma.

The gateways of all dharmas—those obtained, those accomplished, those entered into, those manifested before one, all their spheres of activity, all their observations, all their realizations, all their purifications, all their comprehensions, and all their establishments—cannot be fully described even in unspeakable eons.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they are able to fully comprehend all samādhis—those that are innumerable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, uncountable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and even unspeakably unspeakable.”

In each and every samādhi, all its realms are immeasurable and vast; whether entering, arising from, or abiding within those realms, he clearly perceives without exception all their characteristics, all their manifestations, all their spheres of activity, all their continuities, all their intrinsic natures, all their cessations, and all their deliverances.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the four rivers flowing from the palace of the great Nāga King Anavatapta; they are free from turbidity, unmixed with impurities, devoid of filth, and their radiant color is as pure as space.

On each of the four sides of that pond there is an opening; from each opening flows out a river: from the mouth of the elephant issues the Gaṅgā River, from the mouth of the lion issues the Sītā River, from the mouth of the ox issues the Sindhu River, and from the mouth of the horse issues the Vakṣu River.

When those four great rivers flow forth, silver sand flows from the mouth of the Gaṅgā, diamond sand flows from the mouth of the Sītā, golden sand flows from the mouth of the Sindhu, and lapis lazuli sand flows from the mouth of the Vakṣu;

the mouth of the Gaṅgā is the color of white silver, the mouth of the Sītā is the color of diamond, the mouth of the Sindhu is the color of yellow gold, and the mouth of the Vakṣu is the color of lapis lazuli, with each river-mouth being one yojana in width.

Once these four great rivers have flowed out, each circles the great lake seven times and then divides into four branches according to its respective direction, surging and rushing forward to enter the great ocean.

As the river winds and meanders, between each turn there are *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* lotuses formed of celestial jewels. Their wondrous fragrances waft forth and their exquisite colors are pure;
with various petals and various calyxes and filaments—all made of diverse jewels—they naturally reflect and penetrate one another, all emitting radiance that illuminates and manifests each other.

The circumference of that Lake Anavatapta is fifty yojanas; its bottom is strewn with exquisite sand of various jewels and adorned with diverse mani-gems. Its shores are embellished with immeasurable wonderful treasures, and the sublime fragrance of sandalwood wafts throughout it. It is completely filled with *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* lotuses, as well as other precious flowers; when stirred by a gentle breeze, their fragrance permeates afar, and groves of flowers and jewel-trees surround it on all sides.
When the sun rises, it universally illuminates all things within and without the ponds and rivers; their reflections join and their splendors connect to form a net of light.

Whether these myriad objects are distant or near, high or low, broad or narrow, coarse or fine—even down to the smallest single grain of sand or mote of dust—all are made of wondrous jewels. Their radiance is so transparent and penetrating that the reflection of the solar disc appears within every one of them, and they likewise reflect one another’s images in succession.
These myriad reflections neither increase nor decrease, neither merge nor disperse; they are all clearly perceived exactly as their original substances.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as the great lake Anavatapta flows from its four mouths as four rivers that enter the great ocean;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who likewise flows from the four analytical eloquences (*pratisaṃvid*) as all manner of practices, ultimately entering the ocean of omniscience.
Just as the great river Gaṅgā flows from the mouth of a silver-colored elephant, carrying silver sands;

so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who, through the eloquence of meaning, expounds all the gateways of meaning taught by all Tathāgatas, giving rise to all pure and white dharmas, and ultimately entering the ocean of unimpeded wisdom.
Just as the great river Sītā flows from the lion’s mouth of vajra-color, carrying with it sands of vajra;

so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: by means of the eloquence of the Dharma, they preach the vajra-words of the Buddha for the sake of all sentient beings, drawing forth vajra-wisdom and ultimately entering the ocean of unimpeded wisdom.
Just as the great river Sindhu flows from the mouth of a golden ox, carrying sands of gold;

so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: through his eloquence and refined speech, he expounds the skillful means of dependent origination that accord with the world, awakening sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice, taming and maturing them, until they ultimately enter the ocean of the skillful means of dependent origination.
Just as the great river Vārakṣu flows from the horse-mouth of lapis lazuli-colored mountains, raining down sands of lapis lazuli;

so too is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who, with inexhaustible eloquence, rains down hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of ineffable teachings, causing all who hear them to be thoroughly moistened and ultimately enter the ocean of the Buddhas' Dharma.

Just as the four great rivers, flowing in accordance with the Anavatapta Lake, encircle it and enter the ocean from the four directions, so too is it with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: having accomplished bodily action that accords [with wisdom], verbal action that accords [with wisdom], and mental action that accords [with wisdom]; and having accomplished bodily action preceded by wisdom, verbal action preceded by wisdom, and mental action preceded by wisdom, they flow forth in the four directions and ultimately enter the ocean of all-knowledge.
O Son of the Buddha!
What is called the "four directions" of a bodhisattva?
O Son of the Buddha!
That is to say:

beholding all Buddhas and thereby attaining awakening; hearing all dharmas and receiving and upholding them without forgetting; perfecting all practices of the pāramitās; and teaching the Dharma with great compassion to satisfy sentient beings.
Just as four great rivers surround a large lake, and within its midst blue lotuses (*utpala*), red lotuses (*padma*), yellow lotuses (*kumuda*), and white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*) are found everywhere;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva: within the heart of enlightenment, they do not abandon sentient beings, but through teaching the Dharma and taming them, cause them all to fulfill immeasurable samādhis and perceive the pure adornments of Buddha-lands.
Just as the Great Lake Anavatapta is surrounded by jewel trees,
so too is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva likewise surrounded by the adornments of manifested Buddha-lands, causing all sentient beings to incline toward Bodhi.
Just as the Great Lake Anavatapta is fifty yojanas in length and breadth, pure and free from turbidity;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva: the bodhicitta is immeasurable in extent, filled with roots of goodness, and pure without turbidity.
Just as the Great Lake Anavatapta has its shores adorned with immeasurable jewels and is filled everywhere with the scent of sandalwood scattered within it, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:

with hundreds of thousands of billions of the ten kinds of jewel-like wisdom, they adorn the shores of the great vow of the bodhicitta, universally scattering all manner of excellent and wondrous fragrances of virtue.
Just as the Great Lake Anavatapta has its bottom strewn with golden sand and is adorned with various interspersed mani jewels, so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:

with subtle and wondrous wisdom they observe everywhere, adorned by the various dharma-jewels of inconceivable Bodhisattva liberation; they attain the unimpeded light of all dharmas, abide in that which all Buddhas abide in, and enter into all profound skillful means.

Just as the Nāga King Anavatapta is forever free from all the heat and afflictions inherent among nāgas, so too is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva forever free from all worldly sorrow and affliction; though manifesting birth, he remains without defilement or attachment.
Just as the four great rivers moisten all the lands of Jambudvīpa and, having moistened them, enter the great ocean;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who, by means of the river of the four knowledges, moistens gods, humans, śramaṇas, and brahmins, causing them all to enter the great ocean of the wisdom of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, adorned with the ten powers.
What are these four?
First is the river of the wisdom of vows, which constantly and without rest protects and subdues all sentient beings;

second is the river of the wisdom of the perfections (*pāramitā*), which cultivates the practices of enlightenment to benefit sentient beings, continuing uninterruptedly through the past, future, and present, until finally entering the ocean of the wisdom of all Buddhas.
Third is the river of wisdom of the Bodhisattva’s samādhis, adorned with innumerable samādhis; therein one beholds all Buddhas and enters the ocean of all Buddhas.

Fourth is the river of wisdom of great compassion, which through the sovereignty of great kindness universally rescues sentient beings; it employs skillful means to gather them in without ceasing, practicing the gateways of secret merit until finally entering the great ocean of the ten powers.
Just as the four great rivers, once they have flowed forth from Lake Anavatapta, never reach exhaustion and enter the great ocean;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who, through the power of great vows, cultivates the bodhisattva practices and possesses inexhaustible sovereign knowledge and vision, ultimately entering the ocean of all-knowledge.
Just as the four great rivers enter the great ocean and nothing can obstruct them from doing so, even so it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:

constantly and diligently cultivating the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, they accomplish all the light of wisdom, abide in all the dharmas of the Buddhas' bodhi, and enter the wisdom of the Tathāgata without any obstruction.
Just as the four great rivers rush toward the ocean, flowing through it for countless kalpas without ever becoming weary or exhausted;

so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: by means of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, they cultivate the bodhisattva conduct throughout all future kalpas, entering the ocean of the Tathāgatas without ever giving rise to weariness.
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as when the sun’s rays emerge, the golden sands, silver sands, diamond sands, lapis lazuli sands, and all other various kinds of precious substances within the Anavatapta Lake all manifest the reflections of the sun;
and those golden sands and all other precious substances likewise each reflect one another’s images, mutually mirroring and penetrating one another without any obstruction.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise; dwelling in this samādhi, within each and every pore of his own body, he sees Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields. He also sees all the lands, bodhimaṇḍas, and assemblies belonging to those Buddhas, and at each Buddha’s place, he hears the Dharma, receives and upholds it, believes and understands it, and makes offerings to them. He passes through unspeakably unspeakable billions of nayutas of kalpas without perceiving the length or brevity of time, and yet the various assemblies do not feel crowded or cramped.

Why is this? Because by means of a subtle and wondrous mind, they enter the boundless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); because they enter the unequalled distinctions of karmic results; because they enter the inconceivable realm of samādhi; because they enter the inconceivable realm of contemplation; because they enter the sovereign realm of all Buddhas; because they obtain the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas; because they obtain the great supernormal powers (*ṛddhibala*) of all Buddhas; because they obtain the ten powers (*daśabala*) of all Tathāgatas, which are difficult to attain and difficult to know; because they enter the perfected realm of the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; and because they obtain the tireless supernormal power of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Although a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is able to enter and emerge from meditative concentration in a single thought-moment, they do not abandon remaining in concentration for long periods, nor do they have any attachment to it.
Although they do not dwell in dependence upon any objective sphere, they likewise do not relinquish all objects of focus.”
Although they skillfully enter the limit of the moment, they manifest the spiritual powers of a Buddha for the benefit of all sentient beings without ever feeling weary;
although they equally enter the Dharma-realm, they do not perceive its boundaries;

although they have no abiding place and no location, they constantly advance upon the path of omniscience, using the power of transformation to universally enter among immeasurable multitudes of sentient beings and fully adorn all worlds.
Although they are free from the inverted conceptualizations of the world and have transcended all stages of conceptualization, they do not abandon the various marks of phenomena;
although they are fully endowed with skillful means, they are ultimately pure;
and although they do not conceptually differentiate the bodhisattva stages, they have already entered them all with excellence.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as space, though it can contain all things, is free from the notions of existence and non-existence;
so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: though he universally enters into all worlds, he is free from the perception of a world.
Although they diligently deliver all sentient beings, they are free from the notion of sentient beings;
although they profoundly understand all phenomena, they are free from the notion of phenomena;
although they delight in beholding all Buddhas, they are free from the notion of Buddhas.
Although they skillfully enter various samādhis, they know that the self-nature of all phenomena is like suchness, remaining free from any defilement or attachment;
although they expound inexhaustible phrases of the Dharma with boundless eloquence, their minds always abide in the dharma that transcends words;
although they delight in contemplating the ineffable Dharma, they constantly manifest pure sounds and voices.
Although they abide in the limit of all dharmas that transcend verbal expression, they constantly manifest various forms and appearances;
although they teach and transform sentient beings, they know that all dharmas are ultimately empty by nature;
although they diligently cultivate great compassion to deliver sentient beings, they know that the realm of sentient beings is inexhaustible and undispersed.
Although they thoroughly realize that the dharma-realm is eternally abiding and unchanging, they constantly and tirelessly subdue sentient beings through the three wheels;

although they always dwell securely where the Tathāgatas dwell, their wisdom is pure and their minds are free from fear as they analytically expound various dharmas and turn the wheel of Dharma without ever ceasing.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the ninth skillful wisdom of the great samādhi of mastery over the dharma-realm of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
*The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Great Vaipulya*, Scroll Forty-Two.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Forty-three.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Twenty-seven, Part Four: The Forty Samādhis.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of the Unobstructed Wheel?
O Son of the Buddha!”

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva enters this samādhi, they abide in unimpeded physical action, unimpeded verbal action, and unimpeded mental action; they abide in unimpeded Buddha-lands, attain unimpeded wisdom for maturing sentient beings, and acquire unimpeded wisdom for taming sentient beings. They emit unimpeded light, manifest unimpeded nets of light, display unimpeded and vast transformations, and turn the unimpeded, pure wheel of Dharma. They attain the unimpeded sovereignty of a Bodhisattva, universally enter the powers of all Buddhas, and universally abide in the wisdom of all Buddhas. They perform what Buddhas do, purify what Buddhas purify, manifest the spiritual powers of Buddhas, and cause the Buddhas to rejoice. They practice the conduct of the Tathāgatas, abide in the path of the Tathāgatas, and constantly draw near to immeasurable Buddhas, performing the works of Buddhas and continuing the lineage of Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in this samādhi, they contemplate all-knowledge; they contemplate all-knowledge collectively, contemplate all-knowledge individually, accord with all-knowledge, manifest all-knowledge, take all-knowledge as their object, perceive all-knowledge, perceive all-knowledge collectively, and perceive all-knowledge individually. Regarding the vast vows, vast mind, vast practices, vast destinations, vast entries, vast radiance, vast manifestations, vast protective mindfulness, vast transformations, and vast path of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, they do not cease or retreat, never rest nor substitute, never grow weary nor abandon, never scatter nor become distracted, but always progress and perpetually continue.”
Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have, among all dharmas, accomplished great vows and set forth upon the Mahāyāna, entering the ocean of great skillful means of the Buddha-dharma;

by the power of their supreme vows, they have attained mastery in the wisdom that clearly illuminates all practices performed by bodhisattvas, are fully endowed with the supernatural transformations of a bodhisattva, and are well able to protect and mindfully care for all sentient beings.

They are protected and sustained by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present; they constantly give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings and accomplish the unchanging Dharma of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like a person who places a maṇi jewel within colored clothing; although that maṇi jewel takes on the color of the cloth, it does not abandon its own nature.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: having accomplished wisdom as their mental jewel, they perceive all-encompassing omniscience appearing clearly everywhere, yet they do not abandon the various practices of a bodhisattva.

Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have made great vows to benefit all sentient beings, to deliver all sentient beings, to serve all Buddhas, to adorn and purify all worlds, to comfort sentient beings, and to enter deeply into the ocean of Dharma;

for the sake of purifying the realm of sentient beings, they manifest great sovereignty, bestow gifts upon sentient beings, universally illuminate the world, and enter the gate of infinite illusory transformations, never retreating, never turning back, and never becoming weary or exhausted.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is, for example, like space, which sustains all worlds—whether they are forming or abiding—without weariness or fatigue, without weakness or decay, without scattering or destruction, without change or alteration, without distinction, and without abandoning its own nature.
Why is this? Because it is the inherent nature of space that phenomena should be thus.
It is the same for the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: having established immeasurable great vows to deliver all sentient beings, their mind never tires or grows weary.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like nirvana; throughout the past, future, and present, immeasurable sentient beings attain extinction within it, yet it never grows weary or exhausted. Why is this?
All dharmas are pure by their very nature; this is called nirvana. How, then, could there be weariness within it?

It is the same for the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: desiring to deliver all sentient beings and cause them all to transcend [suffering], he appears in the world. How, then, could he give rise to a mind of fatigue or weariness?
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as sarvajñā (omniscience) enables all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present to be born—having been born, being born, or yet to be born—into the family of the Buddhas, and even leads them to the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi, never becoming weary or fatigued.
Why is this? Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) are non-dual, and because there is no attachment to any phenomena.
It is the same for the bodhisattva mahāsattva: since his mind dwells in equanimity within all-knowledge, how could he have a mind of weariness or exhaustion?
“O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva possesses a single lotus flower, vast and expansive, reaching to the limits of the ten directions. It is adorned with unspeakable numbers of petals, unspeakable jewels, and unspeakable perfumes;
those unspeakable jewels, in turn, each manifest various kinds of precious gems, pure, exquisite, and perfectly well-established.”
Its flowers constantly emit multicolored radiance, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions without obstruction;
a net of pure gold covers it from above;
and as precious bells sway gently, they produce subtle and wondrous sounds, which proclaim and expound the Dharma of omniscience.

This great lotus is fully endowed with the pure adornments of the Tathāgata; it arises from all roots of goodness, is manifested through spiritual power, and has auspiciousness as its hallmark. It possesses ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* pure merits, is accomplished through the wondrous path of the bodhisattvas, and flows forth from the mind of omniscience. Within it, the reflections of the Buddhas of the ten directions appear; the world gazes upon it as if it were a stūpa, and among sentient beings, there are none who do not pay it homage. It is born from the true Dharma that thoroughly understands illusion, and no analogy in any world can describe it.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sat cross-legged upon this flower, his body being proportionate in size to the flower.

Empowered by the spiritual authority (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Buddhas, each and every pore of the Bodhisattva’s body emitted light rays numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of Buddha-fields. From each individual light ray appeared mani-jewels numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of Buddha-fields; these jewels were all named:

The Universal Radiance Treasury is adorned with various forms and colors, accomplished through immeasurable merits; it is covered above by nets of myriad jewels and flowers, strewn with hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of supreme, wondrous fragrances, and further embellished with infinite colors and diverse ornaments, while inconceivable canopies of jewel-adornments manifest to cover its summit.
Each and every mani jewel manifested pavilions as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
each and every pavilion manifested lion thrones of lotus-treasury as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
and each and every lion throne manifested rays of light as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of buddha-fields.
Each ray of light manifests as many color-forms as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields;
each color-form manifests as many circles of light as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields;
and each circle of light manifests as many Vairocana-mani-jewel flowers as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields.
Upon each flower appeared terraces as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
upon each terrace appeared Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
and each Buddha manifested spiritual transformations as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields.
Each and every supernatural transformation purifies an assembly of sentient beings as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
within each such assembly of sentient beings, there appear the sovereign powers of as many Buddhas as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields;
and from each such sovereign power, there rains down as many teachings of the Buddha as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields.
Each and every Buddha-dharma contains as many sūtras as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields;
each and every sūtra explains as many Dharma-gates as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields;

and within each and every Dharma-gate, there are as many wheels of Dharma entered by vajra-wisdom as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, each expounded with distinct terminology and phrasing.
Each and every wheel of Dharma matures as many realms of sentient beings as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields;

within each and every realm of sentient beings, there are as many sentient beings as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields, who are brought to discipline within the Buddha-dharma.
“O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this samādhi, they manifest such realms of supernatural power and immeasurable transformations; yet, knowing them all to be like illusions, they remain unstained by attachment and dwell securely in the boundless, ineffable Dharma.”

The self-nature purity, the true reality of the dharma-realm, and the tathāgata-lineage, within the unobstructed limit, neither go nor come; they are neither prior nor subsequent, profoundly deep and bottomless, attained through direct perception, entered by means of wisdom from within, and not realized through another.
With a mind that is neither deluded nor discursive, it is praised by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present; it flows forth from the power of all Buddhas and enters the realm of all Buddhas.

With a nature that accords with reality, they realize it through the pure eye and perceive it universally with the wisdom eye; having accomplished the Buddha-eye, they serve as bright lamps for the world, traversing the sphere of experience known by the knowledge-eye and extensively revealing subtle and wondrous Dharma gates.

Having perfected the bodhicitta, they proceed as superior beings; they encounter no obstacles amidst all sensory realms, enter the lineage of wisdom to give rise to all forms of knowledge, and—transcending the laws of worldly birth—manifest births through supernatural transformations and skillful means to discipline and subdue others.

All of these were nothing but skillful means; their merit, understanding, and aspirations were entirely pure, most subtle and perfectly complete. Their wisdom was as vast as space, and they were well able to observe the realm of the noble ones. Their power of faith, conduct, and vows was firm and unshakable; their merit was inexhaustible and praised by the world.

Within the treasury perceived by all Buddhas, at the site of great enlightenment—the ocean of omniscience—one gathers a multitude of exquisite jewels for the sake of those of great wisdom; like a lotus, it is pure by its very nature, and all sentient beings who behold it give rise to joy and obtain benefit.
The light of wisdom shines universally, seeing immeasurable Buddhas and purifying all dharmas; their conduct is tranquil, and they attain ultimate non-obstruction regarding all Buddha-dharmas.

Constantly employing skillful means, they abide within the meritorious practices of the Buddha-bodhi and thereby give rise to them; endowed with the wisdom of a bodhisattva, they are the foremost among bodhisattvas and are collectively protected and remembered by all Buddhas.

Attaining the majestic spiritual power of a Buddha and perfecting the Buddha-dharmakāya, their power of mindfulness is inconceivable; they focus on a single object within the sensory realm yet remain without any objective referent. Their practice is vast, signless, and unimpeded, equal to the dharma-realm, immeasurable and boundless.

The enlightenment realized is like space: boundless, free from attachment, universally benefiting all worlds, flowing forth from the roots of goodness of the ocean of omniscience, and capable of penetrating all immeasurable realms.

Having already fully accomplished the dharma of pure giving, they abide in the bodhisattva mind, purify the bodhisattva lineage, and are able to accord with and give rise to the enlightenment of all Buddhas. They attain skillfulness in all Buddha-dharmas, possess subtle and wondrous practices, and achieve firm and steadfast power.
The sovereign spiritual power of all Buddhas is difficult for sentient beings to hear; yet Bodhisattvas fully know how to enter the gate of non-duality and abide in the dharma of signlessness.

Although they have forever relinquished all signs, they are able to extensively expound upon various dharmas, according to the inclinations, desires, and understandings of sentient beings, thereby bringing them all to subdual and causing them all to rejoice.
Taking the Dharma-realm as his body, he is free from discrimination; the sphere of his wisdom is inexhaustible; his resolve is ever courageous, and his mind is constantly equanimous.

He perceives the limits of the merits of all Buddhas, understands the sequential distinctions of all kalpas, reveals all dharmas, dwells securely in all lands, purifies all Buddha-fields, manifests the radiance of all true teachings, expounds all Buddha-dharmas of the past, future, and present, and demonstrates the abodes where Bodhisattvas dwell.

They become bright lamps for the world, giving birth to all roots of goodness; they forever leave the mundane world behind and are constantly born in the presence of Buddhas, attaining the Buddha’s wisdom with the highest clarity.
