The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of incomparable and inconceivable realms."
What are these ten? They are as follows:
all Buddhas sit in a single full-lotus posture, pervading the infinite worlds of the ten directions;
All Buddhas proclaim a single phrase of meaning, which is fully capable of revealing all Buddha-dharmas;
all Buddhas emit a single ray of light, which is fully capable of universally illuminating all worlds;
within a single body, all Buddhas are fully capable of manifesting all bodies.
All Buddhas, within a single location, are able to manifest all worlds;
all Buddhas, within a single wisdom, are able to decisively comprehend all dharmas without any obstruction;
all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are able to travel everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas fully manifest the immeasurable majestic virtue of the Tathāgatas;
in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas universally take as their object of focus the Buddhas and sentient beings of the three periods of time, their minds remaining undisturbed;
in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas are identical in essence with all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, being non-dual.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are able to give birth to ten kinds of wisdom."
What are these ten? They are as follows:
All Buddhas know that all phenomena have no point of departure or destination, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom of vows for dedication;
All Buddhas know that all phenomena are devoid of self-nature, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom of the pure body;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are fundamentally non-dual, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom of awakening;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are without self and without sentient beings, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that disciplines sentient beings.
All Buddhas know that all phenomena are fundamentally without marks, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that thoroughly understands all marks;
all Buddhas know that all worlds have no arising or ceasing, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that thoroughly understands arising and ceasing;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are without fabrication, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that knows the fruits of karma.
All Buddhas know that all phenomena are beyond verbal expression, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that thoroughly understands verbal expression;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are without defilement or purity, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that knows defilement and purity;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are without arising or ceasing, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that thoroughly understands arising and ceasing.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of universal entry dharmas."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
all Buddhas possess a pure and wondrous body that universally enters the three periods of time;
All Buddhas are fully endowed with the three kinds of mastery, universally transforming sentient beings;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with all dhāraṇīs, universally able to receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with the four kinds of eloquence, universally turning the pure wheel of Dharma.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with impartial great compassion, never abandoning any sentient being;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with profound meditative concentration, constantly and universally observing all sentient beings;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with roots of goodness for the benefit of others, subduing sentient beings without ceasing.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with an unimpeded mind, universally able to abide securely within all dharma-realms;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with unimpeded spiritual power, universally manifesting all Buddhas of the three periods of time in a single thought-moment;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with unimpeded wisdom, universally establishing the kalpas of the three periods of time in a single thought-moment.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of vast dharmas that are difficult to believe and accept."
What are these ten? They are:
all Buddhas are able to utterly destroy all Māras;
All Buddhas are able to subdue all non-Buddhists;
all Buddhas are able to tame all sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice;
all Buddhas are able to travel to all worlds to transform and guide all classes of beings.
All Buddhas are fully able to realize the profound realm of phenomena through their wisdom;
all Buddhas are fully able to manifest various bodies from their non-dual body, filling all worlds;

all Buddhas are fully able to give rise to the four types of eloquence with pure voices to preach the Dharma without interruption, such that for all who believe and accept it, the merit shall not be in vain.
All Buddhas are able to manifest as many Buddhas as there are atoms in all worlds from within a single pore, without interruption;

all Buddhas are able to manifest within a single atom as many lands as there are atoms in all worlds, complete with various sublime and wondrous adornments, constantly turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma therein to teach and transform sentient beings, yet the atom does not enlarge and the worlds do not diminish, for they always abide in the Dharma-realm through realized wisdom.

All Buddhas have fully penetrated the pure Dharma-realm, using the light of wisdom to shatter the darkness of worldly delusion, causing all to attain clear understanding of the Buddha-dharma, and following after the Tathāgatas to dwell within the ten powers.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of great merit that are pure and free from faults."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
all Buddhas possess great majestic virtue and are pure, being free from faults;
All Buddhas are born into the family of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; their lineage is disciplined and excellent, being pure and free from faults.
All Buddhas, throughout the limits of the future, have minds that dwell nowhere, being pure and free from faults.
All Buddhas have no attachment whatsoever to the phenomena of the three periods of time, being pure and free from faults.
All Buddhas know that the various natures are all of one single nature; they come from nowhere and are pure, being free from faults.
The merit and virtue of all Buddhas throughout the past and the future are inexhaustible, equal to the Dharma-realm, and are pure, being free from faults.
All Buddhas possess boundless physical forms that pervade the lands of the ten directions, taming all sentient beings according to the time, and are pure, being free from faults.

All Buddhas have attained the four fearlessnesses and are free from all terrors; amidst great assemblies, they roar the lion’s roar, clearly discerning and analyzing all dharmas, pure and free from faults.

All Buddhas enter parinirvāṇa after unspeakably unspeakable kalpas, yet sentient beings who hear their names obtain immeasurable merit, no different from when the Buddhas are present, pure and free from faults.

All Buddhas dwell afar in worlds that are unspeakably unspeakable in number, yet if there are sentient beings who maintain single-minded right mindfulness, they shall all see them, pure and free from faults.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of ultimate purity."
What are these ten? They are as follows:
the ultimate purity of the great vows of all Buddhas in their past lives;
The Brahma-conduct maintained by all Buddhas is ultimately pure;
all Buddhas are ultimately pure in their freedom from worldly delusions;
all Buddhas are ultimately pure in their adornment of buddha-fields.
The retinues of all buddhas are ultimately pure; the lineages of all buddhas are ultimately pure;
the physical bodies and marks of excellence of all buddhas are ultimately pure.
The Dharma-body of all Buddhas is unstained and ultimately pure;
the omniscient wisdom of all Buddhas is unimpeded and ultimately pure;
and the liberation and mastery of all Buddhas, having accomplished what was to be done and reached the further shore, are ultimately pure.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
In all worlds and at all times, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, perform ten kinds of Buddha-activities."
What are the ten? First, if there are sentient beings who single-mindedly recollect [the Buddha], he will manifest before them;
second, if there are sentient beings whose minds are not disciplined or compliant, he will preach the Dharma for them.
Third, if there are sentient beings who can give rise to pure faith, he will certainly cause them to obtain immeasurable roots of goodness;
fourth, if there are sentient beings who can enter the stage of the Dharma, he causes them all to realize it through direct manifestation, such that there is nothing they do not understand;
fifth, in teaching and transforming sentient beings, he never experiences weariness or fatigue.
Sixth, they travel through all Buddha-fields, coming and going without obstruction;
seventh, their great compassion never abandons any sentient being;
eighth, they manifest transformation bodies that are perpetually uninterrupted.
Ninth, they possess mastery over spiritual powers (abhijñā) that never cease;
tenth, they dwell securely within the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) and are able to observe it universally.
These are the ten.
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of inexhaustible oceans of wisdom-dharma. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the dharma of the boundless dharma-body and inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas;
the dharma of the immeasurable buddha-activities and inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas.
The dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom that is the realm of the Buddha-eye of all Buddhas;
the dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom regarding the immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable roots of goodness of all Buddhas;
and the dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom that universally rains down all the sublime Dharma of ambrosia of all Buddhas.
The Dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom regarding the merits of all Buddhas praised by all Buddhas;
the Dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom regarding the various vows and practices cultivated by all Buddhas in the past;
and the Dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom regarding all Buddhas constantly performing Buddha-works throughout the limits of the future.
The dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom that all Buddhas fully know the mental activities of all sentient beings;
the dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom adorned with the merit and knowledge of all Buddhas, which none can surpass.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten kinds of eternal laws."
What are these ten?
They are: all Buddhas constantly practice all the pāramitās;
All Buddhas are eternally free from delusion regarding all phenomena;
all Buddhas are eternally endowed with great compassion;
all Buddhas are eternally possessed of the ten powers.
All Buddhas constantly turn the wheel of Dharma;
all Buddhas constantly manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings;
all Buddhas always delight in taming and subduing all sentient beings.
The minds of all Buddhas are always in right mindfulness of the non-dual Dharma;
having transformed sentient beings, all Buddhas constantly manifest entry into nirvana without remainder, for the realm of the Buddhas is boundless.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten kinds of methods for expounding the immeasurable teachings of the Buddhas."
What are these ten? They are as follows:
all Buddhas proclaim the gateways to the infinite realms of sentient beings;
All Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable practices of sentient beings;
all Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable karmic fruits of sentient beings;
all Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable means for transforming sentient beings.
All Buddhas expound infinite gateways for purifying sentient beings;
all Buddhas expound infinite gateways of bodhisattva practices;
all Buddhas expound infinite gateways of bodhisattva vows.
All Buddhas expound the infinite gateways of the formation and destruction kalpas of all worlds;
all Buddhas expound the infinite gateways of the bodhisattvas’ profound resolve to purify Buddha-lands;
all Buddhas expound the infinite gateways of the successive appearance of all Buddhas of the three periods of time throughout all worlds in their respective kalpas.
All Buddhas expound the gateways to the wisdom of all Buddhas;
this is the tenth.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, perform ten kinds of Buddha-works for the sake of sentient beings.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
All Buddhas manifest physical bodies to perform Buddha-work for sentient beings;
all Buddhas produce sublime sounds to perform Buddha-work for sentient beings;
all Buddhas accept offerings to perform Buddha-work for sentient beings.
All Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings through non-appropriation;
all Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings by means of earth, water, fire, and wind;
all Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings by manifesting all objective spheres of perception through the sovereign power of their spiritual transformations.
All Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings through their various names and titles;
all Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings by means of the realms of their buddha-fields;
all Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings by adorning and purifying their buddha-fields.
All Buddhas perform the work of a Buddha for sentient beings through silence and wordlessness.
This is the tenth.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of most excellent dharmas. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
The great vows of all Buddhas are firm and solid, incapable of being thwarted or destroyed; what they have spoken they must surely do, for their words are without duality.
All Buddhas, desiring to fulfill every merit, cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva throughout all future eons without ever giving rise to weariness or fatigue.
All Buddhas, desiring to subdue even a single sentient being, travel to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds; in this manner, they act for the sake of all sentient beings without interruption.
All Buddhas regard with great compassion and universal impartiality both those sentient beings who have faith and those who revile them;
from their first aspiration until their attainment of Buddhahood, all Buddhas never retreat or lose the bodhicitta;
having accumulated immeasurable virtuous merits, all Buddhas dedicate them toward the nature of omniscience, remaining forever free from attachment to any worldly realm.

All Buddhas, having trained in the three karmas under all other Buddhas, practice only the conduct of Buddhas and not the conduct of the two vehicles; they dedicate all toward the nature of omniscience to achieve unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

All Buddhas radiate great light, which shines impartially upon all places and illuminates the teachings of all Buddhas, causing the minds of all Bodhisattvas to become pure and fulfilling their omniscience.

All Buddhas renounce worldly pleasures, remaining without greed or attachment, while universally wishing for the world to be free from suffering and attain happiness, devoid of all frivolous proliferation.

All Buddhas, out of compassion for sentient beings who undergo various sufferings, protect the lineage of the Buddhas, traverse the realm of the Buddhas, transcend birth and death, and attain the stage of the Ten Powers.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten kinds of unobstructed abodes."
What are these ten? They are:
all Buddhas are able to go to all worlds and abide therein without obstruction;
All Buddhas are able to abide in all worlds with unobstructed dwelling;
all Buddhas are able to abide in all worlds with unobstructed dwelling while walking, standing, sitting, or reclining;
all Buddhas are able to abide in all worlds with unobstructed dwelling while expounding the True Dharma.
All Buddhas are able to dwell without obstruction in the Tuṣita Heaven palaces throughout all worlds;
all Buddhas are able to enter the Dharma-realm and dwell without obstruction throughout all three periods of time;
all Buddhas are able to sit at the sites of enlightenment throughout the entire Dharma-realm and dwell without obstruction.
All Buddhas are able to contemplate the mental activities of all sentient beings in every moment of thought, teaching and taming them through three kinds of mastery while abiding without obstruction;
all Buddhas are able to abide with a single body in the presence of immeasurable and inconceivable Buddhas and in all places to benefit sentient beings while abiding without obstruction;
all Buddhas are able to reveal and expound the True Dharma taught by immeasurable Buddhas while abiding without obstruction.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of most excellent and unsurpassed adornments."
What are these ten?
All Buddhas are fully endowed with all the primary marks and secondary signs; this is the first, most supreme, and unsurpassed bodily adornment of the Buddhas.

All Buddhas are fully endowed with sixty kinds of vocal tones; each tone has five hundred divisions, and each division is adorned by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of pure sounds. Within all assemblies throughout the dharma-realm, they are free from any fear, and as great lion-voices, they expound the profound meaning of the Tathāgata’s Dharma. Among sentient beings who hear them, there are none who do not rejoice; according to their faculties and inclinations, all are brought to subdual. This is the second supreme and unsurpassed adornment of speech of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are endowed with the ten powers, the great samādhis, and the eighteen unique qualities that adorn their mental karma; their spheres of activity are unimpeded and thoroughly penetrating, and they have attained all Buddha-dharmas without exception. Adorned by the adornment of the dharma-realm, they clearly perceive within a single thought-moment the various distinct activities of the minds of sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm—past, future, and present—all their differences. This is the third supreme and unsurpassed mental adornment of the Buddhas.

All Buddhas are able to emit countless rays of light; each ray has an unspeakable number of networks of light as its retinue, universally illuminating all Buddha-lands, extinguishing all darkness in the world, manifesting the appearance of immeasurable Buddhas, with bodies that are equal and entirely pure. The Buddha-deeds they perform are never in vain, enabling sentient beings to reach the stage of non-retrogression. This is the fourth supreme and unsurpassed adornment of light of all Buddhas.

Whenever all Buddhas manifest a smile, they emit from their mouths hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asankhyeyas of light rays. Each individual ray possesses immeasurable, inconceivable, and manifold colors that pervade and illuminate all worlds throughout the ten directions. Amidst the great assembly, they utter words of truth, bestowing upon immeasurable, countless, and inconceivable sentient beings the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. This is the fifth supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the smile manifested by all Buddhas, which transcends worldly delusion.

All Buddhas possess the Dharma-body, which is pure and unimpeded; they have attained ultimate penetration into all phenomena and abide in the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) without limit. Although they dwell in the world, they are not defiled by the world; having realized the true nature of the world, they practice supramundane dharmas. Their path of speech is severed, and they transcend the aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and sense bases (āyatana). This is the sixth most supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the Dharma-body of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess immeasurable, eternal, and wondrous radiance; with unspeakably unspeakable varieties of color and form as their adornment, they constitute a treasury of light that gives birth to immeasurable, perfect radiance, universally illuminating the ten directions without obstruction. This is the seventh supreme, unsurpassed, eternal, and wondrous adornment of light of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess infinite wondrous forms, lovely wondrous forms, pure wondrous forms, wondrous forms that manifest according to the mind, wondrous forms that outshine all within the three realms, and unsurpassed wondrous forms that have reached the other shore; this is the eighth most supreme and unsurpassed adornment of wondrous form of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are born from the Buddha-lineage throughout the three periods of time; they have accumulated a multitude of precious virtues, are ultimately pure, and are free from all faults. They transcend worldly censure and are adorned with the most supreme, pure, and wondrous practices among all dharmas. Having fully accomplished the wisdom of all-knowledge, their lineage is pure and cannot be reviled or disparaged. This is the ninth supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the lineage of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas adorn their bodies with the power of great compassion; they are ultimately pure and free from all craving, their physical activities forever stilled and their minds well-liberated. Those who behold them never tire of the sight, for they rescue and protect all worlds with great compassion.

As the foremost field of merit and the unsurpassed recipients of offerings, they take pity upon and benefit all sentient beings, causing them all to increase their immeasurable accumulations of merit and wisdom. This is the tenth supreme, unsurpassed adornment of the meritorious virtues of great kindness and great compassion of all Buddhas.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of sovereign dharmas."
What are the ten? They are as follows:

All Buddhas have attained complete mastery over all phenomena; they are clearly proficient in various bodies of phrases and bodies of syllables, and they expound all dharmas with unimpeded eloquence. This is the first dharma of mastery belonging to the Buddhas.

All Buddhas transform sentient beings without ever missing the proper time; according to their aspirations and inclinations, they preach the True Dharma, causing them all to be tamed without interruption. This is the second sovereign dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are able to cause all worlds throughout the entirety of space—infinitely and innumerably adorned with various ornaments—to shake in six ways, causing those worlds to either rise or fall, expand or contract, conjoin or disperse, yet without ever harming a single sentient being. The beings therein do not perceive or know [these changes], nor do they harbor doubt or wonder; this is the third sovereign power of the Buddhas.

All Buddhas, by means of their supernormal powers, are able to completely adorn and purify all worlds; in a single thought-moment, they universally manifest the adornments of all worlds. These adornments could not be fully described even in the course of incalculable eons; they are entirely free from defilement, incomparably pure, and all matters concerning the adornment and purification of all Buddha-fields are made to enter equally into a single field. This is the fourth sovereign dharma of the Buddhas.

When all Buddhas perceive even a single sentient being who should be transformed, they remain for that being’s sake throughout unspeakably unspeakable kalpas, even until the end of the future limit, sitting in the full lotus posture with body and mind free from weariness. They maintain focused mindfulness without ever forgetting, skillfully taming and subduing them without missing the proper time.
As it is for one sentient being, so it is for all sentient beings; this is the fifth sovereign dharma of the Buddhas.
All Buddhas are able to travel everywhere throughout all worlds to the places where all Tathāgatas practice, yet they never for a moment abandon the entire Dharma-realm.

Throughout the ten directions, each being distinct, there are immeasurable oceans of worlds in every single direction; within each ocean of worlds, there are immeasurable types of worlds. By means of their spiritual power, the Buddhas reach them all in a single thought-moment and turn the unimpeded, pure wheel of Dharma. This is the sixth sovereign dharma of the Buddhas.

All Buddhas, desiring to discipline and transform all sentient beings, attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in every thought-moment; yet regarding all Buddha-dharmas, they have neither already fully awakened to them nor are they yet to awaken to them. Furthermore, they do not abide in the stage of those still in training (*śaikṣa*), yet they know and see all things with unimpeded penetration, possessing immeasurable wisdom and immeasurable mastery to teach, transform, and discipline all sentient beings—this is the seventh sovereign dharma of the Buddhas.

All Buddhas are able to perform the Buddha-work of the ear-faculty through the eye-faculty; they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the nose-faculty through the ear-faculty; they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the tongue-faculty through the nose-faculty; they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the body-faculty through the tongue-faculty; they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the mind-faculty through the body-faculty. They are able to abide within all worlds in the various mundane and supramundane realms of the mind-faculty, and within each and every such realm, they are able to perform immeasurable and vast Buddha-works. This is the eighth sovereign dharma of the Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess the ninth sovereign power of the Buddhas: within each and every pore of their bodies, they can accommodate all sentient beings; yet each individual being’s body is equal in size to unspeakably many Buddha-fields without any sense of confinement. Each sentient being can traverse countless worlds with every step, continuing in this manner through the end of countless eons, seeing all Buddhas appearing in the world to teach and transform sentient beings, turning the pure wheel of Dharma, and revealing the ineffable teachings of the past, future, and present.

Furthermore, they see all sentient beings throughout the entirety of space, taking birth in various realms of existence, fully endowed with their dignified deportment, comings and goings, and all manner of enjoyments, moving within these states without any obstruction. This is the ninth sovereign power of the Buddhas.

In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas manifest as many Buddhas as there are atoms in all worlds; each and every Buddha attains equal and perfect enlightenment upon a Lotus-Treasury Lion Throne within a world of vast adornment of various exquisite lotuses throughout the entire Dharma-realm, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas.

Just as in the world of vast adornment of various exquisite lotuses, so it is in all unspeakably unspeakable numbers of pure worlds throughout the Dharma-realm, with their various adornments, various realms, various forms, various manifestations, and various kalpas.

Just as it is in a single thought-moment, so it is throughout all thought-moments across immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) eons: in one thought-moment everything is manifested, and in one thought-moment one dwells for immeasurable time, yet without ever employing even the slightest power of expedient means; this is the tenth sovereign dharma of the Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of immeasurable, inconceivable, and perfected Buddha-dharmas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
each and every pure mark of all Buddhas is endowed with a hundred merits;
all Buddhas have fully accomplished all Buddha-dharmas.
All Buddhas have fully accomplished all roots of goodness;
all Buddhas have fully accomplished all merits and virtues;
all Buddhas are able to teach and transform all sentient beings.
All Buddhas are able to act as lords for sentient beings;
all Buddhas have fully accomplished pure Buddha-fields;
all Buddhas have fully accomplished the knowledge of all-knowledge.
All Buddhas fully accomplish the physical body with its marks and signs, such that those who behold it obtain benefit and their merit is never in vain;
all Buddhas possess the equal and true Dharma of all Buddhas;
and after all Buddhas have performed the work of a Buddha, there are none who do not manifest entry into nirvana.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of skillful means."
What are these ten?

All Buddhas thoroughly understand that all phenomena are free from conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), yet they are able to reveal the roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) of all Buddhas; this is the first skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*).

All Buddhas know that all phenomena are entirely without anything seen; they do not cognize one another, being neither bound nor liberated, neither receiving nor accumulating, and without attainment. They have reached the ultimate other shore with sovereign mastery, yet regarding the reality of all phenomena, they know them to be neither different nor distinct. Having attained sovereignty, they are without self and without reception, and they do not destroy the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Having already reached the stage of great sovereign mastery, they are constantly able to observe the entire dharma-realm; this is the second skillful means.

All Buddhas are eternally free from all marks; their minds dwell nowhere, yet they are able to know all things without confusion or error. Although they know that all marks lack intrinsic nature, they are able to skillfully enter into them according to their true essence. Furthermore, they manifest immeasurable physical bodies (*rūpakāya*) and the inexhaustible, manifold adornments of all pure Buddha-lands. By gathering the lamp of wisdom, they extinguish the delusions of sentient beings; this is the third skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*).

All Buddhas abide in the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), not abiding in the past, future, or present; for within the nature of suchness (tathatā), there are no characteristics of the three periods of time—past, future, or present. Yet, they are able to expound upon the appearance in the world of immeasurable Buddhas of the past, future, and present, causing those who hear it to universally perceive the realm of all Buddhas. This is the fourth skillful means (upāya-kauśalya).

The body, speech, and mental activities of all Buddhas are without fabrication; they neither come nor go, nor do they abide. Transcending all calculable phenomena, they have reached the further shore of all dharmas and serve as the treasury of all teachings. Possessing immeasurable wisdom, they thoroughly comprehend all mundane and supramundane dharmas; their wisdom is unimpeded, and they manifest immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers to subdue all sentient beings within the entire dharma realm—this is the fifth skillful means.

All Buddhas know that all phenomena are invisible; they are neither one nor different, neither finite nor infinite, neither coming nor going, and all lack intrinsic nature, yet they do not contradict the various phenomena of the world.

Those who possess all-knowledge perceive all phenomena within the absence of intrinsic nature; they attain mastery over phenomena, extensively expound all dharmas, and always abide in the true nature of suchness—this is the sixth skillful means.

All Buddhas, within a single moment, know all times; possessing pure roots of goodness, they enter the state of correctness without attachment. Regarding days, months, years, kalpas, and the periods of formation and destruction—throughout such times as these, they neither abide nor abandon them, yet they are able to manifest day and night, the first, middle, and last watches, one day, seven days, half-months, months, years, hundreds of years, one kalpa, many kalpas, inconceivable kalpas, unspeakable kalpas, and even until the end of the future limit of kalpas, constantly turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, without interruption, without retreating, and without rest. This is the seventh skillful means.

All Buddhas eternally abide in the Dharma-realm, having accomplished the immeasurable fearlessnesses of all Buddhas, as well as incalculable eloquence, immeasurable eloquence, inexhaustible eloquence, uninterrupted eloquence, boundless eloquence, unshared eloquence, infinite eloquence, true eloquence, the eloquence that skillfully reveals all phrases, and the eloquence regarding all dharmas. According to their faculties, natures, inclinations, and understandings, they expound unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sūtras through various dharma-gates—excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, and entirely consummate. This is the eighth skillful means.
All Buddhas abide in the pure dharma-realm, knowing that all phenomena are fundamentally without names: they have no name of the past, no name of the present, and no name of the future;
they have no name of sentient beings and no name of non-sentient beings;
they have no name of lands and no name of non-lands.
There is no name for phenomena, nor any name for non-phenomena;
there is no name for merit, nor any name for non-merit;
there is no name for bodhisattvas, nor any name for buddhas.
There is no name of number, nor is there any name that is not a number;
there is no name of arising, nor any name of cessation;
there is no name of existence, nor any name of non-existence.
There is no single name, nor are there various names.
Why is this? Because the essential nature of all phenomena is inexpressible.

All dharmas have no direction and no location; they cannot be explained as a collection, nor can they be explained as a dispersion, nor can they be explained as one, nor can they be explained as many. They are beyond the reach of sound, and all speech is utterly cut off. Although they follow various worldly expressions, they do not rely on anything and involve no fabrication. Being far removed from all false conceptualizations and attachments, they thus ultimately reach the other shore.
This is the ninth skillful means: All Buddhas know that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is quiescent;

because they are unarisen, they are not form (*rūpa*); because they are free from conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), they are not feeling (*vedanā*); because they lack names and numbers, they are not perception (*saṃjñā*); because they lack volitional construction (*abhisamskāra*), they are not formations (*saṃskāra*); because they lack grasping, they are not consciousness (*vijñāna*); because they lack bases of entry, they are not the sense-bases (*āyatana*); because they are non-apprehendable, they are not the elements (*dhātu*). Nevertheless, they do not destroy any phenomena, for their intrinsic nature is non-arising, like space.
All phenomena are entirely empty and quiescent; they have no karmic fruit, no cultivation, no accomplishment, and no arising;
they are neither numbered nor unnumbered, neither existent nor non-existent, neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure, neither entering nor exiting, and neither abiding nor...

Not abiding, neither disciplined nor undisciplined, neither sentient beings nor non-sentient beings, neither life-span nor no life-span, neither with causes and conditions nor without causes and conditions,
yet being able to fully comprehend all sentient beings of the fixed-in-rightness, the fixed-in-wrongness, and the indeterminate classes, and for their sake preach the sublime [Dharma].
To reach the other shore through the Dharma and Vinaya, to achieve the ten powers and the four fearlessnesses,
to be able to roar the lion’s roar, to possess all-knowledge, and to abide in the realm of the Buddha— this is the tenth skillful means.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of skillful means accomplished by all Buddhas.
*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Forty-six.
The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sutra, Scroll Forty-seven.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Shikshananda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Thirty-three, Part Two: The Inconceivable Dharmas of the Buddha.
“O Son of the Buddha!

The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of vast buddha-activities that are immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. All the gods and humans of every world cannot know them; even all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, and present cannot know them, except through the power of the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual authority.”
What are these ten? They are as follows:
"All Buddhas, in the Tuṣita Heavens of all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm..."
All manifest birth, cultivate the bodhisattva practices, and perform great Buddha-works;
with immeasurable physical forms, immeasurable majestic virtue, immeasurable radiance, immeasurable sounds,
immeasurable modes of speech, immeasurable samādhis, and immeasurable spheres of activity of wisdom, they gather in all people.
...Devas, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, asuras, and others;
possessing great compassion that is unimpeded and ultimate great pity, he benefits all sentient beings with equality—
either causing them to be born in the heavens, or causing them to be born as humans, or purifying their faculties, or disciplining their minds, or at times...
To teach the distinctions of the three vehicles, or at times to teach the perfect single vehicle,
universally delivering all beings and causing them to transcend birth and death— this is the first vast buddha-work.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas descend from the Tuṣita Heaven into their mothers’ wombs;
by means of the ultimate samādhi, they contemplate the dharma of taking birth as being like an illusion, like a transformation, like a shadow, like space, and like a mirage, in accordance with—”
Receiving joyfully, immeasurable and unimpeded, entering the dharma of non-contention, giving rise to non-attached wisdom,
pure through the departure from desire, accomplishing the vast and wondrous treasury of adornments, receiving his final body,
and dwelling in a great jewel-adorned pavilion to perform buddha-work— whether performing buddha-work through supernatural power or...
They perform Buddha-works by means of right mindfulness; or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting spiritual powers;
or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting the sun of wisdom; or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting the vast realms of all Buddhas;
or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting the immeasurable radiance of all Buddhas; or they enter countless, vast samādhis.
They perform buddha-works, or manifest arising from those various samādhis to perform buddha-works.
O Son of the Buddha!
At that time, while the Tathāgata was within his mother’s womb, he performed buddha-works by manifesting various appearances for the sake of benefiting all worlds.
That is to say:

they may manifest their initial birth, or manifest as a youth, or appear in the palace, or manifest leaving the home life; or again, they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment, or manifest the turning of the sublime wheel of Dharma, or manifest entry into parinirvāṇa. Thus, through various skillful means, they perform buddha-work in all directions, all networks, all lineages, all species, and in all worlds.
This is the second vast buddha-work.
"O Son of the Buddha!

All the virtuous karmas of all Buddhas are already purified; all their births and wisdoms are already clear and pure. Yet, by manifesting birth through the laws of existence, they guide the deluded masses, causing them to attain awakening and to fully practice all manner of goodness."

For the sake of sentient beings, he manifests birth in a royal palace; yet all Buddhas have already renounced all sensory desires, palaces, and the music of courtesans, remaining free from any attachment or defilement. They constantly contemplate that all phenomena are empty and devoid of intrinsic nature, and that all objects of pleasure are entirely unreal.

They maintain the pure precepts of a Buddha to ultimate perfection. Contemplating the inner palace, wives, concubines, and attendants, they give rise to great compassion; contemplating the false and unreal nature of sentient beings, they give rise to great kindness; contemplating that there is not a single thing in the world worth delighting in, they give rise to great joy; and attaining mastery of mind over all dharmas, they give rise to great equanimity.
Possessing the merits of a Buddha, they manifest within the Dharma-realm with perfect physical marks and a pure retinue, yet remain unattached to anything at all.

He expounds the Dharma for the multitude using voices that accord with their respective types, causing them to develop a profound sense of weary detachment toward worldly phenomena. He demonstrates the fruits attained according to their respective practices and further employs skillful means to teach and transform them as appropriate.
Those who are not yet matured he causes to reach maturity; those already matured he causes to attain liberation. Performing the work of a Buddha, he ensures they do not regress.

Furthermore, with a heart of vast compassion, he constantly preaches various dharmas for the sake of sentient beings, and again manifests three kinds of mastery to bring them to awakening and purify their minds.
Although he dwells within the inner palace, he is beheld by all; yet throughout all worlds, he performs the Buddha-work.
With great wisdom and great diligence, he manifests various supernatural powers of the Buddhas, unimpeded and inexhaustible.
They constantly abide in three kinds of skillful means of action, namely:

bodily action that is ultimately pure; verbal action that always proceeds in accordance with wisdom; and mental action that is profoundly deep and free from obstruction. By these skillful means, they benefit sentient beings.
This is the third vast Buddha-activity.
"O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas manifest dwelling in various adorned palaces, yet they observe them with detachment and renounce them to leave the household life. This is because they wish to cause sentient beings to understand that all worldly phenomena are mere conceptual constructions, impermanent, and subject to decay; thereby causing them to give rise to deep disenchantment, not produce defiled attachments, forever sever the afflictions of worldly craving and love, cultivate pure conduct, and benefit all sentient beings."

When he went forth from home, he abandoned worldly deportment and dwelt in the Dharma of non-contention. He fulfilled his original vows and immeasurable merits, extinguishing the darkness of worldly delusion with the light of great wisdom. He became a supreme field of merit for all the world, constantly praising the Buddha’s virtues for the sake of sentient beings, causing them to plant various roots of goodness before the Buddha and perceive the true meaning with the eye of wisdom.

Furthermore, he praised and spoke of renunciation for the sake of sentient beings—pure and faultless, leading forever to liberation—and remained for a long time as a lofty banner of wisdom for the world.
This is the fourth vast buddha-work.
"O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas possess all-knowledge; they have fully known and seen immeasurable dharmas. Having attained supreme perfect enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, they have subdued all Māras, their majestic virtue being uniquely supreme."

His body fills all worlds; the miraculous powers he manifests are boundless and inexhaustible; he has attained mastery over all meanings within the sphere of omniscience; and he has brought all cultivated merits to complete perfection.

That seat of enlightenment was fully adorned and pervaded all worlds throughout the ten directions; thereupon the Buddha turned the sublime wheel of Dharma, proclaiming all the practices and vows of bodhisattvas, revealing the infinite realms of all Buddhas, causing all bodhisattvas to attain realization and entry, and to cultivate various kinds of pure and wondrous conduct.

Furthermore, they are able to guide all sentient beings, causing them to plant roots of goodness and be born within the ground of equality of the Tathāgatas; they abide in the boundless, wondrous practices of all bodhisattvas and accomplish all supreme dharmas of merit. They thoroughly and skillfully understand all worlds, all sentient beings, all buddha-fields, all dharmas, all bodhisattvas, all teachings and transformations, all three periods of time, all methods of subduing, all spiritual manifestations, and the inclinations and desires of the minds of all sentient beings, thereby performing the work of a Buddha.
This is the fifth vast buddha-work.
"O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas turn the wheel of non-retrogression, so as to cause all bodhisattvas not to fall back."
They turn the wheel of the Dharma of immeasurable extent, so that all worlds may fully understand;
they turn the wheel of awakening all beings, for they can let out the great lion’s roar with fearlessness;
they turn the wheel of the treasury of wisdom of all dharmas, opening the gate of the Dharma-treasury to eliminate the veil of darkness.
They turn the wheel of unimpeded Dharma, because it is equal to space;
they turn the wheel of non-attachment, because they contemplate all phenomena as being neither existent nor non-existent;
they turn the wheel that illuminates the world, because they cause all sentient beings to purify their Dharma-eye.
They turn the wheel of Dharma of omniscience, because it pervades all phenomena throughout the three periods of time;
they turn the single wheel of Dharma common to all Buddhas, because all Buddha-dharmas are not mutually contradictory.

All Buddhas, by means of such immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Dharma wheels, perform inconceivable Buddha-works according to the differences in the mental activities of sentient beings.
This is the sixth vast buddha-work.
"O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas enter all royal capitals and towns to perform buddha-works for the sake of all sentient beings; that is to say:"

The capital cities of human kings, the capital cities of heavenly kings, and likewise the capital cities of all such kings as dragon kings, yakṣa kings, gandharva kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings, rākṣasa kings, and piśāca kings.

As he entered the city gate, the great earth shook, and a brilliant light shone everywhere. The blind regained their sight, the deaf their hearing, the insane their composure, and the naked were clothed. All those who suffered in grief and pain attained peace and happiness.

All musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck; all ornaments, whether worn or not, emitted wondrous sounds, such that among all living beings who heard them, there was none who did not rejoice.

The form bodies (*rūpakāya*) of all Buddhas are pure, endowed with the primary and secondary marks (*lakṣaṇa-vyañjana*), and those who behold them never tire of doing so; they are able to perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.
That is to say:

whether looking around, observing, moving, stretching or contracting [the limbs], walking, standing, sitting, lying down, remaining silent, speaking, manifesting supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), preaching the Dharma, or issuing instructions—all such acts constitute the performance of Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.

All Buddhas, throughout all infinite worlds, within the ocean of the various inclinations and joys of sentient beings, universally exhort them to practice mindfulness of the Buddha, to constantly and diligently observe, to plant various roots of goodness, and to cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva;

they praise the Buddha’s physical marks as being most subtle and supreme, difficult for any sentient being to encounter, and that if one should behold him and give rise to faith, then all immeasurable wholesome dharmas will be produced, and the merits of the Buddha will be gathered until they are universally pure.

Having thus praised the merits of the Buddha, his emanations went everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions, causing all sentient beings to behold and revere him, contemplate and observe him, serve and make offerings to him, plant various roots of goodness, receive the Buddha’s joy, increase the seeds of Buddhahood, and all attain buddhahood.

Performing the work of a Buddha through such practices, he may manifest a physical body for the sake of sentient beings, or produce sublime sounds, or simply smile, thereby causing them to have faith and joy; they then pay homage by bowing their heads to his feet, bending their bodies with palms joined, praising and extolling him, and inquiring after his well-being as he performs the work of a Buddha.

All Buddhas, through such immeasurable, innumerable, ineffable, and inconceivable varieties of Buddha-works, throughout all worlds, according to the inclinations of the hearts of sentient beings, employ their power of original vows, the power of great compassion, and the power of all-encompassing wisdom to skillfully teach and transform them, causing them all to be subdued and disciplined.
This is the seventh vast buddha-work.
"O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas may perform buddha-works while dwelling in forest hermitages (āraṇya);..."
Some perform buddha-work while dwelling in places of tranquility;
some perform buddha-work while dwelling in secluded and empty places;
and some perform buddha-work while dwelling in the abodes of Buddhas.
Some perform Buddha-works while abiding in samādhi;
some perform Buddha-works while dwelling alone in groves and gardens;
and some perform Buddha-works while remaining hidden and unmanifest.
Some perform Buddha-works while abiding in profound wisdom;
some perform Buddha-works while abiding in the incomparable realm of all Buddhas;

and some perform Buddha-works while abiding in various invisible bodily activities, skillfully teaching and transforming sentient beings without rest according to their mental inclinations, desires, and understandings.
Some perform buddha-work by seeking omniscience through a celestial body;
some perform buddha-work by seeking omniscience through the bodies of nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth;
or some perform buddha-work by seeking omniscience through the bodies of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas.
At times they perform Buddha-work by preaching the Dharma, and at times they perform Buddha-work through silent stillness;
at times they perform Buddha-work by speaking of a single Buddha, and at times by speaking of many Buddhas;
or they perform Buddha-work by explaining all the practices and vows of all Bodhisattvas as being a single practice and vow.
Some say that bodhisattvas perform buddha-work by means of a single practice and a single vow acting as immeasurable practices and vows;
some say that they perform buddha-work by teaching that the realm of the Buddha is itself the realm of the world;
and some say that they perform buddha-work by teaching that the realm of the world is itself the realm of the Buddha.
Some say that the Buddha’s realm is a non-realm, yet therein he performs buddha-work;
some abide for a single day, or a single night, or half a month, or a month, or a year, or even for unspeakable eons, performing buddha-work for the sake of all sentient beings.
This is the eighth vast buddha-work.
"O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas are the treasury that gives birth to pure roots of goodness; they cause all sentient beings to give rise to pure faith and understanding within the Buddha-dharma, to bring their faculties under control, and to forever leave the world behind."
They cause all bodhisattvas to possess the illumination of wisdom on the path to enlightenment, so that they do not rely on others for awakening.
They may manifest nirvana to perform buddha-work;
or they may manifest that all things in the world are impermanent to perform buddha-work.
Some perform buddha-works by speaking of the Buddha-body;
some perform buddha-works by speaking of how all that was to be done has been fully accomplished;
and some perform buddha-works by speaking of the perfection of merit without deficiency.
Some perform Buddha-work by teaching the eternal severance of the root of all existence;
some perform Buddha-work by causing sentient beings to feel weary of and detached from the world, thereby conforming to the Buddha-mind;
and some perform Buddha-work by teaching that life ultimately ends in exhaustion.
Some perform Buddha-works by teaching that there is nothing in the world worth delighting in;
some perform Buddha-works by proclaiming the making of offerings to all Buddhas throughout the limits of the future;
and some perform Buddha-works by teaching that the Buddhas turn the pure wheel of Dharma, causing those who hear it to give rise to great joy.
In some cases, they perform Buddha-work by proclaiming the realm of all Buddhas, causing beings to resolve their minds for enlightenment and cultivate various practices;
in some cases, they perform Buddha-work by proclaiming the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha, causing beings to resolve their minds to always delight in seeing the Buddha;
in some cases, they perform Buddha-work by proclaiming the purification of the faculties, causing beings to diligently seek the Buddha-way with minds free from indolence or retreat.
Or they may go to all Buddha-lands to perform Buddha-work by observing the various causes and conditions of all realms;

or they may transform the bodies of all sentient beings into the body of a Buddha, causing all indolent and heedless beings to abide in the pure prohibitions and precepts of the Tathāgata, thereby performing Buddha-work.
This is the ninth vast buddha-work.
"O Son of the Buddha!
When all Buddhas enter nirvana, immeasurable sentient beings wail and weep, giving rise to great sorrow and affliction; looking at one another, they speak these words:"
"The Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, possesses great compassion; out of pity, he benefits all the world, serving as a savior and a refuge for all sentient beings.
The appearance of a Tathāgata is difficult to encounter, and now this unsurpassed field of merit has forever perished."
Thus, by causing all sentient beings to wail with grief and yearn with longing, he performs the work of a Buddha.

Furthermore, for the sake of transforming and delivering all devas, humans, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, he spontaneously shatters his own body into śarīras—immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable—in accordance with their inclinations and desires, so that all sentient beings may give rise to pure faith, respect and honor him, joyfully make offerings, and cultivate various merits until they are fully perfected.

Furthermore, they shall raise stupas and adorn them in various ways, making offerings within the palaces of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, the palaces of the yakṣas, and within the palaces of the gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.

Their teeth, claws, and hair shall all be used to erect stupas, so that all who see them will mindfully recollect the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha; they will have unwavering faith and joy, being sincere, respectful, and reverent; wherever they may be, they will practice giving and making offerings, cultivating all manner of meritorious virtues.

By virtue of this merit, they will either be born in the heavens or dwell among humans, with noble and honorable lineage and abundant wealth; their entire retinue will be pure, they will not enter the evil realms, and will always be born in the good paths. They will constantly behold the Buddhas, be endowed with all pure dharmas, and swiftly attain liberation from the three realms of existence. Each, according to their own vows, will obtain the fruit of their respective vehicle, repay the kindness of the Tathāgata’s knowledge, and forever serve as a refuge for the world.
O Son of the Buddha!

Although the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have entered parinirvāṇa, they still serve as inconceivable fields of pure merit for sentient beings—the supreme field of merit of inexhaustible virtue—causing all sentient beings to be fully endowed with roots of goodness and to perfect their merit and blessings.
This is the tenth vast buddha-activity.
"O Son of the Buddha!

These buddha-activities are immeasurable, vast, and inconceivable; they cannot be known by any gods or humans in all worlds, nor by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, or present, except through the empowerment of the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual power."
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of sovereign dharmas of non-dual conduct. What are these ten?
That is to say:
all Buddhas are able to skillfully expound the words of prophecy, which are definitive and non-dual;
all Buddhas are able to accord with the mental inclinations of sentient beings, causing their aspirations to be fulfilled, which is definitive and non-dual.
All Buddhas are able to manifest and awaken to all dharmas and expound their meaning with definitive non-duality;
all Buddhas are able to be fully endowed with the wisdom of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, with definitive non-duality;
all Buddhas know that all moments (*kṣaṇa*) of the three periods of time are a single moment, with definitive non-duality.
All Buddhas know that all Buddha-fields of the three periods of time enter into a single Buddha-field, which is definitively non-dual;
all Buddhas know that all Buddha-speech of the three periods of time is the speech of a single Buddha, which is definitively non-dual;
all Buddhas know that the essential nature of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and all sentient beings they transform is equal, which is definitively non-dual.
All Buddhas know that the nature of worldly phenomena and the nature of the Buddha-dharma are without distinction, being definitively non-dual;
all Buddhas know that all roots of goodness belonging to all Buddhas of the three periods of time are a single root of goodness, being definitively non-dual.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten kinds of abodes, by which they abide in all dharmas."
What are the ten? They are:
all Buddhas abide in the awakening to the entire dharma-realm;
All Buddhas abide in speech of great compassion;
all Buddhas abide in their fundamental great vows;
all Buddhas abide in never abandoning the taming of sentient beings.
All Buddhas abide in the dharma of selflessness;
all Buddhas abide in impartial benefit;
all Buddhas abide in the dharma of non-forgetfulness.
All Buddhas abide in a mind free from obstruction;
all Buddhas abide in a mind of constant right concentration;
all Buddhas abide in the equal entry into all phenomena, never deviating from the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of knowledge of all phenomena without exception."
What are the ten? They are:
knowing that all phenomena of the past have completely ceased without exception;
He knows all future phenomena exhaustively without exception;
he knows all present phenomena exhaustively without exception;
he knows all phenomena of speech exhaustively without exception.
They know all paths in all worlds exhaustively, without exception;
they know the minds of all sentient beings exhaustively, without exception;
and they know all the various stages of the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas—superior, middling, and inferior—exhaustively, without exception.
They know the perfect wisdom and all roots of goodness of all Buddhas to be neither increasing nor decreasing, exhausting them without remainder;
they know that all phenomena arise from conditions, exhausting them without remainder;
and they know all varieties of world-systems, exhausting them without remainder.
To know all the various phenomena within the entire realm of reality, like Indra’s net, without exception—
this is the tenth.
"O Son of the Buddha!..."
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of powers. What are these ten?
They are as follows:

The power of vast strength, the power of the supreme, the power of the infinite, the power of great majesty and virtue, the power that is difficult to acquire, the power of non-retrogression, the power of firmness, the power that cannot be destroyed, the inconceivable power of all worlds, and the power that no sentient being can move.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of great Nārāyaṇa-bannered valiant dharmas."
What are these ten? They are as follows:

"The bodies of all Buddhas are indestructible; their lives cannot be severed; they cannot be affected by worldly poisons; and the calamities of water, fire, and wind in all worlds cannot harm the Buddha's body."

All the Māras, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, piśācas, rākṣasas, and others, exerting all their power, rained down great golden vajras as large as Mount Sumeru and the Iron Ring Mountains, filling the trichiliocosm and falling all at once; yet they could not cause the Buddha’s mind to feel alarm or fear, nor did even a single hair of his body stir, for whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, he remained forever unchanged.
In all directions, far and near, wherever the Buddha dwells, if he does not permit it, rain cannot fall;
even if he does not restrain it and rain falls, it will ultimately cause no harm.
If there are sentient beings who are sustained by the Buddha and dispatched by the Buddha, they cannot even be harmed; how much less so the body of the Tathāgata!
This is the foremost Dharma of the great Nārāyaṇa-bannered valor of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas can take all the Sumeru Kings, Iron Ring Mountains, Great Iron Ring Mountains, great oceans, mountain forests, palaces, and dwellings within all worlds of the entire Dharma-realm, and place them within a single pore; yet throughout all future kalpas, sentient beings do not perceive or know this, except for those who are empowered by the spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
"O Son of the Buddha!

At that time, all Buddhas, within a single pore, sustain as many worlds as there are, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, without giving rise to even a single thought of weariness."
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as space universally sustains all worlds throughout the entire dharma-realm without ever becoming weary or fatigued, so too do all Buddhas sustain all worlds within a single pore.
This is the second Dharma of the great Māra-Indra-like banner of valorous strength of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas are able, in a single thought-moment, to take steps numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable worlds; with each step, they pass through lands numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields. Traveling in this manner, they do so for kalpas numbering as many as the atoms in all worlds."
O Son of the Buddha!
Suppose there were a great mountain of diamond equal in measure to all the Buddha-fields traversed above.
If there were as many such mountains of diamond as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, the Buddhas would be able to place all these mountains within a single pore.

The pores of the Buddha’s body are equal in number to the pores of all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm. Within each and every pore, he places as many great diamond mountains as there are pores; carrying these mountains, he travels through the ten directions, entering all worlds throughout the entirety of empty space. From the beginningless past to the endless future, throughout all kalpas, he never rests; yet his body suffers no injury nor does it experience fatigue, for his mind always abides in samādhi without distraction.
This is the third great Nārāyaṇa-banner of valorous strength of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!

After all Buddhas have finished their single meal in one sitting, they sit cross-legged and pass through unspeakable eons of the past and future, entering the inconceivable bliss experienced by Buddhas. Their bodies remain steadfast, tranquil and unmoving, yet they do not abandon the work of transforming sentient beings."
O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose there were someone who, using the tip of a hair, measured every single world throughout the entirety of space one by one; yet the Buddhas could sit cross-legged upon the space of a single hair-tip, remaining there until the end of all future kalpas.
As it is with the space of one hair-tip, so it is with the space of every hair-tip.
O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose all sentient beings in every world throughout the ten directions were such that the size of each individual being’s body was equal to the measure of unspeakably many Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms, and their weight were likewise so; yet the Buddhas could place all those beings upon the tip of a single finger for as many kalpas as exist until the end of time.

This would be true for every finger-tip as well, carrying all those beings into every single world throughout the entirety of space, filling the whole dharma-realm without exception, while the Buddhas’ bodies and minds would never experience weariness or fatigue.
This is the fourth great Nārāyaṇa-banner of heroic vigor of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas are able, within a single body, to manifest as many heads as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; from each head, they manifest as many tongues as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; from each tongue, they produce as many distinct sounds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields—sounds that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm hear without exception. Each sound expounds as many collections of Sūtras as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; each collection of Sūtras expounds as many Dharmas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; and each Dharma contains as many words, phrases, and meanings as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
He spoke in this manner for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
when those eons were exhausted, he spoke further for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
continuing in this sequence until he had exhausted the number of atoms in all worlds, and the number of mental thoughts of all sentient beings.
The kalpas of the future limit may yet be exhausted, but the turning of the wheel of Dharma by the emanation bodies of the Tathāgata is inexhaustible.

That is to say: the wheel of Dharma expounded through wisdom; the wheel of Dharma that severs all doubts; the wheel of Dharma that illuminates all phenomena; the wheel of Dharma that opens the treasury of non-obstruction; the wheel of Dharma that causes immeasurable sentient beings to rejoice and be tamed; the wheel of Dharma that reveals all bodhisattva practices; the wheel of Dharma that rises high like the perfect sun of great wisdom; the wheel of Dharma that universally kindles the bright lamp of wisdom to illuminate the world; and the wheel of Dharma adorned with various forms of eloquence and fearlessness.
Just as a single Buddha-body, by means of its supernormal powers, turns such various wheels of Dharma that no worldly phenomena can serve as an analogy for them;

so too, throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space, in every location the size of a single hair-tip, there are worlds numbering as many as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields. Within each of these worlds, in every thought-moment, there appear emanation bodies numbering as many as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields. Each of these emanation bodies is likewise identical: the sounds, words, phrases, and meanings they proclaim fill the entire Dharma-realm, and all sentient beings therein understand them. Yet the Buddha’s speech remains unchanged, uninterrupted, and inexhaustible.
This is the fifth great Nārāyaṇa-banner of heroic vigor of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas adorn their chests with marks of virtue, which are as indestructible as vajra, as they sit cross-legged beneath the Bodhi tree."

The hosts of Māra’s army are infinite in number; their various and diverse forms are most terrifying, such that no sentient being who beholds them fails to be struck with alarm and dread, all falling into madness or even meeting death.

Thus the hosts of Māra filled the entirety of space. When the Tathāgata saw them, his mind was free from fear; his countenance remained unchanged, not a single hair stood on end, and he was unmoved and undisturbed. Free from discrimination, detached from all joy and anger, he dwelt in tranquil purity within the state of a Buddha. Possessing the power of compassion, with his faculties fully subdued and his mind fearless, he could not be shaken by any of the Māra hosts. Instead, he was able to crush and subdue the entire army of Māras, causing them to turn their hearts, prostrate themselves, and take refuge. Thereafter, he further transformed them through the three wheels of teaching, leading them all to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* so that they would never again fall back.
This is the sixth great Nārāyaṇa-bannered, heroic dharma of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess an unimpeded voice; that voice pervades the worlds of the ten directions, and those sentient beings who hear it are naturally subdued."

The sounds emitted by those Tathāgatas cannot be obstructed by any mountains, such as Mount Sumeru; nor can they be obstructed by any palaces, including those of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, or non-humans; nor can they be obstructed by any loud or high-pitched sounds from any world-systems.
According to those who are to be transformed, there is not a single sentient being who does not hear [the teaching], and all fully comprehend its words, phrases, and meanings.
This is the seventh great Nārāyaṇa-banner of heroic vigor of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The minds of all Buddhas are without obstruction; throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable eons, they have been perpetually and perfectly pure."

All Buddhas of the past, future, and present are of one and the same essence; they are without turbidity or obscuration, without self or what belongs to a self, neither internal nor external. Having realized that objects are empty and quiescent, they do not give rise to deluded thoughts;
they have no basis and nothing to be done, they do not dwell upon any signs, and they have forever severed conceptual discrimination.
Their fundamental nature is pure; they have abandoned all攀缘 (pān-yuan) and recollections, and they are always free from conflict regarding all phenomena.
Abiding in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), pure through the departure from desire, they enter the true dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) and expound it inexhaustibly;
free from all deluded thoughts regarding the measurable and the immeasurable, they sever all verbal expressions concerning the conditioned (*saṃskṛta*) and the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*);

having fully penetrated the ineffable and boundless realm, they possess unimpeded and inexhaustible wisdom and skillful means, accomplishing the ten powers and all adornments of merit and purity, and expounding various immeasurable dharmas, all of which do not contradict the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
Regarding all phenomena within the dharma-realm across the three periods of time, they are entirely equal and without distinction, reaching ultimate mastery;

they enter the most supreme treasury of all dharmas, maintaining right mindfulness without confusion regarding all dharma-gates, dwelling peacefully in all Buddha-lands of the ten directions without wavering;

they attain uninterrupted wisdom, knowing all dharmas exhaustively and without remainder, having exhausted all outflows, with their minds well-liberated and their wisdom well-liberated, abiding in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), penetrating without obstruction, and their minds always in right concentration.
To comprehend, in a single thought-moment, all phenomena of the three periods of time as well as the mental activities of all sentient beings, without any obstruction—
this is the eighth great Nārāyaṇa-banner of valorous strength of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess a single Dharma-body; an immeasurable body of spheres of experience; a boundless body of merit; an inexhaustible body in the world;
a body unstained by the three realms; a body that manifests according to thought; and a non-...”
The body that is truly real and not false, equal and pure; the unconditioned and indestructible body that neither comes nor goes;

the body of the self-nature of phenomena, which is the single mark of being markless; the body that is omnipresent, being without location or direction; the body of infinite forms and marks through sovereign spiritual transformations;
the body that universally enters all things by manifesting in various ways; the body of the sublime Dharma’s directions...
The body that is the treasury of physical ease and wisdom; the body that universally illumines; the body that manifests the equality of all dharmas;
the body that pervades the entire dharma-realm; the body that is immovable and non-conceptual, neither existent nor non-existent, and eternally pure;

and the body that, being neither expedient nor non-expedient, neither extinguished nor non-extinguished, accords with the various inclinations and understandings of all sentient beings according to how they are to be transformed.
He manifests a body born from the jewels of all merits; a body possessing the *tathatā* of all Buddha-dharmas;
a body whose intrinsic nature is quiescent and unobstructed; a body that has perfected all unimpeded dharmas;
a body that dwells pervasively throughout the pure *dharmadhātu*; and a body that divides its forms to be universally present in all worlds.
The body that is without objective support, without regression, eternally liberated, endowed with all-knowledge, and universally penetrating—
this is the ninth great Nārāyaṇa-banner of valorous strength of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas equally awaken to all the dharmas of all Tathāgatas and equally cultivate all the practices of all Bodhisattvas;
whether in their vows or their wisdom, they are pure and equal, like a great ocean, having attained complete fulfillment.”

The power of their practice is supreme and preeminent; they never retreat or falter, dwelling in the immeasurable realms of various samādhis, manifesting all paths, exhorting toward good and admonishing against evil.

Their power of wisdom is foremost as they expound the Dharma with fearlessness, skillfully answering every question that arises. Their wisdom in preaching the Dharma is impartial and pure; their actions of body, speech, and mind are entirely unadulterated. Abiding where the Buddhas abide within the lineage of all Buddhas, they perform the Buddha-work through the wisdom of a Buddha.

Dwelling in omniscience, they expound immeasurable dharmas that have no root and no limit; their supernormal powers and wisdom are inconceivable, such that none in any world can fully comprehend them.

Their wisdom penetrates deeply, perceiving all phenomena as subtle, vast, immeasurable, and boundless; they skillfully master the Dharma-gates of the three periods of time and are able to enlighten all worlds.
With supramundane wisdom, they perform unspeakably diverse Buddha-activities within all mundane realms, achieving non-retrogressive wisdom and entering the ranks of the Buddhas.
Although they have already realized the ineffable Dharma that transcends words and letters, they are nevertheless able to manifest and teach through various forms of speech.

By means of the wisdom of Samantabhadra, one gathers all virtuous practices and accomplishes the wondrous wisdom that accords with a single thought-moment, thereby being able to fully awaken to and understand all phenomena. Just as previously contemplated, for all sentient beings, one bestows the Dharma according to their respective vehicles;

regarding all phenomena, all worlds, all sentient beings, and all three periods of time within the Dharmadhātu—such realms being boundless in measure—one is able to know and see them all through unimpeded wisdom.
O Son of the Buddha!

In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas appear in the world according to those who are to be transformed; they dwell in pure lands, attain equal and perfect enlightenment, and manifest supernatural powers to awaken the mind, intellect, and consciousness of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time, never missing the proper moment.
O Son of the Buddha!

Sentient beings are boundless, worlds are boundless, the dharma-realm is boundless, and the three periods of time are boundless; even the most supreme Buddhas are boundless. Within all these, they manifest the attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment, using the wisdom and skillful means of a Buddha to awaken others without ceasing.
O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas, by means of their supernormal powers, manifest most wondrous bodies and abide in boundless realms; through the skillful means of great compassion and with minds free from obstruction, they constantly expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings at all times.
This is the tenth great Nārāyaṇa-bannered, heroic, and valiant dharma of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
