These immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable great Nārāyaṇa-bannered, heroic, and valiant dharmas of all Buddhas cannot be understood by any sentient beings of the past, future, or present, nor by those of the two vehicles, except for those empowered by the spiritual power of the Tathāgata."
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of definitive dharmas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
all Buddhas invariably descend from Tuṣita after their lifespan there has ended;
all Buddhas invariably manifest birth and remain in the womb for ten months.
All Buddhas are certain to feel weary of the mundane world and joyfully seek to leave the household life;
all Buddhas are certain to sit beneath the Bodhi tree and attain equal and perfect enlightenment, awakening to all Buddha-dharmas;
all Buddhas are certain to awaken to all phenomena in a single thought-moment and manifest spiritual powers throughout all worlds.
All Buddhas are certain to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma in accordance with the proper time;
all Buddhas are certain to preach the Dharma and bestow predictions of enlightenment upon beings according to the roots of goodness they have planted, at the appropriate time;
all Buddhas are certain to perform the works of a Buddha in accordance with the proper time.
All Buddhas are certainly able to bestow predictions of enlightenment upon all bodhisattvas who have attained accomplishment;
all Buddhas are certainly able to universally answer the questions of all sentient beings in a single thought-moment.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of swift dharmas."
What are these ten? They are as follows:
if anyone beholds any of the Buddhas, they will swiftly attain liberation from all evil realms of existence.
If anyone beholds any of the Buddhas, they will swiftly attain the perfection of supreme merit;
if anyone beholds any of the Buddhas, they will swiftly be able to accomplish vast roots of goodness;
if anyone beholds any of the Buddhas, they will swiftly attain rebirth in the pure and wondrous heavens.
If any behold all the Buddhas, they will swiftly be able to eliminate all doubts and delusions.

If those who have already resolved to attain Bodhicitta behold them, they will swiftly achieve vast faith and understanding, never again to regress, and will be able to teach and transform sentient beings according to their needs; if they have not yet resolved to attain it, they will swiftly generate the mind of Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
If those who have not yet entered the stage of certainty behold all the Buddhas, they will swiftly enter that stage of certainty.
If anyone beholds any of the Buddhas, they will swiftly purify all mundane and supramundane faculties;
if anyone beholds any of the Buddhas, they will swiftly eliminate all obstacles;
if anyone beholds any of the Buddhas, they will swiftly attain fearless eloquence.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten kinds of pure dharmas that should always be recollected."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect the past causes and conditions of all Buddhas;
All Bodhisattvas should constantly keep in mind the pure and supreme conduct of all Buddhas;
all Bodhisattvas should constantly keep in mind how all Buddhas have fulfilled the perfections;
all Bodhisattvas should constantly keep in mind how all Buddhas have accomplished their great vows.
All Buddhas have accumulated roots of goodness; all bodhisattvas should constantly keep this in mind.
All Buddhas have already perfected the holy life; all bodhisattvas should constantly keep this in mind.
All Buddhas have manifested the attainment of perfect enlightenment; all bodhisattvas should constantly keep this in mind.
The form-bodies of all Buddhas are immeasurable; all Bodhisattvas should constantly keep this in mind.
The supernormal powers of all Buddhas are immeasurable; all Bodhisattvas should constantly keep this in mind.
The ten powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas are immeasurable; all Bodhisattvas should constantly keep these in mind.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten kinds of abodes of omniscience."
What are these ten? They are as follows:
All Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, fully know the minds and mental activities of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time;
In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas fully know all the karmas accumulated by all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time, as well as the retributions of those karmas;
in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas fully know what is appropriate for all sentient beings and teach and subdue them through the three wheels;

in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas exhaustively know all mental characteristics of all sentient beings within the entire dharma-realm, manifesting the appearance of a Buddha everywhere so that they may see him, thereby gathering and sustaining them through skillful means.

In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas universally accord with the inclinations, desires, and understandings of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, manifesting the teaching of the Dharma to bring them to subdual;
in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas fully know the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm and manifest spiritual powers for their sake;

in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas appear throughout all places, manifesting their arising according to those sentient beings who are ready to be transformed, and teach that the Buddha-body is not to be grasped or attached to.
In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas universally reach every place throughout the entire Dharma-realm and all sentient beings in their respective realms of existence;
in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas respond to those among sentient beings who have mindfulness, appearing wherever they may be without exception;
in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas fully know the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings, manifesting for them immeasurable forms and appearances.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of immeasurable and inconceivable Buddha-samādhis."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
All Buddhas are eternally in right concentration; within a single thought-moment, they pervade all places and universally expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
All Buddhas are constantly in right concentration; within a single thought-moment they pervade all places, universally preaching the limit of non-self to sentient beings.
All Buddhas constantly abide in right concentration; within a single thought-moment they pervade all places, universally entering the three periods of time.
All Buddhas constantly abide in right concentration; within a single thought-moment they pervade all places, universally entering the vast Buddha-lands of the ten directions.
All Buddhas eternally abide in right concentration; in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places, universally manifesting immeasurable and diverse Buddha-bodies.

All Buddhas eternally abide in right concentration; in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places, manifesting body, speech, and mind according to the various mental understandings of sentient beings.
All Buddhas eternally abide in right concentration; in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places, preaching all dharmas as the true limit (bhūtakoṭi) free from desire.
All Buddhas eternally abide in right concentration; in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places, expounding the self-nature of all dependent origination.

All Buddhas eternally abide in right concentration; in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places, manifesting the vast adornments of immeasurable mundane and supramundane realms, causing all sentient beings to constantly behold the Buddha.

All Buddhas eternally abide in right concentration; in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places, causing all sentient beings to fully penetrate all Buddha-dharmas and immeasurable liberations, ultimately reaching the unsurpassed shore.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of unimpeded liberation."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
all Buddhas are able to manifest within a single atom unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas appearing in the world;
All Buddhas are able, within a single atom, to manifest unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas turning the pure wheel of Dharma;
all Buddhas are able, within a single atom, to manifest unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings receiving transformation and being tamed;
all Buddhas are able, within a single atom, to manifest unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands.
All Buddhas are able to manifest, within a single atom, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of bodhisattvas receiving their predictions of enlightenment;
all Buddhas are able to manifest, within a single atom, all Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
all Buddhas are able to manifest, within a single atom, all world-systems of the past, future, and present.
All Buddhas are able to manifest all supernatural powers of the past, future, and present within a single atom;
all Buddhas are able to manifest all sentient beings of the past, future, and present within a single atom;
all Buddhas are able to manifest all Buddha-activities of the past, future, and present within a single atom.
"These are the ten.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 47;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 48.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Thirty-Four: The Ocean of Marks of the Ten Bodies of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!
I shall now expound for you the ocean of marks possessed by the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!”
Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head are thirty-two marks of a Great Man adorned with jewels.

Among these is a mark of a Great Man named "Illuminating All Directions by Universally Emitting Immeasurable Nets of Great Radiance. It is adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels; its hair is pervasive, soft, and dense, each strand emitting the light of *maṇi* jewels that fills all boundless worlds, manifesting the physical forms and perfect characteristics of the Buddha's body throughout them. This is the first.
Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of the Radiance of the Buddha-Eye;

adorned with various kinds of mani-jewel kings, it emits golden light like the radiance emitted from the tuft of hair between the eyebrows. This light universally illumines all worlds; this is the second.

Next is a mark of a great person named Cloud Filling the Dharma Realm, adorned with exquisite jewel wheels that emit the lamp-light of the Tathāgata’s merit and wisdom, universally illuminating all oceans of worlds throughout the dharma realms of the ten directions, wherein all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are universally manifested; this is the third.

Next there is a mark of a great man called Manifesting Universal Radiance Clouds, adorned with various kinds of true gold and mani-jewels; all these exquisite jewels emit light that illuminates inconceivable Buddha-lands, wherein all Buddhas appear. This is the fourth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud Emitting Precious Radiance, adorned with the purity of the sovereign maṇi-jewel and having lapis lazuli as its stamens; its light illuminates all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, universally manifesting various spiritual transformations therein and praising the wisdom and merit practiced by the Tathāgata in the past. This is the fifth.

Next is a mark of a great man called the Cloud of the Great Sovereignty of the Tathāgata Pervading the Dharma Realm. It has as its crown the jewel-flame maṇi of the bodhisattva’s spiritual transformations; it possesses as its garland the wheel of jewel-flame light that awakens one to the powers of the Tathāgata; its light universally illumines the worlds of the ten directions, therein manifesting all Tathāgatas seated at the site of enlightenment, with clouds of omniscience filling the void and the infinite dharma realm. This is the sixth.
Next is a mark of a great man called the Tathāgata’s Universal Lamp Cloud;

it is adorned by a great sovereign ocean of jewels that causes the lands of the dharma-realm to tremble, emitting pure light that fills the dharma-realm, within which the oceans of merit of all bodhisattvas of the ten directions and the oceans of the wisdom-flags of the Buddhas of the past, present, and future are universally manifested. This is the seventh.

Next is a mark of a great man called "Universal Illumination of the Vast Clouds of All Buddhas," adorned with Indra-ratnas, wish-fulfilling king jewels, and mani king jewels. It constantly emits the radiant light of the flaming lamps of bodhisattvas, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions. Within it appear the ocean of the various physical forms of all buddhas, the ocean of their great sounds, and the ocean of their pure powers; this is the eighth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Perfect Radiance, adorned with various jewel flowers made of exquisite lapis lazuli and king of maṇi jewels. All manner of precious gems extend great networks of flames that fill the ten directions; all sentient beings in all worlds see the Tathāgata sitting before them, praising the merits of the dharma-body of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and causing them to enter the pure realm of the Tathāgata. This is the ninth.

Next is a mark of a great man called "Universal Radiance Cloud of the Treasury of Bodhisattva Practices," adorned with exquisite flowers of various jewels. Its jewel-light universally illuminates immeasurable worlds, its jewel-flames universally cover all lands, and it penetrates the dharma-realm of the ten directions without obstruction. It vibrates with the Buddha’s voice, proclaiming the vast ocean of Dharma; this is the tenth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Universal Radiant Illumination, adorned with *vaiḍūrya*, *indra*, and *vajra-maṇi* jewels. The light and color of the *vaiḍūrya* jewels are clear and penetrating, universally illuminating all oceans of worlds and emitting sublime sounds that fill the Dharma-realm. All such things are manifested from the ocean of great merit and wisdom of all Buddhas; this is the eleventh.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment, adorned with various jewel flowers. All these jewel flowers emit radiance, and within them, Tathāgatas sit at their sites of enlightenment, filling all boundless worlds and causing all worlds to become universally pure, forever severing all false conceptualizations and discriminations; this is the twelfth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Radiant Illumination, adorned with ocean-like heart-kings of mani-jewels from the treasury of jewel-flames. It emits great light, within which appear immeasurable bodhisattvas and the practices they perform; the oceans of all Tathāgatas’ bodies of wisdom, dharma-bodies, and various physical forms fill the entire Dharma-realm. This is the thirteenth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud Adorned with Universal Radiance, which is adorned with diamond flowers and lapis lazuli jewels; it emits great light, within which are great jewel lotus thrones, fully adorned and pervading the entire Dharma-realm, spontaneously proclaiming the four practices of bodhisattvas, their sound reaching throughout the oceans of all Dharma-realms—this is the fourteenth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of the Ocean-like Practice of Manifesting the Samādhi of the Buddha, which in a single thought-moment manifests the infinite adornments of the Tathāgata, universally adorning all inconceivable oceans of worlds throughout the entire Dharma-realm; this is the fifteenth.

Next is a mark of a great man named Cloud Universally Illuminating the Ocean of Transformations; it is adorned with exquisite jewel lotuses as large as Mount Sumeru, and the radiance of various jewels arises from the Buddha’s vows, manifesting infinite transformations without end. This is the sixteenth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Liberation of All Tathāgatas, adorned with pure and wondrous jewels, emitting great radiance that adorns all the lion seats of the Buddhas, manifesting the physical forms of all Buddhas as well as the infinite Buddha-dharmas and oceans of Buddha-lands; this is the seventeenth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Sovereign Expedient Means Universally Illuminating, adorned with *vaiḍūrya* flowers, true-gold lotuses, king-of-mani lamps, and clouds of the flames of the wondrous Dharma. It emits the pure light of the dense clouds of jewel-flames of all Buddhas, filling the entire dharma-realm, and within it universally manifests all manner of exquisite ornaments; this is the eighteenth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Awakening to the Buddha-lineage, adorned with immeasurable jewel-lights, complete with a thousand-spoked wheel, pure both within and without, born from roots of goodness cultivated in the past. Its light shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions, giving rise to the sun of wisdom and proclaiming the ocean of Dharma; this is the nineteenth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Sovereignty Manifesting the Marks of All Tathāgatas, adorned with necklaces of various jewels and beryl flowers. It extends great jewel-flames that fill the Dharma-realm, within which are universally manifested infinite Buddhas of the past, future, and present, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields. Like lion kings, they are courageous and fearless, fully endowed with physical marks and wisdom; this is the twentieth.
Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud Illuminating the Entire Dharma Realm;

it is adorned with the pure and magnificent jewel-marks of a Tathāgata, emitting great radiance that universally illumines the dharma realm and manifests the wondrous treasury of wisdom of all infinite and boundless Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. This is the twenty-first.

Next is a mark of a great man called the Cloud of the Tathāgata Vairocana’s Marks, adorned with exquisite jewel flowers and pure, wonderful moons of lapis lazuli. It emits immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of lights from mani jewels, filling all of space and the dharma-realm. Within it, immeasurable buddha-fields are manifested, each containing a Tathāgata sitting in the full lotus posture; this is the twenty-second.

Next is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Light Shining Universally upon All Buddhas," adorned with exquisite lamps made of various jewels. It emits pure radiance that shines throughout all worlds in the ten directions, manifesting all Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma; this is the twenty-third.

Next is a mark of a great man called "Universal Manifestation of All Clouds of Adornments," adorned with various jewel flames that emit pure light filling the dharma-realm. In every thought-moment, it constantly manifests unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas seated at their sites of enlightenment; this is the twenty-fourth.
Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Sounds Emanating from All Dharma Realms;

it is adorned with oceans of mani jewels and exquisite sandalwood, extending a vast net of flames that fills the dharma realm, wherein subtle and wondrous sounds are universally proclaimed to reveal to all sentient beings the ocean of all karmas—this is the twenty-fifth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud Universally Illuminating the Transformation Wheels of All Buddhas, adorned by the Tathāgata’s pure eyes. Its light shines upon all worlds in the ten directions, universally manifesting within them all the various ornaments possessed by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present. Furthermore, it emits wondrous sounds that expound the inconceivable and vast ocean of Dharma; this is the twenty-sixth.

Next is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of the Buddha-Ocean Illumined by Light. Its radiance universally illumines all worlds throughout the entire dharma-realm without obstruction; within it, there are Tathāgatas sitting cross-legged everywhere. This is the twenty-seventh.

Next is a mark of a great man called Jewel Lamp Cloud, which emits the vast radiance of the Tathāgata, universally illuminating all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions; within it, there are universally manifested all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as inconceivable oceans of sentient beings—this is the twenty-eighth.
Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Non-differentiation of the Dharma Realm;

it emits the light of the Tathāgata’s great wisdom, universally illuminating the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, all the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of bodhisattvas, and the infinite oceans of Dharma. Within these, it manifests various kinds of spiritual powers and produces wondrous sounds that, according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, expound the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, causing them to dedicate their merit. This is the twenty-ninth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud Universally Illuminating All Worlds-Oceans Abiding Securely, which emits jewel-light that fills all space and the dharma-realm; within it, pure and wondrous sites of enlightenment and the adorned physical forms of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas appear everywhere, causing those who see them to attain the state of "seeing nothing. This is the thirtieth.

Next is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Pure Radiant Flames of All Jewels, which emits immeasurable pure light from mani-jewels of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, universally illuminating all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions. Within it, oceans of Bodhisattvas appear everywhere, all fully endowed with the spiritual powers of the Tathāgatas, constantly roaming through the entire network of lands throughout the void of space in the ten directions; this is the thirty-first.

Next is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Adornments Universally Illuminating the Entire Dharma Realm," situated at the very center, gradually rising upward. It is adorned with Jāmbūnada gold and Indra-nets, emitting clouds of pure light that fill the dharma realm. In every thought-moment, it constantly manifests the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in all worlds; this is the thirty-second.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head, there are thirty-two such marks of a Great Man (mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa) that serve as his adornment.
O Son of the Buddha!"

Between the eyebrows of the Tathāgata is a mark of greatness called Cloud of Light Pervading the Dharma Realm, adorned with mani-jewel flowers. It radiates great light, possessing the colors of all jewels; it is as transparent and pure as the sun and moon. This light universally illumines the lands of the ten directions, within which the bodies of all Buddhas are manifested, and from which wonderful sounds emerge to proclaim the ocean of the Dharma. This is the thirty-third.
The Tathāgata’s eye possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of Sovereign Universal Vision;
it is adorned with various exquisite jewels, and the light of its mani-gems is pure and translucent, seeing all things everywhere without obstruction. This is the thirty-fourth.
The Tathāgata’s nose possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of All Supernormal Powers and Wisdom.

It is adorned with pure and wondrous jewels, and the radiance of various precious gems completely covers it. Within this, immeasurable transformation Buddhas appear, seated upon precious lotus flowers, traveling to all worlds to expound the inconceivable ocean of the Buddha-dharma for all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings; this is the thirty-fifth.

The Tathāgata’s tongue possesses a mark of a great man called "Cloud Manifesting the Reflections of Sound," adorned with various colors and exquisite jewels, accomplished through the roots of goodness cultivated in past lives. His tongue is broad and long, completely covering all oceans of worlds. Whenever the Tathāgata smiles joyfully, he invariably emits the light of all *maṇi* jewels; this light shines universally throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions, enabling the minds of all beings to attain cool serenity. All Buddhas of the past, future, and present appear vividly within that light, all intoning vast and subtle sounds that pervade all lands for immeasurable eons. This is the thirty-sixth [mark].
The Tathāgata’s tongue further possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of the Dharma Realm;

its surface is flat and even, adorned with various jewels, emitting wondrous jewel-light of perfect color and form, just like the light emitted from between his eyebrows. This light universally illumines all Buddha-lands, which are composed solely of dust and lack intrinsic nature. Within this light, moreover, appear immeasurable Buddhas, all of whom emit sublime sounds to expound all dharmas. This is the thirty-seventh.
The Tathāgata’s tongue-tip possesses a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Radiance Illumining the Dharma Realm.

It is adorned with the king of wish-fulfilling jewels and naturally and constantly emits golden jewel-flames, within which the oceans of all Buddhas are reflected. Furthermore, it vibrates with wondrous sounds that fill all boundless worlds; within each sound, every possible sound is contained, all expounding the sublime Dharma so that listeners’ hearts rejoice. They savor and contemplate it for immeasurable eons without forgetting. This is the thirty-eighth [mark].
Furthermore, on the tip of the Tathāgata’s tongue is another mark of a great man called Cloud Illuminating the Dharma Realm.

It is adorned with the sovereign king of mani jewels, which radiates subtle light of manifold colors and forms that fills the infinite lands of the ten directions. Throughout the entire dharma realm, there is nothing that is not purified; within it, there are all manner of infinite Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, each emitting sublime sounds to provide various teachings and revelations. All Bodhisattvas receive these teachings directly before them. This is the thirty-ninth mark.
On the upper palate of the Tathāgata’s mouth is a mark of a great man called "Cloud Manifesting the Inconceivable Dharma Realm.

It is adorned with Indra-blue jewels and lapis lazuli, emitting clouds of pure light from the flames of fragrant lamps that fill all dharma realms throughout the ten directions. It manifests various supernatural powers and skillful means, universally expounding the profound and inconceivable Dharma across all oceans of worlds; this is the fortieth.
On the lower tooth of the right molar of the Tathāgata’s mouth there is a mark of a great man, named Buddha-tooth Cloud.

It is adorned with wheels of various precious maṇi jewels in the shape of the svastika, emitting great light that universally illumines the Dharma-realm. Within it, the bodies of all Buddhas are universally manifested, circulating throughout the ten directions to awaken all living beings; this is the forty-first.
On the upper right molar of the Tathāgata’s mouth is a mark of a great man called Jewel-Flame Sumeru-Treasury Cloud.

It is adorned with a treasury of *maṇi* jewels and emits pure light from vajra-fragrant flames. Each ray of light fills the entire Dharma-realm, manifesting the spiritual powers of all Buddhas and further revealing the pure and wondrous sites of enlightenment in all worlds of the ten directions; this is the forty-second.
On the lower left molar of the Tathāgata’s mouth is a mark of a great man called Jewel Lamp Universally Illuminating Cloud.

It is adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels that unfurl flowers and emit fragrances; it radiates clouds of lamp-flame light and pure brilliance that fill all oceans of worlds, within which appear all Buddhas seated upon lion thrones in the Lotus Treasury, surrounded by assemblies of bodhisattvas. This is the forty-third.
On the upper left molar of the Tathāgata’s mouth there is a mark of a great man, named "Tathāgata-Cloud Manifesting Radiance.

It is adorned with pure light, Jambūnada gold, jewel nets, and precious flowers. It emits great wheels of flame that fill the Dharma-realm, within which all Buddhas are universally manifested. By means of supernormal powers, it distributes the milk of the Dharma, the lamp of the Dharma, and the jewels of the Dharma throughout the void, teaching and transforming the assembly of all Bodhisattvas; this is the forty-fourth.
The Tathāgata’s teeth possess a mark of a great man called "Cloud Universally Manifesting Radiance.

Each space between the teeth is adorned with an ocean of marks; when he smiles, they all emit light, possessing the colors of various jewels and the blazing flames of *maṇi* gems that swirl and turn to the right. This radiance spreads throughout the Dharma-realm, filling it entirely, as he utters the Buddha’s voice to proclaim the practices of Samantabhadra. This is the forty-fifth.

The Tathāgata’s lips possess a mark of a great man called "Manifesting Clouds of All Jewel Radiance," which emits vast light in the colors of Jambūnada gold, lotus, and all kinds of jewels, illuminating the entire Dharma-realm and causing it to be completely purified; this is the forty-sixth.

“The Tathāgata’s neck possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Illumining All Worlds,’ adorned with the king of *maṇi* jewels. It is formed of deep blue lotus fibers, soft, supple, and smooth, emitting the pure light of Vairocana that fills all worlds throughout the ten directions, within which all Buddhas are universally manifested. This is the forty-seventh.
On the Tathāgata’s right shoulder is a mark of a great man called Buddha’s Vast Cloud of All Jewels;

it emits light of all jewel colors, true gold color, and lotus-petal color, forming a net of jewel flames that universally illumines the Dharma-realm, within which all bodhisattvas are everywhere manifested—this is the forty-eighth.
On the Tathāgata’s right shoulder there is another mark of a great man called "Cloud of the Most Victorious Jewel Universally Illuminating.
Its color is pure like Jambu-river gold, emitting mani-jewel light that fills the Dharma-realm, within which all bodhisattvas are universally manifested; this is the forty-ninth.
On the Tathāgata’s left shoulder is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Supreme Light Illuminating the Dharma Realm.

Just as his crown and the space between his eyebrows are variously adorned, it emits multitudes of jewel-lights in the colors of Jambūnada gold and lotuses, forming a great web of flames that fills the dharma realm. Within it, he manifests all spiritual powers; this is the fiftieth.
On the Tathāgata’s left shoulder there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Pervasive Radiance.

This mark spirals to the right and is adorned with sovereign maṇi-jewels of Jambūnada gold. It emits the light of flaming blossoms and fragrances of various jewels, filling the entire Dharma-realm. Within it, all Buddhas and all pure, adorned lands are universally manifested. This is the fifty-first.
On the Tathāgata’s left shoulder there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Universal Radiance;

this mark spirals to the right, is subtly and densely adorned, and emits the pure light of clouds of Buddha-lamp flames that pervade the entire Dharma-realm. Within it appear all the various adornments of all bodhisattvas, each exquisitely beautiful. This is the fifty-second.
On the chest of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man, shaped like a svastika, named Auspicious Ocean Cloud.

It is adorned with mani-jewel flowers and emits various wheels of light-flames in all jewel colors, filling the dharma-realm and universally purifying it. Furthermore, it produces wondrous sounds that proclaim the ocean of Dharma; this is the fifty-third.

To the right of the auspicious mark is a mark of greatness called "Cloud Manifesting Radiant Light," adorned with Indra’s net. It emits great circles of light that fill the dharma-realm, within which immeasurable Buddhas are universally manifested; this is the fifty-fourth.
To the right of the auspicious marks, there is another mark of a great man called "Universal Manifestation Clouds of Tathāgatas.

It is adorned with the mani-jewel crowns of all bodhisattvas and emits great light that universally illuminates all worlds in the ten directions, causing them all to become pure. Within it, the Buddhas of the past, future, and present are manifested sitting at their sites of enlightenment, universally manifesting spiritual powers and extensively proclaiming the ocean of Dharma; this is the fifty-fifth.

To the right of the auspicious mark, there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Blooming Flowers, adorned with mani-jewel flowers. It emits the pure radiance of jewel-fragrant flame-lamps, appearing like lotus blossoms that fill the worlds; this is the fifty-sixth.

To the right of the auspicious mark, there is another mark of a great man called "Delightful Golden Cloud," adorned with the heart-king treasury of all jewels and the king of maṇi-jewels. It emits pure light that illuminates the dharma-realm, within which it universally manifests like the vast and radiant light of the Buddha-eye maṇi-jewel treasury; this is the fifty-seventh.
To the right of the auspicious mark, there is another mark of a great man called Buddha-Ocean-Cloud (*buddha-sāgara-megha*).

It is adorned with Vaiḍūrya jewels, incense lamps, and flower garlands, emitting the pure radiance of great flames from incense lamps of the sovereign maṇi-jewel kings that fill the void of space. This light pervades all lands throughout the ten directions, universally manifesting within them the assemblies at sites of enlightenment; this is the fifty-eighth.
To the left of the auspicious mark is a mark of greatness called Manifesting Clouds of Radiance.

It is adorned by countless bodhisattvas seated upon precious lotus flowers, emitting various intermingled jewel-flame radiances from mani-kings that universally purify all oceans of dharma realms. Within these, they manifest infinite buddhas and the sublime voices of those buddhas expounding all dharmas; this is the fifty-ninth.

To the left of the auspicious mark, there is another mark of a great man called "Manifesting Clouds of Light Pervading the Entire Dharma Realm," adorned with oceans of mani jewels. It emits great radiance that pervades all lands, within which the assemblies of all bodhisattvas are universally manifested; this is the sixtieth.

To the left of the auspicious mark, there is another mark of a great man called Universal Victorious Cloud, adorned with a jeweled wheel garland of sun-bright mani-kings; it emits great flames of light that fill the oceans of worlds throughout the Dharma-realm, within which all worlds, all Tathāgatas, and all sentient beings are manifested—this is the sixty-first.
To the left of the auspicious mark, there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Wondrous Sounds Turning the Wheel of Dharma.

It is adorned with the pure fragrant filaments of the lamps of all dharmas and emits great radiance that fills the dharma-realm. Within it, the oceans of marks and the oceans of minds of all Buddhas are universally manifested; this is the sixty-second.
To the left of the auspicious mark, there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Adornments.

It is adorned by the oceans of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present; it emits pure light that purifies and adorns all Buddha-lands, and within them, it universally manifests all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, as well as the practices performed by those Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. This is the sixty-third.

“The Tathāgata’s right hand has a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Illuminating the Ocean,’ adorned with various jewels, which constantly emits pure light like lunar flames that fills all worlds throughout space, and utters a great sound praising the practices of all Bodhisattvas; this is the sixty-fourth.

The Tathāgata’s right hand further possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of Manifesting Radiance, adorned with *vaiḍūrya*, indranīla, and maṇi-jewel flowers. It emits great light that universally illuminates all worlds—such as the Lotus Treasury and Maṇi Treasury worlds—in which the bodhisattvas dwell throughout the ten directions. Within these, it manifests infinite Buddhas sitting beneath Bodhi trees with pure Dharma-bodies, shaking all lands in the ten directions; this is the sixty-fifth.
The Tathāgata’s right hand further possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud Universally Adorned and Purified by a Garland of Lamp Flames.

It is adorned with Vairocana jewels, emitting great radiance that forms a net of transformations, within which all the hosts of bodhisattvas are universally manifested; they all wear jeweled crowns and expound the ocean of all practices. This is the sixty-sixth.

The Tathāgata’s right hand further possesses a mark of a great man called "Universal Manifestation of All Jewel Clouds," adorned with lotus-flame lamps that emit ocean-treasury light pervading the entire Dharma-realm; within this light, infinite Buddhas are universally manifested sitting upon lotus thrones—this is the sixty-seventh.
The Tathāgata’s right hand further possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of Radiance, adorned with an ocean of mani-jewel flames.

It emits pure light from multitudes of jewel-flames, incense-flames, and flower-flames, filling all the networks of worlds. Within these, the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas are universally manifested; this is the sixty-eighth.

The Tathāgata’s left hand possesses a mark of a great man called "Pure Lamp Cloud of Vaiḍūrya," adorned with the exquisite colors of precious ground; it emits the golden radiance of the Tathāgata and constantly manifests all manner of supreme and wondrous ornaments in every thought-moment. This is the sixty-ninth.

Furthermore, on the Tathāgata’s left hand there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Sounds of the Wisdom Lamp of All Lands, adorned with Indra-nets and diamond flowers, emitting the pure radiance of Jāmbūnada gold that universally illumines all worlds in the ten directions; this is the seventieth.

Furthermore, on the Tathāgata’s left hand there is another mark of a great man called "Cloud of Radiant Light Resting upon a Jewel Lotus," adorned with exquisite flowers of various jewels. It emits great light like the Lamp of Mount Sumeru, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions; this is the seventy-first.
The Tathāgata’s left hand further possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud Illuminating the Dharma Realm.

It is adorned with exquisite jewel garlands, jewel wheels, jewel vases, Indra-nets, and various wondrous signs. It emits great radiance that universally illumines all lands throughout the ten directions, within which it manifests all dharma realms, all oceans of worlds, and all Tathāgatas seated upon lotus thrones; this is the seventy-second.

On the right hand of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Revolving Oceans of Lands and Kalpas Manifesting All," adorned with all kinds of jewel flowers from the water-moon-flame-treasury maṇi-kings. It emits great light that fills the dharma-realm, and from within it constantly issue forth subtle and wondrous sounds that fill the lands of the ten directions; this is the seventy-third.

On the left hand of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Abiding in All Jewel Clouds," adorned with indranīla and vajra jewels. It emits the light of various jewels from the king of maṇis, filling the entire Dharma-realm, within which all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are universally manifested; this is the seventy-fourth.

On the palm of the Tathāgata’s right hand is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Radiance," adorned with a thousand-spoked jewel wheel of *maṇi* kings. It emits precious light that spirals to the right and fills the entire Dharma-realm; within it, all Buddhas appear universally, each Buddha’s body ablaze with radiant flames, preaching the Dharma to deliver beings and purifying all worlds. This is the seventy-fifth.

On the palm of the Tathāgata’s left hand is a mark of a great man called "The Blazing Wheel Universally Increasing and Manifesting Clouds of Dharma-Field Maṇḍalas. It is adorned with thousand-spoked wheels of sun-light maṇi-kings and emits great radiance that fills all oceans of worlds. Within it, he manifests all bodhisattvas and expounds the ocean of all practices of Samantabhadra; they universally enter all Buddha-lands, each awakening immeasurable sentient beings. This is the seventy-sixth.

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of a great man known as the ‘Universal Emanation of Clouds of Buddha-Sounds from the Sheathed Genitals,’ adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels. It emits the radiant light of mani-lamp flower-flames; this light is fiercely blazing, endowed with the colors of all kinds of jewels, and universally illumines the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm. Within it, the travels and comings and goings of all Buddhas are everywhere manifested throughout. This is the seventy-seventh [mark].”
On the Tathāgata’s right hip is a mark of a great man called Jewel Lamp Garland Universal Illumination Cloud.

Adorned with various maṇi jewels, it emits inconceivable jewel-flame radiance that spreads throughout all dharma-realms in the ten directions. It shares a single characteristic with the space-dharma realm, yet is able to produce all manner of marks; within each and every mark, the sovereign spiritual transformations of all Buddhas are fully manifested. This is the seventy-eighth.

On the Tathāgata’s left hip is a mark of a great man called Cloud Manifesting the Radiance that Pervades All Oceans of the Dharma Realm and Envelops Space. It is like a lotus flower, adorned with pure and wondrous jewels, emitting networks of light that shine throughout all dharma realms of the ten directions. Within them, clouds of various forms appear everywhere; this is the seventy-ninth.

On the Tathāgata’s right thigh is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Universal Manifestation, adorned with mani-jewels of myriad colors. His thigh and calf are in perfect proportion, emitting the wondrous Dharma-light of mani-flames; in a single thought-moment, he can universally manifest the ocean of marks of the gait of all jewel-kings. This is the eightieth.
On the Tathāgata’s left thigh is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of the Infinite Ocean of Marks Manifesting All Buddhas.

It is adorned by all oceans of jewels arranged in harmonious order; it traverses vast distances, radiating pure light that universally illumines sentient beings, causing them all to aspire to the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma. This is the eighty-first.
On the right side of the Tathāgata’s leg, above the hams of the king of eneya deer, there is a mark of a great man called Cloud of All Dharmadhātus of Empty Space.

It is adorned with exquisite jewels of radiant light; its form is perfectly round and straight, enabling him to stride with grace. It emits pure, Jambu-river gold-colored light that shines throughout all Buddha-worlds, producing a great sound that causes them all to tremble. Furthermore, it manifests all Buddha-lands, abiding in space adorned with jewel flames, from which immeasurable bodhisattvas are miraculously manifested. This is the eighty-second [mark].
On the left side of the Tathāgata’s leg, at the calf of the Enīya Deer King, there is a mark of a great man called Ocean Cloud of Adornments.

Its color is like genuine gold; it can travel throughout all Buddha-fields, emitting pure light of all kinds of jewels that fills the Dharma-realm and performs the work of a Buddha. This is the eighty-third.
The Tathāgata’s precious calves possess the mark of a great man called Cloud Universally Manifesting the Images of the Dharma Realm;

these hairs curl to the right, and from the tip of each hair is emitted a jewel-light that fills all dharma realms throughout the ten directions, manifesting the spiritual powers of all Buddhas. From all his pores, light is likewise emitted, within which all Buddha-lands appear. This is the eighty-fourth [mark].
“Beneath the feet of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Abiding in the Ocean of All Bodhisattvas.

Its color is like vajra and pure Jambūnada-gold lotus; it emits jewel radiance that universally illumines the oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions. Clouds of precious incense flames pervade everywhere; when he lifts his foot to take a step, the fragrance circulates, possessing the colors of all jewels and filling the Dharma-realm. This is the eighty-fifth [mark].”

Upon the Tathāgata’s right foot is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Universal Radiance Illumining All," adorned with all kinds of precious jewels; it emits great light that fills the Dharma-realm and manifests all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. This is the eighty-sixth.

Upon the Tathāgata’s left foot is a mark of a great man called "Universal Manifestation of the Clouds of All Buddhas," adorned with *maṇi* jewels from the treasury of treasures. It radiates precious light, and in every thought-moment it manifests the supernatural transformations and powers of all Buddhas, as well as their oceans of Dharma and the sites of enlightenment where they sit, continuing without interruption throughout all kalpas until the end of the future; this is the eighty-seventh.

Between the toes of the Tathāgata’s right foot is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Light Illuminating All Dharma Realms and Oceans," adorned with various ornaments such as the thousand-spoked flaming wheel of the Sumeru Lamp Mani King. It emits great light that fills all world-oceans throughout the ten directions of all dharma realms, universally manifesting therein all the various jewel-adorned marks of all Buddhas; this is the eighty-eighth [mark].
Between the toes of the Tathāgata’s left foot is a mark of a great man called "Manifesting the Ocean-Clouds of All Buddhas.

It is adorned with mani-jewel flowers, fragrant flames, garlands of lamps, and all kinds of jewel wheels. It constantly emits the pure radiance of a jewel-ocean that fills the void and reaches all worlds throughout the ten directions. Within it, it manifests the perfect voices, the svastika symbols, and other marks of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, benefiting immeasurable sentient beings. This is the eighty-ninth [mark].

On the right heel of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Sovereign Radiance, adorned with indranīla gems and powdered jewels. It constantly emits the wondrous jewel-light of the Tathāgata; this light is exquisite and fills the Dharma-realm, all of one single characteristic without distinction. Within it are manifested all Buddhas seated at the site of enlightenment, expounding the sublime Dharma. This is the ninety-first [mark].

On the left heel of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Manifesting the Ocean-Cloud of All Dharmas through the Proclamation of Sublime Sounds. It is adorned with oceans of transformation maṇi-jewels, Sumeru-flower maṇi-jewels of fragrant flames, and lapis lazuli. It emits great radiance that fills the Dharma-realm, within which the spiritual powers of all Buddhas are universally manifested. This is the ninety-first.
On the right foot of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Radiant Light Manifesting All Adornments.

It is composed of various jewels, exquisitely adorned, and emits pure light the color of Jambūnada gold that universally illumines all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions. The appearance of this light is like a great cloud, universally covering the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas; this is the ninety-second [mark].
On the sole of the Tathāgata’s left foot is a mark of a great man called Cloud Manifesting All Colors and Forms.

It is adorned with Vairocana-jewel of the treasury of all lunar flames and Indra-nīla jewels. Moment by moment, it travels through the oceans of all dharma-realms, emitting the radiant light of mani-lamp incense-flames; this light pervades and fills all dharma-realms. This is the ninety-third.

Around the circumference of the Tathāgata’s right foot is a mark of a great man called Universal Treasury Cloud (*Samantagarbha-megha*), adorned with indranīla vajra-jewels that emit jewel-light filling the void of space; within this light appear all Buddhas seated upon lion-thrones of the king of maṇi-jewels at their sites of enlightenment. This is the ninety-fourth.

Around the circumference of the Tathāgata’s left foot is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Light Universally Illuminating the Dharma Realm, adorned with mani-jewel flowers. It emits great radiance that fills the dharma realm as a single mark of equality, within which are manifested the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas and bodhisattvas. With a great and wondrous voice, it expounds the inexhaustible dharma-gates of the dharma realm; this is the ninety-fifth.
On the tip of the Tathāgata’s right toe is a mark of a great man called "Cloud Manifesting Adornments.

It is most lovely and delightful, adorned with pure Jambūnada gold. It emits great light that fills all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, within which are manifested the various merits, spiritual powers, and transformations of the inexhaustible ocean of dharmas of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. This is the ninety-sixth.
On the tip of the Tathāgata’s left toe is a mark of a great man called "Cloud Manifesting the Spiritual Transformations of All Buddhas.

It is adorned with inconceivable Buddha-radiance, moon-flames, universal fragrance, and wheels of mani-jewel flames, emitting pure light of various jewel colors that fills all oceans of worlds. Within it, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are manifested, expounding the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas; this is the ninety-seventh.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Vairocana Tathāgata possesses such great marks of a superior person (mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa) as numerous as the atoms within ten Flower Treasury World-Oceans;
each and every part of his body is adorned with the wondrous signs of various jewels.”
Chapter 35: The Merit of the Tathāgata’s Minor Marks and Radiance. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has a secondary mark (anuvyañjana) named "Perfect King.
From within this secondary mark, a great radiance issues forth, which is named:
Blazing and intense, with seven million asaṃkhyeya rays of light as its retinue.
Son of the Buddha!
When I was a bodhisattva, I emitted a great light from the Tuṣita heaven palace, named:
King Radiant Banner illuminates worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields.

Among the sentient beings in the hells within those worlds, those who encounter this light find all their sufferings stilled and obtain ten kinds of pure eyes; their ears, noses, tongues, bodies, and minds are likewise transformed. All of them give rise to joy, leaping for gladness and celebrating, and upon the end of their lives there, they are reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
In that heaven there is a drum named "Extremely Delightful.
Once those devas have been born there, this drum emits a sound and addresses them, saying:
"O sons of the gods!
Because you have been heedful in mind, you have planted various roots of goodness under the Tathāgata and have in the past drawn near to many spiritual friends."
"By the great majestic spiritual power of Vairocana, he passed away from that life and was reborn in this heaven.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The thousand-spoked wheels on the soles of the Bodhisattva’s feet are named:"
The Universal Radiance King has a secondary mark called "Perfect King," which constantly emits forty kinds of light.
Among them is a light named Pure Merit,

which can illuminate worlds as numerous as the atoms within billions of nayutas of Buddha-lands, causing all sentient beings— according to their various karmic actions and various inclinations— to reach maturity.
Sentient beings in the Avīci Hell who encounter this light all reach the end of their lives and are reborn in Tuṣita Heaven.
Once reborn there, they hear the sound of celestial drums proclaiming to them:
"Excellent, excellent!
"O sons of the gods!
You should pay homage to the Bodhisattva Vairocana, who has entered the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement.
At that time, having heard these exhortations from the sound of the celestial drum, all the sons of the gods conceived this thought:
"How marvelous and rare!
For what reason has this sublime sound been produced?
At that time, the celestial drum addressed the devaputras, saying:
"The voice I have uttered is accomplished through the power of all roots of goodness.
O sons of the gods!
Just as I speak of a 'self,' yet I do not cling to a self, nor do I cling to what belongs to a self; "
All Buddhas are likewise; though they call themselves Buddhas, they do not cling to a self, nor do they cling to what belongs to a self.
O sons of the gods!
Just as my voice does not come from the east, nor from the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, or from above or below;
The attainment of Buddhahood through the retribution of karma is likewise not something that comes from the ten directions.
O sons of the gods!

For example, when you were formerly in hell, neither the hell nor your body came from the ten directions; rather, it was due to your inverted evil karma and the fetters of ignorance that you gave rise to a body in hell, which has no root and no place of origin.
"O sons of the gods!
It is by the power of the majestic virtue of the Bodhisattva Vairocana that this great radiance is emitted; yet this radiance does not come from the ten directions, O sons of the gods!"

My celestial drum sound is likewise: it does not come from the ten directions, but by the power of the roots of goodness of samādhi and the majestic power of the prajñāpāramitā, it produces such pure sounds and manifests such various forms of mastery.
"O sons of the gods!
For example, the King of Mountains, Sumeru, possesses the sublime palaces and various musical instruments of the Heaven of the Thirty-three; yet these instruments do not come from the ten directions.
My celestial drum-sound is likewise: it does not come from the ten directions."
"O sons of the gods!

Suppose all the worlds, numbering as many as the atoms in a hundred million nayutas of Buddha-fields, were ground into dust; for as many sentient beings as there are atoms in that dust, I preach the Dharma according to their inclinations, causing them great joy. Yet, toward them, I feel no weariness, no discouragement, no pride, and no negligence."
"O sons of the gods!

It is likewise for the Bodhisattva Vairocana when he dwells in the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement: from within a single secondary mark (anuvyañjana) upon his right palm, he emits a single ray of light that manifests immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers. Even all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas cannot know them, let alone ordinary sentient beings!"
"O sons of the gods!

You should go to where that bodhisattva is, attend upon him, and make offerings to him; do not again become greedily attached to the pleasures of the five desires, for attachment to the pleasures of the five desires obstructs all roots of goodness."
"O sons of the gods!
It is as if the kalpa-fire were to burn Mount Sumeru, utterly consuming it until nothing remains;
so too is it with greed that entangles the mind—it can never give rise to the thought of mindfulness of the Buddha."
O sons of the gods!
You should recognize kindness and repay it with gratitude.
O sons of the gods!
There are sentient beings who do not know how to repay kindness; they frequently meet with untimely deaths and are reborn in the hells.
O sons of the gods!
In the past, while you were within the hells, you were graced by this light shining upon your bodies, whereby you abandoned that place and were born here.
"You all should now swiftly dedicate [your merit] to increase your roots of goodness.
O sons of the gods!
Just as my celestial drum is neither male nor female, yet can produce immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable things; [so too should you]."
You, O son of heaven and daughter of heaven, are likewise thus: being neither male nor female, you are nevertheless able to enjoy various sublime palaces and gardens.
Just as my celestial drum is neither born nor extinguished, so too are form, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness neither born nor extinguished.
"If you are able to awaken to and understand this, you should know that you have entered the Samādhi of the Seal of Non-Reliance.

At that time, having heard these words, the sons of the gods experienced what they had never known before. They immediately manifested ten thousand clouds of flowers, ten thousand clouds of incense, ten thousand clouds of music, ten thousand clouds of banners, ten thousand clouds of canopies, and ten thousand clouds of songs and praises.

Having created these manifestations, they together proceeded to the palace where the Bodhisattva Vairocana resided. With palms joined in reverence, they stood to one side, desiring to behold him, yet they were unable to see him.
At that time, a certain son of heaven spoke these words:

"The Bodhisattva Vairocana has already passed away from here and been born into the human world in the house of King Śuddhodana; riding upon a sandalwood palatial pavilion, he dwells within the womb of Queen Māyā."

At that time, the sons of the gods, observing with their divine eyes, saw that the Bodhisattva’s body was dwelling in the human world within the house of King Śuddhodana, being served and honored by the Brahma and Desire Realm heavens.
The assembly of devaputras all thought to themselves:
"If we do not go to where the Bodhisattva is to inquire after his well-being, or even if we should give rise to a single moment of attachment to this celestial palace, it would be improper."
At that time, each of the sons of heaven, accompanied by a retinue of ten nayutas, was about to descend to Jambudvīpa.
Then, a voice issued from the celestial drum, proclaiming:
"O sons of heaven!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not pass away from this life to be reborn in that realm; rather, by means of their supernormal powers, they cause sentient beings to see them according to what is appropriate for each being's mind.
"O sons of the gods!
Just as I, at this moment, am not something seen by the eye yet am able to produce sound;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who enters the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement: he is not seen by the eye, yet is able to manifest birth in various places, free from discrimination, devoid of pride, and without attachment."
"O sons of the gods!

You should resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, purify your minds, abide in virtuous deportment, and repent to eliminate all karmic obstructions, afflictive obstructions, retributive obstructions, and obstructions of view.

With bodies as numerous as all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, with heads as numerous as all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, and with tongues as numerous as all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, you should, by means of as many virtuous physical, verbal, and mental actions as there are sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, repent and eliminate all obstructive faults and evils."
At that time, having heard these words, the sons of the gods attained what they had never experienced before; their hearts were filled with great joy, and they asked him, saying:
"How does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva repent and eliminate all faults and evils?"
At that time, by the power of the roots of goodness from the Bodhisattva’s samādhi, the celestial drum emitted a voice and proclaimed:
"O sons of the gods!

The Bodhisattva knows that all karmas do not come from the east, nor do they come from the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, or from above or below; yet they accumulate together and abide within the mind."
They arise solely from inversion and have no place of abiding.
Thus do Bodhisattvas clearly perceive with certainty, free from doubt.
O sons of the gods!
Just as my celestial drum proclaims karma, proclaims retribution, proclaims conduct, proclaims precepts, proclaims joy, proclaims peace, and proclaims various samādhis;

so too do the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas likewise proclaim "self," proclaim "what belongs to self," proclaim "sentient beings," and proclaim the various karmas of greed, anger, and delusion—yet in reality, there is no self and nothing that belongs to a self.
All karmic actions performed and the retributive fruits of the six realms of existence cannot be found when sought throughout the ten directions.
O sons of the gods!
It is like my voice, which is neither born nor extinguished; yet the devas who have committed evil do not hear any other sound, but hear only the voice that awakens them from the hells.
All karmic actions are likewise thus: they neither arise nor perish; yet, according to what is cultivated and accumulated, one receives their retribution.
O sons of the gods!
Just as the sounds produced by my celestial drum cannot be exhausted throughout immeasurable eons and are without interruption, yet neither coming nor going can be apprehended.
O sons of the gods!

If there were coming and going, there would be the extremes of annihilation and permanence; yet all Buddhas never preach a doctrine of annihilation or permanence, except as a skillful means to bring sentient beings to maturity.
"O sons of the gods!
Just as my voice, throughout immeasurable worlds, is heard by all sentient beings according to their respective mental dispositions;
so too it is with all Buddhas—they cause all sentient beings to behold them according to their respective mental dispositions."
"O sons of the gods!
It is as if there were a crystal mirror named 'Able to Reflect,' pure and transparently clear, equal in size to ten worlds;
Within all the immeasurable and boundless lands, the images of all mountains and rivers, all sentient beings, and even those in the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts, all appear therein.
"O sons of the gods! What do you think?
Can those various reflections be said to come into the mirror or go out from the mirror?"
He replied, "No, O sons of the gods. "Sons of the gods! [he continued].
All karmic actions are likewise so: although they can produce the fruits and retributions of karma, they have no place from which they come or to which they go.
O sons of the gods!
Just as a magician deceives the eyes of men with illusions, you should know that all karmic actions are likewise so.
"If one understands in this way, it is true repentance, and all evil deeds will become entirely purified.

When this Dharma was being taught, among the worlds as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, the devaputras of the Tuṣita Heaven attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti);
and immeasurable, inconceivable, and incalculable devaputras of the six desire realms resolved their minds toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
All the celestial maidens among the six heavens of the desire realm cast off their female bodies and resolved upon supreme bodhicitta.

At that time, having heard this exposition of Samantabhadra’s Vast Dedication, the sons of the gods attained the ten stages (*bhūmi*), acquired the samādhi adorned with all powers, and, through purifying their three karmas as many times as there are sentient beings, repented and eliminated all heavy obstacles. Thereupon, they beheld lotus flowers made of the seven precious gems, as numerous as the atoms within hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayuta* Buddha-fields;
upon each flower sat a bodhisattva in the full lotus posture, emitting great radiance.
From each of those secondary marks (*anuvyañjana*) of the bodhisattvas, rays of light equal in number to all sentient beings are emitted.

Within those rays of light, there are Buddhas equal in number to all sentient beings, sitting cross-legged and preaching the Dharma according to the minds of sentient beings; yet this is still but a small fraction of the power of the Stainless Samādhi (*vimala-samādhi*).

At that time, those devaputras, with the aforementioned various flowers, further manifested from each and every pore of their bodies clouds of exquisite flowers equal in number to all sentient beings, as an offering to Vairocana Tathāgata; they held them and scattered them over the Buddha, and they all came to rest upon the body of the Buddha.
Those clouds of incense rained down universally upon worlds as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-fields.

Any sentient beings whose bodies were touched by this fragrance experienced physical peace and bliss, just like a bhikṣu who has entered the fourth dhyāna; all their karmic obstructions were completely extinguished.

If there are those who hear this, those sentient beings will realize that regarding form, sound, fragrance, taste, and touch, they possess five hundred afflictions internally and five hundred afflictions externally: twenty-one thousand characterized by a predominance of greed, twenty-one thousand characterized by a predominance of hatred, twenty-one thousand characterized by a predominance of delusion, and twenty-one thousand characterized by equal proportions of these three; they will fully understand that all such things are entirely false and illusory.
Having known this, they accomplish the pure roots of goodness of the Sovereign Radiance of Fragrant Banner Clouds.
If there are sentient beings who see their canopy, they plant roots of goodness equal to one *gaṅgā*-sāgara of sands for each of the Pure Golden Net Universal Monarchs.
"O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva dwelling in this position of a Wheel-Turning King teaches and transforms sentient beings throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms within hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields."
O Son of the Buddha!

It is, for example, like the World-Honored One Candraprabhajñāna Tathāgata in the Mirror-like World, who constantly manifests his body within immeasurable worlds to appear before bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās to listen to the Dharma. He extensively expounds upon the accounts of his past lives, never ceasing for even a single thought-moment.
If there are sentient beings who hear the name of that Buddha, they will certainly attain rebirth in his buddha-land;

it is likewise with the Bodhisattva who dwells securely in the rank of the Pure Golden Net Wheel-Turning King: if anyone briefly encounters his light, they will certainly attain the tenth stage of a bodhisattva by virtue of the power of the roots of goodness previously cultivated.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as one who attains the first dhyāna, though not yet having reached the end of life, sees all the palaces in the Brahma-heaven and experiences the peace and bliss of the Brahma-world;
so it is for all who attain the various dhyānas.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in the station of a Wheel-Turning King with a Pure Golden Net, they emit the pure radiance from their maṇi-crest.

If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they all attain the tenth stage of a bodhisattva; they achieve immeasurable radiance of wisdom, obtain ten kinds of pure eyes, and even ten kinds of pure minds; they become fully endowed with immeasurable, profound samādhis, and thus achieve such pure physical eyes.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose there were someone who took billions of nayutas of buddha-fields and ground them into atoms; then, for each atom, he again took as many buddha-fields as there were atoms and ground them into atoms. Taking all these atoms and placing them in his left hand, he traveled eastward, dropping one atom after passing as many worlds as there were atoms.

Continuing thus eastward until all these atoms were exhausted, and doing likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir—if one were to take all the worlds in the ten directions, both those where atoms were placed and those where they were not, and consolidate them all into a single buddha-field.”
"Ratnapāṇi! What do you think?
Is such a buddha-field vast, immeasurable, and inconceivable?"
He replied: "No!
Such a buddha-field is vast and immeasurable, rare and extraordinary, and inconceivable."
"If there are sentient beings who, upon hearing this parable, are able to give rise to faith and understanding, you should know that they are even more rare and extraordinary.
The Buddha said, "Bhadrabāhu!"
"So it is, so it is! It is just as you have said!

If there are good sons or good daughters who, upon hearing this parable, give rise to faith, I bestow upon them this prediction: they shall certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and shall obtain the unsurpassed wisdom of a Tathāgata."

"Ratnapāṇi! Suppose there were a person who reduced to fine dust as many vast Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a thousand billion Buddha-fields, as previously described; and suppose they were to take those atoms and, following the previous analogy, exhaust them one by one until they had reconstructed a single Buddha-field, only to reduce that again to dust—continuing this process in succession for eighty such cycles.

A Bodhisattva’s pure physical eye, born of karmic retribution, can clearly perceive all the atoms within all such vast Buddha-fields in a single thought-moment. Furthermore, such a person sees Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion vast Buddha-fields, whose pure radiance is like that of a crystal mirror, illuminating worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields."
"Ratnapāṇi! All these are accomplished through the roots of goodness and the merit of the profound samādhi of the Universal Monarch of the Pure Golden Net.
— *The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha*, Fascicle 48.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Fascicle Forty-nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Thirty-six: The Conduct of Samantabhadra. Chapter Thirty-six: The Conduct of Samantabhadra.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra again addressed the great assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!

What has been expounded just now is merely a brief description of a small portion of the Tathāgata’s realm, presented in accordance with what is appropriate for the faculties and capacities of the various beings."

Why is this? Because the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, appear in the world for the sake of all sentient beings who, out of ignorance, commit evil; who conceive of a self and what belongs to a self; who are attached to the body; who are subject to perversions, doubts, and false views and discriminations; and who are constantly bound by the fetters of affliction, following the stream of birth and death and remaining far removed from the path of the Tathāgata. Thus, they arise in the world.
O Son of the Buddha!
I do not see a single dharma that constitutes such a great transgression as when bodhisattvas give rise to a mind of anger toward other bodhisattvas. Why is this?
O Son of the Buddha!
If a bodhisattva gives rise to a mind of anger toward another bodhisattva, they immediately bring about one million gates of obstacles.
What are these one million obstacles?
That is to say:
the obstacle of not seeing bodhi;
the obstacle of not hearing the true Dharma;
The obstacle of being born in impure worlds;
the obstacle of being born in the various evil destinies;
and the obstacle of being born in places of hardship.
The obstacle of many various diseases;
the obstacle of being frequently slandered and reviled;
the obstacle of being born into realms of dull and obtuse faculties.
The obstacle of the loss of right mindfulness;
the obstacle of the deficiency of wisdom;
and the obstacle of the eye.
The obstruction of the ear;
the obstruction of the nose; the obstruction of the tongue;
The obstacle of the body;
the obstacle of the mind;
the obstacle of evil associates.
The obstacle of associating with evil companions;
the obstacle of delighting in practicing the Hīnayāna;
and the obstacle of delighting in frequenting the vulgar and ordinary.
The obstacle of not having faith in or delighting in those of great majestic power;
the obstacle of delighting in dwelling together with those who have abandoned right view;
and the obstacle of being born into the families of non-Buddhist sects.
The obstacle of dwelling within the realm of Māra;
the obstacle of being separated from the Buddha’s true teaching;
and the obstacle of not seeing virtuous friends.
The obstacle of hindering roots of goodness;
the obstacle of increasing unwholesome dharmas;
and the obstacle of obtaining inferior states.
The obstacle of being born in a frontier region;
the obstacle of being born into a family of evil people;
and the obstacle of being born among malevolent deities.
Obstacles arising from birth among evil nāgas, evil yakṣas, evil gandharvas, evil asuras, evil garuḍas, evil kiṃnaras, evil mahoragas, and evil rākṣasas;
obstacles of having no delight in the Buddha-dharma;
and obstacles of practicing the ways of the ignorant.
The obstacle of attachment to the Hīnayāna;
the obstacle of lack of interest in the Mahāyāna;
and the obstacle of a nature prone to frequent fear and terror.
The obstacle of constant mental anxiety and distress;
the obstacle of attachment to birth and death;
the obstacle of lack of single-minded devotion to the Buddha-dharma.
The obstacle of not delighting in seeing or hearing the Buddha’s sovereign supernormal powers;
the obstacle of failing to attain the various faculties of a bodhisattva;
and the obstacle of not practicing the pure conduct of a bodhisattva.
The obstacle to the bodhisattva’s profound resolve;
the obstacle to the non-arising of the bodhisattva’s great vows;
and the obstacle to the non-activation of the mind of omniscience.
There is the obstacle of indolence regarding the bodhisattva practices;
the obstacle of being unable to purify all karmic hindrances;
and the obstacle of being unable to gather great merit.
The obstacle of the intellect being unable to become clear and sharp;
the obstacle of severing the vast wisdom;
and the obstacle of failing to protect and maintain the various practices of a bodhisattva.
The obstacle of delighting in slandering the words of the Omniscient One;
the obstacle of distancing oneself from the bodhi of all Buddhas;
the obstacle of delighting in dwelling within the realm of the Māras;
The obstacle of not exclusively cultivating the realm of the Buddhas;
the obstacle of not resolutely generating the bodhisattva’s great vow;
the obstacle of not delighting in dwelling together with bodhisattvas.
The obstacle of not seeking the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva;
the obstacle of a nature characterized by excessive views and doubt;
and the obstacle of a mind that is perpetually ignorant and dark.
Because they are unable to practice the impartial giving of a bodhisattva, the obstacle of non-renunciation arises;
because they are unable to uphold the precepts of the Tathāgata, the obstacle of breaking the precepts arises;
and because they are unable to enter the gate of forbearance, the obstacles of delusion, malice, and anger arise.
Because they are unable to practice the great diligence of a bodhisattva, the defilement-obstruction of indolence arises;
because they are unable to attain the various samādhis, the obstruction of distraction arises;
and because they do not cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), the obstruction of faulty wisdom arises.
The obstacle of lack of skill regarding what is possible and what is impossible;
the obstacle of lack of skillful means regarding the deliverance of sentient beings;
and the obstacle of being unable to discern the wisdom of a bodhisattva.
Within the bodhisattva’s dharma of renunciation, there is the obstacle of being unable to comprehend it;
because they have not accomplished the ten kinds of vast eyes of a bodhisattva, there is the obstacle of having eyes like those of one born blind;
because their ears do not hear the unimpeded Dharma, there is the obstacle of having a mouth like that of a mute sheep.
Because they do not possess the primary and secondary marks, there is the obstacle of the impairment of the nose faculty;
because they cannot discern the languages of sentient beings, there is the obstacle of the failure to perfect the tongue faculty;
because they treat sentient beings with contempt, there is the obstacle of the failure to perfect the body faculty.
Because the mind is frequently deranged and turbulent, one accomplishes the obstruction of the mental faculty;
because one does not maintain the three types of restraint, one accomplishes the obstruction of physical karma;
and because one constantly gives rise to the four kinds of faults, one accomplishes the obstruction of verbal karma.
Because they frequently give rise to greed, anger, and false views, they accomplish the obstacle of mental karma;
the obstacle of seeking the Dharma with a thieving mind;
and the obstacle of severing the realm of the Bodhisattvas.
There is the obstacle of generating cowardice and despondency regarding the courageous dharmas of a bodhisattva;
the obstacle of generating indolence regarding the path of renunciation of a bodhisattva;
and the obstacle of generating cessation regarding the gateways of the light of wisdom of a bodhisattva.
The obstacle of generating a weak and inferior mind regarding the bodhisattva’s power of mindfulness;
the obstacle of being unable to uphold the Tathāgata’s teachings;
and the obstacle of being unable to draw near to the bodhisattva’s path of transcendence.
It is an obstacle to practicing the bodhisattva’s path without loss or ruin;
an obstacle to conforming with the correct stage of the two vehicles;
and an obstacle to distancing oneself from the lineage of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
“O Son of the Buddha!
If a bodhisattva gives rise to even a single thought of anger toward other bodhisattvas, they will bring about as many as one million such gateways of obstacles. Why is this?
"O Son of the Buddha!
I do not see any single dharma that constitutes a greater transgression than for Bodhisattvas to give rise to a mind of anger toward other Bodhisattvas.
Therefore, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who wish to swiftly fulfill all the practices of a Bodhisattva should diligently cultivate ten kinds of dharmas."

What are these ten?
