he expounds the Dharma that causes Bodhisattvas not to regress.
He taught the Dharma that praises the virtues of the Buddha;
he taught the Dharma concerning the equality of all Buddhas and the practice of all Bodhisattvas, which accords with the realm of all Tathāgatas.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed skill in preaching the Dharma.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of upholding.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
They uphold all roots of merit and goodness that have been accumulated;
they uphold all the teachings spoken by all Tathāgatas;
and they uphold all parables.
The door of maintaining the principles of all dharmas;
the door of maintaining all *dhāraṇī*s that bring forth [realization];
and the maintenance of all dharmas that eliminate doubt and confusion.
He upholds all dharmas that accomplish the practices of bodhisattvas;
he upholds the gate of the samādhi of equality spoken by all Tathāgatas;
and he upholds the gate of illumination of all dharmas.
They maintain the power of the miraculous play of the supernatural faculties of all Buddhas; these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s power of sustaining the unsurpassed, great wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of eloquence possessed by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
eloquence that is non-conceptual regarding all phenomena;
eloquence that is without activity regarding all phenomena;
The eloquence of non-attachment toward all phenomena;
the eloquence of thorough realization of the emptiness of all phenomena;
the eloquence of freedom from doubt and darkness regarding all phenomena;
The eloquence of being empowered by the Buddha regarding all phenomena;
the eloquence of self-awakening regarding all phenomena;
and the eloquence of skill in the differentiation of words and phrases regarding all phenomena.
The eloquence of speaking the truth regarding all phenomena;
the eloquence that gladdens the minds of all sentient beings according to their inclinations.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed and skillful eloquence of the Tathāgata.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of mastery."
What are the ten? They are:
mastery in teaching and disciplining all sentient beings;
Mastery in universally illuminating all phenomena;
mastery in cultivating all practices of the roots of goodness;
and mastery in vast wisdom.
Mastery over precepts that are without dependence;
mastery in dedicating all roots of goodness toward enlightenment;
and mastery in non-retrogressive diligence.
The mastery of destroying all māras through wisdom;
the mastery of causing [beings] to resolve upon bodhicitta according to their inclinations;
and the mastery of manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment according to those who are to be transformed.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed sovereignty of great wisdom.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of non-attachment. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
Non-attachment toward all worlds;
non-attachment toward all sentient beings;
non-attachment toward all phenomena.
They are unattached to all that is done;
they are unattached to all roots of goodness;
they are unattached to all places of rebirth.
Non-attachment toward all vows;
non-attachment toward all practices;
non-attachment toward all bodhisattvas.
To be unattached toward all Buddhas—
this is the tenth.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will be able to swiftly transform all conceptual perceptions and attain unsurpassed, pure wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of impartial mind. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the mind of equanimity that accumulates all merits;
the mind of equanimity that gives rise to all distinct vows;
An impartial mind toward the bodies of all sentient beings;
an impartial mind toward the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
and an impartial mind toward all phenomena.
A mind of equanimity toward all pure and impure lands;
a mind of understanding equanimity toward all sentient beings;
and a mind of equanimity that makes no distinctions regarding any conditioned phenomena.
The mind of equanimity regarding the powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas;
and the mind of equanimity regarding the wisdom of all Tathāgatas. These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide within these, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great mind of equanimity.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of birth of wisdom."
What are these ten? They are:
knowing the wisdom that gives rise to the understandings of all sentient beings;
The wisdom born from knowing the various distinctions of all buddha-fields;
the wisdom born from knowing the boundaries of the networks of the ten directions;
and the wisdom born from knowing all worlds, whether inverted or upright.
The wisdom born from knowing that all phenomena abide extensively in both a single nature and manifold natures;
the wisdom born from knowing all various bodies;
and the wisdom born from knowing that all inverted delusions of the world are entirely without attachment.
They give rise to the wisdom that knows all phenomena ultimately transcend through a single path;
they give rise to the wisdom that knows the Tathāgata’s spiritual power can enter all dharma-realms;
and they give rise to the wisdom that knows the Buddha-seed of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time is never severed.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will have no lack of thorough understanding regarding all phenomena.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of transformations. What are the ten?
They are as follows:
The transformation of all sentient beings;
the transformation of all bodies;
the transformation of all lands;
The transformation of all offerings;
the transformation of all sounds;
the transformation of all practices and vows.
All transformations for teaching and taming sentient beings;
all transformations of attaining perfect enlightenment;
all transformations of preaching the Dharma;
All empowerments and transformations— these are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the full perfection of all unsurpassed transformative dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of sustaining powers of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
being sustained by the power of the Buddha; being sustained by the power of the Dharma;
The sustaining power of sentient beings;
the sustaining power of karma;
the sustaining power of conduct.
Sustained by the power of aspiration;
sustained by the power of the objective sphere;
sustained by the power of time.
The upholding by the power of goodness;
the upholding by the power of wisdom. These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme power of mastery and sustenance over all dharmas.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 53;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 54.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree,
Part Two of Chapter Thirty-Eight, "Leaving the World," Part Two:
"O Son of the Buddha!..."
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of great consolation. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
All bodhisattvas give rise to this thought:
"Throughout all future ages, whenever any buddhas appear in the world, I shall follow and serve them all, causing them to rejoice."
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and solace. He further thought:
"When those Tathāgatas appear in the world, I shall respectfully make offerings to them all with unsurpassed requisites."
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and solace. He further thought:

"When I offer worship to the Buddhas, those Tathāgatas will surely instruct me in the Dharma. With a profound mind of reverence, I shall listen to and receive it, practicing according to the teachings; thus, I shall certainly attain birth in the bodhisattva stages—whether already attained, presently being attained, or yet to be attained."
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and solace. He further thought:
"I shall practice the bodhisattva path for unspeakably unspeakable eons, always remaining in the company of all Buddhas and bodhisattvas."
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and solace. He further thought:
"In the past, before I had resolved to attain unsurpassed, great bodhicitta, I was subject to various fears, namely:"

The fear of lacking livelihood, the fear of ill repute, the fear of death, the fear of falling into evil realms, and the fear of the majesty of great assemblies—all these are entirely abandoned from the moment of first generating the resolve.
They are neither startled nor terrified, neither fearful nor apprehensive, neither timid nor afraid; they cannot be destroyed by any māras or by any non-Buddhists.
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and comfort. He further thought:
"I shall cause all sentient beings to attain unexcelled bodhi."

Once I have attained enlightenment, I shall practice the bodhisattva path in the presence of those Buddhas for the remainder of my life, making offerings with great faith by providing all necessary articles of worship;
and after their parinirvāṇa, I shall erect immeasurable stūpas for each of them to honor their relics, and uphold and protect all their bequeathed teachings.
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and comfort. He further thought:

"I shall adorn every world throughout the ten directions with unsurpassed adornments, causing them all to be fully endowed with various wonderful, equal, and pure qualities; furthermore, by means of various great supernormal powers, I shall sustain and shake them, and cause their radiant light to shine forth everywhere."
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and solace. He further thought:

"I shall sever the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings, purify the desires and inclinations of all sentient beings, awaken the minds and intentions of all sentient beings, extinguish the afflictions of all sentient beings, close the gates to the evil realms for all sentient beings, open the gates to the auspicious destinies for all sentient beings, shatter the darkness of all sentient beings, bestow light upon all sentient beings, cause all sentient beings to leave behind all demonic activities, and lead all sentient beings to the place of peace and security."
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and solace.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further thought:
"The Tathāgatas, the Buddhas, are like the udumbara flower; they are difficult to encounter, and in immeasurable kalpas one may not behold even a single one."

In future ages, whenever I wish to see the Tathāgata, I shall immediately behold him. The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, will never abandon me; they will always abide where I am, enabling me to see them and preaching the Dharma for me without interruption.
Having heard the Dharma, my mind and thoughts will become pure, free from flattery and crookedness, upright and without guile, and in every moment of thought, I shall constantly see all the Buddhas.
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and solace. He further thought: "In the future, I shall attain Buddhahood.

By the spiritual power of a Buddha, throughout all worlds, for the sake of all sentient beings, I shall individually manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment and deliver the pure, fearless Great Lion’s Roar. With my original great vows pervading the entire Dharma-realm, I shall beat the Great Dharma Drum, rain down the Great Dharma Rain, and perform the Great Dharma Gift. Throughout immeasurable eons, I shall constantly expound the True Dharma; sustained by great compassion, my actions of body, speech, and mind shall never know weariness."
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and consolation.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of great joy and consolation of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the great consolation of the wisdom of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of profound entry into the Buddha-dharma."
What are the ten? They are: entering all worlds of the past;
They enter all worlds of the future;
they enter the enumeration of worlds, the activities of worlds, the descriptions of worlds, and the purification of worlds in the present age;
and they enter the various natures of all worlds.
Entering into the various karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
entering into the various practices of all bodhisattvas;
knowing the succession of all past buddhas;
They know the succession of all future Buddhas;
they know all present Buddhas throughout the ten directions, equal to space and the dharma-realm, as well as their lands, assemblies, and their teaching of the Dharma for the sake of taming beings;

they know worldly dharmas, the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas. Although they know that all dharmas are without discrimination, they preach various teachings; because they enter the dharma-realm without entering anything, they preach according to those dharmas without any grasping or attachment.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain entry into the profound nature of the great wisdom of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of bases for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas; relying upon these, Bodhisattvas practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva. What are the ten?
That is to say:
practicing the bodhisattva conduct by relying on making offerings to all buddhas;
practicing the bodhisattva conduct by relying on taming all sentient beings;
Relying upon and drawing near to all virtuous friends, one practices the bodhisattva conduct;
relying upon the accumulation of all roots of goodness, one practices the bodhisattva conduct;
relying upon the purification of all buddha-fields, one practices the bodhisattva conduct.
Relying on never abandoning any sentient being, one practices the bodhisattva conduct;
relying on deeply entering all perfections (pāramitās), one practices the bodhisattva conduct;
relying on fulfilling all bodhisattva vows, one practices the bodhisattva conduct.
Relying on the immeasurable bodhicitta, one practices the conduct of a bodhisattva;
relying on the bodhi of all Buddhas, one practices the conduct of a bodhisattva.
These are the ten.
Bodhisattvas rely on these practices to carry out the bodhisattva conduct.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten ways of generating a mind of fearlessness."
What are the ten? They are:
extinguishing all obstructive karma and giving rise to a mind of fearlessness;
To protect and uphold the True Dharma after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, they give rise to a mind of fearlessness;
to subdue all Māras, they give rise to a mind of fearlessness;
and not begrudging their own bodies or lives, they give rise to a mind of fearlessness.
They give rise to a mind of fearlessness by crushing all the heterodox arguments of external paths;
they give rise to a mind of fearlessness by causing all sentient beings to rejoice;
they give rise to a mind of fearlessness by causing all those in the assembly to be entirely joyful.
They give rise to a fearless mind by subduing all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas;
they give rise to a fearless mind by departing from the stages of the two vehicles and entering the profound Dharma;
and they give rise to a fearless mind by practicing the bodhisattva path for unspeakably unspeakable eons without weariness or fatigue.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom and the mind of fearlessness.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give rise to ten kinds of minds free from doubt, such that their minds have no uncertainty regarding any of the Buddha-dharmas.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:
"I shall gather in all sentient beings through giving;
I shall gather in all sentient beings through ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity."
When this thought is generated, it is certain and without doubt;
if a doubting mind were to arise, such a thing would be impossible.
This is the first generation of the mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva forms this thought:
"When all future Buddhas appear in the world, I shall serve and make offerings to them all.
When he gives rise to this mind, he is resolute and free from doubt.
If one were to give rise to a doubting mind, such a thing is impossible.
This is the second development of a mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects as follows:
"I shall adorn all worlds throughout their entirety with various and wondrous nets of light.
When one gives rise to this thought, it is certain and beyond doubt;
for it is impossible that any doubt should arise.
This is the third generation of the mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects:
"I shall cultivate the bodhisattva practices throughout all future kalpas."

Innumerable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and unspeakably unspeakable—surpassing all calculation and reaching to the ultimate limits of the dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and all sentient beings—I shall bring them all to maturity through the unsurpassed methods of teaching and taming.
"When one gives rise to this mind, it is certain and without doubt;
if a doubting mind were to arise, such a thing would be impossible.
This is the fourth generation of the mind of non-doubt."
Furthermore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects in this way:
"I shall practice the bodhisattva conduct, fulfill my great vows, and, possessing all-knowledge, abide securely within it."
When this mind is generated, it is certain and free from doubt;
were a doubting mind to arise, such a thing would be impossible.
This is the fifth generation of the mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:
"I shall universally practice the bodhisattva path for the sake of all worlds, becoming the pure radiance of all dharmas and illuminating all existing Buddha-dharmas."
When generating this mind, one must be resolute and free from doubt;
it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise.
This is the sixth generation of the mind of non-doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:
"I shall know that all dharmas are the Buddha-dharmas; according to the minds of sentient beings, I will expound them for their sake, causing them all to attain awakening."
"When generating this mind, one must be resolute and free from doubt;
were doubt to arise, it would be impossible.
This is the seventh generation of the mind free from doubt."
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:
"I shall attain the gate of non-obstruction regarding all phenomena, because I know that all obstructions are unapprehendable;
with such a mind, free from doubt and dwelling in true reality, I shall proceed until the attainment of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"When this mind is generated, it is resolute and free from doubt;
for it to give rise to doubt is impossible.
This is the eighth generation of the mind free from doubt."
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:

"I shall know that there is no dharma whatsoever that is not a supramundane dharma; having distanced myself from all false imaginings and inversions, I shall adorn myself with a single adornment, yet remain without any adornment;
I shall realize this for myself, without depending on another for awakening."
When one gives rise to this mind, it is certain and free from doubt;
were a doubting mind to arise, such a thing would be impossible.
This is the ninth arousal of the mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:

"I shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment regarding all phenomena because I am free from all false conceptualizations and inversions; because I have attained the wisdom of instantaneous correspondence; because neither identity nor difference can be apprehended; because I am free from all numerical reckonings; because I have reached the ultimate unconditioned; because I am free from all verbal expression; and because I abide at the limit of the ineffable realm."
When generating this mind, one must be resolute and free from doubt;
it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise.
This is the tenth generation of the mind of non-doubt.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, their minds will have no doubts regarding any of the Buddha-dharmas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of inconceivabilities."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
all roots of goodness are inconceivable.
All vows are inconceivable. Knowing that all phenomena are like illusions is inconceivable.
To resolve upon bodhicitta and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, such that roots of goodness are never lost and there is no conceptual discrimination, is inconceivable.
Although they have deeply penetrated all dharmas, they do not take up extinction, because all their vows have not yet been fully accomplished—this is inconceivable.

While practicing the bodhisattva path, they manifest the descent of the spirit, entry into the womb, birth, renunciation, asceticism, proceeding to the site of enlightenment, subduing the hosts of Māra, attaining supreme perfect awakening, turning the wheel of the true Dharma, and entering parinirvāṇa; their sovereign spiritual transformations never cease, and they do not abandon their compassionate vows as they rescue and protect sentient beings—this is inconceivable.

Although they can manifest the sovereign spiritual transformations of the ten powers of a Tathāgata, they do not abandon their mind of equality with the dharma-realm as they teach and transform sentient beings; this is inconceivable.

To know that all dharmas are signless is itself a sign; signs are signless. Non-discrimination is discrimination; discrimination is non-discrimination. That which is not existent is existent; existence is non-existence. Non-action is action; action is non-action. That which is not speech is speech; speech is non-speech. This is inconceivable.

He knows that the mind is equal to bodhi; he knows that bodhi is equal to the mind; and he knows that the mind and bodhi are equal to sentient beings. Furthermore, he does not give rise to inversion of mind, inversion of perception, or inversion of view; this is inconceivable.

In every moment of thought, they enter the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodha-samāpatti*), exhausting all outflows (*āsrava*) without yet realizing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), nor do they exhaust their roots of goodness associated with outflows;
though they know all phenomena to be without outflows, they know the exhaustion of outflows and the cessation of outflows;

though they know that the Buddha-dharma is identical to worldly phenomena and worldly phenomena are identical to the Buddha-dharma, they do not differentiate worldly phenomena within the Buddha-dharma, nor do they differentiate the Buddha-dharma within worldly phenomena.
All dharmas enter the dharma-realm because there is nothing to enter;
one knows that all dharmas are non-dual because they are without change or transformation.
This is the tenth inconceivable [quality].
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of inconceivability of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
If Bodhisattvas abide within them, they will attain all the unsurpassed, inconceivable dharmas of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of skillful esoteric speech for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
skill in esoteric language regarding all Buddha-sūtras;
and skill in esoteric language regarding all places of rebirth.
Skillful esoteric speech regarding all bodhisattvas’ supernormal powers, transformations, and attainment of perfect enlightenment;
skillful esoteric speech regarding the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
and skillful esoteric speech regarding the defilement and purification arising from all sentient beings.
The skillful esoteric language regarding the gate of ultimate non-obstruction in all phenomena;
the skillful esoteric language regarding how, within every single location of all space-realms, there are worlds either forming or decaying without any intervening empty space;

and the skillful esoteric language regarding how, throughout the entire dharma-realm and all ten directions, down to the most minute points, Tathāgatas manifest their initial birth, up to their attainment of Buddhahood and entry into parinirvāṇa, filling the dharma-realm such that they are perceived distinctly in their entirety.

Because he perceives that all sentient beings are equal in their nirvana and are subject to no change, yet he does not abandon his great vows; because he seeks to fulfill the vow for omniscience that has not yet been perfected, this is the skillful esoteric teaching.

Although he knows that all dharmas are realized without depending on another, he does not forsake spiritual friends, but increases his reverence toward the Tathāgatas; being in harmonious union with spiritual friends as non-dual, he cultivates and plants all roots of goodness, dedicating them toward peaceful abiding; sharing the same activity, the same essence, the same liberation, and the same accomplishment—this is the skillful esoteric teaching.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, skillful, and subtle secret speech.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of skillful analytical wisdom. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
The skillful analytical wisdom that enters all lands;
the skillful analytical wisdom that enters the abodes of all sentient beings;
and the skillful analytical wisdom that enters the mental activities of all sentient beings.
The skillful wisdom of discerning the faculties of all sentient beings;
the skillful wisdom of discerning the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
and the skillful wisdom of discerning the practices of all śrāvakas.
The skillful analytical wisdom that enters into all the practices of pratyekabuddhas;
the skillful analytical wisdom that enters into all the practices of bodhisattvas;
and the skillful analytical wisdom that enters into all worldly dharmas.
The skillful analytical wisdom that enters into all Buddha-dharmas— this is the tenth.
If bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the supreme, skillful analytical wisdom of all Buddhas regarding all phenomena.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of entry into samādhi for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
entering samādhi within all worlds;
entering samādhi within the bodies of all sentient beings;
Entering samādhi in all dharmas;
entering samādhi in beholding all Buddhas;
entering samādhi while abiding through all kalpas;
Arising from samādhi, they manifest inconceivable bodies and enter samādhi;
they enter samādhi within the bodies of all Buddhas;
they enter samādhi through awakening to the equality of all sentient beings.
In a single thought-moment, they enter the samādhi of the wisdom that enters all bodhisattva samādhis;
in a single thought-moment, they enter the samādhi that accomplishes all the practices and vows of all bodhisattvas without obstruction and without cessation through unimpeded wisdom.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the dharma of the unsurpassed skillful samādhi of all buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of universal entry. What are the ten?
They are as follows:
Pervasive entry into sentient beings;
pervasive entry into lands;
pervasive entry into the various characteristics of the world;
The universal entry of fire;
the universal entry of water;
the universal entry of the Buddha.
The universal entry into majestic adornment;
the universal entry into the Tathāgata’s body of boundless merit;
and the universal entry into all various modes of teaching the Dharma.
The universal entry into the various offerings to all Tathāgatas constitutes the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme and great wisdom of universal entry.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten gates of liberation for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
They are: the liberation door of a single body pervading all worlds;
and the liberation door of manifesting infinite varieties of physical forms in all worlds.
The liberation door of entering all worlds into a single buddha-field;
the liberation door of universally sustaining all realms of sentient beings;
and the liberation door of filling all worlds with bodies adorned by all buddhas.
The liberation door of perceiving all worlds within one's own body;
the liberation door of proceeding to all worlds in a single thought-moment;
and the liberation door of manifesting the appearance of all Tathāgatas in a single world.
The liberation door of a single body filling the entire dharma-realm;
the liberation door of manifesting the playful supernatural powers of all Buddhas within a single thought-moment.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed gate of liberation.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of supernormal powers (abhijñā).
What are the ten? They are:
the supernormal knowledge of the skillful means of recollecting past lives;
The supernormal power of the unimpeded skillful means of the divine ear;
the supernormal power of the skillful means of knowing the inconceivable mental activities of other sentient beings;
and the supernormal power of the skillful means of observing with the divine eye without any obstruction.
The skillful wisdom-penetration that manifests inconceivable great supernormal powers in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
the skillful wisdom-penetration that universally manifests a single body throughout immeasurable worlds;
and the skillful wisdom-penetration that, in a single thought-moment, enters unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds.
The skillful means and wisdom of manifesting infinite ornaments of birth to adorn inconceivable worlds;
the skillful means and wisdom of manifesting unspeakable transformation bodies;
and the skillful means and wisdom of manifesting the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in unspeakable worlds in accordance with the minds of inconceivable sentient beings.
These are the ten.

If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed and great skillful supernormal powers, manifesting in various ways for all sentient beings to cause them to practice and learn.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of clarity. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the skillful wisdom-light that knows the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
and the skillful wisdom-light that knows the realms of all sentient beings to be quiescent, pure, and free from all conceptual proliferation.

They know that the various objects of focus of all sentient beings are but a single characteristic, entirely unapprehendable; they realize that all phenomena are like adamant, through the clarity of skillful wisdom.
He possesses the skillful light of wisdom that can, through immeasurable and subtle sounds, cause [his voice] to be heard throughout all worlds in the ten directions;
he possesses the skillful light of wisdom that universally destroys all mental attachments and defilements.
The skillful wisdom-light that is able to manifest through expedient means both taking birth and not taking birth;
the skillful wisdom-light that abandons all realms of perception and sensation.

Knowing that all phenomena are neither with marks nor without marks, being of a single nature yet devoid of intrinsic nature, and free from conceptual discrimination, one is nevertheless able to comprehend the various phenomena; throughout immeasurable eons, one analyzes and expounds them, abiding in the dharma-realm, attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and possessing the clarity of skillful wisdom.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that all sentient beings are fundamentally unborn from the very beginning,
for he has thoroughly realized that the taking of birth is unapprehendable; thus, he knows causes, knows conditions, knows phenomena, knows objects,
knows conduct, knows birth, knows cessation, knows verbal expression, knows delusion, and knows the departure from delusion.
...knowing perversion, knowing freedom from perversion, knowing defilement, knowing purity, knowing birth-and-death,
knowing nirvana, knowing attainability, knowing unattainability, knowing attachment,
knowing non-attachment, knowing abiding, knowing movement, knowing going, knowing returning, knowing arising, and knowing...
They do not give rise to [defilements], they know destruction, they know renunciation, they know maturation, they know the faculties, and they know how to discipline;
they teach and transform beings in various ways as appropriate, never forgetting the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Why is this? It is because a bodhisattva generates the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi solely for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, and has no other purpose.
Therefore, the bodhisattva constantly transforms sentient beings without physical fatigue, never contravening the activities of all worldly realms.
This is called the luminous wisdom of skillfulness regarding dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*).
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva has no attachment toward the Buddha and does not give rise to a mind of attachment;
has no attachment toward the Dharma and does not give rise to a mind of attachment;
has no attachment toward the buddha-fields and does not give rise to a mind of attachment.
Being unattached toward sentient beings, they do not give rise to a mind of attachment;
yet, while not perceiving the existence of sentient beings, they perform the work of teaching, transforming, and preaching the Dharma.

Nevertheless, they do not abandon the various practices of a bodhisattva, their great compassion and great vows, nor do they cease seeing the Buddhas, hearing the Dharma, practicing in accordance with it, and relying upon it.
The Tathāgata plants all roots of goodness and reverently makes offerings without ceasing;
he is able to shake immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions by means of his supernormal powers, for his mind is vast and equal to the Dharma-realm.
Thus, he knows the various ways of teaching the Dharma, knows the number of sentient beings, knows the distinctions among sentient beings, and knows the arising of suffering.
With the cessation of suffering, they realize that all conditioned phenomena are like reflections; they practice the bodhisattva path, forever severing the root of all rebirth.

Solely for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, they practice the bodhisattva path without anything to be practiced, conforming to the lineage of all Buddhas and giving rise to a mind like the king of great mountains.
Knowing all things to be false and inverted, they enter the gateway of the knowledge of all modes; their wisdom is vast and unshakable,
and they shall attain perfect enlightenment to impartially ferry all sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death with skillful and luminous wisdom.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great, skillful wisdom-illumination.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of liberation.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
Liberation from afflictions;
liberation from wrong views;
liberation from all forms of grasping.
Liberation through the aggregates, elements, and sense bases;
liberation that transcends the two vehicles;
and liberation through the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena.
The liberation of being free from attachment to all worlds, all lands, all sentient beings, and all phenomena;
the liberation of infinite abiding;
and the liberation of initiating all bodhisattva practices to enter the Tathāgata’s stage of non-discrimination.
Within a single thought-moment, they are able to fully comprehend the liberation of all three periods of time;
this is the tenth.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they can perform the unsurpassed work of a Buddha, teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of groves. What are these ten?
That is to say:
birth and death are the bodhisattva’s grove, because there is no weariness or abandonment;
teaching and transforming sentient beings are the bodhisattva’s grove, because there is no fatigue.
Abiding through all kalpas is the bodhisattva’s grove, for it encompasses all great practices;
purifying worlds is the bodhisattva’s grove, for it is where they themselves dwell;
all the palaces of Māra are the bodhisattva’s grove, for they subdue those hosts.
Contemplating the teachings one has heard is the park and grove of a bodhisattva, because of investigating them according to reality;

the six perfections, the four means of attraction, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment are the park and grove of a bodhisattva, because they continue the domain of their compassionate father;
the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the eighteen unique qualities, and even all Buddha-dharmas are the park and grove of a bodhisattva, because they do not dwell upon other dharmas.

The manifestation of the sovereign spiritual powers and majestic might of all bodhisattvas is the bodhisattva’s grove, for by means of great supernormal power they turn the wheel of the true Dharma to subdue sentient beings without ceasing;

manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment for all sentient beings in all places in a single thought-moment is the bodhisattva’s grove, for the Dharma-body pervades all worlds throughout the entirety of space.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed practice of great bliss, free from sorrow and affliction.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of palaces.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The bodhicitta is the palace of the bodhisattva, because it is never forgotten;
the merit and wisdom of the ten paths of wholesome action are the palace of the bodhisattva, because they transform sentient beings in the desire realm;
the meditative concentrations of the four Brahma-abodes are the palace of the bodhisattva, because they transform sentient beings in the form realm.
To be born in the Śuddhāvāsa heavens is a palace of the bodhisattva, because they are unstained by any afflictions;
to be born in the formless realm is a palace of the bodhisattva, because they cause all sentient beings to leave behind places of hardship;
to be born in defiled worlds is a palace of the bodhisattva, because they cause all sentient beings to sever their afflictions.
Manifesting as dwelling within the inner palace with wife, children, and retinue is the bodhisattva’s palace, for the sake of bringing to maturity those beings who shared his past practices;
manifesting as residing as a wheel-turning monarch, a world-protector, Śakra, or Brahmā is the bodhisattva’s palace, for the sake of taming those beings whose minds are autonomous;

abiding in all bodhisattva practices and sporting with supernatural powers with complete mastery is the bodhisattva’s palace, for the sake of skillfully sporting in the various dhyānas, liberations, samādhis, and wisdoms.

The consecration and prediction of all Buddhas as the Sovereign of Unsurpassed Mastery and the King of All-Knowledge is the palace of the bodhisattva, for it abides in the adornment of the ten powers and performs the sovereign activities of a king of all dharmas.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will receive the empowerment of the Dharma and attain sovereign mastery of spiritual powers throughout all worlds.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of delight.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
They delight in right mindfulness, because their minds are not distracted;
they delight in wisdom, because they discern all phenomena;
they delight in visiting the abodes of all Buddhas, because they never tire of hearing the Dharma.
They delight in all Buddhas, because they fill the ten directions without limit;
they delight in Bodhisattvas, because they manifest their bodies through immeasurable gateways for the sake of all sentient beings with sovereign mastery;
they delight in all gates of samādhi, because by entering a single gate of samādhi, they enter all gates of samādhi.
They delight in dhāraṇīs, because they uphold the Dharma without forgetting and transmit it to sentient beings;
they delight in unimpeded eloquence, because they can analyze and expound upon a single word or phrase of the sutras endlessly throughout unspeakable eons;
they delight in attaining perfect enlightenment, because for the sake of all sentient beings they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment through their bodies by means of infinite gateways.
They delight in turning the wheel of Dharma, because they destroy and eliminate all heterodox teachings.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed dharma-bliss of all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of adornments of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the adornment of power, because it is indestructible;
the adornment of fearlessness, because nothing can subdue it.
Adornment of meaning, because the ineffable meanings are explained without end;
adornment of Dharma, because the eighty-four thousand clusters of teachings are observed, expounded, and never forgotten;
adornment of vows, because the great oaths undertaken by all bodhisattvas never regress.
Adornment of conduct, because one departs [from suffering] by cultivating the practices of Samantabhadra;
adornment of lands, because all lands are made into a single land;
adornment of universal sound, because the rain of Dharma falls throughout all Buddha-worlds.
The adornment of power-maintenance, because one practices countless deeds throughout all kalpas without interruption;

and the adornment of transformation, because one manifests within the body of a single sentient being as many bodies as there are sentient beings, enabling all sentient beings to know and see them, so that they never regress in their quest for omniscience.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain all the unsurpassed dharma-adornments of the Tathāgata.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give rise to ten kinds of immovable minds.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
An unshakable mind that is able to relinquish all that one possesses;
an unshakable mind that contemplates and examines all Buddha-dharmas;
and an unshakable mind that recollects and makes offerings to all Buddhas.
The immovable mind that vows never to harm or afflict any sentient being;
the immovable mind that universally gathers in all sentient beings without discriminating between enemies and kin;
and the immovable mind that seeks all Buddha-dharmas without ever resting.
For as many unspeakably unspeakable eons as there are sentient beings, they practice the bodhisattva conduct with a mind that never grows weary or tired, and which is without regression or wavering;

they achieve a rooted faith, an unturbid faith, a pure faith, an utterly pure faith, a stainless faith, a transparent faith, a faith that reverently makes offerings to all Buddhas, a non-regressive faith, an inexhaustible faith, an indestructible faith, and a faith of great joy and exultation that is unwavering;
and they achieve an unwavering mind that gives birth to the path of skillful means for omniscience.
To hear all the dharmas of the practices of bodhisattvas, to accept them with faith, not to slander them,
and to have an unshakable mind— this is the tenth. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed, unshakable mind of omniscience.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of non-abandonment of the profound and great resolve by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
not abandoning the profound and great resolve to bring to full completion the bodhi of all Buddhas;
not abandoning the profound and great resolve to teach, transform, and subdue all sentient beings.
The profound and great resolve that does not abandon nor sever the lineage of all Buddhas;
the profound and great resolve that does not abandon the cultivation of intimacy with all spiritual friends;
the profound and great resolve that does not abandon the making of offerings to all Buddhas.
The profound and great resolve that does not abandon the single-minded pursuit of all the meritorious dharmas of the Mahāyāna;
the profound and great resolve that does not abandon the practice of the holy life and the maintenance of pure precepts in the presence of all Buddhas;
and the profound and great resolve that does not abandon the close attendance upon all Bodhisattvas.
The great resolve that does not abandon the skillful means for seeking all Buddha-dharmas and protects and sustains them;
the great resolve that does not abandon the fulfillment of all bodhisattva practices and vows, and the gathering of all Buddha-dharmas.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in them, they will be able to never abandon any of the Buddha-dharmas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of wisdom-observation.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
The wisdom-insight that skillfully analyzes and explains all phenomena;
the wisdom-insight that understands all roots of goodness throughout the three periods of time;
and the wisdom-insight that understands the sovereign transformations of all bodhisattva practices.
The wisdom-contemplation that understands the gateways to the meaning of all phenomena;
the wisdom-contemplation that understands the majestic power of all Buddhas;
the wisdom-contemplation that understands all dharani-gateways.
The wisdom-contemplation that universally proclaims the True Dharma in all worlds;
the wisdom-contemplation that enters the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
and the wisdom-contemplation that knows the inconceivable [realms] of all ten directions.
The wisdom-light that knows all Buddha-dharmas and observes with unimpeded wisdom—
this is the tenth.
If bodhisattvas abide in these, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme great wisdom of observation.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of Dharma-teachings for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
teaching that all phenomena arise from conditions;
teaching that all phenomena are entirely like illusions.
To teach that all phenomena are without conflict;
to teach that all phenomena are without limit;
to teach that all phenomena have no basis of reliance.
He teaches that all phenomena are like adamant;
he teaches that all phenomena are entirely suchness;
he teaches that all phenomena are entirely quiescent.
To teach that all phenomena are entirely transcendent;
and to teach that all phenomena abide in a single meaning, being perfected by their own nature.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will be able to skillfully explain all dharmas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of purity."
What are the ten? They are:
the purity of the profound mind;
Purity through the severance of doubt;
purity through the departure from views;
purity of the objective sphere.
Seeking the purity of all-knowledge;
the purity of eloquence;
and the purity of fearlessness.
They abide in the purity of all bodhisattva wisdom;
they receive the purity of all bodhisattva vows;
and they fully accomplish the purity of unsurpassed enlightenment, the thirty-two marks of a hundredfold merit, the pure white dharmas, and all roots of goodness.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain all the unsurpassed, pure dharmas of the Tathāgatas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of seals.
What are the ten? They are as follows:

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva understands the suffering of suffering, the suffering of change, and the suffering of conditioned formations, they single-mindedly seek the Buddha-dharma without giving rise to indolence; they practice the Bodhisattva path without weariness or laxity, remaining without alarm, fear, dread, or terror; they do not abandon their great vows, seeking all-knowledge with steadfastness and non-retrogression until they ultimately attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi—this is the first seal.

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees sentient beings who are foolish and deranged, who may revile and insult one another with coarse, vile, and evil speech, or who may inflict harm upon one another with swords, staves, tiles, or stones, he never abandons the bodhicitta because of such circumstances. Instead, remaining patient and gentle, he exclusively cultivates the Buddha-dharma, abides in the most supreme path, and enters the stage of "certainty" (niyāma). This is the second seal.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva hears the teaching of the profound Buddha-dharma associated with omniscience, they are able, by means of their own wisdom, to have deep faith and acceptance, to comprehend it, and to enter into it; this is the third seal.
Furthermore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects thus:
"I have resolved with a profound mind to seek all-knowledge; I shall attain buddhahood and realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

All sentient beings wander through the five destinies, undergoing immeasurable suffering; I shall also cause them to give rise to the bodhicitta, to have deep faith and joy, to cultivate diligence with vigor, and to remain firm and non-regressive.
This is the fourth seal.
A bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that the wisdom of the Tathāgata is without limit; they do not attempt to fathom the wisdom of the Tathāgata through fixed boundaries.
Because the bodhisattva has previously heard from immeasurable Buddhas that the wisdom of the Tathāgata is without limit, they are able to refrain from measuring it by means of fixed boundaries.
All that is expressed through the written words of the entire world has its limits; none can fully know the wisdom of the Tathāgata.
This is the fifth seal.

When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attain toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi a most excellent desire, a profound desire, a vast desire, a great desire, a manifold desire, an unconquerable desire, an unsurpassed desire, a firm desire, a desire that cannot be destroyed by any Māras or non-Buddhists together with their retinues, and a desire for omniscience that never regresses—when Bodhisattvas abide in such desires as these, they ultimately do not regress from unsurpassed enlightenment. This is the sixth seal.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the bodhisattva path, they disregard their own bodies and lives and cannot be thwarted or destroyed. This is because they have resolved their minds toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), because the nature of all-knowledge is ever-present before them, and because they have attained the light of the wisdom of all Buddhas; thus, they never abandon the Buddha-enlightenment (*buddhabodhi*) and never abandon spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). This is the seventh seal.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees a son of good family or a daughter of good family who is advancing toward the Great Vehicle, and causes them to increase their aspiration for the Buddha-dharma, causes them to dwell securely in all roots of goodness, causes them to embrace the mind of omniscience, and causes them not to retreat from unsurpassed enlightenment—this is the eighth seal.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva causes all sentient beings to attain a mind of equanimity, exhorts them to diligently cultivate the path to omniscience, and preaches the Dharma with a heart of great compassion, causing them never to regress from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; this is the ninth seal.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva shares the same roots of goodness as all Buddhas of the three periods of time, never severing the lineage of all Buddhas, and ultimately attaining the knowledge of all modes; this is the tenth seal.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten seals of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
By means of these, the bodhisattva swiftly accomplishes anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and becomes fully endowed with the supreme seal of wisdom regarding all the dharmas of the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of illumination of wisdom for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the illumination of wisdom that knows one will certainly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
and the illumination of wisdom that beholds all Buddhas.
The light of wisdom that perceives the death and rebirth of all sentient beings;
the light of wisdom that understands all dharma-gates of the sūtras;
the light of wisdom that, relying on spiritual friends, gives rise to the bodhicitta and accumulates all roots of goodness.
The light of wisdom that manifests the illuminating radiance of the knowledge of all Buddhas;
the light of wisdom that teaches and transforms all sentient beings, causing them all to dwell securely in the stage of the Tathāgata;
and the light of wisdom that expounds inconceivable and vast Dharma gates.
The light of wisdom that skillfully understands the power and majesty of the supernatural faculties of all Buddhas;
and the light of wisdom that fulfills all the pāramitās.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the illumination of the supreme wisdom-light of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of peerless abodes of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, which no sentient beings, Śrāvakas, or Pratyekabuddhas can equal."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
although a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), he does not realize it, because all his vows have not yet been fulfilled. This is the first peerless dwelling.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva plants all roots of goodness equal to the dharma-realm, yet has no slight attachment therein; this is the second peerless dwelling.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva conduct, knowing that all things are like illusions because all dharmas are utterly quiescent, he gives rise to no doubt or confusion regarding the Buddha-dharma; this is the third peerless dwelling.

Although the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is free from all worldly conceptualizations, he is nevertheless able to apply his attention, practicing the bodhisattva conduct for unspeakable eons, fulfilling his great vows, and never giving rise to a mind of weariness or exhaustion in the interim; this is the fourth peerless dwelling.
The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva has no grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, because the nature of all phenomena is quiescent; yet, he does not realize nirvāṇa. Why is this?
Because the path to omniscience has not yet been fully perfected, this is the fifth peerless dwelling.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that all kalpas are in truth no-kalpas, yet he truly speaks of the number of all kalpas; this is the sixth peerless dwelling.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all dharmas are entirely without activity, yet does not abandon the practice of the path as he seeks all Buddha-dharmas, this is the seventh peerless dwelling.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that the three realms are mind-only and the three periods of time are mind-only, yet he thoroughly understands that this mind is immeasurable and boundless; this is the eighth peerless dwelling.
For the sake of a single sentient being, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva conduct for unspeakable eons, desiring to establish them on the ground of all-knowledge;
as he does for one sentient being, so he does for all sentient beings, yet without giving rise to weariness or fatigue—this is the ninth peerless dwelling.
Although the bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices with full perfection, he does not realize awakening. Why is this?
The bodhisattva forms this thought:

"What I have undertaken was originally for the sake of sentient beings; therefore, I should remain long within birth and death, employing skillful means to benefit them and cause them all to dwell securely in the unsurpassed path of the Buddha."
This is the tenth peerless dwelling.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of peerless dwellings of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they shall attain the unsurpassed great wisdom and the peerless dwelling of all Buddha-dharmas.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sutra*, Scroll 54;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sutra*, Scroll 55.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Thirty-Eight, Part Three: Leaving the World.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give rise to ten kinds of non-inferior minds. What are these ten?
O Son of the Buddha!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
"I shall subdue all the celestial Māras and their retinues.
This is the first mind free from inferiority.
Furthermore, one forms this thought:
"I shall utterly destroy all non-Buddhists and their false teachings.
This is the second mind that is free from inferiority.
Furthermore, one forms this thought:
"I shall instruct all sentient beings with kind words and cause them all to rejoice.
This is the third mind free from inferiority.
Furthermore, one forms this thought:
"I shall fully accomplish all practices of the pāramitās that pervade the entire dharma-realm.
This is the fourth mind free from inferiority.
Furthermore, one forms this thought:
"I shall accumulate the treasury of all merit.
This is the fifth mind that is not inferior.
Furthermore, they form this thought:
"Unsurpassed Bodhi is vast and difficult to accomplish; I shall practice so as to bring it entirely to fulfillment.
This is the sixth mind free from inferiority.
Furthermore, they form this thought:
"I shall, by means of unsurpassed teaching and unsurpassed discipline, teach and discipline all sentient beings.
This is the seventh mind free from inferiority.
Furthermore, they form this thought:
"All worlds are diverse and different; I shall attain equal and perfect enlightenment with infinite bodies.
This is the eighth mind free from inferiority.
Furthermore, he reflects:

"When I practice the bodhisattva path, if there are sentient beings who come to beg from me for my hands, feet, ears, nose, blood, flesh, marrow, wife, children, elephants, horses, or even my royal throne, I shall be able to relinquish all such things without giving rise to a single thought of regret or sorrow. I do so solely for the benefit of all sentient beings, seeking no karmic reward, with great compassion as my primary motive and great kindness as my ultimate goal."
This is the ninth mind that is not inferior.
Furthermore, one forms this thought:

"All Buddhas of the three times, all Buddha-dharmas, all sentient beings, all lands, all worlds, all three times, the entire realm of empty space, the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the entire realm of linguistic designations, and the entire realm of quiescent nirvāṇa—all such various dharmas as these, I shall, by means of wisdom corresponding to a single thought-moment, fully know and fully awaken to them, fully see and fully realize them, fully cultivate and fully sever them; yet within them, there is no discrimination, freedom from discrimination, no variety, no distinction, no merit, no objective sphere, neither existence nor non-existence, neither one nor two."
By means of non-dual wisdom, one knows all dualities; by means of signless wisdom, one knows all signs;
by means of non-conceptual wisdom, one knows all conceptualizations; by means of non-differentiating wisdom, one knows all differences;
by means of non-distinctive wisdom, one knows all distinctions; and by means of non-worldly wisdom, one knows all worlds.
By means of non-worldly wisdom, one knows all worlds; by means of non-sentient-being wisdom, one knows all sentient beings;
by means of non-attachment wisdom, one knows all attachments; by means of non-abiding wisdom, one knows all abodes;
by means of non-defilement wisdom, one knows all defilements; and by means of inexhaustible wisdom, one knows all things.
Through the wisdom that exhaustively realizes the ultimate dharma-realm, they manifest bodies in all worlds;
through the wisdom that transcends speech and sound, they manifest ineffable sounds and voices; through the wisdom of a single self-nature, they enter into the absence of self-nature;
and through the wisdom of a single objective realm, they manifest manifold realms.
Knowing that all phenomena are ineffable, yet manifesting the speech of great mastery, they realize the stage of omniscience;
for the sake of teaching and taming all sentient beings, they manifest great supernormal powers and transformations throughout all worlds.
"This is the tenth mind that is not inferior.
Sons of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of minds that are not inferior which a bodhisattva mahāsattva generates."
If bodhisattvas abide in this mind, they will attain all the most supreme and non-inferior Buddha-dharmas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mountain-like superior minds regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
What are the ten? O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva constantly applies his mind to diligently cultivate all dharmas of omniscience, this is the first mountain-like superior mind.
Constantly observing that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty and unattainable is the second mountain-like superior mind.

Vowing to practice the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons and to cultivate all pure and white dharmas, and by abiding in all pure and white dharmas, knowing and seeing the immeasurable wisdom of the Tathāgata is the third mountain-like superior mind.

For the sake of seeking all Buddha-dharmas, one reverently serves all spiritual friends with an impartial mind, without divergent aspirations or a mind that steals the Dharma; one gives rise only to respect and never harbors ulterior motives, being able to relinquish everything one possesses—this is the fourth mountain-like superior mind.

If there are sentient beings who revile, slander, beat, or hack and carve them, causing pain to their physical forms even unto the taking of their lives—if they can endure all such matters as these, never giving rise to a distracted mind or a mind of anger and malice because of them, nor ever withdrawing or abandoning their great vow of great compassion, but rather causing it to increase without ceasing.
Why is this? Because the bodhisattva has achieved the renunciation of all phenomena as they truly are,
and because he has attained mastery over the patience and gentleness that realize the dharmas of all Tathāgatas.
This is the fifth mountain-like superior mind.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes superior great merits, namely:

superior merit of devas, superior merit of humans, superior merit of form, superior merit of power, superior merit of retinue, superior merit of desire, superior merit of sovereignty, superior merit of mastery, superior merit of fortune, and superior merit of wisdom.
Although they have accomplished such virtues, they never give rise to stained attachment toward them—namely:
they do not cling to flavors, they do not cling to desires, they do not cling to wealth, and they do not cling to retinues;

rather, they take profound delight in the Dharma, following the Dharma in their departure, abiding in the Dharma, tending toward the Dharma, and reaching the ultimate in the Dharma. They rely on the Dharma, take refuge in the Dharma, find shelter in the Dharma, and dwell in the Dharma; they protect the Dharma, love the Dharma, yearn for the Dharma, and contemplate the Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!
Although Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fully experience various kinds of Dharma-joy, they always remain far removed from the realms of Māra. Why is this?
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, in past lives, gave rise to this thought:
"I shall cause all sentient beings to forever leave the realm of all Māras and abide in the realm of the Buddhas."
This is the sixth mountain-like superior mind.
Although Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have diligently practiced the bodhisattva path for immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas in their quest for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi without slackening, they still think:
"I have only now first resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Practicing the bodhisattva path, one is neither startled, nor terrified, nor afraid.

Although one could attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in a single thought-moment, for the sake of sentient beings, one practices the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons without ceasing; this is the seventh mountain-like superior mind."

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that the natures of all sentient beings are not harmonious or virtuous; they are difficult to discipline and difficult to liberate, unable to recognize kindness and unable to repay it. For this reason, he generates a great vow for their sake, desiring to cause them all to attain mastery over mind and intention, to act without obstruction, to abandon evil thoughts, and not to give rise to afflictions toward others. This is the eighth mountain-like superior mind.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:
"It is not another who causes me to resolve upon Bodhicitta, nor do I wait for others to assist me in my practice. I have resolved upon it myself;
I shall gather all the Buddha-dharmas, vowing to exert myself with self-reliance, practicing the Bodhisattva path throughout the kalpas of the future until I attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

Therefore, as I now cultivate the bodhisattva practice, I shall purify my own mind and also purify the minds of others; I shall know my own realm and also know the realms of others, so that I may become entirely equal to the realms of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
This is the ninth mountain-like superior mind. A bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates in this way:

"There is not a single dharma that practices the bodhisattva path; there is not a single dharma that fulfills the bodhisattva path; there is not a single dharma that teaches and subdues all sentient beings; there is not a single dharma that makes offerings to and reveres all Buddhas; there is not a single dharma that has already attained, is now attaining, or will attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi); there is not a single dharma that has already been taught, is now being taught, or will be taught. Both the speaker and the dharma are unobtainable, yet one does not abandon the vow for unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment."
Why is this? Because when a bodhisattva seeks all dharmas, they find nothing at all; it is in this way that they give rise to anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Therefore, although there is nothing to be attained regarding phenomena, one diligently cultivates superior wholesome karma, purifies the remedies, brings wisdom to perfection, and increases in every thought-moment until all qualities are fully complete.
Their minds are neither startled nor terrified by this, and they do not form such a thought as:
"If all phenomena are entirely quiescent, what purpose do I have in seeking the path of unsurpassed bodhi?"
"This is the tenth mountain-like superior mind.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten mountain-like superior minds of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas regarding Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
If bodhisattvas abide therein, they attain the sovereign mind of the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom, which is like the king of mountains.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of ocean-like wisdom for entering anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
What are these ten? They are:
entering into all the infinite realms of sentient beings; this is the first ocean-like wisdom.
To enter all worlds without giving rise to discrimination is the second ocean-like wisdom.
To know that the entire realm of space is infinite and unobstructed, universally entering the net of all differentiated worlds throughout the ten directions, is the third ocean-like wisdom.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas skillfully enter the dharma-realm, namely:

entering without obstruction, entering without interruption, entering without permanence, entering the immeasurable, entering the unborn, entering the unceasing, and entering all things; because they fully understand these, this is the fourth ocean-like wisdom.

The bodhisattva mahāsattva fully understands all the roots of goodness accumulated, currently being accumulated, and yet to be accumulated by the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, Dharma-preachers, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all ordinary beings of the past, future, and present; as well as all the roots of goodness through which the Buddhas of the three times have already attained, are now attaining, or will attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi); and all the roots of goodness from the teachings preached, currently being preached, or yet to be preached by the Buddhas of the three times to discipline all sentient beings. Regarding all these, he comprehends them entirely, deeply believes in them with sympathetic joy (anumodanā), and vows to cultivate them with delight, never becoming weary or satisfied. This is the fifth ocean-like wisdom.

In every moment of thought, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva enters into unspeakable eons of the past. Within a single eon, whether it be ten billion Buddhas appearing in the world, a hundred billion Buddhas appearing in the world, a hundred thousand billion Buddhas appearing in the world; or an infinite number, an immeasurable number, a boundless number, an incomparable number, an incalculable number, an ineffable number, an inconceivable number, an unfathomable number, an unspeakable number, or an unspeakably unspeakable number—transcending all calculation—of World-Honored Buddhas who have appeared in the world; as well as their respective sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), assemblies of disciples and bodhisattvas, and their preaching of the Dharma for the subduing of all sentient beings; the lengthening or shortening of their lifespans, and the duration for which the Dharma remains—all such things he clearly perceives.
As it is with one kalpa, so it is with all kalpas.
He also fully knows all sentient beings in kalpas devoid of Buddhas who plant various roots of goodness for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
he also fully knows those sentient beings whose roots of goodness have matured and who shall see a Buddha in a future age.
Thus observing unspeakably, unspeakably many eons of the past, their minds never grow weary or satisfied; this is the sixth ocean-like wisdom.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas enter the future, they observe and discern all eons as infinite and boundless, knowing which eons have Buddhas and which eons have no Buddhas; in which eons how many Tathāgatas appear in the world, what the name of each individual Tathāgata is, in which world they dwell, what the name of that world is, how many sentient beings they deliver, and for how long their lifespan lasts.
Observing in this manner, they fully comprehend everything throughout the limits of the future; being inexhaustible and never weary of it, this is the seventh ocean-like wisdom.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva enters the present age to observe and contemplate, and in every moment of thought, he universally perceives the unspeakably many worlds of infinite varieties throughout the ten directions. In each of these, there are Buddhas who have already attained, are now attaining, or will attain unexcelled bodhi; they proceed to the site of enlightenment beneath the bodhi tree, sit upon the auspicious grass, subdue the armies of Māra, and realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Rising from there, they enter cities and towns, ascend to celestial palaces, preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma, turn the great wheel of Dharma, manifest supernatural powers, and discipline sentient beings; finally, they entrust them with the Dharma of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, relinquish their life-span, and enter parinirvāṇa.
After entering parinirvāṇa, they shall compile the Dharma-piṭaka so that it may long abide in the world, and they shall adorn the Buddha-stūpas with various kinds of offerings.

I also see all the sentient beings in those worlds who, encountering the Buddha and hearing the Dharma, receive, uphold, recite, remember, and contemplate it, thereby increasing their wisdom and understanding.
Observing in this manner throughout the ten directions, one remains without error regarding the Buddha-dharma.
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands that all Buddhas are entirely like dreams, yet is able to go to the abodes of all Buddhas to pay them respect and make offerings.

At that time, the bodhisattva is not attached to his own body, not attached to the Buddhas, not attached to the world, not attached to the assembly, not attached to the teaching of the Dharma, and not attached to the number of kalpas; yet he sees the Buddha, hears the Dharma, observes the world, and enters into the succession of kalpas without ever becoming weary or satisfied. This is the eighth ocean-like wisdom.

Throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons, in each and every eon, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva makes offerings and pays homage to unspeakably unspeakable, immeasurable Buddhas. He manifests his own death in this life and rebirth in another, making offerings surpassing all those of the triple world with every kind of requisite, while also making offerings to Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and the entire great assembly.
After each Tathāgata has entered Parinirvāṇa, he honors their relics with unsurpassed requisites and extensively practices giving to satisfy all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!

With an inconceivable mind, a mind that seeks no reward, a consummate mind, and a mind of benefit, for the sake of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons, makes offerings to all Buddhas, benefits sentient beings, protects and upholds the True Dharma, and reveals and expounds it. This is the ninth ocean-like wisdom.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, in the presence of all Buddhas, all bodhisattvas, and all Dharma-preachers, single-mindedly and exclusively seek the teachings spoken by bodhisattvas, the teachings studied by bodhisattvas, the teachings taught by bodhisattvas, the practices cultivated by bodhisattvas, the pure dharmas of bodhisattvas, the maturing dharmas of bodhisattvas, the taming dharmas of bodhisattvas, the impartial dharmas of bodhisattvas, the dharmas of renunciation of bodhisattvas, and the dharmas of dhāraṇī of bodhisattvas.
Having obtained these dharmas, they uphold, recite, analyze, and explain them without ever feeling weary or satisfied;

they cause immeasurable sentient beings to give rise to a mind corresponding to omniscience within the Buddha-dharma, to enter the true mark, and to attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
In this way, the Bodhisattva never grows weary or satiated throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons; this is the tenth ocean-like wisdom.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of ocean-like wisdom through which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas enter into Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the ocean of the unsurpassed, great wisdom of all Buddhas.
"Sons of the Buddha!
Regarding Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, there are ten jewel-like abodes for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."
What are the ten? O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to travel to the abodes of all Tathāgatas in countless worlds, where he gazes upon them, pays homage by prostrating at their feet, and serves and makes offerings to them; this is the first jewel-like dwelling.

In the presence of inconceivable Tathāgatas, one hears the True Dharma, receives and upholds it, and maintains it in mind without allowing it to be forgotten; one analyzes and contemplates it so that awakening wisdom increases. Such actions fill the ten directions; this is the second jewel-like dwelling.
To pass away from this world-system and manifest birth in another, yet remain entirely unconfused regarding the Buddha-dharma—this is the third jewel-like abiding.

To know that all dharmas arise from a single dharma, and to be able to analyze and expound them individually, because the various meanings of all dharmas ultimately converge upon a single meaning—this is the fourth jewel-like abiding.

Knowing how to become weary of and detached from afflictions, knowing how to bring afflictions to rest, knowing how to guard against afflictions, and knowing how to eliminate and sever afflictions; practicing the bodhisattva path without realizing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), yet ultimately reaching the further shore of that limit of reality; possessing skillful means and being well-trained in what is to be learned; causing all former vows and practices to reach full completion; and remaining free from physical fatigue—this is the fifth jewel-like dwelling.
Knowing that all mental discriminations of sentient beings have no location, yet still speaking of various directions and places;
although there is no discrimination and no volitional construction, one practices and acts for the sake of taming all sentient beings—this is the sixth jewel-like abiding.
Knowing that all phenomena are of one and the same nature, namely:

It is without intrinsic nature, without various natures, without immeasurable natures, without calculable natures, and without measurable natures; it is without form and without characteristics, such that neither unity nor multiplicity can be apprehended. Yet, one definitively knows and realizes: "This is the Dharma of the Buddhas; this is the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas; this is the Dharma of the Pratyekabuddhas; this is the Dharma of the Śrāvakas; this is the Dharma of ordinary beings; this is wholesome Dharma; this is unwholesome Dharma; this is mundane Dharma; this is supramundane Dharma; this is faulty Dharma; this is faultless Dharma; this is contaminated Dharma; this is uncontaminated Dharma"; and so on, up to: "This is conditioned Dharma; this is unconditioned Dharma. This is the seventh jewel-like abiding.
