The bodhisattva-mahāsattva seeks the Buddha but finds him unobtainable; seeks the bodhisattva but finds him unobtainable; seeks the Dharma but finds it unobtainable; and seeks sentient beings but finds them unobtainable; yet he does not abandon his vow to discipline sentient beings and lead them to achieve perfect enlightenment in all dharmas.

Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas skillfully observe and know the conceptual discriminations of all sentient beings, and they know the spheres of experience of all sentient beings; through skillful means, they transform and guide them so that they may attain nirvāṇa.
This is because they desire to fulfill their vows to transform sentient beings and thus ardently practice the bodhisattva path.
This is the eighth jewel-like dwelling.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that skillful teaching of the Dharma and the manifestation of nirvāṇa are all the various expedient means for delivering sentient beings; they are all established by the mind’s perception, yet they are neither inverted nor false.

Why is this? Because the Bodhisattva thoroughly understands that all phenomena are equal throughout the three periods of time, unshakable like suchness, and non-abiding in the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*). He does not perceive even a single sentient being who has been transformed, is being transformed, or will be transformed; nor does he perceive for himself anything to be practiced. He realizes that there is not the slightest phenomenon—whether arising or ceasing—that can be apprehended, yet he relies upon all phenomena so that his vows do not become empty.
This is the ninth jewel-like abiding.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, in the presence of each of the inconceivable and immeasurable Buddhas, hear the unspeakably unspeakable teachings of prophecy—wherein the names differ and the kalpas vary—and hear them thus continuously from one kalpa up to unspeakably unspeakable kalpas, they practice accordingly.

They are not startled, not terrified, not deluded, and not confused. This is because they know that the Tathāgata’s wisdom is inconceivable; because the Tathāgata’s words of prophecy are non-dual; because of the superior power of their own practices and vows; and because they respond to those to be transformed according to their needs, causing them to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and fulfill all vows throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm. This is the tenth jewel-like abiding.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten jewel-like abodes of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
If Bodhisattvas dwell securely in these dharmas, they shall attain the jewel of the unsurpassed, great wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give rise to ten kinds of adamantine Mahāyāna vows. What are these ten?
O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:
"All dharmas are without limit and cannot be exhausted."
"I shall, by means of the wisdom that exhausts the three periods of time, universally awaken to and comprehend all things without exception.
This is the first adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects:
"If there are immeasurable and boundless sentient beings within the space of a single hair-tip, how much more so throughout the entire Dharma-realm!"
"I shall bring them all to final liberation through unsurpassed nirvāṇa.
This is the second adamantine resolve of the Mahāyāna.
Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"The worlds of the ten directions are immeasurable, boundless, without limit, and inexhaustible.
I shall adorn all such worlds with the most supreme adornments of the Buddha-lands, so that all their adornments shall be entirely real."
This is the third adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects:
"All sentient beings are immeasurable, boundless, without limit, and inexhaustible."
"I shall dedicate all roots of goodness toward that light of unsurpassed wisdom so as to illuminate it.
This is the fourth adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:
"All Buddhas are immeasurable, boundless, without limit, and inexhaustible."
I shall dedicate the roots of goodness I have planted as offerings, pervading them all without any deficiency; only then shall I attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"This is the fifth adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas see all Buddhas and hear the Dharma they preach, they give rise to great joy. They do not cling to their own bodies, nor do they cling to the bodies of the Buddhas. They understand that the body of the Tathāgata is neither real nor unreal, neither existent nor non-existent, neither having a nature nor lacking a nature, neither form nor formless, neither with marks nor markless, neither arising nor ceasing; it truly has no existence, yet it does not destroy existence."
Why is this? Because one must not grasp at or become attached to any intrinsic nature or characteristics.
This is the sixth adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
O Son of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas encounter sentient beings who revile, scold, or disparage them; or who beat, flog, or strike them; or who cut off their hands and feet, or sever their ears and noses, or gouge out their eyes, or decapitate their heads—they are able to endure all such things and never, on account of these, give rise to a mind of anger or malice.
For unspeakably, unspeakably many incalculable eons, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices, gathering in and never abandoning sentient beings.

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have skillfully observed that all phenomena possess no dual characteristics; their minds are unshakable and undisturbed, and they are able to relinquish their own bodies and endure all suffering.
This is the seventh adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects as follows:
"In future ages, which are immeasurable, boundless, without limit, and inexhaustible, I shall exhaustively pass through those kalpas,
practicing the Bodhisattva path and transforming sentient beings within a single world; as it is with one world,
so it shall be for all worlds throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, yet my mind shall not be startled, nor terrified, nor afraid."
Why is this? Because the Dharma of the bodhisattva path ought to be thus, as one practices for the sake of all sentient beings.
This is the eighth adamantine resolve of the Mahāyāna.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:

'Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi has the mind as its root. If the mind is pure, one can fulfill all roots of goodness and will certainly attain mastery over the Buddha-bodhi; should one wish to achieve Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, it shall be accomplished at will.'"

If one wishes to sever all conditions for grasping and abide in the path of single-mindedness, I too am capable of attaining it; yet I do not sever them, because I desire to bring the Buddha-bodhi to ultimate completion, and thus I do not immediately realize unsurpassed bodhi.
Why is this? It is because one fulfills the original vow by practicing the bodhisattva path throughout all worlds to transform sentient beings.
This is the ninth adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that the Buddha is unobtainable, enlightenment is unobtainable, the Bodhisattva is unobtainable, all phenomena are unobtainable, sentient beings are unobtainable, the mind is unobtainable, conduct is unobtainable, the past is unobtainable, the future is unobtainable, the present is unobtainable, all worlds are unobtainable, and both the conditioned and the unconditioned are unobtainable.

In this way, the bodhisattva dwells in tranquility, dwells in profundity, dwells in cessation, dwells in non-contention, dwells in the ineffable, dwells in non-duality, dwells in equality, dwells in intrinsic nature, dwells in accordance with reality, dwells in liberation, dwells in nirvāṇa, and dwells in the limit of reality; yet they do not abandon any of their great vows, do not abandon the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), do not abandon the bodhisattva practices, do not abandon the training of sentient beings, do not abandon the perfections (*pāramitās*), do not abandon the subduing of sentient beings, do not abandon the service of the Buddhas, do not abandon the exposition of all dharmas, and do not abandon the adornment of world-systems.

Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have made great vows; although they thoroughly comprehend the characteristics of all phenomena, their great compassion increases even further, they fully practice immeasurable merits, and they do not abandon sentient beings in their hearts.

Why is this? "All dharmas are utterly non-existent; yet ordinary people, deluded and ignorant, neither know nor perceive them. I shall cause them all to attain awakening, so that they may clearly and distinctly illuminate and understand the nature of all dharmas."
Why is this? Because all Buddhas abide in quiescent extinction, yet with a heart of great compassion, they preach the Dharma and transform sentient beings throughout all worlds without ever ceasing.
How could I now abandon great compassion?

Furthermore, I have previously awakened the mind of vast vows, the mind determined to benefit all sentient beings, the mind to accumulate all roots of goodness, the mind to abide in skillful dedication, the mind to give birth to profound wisdom, the mind to embrace all sentient beings, and the mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings;
I have spoken words of truth and not of falsehood, vowing to grant all sentient beings the unsurpassed Great Dharma and vowing that the lineage of all Buddhas shall never be severed.

Now that all sentient beings have not yet attained liberation, have not yet achieved perfect enlightenment, and have not yet perfected the Buddha-dharma, their great vows remain unfulfilled; how can you wish to abandon great compassion?
This is the tenth adamantine Mahāyāna vow-mind.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of adamantine Mahāyāna vow-minds that a bodhisattva mahāsattva generates.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme great supernormal knowledge of vajra-nature. "O Sons of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of great undertakings."
What are these ten?
O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:
"I shall offer worship and respect to all Buddhas.
This is the first great arousal of the aspiration.
Furthermore, one forms this thought:
"I shall nurture all the roots of goodness possessed by all bodhisattvas.
This is the second great arousal of the mind.
Furthermore, one forms this thought:

"After the parinirvāṇa of all Tathāgatas, I shall adorn their stūpas and make offerings to them with every kind of flower, every kind of garland, every kind of incense, every kind of unguent, every kind of powdered incense, every kind of robe, every kind of parasol, every kind of banner, and every kind of pennant; furthermore, I shall uphold and protect their True Dharma."
This is the third great undertaking.
Furthermore, he forms this thought:
"I shall teach and discipline all sentient beings, causing them to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"This is the fourth great undertaking.
Furthermore, he forms this thought:
'I shall adorn all worlds with the unsurpassed adornments of the buddha-fields.'"
This is the fifth great undertaking.
Furthermore, he forms this thought:

"I shall give rise to the mind of great compassion; for the sake of even a single sentient being, in every world, I shall individually practice the bodhisattva path throughout each and every kalpa until the end of the future."

Just as for one sentient being, so it is for all sentient beings; he causes them all to attain the unsurpassed enlightenment of a Buddha, never giving rise to even a single thought of weariness or indolence.
This is the sixth great undertaking.
Furthermore, he reflects:
"Those Tathāgatas are immeasurable and boundless; I shall, at the site of a single Tathāgata, pass through inconceivable kalpas in respectful service and offering."
"As it is with one Tathāgata, so it is with all Tathāgatas.
This is the seventh great undertaking.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects thus:
"After those Tathāgatas have entered parinirvāṇa, I shall erect for each and every one of them a precious stūpa for all their relics, its height and breadth equal to unspeakable numbers of worlds;

I shall likewise create images of the Buddhas in the same manner, and for inconceivable kalpas, I shall make offerings with all kinds of jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, incense, flowers, and robes, never giving rise to even a single thought of weariness or fatigue."

For the sake of accomplishing the Buddha-dharma, for the sake of making offerings to all Buddhas, for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings, and for the sake of protecting, upholding, revealing, and expounding the True Dharma.
This is the eighth great undertaking.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects:
"By means of these roots of goodness, I shall realize unexcelled bodhi, attain entry into the stage of all Tathāgatas, and become equal in essence to all Tathāgatas."
This is the ninth great undertaking.
Furthermore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:

"Once I have attained perfect enlightenment, throughout unspeakable eons in all worlds, I shall expound the true Dharma and manifest inconceivable, sovereign supernormal powers; my body, speech, and mind shall never grow weary, nor shall I ever depart from the true Dharma."

Sustained by the power of the Buddha, they diligently practice great vows for the sake of all sentient beings; with great loving-kindness as their foremost priority and great compassion brought to ultimate fulfillment; having realized the dharma of signlessness and abiding in truthful speech; having realized that all dharmas are utterly quiescent;

knowing that all sentient beings are ultimately ungraspable yet not contradicting the workings of karma; being of one essence with the Buddhas of the three periods of time; pervading the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space; penetrating the signlessness of all phenomena; accomplishing the state of neither arising nor ceasing; and being fully endowed with all Buddha-dharmas—they subdue sentient beings through the power of their great vows and perform the great work of a Buddha without rest.
"This is the tenth great undertaking.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of great undertakings of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas."
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will not sever their bodhisattva practices and will become fully endowed with the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great wisdom.
"Sons of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of ultimate great tasks."
What are these ten? They are:
the ultimate great task of reverently making offerings to all Tathāgatas;
The ultimate great task of being able to rescue and protect all sentient beings according to their needs;
the ultimate great task of single-mindedly seeking all Buddha-dharmas;
and the ultimate great task of accumulating all roots of goodness.
The ultimate great matter of contemplating all Buddha-dharmas;
the ultimate great matter of fulfilling all vows;
the ultimate great matter of accomplishing all bodhisattva practices;
The ultimate great task of serving all spiritual friends;
the ultimate great task of proceeding to the abodes of all Tathāgatas in all worlds;
and the ultimate great task of hearing and upholding the true Dharma of all Buddhas.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the ultimate realization of the great wisdom of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of indestructible faith for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
indestructible faith in all Buddhas;
indestructible faith in all Buddha-dharmas;
Unwavering faith in all noble Saṅghas;
unwavering faith in all bodhisattvas;
and unwavering faith in all spiritual friends.
Unwavering faith in all sentient beings;
unwavering faith in all the great vows of bodhisattvas;
and unwavering faith in all the practices of bodhisattvas.
Indestructible faith in reverently making offerings to all Buddhas;
indestructible faith in the bodhisattvas’ skillful and secret means for teaching and taming all sentient beings.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain unshakable faith in the supreme, great wisdom of all buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of receiving the prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*). What are these ten?
They are as follows:
They receive the prediction of enlightenment by possessing profound internal understanding;
they receive the prediction of enlightenment by being able to give rise to all the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva in accordance with reality;
and they receive the prediction of enlightenment by cultivating vast practices.
Receiving the prediction of enlightenment in the presence [of the Buddha]; receiving the prediction of enlightenment in the absence [of the Buddha];
and receiving the prediction of enlightenment through the realization of bodhi by means of one's own mind.
One receives the prediction of enlightenment by accomplishing patience;
one receives the prediction by teaching and taming sentient beings;
and one receives the prediction by bringing all kalpas to ultimate completion.
They attain the prophecy of enlightenment through mastery over all bodhisattva practices; these are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they shall receive the prophecy from all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of dedication of roots of goodness by which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are able to dedicate all their roots of goodness.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
may my roots of goodness be identical with the vows of spiritual friends; may they be accomplished in this way, and not otherwise.
May my roots of goodness be identical with the mind of the spiritual friend; may they be accomplished in this way, and not otherwise.
May my roots of goodness be identical with the conduct of the spiritual friend; may they be accomplished in this way, and not otherwise.
May my roots of goodness be identical with the roots of goodness of the spiritual friend; may they be accomplished in this way, and not otherwise.
May my roots of goodness be equal to those of spiritual friends; may they be accomplished in this way, and not otherwise.
May my roots of goodness be equal to the mindfulness of spiritual friends; may they be accomplished in this way, and not otherwise.
May my roots of goodness be equal to the purity of spiritual friends; may they be accomplished in this way, and not otherwise.
May my roots of goodness be identical with those of the spiritual friends in which they abide; may I achieve such accomplishment, and not another.
May my roots of goodness be identical with the fulfillment achieved by the spiritual friends; may I achieve such accomplishment, and not another.
May my roots of goodness be identical with the indestructibility of the spiritual friends; may I achieve such accomplishment, and not another.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed dedication of roots of goodness.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten ways of attaining wisdom.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
One attains wisdom through mastery over giving;
one attains wisdom through profound understanding of all Buddha-dharmas;
one attains wisdom through entry into the boundless wisdom of the Tathāgata.
They attain wisdom that can sever doubt and realize insight regarding all questions and answers;
they attain wisdom by entering into the meanings understood by the wise;
and they attain wisdom through a profound understanding of the skillful mastery of vocal expression employed by all Tathāgatas within all Buddha-dharmas.

The wisdom by which one deeply understands that even a small root of goodness planted before the Buddhas will necessarily fulfill all pure dharmas and result in attaining the immeasurable wisdom and insight of a Tathāgata;
the wisdom by which one accomplishes the inconceivable abodes of a bodhisattva;
and the wisdom by which one is able, within a single thought-moment, to travel to unspeakably many Buddha-fields.

They awaken to the bodhi of all Buddhas; they enter all dharma-realms and hear and retain all that the Buddhas have taught; they penetrate deeply into the various adorned speech and sounds of all Tathāgatas and attain wisdom.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed wisdom of direct realization of all buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of immeasurable, boundless, and vast resolve.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
Before all Buddhas, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind;
observing the realms of all sentient beings, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind;
observing all lands, all worlds, and all dharma-realms, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind.
Observing that all phenomena are like empty space, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind;
observing the vast practices of all bodhisattvas, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind;
maintaining right mindfulness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind.
Observing the inconceivable fruits of various karmas, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind;
adorning and purifying all Buddha-fields, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind;
entering universally into all great assemblies of Buddhas, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind.
Contemplating the sublime voices of all Tathāgatas, they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind.
This is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide in this mind, they will attain the ocean of immeasurable, boundless, and vast wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of treasuries. What are these ten?
That is to say:
knowing that all phenomena are the treasury for initiating meritorious conduct;
knowing that all phenomena are the treasury of right reflection;
Knowing that all phenomena are the treasury of illumination through dhāraṇīs;
knowing that all phenomena are the treasury of eloquent exposition;
knowing that all phenomena are the treasury of the ineffable, well-awakened reality.
To know that all Buddhas’ sovereign supernormal powers constitute the treasury of observation and manifestation;
to know that all dharmas constitute the treasury of skillful production and equality;
and to know that all dharmas constitute the treasury of constantly seeing all Buddhas.
To know that all inconceivable eons are perfectly understood as abiding like illusions is the treasury;
to know all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is the treasury that gives rise to joy and pure faith.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the treasury of the unsurpassed wisdom of all buddhas and will be able to fully subdue all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of discipline for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the discipline of not giving rise to slander toward any of the Buddha-dharmas;
and the discipline of an indestructible mind of faith and joy toward all Buddhas.
The discipline of giving rise to respect and reverence toward all bodhisattvas;
the discipline of never abandoning the mind of affection and delight toward all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*);
and the discipline of not giving rise to thoughts of recollection toward any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
The discipline of remaining far removed from all that causes regression from the bodhisattva path;
the discipline of not giving rise to any thoughts of harming sentient beings;
and the discipline of cultivating all roots of goodness so that they reach ultimate perfection.
The discipline that is able to subdue all māras;
and the discipline that brings all pāramitās to fulfillment.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme discipline of great wisdom.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
mastery over life, because one abides in a lifespan for unspeakable eons;
Mastery over the mind, because wisdom can enter into incalculable samādhis;
mastery over requisites, because one can adorn all worlds with immeasurable ornaments;
mastery over karma, because one receives retribution according to the appropriate time.
Mastery over birth, because of manifesting birth in all worlds;
mastery over resolve, because of seeing Buddhas filling all worlds;
mastery over vows, because of attaining perfect enlightenment in various lands according to one's desire and at any time.
Mastery over spiritual powers, because they manifest all great supernormal transformations;
mastery over phenomena, because they manifest boundless gateways to the Dharma;
and mastery over wisdom, because in every thought-moment they manifest the Tathāgata’s ten powers, fearlessnesses, and the attainment of perfect enlightenment.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the perfection of all Buddhas' pāramitās, wisdom, spiritual powers, and mastery over enlightenment.

Chapter Thirty-Eight, Part Four: The Chapter on Transcending the World.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded functions."
What are these ten? They are:
the unimpeded function regarding sentient beings;
The unimpeded function of the buddha-field;
the unimpeded function of the Dharma;
the unimpeded function of the body;
The unimpeded function of vows;
the unimpeded function of the objective realm;
the unimpeded function of wisdom;
The unimpeded function of supernormal powers;
the unimpeded function of spiritual power;
the unimpeded function of strength.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the unimpeded activity of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas regarding the equality of all sentient beings?
O Son of the Buddha!”
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded activities regarding sentient beings. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
The unimpeded function of knowing that all sentient beings are devoid of the nature of sentient beings;
the unimpeded function of knowing that all sentient beings are sustained solely by conceptualization;
and the unimpeded function of preaching the Dharma for all sentient beings without ever missing the proper time.
The unimpeded function of universally manifesting throughout all realms of sentient beings;
the unimpeded function of placing all sentient beings within a single pore without any crowding;
and the unimpeded function of manifesting all worlds in other directions for all sentient beings so that they may see them all.
They manifest the unimpeded function of appearing in the bodies of Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protecting Devas for the sake of all sentient beings;
they manifest the unimpeded function of the tranquil deportment of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas for the sake of all sentient beings;
and they manifest the unimpeded function of the bodhisattva practices for the sake of all sentient beings.
To manifest for all sentient beings the physical forms and marks of excellence of all Buddhas, the power of all-knowledge, and the unimpeded function of attaining equal and perfect enlightenment—
this is the tenth.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of unimpeded functions regarding the buddha-lands of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the unimpeded function of making all lands into a single land;
the unimpeded function of causing all lands to enter into a single pore;
The unimpeded function of knowing that all lands are inexhaustible;
the unimpeded function of filling all lands while sitting cross-legged in a single body;
and the unimpeded function of manifesting all lands within a single body.
The unimpeded function of shaking all lands without causing sentient beings to feel fear;
the unimpeded function of adorning a single land with the adornments of all lands;
and the unimpeded function of adorning all lands with the adornments of a single land.
By means of the unimpeded power that manifests to sentient beings a single Tathāgata and a single assembly within all Buddha-fields;

and by means of the unimpeded power that universally manifests to all sentient beings all small, medium, large, vast, deep, upward-facing, downward-facing, sideways-facing, and upright worlds throughout the networks of all directions in their infinite variety.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded application of dharmas."
What are these ten? They are:

knowing that all phenomena enter into a single phenomenon, and a single phenomenon enters into all phenomena, yet without contradicting the unimpeded function of the mental understandings of sentient beings;
The unimpeded function of giving birth to all phenomena from the *prajñāpāramitā* and explaining them to others so that they all attain awakening;
the unimpeded function of knowing that all phenomena are beyond words and letters, yet enabling all sentient beings to gain entry into this realization;
and the unimpeded function of knowing that all phenomena enter into a single characteristic (*ekalakṣaṇa*), yet being able to expound immeasurable characteristics of phenomena.
The unimpeded function of knowing that all phenomena transcend verbal expression, yet being able to expound infinite dharma-gates for others;
the unimpeded function of skillfully revolving the universal wheel of syllables regarding all phenomena;
and the unimpeded function of entering all phenomena into a single dharma-gate without contradiction, such that one could explain them for unspeakable eons without exhaustion.
Because all phenomena enter into the Buddha-dharma, there is the unimpeded function of causing all sentient beings to attain awakening and understanding;
because one knows that all phenomena have no boundaries, there is the unimpeded function;

because one knows that all phenomena have the boundary of non-obstruction, being like an illusory net with infinite distinctions, there is the inexhaustible unimpeded function of preaching for sentient beings throughout immeasurable eons.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded functions of the body."
What are the ten? They are:
the unimpeded application of causing the bodies of all sentient beings to enter one's own body;
The unimpeded function of entering the bodies of all sentient beings with one's own body;
the unimpeded function of all Buddha-bodies entering the body of a single Buddha;
and the unimpeded function of the body of a single Buddha entering the bodies of all Buddhas.
The unimpeded function of all lands entering one’s own body;
the unimpeded function of filling all phenomena of the three periods of time with a single body to manifest to sentient beings;
and the unimpeded function of manifesting infinite bodies within a single body while entering samādhi.
The unimpeded function of manifesting within a single body as many bodies as there are sentient beings and thereby attaining perfect enlightenment;

the unimpeded function of manifesting the body of a single sentient being within the bodies of all sentient beings, and manifesting the bodies of all sentient beings within the body of a single sentient being;
and the unimpeded function of manifesting the Dharma-body within the bodies of all sentient beings, and manifesting the bodies of all sentient beings within the Dharma-body.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded application of vows."
What are the ten? They are:
employing all the vows of all bodhisattvas as one's own vows through unimpeded application;
The unimpeded function of manifesting the attainment of self-enlightenment through the power of the vows made by all Buddhas to achieve bodhi;
the unimpeded function of attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* spontaneously in accordance with those beings to be transformed;
and the unimpeded function of never severing great vows throughout all infinite eons.
They remain far removed from the body of consciousness and do not cling to the body of wisdom; they manifest all bodies through the unimpeded function of sovereign vows;
they relinquish their own bodies to fulfill the vows of others through unimpeded function;
and they universally transform all sentient beings without abandoning their great vows through unimpeded function.
The unimpeded function of practicing the bodhisattva path throughout all kalpas while never severing great vows;

the unimpeded function of manifesting perfect enlightenment within a single pore, and by the power of vows, pervading all buddha-lands to thus manifest for each and every sentient being across unspeakably unspeakable worlds;

the unimpeded function of proclaiming a single phrase of Dharma that encompasses the entire dharma-realm, raising great clouds of the True Dharma, flashing the lightning of liberation, thundering the roar of the Real Dharma, and raining down the nectar of immortality to saturate the realms of all sentient beings through the power of great vows.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded functions regarding their spheres of activity."
What are these ten? They are:
the unimpeded function of abiding within the realm of the Dharma-dhatu while not abandoning the realm of sentient beings;
The unimpeded function of abiding in the realm of the Buddhas without abandoning the realm of Māras;
the unimpeded function of abiding in the realm of nirvāṇa without abandoning the realm of birth and death;
and the unimpeded function of entering the realm of omniscience without severing the realm of the bodhisattva lineage.
The unimpeded function of abiding in the realm of tranquility while not abandoning the realm of distraction;

the unimpeded function of abiding in the realm that is without going, without coming, without conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), without characteristics, without intrinsic nature, and beyond verbal expression—like the realm of space—while not abandoning the realm of the conceptual proliferation of all sentient beings;
and the unimpeded function of abiding in the realm of the powers and liberations while not abandoning the realms of all spatial directions.
The unimpeded power of entering the realm of the limit of non-existence of sentient beings, yet never abandoning the teaching and transformation of all sentient beings;
the unimpeded power of abiding in the realms of meditative concentration, liberation, supernormal powers, clear wisdom, and tranquility, yet manifesting birth in all worlds;

and the unimpeded power of abiding in the realm of the Tathāgata’s adornment of all practices and the attainment of perfect enlightenment, yet manifesting the tranquil deportment of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded application of wisdom."
What are these ten? They are:
the unimpeded application of inexhaustible eloquence;
The unimpeded function of never forgetting or losing any *dhāraṇī*;
the unimpeded function of being able to definitively know and definitively explain the faculties of all sentient beings;
and the unimpeded function of knowing, within a single thought-moment, the mental activities of all sentient beings through unimpeded wisdom.

The unimpeded function of knowing the desires, latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), habitual perfumings (*vāsanā*), and the diseases of affliction of all sentient beings, and accordingly administering the medicine;
the unimpeded function of being able, in a single thought-moment, to enter the ten powers (*daśabala*) of the Tathāgata;
and the unimpeded function of knowing, by means of unimpeded wisdom, all kalpas of the three periods of time and the sentient beings therein.
The unimpeded function of manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment in every moment of thought to demonstrate to sentient beings without interruption;
the unimpeded function of knowing the karma of all sentient beings through the perception of a single sentient being;
and the unimpeded function of understanding the speech of all sentient beings through the sound of a single sentient being.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of unimpeded applications of supernormal powers."
What are these ten? They are:
the unimpeded function of manifesting the bodies of all worlds within a single body;
The unimpeded power of hearing and receiving all the teachings expounded within the assemblies of all Buddhas within a single Buddha’s assembly;
the unimpeded power of accomplishing ineffable, unsurpassed enlightenment within the mental thought of a single sentient being and awakening the minds of all sentient beings;
and the unimpeded power of manifesting the diverse vocal expressions of all worlds with a single voice, enabling all sentient beings to each attain understanding.

The unimpeded function of manifesting within a single thought-moment all the various distinctions of karmic fruits throughout all kalpas of the past, causing all sentient beings to fully know and see them;
the unimpeded function of a single atom appearing as vast Buddha-fields with infinite adornments;
and the unimpeded function of causing all worlds to be fully endowed with adornments.
The unimpeded function of universally entering all three periods of time;
the unimpeded function of emitting the great light of the Dharma to manifest the bodhi of all Buddhas and the practices and vows of all sentient beings;

and the unimpeded function of skillfully guarding all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, the World Protectors, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, as well as all the ten powers of the Tathāgatas and the roots of goodness of bodhisattvas.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas attain this unimpeded function, they are then able to universally enter all Buddha-dharmas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of unimpeded applications of spiritual power.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The unimpeded function of placing unspeakably many worlds within a single atom;
the unimpeded function of manifesting within a single atom all Buddha-fields equal in extent to the Dharma-realm;

and the unimpeded function of placing the waters of all great oceans within a single pore while traveling back and forth through the worlds of the ten directions without disturbing or harming sentient beings.
The unimpeded function of manifesting all miraculous powers within one’s own body such that unspeakably many worlds are contained therein;
the unimpeded function of binding incalculable Diamond Ring Mountains with a single hair and traveling through all worlds without causing sentient beings to feel fear;

and the unimpeded function of making an unspeakable eon into a single eon and a single eon into an unspeakable eon, while manifesting within them the distinctions of formation and destruction without causing sentient beings to feel fear in their minds.
The unimpeded function of manifesting the various transformations and destructions of the calamities of water, fire, and wind in all worlds, yet without causing affliction to sentient beings;

the unimpeded function of being able to protect and sustain all the necessities of life for all sentient beings when all worlds are destroyed by the three calamities, ensuring they suffer no loss or deficiency;

and the unimpeded function of holding inconceivable worlds with a single hand and casting them beyond unspeakable numbers of worlds, without causing sentient beings to have any thought of alarm or fear.
To declare that all lands are identical to empty space, causing all sentient beings to fully awaken to and understand this unimpeded function—
this is the tenth.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of unimpeded functions of power.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The unimpeded power of sentient beings, because it teaches, transforms, and subdues them without ever abandoning them;
the unimpeded power of lands, because it manifests unspeakable adornments to adorn them;
the unimpeded power of dharmas, because it causes all bodies to enter the bodyless state.
The unimpeded function of the power of eons, because spiritual practice is uninterrupted;
the unimpeded function of the power of the Buddha, because it awakens those who are asleep;
the unimpeded function of the power of conduct, because it encompasses all bodhisattva practices.
The Tathāgata’s unimpeded power of strength, for the sake of delivering all sentient beings;
the unimpeded power of strength without a teacher, for the sake of self-awakening to all dharmas;
the unimpeded power of the strength of all-knowledge, for the sake of attaining perfect enlightenment through all-knowledge.
The power of great compassion has unimpeded function because it does not abandon any sentient being.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are called the ten kinds of unimpeded functions of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If one attains these ten unimpeded functions, whether they wish to realize or not realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, it will accord with their intent without obstruction; yet, even though they have attained perfect enlightenment, they do not cease practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva.
For what reason?
Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have made great vows and enter the gate of boundless, unimpeded function, skillfully manifesting [all things].
"O Son of the Buddha!..."
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of playful manifestations. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
manifesting the body of a buddha-field through the body of a sentient being, yet without destroying the body of the sentient being—this is the playful manifestation of a bodhisattva;
To manifest the body of a buddha-field as the body of a sentient being, yet without destroying the body of the buddha-field, is the playful mastery of a bodhisattva;
to manifest the bodies of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas within the body of a buddha, yet without diminishing the body of the Tathāgata, is the playful mastery of a bodhisattva;
to manifest the body of a Tathāgata within the bodies of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, yet without increasing the bodies of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, is the playful mastery of a bodhisattva.

To manifest the body of one who has attained perfect enlightenment while within the body of bodhisattva practice, yet without interrupting that body of bodhisattva practice, is the playful sport of a bodhisattva;

to manifest the body of one practicing bodhisattva conduct while within the body of one who has attained perfect enlightenment, yet without diminishing that body of realized *bodhi*, is the playful sport of a bodhisattva;
to manifest the body of birth and death within the realm of *nirvāṇa*, yet without being attached to birth and death, is the playful sport of a bodhisattva.
To manifest nirvana within the realm of birth and death, yet not ultimately enter into nirvana, is the play of a bodhisattva;
to enter into samādhi while manifesting all activities of walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, yet not relinquishing the meditative absorption of samādhi, is the play of a bodhisattva.

Having heard and received the Dharma from a single Buddha, their body remains unmoving; yet, through the power of samādhi, they manifest their bodies individually within the assemblies of unspeakably many Buddhas. Without dividing their bodies and without arising from meditative absorption, they continue to hear and receive the Dharma without interruption. Thus, in every thought-moment, from each samādhi-body, they produce unspeakably unspeakable numbers of samādhi-bodies. Even if all successive kalpas were to come to an end, the bodhisattva’s samādhi-bodies would never be exhausted; this is the bodhisattva’s play.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great wisdom-play.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of spheres of activity.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
To manifest the gates of the infinite Dharma-realm and cause sentient beings to enter it is the realm of the Bodhisattva;
to manifest the immeasurable and wondrous adornments of all worlds and cause sentient beings to enter them is the realm of the Bodhisattva;
to transform and proceed to all realms of sentient beings, awakening them all through skillful means, is the realm of the Bodhisattva.
To manifest the body of a bodhisattva from the body of a Tathāgata, and to manifest the body of a Tathāgata from the body of a bodhisattva—this is the domain of the bodhisattva.
To manifest world-systems within the realm of empty space, and to manifest the realm of empty space within world-systems—this is the domain of the bodhisattva.
To manifest the realm of nirvāṇa within the realm of birth and death, and to manifest the realm of birth and death within the realm of nirvāṇa—this is the domain of the bodhisattva.
To produce the speech of all Buddha-dharmas from within the speech of a single sentient being is the realm of the bodhisattva;
to manifest a single body with boundless bodies, and to manifest all differentiated bodies from a single body, is the realm of the bodhisattva;
to fill the entire dharma-realm with a single body is the realm of the bodhisattva.

To cause all sentient beings within a single thought-moment to resolve upon Bodhicitta, each manifesting infinite bodies and attaining equal and perfect enlightenment—this is the realm of the Bodhisattva.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the realm of the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of powers. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
The power of profound resolve, because it is unmixed with any worldly sentiments;
the power of superior profound resolve, because it does not abandon any of the Buddha-dharmas;
and the power of skillful means, because all that is undertaken is brought to ultimate completion.
The power of wisdom, because it thoroughly understands all mental activities;
the power of aspiration, because it fulfills all that is sought;
the power of practice, because it remains uninterrupted throughout the limits of the future.
The power of the vehicles, which is able to give birth to all vehicles while never abandoning the Great Vehicle;
the power of spiritual transformations, which within each and every pore manifests the appearance of all Tathāgatas in all pure worlds;
and the power of enlightenment, which causes all sentient beings to resolve to attain Buddhahood without interruption.
The power of turning the wheel of Dharma, because in proclaiming a single phrase of the Dharma, one accords with the faculties, inclinations, and desires of all sentient beings.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the ten powers of the unsurpassed omniscience of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of fearlessness. What are these ten?
O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to hear and retain all speech, forming this thought:
"Suppose there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings coming from the ten directions to question me regarding hundreds of thousands of great Dharmas."
Regarding that question, I did not perceive even the slightest sign of it being difficult to answer;

because I perceived none, my mind attained fearlessness, reaching the ultimate shore of great fearlessness, such that I am able to respond to whatever is asked, severing all doubts without any timidity.
"This is the first fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva attains the unimpeded eloquence of the Tathāgata’s consecration, reaching the ultimate further shore of revealing the secrets of all written characters, words, and sounds, they form this thought:"
"Suppose there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings coming from the ten directions, questioning me with immeasurable dharmas.
In those questions, I do not perceive even the slightest sign of difficulty in answering;

because I perceive none, my mind attains fearlessness, reaching the ultimate shore of great fearlessness. According to their questions, I am able to respond to them all, severing their doubts and uncertainties without any apprehension."
"This is the second fearlessness of a bodhisattva. Son of the Buddha!

A bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that all phenomena are empty; they are devoid of self and devoid of what belongs to a self; there is no action and no agent, no knower, no life-principle, no nourisher, and no *pudgala*; they are free from the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, and have forever transcended all views. With a mind like space, they form this thought:"
"I do not see any subtle mark in sentient beings that can harm my physical, verbal, or mental actions.
Why is this? Because the Bodhisattva has distanced himself from "self" and "what belongs to self," he does not perceive even the slightest nature or characteristic in any phenomena.

Because they do not perceive [such things], their minds attain fearlessness; they ultimately reach the shore of that great fearlessness, remaining firm, courageous, and indestructible—this is the third fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!

Protected by the power of the Buddhas and sustained by the power of the Buddhas, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in the majestic deportment of the Buddhas; his conduct is true and without change, and he forms this thought:
"I do not see even the slightest aspect of my deportment that would cause sentient beings to give rise to reproach."
Because he does not see [such faults], his mind attains fearlessness, and he teaches the Dharma with composure amidst the great assembly; this is the fourth fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s actions of body, speech, and mind are entirely pure, bright white and gentle, and far removed from all evils; he forms this thought:
"I do not perceive even the slightest aspect within my actions of body, speech, and mind that is worthy of censure."
Because he does not see [them], his mind attains fearlessness, enabling him to establish sentient beings in the Buddha-dharma; this is the fifth fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are constantly attended and guarded by the Vajrapāṇi-dharaṇīs, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, and others; all Tathāgatas protect and mind them without ever abandoning them.
The bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
"I do not see any demons, non-Buddhists, or sentient beings with [wrong] views who are able to come and obstruct even a slight portion of my practice of the bodhisattva path."

Because they do not perceive [such things], their minds attain fearlessness; having ultimately reached the shore of that great fearlessness, they give rise to a heart of joy and practice the bodhisattva conduct—this is the sixth fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has already achieved the first faculty of mindfulness (*smṛtīndriya*), his mind is never forgetful of what the Buddha has approved, and he forms this thought:
"Regarding the words, phrases, and dharmas of the path to awakening taught by the Tathāgata, I do not perceive therein even the slightest sign of forgetfulness."

Because they do not perceive [such things], their minds attain fearlessness; they uphold all the true Dharma of the Tathāgatas and practice the bodhisattva path—this is the seventh fearlessness of a bodhisattva.

O Son of the Buddha! The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has fully mastered wisdom and skillful means; he has attained the ultimate perfection of all the powers of a Bodhisattva. He constantly and diligently teaches and transforms all sentient beings, and perpetually binds his heart of aspiration to the Bodhi of the Buddhas. Yet, out of compassion for sentient beings and for the sake of bringing them to maturity, he manifests birth within a world turbid with afflictions, appearing in a noble lineage, surrounded by a perfect retinue, with all desires fulfilled at will and abounding in joy and pleasure. He then reflects:

"Although I am gathered here with this retinue, I do not see even the slightest sign in which I might become attached, such that I would neglect my cultivation of dhyāna, liberation, various samādhis, dhāraṇīs, eloquence, and the dharmas of the Bodhisattva path."

Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have attained mastery over all dharmas and reached the other shore; they cultivate the bodhisattva practices with a vow never to sever them, and they do not perceive any single realm in the world that can delude or confuse the bodhisattva path.

Because they do not perceive [such things], their minds attain fearlessness; they ultimately reach the great shore of fearlessness and, through the power of their great vows, manifest birth in all worlds. This is the eighth fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva never forgets the mind of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge). Riding upon the Great Vehicle, he practices the conduct of a Bodhisattva; by the power of the great mind of omniscience, he manifests all the tranquil deportments of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, and reflects:
"I do not perceive in myself even the slightest sign of seeking deliverance through the two vehicles."

Because they do not perceive [such things], their minds attain fearlessness; they reach the shore of that supreme, great fearlessness and are universally able to manifest all vehicles and paths, ultimately fulfilling the equality of the Great Vehicle. This is the ninth fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes all pure and white dharmas, is fully endowed with roots of goodness, perfects the supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), and ultimately abides in the Bodhi of all Buddhas. Having fulfilled all the practices of a Bodhisattva and received the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) of omniscience from all Buddhas, they constantly transform sentient beings while practicing the Bodhisattva path, thinking thus:
"I do not see a single sentient being who should be brought to maturity whom I cannot manifest the sovereign power of all Buddhas to mature."

Because they do not perceive [any such thing], their minds attain fearlessness; they ultimately reach the great shore of fearlessness, never ceasing the bodhisattva practices and never abandoning the bodhisattva vows. According to the needs of all sentient beings to be transformed, they manifest the realm of a Buddha to guide and deliver them. This is the tenth fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of fearlessness of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme, great fearlessness of all Buddhas, yet they do not abandon the fearlessness of Bodhisattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of uncommon dharmas of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices the six pāramitās spontaneously, without relying on the instruction of others: he always delights in great giving and does not give rise to stinginess;
he constantly maintains pure precepts and commits no transgressions.
Fully endowed with patience, their minds remain unshakable;
possessing great vigor, they never retreat;
skillfully entering all meditative absorptions, they are forever free from distraction.
Skillfully cultivating wisdom, they completely eliminate all wrong views.
This is the first uncommon dharma of practicing the six perfections in accordance with the path of the pāramitās, independent of instruction from others.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are universally able to embrace and sustain all sentient beings.
That is to say:

Practicing generosity with both material wealth and the Dharma, maintaining present right mindfulness, speaking with a gentle countenance and loving words, his heart filled with joy, he reveals the meaning as it truly is, enabling others to realize the Bodhi of all Buddhas; free from hatred or partiality, he benefits all equally.
This is the second unshared quality: by not relying on the instruction of others, one diligently gathers sentient beings in accordance with the path of the four means of attraction.
O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is skillful in dedication, namely:

Dedication without seeking karmic retribution; dedication in accordance with the Bodhi of the Buddha; dedication without attachment to any worldly meditative concentrations or samādhis; dedication for the benefit of all sentient beings; and dedication so as not to sever the wisdom of the Tathāgata.
This is the third uncommon quality: spontaneously, without being taught by others, giving rise to roots of goodness for the sake of all sentient beings and seeking the Buddha’s wisdom.

O Son of the Buddha! The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has reached the ultimate shore of skillful means; his mind constantly looks back upon all sentient beings, never wearying of the mundane realms of the ordinary and the foolish, nor taking pleasure in the path of transcendence of the two vehicles. He does not cling to his own happiness but exerts himself only in transforming and delivering others. He is well able to enter and emerge from meditative concentrations and liberations, attaining complete mastery over all samādhis. As he comes and goes through birth and death, it is like wandering through a garden or a park, never for a moment giving rise to a heart of weariness or exhaustion.
Sometimes they dwell in the palaces of Māra; sometimes they become Śakra, Brahmā, or the lords of the world. There is no place of birth where they do not manifest their bodies.
Sometimes they leave the household life among the ranks of non-Buddhists, yet they always remain far removed from all false views.
Regarding all worldly literature, incantations, scripts, seals, and mathematics, even down to the arts of play, song, and dance, they manifest them all, being skillful and refined in every way.
At times, he manifests as an upright and beautiful woman, whose wisdom and talent are foremost in the world;
she is able to inquire about and expound upon all mundane and supramundane dharmas, resolving doubts through dialogue to reach ultimate perfection;
she has fully mastered and reached the further shore of all mundane and supramundane matters, and all sentient beings constantly come to gaze upon her in reverence.
Although they manifest the deportment of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, they do not lose the mind of the Mahāyāna;
although they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment in every thought-moment, they do not cease their bodhisattva practices.
This is the fourth unshared quality: skillful means that reach the ultimate shore without depending on the instruction of others.
Son of the Buddha!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva well knows the path that unifies provisional and ultimate truth; with mastery over wisdom, they arrive at the final consummation.

That is to say: dwelling in nirvana yet manifesting birth and death; knowing there are no sentient beings yet diligently practicing the work of teaching and transforming them; abiding in ultimate quiescence yet manifesting the arising of afflictions; dwelling in the single, solid, and dense *dharmakāya* of wisdom yet universally manifesting the bodies of immeasurable sentient beings; constantly entering deep meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*) yet manifesting the enjoyment of sensual pleasures; always remaining far removed from the three realms (*tridhātu*) yet not abandoning sentient beings; always delighting in the joy of the Dharma yet appearing with female attendants, singing, and playing; though his body is adorned with all the marks and signs of excellence (*lakṣaṇa-vyañjana*), he manifests the forms of the ugly, the poor, and the lowly; constantly accumulating a multitude of virtues and being free from all faults and evils, yet manifesting birth in the hells, as animals, or as hungry ghosts; and although he has already reached the further shore of Buddha-wisdom, he does not abandon the wisdom-body of a bodhisattva.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have accomplished such immeasurable wisdom, even Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas cannot know it, let alone all ignorant sentient beings!
This is the fifth unique quality, not derived from the instruction of others, wherein both the provisional and the ultimate are practiced simultaneously.
O Son of the Buddha!
The physical, verbal, and mental actions of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva are entirely pure, as they proceed in accordance with wisdom.
That is to say:
being fully endowed with great compassion and forever free from the intent to kill, up to being fully endowed with right understanding and devoid of false views.
This is the sixth unique quality (āveṇika-dharma): that his physical, vocal, and mental actions follow wisdom without depending on the instruction of others.
O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is fully endowed with great compassion; he does not abandon sentient beings, but undergoes all manner of sufferings on their behalf—namely, the sufferings of the hells, the sufferings of animals, and the sufferings of hungry ghosts.

For the sake of benefiting others, they do not give rise to weariness or fatigue; they focus solely on liberating all sentient beings, never becoming addicted to or defiled by the realms of the five desires, and always exerting themselves diligently to eliminate all forms of suffering.
This is the seventh unique quality, which is that one constantly gives rise to great compassion without depending on the instruction of others.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are always a joy for sentient beings to behold; Brahmā kings, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and all other sentient beings never tire of seeing them.

Why is this? Because for a vast period of time since the distant past, the conduct and actions of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva have been pure and free from fault; therefore, sentient beings never grow weary of seeing him.
This is the eighth unique quality, not derived from the instruction of others, by which all sentient beings delight in beholding him.
O Son of the Buddha!

A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, having adorned himself with the great vow for *sarvajñatā* (omniscience), possesses a firm resolve and aspiration; even while dwelling among the perils of ordinary beings, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, he never regresses or loses the bright, pure, and wondrous jewel of the mind of omniscience.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like a precious gem named "Pure Adornment," which,
when placed in muddy water, does not change its luster or color, yet is able to cause all turbid water to become completely clear and pure.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: although they dwell among the ignorant, the foolish, and those in turbid and defiled places, they never lose or destroy the pure jewel-like mind that seeks all-knowledge; rather, they are able to cause those evil sentient beings to distance themselves from false views, afflictions, and impurities, so that they may attain the pure jewel-like mind that seeks all-knowledge.
This is the ninth uncommon quality: not losing the jewel of the mind of omniscience while dwelling in places of great hardship, without depending on the instruction of others.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva achieves the wisdom of the realm of self-awakening, attaining spontaneous realization without a teacher, reaching the ultimate state of mastery and the further shore, and wearing the crown of the stainless Dharma-scarf upon his head, yet does not abandon the cultivation of intimacy with virtuous friends and always delights in honoring all Tathāgatas—this is the tenth uncommon quality: attaining the supreme Dharma without depending on the instruction of others, never parting from spiritual mentors, and never ceasing to honor the Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of uncommon dharmas of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
If Bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the unsurpassed, vast, and uncommon dharmas of the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of karma. What are these ten?
That is to say:
because they are able to completely adorn and purify all worlds;
and because they are able to make offerings to all Buddhas.
All the deeds of bodhisattvas, because they plant identical roots of goodness;
all the deeds of sentient beings, because they are able to teach and transform them all;
all future deeds, because they encompass them until the very end of the future;
The karma of all supernatural powers, because they do not depart from a single world-system yet reach all world-systems;
the karma of all radiance, because they emit light of boundless colors, within each ray of which there appears a lotus throne where a bodhisattva sits cross-legged;
the karma of ensuring that the lineage of the Triple Gem is never severed, because after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddhas, they protect, maintain, and uphold the teachings of all Buddhas.
All transformative activities, because they preach the Dharma and teach and transform all sentient beings in all worlds;
all sustaining activities, because within a single thought-moment they manifest according to whatever the minds of sentient beings desire, causing all vows to be completely fulfilled.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed and vast karma of the Tathāgata.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of bodies.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
The non-coming body, because it does not undergo birth in any world;
the non-going body, because it cannot be found by seeking in any world;
the non-substantial body, because it is attained in accordance with reality throughout all worlds.
It is the non-empty body, because it reveals the world through the principle of suchness;
it is the inexhaustible body, because it continues without interruption until the end of the future;
it is the firm and solid body, because no demons whatsoever can destroy it.
The immovable body, because no demons or non-Buddhists can shake it;
the body endowed with marks, because it manifests the pure marks of a hundred merits;
the markless body, because the ultimate nature of all phenomena is entirely without marks.
It pervades all bodies, because it is one and the same body as the Buddhas of the three periods of time. These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide securely in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed and inexhaustible body.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of physical action (*kāyakarman*). What are the ten?
That is to say:
the bodily karma that fills all worlds with a single body;
and the bodily karma that is able to manifest itself before all sentient beings.
The bodily action of being able to take birth in all realms of existence;
the bodily action of traveling through all worlds;
and the bodily action of proceeding to the assemblies of all Buddhas.
The physical activity of being able to universally cover all worlds with a single hand;
the physical activity of being able to grind the vajra-rimmed mountains of all worlds into fine dust with a single hand;
and the physical activity of manifesting within one's own body the formation and destruction of all buddha-fields to show them to sentient beings.
The karma of body that accommodates the bodies of all realms of sentient beings within a single body;
and the karma of body by which one universally manifests all pure Buddha-lands within one's own body, such that all sentient beings therein attain enlightenment.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed buddha-activity of the Tathāgata and be able to awaken all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of bodies. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the body of all pāramitās, because of practicing them all correctly;
the body of the four means of integration, because of not abandoning any sentient beings.
The body of great compassion, because it undergoes immeasurable suffering on behalf of all sentient beings without weariness;
the body of great loving-kindness, because it rescues and protects all sentient beings;
the body of merit and virtue, because it benefits all sentient beings.
The wisdom-body, because it is of one and the same nature as the bodies of all Buddhas;
the dharma-body, because it is forever free from rebirth within the various realms of existence;
the skillful means-body, because it manifests before all beings in every place.
The body of supernormal power, because it manifests all miraculous transformations;
the body of enlightenment, because it attains perfect awakening according to the inclination and the time.
These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s body of unsurpassed, great wisdom.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of speech."
What are the ten? They are:
gentle speech, so as to bring peace and security to all sentient beings;
Nectar-like speech, because it causes all sentient beings to become completely refreshed;
non-deceptive speech, because all that is spoken accords with reality;
truthful speech, because there is not even a single falsehood, even in dreams.
It is the vast speech, for it is revered by all Śakras, Brahmās, and the Four Great Kings;
it is the profound speech, for it reveals the nature of phenomena (dharmatā);
it is the firm speech, for its teaching of the Dharma is inexhaustible.
It is speech that is upright, for its utterances are easy to understand;
it is speech of manifold kinds, for it manifests according to the occasion;
it is speech that awakens all sentient beings, for it causes them to comprehend according to their inclinations and desires.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, subtle, and wondrous speech.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of purified verbal karma.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
To delight in hearing the voice of the Tathāgata is to purify verbal action;
to delight in hearing the exposition of the bodhisattva’s merits is to purify verbal action;
and to refrain from speaking words that all sentient beings find unpleasant to hear is to purify verbal action.
Purifying vocal karma by truly distancing oneself from the four faults of speech;
purifying vocal karma by joyfully and exultantly praising the Tathāgata;
and purifying vocal karma by loudly extolling the Buddha’s actual merits at the stūpas of the Tathāgata.
Purifying verbal karma by bestowing the Dharma upon sentient beings with a profound and pure mind;
purifying verbal karma by using music, songs, and hymns to praise the Tathāgata;
and purifying verbal karma by listening to the True Dharma in the presence of all Buddhas without begrudging one’s own body or life.
Sacrificing one’s own body to serve all bodhisattvas and Dharma masters, thereby receiving the sublime Dharma and purely cultivating verbal karma—
this is the tenth.
"O Son of the Buddha!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva purifies their verbal karma through these ten matters, they will obtain ten kinds of protection.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The Deva Kings were at their head, with all the hosts of devas providing protection;
the Nāga Kings were at their head, with all the hosts of nāgas providing protection;
the Yakṣa Kings, Gandharva Kings, Asura Kings, Garuḍa Kings, Kiṃnara Kings, Mahoraga Kings, and Brahmā Kings were each at their head, every one accompanied by his own retinue to provide protection.
With the Tathāgata, the Dharma King, as their head, all Dharma masters provide complete protection.
This is the tenth.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Once the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has attained this protection, they are able to accomplish ten great deeds.
What are these ten? They are as follows:

They cause all sentient beings to rejoice; they are able to travel to all worlds; they are able to fully understand all faculties; they cause all inclinations to be purified; they cause all afflictions to be severed; they cause all habitual tendencies to be abandoned; they cause all desires and pleasures to be bright and pure; they cause all profound intentions to increase; they cause all dharma realms to be pervaded; and they cause all nirvana to be clearly seen everywhere.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mind."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
a mind like the great earth, because it can sustain and cause all the roots of goodness of all sentient beings to grow;
It is like the heart of the great ocean, for the waters of the Dharma of the immeasurable and boundless great wisdom of all Buddhas flow into it;
it is like the heart of Sumeru, the king of mountains, for it places all sentient beings in the state of the most supreme mundane and supramundane roots of goodness;
it is like the heart of the king of mani jewels, for its aspiration is pure and free from defilement.
The mind is like a vajra, for it penetrates all phenomena with certainty;
the mind is like the Vajra-encircling Mountains, for no māras or non-Buddhists can shake it;
the mind is like a lotus, for no worldly dharmas can defile it.
It is like the mind of the udumbara flower, for it is difficult to encounter throughout all kalpas;
it is like the mind of the pure sun, for it destroys the obscurations of darkness;
it is like the mind of space, for it is immeasurable.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great, and pure mind.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of generating the mind of enlightenment.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
I shall generate the mind: "I must deliver and liberate all sentient beings";
I shall generate the mind: "I must cause all sentient beings to sever and eliminate their afflictions";
I shall generate the mind: "I must cause all sentient beings to extinguish their habitual tendencies."
I resolve to sever all doubt and uncertainty;
I resolve to eliminate all suffering and affliction of sentient beings;
I resolve to eradicate all hardships and calamities of the evil realms.
I resolve that I shall reverently accord with the minds of all Tathāgatas;
I resolve that I shall skillfully train in all that is to be learned by all Bodhisattvas;
I resolve that I shall manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment by all Buddhas at every single tip of a hair-pore throughout all worlds.
I shall strike the unsurpassed Dharma drum in all worlds, so that all sentient beings may, according to their faculties and inclinations, fully attain awakening and understanding in their minds.
This is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed mind of great initiative and activity.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of all-pervading minds."
What are the ten? They are:
the mind that pervades all space, because its resolve is vast;
The mind that pervades all dharma-realms, because it penetrates deeply into the boundless;
the mind that pervades all three periods of time, because it knows them all in a single thought-moment;

the mind that pervades the appearance of all Buddhas, because it clearly understands their entry into the womb, birth, renunciation, attainment of enlightenment, turning of the wheel of Dharma, and parinirvāṇa.
It pervades the minds of all sentient beings, because it fully knows their faculties, desires, and habitual tendencies;
it pervades the mind of all wisdom, because it understands the dharma-realm in accordance with its nature;
it pervades all infinite minds, because it knows the distinctions within the various nets of illusion.
The mind that pervades all is the mind of non-arising, because it does not apprehend the intrinsic nature of any phenomena;
the mind that pervades all is the unobstructed mind, because it does not dwell upon its own mind or the minds of others;
the mind that pervades all is the sovereign mind, because it universally manifests the attainment of Buddhahood in a single thought-moment.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the immeasurable, unsurpassed Buddha-dharmas, which are universally adorned.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of faculties.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The faculty of joy, because one’s faith in all Buddhas is indestructible;
the faculty of aspiration, because one fully awakens to and understands all the Buddha-dharma heard;
the faculty of non-retrogression, because all undertakings are brought to ultimate completion.
The faculty of abiding securely, because it does not sever any bodhisattva practice;
the subtle faculty, because it enters the sublime principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*;
the tireless faculty, because it brings all matters concerning sentient beings to ultimate completion.
The Vajra-root, because it realizes and knows the nature of all phenomena;
the Vajra-flame-root, because it universally illumines the spheres of all Buddhas;
the Undifferentiated-root, because all Tathāgatas share one and the same body.
The faculty of the unobstructed limit, because it penetrates deeply into the ten powers of the Tathāgata. These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme, great wisdom of the perfected faculties.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of profound resolve for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the profound mind that is unstained by any worldly dharmas;
the profound mind that is unmixed with any paths of the two vehicles;
The profound mind that thoroughly realizes the bodhi of all Buddhas;
the profound mind that accords with the path of the knowledge of all-knowledge;
the profound mind that cannot be moved by any demons or non-Buddhists.
The profound resolve to purely cultivate the perfect wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
the profound resolve to receive and uphold all teachings as they are heard;
and the profound resolve to remain unattached to any place of rebirth.
The profound resolve to be fully endowed with all subtle wisdom;
