and because he seeks to teach, transform, and subdue the various armies of Māra, he manifests the subduing of Māra.

To cause those among the devas and people of the world who delight in military arrays to all come together to witness it, and because their minds were thereby tamed, he manifested the subduing of Māra;
to demonstrate that the power possessed by the Bodhisattva is such that none in the world can oppose it, he manifested the subduing of Māra;
and to inspire the courageous strength of all sentient beings, he manifested the subduing of Māra.
Out of compassion for all sentient beings of the final age, he manifests the subduing of Māra;

wishing to demonstrate that even at the site of enlightenment there are still demonic armies who come to cause provocation and affliction, and that only thereafter can one transcend the realm of Māra, he manifests the subduing of Māra;

and to reveal that the functioning of afflictions and karma is weak and inferior while the power of the roots of great kindness and goodness is mighty and flourishing, he manifests the subduing of Māra.
In order to accord with the practices of this defiled and evil world, he manifests the subduing of Māra.
This is the tenth.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten ways of accomplishing the powers of a Tathāgata. What are these ten?
They are as follows:
Because they transcend all māras, afflictions, and karma, they achieve the power of a Tathāgata;
because they are fully endowed with all bodhisattva practices and sport within all bodhisattva samādhi-gates, they achieve the power of a Tathāgata;
because they are fully endowed with all the vast meditative concentrations of bodhisattvas, they achieve the power of a Tathāgata.
Because they fulfill all pure factors conducive to enlightenment, they achieve the power of a Tathāgata;
because they attain the light of wisdom regarding all phenomena and skillfully contemplate and discern them, they achieve the power of a Tathāgata;
because their bodies pervade all worlds, they achieve the power of a Tathāgata.
Because the sounds of the speech he utters are entirely equal to the minds of all sentient beings, he achieves the power of a Tathāgata;
because he is able to sustain and empower all things through his supernormal powers, he achieves the power of a Tathāgata;

and because his physical, verbal, and mental activities are identical and no different from those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and because he comprehends the phenomena of the three periods in a single thought-moment, he achieves the power of a Tathāgata.
They attain the samādhi of the wisdom of excellent awakening and are endowed with the ten powers of a Tathāgata— namely,
from the power of knowing what is possible and what is impossible up to the power of the exhaustion of outflows— thereby accomplishing the powers of a Tathāgata.
These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas are endowed with these ten powers,
they are called Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten matters concerning the turning of the great wheel of Dharma by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. What are these ten?
First, they are fully endowed with the pure wisdom of the four fearlessnesses;
second, they give rise to the four analytical eloquences and accordant sounds;
third, they are skillfully able to expound and clarify the characteristics of the four noble truths.
Fourth, they accord with the unimpeded liberation of all Buddhas;
fifth, they are able to cause the minds of sentient beings to be filled with pure faith;
sixth, all their speech is never in vain, as it can extract the poisonous arrows of suffering from sentient beings.
Seventh, they are sustained by the empowering power of the vow of great compassion;
eighth, the sounds they emit pervade all worlds throughout the ten directions;
ninth, they preach the Dharma without interruption for incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*).
Tenth, whatever Dharma they teach is all able to give rise to the dharmas of the faculties, powers, factors of awakening, meditative concentrations, liberations, samādhis, and so forth.
O Son of the Buddha!
The Tathāgatas, the Buddhas, turn the wheel of Dharma through such immeasurable varieties of deeds as these.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha turns the wheel of Dharma, he plants seeds of pure and white dharmas within the minds of sentient beings through ten matters, so that none pass by in vain."
What are these ten?
They are: by virtue of the power of past vows;
Because they are sustained by great compassion;
because they do not abandon sentient beings;
and because, possessing mastery over wisdom, they preach the Dharma according to the inclinations of those beings.
Because it necessarily accords with the proper time and never misses its mark;
because it conforms to what is appropriate and never speaks erroneously;
and because it possesses the wisdom of the three periods of time and understands them thoroughly.
His body is most excellent, for there is none equal to it;
his speech is sovereign, for none can fathom it;
his wisdom is sovereign, for whatever he utters brings all to awakening.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Having performed the work of a Buddha, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha manifests parinirvāṇa for the sake of observing ten kinds of meanings."
What are these ten? They are:
demonstrating that all conditioned phenomena are truly impermanent;
To show that all conditioned phenomena are not secure;
to show that Great Nirvana is a place of security because it is free from fear;
and because humans and devas delight in attachment to the form-body, to manifest to them that the form-body is an impermanent dharma, so as to cause them to aspire to abide in the pure Dharma-body.
It demonstrates that the power of impermanence is irreversible;
it demonstrates that all conditioned phenomena do not abide according to one's will, for they lack autonomy;
it demonstrates that all existence within the three realms is like an illusion or a transformation, for it is not solid or enduring.
He demonstrates that the nature of nirvāṇa is ultimately firm and indestructible;
he demonstrates that all phenomena are without birth or arising, yet possess the characteristics of aggregation and disintegration.
O Son of the Buddha!

When the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have completed their Buddha-work, fulfilled their vows, turned the wheel of Dharma, and brought to maturity all those who were to be transformed and delivered; and when there are bodhisattvas who have received the honorable title and attained the prediction of enlightenment—the Dharma-nature dictates that they thus enter the unchanging Great Parinirvāṇa.
"O Son of the Buddha!
It is for the sake of contemplating these ten meanings that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha manifests parinirvāṇa.
O Son of the Buddha!"
This Dharma door is named "The Vast and Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas.

It has been proclaimed by immeasurable Buddhas; it enables the wise to comprehend immeasurable meanings and gives rise to joy, and it causes the great vows and great practices of all bodhisattvas to continue in succession.
O Son of the Buddha!

If there are sentient beings who hear this Dharma, and having heard it, believe and understand it; and having understood it, practice it accordingly, they will surely and swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Why is this? Because they practice according to what has been taught.
O Son of the Buddha!

If bodhisattvas do not act according to what they have said, it should be known that such persons are forever estranged from the bodhi of the Buddha; therefore, a bodhisattva should act according to what they have said.
O Son of the Buddha!

This "Flower of the Definitive Meaning of the Sphere of Action for All Bodhisattva Virtues" universally enters into all phenomena and universally gives rise to all-knowledge. It transcends all worlds, departs from the paths of the two vehicles, and is not shared with any sentient beings. It is able to illuminate all dharma-gates and increase the supramundane roots of goodness in all beings. Regarding this chapter on the Dharma-gate of Departing from the World, you should respect it, listen to it, receive it, recite and uphold it, contemplate it, aspire to it, and practice it.
If one can do so, know that such a person will swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

When this chapter was being taught, through the spiritual power of the Buddha and because the nature of this Dharma-gate is thus, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable worlds in the ten directions all shook violently, and a great light shone everywhere.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions all appeared before Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
Son of the Buddha!"

You are now able to expound this "Chapter on the Dharma Door of Universal Entry into All Worldly and Transcendent Dharmas," which is the definitive meaning of the flowers of the spheres of practice and merit of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
You have already well studied this Dharma and well expounded this Dharma.
We Buddhas all rejoice in your protection and upholding of this Dharma through your majestic power.
Just as we Buddhas rejoice in you, so do all other Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
We Buddhas, with one mind, shall all protect and uphold this sutra, so that all bodhisattvas of the present and future who have not yet heard it shall all be able to hear it.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the entire assembly in the ten directions as far as the Dharma-realm and spoke in verse:
“Having practiced austerities for immeasurable eons, Born from the true Dharma of immeasurable Buddhas,
Causing immeasurable multitudes to abide in Bodhi— Listen as I speak of those peerless deeds.”
Making offerings to immeasurable Buddhas while abandoning attachment, Extensively delivering all living beings without forming conceptual notions,
Seeking the Buddha’s merits with a mind free of dependence— I shall now describe those supreme and wondrous practices.
Free from the māras of the three realms, afflictions, and karma, Possessing the supreme conduct of noble merit,
With all delusions extinguished and the mind serene— I shall now describe the path he has traveled.
Forever free from all worldly deceptions and illusions, they manifest various transformations for the sake of sentient beings;
as the mind arises, abides, and ceases, they display myriad phenomena, explaining these capabilities to bring joy to the multitude.

Seeing all sentient beings oppressed and constrained by birth, old age, death, afflictions, and calamities, he desires to bring them liberation and teaches them to resolve their minds [on enlightenment]; one should listen to and receive his meritorious conduct.
Generosity, morality, patience, diligence, meditation, and wisdom, Along with skillful means, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity—
If one constantly practices these for hundreds of thousands of millions of eons, O Benevolent One, you should now hear of that person’s merit.
Seeking enlightenment for billions of kalpas, Without begrudging any body or life,
Vowing to benefit all beings and not oneself— I shall now describe those acts of compassionate mercy.
To expound his virtues for immeasurable billions of eons would not be even as much as a single drop from the ocean;
his merit is peerless and beyond description, yet I shall now briefly explain it through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power.
Their minds are without high or low; seeking the Way, they never grow weary.
They cause all sentient beings everywhere to abide in goodness and increase their pure dharmas.
Their wisdom universally benefits others, like trees, rivers, and springs.
Just as the great earth is the foundation upon which all things depend,
so too is the Bodhisattva like a lotus flower: with compassion as its root and tranquility as its stem,
with wisdom as its many stamens and the categories of ethical discipline as its fragrant purity.
The Buddha emits the light of Dharma, causing them to blossom;
unattached to the waters of conditioned existence, all who see it rejoice.
The Bodhisattva’s tree of sublime Dharma grows from the ground of the upright mind.
Faith is the seed, compassion the root; wisdom constitutes the trunk, while skillful means are the branches.
The five perfections form its dense foliage, meditative concentration its leaves, and supernormal powers its flowers; omniscience is the fruit.
With the supreme powers as its parasitic vine, it casts a shade that covers the three realms.
The Bodhisattva, the Lion King, has the pure white Dharma for his body;
the Four Truths are his feet, and right mindfulness is his neck.
With eyes of loving-kindness and wisdom as his crest, with the silken band of liberation bound upon his crown,
he roars the Dharma within the valley of ultimate emptiness, terrifying all the māras.
As a leader of merchants, the Bodhisattva gazes universally upon all living beings.
In the vast wilderness of birth and death, in places of affliction and peril,
where they are seized by demonic thieves, blinded by ignorance and lost from the right path—
you show them the straight road and lead them into the city of fearlessness.
The Bodhisattva beholds sentient beings afflicted by the diseases of the three poisons and various sufferings, tormented throughout the long night; for their sake,
he gives rise to great compassion and extensively expounds the gates of remedial practice.
The eighty-four thousand kinds [of teachings] extinguish all suffering and affliction.
The Bodhisattva, as a Dharma King, transforms sentient beings through the Right Path,
causing them to distance themselves from evil and cultivate goodness, and to single-mindedly seek the merits of the Buddha.
In the presence of all Buddhas, they receive the consecration and the sublime prediction;
they extensively bestow the wealth of the noble ones—the precious jewels of the factors of enlightenment.
When Bodhisattvas turn the wheel of Dharma, it is just as the Buddhas have turned it.
With the hub of precepts and the rim of samādhi, adorned with wisdom and wielding the sword of insight,
he has already shattered the thieves of affliction and utterly destroyed the host of demonic adversaries;
when all those of external paths behold him, none fail to scatter.
The ocean of a bodhisattva’s wisdom is deep and vast, without limit;
Filled with the flavor of the True Dharma, it is replete with the jewels of the factors of enlightenment.
Its great resolve has no shore or boundary, And omniscience serves as its tide.
Sentient beings cannot fathom them; speaking of them would never reach an end.
The Bodhisattva is like Mount Sumeru, towering above the world;
with the peaks of supernatural powers and samādhi, his great mind rests unmoving.
If there are those who draw near, they share in his wisdom and form;
transcending all objective realms, there is nothing that he does not perceive.
The Bodhisattva is like a vajra, resolutely seeking all-encompassing knowledge.
With faith and ascetic practice, steadfast and unshakable;
their minds free from fear, they benefit all living beings.
All demons and afflictions are utterly crushed and extinguished.
The Bodhisattva’s great compassion is like dense, heavy clouds;
The three insights flash like lightning, and the supernormal powers roar like thunder.
Universally employing the four analytical eloquences, He rains down the water of the eightfold meritorious qualities.
Moistening and saturating all beings, it causes them to eliminate the heat of afflictions.
The Bodhisattva’s city of the True Dharma has Prajñā as its walls,
shame and remorse as its deep moats, and wisdom as its defensive ramparts.
He widely opens the gates of liberation, Constantly guarding with right mindfulness;
The Four Truths form a level royal road, And the Six Supernatural Powers assemble his weapons.
Furthermore, he erects the great Dharma banner, Which stands all around and pervades beneath it.
The various hosts of Māras within the three realms of existence Can none of them enter.
The Bodhisattva-Garuḍa has the power of *rddhi* as his firm feet,
Skillful means and valor as his wings, And compassion as his bright and pure eyes.
Abiding at the tree of omniscience, he gazes upon the great ocean of the three realms of existence;
grasping and lifting up devas, humans, and nāgas, he establishes them on the shore of nirvāṇa.
The sun of the Bodhisattva’s True Dharma has appeared in the world.
The wheel of the perfection of the aggregate of ethical discipline, Moving swiftly with the bases of supernormal power,
Illuminating with the light of wisdom, It grows the medicinal herbs of the faculties and powers,
Extinguishes the darkness of the afflictions, And dries up the ocean of craving and desire.
The moon of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom-light takes the Dharma-realm as its wheel;
Wandering through ultimate emptiness, there is nowhere in the world it does not appear.
Within the consciousness-mind of the triple world, It increases and decreases according to the times.
Among the constellations of the two vehicles, there is none to equal them.
The Bodhisattva, the Great Dharma King, has a body adorned with merit;
his marks and signs are all complete, and both humans and devas gaze up in reverence.
With the eye of purity through skillful means, and the vajra of wisdom,
he attains mastery over all phenomena and transforms sentient beings through the Way.
This Bodhisattva, a Great Brahmā King, possesses sovereign power that transcends the three realms of existence.
Karma and delusions are all severed; Loving-kindness and equanimity are fully possessed.
Manifesting bodies in every place, One awakens others with the sound of the Dharma.
Within those three realms, One uproots the foundations of all false views.
The Bodhisattva Sovereign Deity has transcended the realm of birth and death;
his sphere of experience is ever pure, and his wisdom never regresses.
Having severed the paths of the inferior vehicles, he receives the various methods of empowerment.
Endowed with merit and wisdom, his fame is heard everywhere.
The Bodhisattva’s mind of wisdom is as pure as space;
it has no intrinsic nature and no place of dependence, for nothing therein can be apprehended.
Possessing great sovereign power, they are able to accomplish worldly affairs;
naturally endowed with pure conduct, they cause sentient beings to be likewise.
This is the stage of the Bodhisattva’s skillful means, which brings benefit to all sentient beings.
The water of the Bodhisattva’s compassion washes away all afflictions;
The fire of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom burns the fuel of delusive habits;
The wind of the Bodhisattva’s non-abiding travels through the three realms of existence.
The Bodhisattva is like a precious jewel, capable of relieving poverty and distress;
The Bodhisattva is like a diamond, capable of shattering inverted views;
The Bodhisattva is like a jeweled necklace, adorning the bodies within the three realms of existence.
The Bodhisattva is like a mani jewel, increasing all practices;
The Bodhisattva’s virtue is like a flower, constantly blossoming the factors of enlightenment;
The Bodhisattva’s vow is like a garland, forever bound upon the heads of sentient beings.
The fragrance of the Bodhisattva’s pure precepts, firmly maintained without transgression;
the Bodhisattva’s wisdom as an ointment, universally perfuming the three realms;
the Bodhisattva’s power like a canopy, able to shield against the dust of afflictions.
The Bodhisattva’s wisdom is like a banner, capable of crushing the enemy of self-conceit;
Sublime conduct serves as the brocade, adorning his wisdom;
Shame and remorse serve as his garments, universally covering all living beings.
The Bodhisattva’s unimpeded vehicle—by mounting it, one exits the triple world;
The Bodhisattva’s elephant of great strength—its mind is well-tamed;
The Bodhisattva’s horse of divine power—its stride leaps beyond all realms of existence.
The Bodhisattva is a dragon of Dharma, raining universally upon the minds of sentient beings;
the Bodhisattva is the Udumbara flower, difficult to encounter in this world;
the Bodhisattva is a great and valiant general, who subdues all demons.
The Bodhisattva turns the wheel of Dharma, just as the Buddha has turned it;
the Bodhisattva’s lamp dispels darkness, so that sentient beings see the right path;
the river of the Bodhisattva’s merit flows constantly in accordance with the right path.
The Bodhisattva’s bridge of diligence widely ferries across all classes of beings;
with great wisdom and vast vows, together forming a sturdy ship,
they guide and receive all sentient beings, establishing them on the shore of Bodhi.
The Bodhisattva’s pleasure garden is the true joy of sentient beings;
The Bodhisattva’s flower of liberation adorns the palace of wisdom;
The Bodhisattva is like a wondrous medicine, Extinguishing the disease of afflictions.
The Bodhisattva is like the Snowy Mountains, Producing the medicine of wisdom.
The Bodhisattva is equal to the Buddha, Awakening all living beings.
What else could the Buddha-mind be? Perfect Enlightenment awakens the world.
Just as the Buddha has come, so do the Bodhisattvas come;
just as the All-Knowing One does, they enter the Universal Gate through wisdom.
The Bodhisattvas skillfully guide all living beings.
The Bodhisattva naturally awakens to the realm of all-knowledge;
The Bodhisattva’s immeasurable power cannot be destroyed by the world;
With fearless wisdom, the Bodhisattva knows sentient beings and all phenomena.
Throughout all worlds, the various distinctions of forms and appearances,
as well as sounds and names, they are able to discern and know them all.
Though detached from name and form, they manifest all manner of appearances.
All sentient beings are unable to fathom their path.
Such virtues as these, the Bodhisattva fully accomplishes;
realizing that all natures are devoid of intrinsic nature, they have no attachment to existence or non-existence.
Such is all-encompassing wisdom— Inexhaustible and without dependence.
I shall now expound it, To bring joy to all sentient beings.
Though they know the characteristics of all phenomena Are like illusions, entirely empty and quiescent,
By means of a heart of compassionate vows and the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha,
he manifests various and immeasurable miraculous transformations;
you all should listen to and receive these manifold merits.
A single body can manifest immeasurable and diverse bodies;
without mind and without objective realm, it universally responds to all beings.
Within a single sound, it fully expounds all vocal expressions.
The languages and dharmas of sentient beings— He can produce them all according to their kind.
Having forever left behind the body of afflictions, He manifests a body of sovereign mastery;
Knowing that dharmas are inexpressible, He yet delivers various teachings.
Their minds are ever in tranquil extinction, pure as space;
yet they universally adorn the lands, manifesting themselves before all beings.
Without any attachment to the body, they are nevertheless able to manifest physical forms.
Throughout all worlds, they take birth according to what is appropriate;
though born in all places, they do not abide in the act of taking birth.
Knowing the body to be like space, it manifests in various ways according to the mind.
The bodies of the Bodhisattvas are boundless, appearing universally in all places;
they constantly pay respectful homage and make offerings to the Most Victorious Honored One among Two-legged Beings,
with incense, flowers, various musical performances, banners, pennants, and precious canopies.
Always with a profound and pure mind, they make offerings to all Buddhas.
Never departing from the assembly of a single Buddha, they are universally present at the abodes of all Buddhas;
amidst those great assemblies, they pose difficult questions and listen to the Dharma.
Hearing the Dharma, they enter samādhi through each and every immeasurable gate;
emerging from concentration is likewise so, manifesting without end.
Through wisdom and skillful means, they realize that all worlds are like illusions.
Yet they can manifest within the world all manner of illusory phenomena;
they display various forms, as well as mind and speech,
entering into the web of conceptualizations while remaining forever unattached.
Sometimes they manifest the initial aspiration for enlightenment to benefit the world;
sometimes they manifest long-term cultivation that is vast and boundless—
through generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
The four Brahmavihāras, the four Saṃgrahavastus, and so forth— All these most excellent dharmas;
Either they are fully perfected through actual practice, And one attains patience free from conceptual construction;
Or they appear as being bound to one more birth, Wherein all Buddhas confer the empowerment.
Sometimes manifesting in the form of a śrāvaka, or again manifesting as a pratyekabuddha,
they enter parinirvāṇa in every place, yet do not abandon the practice of bodhi.
Sometimes manifesting as Śakra, or manifesting as Brahmā,
Sometimes surrounded by celestial maidens, sometimes dwelling alone in silent retreat;
sometimes manifesting as a bhikṣu, tranquilizing and disciplining his mind;
sometimes appearing as a sovereign king, governing the laws of the world.
Sometimes they manifest as women skilled in arts; sometimes they manifest as practitioners of asceticism;
sometimes they manifest as experiencing the five desires; or they manifest as entering various meditative absorptions.
Sometimes they manifest their initial birth; or as youth, or as old age and death.
If there are those who attempt to conceptualize him, their minds will become suspicious and fall into madness.
Whether manifesting in celestial palaces, or appearing for the first time descending as a spirit,
or entering or dwelling in a womb, or attaining Buddhahood and turning the wheel of Dharma— [all these are beyond thought].
Sometimes taking birth, sometimes entering nirvana; sometimes appearing to enter a school, or dwelling among palace ladies;
sometimes leaving the secular world to practice dhyāna.
Sometimes sitting beneath the Bodhi tree, spontaneously attaining perfect enlightenment.
Sometimes they manifest turning the wheel of Dharma; sometimes they manifest first seeking the Way.
Sometimes they manifest as the body of a Buddha, sitting in meditation across immeasurable lands;
sometimes they cultivate the non-retrogressive path, accumulating the requisites for Bodhi.
Deeply entering incalculable kalpas, they have all reached the other shore;
immeasurable kalpas are a single thought-moment, and a single thought-moment is immeasurable kalpas.
All kalpas are not kalpas, yet for the sake of the world they manifest as kalpas.
Without coming or accumulation, they accomplish the affairs of all kalpas.
Within a single atom, one universally beholds all Buddhas;
throughout all places in the ten directions, there is nowhere they do not exist.
The lands, the sentient beings, and all phenomena— He sees them all in their proper succession;
Even after passing through immeasurable eons, They are ultimately inexhaustible.
The Bodhisattva knows that sentient beings Are vast and without limit.
The body of that single sentient being arises from immeasurable causes and conditions.
Just as one knows the immeasurable within the one, so it is with all things;
according to what they have realized, they teach those who have not yet learned.
He fully knows the faculties of sentient beings, that they differ as superior, middling, or inferior;
he also knows when faculties shift, who is ready for transformation and who is not;
and how one faculty and all faculties arise through the power of successive causes and conditions.
Subtle and individually distinct, they follow in sequence without confusion.
Furthermore, he knows their inclinations and understandings, as well as all habitual tendencies of the afflictions;
he also knows all mental activities of the past, future, and present.
Thoroughly comprehending all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), they are neither coming nor going;
having understood their nature, he preaches the unsurpassed Dharma.
Whether defiled or pure, he fully understands all their various modes of activity.
In a single thought one attains Bodhi, And accomplishes all-encompassing wisdom.
Abiding in the inconceivable state of a Buddha, With a mind of ultimate wisdom,
In a single thought one is able to know entirely The conduct of all sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva’s wisdom of supernormal powers, having attained mastery through its efficacy,
can travel to boundless lands within a single thought-moment.
Traveling with such swiftness, they continue thus for the duration of countless eons.
There is nowhere it does not pervade, yet not even a hair’s breadth is moved.
It is like a skilled illusionist who manifests all manner of forms;
yet if one seeks within that illusion, there are neither forms nor non-forms.
The Bodhisattva is also like this: through the illusory power of skillful wisdom, they manifest all manner of forms, filling the world.
They are like the pure sun and moon, shining brightly in the void of space.
Appearing as reflections in all waters, yet not mixed with the water;
know that the Bodhisattva’s pure Wheel of Dharma is likewise:
appearing within the mental waters of the world, yet not mixed with the world.
Just as when a person in a dream performs various deeds,
though they pass through billions of years, the single night has not yet ended;
so too the Bodhisattva, abiding in the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), manifests all manner of things.
Though immeasurable eons may reach their end, the wisdom of a single thought is inexhaustible.
Just as within mountain valleys and palatial halls,
all manner of sounds echo back, yet in reality there is no discrimination.
The Bodhisattva abiding in the nature of phenomena, by means of sovereign wisdom,
can extensively produce sounds according to the various types of beings,
yet remains free from discrimination. It is like seeing a mirage and perceiving it as water.
Chasing after [it], they cannot drink; as they toss and turn, their thirst increases all the more.
One should know that the afflicted minds of sentient beings are likewise;
the Bodhisattva gives rise to compassion and rescues them, causing them to transcend [suffering].
Contemplate form as a mass of foam, sensation as a bubble upon the water,
perception as a mirage in the heat, and mental formations as a plantain tree.
Consciousness is like a magical illusion, manifesting all manner of phenomena.
Knowing the aggregates thus, the wise have no attachments.
All sense-bases are entirely empty and still, like the movement of a mechanical puppet;
the nature of the elements is eternally detached, yet they falsely appear within the world.
The Bodhisattva abides in reality, the supreme meaning of quiescence;
he extensively proclaims it in various ways, yet his mind has no point of reliance.
There is neither coming nor going, and likewise, there is no abiding.
The causes of afflictions, karma, and suffering—these three constantly circulate.
Dependent origination is neither existent nor non-existent; it is neither real nor unreal.
Thus one enters the Middle Way, and speaks without attachment.
Able, within a single thought-moment, to universally manifest the minds of the three periods of time,
And all the various phenomena of the realms of desire, form, and formlessness;
In accordance with the three codes of discipline, they expound the three doors of liberation.
He establishes the paths of the three vehicles and achieves all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).
He thoroughly understands what is possible and what is impossible (*sthānāsthāna*), as well as all karmas, the faculties (*indriya*),
the elements (*dhātu*), the liberations (*vimokṣa*), meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), and the paths leading to all destinations (*sarvatragāminī-pratipad*).
Recalling past lives and possessing the divine eye, they have eliminated all delusions;
yet though they know the ten powers of a Buddha, they have not yet attained them.
Thoroughly realizing that all phenomena are empty, they constantly seek the sublime Dharma.
Not conjoined with afflictions, yet not exhausting the outflows;
widely knowing the path of deliverance, he delivers sentient beings.
Having attained fearlessness therein, he does not abandon the cultivation of all practices.
Without error and without contradicting the Way, Nor losing right mindfulness,
with vigor, aspiration, and samādhi, And with insight that suffers no diminution;
The three aggregates are all pure, And one clearly penetrates all three periods of time.
With great compassion for all sentient beings, They are entirely without obstruction.
By entering this Dharma-gate, They achieve such conduct;
I shall now describe a small portion Of the meaning of their merit and adornments.
Exhausting countless eons, one could speak of those practices without end;
I now describe but a small portion, like a single mote of dust upon the great earth.
Abiding in reliance upon the Buddha’s wisdom, give rise to thoughts of its wondrous excellence.
Practicing the most supreme conduct, Endowed with great compassion,
Diligent and self-abiding in peace, They transform and guide all sentient beings;
Abiding securely within pure precepts, They possess the practices for receiving predictions of enlightenment.
They are able to enter into the Buddha’s virtues, the conduct of sentient beings, and the lands;
they fully know all kalpas and worlds, yet have no thought of weariness or fatigue.
Possessing the dhāraṇī of discerning wisdom, they penetrate the true meaning.
Contemplating and proclaiming the peerless, the tranquil, and the perfectly awakened one;
having aroused the mind of Samantabhadra and cultivated its practices and vows,
through the power of the causes and conditions of compassion, the aspiration for the Path becomes pure.
Practicing the pāramitās, he ultimately awakens through wisdom;
realizing the mastery of power, he attains unsurpassed bodhi.
Having perfected the wisdom of equality, he expounds the most supreme Dharma.
Able to uphold and possess wondrous eloquence, one attains the station of the Dharma King.
Far removed from all attachments, one expounds the equality of mind;
giving birth to wisdom, one manifests transformation and attains Bodhi.
Abiding through all kalpas, the wise one experiences great solace;
through deep penetration and reliance, they are fearless and free from doubt.
Having thoroughly realized the inconceivable, they skillfully and subtly discern with excellence.
Skillfully entering all samādhis, he universally perceives the realm of wisdom.
Having perfected all liberations, he sports with the supernormal powers and clarities;
forever free from all fetters, he wanders at will through the groves and gardens.
With pure dharmas as their palace, all conditioned phenomena are a source of joy;
manifesting immeasurable adornments, their minds remain unmoved amidst the world.
With deep resolve they observe well, and with wondrous eloquence they can expound the teachings.
The seal of pure bodhi, with the light of wisdom illuminating all;
dwelling in a state beyond compare, their mind is not inferior.
Their resolve is like a great mountain, and the planting of their virtues is like a deep ocean.
Abiding in the Dharma like a treasure, with a mind of armor and vows,
one initiates the Great Task that can ultimately never be destroyed.
Having received the prophecy of enlightenment, one abides in a vast and expansive mind.
The secret treasury is inexhaustible, awakening to all phenomena.
Worldly wisdom is entirely sovereign, its wondrous function unimpeded;
so too are all realms of sentient beings and their various dharmas.
Their bodies, vows, and objective realms, as well as their wisdom and supernormal powers,
are manifested throughout the world in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions.
Their playful displays and spheres of activity are sovereign and cannot be restrained.
The powers, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities, adorned by all karmic deeds;
all bodies and bodily actions, as well as speech and the purification of speech—
because they have attained protection, they accomplish ten kinds of tasks.
The Bodhisattva’s arousal of the mind, as well as the pervasiveness of that mind,
leaves the faculties undistracted, thereby attaining the most excellent faculties.
With a profound mind and an ever-increasing superior mind, they remain far removed from flattery and deception.
With various kinds of definitive understanding, they universally enter the world.
Abandoning those habitual tendencies of affliction, they take up this most excellent path;
skillfully cultivating it until it is perfected, they attain all-encompassing wisdom.
Free from regression, they enter the stage of certainty, decisively realizing nirvana;
they give birth to the path of the Buddha-dharma and achieve the title of virtue.
This includes the path and the immeasurable paths, up to the path of adornment.
Abiding well in successive stages, entirely free from attachment;
with hands, feet, and internal organs, with the vajra as his heart,
clad in the armor of compassion, and fully equipped with all manner of weapons.
Wisdom and insight are his eyes; the practice of bodhi is his ears;
pure precepts are his nose, extinguishing darkness without obstruction.
Eloquence is his tongue; his body reaches everywhere.
With supreme wisdom as the mind, one performs all activities while walking or staying.
Upon the lion throne at the site of enlightenment, one lies in the Brahma-posture with space as the dwelling.
Through these practices and observations, one universally illuminates the realm of the Tathāgata.
Observing the conduct of all sentient beings, Displaying prowess and letting out roars, Free from greed, they practice pure giving; Abandoning pride, they uphold pure precepts;
Without anger, they are ever patient; Without indolence, they are constantly diligent.
Having attained mastery in meditative concentration, their wisdom has no further object of activity;
they rescue others with compassion without weariness, delighting in the Dharma and relinquishing afflictions;
amidst all sensory realms, they understand both the meaning and the Dharma.
Merit is fully perfected, and wisdom is like a sharp sword;
universally illuminating those who delight in much hearing, they clearly understand the path toward the Dharma.
Knowing Māra and the paths of Māra, they vow to abandon them all.
Beholding the Buddhas and the deeds of the Buddhas, they resolve to embrace them all;
free from pride, they cultivate wisdom and are not sustained by the power of Māra.
Sustained by the Buddhas, they are likewise sustained by the Dharma.
Manifesting as dwelling in Tuṣita Heaven, And manifesting the end of that life;
Manifesting as dwelling in the mother’s womb, And also manifesting the subtle transition [to rebirth].
Manifesting birth and the smile, And also manifesting the seven steps.
He manifests the practice of various arts and also shows himself dwelling in the deep palace;
he leaves the home life to practice austerities and proceeds to the site of enlightenment;
sitting upright, he emits radiant light and awakens all living beings.
Having subdued Māra and attained perfect enlightenment, he turned the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma;
having fully completed all that was to be manifested, he entered Great Parinirvāṇa.
Those practices of the Bodhisattvas were cultivated through immeasurable eons.
Vast and without limit, I now speak but a small portion of it.
Though I cause immeasurable multitudes to dwell securely in the Buddha’s virtues,
within both sentient beings and phenomena, there is ultimately nothing to be grasped.
Fully endowed with such practices, they sport in the various supernormal powers:
placing myriad lands upon the tip of a hair for billions of kalpas;
holding infinite lands in their palms, traveling everywhere without weariness of body.
Returning them to their original places, sentient beings remain unaware.
With all manner of various adornments, the Bodhisattva places the buddha-fields within a single pore, yet causes everyone to see them as they truly are.
Furthermore, with a single pore, he universally receives all oceans;
yet the great seas neither increase nor decrease, and sentient beings suffer no harm.
Taking up the immeasurable Iron Ring Mountains in his hand, he crushes them into dust.
Upon each atom, there is one world-system, as numerous as all these atoms.
Taking all these atomic world-systems and further pulverizing them into dust—
such atoms may be known, but the wisdom of the Bodhisattva is immeasurable.
From within a single pore, he emits immeasurable rays of light;
the radiance of the sun, moon, and stars, the glow of mani-jewels and fire,
and all the lights of the devas are entirely eclipsed by them.
Extinguishing the sufferings of all evil realms, they preach the unsurpassed Dharma for them.
Amidst the various and diverse sounds of all worlds,
the Bodhisattva can manifest them all with a single voice.
He definitively and analytically expounds all the teachings of the Buddhas,
causing all living beings to hear them and rejoice greatly.
He places all past eons within the future and the present.
The kalpas of the future and the present are placed back into the past;
he manifests immeasurable lands undergoing combustion, formation, and abiding;
all worlds are entirely contained within a single pore.
All Buddhas of the future and the present throughout the ten directions appear clearly and distinctly within his body;
he profoundly understands the nature of transformation and skillfully responds to the minds of sentient beings.
He manifests various bodies, yet remains entirely unattached to them.
He may appear in the forms of beings in the six realms of existence, in the bodies of all sentient beings,
in the bodies of Brahmā, Śakra, and the World-Protectors, or in the bodies of the multitudes of devas and humans.
The bodies of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, the bodies of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
sometimes manifesting as bodhisattva bodies, they practice for the sake of all-knowledge.
They skillfully enter the various nets of conceptualization of sentient beings—whether inferior, middling, or superior.
Manifesting the attainment of enlightenment, as well as all Buddha-fields;
thoroughly understanding the web of conceptualizations, attaining mastery over such thoughts;
demonstrating the practice of the bodhisattva path and all matters of skillful means.
He manifests such vast and manifold supernatural transformations;
such realms as these, none in the world can know.
Though he manifests, there is nothing manifested; ultimately, his excellence increases ever further.
In accordance with the minds of sentient beings, He causes them to practice the path of reality.
Body, speech, and mind are equal like space;
Pure precepts serve as ointment, And manifold practices serve as clothing.
The Dharma-silk adorns the pure topknot; the maṇi-jewel of omniscience, with its merit reaching everywhere, consecrates him as he ascends the royal throne.
The pāramitās serve as his wheels, and the various supernormal powers as his elephants.
Divine power is sufficient to serve as his horse; wisdom is his bright pearl.
Sublime conduct is his court lady; the four means of integration are his minister of the treasury.
Skillful means is his general of the army—the Bodhisattva is thus a Wheel-Turning King.
Samādhi is the city wall, emptiness and stillness the palace;
Compassion is the armor, wisdom the sword, Mindfulness the bow and clear, sharp arrows.
The canopy of supernormal power is raised high, And the banner of wisdom is erected far aloft.
The power of patience is unshakable, Directly shattering the army of the Māra King.
Dhāraṇī serves as level ground, Multitudinous practices serve as flowing rivers,
Pure wisdom serves as a bubbling spring, And sublime insight forms a forest.
Emptiness is a clear and pure pool, The factors of enlightenment are its blooming lotuses.
Adorned by his own supernormal powers, He constantly delights in samādhi.
Contemplation serves as his handmaidens, And nectar is his choice food.
Taking the flavor of liberation as their drink, they sport within the three vehicles.
These practices of the bodhisattvas are subtle and ever-increasing;
though they practice for immeasurable eons, their minds never grow weary or satisfied.
Making offerings to all Buddhas, purifying all lands,
and causing all beings everywhere to dwell securely in omniscience;
though one might know the number of every atom within all lands, [the merit of this practice remains beyond measure].
The entire realm of empty space might be measured by a single grain of sand;
The minds of all sentient beings might be known by counting every thought-moment;
But the various merits of the Buddha’s heirs can never be fully described.
Desiring to be endowed with these merits and all sublime dharmas;
desiring to cause all sentient beings to leave suffering behind and always abide in peace and joy;
desiring to make one’s body, speech, and mind entirely equal to those of all Buddhas—
"One should resolve upon the vajra-mind and train in these meritorious practices.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 59;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 60.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.

The Bodhisattva Māravijayaghoṣa, the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇopāyameghagarjita-ghoṣa,
the Bodhisattva Sarvalokaduḥkhapraśamanāśvāsana-ghoṣa, the Bodhisattva Dharmottara, the Bodhisattva Jayottara, the Bodhisattva Jñānottara,
the Bodhisattva Puṇyasumerūttara, the Bodhisattva Guṇakarketanottara, and the one named...
The Bodhisattva Renowned Above, the Bodhisattva Universal Radiance Above, the Bodhisattva Great Compassion Above, the Bodhisattva Ocean of Wisdom Above,
the Bodhisattva Buddha-Lineage Above, the Bodhisattva Victorious Light, the Bodhisattva Victorious Virtue, the Bodhisattva Supreme Victory,
the Bodhisattva Universal Illumination Victory, the Bodhisattva Dharma Victory, and the Bodhisattva Moon Victory.
Gaganagañja Bodhisattva, Ratnagañja Bodhisattva, Dhvajagañja Bodhisattva, Jñānagañja Bodhisattva,
Śālendrarāja Bodhisattva, Dharmeśvararāja Bodhisattva, Gajeśvararāja Bodhisattva, Brahmeśvararāja Bodhisattva, Parvateśvararāja Bodhisattva, and Gaṇeśvara Bodhisattva.
King Bodhisattva, Swift Sovereign King Bodhisattva, Tranquil Sovereign King Bodhisattva,
Immovable Sovereign King Bodhisattva, Powerful Sovereign King Bodhisattva, Supreme Sovereign King Bodhisattva,
Tranquil Sound Bodhisattva, Unobstructed Sound Bodhisattva, Earth-Trembling Sound Bodhisattva.
[Sāgara-]Samudra-nirghoṣa Bodhisattva, Megha-svara Bodhisattva, Dharma-prabhā-svara Bodhisattva,
Gaganasvara Bodhisattva, Sarvasattva-kuśalamūla-nirdeśa-svara Bodhisattva, Sarvamahāpraṇidhāna-darśana-svara Bodhisattva,
Bodhimanda-svara Bodhisattva, Sumeru-prabha-bodhi Bodhisattva, and Gaganaprabha Bodhisattva...
The Bodhisattva Awakening, the Bodhisattva Awakening Free from Defilement, the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Awakening, the Bodhisattva Good Awakening,
the Bodhisattva Awakening that Universally Illuminates the Three Times, the Bodhisattva Vast Awakening, the Bodhisattva Universal Radiance Awakening,
the Bodhisattva Dharma-realm Radiance Awakening... such as these were five hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Together with these people, all these bodhisattvas have fully accomplished the practices and vows of Samantabhadra; their spheres of activity are unimpeded, as they pervade all buddha-fields;
they manifest infinite bodies, as they draw near to all Tathāgatas.
Their pure eyes are unobstructed, for they behold the miraculous transformations of all Buddhas;
their reach is infinite, for they constantly and universally visit all places where Tathāgatas attain perfect enlightenment;
their radiance is boundless, for they universally illumine the ocean of all true dharmas with the light of wisdom.
Their preaching of the Dharma is inexhaustible, for their pure eloquence is endless throughout boundless eons;
they are equal to the realm of empty space, for all that their wisdom engages is utterly pure;
they have no point of dependence, for they manifest form-bodies in accordance with the minds of sentient beings.
He had eliminated the cataracts of ignorance, for he realized that the realm of sentient beings is devoid of any self;
his wisdom was equal to space, for he illuminated the Dharma-realm with a great net of light.

He was accompanied by a community of five hundred śrāvakas, all of whom had awakened to the ultimate truth, realized the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), deeply penetrated the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and forever transcended the ocean of existence.
Relying upon the virtues of the Buddha, they are free from the fetters, latent tendencies, and bonds, abiding in the state of non-obstruction;
their minds are as tranquil as space, having forever severed doubt and confusion regarding the Buddhas, and they enter with deep faith into the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom.

Together with immeasurable lords of the world, they had all made offerings to countless Buddhas in the past; they were constantly able to benefit all sentient beings, acting as uninvited friends who diligently guarded them with a vow never to abandon them.

They entered the gate of supreme wisdom within the world, were born from the Buddha’s teaching, protected the Buddha’s true Dharma, gave rise to great vows, ensured the lineage of the Buddhas would not be severed, were born into the family of the Tathāgatas, and sought after all-encompassing wisdom.
At that time, the bodhisattvas of great virtue, the śrāvakas, and the kings of the world together with their retinues all had this thought:
"The realm of the Tathāgata, the wisdom-practice of the Tathāgata, the empowerment of the Tathāgata, the powers of the Tathāgata,
the fearlessnesses of the Tathāgata, the samādhis of the Tathāgata, the abode of the Tathāgata, and the masteries of the Tathāgata— "
The body of the Tathāgata and the wisdom of the Tathāgata cannot be penetrated,
cannot be entered, cannot be believed and understood, cannot be comprehended, cannot be endured, cannot be observed,
cannot be discerned, cannot be revealed, and cannot be elucidated by any gods or humans in all the worlds.
There is no one capable of causing sentient beings to understand it, except through the power of the Buddhas' empowerment, the power of the Buddhas' supernormal knowledges,
the power of the Buddhas' majestic virtue, the power of the Buddhas' original vows, as well as the power of their own roots of goodness from past lives,
the power of being sustained by spiritual friends, the power of profound and pure faith, and the power of great and clear understanding.
the power of strength, the power of the pure mind that inclines toward bodhi, and the power of the vast vow to seek all-knowledge.
We pray only that the World-Honored One will accord with our various desires, various understandings, various knowledges,
various modes of speech, various masteries, various stages of abiding, and various...
The purity of the faculties, various skillful means of the mind, various mental objects,
various bases of the Tathāgata’s merits, and the various ways of hearing and receiving all the teachings spoken—
these manifest the Tathāgata’s past pursuit of the mind set on omniscience, the great bodhisattva vows he formerly aroused, and that which he formerly purified.
The various pāramitās; the bodhisattva stages entered in the past; the bodhisattva practices perfected in the past;
the skillful means accomplished in the past; the paths cultivated in the past; the dharmas of renunciation attained in the past;
the miraculous feats performed in the past; and all the causal roots of past lives.
The conditions for attaining perfect enlightenment, turning the sublime wheel of Dharma, purifying Buddha-fields, taming sentient beings,
opening the city of the Dharma of all-knowledge, showing the path to all sentient beings, entering into the dwellings of all sentient beings,
receiving the offerings of all sentient beings, and preaching the Dharma of distribution for all sentient beings.
“May you explain for us such dharmas as these: the merit of giving, and manifesting the images of all Buddhas for the sake of all sentient beings!

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the bodhisattvas, took great compassion as his body, great compassion as his gate, and great compassion as his head; employing the dharma of great compassion as his skillful means, he pervaded empty space and entered the *siṃhavijṛmbhita-samādhi* (the Lion’s Stretch Samādhi).
Having entered this samādhi, all worlds were universally adorned and purified.
At that moment, this Great Adorned Pavilion suddenly became vast and expansive, without any limit.
The ground is made of diamond, covered above by a king of jewels; immeasurable jewel flowers and various maṇis are scattered throughout, filling every place.
The pillars are made of lapis lazuli, composed of many treasures and adorned with great light maṇis; Jāmbūnada-gold wish-fulfilling jewel kings are placed all around upon them as ornaments.

The perilous towers extend far, with galleries projecting alongside them; the roof-rafters and buildings support one another, while windows and doors reflect each other’s light. The steps, courtyards, balconies, and railings are all fully provided, and everything is adorned with exquisite jewels.
These jewels are fashioned entirely into the forms of humans and devas—firm, wonderful, and foremost in the world—with nets of *maṇi* jewels covering them from above.
At the sides of all the gates, banners and streamers were erected, all emitting light that pervaded the entire Dharma-realm.
Outside the site of enlightenment, the steps and railings were infinite and beyond description, all of which were fashioned from mani jewels.

At that time, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, the Jeta Grove suddenly became vast and expansive, its dimensions exactly equal to those of unspeakably many buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within them.

Adorned with the interlacing of all manner of exquisite jewels, unspeakable numbers of gems were spread across its ground; it was enclosed by walls of incalculable jewels, and jeweled tala trees lined the sides of the path.
Within that space, there were furthermore immeasurable fragrant rivers, filled to the brim with scented water, surging and swirling in eddies;
all manner of precious flowers turned to the right as they flowed, spontaneously producing the sounds of the Buddha-dharma;
and inconceivable precious *puṇḍarīka* lotuses, in full bloom, spread across the surface of the water.
Various jewel-flower trees are planted in rows along its banks;
there are inconceivable varieties of terraces and pavilions, all arranged in successive order along the shore and completely covered by nets of *maṇi* jewels.
Incalculable jewels radiated great light, and incalculable jewels adorned the ground.
Various exquisite incenses were burned, their fragrance wafting in dense clouds.
Furthermore, immeasurable and diverse jeweled banners were erected, namely:

There were banners of precious incense, banners of precious robes, banners of precious streamers, banners of precious silken cloth, banners of precious flowers, banners of precious necklaces, banners of precious garlands, banners of precious bells, banners of *maṇi* jewel canopies, great *maṇi* jewel banners, *maṇi* jewel banners of universally illuminating radiance, *maṇi* king banners that emit the sounds of the names of all Tathāgatas, lion *maṇi* king banners, *maṇi* king banners that proclaim the ocean of the past lives of all Tathāgatas, and *maṇi* king banners that manifest the reflections of the entire dharma-realm; these were arrayed in rows, adorning the ten directions in their entirety.

At that time, in the void above the Jeta Grove, there appeared inconceivable clouds of celestial palaces, countless clouds of fragrant trees, unspeakable clouds of Mount Sumerus, unspeakable clouds of musical instruments, unspeakable clouds of precious lotuses emitting exquisite sounds of song and praise for the Tathāgata, unspeakable clouds of precious thrones spread with celestial robes upon which Bodhisattvas sat to extol the virtues of the Buddha, unspeakable clouds of the forms of various heavenly kings and mani-jewels, unspeakable clouds of white pearls, unspeakable clouds of red pearl pavilions and ornaments, and unspeakable clouds raining down adamantine, solid jewels; all remained in the void, surrounding and filling it entirely as a magnificent adornment.
Why is this? Because the roots of goodness of the Tathāgata are inconceivable; because the pure dharmas of the Tathāgata are inconceivable;
because the majestic power of the Tathāgata is inconceivable; and because the Tathāgata is able to manifest transformations from a single body at will, pervading all things.
Because the world is inconceivable, the Tathāgata is able, through his supernatural powers, to cause all Buddhas and the adornments of all Buddha-lands to enter his own body;
because it is inconceivable, the Tathāgata is able to universally manifest the reflections of the entire Dharma-realm within a single minute atom;
and because it is inconceivable, the Tathāgata is able [to do so] within a single pore.
Because they manifest the inconceivability of all Buddhas of the past;
because each and every ray of light emitted by the Tathāgata is able to universally illuminate all worlds in an inconceivable manner;
and because the Tathāgata is able to produce from a single pore clouds of emanations as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, filling all Buddha-lands.

Because the earth is inconceivable, the Tathāgata is able to universally manifest within a single pore all the world-systems of the ten directions throughout their inconceivable kalpas of formation, abiding, and destruction.

Just as one sees the pure and magnificent adornments of the Buddha-land here in this Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, so too does one see them throughout all worlds in the ten directions, pervading the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
That is to say:
seeing the body of the Tathāgata dwelling in the Jeta Grove, with the assembly of bodhisattvas completely filling it;
seeing clouds of all manner of adornments raining down everywhere; and seeing clouds of the radiance of all precious jewels raining down everywhere.
He saw clouds raining down all kinds of mani-jewel clouds; he saw clouds raining down all kinds of ornamental canopies that overspread the buddha-fields;
he saw clouds raining down all kinds of celestial bodies; he saw clouds raining down all kinds of flower trees;
he saw clouds raining down all kinds of garment trees; he saw clouds raining down all kinds of jewel garlands.
He saw clouds of necklaces that continued in succession without interruption, pervading the entire great earth; he saw clouds raining down all manner of ornaments everywhere;
he saw clouds raining down all kinds of fragrances in forms corresponding to the shapes of sentient beings everywhere;
he saw clouds raining down nets of exquisite jewel flowers in continuous succession without end everywhere; he saw clouds raining down all [various] things everywhere.
He saw clouds of celestial maidens holding precious banners and pennants circling and moving back and forth in the void;
he saw clouds raining down all manner of precious lotus flowers, from the petals of which various musical sounds spontaneously emerged;
and he saw clouds raining down all kinds of lion thrones adorned with jeweled nets and necklaces.
At that time, to the east, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
there was a world named Golden Lamp Cloud Banner;
the Buddha there was named Vairocana Supreme Virtue King.

In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Vairocana-Vow-Radiance, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many buddha-lands, came to where the Buddha was. By means of their spiritual powers, they all raised various clouds, namely:

clouds of celestial flowers, clouds of celestial incense, clouds of celestial powdered incense, clouds of celestial garlands, clouds of celestial jewels, clouds of celestial ornaments, clouds of celestial jeweled canopies, clouds of celestial exquisite garments, clouds of celestial jeweled banners and pennants, and clouds of all kinds of exquisite jeweled adornments, filling the entirety of space.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested in the eastern direction a precious, adorned pavilion and a lion throne of the treasury of universally illuminating jewel lotuses. Enveloping his body with a net of wish-fulfilling jewels, he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the south, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields,
there is a world named Vajragarbha;
the Buddha there is named Universal Radiance Invincible Treasury King.

In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Invincible Vigor King, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, came toward the place where the Buddha was. He carried nets of all kinds of precious incense, necklaces of all kinds of jewels, bands of all kinds of precious flowers, bands of all kinds of precious garlands, necklaces of all kinds of vajra-jewels, nets of all kinds of maṇi-gems, bands of all kinds of precious robes, bands of all kinds of precious necklaces, bands of all kinds of maṇis of supreme radiance, and necklaces of all kinds of lion-maṇi jewels; by means of his spiritual power, he caused these to pervade all oceans of worlds.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested, in the southern direction, a pavilion adorned with *maṇi* jewels that illuminates the entire world, as well as a lion throne of jewel-lotus matrix that shines throughout the ten directions. Covering his body with a net of all kinds of precious flowers, he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the west, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields,
there is a world named Mani-jewel Lamp Sumeru Banner; the Buddha there is named Dharma-realm Wisdom Lamp.
In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Universal Victory,
Unsurpassed Majestic Virtue King, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds,
came toward the place where the Buddha was; all of them, by means of their spiritual powers, produced various kinds of ointments as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
Clouds of Mount Sumeru of incense smoke; clouds of Mount Sumeru of various colored fragrant waters, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
clouds of Mount Sumeru of light-manifesting *maṇi* jewel-kings, equal in number to all the atoms of the great earth, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Clouds of Mount Sumeru banners adorned with various wheels of radiant flames;
clouds of Mount Sumeru adorned with various colored *vajra-garbha* maṇi-kings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
and clouds of Mount Sumeru consisting of Jāmbūnada maṇi-jewel banners that universally illuminate all worlds, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Clouds of *maṇi* jewels like Mount Sumeru manifesting all phenomena throughout unspeakably many Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms;
clouds of *maṇi* jewel-kings like Mount Sumeru manifesting the marks and embellishments of all Buddhas throughout unspeakably many Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms;
clouds manifesting all Tathāgatas throughout unspeakably many Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms...
To explain the causal origins of these events, there appeared clouds of *maṇi-rāja-sumeru* jewels representing the practices performed by all bodhisattvas,
and clouds of *maṇi-rāja-sumeru* jewels manifesting all Buddhas seated at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*),
as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, filling the entire dharma-realm.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested to the west a pavilion of all kinds of fragrant kings, covered above by a net of genuine jewels. He further manifested a lion throne within a treasury of precious lotuses, adorned with Indra’s shadow-banner, and draped his body in a net of mani-jewels of exquisite color. Adorning his head with a heart-king jewel crown, he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the north, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
there is a world named Jewel-Raiment Radiant Banner;
the Buddha there is named Great Radiance Illuminating the Dharma-Realm of Space.

In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Unobstructed Supreme Treasury King, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came toward the place where the Buddha was.

By means of their spiritual powers, they all manifested clouds of all kinds of precious robes, namely: clouds of yellow precious radiant robes; clouds of robes perfumed by various fragrances; clouds of sun-banner *maṇi*-king robes; clouds of blazing golden *maṇi* robes; clouds of robes with the flames of light from all jewels; clouds of exquisite *maṇi* robes bearing the images of all the stars; clouds of white jade-radiant *maṇi* robes; clouds of *maṇi* robes of supreme brilliance whose light shines everywhere; clouds of *maṇi* robes of overwhelming majesty whose light shines everywhere; and clouds of *maṇi* robes of the ocean of adornments—filling the entirety of space.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested in the northern quarter a pavilion adorned with an ocean of mani-jewels and a lion throne of lapis lazuli lotus-treasury. He covered his body with a net of lion-majesty mani-kings, wore a pure jewel-king as a crest-gem, and sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the northeast, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands,
there is a world named Net of All Joyful Pure Radiance; the Buddha there is named Unobstructed Eye.

In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named King of the Moon of Vows that Manifests the Dharma Realm, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to where the Buddha was. By means of their spiritual powers, they all raised clouds of precious pavilions, clouds of incense pavilions, clouds of burning incense pavilions, clouds of flower pavilions, clouds of sandalwood pavilions, clouds of diamond pavilions, clouds of mani-jewel pavilions, clouds of gold pavilions, clouds of robe pavilions, and clouds of lotus pavilions, which completely covered all worlds throughout the ten directions.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested in the northeast a great maṇi pavilion of the gateways to all dharma realms, along with a lion throne of the peerless fragrant king lotus treasury. He covered his body with a net of maṇi flowers, donned a crown of the wondrous jewel-treasury maṇi king, and sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the southeast, past as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands,
there is a world named Fragrant Cloud Adorned Banner;
the Buddha there is named Dragon Sovereign King.

In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named King of the Radiant Flame of Dharma-Wisdom, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came toward the place where the Buddha was. By means of their spiritual powers, they all brought forth clouds of perfect golden light, clouds of perfect light of immeasurable jewel colors, clouds of perfect light from the Tathāgata’s ūrṇā-kośa, clouds of perfect light of various jewel colors, clouds of perfect light from the lotus-treasury, clouds of perfect light from the branches of various jewel trees, clouds of perfect light from the Tathāgata’s uṣṇīṣa, clouds of perfect Jāmbūnada-golden light, clouds of perfect solar light, and clouds of perfect lunar light, filling the entirety of space.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested in the southeast a most supreme jewel-luminous pavilion of Vairocana and a lion throne of vajra-maṇi lotus-treasury. With a net of maṇi-kings of various jewel-flames covering his body, he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the southwest, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
there is a world named Sunlight Maṇi Treasury;
the Buddha there is named King of the Moon of Wisdom Universally Illuminating All Dharmas.
In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Wisdom Banner King Who Crushes All Māra Armies.

Accompanied by as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, he came toward the place where the Buddha was. From every one of his pores, he emitted clouds of flower-flames, incense-flames, jewel-flames, vajra-flames, burning-incense-flames, lightning-flash-flames, Vairocana-maṇi-jewel-flames, clouds of all golden light-flames, clouds of light-flames from the supreme treasury maṇi-kings, and clouds of light-flames from the ocean of light of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time—each emerging from every pore and pervading the entire realm of space.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested in the southwest a great maṇi-jewel pavilion called the "Luminous Net Universally Manifesting the Dharma Realms of the Ten Directions," as well as a lion throne of fragrant lamps and flaming jewel lotus-treasures. Covering his body with a net of stainless-treasury maṇis, and wearing a crown adorned with the "Maṇi King Resounding the Aspiration for Liberation of All Sentient Beings," he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the northwest, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields,
there is a world named Vairocana-Vow-Maṇi-Rāja-Garbha;
the Buddha there is named Samantaprabha-Parama-Sumeru-Rāja.
In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named:

The Bodhisattva Praṇidhijñānāvabhāsa-dhvaja, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came toward the place where the Buddha was. In every thought-moment, from all his marks and signs of excellence, from all his pores, and from all his limbs and members, there issued forth clouds of images of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; clouds of images of all bodhisattvas; clouds of images of the assemblies of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of all the transformation bodies of the Tathāgatas; clouds of images of all the birth-stories of the Tathāgatas; clouds of images of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; clouds of images of the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of the supernatural transformations of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of all lords of the world; and clouds of images of all pure lands, filling the entirety of space.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet; then, in the northwest, he manifested a pavilion adorned with *maṇi* jewels that universally illumines the ten directions, as well as a lion throne within a treasury of precious lotuses that universally illumines the world. He covered his body with a net of invincible radiance pearls, donned a *maṇi* jewel crown of universal light, and sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
Below, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, beyond the oceans of worlds,
there is a world named Universal Illumination of the Perfect Light of All Tathāgatas;
the Buddha there is named King of the Banner of Wisdom with Unobstructed Characteristics of Space.
In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named King of Courageous Wisdom Who Shatters All Obstacles, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds,
came toward the place where the Buddha was; from all his pores, he issued forth the speech of all sentient beings.
From the cloud of oceanic sounds, there issues forth the cloud of oceanic sounds proclaiming all the skillful means of the practice of Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time;
from it issues forth the cloud of oceanic sounds proclaiming all the skillful means of the vows undertaken by Bodhisattvas;
from it issues forth the cloud of oceanic sounds proclaiming all the skillful means for the complete fulfillment of the pure pāramitās of Bodhisattvas; from it issues forth...
Clouds of sound from the perfected practices of all bodhisattvas pervading all lands; clouds of sound proclaiming the sovereign power of accomplishing all bodhisattva attainments;

clouds of sound proclaiming the sovereign power of all Tathāgatas proceeding to the site of enlightenment, defeating the hosts of Māra, and attaining equal and perfect awakening; clouds of sound proclaiming all Tathāgatas...
The gateway of the Sūtra for Turning the Wheel of Dharma is named Cloud of Oceanic Sounds;
it issues forth clouds of oceanic sounds of skillful means that teach all methods for converting and subduing sentient beings according to their needs;

it issues forth clouds of oceanic sounds of skillful means that universally cause all sentient beings to realize wisdom at all times, in accordance with their roots of goodness and the power of their vows.

The Sound Cloud arrived at the Buddha’s abode, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and immediately manifested below him a palace of all Tathāgatas, adorned with various jewels, together with a pavilion and a lion throne within a treasury of all precious lotuses. Wearing a *maṇi* jewel crown that universally manifests the reflections of the site of enlightenment, he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
Above, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
there is a world named Inexhaustible Exposition of the Buddha-lineage;
the Buddha there is named Light-Sound of the Universal Wisdom-Wheel.
In that Buddha’s assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Vow of the Differentiations of the Dharma Realm, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds,
set out from that place of enlightenment and came toward this Sahā world to the presence of Śākyamuni Buddha, [prostrating] at all his marks and signs of excellence.
Within all pores, all parts of the body, all limbs and joints, all ornaments, and all garments, he manifests all past Buddhas such as Vairocana,
all future Buddhas— both those who have already received their prophecy and those who have not— and all present [Buddhas].

In all lands throughout the ten directions, all Buddhas together with their assemblies likewise manifest the ocean of past narratives concerning the practice of the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) and all those who received such gifts; they likewise manifest the ocean of past narratives concerning the practice of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*);
and they likewise manifest the ocean of past narratives concerning the practice of the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*).
He also manifested the ocean of past fundamental events in which he severed his limbs through the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) with an undisturbed mind;
he also manifested the ocean of past fundamental events in which he practiced the perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*) with courageous and non-retrogressive energy;
and he also manifested the ocean of past fundamental events in which he sought the ocean of the perfection of meditation (*dhyāna-pāramitā*) of all Tathāgatas and attained its accomplishment.
He manifested the ocean of past events of seeking all Buddhas, turning the wheel of Dharma, and accomplishing the teachings while giving rise to a courageous mind and relinquishing everything;

he also manifested the ocean of past events of delighting to see all Buddhas, delighting to practice all bodhisattva paths, and delighting to transform all realms of sentient beings; and he also manifested...
They also manifest the ocean of past fundamental events concerning all the pure adornments of the great vows made by bodhisattvas;
they also manifest the ocean of past fundamental events concerning the courageous purity of the power-pāramitā achieved by bodhisattvas;
and they also manifest the ocean of past fundamental events concerning the fulfillment of the wisdom-pāramitā cultivated by all bodhisattvas.
All such oceans of past events completely pervade the vast Dharma-realm.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s presence, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and immediately manifested in the space above a pavilion adorned with all vajra-treasuries and a lion throne within a lotus treasury of indranīla-vajra-kings. He covered his body with a net of mani-jewel kings of universal precious radiance, and taking as his crest-jewel the mani-kings that proclaim the names of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.

In this way, all Bodhisattvas of the ten directions together with their retinues are born from the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. With the eye of pure wisdom, they behold the Buddhas of the three periods of time; they universally hear the oceans of *sūtras* and the wheels of Dharma turned by all the Tathāgatas, having already attained the further shore of mastery in all Bodhisattva practices.

In every thought-moment, they manifest great spiritual transformations and draw near to all the Tathāgatas. A single body of theirs fills all worlds and all the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas. Within a single atom, they universally manifest all worldly realms, teaching and maturing all sentient beings without ever missing the proper time. From a single pore, they emit the sounds of the teachings spoken by all the Tathāgatas.

They know that all sentient beings are entirely like illusions; they know that all Buddhas are entirely like reflections; they know that taking birth in all realms of existence is entirely like a dream; they know that all karmic retributions are like images in a mirror; they know that the arising of all births is like a mirage in the heat; they know that all worlds are entirely like magical transformations.

They have accomplished the Tathāgata’s ten powers and fearlessnesses, possessing courageous mastery and able to roar the lion’s roar; they have deeply entered the great ocean of inexhaustible eloquence and attained the wisdom of all dharmas regarding the ocean of the speech of all sentient beings.
Their conduct within the dharma-realm of empty space is unimpeded, and they know that all dharmas are without obstruction.
