The spheres of supernatural power of all bodhisattvas are entirely purified; with courageous and diligent effort, they subdue the armies of Māra.
Constantly using wisdom, they thoroughly comprehend the three periods of time, knowing that all phenomena are like empty space—without conflict and without attachment.

Although they exert themselves with diligence, they know that omniscience ultimately comes from nowhere; although they contemplate the spheres of experience, they know that all existence is utterly unobtainable.

Through the wisdom of skillful means, they enter all dharma-realms; through the wisdom of equality, they enter all lands. By the power of mastery, they cause all worlds to enter into one another, taking birth in every location throughout all worlds and beholding the various forms and characteristics of all worlds.
Within the realm of the minute, they manifest vast lands; within the realm of the vast, they manifest minute lands.

In a single moment before a single Buddha, they receive the empowerment of the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas; they see everywhere throughout the ten directions without confusion, and in a single kṣaṇa, they are able to travel to them all.
In this manner, all these bodhisattvas filled the Jeta Grove; this was entirely through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the chief great śrāvakas—Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Revata, Subhūti, Aniruddha, and Nanda—[were also present].
The great śrāvakas, such as Kapphiṇa, Kātyāyana, and Pūrṇa, who were all in the Jeta Grove,
did not perceive at all the Tathāgata’s supernatural power, the Tathāgata’s majestic excellence, the Tathāgata’s sphere of activity,
the Tathāgata’s playful manifestations, the Tathāgata’s miraculous transformations, the Tathāgata’s supreme sovereignty, or the Tathāgata’s sublime conduct.
...the majestic power of the Tathāgata, the sustaining presence of the Tathāgata, and the pure lands of the Tathāgata; likewise, they do not see the inconceivable realm of the Bodhisattvas,

the great assemblies of Bodhisattvas, the universal entry of Bodhisattvas, the universal arrival of Bodhisattvas, the universal approach of Bodhisattvas, the spiritual transformations of Bodhisattvas, the playful displays of Bodhisattvas, or the Bodhisattvas themselves.
The retinues of the bodhisattvas, the locations of the bodhisattvas, the lion thrones adorned by the bodhisattvas,
the palaces of the bodhisattvas, the dwellings of the bodhisattvas, the mastery of the samādhis entered by the bodhisattvas, the observations of the bodhisattvas,
the yawns of the bodhisattvas, the valor of the bodhisattvas, the offerings of the bodhisattvas, and the predictions of enlightenment for the bodhisattvas.
...the maturation of bodhisattvas, the heroic vigor of bodhisattvas, the purity of the bodhisattva’s dharma-body, the perfection of the bodhisattva’s wisdom-body,
the manifestation of the bodhisattva’s vow-body, the accomplishment of the bodhisattva’s form-body,
the complete purity of the bodhisattva’s various marks, the adornment of the bodhisattva’s constant radiance with manifold colors, and the emission of the bodhisattva’s...
The Great Net of Light, the Bodhisattvas’ arising of clouds of transformations, the Bodhisattvas’ bodies pervading the ten directions,
and the Bodhisattvas’ perfection of all practices—
such matters as these were entirely unseen by all the Śrāvakas and great disciples.
Why is this? It is because their roots of goodness are not identical; because they originally did not cultivate the roots of goodness for witnessing the sovereign power of the Buddhas;
because they originally did not praise or speak of the pure merits of all Buddha-fields throughout the worlds of the ten directions; and because they originally did not extol...

Because they have marveled at the various supernatural transformations of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; because they originally did not resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* while transmigrating within the flow of birth and death;
because they originally did not cause others to abide in the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*);
because they originally were unable to ensure that the lineage of the Tathāgatas would not be severed; and because they originally did not embrace [the Dharma].
Because they did not, for the sake of all sentient beings, originally exhort others to practice the bodhisattva pāramitās;
because, while originally wandering in the flow of saṃsāra, they did not exhort sentient beings to seek the supreme eye of great wisdom;

because they did not originally cultivate the various roots of goodness that give rise to omniscience (sarvajñatā); and because they did not originally achieve the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world.
Because they have not, from the beginning, cultivated the roots of goodness; because they have not, from the beginning, attained the supernormal knowledge for purifying Buddha-fields;

because they have not, from the beginning, attained the objects of knowledge known by the eyes of all bodhisattvas; because they have not, from the beginning, sought the roots of goodness for the uncommon enlightenment that transcends the world;
because they have not, from the beginning, made the great vows of all bodhisattvas; because they have not, from the beginning, followed...
Because they are born through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, they originally did not know that all phenomena are like illusions and Bodhisattvas are like dreams;
because they originally did not attain the vast and great joy of the Mahāsattvas.
All such things are the domain of the wisdom-eye of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, and are not shared with any of the followers of the two vehicles.

For this reason, the great śrāvakas were unable to see, unable to know, unable to hear, unable to enter, unable to attain, unable to recollect, unable to observe, unable to deliberate, unable to contemplate, and unable to discern them;
therefore, although they were within the Jeta Grove, they did not see the Tathāgata’s great supernatural transformations.

Furthermore, because the great śrāvakas lack such roots of goodness, lack such an eye of wisdom, lack such samādhis, lack such liberations, lack such supernormal powers, lack such majestic virtue, lack such power, lack such mastery, lack such abodes, and lack such spheres of activity, they are therefore unable to know it, unable to see it, unable to enter it, unable to realize it, unable to abide in it, unable to understand it, unable to observe it, unable to endure it, unable to approach it, and unable to traverse it.

Furthermore, they are unable to extensively expound, explain, praise, and manifest it for others; nor can they guide, encourage, inspire, cause them to incline toward it, cause them to practice it, cause them to dwell securely in it, or cause them to realize its entry.

Why is this? Because the great disciples have attained liberation by relying on the Śrāvaka vehicle; they have accomplished the path of the śrāvakas, fulfilled the practices of the śrāvakas, and abide in the fruit of the śrāvakas. Having attained definitive wisdom regarding the truth of non-existence (*abhāva-satya*), they dwell eternally in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) in ultimate tranquility. They are far removed from great compassion, having abandoned sentient beings and abiding in their own affairs.

Regarding that wisdom, they are unable to accumulate it, unable to practice it, unable to abide in it, unable to aspire for it, unable to accomplish it, unable to purify it, unable to enter it, unable to penetrate it, unable to know and see it, and unable to realize it.
Therefore, although they were within the Jeta Grove in the presence of the Tathāgata, they did not see such a vast and great miraculous manifestation.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is as if there were hundreds of thousands of billions of immeasurable hungry ghosts on the banks of the Ganges—naked, famished and parched, their entire bodies scorched, with crows, vultures, jackals, and wolves vying to seize them. Driven by thirst and seeking water to drink, though they stood by the riverbank, they did not see the river.
Should there be anyone who sees it, they see it as parched and dried up. Why is this?
Because it is shrouded by profound and heavy karmic obstructions.

Those great śrāvakas were likewise; although they resided within the Jeta Grove, they did not perceive the Tathāgata’s vast and great supernormal powers, because their eyes were shrouded by the cataracts of ignorance and because they had never planted the roots of goodness belonging to the stage of *sarvajñatā*.

It is, for example, as if there were a person who, while sleeping soundly and peacefully in a great assembly, suddenly dreamed of the Great City of Sudarśana where Śakra dwells atop Mount Sumeru. There, the palaces and gardens were adorned with every kind of excellence; hundreds of thousands of millions of devaputras and apsaras scattered celestial flowers until they covered the ground everywhere. Various trees of clothing produced exquisite garments, various trees of flowers blossomed with wondrous blooms, and various trees of music played celestial melodies.

Celestial maidens sang beautiful songs, and immeasurable devas enjoyed themselves therein. The person saw himself wearing celestial robes, dwelling, staying, and wandering throughout that entire place.
Although all the people within that great assembly were in the same place, they neither knew nor saw [him].
Why was this? Because what was seen in the dream could not be seen by that great multitude.

All bodhisattvas and the various kings of the world are likewise thus: because they have long accumulated the power of roots of goodness; because they have made the vast vow for omniscience; because they have studied all the merits of the Buddhas; because they have practiced the path adorned by bodhisattvas; because they have perfected the dharma of the knowledge of omniscience; because they have fulfilled all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra; because they have entered all the bodhisattva stages of wisdom; because they sport in all the samādhis wherein bodhisattvas dwell; and because they are already able to observe the realm of wisdom of all bodhisattvas without obstruction—they all behold the inconceivable, sovereign, and miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One.
All the great disciples among the śrāvakas were unable to see or know [this], because they lacked the pure eye of a bodhisattva.
It is like the Snowy Mountains, which abound with various medicinal herbs;
a skilled physician who visits them can distinguish them all, yet the hunters and herdsmen who dwell constantly on that mountain do not see those medicines.

It is the same in this case: because the bodhisattvas have entered the realm of wisdom and possess the power of mastery, they are able to see the vast and great spiritual transformations of the Tathāgata;

whereas the great disciples, seeking only their own benefit and not desiring to benefit others, and seeking only their own peace and not desiring to bring peace to others, do not know or see [these things], even though they are within the forest.

For example, suppose there were various treasure troves within the earth, filled with all kinds of rare and wondrous jewels. There was a man, wise and discerning, who was skilled at identifying all hidden stores; moreover, he possessed great power of merit and virtue, enabling him to take whatever he desired with ease. He used these riches to support his parents, to provide for his relatives, and to care for the elderly, the sick, and the destitute, providing for them all equally.
Yet those who lacked wisdom and merit, though they might come to the place where the treasures lay, would neither know nor see them, and thus would receive no benefit.

It is the same in this case: the great Bodhisattvas possess the eye of pure wisdom and are able to enter the inconceivable and profound realm of the Tathāgata; they can perceive the Buddha’s spiritual power, enter various Dharma-gates, roam through the ocean of samādhis, make offerings to all Buddhas, awaken sentient beings through the True Dharma, and gather in sentient beings by means of the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*).
The great Śrāvakas, however, are unable to see the Tathāgata’s spiritual power, nor can they see the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
For example, it is like a blind person who reaches a great island of jewels; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they are unable to see any of the various treasures.
Because they do not see them, they cannot gather them, nor can they enjoy their use.

It is likewise here: although the great disciples were in the grove in the presence of the World-Honored One, they did not see the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual power, nor could they behold the great assembly of bodhisattvas.
Why is this? Because there is no bodhisattva who, lacking the unimpeded pure eye, can successively awaken to and enter the dharma-realm to perceive the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
For example, suppose there is a person who has obtained a pure eye called "Stainless Radiance," which no dark forms whatsoever can obstruct.

At that time, while it is night and in the darkness, this person stands amidst a multitude of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of people— whether they are walking, standing, sitting, or lying down— and every aspect of those people's physical forms and deportment is seen in its entirety by this person with the clear eye.
Just as those with clear vision cannot perceive the deportment and movements of one who possesses majestic dignity, so too is the Buddha:
having accomplished the eye of wisdom, pure and unobstructed, he clearly perceives all worlds;
yet when he manifests supernatural transformations while surrounded by a multitude of great bodhisattvas, the great disciples are entirely unable to see them.
For example, suppose a bhikṣu among a great assembly enters the meditative concentrations of the totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*), namely:

the totality of earth, the totality of water, the totality of fire, the totality of wind, the totality of blue, the totality of yellow, the totality of red, the totality of white, the totality of space, the totality of the bodies of various sentient beings, the totality of all sounds and voices, and the totality of all objects of focus.
When he enters these concentrations, he perceives their respective objects, while the rest of the great assembly cannot perceive them at all, except for those who themselves abide in this samādhi.
The inconceivable realm of the Buddhas manifested by the Tathāgata is likewise so: it is fully seen by Bodhisattvas, yet remains unseen by Śrāvakas.

It is like a person who applies a medicine for invisibility to their eyes; while among a great assembly, no one can see them as they come, go, sit, or stand, yet they are able to perceive all matters within that assembly.

One should know that the Tathāgata is likewise: transcending the world and seeing the entire world, he cannot be seen by any śrāvakas, except for those great bodhisattvas who are heading toward the realm of omniscience.
Just as when a person is born, there are two deities that constantly follow them:
one is called "Born Together" (Sahaja) and the other is called "Same Name" (Samānanāman).
Just as devas constantly see humans, yet humans do not see the devas, one should know that it is likewise with the Tathāgata:
while manifesting great supernormal powers within the great assemblies of bodhisattvas, all the mahāśrāvakas are unable to see them.

For example, it is like a bhikṣu who has attained mastery over the mind and enters the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*); the functions of his six sense faculties all cease to operate, and he neither knows nor perceives any speech;
yet, because he is sustained by the power of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), he does not pass into parinirvāṇa.

All śrāvakas are likewise; although they dwell within the Jeta Grove and possess the six sense faculties, they do not know, see, understand, or enter into the sovereign power of the Tathāgata or the various activities performed by the assembly of bodhisattvas.

Why is this? The realm of the Tathāgata is profoundly deep and vast; it is difficult to see, difficult to know, difficult to fathom, and difficult to measure. It transcends all worlds, is inconceivable, and cannot be destroyed. It is not the realm of any of the followers of the two vehicles.

Therefore, such matters as the sovereign spiritual power of the Tathāgata, the assembly of bodhisattvas, and the Jeta Grove pervading all pure worlds—these things are entirely unknown and unseen by the great śrāvakas, for they are not their proper vessel.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vairocanapraṇidhānaraśmi, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“You all should observe: The inconceivable path of the Buddhas, Manifesting supernormal powers Right here in this Jeta Grove.”
Through the majestic spiritual power of the Sugata, That which is manifested is infinite;
All beings in every world Are deluded and cannot comprehend it.
The profound and wondrous Dharma of the Dharma-King Is immeasurable and difficult to conceive.
The various supernormal powers he manifests cannot be fathomed by anyone in the world.
Because he has realized that all phenomena are signless, he is called a Buddha;
yet he is adorned with the primary and secondary marks, whose praises can never be fully extolled.
Now, within this grove, you manifest great supernormal powers—
profound and boundless, such that words cannot describe them.
Behold these beings of great majesty, the immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas.
From the lands of the ten directions, they come to behold the World-Honored One;
their vows are all fully realized, and their conduct is without obstruction;
throughout all worlds, there is none who can fathom them.
All the pratyekabuddhas, as well as those great śrāvakas,
are entirely unable to know the sphere of the bodhisattva’s practice.
With great wisdom, the bodhisattva brings all the stages (bhūmis) to ultimate perfection.
He erects the banner of courageous valor, Difficult to crush and difficult to move.
Those great beings of renowned fame, Through the power of immeasurable samādhis,
Manifest various spiritual transformations That completely fill the entire dharma realm.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King Indestructible Diligence, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Behold, O sons of the Buddhas, The treasury of wisdom and merit,
Who have perfected the practices for enlightenment And bring peace and security to all worlds.”
His mind is fundamentally luminous and penetrating, skillfully entering all samādhis;
his wisdom is boundless, and his sphere of activity is immeasurable.
Now, this Jetavana Grove is adorned in every way with various splendors.
The assembly of Bodhisattvas gathers like clouds, dwelling in close proximity to the Tathāgata.
Behold this immeasurable ocean-like multitude, free from attachment,
who have come from the ten directions to this place and sit upon seats of precious lotuses.
Neither coming nor abiding, without reliance and free from conceptual proliferation,
the stainless mind is unimpeded, reaching the ultimate limit of the dharma-realm.
It establishes the banner of wisdom, firm and unshakable.
Knowing that there is no dharma of transformation, yet manifesting the deeds of transformation;
simultaneously proceeding to all the Buddhas throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions, yet without dividing the body.
Behold the Lion of the Śākyas and his power of sovereign supernormal faculties,
which causes the assembly of bodhisattvas to gather here all together.
All the teachings of the Buddhas are entirely equal throughout the dharma-realm.
Because of their verbal expressions, they appear different, yet this assembly has fully realized that all Buddhas eternally abide in the state of equality within the dharma-realm;
as they expound the various distinct teachings, their eloquence is inexhaustible.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Universal Supreme Unsurpassed Majestic Virtue King, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Behold the Unsurpassed One, Whose vast wisdom is perfected;
Skilled in discerning the timely and the untimely, He expounds the Dharma for the sake of the multitudes.”
He subdues all non-Buddhists and all their various heterodox arguments;
universally following the minds of sentient beings, he manifests his supernormal powers.
Perfect Enlightenment is neither finite, nor is it infinite.
Whether finite or infinite, the Muni has completely transcended them all.
Like the sun in the sky, which shines upon every place;
so too is the Buddha’s wisdom, which thoroughly understands the phenomena of the three periods of time.
Just as on the night of the fifteenth, the lunar disk is without diminution or defect;
so too is the Tathāgata, for whom all pure dharmas (*śukla-dharma*) are perfectly complete.
Just as the sun in the sky moves without ceasing for even a moment; [so too is the Tathāgata].
The Tathāgata is likewise; his miraculous transformations are ever-continuing.
Just as the lands of the ten directions are unimpeded within space, so too does the Lamp of the World manifest transformations within the world.
Just as the earth in this world is the support for all living beings,
so too is the Wheel of Dharma of the Lamp that Illumines the World their support.
Just as a fierce and swift wind encounters no obstruction in its course, [so too is the Wheel of Dharma].
The Buddha-dharma is likewise: it swiftly pervades the world.
Just as the great wheel of water is that upon which the world rests, so too is the wheel of wisdom that upon which the Buddhas of the three times rely.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King Unobstructed Supreme Treasury, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Just as a great mountain of jewels Benefits all sentient beings;
So too is the Buddha-mountain, Universally benefiting the world."
Just as the waters of the great ocean are clear, pure, and free from turbidity;
seeing the Buddha is likewise able to eliminate all thirst and craving.
Just as Mount Sumeru rises out from the midst of the great ocean;
The Lamp of the World is likewise, arising from the ocean of Dharma.
As the sea contains all manner of jewels that satisfy every seeker, so too is the Teacherless Wisdom: all who behold it attain awakening.
The Tathāgata’s profound wisdom is immeasurable and beyond count;
therefore, through his supernormal powers, he manifests what is inconceivable.
Just as a skilled illusionist manifests all manner of things, so does he display these wonders.
The Buddha’s wisdom is likewise, manifesting all powers of mastery.
Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel can satisfy every desire,
so too does the Most Victorious One fulfill all pure aspirations.
Just as a bright and pure jewel universally illuminates all things,
so too is the Buddha's wisdom, universally illuminating the minds of all living beings.
Just as an eight-sided jewel reflects equally upon all directions, [so does the Buddha’s wisdom reflect all things].
The Unobstructed Lamp is likewise, universally illuminating the dharma-realm.
Just as the water-purifying jewel can clear all turbid waters;
so too is it when one beholds the Buddha—the faculties become entirely pure.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of the Moon of Vows Manifesting the Dharma Realm, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Just as the sapphire jewel Can turn all colors blue, So it is for those who see the Buddha: They all give rise to the practice of bodhi."
Within each and every atom, the Buddha manifests his supernatural powers,
causing immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas to all become pure.
This profound and subtle power is infinite and beyond comprehension.
The realm of the Bodhisattvas cannot be fathomed by the world.
The body manifested by the Tathāgata is adorned with pure marks;
it enters universally into the Dharma-realm and brings all Bodhisattvas to fulfillment.
In an inconceivable Buddha-land, he attained perfect enlightenment;
it is filled with all bodhisattvas and world-rulers.
Śākyamuni, the Unsurpassed Honored One, possesses complete mastery over all dharmas.
He manifests supernormal powers, boundless and immeasurable.
The various practices of the Bodhisattvas are infinite and inexhaustible;
the Tathāgata, through his power of mastery, manifests them all.
The Son of the Buddha, having skillfully practiced and studied the profound realms of all phenomena,
has attained unimpeded wisdom and clearly understands all dharmas.
Through the majestic spiritual power of the Sugata, he turns the wheel of Dharma for the sake of the multitudes.
His spiritual transformations pervade everywhere, causing the entire world to be pure.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom is perfect and complete, and his realm is likewise pure;
he is like a great dragon king who universally delivers all living beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of the Radiant Flame of Dharma-Wisdom, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, And their great disciples, the śrāvakas—
None of them can know The matter of the Buddha’s lifting and setting down his feet.”
Throughout the past, future, and present, all the Pratyekabuddhas likewise do not know the Tathāgata’s act of lifting and lowering his feet;
how much less so the ordinary worldlings, who are bound and fettered by the afflictions?
With the mind and consciousness shrouded by ignorance, how could one know the Teacher?
The Perfectly Awakened One’s unimpeded wisdom transcends the path of language;
its measure is unfathomable—who could possibly know or see it?
Just as the light of the bright moon, No one can measure its limits;
So too is the Buddha’s supernormal power, Whose end or limit cannot be seen.
Each and every skillful means, Transformed in every thought-moment—
Even throughout immeasurable eons, one cannot fully comprehend them through contemplation.
Contemplating the omniscience and the inconceivable Dharma,
one finds that no limit can be reached within each and every gateway of skillful means.
If there are those who give rise to vast vows regarding this Dharma,
for them this realm will not be difficult to know and see.
Through courageous and diligent cultivation, they will enter the inconceivable great ocean of Dharma.
With a mind free from obstruction, one enters this gateway of skillful means;
with the mind and its faculties already subdued, and aspirations vast and wide,
one shall attain great bodhi, the most supreme state.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jñānaketudhvajarāja, who had shattered all demonic armies, receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The body of wisdom is not a physical body; It is unimpeded and inconceivable.
Should anyone attempt to conceive of it, No one at all could ever reach it.”
From inconceivable karma, this pure body has arisen;
With its extraordinary and wondrous adornments, it is unattached to the three realms.
Its radiance illuminates all things, and the entire dharma-realm is utterly pure.
Opening the gate of the Buddha’s bodhi, giving birth to all manner of wisdom;
like the sun in the world, universally radiating the light of insight,
far removed from all dust and defilement, extinguishing and eliminating every hindrance.
Universally purifying the three realms of existence, forever severing the flow of birth and death,
accomplishing the path of a bodhisattva, and giving rise to unsurpassed enlightenment;
manifesting infinite forms, yet these forms have no place of dependence.
Though what is manifested is immeasurable, all is inconceivable.
In a single moment of thought, one can awaken to all phenomena;
how then could one wish to measure the limits of the Tathāgata’s wisdom?
In a single thought, they fully comprehend all phenomena of the three periods of time;
therefore, it is said that the Buddha’s wisdom is inexhaustible and indestructible.
The wise should thus single-mindedly contemplate the Bodhi of the Buddha.
This thought is inconceivable; one cannot grasp it through thinking.
Bodhi is ineffable, transcending the path of language;
from this all Buddhas are born—this Dharma is inconceivable.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of the Banner of the Light of Vow-Knowledge, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“If one can skillfully observe The inexhaustible ocean of bodhi,
Then one will leave behind deluded thoughts And resolutely uphold the Dharma.”
If one attains a resolute mind, one can then cultivate sublime conduct;
through meditative stillness and self-reflection, one forever severs all doubts and delusions.
One’s mind will not grow weary, nor will there be any indolence.
Progressing through successive stages of cultivation, one ultimately fulfills all Buddha-dharmas.
Having already accomplished faith and wisdom, one causes them to increase in every thought-moment;
always delighting in and constantly observing the dharma that is without attainment and without reliance.
Throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, all the meritorious deeds they have cultivated are entirely dedicated toward the path sought by all Buddhas;
though they remain within the cycle of birth and death, their minds are free from defilement and attachment.
Abiding securely in all Buddha-dharmas, they always delight in the conduct of the Tathāgatas.
Regarding everything that exists in the world— the aggregates, elements, and all such phenomena—
they relinquish it all and seek exclusively the virtues of the Buddha.
Ordinary beings, ensnared by delusive confusion, Constantly transmigrate within the world;
The Bodhisattva’s mind is unimpeded, Rescuing them and bringing them to liberation.
The Bodhisattva’s practice is difficult to extol, None in all the world can conceive of it.
Universally eliminating all suffering, Bestowing happiness upon all living beings;
Having already attained the wisdom of Bodhi, He further takes pity on all sentient beings.
His radiance illuminates the world, Liberating the entire multitude.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vīramatijñānarāja, who shatters all obstacles, receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, The name of a Buddha is difficult even to hear;
How much more so to draw near him And forever sever all doubts and delusions!”
The Tathāgata, the lamp of the world, has thoroughly realized all dharmas;
he universally generates merit throughout the three periods of time and causes all beings to be completely purified.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body is praised and admired by all.
For billions of eons they constantly gaze upon him, their minds never weary or satisfied.
If there are sons of the Buddha who contemplate the Buddha’s wondrous form-body,
they will surely abandon all attachments and turn toward the path of Bodhi.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body Constantly emits a vast and great sound;
With unimpeded eloquence, He opens the gate of the Buddha’s bodhi;
Awakening all sentient beings, In measureless and inconceivable ways.
Causing them to enter the gateway of wisdom, He bestows upon them the prophecy of enlightenment.
When the Tathāgata appears in the world, He serves as the great field of merit for the world;
Universally guiding all sentient beings, He causes them to accumulate meritorious deeds.
If one makes offerings to the Buddha, one will forever eliminate the fear of the evil realms,
extinguish all suffering, and achieve a body of wisdom.
If one beholds the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings, one can give rise to a vast and great mind.
Such a person constantly encounters the Buddhas, Increasing the power of their wisdom.
If they see the Supreme among Men, They resolve their intent upon Bodhi;
Such a person can know for themselves That they shall surely attain Perfect Enlightenment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātu-prabheda-praṇidhijñānābhijñārāja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Śākyamuni, the Unsurpassed Honored One, Is endowed with all merits;
Those who behold him attain purity of mind And dedicate themselves to great wisdom.”
The Tathāgata, with great compassion, appears in the world;
for the sake of all living beings, he turns the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma.
For countless eons, the Tathāgata has undergone diligent toil for the sake of sentient beings.
How can those in the world repay the kindness of the Great Teacher?
It would be better to undergo the sufferings of the evil realms for immeasurable eons than ever to abandon the Tathāgata in the pursuit of liberation.
I would rather take the place of all sentient beings and undergo every kind of suffering,
never abandoning the Buddha in my quest for peace and happiness;
I would rather dwell in the various evil realms and constantly hear the name of the Buddha.
I would not wish to be born in the happy realms, even for a moment, were it to mean not hearing of the Buddha.
I would rather be born in all the various hells, each for countless eons;
I would never abandon the Buddha to seek escape from the miserable destinies.
For what reason do you wish to dwell long in all the evil realms?
It is because by seeing the Tathāgata, your wisdom will increase.
If one is able to see the Buddha, all suffering will be extinguished.
One is able to enter the realm of great wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
If one succeeds in seeing the Buddha, one abandons all obstacles;
nurturing inexhaustible merit, one accomplishes the path to Bodhi.
The Tathāgata can forever sever all doubts of sentient beings;
according to what their hearts desire, he causes them all to be fully satisfied.
— *The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Great Vaipulya*, Fascicle Sixty.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Sixty-One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree, Part Two.
Chapter Thirty-Nine: Entering the Dharma Realm, Part Two.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra surveyed the entire assembly of bodhisattvas. Employing skillful means equal to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), skillful means equal to the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and skillful means equal to the realm of sentient beings (*sattvadhātu*); being equal to the three periods of time, equal to all eons, equal to the karma of all sentient beings, equal to the inclinations of all sentient beings, equal to the understandings of all sentient beings, equal to the faculties of all sentient beings, equal to the timing for the maturation of all sentient beings, and employing skillful means equal to the light and shadows of all phenomena—for the sake of these bodhisattvas, he used ten dharma-phrases to open up, reveal, illuminate, and expound this Lion’s Stretch Samādhi (*siṃhavijṛmbhita-samādhi*).
What are these ten? They are as follows:
expounding the dharma-words that reveal the sequential emergence of all Buddhas and the sequential formation and destruction of all Buddha-fields within every atom of the entire dharma-realm;

They expound the Dharma verses that can manifest, within all Buddha-lands equal in extent to the realm of empty space, the sounds of praising the Tathāgata’s merits throughout all kalpas until the end of the future;

they expound the Dharma verses that can manifest, within all Buddha-lands equal in extent to the realm of empty space, the infinite and boundless gateways of the Tathāgata’s appearance in the world and his attainment of perfect enlightenment;

they expound the Dharma verses that can manifest, within all Buddha-lands equal in extent to the realm of empty space, the Buddhas sitting at the site of enlightenment amidst assemblies of bodhisattvas.

He expounds the Dharma-phrases that, from every single pore, manifest in every thought-moment transformation-bodies equal in number to all Buddhas of the three periods of time, filling the entire Dharma-realm;
he expounds the Dharma-phrases that enable a single body to fill all oceans of lands throughout the ten directions, appearing with universal equality;
and he expounds the Dharma-phrases that enable the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas of the three periods of time to appear universally within all realms.

He preached the Dharma-phrases that enable the manifestation, within every atom of all Buddha-fields, of the various spiritual transformations of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields of the three periods of time, continuing for immeasurable eons;

he preached the Dharma-phrases that enable the production from every pore of the ocean-like sounds of the great vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, continuing until the end of future eons to awaken and guide all bodhisattvas;

and he preached the Dharma-phrases that enable the Buddha’s lion throne to equal the extent of the Dharma-realm, with the assemblies of bodhisattvas and the adornments of the site of enlightenment being without distinction, turning various subtle and wondrous wheels of Dharma throughout all future eons.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
With these ten as the foremost, there are dharma-words as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields; all are the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to reiterate this meaning, relying on the Buddha’s spiritual power, observed the Tathāgata, observed the assembly, observed the inconceivable realms of all Buddhas, observed the boundless samādhis of all Buddhas, observed the inconceivable oceans of worlds, observed the inconceivable wisdom of dharmas that are like illusions, observed the inconceivable equality of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, and observed all immeasurable and boundless methods of verbal expression, and then spoke in verse:
Within each and every pore, Are oceans of lands as numerous as atoms,
In all of which Tathāgatas sit, Each surrounded by assemblies of Bodhisattvas.
Within each and every pore, Are immeasurable oceans of lands.
The Buddha sits upon the seat of enlightenment, pervading thus the entire Dharma-realm.
Within every single pore, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of all lands are surrounded by assemblies of Bodhisattvas, who proclaim for them the conduct of Samantabhadra.
The Buddha sits within a single land, yet fills the realms of the ten directions;
clouds of immeasurable bodhisattvas all gather at his abode.
As numerous as the atoms of billions of lands are the oceans of merit of these bodhisattvas.
Together they rose from within the assembly, filling the realms of the ten directions.
All abiding in the conduct of Samantabhadra, they all traverse the ocean of the Dharma-realm;
universally manifesting in all lands, they enter equally into the assemblies of all Buddhas.
Sitting peacefully in all lands, they hear all dharmas;
within each and every realm, they cultivate various practices for billions of eons.
The practices cultivated by these Bodhisattvas are the universally radiant practices of the ocean of Dharma.
Entering the ocean of great vows, Abiding on the ground of the Buddha’s realm,
Thoroughly comprehending the conduct of Samantabhadra, Giving birth to all Buddha-dharmas,
Possessing the ocean of the Buddha’s merits, He extensively manifests miraculous deeds.
"Bodies like clouds, as numerous as atoms, pervade all lands, universally raining down the Dharma of ambrosia, causing all beings to abide in the Buddha-way.

At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to cause all bodhisattvas to dwell securely in the Tathāgata’s Great Lion-Stretch Samādhi, emitted a great radiance from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows; the name of that light was:

The gateway of universally illuminating the dharma-realm of the three periods of time has for its retinue unspeakably many light rays, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-lands; it universally illuminates all the oceans of worlds and the lands of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions.

At that time, the great assembly of bodhisattvas in the Jeta Grove all beheld within every single atom of all Buddha-lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm and space-realm, a number of Buddha-fields equal to the atoms of all Buddha-lands—each with various names, various colors, various purities, various abodes, and various forms.

In this way, within all these lands, there were great bodhisattvas seated upon lion thrones at sites of enlightenment, attaining perfect awakening, surrounded before and behind by assemblies of bodhisattvas, and honored by the lords of the world;
or he saw them, amidst assemblies as vast as unspeakable buddha-fields, emitting sublime sounds that filled the dharma-realm as they turned the wheel of the true Dharma.

Or he may see [the Buddha] in celestial palaces, dragon palaces, yakṣa palaces, or within the palaces of gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans; or among humans in villages, towns, settlements, royal capitals, and great cities. There he manifests various lineages, various names, various bodies, various marks, and various radiances; he abides in various modes of conduct, enters various samādhis, and displays various supernatural transformations. At times, he himself uses various voices and languages, or causes various bodhisattvas and others within various great assemblies to speak various teachings in various words and phrases.
Within this assembly, the great multitude of bodhisattvas beheld such profound samādhi and great supernormal powers of these Buddhas,
the Tathāgatas; likewise, throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space— in all directions of east, west, south, north,
the four intermediate points, above, and below— within the oceans of all quarters, they abide according to the mental conceptions of sentient beings, beginning...
From the past limit up to the present, within all lands, the bodies of all sentient beings, and all paths of space—
within each and every location the size of a hair-tip, there are successively established lands as numerous as atoms,
each with various karmic origins, and in each there is a site of enlightenment with an assembly of bodhisattvas.
All likewise perceived the Buddha’s spiritual power: it does not destroy the three periods of time, nor does it destroy the world;

it manifests its reflection within the minds of all sentient beings, produces sublime sounds according to the inclinations of the hearts of all sentient beings, universally enters into all assemblies, and universally appears before all sentient beings.
While their physical forms differ, their wisdom is without distinction; they reveal the Buddha-dharma as appropriate to each being, teaching and taming all sentient beings without ever ceasing.

Those who behold this supernatural power of the Buddha have all been gathered by the roots of goodness of Vairocana Tathāgata in former times; or they were previously gathered through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*); or they were brought to maturity through seeing, hearing, remembering, or drawing near [to him]; or he taught them in the past to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; or they planted roots of goodness together with various Buddhas in the past; or they were taught and brought to maturity in the past through the skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) of omniscience.
Therefore, they all attain entry into the Tathāgata’s inconceivable and profound samādhi, and the great supernormal powers that pervade the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space:

some enter the Dharma-body; some enter the form-body; some enter the practices accomplished in the past; some enter the fulfillment of the various pāramitās; some enter the wheel of adorned and pure conduct; some enter the various bodhisattva stages; some enter the power of attaining perfect enlightenment; some enter the undifferentiated great miraculous transformations of the samādhis in which the Buddha dwells; some enter the Tathāgata’s powers, fearlessnesses, and wisdom; and some enter the ocean of the Buddha’s unimpeded eloquence.

Those bodhisattvas, by means of various understandings, various paths, various gateways, various entries, various principles, various conformities, various wisdoms, various aids to the path, various skillful means, and various samādhis, enter such oceans of the skillful means of the spiritual transformations of Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields.
What are the various samādhis?
They are as follows:
the samādhi of universally adorning the dharma-realm; the samādhi of universally illuminating the unobstructed realm of all three periods of time.
The Samādhi of the Light of Wisdom on the Non-differentiation of the Dharma-realm; the Samādhi of Entering the Tathāgata’s Sphere Without Wavering;
the Samādhi of Universally Illuminating the Boundless Void; the Samādhi of Entering the Power of the Tathāgata;
the Samādhi of the Buddha’s Fearlessness, Valiant Ferocity, and Adornment; and the Samādhi of the Revolving Treasury of the Entire Dharma-realm.
The Samādhi of the Moon Universally Manifesting Throughout All Dharma Realms with Unimpeded Sound and Great Explication;
the Samādhi of the Light of Universally Pure Dharmas; the Samādhi of the Unobstructed Silken Banner of the Dharma King;
the Samādhi of Seeing the Ocean of All Buddhas Within Every Single Realm; and the Samādhi of Manifesting the Body Throughout All Worlds.
The samādhi of entering the realm of the Tathāgata’s undifferentiated body;
the samādhi of the treasury of great compassion that accords with all worlds; the samādhi of knowing that all dharmas leave no trace;
the samādhi of knowing that all dharmas are ultimately quiescent; and the samādhi of being able to manifest transformations throughout the world despite having nothing to be attained.
The samādhi of [the Buddha’s] body, the samādhi of universally entering all lands, the samādhi of adorning all buddha-lands and attaining perfect enlightenment,
the samādhi of observing the distinctions in the physical marks of the lords of all worlds,
the samādhi of observing the realms of all sentient beings without obstruction, and the samādhi capable of giving birth to the mothers of all Tathāgatas.
The samādhi of entering the path of merit that enters the ocean of all Buddhas through practice;
the samādhi of manifesting spiritual transformations within each and every realm until the end of the future; the samādhi of entering the ocean of the past deeds of all Tathāgatas;
the samādhi of protecting and upholding the lineage of all Tathāgatas until the end of the future; and by means of resolute understanding...
The samādhi that powerfully purifies all oceans of Buddha-fields in the ten directions of the present;
the samādhi that universally illuminates all places where Buddhas dwell in a single thought-moment; the samādhi of entering the unobstructed limit of all realms;
the samādhi that causes all worlds to become a single Buddha-field; and the samādhi that brings forth all the transformation bodies of the Buddhas.
The samādhi of knowing the ocean of all faculties through the wisdom of the Vajra King; the samādhi of knowing that all Tathāgatas are of one and the same body;
the samādhi of knowing that all that is established within the dharma-realm dwells entirely within the limit of mental recollection;
and the samādhi of manifesting parinirvāṇa within the vast lands of all dharma-realms.
The samādhi of causing [beings] to abide in the supreme state; the samādhi of manifesting various distinct bodies for all sentient beings within all Buddha-fields;
the samādhi of universally entering the wisdom of all Buddhas; the samādhi of knowing the nature and characteristics of all phenomena;
the samādhi of universally knowing the phenomena of the three periods of time in a single thought-moment; and the samādhi of universally manifesting the Dharma in every thought-moment.
The Samādhi of the Body of the Realms; the Samādhi of Knowing the Successive Arisings of All Tathāgatas through the Lion’s Valiant Wisdom;
the Samādhi of the Perfect Eye of Wisdom regarding the Sphere of All Dharma Realms; the Samādhi of Valiantly Advancing toward the Ten Powers;
and the Samādhi of Emitting the Perfect Radiance of All Meritorious Qualities to Universally Illuminate the World.
The Samādhi of Unobstructed Darkness, the Samādhi of the Immovable Treasury, the Samādhi of Preaching a Single Dharma that Universally Enters All Dharmas,
the Samādhi of Explaining and Interpreting a Single Dharma through the Distinctions of All Vocal Expressions, the Samādhi of Expounding the Non-dual Dharma of All Buddhas,
the Samādhi of Knowing the Unobstructed Limit of the Three Times, and the Samādhi of Knowing All Kalpas Without Differentiation.
The Samādhi of Distinction; the Samādhi of Entering the Subtle Expedient Means of the Ten Powers;
the Samādhi of Accomplishing All Bodhisattva Practices Without Interruption Throughout All Kalpas; the Samādhi of Universally Manifesting the Body in the Ten Directions;
the Samādhi of Attaining Perfect Enlightenment with Sovereignty over the Dharma-realm; the Samādhi of Producing All Peaceful Experiences; and the Emergence...
The samādhi of adorning the realm of empty space with all ornaments; the samādhi of emitting clouds of transformation bodies equal in number to sentient beings in every thought-moment;
the samādhi of the moonlight radiance of the Tathāgata’s pure void;
the samādhi of constantly seeing all Tathāgatas dwelling in empty space; and the samādhi of revealing the adornments of all Buddhas.
The Samādhi of the Lamp Illuminating the Meaning of All Dharmas; the Samādhi of Illuminating the Sphere of the Ten Powers;
the Samādhi of the Perception of the Banners of All Buddhas of the Three Times; the Samādhi of the Single Secret Treasury of All Buddhas;
the Samādhi of Bringing All Deeds to Ultimate Perfection in Every Thought-moment; the Samādhi of the Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit; and the Samādhi of Beholding Boundless Buddhas.
The Samādhi of Boundless Realms; the Samādhi of Firmly Abiding in All Dharmas; the Samādhi of Manifesting and Causing the Knowledge and Vision of All the Transformations of All Tathāgatas;
the Samādhi of the Constant Appearance of the Buddha-Sun in Every Thought-Moment;
the Samādhi of Fully Knowing All Dharmas of the Three Times in a Single Day; and the Samādhi of Universally Proclaiming through Sound that the Nature of All Dharmas is Quiescent.
The samādhi of cessation; the samādhi of seeing the sovereign power of all Buddhas; the samādhi of the blooming lotus of the dharma-realm;
the samādhi of contemplating all phenomena as being like space, having no place of abiding; the samādhi of universally entering one direction within the ocean of the ten directions;
the samādhi of entering the sourceless and bottomless depths of the entire dharma-realm; and the ocean of all phenomena.
The Samādhi of Peaceful Body Emitting All Radiance; the Samādhi of Manifesting All Supernatural Powers and Great Vows in a Single Thought-moment;
the Samādhi of Attaining Perfect Enlightenment at All Times and in All Places;
the Samādhi of Entering All Dharma Realms through a Single Adornment; and the Samādhi of Universally Manifesting the Bodies of All Buddhas.
The Samādhi of Knowing the Vast and Exalted Supernatural Powers of All Sentient Beings;
the Samādhi of the Body Pervading the Dharma-realm in a Single Thought-moment; the Samādhi of Manifesting the Pure Dharma-realm of the One Vehicle;
the Samādhi of Entering the Universal Gateway Dharma-realm to Display Great Adornments; and the Samādhi of Sustaining the Dharma Wheels of All Buddhas.

The samādhi of adorning a single dharma-gate with all dharma-gates; the samādhi of gathering all realms of sentient beings through the vows and practices of Indra’s net; the samādhi of discerning the gates of all worlds;
the samādhi of traveling freely upon the lotus-vehicle; and the supernormal power of knowing the various distinctions among all sentient beings.
The samādhi of wisdom; the samādhi that causes one’s body to constantly appear before all sentient beings;
the samādhi of knowing the ocean of the various sounds and languages of all sentient beings; the samādhi of the supernatural power of knowing the various wisdoms of all sentient beings;
the samādhi of the treasury of great compassion and equanimity; and the samādhi of all Buddhas entering the limit of the Tathāgata.
The Samādhi of the Lion’s Stretching that Observes the Sphere of Liberation of All Tathāgatas... By means of such samādhis,

as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, the Bodhisattva entered the ocean of miraculous transformations of the Samādhi of Vairocana Tathāgata, which in every thought-moment fills the entire Dharma-realm.

All those bodhisattvas were fully endowed with great wisdom and supernormal powers; they were clear-sighted, sharp, and sovereign, dwelling in the various stages (*bhūmi*) and universally observing all things with vast wisdom.

Born from the lineage of all wisdoms, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) was ever present before them. Having attained the pure eye of wisdom free from the cataracts of delusion, they acted as guides for all sentient beings.
Abiding in the equality of the Buddhas, they were without discrimination regarding any phenomena.
Thoroughly comprehending all realms, they know that the nature of all worlds is fundamentally quiescent and devoid of any place of dependence;
they travel universally to all Buddha-lands without attachment, fully observe all phenomena without abiding, and enter everywhere into the palaces of the sublime Dharma without coming from anywhere;
they teach and transform all worlds, universally manifesting places of peace and security for all sentient beings.
Wisdom and liberation are their sphere of activity;
they constantly abide in the body of wisdom at the limit of detachment from craving, transcending the ocean of all existence and manifesting the limit of reality;
with the perfection of the light of wisdom, they universally perceive all phenomena.
Abiding in samādhi, steadfast and immovable;

constantly giving rise to great compassion for all sentient beings; knowing that all dharma-gates are entirely like illusions, all sentient beings are entirely like dreams, all Tathāgatas are entirely like shadows, all speech and sounds are entirely like echoes, and all dharmas are entirely like transformations;
skillfully able to accumulate sublime practices and vows, with perfected wisdom, pure ingenuity, and a mind of ultimate tranquility.
They skillfully enter the realm of all dhāraṇīs, possess the power of samādhi, and are courageous and fearless;
they have attained the eye of clear wisdom, abide at the limit of the dharma-realm, and reach the state where all phenomena are non-apprehendable;
they cultivate the boundless great ocean of wisdom, reach the ultimate further shore of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and are sustained by the perfection of wisdom.

Through the perfection of supernormal powers (*abhijñā-pāramitā*), they universally enter the world; through the perfection of meditative concentration (*samādhi-pāramitā*), they attain mastery over the mind;

through non-erroneous wisdom, they know all meanings; through the wisdom of skillful discernment, they reveal the treasury of the Dharma; through the wisdom of manifest realization, they explain and interpret words and phrases; through the power of great vows, they preach the Dharma inexhaustibly;

and with the fearless great lion’s roar, they constantly delight in observing the phenomena that have no basis of dependence. With the pure eye of Dharma, they universally observe all things; with the moon of pure wisdom, they illuminate the formation and destruction of the world; and with the light of wisdom, they illumine the true reality.
Their merit and wisdom are like a mountain of adamant, beyond the reach of any analogy;
they skillfully contemplate all phenomena, causing the faculty of wisdom to increase;
through courageous diligence, they crush and subdue all Māras.
With immeasurable wisdom, their majestic radiance blazes intensely;
their bodies transcend all worlds, and they have attained unimpeded wisdom regarding all dharmas, skillfully realizing the limits of both the exhausted and the inexhaustible;
abiding at the universal limit, they enter the limit of reality, and the wisdom of signless contemplation is ever present before them.
Skillfully accomplishing all bodhisattva practices, they know all realms through non-dual wisdom; they universally behold all destinies within all worlds and travel throughout all buddha-lands.
With the lamp of wisdom perfected, they are free from all obscurations regarding all phenomena; emitting the pure light of Dharma, they illuminate the worlds of the ten directions.

They serve as the true field of merit for all worlds; whether seen or heard, their aspirations are all fulfilled. Their merit and virtue are so lofty and great that they transcend all worlds; courageous and fearless, they subdue all those of external paths.
They emit subtle and wondrous sounds that pervade all lands, universally beholding all Buddhas with a mind never weary;
having attained mastery over the Buddha-dharmakāya, they manifest bodies according to those to be transformed, a single body filling all buddha-fields;
having attained mastery of pure supernormal powers, they ride the vessel of great wisdom, proceeding without obstruction, their wisdom perfected and pervading the entire dharma-realm.
It is like the rising sun that shines universally upon the world, manifesting its forms according to the minds of sentient beings;
knowing the faculties, natures, and inclinations of all beings, it enters the realm of non-contention regarding all phenomena;
knowing that the nature of all dharmas is without birth or arising, it is able to cause the small and the great to enter one another with sovereign ease.
They have definitively resolved the profound course of the Buddha-ground; they expound profound meanings through inexhaustible phrases, manifesting an ocean of all *sūtras* within a single phrase;
they have attained the body of the great wisdom *dhāraṇī*, such that whatever they receive and uphold is never forgotten;
in a single thought-moment they can recall the events of immeasurable eons, and in a single thought-moment they fully know the wisdom of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time.

Constantly using all dharani-gates, they expound the boundless ocean of the Buddhas' teachings; they perpetually turn the pure wheel of Dharma that never regresses, causing all sentient beings to give rise to wisdom;
they attain the light of wisdom of the Buddha-realm and enter the profound samadhi of "Excellent Vision";
they enter the realm of non-obstruction regarding all phenomena, achieving sovereign mastery over supreme wisdom regarding all phenomena, with all spheres of experience purified and adorned.
They universally enter all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, reaching every single location without exception;

within each and every atom they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment, displaying all forms within the nature of formlessness, and through every direction they universally enter a single direction.

These bodhisattvas possess such infinite treasuries of merit, wisdom, and virtue that they are constantly praised by all Buddhas; though various words and phrases were used to describe their virtues, they could never exhaust them. There was not one among them who was not present in the Jeta Grove, having deeply entered the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s merits and beholding all that was illuminated by the Buddha’s radiance.

At that time, the bodhisattvas attained the light of the inconceivable True Dharma; their hearts were filled with great joy, and from their own bodies, the pavilions, the various ornaments, and the lion thrones upon which they sat—extending through all things throughout the Jeta Grove—they manifested clouds of manifold great adornments, filling the entire dharma-realm of the ten directions.
That is to say:
in every thought-moment, they emit great clouds of light that fill the ten directions, fully awakening all sentient beings;

they produce clouds of all kinds of mani-jewel bells that fill the ten directions, emitting subtle and wondrous sounds that extol and praise all the merits of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
They emit clouds of all kinds of music that fill the ten directions, and within these sounds they proclaim the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
they emit clouds of the various vows, practices, and physical forms of all bodhisattvas that fill the ten directions, proclaiming all the great vows of the bodhisattvas;
they emit clouds of the sovereign transformations of all Tathāgatas that fill the ten directions, producing the speech and sounds of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
They emit clouds of the bodies of all bodhisattvas, adorned with the primary and secondary marks, filling the ten directions, proclaiming the successive appearances of all Tathāgatas in all lands;

they emit clouds of the sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, filling the ten directions, manifesting the adornments of the merits of all Tathāgatas attaining perfect enlightenment;
they emit clouds of all dragon kings, filling the ten directions, raining down all kinds of incense.
They emit clouds of bodies of all World-Honored Lords that fill the ten directions, expounding the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
they emit clouds of pure Buddha-lands adorned with all kinds of jewels that fill the ten directions, manifesting all Tathāgatas turning the wheel of the True Dharma.

Because these bodhisattvas have attained the light of the inconceivable Dharma, it is by the very nature of things that they manifest such clouds of great miraculous transformations and adornments, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many buddha-fields.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, wishing to proclaim once more these miraculous events within the Jeta Grove, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“You should behold this Jeta Grove, Where, through the Buddha’s boundless majestic power, All manner of adornments are manifested,
Pervading the entirety of the dharma-realm in the ten directions.”
All the lands throughout the ten directions, with their boundless varieties of great adornments,
appear clearly and distinctly within the spheres of his seat and other such realms.
From the pores of all the Buddha-sons emerge clouds of variously adorned jewel-flames,
as well as the subtle and wondrous voices of the Tathāgatas, filling all lands throughout the ten directions.
Within the flowers of the jewel trees, a wondrous body appears; its color and marks are like those of Brahmā.
Arising from meditative concentration, it walks with measured steps; its deportment in advancing and retreating is ever tranquil.
Within each and every pore of the Tathāgata, He constantly manifests inconceivable transformation bodies;
Each is like the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, Adorned with all manner of excellent marks and signs.
From the midst of the sky above the Jetavana Grove, all manner of adornments emitted wondrous sounds,
universally proclaiming that all bodhisattvas of the three periods of time have accomplished an ocean of all virtues.
The various jewel trees within the Jeta Grove likewise emit immeasurable, wondrous sounds,
expounding upon the diverse oceans of karma of all sentient beings, each distinct from the other.
All the various realms within the forest manifest all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
each one displays great supernormal powers, as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of lands of the ten directions.

All the lands throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within all oceans of worlds, entirely enter into a single pore of the Tathāgata; their successive adornments are all clearly perceived.
All manner of adornments manifest as Buddhas, In numbers equal to sentient beings, pervading the world;
Each one emits great radiance, Transforming all classes of beings according to their needs.
Clouds of fragrant flames, myriad flowers, and jewel treasuries— every kind of exquisite and wondrous adornment—
are vast and expansive like space, pervading all lands throughout the ten directions.
All Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, And all their adorned, wondrous sites of enlightenment—
Within the realm of this grove, Every form and image appears clearly.
All the sons of the Buddhas, Samantabhadra, Who have adorned lands for oceans of hundreds of thousands of kalpas—
Their number being as infinite as all sentient beings— There is none who does not behold them within this grove.

At that time, because they were illuminated by the light of the Buddha’s samādhi, those bodhisattvas immediately entered such a samādhi. Each one attained unspeakably many gates of great compassion, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
From every single pore of their bodies, there issued forth unspeakably many rays of light, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
From each and every ray of light, there manifested unspeakably many transformed bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
His physical form and features were like those of the lords of the world; he appeared before all sentient beings, pervading and filling the dharma-realm of the ten directions.

Through various skillful means, he taught and tamed them, sometimes manifesting unspeakably many celestial palaces as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field as gates of impermanence, or sometimes manifesting unspeakably many...
The gateways of birth for all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field;
or manifesting the gateways of practice of all bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;

or manifesting the gateways of dream-visions, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields; or manifesting the gateways of the great vows of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
They may manifest gates of shaking worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;

they may manifest gates of discerning worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields; they may manifest gates of appearing in birth within worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
or they may manifest gates of the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.

...the gate of the *pāramitā*, or manifesting the gate of the *śīla-pāramitā* consisting of the various ascetic practices and cultivation of merits by all Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
or manifesting the gate of the *kṣānti-pāramitā* consisting of the severing of limbs and members, numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
or manifesting [the gate of the *dāna-pāramitā*] numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields...
There are gateways of the perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*) as numerous as atoms;
or they manifest gateways of all bodhisattvas cultivating various samādhis, meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), and liberations as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
or they manifest gateways of the light of wisdom that perfects the path of the Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields; or they manifest...
The gateway of seeking the Buddha-dharma with diligence for the sake of even a single word or phrase, discarding countless bodies and lives as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field;
or the gateway of manifesting, for unspeakably many eons as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, drawing near to all Buddhas and inquiring about all dharmas with a mind free from weariness;
or the gateway of manifesting, in accordance with... [unspeakably many eons as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field]...
To bring all sentient beings to maturity through skillful means according to their timing, seasons, and inclinations, he leads them to abide in the gateway of the light of the ocean of omniscience;

or he manifests the gateway of the power of a bodhisattva’s merit and wisdom by subduing hosts of Māras and restraining all non-Buddhists, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields; or he manifests [the same] in unspeakably many Buddha-fields...
The gate of wisdom that knows all arts and crafts, as numerous as the atoms in a mote of dust;
or the manifestation of the gate of wisdom that knows the distinctions among all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

or the manifestation of the gate of wisdom that knows the distinctions among all phenomena, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields; or the manifestation of the gate of wisdom that knows... [the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields].
The gate of wisdom that knows the differences in the mental inclinations of all sentient beings, as numerous as atoms;
or the manifestation of gates of wisdom that know the faculties, conduct, afflictions, and habitual tendencies of all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
or the manifestation of gates of wisdom that know the various karmas of all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
The gate of wisdom, or the manifestation of gates for awakening all sentient beings as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields...
By means of such expedient gates as these, numbering as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, he proceeds to the dwelling places of all sentient beings to bring them to maturity.
That is to say:

they may go to the palaces of devas, or to the palaces of nāgas, or to the palaces of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas; or they may go to the palace of Brahmā, or to the palace of a human king, or to the palace of King Yama, or to the abodes of animals, hungry ghosts, and hell-beings—thereby gathering in all sentient beings through impartial great compassion, impartial great vows, impartial wisdom, and impartial skillful means.

Some are tamed upon seeing him; some are tamed upon hearing him; some are tamed by recollecting him; some are tamed by hearing his voice; some are tamed by hearing his name; some are tamed by seeing his halo; and some are tamed by seeing his lattice of light.
According to the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings, he goes to each of their places to cause them to obtain benefit.
O Son of the Buddha!

All these bodhisattvas in this Jeta Grove, for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity, sometimes manifest themselves within various exquisitely adorned palaces; at other times, they manifest themselves dwelling upon jeweled lion-thrones within their own towers, surrounded by assemblies at sites of enlightenment, so that they may be seen throughout the ten directions, yet without ever departing from this Jeta Grove where the Tathāgata resides.
O Son of the Buddha!
These bodhisattvas sometimes manifest clouds of immeasurable transformation bodies, or they manifest their bodies as solitary and peerless.
That is to say:

Sometimes they manifest in the form of a śramaṇa, sometimes in the form of a brāhmaṇa, sometimes in the form of an ascetic, sometimes in the form of one in full vigor; sometimes they manifest in the form of a king of physicians, sometimes in the form of a merchant leader, sometimes in the form of one of pure livelihood, sometimes in the form of a musician or performer, sometimes in the form of one who serves the devas, and sometimes in the form of a craftsman or technician.

They go to all villages, camps, cities, royal capitals, towns, and wherever sentient beings dwell; according to what is appropriate for them, they perform the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all worlds—like a celestial net of Indra—by means of various forms, various modes of deportment, various voices, various discourses, and various abodes.

Some spoke of all the worldly arts and crafts; some spoke of the lamp of wisdom that illuminates the world; some spoke of the adornments produced by the karmic power of all sentient beings; some spoke of the establishment of the various vehicles and stages within the lands of the ten directions; and some spoke of the realm of all phenomena illuminated by the lamp of knowledge, which teaches and brings all sentient beings to fulfillment—yet none of them ever departed from this Jeta Grove, the abode of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī emerged from the Well-Situated Pavilion (Susthitakūṭāgāra) together with immeasurable fellow bodhisattvas,
as well as the various vajra-spirits who constantly attend and guard him, the various body-spirits who universally make offerings to all Buddhas for the sake of sentient beings,
and the various foot-following spirits who have long since made firm vows to always follow him.
The Earth Goddess named Delighting in Hearing the Sublime Dharma; the Water Goddess named Constantly Cultivating Great Compassion;
the Fire Goddess named Radiance of Wisdom-Light; the Wind Goddess named Diadem of Maṇi-Jewels; the Directional Goddess named Thoroughly Proficient in All Rituals of the Ten Directions;
the Night Goddess named Diligently Devoted to Eradicating the Darkness of Ignorance; and the One Whose Mind is Single-minded and Untiring.
The Lord of Day Deities who illuminate the sun of the Buddha; the Lord of Space Deities who adorn the entire realm of phenomena and all of space;
the Lord of Ocean Deities who universally deliver sentient beings across the ocean of existence;

the Lord of Mountain Deities whose great and lofty roots of goodness for accumulating the aids to the path toward omniscience are like mountains; and those who constantly and diligently protect all sentient beings.
The City Lord of the Citadel of Bodhicitta; the Great Nāga Kings who constantly and diligently protect the unsurpassed Dharma-citadel of the wisdom of omniscience;
the Yakṣa Kings who constantly and diligently protect all sentient beings; the Gandharva King who constantly causes the joy of all sentient beings to increase;
and the [Kumbhāṇḍa] King who constantly and diligently eliminates the realm of hungry ghosts.
The Bhāṇḍa King constantly vows to deliver all sentient beings from the ocean of existence;
the Garuḍa King vows to achieve the bodies of all Tathāgatas that transcend the world; the Asura King, upon seeing the Buddha, rejoices and bows with reverence;
and the Mahoraga King is ever weary of birth and death and constantly delights in beholding the Buddha.
The Great Heavenly Kings, honoring the Buddha, praised and made offerings to the Great Brahma Kings.

Mañjuśrī, together with a multitude of bodhisattvas adorned with such merits, emerged from their respective abodes and proceeded to where the Buddha was. They circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right for immeasurable turns and presented various kinds of offerings with all manner of ritual implements.
Having completed the offerings, they took their leave and traveled south toward the human realm.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, saw the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī together with a vast assembly of bodhisattvas, magnificently adorned, departing from the Jeta Grove and traveling southward through the human realms.
He then thought to himself:
"I shall now go to the south together with Mañjuśrī."

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, surrounded by six thousand bhikṣus before and behind him, departed from his dwelling and went to where the Buddha was. He prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and reported everything in detail to the World-Honored One.
Having received the World-Honored One’s permission, he circumambulated him three times to the right, took his leave, and departed for the place where Mañjuśrī was.
These six thousand bhikṣus were those with whom Śāriputra himself had lived together; they had not long since gone forth into the homeless life, namely:

the bhikṣu Sāgarabuddhi, the bhikṣu Sujāta, the bhikṣu Puṇyaprabha, the bhikṣu Mahākumāra, the bhikṣu Vidyujjāta, the bhikṣu Viśuddhacārin, the bhikṣu Devaśrī, the bhikṣu Indramati, the bhikṣu Brahmajaya, and the bhikṣu Śāntamati...

There were six thousand such individuals, all of whom had previously made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, deeply planted roots of goodness, possessed vast power of understanding, and had clear and penetrating eyes of faith. Their minds were broad and expansive; they contemplated the realm of the Buddhas, realized the fundamental nature of all phenomena, and brought great benefit to sentient beings. They constantly delighted in diligently seeking the merits of all Buddhas—all of these were accomplished through the teaching and transformation by Mañjuśrī.
At that time, while walking along the path, the Venerable Śāriputra observed the bhikṣus and said to Sāgarabuddhi:
"Sāgarabuddhi! You should observe the pure body of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, which no devas or humans can conceive."
You should observe how Mañjuśrī’s halo shines with penetrating brilliance, causing immeasurable sentient beings to give rise to a heart of joy.
You should observe how Mañjuśrī is adorned by a net of light, extinguishing the immeasurable sufferings and afflictions of sentient beings.
You should observe that this assembly of Mañjuśrī is complete, for they are all sustained by the roots of goodness cultivated by bodhisattvas in the past.
You should observe the path traversed by Mañjuśrī; eight paces to his left and right, it is level and magnificently adorned.
You should observe the place where Mañjuśrī dwells; throughout the ten directions, a site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) constantly follows him as he moves.

You should observe the path upon which Mañjuśrī travels; it is fully adorned with immeasurable merit, and on both its left and right sides, great hidden treasuries exist from which all kinds of rare jewels spontaneously emerge.
You should observe how, as a result of the roots of goodness from Mañjuśrī’s past offerings to the Buddhas, treasuries of adornments emerge from among all the trees.
You should observe how Mañjuśrī causes the lords of the world to rain down clouds of offering articles, prostrating and paying homage as an act of worship.
