You should observe Mañjuśrī: whenever all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions are about to preach the Dharma, they all emit light from the white tuft between their eyebrows, which comes to illuminate his body and enters through the crown of his head.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra extolled, praised, revealed, and expounded upon how the youth Mañjuśrī was thus adorned with such immeasurable qualities.

When those bhikṣus heard this teaching, their minds became pure, their faith and understanding firm, and they were so overcome with joy that they could not contain themselves. Their bodies leaped for joy; their physical forms became supple, their faculties were delighted, and all their sorrows and sufferings were eliminated. All defilements and obstructions were utterly exhausted; they constantly beheld the Buddhas, sought the True Dharma deeply, and were endowed with the faculties of a bodhisattva. They attained the power of a bodhisattva, and great compassion and great vows arose spontaneously within them. They entered the profound realm of the various perfections (*pāramitās*), and the oceans of Buddhas of the ten directions were ever present before them.

Developing deep faith and delight in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), they addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: "We pray only that the Great Master will lead us to the presence of that Supreme Person."
Then Śāriputra immediately went with him; having arrived at that place, he said:
"Virtuous one! These bhikṣus wish to have an audience with you."
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, surrounded by immeasurable sovereign bodhisattvas and his great assembly, turned to look at the bhikṣus like an elephant king.
Then, the bhikṣus prostrated at his feet, joined their palms in reverence, and spoke these words:
"We now pay homage, offer respectful worship, and dedicate all other roots of goodness we possess."
I pray that the benevolent Mañjuśrī, the preceptor Śāriputra, and the World-Honored One Śākyamuni will all bear witness!
Just as you possess such a physical body, such a voice, such marks and signs of excellence, and such sovereign mastery, may I likewise attain them all in their entirety.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī addressed the bhikṣus, saying: "Bhikṣus!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family accomplishes the ten ways of approaching the Mahāyāna, they will be able to swiftly enter the stage of the Tathāgata, let alone the stages of a bodhisattva!"
What are these ten? They are as follows:
accumulating all roots of goodness with a mind free from weariness or fatigue.
Seeing all buddhas, they serve and make offerings to them with a mind free from weariness.
Seeking all buddha-dharmas, their minds are free from weariness.
Practicing all pāramitās, their minds are free from weariness.
They accomplish all bodhisattva samādhis with a mind free from weariness.
They enter sequentially into all three periods of time with a mind free from weariness.
They universally adorn and purify the buddha-fields of the ten directions with a mind free from weariness.
They teach and discipline all sentient beings with hearts free from weariness or fatigue.
Throughout all lands and throughout all eons, they accomplish the practices of a bodhisattva with hearts free from weariness or fatigue.
For the sake of maturing a single sentient being, they practice as many perfections as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields, thereby accomplishing the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
proceeding in this manner, for the sake of maturing the entire realm of sentient beings, they accomplish all the powers of a Tathāgata without their minds ever becoming weary or exhausted.

“Bhikṣus! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family accomplishes deep faith and gives rise to these ten kinds of tireless minds, they will be able to nurture all roots of goodness, abandon all realms of birth and death, transcend all worldly lineages, avoid falling into the stages of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, be born into the family of all Tathāgatas, fulfill all Bodhisattva vows, study all the merits of the Tathāgatas, practice all the various conducts of Bodhisattvas, attain the powers of the Tathāgata, subdue all Māras and heterodox teachers, eliminate all afflictions, enter the stages of Bodhisattvas, and draw near to the stage of the Tathāgata.”
At that time, having heard this Dharma, the bhikṣus attained a samādhi called "Unobstructed Eye Seeing the Realm of All Buddhas.

Because they had attained this samādhi, they saw all the Tathāgatas, Buddhas, in the infinite and boundless worlds of the ten directions, as well as all their respective sites of enlightenment and their assemblies.
They also see all sentient beings in every realm of existence throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
they also see all the various distinctions among those worlds;
and they also see every single atom within all those worlds.
Furthermore, they clearly see all the palaces where sentient beings dwell within those worlds, adorned with various kinds of jewels;
they also hear the diverse voices of those Buddhas and Tathāgatas as they expound the Dharma through various phrases and explanations, understanding them all completely;
and they are also able to observe the faculties, minds, and desires of all sentient beings within those worlds.
They are also able to recollect the ten prior and subsequent births of all sentient beings in that world;
they are also able to recollect the events of ten eons of the past and ten eons of the future in that world;

and they are also able to recollect the ten accounts of past lives, the ten attainments of perfect enlightenment, the ten turnings of the wheel of Dharma, the ten kinds of supernormal powers, the ten kinds of preaching the Dharma, the ten kinds of instruction, and the ten kinds of eloquence of those Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, they accomplish ten thousand bodhicittas, ten thousand samādhis, and ten thousand pāramitās, all of which are completely pure;
they attain the perfect radiance of great wisdom and obtain the ten supernormal powers of a bodhisattva—supple and subtle—and abide in the bodhicitta, firm and immovable.
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva exhorted the bhikṣus to abide in the conduct of Samantabhadra;
having abided in the conduct of Samantabhadra, they entered the ocean of great vows;
having entered the ocean of great vows, they fulfilled the ocean of great vows.
Because they have accomplished the ocean of great vows, their minds are pure;
because their minds are pure, their bodies are pure;
because their bodies are pure, their bodies are light and agile.
Because his body is pure and light, he attains great supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) from which there is no regression;

having attained these supernormal powers, he never leaves the presence of Mañjuśrī’s feet, yet manifests his body before all Buddhas throughout the ten directions, fully accomplishing all Buddha-dharmas.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Sixty-one;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Sixty-two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
Entering the Dharma Realm, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Three.

At that time, after Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva had exhorted the bhikṣus to resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he traveled south by stages through the human realms until he reached the eastern side of the City of Blessings. There he stayed within the Śāla Grove of the Banner of Adornment, at the site of a great stūpa where former Buddhas had once resided to teach and transform sentient beings; it was also a place where, in the past, the World-Honored One had practiced the bodhisattva path and was able to relinquish that which is most difficult to give up.

Therefore, the fame of this grove is heard throughout immeasurable Buddha-fields; it is constantly honored by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.

At that time, when Mañjuśrī and his retinue had arrived at this place, he immediately preached the Sūtra of the Universal Illumination of the Dharma Realm right there, with one hundred trillion nayutas of sūtras as its retinue.
While this sutra was being preached, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nāgas from the great ocean came to that place;
having heard this Dharma, they felt profound revulsion for the nāga realm and sincerely sought the Buddha-way, all of them casting off their nāga bodies to be reborn among devas and humans.
Ten thousand nāgas attained non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
furthermore, immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings were each brought to spiritual discipline within the three vehicles.

At that time, when the people of the City of Blessings heard that the youth Mañjuśrī was at the great stupa in the Śāla Grove of the Banner of Adornment, a vast multitude emerged from the city and went to where he was.
At that time, there was an upāsaka named Mahāmati, who, together with a retinue of five hundred upāsakas— namely, the upāsaka Sudatta, the upāsaka Vasudatta, the upāsaka Puṇyaprabha,

the upāsaka Yaśasvin, the upāsaka Dattayaśas, the upāsaka Candravatsa, the upāsaka Sumati, the upāsaka Mahāmati, the upāsaka Bhadrapāla, and the upāsaka Bhadraśreṣṭhin— and five hundred such upāsakas, approached the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was. They prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side.
Furthermore, there were five hundred upāsikās, namely:

the upāsikā Mahāmati, the upāsikā Suprabhā, the upāsikā Surūpā, the upāsikā Ruciragātrā, the upāsikā Bhadrā, the upāsikā Bhadraguṇā, the upāsikā Bhadraprabhā, the upāsikā Dhvajaprabhā, the upāsikā Guṇaprabhā, and the upāsikā Sunetrā... these and other such five hundred upāsikās approached the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side.
Furthermore, there were five hundred youths, namely:

the youth Sudhana, the youth Sucarita, the youth Susīla, the youth Suvinaya, the youth Suvikrama, the youth Sucintita, the youth Sumati, the youth Sambodhi, the youth Sunetra, the youth Subāhu, the youth Suprabha... these and other such five hundred youths approached the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit to one side.
Furthermore, there were five hundred maidens, namely:

the maiden Bhadrikā, the daughter of the householder Mahāprajña, the maiden Yaśodharā, the maiden Surūpā, the maiden Dṛḍhamati, the maiden Kalyāṇaguṇā, the maiden Guṇavatī, the maiden Brahmadattā, the maiden Guṇaprabhā, and the maiden Suprabhā... these and others, numbering five hundred maidens, came to the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side.

At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, knowing that the people of Puṇyavatī had all gathered, manifested a body of sovereign mastery according to their inclinations; his majestic radiance blazed forth, eclipsing the entire assembly.

Through sovereign great kindness, he brought them refreshing coolness; through sovereign great compassion, he gave rise to the intention to preach the Dharma; through sovereign wisdom, he understood their inclinations; and with vast eloquence, he was about to preach the Dharma for them.
Furthermore, at that time, he observed for what causes and conditions the youth Sudhana had received his name.

He knew that when this boy first entered the womb, seven jeweled pavilions spontaneously appeared within his house; beneath these pavilions were seven hidden treasuries, and upon these treasuries, the earth itself split open to produce sprouts of the seven precious substances—namely:
gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, pearl, musaragalva, and agate.
The youth Sudhana remained in the womb for ten months before being born, his physical form and limbs perfectly proportioned and complete.
Then, seven great treasuries—each measuring seven cubits in length, breadth, and height—emerged from the earth, radiating brilliant light.
Furthermore, within the house there spontaneously appeared five hundred precious vessels, naturally filled to the brim with all kinds of objects. Namely:

In adamantine vessels were placed all manner of incenses; in incense vessels were placed various garments; in vessels of beautiful jade were filled with various superior flavors of food and drink; in maṇi vessels were filled with various extraordinary and rare jewels. Silver was placed in gold vessels, and gold was placed in silver vessels; in vessels of gold and silver were filled with lapis lazuli and maṇi jewels; crystal vessels were filled with giant clam shells (*śaṅkha*); giant clam shell vessels were filled with crystal; agate vessels were filled with pearls; pearl vessels were filled with agate; fire-maṇi vessels were filled with water-maṇi, and water-maṇi vessels were filled with fire-maṇi...
In this manner, five hundred such precious vessels appeared spontaneously.
Furthermore, a rain of various jewels and all kinds of wealth fell, causing all storehouses to be completely filled.
For these reasons, his parents, relatives, and skilled physiognomists together named this boy Sudhana.

Furthermore, it was known that this youth had already made offerings to the Buddhas of the past, deeply planted roots of goodness, possessed vast faith and understanding, and always delighted in drawing near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). His actions of body, speech, and mind were entirely free from fault; he purified the bodhisattva path, sought omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and became a vessel for the Buddha-dharma. His mind was as pure as space, and he directed his merit toward enlightenment (*bodhi*) without any obstruction.
At that time, after Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva had thus observed the youth Sudhana, he comforted and exhorted him, and expounded for him all the Buddha-dharmas.

That is to say: teaching the dharma of the accumulation of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the continuity of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the succession of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the purity of the assemblies of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the turning of the wheel of Dharma and the guidance of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the physical marks and minor signs of the form bodies of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the accomplishment of the Dharma bodies of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the eloquence and speech of all Buddhas; teaching the dharma of the radiance and illumination of all Buddhas; and teaching the dharma of the equality and non-duality of all Buddhas.

At that time, after the youth Mañjuśrī had taught this Dharma to the youth Sudhana and the great assembly, he earnestly exhorted them, increased their spiritual power, and inspired them with joy, causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and to recollect their past roots of goodness.
Having performed these deeds, he then preached the Dharma to sentient beings at that very spot according to their needs, and subsequently departed.
At that time, having heard from Mañjuśrī such various merits of the Buddha, the youth Sudhana single-mindedly and diligently sought anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Following Mañjuśrī, he spoke in verse:
"The three realms of existence are its city walls; Pride and arrogance are its ramparts;
The various destinies are its gates; The waters of craving are its moats."
Enveloped by the darkness of ignorance, with the fires of greed and hatred blazing fiercely,
the King of Māra acts as their sovereign, and the childish rely upon him for their dwelling.
Greed and craving serve as their fetters, while flattery and deception serve as their reins.
Doubt obscures their eyes, leading them to enter various wrong paths.
Due to stinginess, envy, and arrogance, they enter the three evil realms or fall among the various destinies,
subject to the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death.
The sun of pure wondrous wisdom, The wheel of perfect great compassion,
Able to dry up the ocean of afflictions— I pray you, grant me a moment of your observation!
The moon of pure wondrous wisdom, The stainless wheel of great loving-kindness,
Bestowing peace upon all, may you deign to look upon me with compassion!
Sovereign of the entire Dharma-realm, with the Jewel of the Dharma as your guide,
traveling through space without hindrance, may you deign to instruct me!
Great caravan leader of merit and wisdom, Bravely seeking bodhi for the universal benefit of all sentient beings, I pray that you will graciously protect me!
Clad in the armor of patience, Holding the sword of wisdom in hand.
Mastery over the hosts of Māra, may you deign to deliver me!
Abiding on the peak of the Sumeru of Dharma, with the daughters of Samādhi ever in reverent attendance,
Having destroyed the asuras of delusion, O Śakra, may you look upon me!
The three realms of existence are the abode of the ignorant and foolish; they are the cause for the lands and destinies of delusion and karma.
You, O Benevolent One, have fully subdued them all, showing me the Way like a lamp!
You have abandoned all evil destinies and purified all virtuous paths.
O You who transcend all worlds, show me the gate of liberation!
The world clings to inverted views, conceiving of permanence, pleasure, self, and purity;
With the eye of wisdom, You are able to leave them all behind—open for me the gate of liberation!
Well-knowing the paths of error and correctness, with a discerning mind free from fear;
you who have attained complete certainty—show me the path to Bodhi!
Abiding on the ground of the Buddha’s right view, grow the tree of the Buddha’s merit!
Rain down the Buddha’s sublime Lotus Dharma, and show me the path to bodhi!
The Buddhas of the past, future, and present pervade every place;
Like the sun rising in the world, speak of that path for my sake!
Well-knowing all karmas, deeply penetrating the practices of all vehicles;
O person of certain wisdom, show me the Mahāyāna!
May the wheel of vows have great compassion as its hub, faith as its axle, and firm endurance as its linchpin.
Adorned with the jewels of merit, may it carry me in this vehicle!
With the vast casket of dhāraṇī, the canopy adorned with compassion,
and the bells of eloquence ringing out, may it carry me in this vehicle!
Brahmacarya is the mattress, samādhi the handmaidens;
the Dharma drum resounds with wondrous tones—may you grant me this vehicle!
The four means of integration are inexhaustible treasuries, and merit is the jewel of adornment.
May shame and remorse serve as its harness and bridle; I pray you grant me this vehicle!
May it constantly turn the wheel of giving, Perpetually anointed with the fragrance of pure precepts, And firmly adorned with patience; May I be made to mount this vehicle!
The samādhi of dhyāna is the box, wisdom and skillful means are the yoke;
may you subdue me so that I do not regress, and cause me to mount this vehicle!
With the pure wheel of great vows and the firm power of dhāraṇī,
Accomplished through wisdom, may it carry me upon this vehicle!
With universal conduct as its protective rim and a compassionate heart as its gentle turning,
moving everywhere without fear— may it carry me upon this vehicle!
Firm as a vajra, skillful like an illusion,
Unobstructed in all things— may I be carried by this vehicle!
Vast and utterly pure, it brings universal happiness to all sentient beings.
May space, the dharma-realm, and so forth, cause me to mount this vehicle!
May it purify the wheel of karmic afflictions, sever the suffering of saṃsāra,
and destroy Māras and non-Buddhists— may it cause me to mount this vehicle!
Wisdom fills the ten directions, its adornments pervading the entire Dharma-realm;
it universally moistens all classes of sentient beings—may I mount this vehicle!
Pure as empty space, it utterly eliminates craving and views.
Benefiting all sentient beings, may you cause me to mount this vehicle!
May the power of your vows proceed with swift speed, and may your mind abide in stable tranquility;
universally transporting all conscious beings, may you cause me to mount this vehicle!
As the earth does not waver, And as water universally benefits all, So may you transport sentient beings; May I be enabled to mount this vehicle!
The wheel of the four means of integration, The pure light of dhāraṇī;
O Sun of Wisdom, I pray you show me so that I may see!
Having entered the city of the Dharma King, having donned the crown of the Wisdom King,
and having bound the silken ribbon of the Sublime Dharma, I pray you look upon me with compassion!
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva turned like an elephant king, gazed at Sudhana, and spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent!

"Good son! You have already resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and you further desire to draw near to various spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) to inquire about the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."

"Good son! To draw near to and make offerings to spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) is the primary causal condition for possessing all-knowledge (sarvajñatā); therefore, do not give rise to weariness or aversion toward this."
Sudhana said: "I pray that the Noble One will explain to me in detail: how should a bodhisattva study the bodhisattva conduct?
How should a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva conduct?"
How should one proceed toward the bodhisattva practice?
How should one engage in the bodhisattva practice?
How should one purify the bodhisattva practice?
How should one enter the bodhisattva practice?
How should one accomplish the bodhisattva practice?
How should one accord with the bodhisattva practice?
How should one recollect the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one expand and broaden the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one cause the conduct of Samantabhadra to be swiftly brought to full completion?
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva spoke these verses to the youth Sudhana:
“Excellent, treasury of merit! That you have come to my presence, Having given rise to a heart of great compassion, And diligently seeking unsurpassed enlightenment.”
Having already made vast vows to eliminate the suffering of sentient beings,
you practice the bodhisattva path for the sake of all worlds.
If there are bodhisattvas who do not weary of the sufferings of birth and death,
Thus you shall fulfill the path of Samantabhadra, Which none can ever destroy.
With the light of merit, the power of merit, The abode of merit, and the pure ocean of merit;
For the sake of all sentient beings, May you vow to cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra.
You behold the boundless limits, hearing the Dharma from all the Buddhas of the ten directions, receiving and upholding it without forgetfulness.
Throughout the realms of the ten directions, you universally see immeasurable Buddhas.
Accomplishing the ocean of all vows, Fulfilling the bodhisattva practices;
If one enters the ocean of skillful means And abides securely in the Buddha’s enlightenment,
Able to follow and learn from the Teacher, One shall attain all-knowledge.
Pervading all lands throughout kalpas as numerous as atoms,
you practice the conduct of Samantabhadra and accomplish the path to enlightenment.
Throughout immeasurable lands and oceans of boundless kalpas, you...
Practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra, you have fulfilled all great vows.
These immeasurable sentient beings, hearing of your vows, rejoice;
they all resolve upon Bodhi and vow to study the vehicle of Samantabhadra.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī had spoken these verses, he addressed the youth Sudhana,
saying: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
"You have already resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and seek the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Good son! If there are sentient beings who can resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, this matter is difficult."
Once one has been able to resolve the mind [of enlightenment], seeking the bodhisattva practices is even more difficult. "Good son!
If you wish to accomplish the wisdom of all wisdoms, you should resolutely seek a true spiritual friend."

"Good son! In seeking a spiritual friend, do not give rise to weariness or indolence; upon seeing a spiritual friend, do not give rise to complacency or satiety; you should comply with all the instructions of the spiritual friend, and regarding the skillful means of the spiritual friend, do not perceive any faults."
“Good son! To the south of here, there is a land named Supreme Bliss;”
In that land there is a mountain named Wondrous Peak;
upon that mountain there is a bhikṣu named:
"Dechen, you should go and ask:
How does a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
"How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva practices?
And how does a bodhisattva swiftly attain the full perfection of the practices of Samantabhadra?
The bhikṣu Meghaśrī shall explain this for you."

At that time, having heard these words, the youth Sudhana leaped for joy; he prostrated himself at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and wept with tears streaming down his face.

Taking his leave, he traveled south toward the land of Saṃbhava. Ascending Mount Sumeru, he surveyed the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below, searching everywhere out of longing and yearning to behold the bhikṣu Meghaśrī.
After seven days had passed, he saw that bhikṣu walking slowly in a meditative circuit on a separate mountain.
Having seen him, he approached, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, stood before him, and spoke these words:
"Noble One!..."
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva practice.
Up to: "How should one swiftly bring the practices of Samantabhadra to full completion?
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I only pray that you will look upon me with compassion and explain for my sake:
how does a bodhisattva achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?"
Then, the bhikṣu Meghaśrī said to Sudhana:
“Excellent, excellent, noble son!
You have already been able to resolve your mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and you are further able to inquire about the practices of all bodhisattvas.
Such a matter is the most difficult among difficulties.

That is to say: seeking the bodhisattva practice; seeking the bodhisattva realm; seeking the bodhisattva path of transcendence; seeking the bodhisattva path of purity; seeking the bodhisattva’s pure and vast mind; seeking the bodhisattva’s accomplishment of supernormal powers; seeking the bodhisattva’s manifestation of the gates of liberation; seeking the bodhisattva’s manifestation of the activities performed in the world; seeking the bodhisattva’s accordance with the minds of sentient beings; seeking the bodhisattva’s gates of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa; and seeking the bodhisattva’s observation of the conditioned and the unconditioned with a mind free from attachment.

“Good son! I have attained the power of sovereign and definitive understanding; my eye of faith is pure, and the light of wisdom shines radiantly. I universally contemplate all realms, free from all obstructions, skillfully observing with a universally penetrating clarity. Possessing pure conduct, I travel to all lands throughout the ten directions to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas, constantly mindfulness of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, upholding the true Dharma of all Buddhas, and constantly beholding all Buddhas of the ten directions.”
That is to say: seeing one Buddha, two Buddhas, ten Buddhas, a hundred Buddhas, a thousand Buddhas, a hundred thousand Buddhas,
a billion Buddhas, ten billion Buddhas, a hundred billion Buddhas, a trillion Buddhas, a nayuta of Buddhas in the eastern direction;
From ten billion Buddhas, a hundred nayuta-koṭis of Buddhas, a thousand nayuta-koṭis of Buddhas,
a hundred thousand nayuta-koṭis of Buddhas, up to seeing those who are innumerable,
immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, and unquantifiable—
He speaks of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas, up to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in four continents,
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a thousand-world system, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a two-thousand-world system,
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a three-thousand-world system, and Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field.
Buddhas, even as many Buddhas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
as it is in the eastern direction, so it is in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.

Within each and every direction, all the Buddhas—possessing various physical marks, various appearances, various supernormal powers, various playful manifestations, various assemblies adorning their sites of enlightenment, various radiances shining boundlessly, various lands, and various lifespans—manifest various gateways to the attainment of perfect enlightenment according to the diverse inclinations of sentient beings, and therein let out the lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

“Good son! I have only attained this ‘Dharma-door of Universally Seeing the Sphere of Wisdom and Light that Recollects All Buddhas. How could I possibly comprehend the boundless wisdom and pure practices of the great bodhisattvas?”
That is to say:

the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through the universal illumination of the light of wisdom, because one constantly perceives all the various palaces of all buddha-lands as entirely adorned and pure;

and the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha for the sake of all sentient beings, because according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, they are all caused to see the Buddha and attain purity.
The gate of mindfulness of the Buddha that causes one to dwell securely in power, because it causes entry into the ten powers of the Tathāgata;
the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha that causes one to dwell securely in the Dharma, because it allows one to see immeasurable Buddhas and hear the Dharma;
the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha that illuminates all directions, because it perceives the oceans of Buddhas throughout all worlds as entirely equal and without distinction.
The gate of mindfulness through entering the invisible realm, because one perceives all the sovereign spiritual powers and deeds of the Buddhas within every subtle environment;
the gate of mindfulness by abiding throughout all eons, because one constantly beholds the Tathāgata’s various activities throughout all kalpas without ever ceasing;
the gate of mindfulness by abiding in all times, because one constantly sees the Tathāgata at all times, drawing near and dwelling together with him without ever being parted.
They dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all lands, because they see the Buddha-body in all realms as transcending all things and being without equal;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all worlds, because they universally behold all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time according to the inclinations of their own minds;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all objects, because they see all Tathāgatas appearing in succession within all objective spheres.
They dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through quiescent extinction, because in a single thought-moment they see all Buddhas manifesting parinirvāṇa in all lands;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through remoteness, because in a single day they see all Buddhas departing from their respective abodes;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through vastness, because their minds constantly contemplate each and every Buddha-body pervading all dharma-realms.
They dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha as subtle, because they go to the presence of every Tathāgata appearing upon a single hair-tip to serve them;

they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha as adorned, because within a single thought-moment they see all lands where various Buddhas have attained perfect enlightenment and manifest spiritual transformations;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha as performing deeds, because they see all Buddhas appearing in the world, emitting the light of wisdom and turning the wheel of Dharma.
They dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through mastery of mind, for they know that all Buddhas manifest their forms according to the desires and inclinations within their own minds;

they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through their own karma, for they know that by manifesting reflections according to the karma accumulated by sentient beings, they cause them to awaken;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through spiritual transformations, for they see the vast lotus flowers upon which the Buddhas sit, blossoming throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Abiding in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha within the void, they observe the clouds of bodies of the Tathāgata that adorn the Dharma-realm and the realm of space.
How then could I know or describe their meritorious conduct?
“Good son! In the south there is a land named Sāgaradvāra;”
There is a bhikṣu there named Sāgaramegha. Go to him and ask:
"How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
The bhikṣu Sāgaramegha can explain in detail the causes and conditions for initiating vast roots of goodness."

"Good son! The bhikṣu Sāgaramegha shall cause you to enter the stage of vast assistance on the path; he shall cause you to give birth to the power of vast roots of goodness; he shall explain for you the causes for generating the bodhicitta; he shall cause you to give birth to the light of the vast vehicle; he shall cause you to cultivate the vast pāramitās; he shall cause you to enter the ocean of vast practices; he shall cause you to fulfill the wheel of vast vows; he shall cause you to purify the gate of vast adornments; and he shall cause you to give birth to the power of vast compassion."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the bhikṣu Meghaśrī, circumambulated him to the right while gazing upon him, and took his leave.

At that time, Sudhana reflected single-mindedly on the instructions of the spiritual friend; with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the light of wisdom, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the bodhisattva’s liberation, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the bodhisattva’s samādhi, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the bodhisattva’s great ocean, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the manifestation of all buddhas before one, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the locations of all buddhas, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the conduct of all buddhas, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of all buddhas being equal to the realm of empty space, with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the sequential appearance of all buddhas, and with right mindfulness he contemplated the gateway of the skillful means entered by all buddhas.

Traveling south by stages, he arrived at the country of Samudramukha, where he prostrated at the feet of the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha. Having circumambulated him to the right, he joined his palms before him and spoke these words:
"Noble One!..."

I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to enter the ocean of all unsurpassed wisdom; yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva is able to renounce the secular household and be born into the family of the Tathāgata.
How can one cross the ocean of birth and death and enter the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom?
How can one leave the stage of ordinary beings and enter the stage of the Tathāgata?
How can one sever the flow of birth and death and enter the flow of the Bodhisattva’s practice?
How can one shatter the wheel of birth and death and accomplish the wheel of the bodhisattva’s vows?
How can one extinguish the realm of Māra and manifest the realm of the Buddha?
How can one dry up the ocean of craving and desire and expand the ocean of great compassion?
How can one close the gates of the many difficulties and evil destinies, and open the gates of the heavens and nirvana?
How can one exit the city of the triple world and enter the city of all-knowledge?
"How can one renounce all objects of pleasure and enjoyment, using them entirely for the benefit of all sentient beings?
At that time, the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha said to Sudhana:
"O son of good family!
“Have you already resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
Sudhana replied, “Indeed!”
"I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Sāgaramegha said, "Noble son!"
If sentient beings do not plant roots of goodness, they cannot give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Only by attaining the light of universal roots of goodness, possessing the light of wisdom from the samādhi of the true path, producing various vast oceans of merit, increasing pure and white dharmas without weariness, serving spiritual friends without generating fatigue or aversion, disregarding body and life without hoarding anything, having a mind equal to the earth without high or low, being by nature always compassionate toward all sentient beings, focusing their thoughts exclusively on all realms of existence without abandoning them,
and constantly delighting in observing the realm of the Tathāgata— only through such means can they give rise to the bodhicitta.
"To generate the bodhicitta means:
to generate the mind of great compassion, for the sake of universally rescuing all sentient beings;..."
He generates the mind of great compassion, because he equally benefits all worlds;
he generates the mind of peace and happiness, because he causes all sentient beings to extinguish all sufferings;
he generates the mind of benefit, because he causes all sentient beings to depart from unwholesome dharmas.
They give rise to a mind of compassion, because they protect all who are afraid;
they give rise to an unimpeded mind, because they abandon all obstacles;
they give rise to a vast mind, because it pervades the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
They give rise to a boundless mind, for it reaches everywhere throughout the realm of empty space;
they give rise to a vast and expansive mind, for it perceives all Tathāgatas;
they give rise to a pure mind, for its wisdom regarding the phenomena of the three periods of time is never in conflict.
They give rise to the mind of wisdom, because they universally enter the ocean of all wisdom. "Good son!
I have dwelt in this country of Sāgaradvāra for twelve years, constantly taking the great ocean as my sphere of activity."

That is to say: contemplating that the great ocean is vast and immeasurable; contemplating that the great ocean is profoundly deep and difficult to fathom; contemplating that the great ocean becomes gradually deeper and wider; contemplating that the great ocean is wonderfully adorned with immeasurable and marvelous treasures; contemplating that the great ocean accumulates immeasurable waters; contemplating that the colors of the water in the great ocean are diverse and inconceivable; contemplating that the great ocean is the dwelling place of immeasurable sentient beings; contemplating that the great ocean accommodates sentient beings of various massive bodies; contemplating that the great ocean can receive the rain poured down by great clouds; and contemplating that the great ocean neither increases nor decreases.
“Good son! While I was reflecting, I further thought:
‘Within this world, is there perhaps any ocean more vast and expansive than this?’”
Are there any oceans that surpass this one in measurelessness?
Are there any oceans that surpass this one in profundity?
Are there any oceans that surpass this one in excellence?

"Good son! When I was reflecting in this way, beneath this sea, a great lotus flower suddenly appeared. It had a stem made of the invincible Indra-nīla jewel, a calyx of vaidūrya, leaves of Jāmbūnada gold, a pedestal of agallochum, and filaments of agate; it bloomed and spread wide, covering the entire great ocean."
A million asura kings grasped its stalk; a million nets adorned with mani-jewels covered it from above;
a million naga kings showered it with fragrant water; a million garuḍa kings held various necklaces and precious silk ribbons that hung down all around;
and a million rākṣasa kings gazed upon it with hearts of loving-kindness.
Upon examination, one million yakṣa kings paid homage with reverent prostrations; one million gandharva kings offered praise and worship with various kinds of music;

and one million celestial kings rained down all manner of heavenly flowers, heavenly garlands, heavenly incense, heavenly burning incense, heavenly unguents, heavenly powdered incense, and exquisite heavenly garments.
Banners, streamers, and canopies; a million Brahma kings prostrating with their heads in reverent worship; a million Śuddhāvāsa devas joining their palms in salutation;
a million wheel-turning monarchs each making offerings adorned with the seven treasures;
a million ocean deities appearing simultaneously to pay homage with respectful prostration; and a million flavor-radiant maṇi jewels whose light shines everywhere.
It was adorned with a million maṇi-jewels of pure merit; it possessed a million maṇi-jewels of universal light as its pure treasury; a million supreme maṇi-jewels radiated brilliant splendor;
a million maṇi-jewels of wondrous treasury shone boundlessly; and a million Jambū-dhvaja maṇi-jewels were arranged in succession.
The procession was adorned with a million indestructible, pure, and majestic *vajra-siṃha-maṇi* jewels;
a million vast and pure *sūryagarbha-maṇi* jewels; a million delightful *ramaṇīya-maṇi* jewels of various colors;
and a million *cintāmaṇi* wish-fulfilling jewels that radiated an inexhaustible brilliance.

This great lotus flower arises from the roots of goodness of the Tathāgata’s appearance in the world; all bodhisattvas give rise to faith and joy toward it. It manifests before everyone throughout the worlds of the ten directions; it is born from dharmas like illusions, born from dharmas like dreams, and born from pure karma. Adorned by the dharma-gate of non-contention, it enters the seal of the unconditioned and dwells in the gate of non-obstruction. Pervading all lands throughout the ten directions, it accords with the profound realm of all Buddhas; even if one were to praise its merits for hundreds of thousands of countless kalpas, they could never be exhausted.
"At that time, I saw upon that lotus a Tathāgata sitting in the full lotus posture, his body extending from there upward to the Peak of Existence (*bhavāgra*).

The precious lotus throne was inconceivable; the assembly at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) was inconceivable; the perfection of the primary marks was inconceivable; the fulfillment of the secondary characteristics was inconceivable; the miraculous transformations were inconceivable; the purity of physical form was inconceivable; the mark of the invisible crown of the head was inconceivable; the mark of the broad and long tongue was inconceivable; skillful speech was inconceivable; the perfect voice was inconceivable; boundless power was inconceivable; pure fearlessness was inconceivable; and vast eloquence was inconceivable."

Furthermore, one should reflect that the various practices cultivated by that Buddha in the past are inconceivable; his attainment of the Way with sovereign mastery is inconceivable; his proclamation of the Dharma with wondrous sounds is inconceivable; his universal manifestation of various adornments is inconceivable; the distinct differences perceived on his left and right according to those who behold him are inconceivable; and the fulfillment of all benefits for sentient beings is inconceivable.

"At that time, this Tathāgata extended his right hand and stroked the crown of my head, expounding for me the Dharma-gate of the Universal Eye. He revealed the realm of all Tathāgatas, manifested all the practices of Bodhisattvas, and elucidated the wondrous teachings of all Buddhas. All wheels of Dharma enter therein; it can purify all Buddha-lands, crush all heterodox and erroneous doctrines, extinguish all hosts of Māras, cause all sentient beings to give rise to joy, illumine the mental activities of all sentient beings, understand the various faculties of all sentient beings, and cause them all to attain awakening according to their minds."
"I have heard this Dharma-gate from that Tathāgata; I have received, upheld, recited, and contemplated it with mindfulness and observation.

Suppose there were someone who, using ink equal in volume to the great ocean and pens as numerous as the Mount Sumerus, were to write down this Universal Eye Dharma-gate—writing out a single gate within a single chapter, a single dharma within a single gate, a single meaning within a single dharma, and a single phrase within a single meaning—they would not be able to record even a small fraction of it, let alone the whole!

“Good son! For twelve hundred years at the place of that Buddha, I upheld this Dharma-gate of the Universal Eye. Day by day, through the light of the *dhāraṇī* of hearing and retaining, I received countless chapters;
through the light of the *dhāraṇī* of the gate of tranquility, I entered into countless chapters.”
By means of the light of the *Anantāvarta-dhāraṇī*, they universally enter into countless chapters;
by means of the light of the *Bhūmyanupraveśa-dhāraṇī*, they discern countless chapters;
by means of the light of the *Prabhāva-dhāraṇī*, they universally encompass countless chapters.
By means of the light of the Padmavyūha-dhāraṇī, they bring forth countless chapters;
by means of the light of the Viśuddhavāk-svara-dhāraṇī, they expound countless chapters;
by means of the light of the Gaganagañja-dhāraṇī, they reveal countless chapters.
By the radiance of the *Ratnakūṭa-dhāraṇī*, one expands and broadens countless categories;
by the radiance of the *Sāgaragarbha-dhāraṇī*, one analyzes and distinguishes countless categories.

If there are sentient beings coming from the ten directions—whether they be devas or deva-kings, nāgas or nāga-kings, yakṣas or yakṣa-kings, gandharvas or gandharva-kings, asuras or asura-kings, garuḍas or garuḍa-kings, kiṃnaras or kiṃnara-kings, mahoragas or mahoraga-kings, humans or human kings, or Brahmās or Brahmā-kings—if all such beings come to my presence, I shall for their sake reveal, explain, extol, and praise [this teaching], causing them all to delight in, enter into, and abide securely within this Dharma-gate of the Universal Eye of the Radiance of the Practices of All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
“Good son! I know only this Universal Eye Dharma-door.
As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, they enter deeply into the ocean of all bodhisattva practices, practicing according to the power of their vows;”
They enter the ocean of great vows, because they abide in the world for immeasurable eons;
they enter the ocean of all sentient beings, because they extensively benefit them according to their inclinations;
they enter the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings, because they give rise to the light of unimpeded wisdom of the ten powers.
They enter the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings, in order to teach and transform them according to the proper time so that they are all brought to subjection;
they enter the ocean of all lands, in order to fulfill their original vows by adorning and purifying Buddha-fields;
they enter the ocean of all Buddhas, in order to vow to constantly make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
They enter the ocean of all dharmas, for they are able to awaken to and penetrate them all through wisdom;
they enter the ocean of all merits, for they practice each one until it is fully perfected;
they enter the ocean of the speech and languages of all sentient beings, for they turn the wheel of the true Dharma in all lands.
"How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct? 'Good son!
Sixty yojanas from here, traveling south along the road to Laṅkā, there is a village named..."
At the seashore, there was a bhikṣu named Supratiṣṭhita.
"Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva purify the bodhisattva conduct?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Sāgaramegha, circumambulated him to the right, gazed up at him with reverence, and took his leave to depart.

At that time, the youth Sudhana focused his mind exclusively on the instructions of the spiritual friends; he focused his mind exclusively on the Dharma-gate of the Universal Eye; he focused his mind exclusively on the Buddha’s spiritual power; he focused his mind exclusively on upholding the clouds of Dharma-phrases; he focused his mind exclusively on entering the gates of the ocean of Dharma; he focused his mind exclusively on contemplating the distinctions of the Dharma; he deeply entered the eddies of the Dharma; he universally entered the space of the Dharma; he purified the obscurations of the Dharma; and he observed the abodes of the Dharma-treasures.
Traveling south by stages, he arrived at the coastal village of Laṅkāmārga. Surveying the ten directions, he sought out Suvilīta.

There he saw this bhikṣu walking back and forth in mid-air; he was surrounded by countless devas who paid him homage, scattering celestial flowers and performing divine music. Innumerable banners, standards, and silken streamers filled the entire sky as offerings.
Furthermore, great nāga kings in the sky raised inconceivable clouds of agallochum incense, accompanied by thunder and flashing lightning, as offerings.
The King of the Kinnaras played various musical instruments, offering praise according to the Dharma as an act of worship;
the King of the Mahoragas, with inconceivably subtle and exquisite garments, spread them all around in mid-air, his heart filled with joy, as an act of worship;
the King of the Asuras raised clouds of inconceivable mani-jewels, adorned with immeasurable radiance and diverse ornaments, filling the entirety of space as an act of worship.

The Garuḍa kings appeared in the form of youths, surrounded by immeasurable celestial maidens; having fully accomplished a mind free from the intent to harm, they joined their palms in the air to make offerings.

Inconceivable numbers of rākṣasa kings, surrounded by immeasurable rākṣasas, possessed bodies of immense size that were most terrifying; yet, seeing the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita’s mastery over a heart of compassion, they bowed their bodies, joined their palms, and gazed up at him in worship.
Inconceivable numbers of yakṣa kings, each surrounded by their own respective hosts, stood on all four sides, reverently guarding him.
Inconceivable numbers of Brahma kings, bowing their bodies with palms joined in the midst of the void, extolled and praised him according to human conventions;
inconceivable numbers of Śuddhāvāsa devas, together with their palaces in the midst of the void, reverently joined their palms and made great vows.
At that time, having witnessed these events, the youth Sudhana felt great joy; he joined his palms in reverent salutation and spoke these words:
"Noble One!..."
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva practices the Buddha-dharma,
nor how they accumulate the Buddha-dharma.
How does one become fully endowed with the Buddha-dharma?
How does one cultivate the Buddha-dharma through perfuming?
How does one cause the Buddha-dharma to increase?
What is the comprehensive inclusion of the Buddha-dharma?
What is the ultimate fulfillment of the Buddha-dharma?
What is the purification of the Buddha-dharma?
What is the profound and pure Buddha-dharma?
What is the thorough penetration of the Buddha-dharma?
I have heard that the Noble One is skilled in providing instruction; I only pray that you will take pity on me and explain it for my sake.
How does a bodhisattva not forsake the vision of the Buddha, but instead constantly and diligently practice in his presence?
How does a bodhisattva not forsake other bodhisattvas, but share the same roots of goodness as all bodhisattvas?
How does a bodhisattva not abandon the Buddha-dharma, but instead attain clear realization through wisdom?
How does a bodhisattva not abandon their great vows, yet universally benefit all sentient beings?
How does a bodhisattva not abandon the various practices, dwelling through all kalpas with a mind free from weariness?
How does a bodhisattva not abandon buddha-fields, being universally able to adorn and purify all worlds?
How does a bodhisattva not abandon the power of the Buddha, yet is able to fully know and see the sovereign mastery of the Tathāgata?

How does a bodhisattva not abandon the conditioned (*saṃskṛta*), yet likewise does not abide therein, appearing throughout all realms of existence like a magical transformation, manifesting the undergoing of birth and death while cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva?
How does a bodhisattva not abandon hearing the Dharma, so as to be able to fully receive and uphold the true teachings of all Buddhas?
How does a bodhisattva not abandon the light of wisdom, so as to universally enter the sphere of activity of the wisdom of the three periods of time?
At that time, the bhikṣu Susthita said to Sudhana:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son!"

You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; now you further resolve to seek and inquire about the Buddha-dharma, the dharma of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and the dharma of self-existence (*svayambhū*).

“Good son! I have already accomplished the bodhisattva liberation door of non-obstruction. Whether coming or going, whether walking or standing still, as I contemplate in accordance with reality, practice, and observation, I immediately attain the light of wisdom called ‘Ultimate Non-obstruction.’”
Because they have attained this light of wisdom, they know the mental activities of all sentient beings without obstruction;
they know the deaths and births of all sentient beings without obstruction; they know the past lives of all sentient beings without obstruction;
they know the events of future kalpas of all sentient beings without obstruction; they know one...

They are unimpeded regarding the present affairs of all sentient beings; they are unimpeded in knowing the various distinctions of the languages and sounds of all sentient beings; they are unimpeded in resolving all the doubts of all sentient beings;
they are unimpeded in knowing the faculties of all sentient beings; and they act in accordance with all sentient beings...
When beings are ready to be transformed, they are able to go to them all without any hindrance;
they know all moments (*kṣaṇa*), instants (*lava*), and hours (*muhūrta*), as well as the divisions of day and night, without any hindrance;
they know the sequential flow of the ocean of the three periods of time without any hindrance; and they are able to travel throughout all the ten directions with their bodies.
The Buddha-fields are without obstruction.
Why is this? Because they have attained the power of supernatural faculties that are non-abiding and unconditioned.

“Good son! Because I have attained this power of supernatural faculties, I may walk, stand, sit, or lie down in mid-air; I may become invisible or manifest; I may appear as a single body or as many bodies; I pass through walls as if through empty space;
and I sit cross-legged in the air, coming and going with ease like a bird.”
He enters the earth as if it were water and treads upon water as if it were solid ground; smoke and flames issue forth from every part of his body above and below, like a great mass of fire.
At times he causes the entire great earth to tremble; at times he touches the sun and moon with his hand; and at times he manifests his body reaching as high as the Brahma-palace.

Some manifest clouds of burning incense, some manifest clouds of jewel-flames, some manifest clouds of transformations, and some manifest clouds of light-nets; all are vast and expansive, completely covering the ten directions.

In a single thought-moment, they may pass beyond one world in the eastern direction, two worlds, a hundred worlds, a thousand worlds, a hundred thousand worlds, even up to immeasurable worlds, and even up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds;
or they may pass beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, or beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

In all those Buddha-lands, before the presence of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, they listen to the preaching of the Dharma; at each and every Buddha’s place, they manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-fields, and from each body, they rain down clouds of offerings as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-fields—namely:

clouds of all kinds of flowers, clouds of all kinds of incense, clouds of all kinds of garlands, clouds of all kinds of powdered incense, clouds of all kinds of ointment incense, clouds of all kinds of parasols, clouds of all kinds of robes, clouds of all kinds of banners, clouds of all kinds of pennants, and clouds of all kinds of canopies—using these clouds of all manner of bodies to make offerings.
Whatever has been proclaimed by each and every Tathāgata, I uphold it all;
whatever adornments exist in each and every land, I remember them all.
As it is in the eastern direction, so it is likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
In all such worlds, whatever sentient beings see my form shall all certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

I clearly perceive all sentient beings in those worlds; according to their size, their superior or inferior capacities, and their suffering or joy, I manifest in forms identical to theirs to teach and bring them to maturity.
"If there are sentient beings who draw near to me, I cause them all to dwell securely in this Dharma-gate.
Good son! I know only this unimpeded gate of liberation for universally and swiftly making offerings to all Buddhas and bringing sentient beings to maturity."

As for the bodhisattvas’ precepts of great compassion, the precepts of the perfections, the precepts of the Great Vehicle, the precepts corresponding to the bodhisattva path, the unobstructed precepts, the non-retrogressive precepts, the precepts of not abandoning the bodhicitta, the precepts that always take the Buddha-dharma as their object, the precepts of constant mental attention toward omniscience, the space-like precepts, the precepts that have no dependence on any world, the faultless precepts, the undiminished precepts, the unimpaired precepts, the unmixed precepts, the unturbid precepts,
the remorseless precepts, the pure precepts, the dust-free precepts, and the stainless precepts— how could I possibly know or describe such virtues?
"Good son! To the south from here there is a land named Darbhada, and a city named..."
He was sovereign;
among his followers was one named Megha.

How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him to the right while gazing up at him with reverence, and then took his leave and departed.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
The Fourth Part of the Thirty-ninth Chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded and correct mindfulness, entered deeply into the dharma-gate of the Light of Dharma. He focused his thoughts exclusively on the Buddha, never severing his connection to the Triple Gem. He praised the nature of detachment from desire, recollected how spiritual friends universally illumine the three periods of time, and remembered his great vows to universally rescue all sentient beings. He did not cling to conditioned phenomena, but thoroughly contemplated the self-nature of all dharmas, being able to adorn and purify all worlds, while his mind remained free from attachment within the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Traveling south by stages, he arrived at the city of Vaśavartin and sought out Megha.

There he saw the man in the midst of a marketplace, seated upon a lion throne for preaching the Dharma, surrounded by an assembly of ten thousand people, expounding the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of the Wheel-Syllable.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined before him, spoke these words: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how one should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
How does one circulate through the various realms of existence while never forgetting the bodhicitta?
How does one attain an equanimous mind that is firm and immovable?
How does one obtain a pure mind that cannot be thwarted or destroyed?
How does one give rise to the power of great compassion that is ever free from weariness?
How does one enter into dhāraṇīs so as to attain universal purity?
How does one generate the vast radiance of wisdom, becoming free from all obscurations of darkness regarding all phenomena?
How does one possess the power of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) and eloquence (*pratibhāna*) to decisively comprehend the treasury of all profound meanings?
How does one attain the power of right mindfulness (*samyaksmṛti*) to remember and uphold all the various wheels of Dharma (*dharmacakra*)?
How does one attain the power of pure rebirths, so as to universally expound all dharmas across all realms of existence?
How does one attain the power of wisdom, so as to be able to definitively discern the meaning of all dharmas?
At that time, Megha said to Sudhana:
"Noble son, have you already resolved to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
Sudhana said, “Yes! I have already set my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”

Megha immediately descended from his lion throne and prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground before Sudhana. He scattered gold and silver flowers, priceless jewels, and exquisite powdered sandalwood, as well as immeasurable varieties of garments over him. Furthermore, he scattered immeasurable kinds of incense, flowers, and various ritual offerings as an act of worship. Then, rising up, he praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
"O son of good family!
You are indeed able to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O son of good family!"
If there are those who can resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they shall not sever the lineage of all Buddhas;
they shall adorn and purify all Buddha-fields; they shall bring all sentient beings to maturity;
they shall thoroughly penetrate the nature of all phenomena; and they shall awaken to and understand the seeds of all karmic actions.
This constitutes the fulfillment of all practices; it constitutes the non-interruption of all great vows;
it constitutes the realization, according to reality, of the nature of detachment from craving; it enables the clear vision of the distinctions between the three periods of time;
it causes faith and understanding to become forever firm; it constitutes being sustained by all Tathāgatas; and it constitutes [the state of] all Buddhas.
When one recollects [the Buddha], one becomes equal to all bodhisattvas; one is praised and rejoiced in by all worthies and sages;
one is venerated and visited by all Brahma kings; one is offered worship by all celestial lords;
one is protected by all yakṣas; one is guarded by all rākṣasas; and one is... [one]... by all... [gods].
All the dragon kings will come forward to welcome him; all the kinnara kings will sing songs of praise for him;
all the lords of the world will extol him with joy; and he shall cause the entire realm of sentient beings to attain peace and security.

That is to say: causing them to abandon the evil realms; causing them to emerge from difficult circumstances; severing the root of all poverty; giving rise to the happiness of all devas and humans; encountering and drawing near to spiritual friends; hearing and upholding the vast Dharma; generating the bodhicitta; purifying the bodhicitta; illuminating the path of the bodhisattvas; entering the wisdom of the bodhisattvas; and abiding in the stages of the bodhisattvas.

“Good son! You should know that the deeds performed by a bodhisattva are exceedingly difficult; they are difficult to emerge from and difficult to encounter. It is even more difficult to behold a bodhisattva.
This is because the bodhisattva serves as a protector for all sentient beings, causing them to grow, develop, and reach fulfillment.”
To provide succor for all sentient beings by uprooting them from all suffering and hardship;
to serve as a place of reliance for all sentient beings by protecting the world;
and to act as a refuge for all sentient beings so that they may be freed from fear.
The Bodhisattva is like a wind-wheel, for he sustains all worlds and prevents them from falling into the evil destinies;
he is like the great earth, for he causes the roots of goodness in sentient beings to grow;
he is like the great ocean, for his merit is full and inexhaustible.
Like the pure sun, because the radiance of wisdom shines everywhere;
like Mount Sumeru, because the roots of goodness rise high above;
like the bright moon, because the light of knowledge appears.
He is like a valiant general, for he crushes and subdues the armies of Māra;
he is like a sovereign, for he attains mastery within the city of the Buddha-dharma;
he is like a fierce fire, for it utterly consumes the sentient beings' attachment to the self and to love.
Like a great cloud, because it pours down the rain of immeasurable sublime Dharma;
like seasonal rain, because it causes all sprouts of the roots of faith to grow;
like a helmsman, because it shows and guides to the ferry-crossings of the ocean of Dharma.
"Like a bridge, he enables others to cross the ocean of birth and death.
Having thus praised Sudhana and caused all the bodhisattvas to rejoice, Megha emitted various rays of light from his mouth, which universally illuminated the trichiliocosm.
Once the sentient beings therein had encountered this light, all the nāgas, devas, and others, up to the Brahmā heavens, came to the place where Megha was.
The Mahāsattva Megha then, through skillful means, revealed, expounded, analyzed, and explained for them the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of the Chapter on the Wheel of Syllables.
When those sentient beings had heard this Dharma, they all attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Megha then returned to his original seat and addressed Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!

I have attained the *Svaraghoṣa-dhāraṇī*, by which I am able to discern and understand all the languages of the devas within the trichiliocosm, as well as the languages of nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all the Brahmā deities.
"In this same way, throughout the trichiliocosm and across the countless worlds of the ten directions—even those that are unspeakably unspeakable—all are likewise thus. Good son!"
I know only this Dharma-gate of the Radiance of the Bodhisattva’s Wondrous Sound Dhāraṇī.

As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they are able to universally enter the ocean of the various perceptions of all sentient beings, the ocean of their various designations, the ocean of their various names and titles, and the ocean of their various languages; they are able to universally enter the ocean of expounding all profound and secret phrases of the Dharma, the ocean of expounding all ultimate phrases of the Dharma, the ocean of expounding how within a single object of focus there are the phrases of the objects of focus of all three periods of time, the ocean of expounding superior phrases of the Dharma, the ocean of expounding most superior phrases of the Dharma, the ocean of expounding differentiated phrases of the Dharma, and the ocean of expounding all differentiated phrases of the Dharma; they are able to universally enter the ocean of all worldly incantations and arts, the wheel of adornment of all sounds, and the limit of the wheels of all differentiated syllables.
How could I now possibly know or speak of such merits?
“Good son! From here, travel south; there is a village named Vanavāsin.
There is a householder there named Vimukta. Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva practice?
How does a bodhisattva accomplish the bodhisattva practice?
How does a bodhisattva gather the bodhisattva practice?
"How does a bodhisattva contemplate the conduct of a bodhisattva?

At that time, because of his spiritual friend, the youth Sudhana conceived a profound sense of reverence for the teachings of omniscience, planted deep roots of pure faith, and greatly increased his own merit.
He prostrated at Megha’s feet, weeping with tears streaming down his face; he circumambulated him countless times, gazing up at him with longing and devotion, and then took his leave and departed.

At that time, the youth Sudhana contemplated the gate of the light-adornment of the bodhisattvas’ unimpeded dharanis; he entered deeply into the ocean-gate of the bodhisattvas’ languages; he recollected the gate of the bodhisattvas’ subtle skillful means for knowing all sentient beings; he observed the gate of the bodhisattvas’ pure minds; he accomplished the gate of the bodhisattvas’ radiance of roots of goodness; he purified the gate of the bodhisattvas’ teaching and transforming of sentient beings; he clarified and sharpened the gate of the bodhisattvas’ wisdom for gathering in sentient beings; he made firm the gate of the bodhisattvas’ vast aspirations and joys; he sustained the gate of the bodhisattvas’ supreme aspirations and joys; he purified the gate of the bodhisattvas’ various modes of faith and understanding;
and he contemplated the gate of the bodhisattvas’ immeasurable virtuous minds; his vows were firm and steadfast, and his mind was free from weariness.
Adorned with the armor of all [virtuous] qualities, their diligent and profound resolve is irreversible, and they possess indestructible faith;
their minds are as firm as adamant and as invincible as Nārāyaṇa, such that none can destroy them;
they uphold the instructions of all spiritual friends and attain indestructible wisdom regarding all spheres of experience.
Universally pure in all gates, their conduct is unimpeded;
the light of their wisdom is perfected, universally illuminating all things;

they are fully endowed with the radiance of the dhāraṇīs of all stages, thoroughly understanding the various distinctions within the dharma-realm, being without dependence or abiding, equal and non-dual.
Inherently pure and universally adorned, they have attained ultimate perfection in all their activities; their wisdom is pure and free from all attachments;
they know the diverse phenomena of the ten directions with unobstructed intelligence;
and they travel to the various locations throughout the ten directions without their bodies ever becoming weary.
They attain clear understanding of the distinct karmas throughout the ten directions;
they perceive all Buddhas throughout the ten directions without exception;
and they penetrate deeply into the distinct times throughout the ten directions.
The pure and wondrous Dharma fills their minds; the illumination of the Samādhi of Universal Wisdom shines upon their minds; their hearts constantly and universally enter the realm of equanimity;
touched by the wisdom of the Tathāgatas, the stream of all-knowledge flows on without interruption; whether in body or mind, they are never separated from the Buddha-Dharma;
empowered by the spiritual strength of all Buddhas and illuminated by the light of all Tathāgatas.
Having fulfilled his great vow, he willed his body to pervade the entire network of all lands, and his body universally entered into the entirety of the dharma-realm.
Traveling by stages for twelve years, he arrived at the city of Vairambhya and searched everywhere for the elder Vimokṣaka.
Having seen him, he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground; rising up with palms joined, he said:
"Noble One! That I have now been able to meet with a spiritual friend is for me the attainment of vast and excellent benefit."

Why is this? Because a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) is difficult to see, difficult to hear of, difficult to appear before, difficult to serve, difficult to approach, difficult to receive as a guide, difficult to encounter, difficult to dwell with, difficult to please, and difficult to follow.
"I have now encountered this assembly and have attained a wholesome benefit. Noble One!
I have already previously resolved my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to serve all..."
For the sake of the Buddha; because of the desire to encounter all Buddhas, because of the desire to see all Buddhas, because of the desire to contemplate all Buddhas,
because of the desire to know all Buddhas, because of the desire to realize the equality of all Buddhas,
because of the desire to give rise to the great vows of all Buddhas, and because of the desire to fulfill all...
By virtue of the Buddha’s great vows, it is because he desires to be fully endowed with the light of all buddha-wisdom;
because he desires to accomplish all the various practices of all buddhas; because he desires to attain all the supernormal powers of all buddhas;
because he desires to be fully endowed with all the powers of all buddhas; because he desires to obtain all the fearlessnesses of all buddhas; because he desires to hear all...
Because of the Buddha-dharma; because they desire to receive all Buddha-dharmas; because they desire to uphold all Buddha-dharmas;
because they desire to understand all Buddha-dharmas; because they desire to protect all Buddha-dharmas;
because they desire to be of one body with the assembly of all bodhisattvas; because they desire to be of one body with all bodhisattvas...
Because their roots of goodness and so forth are without distinction, in order to fulfill all the perfections (*pāramitā*) of bodhisattvas,
in order to accomplish all the practices cultivated by bodhisattvas, in order to give birth to all the pure vows of bodhisattvas,
and in order to attain the treasury of the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas and bodhisattvas.
It is because they desire to obtain the great light of inexhaustible wisdom, the treasury of all bodhisattva dharmas;
because they desire to obtain the vast treasury of all bodhisattva samādhis; because they desire to accomplish the immeasurable and innumerable treasury of all bodhisattva supernormal powers;
and because they desire to teach and subdue beings by means of the treasury of great compassion.
It is because they cause all sentient beings to ultimately reach the furthest limit; because they wish to manifest the treasury of spiritual transformations;
because they wish to attain mastery over all treasuries of sovereignty through their own minds;
and because they wish to enter the treasury of purity, adorning it with all manner of marks.

“Noble One! I have now come before you with such a mind, such an intention, such a delight, such a desire, such a longing, such a reflection, such a reverence, such a means, such a culmination, and such humility.”

I have heard that the Noble One is well able to instruct and exhort the assembly of bodhisattvas; that he can, through skillful means, elucidate what has been attained, show them the path, provide them with a bridge, and grant them the Dharma-gates;

causing them to eliminate the obstacles of delusion, pull out the arrows of hesitation, cut the net of doubt, illuminate the dense forest of the mind, wash away the turbidity of mental defilements, make the mind pure white, cool the mind, rectify the mind’s crookedness, sever the mind from birth and death, cease unwholesome states of mind, and liberate the mind from attachments;

causing the mind to be liberated from points of attachment, moving the mind away from places of stained craving, enabling it to swiftly enter the realm of omniscience, and causing it to quickly reach the unsurpassed city of Dharma.

They cause them to abide in great compassion, to abide in great loving-kindness, to enter the bodhisattva practices, to cultivate the gates of samādhi, to enter the stage of realization, to contemplate the nature of phenomena, to increase their power, and to practice the path, so that their minds are equanimous toward all things.
I only pray that the Noble One will explain for me:
how should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
By practicing according to these instructions, may they quickly attain purity and quickly attain clarity!

At that time, by the power of his past roots of goodness, the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, and the power of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta’s mindfulness, the elder Vimukta immediately entered a bodhisattva samādhi-gate called the Boundless Revolving Dhāraṇī that Universally Encompasses All Buddha-fields.
Having entered this samādhi, one attains a purified body.

Within that body, there appear in each of the ten directions as many Buddhas as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields, along with their Buddha-lands, assemblies, sites of enlightenment, various radiances, and all manner of adornments. There also appear the supernatural transformations and miraculous powers practiced by those Buddhas in the past, as well as all their great vows, the factors conducive to the Path, the practices for transcendence, and their pure adornments. One also beholds the Buddhas attaining perfect enlightenment, turning the sublime Wheel of Dharma, and teaching and transforming sentient beings.
All of these appeared within his body without any obstruction;
their various forms and various sequences remained as they were, without being confused, namely:
various lands, various assemblies, various sites of enlightenment, and various adornments.

Within them, the various Buddhas manifest diverse supernatural powers, establish diverse vehicles and paths, and demonstrate diverse gateways of vows. In some worlds, they perform buddha-works while residing in the Tuṣita Heaven; in others, they perform buddha-works after passing away from the Tuṣita Heaven.

Likewise, some dwell in the womb, or are born, or reside in the palace, or renounce the world, or proceed to the site of enlightenment, or defeat the armies of Māra, or are reverently surrounded by devas and nāgas, or are entreated by the lords of the world to preach the Dharma, or turn the wheel of Dharma, or enter parinirvāṇa, or distribute their relics, or erect stupas and temples.
