Those Tathāgatas, amidst various assemblies, various worlds, various modes of rebirth,
various lineages, various desires and pleasures, various karmic actions, various languages, various faculties and natures,
and among all sentient beings with their various afflictions, latent tendencies, and habitual propensities— whether dwelling therein...
In subtle maṇḍalas, or in vast maṇḍalas, or in maṇḍalas measuring one yojana, or in maṇḍalas measuring ten yojanas,
or in maṇḍalas measuring as many yojanas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields—
by means of various supernormal powers and various modes of speech—
With various sounds, various Dharma-gates, various dhāraṇī-gates, and various doors of eloquence,
and by means of various oceans of noble truths and various fearless lion’s roars of a Great Teacher,
he speaks of the various roots of goodness and various recollections of all sentient beings, bestows various predictions of enlightenment upon bodhisattvas, and expounds—

Regarding the various teachings of all Buddhas, Sudhana was able to hear and receive every word spoken by those Tathāgatas; he also beheld the inconceivable samādhis and miraculous transformations of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the householder Vimokṣa arose from samādhi and addressed the youth Sudhana, saying:
"Good son! I have entered and emerged from the Tathāgata’s liberation door of unimpeded adornment."

“Good son! When I enter and emerge from this gate of liberation, I see in the eastern direction the world-system named Jāmbūnada-golden Radiance, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nāgeśvararāja is surrounded by an assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Vairocanagarbha as the foremost;

furthermore, I see in the southern direction the world-system named Swift Power, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samantagandha is surrounded by an assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Cittarāja as the foremost.”

Furthermore, he saw in the western direction the world of Fragrant Light, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sumerupradīparāja was surrounded by an assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Mind as the leader;

he also saw in the northern direction the world of Kāṣāyadhvaja, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Indestructible Vajra was surrounded by an assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Vajrapadavikrama as the leader;

and he also saw in the northeastern direction the world of All Supreme Jewels, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Non-apprehending Realm Eye was surrounded by an assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Non-apprehending Skillful Transformation as the leader.

Furthermore, in the southeast, he saw the world called Fragrant Flame Radiance, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Gandhapradīpa was surrounded by an assembly at his place of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Vajrajvālāprajñā as the leader;

furthermore, in the southwest, he saw the world called Wisdom Sun Universal Radiance, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmadhātucakraketu was surrounded by an assembly at his place of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Sarvanirmāṇaketudarśin as the leader;

furthermore, in the northwest, he saw the world called Universally Pure, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sarvabuddharatnottaraketu was surrounded by an assembly at his place of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Dharmadhvajendra as the leader.

Furthermore, I saw the Buddhas appearing in succession above in the world-system of Infinite Worlds: the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Boundless Wisdom Light Perfect Banner, surrounded by an assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Dharma-realm Gate Banner King as the leader;

and I also saw the Buddha below in the world of Radiance: the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Unobstructed Wisdom Banner, surrounded by an assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva All-World Realm Banner King as the leader.
“Good son! I see as many Tathāgatas in each of the ten directions as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
Those Tathāgatas do not come here, nor do I go to them.”
If I wish to see the Tathāgata Amitābha in the world Sukhāvatī, I see him immediately according to my wish;

if I wish to see the Tathāgata Vajraprabha in the world Candana, the Tathāgata Ratnaprabha in the world Sugandha, the Tathāgata Ratnapadmaprabha in the world Padma, the Tathāgata Śāntaprabha in the world Suvarṇa, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the world Abhirati, the Tathāgata Siṃha in the world Supratiṣṭhita, the Tathāgata Candrabuddhi in the world Ādarśaprabha, and the Tathāgata Vairocana in the world Ratnasiṃhavyūha—all such ones as these, I see them all immediately.
Yet that Tathāgata does not come here, nor do I go there.
I know that all Buddhas and my own mind are entirely like dreams;
I know that all Buddhas are like reflections and my own mind is like water.
One knows that all the physical forms and characteristics of all Buddhas, as well as one's own mind, are entirely like illusions;
one knows that all Buddhas and one's own mind are entirely like echoes.
I know this and remember it thus:
all the Buddhas whom I have seen are entirely due to my own mind. "Good son!

It should be known that when Bodhisattvas cultivate all Buddha-dharmas, purify all Buddha-fields, accumulate sublime practices, subdue sentient beings, and give rise to great vows; when they enter the gate of inconceivable liberation that freely sports in omniscience, attain the Bodhi of Buddhas, manifest great supernatural powers, travel everywhere throughout the dharma-realms of the ten directions, and universally enter all kalpas with subtle wisdom—all such things arise entirely from their own minds.

"Therefore, noble son, you should support your own mind with wholesome dharmas; you should moisten your own mind with the water of the Dharma; you should purify your own mind regarding sense objects; you should fortify your own mind with diligence; you should broaden your own mind with patience; you should whiten your own mind through the realization of wisdom; you should sharpen your own mind with discerning wisdom; you should develop your own mind through the sovereignty of the Buddhas; you should expand your own mind through the equality of the Buddhas; and you should examine your own mind with the ten powers of the Buddhas."
“Good son! I have only attained entry into and emergence from this liberation door of the Tathāgata’s Unobstructed Adornment.

As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who have attained unobstructed wisdom and abide in unobstructed conduct; who have attained the samādhi of constantly seeing all Buddhas and the samādhi of not abiding in the limit of nirvāṇa; who have thoroughly mastered the universal gateway of the realm of samādhi and are entirely equal regarding the dharmas of the three periods of time; who are able to skillfully manifest divided bodies throughout all lands and abide in the state of equality of all Buddhas; for whom the realms of the ten directions all appear before them, and whose wisdom observation is such that nothing is not clearly understood; in whose bodies all worlds are manifested in their formation and destruction, yet who give rise to no thought of duality regarding their own bodies or those worlds—[I am like this].”
"Regarding such sublime practices, how could I possibly know them or speak of them? 'Good son!
Traveling south from here, at the edge of Jambudvīpa, there is a land named..."
In Marigala, there was a bhikṣu named Sāgaradhvaja.
“Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the elder Vimokṣa, circumambulated him to the right, gazed upon him, extolled and praised him, and with longing and veneration, wept tears of sorrow as he single-mindedly recollected him.
Relying upon spiritual friends, serving spiritual friends, and honoring spiritual friends, one perceives omniscience through spiritual friends;
one does not give rise to opposition toward spiritual friends, harbors no flattery or deception toward spiritual friends, and always remains compliant with spiritual friends;
one conceives of spiritual friends as a compassionate mother, because they cause one to abandon all unbeneficial dharmas.
He conceived the thought of his spiritual friend as a compassionate father, for it was he who gave birth to all wholesome dharmas.
Having paid his respects and departed,
at that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded right mindfulness, contemplated the instructions of that elder.
This teaching causes one to recollect that inconceivable liberation gate of bodhisattvas, to contemplate that inconceivable light of wisdom of bodhisattvas,
to enter deeply into that inconceivable door of the dharma-realm, to proceed toward that inconceivable universal entrance of bodhisattvas,
and to clearly behold those inconceivable miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas.
They comprehend that inconceivable universal entry into Buddha-fields; they discern that inconceivable adornment of the Buddhas' powers;
they contemplate those inconceivable stages of the bodhisattvas' samādhis and liberations;
they thoroughly master those inconceivable distinctions of worlds, reaching ultimate non-obstruction; and they cultivate that inconceivable...
With a firm and profound resolve, the Bodhisattva gave rise to those inconceivable great vows and pure deeds of a Bodhisattva.
Traveling south by stages, he reached the village of Pāṭalī on the borders of Jambudvīpa, where he searched everywhere for the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.

He then saw him sitting cross-legged beside the place for walking meditation, having entered into samādhi; he was free from inhalation and exhalation, devoid of distinct thoughts or perceptions, his body peaceful and unmoving.

From beneath his feet, there emerged countless hundreds of thousands of billions of elders, householders, and brahmins, all their bodies adorned with various ornaments, wearing jeweled crowns with bright pearls bound upon their heads. They traveled everywhere throughout all worlds in the ten directions, raining down all kinds of jewels, all necklaces, all garments, all food and drink of the finest flavor according to the Dharma, all flowers, all garlands, all incenses, all ointments, and all requisites for the enjoyment of desires. In every place, they rescued and gathered in all impoverished sentient beings and comforted all those suffering in affliction, causing them all to rejoice with pure minds and to achieve the path of unsurpassed bodhi.

From his two knees, there emerged countless hundreds of thousands of billions of kṣatriyas and brahmins, all of whom were wise and intelligent. They possessed various complexions, various physical forms, and various garments, all exquisitely adorned. They pervaded all worlds throughout the ten directions, gathering in sentient beings through kind speech and shared activities.
That is to say:
they cause the poor to be sufficient, the sick to be healed, the endangered to be secure, and the terrified to find peace; they cause all who possess sorrow and suffering to attain joy.
Furthermore, through skillful means, they exhort and guide them, causing all to abandon evil and dwell securely in wholesome dharmas.

From his waist, there emerged immeasurable sages, as numerous as all living beings—some wearing garments of grass, others wearing garments of tree bark—all holding water-pots and possessing tranquil, dignified deportment. They traveled back and forth throughout the worlds of the ten directions, and amidst the void, with the wondrous voice of a Buddha, they praised the Tathāgata and expounded all dharmas;
some spoke of the path of pure brahmacarya, causing them to practice it and subdue their faculties;
others spoke of how all dharmas lack intrinsic nature, leading them to contemplate this and give rise to wisdom.

In some instances, he explains the conventions of worldly discourse; in others, he reveals the expedient means for attaining the knowledge of all-knowledge, so that beings may each cultivate their respective practices according to the proper sequence.
From his two flanks, there emerged inconceivable nāgas and inconceivable nāga maidens, manifesting inconceivable supernatural transformations of the nāgas, namely:

Raining down inconceivable clouds of incense, inconceivable clouds of flowers, inconceivable clouds of garlands, inconceivable clouds of precious canopies, inconceivable clouds of precious banners, inconceivable clouds of exquisite jewel ornaments, inconceivable clouds of great maṇi jewels, inconceivable clouds of precious necklaces, inconceivable clouds of precious thrones, inconceivable clouds of precious palaces, inconceivable clouds of precious lotuses, inconceivable clouds of precious crowns, and inconceivable clouds of celestial bodies and celestial maidens—all pervading the void as adornments, filling all worlds in the ten directions and making offerings at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas, causing all sentient beings to give rise to joy.

From the svastika on his chest, there emerged hundreds of thousands of billions of asura kings, all of whom manifested inconceivable and sovereign illusory powers, causing the hundred worlds to tremble violently, all the oceans to spontaneously surge and boil, all the mountain kings to collide with one another, all the celestial palaces to shake, all the radiances of the māras to be eclipsed, and all the hosts of māra soldiers to be subdued;

they caused all sentient beings everywhere to abandon arrogance, eliminate anger and malice, shatter the mountains of affliction, stifle all evil dharmas, foster an end to strife, and dwell forever in mutual harmony and kindness.

Furthermore, by means of the power of illusion, they awaken sentient beings, causing them to extinguish evil deeds, to fear birth and death, to emerge from the various realms of existence, to become free from defiled attachment, to abide in the mind of unsurpassed bodhi, to cultivate all the practices of bodhisattvas, to dwell in all the pāramitās, to enter all the bodhisattva stages, to contemplate all subtle and wondrous Dharma gates, and to know the skillful means of all buddhas.
Such deeds were performed, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
From his back, for those who were to be delivered by means of the Two Vehicles, he manifested countless hundreds of thousands of billions of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
and for those attached to a self, he taught that there is no self.
For those who cling to permanence, he teaches that all conditioned phenomena are impermanent;
for those whose temperament is dominated by greed, he teaches the contemplation of impurity;
for those whose temperament is dominated by hatred, he teaches the contemplation of loving-kindness.
For those who act out of delusion, he teaches the contemplation of dependent origination;
for those with equal proportions of the afflictions, he teaches the dharmas of the sphere corresponding to wisdom;
for those who delight in and cling to sense objects, he teaches the dharma of non-existence.
For those who delight in dwelling in tranquility, he teaches the Dharma of generating great vows to universally benefit all sentient beings.
Such deeds as these pervade the entire dharma-realm.

From his two shoulders emerged countless hundreds of thousands of billions of yakṣas and rākṣasa kings, with various forms and various complexions, some tall and some short, all of whom were terrifying. Surrounded by immeasurable retinues, they protected all sentient beings who practice goodness, as well as the assemblies of worthies, sages, and bodhisattvas—both those who are correctly established and those who are in the process of being so established.
At times they manifest as Vajrapāṇi deities to protect the Buddhas and their dwelling places, or they universally protect all worlds.
To those who have fear, may they attain peace and security;
to those who are ill, may they attain recovery;
to those who suffer distress, may they attain liberation from it.
For those with transgressions and evils, he causes them to feel weary of them and repent;
for those beset by calamities and misfortunes, he causes them to be extinguished.
Thus benefiting all sentient beings, he causes them all to abandon the cycle of birth and death and to enter the True Dharma Wheel.
From his abdomen issued forth countless hundreds of thousands of billions of kinnara kings, each surrounded before and behind by countless kinnara maidens;
furthermore, there issued forth countless hundreds of thousands of billions of gandharva kings, each surrounded before and behind by countless gandharva maidens.
Each played countless hundreds of thousands of celestial musical instruments, singing praises of the true nature of all phenomena, singing praises of all Buddhas,
singing praises of the generation of the bodhicitta, singing praises of the cultivation of the bodhisattva practices,
and singing praises of the gateways through which all Buddhas attain perfect enlightenment. Singing...
They praise the gate of all Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma; they sing praises to the gate of all Buddhas manifesting spiritual transformations;
they reveal and expound the gate of all Buddhas entering parinirvāṇa;
they reveal and expound the gate of protecting the teachings of all Buddhas; and they reveal and expound [the gate] that causes all sentient beings to...
The Gate of Joy reveals and expounds the gate of purifying all Buddha-fields;
it reveals and expounds the gate of manifesting all subtle and wondrous Dharma-gates; it reveals and expounds the gate of relinquishing all obstacles;
it reveals and expounds the gate of generating all roots of goodness.
In this manner, throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the Dharma-realm,

from his face-gate there emerged countless hundreds of thousands of billions of universal wheel-turning monarchs (*cakravartin*), fully endowed with the seven treasures and surrounded by the fourfold army; they emitted the light of great relinquishment and rained down immeasurable jewels,
causing all who were impoverished to be fully satisfied and leading them to forever sever the practice of taking what is not given.
He gave away hundreds of thousands of beautiful maidens, his mind free from attachment, so as to cause them to forever sever the practice of sexual misconduct;
to cause them to give rise to a heart of compassion and refrain from taking life;
and to cause them to ultimately always speak words of truth, never engaging in false, deceptive, or useless speech.
They cause others to adopt speech that does not sow discord;
they cause them to speak with gentleness, free from harshness or malice;
and they cause them to constantly expound upon meanings that are profound, definitive, and clear, rather than engaging in meaningless or frivolous rhetoric.
For them, he preaches few desires, so that they may eliminate craving and possess minds free from defilement;
for them, he preaches great compassion, so that they may eliminate anger and attain purity of mind;

for them, he preaches the true meaning, so that they may investigate all phenomena, penetrate deeply into causes and conditions, clearly understand the principles of the truths, uproot the thorns of false views, shatter the mountains of doubt, and completely extinguish all obstacles.
Thus performed, these acts filled the entire Dharma-realm.

From his two eyes, he emitted countless hundreds of thousands of billions of solar discs, which universally illuminated all the great hells and evil realms, causing all beings therein to be free from suffering;
furthermore, they shone upon the intervals between all worlds, causing the darkness to be dispelled.
Furthermore, they illuminate all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, causing them all to abandon the cataracts of ignorance;
in defiled lands, they radiate pure light; in lands of white silver, they radiate golden light;
in lands of gold, they radiate white silver-colored light; and in lands of lapis lazuli, they radiate crystal-colored light.
The crystal lands emit light the color of lapis lazuli; the mother-of-pearl lands emit light the color of agate;
the agate lands emit light the color of mother-of-pearl; the indranīla lands emit light the color of the sun-treasury maṇi king;
the sun-treasury maṇi king lands emit light the color of indranīla; and the red pearl lands...
The land of the Moonlight Net Treasury Maṇi King emits light in the color of maṇi jewels;
the land of the Moonlight Net Treasury Maṇi King emits light in the color of red pearls; lands formed from a single jewel emit light in the colors of various jewels;
and lands formed from various jewels emit light in the color of a single jewel, illuminating the minds of all sentient beings.
Within this dense forest, they accomplish the immeasurable tasks of all sentient beings and adorn all worldly realms,
causing the minds of all beings to attain refreshing clarity and giving rise to great joy.
Such deeds were performed, filling the entire Dharma-realm.

From the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows, there emerged hundreds of thousands of billions of Śakras, all of whom had attained mastery over their spheres. Maṇi jewels were bound upon their heads, their light illuminating all the celestial palaces, shaking all the kings of Mount Sumeru, and awakening the great assemblies of all the devas;

they extolled the power of merit, spoke of the power of wisdom, generated the power of joy, sustained the power of resolve, purified the power of mindfulness, strengthened the power of the bodhicitta they had produced, and praised the delight of seeing the Buddha.
They cause the removal of worldly desires and praise the joy of hearing the Dharma;
they cause weariness with worldly objects and praise the joy of contemplating wisdom;

they cause the severance of worldly defilements, the cessation of the battle of the asuras, the ending of the strife of afflictions, and the extinguishing of the fear of death; they inspire the vow to subdue Māra, establish the Sumeru King of Mountains of the True Dharma, and accomplish all the tasks of sentient beings.
Such deeds were performed, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.

From his forehead, there emerged hundreds of thousands of billions of Brahmā deities, whose physical forms were dignified and majestic, peerless in the world; their deportment was serene and their voices were exquisite. They exhorted the Buddha to preach the Dharma and extolled the Buddha’s merits, causing all Bodhisattvas to rejoice and enabling them to accomplish immeasurable works for sentient beings throughout all worlds in the ten directions.

From above their heads, there emerged multitudes of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-fields; all were adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, emitting boundless light and expounding various practices.
That is to say:
praising the virtue of giving so as to cause others to abandon stinginess and greed, thereby attaining a world adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels;
extolling and praising the merit of upholding the precepts so as to cause all sentient beings to forever sever all evils and abide in the Bodhisattva’s precepts of great compassion.
He taught that all phenomena exist yet are entirely like dreams; he taught that all sensual pleasures lack any true flavor, so as to cause sentient beings to be freed from the bonds of affliction;
he taught the power of patience, so as to cause them to attain mastery over their minds regarding all dharmas;
and he praised the golden body, so as to cause sentient beings to leave behind the defilement of anger, to give rise to remedial practices, and to sever the path of animal rebirth.
He praised the practice of vigor, causing them to distance themselves from worldly negligence and to diligently cultivate all immeasurable, wondrous dharmas;
furthermore, he extolled the dhyāna-pāramitā, causing their minds to attain mastery over all things;
and he expounded the prajñā-pāramitā, revealing right view so that all sentient beings might delight in sovereign wisdom and extract the poison of all views.

Furthermore, he expounds various worldly activities in accordance with the world, enabling all sentient beings to attain birth at will within the various realms of existence even while remaining free from birth and death;
he further manifests supernatural transformations and explains mastery over lifespan, causing all sentient beings to give rise to great vows;
and he further expounds upon the power of accomplishing dhāraṇīs, the power of generating great aspirations, the power of purifying samādhis, and the power of attaining birth at will.
Furthermore, he expounded for them various kinds of wisdom, namely:

the wisdom that universally knows the faculties of all sentient beings; the wisdom that universally knows all mental activities; the wisdom that universally knows the ten powers of the Tathāgatas; and the wisdom that universally knows the sovereign mastery of all Buddhas.
Such deeds were performed, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.

From the crown of his head, there issued forth hundreds of thousands of billions of Tathāgata bodies; their forms were peerless, adorned with the pure major and minor marks, and their majestic radiance was as brilliant as a mountain of pure gold. Immeasurable light shone universally throughout the ten directions, and they uttered sublime sounds that filled the Dharma-realm. Manifesting immeasurable great supernormal powers, they rained down the rain of Dharma upon all worlds.
That is to say:
for the bodhisattvas seated at the site of enlightenment, it rains the rain of the Dharma of universal knowledge and equality;
for the bodhisattvas at the stage of consecration, it rains the rain of entering the universal gate.
For the Bodhisattvas at the stage of Dharma Prince, they rain down the Dharma rain of Universal Adornment;
for the Bodhisattvas at the stage of Youthful Child, they rain down the Dharma rain of the Solid Mountain;
for the Bodhisattvas at the stage of Non-retrogression, they rain down the Dharma rain of the Ocean Treasury.
For the bodhisattvas at the stage of accomplishing the right mind, he rains down the rain of the Dharma of universal realms;
for the bodhisattvas at the stage of being endowed with skillful means, he rains down the rain of the Dharma of the gateways of self-nature;
for the bodhisattvas at the stage of noble birth, he rains down the rain of the Dharma that accords with the world.
For Bodhisattvas at the stage of cultivation, he rains down the Dharma-rain of universal compassion;
for newly initiated Bodhisattvas, he rains down the Dharma-rain of the treasury of accumulations;
for Bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds, he rains down the Dharma-rain of gathering in sentient beings.
For the sake of all bodhisattvas who possess faith and understanding, he rains down the rain of Dharma that universally manifests inexhaustible realms;
for the sake of all sentient beings in the realm of form, he rains down the rain of Dharma from the universal gate;
for the sake of all Brahmā devas, he rains down the rain of Dharma from the universal treasury.
For the various Īśvara devas, he rains down the Dharma rain of the power of birth;
for the hosts of Māras, he rains down the Dharma rain of the mind-banner;
for the various Nirmanarati devas, he rains down the Dharma rain of pure mindfulness.
For the Tuṣita devas, he rains down the Dharma rain of generating the aspiration for enlightenment;
for the Yāma devas, he rains down the Dharma rain of joy;
for the Trāyastriṃśa devas, he rains down the Dharma rain of swiftly adorning the realm of space.
For the yakṣa kings, they rain down the Dharma-rain of joy;
for the gandharva kings, they rain down the Dharma-rain of the vajra-wheel;
for the asura kings, they rain down the Dharma-rain of the great realm.
For the garuḍa kings, he rains down the Dharma rain of boundless radiance;
for the kinnara kings, he rains down the Dharma rain of all-world-surpassing wisdom;
for the human kings, he rains down the Dharma rain of non-attachment.
For the dragon kings, he rains down the Dharma rain of the Banner of Joy;
for the mahoraga kings, he rains down the Dharma rain of Great Rest;
for the sentient beings in the hells, he rains down the Dharma rain of the Adornment of Right Mindfulness.
For all animals, he rains down the Dharma rain of the treasury of wisdom;
for the sentient beings in the realm of King Yama, he rains down the Dharma rain of fearlessness;
and for the sentient beings in places of calamity and distress, he rains down the Dharma rain of universal consolation.
He caused all beings to enter the assemblies of the noble ones.
Such deeds as these filled the entire Dharma-realm.

Furthermore, from every single pore of his body, the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja emitted networks of light equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-lands. Each network of light possessed incalculable colors and forms, incalculable adornments, incalculable spheres of influence, and incalculable activities, filling all the Dharma-realms throughout the ten directions.

At that time, the youth Sudhana single-mindedly observed the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, giving rise to a profound sense of longing and veneration. He recollected that samādhi-liberation; he contemplated that inconceivable bodhisattva-samādhi; he contemplated that inconceivable ocean of skillful means for benefiting sentient beings; he contemplated that inconceivable gate of universal adornment through non-action; he contemplated that pure wisdom which adorns the dharma-realm; he contemplated that wisdom empowered by the Buddhas; he contemplated that power of the bodhisattvas’ mastery in manifestation; he contemplated that firm power of the bodhisattvas’ great vows; and he contemplated that expanding power of the bodhisattvas’ various practices.

Remaining thus established, he reflected and observed for one day and one night, and continued in this manner for seven days and seven nights, a fortnight, a month, and even up to six months and another six days.
After this had passed, the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja emerged from samādhi.
Sudhana the youth praised him, saying:
"Noble One!..."

How rare and extraordinary! This samādhi is most profound; this samādhi is most vast; the realm of this samādhi is immeasurable; the spiritual power of this samādhi is inconceivable; the radiance of this samādhi is peerless; the adornments of this samādhi are innumerable; the majesty of this samādhi is irresistible; the realm of this samādhi is impartial; this samādhi universally illumines the ten directions; and the benefit of this samādhi is limitless, for it is able to extinguish the immeasurable sufferings of all sentient beings.
That is to say:
because it enables all sentient beings to leave behind poverty and suffering; because it delivers them from the hells; because it frees them from the realm of animals;

because it closes the gates to the various states of misfortune; because it opens the paths to the human and celestial realms; and because it causes the sentient beings of the human and celestial realms—
Because it brings joy and bliss, because it causes one to delight in the realm of dhyāna, because it can cause the increase of conditioned happiness,
because it can manifest the happiness of transcending existence, because it can induce the arousal of the bodhicitta,
because it can cause the growth of the practices of merit and wisdom, and because it can cause the increase of the mind of great compassion, it can...
Because it gives rise to the power of great vows; because it enables the clear understanding of the bodhisattva path;
because it enables the adornment of ultimate wisdom; because it enables the entry into the realm of the Mahāyāna; because it enables the illumination and realization of the conduct of Samantabhadra;
because it enables the attainment of the light of wisdom of all the bodhisattva stages; because it enables the accomplishment of...
Because of all the vows and practices of all bodhisattvas, they are able to cause others to dwell securely within the realm of the knowledge of all-knowledge. Noble One!
"What is the name of this samādhi?
The bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja replied, "Good son!..."
This samādhi is named "Universal Eye of Renunciation and Attainment," and is also named "Pure Radiance of the Sphere of Prajñāpāramitā," and is also named:
The Gate of Universal Adornment and Purity. Good son!
Because I have practiced the *prajñāpāramitā*, I have attained this samādhi of Universal Adornment and Purity, as well as one million *asaṃkhyeya* samādhis.
Sudhana said, "Noble One! Is the ultimate realm of this samādhi only like this?"
Sāgaradhvaja said: "Good son!
When entering this samādhi, one clearly knows all worlds without any obstruction."
They travel to all worlds without obstruction;
they transcend all worlds without obstruction; they adorn all worlds without obstruction.
They cultivate and purify all worlds without obstruction;
they adorn and cleanse all worlds without obstruction;
they behold all Buddhas without obstruction.
They contemplate the vast majesty and virtue of all Buddhas without obstruction;
they know the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas without obstruction;
and they realize the various great powers of all Buddhas without obstruction.
They enter the ocean of all Buddhas' merits without obstruction;
they receive the immeasurable, wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas without obstruction;
and they enter into the cultivation of sublime practices within all Buddha-dharmas without obstruction.
They realize the wisdom of the equality of all Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma, without obstruction;
they enter the ocean-like assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas, without obstruction;
and they contemplate the Buddha-dharma of the ten directions, without obstruction.
They embrace sentient beings of the ten directions through great compassion, without obstruction;
they constantly give rise to great kindness that fills the ten directions, without obstruction;
and they behold the Buddhas of the ten directions with a mind never satiated, without obstruction.
They enter the ocean of all sentient beings without obstruction;
they know the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings without obstruction;
and they possess unobstructed knowledge of the distinctions among the various faculties of all sentient beings.
“Good son! I know only this light of the samādhi of the *prajñāpāramitā*.

As for those bodhisattvas who enter the ocean of wisdom, purify the realm of the dharma-dhātu, reach all destinies, pervade immeasurable lands, possess mastery over dhāraṇīs, have purified samādhis, have vast supernormal powers, possess inexhaustible eloquence, skillfully explain the stages, and serve as a refuge for sentient beings—[I do not know their ways].”

But how could I possibly know their wondrous conduct, discern their merits, comprehend their practices, clarify their realms, investigate their powers of aspiration, enter their essential gateways, reach their realizations, explain their factors of the path, abide in their samādhis, perceive their mental objects, or attain their all-pervading, equalizing wisdom?
“Good son! From here, travel south; there is a dwelling place named Sea Tide.
There is a grove there named Universal Adornment;
within that grove, there is an upāsikā named:
"Śūraṃgama, go there and ask:
'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"

Then, at the place of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, the youth Sudhana attained a firm and solid body, acquired the wealth of the sublime Dharma, entered profound realms, and his wisdom became clear and penetrating. His samādhis shone forth, he dwelt in pure understanding, and he beheld the most profound dharmas. His mind was settled in all gates of purity; the radiance of his wisdom filled the ten directions. His heart was filled with joy, and he leaped for immeasurable delight.

Prostrating himself with his five limbs touching the ground, he bowed at the bhikṣu’s feet, circumambulated him countless times, and gazed upon him with reverence. He contemplated and observed him, sighing with admiration and longing, holding his name in mind, visualizing his deportment, recollecting his voice, and reflecting upon his samādhis and the spheres of activity of his great vows. Having received the pure radiance of his wisdom, he took his leave and departed.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Sixty-three;
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Sixty-four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
The Fifth Part of the Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm, Number Thirty-Nine, Part Five.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, empowered by the strength of his spiritual friends, relying upon the instructions of his spiritual friends, and recollecting the words of his spiritual friends, felt deep love and joy for them in his heart, and thought to himself:
"It is because of my spiritual friends that I have been able to see the Buddhas;..."
It is because of spiritual friends that I have been enabled to hear the Dharma.
Spiritual friends are my teachers and preceptors, for they instruct and guide me in all the Buddha-dharmas;
spiritual friends are my eyes, for they enable me to see the Buddhas as vast as space.
“Spiritual friends are my ferry and crossing, for they enable me to enter the lotus ponds of all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas.

Gradually traveling south, he reached the shore of the ocean tides and beheld the Garden of Universal Adornment, surrounded on all sides by walls of various jewels, with rows of all kinds of jewel trees standing in solemn array;
and all the jewel-flower trees rained down myriad exquisite blossoms, which were strewn across the ground.
All the trees of precious incense emit fragrant vapors that universally permeate the ten directions;
all the trees of precious garlands rain down great jeweled garlands, hanging down everywhere;
all the trees of the sovereign king of *maṇi* jewels rain down great *maṇi* jewels, spreading and filling all places.
All the jewel-clothing trees rain down garments of various colors, which are spread out everywhere according to what is appropriate;
all the musical-instrument trees produce sounds when stirred by the wind, their melodies so exquisite that they surpass the music of the heavens;
and all the ornamentation trees each rain down rare and wonderful treasures, distributed everywhere to serve as adornments.
The ground was pure and level, free from elevations or depressions, and within it were a million halls composed of great maṇi jewels;
a million pavilions with Jāmbūnada gold covering their tops;
and a million palaces adorned with the interlacing of Vairocana maṇi jewels.
There were ten thousand bathing pools composed of various jewels;
railings made of the seven treasures surrounded them on all sides;
and stairways of the seven treasures were distributed across the four directions.

The water of eight virtues is serene and overflowing; its fragrance is like celestial sandalwood, and golden sand is spread across its bottom. The water is clear, with precious jewels interspersed throughout.
Ducks, geese, peacocks, and *kukila* birds sport within it, emitting harmonious and elegant sounds.
Rows of precious *tāla* trees stand in circumference, covered by jeweled nets and draped with golden bells; as a gentle breeze stirs them, they constantly produce beautiful music.
He bestowed great jeweled canopies, surrounded by jewel trees, and erected countless mani-jewel banners whose radiance illuminated hundreds of thousands of yojanas.

Within this space were further a million ponds, their bottoms covered with layers of black sandalwood mud; exquisite jewels formed lotus flowers spread across the water, and the light and colors of great mani-flowers shone brilliantly.
Within the garden, there is furthermore a vast palace named Adorned Banner (*Vyūha-dhvaja*).

Its floor is composed of the wondrous jewels of the ocean-treasury; its pillars are made of lapis lazuli; it is covered above with Jāmbūnada gold; it is adorned with light-treasury *maṇi* gems; countless jewel-kings emit blazing flames; and it is decorated with multi-storied towers and side galleries of various kinds.
The supreme Aruṇa incense-king and the Awakening Incense-king both produce exquisite fragrances that universally permeate all things.
Within those palaces, there were further immeasurable jewel lotus thrones arranged all around, namely:

the Maṇi-jewel lotus throne illuminating the ten directions; the Vairocana-maṇi-jewel lotus throne; the Maṇi-jewel lotus throne illuminating the world; the Maṇi-jewel lotus throne of the wondrous treasury; the Maṇi-jewel lotus throne of the lion treasury; the Maṇi-jewel lotus throne of the stainless treasury; the Maṇi-jewel lotus throne of universal gates; the Maṇi-jewel lotus throne of radiant adornment; the pure maṇi-king jewel lotus throne abiding in the great ocean treasury; and the vajra-siṃha-maṇi-jewel lotus throne.
Within the garden there were further ten million kinds of canopies, namely:

canopies of garments, canopies of garlands, canopies of incense, canopies of flowers, canopies of branches, canopies of maṇi jewels, canopies of pure gold, canopies of ornaments, canopies of music, canopies of the miraculous transformations of the elephant king, canopies of the miraculous transformations of the horse king, and canopies of the maṇi jewels worn by Śakra... such as these, numbering in the millions.
There were a million great jewel nets covering it from above, namely:

nets of jeweled bells, nets of jeweled canopies, nets of jeweled bodies, nets of sea-treasury pearls, nets of dark-blue lapis lazuli *maṇi* jewels, nets of *siṃha-maṇi* jewels, nets of moonlight *maṇi* jewels, nets of various forms and fragrant incense, nets of jeweled crowns, nets of jeweled necklaces... such as these, numbering in the millions.
There were ten million great radiances that shone forth, namely:

the radiance of the *jvālā-prabhā* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *sūryagarbha* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *candradhvaja* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *gandhārcis* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *vijayagarbha* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *padmagarbha* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *jvālādhvaja* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *mahādīpa* maṇi-jewel, the radiance of the *samantābhāsadaśadik* maṇi-jewel, and the radiance of the *gandhaprabhāsa* maṇi-jewel... such as these, numbering in the millions.

A constant rain of a million ornaments falls; a million black sandalwood incenses emit wondrous sounds; a million *mandārava* flowers, surpassing those of the devas, are scattered about; a million necklaces and pendants, surpassing those of the devas, serve as adornments; a million exquisite jewel garlands and sashes, surpassing those of the devas, hang down everywhere; a million garments of various colors, surpassing those of the deva hosts, appear; a million multicolored *maṇi* jewels radiate brilliant light everywhere; a million sons of gods joyfully gaze upon him with heads bowed in prostration; a million celestial maidens cast themselves down from the void; and a million bodhisattvas respectfully approach him, ever delighting in hearing the Dharma.

At that time, the upāsikā Śreṣṭhadattā sat upon a throne of pure gold. She wore a crown of ocean-treasury pearl nets and hung upon her arms golden armlets of precious jewels that surpassed those of all the devas. Her deep blue hair hung down, and her head was adorned with a great maṇi net; she had maṇi-jewels shaped like lion mouths as ear-ornaments and the king of wish-fulfilling maṇi-jewels as a necklace. Nets of every kind of jewel draped over and covered her body, while hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings bowed their heads in reverent respect.
From the east, immeasurable sentient beings came to his abode—
namely, Brahmā, the Brahmakāyika gods, Mahābrahmā, the Brahmapurohita gods, and the Vaśavartin gods, as well as all humans and non-humans;
the same was true for the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.

Whoever beholds this upāsikā shall have all their sufferings of illness completely extinguished; they shall be freed from the defilements of affliction, uproot the thorns of false views, and shatter the mountains of hindrances. They shall enter the unimpeded and pure realm, increase and clarify all roots of goodness, and nurture the faculties.
They shall enter the gate of all wisdom, the gate of all dhāraṇīs, and the gates of all samādhis, all great vows, all sublime practices, and all merits—all of which shall manifest before them.
His mind was vast and expansive; endowed with supernormal powers, his body was without obstruction, reaching all places.

At that time, the youth Sudhana entered the Park of Universal Adornment and, after surveying it thoroughly, saw the laywoman Śrīprabhā seated upon a sublime throne. He approached her, prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and said: "Noble Lady!
I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how one should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray you, speak for me! Viśva said:
"O son of good family!
I have attained but a single gate of liberation as a bodhisattva; yet, for anyone who sees, hears, remembers me, dwells with me, or makes offerings to me, none of these shall be in vain.

"Good son! If there are sentient beings who have not planted roots of goodness, who are not sustained by virtuous friends, and who are not protected and remembered by the Buddhas, such persons shall ultimately never see me."
“Good son! Any sentient beings who behold me shall all attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Good son!”
The Buddhas of the eastern direction constantly come here, taking their seats upon jeweled thrones to preach the Dharma for me;

likewise, all the Buddhas of the southern, western, and northern directions, as well as those of the four intermediate points, the zenith, and the nadir, all come here, taking their seats upon jeweled thrones to preach the Dharma for me.
"Good son! I am never apart from seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma, dwelling together with all the bodhisattvas. Good son!"

In this great assembly of mine, there are eighty-four thousand billion nayutas who all share my practice in this garden; they have all attained the stage of non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, all other sentient beings dwelling in this garden have likewise universally entered the stage of non-retrogression.
Sudhana said, "Noble One,
how long has it been since you first resolved your mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi? He replied:
“Good son! I recall that in the past, at the place of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I practiced the holy life, reverently made offerings, heard the Dharma, and received it with devotion;
prior to that, at the place of Vimala Buddha, I left the household life to study the Way and received and upheld the True Dharma.”
Prior to that, at the place of the Buddha Subhadhvaja;
prior to that, at the place of the Buddha Vijayasumeru;
prior to that, at the place of the Buddha Padmaguṇagarbha.
Prior to that, in the presence of Vairocana Buddha;
prior to that, in the presence of Samantanetra Buddha;
prior to that, in the presence of Brahmarāja Buddha.
Prior to that, he was in the presence of the Buddha Vajra-Ṣṛṅga;
prior to that, he was in the presence of the Buddha Varuṇadeva. Good son!

I recall that in the past, throughout immeasurable kalpas and immeasurable lifetimes, I served, revered, and made offerings to thirty-six Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in succession; I heard their teachings, received and upheld them, and purely cultivated the holy life.
Regarding what has passed beyond this, it is known by the Buddha’s wisdom and is not something I can fathom. "Good son!
The initial resolve of a bodhisattva is immeasurable, for it fills the entire dharma realm."
The gate of the Bodhisattva’s great compassion is immeasurable, for it universally enters all worlds;
the gate of the Bodhisattva’s great vows is immeasurable, for they ultimately pervade the dharma-realm of the ten directions;
the gate of the Bodhisattva’s great kindness is immeasurable, for it universally covers all sentient beings.
The practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas are immeasurable, for they are practiced throughout all lands and throughout all eons;
the power of the Bodhisattvas' samādhis is immeasurable, for it causes them never to regress from the Bodhisattva path;
the power of the Bodhisattvas' dhāraṇīs is immeasurable, for it is able to sustain all worlds.
The power of the Bodhisattvas’ wisdom-light is immeasurable, for it universally enables them to realize and enter the three periods of time;
the power of the Bodhisattvas’ supernormal faculties is immeasurable, for they universally manifest throughout all networks of lands;
the power of the Bodhisattvas’ eloquence is immeasurable, for with a single voice, all can be understood.
"The pure body of a Bodhisattva is immeasurable, for it pervades all Buddha-fields. Sudhana said,
"Noble One, how long will it be before you attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
He replied: "Good son!

A bodhisattva does not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and taming even a single sentient being; nor does he resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and taming a hundred sentient beings; nor, indeed, does he resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and taming as many as unspeakably unspeakable numbers of times more sentient beings."

They do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and transforming the sentient beings of a single world-system, nor even for the sake of teaching and transforming the sentient beings of unspeakably unspeakable multiples of world-systems;

they do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and transforming the sentient beings of worlds as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa, nor for the sake of teaching and transforming the sentient beings of worlds as numerous as the atoms in a trichiliocosm, nor even for the sake of teaching and transforming the sentient beings of worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of trichiliocosms;
they do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of making offerings to a single Tathāgata, nor even for the sake of making offerings to unspeakably unspeakable multiples of Tathāgatas.

They do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of making offerings to the Tathāgatas who appear successively in a single world-system; nor do they resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of making offerings to the Tathāgatas who appear successively in as many world-systems as there are atoms in an unspeakably unspeakable number of world-systems.

They do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of making offerings to the Tathāgatas who appear successively in as many worlds as there are atoms in a single trichiliocosm; nor do they resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of making offerings to the Tathāgatas who appear successively in as many worlds as there are atoms in an unspeakably unspeakable number of Buddha-fields.

They do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of purifying a single world-system; nor do they resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of purifying as many world-systems as there are atoms in an unspeakably unspeakable number of world-systems.

They do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of purifying a number of worlds equal to the atoms in one trichiliocosm, nor even for the sake of purifying a number of worlds equal to the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of trichiliocosms;

they do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of upholding the bequeathed Dharma of a single Tathāgata, nor even for the sake of upholding the bequeathed Dharma of unspeakably unspeakable multiples of Tathāgatas;

they do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of upholding the bequeathed Dharma of a Tathāgata in a single world, nor even for the sake of upholding the bequeathed Dharma of Tathāgatas in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of worlds.

They do not generate the bodhicitta for the sake of upholding the bequeathed Dharma of Tathāgatas in as many worlds as there are atoms in one Jambudvīpa, nor even for the sake of upholding the bequeathed Dharma of Tathāgatas in as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of Buddha-fields.
Thus, this brief explanation is not for the sake of fulfilling the vows of a single Buddha, nor for the sake of going to a single Buddha-land,
nor for the sake of entering a single Buddha’s assembly, nor for the sake of upholding a single Buddha’s Dharma-eye,
nor for the sake of turning a single Buddha’s wheel of Dharma, nor for the sake of knowing the sequence of kalpas within a single world-system.
It is not for the sake of knowing the ocean of the minds of even a single sentient being; it is not for the sake of knowing the ocean of the faculties of even a single sentient being;
it is not for the sake of knowing the ocean of the karma of even a single sentient being; it is not for the sake of knowing the ocean of the conduct of even a single sentient being;
it is not for the sake of knowing the ocean of the afflictions of even a single sentient being; it is not for the sake of knowing a single sentient being...

Because of the ocean of habitual tendencies of afflictions, and even for the sake of knowing the ocean of habitual tendencies of afflictions of sentient beings as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, they resolve upon bodhicitta.
They resolve upon the bodhicitta because they wish to teach and discipline all sentient beings without exception;
they resolve upon the bodhicitta because they wish to serve and make offerings to all Buddhas without exception;
they resolve upon the bodhicitta because they wish to adorn and purify all Buddha-fields without exception; they resolve upon the bodhicitta because they wish to protect and uphold all...
They resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to fully realize the correct teachings of all Buddhas without exception;

they resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to fulfill the vows of all Tathāgatas without exception; they resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to travel to all Buddha-lands without exception;
and they resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to enter the assemblies of all Buddhas without exception.
One generates the bodhicitta because one desires to know, without exception, the sequential order of all kalpas within all worlds;
one generates the bodhicitta because one desires to know, without exception, the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings;
one generates the bodhicitta because one desires to know, without exception, the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings; one desires...
One generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to know the ocean of the karma of all sentient beings without exception;

one generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to know the ocean of the conduct of all sentient beings without exception; one generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to extinguish the ocean of all afflictions of all sentient beings without exception;
one [generates the bodhicitta] because one wishes to uproot the afflictions of all sentient beings...
They resolve upon the mind of enlightenment because they have mastered the oceans of practices without exception. Good son!
To speak of it in brief, bodhisattvas resolve upon the mind of enlightenment by means of such skillful means and practices numbering in the hundreds of thousands of koṭis of asaṃkhyeyas.
“Good son! Because the bodhisattva’s practice universally enters all dharmas and realizes them all, and because it universally enters all lands and purifies them all. Therefore, good son!”
"When all worlds have been purified to their ultimate extent, my vow shall then end;
when the afflictions and habitual tendencies of all sentient beings have been uprooted to their ultimate extent, my vow shall then be fulfilled.
Thus spoke the youth Sudhana.
“Noble One! What is the name of this liberation? He replied:
“Good son! This liberation is named ‘The Banner of Peaceful Security Free from Sorrow.’”
"Good son! I know only this single gate of liberation.
As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, their minds are like the ocean, able to receive and contain all Buddha-dharmas."
Like Mount Sumeru, his resolve is firm and steadfast, incapable of being shaken;
like the *sudarśana* medicine, he can eliminate the grave illnesses of affliction in sentient beings;
like the bright and pure sun, he can shatter the dark obstructions of ignorance in sentient beings.
Just as the great earth serves as the foundation for all sentient beings;
just as a favorable wind brings about benefit and profit for all sentient beings;
and just as a bright lamp generates the light of wisdom for sentient beings.
Like a great cloud, he is able to rain down the Dharma of quiescence for the sake of sentient beings;
like the pure moon, he is able to radiate the light of merit and virtue for the sake of sentient beings;
and like Śakra, he is able to protect all sentient beings.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
"Good son! To the south of here, at the place where the ocean tides reach, there is a land named:
Narasu; there was also a seer therein named Vimuṣya.
"Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and wept with tears streaming down as he reflected thus:

“It is difficult to attain enlightenment; it is difficult to draw near to spiritual friends; it is difficult to encounter spiritual friends; it is difficult to obtain the faculties of a bodhisattva; it is difficult to purify the faculties of a bodhisattva; it is difficult to meet with spiritual friends who practice together; it is difficult to investigate according to reality; it is difficult to practice in accordance with the teachings; it is difficult to encounter the skillful means that give rise to the wholesome mind; and it is difficult to encounter the light of the Dharma that increases all-knowledge.”
Having formed this thought, he took his leave and departed. At that time, the youth Sudhana reflected in accordance with the true teaching of the Bodhisattvas;

he reflected in accordance with the pure conduct of the Bodhisattvas. He gave rise to a mind that increases the power of a Bodhisattva’s merit; he gave rise to a mind that clearly perceives all Buddhas; he gave rise to a mind that brings forth all Buddhas; he gave rise to a mind that increases all great vows; he gave rise to a mind that universally perceives all phenomena throughout the ten directions; he gave rise to a mind that clearly illuminates the true nature of all phenomena; he gave rise to a mind that universally disperses all obstacles; he gave rise to a mind that observes the Dharma-realm without darkness; he gave rise to a mind adorned by the jewel of a purified intention; and he gave rise to a mind that subdues and overcomes all Māras.
Traveling gradually, he arrived at the kingdom of Nalasura and searched everywhere for Vimalakṣa. He saw a great forest adorned with incalculable trees, namely:
various leafy trees spreading their branches wide; various flowering trees in full and brilliant bloom;

various fruit trees ripening in succession; various jewel-trees raining down mani-fruit; great sandalwood trees standing in rows everywhere; various aloeswood trees constantly emitting fine fragrances; delightful fragrance-trees adorned with exquisite scents; pāṭala trees surrounding it on all four sides; nyagrodha trees with towering trunks; jambūnada-trees constantly raining sweet fruit; and blue lotuses (utpala) and red lotuses (padma) adorning the ponds.

At that time, the youth Sudhana saw the seer sitting upon a layer of grass beneath a sandalwood tree, leading ten thousand disciples. Some wore deerskins, some wore tree bark, and others had woven grass for clothing; their topknots and earrings hung down to their temples as they surrounded him on all sides.
Having seen him, Sudhana went to his location, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, and spoke these words:
"I have now encountered a true spiritual friend."
A spiritual friend is a gateway to all-knowledge, for they enable me to enter the path of reality;
a spiritual friend is a vehicle to all-knowledge, for they enable me to reach the stage of the Tathāgata;
a spiritual friend is a ship to all-knowledge, for they enable me to reach the island of the jewels of wisdom.
A spiritual friend is a torch leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to give birth to the light of the ten powers;
a spiritual friend is a path leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to enter the city of nirvana;
a spiritual friend is a lamp leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to see the level and uneven paths.
A spiritual friend is a bridge leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to cross over dangerous and evil places;
a spiritual friend is a parasol leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to give rise to the coolness of great compassion;
a spiritual friend is an eye leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to see the gateway of the nature of phenomena.
"A spiritual friend is one who leads me toward the tide of all-knowledge, so that I may be filled with the waters of great compassion.
Having spoken these words, he rose from the ground, circumambulated him countless times, and stood before him with palms joined, saying: "Noble One!"
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Holy One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me! At that time, Vimalakṣa looked toward his assembly and said, "Good son!..."
This youth has already resolved his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
O son of good family!

This youth universally bestows fearlessness upon all sentient beings; this youth universally brings about the benefit of all sentient beings; this youth constantly contemplates the ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas; this youth desires to drink the nectar-rain of all Dharmas; this youth desires to fathom the vast ocean of all Dharmas; this youth desires to cause sentient beings to dwell within the ocean of wisdom; this youth desires to universally give rise to vast clouds of compassion; this youth desires to universally rain down the vast rain of Dharma; this youth desires to universally illuminate the world with the moon of wisdom; this youth desires to extinguish the poisonous heat of afflictions in the world; and this youth desires to increase all roots of goodness in all conscious beings.

At that time, having heard these words, the assembly of sages each scattered various kinds of exquisite incense and flowers over Sudhana, prostrated themselves in worship, and, surrounding him with reverence, spoke as follows:

"This youth shall surely rescue and protect all sentient beings; he shall surely extinguish the sufferings of the various hells; he shall surely sever forever the paths of the animals; he shall surely cause the realm of King Yama to be overturned; he shall surely close the gates to all places of peril; he shall surely dry up the ocean of craving and desire; he shall surely cause sentient beings to eternally extinguish the aggregates of suffering; he shall surely forever shatter the darkness of ignorance; he shall surely forever sever the bonds of greedy attachment; he shall surely surround the world with the Great Cakravāḍa Mountains of merit; he shall surely manifest the world with the Great Jewel Sumeru of wisdom; he shall surely bring forth the sun of pure knowledge; he shall surely reveal the Dharma-treasury of roots of goodness; and he shall surely cause the world to clearly discern the treacherous from the easy."
Then, Vimalagupta addressed the assembly of seers, saying:
"O sons of noble family!
If there are those who can resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they will surely accomplish the path to all-knowledge."
"This son of good family has already resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi; he shall purify the ground of all the merits of the Buddhas.
Then, Vimalakṣa said to the youth Sudhana:
"Son of good family!"
"I have attained the Bodhisattva liberation called 'Incomparable Banner.
Sudhana said to him, "Noble One!"
"What is the sphere of liberation of Anabhibhūdhvaja?
At that time, the seer Vimilāya extended his right hand, rubbed the crown of Sudhana’s head, and took Sudhana’s hand.

At that moment, Sudhana saw his own body go to worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields in the ten directions, arriving at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields. He beheld those buddha-fields and their assemblies, the physical marks and signs of those Buddhas, and their various adornments.

He also heard those Buddhas preaching the Dharma according to the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings; he thoroughly understood every word and phrase, receiving and upholding them individually without any confusion.
He also knew how those Buddhas purified their vows through various forms of understanding.
They also know that those Buddhas have accomplished all powers through their pure vows;
they also see the physical forms manifested by those Buddhas according to the minds of sentient beings;
and they also see the great networks of light of those Buddhas, with their various colors, pure and perfect.
They also know the power of the great light of the unimpeded wisdom of those Buddhas;

furthermore, they see themselves in the presence of those Buddhas for a day and night, or seven days and nights, half a month, one month, one year, ten years, a hundred years, a thousand years, or even for a hundred million years, or an ayuta-koti years, or a nayuta-koti years, or for half a kalpa, or for one kalpa, a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, or for hundreds of thousands of kotis, up to as many kalpas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
At that time, because the light of the wisdom of the Bodhisattva’s liberation of the Invincible Banner illuminated him, the youth Sudhana attained the light of the Samādhi of the Vairocana Treasury;
because the light of the Samādhi of the liberation of inexhaustible wisdom illuminated him, he attained the light of the Dhāraṇī of Universally Encompassing All Directions;
and because the light of the Gate of the Vajra-Wheel Dhāraṇī illuminated him, he attained the light of the Samādhi of the Mind of Utterly Pure Wisdom.
Because they are illuminated by the light of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Universal Gate Adornment Treasury, they attain the light of the Buddha’s Space-Treasury Wheel Samādhi;
because they are illuminated by the light of the Samādhi of the Dharma-Wheel of all Buddhas, they attain the light of the Samādhi of the Inexhaustible Wisdom of the Three Times.
Then, that seer released Sudhana’s hand, and the youth Sudhana immediately saw himself restored to his original place.
At that time, the seer addressed Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!
"Do you remember? Sudhana replied, "Yes! I do."
"This is the power of the noble spiritual friends," the rishi said.
"O son of good family!"
I know only this Bodhisattva liberation of the "Incomparable Banner. As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have accomplished all supreme samādhis and attained mastery at all times;

who, in a single thought-moment, give birth to the immeasurable wisdom of all Buddhas and adorn it with the lamp of Buddha-wisdom to universally illumine the world; who, in a single thought-moment, universally enter the realms of the three periods of time; who manifest divided bodies to travel everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions; whose bodies of wisdom universally enter all dharma-realms; who appear before all sentient beings according to their minds, observing their faculties and conduct to benefit them; and who radiate pure light that is most lovely and delightful—[I do not know their ways].

How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct, their sublime vows, their adornment of buddha-fields, the realm of their wisdom, the range of their samādhis, their miraculous transformations of supernatural powers, their playful mastery of liberation, the distinctions of their physical marks, the purity of their voices, or the radiance of their wisdom?
“Good son! To the south of here, there is a village named Īśāna;”
There is a brahmin named Jvalanānta. Go to him and ask:
"How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

At that time, the youth Sudhana, filled with joy and leaping for gladness, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and took his leave to travel south.

At that time, because the youth Sudhana was illumined by the Bodhisattva liberation of the Invincible Banner, he dwelt in the inconceivable spiritual power of all Buddhas; he realized the inconceivable wisdom of the Bodhisattva’s liberations and supernormal powers; he attained the light of wisdom of the inconceivable Bodhisattva samādhis; he attained the light of wisdom of the samādhis cultivated at all times; he attained the light of wisdom of the samādhi that knows all objective realms abide solely in conceptualization; and he attained the light of wisdom of the supreme excellence of all worlds.
He manifested his body in all places, preaching the non-dual, non-conceptual, and equal Dharma with ultimate wisdom, and universally illuminating all realms with clear and pure wisdom.
Whatever teachings he heard, he was able to endure and accept them with pure faith and understanding, attaining certain and lucid clarity regarding the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

Their minds never abandon the sublime conduct of Bodhisattvas; they seek omniscience with perpetual non-retrogression; they have attained the light of wisdom of the ten powers; they diligently seek the sublime Dharma without ever becoming weary; through correct practice, they enter the realm of the Buddhas; they give rise to the immeasurable adornments of Bodhisattvas; and their boundless great vows are entirely purified.
With inexhaustible wisdom, they know the net of infinite worlds; with a heart free from cowardice, they deliver the ocean of immeasurable sentient beings.

They fully comprehend the spheres of practice of infinite bodhisattvas; they see the various distinctions of infinite worlds; they see the various adornments of infinite worlds; they enter the subtle spheres of infinite worlds; they know the various names of infinite worlds; they know the various languages of infinite worlds; they know the various inclinations of infinite sentient beings; they see the various practices of infinite sentient beings; they see the practices for maturing infinite sentient beings; they see the diverse perceptions of infinite sentient beings; and they keep their spiritual friends in mind.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at the village of Īśāna, where he saw the ascetic Śūramgama performing various austerities in his quest for omniscience.

On all four sides were masses of fire like great mountains, and in their midst stood a mountain of blades with peaks of infinite height; [the ascetic] would climb that mountain and cast himself into the flames.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and spoke these words: “Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice.”
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will explain it to me! The brahmin said:
“Good son! If you can now ascend this mountain of swords and cast yourself into this mass of fire, all the practices of the bodhisattvas will become completely purified.
At that time, the youth Sudhana thought to himself:

"It is difficult to obtain a human body; it is difficult to be free from all calamities; it is difficult to attain a state free from calamities; it is difficult to encounter the pure Dharma; it is difficult to meet a Buddha; it is difficult to possess all the faculties; it is difficult to hear the Buddha’s Dharma; it is difficult to encounter virtuous people; it is difficult to meet true spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra); it is difficult to receive the correct teaching according to the principle; it is difficult to attain right livelihood; and it is difficult to practice in accordance with the Dharma."
Could this not be Māra, or one sent by Māra?

Could this not be a member of Māra’s treacherous and evil faction, falsely manifesting the appearance of a Bodhisattva and a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), intending to create obstacles for my roots of goodness and obstacles for my life, hindering my cultivation of the path to omniscience, dragging me into the various evil realms, and seeking to obstruct my Dharma-gate and my Buddha-Dharma?
While he was thinking this, ten thousand Brahmā devas in the midst of the sky spoke these words:
"Good man, do not think such a thought!"
Do not harbor such thoughts!
This noble one has attained the radiance of the Vajrajvālā-samādhi and exerts great diligence to deliver all sentient beings, his mind never regressing;

he desires to exhaust the ocean of all craving and attachment, to sever the net of all false views, to burn the firewood of all afflictions, to illuminate the dense forest of all delusions, to cut off the fear of all old age and death, to destroy all obstacles of the three periods of time, and to radiate the light of all dharmas.
“Good son! Most of my Brahmā devas are deeply attached to false views; they all claim for themselves that they are the sovereign, the creator, and that within the world, they are the most supreme.”

Seeing the brahmin performing the penance of being scorched by five fires, they found no pleasure in their own palaces and could find no flavor in the various meditative concentrations; thus, they all came together to the place where the brahmin was.

At that time, the brahmin, through his supernormal powers, manifested great ascetic practices and preached the Dharma for us, enabling us to extinguish all views, eliminate all pride, abide in great loving-kindness, practice great compassion, give rise to a vast mind, and resolve upon Bodhicitta; so that we might constantly see all Buddhas, perpetually hear the wondrous Dharma, and have no mental obstructions in any place.
Furthermore, ten thousand māras were in the air, scattering celestial maṇi jewels upon the brāhmaṇa and saying to Sudhana:
"O son of good family!

When this brahmin was performing the austerity of being scorched by the five fires, the radiance of those flames so overwhelmed the splendor of all the ornaments of my palaces that they appeared like a mass of ink; it caused me to feel no pleasure or attachment toward them, and so I, together with my retinue, came to his side.
This brahmin has preached the Dharma for me, causing myself and immeasurable sons of gods and daughters of gods to attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Furthermore, ten thousand kings of the Śakras, in the midst of the void, each scattered celestial flowers and spoke these words: "O noble son!

When this brahmin was performing the austerity of being scorched by the five fires, the radiance of that fire so overwhelmed all the ornaments and decorations of our palaces that they appeared like a mass of ink; it caused us to lose all attachment to them, and we immediately came to his side together with our retinues.

This brahmin has preached the Dharma for me, enabling me to attain mastery over my mind, mastery over afflictions, mastery over rebirth, mastery over all karmic obstructions, mastery over all samādhis, mastery over the articles of adornment, mastery over the span of life, and even mastery over all the Buddha-dharmas.
Furthermore, ten thousand kings of the Nirmāṇarati devas, in the midst of the sky, performed celestial music as an offering of respect and made these words:
"O son of good family!

When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, the radiance of that fire illuminated my palace, its various ornaments, and all the court ladies; it caused us to no longer experience sensual pleasure nor seek after it, making our bodies and minds supple. Thereupon, we came together with the multitude to the place where he was.

At that time, the brahmin preached the Dharma for me, enabling our minds to attain purity, clarity, wholesomeness, and flexibility; causing joy to arise within us, and even leading us to attain a pure body—the purity of the ten powers—and to give birth to infinite bodies, and even leading us to attain the Buddha-body, the Buddha-speech, the Buddha-voice, and the Buddha-mind, fully accomplishing the wisdom of all-knowledge.

Furthermore, ten thousand Tuṣita kings, sons of gods, and goddesses, along with immeasurable retinues, rained down various wonderful incenses from the midst of the sky, paid homage by prostrating themselves with their heads at his feet, and spoke these words:
“O Son of Good Family!
When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, it caused us gods and our retinues to lose all attachment to pleasure within our own palaces, and we went together to where he was.

Hearing his preaching of the Dharma enables us to be free from craving for sensory realms, to have few desires and be content, to give rise to joy in our hearts, to attain fulfillment of mind, to produce various roots of goodness, to resolve upon Bodhicitta, and even to bring all Buddha-dharmas to perfection.

Furthermore, ten thousand gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, together with their retinues, sons of gods, and daughters of gods, surrounded him from front and behind; in the midst of the air, they rained down māndārava flowers as an offering of reverent worship, and spoke these words:
"O son of good family!
When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, it caused us gods to lose our attachment to celestial music, and we went together to where he was.

At that time, the brahmin expounded for us how all phenomena are impermanent and subject to decay, leading us to renounce all sensual pleasures, causing us to sever arrogance and heedlessness, and inspiring us to love and delight in unsurpassed bodhi.
Furthermore, noble son!
