Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
In the eighth part of the thirty-ninth chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm," at that time,
after the youth Sudhana had heard the Dharma from the laywoman Acalā, he focused his mind on recollecting all her instructions, receiving them with full faith, and contemplating and examining them.

Traveling gradually through various kingdoms and towns, he arrived at the city of Vārāṇasī. At sunset, he entered that city, searching everywhere among the market stalls, neighborhoods, and the sides of the four-way intersections for the Parivrājaka wanderers.
To the east of the city there is a mountain named Sudarśana.
At the hour of midnight,
the youth Sudhana saw the grasses, trees, crags, and peaks upon its summit illuminated by a radiance as brilliant as the rising sun.
Having seen this, he was filled with great joy and thought to himself:
"I shall surely find a spiritual friend here.

He then departed from the city and ascended that mountain, where he saw the non-Buddhist practitioner walking slowly in meditation upon a level area of the mountaintop. His physical form was perfect and his majestic radiance shone so brightly that even the Great Brahmā King could not surpass it; he was surrounded by ten thousand hosts of Brahmās.
He went to where [the elder] was, prostrated with his head at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined before him, spoke these words: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice."
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will explain it to me! Sarvagāmin replied:
“Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family!

I have already established myself in the bodhisattva practice that reaches all places; I have already accomplished the samādhi-gate of universally observing the world; I have already accomplished the supernatural power of non-reliance and non-action; and I have already accomplished the universal gate of prajñāpāramitā.”

"Good son! Throughout all the various locations in the world, with their diverse forms and appearances, diverse modes of conduct and understanding, and all the realms of existence where beings pass away and are reborn—I am everywhere."
That is to say:

the realm of devas, the realm of nāgas, the realm of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, hell-beings, animals, the realm of King Yama, humans, non-humans, and so forth—all such realms; some abide in various views, some believe in the Two Vehicles, and others believe in and delight in the path of the Mahāyāna.
Among all these sentient beings, I benefit them through various skillful means and various gateways of wisdom.
That is to say:
for some, I expound upon the various arts and crafts of all the worlds, enabling them to attain the wisdom of the *dhāraṇī* of all skillful techniques;
For some, they expound the skillful means of the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) to enable them to fulfill the path to all-knowledge;
for others, they expound the various *pāramitās* to cause them to dedicate [their merit] toward the stage of all-knowledge;
and for others, they praise the great bodhicitta to ensure they do not lose their resolve for the unsurpassed way.
Sometimes, in order to praise the practices of all bodhisattvas and cause them to fulfill their vows to purify buddha-fields and deliver sentient beings;

sometimes, in order to expound upon the various retributions of suffering, such as those in the hells, resulting from the commission of evil deeds, so that they may develop a profound sense of weary detachment toward unwholesome karma;

or sometimes, in order to expound upon how making offerings to all Buddhas and planting roots of goodness will certainly result in the fruit of omniscience, so that they may give rise to a heart of joy.
In some cases, they praise and expound upon all the merits of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, causing beings to delight in the Buddha-body and seek all-knowledge;
in some cases, they praise and expound upon the majestic power of the Buddhas, causing them to aspire to and delight in the indestructible body of a Buddha;
and in some cases, they praise and expound upon the sovereign body of the Buddha, causing them to seek the Tathāgata’s great majestic essence that cannot be eclipsed by anything else.
"Furthermore, noble son!

Within this city of Tuṣāra, in every location and among all classes of people—whether men or women—I employ skillful means to manifest in forms identical to theirs, preaching the Dharma to them according to their needs."
All sentient beings are unable to know who I am or from where I have come; they are only intended to practice according to reality upon hearing this. Good son!
Just as he benefited sentient beings in this city, he likewise benefited all those dwelling in the cities, towns, and villages throughout Jambudvīpa, in every place where people reside.

“Good son! Within Jambudvīpa, there are ninety-six schools, each giving rise to divergent views and developing attachments; I have skillfully tamed them all therein, causing them to abandon every such view.
As it is with Jambudvīpa, so it is with the other four continents.”
As it is with the four continents, so it is with the trichiliocosm;

as it is with the trichiliocosm, so it is with the oceans of sentient beings in the infinite worlds of the ten directions. Within all of these, I manifest various physical bodies through various skillful means and various Dharma gates, according to the inclinations of the minds of those beings, preaching the Dharma with various voices and sounds to bring them benefit.
“Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva practice of reaching all places. As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, their bodies are equal in number to all sentient beings;

they attain a body that is non-differentiated from sentient beings, and with their transformation bodies, they enter universally into all realms of existence. They manifest birth in every location, appearing before all sentient beings; their pure radiance shines throughout the world, and they abide through all kalpas by means of unimpeded vows. They attain peerless practices like those of Indra’s net, constantly and diligently benefiting all sentient beings; they dwell together with them forever without attachment, remaining equanimous throughout the three periods of time, illuminating everywhere with the wisdom of selflessness, and observing all things with the treasury of great compassion.”
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? "Good son!
To the south of here, there is a land named:
It was vast;
there was a merchant who sold incense named Utpalaka.
"Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave.

At that time, by the instruction of his spiritual friend, the youth Sudhana disregarded body and life; he was not attached to wealth and treasures, took no pleasure in crowds of people, did not indulge in the five desires, felt no longing for his kinsmen, and held no weight for royal rank.

He desired only to transform and deliver all sentient beings, desired only to adorn and purify all Buddha-lands, desired only to make offerings to all Buddhas, desired only to realize and know the true nature of all phenomena, and desired only to cultivate and accumulate [virtues].
May all the great oceans of merit of all Bodhisattvas be fulfilled; may I never retreat from the cultivation of all merits;
may I constantly cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva throughout all kalpas by the power of great vows;
may I universally enter the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas; and may I, through a single gate of samādhi, universally...
I manifest the sovereign spiritual power of all samādhi-gates; I pray that within a single pore of the Buddha, I may behold all Buddhas without ever feeling weary or satisfied;
I pray that I may attain the light of wisdom of all dharmas and be able to uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas, single-mindedly seeking such merits of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Traveling by stages, he arrived at the kingdom of Vast and went to the householder’s residence. He prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood with palms joined, saying: “Noble One!

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to seek the equal wisdom of all Buddhas, desiring to fulfill the immeasurable great vows of all Buddhas, desiring to purify the supreme form-bodies of all Buddhas, desiring to behold the pure dharma-bodies of all Buddhas, desiring to know the vast wisdom-bodies of all Buddhas, desiring to purify and cultivate all the practices of Bodhisattvas, desiring to illuminate all the samādhis of Bodhisattvas, desiring to dwell securely in all the dhāraṇīs of Bodhisattvas, desiring to eliminate all obstacles whatsoever, and desiring to travel through all worlds in the ten directions; yet I do not yet know how a Bodhisattva should learn the Bodhisattva conduct, how a Bodhisattva should cultivate the Bodhisattva path, so as to give birth to the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
The elder said: "Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! You are indeed able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Noble son!"
I am skilled at discerning all fragrances and also know the methods for compounding all perfumes, namely:
all incenses, all burning incenses, all unguents, and all powdered incenses.

He also knows the origins from which all such kings of fragrances arise, and he thoroughly understands the various perfumes of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.

Furthermore, I thoroughly understand and discern the fragrances that treat various diseases, the fragrances that sever all evils, the fragrances that produce joy, the fragrances that increase afflictions, the fragrances that extinguish afflictions, the fragrances that cause attachment to the conditioned, the fragrances that cause weariness with and detachment from the conditioned, the fragrances that abandon pride and negligence, the fragrances that inspire the mind to recollect the Buddha, the fragrances that realize and understand the Dharma-gates, the fragrances enjoyed by the noble ones, the diverse fragrances of all Bodhisattvas, and the fragrances of all the Bodhisattva stages. Regarding such fragrances as these—their forms, characteristics, arising, manifestation, accomplishment, purity, peace, skillful means, spheres of activity, majestic power, functions, and their fundamental sources—I have attained complete mastery over them all.
“Good son! Among humans there is a fragrance called Elephant Treasury (Gajagarbha),
which is produced from the fighting of dragons.
If one burns a single pellet, a great cloud of incense will immediately arise, pervading the royal capital, and for seven days it will rain down fine fragrant rain.
If it touches the body, the body becomes golden;
if it touches clothing, palaces, or pavilions, they likewise all become golden.

If the wind carries [the fragrance] into the palaces and sentient beings smell it, for seven days and seven nights they will be filled with joy; their bodies and minds will be blissful, free from all illnesses, and they will not harm one another. They will be free from all sorrow and suffering, without alarm or fear, without distraction or anger, regarding one another with a heart of loving-kindness and with pure intentions.
Having known this, I preach the Dharma for them, causing them to resolve with certainty to give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. "Good son!
On Mount Malaya grows sandalwood incense known as "Ox-head";
if one anoints the body with it, even if one enters a pit of fire, the flames cannot burn them.
Good son! Within the ocean there is a fragrance named Invincible;
If one uses this to smear upon drums and various conch shells, when their sounds are produced, all enemy armies will naturally retreat and disperse. Good son!
From the banks of Lake Anavatapta emerges the agallochum incense, named:
As for Padmagarbha, a single pellet of its incense is as large as a sesame seed;
if it is burned, its fragrance pervades the entire Jambudvīpa realm, and all sentient beings who smell it are freed from all transgressions, their categories of precepts becoming pure.
Good son! On the Snowy Mountains there is a fragrance named Aruṇa;

If there are sentient beings who smell this fragrance, their minds will certainly become free from all defiled attachments; when I preach the Dharma for them, there are none who do not attain the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement.
"Good son! Within the realm of the rākṣasas there is an incense named Ocean Treasury;
this incense is used exclusively by wheel-turning kings."
If one burns a single pellet and uses it as incense, the king and his fourfold army will all ascend into the void.
Son of good family!
Among the gods of the Heaven of Good Dharma, there is an incense named:
Pure Adornment;
if one burns a single pellet to incense it, it causes the hearts of all the devas to turn toward the Buddha. Good son!
In the Suyāma Heaven there is an incense called Pure Treasury;
if one pellet is burned to perfume the air, the hosts of the Suyāma Heaven will all gather like clouds before that Heavenly King to listen to the Dharma together.
"Good son! In the Tuṣita Heaven there is a fragrance named Saindhava; "

Before the seat of a Bodhisattva bound to one more birth, he burned one pellet, which raised a great cloud of incense that pervaded the entire Dharma-realm and rained down all manner of offerings, making offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
"Good son! The Heaven of Skillful Transformations has an incense named 'Captivating the Mind';"
"If one burns a single pellet, for seven days there will be a universal rain of all manner of ornaments. Good son,
I know only this method of compounding incense."

As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who have distanced themselves from all evil habitual tendencies, who are untainted by worldly desires, who have forever severed the snares of the afflictions and Māras, who have transcended all realms of existence, who adorn themselves with the fragrance of wisdom, who are entirely without attachment to any world, who are fully accomplished in the precept of non-attachment, who possess pure wisdom free from attachment, who traverse the sphere of non-attachment, and who are entirely without clinging in all places—
their minds being equanimous, without attachment and without dependence— how could I possibly know their sublime conduct?
How can one describe their merits?
How can one manifest all their gates of pure precepts?
How can one demonstrate that their actions are free from error and failure?
"How do you distinguish their bodily, verbal, and mental conduct that is free from defilement? 'Good son!
To the south of here, there is a great city named:'"
There was a pavilion;
within it was a shipmaster named Vasiṣṭha.
"Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave.
At that time, the youth Sudhana headed toward the city of Lokeśvaragṛha, observing the road.
That is to say:

he observed whether the road was high or low, he observed whether the road was level or rugged, he observed whether the road was pure or defiled, and he observed whether the road was crooked or straight.
Traveling by stages, he reflected thus:
"I shall draw near to that spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).
A spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the practice of the bodhisattva path; it is the cause for accomplishing [the cultivation of]..."
This is the cause for accomplishing the practice of the path of the perfections; it is the cause for accomplishing the practice of the path that gathers in sentient beings;
it is the cause for accomplishing the practice of the path that enters the dharma-realm universally without obstruction;

it is the cause for accomplishing the practice that causes all sentient beings to eliminate false wisdom; it is the cause for accomplishing the practice that causes all sentient beings to depart from...
It is the cause for the path of pride; it is the cause for accomplishing the practice that causes all sentient beings to extinguish the afflictions;
it is the cause for accomplishing the practice that causes all sentient beings to abandon all views;
it is the cause for accomplishing the practice that causes all sentient beings to extract all thorns of evil; it is the accomplishment of the practice.
To cause all sentient beings to reach the causal path to the city of omniscience. Why is this?
Because it is through the presence of spiritual friends that one attains all wholesome dharmas.
"By the power of spiritual friends, one attains the path to omniscience;
therefore, spiritual friends are difficult to see and difficult to encounter. Thus he reflected.

Traveling by stages, he eventually arrived at that city and saw the shipmaster standing on the seashore outside the city gate, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of merchants and an immeasurable multitude of people, who were expounding the Dharma of the great ocean and skillfully revealing the ocean of the Buddha’s merits.
Having seen him, Sudhana went to his place, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined before him, spoke these words: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me! The boatman replied, "Excellent, excellent!

"Good son! You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Now you are further able to inquire about the cause for generating great wisdom; the cause for severing all causes of the suffering of birth and death; the cause for proceeding to the great jewel-island of omniscience; the cause for accomplishing the indestructible Mahāyāna; the cause for remaining far removed from the fears of birth and death characteristic of the two vehicles and dwelling in the whirlpools of various tranquil samādhis; the cause for the pure path that, mounting the chariot of great vows, performs the practices of a bodhisattva everywhere without obstruction; the cause for the pure path of indestructible wisdom adorned by the practices of a bodhisattva; the cause for the pure path of universally observing all dharmas of the ten directions without obstruction; and the cause for the pure path that swiftly enables entry into the ocean of omniscience."
“Good son! Here, on the coastal road of this city, I purely cultivate the bodhisattva practice of the banner of great compassion. Good son!”
Observing the impoverished sentient beings within Jambudvīpa, for their benefit, I practice various ascetic disciplines so that all their aspirations may be fully satisfied.
First, one satisfies their desires with worldly things;

then, one bestows the wealth of the Dharma to bring them joy, to cause them to cultivate meritorious deeds, to give rise to the path of wisdom, to increase the power of their roots of goodness, to inspire the bodhicitta, to purify their bodhi-vow, to strengthen the power of great compassion, to cultivate the path that extinguishes birth and death, to engender the practice of never wearying of birth and death, to gather in the ocean of all sentient beings, to cultivate the ocean of all merits, to illuminate the ocean of all dharmas, to behold the ocean of all Buddhas, and to enter the ocean of the knowledge of all-knowledge.
"Good son! Abiding here, I contemplate in this way, attend to things in this way, and thus benefit all sentient beings. Good son!"
I know all the jewel islands in the ocean, all the locations of jewels, all categories of jewels, and all varieties of jewels.
I know how to purify all jewels, drill all jewels, extract all jewels, and fashion all jewels.
I know all jewel vessels, all uses of jewels, all realms of jewels, and all radiances of jewels.
I know all the abodes of the nāgas, all the abodes of the yakṣas, and all the abodes of the bhūtas; I skillfully avoid them all to escape their various perils.
He also skillfully distinguishes and knows the eddies and whirlpools, the shallow and deep, the distance of the waves, and the various differences in the color and quality of the water.

He also skillfully distinguishes and knows the movements and degrees of the sun, moon, and stars; the day and night, the morning and evening, and the lengthening or shortening of the shadows and time-measures.
He also knows whether the iron and wood of the ship are strong or brittle, whether its mechanisms are stiff or smooth, the volume of the water, and whether the winds are headwinds or tailwinds;
thus, he clearly understands all signs of safety and danger, proceeding when it is appropriate to proceed and stopping when it is appropriate to stop.
"Good son! Having accomplished such wisdom, I am constantly able to benefit all sentient beings. Good son!"

I shall transport the assembly of merchants on an excellent ship along a secure path, further teaching them the Dharma to bring them joy, leading them to the Isle of Jewels so that they may be fully provided with all manner of precious treasures, and thereafter escorting them back to Jambudvīpa.
"Good son! I navigate this great ship back and forth in this manner, never allowing it to suffer even the slightest damage.

If there are sentient beings who see my body or hear my Dharma, I cause them to never again fear the ocean of birth and death; they will surely enter the ocean of all-knowledge, surely be able to exhaust the ocean of all cravings and desires, be able to illuminate the ocean of the three periods of time with the light of wisdom, be able to end the ocean of suffering of all sentient beings, be able to purify the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings, quickly be able to adorn and purify the ocean of all lands, universally be able to travel to the great oceans of the ten directions, universally know the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings, universally understand the ocean of the practices of all sentient beings, and universally accord with the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings."
“Good son! I have attained only this practice of the Banner of Great Compassion;
yet for those who see me, hear me, dwell with me, or remember me, all such encounters are never in vain.”

As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who are skillfully able to traverse the great ocean of birth and death; who remain unstained by the ocean of all afflictions; who are able to relinquish the ocean of all false views; who are able to contemplate the ocean of the nature of all phenomena; who are able to gather the ocean of sentient beings through the four means of attraction; who have already well established themselves in the ocean of omniscience; who are able to extinguish the ocean of attachments of all sentient beings; who are able to dwell with equanimity throughout the ocean of all times; who are able to deliver the ocean of sentient beings through their supernormal powers;
and who are able to discipline the ocean of sentient beings according to the proper time—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Ramanīya;
Among them is an elder named Anuttarajaya. Go to him and ask:
"How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and wept with tears streaming down; never wearying in his quest for a spiritual friend, he took his leave and departed.

At that time, the youth Sudhana gave rise to a mind of great loving-kindness that pervades all, and a mind of great compassion that moistens and nurtures, continuing without interruption. Adorned with the two kinds of merit and wisdom, he cast off all defilements of affliction and realized the equality of all phenomena. His mind was free from high or low; he extracted the thorns of unwholesomeness, extinguished all hindrances, and made firm diligence his ramparts and moats. He took profound samādhi as his garden, used the sunlight of wisdom to shatter the darkness of ignorance, used the wind of skillful means to open the flowers of wisdom, and filled the Dharma-realm with unimpeded vows. With a mind constantly manifesting entry into the city of omniscience, he thus sought the path of the Bodhisattva.
Traveling by stages, he arrived within that city.

He saw Anuttarajaya in the Great Adorned Banner无忧林 (Aśoka) Grove to the east of the city, surrounded by immeasurable merchants and hundreds of thousands of householders as he adjudicated various human affairs;

he was preaching the Dharma for them, causing them to forever uproot all pride (*māna*), to be free from "I" and "mine," to renounce their accumulated hoards, to extinguish the stains of stinginess and envy, to attain purity of mind, to be free from all turbidity, to obtain the power of pure faith, to always delight in seeing the Buddha, to receive and uphold the Buddha-Dharma, to give rise to the power of a bodhisattva, to initiate bodhisattva practices, to enter bodhisattva samādhis, to attain bodhisattva wisdom, to abide in bodhisattva right mindfulness, and to increase the bodhisattva’s aspiration and resolve.

At that time, after the youth Sudhana had observed the elder preaching the Dharma to the assembly, he prostrated himself on the ground, bowing at his feet. After a long while, he rose and said: "Noble One!
I am Sudhana! I am Sudhana!
I am solely seeking the conduct of a bodhisattva; how does a bodhisattva learn the conduct of a bodhisattva?

How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva path? While practicing and training accordingly, how can they always be able to transform and deliver all sentient beings; always be able to manifest before and behold all Buddhas; always be able to hear and receive all Buddha-dharmas; always be able to uphold and maintain all Buddha-dharmas; always be able to enter all Dharma-gates; enter all lands to learn the bodhisattva practices; dwell through all kalpas cultivating the bodhisattva path; be able to know the spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas; be able to receive the protective mindfulness of all Tathāgatas; and be able to attain the wisdom of all Tathāgatas?
At that time, the elder said to Sudhana:
"Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"
"You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Son of good family!
I have accomplished the power of the bodhisattva practice-door that reaches all places—a spiritual power that is non-reliant and effortless."
"Good son! What is the bodhisattva practice gate that reaches all places? Good son!"
Within this trichiliocosm, among all sentient beings of the desire realm— namely, all those in the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
all in the Yāma Heaven, all in the Tuṣita Heaven, all in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, all in the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, and all in the Heaven of Māra— [I am the foremost].
And among all other devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas,
gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
and among all sentient beings dwelling in villages, camps, cities, towns, and every other habitation.
And he preaches the Dharma for them, causing them to abandon what is contrary to the Dharma, causing them to cease contentious debate, causing them to eliminate strife and warfare,
causing them to stop anger and competition, causing them to break the knots of enmity, causing them to untie their bonds, causing them to escape from prison,
causing them to be free from fear, and causing them to sever all evil karma, from killing up to wrong views— this is impossible.
He causes all improper activities to be prohibited;
he causes them to practice all wholesome dharmas and to study all arts and crafts, thereby bringing benefit to the world;
for their sake, he analyzes various treatises to inspire joy and bring about gradual maturation.
Following along with those of external paths, I preach the supreme wisdom for them, causing them to sever all views and enter the Buddha-dharma.
Even unto all the Brahmā devas of the form realm, I likewise preach for them the Dharma that transcends and surpasses [their own].

Just as I have taught here in this trichiliocosm, so too throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields in the ten directions, I have everywhere taught the Dharma of the Buddhas, the Dharma of Bodhisattvas, the Dharma of Śrāvakas, and the Dharma of Pratyekabuddhas;
I have taught of the hells, of sentient beings in the hells, and of the path leading to the hells;
I have taught of animals, the various distinctions among animals, the suffering experienced by animals, and the path leading to the animal realm.
He speaks of the world of King Yama; he speaks of the suffering in the world of King Yama; he speaks of the path leading to the world of King Yama.
He speaks of the world of devas; he speaks of the bliss in the world of devas; he speaks of the path leading to the world of devas. He speaks of the world of humans;
he speaks of the suffering and bliss in the world of humans; he speaks of the path leading to the world of humans.

Desiring to reveal and manifest the merits of bodhisattvas; desiring to cause them to abandon the faults and afflictions of birth and death; desiring to cause them to know and see the sublime merits of those who possess all-knowledge; desiring to cause them to know that within the various realms of existence beings suffer through delusion; desiring to cause them to know and see the unobstructed Dharma; desiring to demonstrate the causes for the arising of all worlds; desiring to demonstrate that the cessation of all worlds is bliss; desiring to cause sentient beings to abandon all conceptual attachments; desiring to cause them to realize the Buddha’s reliance-free Dharma; and desiring to cause them to forever extinguish the wheel of all afflictions and to be able to turn the Wheel of the Tathāgata’s Dharma—I preach such a Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
“Good son! I only know this dharma-door of purifying the bodhisattva practice that reaches all places, which possesses the power of spiritual penetrations that are non-reliant and effortless.
Just as all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are fully endowed with all sovereign supernormal powers and are able to travel everywhere to all buddha-fields, attaining the stage of the Universal Eye;

hearing all sounds and speech, universally entering the wisdom that is sovereign over all dharmas, being free from conflict, and possessing incomparable courage and vigor; emitting the sound of equanimity with their broad and long tongues;
their bodies being wondrous and excellent, identical to those of all bodhisattvas, and ultimately non-dual and without distinction from all Tathāgatas;
The body of wisdom is vast and expansive, universally entering the three periods of time; its sphere of activity is boundless, equal to empty space.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
“Good son! To the south of here, there is a land named Sūna;”
In that land there is a city named Karṇikāvana;
there is a bhikṣuṇī named:
Siṃhaviḍambana, go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and took his leave.
At that time, Sudhana traveled by stages until he reached that city, where he searched everywhere for this bhikṣuṇī.
Countless people all said to him: "Good man!
This bhikṣuṇī is preaching the Dharma for the benefit of immeasurable sentient beings within the Sūryaprabha Garden, which was donated by King Prasenajit."
Then, the youth Sudhana went to that garden and surveyed it thoroughly.
Within the garden, he saw a great tree named Pūrṇacandra (Full Moon),
shaped like a multi-storied pavilion, emitting a great radiance that illuminated an area of one yojana.
He saw a leafy tree named Universal Canopy,
shaped like a parasol, emitting a deep blue radiance like lapis lazuli;
he saw a flowering tree named:
The Flower Treasury [World-System] is vast and lofty in form, like the king of snow mountains; it rains down various wondrous flowers without end, like the Pārijātaka tree in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
Furthermore, he saw a tree of ambrosial fruit, shaped like a mountain of gold, constantly emitting light, and fully endowed with all kinds of various fruits;
he also saw a mani-jewel tree named Vairocana-garbha,
its form beyond compare, with a heart-king mani-jewel at its summit and adorned throughout by mani-jewels of incalculable colors and forms.
Furthermore, there are clothing trees,
named "Pure," adorned with various colored garments hanging down;
furthermore, there are musical instrument trees, named:
The sound of their joyful singing was exquisite and surpassed all celestial music;
furthermore, there were fragrance trees named "Universal Adornment," which constantly emitted sublime scents that perfumed the ten directions without obstruction.

Within the garden, there are further springs, streams, and ponds, all adorned with the seven treasures. Black sandalwood mud accumulates within them, while exquisite golden sand is spread across their bottoms. They are filled to the brim with water possessing the eight virtues, and blue lotuses (*utpala*), red lotuses (*padma*), yellow lotuses (*kumuda*), and white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*) cover their surfaces. Countless jewel trees stand in rows all around.

Beneath each of the jewel trees were spread lion thrones, adorned with various kinds of exquisite jewels, covered with celestial robes, perfumed with various wonderful incenses, draped with precious silk streamers, and provided with precious canopies. Nets of Jambu-river gold completely covered them above, and as jeweled bells swayed gently, they produced sublime sounds.

In some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones of the Lotus-Treasury; in some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones of the Fragrance-King Mani-Treasury; in some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones of the Dragon-Adorned Mani-King Treasury; in some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones of the Jewel-Lion-Cluster Mani-King Treasury; in some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones of the Vairocana Mani-King Treasury; and in some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones of the Universal-Vairocana Mani-King Treasury.
Each of these individual thrones was surrounded by one hundred thousand jewel lion thrones, each of which was endowed with immeasurable adornments.
This great garden is filled everywhere with various jewels, like a treasure island in the great ocean.
Kāliṅga cloth is spread upon its ground—supple, exquisite, and capable of producing a pleasant touch; when stepped upon, it sinks to the ankle, and when lifted, it returns to its original state.

Countless birds emit harmonious and elegant sounds, and the precious sandalwood groves are magnificently adorned. Various wonderful flowers rain down perpetually without end, just like Śakra’s Garden of Miscellaneous Flowers.
The incomparable king of incenses perfumes everything universally, like Śakra’s Hall of Good Dharma (*Sudharmā*).

From the trees of music, the precious *tāla* trees, and the nets of various jeweled bells, exquisite sounds emerge, like the songs produced by the celestial maidens of excellent speech in the realm of Maheśvara.
Various wish-fulfilling trees were adorned with the hanging display of diverse, exquisite garments, resembling the great ocean.
There were hundreds of thousands of pavilions of immeasurable colors, adorned with myriad jewels, like the Great City of Sudarśana in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
The precious canopy spread afar like the peak of Mount Sumeru;
its radiance shone everywhere like the palace of the Brahma King.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld this great garden, with its immeasurable merits and manifold adornments—all of which were accomplished through the karmic retribution of Bodhisattvas, arisen from supramundane roots of goodness, and flowing forth from the merit of making offerings to all Buddhas. Nothing in any world could equal it; all of this was achieved by the Bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā through her realization that phenomena are like illusions and her accumulation of vast, pure merit and virtuous karma.
The devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, as well as immeasurable sentient beings from the trichiliocosm, all entered this garden without it becoming cramped.
Why was this? It was because of the inconceivable power of the bhikṣuṇī’s majestic spiritual authority.

At that time, Sudhana saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā seated upon great lion thrones beneath all the various jewel trees. Her physical form was upright and majestic; her deportment was tranquil; her faculties were well-tamed and harmonious, like those of a great elephant king;
her mind was free from defilement, like a pure pool;
she universally fulfilled all requests, like a wish-fulfilling gem.
Untainted by worldly dharmas, like a lotus flower;
with a mind free from fear, like a lion king;
upholding the pure precepts so as to be unshakable, like Mount Sumeru.
It causes the minds of those who behold it to attain refreshing clarity, like a king of exquisite fragrance;
it can eliminate the heat of the afflictions of sentient beings, like the wondrous sandalwood from the Snowy Mountains;
when sentient beings behold it, all their sufferings are extinguished, like the sovereign medicinal herb Sudarśana.
Those who behold him do not see him as empty, like the deity Vairocana;
he is able to nurture the sprouts of all roots of goodness, like a fertile and rich field.
Seated upon each and every throne, the assemblies differ, and the Dharma-gates he expounds likewise vary accordingly.
Or she may see her seated, surrounded by a host of Śuddhāvāsa devas with the Great Lord Maheśvara as their leader;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a Dharma gate called "Inexhaustible Liberation."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by a multitude of Brahma devas, with the Brahma King as their chief, whom they all cherished;
for these bhikṣuṇīs she taught a dharma-gate called the "Pure Wheel of Vocal Sounds with Universal Gate Differentiations."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by the sons and daughters of the gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, with the Lord of that heaven as their chief;
for these she preached a Dharma-door named "The Pure Mind of a Bodhisattva."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by devas and devīs of the Sunirmita Heaven, with the Sunirmita King as their leader;
for these beings, this bhikṣuṇī was preaching a dharma-gate named "The Fine Adornment of All Dharmas."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by the sons and daughters of the gods of Tuṣita Heaven, with the King of Tuṣita at their head;
for these she preached a Dharma-door named "The Revolving Treasury of the Mind."
Or she may see her seated on a throne, surrounded by the sons and daughters of the Suyāma devas, with the King of the Suyāma devas at their head;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a dharma-gate called "Boundless Adornment."
Or they may see her seated, surrounded by the sons and daughters of the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three, with Śakra Devānām Indra as their leader;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a dharma-gate called the "Gate of Disenchantment."

In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by the naga kings Śataraśmi, Nanda, Upananda, Mānasvin, Elāpattra, Anavatapta, and other sons and daughters of the nagas, with the naga king Sāgara as their leader;
for these she was preaching a dharma-gate called "The Radiant Adornment of the Buddha’s Sphere of Supernatural Powers."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of yakṣas with the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa as their leader;
for them, this bhikṣuṇī was preaching a dharma-gate called "The Treasury that Protects and Saves All Sentient Beings."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of gandharvas, with the Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra as their leader;
for these she preached a dharma-gate called "Inexhaustible Joy."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of asuras, with the asura king Rāhu at their head;
for them, this bhikṣuṇī was preaching a dharma-gate called "The Gate of Wisdom for Swift Adornment of the Dharma Realm."
Or she may see her sitting on a seat, surrounded by a host of garuḍas, with the garuḍa king Citihasta as their leader;
this bhikṣuṇī is expounding for them a dharma-gate called "Terrorizing the Ocean of All Existences."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of kinnaras, with the great tree-king Kinnara-rāja at their head;
for these she preached a dharma-door named "The Radiance of the Buddha’s Conduct."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of mahoragas, with the mahoraga king Āmra as their leader;
for them, this bhikṣuṇī expounded a Dharma gate called "Generating a Mind of Joyful Delight toward the Buddha."
Or she may see her seated, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of men and women;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a dharma-gate named "Excellence of Practice."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of rākṣasas, with the Great Tree Rākṣasa King— who constantly robs others of their vital essence—
as their leader; for these she preached a Dharma gate called "Generating a Mind of Compassion."
In some places he saw her seated, surrounded by sentient beings who have faith and delight in the Śrāvaka vehicle;
for these, the bhikṣuṇī was preaching a dharma-gate named "Light of Supreme Wisdom."
Or she may be seen seated, surrounded by sentient beings who have faith and delight in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a Dharma gate called "The Vast Radiance of the Buddha's Virtues."
Or she may be seen seated, surrounded by sentient beings who have faith and delight in the Mahāyāna;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a dharma-gate called the "Gate of the Radiant Wisdom of the Samādhi of Universal Doors."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas who had first resolved their minds on enlightenment;
this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a dharma-gate called "The Assembly of All Buddhas' Vows."
In some places he saw her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the second stage;
for them, this bhikṣuṇī was preaching a dharma-gate named "Stainless Wheel."
Or she may see her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the third stage;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a dharma-gate named "Adornment of Tranquility."
Or she may see her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the fourth stage;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching for them a dharma-gate called "Giving Birth to the Realm of All-Knowledge."
Or she may see her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the fifth stage,
as this bhikṣuṇī teaches them a dharma-gate called "The Treasury of Exquisite Flowers."
In some places he saw her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the sixth stage;
this bhikṣuṇī was teaching them a dharma-gate called the "Vairocana Treasury."
Or she may see her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the seventh stage,
as this bhikṣuṇī teaches them a dharma-gate called "The Stage of Universal Adornment."
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the eighth stage;
for them, this bhikṣuṇī was preaching a dharma-gate called "The Body of the Realm of the Entire Dharmadhātu."
Or she may see her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the ninth stage;
this bhikṣuṇī is expounding for them a dharma-gate named "The Adornment of the Power of Non-Apprehension."
Or he may see her seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the tenth stage;
this bhikṣuṇī is preaching a dharma-door called the "Unobstructed Wheel."
Or they may see her seated, surrounded by Vajrapāṇi spirits;
this bhikṣuṇī is expounding for them a Dharma gate called "Vajra-Wisdom Nārāyaṇa Adornment."

The youth Sudhana, having seen all these sentient beings of every realm who were already matured, already tamed, and capable of serving as vessels for the Dharma, all entered this garden and sat down, surrounding him beneath their respective seats.

The bhikṣuṇī Siṃhahanu expounded the Dharma according to the differences in their inclinations, understandings, superiorities, and inferiorities, enabling them to attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
For what reason?

This bhikṣuṇī entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Universal Eye Renunciation and Attainment," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Expounding All Buddha-Dharmas," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Differentiation of the Dharma Realm," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Shattering All Obstructive Wheels," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Generating the Wholesome Minds of All Sentient Beings," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Exquisite Adornment," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Unobstructed Treasury of Reality," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Perfection of the Dharma Realm," the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Treasury of the Mind," and the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Universal Source Treasury. With these ten gates of the perfection of wisdom as her foremost, she entered countless millions of such gates of the perfection of wisdom.

All the bodhisattvas and sentient beings within this Sunlight Garden were first inspired to resolve their minds on awakening by the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā; they have upheld the true Dharma, contemplated and practiced it, and attained non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, seeing the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā’s gardens, her seats, her walking paths, her assemblies, her supernormal powers, and her eloquence, and further hearing this inconceivable dharma-gate, his mind was moistened by the vast clouds of Dharma; he then formed this thought:
“I shall circumambulate her to the right hundreds of thousands of times.”
At that time, the bhikṣuṇī emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated the park and the assembly’s adornments.
Sudhana immediately saw himself and all the trees within the grove circumambulating this bhikṣuṇī to the right, passing through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of circuits.
Having completed his circumambulation, the youth Sudhana stood with palms joined and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva."
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain it to me! The bhikṣuṇī said:
“Good son! I have attained a liberation named ‘Accomplishing All-Knowledge.’”
Sudhana said: "Noble One! For what reason is he named:?"
"How does one achieve all-knowledge? The bhikṣuṇī said, "Noble son!"
"This light of wisdom universally illumines all phenomena of the three periods of time within a single thought-moment.
Sudhana said: "Noble One!"
"What is the sphere of this light of wisdom? The bhikṣuṇī replied, "Noble son!"
Having entered this gate of the light of wisdom, I attained the King of Samādhis that gives birth to all dharmas;

by means of this samādhi, I obtained a mind-made body and went to the Tuṣita palaces in all worlds throughout the ten directions, where Bodhisattvas bound to one more birth reside. Before each and every Bodhisattva, I manifested bodies as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, and from each body, I performed offerings as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
That is to say:

manifesting the bodies of celestial kings up to the bodies of human kings, I hold aloft clouds of flowers, clouds of garlands, burning incense, ointment incense, and powdered incense; as well as robes, necklaces, banners, pennants, silk canopies, jeweled nets, jeweled curtains, jeweled treasuries, and jeweled lamps—all such articles of adornment, I hold them all and offer them in worship.

Just as I made offerings to the Bodhisattvas dwelling in the Tuṣita heaven, so too did I make such offerings to each and every Tathāgata—whether they were dwelling in the womb, emerging from the womb, living as householders, leaving the home life, proceeding to the site of enlightenment, attaining equal and perfect awakening, turning the wheel of the true Dharma, or entering into parinirvāṇa—and likewise during the intervals between these stages, whether they were dwelling in celestial palaces, dragon palaces, or even human palaces.
If there are sentient beings who know that I thus make offerings to the Buddha, they shall all attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
if there are sentient beings who come to my place, I shall immediately expound the Prajñāpāramitā for them.
“Good son! I see all sentient beings without discriminating the marks of sentient beings, because my eye of wisdom sees clearly;
I hear all speech without discriminating the marks of speech, because my mind has no attachments.”
They behold all Tathāgatas without discriminating the marks of a Tathāgata, because they have thoroughly realized the Dharma-body;
they sustain all wheels of the Dharma without discriminating the marks of the wheel of the Dharma, because they have awakened to the self-nature of phenomena;
and in a single thought-moment they universally know all phenomena without discriminating the marks of various phenomena, because they know that phenomena are like illusions.
“Good son! I know only this liberation of accomplishing all-knowledge. As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, their minds are free from discrimination and they universally know all phenomena;

sitting upright in a single body, they fill the Dharma-realm; within their own bodies they manifest all lands; in a single thought-moment they reach the abodes of all Buddhas; within their own bodies they universally manifest the spiritual powers of all Buddhas; with a single hair they lift up unspeakably many Buddha-worlds; within a single pore of their own body they manifest the formation and destruction of unspeakable worlds; in a single thought-moment they dwell together with unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings; and in a single thought-moment they enter into unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all kalpas.”
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct? "Good son!
To the south of here, there is a land named:
perilous difficulties;
in this land there is a city named Jewel Adornment;
Among them is a woman named Vasumitrā. Go to her and ask:
"How should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and then took his leave and departed.

The Ninth Part of the Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm, the Thirty-ninth, Part Nine.

At that time, the youth Sudhana’s mind was illuminated and opened by the light of great wisdom; he contemplated and observed the nature of all dharmas, attained the *dhāraṇī* gate of understanding all speech and sounds, attained the *dhāraṇī* gate of upholding all wheels of the Dharma, attained the power of great compassion that serves as a refuge for all sentient beings, attained the gate of light for observing the principles and meanings of all dharmas, attained pure vows that fill the entire dharma realm, attained the light of wisdom that universally illumines all dharmas throughout the ten directions, attained the sovereign power to universally adorn all worlds, and attained the vow to universally initiate the complete karma of all bodhisattvas.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at the city of Ratnavyūha in the perilous kingdom of Durgama, searching everywhere for the maiden Vasumitrā.
There were people in the city who did not know of this woman’s merit and wisdom, and they thought to themselves:

"This youth has tranquil faculties and clear intelligence; he is neither deluded nor distracted. He gazes steadily for a full fathom without weariness or fatigue, free from attachment. His eyes do not blink and his mind is unmoving; he is profound and vast, like the great ocean."

One should not harbor thoughts of lustful attachment or perverted views toward this woman, Vāsuladattā; one should not conceive notions of purity or desire, nor should one be captivated by her physical beauty.

"This youth does not engage in the conduct of Māra, does not enter the realm of Māra, does not sink into the mire of desire, and is not bound by Māra; since he is already capable of refraining from what ought not to be done, with what intention does he seek this girl?"
Among them, there was one who had previously known that this woman possessed wisdom, who said to Sudhana:
"Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family!"
That you are now able to seek out and search for the woman Vasumitrā, you have already attained vast and excellent benefit.
Son of good family!

You should resolutely seek the state of Buddhahood; you should resolutely desire to act as a refuge for all sentient beings; you should resolutely desire to extract the poisonous arrows of craving from all sentient beings; and you should resolutely desire to shatter all notions of purity regarding female forms held by all sentient beings.
“Good son! The woman Vasumitrā dwells in her own home, located north of the marketplace within this city.
When the youth Sudhana heard these words, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he then proceeded to her gate.
He beheld that residence, vast and magnificent, with jeweled walls, jeweled trees, and jeweled moats, each surrounded by tenfold enclosures.

Within these jeweled moats, fragrant waters overflowed, with golden sand spread upon the ground; celestial jewel-flowers—utpala, padma, kumuda, and puṇḍarīka—completely covered the surface of the water.

Palaces and pavilions were distributed everywhere, with gates, portals, windows, and casements set in alternating rows, all adorned with decorative nets and bells, and fully arrayed with banners and streamers made of countless rare and wondrous treasures.

The ground is made of lapis lazuli, interspersed with various jewels; it is perfumed with burning aloeswood and anointed with sandalwood. Suspended from above are clusters of precious bells that produce melodic sounds when stirred by the wind, while celestial flowers are scattered, covering the entire ground.
Its manifold splendors and beauties are beyond description; there are hundreds of thousands of treasuries of rare gems, and ten great groves serve as its adornments.

At that time, Sudhana saw this woman, whose countenance was dignified and majestic, whose physical marks were perfect, and whose skin was golden in color. Her eyes and hair were deep blue; she was neither tall nor short, neither coarse nor delicate, such that no human or celestial being in the realm of desire could compare with her.
Her voice was exquisite and transcended all the Brahma worlds; she possessed the full range of all sentient beings' diverse languages and sounds, understanding them all without exception.
She had profoundly mastered the meaning of words, was skillful in discourse, had attained the wisdom of illusion, and had entered the gate of expedient means.
His body was adorned with various necklaces of many jewels and all manner of ornaments, and he wore upon his head a crown made of wish-fulfilling *maṇi* gems;
furthermore, he was surrounded by immeasurable retinues who shared the same roots of goodness, identical practices and vows, and possessed an inexhaustible treasury of great merit.
At that time, the woman Vasumitrā emitted a vast radiance from her body, which universally illuminated all the palaces within the residence;
those who encountered this light found their bodies cooled and refreshed.
At that time, Sudhana went before him, prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct."
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Holy One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will explain it to me! He then replied:
“Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called ‘Transcending the Limit of Desire,’ by which I manifest my body according to their inclinations and desires.”
If a deva sees me, I appear as a celestial maiden, with a form and radiance unsurpassed and peerless;
likewise, even when humans, non-humans, and others see me, I manifest as a human or non-human maiden, appearing to each according to their inclinations so that all may behold me.

"If there are sentient beings who, being entangled by the desires of their minds, come to me, I preach the Dharma for them; having heard the Dharma, they become free from greed and attain the Bodhisattva samādhi of the unattached realm.
If there are sentient beings who see me even for a moment, they become free from greed and attain the Bodhisattva samādhi of joy.
If there are sentient beings who speak with me even for a moment, they become free from greed and attain the Bodhisattva samādhi of unimpeded sound."
If there are sentient beings who briefly take my hand, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Universally Visiting All Buddha-fields;
if there are sentient beings who briefly ascend my seat, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Radiance of Liberation;
if there are sentient beings who briefly gaze upon me, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Tranquil Adornment.
If there are sentient beings who see me yawn, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi for Subduing Non-Buddhists;
if there are sentient beings who see my eyes blink, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Radiance of the Buddha’s Realm;
if there are sentient beings who embrace me, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Gathering All Sentient Beings and Never Abandoning Them.
If there are sentient beings who kiss my lips, they shall be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi for Increasing the Treasury of Merit for All Sentient Beings.

Any sentient beings who draw near to me shall all dwell at the limit of freedom from desire and enter the Bodhisattva Stage of Omniscience, attaining the unimpeded liberation that manifests before them.
Sudhana said, "Noble One,
what roots of goodness have you planted and what meritorious deeds have you cultivated to achieve such sovereign mastery? He replied:
“Good son! I recall that in the past, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Uccagāmin (High Conduct);”
The capital city of that king was named Wondrous Gate (Sudvāra). Good son!

Out of compassion for sentient beings, that Tathāgata of Exalted Conduct entered the royal city; as he stepped upon its threshold, the entire city shook, suddenly becoming vast and expansive, adorned with myriad jewels. Immeasurable lights shone upon one another, various precious flowers were strewn across the ground, celestial music played in unison, and all the devas filled the void of space.
"Good son! At that time, I was the wife of a householder, named Śrīmati; "
Witnessing the Buddha’s supernatural power, her mind attained awakening; she then went with her husband to the place where the Buddha was and made an offering of a single precious coin.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī was serving as the Buddha’s attendant and expounded the Dharma for me, causing me to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“Good son! I know only this bodhisattva liberation of the limit of detachment from greed.
As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they have accomplished boundless wisdom of skillful means; their treasury is vast, and their sphere of activity is peerless.”
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? "Good son!
To the south of here, there is a city named:
Sudatta; among them was a lay devotee named Viśvantara,
who constantly made offerings at the stūpa of the Buddha Candanāsanarāja.
"Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave.

At that time, the youth Sudhana traveled by stages until he reached the city of Supāraga. He went to the house of the lay devotee, prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me! The householder replied, "Good son!..."
I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called "The Limit of Non-Nirvāṇa. Good son!
I do not give rise to the thought:
"The Tathāgata has already entered parinirvāṇa," or "The Tathāgata is currently entering parinirvāṇa," or "The Tathāgata will enter parinirvāṇa."

"I know that among all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, in all worlds throughout the ten directions, there is ultimately none who enters parinirvāṇa; it is only for the sake of taming sentient beings that they manifest such a display."
“Good son! When I opened the door of the Tathāgata’s stūpa containing the sandalwood throne, I attained a samādhi named ‘The Inexhaustibility of the Buddha-seed.’”
“Good son! In every thought-moment I enter this samādhi, and in every thought-moment I come to know all immeasurable and most excellent matters. Sudhana said:
“What is the objective sphere (*gocara*) of this samādhi?
The householder replied, “Good son!
Entering this samādhi, I saw, in their proper sequence, all the Buddhas of this world, namely:
Buddha Kāśyapa, Buddha Kanakamuni, Buddha Krakucchanda, Buddha Śikhin, Buddha Vipaśyin, Buddha Tiṣya, Buddha Puṣya, Buddha Anuttarajaya, and Buddha Anuttarapadma;

with these as their leaders, in a single thought-moment, I saw one hundred Buddhas, one thousand Buddhas, one hundred thousand Buddhas, ten million Buddhas, a billion Buddhas, ten billion Buddhas, a hundred billion Buddhas, an ayuta of billions of Buddhas, nayuta of billions of Buddhas, and even as many Buddhas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable worlds—all of them, I saw in succession.

I also see those Buddhas from their initial generation of the mind, through their planting of various roots of goodness, their acquisition of supreme spiritual powers, their fulfillment of great vows, their practice of wondrous conduct, their perfection of the *pāramitās*, their entry into the bodhisattva stages, their attainment of pure patience, their subduing of the armies of Māra, their realization of perfect enlightenment, the purity of their lands, their being surrounded by assemblies, their emission of great light, their turning of the wonderful wheel of Dharma, and their miraculous manifestations;
all these various distinctions I am able to maintain, I am able to remember, I am able to observe, and I can analyze and reveal them.
All Buddhas of the future, such as Maitreya Buddha, and all Buddhas of the present, such as Vairocana Buddha, are likewise entirely so.

Just as in this world, so it is in all worlds throughout the ten directions: all Buddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the assemblies of bodhisattvas of the three periods of time are likewise entirely so.
“Good son! I have attained only this Bodhisattva liberation of the limit of non-parinirvāṇa.

As for the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who with the wisdom of a single thought universally know the three periods of time, and in a single thought enter all samādhis; whose minds are constantly illuminated by the sun of the Tathāgata’s wisdom; who have no discrimination regarding any phenomena; who realize that all Buddhas are entirely equal, and that the Tathāgata, myself, and all sentient beings are identical and without duality; who know that the self-nature of all phenomena is pure, being without thought or movement, yet are able to universally enter all worlds, free from all discrimination, dwelling in the seal of the Buddha-dharma, and are able to awaken all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm;”
How then could I know or describe their meritorious conduct? "Good son,
to the south of here there is a mountain named:
Potalaka; there dwells a bodhisattva named Avalokiteśvara.
Go to him and ask:
"How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then he spoke in verse:
“Upon the sea there is a mountain where many sages and worthies dwell; composed of various jewels, it is exceedingly pure.
Flowers, fruits, and groves fill it everywhere, and springs, streams, ponds, and marshes are all fully present.”
The heroic being Avalokiteśvara, for the benefit of sentient beings, dwells upon this mountain;
you should go and inquire about all his merits, and he will show you the great skillful means.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and gazing up at him with earnest devotion, took his leave and departed.

At that time, Sudhana reflected single-mindedly upon the instructions of that householder; he entered the treasury of the bodhisattva’s liberation, attained the power of a bodhisattva’s ability to recollect according to thought, remembered the successive appearance of those Buddhas, recalled the continuous succession of those Buddhas, maintained the sequence of the names of those Buddhas, contemplated the sublime Dharma taught by those Buddhas, knew the complete adornments of those Buddhas, beheld those Buddhas attaining perfect enlightenment, and understood the inconceivable activities of those Buddhas.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at that mountain and searched everywhere for this great bodhisattva.

To its western side, within the rocky valleys, he saw streams of water winding and reflecting light, where the forests were lush and verdant, and soft, fragrant grasses spread across the ground, curling to the right.

The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara sat cross-legged upon a diamond-jewel throne, surrounded by immeasurable bodhisattvas who were all seated upon jewel thrones in reverent attendance; he then proclaimed the Dharma of Great Compassion, causing them to embrace and sustain all sentient beings.
Having seen this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; joining his palms, he gazed intently at him without blinking for even a moment, thinking thus:
"The spiritual friend is the Tathāgata;
the spiritual friend is the cloud of all dharmas."
A spiritual friend is a treasury of all merits;
a spiritual friend is difficult to encounter;
a spiritual friend is the cause for the jewels of the ten powers.
A spiritual friend is the inexhaustible torch of wisdom;
a spiritual friend is the sprout of the roots of merit;
a spiritual friend is the gateway to all-knowledge.
"A spiritual friend is a guide across the ocean of wisdom;
a spiritual friend is the equipment for the path that leads to all-knowledge.
Having said this, he immediately went to where the great bodhisattva was.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara saw Sudhana from afar and addressed him, saying:

"Welcome! You have resolved upon the Mahāyāna mind to universally embrace all sentient beings; you have given rise to an upright mind to single-mindedly seek the Buddha-dharma; your great compassion is profound and heavy as you rescue and protect all; the wondrous practices of Samantabhadra manifest continuously before you; your great vows and deep resolve are perfect and pure; you diligently seek the Buddha-dharma and are able to receive it all; you accumulate roots of goodness without ever becoming weary; and you follow spiritual friends, never disobeying their instructions."
Born from the great ocean of Mañjuśrī’s merit and wisdom, his mind was fully matured and he attained the power of the Buddhas.

Having already obtained the light of vast samādhis, he single-mindedly sought the profound and wondrous Dharma; constantly beholding all Buddhas, he gave rise to great joy. His wisdom was pure like space; having himself attained clarity, he further explained it to others, dwelling securely in the light of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, circumambulated him countless times, and stood with palms joined, saying: "Noble One!"
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct,
nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me! The Bodhisattva replied, "Excellent, excellent!
"Good son! You have already been able to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Good son!"
I have already accomplished the liberation door of the Bodhisattva’s practice of great compassion. Noble son!
By means of this liberation door of the Bodhisattva’s practice of great compassion, I impartially teach and transform all sentient beings in an uninterrupted succession.
"Good son! Abiding in this gate of practice of great compassion, I am always present before all Tathāgatas and universally manifest myself before all sentient beings."
They may gather in sentient beings through giving;
or they may gather them in through kind speech, beneficial conduct, or cooperation;
or they may gather them in by manifesting a physical form.
Sometimes they manifest various inconceivable nets of pure light of diverse colors to gather in sentient beings;

sometimes by means of their voice, sometimes by means of their dignified demeanor, sometimes by preaching the Dharma, or sometimes by manifesting spiritual transformations, they cause the minds of beings to awaken and attain maturity;
or they manifest forms identical to those of the beings themselves, dwelling together with them to bring them to maturity.
“Good son! I practice this gateway of the conduct of great compassion, vowing to always protect and deliver all sentient beings.

I vow that all sentient beings shall be free from the fear of perilous paths, the fear of feverish affliction, the fear of confusion, the fear of bondage, the fear of slaughter, the fear of poverty, the fear of being unable to survive, the fear of ill repute, the fear of death, the fear of large crowds, the fear of evil destinies, the fear of darkness, the fear of displacement, the fear of separation from loved ones, the fear of encountering enemies, the fear of physical oppression, the fear of mental oppression, and the fear of sorrow and lamentation.”
Furthermore, he made this vow:
"May all sentient beings, whether they think of me, call my name, or behold my body, all be delivered from every fear."
"Good son! By these skillful means, I cause all sentient beings to be free from fear; having done so, I further instruct them to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, never to regress."
“Good son! I have attained only this gate of the Bodhisattva’s practice of great compassion.

As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who have already purified all the vows of Samantabhadra, who already abide in all the practices of Samantabhadra, who constantly practice all wholesome dharmas, who constantly enter all samādhis, who constantly dwell throughout all infinite eons, who constantly know all dharmas of the three periods of time, who constantly visit all infinite lands, who constantly extinguish the evils of all sentient beings, who constantly increase the virtues of all sentient beings, and who constantly sever the stream of birth and death for all sentient beings;”
"How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
At that time, there was a bodhisattva from the east named Samantagāmin,
who came through the air to the summit of the Cakravāḍa mountain range in this Sahā world and pressed his foot upon the ground.
That Sahā world shook in six ways, all of it adorned with various jewels.

The Bodhisattva Saṃcodana emitted a radiance from his body that eclipsed all the light of the sun, moon, stars, and lightning; the light of the eight classes of beings—devas, nāgas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kiṃnaras—as well as that of Śakra, Brahmā, and the World Protectors, was like a mass of ink.

That light universally illuminated all the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, and the abode of King Yama, causing all the sufferings of the evil destinies to be extinguished, so that afflictions did not arise and all sorrow and lamentation were abandoned.
Furthermore, throughout all Buddha-lands, they cause a universal rain of all kinds of flowers, incense, necklaces, robes, banners, and canopies;
with all such articles of adornment, they make offerings to the Buddhas.

Furthermore, in accordance with the inclinations of sentient beings' minds, he manifested his body universally within all palaces, causing all who saw him to rejoice; thereafter, he proceeded to the abode of Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed Sudhana, saying: "Noble son,
do you see the Bodhisattva Samantagāmin coming to this assembly?"
He replied, “I have seen them.
The Buddha said:
“Good son! You may go and ask him:
‘How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?’”
At that time, the youth Sudhana respectfully received his instruction and immediately went to where that bodhisattva was. He prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should study the bodhisattva practice,
nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me! The Bodhisattva Samyaktva said: "Good son!..."
"I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'Universal Gateway Swift Movement. Sudhana said:
“Noble One! Under which Buddha did you obtain this Dharma-gate?
From what buddha-field have you come, and how far is it from here?”
"How long has it been since it was sent? He replied,
"O son of good family!"
This matter is difficult to know; it cannot be comprehended by any in the world—whether devas, humans, asuras, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas.

It can only be understood by those bodhisattvas who are courageous and diligent, who are without retreat or fear, who have been embraced by all spiritual friends and are held in the mindfulness of all Buddhas, who are fully endowed with roots of goodness, whose aspirations are pure, who have attained the faculties of a bodhisattva, and who possess the eye of wisdom, being able to hear, retain, understand, and explain it.
Sudhana said, “Noble One!
Relying on the spiritual power of the Buddha and the power of the spiritual friend, I am able to believe and accept [your teaching]; I pray that you will speak for me!”
The Bodhisattva Samyaktvaniyata said: "Good son!

I have come from the world-system called Wondrous Treasury (*Prabhūtaratna*) in the eastern direction, from the presence of the Buddha Universal Victorious Birth (*Samantavijayajanan*). I received this Dharma-gate from that Buddha and have been traveling from there for an incalculable, incalculable number of kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field. In every single thought-moment, I take strides as numerous as the atoms within an incalculable, incalculable number of Buddha-fields; with each step, I pass through as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in an incalculable, incalculable number of worlds."
I enter every single Buddha-field, going to the abodes of those Buddhas and making offerings with exquisite articles of worship;
these articles of worship are all produced by the unsurpassed mind, sealed by the unconditioned Dharma, approved by all Tathāgatas, and praised by all Bodhisattvas.

"Good son! Furthermore, I universally behold all sentient beings in those worlds; I know their minds completely and know their faculties completely. According to their inclinations and understandings, I manifest my body and preach the Dharma, or emit radiance, or bestow wealth and treasures—using various skillful means to teach, transform, and subdue them without ceasing."
As it is from the east, so it is likewise from the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions,
and from above and below. "Good son,
I have attained only this Bodhisattva liberation of Universal Swift Movement, which enables one to swiftly reach all places."

As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who reach everywhere throughout the ten directions, whose sphere of wisdom is equal and without distinction, who skillfully manifest their bodies so as to pervade the entire Dharma-realm, who arrive at all paths, enter all lands, know all dharmas, and reach all worlds; who impartially expound all Dharma-gates, simultaneously illuminating all sentient beings, and who give rise to no discrimination regarding the Buddhas and encounter no obstacles in any place—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
“Good son! To the south of here there is a city named Dravati;”
Within it there is a deity named Mahādeva.
Go to him and ask:
"How should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave.

At that time, the youth Sudhana entered the vast conduct of Bodhisattvas, sought the sphere of Bodhisattva wisdom, beheld the miraculous feats of Bodhisattvas, contemplated the supreme merits of Bodhisattvas, gave rise to great joy of Bodhisattvas, initiated firm diligence of Bodhisattvas, entered the inconceivable and sovereign liberation of Bodhisattvas, practiced the ground of Bodhisattva merit, observed the ground of Bodhisattva samādhi, dwelt in the ground of Bodhisattva dhāraṇī, entered the ground of Bodhisattva great vows, attained the ground of Bodhisattva eloquence, and perfected the ground of Bodhisattva powers.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at that city and inquired where Mahādeva was currently staying.
Everyone replied,
