"He is within this city, manifesting a vast body and preaching the Dharma to the multitude."
At that time, Sudhana went to the place where Mahādevī was, prostrated at her feet, and with palms joined before her, spoke these words: “Noble Lady!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct.”
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Holy One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me!

At that time, Mahādeva extended his four hands, took water from the four great oceans to wash his own face, and holding various golden flowers, he scattered them over Sudhana and addressed him, saying:

“Good son! All bodhisattvas are difficult to behold and difficult to hear of; they rarely appear in the world and are the most supreme among sentient beings. They are the *puṇḍarīka* lotuses among all people, a refuge for sentient beings, a salvation for sentient beings, a place of peace and security for all worlds, and a great light for all worlds. To those who are deluded, they show the secure path of right practice;
as great guides, they lead all sentient beings into the gateway of the Buddha-dharma.”
Acting as generals of the Great Dharma, they are well able to guard the city of omniscience.

Such Bodhisattvas are difficult to encounter; only those whose body, speech, and mind are free from fault can thereafter behold their forms and hear their eloquence, which remains ever present before them at all times.
“Good son! I have already accomplished a bodhisattva liberation called ‘Cloud Net.’”
Sudhana said: "Noble One! What is the sphere of the liberation called Cloud-Net?"

At that time, Mahādeva manifested before Sudhana heaps of gold, heaps of silver, heaps of lapis lazuli, heaps of crystal, heaps of mother-of-pearl, heaps of agate, heaps of great-flame jewels, heaps of stainless-treasury jewels, heaps of great-radiance jewels, heaps of jewels that universally manifest the ten directions, heaps of jeweled crowns, heaps of jeweled seals, heaps of jeweled necklaces, heaps of jeweled earrings, heaps of jeweled bracelets, heaps of jeweled chains, heaps of pearl nets, heaps of various kinds of maṇi-jewels, heaps of all manner of ornaments, and heaps of wish-fulfilling maṇis, each as vast as a great mountain.

Furthermore, he manifested all kinds of flowers, all kinds of garlands, all kinds of incense, all kinds of burning incense, all kinds of unguents, all kinds of garments, all kinds of banners and streamers, all kinds of music, and all kinds of implements for the enjoyment of the five desires, each piled as high as mountains;
and he also manifested countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of young maidens.
Then that Mahādeva said to Sudhana:
"O son of good family!

You may take these things to make offerings to the Tathāgata, cultivate various merits, and bestow them upon all; thereby you shall gather in sentient beings and cause them to practice and study the dānapāramitā, being able to relinquish what is difficult to relinquish."
"Good son! Just as I have manifested these objects for you to teach you the practice of giving, so it is for all sentient beings;

I cause them all to be perfumed by these roots of goodness, so that they may reverently make offerings at the shrines of the Triple Gem and to spiritual friends, increase wholesome dharmas, and give rise to the aspiration for unexcelled bodhi."
“Good son! If there are sentient beings who are greedily attached to the five desires and are self-indulgent, for their sake I manifest impure realms;
if there are sentient beings who harbor anger, pride, and engage in much contention, for their sake I manifest extremely terrifying forms, such as rākṣasas drinking blood and devouring flesh.”
Having caused them to see this, they become struck with alarm and dread, their minds become supple and gentle, and they abandon their bonds of enmity.
If there are sentient beings who are dull-witted or indolent, he manifests for them kings, thieves, water, fire, and various grave illnesses;
having caused them to see these, their hearts are filled with fear and terror, and knowing the existence of sorrow and suffering, they exert themselves with self-encouragement.
By means of such various skillful expedients, they cause [beings] to abandon all unwholesome practices and cultivate wholesome dharmas;
they cause them to eliminate all obstacles to the pāramitās and to fulfill the pāramitās;
and they cause them to transcend all perilous paths of obstruction and reach the realm free from hindrance.
“Good son! I know only this liberation of the Cloud-Net.
As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they are like Śakra, having already been able to crush and subdue the asura armies of all afflictions;”
They are like a great body of water, capable of universally extinguishing the fires of affliction of all sentient beings;
they are like a fierce fire, capable of universally drying up the waters of craving and desire of all sentient beings;
they are like a great wind, capable of universally blowing down the banners of dogmatic views and attachments of all sentient beings.
Like a vajra, it is able to shatter the mountains of the view of self in all sentient beings.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
“Good son! In this Jambudvīpa,
within the Bodhimaṇḍa of the kingdom of Magadha, there is a presiding earth goddess named Anvaya.”
"Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Mahādeva, circumambulated him countless times, took his leave, and departed.

At that time, the youth Sudhana traveled by stages until he reached the abode of the goddess Anuvartinī within the Bodhimaṇḍa in the kingdom of Magadha. There were one million earth-deities dwelling together therein, who said to one another:

"This youth who has come here is the treasury of the Buddhas; he will surely serve as a place of refuge for all sentient beings, and he will surely shatter the eggshell of ignorance for all sentient beings."

This person has already been born into the lineage of the Dharma King; his head shall be crowned with the stainless, unobstructed silk band of the Dharma, he shall open the great treasure-store of wisdom, and he shall subdue all heterodox arguments and divergent paths.

At that time, ten million earth deities, including the Earth-Abiding Goddess, emitted a great radiance that illuminated the entire trichiliocosm. They caused the great earth to tremble and roar simultaneously, while various precious objects adorned every place;

their shadows were pure and their light flowed, reflecting one another with perfect clarity. All leafy trees grew at once, all flowering trees blossomed together, and all fruit trees ripened without exception. All rivers poured into one another, and all ponds and pools became completely full.

A fine rain of fragrance fell, sprinkling the ground everywhere, while the wind blew flowers that scattered over it. Countless musical instruments played in unison, and the celestial ornaments all produced beautiful sounds.
The king of oxen, the king of elephants, the king of lions, and others all gave rise to joy, leaping and bellowing with sounds like those produced by the collision of great mountains;
a thousandfold hidden treasures spontaneously surged forth from the earth.
At that time, the Earth Goddess Anvaya addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Welcome, young man!
You have planted roots of goodness in this very place; I shall manifest them for you. Do you wish to see them?"
At that time, Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Earth Goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and stood with palms joined, saying:
"Noble One! Indeed!"
"I wish to see them.
At that time, the earth goddess Anvaya pressed her foot upon the ground, and hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* treasuries spontaneously surged forth, and she declared:
"O son of good family!

This treasure trove now follows you; it is the fruit and retribution of your past roots of goodness, and it is sustained by the power of your merit. You should enjoy it as you wish and with full autonomy.
“Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called ‘the indestructible treasury of wisdom,’ and I constantly use this dharma to bring sentient beings to fulfillment.”

“Good son! I remember that since the time of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I have constantly followed the Bodhisattva, respectfully guarding him and observing all his mental activities, the sphere of his wisdom, all his vows, his various pure practices, all his samādhis, his vast supernormal powers, his great sovereign strength, and his indestructible dharmas. I have witnessed him travel throughout all Buddha-lands, universally receive the predictions of all Tathāgatas, turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas, extensively expound all the gateways of the sūtras, cause the light of the Great Dharma to shine everywhere, teach and subdue all sentient beings, and manifest all the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas—all of this I have been able to receive and all of this I have been able to remember and uphold.”
“Good son! In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru,
there was an eon named Adornment, and a world named...
Candradhvaja, the Buddha there is named Sunetra;
it was from that Buddha that you obtained this Dharma-gate,
son of good family!

As I enter and emerge from this Dharma-door, practicing and increasing it, I constantly behold all Buddhas and have never been separated from them. From the time I first attained this until the Bhadrakalpa, throughout that interval, I have encountered Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields; I have served them all, honoring and making offerings to them.
I have also seen those Buddhas proceed to the seat of enlightenment and manifest great supernormal powers;
I have also seen all the roots of goodness and merits of those Buddhas.
“Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of the indestructible treasury of wisdom.

As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, they constantly follow all Buddhas and are able to uphold everything spoken by all Buddhas; they enter the profound wisdom of all Buddhas, pervading the entire Dharma-realm in every thought-moment; they become equal to the body of a Tathāgata, give birth to the mind of all Buddhas, possess all Buddha-dharmas, and perform the works of all Buddhas.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa, in the kingdom of Magadha, in the city of Kapilavastu, there is a night goddess named:
Vasavartī, go to her and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Earth Goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and took his leave.

At that time, Sudhana focused his mind on contemplating the instructions of the goddess Anala; he recollected the Bodhisattva’s liberation of the indestructible treasury of wisdom, cultivated her samādhi, studied her rules of conduct, observed her spiritual play, entered into her subtlety, attained her wisdom, realized her equanimity, knew its boundlessness, and fathomed its profound depth.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at that city and entered through the eastern gate. He stood there for no long time before the sun set.
Following the instructions of the various bodhisattvas, his heart was filled with longing to see that Night Goddess; regarding the spiritual friend as a Tathāgata, he further thought:
"Through a spiritual friend, one attains the all-pervading eye, which can clearly perceive the realms of the ten directions."
Through spiritual friends, one attains vast understanding and is able to universally comprehend all objects of perception;
through spiritual friends, one attains the eye of samādhi and is able to universally observe all dharma-gates;
through spiritual friends, one attains the eye of wisdom and is able to universally and clearly illuminate the oceans of lands in the ten directions.

While he was reflecting thus, he saw that night goddess in the midst of the sky, seated upon a lion throne of fragrant lotus-treasury within a jeweled pavilion. Her body was the color of pure gold, her eyes and hair were deep blue, and her form was so upright and majestic that all who saw her rejoiced. She was adorned with necklaces of various jewels, wore crimson robes, and bore a Brahma-crown upon her head, while all the constellations shone brilliantly upon her person.

From each and every pore upon his body, there appeared the images of him transforming and delivering immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings of the evil realms, causing them to escape from perilous difficulties;
these sentient beings were either born among humans, or born in the heavens, or were directed toward the enlightenment of the two vehicles, or were practicing the path to all-knowledge.

Furthermore, within each and every one of his pores, he manifests various skillful means of instruction: sometimes manifesting his physical body, sometimes preaching the Dharma; sometimes manifesting the path of the Śrāvaka vehicle, sometimes manifesting the path of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle; or manifesting the various practices of Bodhisattvas, the valor of Bodhisattvas, the samādhis of Bodhisattvas, the masteries of Bodhisattvas, the abodes of Bodhisattvas, the observations of Bodhisattvas, the lion-like stretches of Bodhisattvas, and the playful liberations of Bodhisattvas—thus maturing sentient beings through such diverse means.

Having seen and heard this, the youth Sudhana was filled with great joy; he prostrated himself upon the ground to pay homage at the feet of the night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and with palms joined before her, spoke these words: "Noble One!"
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; I hope that, by relying on spiritual friends, I may obtain the treasury of the dharmas of all the Tathāgatas’ merits.
“I only pray that you will show me the path of omniscience, so that by walking upon it, I may reach the stage of the Ten Powers!
Then, that night goddess said to Sudhana:
“Excellent, excellent!
"Good son! You are able, with a profound mind, to revere the spiritual friend, delight in hearing their words, and practice their teachings;
because you practice them, you will certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
“Good son! I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called ‘The Radiance of the Dharma that Shatters the Darkness of Ignorance of All Sentient Beings. Good son!”
Toward sentient beings of evil wisdom, I give rise to a mind of great loving-kindness;
toward sentient beings of unwholesome karma, I give rise to a mind of great compassion;
and toward sentient beings who perform wholesome karma, I give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy.
Toward sentient beings who engage in both wholesome and unwholesome conduct, they give rise to a mind of non-duality;
toward defiled sentient beings, they give rise to a mind that causes them to produce purity;
toward sentient beings on false paths, they give rise to a mind that causes them to produce right practice.
Toward sentient beings of inferior understanding, they give rise to the mind that inspires great understanding;
toward sentient beings who delight in birth and death, they give rise to the mind that causes them to abandon cyclic existence;
toward sentient beings dwelling in the paths of the two vehicles, they give rise to the mind that causes them to abide in omniscience.
"Good son! Because I have attained this liberation, my mind is always in constant association with such a state of mind. Good son!"

During the stillness of the night when ghosts, spirits, thieves, and various evil beings roam; when thick clouds and heavy mists prevail, and amidst fierce winds and torrential rains, such that the sun, moon, and stars are all obscured and their forms unseen—I behold sentient beings who, whether entering the sea or traveling on land, in mountain forests, wildernesses, or places of peril and difficulty, may encounter bandits, lack provisions, become disoriented regarding the directions, or lose their way, trembling with fear and anxiety, unable to escape.
At such times, I immediately employ various skillful means to rescue and provide for them.
For those who have encountered shipwrecks at sea, he manifests as a shipmaster, a king of fish, a king of horses, a king of turtles, a king of elephants, a king of asuras, and even a sea deity;

for the sake of those sentient beings, he halts violent winds and rains, calms great waves, guides them along their path, and points out the islands and shores, enabling them to escape fear and attain complete peace and security.
Again, he forms this thought:
"By means of these roots of goodness, I dedicate them to all sentient beings, wishing that they may abandon and leave behind all sufferings.

For the sake of all sentient beings on land who encounter terror in the darkness of night, he manifests various lights such as the sun, the moon, the stars, the morning glow, and evening lightning; or he manifests as houses or as throngs of people, enabling them to escape the calamity of fear.
Again, he forms this thought:
"By means of these roots of goodness, I dedicate them to all sentient beings, so that they may all eliminate the darkness of their various afflictions.

Among all sentient beings, there are those who cherish their lives, those who love fame, those who covet wealth and treasures, those who value official rank, those who are attached to sons and daughters, and those who dote on wives and concubines; when their desires are not fulfilled, they give rise to much sorrow and fear.
I shall rescue and deliver them all, causing them to be free from suffering.
For those who encounter obstacles while traveling through mountainous and perilous regions, I shall manifest as benevolent deities to appear before and approach them;
for those in need, I shall manifest as auspicious birds, uttering songs to comfort and gladden them.
Acting as a divine medicine, they radiate light and brilliance;
they show them the fruit trees, show them the springs and wells, show them the upright path, and show them the level ground, causing them to escape all sorrow and calamity.

"For those traveling through vast wildernesses, dense forests, and perilous paths—entangled by creeping vines and obscured by clouds and mist—who are filled with terror, he shows them the correct path and enables them to attain liberation."
They form this thought:

"May all sentient beings cut down the dense forest of views, sever the net of craving, emerge from the wilderness of birth and death, extinguish the darkness of afflictions, enter the level and straight path of omniscience, and reach the state of fearlessness and ultimate peace."
"Good son! If there are sentient beings who, being attached to their countries and lands, experience sorrow and suffering;
I employ skillful means to cause them to give rise to weary detachment."
He forms this thought:
"May all sentient beings not be attached to the aggregates and may they abide in the realm of the omniscience (sarvajñatā) of all Buddhas. "Good son!
If there are sentient beings who delight in and cling to villages, who crave and love their dwellings, who constantly abide in darkness and undergo various sufferings;
for them I preach the Dharma to cause them to give rise to weary detachment, to bring them to fulfillment in the Dharma, and to cause them to abide in accordance with the Dharma.
They form this thought:

"May all sentient beings never again crave or delight in the villages of the six sense bases; may they swiftly attain liberation from the realm of birth and death, and ultimately dwell in peace within the city of omniscience."

“Good son! If there are sentient beings walking in the darkness of night who are confused about the ten directions, perceiving a level road as a perilous one and perceiving a perilous road as a level one; taking high for low and low for high, their minds are deluded and they give rise to great suffering and affliction.”
I employ skillful means to extend my light so as to reach them: to those who wish to emerge, I show them the gateway;
to those who wish to travel, I show them the path;
to those who wish to cross ditches and moats, I show them the bridge.
To those wishing to cross rivers or seas, he provides boats and rafts;
to those who delight in observing the directions, he shows them the locations that are perilous or secure, difficult or easy;
to those wishing to rest, he points out cities, water, and groves of trees.
He forms this thought:
"Just as I have here illuminated and dispelled the darkness of night, enabling all worldly affairs to be fully expressed and recounted;
may I likewise universally illuminate and bring to clear understanding, with the light of wisdom, the long night of birth and death and the regions of ignorance for all sentient beings."
These sentient beings lack the eye of wisdom; they are shrouded by the perversions of perception, thought, and view.
They perceive the impermanent as permanent, the suffering as happiness, the non-self as self, and the impure as pure.

They are firmly attached to the notions of a self, a person, a sentient being, and to the phenomena of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases. Confused regarding cause and effect, they do not recognize what is wholesome.

They commit evil, harming sentient beings, and even holding wrong views; they are unfilial toward their parents, disrespectful toward śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, ignorant of the wicked, and fail to recognize the virtuous;
they are greedily attached to evil deeds, abide in false teachings, slander the Tathāgata, destroy the true Wheel of Dharma, and [act against] the bodhisattvas.
They will revile, humiliate, and harm others; they will disparage the Mahāyāna path and sever the bodhicitta;
they will turn against those who have been kind to them by killing them, and harbor constant resentment toward those who owe them no debt;

they will slander the noble ones and saints, associate with evil companions, steal the property of stūpas and monasteries, and commit the five heinous crimes (*pañcānantarya*); before long, they shall fall into the three evil destinies.
May I, by means of the light of great wisdom, swiftly shatter the darkness of ignorance of those sentient beings and cause them to quickly resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Once they have thus resolved their minds, he shows them the vehicle of Samantabhadra and opens the path of the ten powers; he also reveals the realm of the Tathāgatas, the Dharma Kings, as well as the all-knowledge city of all Buddhas, the conduct of all Buddhas, the sovereignty of all Buddhas, the accomplishments of all Buddhas, and the dhāraṇīs of all Buddhas. He demonstrates how all Buddhas share a single body and the state of equality of all Buddhas, causing them to dwell securely therein.

“Good son! All sentient beings may be entangled by illness, or assailed by old age, or afflicted by poverty, or encounter calamities and disasters, or violate the king’s law and stand on the verge of execution, having no one to rely upon and giving rise to great fear;
I rescue and deliver them all, enabling them to attain peace and security.”
Again, he formed this thought:

"May I universally gather in all sentient beings through the Dharma, causing them to be liberated from all afflictions, birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and distress; may they draw near to virtuous friends, constantly practice the gift of Dharma, diligently perform wholesome deeds, swiftly attain the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body, and abide in the ultimate state that is immutable."

“Good son! All sentient beings enter the dense forest of views and dwell upon false paths; they give rise to false discrimination regarding all objects of experience and constantly perform unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind. They falsely engage in various kinds of wrong ascetic practices, conceiving the notion of true awakening where there is no true awakening, and the notion of non-awakening where there is true awakening. Captured by evil associates, they give rise to evil views and are on the verge of falling into the evil realms.
I rescue and protect them through various gates of skillful means, causing them to abide in right view and be reborn among humans and devas.”
Again, he formed this thought:

"Just as I have rescued these sentient beings who were about to fall into the evil realms, may I universally rescue all sentient beings, causing them all to be liberated from every suffering, to abide in the supramundane noble path of the *pāramitās*, to attain non-retrogression in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), to fulfill the vows of Samantabhadra, to draw near to omniscience, and without abandoning the practices of all bodhisattvas, to always diligently teach and transform all sentient beings."

At that time, the night goddess Vāsantī, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, and empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
“This door of my liberation Gives birth to the radiance of pure dharmas;
It can shatter the darkness of ignorance, And is expounded only when the time is right.”
In the past, throughout boundless eons, I diligently practiced vast compassion, universally covering all worlds; sons of the Buddha should train themselves accordingly.
This ocean of tranquil great compassion gives birth to the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
It can extinguish the suffering of sentient beings; you should enter this gate.
It can produce worldly happiness and also produce supramundane happiness;
it brings joy to my heart; you should enter this gate.
Having abandoned the afflictions of the conditioned, And having distanced yourself from the fruits of the śrāvakas, Purify the powers of all Buddhas; You should enter this gate.
My eyes are exceedingly pure, Seeing universally the lands of the ten directions.
I also see within them Buddhas, seated beneath Bodhi trees,
their bodies adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, surrounded by immeasurable multitudes;
from every single pore, various kinds of light radiate forth.
Beholding all classes of sentient beings, dying here and being born there,
revolving within the five destinies and constantly undergoing immeasurable suffering—
my ears are exceedingly pure, hearing all without exception.
The ocean of all languages, they hear it all and can retain it;
the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Buddhas, with sounds incomparably sublime—
all the various syllables and scripts, they are able to remember and hold them all.
My nose is exceedingly pure; regarding all phenomena, it is without obstruction.
All things are under my mastery—enter this gate, you should!
My tongue is exceedingly vast; pure and excellent, it is capable of eloquent speech.
I expound the wondrous Dharma according to need; you should enter this gate.
My body is exceedingly pure, equal to suchness throughout the three periods of time;
in accordance with the minds of all sentient beings, it manifests in every way.
My mind is pure and unimpeded, like space containing the myriad forms;
I universally contemplate all Tathāgatas, yet without making any distinctions.
I clearly know the infinite lands and the entire ocean of all minds.
Regarding the sense faculties and their objects of desire, he makes no conceptual distinctions.
By means of his great supernormal powers, he causes immeasurable lands to tremble;
his body pervades them all as he tames those beings who are difficult to tame.
My merit is exceedingly vast, like space, without end;
I make offerings to all Tathāgatas, benefiting all sentient beings.
My wisdom is broad and pure, thoroughly understanding the ocean of all dharmas.
To extinguish the delusions of sentient beings, you should enter this gate.
I know the Buddhas of the three periods of time, as well as all dharmas;
I also understand their skillful means, and this gate is universally peerless.
Within each and every atom, one sees all lands of the three periods of time, and also beholds all those Buddhas; this is the power of the Universal Gate.
Within the atoms of the lands of the ten directions, one sees Vairocana everywhere.
"Sitting beneath the Bodhi tree, he attained enlightenment and expounded the wondrous Dharma.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the Night Goddess:
"How long has it been since you first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
"How long has it been since you attained this liberation, that you are now able to benefit sentient beings in such a way?
The deity replied, "Good son!..."
In the distant past, more than as many eons ago as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru,
there was an eon named Tranquil Light and a world named Birth of Wondrous Jewels, in which five hundred million buddhas appeared.
In that world there is a set of four continents named Jewel Moon Lamp Light; there is a city named Lotus Light, and its king is named...
The King of Good Dharma-Attainment transformed others through the gift of the Dharma, accomplishing the seven treasures and ruling over the four continents under heaven.
The king had a queen named Dharmamati-candra (Moon of Dharma-Wisdom), who was deep in sleep late at night.
At that time, to the east of that city there was a great forest named Tranquil Abiding.
Within the forest stood a great Bodhi tree named Adorned Body of All-Light Maṇi King Producing the Radiance of the Spiritual Powers of All Buddhas.

“At that time, there was a Buddha named Sarvadharma-ghoṣarāja (King of the Thunder-Sound of All Dharmas) who attained equal and perfect enlightenment beneath this tree, emitting vast radiance of immeasurable colors that shone everywhere throughout the world-system called Utpanna-maṇiratna (Born of Wondrous Jewels).”
Within the city of Padmaprabhā, there was a night goddess named Vimalacandrā.
She went to the queen Dharmamaticandrā and, by moving her body ornaments, awakened the queen and addressed her, saying:

"Queen, you should know that the Tathāgata Sarvadharmameghanirghoṣarāja has attained unsurpassed enlightenment in the Forest of Tranquil Abiding, and he is extensively expounding the sovereign spiritual powers and merits of all Buddhas, as well as the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."
He caused the king’s consort to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and to make offerings to that Buddha, as well as to the assembly of bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and the Saṅgha.
“Good son! As for the king’s consort Dharmamati-candrā at that time, could she have been anyone else?
It was I myself!”

"Because I have planted roots of goodness by generating the bodhicitta in the presence of that Buddha, for as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, I have not been born in the miserable realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals, nor have I been born into low-born families. My faculties are complete, I am free from all suffering, and my merit and virtue are preeminent among gods and humans. I am never born in an evil age and am never separated from Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and great spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), constantly planting roots of goodness in their presence. For eighty eons, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, I have always experienced peace and happiness, yet I have not yet perfected the faculties of a Bodhisattva."
"After this kalpa has passed, and after ten thousand more kalpas have elapsed, prior to the Bhadrakalpa,
there was a kalpa named Sarvavyūhaprabhāsa, and a world named Vimalaprabhā."
In that world, purity and impurity are intermingled, and five hundred buddhas appear therein.
The first of these buddhas is named Sumeruketuśāntasuvilocana Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
I am the elder named Yaśas; my daughter's name is:
Her wondrous wisdom-light was upright and exquisite.

By the power of her vows, that Night Goddess Pure Moon was born in the city of King Wondrous Banner within a four-continent world-system in the Stainless World; she acts as a night goddess and is named Pure Eye.

Once, while I was resting in sleep late at night by my parents' side, that One of Pure Eyes came to me, shaking my house and emitting a great radiance. Manifesting his body, he praised the virtues of the Buddha, saying:
"The Tathāgata Wondrous Eye sits upon the seat of enlightenment; he has just attained perfect awakening."
He exhorted me, my parents, and all our kinsmen to see the Buddha quickly;
acting as our guide, he led us to the Buddha’s presence and extensively offered worship.
"As soon as I saw the Buddha, I immediately attained a samādhi called 'The Light-Wheel of Wisdom for Manifesting the Seeing of Buddhas and Taming Sentient Beings Throughout the Three Times.

Because I have obtained this samādhi, I am able to recollect as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, and I also see the appearance of all the Buddhas therein, and I hear the sublime Dharma from those Buddhas."
By virtue of hearing the Dharma, he immediately attained this liberation of the light that destroys the darkness of all sentient beings.

Having attained this liberation, he saw his own body pervading worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field; he also saw all the Buddhas in those worlds, and saw himself in the presence of those Buddhas.

Furthermore, he saw all the sentient beings in those worlds, understanding their speech and sounds, discerning their faculties and natures, and knowing that they had been gathered and sustained by him as a virtuous friend in the past. Accordingly, he manifested his body to them according to their inclinations, causing them to give rise to joy.
"At that time, the liberation I had attained increased moment by moment without interruption;
furthermore, I saw my own body traveling throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in a hundred buddha-fields without interruption;
I also saw my own body traveling throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in a thousand buddha-fields without interruption."
Furthermore, one sees one's own body traveling everywhere throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields.
In this manner, moment by moment, one reaches worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, and likewise sees all the Tathāgatas within those worlds;
one also sees one's own body in the presence of those Buddhas, hearing the sublime Dharma, receiving and upholding it, recollecting it, observing it, and attaining definitive understanding of it.
I also know the oceans of past deeds and the oceans of great vows of those Buddhas; I likewise purify the Buddha-lands that those Tathāgatas have adorned and purified.
I also see all sentient beings in those worlds and manifest bodies for them according to their needs to teach, transform, and subdue them.
This door of liberation increases moment by moment, continuing in this manner until it completely fills the Dharma-realm.
"Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva liberation called 'The Radiant Light of the Dharma that Shatters the Darkness of All Sentient Beings. "

Just as all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas accomplish the boundless practices and vows of Samantabhadra, universally entering the ocean of all Dharma-realms; attain the Bodhisattvas’ sovereign samādhi of the Vajra-Wisdom Banner, giving rise to great vows and sustaining the lineage of the Buddhas;
in every thought-moment, fulfilling the ocean of all great merits and purifying all vast worlds;
and with sovereign wisdom, teaching and maturing all sentient beings.
With the sun of wisdom, they eliminate all darkness and obstructions in the world;
with courageous wisdom, they awaken all sentient beings from their torpor and slumber;
with the moon of wisdom, they resolve all doubts and uncertainties of sentient beings.
With a pure voice, they sever all attachments to existence;
within every single atom of the entire dharma-realm, they manifest all sovereign spiritual powers; their eye of wisdom is clear and pure, seeing the three periods of time with equality.
"And how could I possibly know her wondrous conduct, speak of her merits, enter her realm, or demonstrate her sovereign mastery? 'Good son!
Within the Bodhimaṇḍa in the kingdom of Magadha here in Jambudvīpa, there is a night goddess named:'"
Samantaguṇaviśuddhaprabha, it was from him that I first resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; he constantly awakened me with the sublime Dharma.
"Go to her and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana addressed the goddess Vāsantī in verse, saying:
“Beholding your pure body, with its marks and signs surpassing the world, you are like Mañjuśrī, and also like the King of Jewel Mountains.
Your Dharma-body is pure; throughout the three periods of time, it is entirely equal.”
The entire world enters within you, yet the processes of formation and destruction encounter no obstruction.
As I observe all realms of existence, I see your form in every one;
within each and every pore, the stars and moon are distributed.
Your mind is exceedingly vast, like space pervading the ten directions;
all Buddhas enter therein, pure and free from discrimination.
From within each and every pore, you emit countless rays of light.
Before the presence of all Buddhas of the ten directions, They rain down ornaments everywhere.
Within each and every pore, They manifest countless bodies,
Throughout the lands of the ten directions, Skillfully delivering sentient beings.
Within each and every pore, he manifests immeasurable lands;
according to the inclinations of all sentient beings, he purifies them in various ways.
If there are sentient beings who hear his name or behold his body, [they shall attain liberation].
They shall all obtain the benefits of merit and accomplish the path to enlightenment.
Having remained in the evil realms for many eons, they have finally been able to see and hear you;
they should likewise receive this with joy, for it causes the afflictions to be extinguished.
"Even if one were to spend eons as numerous as the atoms within a thousand lands extolling the virtue of a single pore of yours,
those eons might yet come to an end, but your merit would never be exhausted.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and then took his leave and departed.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, the Great Vaipulya,
Fascicle Sixty-eight and Fascicle Sixty-nine,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.

The Tenth of the Entry into the Dharma Realm Chapter, the Thirty-Ninth. At that time, the youth Sudhana thoroughly understood the Bodhisattva-treasury born from that night goddess Vasanti’s initial aspiration for enlightenment; the Bodhisattva vows she had made; the Bodhisattva perfections she had purified; the Bodhisattva stages she had entered; the Bodhisattva practices she had cultivated; the path of renunciation she had traversed; the ocean of light of omniscience; her mind that universally rescues all sentient beings; her pervasive cloud of great compassion; and how she is able to constantly give rise to the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra throughout all Buddha-fields until the end of the future.

Traveling by stages, he arrived at the place of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and with palms joined before her, spoke these words: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know how a bodhisattva practices the bodhisattva stages (*bodhisattvabhūmi*),
nor how one gives birth to the bodhisattva stages.
"How does one accomplish the stages of a bodhisattva?
The night goddess replied,
"Excellent, excellent!
"Noble son! You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; you now further inquire about the practice, the emergence, and the accomplishment of the bodhisattva stages."
“Good son! If a bodhisattva accomplishes ten dharmas, they can bring the bodhisattva practice to fulfillment. What are these ten?
First, they attain the samādhi of purity and constantly see all Buddhas;
second, they attain the pure eye and constantly contemplate the marks and signs that adorn all Buddhas;
third, they know the ocean of immeasurable and boundless merits of all Tathāgatas.
Fourth, they know the ocean of light of the infinite Buddha-dharmas, which is equal to the dharma-realm;
fifth, they know that each and every pore of all Tathāgatas emits an ocean of great light rays, as numerous as all sentient beings, to benefit all infinite sentient beings;
sixth, they see that from each and every pore of all Tathāgatas there issues forth an ocean of flaming radiance in the colors of all jewels.

Seventh, in every moment of thought, they manifest an ocean of all Buddhas' transformations that fills the Dharma-realm, ultimately bringing sentient beings to maturity within the sphere of all Buddhas;
eighth, they attain the Buddha’s voice, which is identical to the ocean of the speech and sounds of all sentient beings, and turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
ninth, they know the infinite ocean of names of all Buddhas.
Tenth, knowing the inconceivable power of mastery with which all Buddhas discipline sentient beings.
Son of good family,
when a bodhisattva accomplishes these ten kinds of dharmas, they are able to fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva.
“Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called ‘Universal Pacing in the Joy of Tranquil Meditative Concentration.’”

They universally behold all Buddhas of the three periods of time, as well as those Buddhas’ pure lands, sites of enlightenment, assemblies, supernormal powers, names, teachings, lifespans, voices, and physical marks; though these are all diverse and different, they perceive them all clearly and without attachment.
Why is this? Because one knows that all Tathāgatas do not go, for the realms of existence have been eternally extinguished;
nor do they come, for their essential nature is unborn.
It is not arising, because the Dharma-body is equal;
it is not ceasing, because there are no marks of arising;
it is not real, because it abides in dharmas that are like illusions.
It is not false, because it benefits sentient beings;
it is not subject to transition, because it transcends birth and death;
it is not subject to destruction, because its nature is eternally unchanging.
It is of one mark, because it is entirely free from verbal expression;
it is markless, because its intrinsic nature and characteristics are fundamentally empty. "Good son!

When I thus realized all Tathāgatas, I clearly understood, accomplished, increased, contemplated, and observed the Bodhisattva liberation door of "Universal Striding in the Joy of Tranquil Meditative Concentration. Firmly adorning it, I gave rise to no conceptualizations or discriminations, protected all sentient beings with great compassion, and with an unmoving single mind, cultivated the first dhyāna.
Stilling all mental karma and gathering in all sentient beings, with courageous power of wisdom and a heart of joyful gladness, I cultivated the second dhyāna.
Contemplating the intrinsic nature of all sentient beings and becoming weary of and detached from birth and death, I cultivated the third dhyāna.
They are able to extinguish all the suffering and feverish afflictions of all sentient beings, and practice the fourth dhyāna.

They increase and perfect the vows for omniscience, give birth to the ocean of all samādhis, enter the gates of the ocean of bodhisattva liberations, sport in all supernatural powers, accomplish all transformations, and through pure wisdom, universally enter the Dharma-realm.
“Good son! When I cultivated this liberation, I brought sentient beings to maturity through various skillful means.
That is to say:”

Toward householders who are heedless, they cause them to give rise to the perception of impurity, the perception of loathsomeness, the perception of exhaustion, the perception of oppression, the perception of bondage, the perception of a rākṣasa, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, the perception of emptiness, the perception of non-arising, the perception of lack of self-mastery, and the perception of old age, sickness, and death.

They themselves do not give rise to attachment or delight in the five sensual desires, and they also exhort sentient beings not to cling to the pleasures of desire, but to abide solely in the joy of the Dharma, departing from the household life and entering the homeless state.

If there are sentient beings dwelling in secluded places, I shall silence all evil sounds for them; during the stillness of night, I shall preach the profound Dharma for them, provide the conditions for practicing in accordance with it, open the gate of renunciation, show the correct path, act as a light for them, remove their dark obstructions, extinguish their fears, praise the work of renunciation, extol the Buddha, the Dharma, the Sangha, and spiritual friends for possessing all virtues, and likewise extol the practice of associating with spiritual friends.
"Furthermore, good son!
When I cultivated liberation, I caused all sentient beings not to give rise to unrighteous greed, not to produce perverse discrimination, and not to commit various sinful karmas."
If there are [unwholesome] deeds already committed, cause them all to cease;

if there are wholesome dharmas not yet arisen, the perfections not yet practiced, omniscience not yet sought, great compassion not yet aroused, or the karma of humans and devas not yet created, cause them all to arise;
if they have already arisen, cause them to increase.
I provide such causes and conditions conducive to the Path, even unto the attainment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). "Good son!
I have attained only this Bodhisattva liberation door of the universal stride in the bliss of tranquil meditative concentration."

As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are fully endowed with all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, who have thoroughly realized the entire boundless Dharma-realm, who are constantly able to increase all roots of goodness, who illuminate and perceive the ten powers of all Tathāgatas, who abide in the realm of all Tathāgatas, who dwell perpetually within birth and death with minds free from obstruction, who are swiftly able to fulfill all vows for omniscience, who are universally able to travel to all worlds, who are able to behold all Buddhas, who are able to hear and receive all Buddha-dharmas,

and who are able to shatter the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings and produce the light of all wisdom within the great night of birth and death— how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son! Not far from here,
to the right of the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Joyful Eyes Surveying Sentient Beings."
“Go to her and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, wishing to reiterate the meaning of this liberation, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"If one possesses a mind of faith and understanding, they shall see all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
that person’s eyes are pure, able to enter the ocean of all Buddhas.
Behold the bodies of the Buddhas, adorned with pure marks."
With the supernatural power of a single thought, The entire Dharma-realm is completely filled.
Rocana Tathāgata, having attained perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening,
Turns the pure wheel of Dharma throughout all realms of reality.
The Tathāgata knows the nature of phenomena, Which is quiescent and without duality;
With a pure form adorning his body, He manifests throughout all worlds.
The Buddha-body is inconceivable, Pervading and filling the entire Dharma-realm.
Universally manifesting in all lands, there is nothing that is not seen.
The Buddha-body is ever-luminous, equal in number to the atoms within all lands;
with various pure colors, it pervades the entire Dharma-realm in every thought-moment.
From a single pore of the Tathāgata, He emits inconceivable light,
Universally illuminating all sentient beings, Causing their afflictions to be extinguished.
From a single pore of the Tathāgata, He brings forth inexhaustible emanations.
Pervading the entire Dharma-realm, they eliminate the suffering of sentient beings.
The Buddha utters a single wondrous sound, yet all beings understand it according to their own kind;
he rains down the vast Dharma everywhere, causing them to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
In the past, when the Buddha cultivated all practices, he already took me under his care;
therefore, I am able to see the Tathāgata, who universally manifests in all lands.
The Buddhas appear in the world in numbers equal to the count of sentient beings.
The various realms of liberation are beyond what I can know.
All the Bodhisattvas enter into a single pore of the Buddha;
such wondrous liberation is beyond what I can know.
"Near here there is a night goddess named Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā;
you should go to her and ask how to practice the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, revering the instructions of the spiritual friend and practicing according to the words of the spiritual friend, thought to himself:
"Spiritual friends are difficult to see and difficult to encounter;
seeing a spiritual friend causes the mind to be free from distraction."
Seeing a spiritual friend shatters the mountains of obstacles;
seeing a spiritual friend enters the ocean of great compassion to rescue and protect sentient beings;
seeing a spiritual friend attains the light of wisdom that universally illumines the Dharma-realm.
By seeing spiritual friends, one is able to practice the path to all-knowledge;
by seeing spiritual friends, one is able to universally behold the oceans of Buddhas in the ten directions;
by seeing spiritual friends, one attains the vision of all Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma, retaining it in memory without forgetting.
Having formed this thought, he resolved to go to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.

At that moment, the goddess Pramuditā empowered the youth Sudhana, causing him to understand how approaching spiritual friends can give rise to all roots of goodness and cause them to increase and reach maturity.
That is to say:
causing them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), they can cultivate the requisites for awakening;
causing them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, they can give rise to a courageous mind.
To cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can perform deeds that are difficult to destroy;
to cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can attain power that is difficult to subdue;
to cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can enter boundless regions.
To cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can practice for a long duration;
to cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can accomplish boundless karmic deeds;
to cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can traverse immeasurable paths.
They cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can swiftly attain power and travel to all lands;
they cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can reach everywhere throughout the ten directions without ever leaving one's original place.
At that time, the youth Sudhana suddenly had this thought:
"By drawing near to spiritual friends, one is able to courageously and diligently cultivate the path to all-knowledge;
by drawing near to spiritual friends, one is able to swiftly give birth to the ocean of great vows."
By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to undergo boundless suffering for all sentient beings throughout all future eons;
by associating with spiritual friends, one is able to don the armor of great diligence, such that the sound of preaching the Dharma within a single atom pervades the entire Dharma-realm;
by associating with spiritual friends, one is able to swiftly travel to the oceans of all directions.
By associating with spiritual friends, one cultivates the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all future kalpas within the space of a single hair-pore;
by associating with spiritual friends, one practices the conduct of a bodhisattva in every thought-moment, ultimately dwelling securely on the stage of omniscience;
by associating with spiritual friends, one is able to enter the paths of adornment consisting of the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to constantly and universally enter the gates of all dharma-realms;
by associating with spiritual friends, while always taking the dharma-realm as one's object without ever wavering from it, one is able to travel everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions.
At that time, having formed this thought, the youth Sudhana went to where the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana was.

He saw that night goddess in the assembly circle of the Tathāgata’s place of enlightenment, seated upon a lion throne of lotus-womb, having entered the liberation called "The Banner of Universal Joy of Great Power. From every single pore of her body, she emitted clouds of immeasurable kinds of transformation bodies, which, according to what was appropriate for each, preached the Dharma with wondrous voices, universally gathering in all immeasurable sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice and obtain benefit.
That is to say:

they emit clouds of immeasurable transformation bodies that fill all worlds throughout the ten directions, preaching the bodhisattva practice of the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*); they are entirely without attachment to any things and bestow gifts universally upon all sentient beings;
their minds are impartial and free from contempt, giving both internally and externally, able to relinquish even that which is difficult to give.

Furthermore, they emit clouds of transformation bodies as numerous as all sentient beings, filling the Dharma-realm and appearing before all beings everywhere. They proclaim the upholding of pure precepts without deficiency or transgression; that the cultivation of various ascetic practices is fully perfected; that there is no dependence upon any worldly realm; and that there is no attachment to any sensory objects. They speak of wandering through the cycle of birth and death; they speak of the flourishing and decline, the suffering and joy, of humans and devas; they speak of how all sensory realms are impure; they speak of how all phenomena are impermanent; and they speak of how all conditioned activities are suffering and devoid of flavor. Thus, they cause all in the world to abandon perversion, abide in the realm of the Buddhas, and uphold the precepts of the Tathāgata.
Thus they expound various forms of ethical conduct, the fragrance of which perfumes everywhere, causing all sentient beings to reach full maturity. Furthermore,
they manifest clouds of various bodies as numerous as all living beings, proclaiming the ability to endure all manner of suffering—
namely, being cut, beaten, reviled, and humiliated— with minds that remain serene, unmoving, and undisturbed.

Regarding all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), they are neither dejected nor haughty; toward all sentient beings, they do not give rise to pride (*māna*); and regarding the nature of all phenomena (*dharmatā*), they abide in patient endurance (*kṣānti*).
They speak of the bodhicitta as being inexhaustible; because the mind is inexhaustible, wisdom is also inexhaustible, universally severing the afflictions (*kleśa*) of all sentient beings.
They describe the lowly, ugly, and incomplete bodies of sentient beings, causing them to develop weary detachment (*nirveda*).
They praise the supreme body of the Tathāgatas, pure and of wondrous form, causing beings to give rise to joy.
Through such skillful means, they bring sentient beings to maturity.

Furthermore, they emanate clouds of various bodies equal in number to the realms of sentient beings, and according to the inclinations of the minds of those beings, they preach courageous diligence and the methods for cultivating the aids to the path of omniscience.
With courageous diligence, they subdue the enmity of Māra;
with courageous diligence, they give rise to the bodhicitta, remaining unshakable and non-regressive;
with courageous diligence, they deliver all sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death.
With courageous diligence, they eliminate all hardships of the evil realms;
with courageous diligence, they shatter the mountain of ignorance;
with courageous diligence, they make offerings to all Buddhas and Tathāgatas without ever becoming weary.
With courageous diligence, they uphold the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas;
with courageous diligence, they shatter and disperse all mountains of obstacles;
with courageous diligence, they teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity.
With courageous diligence, they adorn and purify all Buddha-lands.
Through such skillful means, they bring sentient beings to maturity.

Furthermore, they manifest various clouds of infinite bodies, using diverse expedients to cause all sentient beings to give rise to joy in their hearts, abandon evil intentions, and grow weary of all desires.
He teaches them shame and remorse, causing all sentient beings to guard and conceal their sense faculties;
he teaches them the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-conduct;
and he teaches them that the desire realm is the domain of Māra, causing them to give rise to fear.

To manifest a lack of delight in worldly sensual pleasures and a dwelling in the joy of the Dharma; to lead them, in due order, into the bliss of the various dhyānas and samādhis, causing them to contemplate and investigate so as to eliminate all afflictions;

and furthermore, to expound upon the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis, their spiritual powers, transformations, and sovereign play, so that all sentient beings may be filled with joy and gladness, free from sorrow and fear, their minds purified, their faculties sharpened, and their cultivation of the Dharma increased through deep appreciation.

Furthermore, they emit various clouds of bodies equal in number to the realm of sentient beings, in order to teach them to travel to lands in the ten directions to make offerings to all Buddhas, teachers, and true spiritual friends; to receive and uphold the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas with diligent and tireless effort;

and to expound upon and praise the ocean of all Tathāgatas, observe the ocean of all dharma-gates, reveal the essential natures and characteristics of all dharmas, open up all gates of samādhi, expand the realm of wisdom, and exhaust the ocean of doubts of all sentient beings;
and to manifest the vajra of wisdom to shatter the mountains of views of all sentient beings.
Raising the sun-disk of wisdom, they shatter the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings,
causing them all to rejoice and attain omniscience.

Furthermore, they manifest various clouds of bodies equal in number to the realms of sentient beings, universally appearing before all beings and preaching the Dharma with diverse words and phrases according to their respective needs.
In some cases, he speaks of worldly supernatural powers and the power of merit;

in others, he explains that the three realms are entirely terrifying, causing them to cease performing worldly karmic actions, to leave the sphere of the three realms, and to emerge from the dense forest of views;
or he praises the path of omniscience, causing them to transcend the stages of the two vehicles.
For some, they expound upon neither abiding in saṃsāra nor abiding in nirvāṇa, causing them not to become attached to the conditioned or the unconditioned;
for others, they expound upon dwelling in celestial palaces up to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), causing them to rejoice and resolve to attain bodhicitta.
By such skillful means, they teach and transform sentient beings, causing them all to ultimately attain omniscience.

And the night goddess who awakened me at that time was but an emanation of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra!
At that time, I was the King’s precious daughter; having been awakened by that night goddess, she led me to see the Buddha and inspired in me the resolve for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

From that time forth, for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, I have never fallen into the evil realms, but have always been born among humans and devas. In every place, I have constantly beheld all Buddhas, until finally, in the presence of the Buddha Lamp of Wondrous Virtue Banner, I attained this bodhisattva liberation of the Universal Joy Banner of Great Power. By means of this liberation, I thus benefit all sentient beings.
“Good son! I have attained only this liberation door of the Universal Joy Banner of Great Power.
As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, in every thought-moment they go before all Tathāgatas and are able to swiftly enter the ocean of all-knowledge;”
In every thought-moment, through the gateway of resolute departure, they enter the ocean of all great vows;
in every thought-moment, through the gateway of the ocean of vows, they give rise to all practices throughout all future eons, moment by moment.
Within each and every practice, they manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-lands; each body universally enters every gateway of the dharma-realm;
and within each gateway of the dharma-realm, throughout all buddha-lands, they teach various sublime practices in accordance with the minds of sentient beings.
Within every single atom of all lands, one sees oceans of infinite Tathāgatas;
at the site of each and every Tathāgata, one sees the spiritual powers of all Buddhas pervading the entire Dharma-realm;
and at the site of each and every Tathāgata, one sees the cultivation of bodhisattva practices throughout past kalpas.
In the presence of each and every Tathāgata, they receive and uphold all wheels of Dharma;
in the presence of each and every Tathāgata, they behold the entire ocean of miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? "Good son!
Within this assembly, there is a night goddess named:
Samantamukha-paritrāṇa-viśuddhaguṇa, go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva enter the bodhisattva conduct and purify the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and took his leave.
*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 69; *The Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 70.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Eleven: Entering the Dharma Realm.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard from the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā the liberation door of the Universal Banner of Joy, believed, understood, and entered it. He comprehended and accorded with it, contemplated and practiced it, and kept in mind all the instructions of his spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) without ever abandoning them for a moment. His faculties were not distracted; with a single-minded resolve, he wished to see his spiritual friend. Diligently seeking throughout the ten directions without weariness, he vowed to always remain in close proximity to him to generate all merits, to share the same roots of goodness as his spiritual friend, to attain the skillful means of his spiritual friend, and to enter the ocean of diligence by relying upon his spiritual friend, never being separated from him for immeasurable eons.
Having made this vow, he went to where the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā was.

At that time, the night goddess manifested for the youth Sudhana the spiritual power of a bodhisattva’s liberation for taming sentient beings; her body was adorned with all the marks and signs of excellence, and from between her two eyebrows she emitted a great light called "The Pure Banner of Universally Illuminating Wisdom-Lamps," with immeasurable rays of light as its retinue, which shone everywhere throughout all worlds.
Having illuminated the world, [the light] entered the crown of Sudhana’s head and filled his entire body.
At that moment, Sudhana attained the samādhi called "The Ultimate Pure Wheel.

Having attained this samādhi, he saw within the space between the two goddesses all the atoms of earth, water, and fire, as well as the atoms of diamond, mani-jewels, and various precious gems, along with flowers, incense, necklaces, and all manner of ornaments. Within each and every one of these atoms, he saw worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field undergoing their cycles of formation and destruction.
He also beheld the vast accumulations of all the great elements— earth, water, fire, and wind—
and saw all worlds connected together, all supported and sustained by the earth-wheel.

He saw all manner of mountains and seas, rivers and ponds, forests and groves, and various palaces—namely, the palaces of devas, the palaces of nāgas, the palaces of yakṣas, and even the palaces and dwellings of mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth;

he saw all the abodes of the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of King Yama; he saw the revolving of the various destinies, the coming and going of birth and death, and how beings receive retribution according to their karma, each distinct and different—all of this he beheld without exception.
Furthermore, he saw the distinctions among all worlds, namely:

some worlds were defiled, some were pure; some worlds tended toward defilement, some tended toward purity; some worlds were both defiled and pure, some were both pure and defiled; some worlds were exclusively pure; some worlds were level and upright, some were inverted, and some were tilted.
In this way, within all worlds and all realms of existence, one sees this Night Goddess Universal Savior of Sentient Beings at all times and in all places;
according to the differences in the physical forms, speech, conduct, and understanding of sentient beings,
she manifests before them all through the power of skillful means to transform and deliver them as is appropriate, causing them to...
May the sentient beings in the hells be freed from all suffering and poison; may the sentient beings in the animal realm not devour one another;
may the sentient beings in the realm of hungry ghosts be free from hunger and thirst; may the nāgas and others be liberated from all fears;
may the sentient beings of the desire realm be freed from the sufferings of the desire realm; and may the sentient beings of the human realm be freed from the fear of dark nights and from slander.
Fear of ill repute, fear of the great assembly, fear of being unable to make a living, fear of death, fear of the evil realms,
fear of severing the roots of goodness, fear of regressing from the bodhicitta, fear of encountering evil associates,
fear of being separated from virtuous friends, fear of falling into the stages of the two vehicles, fear of the various forms of birth and death, and fear of beings of different species.
They cause one to completely abandon all such fears as: the fear of living together [with the unwholesome], the fear of being born in an evil age,

the fear of being born into an evil lineage, the fear of committing evil karma, the fear of the obstructions of karma and afflictions, and the fear of being bound by attachment to various conceptualizations.
Furthermore, seeing all sentient beings—whether born from eggs, from wombs, from moisture, or by transformation;

whether possessing form or formless; whether with perception, without perception, or neither with nor without perception—he appears before them all, constantly and diligently providing rescue and protection, in order to fulfill the power of the Bodhisattva’s great vows. Deeply...
By the power of entering the bodhisattva samādhis; by the power of the steadfast superknowledges of bodhisattvas;
by the power of giving birth to the practices and vows of Samantabhadra; by the power of increasing and expanding the ocean of bodhisattva great compassion;

by attaining the unimpeded great loving-kindness that universally covers all sentient beings; by attaining the universal bestowal of immeasurable joy and bliss upon sentient beings; and by attaining universal gathering—
For the sake of the wisdom and skillful means of all sentient beings; for the sake of attaining the vast liberation, mastery, and supernormal powers of a bodhisattva;
for the sake of adorning and purifying all buddha-fields; for the sake of awakening to the realization of all dharmas;
for the sake of making offerings to all buddhas; for the sake of upholding all the teachings of the buddhas; and for the sake of accumulating all roots of goodness.
Because they cultivate all sublime practices through their faculties; because they enter the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings without obstruction;
because they know the various faculties of all sentient beings to teach and mature them;

because they purify the faith and understanding of all sentient beings and remove their evil obstructions; because they shatter the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings; and cause them to attain...

Because of the pure radiance of omniscience, at that time, the youth Sudhana, having witnessed this night goddess’s inconceivable and profound sphere of spiritual power—the Bodhisattva liberation of universally manifesting and subduing all sentient beings—was filled with immeasurable joy; he prostrated himself with his head at her feet and gazed up at her with single-minded devotion.
Then, that night goddess cast off her form adorned with the marks of a bodhisattva and returned to her original appearance, yet she did not relinquish her sovereign spiritual power.
At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in reverence, withdrew to stand to one side, and praised her in verse:
"I, Sudhana, have beheld such great spiritual power as this."
His heart gave rise to joy, and he spoke a verse in praise:
"I behold your venerable and wondrous body, adorned with all the marks;
like stars in the sky, every part is perfectly pure and radiant."
The sublime light he emits is as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable lands;
with various subtle and wondrous colors, it shines universally throughout the ten directions.
From every single pore, he emits rays of light as many as the thoughts in the minds of sentient beings.
From the tip of each ray of light, precious lotus flowers emerge;
from within these flowers, transformation bodies appear, capable of extinguishing the suffering of sentient beings.
From within the light, wondrous fragrances issue forth, universally perfuming all living beings.
Furthermore, he rains down various flowers as an offering to all Buddhas.
From between his two eyebrows, he emits wondrous light, equal in measure to Mount Sumeru;
it universally touches all sentient beings, causing them to extinguish the darkness of ignorance.
From his mouth he emits pure light, like immeasurable suns,
universally illuminating the vast realm of Vairocana.
From his eyes he emits pure light, like immeasurable moons.
Universally illuminating the lands of the ten directions, They completely extinguish the cataracts of worldly ignorance.
Manifesting various transformed bodies, With features equal in number to all sentient beings,
They fill the realms of the ten directions, Delivering and liberating those in the ocean of the three realms of existence.
Your wondrous body pervades the ten directions, appearing universally before all beings;
you extinguish the terrors of water, fire, thieves, kings, and all other fears.
Having received the instruction of the Joyful-Eyed One, I have now come into the presence of the Honored One.
Beholding the mark between the Honored One’s eyebrows, he emits a great,
pure light that universally illuminates the oceans of the ten directions, completely extinguishing all darkness;
manifesting his supernormal powers, it enters into my body.
Having encountered the Perfect Light, my heart gave rise to great joy;
I attained the samādhi of dhāraṇī and saw the Buddhas of the ten directions everywhere.
In all places I have passed through, I have seen every single atom.
Within each and every atom, one sees as many lands as there are atoms;
some are infinite lands, all entirely turbid and defiled,
where sentient beings undergo various sufferings, constantly lamenting and weeping in sorrow.
There are some defiled and pure lands, where joy is scarce and suffering and grief abound;
there he manifests the forms of the Three Vehicles and goes to those places to deliver beings.
There are some pure and defiled lands, which sentient beings delight to behold.
Bodhisattvas are ever-present, upholding all Buddha-dharmas.
Within every single atom are infinite oceans of pure lands,
adorned and purified by Vairocana Buddha throughout past kalpas.
In all lands, the Buddhas sit beneath the Bodhi tree;
having realized the Way, they turn the wheel of Dharma to deliver all living beings.
I see the Universal Savior Heaven, within those immeasurable lands.
"To all the abodes of the Buddhas, I go everywhere to make offerings.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the youth Sudhana addressed the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, saying: "O Goddess!"
This liberation is now most profound and rare! What is its name?
How long has it been since you attained this liberation?
"What kind of practice must one cultivate to attain purity?
The night goddess said, "Good son!"
This state is difficult to know; it cannot be fathomed by gods, humans, or any of those of the two vehicles. Why is this?

This is because it is the realm of those who dwell in the practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; the realm of those who dwell in the treasury of great compassion; the realm of those who rescue and protect all sentient beings; the realm of those who can purify all three evil realms and eight difficult conditions; the realm of those who can perpetuate the lineage of the Buddhas without interruption within all Buddha-fields; the realm of those who can uphold all Buddha-dharmas; the realm of those who can cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all kalpas to fulfill the ocean of great vows; the realm of those who can extinguish the darkness of ignorance and its obstructions with the light of pure wisdom throughout the ocean of all dharma-realms; and the realm of those who can universally illumine the ocean of skillful means of all three periods of time with the radiance of wisdom in a single thought-moment.
Relying on the power of the Buddha, I shall now speak for you. "Good son!
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there was an eon named:
It was perfectly pure, and the world was named Vairocana-Mahātejas; therein appeared as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru.
That Buddha-world has as its substance the *maṇi* jewels of all fragrant kings; it is adorned with various treasures and rests upon an ocean of stainless radiant *maṇi* king jewels.

Its shape is perfectly circular, formed from both the pure and the impure; it is covered above by clouds of canopies made of all manner of ornaments, and surrounded on all sides by a thousandfold circuit of mountains of maṇi-wheels of every kind of adornment.

There were ten trillion nayutas of four-continent worlds, all exquisitely adorned. In some of these four-continent worlds, sentient beings of evil karma resided; in others, sentient beings of mixed karma resided; in others, sentient beings with roots of goodness resided; and in yet others, there dwelt exclusively pure great bodhisattvas.
"To the east of this realm, on the side of the Cakravāḍa Mountains, there is a world-system of four continents named Jewel Lamp Flower Banner.
Its lands are pure and its food and drink are abundant; rice and grain grow there without the need for plowing or cultivation."
The palaces and towers were all wondrous and marvelous;

wish-fulfilling trees stood in rows everywhere, various incense trees constantly emitted clouds of fragrance, various garland trees constantly produced clouds of garlands, and various flower trees perpetually rained down exquisite blossoms;
various jewel trees produced all manner of rare gems, their immeasurable colored lights shining radiantly in every direction.
Various musical trees produce all manner of music, emitting wondrous sounds as they sway in the wind;
the light of the sun and moon and the sovereign maṇi-jewels illuminate everything, such that they enjoy bliss day and night without interruption.

"In these four continents, there are a hundred trillion nayutas of royal kingdoms. Each kingdom is surrounded by a thousand great rivers, all of which are covered with exquisite flowers that drift and sway with the current, emitting the sounds of celestial music. Precious trees of every kind are planted along their banks, adorned with various rare and wonderful treasures, while boats and ships come and go as people enjoy themselves according to their hearts' desire."
Between each river there are hundreds of billions of cities, and within each city there are hundreds of billions of nayutas of villages;
all such cities and villages are each surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of palaces and groves.
“Within this Jambudvīpa of the four continents, there is a land named Jewel Flower Lamp;
it is peaceful, prosperous, and joyful, with a flourishing population.
The sentient beings therein fully practice the ten virtuous actions.”
A wheel-turning king appeared therein, named Vairocana-Surabha-Maniratna-Padma-Śekhara;

he was born suddenly by transformation within a lotus flower, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, possessed of the seven treasures, and ruled over the four continents, constantly instructing all living beings through the True Dharma.
The king had a thousand sons, handsome and valiant, capable of subduing enemies;

he also had a hundred trillion nayutas of palace ladies and handmaidens, all of whom had planted the same roots of goodness as the king, cultivated the same practices, and were born at the same time. They were as upright and exquisite as celestial maidens, their bodies were of true golden color and constantly emitted radiance, and from every pore they perpetually issued a wondrous fragrance;
he was further endowed with a billion excellent ministers and fierce generals.
