The king had a principal consort named Pūrṇamukhī;

she was the king’s jewel among women, exceptionally beautiful and peerless, with golden skin, deep blue eyes and hair, a voice like the Brahma-sound, and a celestial fragrance upon her body that constantly emitted light illuminating a thousand yojanas.
He had a daughter named Universal Wisdom Flame Wondrous Virtue Eye;
her form was upright and dignified, her appearance exceptionally beautiful, such that sentient beings who beheld her could never tire of gazing upon her.
At that time, the lifespan of sentient beings was immeasurable, though some were of indeterminate duration and met with untimely death;

they possessed various forms and colors, various voices, various names, and various clans; and whether foolish or wise, brave or timid, poor or wealthy, suffering or happy, there were immeasurable categories, all of which were entirely different.
At that time, some person might say to another:
"My body is upright and handsome, while your form is base and ugly.
Having spoken these words, they mutually revile and insult one another, thereby accumulating unwholesome karma.
Because of these karmic actions, their lifespan, physical strength, and all pleasant things were entirely diminished.
At that time, to the north of that city was a Bodhi tree named Universal Radiance Dharma-Cloud Sound Banner.

Its roots were formed by indestructible mani-kings that manifested the adornments of the enlightenment sites of all Tathāgatas in every thought-moment; all manner of manis formed its trunk, and various exquisite jewels formed its leaves, which were distributed in orderly succession, harmoniously proportioned, and perfectly adorned throughout the four directions, above, and below.
They emit precious radiance and produce sublime sounds, proclaiming the profound realm of all Tathāgatas.
Before those trees is a fragrant pond named Jewel Flower Radiance,
Resounding with the Thunder of the Dharma;

Its banks were made of exquisite jewels, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of jewel trees; each tree was shaped like a bodhi tree, with various precious necklaces hanging down all around, and immeasurable pavilions, all fashioned from jewels, adorned the entire site of enlightenment.
Within that fragrant pond, a great lotus flower emerged,
named "Cloud of Adorned Realms Universally Manifesting the States of All Tathāgatas of the Three Times," from which as many Buddhas appeared as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru.

The first of those Buddhas was named Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner; upon this flower, he first attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and expounded the True Dharma for immeasurable thousands of years to bring sentient beings to maturity.

"When that Tathāgata had not yet attained Buddhahood, ten thousand years prior [to his enlightenment], this great lotus emitted a pure light called 'Manifesting All Supernatural Powers to Mature Sentient Beings.

Any sentient beings who encountered this light would have their minds spontaneously awakened, understanding everything without exception, and would know that the Buddha would appear ten thousand years hence."
Nine thousand years ago, he emitted a pure light named "Stainless Lamp for All Sentient Beings";
any sentient being who encountered this light obtained pure eyes, could see all forms, and knew that a Buddha would appear nine thousand years hence.
Eight thousand years ago, he emitted a great light named "The Sound of the Karmic Results of All Sentient Beings.
Any sentient being who encountered this light would immediately come to know for themselves the retributions of their various karmas and realize that a Buddha would appear after eight thousand years.
Seven thousand years ago, he emitted a great light called "Sound Producing All Roots of Goodness.
Any sentient beings who encountered this light had all their faculties made perfectly complete and came to know that a Buddha would appear seven thousand years hence.
Six thousand years ago, he emitted a great light named "Sound of the Buddha’s Inconceivable Realm.
Any sentient beings who encountered this light found their minds to be vast and attained universal mastery, knowing that the Buddha would appear six thousand years hence.
Five thousand years ago, he emitted a great light named "Sound that Adorns and Purifies All Buddha-fields.
Any sentient beings who encountered this light all beheld all the pure Buddha-lands and knew that five thousand years hence, a Buddha would appear.
Four thousand years ago, he emitted a great light named "Lamp of the Non-differentiation of the Realms of All Tathāgatas";
any sentient beings who encountered this light were all able to go and visit all Buddhas and know that a Buddha would appear four thousand years hence.
Three thousand years ago, he emitted a great light named "Lamp Illuminating the Three Times.
Any sentient beings who encountered this light were all able to perceive directly the ocean of past deeds of all Tathāgatas and knew that a Buddha would appear three thousand years hence.
Two thousand years ago, he emitted a great light named "The Tathāgata’s Lamp of Wisdom Free from Obscuration.

Any sentient beings who encountered this light would obtain the universal eye to see the spiritual transformations of all Tathāgatas, all Buddha-lands, and all sentient beings in all worlds, and they would know that a Buddha was destined to appear two thousand years hence.
A thousand years ago, he emitted a great light named "Causing All Sentient Beings to See the Buddha and Accumulate All Roots of Goodness.
If any sentient beings encountered this light, they would attain the Samādhi of Seeing the Buddha and know that the Buddha would appear one thousand years later.
Seven days prior to that, he emits a great light called "Sound of Joy for All Sentient Beings";
if there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they will be able to see all Buddhas everywhere and experience great joy, knowing that the Buddha shall appear after seven days.

When the seven days had passed, all worlds shook throughout; they were pure and undefiled, and in every thought-moment, all the pure Buddha-fields of the ten directions appeared universally, as did their various adornments.
If there were sentient beings whose faculties and natures were matured and who were destined to see the Buddha, they all proceeded to the site of enlightenment.

"At that time, within that world, all the peripheral mountain ranges, all the Sumeru mountains, all the various mountains, all the great oceans, all the lands, all the cities, all the walls, all the palaces, all the music, and all the speech issued forth sounds, praising and expounding upon the realm of the supernatural powers of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas."

Furthermore, they emitted clouds of all kinds of fragrances, clouds of all kinds of burning incense, clouds of all kinds of powdered incense, clouds of all kinds of fragrant mani-jewel images, clouds of all kinds of jewel-flames, clouds of all kinds of flame-treasures, clouds of all kinds of mani-garments, clouds of all kinds of necklaces, clouds of all kinds of exquisite flowers, clouds of the light of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the halo of all Tathāgatas, clouds of all kinds of music, clouds of the vow-sounds of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the ocean of the vocal sounds of all Tathāgatas, and clouds of the marks and embellishments of all Tathāgatas, manifesting the inconceivable signs of the Tathāgatas appearing in the world.

“Good son! This Great Jewel Lotus King, the Adorned Realm of All Tathāgatas Illumining the Three Times, is surrounded by lotuses as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields. Within each of these lotuses is a lion throne made of a treasury of mani jewels, and upon every throne sits a bodhisattva in the full lotus posture.”

“Good son! When that Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner King attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* here, he simultaneously attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in all worlds throughout the ten directions;
according to the minds of sentient beings, he appeared before them all to turn the wheel of Dharma.”
In each and every world, may they cause immeasurable sentient beings to leave behind the suffering of the evil realms;
may they cause immeasurable sentient beings to be born among the devas; may they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
may they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the practice of renunciant bodhi; and may they cause immeasurable sentient beings...
They accomplish the bodhisattva practice of the banner of valor; they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhisattva practice of the light of Dharma;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhisattva practice of pure faculties;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhisattva practice of equal power; they cause immeasurable sentient beings...

The practice of enlightenment that accomplishes entry into the city of Dharma; the practice of enlightenment that causes immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the indestructible power of supernatural penetrations that reaches all places;

the practice of enlightenment that causes immeasurable sentient beings to enter the path of universal-gate skillful means; and the practice of enlightenment that causes immeasurable sentient beings to dwell securely in the gates of samādhi.
He practiced this conduct so as to cause immeasurable sentient beings to achieve the bodhisattva practice that takes all pure objects as its condition;
he caused immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon bodhicitta; he caused immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the path of the bodhisattvas;
and he caused immeasurable sentient beings to dwell securely in the path of the pure pāramitās. He caused immeasurable...
While dwelling in the first stage of a bodhisattva, they cause immeasurable sentient beings to dwell in the second through the tenth stages of a bodhisattva;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to enter the sublime practices and vows of a bodhisattva;
and they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide securely in the pure practices and vows of Samantabhadra.

“Good son! When that Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner manifests such inconceivable and sovereign spiritual power to turn the wheel of Dharma, in each and every one of those worlds, he tames immeasurable sentient beings according to their needs, moment by moment.”

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, knowing that the sentient beings within the city of Ratnakusumapradīpa relied upon their own physical beauty and various sensory realms to give rise to arrogance and to look down upon others, manifested a wondrous body of extraordinary and sublime beauty.

He proceeded to that city and emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated everything, causing all the lights—the light of the noble king, the various exquisite jewels, the sun, moon, and stars, and the bodies of sentient beings—to become completely invisible. It was as if the rising sun eclipsed all other scenes, or like a mass of ink set against Jambūnada gold.
At that time, all the sentient beings spoke thus: "Who is this?
Is it a deva?"
"Is he Brahmā?
He has now emitted this light, causing all the radiance and color of our own bodies to become unmanifest.
Thus they reflected in various ways, yet none were able to understand it.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva was dwelling in the air above the precious palace of that wheel-turning king, and he addressed him, saying:
"Great King, you should know that now, within your kingdom, a Buddha has appeared in the world beneath the Bodhi tree named Universal Radiance Dharma-Cloud Sound Banner."

At that time, the daughter of the holy king, Lotus-Wondrous-Eye, seeing the sovereign radiance of the physical body manifested by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and hearing the sublime sounds issuing from the various ornaments upon his body, her heart was filled with joy, and she formed this thought:
"May all my roots of goodness enable me to obtain such a body, such adornments, such marks and signs, such dignified deportment, and such sovereignty."
Now this Great Sage is able to emit a great radiance within the dark night of the long cycle of birth and death for all sentient beings, revealing the appearance of the Tathāgata in the world;
may I also attain such a state, acting as a light of wisdom for all sentient beings to shatter all the darkness of their ignorance.
"May I never be separated from this spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) in whatever place I take birth. "Good son!

At that time, the Wheel-Turning King was surrounded by his precious queen, his thousand sons, his retinue, his ministers, his assistants, the fourfold army, and the immeasurable people within the city, who followed him before and behind."

By the king’s supernatural power, they all ascended into the air to a height of one yojana, emitting a great radiance that illuminated the four continents, enabling everyone everywhere to behold them. Desiring to lead all sentient beings to go together and see the Buddha, he praised him in verse, saying:
“The Tathāgata has appeared in the world, Universally rescuing all living beings;
You all should rise quickly And proceed to the presence of the Teacher.”
Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, a Buddha appears in the world to proclaim the profound and wondrous Dharma, benefiting all sentient beings.
The Buddha observes all worlds, seeing them constantly deluded by perversion.
Seeing the suffering of saṃsāra and birth-and-death, he gives rise to the mind of great compassion.
For countless billions of kalpas, he has cultivated the practices of bodhi;
his desire to deliver all sentient beings arises from the power of great compassion.
Head, eyes, hands, feet, and all else— He was able to relinquish it all for the sake of seeking bodhi, Throughout such immeasurable kalpas.
In immeasurable billions of kalpas, A Guide is difficult to encounter.
Whether seeing, hearing, or serving him, none of it shall pass in vain.
Now, together with you all, let us go to behold the Honored Tamer,
who sits upon the seat of the Tathāgata, having subdued Māra and attained perfect enlightenment.
Beholding the body of the Tathāgata, He radiates immeasurable light;
With various subtle and wondrous colors, He eliminates all darkness.
From every single pore, He emits inconceivable rays of light.
Universally illuminating all living beings, Causing them all to experience great joy.
You all should now give rise to A vast and resolute mind of diligence;
Go to the abode of that Tathāgata And pay him respectful homage and offerings.

At that time, after the Wheel-Turning Sage King had praised the Buddha with verses and awakened all sentient beings, ten thousand kinds of great clouds of offerings emerged from the roots of goodness of the Wheel-Turning King; he proceeded to the site of enlightenment and approached the place where the Tathāgata was.
That is to say:

clouds of all kinds of jewel canopies, clouds of all kinds of flower curtains, clouds of all kinds of precious robes, clouds of all kinds of jewel-bell nets, clouds of all kinds of fragrant oceans, clouds of all kinds of precious thrones, clouds of all kinds of precious banners, clouds of all kinds of palaces, clouds of all kinds of exquisite flowers, and clouds of all kinds of ornamental implements, which completely adorned and embellished the void of space.

Having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner King, circumambulated him countless hundreds of thousands of times, and sat before the Buddha upon a jewel lotus throne that universally illumines the ten directions.
At that time, the daughter of the Wheel-Turning King—Samantaprajñārci-vicitraguṇanetra—immediately removed all the ornaments from her body and scattered them over the Buddha.
At that time, the ornaments in the void transformed into a precious canopy, from which jeweled nets hung down, held aloft by dragon kings; all the palaces were arranged in rows within it.

Ten kinds of precious canopies surrounded it on all sides, shaped like multi-storied pavilions, pure both inside and out, adorned with clouds of various necklaces, jewel trees, fragrant seas, and *maṇi* gems.
Within this canopy is a Bodhi tree, its branches and leaves lush and flourishing, universally covering the Dharma-realm, manifesting infinite adornments in every thought-moment.
Under this tree sits Vairocana Tathāgata, surrounded before and behind by as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
all have arisen from the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra and abide in the stages of the bodhisattvas.
Abiding in non-differentiation, they also see all the lords of the worlds, and they also see the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgatas;
furthermore, they see the sequential formation and destruction of all kalpas and worlds,
and they also see the sequential appearance of all Buddhas in all those worlds, and they also see all of them.
In every single world-system, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is seen making offerings to the Buddhas and taming sentient beings;
furthermore, all those bodhisattvas are seen to be within the body of Samantabhadra, and one’s own body is also seen within that body.
One also sees that body before all Tathāgatas and all Samantabhadras.
In the presence of the Honored One, in the presence of all Bodhisattvas, and in the presence of all sentient beings,
he also beheld within each and every one of those worlds as many world-systems as there are atoms in a Buddha-field,
with their various boundaries, various supports, various shapes, various natures, various arrangements, and various...
Various adornments, various purities, and clouds of various adornments covered its summit;
there were various names of kalpas, various appearances of Buddhas, various periods of the three times, various locations,
various ways of abiding in the dharma-realm, various entries into the dharma-realm, various ways of abiding in space, and various suchnesses.
They come to the site of enlightenment, with the various supernormal powers of the Tathāgatas,
the various lion thrones of the Tathāgatas, the various oceans of assemblies of the Tathāgatas, the various distinctions among the retinues of the Tathāgatas,
the various skillful means of the Tathāgatas, the various turnings of the wheel of Dharma by the Tathāgatas, and the various sublime voices of the Tathāgatas.
Having beheld the various oceans of the Tathāgatas’ discourses and the various clouds of the Tathāgatas’ sūtras,
their minds became pure and they gave rise to great joy.

The Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Sublime Virtue Banner King preached for him a sūtra titled "The Turning of the Wheel of Dharma by All Tathāgatas," which had as its retinue as many sūtras as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields.

At that time, having heard this sutra, the woman attained ten thousand gates of samādhi; her mind became supple and free from coarseness or rigidity, like one newly conceived, like one just born, or like a śāla tree first sprouting its buds.

The mind of that samādhi is likewise thus, namely: the samādhi of directly beholding all Buddhas; the samādhi of universally illuminating all lands; the samādhi of entering the gates of all three periods of time; the samādhi of proclaiming the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas; the samādhi of knowing the ocean of vows of all Buddhas; the samādhi of awakening all sentient beings to cause them to emerge from the suffering of birth and death; the samādhi of constantly vowing to shatter the darkness of all sentient beings; the samādhi of constantly vowing to extinguish the suffering of all sentient beings; the samādhi of constantly vowing to produce the happiness of all sentient beings; the samādhi of teaching and transforming all sentient beings without ever becoming weary; the samādhi of the unobstructed banner of all Bodhisattvas; the samādhi of universally visiting all pure Buddha-lands...
Having attained these ten thousand samādhis, he further attained the mind of wondrous concentration,
the immovable mind, the joyful mind, the comforting mind, the vast mind, the mind that accords with spiritual friends, the mind that takes as its object the profound all-knowledge,
the mind that abides in the ocean of vast skillful means, and the mind that relinquishes all attachments.
A mind that does not abide in any worldly realm; a mind that enters the realm of the Tathāgatas;
a mind that universally illumines the ocean of all forms; a mind free from affliction and harm; a mind free from arrogance; a mind free from weariness;
a mind free from regression; a mind free from indolence; and a mind that contemplates the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.
The mind that abides in the ocean of all dharma-gates; the mind that observes the ocean of all dharma-gates; the mind that thoroughly knows the ocean of all sentient beings;
the mind that rescues and protects the ocean of all sentient beings; the mind that universally illumines the ocean of all worlds;
the mind that universally generates the ocean of all buddha-vows; and the mind that completely shatters all mountains of obstructions.
The mind that accumulates merit for the path; the mind that directly perceives the ten powers of all Buddhas; the mind that universally illumines the realm of Bodhisattvas;
the mind that increases the Bodhisattva’s aids to the path; and the mind that universally takes as its object the ocean of all directions.
With single-minded contemplation, he reflected upon the great vows of Samantabhadra and gave rise to oceans of vows as numerous as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields of all Tathāgatas:

He vowed to adorn and purify all Buddha-lands; he vowed to subdue and transform all sentient beings; he vowed to universally know the entire Dharma-realm; he vowed to universally enter the ocean of all Dharma-realms; he vowed to cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva in all Buddha-lands throughout all kalpas until the end of time; he vowed never to abandon any bodhisattva practice throughout all kalpas until the end of time; he vowed to draw near to and serve all Tathāgatas; he vowed to attend upon and serve all virtuous friends; he vowed to make offerings to all Buddhas; and he vowed that in every thought-moment he would cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, increasing all-encompassing wisdom without interruption...
Having made such oceans of vows, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, she brought to fulfillment all the great vows of Samantabhadra.

At that time, the Tathāgata further revealed and expounded for the girl the roots of goodness she had accumulated since first resolving her mind, the sublime practices she had cultivated, and the great fruits she had attained; he caused her to awaken and achieve the ocean of vows of all Tathāgatas, so that she would single-mindedly advance toward the stage of omniscience.
“Good son! Furthermore, prior to this, ten great kalpas ago, there was a world named Jewel of Solar Radiance; the Buddha’s name was:
Indraketudhvajarāja, this daughter of exquisite eyes,
within the bequeathed Dharma of that Tathāgata, was exhorted by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to repair a damaged image of the Buddha upon a lotus throne;
having repaired it, she further painted it, and having painted it, she further adorned it with jewels, thereby generating the mind set on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“Good son! I recall that in the past, it was through the spiritual friend Samantabhadra Bodhisattva that I planted these roots of goodness.

Since that time, I have never fallen into the evil realms; I have always been born into the lineages of celestial kings and human kings, possessing a handsome and pleasing appearance with all marks perfectly complete, such that people delight in beholding me. I have constantly seen the Buddhas and have always been able to draw near to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.”
"Up until the present day, he has shown me the way, guided and awakened me, and brought me to maturity, causing me to give rise to joy.
Good son, what do you think?"
At that time, was the Wheel-Turning Sage King Vairocanagarbha-suvicitra-ratnapadma-śekhara anyone else?
It was none other than the present Maitreya Bodhisattva.
The queen at that time, named Perfect Face, was the night goddess Silent Ocean Sound; her current dwelling place is not far from here.
The young girl Wondrous Virtue Eye was none other than myself.

At that time, I was a young girl; the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra exhorted me to repair an image of a lotus seat as a causal condition for unsurpassed bodhi, thereby causing me to give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, I first gave rise to the aspiration for enlightenment;

subsequently, I was guided so that I might behold the Buddha Wondrous Virtue Banner. I untied the necklaces from my body and scattered them as an offering to the Buddha. Witnessing the Buddha’s spiritual power and hearing his preaching of the Dharma, I immediately attained the bodhisattva liberation door of universally manifesting throughout all worlds to discipline sentient beings.
In every thought-moment, I see Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, and I also see their sites of enlightenment, their assemblies, and their pure lands;
I revere them all, honoring and making offerings to them, listening to their preaching of the Dharma, and practicing in accordance with their instructions.

“Good son! After that kalpa of perfect purity in the world-system of Great Majestic Virtue of Vairocana has passed, there is a subsequent world named Jewel Wheel Sublime Adornment; its kalpa is named:”
Mahāprabha, five hundred buddhas appeared therein, all of whom I served, honored, and made offerings to.
The first of those buddhas was named Mahākāruṇikadhvaja.
When he first left the home life, I was a night goddess and reverently made offerings to him.
Subsequently, another Buddha appeared, named Vajranārāyaṇadhvaja.
I was a wheel-turning monarch who reverently made offerings to him;
that Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "The Manifestation of All Buddhas," with as many sūtras as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields serving as its retinue.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Vajra Unobstructed Virtue;
at that time, I was a wheel-turning king and reverently made offerings to him.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "Universally Illuminating the Faculties of All Sentient Beings," with as many sūtras as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru serving as its retinue;
I have received and upheld them all.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Flame Mountain Sublime Adornment;
at that time, I was the daughter of an elder.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "The Treasury Universally Illuminating the Three Times," with as many sūtras as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa serving as its retinue;
I heard them all and received and upheld them according to the Dharma.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Supreme King of the High Peaks of the Ocean of All Dharmas; at that time,
I was an asura king and paid him reverent homage and offerings.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled "Discernment of All Dharma Realms," with five hundred sūtras as its retinue;
I heard them all and received and upheld them in accordance with the Dharma.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Ocean-Mountain Dharma-Light;
I was then a dragon king’s daughter, and I made offerings by raining down clouds of wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "Ocean of Increasing Joy," with a retinue of hundreds of billions of sūtras;
I heard them all and received and upheld them in accordance with the Dharma.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Jewel Flame Mountain Lamp; at that time,
I was a sea deity, and I reverently made offerings by raining down clouds of precious lotus flowers.
That Buddha preached for me a sutra named *Dharmadhātu-upāya-sāgara-prabhā*,
with as many attendant sutras as there are atoms in a buddha-field;
I heard them all and received and upheld them according to the Dharma.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Merit-Ocean Radiance-Wheel; at that time,

I was a rishi with the five supernatural powers who manifested great spiritual transformations, surrounded before and behind by sixty thousand rishis, raining down clouds of fragrant flowers as an offering.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "The Lamp of Non-attachment," with sixty thousand sūtras as its retinue;
I heard them all and received and upheld them according to the Dharma.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Vairocana-Guṇagarbha;
at that time, I was a chief earth goddess named:

Arising from the principle of equality, together with immeasurable earth goddesses, they rained down clouds of all kinds of jewel trees, all kinds of maṇi treasuries, and all kinds of precious necklaces as an offering;
that Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "The Source of the Wisdom-Treasury of All Tathāgatas," with immeasurable sūtras as its retinue.
I have heard them all and have received and upheld them without forgetting. Good son!
Following this sequence, the name of the final Buddha is:
The Lamp of Wondrous Virtue Filling the Dharma Realm of Space;
I was then a courtesan named Beautiful Face, who,
seeing the Buddha entering the city, made offerings through song and dance.
Empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, I leaped into the air and praised the Buddha with a thousand verses;
for my sake, the Buddha emitted from between his eyebrows a light called "Great Radiance Adorning the Dharma Realm," which pervasively touched my body.
Having been bathed by this light, I immediately attained a gate of liberation called "The Non-retrogressive Treasury of Skillful Means in the Dharma Realm. "Good son!
In this world-system, there have been as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, during which all Tathāgatas appeared;
I have served them all, honoring and making offerings to them.
I have remembered all the True Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas, not forgetting even a single word or a single phrase.
Before each and every one of those Tathāgatas, they extol and praise all Buddha-dharmas, extensively performing beneficial deeds for immeasurable sentient beings;

before each and every one of those Tathāgatas, they attain the light of omniscience, manifest the ocean of the dharma-realm of the three periods of time, and enter into all practices of Samantabhadra.
“Good son! By relying on the light of omniscience, I behold immeasurable Buddhas in every thought-moment;
having beheld these Buddhas, all the practices of Samantabhadra that I had not previously attained and had not previously seen are now fully perfected.”
"Why is this? Because they have attained the light of all-knowledge.

At that time, the night goddess Sarvasattvaparitrāṇaśīlā, wishing to further clarify the meaning of this liberation, received the Buddha's spiritual power and spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
“Sudhana, listen as I speak of the profound and difficult-to-see Dharma,
which universally illumines the three periods of time and all their various gateways.
Just as I first resolved my mind upon enlightenment, I single-mindedly sought the virtues of the Buddhas.”
The various liberations you shall enter—listen now with careful attention.
I recall a past age, more eons ago than there are atoms in a buddha-field;
immediately preceding that was an eon named Perfectly Pure.
At that time there was a world named Universal Illuminating Lamp,
wherein Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru appeared in the world:
the first Buddha was named Wisdom Flame, and the next Buddha was named Dharma Banner.
The third was Dharma-Sumeru; the fourth, Virtue-Lion;
the fifth, King of Tranquility; the sixth, Extinction of All Views;
the seventh, High Renown; and the eighth, Great Merit.
The ninth was named Victorious Sun, and the tenth was named Moon Face.
Under these ten Buddhas, he first awakened to the Dharma-gate.
Following this in succession, there appeared another ten Buddhas:
The first is named Abode of Space; the second, Universal Radiance;
the third, Abiding in All Directions; the fourth, Ocean of Right Mindfulness;
the fifth, Exalted and Victorious Light; and the sixth, Sumeru Cloud.
The seventh is named Dharma Flame Buddha; the eighth, Mountain Victorious Buddha;
the ninth, Great Compassion Flower; and the tenth, Dharma Realm Flower.
When these ten appear, the second gateway to awakening is realized.
Following this sequence, there appeared ten more Buddhas:
first, Prabhāketu Buddha; second, Jñāna Buddha; third, Cittārtha Buddha; fourth, Guṇendra Buddha.
The fifth was the Buddha Dayhui; the sixth, Huiwang Buddha;
the seventh, Shengzhi Buddha; the eighth, Guangwang Buddha;
the ninth, Yongmeng Buddha; and the tenth, Lianhua Buddha.
Under these ten Buddhas, he realized the third Dharma-gate.
Following this in succession, there appeared another ten Buddhas:
the first was Ratnārciśikhara, and the second was Guṇasāgara.
The third was Dharmaprabhāsa; the fourth, Padmagarbha;
the fifth, Satvavilocana; the sixth, Gandhaprabhāsarāja;
the seventh, Meruśrī; and the eighth, Gandharvarāja.
The ninth was Maṇigarbha, and the tenth was Śāntavarṇa.
Following this sequence, ten more Buddhas appeared:
the first Buddha was Vistīrṇajñāna, and the next Buddha was Ratnaprabhāsa.
The third was Gaganamegha; the fourth, Viśeṣadhvaja; the fifth, Paripūrṇaśīla; the sixth, Nārāyaṇa;
the seventh, Meruśrī; and the eighth, Guṇacakravartin.
The ninth was Anabhibhūdhvaja, and the tenth was Mahādrumaśaila.
Following these in succession, ten more Buddhas appeared:
the first was Sālagarbha, and the second was Lokādhipateya.
The third is Lofty Radiance; the fourth, Vajra Illumination;
the fifth, Earthly Power; the sixth, Profound Dharma;
the seventh, Sound of Dharma-Wisdom; and the eighth, Sumeru Banner.
The ninth was Supreme Radiance, and the tenth was Wondrous Jewel Light.
Following this in succession, ten more Buddhas appeared:
the first was Brahma Radiance, and the second was Sound of Space.
Third is Dharmadhātuka-śarīra; fourth is Prabhā-maṇḍala; fifth is Prajñā-ketu; sixth is Gaganapradīpa;
seventh is Sūkṣmaguṇa; eighth is Samantāvabhāsa-prabha.
The ninth was Victorious Light of Merit, and the tenth was Cloud of Great Compassion.
Following these in succession, there appeared ten further Buddhas:
the first was Wisdom of the Light of Power, and the second was Universally Manifesting Presence.
The third was Uccagāmin, the fourth was Prabhāśarīra,
the fifth was Dharmasamudgata Buddha, the sixth was Ratnākara Buddha,
the seventh was Vāyuvega, and the eighth was Śūradhvaja.
The ninth was Subhāṣaṇaratnacchatra, and the tenth was Tryadhvāvabhāsa.
Following these in succession, there appeared ten more Buddhas:
the first was Praṇidhānasāgaraprabha, and the second was Vajrakāya.
The third was Meru-guṇa; the fourth, Smṛti-dhvaja-rāja;
the fifth, Guṇa-mati; the sixth, Jñāna-pradīpa; the seventh, Prabhāsa-dhvaja; and the eighth, Vipula-jñāna.
The ninth is the Wisdom of the Dharma-realm, and the tenth is the Wisdom of the Ocean of Dharmas.
Following this sequence, ten further Buddhas appeared:
the first was named Dharma of Generosity, and the next was named Wheel of Merit.
The third was named Cloud of Supreme Excellence; the fourth, Lamp of Patient Wisdom;
the fifth, Sound of Tranquility; the sixth, Banner of Tranquility;
the seventh, Lamp of the World; and the eighth, Profound Great Vow.
The ninth was named Invincible Banner, and the tenth was named Ocean of Wisdom Flames.
Following these in succession, ten more Buddhas appeared:
the first Buddha was Dharma Sovereignty, and the second Buddha was Unobstructed Wisdom.
The third is named Ocean of Wisdom; the fourth is named Multitude of Wondrous Sounds;
the fifth is named Sovereign Bestower; the sixth is named Universally Manifest;
the seventh is named Body According to Desire; the eighth is named Abiding in Supreme Virtue.
The ninth was Svabhāva-buddha, and the tenth was Bhadra-guṇa-buddha.
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, all the Buddhas who appeared therein acted as universal lamps for the world; I have made offerings to them all.
Throughout eons as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field,
I have made offerings to all the Buddhas who appeared; by entering this gate of liberation,
I have practiced for immeasurable eons and attained this path.
"If you can practice accordingly, you too shall attain it before long. "Good son!
I know only this bodhisattva liberation of universally manifesting in all worlds to discipline sentient beings."

As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who have accumulated boundless practices, generated various understandings, manifested various bodies, possessed various faculties, fulfilled various vows, entered various samādhis, displayed various spiritual transformations, were able to contemplate phenomena in various ways, entered various gates of wisdom, and attained various radiances of Dharma—
how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
“Good son! Not far from here,
there is a night goddess named Ocean of Silent Sounds,
seated upon a lotus throne adorned with mani-jewel light banners, surrounded before and behind by a hundred thousand asankhyeyas of night goddesses.”
"Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Seventy;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Seventy-one.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Decree.
The Thirty-Ninth Chapter of the Twelve Entrances into the Dharma Realm, Part Twelve.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard from the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojasri the bodhisattva liberation door of "Universally Manifesting in All Worlds to Discipline Sentient Beings," understood and resolved it with full clarity, dwelling therein with sovereign ease;
he then proceeded to the abode of the night goddess Śāntamatisāgaravatī, prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and standing before her with palms joined, spoke these words:

“Noble One! I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. I wish to rely upon spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) to learn the bodhisattva conduct, enter the bodhisattva conduct, cultivate the bodhisattva conduct, and abide in the bodhisattva conduct.”
I only pray that you will, out of compassion, explain for me:
how does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct?
How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the night goddess said to Sudhana:
"Excellent, excellent,
son of good family!
"You are able to seek the bodhisattva practice by relying on spiritual friends.
Son of good family!
I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door called 'The Vast Adornment of Great Joy Arising in Every Thought-Moment.'"
Sudhana said, “Great Sage! What is the activity of this gate of liberation?”
What is the sphere of activity?
What skillful means are employed?
What observations are made?
The night goddess said:
"Good son! I have given rise to a mind of pure and impartial aspiration; I have given rise to a mind free from all worldly dust."
I arouse a mind of firm resolve for the joy of adornment that is pure and free from defilements;
I arouse a non-retrogressive mind that takes the stage of non-retrogression as its object and never turns back; I arouse an immovable mind like a mountain of jewels adorned with merit;
I arouse a mind that dwells nowhere; and I arouse a mind that appears universally before all sentient beings.
With a heart of rescue and protection, I give rise to a heart that never tires of beholding the ocean of all Buddhas;
I give rise to a heart that seeks the power of the pure vows of all Bodhisattvas; I give rise to a heart that abides in the ocean of the light of great wisdom;
I give rise to a heart that causes all sentient beings to transcend the wilderness of sorrow and affliction. I give rise to...
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon sorrow, grief, and affliction;
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon minds that find displeasure in forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena;
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon the suffering of separation from the beloved and the suffering of encountering the hated.
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon the suffering of adverse conditions, ignorance, and the like;
I resolve to act as a refuge for all sentient beings in perilous difficulties;
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to emerge from the realm of birth-and-death suffering; I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon...

I resolve to cause all sentient beings to achieve the unsurpassed Dharma-bliss of the Tathāgata, which counteracts the mental sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, death, and so forth; I resolve to cause all sentient beings to experience joy and bliss.
"Having generated this mind, I further preach the Dharma for them, causing them to gradually reach the stage of all-knowledge.
That is to say:

if I see sentient beings who delight in and are attached to the palaces and dwellings where they reside, I preach the Dharma for them, enabling them to comprehend the self-nature of all phenomena and to become free from all attachments."
If I see sentient beings who are attached to their parents, brothers, sisters, and so forth, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to join the pure assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;

if I see sentient beings who are attached to their wives and children, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to abandon the defilements of love within birth and death, to give rise to great compassion, and to regard all sentient beings with impartiality and non-duality;

if I see sentient beings dwelling in royal palaces attended by court ladies and maidservants, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to assemble with the multitude of sages and enter the teaching of the Tathāgata.
If I see sentient beings who are stained by and attached to sensory objects, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to enter the realm of the Tathāgata;
if I see sentient beings who are full of anger and resentment, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to abide in the Tathāgata’s perfection of patience;
if I see sentient beings whose minds are indolent, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the pure perfection of vigor.
If I see sentient beings whose minds are distracted, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the Tathāgata’s dhyāna-pāramitā;

if I see sentient beings who have entered the dense forest of views and are obscured by the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to emerge from that dense forest and darkness;
if I see sentient beings who lack wisdom, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the prajñā-pāramitā.
If I see sentient beings defiled by and attached to the triple world, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to transcend birth and death;
if I see sentient beings whose aspirations are inferior, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to fulfill their vows for the enlightenment of a Buddha;
if I see sentient beings dwelling in practices for their own benefit, I preach the Dharma for them to inspire in them the vow to benefit all sentient beings.
If I see sentient beings whose willpower and strength are feeble, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*);
if I see sentient beings with minds shrouded in the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*);
if I see sentient beings who lack physical marks, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the Tathāgata’s pure form-body (*rūpa-kāya*).
If I see sentient beings whose physical forms are ugly and deformed, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the unsurpassed, pure Dharma-body;
if I see sentient beings whose physical appearance is coarse and foul, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the subtle and wondrous form-body of a Tathāgata;
if I see sentient beings whose minds are filled with much anxiety and distress, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the ultimate peace and happiness of a Tathāgata.
If I see sentient beings suffering from poverty, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to obtain the jewel-treasury of bodhisattva merits;
if I see sentient beings dwelling in gardens and groves, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to diligently seek the causes and conditions of the Buddha-dharma;
if I see sentient beings traveling upon roads, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to advance toward the path of omniscience.
If I see sentient beings within villages, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to transcend the triple world;
if I see sentient beings dwelling among humans, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to surpass the paths of the two vehicles and abide in the stage of the Tathāgata;
if I see sentient beings residing in cities and walled towns, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to dwell in the city of the Dharma King.
If I see sentient beings dwelling in the four intermediate directions, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the wisdom of the equality of the three periods of time;
if I see sentient beings dwelling in the various cardinal directions, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the wisdom that perceives all phenomena;
if I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by craving, I preach the gate of the contemplation of impurity for them, so that they may abandon the defiled attachments of birth and death.
If I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by hatred, I teach them the gate of the contemplation of great loving-kindness, causing them to enter it and practice with diligence;
if I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by delusion, I teach them the Dharma so that they may attain clear wisdom and contemplate the ocean of all phenomena;
if I see sentient beings whose conduct is characterized by equal proportions of the afflictions, I teach them the Dharma so that they may enter the ocean of vows of the various vehicles.
If I see sentient beings who delight in the pleasures of birth and death, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to feel weary of and detach from it;

if I see sentient beings who are weary of the suffering of birth and death and are fit to be transformed and delivered by the Tathāgata, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to skillfully manifest taking birth;
if I see sentient beings who are attached to the five aggregates, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to abide in the state of non-reliance.
If I see sentient beings whose minds are inferior, I manifest for them the path of supreme adornment;
if I see sentient beings whose minds give rise to arrogance, I preach for them the dharma-patience of equality;
if I see sentient beings whose minds are deceitful and crooked, I preach for them the straightforward mind of a bodhisattva.

"Good son! By means of these immeasurable gifts of Dharma, I gather in all sentient beings, teaching and taming them through various skillful means, causing them to leave the evil realms, receive the joys of humans and devas, escape the bonds of the triple world, and abide in omniscience.
At that time, I attained a vast ocean of the light of the Dharma of great joy; my mind was serene and expansive, peaceful, secure, and blissful."
"Furthermore, good son!

I constantly observe the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Bodhisattvas, who cultivate various vows and practices, manifest various pure bodies, possess various constant radiances, and emit various rays of light;
who, through various skillful means, enter the gateway to omniscience and enter various samādhis, manifesting various..."
Manifesting various kinds of spiritual transformations, producing oceans of various sounds, possessing bodies adorned with various ornaments,
entering various gates of the Tathāgatas, visiting oceans of various lands, beholding oceans of various Buddhas,
attaining oceans of various eloquences, illuminating various realms of liberation, and obtaining oceans of various lights of wisdom;
They enter oceans of various samādhis, sport within various gates of liberation, and proceed toward omniscience through various doors.
They adorn the space of the dharma-realm with various ornaments and cover the void with clouds of various adornments.
They observe the assemblies at various sites of enlightenment and gather from various worlds.
Entering various buddha-fields, traveling to oceans of various directions, receiving various commands from Tathāgatas,
proceeding from the presence of various Tathāgatas, accompanied by various bodhisattvas, raining down clouds of various adornments,
entering the various skillful means of the Tathāgatas, contemplating the various oceans of the Tathāgatas' teachings, and entering various wisdoms.
"O Haimavat, you sit upon a seat of manifold adornments.
Son of good family!
As I observe this assembly in the bodhimaṇḍa, I perceive that the Buddha’s spiritual power is immeasurable and boundless, and thus I give rise to great joy."
“Good son! I observe that the Tathāgata Vairocana manifests inconceivable, pure form-bodies in every thought-moment;
having seen this, I give rise to great joy.”
Furthermore, he observed that in every thought-moment, the Tathāgata emits great radiance that fills the entire Dharma-realm;
having seen this, he gave rise to great joy.

He also saw that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there appeared oceans of light rays as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-lands, each ray of light having as its retinue light rays as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-lands, each pervading the entirety of the Dharma-realm and extinguishing the suffering of all sentient beings.
Having seen this, he gave rise to great joy.
Furthermore, son of good family!

I observe that from the Tathāgata’s crown and both shoulders, there emerge in every thought-moment clouds of jewel-flame mountains, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, filling all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions.
Having seen this, they gave rise to great joy.
Furthermore, good son!

I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there issue forth clouds of fragrant light as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, filling all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions.
Having seen this, they gave rise to great joy.
Furthermore, good son!

I observe that from each and every mark of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of Tathāgata-bodies adorned with all manner of marks, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, which travel everywhere throughout all worlds in the ten directions.
Having seen this, they gave rise to great joy.
Furthermore, son of good family!

I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of Buddha-transformations as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, manifesting the Tathāgata’s journey from his first resolve, through the cultivation of the pāramitās, the perfection of the path of adornment, and his entry into the bodhisattva stages.
Having seen this, they gave rise to great joy.
Furthermore, son of good family!

I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of bodies of celestial kings, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, along with the sovereign spiritual transformations of celestial kings. These pervade the entire Dharma-realm of the ten directions; to those who are to be liberated by the body of a celestial king, he appears before them and preaches the Dharma.
Having seen this, I gave rise to great joy.

Just as with the cloud-bodies of the celestial kings, so too did the cloud-bodies of the dragon kings, yakṣa kings, gandharva kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings, human kings, and Brahmā kings emerge from every single pore and preach the Dharma in such a manner;
having seen this, in every thought-moment I gave rise to great joy and great faith and delight, equal in measure to the *sarvajñatā* of the Dharma-realm.

That which was previously unattained is now for the first time attained; that which was previously unrealized is now for the first time realized; that which was previously unentered is now for the first time entered; that which was previously unfilled is now for the first time filled; that which was previously unseen is now for the first time seen; that which was previously unheard is now for the first time heard.

Why is this? Because they are able to thoroughly understand the characteristics of the dharma-realm; because they know that all dharmas possess but a single characteristic; because they are able to enter the path of the three periods of time with equanimity; and because they are able to expound all boundless dharmas.
“Good son! I have entered this ocean of light of liberation called ‘The Vast Adornment of Great Joy Arising Moment by Moment.
Furthermore, good son!”
This liberation is boundless, for it universally enters the gates of all dharma-realms;
this liberation is inexhaustible, for it equally gives rise to the mind of the nature of omniscience;
this liberation is limitless, for it enters into the thoughts and perceptions of all sentient beings throughout the boundless reaches of existence.
This liberation is profound, for it is the object of knowledge known by tranquil wisdom;
this liberation is vast, for it pervades the entire domain of all Tathāgatas;
this liberation is indestructible, for it is known by the eye of wisdom of Bodhisattvas.
This liberation is bottomless, for it exhausts the very source and depth of the Dharma-realm.
This liberation is the Universal Gate, for within a single phenomenon one universally perceives all spiritual transformations.
This liberation can never be grasped, for all dharmas and bodies are equal and non-dual.
This liberation is ultimately without birth, for it thoroughly understands all phenomena as being like illusions;
this liberation is like a reflected image, for it is produced by the light of the vows of omniscience;
this liberation is like a magical transformation, for it brings forth the sublime practices of the bodhisattvas born of transformation.
This liberation is like the great earth, for it serves as the foundation upon which all sentient beings rely;
this liberation is like vast water, for it can moisten all things through great compassion;
this liberation is like a great fire, for it dries up the waters of sentient beings' craving and attachment.
This liberation is like a great wind, for it causes all sentient beings to swiftly advance toward omniscience;
this liberation is like the great ocean, for it adorns all sentient beings with various meritorious qualities;
this liberation is like Mount Sumeru, for it brings forth the ocean of the Dharma-treasures of omniscience.
This liberation is like a great city wall, for it is adorned with all sublime dharmas;
this liberation is like space, for it universally accommodates the spiritual powers of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
this liberation is like a great cloud, for it universally rains down the rain of Dharma upon all sentient beings.
This liberation is like the pure sun, for it can shatter the darkness of ignorance in sentient beings;
this liberation is like the full moon, for it fulfills the vast ocean of merit and virtue;
this liberation is like true thusness (*tathatā*), for it is able to pervade all places.
This liberation is like one's own reflection, for it is manifested from one’s own virtuous karma;
this liberation is like an echo, for it preaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate;
this liberation is like a reflected image, for it appears in accordance with the minds of sentient beings.
This liberation is like the king of great trees, for it causes all the flowers of supernormal powers to bloom;
this liberation is like a vajra, for it has been indestructible from the very beginning;
this liberation is like a wish-fulfilling jewel, for it gives rise to immeasurable powers of mastery.
This liberation is like the king of maṇi jewels, the stainless treasury, because it manifests all the supernatural powers of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
this liberation is like the maṇi jewel of the banner of joy, because it can equally produce the sounds of the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas.
"Good son! I shall now speak this parable for you; you should contemplate it and, in accordance with it, enter into realization.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the night goddess Silent Sound-Ocean:
“Great Sage! How should one practice to attain this liberation?
The night goddess replied:
“Good son! A bodhisattva practices ten great dharma-treasuries and attains this liberation. What are these ten?
First, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of giving, satisfying the minds of all sentient beings according to their inclinations;
second, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of pure precepts, universally entering the ocean of all Buddhas' merits;
third, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of forbearance, being able to contemplate the nature of all phenomena everywhere.
Fourth, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of diligence, which proceeds toward all-knowledge and never regresses;
fifth, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of meditative concentration, which can extinguish the feverish afflictions of all sentient beings;
sixth, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of prajñā, which can thoroughly and universally know the ocean of all phenomena.
Seventh, by cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of skillful means, one is able to bring all oceans of sentient beings to full maturity;
eighth, by cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of vows, one practices the bodhisattva path throughout all future kalpas, pervading all Buddha-lands and all oceans of sentient beings;

ninth, by cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of powers, one manifests in every thought-moment within all oceans of the Dharma-realm and all Buddha-lands, attaining equal and perfect enlightenment without ever ceasing.
Tenth, by cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of pure wisdom, one attains the wisdom of the Tathāgata and universally knows all phenomena of the three periods of time without obstruction. Good son!
If bodhisattvas abide in these ten great treasuries of Dharma, they will be able to attain such liberation, which is purified, increased, firmly accumulated, and perfectly established.
Sudhana said, "Noble One! How long has it been since you first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
The night goddess said,
"Noble son! To the east of this Flower Bank Adorned World-Ocean, beyond ten world-oceans, there is a world-ocean named:
All-Pure Light Jewel;
within this ocean of world-systems, there is a world-system lineage named Sound of the Radiance of the Vows of All Tathāgatas.

Within it is a world named Pure Light Golden Adornment, whose substance is composed of all-fragrant diamond-maṇi kings; its shape is like a multi-storied pavilion, with clouds of various wondrous jewels forming its boundaries. It rests upon an ocean of all-jeweled necklaces, covered above by clouds of exquisite palaces, where purity and impurity are intermingled.
"In this world-system, in a past age, there was an eon named Universal Radiance Banner,
a land named Universal Fulfillment Wondrous Treasury, and a site of enlightenment named:
In the realm of All-Jeweled Treasury’s Wondrous Moonlight,
there was a Buddha named Sound of the Non-Retrogressive Dharma Realm, who attained unexcelled, complete,
and perfect enlightenment there; at that time, I was a bodhi-tree deity named:
The Lamp Banner of Perfect Merit and Radiance guarded that site of enlightenment;

I saw that Buddha attain equal and perfect enlightenment, manifest spiritual powers, and resolve his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and at that very moment, I attained a samādhi named "Universally Illuminating the Ocean of the Tathāgata’s Merits."
Within this site of enlightenment, there was subsequently a Tathāgata who appeared in the world,
named Law-tree Majestic Virtue Mountain;
at that time, my life having ended, I was reborn here once more as the night goddess presiding over the site of enlightenment, named:
By the light of his sublime merit and wisdom, seeing that Tathāgata turning the wheel of the true Dharma and manifesting great spiritual powers,
he immediately attained a samādhi named "Universally Illuminating All Realms Free from Greed."
Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named King of the Sound of the Ocean of All Dharmas; at that time,
I was a night goddess, and by virtue of seeing and serving that Buddha and making offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called:
It is the ground where all wholesome dharmas grow.
Next, a Tathāgata appeared in the world,
named Ratnārcis-pradīpa-dhvaja-rāja (Jewel Radiance Lamp Banner King).

At that time, I was a night goddess; because I was able to see the Buddha, attend upon him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called "Cloud of Universal Manifestation of Supernatural Powers and Radiance."
Next, there was a Tathāgata who appeared in the world, named Guṇasumeruprabha;
at that time, I was a night goddess, and by virtue of seeing that Buddha, serving him, and making offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called:
Universally illuminating the oceans of all Buddhas.
Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Dharma-Cloud Sound-King;
At that time, I was a night goddess; because I had the opportunity to see the Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi named "Lamp of the Ocean of All Dharmas."
Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named King Illuminating with the Lamp of Wisdom; at that time,
I was a night goddess, and by virtue of seeing and serving that Buddha and making offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called:
The Lamp of Pure Radiance that Extinguishes the Suffering of All Sentient Beings.
Next, a Tathāgata appeared in the world,
named Dharma-vīra-suvimala-śrī-ketu;

At that time, I was a night goddess; because I had the opportunity to see the Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called "The Radiant Treasury of the Tathāgatas of the Three Times."
Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Siṃhavikrāntadharmajñānapradīpa;
at that time, I was a night goddess, and by virtue of seeing that Buddha, serving him, and making offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called:
The Wheel of Unobstructed Wisdom of All Worlds.
Next, a Tathāgata appeared in the world, named King of the Mountain of the Power of Wisdom;

At that time, I was a night goddess; because I had the opportunity to see the Buddha, attend upon him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called "Universally Illuminating the Faculties and Conducts of All Sentient Beings Throughout the Three Times."

“Good son! In the world-system called Pure Light Gold Adornment, during the eon known as Universal Radiant Banner, there appeared in the world as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a buddha-field.”

At that time, I was sometimes a king of devas, sometimes a king of nāgas, sometimes a king of yakṣas, sometimes a king of gandharvas, sometimes a king of asuras, sometimes a king of garuḍas, sometimes a king of kiṃnaras, sometimes a king of mahoragas, sometimes a king of humans, or a Brahmā king; or I took the body of a deva, the body of a human, the body of a man, the body of a woman, the body of a boy, or the body of a girl—in all these forms, I made various kinds of offerings to all those Tathāgatas and also heard the various dharmas taught by those Buddhas.
When his life there ended, he was reborn in this very world-system, where he practiced the bodhisattva path for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field.

Thereafter, when his life ended, he was born in this Sahā World within the Flower Bank Array Ocean of Worlds; there he encountered the Tathāgata Krakucchanda, served and made offerings to him, and attained a samādhi named "Radiance Free from All Dust and Defilement."
Next, he encountered the Tathāgata Kanakamuni; by serving and making offerings to him, he attained a samādhi named "Universally Manifesting All Oceans of Buddha-lands.
Next, he encountered the Tathāgata Kāśyapa; by serving and making offerings to him, he attained a samādhi named:
I manifested an ocean of the vocal sounds of all sentient beings.
Subsequently, I encountered the Tathāgata Vairocana, who attained perfect enlightenment at this very site of the Way; in every thought-moment, he manifested great supernormal powers.
At that time, upon seeing him, I immediately attained this liberation called "The Great Joyful Adornment Arising in Every Thought-Moment."

"Having attained this liberation, one is able to enter oceans of the establishment of the dharma-realm as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields; therein, one sees every atom within all those buddha-fields in the oceans of the establishment of the dharma-realm, and within each and every atom, there are buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields."

In each and every buddha-field, there is a Vairocana Tathāgata seated at the site of enlightenment, attaining perfect awakening in every thought-moment and manifesting various spiritual transformations;
these manifested transformations each pervade the entire ocean of the dharma-realm.
He also saw himself present before all those Tathāgatas and heard the sublime Dharma they were preaching;

furthermore, he saw from every single pore of all those Buddhas an ocean of emanations issuing forth, manifesting supernatural powers to turn the wheel of the true Dharma according to the inclinations of sentient beings throughout the entire ocean of Dharma-realms, the ocean of worlds, all world-systems, and within all worlds.
I have attained the power of the swift dhāraṇī, by which I receive, uphold, and contemplate all words and meanings;
with clear and penetrating wisdom, I universally enter the treasury of all pure dharmas;
and with sovereign wisdom, I roam freely through the ocean of all profound dharmas.
By means of all-pervasive wisdom, they universally know the vast meanings of the three periods of time;
by means of equalizing wisdom, they universally penetrate the non-differentiated Dharma of all Buddhas.
Thus do they awaken to and understand all dharma-gates.
Within each and every Dharma-gate, one awakens to and understands all clouds of sūtras;
within each and every cloud of sūtras, one awakens to and understands all oceans of dharmas;
within each and every ocean of dharmas, one awakens to and understands all categories of dharmas.
Within each category of phenomena, one awakens to and understands all clouds of phenomena;
within each cloud of phenomena, one awakens to and understands all streams of phenomena;
within each stream of phenomena, there arises an ocean of all great joy.
Each and every ocean of great joy gives birth to all the stages;
each and every stage gives birth to all oceans of samādhi;
each and every ocean of samādhi attains all oceans of seeing the Buddhas.
In each vision of the ocean of Buddhas, one attains the ocean of light of omniscience;
in each ocean of light of omniscience, one universally illumines the three periods of time and pervasively enters the ten directions.
One comes to know the ocean of all past practices of immeasurable Tathāgatas.
They know the ocean of all the past lives of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the ocean of the difficult renunciations and acts of giving of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the ocean of the pure wheels of precepts of immeasurable Tathāgatas.
They know the immeasurable oceans of the pure forbearance of the Tathāgatas;
they know the immeasurable oceans of the vast diligence of the Tathāgatas;
they know the immeasurable oceans of the profound meditative concentration of the Tathāgatas.
They know the ocean of the prajñāpāramitā of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the ocean of the upāyapāramitā of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the ocean of the praṇidhānapāramitā of immeasurable Tathāgatas.
They know the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ power-pāramitās;
they know the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ wisdom-pāramitās;
they know the immeasurable ways in which the Tathāgatas of the past transcended the bodhisattva stages.
He knows how immeasurable Tathāgatas, while dwelling on the bodhisattva stages throughout oceans of immeasurable eons in the past, manifested supernatural powers;
he knows how immeasurable Tathāgatas entered the bodhisattva stages in the past;
and he knows how immeasurable Tathāgatas cultivated the bodhisattva stages in the past.
They know the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ past cultivation of the bodhisattva stages;
they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ past contemplation of the bodhisattva stages;
they know that when those immeasurable Tathāgatas were formerly bodhisattvas, they constantly beheld all Buddhas.
They know that when immeasurable Tathāgatas were formerly bodhisattvas, they saw the entirety of oceans of Buddhas and dwelt together with them throughout oceans of eons;
they know that when immeasurable Tathāgatas were formerly bodhisattvas, they manifested throughout oceans of lands by means of infinite bodies;
they know that when immeasurable Tathāgatas were formerly bodhisattvas, they cultivated vast practices pervading the entire dharma-realm.
They know how immeasurable Tathāgatas, in their past lives as bodhisattvas, manifested various gates of skillful means to discipline and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
they know how immeasurable Tathāgatas radiate great light, universally illuminating the oceans of all lands in the ten directions;
and they know how immeasurable Tathāgatas manifest great supernormal powers, appearing before all sentient beings everywhere.
They know the vast ground of wisdom of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma by immeasurable Tathāgatas;
and they know the manifestation of the ocean of marks by immeasurable Tathāgatas.
They know the ocean of manifested bodies of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the ocean of the vast powers of immeasurable Tathāgatas.
They know those Tathāgatas from their first aspiration until the extinction of the Dharma.
"In every thought-moment, I fully know and see them.
Son of good family! You asked me: "
"How long has it been since you first resolved your mind [for enlightenment]? "Good son!

In the past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in two Buddha-fields, as previously described, in the world-system called Pure Light Adorned with Gold, I was a tree deity of the Bodhi tree. There, hearing the Tathāgata Sound of the Non-regressing Dharma-realm preach the Dharma, I resolved my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Having cultivated the bodhisattva practices for as many eons as there are atoms in two buddha-fields, I was subsequently born within this Bhadrakalpa in this Sahā world.
From Kāśyapa Buddha up to Śākyamuni Buddha, and all future Buddhas of this kalpa, I have in every way approached and made offerings to them.
Just as he makes offerings to all future Buddhas within this world during this Bhadrakalpa,
so too does he approach and make offerings to all future Buddhas throughout all worlds and all kalpas.
"Good son! That world, Adorned with Pure Light Gold, still exists today, and the appearance of Buddhas therein continues without interruption.
You should single-mindedly cultivate this gate of great heroic valor of the Bodhisattvas."
At that time, the Night Goddess Silent Ocean Sound, wishing to reiterate the meaning of this liberation, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
“Sudhana, listen as I speak of this gate of pure liberation;
having heard it, give rise to joy and practice diligently until you reach its ultimate fulfillment.”
In the past, throughout oceans of eons, I gave rise to a heart of great faith and joy,
pure as space, constantly contemplating all-knowledge.
Toward the Buddhas of the three periods of time, I have in every case given rise to a heart of faith and joy.
Together with their assemblies, may they all forever remain in close proximity [to you].
In the past, I once beheld the Buddha making offerings for the sake of sentient beings;
having heard the pure Dharma, my heart was filled with great joy.
Always honoring one's parents, Revering and making offerings to them;
In this way, without rest or indolence, One enters this gate of liberation.
Regarding those who are old, sick, or poor, And whose faculties are incomplete;
I have compassion for all and deliver them all, Causing them to attain peace and security.
From water, fire, kings, and bandits, And from all terrors within the sea;
In the past, I cultivated various practices For the sake of rescuing those sentient beings.
Afflictions constantly blaze, enshrouded and covered by the obstructions of karma;
falling into various perilous paths, I rescue those sentient beings from all evil realms and the immeasurable pains of bitter torment.
Birth, old age, sickness, death, and the like— I vow to completely eliminate them all.
May I, throughout all future kalpas, Universally act for the sake of all sentient beings,
Extinguishing the suffering of birth and death, And enabling them to attain the ultimate bliss of Buddhahood.
“Good son! I only know this liberation of the ‘Adornment of Vast Joy Arising in Every Thought-moment.
As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, they enter deeply into the ocean of all dharma-realms, fully know the number of all kalpas, and universally behold the formation and destruction of all lands;”
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son! Within this assembly of the Tathāgata at this site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named:
He protects all cities and increases their majestic power.
Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded attention, observed the body of the Night Goddess Śāntamatisāgaravatī and spoke these verses:
"Following the instruction of my spiritual friend, I have come to the abode of this celestial goddess.
I see her seated upon a jewel throne, Her physical form boundless in extent."
Not by clinging to signs and forms, nor by calculating the existence of phenomena,
can those of inferior intellect and shallow understanding know the realm of the Honored One.
Even if the gods and humans of the world were to observe it for immeasurable eons, [they could not].
Nor can they be measured, for their physical forms are boundless.
Having transcended the five aggregates and not dwelling in any sense bases,
they have forever severed worldly doubt and manifest sovereign power.
Not grasping at internal or external phenomena, unmoving and unimpeded, with the eye of pure wisdom, one beholds the Buddha’s supernormal powers.
The body is the treasury of the True Dharma; the mind is unimpeded wisdom.
Having attained the illumination of wisdom, they further illuminate all sentient beings.
With minds that accumulate boundless karma, they adorn all worlds;
realizing that the world is entirely mind, they manifest bodies equal in number to all living beings.
Knowing that the world is entirely like a dream, That all Buddhas are like reflections,
and all phenomena are like echoes, They cause sentient beings to be free from attachment.
For the sake of beings of the three periods of time, They manifest their bodies in every thought-moment.
Yet with a mind that dwells nowhere, he preaches the Dharma throughout the ten directions.
Within a single mote of dust are infinite oceans of lands, oceans of Buddhas, and oceans of sentient beings—
all this is the power of this Honored One’s liberation.
Then, having spoken these verses, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.

At that time, the youth Sudhana followed the instructions of the night goddess Silent Ocean Sound, contemplating and examining the Dharma-gate she had taught. He did not forget a single word or phrase; he recollected, reflected upon, and discerned infinite profound intentions, infinite natures of phenomena, and all skillful means, spiritual powers, and wisdom, maintaining this continuity without interruption.
His mind became vast, and he realized and dwelt therein.

He went to the place where the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥprabhā was, and saw that night goddess seated upon a lion throne made of the king of *maṇi* jewels radiating all precious light, surrounded by countless night goddesses. She manifested a body appearing in the forms and colors of all sentient beings; she manifested a body universally facing all sentient beings; she manifested a body unstained by any world; she manifested a body equal in number to all sentient beings; she manifested a body transcending all worlds; she manifested a body that brings all sentient beings to maturity; she manifested a body that swiftly reaches all ten directions; she manifested a body that universally encompasses all ten directions; she manifested a body whose essential nature is ultimately that of a Tathāgata; and she manifested a body that ultimately tames all sentient beings.

Having seen this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined before him, spoke these words: "O Noble One!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva, while practicing the bodhisattva path, benefits sentient beings.
How does one gather sentient beings by means of the unsurpassed gathering?
How does one accord with the teachings of all Buddhas?
How does one draw near to the station of the Dharma King?
"I only pray that you will, out of compassion, explain this for me!
Then, that night goddess addressed Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!
