For the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings; for the sake of adorning and purifying all Buddha-fields; for the sake of making offerings to all Tathāgatas; because you wish to abide through all kalpas to rescue sentient beings; because you wish to guard and protect the lineage of all Buddhas; because you wish to universally enter the ten directions and cultivate all practices; because you wish to universally enter the ocean of all dharma-gates; because you wish to pervade all things with a mind of equanimity; because you wish to universally receive the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas; and because you wish to universally rain down the rain of Dharma according to the inclinations of the hearts of all sentient beings—you inquire about the gates of practice cultivated by all Bodhisattvas.

“Good son! I have attained the Bodhisattva liberation of the Profound, Sovereign, and Wondrous Sound; I am a great Dharma teacher, unimpeded and well-able to reveal the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas;
I possess the power of great vows and great compassion, causing all sentient beings to abide in the bodhicitta.”
They are able to perform all deeds that benefit sentient beings, for they accumulate roots of goodness without ceasing;
they serve as teachers who discipline all sentient beings, leading them to abide in the path to *sarvajñā* (omniscience);
they are the sun of pure Dharma for all worlds, universally illuminating the world to cause roots of goodness to arise.
Their minds are impartial toward all worlds, for they cause all sentient beings to increase in wholesome dharmas;
their minds are pure regarding all sensory objects, for they eliminate all unwholesome karma;
they vow to benefit all sentient beings, for their bodies constantly manifest universally in all lands.
They manifest all past events and causal conditions in order to cause all sentient beings to abide in virtuous conduct;
they constantly attend upon all spiritual friends in order to cause sentient beings to abide in the Buddha's teaching.
“O Son of the Buddha!

By means of these teachings, I bestow the gift of Dharma upon sentient beings, causing them to give rise to pure dharmas (*śukladharma*) and seek all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*). Their minds are as firm and unshakable as the Vajra-Nārāyaṇa treasury; they are well able to discern the power of the Buddhas and the power of Māras; they always draw near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); they shatter the mountain-like obstructions of karma and delusion; they gather the dharmas that assist the path to all-knowledge; and their minds never abandon the ground of all-knowledge.”
"Good son! When I benefit all sentient beings with such light of pure dharmas and gather the roots of goodness that assist the path, I perform ten kinds of observations of the dharma-realm."
What are these ten? They are as follows:
I know that the dharma-realm is immeasurable, because I have attained the light of vast wisdom;
I know the dharma-realm is boundless, for I see all that is known and seen by all Buddhas;
I know the dharma-realm is limitless, for I universally enter all Buddha-lands to reverently make offerings to all Tathāgatas;
I know the dharma-realm has no boundaries, for throughout the entire ocean of the dharma-realm, I manifest the practice of bodhisattva conduct.
I know that the dharma-realm is uninterrupted, because I have entered the uninterrupted wisdom of the Tathāgata;
I know that the dharma-realm is of a single nature, because the single voice of the Tathāgata is understood by all sentient beings without exception;
I know that the nature of the dharma-realm is pure, because I understand the Tathāgata’s vow to universally deliver all sentient beings.
I know that the dharma-realm pervades all sentient beings, because the sublime practices of Samantabhadra are universally pervasive;
I know that the dharma-realm is a single adornment, because the sublime practices of Samantabhadra beautifully adorn it;
I know that the dharma-realm is indestructible, because the roots of goodness of omniscience fill the dharma-realm and are indestructible.

"Good son! By performing these ten kinds of observations of the dharma-realm, I have gathered all roots of goodness and perfected the factors conducive to the path; I have come to understand the vast majesty and virtue of all Buddhas and have deeply entered the inconceivable realm of the Tathāgatas."
"Furthermore, noble son!
Through such right mindfulness and reflection, I have attained ten kinds of Tathāgata’s great majestic dharani-wheels. What are these ten?

They are: the dharani-wheel of universal entry into all dharmas; the dharani-wheel of universal upholding of all dharmas; the dharani-wheel of universal exposition of all dharmas; the dharani-wheel of universally recollecting all Buddhas of the ten directions; the dharani-wheel of universally proclaiming the names of all Buddhas; the dharani-wheel of universally entering the ocean of vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; the dharani-wheel of universally entering the ocean of all vehicles; the dharani-wheel of universally entering the ocean of karma of all sentient beings; the dharani-wheel of swiftly transforming all karma; and the dharani-wheel of swiftly generating all-knowledge.
"Good son! These ten dharani-wheels have ten thousand dharani-wheels as their retinue, and they constantly expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings."
“Good son! For some sentient beings I teach the dharma of the wisdom of hearing; for some sentient beings I teach the dharma of the wisdom of reflection;
for some sentient beings I teach the dharma of the wisdom of cultivation; for some sentient beings I teach the dharma of a single existence; or for some sentient beings...”
To some he taught the Dharma of the existence of all phenomena; to some he taught the Dharma of the ocean of names of a single Tathāgata;
to some he taught the Dharma of the ocean of names of all Tathāgatas; to some he taught the Dharma of a single world-ocean;
to some he taught the Dharma of all world-oceans; to some he taught the Dharma of the ocean of a single Buddha’s prophecy; or to some he taught...
The dharma of the ocean of prophecies granted by all Buddhas; or for some, he speaks of the dharma of the ocean of assemblies and sites of enlightenment of a single Tathāgata;
or for others, he speaks of the dharma of the ocean of assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas;
or for some, he speaks of the dharma of the ocean of wheels of Dharma of a single Tathāgata; or for others, he speaks of the dharma of the ocean of wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; or for...
He may preach the dharma of a single Tathāgata sūtra, or he may preach the dharma of the sūtras of all Tathāgatas;
he may preach the dharma of a single Tathāgata assembly, or he may preach the dharma of the assemblies of all Tathāgatas;
he may preach the dharma of the ocean of the mind of a single *sarvajñatā*, or he may preach [the dharma] of all *sarvajñatās*.
If it is for those with the mental disposition of the ocean-like dharma, he may teach the dharma of liberation through the Single Vehicle,
or he may teach the dharma of liberation through all vehicles. Good son!
By means of such inexpressible Dharma-gates as these, I teach for the sake of sentient beings. "Good son!

I have entered the ocean-like gates of the Tathāgata’s non-differentiated Dharma-realm, where I proclaim the unsurpassed Dharma to universally gather in all sentient beings, remaining in the conduct of Samantabhadra throughout all kalpas of the future."

"Good son! I have attained this profound liberation of sovereign wondrous sound; in every thought-moment, I increase all doors of liberation, and in every thought-moment, I fill the entire Dharma-realm."
Then, the youth Sudhana said to the Night Goddess:
"How marvelous, O Celestial Being!"
"This gate of liberation is so rare!
How long has it been since the Noble One realized it?
The night goddess replied:
“Good son! In the distant past, beyond world-systems as numerous as the atoms of dust in a kalpa,
there was an eon named Vimalaprabhā and a world-system named:

The Cloud of Merits of the Dharma-realm has as its essence the ocean of mani-jewel kings that manifest the karma of all sentient beings; it is shaped like a lotus and dwells within a network of fragrant mani-jewel Sumeru mountains as numerous as the atoms in the four continents. It is adorned with lotuses that produce the sounds of the original vows of all Tathāgatas, and has as its retinue lotuses as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru. Interspersed among them are fragrant mani-jewels as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, and there are four-continent worlds as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru; in each of these four-continent worlds, there are hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of cities.
“Good son! In that world, there is a four-continent system named Wondrous Banner;”
Within it is a royal capital named Universal Jewel Flower Light;
not far from here is a site of enlightenment named:
The palace of the Universal Manifestation Dharma King appeared,
within which Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru emerged; the first of these Buddhas was named King of the Radiance of the Thunderous Sound of the Dharma Ocean.
When that Buddha appeared in the world, there was a wheel-turning king named Pure Sunlight Face,
who, in the presence of that Buddha, received and upheld the *Sūtra of the Revolving Ocean of All Dharmas*.
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, that king left the household life to protect and uphold the True Dharma.
When the Dharma was about to perish, there arose a thousand different sects with a thousand varieties of teachings.
Approaching the final age of the kalpa, the obstructions of karma and delusion will be heavy;

many wicked bhikṣus will engage in much strife and contention, delighting in attachment to sensory realms and failing to seek meritorious qualities. They will take pleasure in discoursing on kings, bandits, women, nations, and oceans, as well as all manner of worldly discourses.
At that time, King Bhikṣu spoke to him, saying:
"How marvelous! How painful!"
"The Buddha has gathered this Dharma-torch throughout an ocean of immeasurable great kalpas; why do you all join together to destroy it?

Having said this, he ascended into the air to a height of seven tala trees. From his body issued immeasurable clouds of flames of various colors, emitting vast nets of light in manifold hues, causing immeasurable sentient beings to eliminate the heat of their afflictions and inspiring immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
By these causes and conditions, the teaching of that Tathāgata shall flourish once again for sixty-five thousand years.
At that time, there was a bhikṣuṇī named Dharmacakra-nirmāṇaprabhā, who was the daughter of this king;

together with a retinue of hundreds of thousands of bhikṣuṇīs, she heard the words of her father, the king, and witnessed his supernormal power. She gave rise to the bodhicitta and became irreversible from it, attaining a samādhi called:
As a lamp for all the Buddha-teachings, he further attained this profound liberation of Sovereign Sublime Sound;
having attained it, his body and mind became supple, and he immediately perceived before him all the spiritual powers of the Tathāgata Dharma-Ocean Thunder-Sound Radiance King.
“Good son, what do you think?

Was that Universal Monarch at that time—who followed the Tathāgata in turning the wheel of the true Dharma and who caused the Final Dharma to flourish after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa—someone else? Could it have been anyone other than [yourself]?”
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is that very person.
As for the bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakrapravartanaprabhā, she is none other than myself.

At that time, I protected the Buddha-dharma, causing one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs to attain non-retrogression in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, enabling them to realize the samādhi of directly beholding all Buddhas, enabling them to attain the *vajraprabha-dhāraṇī* of the dharma-wheel of all Buddhas, and enabling them to enter the ocean of the *prajñāpāramitā* of all dharma-gates.

"Good son! Of these Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, the last Buddha was named:
The Wisdom Lamp of the Dharma-realm City all appeared in the world during the eon of Stainless Radiance.
I have honored, approached, and made offerings to them all, listening to, receiving, and upholding the sublime Dharma they taught;

I also left the household life to study the Path under all those Tathāgatas, protecting and maintaining their teachings, and entering this Bodhisattva liberation of Profound and Sovereign Sublime Sound, using various skillful means to teach and bring immeasurable sentient beings to maturity.
From that time until now, throughout as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-field,
I have made offerings to all the Buddhas who appeared in the world and have practiced their teachings.
“Good son! Since that time, amidst all sentient beings who sleep in the darkness of ignorance during the night of saṃsāra, I alone have attained awakening;
I cause all sentient beings to guard the city of the mind, to abandon the city of the triple world, and to dwell in the unsurpassed dharma-city of omniscience.”

“Good son! I know only this profound liberation of Sovereign Wondrous Sound, which causes all worlds to leave behind discursive speech, to refrain from dualistic speech, to always speak words of truth, and to constantly utter pure speech.”

Just as all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to know the intrinsic nature of all speech, awakening all sentient beings with mastery in every thought-moment; entering the ocean of the vocal sounds of all sentient beings, they fully comprehend all expressions and clearly perceive the ocean of all dharma-doors. Having attained mastery in the dhāraṇī that universally encompasses all dharmas, they preach the Dharma according to the doubts in the minds of sentient beings, ultimately taming all sentient beings and being able to universally gather and sustain them. Skillfully cultivating the unsurpassed deeds of bodhisattvas, they penetrate deeply into the subtle wisdoms of bodhisattvas, are able to skillfully examine the treasuries of bodhisattvas, and are able to freely expound the teachings of bodhisattvas.
Why is this? Because they have already attained the accomplishment of the *dhāraṇī* of all wheels of Dharma.
How then could I know or speak of their meritorious conduct?
“Good son! Within this assembly of the Buddha, there is a night goddess named Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasumana.”
Go to him and ask:
How does a bodhisattva train in all-knowledge?
How does he establish all sentient beings so that they dwell in all-knowledge?
At that time, the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsambhavatejaḥśrī, wishing to reiterate the meaning of this liberation, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"The liberation of the Bodhisattva is profound and difficult to see; It is like space, with the mark of suchness and equality.
Within the boundless reaches of the Dharma-realm, They universally behold all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time."
Giving birth to immeasurable, supreme virtues, Realizing and entering the inconceivable true nature of phenomena,
Increasing all sovereign wisdoms, And opening the path to liberation throughout the three periods of time.
Passing through as many eons as there are motes of dust in a world-system, at that time there was an eon named Pure Light;
the world was called Cloud of Dharma Flames, and its city was named Jewel Flower Radiance.
Among them, the Buddhas who appeared in the world were as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru;
there was a Buddha named Dharma-Ocean Sound who first appeared during this eon,
continuing until the very last Buddha therein, named Dharma-Domain Flame-Lamp King.
To all such Tathāgatas as these, I have made offerings and listened to their teachings.
I beheld the Buddha Dharma-sāgara-ghoṣa, his body universally manifesting in true golden color, adorned with all the marks like a mountain of jewels;
there I resolved my mind, vowing to attain the state of a Tathāgata.
Upon briefly beholding the body of that Tathāgata, I immediately gave rise to the vast mind of Bodhi;
I vowed to diligently seek all-encompassing wisdom, Whose nature is equal to the Dharma-realm and empty space.
Through this, one universally beholds the Buddhas of the three periods of time, as well as the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas;
one also sees the oceans of lands and sentient beings, and thus universally takes them as objects of focus, giving rise to great compassion.
In accordance with the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, you manifest various infinite bodies;
pervading all lands throughout the ten directions, you shake the earth and radiate light to awaken all conscious beings.

I beheld a second Buddha and drew near to him; likewise, I saw the Buddhas of the ocean-like lands of the ten directions, until the final Buddha appeared—just as many as the atoms within Mount Sumeru.
Throughout as many eons as there are motes of dust in all lands,
I have personally approached and reverently served all the Tathāgatas, The lamps that illuminate the world, thereby purifying this liberation.

At that time, because the youth Sudhana had attained entry into this bodhisattva liberation of the profound, sovereign, and wondrous sound, he entered the ocean of boundless samādhis and the ocean of vast dhāraṇīs; he acquired the great supernormal powers of a bodhisattva and obtained the great eloquence of a bodhisattva.
With a heart of great joy, he observed the Night Goddess who Protects the City of All Lords and praised her with these verses:
"You have already traversed the vast ocean of sublime wisdom; You have already crossed the boundless ocean of all realms of existence."
With a long life, free from affliction, and a body that is a treasury of wisdom, you abide among this assembly with majestic power and radiant light.
Having thoroughly realized that the nature of phenomena is like space, you enter universally into the three periods of time without obstruction;
though every thought-moment grasps at all objects, every mind has forever severed all conceptual discrimination.
Thoroughly realizing that sentient beings have no inherent nature, yet giving rise to great compassion for them;
profoundly entering the gate of the Tathāgata’s liberation, he extensively delivers the immeasurable multitudes of the deluded.
Contemplating and reflecting upon all phenomena, They thoroughly understand and realize the nature of all dharmas;
Thus practicing the wisdom of the Buddha, They universally transform sentient beings, leading them to liberation.
The Deva is the teacher who tames sentient beings, revealing the path of the Tathāgata’s wisdom;
for the sake of all conscious beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, he preaches the practice of transcending all worldly fears.
Having already dwelled upon the path of all the Tathāgatas’ vows, Having already received the vast teachings of Bodhi,
Having already cultivated the power of all universal practices, They have already beheld the sovereign mastery of the Buddhas of the ten directions.
The celestial deity’s mind is pure as space, Universally free from all afflictions;
He thoroughly knows the infinite lands of the three periods of time, As well as all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and sentient beings.
The celestial deity understands them all in a single thought—days and nights, days and months, years, and oceans of kalpas;
he also knows all classes of sentient beings, with their various names, signs, and distinct differences.
The places of birth and death for sentient beings in the ten directions— those with form, those without form, those with perception, and those without perception—
they fully understand all according to worldly conventions, and guide them to enter the path of Bodhi.
Having been born into the family of the Tathāgata’s vows, And having entered the ocean of the virtues of all Buddhas,
With the pure Dharma-body and an unimpeded mind, They manifest various forms according to the inclinations of sentient beings.

Then, having spoken these verses, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.

Part Thirteen of the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter, the Thirty-ninth, Part Thirteen.
At that time, the youth Sudhana entered the Bodhisattva liberation door of the Profound and Sovereign Sublime Sound, and his practice advanced further.

He went to the place where the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasamantabhadrā was; there he saw her body within a pavilion of various precious fragrant trees, seated upon a lion throne made of exquisite jewels, surrounded by a million night goddesses.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, joined his palms before him, and spoke these words: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct."
"How does one attain all-knowledge?
I only pray that you will look upon me with compassion and explain this for me!
The night goddess replied:

“Good son! In this Sahā world, when the sun has set, the lotuses have closed, and the multitudes of people have finished their excursions and sightseeing, I see all those sentient beings—whether on mountains, by waters, in cities, or in wildernesses—in all such places, each resolving to return to their own dwellings.
I secretly protect them all, enabling them to attain the right path, reach their destinations, and abide in peace and happiness throughout the night.”
“Good son! If there are sentient beings who,
in the prime of their youth and endowed with fine appearance, are arrogant and heedless, indulging themselves in the five desires,
I manifest for them the signs of old age, sickness, and death, causing them to give rise to dread so that they may abandon all evils.”
Furthermore, he praised various roots of goodness to encourage their cultivation:
for those who were stingy, he extolled generosity;
for those who had violated the precepts, he lauded pure morality.
To those who harbor ill will, they teach them to abide in great loving-kindness;
to those who cherish malice and harm, they cause them to practice patience;
and to those who are indolent, they cause them to arouse diligence.
If there are those who are distracted, cause them to cultivate meditative concentration;
if there are those who abide in wrong wisdom, cause them to study Prajñā;
if there are those who delight in the Hīnayāna, cause them to abide in the Mahāyāna.
For those who delight in and are attached to the various realms of existence within the three worlds, they cause them to abide in the bodhisattva’s perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*);

for those sentient beings whose merit and wisdom are meager and inferior, who are oppressed by their fetters and karma and beset by many obstacles, they cause them to abide in the bodhisattva’s perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*);
for those sentient beings whose minds are dark and dull and who lack wisdom, they cause them to abide in the bodhisattva’s perfection of knowledge (*jñāna-pāramitā*).
“Good son! I have already attained the bodhisattva liberation door called ‘The Radiance of Vast Great Joy Arising. Sudhana said:
“Great Sage! What is the sphere of this gate of liberation?
The night goddess said:
“Good son! Entering this liberation, one is able to know the Tathāgata’s skillful means of wisdom that universally gathers in all sentient beings.
How does he gather them in universally?

"Good son! All the various pleasures experienced by all sentient beings are due to the power of the Tathāgata’s majestic virtue; because they accord with the Tathāgata’s teaching; because they practice the Tathāgata’s words; because they learn the Tathāgata’s conduct; because they obtain the power of the Tathāgata’s protection; because they cultivate the path sealed by the Tathāgata; because they plant the roots of goodness practiced by the Tathāgata; because they rely on the Dharma preached by the Tathāgata; because they are illuminated by the sun-like light of the Tathāgata’s wisdom; and because they are sustained by the power of the Tathāgata’s inherently pure karma."
How is this known to be so? Good son!

Having entered this liberation of the "Light of Great Joy Arising from Birth," I recollect the ocean of bodhisattva practices cultivated by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana in the past, and I see them all clearly.

“Good son! In the past, when the World-Honored One was a bodhisattva, he saw all sentient beings clinging to ‘self’ and ‘what belongs to self,’ dwelling in the dark chamber of ignorance, entering the dense forest of various views, bound by craving and attachment, destroyed by anger, disordered by folly, and entangled by stinginess and envy; thus they transmigrate through birth and death, impoverished and suffering, unable to encounter the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.”
Having seen this, they give rise to a heart of great compassion to benefit sentient beings.
That is to say:
they give rise to the aspiration to obtain all manner of exquisite treasures and requisites to gather in the hearts of sentient beings;

May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the necessities of life so that their minds lack nothing; may they have minds free from attachment toward all worldly affairs; may they have minds free from greedy defilement regarding all sensory objects; may they have minds free from stinginess regarding all possessions; may they have minds free from expectation regarding all karmic rewards; may they have minds free from envy regarding all prosperity and excellence; and may they have minds free from delusion regarding all causes and conditions;
may they give rise to a mind that contemplates the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā);
and may they give rise to a mind that seeks to rescue and protect all sentient beings.
They give rise to a mind that enters deeply into the whirlpools of all phenomena;
they give rise to a mind of great equanimity and loving-kindness abiding toward all sentient beings;
they give rise to a mind of great compassion that employs skillful means toward all sentient beings.
He gives rise to the mind that acts as a great Dharma-canopy to universally cover the hearts of all sentient beings;
he gives rise to the mind that uses the vajra-pestle of great wisdom to shatter the mountains of afflictive obstructions within the hearts of all sentient beings;
he gives rise to the mind that causes all sentient beings to increase in joy and bliss.
They give rise to the mind that aspires for all sentient beings to attain ultimate peace and happiness;
they give rise to the mind that rains down all manner of wealth and treasures according to the desires of sentient beings;
they give rise to the mind that brings all sentient beings to maturity through impartial skillful means.
He gives rise to the mind that desires to satisfy all sentient beings with the wealth of the noble ones;
he gives rise to the mind that vows that all sentient beings shall ultimately attain the fruit of the wisdom of the ten powers.
Having given rise to such minds, he attains the power of a bodhisattva and manifests great spiritual transformations.

Pervading the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space, before all sentient beings, he universally rains down all manner of necessities for life; according to their desires, he completely fulfills their wishes and causes them all to rejoice, without regret or stinginess, continuously and without interruption.

By these skillful means, they universally gather in and transform all sentient beings, bringing them to maturity so that all may escape the hardships of birth and death, yet they do not seek any recompense for their efforts;

they purify the jewel-like minds of all sentient beings, causing them to give rise to the same roots of goodness shared by all Buddhas, and increasing the great ocean of merit and virtue of omniscience.

"In this way, the Bodhisattva matures all sentient beings in every thought-moment; in every thought-moment, they purify all Buddha-lands; in every thought-moment, they universally enter all dharma-realms; in every thought-moment, they pervade the entirety of the realm of space; in every thought-moment, they universally enter all three periods of time; in every thought-moment, they achieve the wisdom that tames all sentient beings; in every thought-moment, they constantly turn all wheels of Dharma; in every thought-moment, they constantly benefit sentient beings through the path of omniscience; in every thought-moment, they universally manifest before all various classes of beings in all worlds throughout all future eons, appearing as all Buddhas attaining equal and perfect enlightenment; and in every thought-moment, they universally cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva in all worlds and throughout all kalpas, never giving rise to dualistic thoughts."
That is to say:

universally entering into all the vast oceans of world-systems and all varieties of world-germs—into worlds of various boundaries, worlds of various adornments, worlds of various essential natures, worlds of various shapes, and worlds of various distributions; there are worlds that are defiled yet mixed with purity, worlds that are pure yet mixed with defilement, worlds that are exclusively defiled, and worlds that are exclusively pure; some are small and some are large, some are coarse and some are subtle, some are upright and some are tilted, and some are inverted and some are face-up.

In this way, throughout all worlds, they practice the various bodhisattva deeds moment by moment, enter the bodhisattva stage, manifest the power of a bodhisattva, and also manifest the bodies of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, causing all sentient beings to universally know and see them according to their own minds.

“Good son! In the past, when the Tathāgata Vairocana was thus practicing the bodhisattva path, he beheld all sentient beings—not cultivating merit, lacking wisdom, attached to ‘self’ and ‘what belongs to self,’ obscured by the cataracts of ignorance, engaging in improper reflection, entering into various false views, failing to recognize cause and effect, following the karma of afflictions, and falling into the deep pit of the perils of birth and death, where they underwent all manner of immeasurable sufferings.”

—Arousing the mind of great compassion, fully cultivating all practices of the *pāramitās*, and extolling and praising the firm roots of goodness for the sake of all sentient beings, so that they may dwell securely, far removed from the sufferings of birth-and-death and poverty, and diligently practice the dharmas of merit and wisdom that assist the path;

preaching for them the various gateways of cause and effect, preaching that karmic retribution is never contradictory, preaching the points of realization within the Dharma, and preaching the inclinations and understandings of all sentient beings, as well as all the lands where they take birth, so that they may not sever the seed of all Buddhas, so that they may protect all the Buddha-teachings, and so that they may abandon all evils.

Furthermore, it is to praise the dharmas that assist the path toward omniscience, to cause all sentient beings to give rise to joy in their hearts, to cause them to practice the gift of Dharma so as to universally gather all beings, to cause them to initiate the conduct of omniscience, to cause them to study and train in the path of the perfections of the great bodhisattvas, to cause them to increase and perfect the ocean of all roots of goodness for omniscience, to cause them to fulfill all noble riches, to cause them to enter the gate of the Buddha’s sovereignty, to cause them to grasp immeasurable skillful means, to cause them to behold the majestic power of the Tathāgata, and to cause them to dwell securely in the wisdom of a bodhisattva.
The youth Sudhana said, "Noble One,
how long has it been since you first resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
The night goddess replied:

“Good son! This place is difficult to believe, difficult to know, difficult to understand, difficult to enter, and difficult to explain; it cannot be known by any in the world, nor by those of the two vehicles.”
Except for those protected by the spiritual power of the Buddhas, embraced by virtuous friends, who have accumulated supreme merit,
whose aspirations are pure, who possess no inferior mind, no defiled mind, and no deceitful mind,
and who have attained a mind of universally illuminating wisdom-light and resolved to universally benefit all sentient beings— [all others] are subject to all afflictions...
With a mind that afflictions and all Māras cannot destroy, a mind that will surely achieve omniscience once aroused,
a mind that does not delight in any of the pleasures of saṃsāra, a mind that can seek the wondrous bliss of all Buddhas,
a mind that can extinguish the suffering and affliction of all sentient beings, a mind that can cultivate the ocean of all Buddha-merits, [and a mind that can contemplate] all phenomena...
The true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) can fully possess all pure faith and resolve; it can transcend the turbulent flood of all birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*);
it can enter the ocean of wisdom of all Tathāgatas; it can resolutely reach the city of the unsurpassed Dharma;
it can courageously enter the realm of the Tathāgatas; it can swiftly proceed toward the stages of all Buddhas; it can immediately...
Having accomplished all powers of knowledge and attained ultimate mastery over the ten powers,
such a person is able to uphold, enter into, and comprehend this.
Why is this? This is the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom; even all bodhisattvas cannot know it, much less other sentient beings!

Nevertheless, by the Buddha’s majestic power, I now wish to cause the minds of those sentient beings who are disciplined and ready for transformation to be swiftly purified, and to cause the minds of those sentient beings who cultivate roots of goodness to attain mastery. Therefore, according to your question, I shall proclaim it for you.
At that time, the night goddess Sarvarukṣusarvapuṣpasaṃkusumitā, wishing to clarify this meaning further, contemplated the realm of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time and spoke in verse:
“O Son of the Buddha, regarding what you have asked— The profound realm of the Buddhas, inconceivable as the atoms of lands over kalpas— It could not be fully described even in an eon.”
Those who are not shrouded by greed, hatred, delusion, pride, or confusion—
such beings as these are able to know the Buddha’s wondrous Dharma.
Those who do not abide in stinginess or envy, nor possess minds turbid with flattery and deception, [are able to know it].
Enveloped by afflictions and karma, yet able to know the realm of the Buddha;
not attached to the aggregates, elements, or sense bases, nor conceiving of a self-body;
such people with inverted views and inverted perceptions can know that which the Buddha has awakened to.
The realm of the Buddha is tranquil; its nature is pure and free from conceptual construction.
Only those who do not cling to the various realms of existence can know this Dharma-nature.
Born into the family of the Buddhas, they are protected by the Buddhas.
Those who uphold the treasury of the Buddha’s Dharma are the domain of the eye of wisdom.
By drawing near to virtuous friends, delighting in the pure and white dharmas,
and diligently seeking the powers of all Buddhas, they rejoice upon hearing this teaching.
The mind is pure and free from discrimination, like the great void;
the lamp of wisdom destroys all darkness—this is their realm.
With a mind of great compassion, they universally cover all worlds.
All things are equal; this is their realm.
With a joyful mind free from attachment, they are able to relinquish everything;
bestowing gifts equally upon all sentient beings—this is their realm.
With a pure mind free from all evils, ultimately without regret,
and practicing in accordance with the teachings of all Buddhas— this is their realm.
They thoroughly understand the intrinsic nature of phenomena as well as the various seeds of karma.
Their minds are free from agitation and disorder; this is their domain.
With courageous and diligent perseverance, they abide with a mind that never regresses;
They assiduously cultivate all-knowledge; this is their domain.
With a mind tranquil, abiding in samādhi, Ultimately cool and free from feverish affliction,
Having cultivated the causes for the ocean of all-knowledge— This is the liberation of the realized one.
Thoroughly knowing the true nature of all things, Deeply entering the gates of the boundless Dharma-realm,
Universally delivering all living beings without exception— This is the liberation of the Lamp of Wisdom.
Thoroughly realizing the true nature of sentient beings, They do not cling to the ocean of all existences;
Like reflections appearing everywhere within the water of the mind— This is the liberation of those on the Right Path.
Born from the skillful means and vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time,
Exerting diligent practice throughout all kalpas and lands— This is the liberation of Samantabhadra.
Universally entering the gates of all dharma realms, They behold the oceans of lands throughout the ten directions,
And likewise see the kalpas of their formation and destruction, Yet their minds remain ultimately free from discrimination.

Within every single atom of the entire dharma-realm, one sees the Tathāgata sitting beneath the tree of enlightenment, attaining bodhi and transforming all beings; this is the liberation of unimpeded vision.
Throughout oceans of immeasurable great kalpas, you have drawn near to and made offerings to spiritual friends;
for the sake of benefiting all living beings, you sought the True Dharma, and having heard it, you remember it without any forgetfulness.
The vast realm of Vairocana is immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable;
receiving the Buddha’s power, I shall explain it for you, so that your profound mind may become utterly pure.
“Good son! In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds,
there was an ocean of worlds named Universal Radiance True Gold Maṇi Mountain;”
Within that ocean of worlds, there appeared a Buddha named King of Silent Majesty,
Mountain of Wisdom Universally Illuminating the Dharma Realm. Good son!
When that Buddha was practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, he purified that world-ocean.
Within that world-ocean, there were world-systems as numerous as the atoms of a world;
in each world-system, there were worlds as numerous as the atoms of a world.
In each and every world, a Tathāgata appeared in the world;
each and every Tathāgata preached as many sūtras as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds;

in each and every sūtra, he bestowed predictions of enlightenment upon as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a buddha-field, manifesting various supernatural powers, expounding various dharma-gates, and delivering immeasurable sentient beings.
“Good son! Within that ocean of world-systems called Universal Radiance True Gold Mani Mountain, there is a world-system type named Universal Adornment Banner.
Within this world-system, there is a world named Universal Radiance of All Jewel Colors;
it has as its substance mani-jewel kings that manifest the reflections of all emanation-buddhas, and its shape is like a celestial city.

It has as its lower boundary mani-jewel kings that manifest the images of the dharma-assembly sites of all Tathāgatas, and it rests upon an ocean of all jewel-flowers, consisting of a mixture of pure and impure realms.

In this world-system, there are as many sets of four continents as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru; among them, one set of four continents stands at the very center, named Banner of All Jewel Mountains.
Each of those four continents is ten thousand yojanas in length and breadth, and each contains ten thousand great cities.
Within Jambudvīpa, there is a royal capital named Cloud-Lamp Adorned with Firm and Wondrous Jewels, surrounded on all sides by ten thousand great cities.
When the lifespan of the people of Jambudvīpa was ten thousand years,
there was a king named Sarvadharmasvaranirghoṣaparipūrṇacchatra, who had five hundred ministers, sixty thousand court ladies, and seven hundred princes;
all these princes were handsome, brave, and robust, possessing great majesty and power.
At that time, the majesty and virtue of that king pervaded all within Jambudvīpa, and he had no enemies.
Later, when the kalpa of that world was nearing its end, the five turbidities arose.

All people have short lifespans, meager resources, and coarse appearances; they experience much suffering and little joy. They do not cultivate the ten wholesome actions but instead devote themselves to evil deeds, quarreling with one another, insulting and humiliating each other, alienating the families of others, and envying their prosperity. Following their own whims, they harbor biased views and greedily seek what is contrary to the Dharma.

Due to these causes and conditions, the winds and rains do not come at their proper times, the crops do not ripen, and all the gardens, grasses, and trees wither away. The people suffer from scarcity and are afflicted by many epidemics; they flee in all directions, finding no one to rely upon. Countless hundreds of thousands of millions of beings gather together and surround the great capital city on all four sides, crying out loudly.
Some raise their hands, some join their palms, some strike their heads against the ground, some beat their breasts with their hands, some kneel and wail long and loud, and some leap up and shout.
Their hair is disheveled, their clothes are tattered and foul, their skin is cracked and split, and their faces have lost all luster as they address the King:
"Great King! Great King! We are now poor, destitute, and exposed;

we suffer from hunger, thirst, cold, and freezing; we are afflicted by disease and physical decay. Pressed by these manifold sufferings, our lives will soon come to an end. We have no refuge and no protector; there is no one to whom we may appeal."

We have now come to take refuge in Your Majesty. Observing Your Majesty’s benevolence and wisdom, we conceive toward you the thought of finding peace and happiness, the thought of finding what is beloved, the thought of finding livelihood, the thought of being cared for, the thought of finding a treasury of jewels, the thought of encountering a bridge or ford, the thought of meeting a road, the thought of finding a boat or raft, the thought of seeing a jewel island, the thought of obtaining wealth and profit, and the thought of ascending to a celestial palace.
At that time, having heard these words, the Great King attained a million *asaṃkhyeya* gates of great compassion; with single-minded contemplation, he uttered ten kinds of words of great compassion.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
"Alas, sentient beings!..."
They have fallen into the bottomless great pit of saṃsāra;
how may I swiftly exert myself to rescue them and cause them to abide upon the ground of all-knowledge?
Alas for these sentient beings!
They are oppressed by all manner of afflictions;
how shall I provide them with protection and enable them to abide securely in all wholesome deeds?
Alas for these sentient beings!
Terrorized by birth, old age, sickness, and death,
how shall I act as their refuge so that they may forever attain peace and security of body and mind?
Alas for these sentient beings!
They are constantly oppressed by the many fears of the world;
how may I provide them with aid so that they may abide in the path of all-knowledge?
Alas for these sentient beings!
Lacking the eye of wisdom, they are constantly shrouded by the view of self and doubt;
how shall I employ skillful means to enable them to resolve their doubts and remove the cataracts of their views?
Alas, sentient beings!
They are constantly deluded by the darkness of ignorance;
how shall I act as a bright torch for them, so that they may clearly behold the city of all-knowledge?
Alas for sentient beings!
They are constantly defiled by stinginess, envy, flattery, and deception;
how shall I enlighten them so that they may realize the pure Dharma-body?
Alas for sentient beings!
For a long time they have drifted and sunk in the great ocean of birth and death;
how shall I universally transport and deliver them, causing them to reach the further shore of supreme enlightenment?
Alas for sentient beings!
Their faculties are stubborn and difficult to subdue;
how shall I act as their charioteer to cause them to be fully endowed with the spiritual powers of all Buddhas?
Alas for sentient beings!
They are like those who are blind and sightless, unable to see the path;
how shall I act as their guide so that they may enter the gateway of all-knowledge?
Having spoken these words, he beat the drum and issued a proclamation:
"I now bestow gifts universally upon all sentient beings; whatever they may require, I shall cause it all to be fully satisfied."

Immediately, he issued a decree throughout all the great and small cities and villages within Jambudvīpa, ordering that all treasuries be opened and various goods be brought out and placed at the crossroads.
That is to say:
gold, silver, lapis lazuli, mani-jewels, and other such treasures;
clothing, food and drink, flowers, incense, necklaces, palaces, houses, couches, and bedding.
He erected great luminous mani-jewel banners; when their light touched bodies, it caused all to be peaceful and secure.
He also provided medicinal decoctions for all causes of illness;
various precious vessels were filled with diverse jewels, vajra vessels with various fragrances, and precious incense vessels with various garments.
Litters, carriages, banners, streamers, silken canopies—
all such articles for the necessities of life— he opened his treasuries and bestowed them all as gifts.

Furthermore, they give away all villages, camps, cities, towns, mountains, marshes, forests, and thickets; wives, children, kinsmen, and even their royal thrones; as well as their heads, eyes, ears, noses, lips, tongues, teeth, gums, hands, feet, skin, flesh, heart, kidneys, liver, and lungs—indeed, they are able to relinquish everything internal and external.
In that city of Cloud-Lamps Adorned with Firm and Wondrous Jewels, there was a gate on the eastern side named Radiance of the Mani Mountain.
Outside that gate, there was a place for the distribution of alms.

That ground was vast, pure, and level, free from pits, ravines, thorns, and pebbles; it was composed entirely of wondrous jewels, strewn with various precious flowers, perfumed with exquisite incenses, and illuminated by various jewel lamps. Clouds of every kind of fragrance filled the void, while countless jewel trees stood in orderly rows. Countless nets of flowers and countless nets of incense covered them from above, and hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of musical instruments constantly produced sublime sounds.
All of these were adorned with exquisite jewels; they were entirely the fruit of the pure karma of bodhisattvas.

Within that assembly, lion thrones were set out, with ground made of ten kinds of jewels and railings of ten kinds of jewels, surrounded on all sides by trees of ten kinds of jewels. Beneath them were diamond jewel wheels, supported and held up together by images of nāgas and devas made of every kind of jewel. They were decorated with various precious objects, with banners and streamers arranged in alternating rows, and covered above by nets of many designs. Immeasurable precious incenses constantly produced clouds of fragrance, various precious garments were distributed everywhere, and hundreds of thousands of musical instruments perpetually played beautiful melodies.
Furthermore, precious canopies were spread above it, constantly emitting immeasurable light of jewel-flames, as brilliant and pure as Jambu-river gold;

they were covered with jeweled nets and hung with various necklaces, while mani-jewel bands were arranged in rows all around, and various jeweled bells perpetually produced wondrous sounds, exhorting all sentient beings to practice wholesome deeds.

At that time, the great king sat upon a lion throne; his appearance was upright and handsome, endowed with all the marks of a superior man. He wore a crown of wondrous jewels that radiated light, and his body, like that of Nārāyaṇa, was indestructible. Every limb was perfectly complete, and his nature was universally virtuous and kind. Born of royal lineage, he attained mastery over both wealth and the Dharma; his eloquence was unimpeded, his wisdom clear and penetrating, and he governed the kingdom with righteousness such that none disobeyed his commands.

"At that time, immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of sentient beings from Jambudvīpa—belonging to various lands, various lineages, various physical forms, various garments, various languages, and various inclinations—all came together to this assembly. Observing that king, they all said:
'This king is a person of great wisdom; he is a Sumeru of merit; he is a moon of virtue. He abides in the vows of a bodhisattva and practices vast giving.'"

At that time, when the king saw those who had come to beg, he gave rise to a mind of compassion, a mind of joy, a mind of reverence, a mind of regarding them as virtuous friends, a vast mind, a continuous mind, a mind of diligence, a mind of non-retrogression, a mind of relinquishment and giving, and a pervasive mind.
“Good son! At that time, when the king beheld those beggars, his heart was filled with great joy for a brief moment;

even if the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the King of the Yāma Heaven, and the King of the Tuṣita Heaven were to experience all their pleasures for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas, they could not equal it.”

The happiness experienced by the Heavenly King Śubhakṛtsna over incalculable kalpas; the happiness experienced by the Heavenly King Vaśavartin over immeasurable kalpas; the Brahma-bliss experienced by the Heavenly King Mahābrahmā over boundless kalpas; the celestial bliss experienced by the Heavenly King Ābhāsvara over inconceivable kalpas; the celestial bliss experienced by the Heavenly King Śubhakṛtsna over inexhaustible kalpas; and the bliss of dwelling in tranquility experienced by the Heavenly Kings of the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens over unspeakable kalpas—all these cannot compare [to it].

“Good son! It is like a person who is kind, compassionate, filial, and fraternal, who, having encountered a world-wide calamity, has lost his parents, wife, children, brothers, and sisters. Suddenly, amidst the vast wilderness and along the roads, they encounter one another; gazing upon and consoling each other, their affection knows no satiety.”
At that time, when the great king saw those who had come to seek [his help], his heart was filled with joy, just as in this case.

"Good son! At that time, because of his spiritual friend, the king’s understanding and aspiration for the Buddha’s bodhi increased; his faculties were perfected, his faith became pure, and his joy was complete."
Why is this? It is because these bodhisattvas diligently cultivate all practices, seek omniscience, vow to benefit all sentient beings,
vow to attain the immeasurable and wondrous bliss of bodhi, and abandon all unwholesome states of mind.
They constantly delight in accumulating all roots of goodness; they constantly vow to rescue and protect all sentient beings;
they constantly delight in observing the path to *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge); they constantly delight in practicing the dharmas of omniscience;
they fulfill the aspirations of all sentient beings; they enter the great ocean of the merits of all Buddhas; and they shatter all demonic activities and delusions.
Mounting the Mountain of Obstructions, he accords with the teachings and practices of all Tathāgatas;
he traverses the unobstructed path of omniscience and has already deeply entered the stream of all-knowledge. The stream of all dharmas is ever present before him;
his great vows are inexhaustible, and as a Great Being, he abides in the dharma of a Great Man, accumulating all the gates of universal liberation.
“Excellent treasury! You are free from all attachments and unstained by any worldly realms; you know that the nature of all phenomena is like space.

Toward those who come to beg, you should conceive the thought of them as your only son, as your parents, as a field of merit, as something difficult to encounter, as a source of benefit and kindness, and with thoughts of them as steadfast, as teachers, and as Buddhas.”

Without discriminating between places, without selecting among classes, and without choosing based on physical appearance, he grants gifts universally to all who arrive according to their desires, with a heart of great compassion that is impartial and unimpeded, satisfying them all:
to those seeking food and drink, he gives food and drink;
to those seeking clothing, he gives clothing.
To those who sought incense and flowers, he gave incense and flowers;
to those who sought garlands and canopies, he gave garlands and canopies;

likewise, he universally bestowed upon sentient beings banners and pennants, necklaces, palaces, gardens, elephants, horses, carriages, seats, bedding, gold, silver, mani-jewels, all manner of precious objects, all storehouses, as well as kinsmen, cities, towns, and villages.

At that time, in this assembly, there was a daughter of a householder named Ratnaprabhā (Jewel Radiance), who was accompanied by sixty young maidens. She was upright and exquisite, a sight pleasing to all who beheld her; her skin was golden, her eyes and hair were deep blue, and her body emitted a wondrous fragrance.

Her mouth produced Brahma-sounds, and she was adorned with most excellent precious garments. She always harbored a sense of shame and remorse, maintained right mindfulness without distraction, and was perfect in her dignified deportment. She respected her teachers and elders, constantly mindful of and acting in accordance with profound and wondrous practices. She remembered and did not forget the teachings she had heard; the roots of goodness from her past lives moistened her heart, which was pure and vast like space. She brought peace equally to all sentient beings, constantly beheld the Buddhas, and sought omniscience.
At that time, the girl Ratnaprabhā, not far from the king, joined her palms in homage and prostrated herself, thinking thus:
“I have gained a great benefit!
I have gained a great benefit!”
"I have now been able to see a great spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).

Toward that king, he conceived the thought of him as a Great Teacher, the thought of him as a spiritual friend, the thought of him as one endowed with compassion, and the thought of him as one capable of providing guidance and support.
With a mind upright and straight, he gave rise to great joy; taking off his own necklaces and ornaments, he offered them to that king and made this aspiration:
"Now this Great King serves as a place of reliance for immeasurable and boundless sentient beings shrouded in ignorance; may I also be thus in the future."

Just as that great king’s known dharmas, his mounted vehicles, the path he has cultivated, his physical marks, his possessions, and the assemblies he gathers are boundless and inexhaustible, invincible and indestructible—may I, in the future, fully attain all such things.
"Wherever they are born, may they all be reborn there with me.
At that time, the Great King, knowing that this young woman had conceived such a thought, addressed her, saying:
"Young woman!..."
"Whatever you desire, I shall grant it all to you.
All that I now possess, I renounce entirely,
so that all sentient beings may attain universal fulfillment."
At that time, the girl Ratnaprabhā, her mind purified by faith and filled with great joy, praised the king in verse, saying: "In the past,
when this city was not yet graced by the Great King’s appearance,
it was utterly devoid of delight, like the abode of hungry ghosts."
Sentient beings kill and harm one another; they steal, indulge in lewdness, and engage in double-tongued speech and untruths.
They utter meaningless and harsh words, covet the wealth and property of others, and harbor malice with hearts full of hatred.
Those with wrong views and unwholesome conduct fall into evil realms at the end of their lives.
Because such beings are shrouded by ignorance and abide in perverted views,
the heavens do not send down rain during droughts.
Because there was no timely rain, all the hundred grains failed to grow;
the grasses and trees withered away, and even the springs and streams ran dry.
Before Your Majesty arose in this world, the fords and ponds were all parched and desolate.
The gardens and groves are filled with many bones; looking at them, they resemble a desolate wilderness.
When the Great King ascends the precious throne, he extensively delivers all living beings;
like a thick oil-cloud covering the eight directions, his universal rain falls everywhere in abundance.
The Great King presides over the common people, universally severing all violence and cruelty;
judicial punishments are entirely suspended, and the orphaned and the solitary are all at peace.
In the past, sentient beings each harmed one another.
Drinking blood and devouring flesh, they have now all given rise to a mind of compassion.
All sentient beings of the past were poor and lacked clothing;
they shielded themselves with grass, emaciated by hunger like hungry ghosts.
Once the Great King had appeared in the world, non-glutinous rice grew spontaneously, and wondrous garments emerged from trees; both men and women were adorned with finery.
In former days, they vied for meager profits and transgressed the Dharma by robbing one another.
Now all things are abundant and sufficient, as if wandering in the garden of Śakra.
In former times, people committed evil; they gave rise to improper greed and defilement, violating and coercing others' wives and maidens in various ways.
Now, seeing other women, Elegant, exquisite, and finely adorned,
My mind remains free from attachment, Just like the gods of the Heaven of Contentment.
In the past, all sentient beings Spoke with false and unreal words.
Unrighteousness brings no benefit; it is through flattery and crookedness that one seeks to win over others' minds.
Today, all classes of living beings have entirely abandoned harsh speech;
their minds being now supple, the words they utter are likewise harmonious and gentle.
In the past, various sentient beings, practicing all manner of heterodox dharmas,
would join their palms in reverent salutation to cattle, sheep, dogs, pigs, and other such creatures. Now,
having heard the King’s True Dharma, they have attained awakening and abandoned their false views.
Fully understanding that the retributions of suffering and joy all arise from causes and conditions,
the Great King utters wondrous sounds; all who hear them rejoice,
for no voices— whether those of Brahmā or Śakra— can equal them.
The Great King’s many precious canopies hang suspended in the midst of space;
supported by pillars of lapis lazuli, they are covered with nets of mani-jewels.
From golden bells there naturally issues the harmonious and elegant voice of the Tathāgata.
Proclaiming the subtle and wondrous Dharma, he eliminates the delusions of sentient beings.
Next, he further expounds at length upon all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions and within all kalpas, including the Tathāgatas and their retinues.
Furthermore, they spoke in succession of all the Tathāgatas of the past throughout the lands of the ten directions and within those realms. Then,
a subtle and wondrous sound issued forth, pervading the entire Jambudvīpa.
He extensively explains the various distinctions of karma among humans, devas, and others.
Having heard this, sentient beings come to know their own store of karmic seeds;
they abandon evil, diligently practice, and dedicate [their merit] toward the Bodhi of the Buddha.
The father of the king was Pure Radiance; the mother of the king was Lotus Light.
When the five turbidities appeared, he occupied the throne and governed the world.
At that time there was a vast garden, and within the garden were five hundred ponds.
Each tree is surrounded by a thousand others, And each is covered with blossoms.
Upon the banks of those ponds, Thousand-pillared halls are erected,
Adorned with railings and such, With nothing left unprepared.
In this degenerate age, when evil dharmas arise, no rain falls for many years;
ponds and streams all run dry, and grasses and trees wither away.
Seven days before the King was born, auspicious and numinous signs first appeared.
All who saw this thought in their hearts:
"The Savior shall now appear.
At that time, during the middle watch of the night, the great earth shook in six ways.
There was a precious lotus pond, its radiance appearing like the sun.
Within the five hundred ponds, waters of merit were full;
withered trees all sprouted branches, and flowers and leaves flourished in abundance.
Once the waters of the pond are full, they flow and spread everywhere,
reaching throughout Jambudvīpa so that there is nowhere they do not moisten and saturate.
The medicinal herbs and various trees, as well as the hundred grains and sprouting crops— [All these] are nourished by them.
Branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits— all were in full abundance.
Ditches, pits, mounds, and all places of various elevations—
this entire earth was nowhere not made level and smooth.
Thorns, gravel, and the like— whatever various impurities there may be—
all within a single thought-instant, are transformed into myriad precious gems.
When sentient beings see this, they rejoice and offer praise.
All said they had gained a wholesome benefit, like a thirsty man drinking sweet water.
Then King Prabhāsa, with his retinue of immeasurable hosts,
all prepared the royal chariot and went out to tour the various gardens.
Within the five hundred ponds, there is a pond named *Ananda*;
upon this pond stands a Dharma Hall, where the Father King resides.
The former king spoke to his consort:
I recall that seven nights ago, at midnight, the earth shook; a light appeared within this place.
Then, from within that lotus pond, a thousand-petaled lotus emerged, its radiance like a thousand suns shining, reaching upward to the summit of Mount Sumeru.
With a stem of vajra and a pedestal of Jambūnada gold,
with petals and leaves of various jewels and filaments of exquisite fragrance,
the King was born upon that flower, sitting upright in the full lotus posture.
Adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, revered by the heavenly deities,
the former great king was filled with joy; he entered the pool, gathered [the child] in his own hands,
and presented him to the queen:
Your son should rejoice:
treasure-troves gush forth from all sides; jeweled trees produce exquisite garments;
and celestial music plays beautiful melodies, filling the void of space.
All sentient beings were filled with great joy;
joining their palms, they exclaimed, "How marvelous!
O Protector of the World, how excellent!"
At that time, the King emitted light from his body, Universally illuminating all things;
he was able to cause The darkness throughout the four continents to vanish And all diseases to be extinguished.
Yakṣas and piśācas, Poisonous insects and various malevolent beasts—
Those who intended to harm others all hid themselves away;
their ill repute vanished and they lost their advantages, while calamities and diseases that had possessed them were extinguished.
Thus, all such sufferings ceased, and everyone rejoiced.
Regarding all classes of sentient beings, Regard one another as parents;
Abandoning evil, give rise to a compassionate heart, And single-mindedly seek all-encompassing wisdom.
Shutting the gates to the evil realms, One reveals the path for humans and devas.
Proclaiming *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), you deliver all living beings.
Having seen the Great King, we have all obtained excellent benefit;
those who were without refuge and without a guide are now all at peace and happy.

At that time, the maiden Ratnaprabhā, having praised King Sarvadharmanirghoṣasamantavyūha with these verses, circumambulated him countless times, joined her palms in prostration, bowed her body in reverence, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, the great king said to the young woman: "Excellent,
young woman!"
That you are able to believe in and know the merits of others is truly rare. Girl!
All sentient beings are unable to believe in and know the merits of others.

O maiden! All sentient beings do not know how to repay kindness; they lack wisdom, their minds are turbid and distracted, and their natures are not clear. They originally possess no willpower and further regress from their practice.
Such people neither believe in nor understand the merits, supernatural powers, and wisdom possessed by Bodhisattvas and Tathāgatas.
"O maiden! You now resolutely seek to attain Bodhi and are able to understand such merits of a bodhisattva.

Having been born now in this Jambudvīpa, you have aroused a courageous mind to universally gather in all sentient beings; your efforts shall not be in vain, and you shall likewise accomplish such merits."
After the King had praised the girl, he personally bestowed priceless precious robes upon the maiden Ratnaprabhā and her retinue, addressing each one individually:
"Put on these robes."
Then, the young maidens knelt with both knees on the ground, received [the garment] with both hands, placed it upon their heads, and then put it on.
Once they had donned the robes, they circumambulated the King to the right; from within all the precious garments, the radiance of all the constellations emerged everywhere.
When the multitude saw them, they all spoke thus:
"These women are all exceedingly beautiful, like the adornment of the stars in a clear night sky."
"Good son! At that time, was the King Sarvadharmanirghoṣasaṃpūrṇachattra anyone else?
He was none other than the present Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana."
King Prabhāsa was King Śuddhodana; Lady Padmaprabhā was Lady Māyā;
and the maiden Ratnaprabhā was none other than myself.

The beings whom that king at that time gathered through the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) are precisely all the bodhisattvas in this assembly; they have all attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and dwell in stages ranging from the first to the tenth. They possess various great vows, have accumulated various aids to the path, have cultivated various sublime practices, are equipped with various adornments, have attained various supernormal powers, and abide in various liberations, occupying various palaces of sublime Dharma within this assembly.
At that time, the Night Goddess Sarvarukṣavṛkṣapraphullanasamantadigvairocanā, wishing to reiterate the meaning of this liberation for the sake of the youth Sudhana, spoke these verses:
“I possess vast eyes that see everywhere throughout the ten directions,
All those wandering in the cycle of the five destinies within the ocean of all world-systems.”
I also see those Buddhas sitting beneath their Bodhi trees;
their spiritual powers pervade the ten directions as they preach the Dharma to deliver sentient beings.
I possess pure ears that universally hear all sounds.
I also hear the Buddha preaching the Dharma, Receiving it with joy and faith.
Possessing the knowledge of others' minds, Without duality and without hindrance,
I am able, within a single thought-moment, To fully comprehend the ocean of all minds.
I have attained the knowledge of past lives, Able to know all kalpas—
both my own and those of others— Discerning them all with complete clarity.
In a single thought-moment, I know The kalpas contained within the atoms of an ocean of lands.
The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and all classes of sentient beings within the five realms—
recalling those Buddhas from their initial aspiration for bodhicitta until they fully perfected every single practice.
I also know those Buddhas who, having accomplished the path to enlightenment,
turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of all beings through various skillful means.
I also know all the oceans of vehicles belonging to those Buddhas.
How long the True Dharma shall abide, and how many sentient beings shall be delivered—
throughout immeasurable kalpas, I have practiced this Dharma-gate;
I now explain it for you, O Son of the Buddha, you should study it.
“Good son! I know only this bodhisattva liberation door of the light of joy born from vastness.
As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who draw near to and make offerings to all buddhas, who enter the great ocean of vows of omniscience, and fulfill the ocean of all the buddhas’ vows;”
They attain courageous wisdom, whereby they universally enter the ocean of all bodhisattva stages from within a single bodhisattva stage;
they attain pure vows, whereby they universally enter the ocean of all bodhisattva practices from within a single bodhisattva practice;
they attain the power of mastery, whereby they universally enter the ocean of all bodhisattva doors of liberation from within a single bodhisattva door of liberation.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son! Within this site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named:
With the power of great vows and diligence, he protects and delivers all sentient beings.
Go to him and ask:
how does a bodhisattva teach and transform sentient beings, causing them to advance toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
How does one adorn and purify all Buddha-fields?
How does one serve all Tathāgatas?
How does one practice all Buddha-dharmas?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 72;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 73.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree,
Part Fourteen of the Thirty-Ninth Chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm," Section Fourteen:
At that time, the youth Sudhana went to the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.
In that divine place, he saw the Night Goddess seated upon a lion throne within the great assembly—
a throne made of the treasury of mani-jewel kings that universally manifests all palaces, and which is covered by a net of mani jewels that universally manifests the lands of the Dharma-realm;
she manifested a body that displays the reflected images of the sun, moon, and stars, and she appeared in accordance with the minds of sentient beings.
They cause them to behold the body that manifests forms identical to those of all sentient beings; the body that manifests an infinite and vast ocean of physical marks;
the body that universally manifests all modes of conduct; the body that universally manifests its appearance throughout the ten directions;
the body that universally tames all sentient beings; and the body of swift and far-reaching supernormal powers.
The body that manifests ceaselessly to benefit sentient beings; the body that manifests as constantly roaming through space to benefit others;
the body that manifests to pay homage at the feet of all Buddhas; the body that manifests as practicing all roots of goodness;

the body that manifests as upholding the Buddha-dharma without forgetfulness; the body that manifests as fulfilling the great vows of Bodhisattvas; and the body that manifests with light filling all directions.

The body that pervades the ten directions; the body that manifests the lamp of the Dharma to universally extinguish the darkness of the world; the body that manifests the pure wisdom that realizes all phenomena are like illusions;
the body that manifests the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) free from the darkness of defilements; the body that manifests the clear understanding of all phenomena through universal wisdom;
the body that manifests ultimate freedom from affliction and fever; the body that manifests indestructible solidity; the body that manifests the absence of...
The body that abides in the power of the Buddhas manifests as a body free from discrimination and detached from defilement; it manifests as the body of the originally pure *dharmatā*.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld such bodies, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field. With single-minded devotion, he prostrated himself, casting his entire body to the ground. After a long while, he rose, joined his palms in reverence, gazed up with admiration, and gave rise to ten kinds of mind toward the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).
What are these ten? They are as follows:
"To regard spiritual friends as one's own self, so that I may apply myself with diligence to accomplishing the factors conducive to the path to all-knowledge;..."
One should conceive toward spiritual friends a mind that views them as the pure fruit of one's own karma, because by attending upon and making offerings to them, one generates roots of goodness;
one should conceive toward spiritual friends a mind that views them as the adornment of bodhisattva practices, so that I may swiftly adorn all bodhisattva practices;
one should conceive toward spiritual friends a mind that views them as the accomplishment of all Buddha-dharmas, for they instruct and guide me to cultivate the Path.
One should generate toward spiritual friends a mind that gives birth, because they give birth to me in the unsurpassed Dharma;
one should generate toward spiritual friends a mind of renunciation, so that through my practice of all the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, I may attain renunciation;
one should generate toward spiritual friends a mind endowed with the ocean of all merit and wisdom, so that I may accumulate all pure dharmas.
One should generate toward spiritual friends a mind of growth, so that I may increase all-knowledge;
one should generate toward spiritual friends a mind endowed with all roots of goodness, so that my aspirations may be fulfilled;

one should generate toward spiritual friends a mind capable of accomplishing great benefit, so that I may dwell with mastery in all Bodhisattva dharmas, perfect the path to all-knowledge, and attain all Buddha-dharmas.
These are the ten. Having generated these thoughts, he attained the same practices as that night goddess and as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a buddha-field.
They are as follows:
They share the same mindfulness, for their minds constantly recollect all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time;
they share the same wisdom, for they discern and resolve the various gateways within the ocean of all dharmas;
they share the same destination, for they are able to turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
They share the same awakening, for they universally enter all three worlds through the wisdom that is equal to space;
they share the same faculties, for they have perfected the roots of pure, radiant wisdom of a bodhisattva;
they share the same mind, for they are skillfully able to cultivate unimpeded merit to adorn all bodhisattva paths.
They share the same objective realm, for they universally illumine the spheres of action of all Buddhas;
they share the same realization, for they attain the pure light that illuminates the ocean of true reality through omniscience;
they share the same meaning, for they are able to comprehend the true nature of all phenomena through wisdom.
They share the same valor, for they are able to shatter all mountains of obstacles;
they share the same form-body, for they manifest bodies in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
they share the same power, for they never regress in their quest for omniscience.
They are equal in fearlessness, for their minds are pure like space;
they are equal in diligence, for they practice the bodhisattva path through immeasurable eons without weariness;
they are equal in eloquence, for they have attained the light of unimpeded wisdom regarding all phenomena.
They are identical in equanimity, for their physical marks are pure and transcend the world;
they are identical in kind words, for they cause all sentient beings to rejoice;
they are identical in sublime voices, for they universally expound the ocean of all Dharma-gates.
They share the same full resonance, for all sentient beings understand according to their respective types;
they share the same pure virtue, for they cultivate the pure merits of the Tathāgatas;
they share the same ground of wisdom, for it is the wheel of Dharma received by all Buddhas.
They share the same holy life, for they dwell securely within the realm of all Buddhas;
they share the same great kindness, for in every thought-moment they universally encompass the ocean of sentient beings in all lands;
they share the same great compassion, for they rain down the Dharma everywhere to moisten and nourish all living beings.
They share the same bodily karma, for they teach and transform all sentient beings through skillful means;
they share the same verbal karma, for they expound all dharma-gates using sounds that accord with the various classes of beings;
they share the same mental karma, for they universally gather in sentient beings and establish them within the realm of omniscience.
They share the same adornment, for they purify all Buddha-fields;
they share the same intimacy, for they draw near to every Buddha who appears in the world;
they share the same exhortation, for they entreat all Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma.
They share the same offerings, for they always delight in making offerings to all Buddhas;
they share the same teaching and transformation, for they discipline and subdue all sentient beings;
they share the same radiance, for they illuminate all dharma-gates.
They share the same samādhi, because they universally know the minds of all sentient beings;
they share the same pervasiveness, because by the power of their mastery they fill all oceans of Buddha-lands while cultivating various practices;
they share the same dwelling place, because they abide in the great supernormal powers of all bodhisattvas.
They share the same retinue, for all bodhisattvas dwell together;
they share the same sphere of entry, for they universally enter the subtlest realms of worlds;
they share the same mental intention, for they universally know all Buddha-fields.
They are identical in their approach, for they universally enter the ocean of all buddha-fields;
they are identical in their skillful means, for they manifest within all buddha-fields;
they are identical in their transcendence, for they are peerless among all buddha-fields.
They are identical in non-retrogression, for they universally enter the ten directions without obstruction;
they are identical in shattering darkness, for they have attained the great radiance of the wisdom of all Buddhas’ realization of bodhi;
