they are identical in the patience of non-arising, for they enter the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas.
They are identical in pervading the entire network of all Buddha-fields, for they reverently make offerings to the Tathāgatas of unspeakably many fields;
they are identical in the realization of wisdom, for they thoroughly understand the oceans of various Dharma-gates;
they are identical in their practice, for they accord with and proceed through all Dharma-gates.
They share the same aspiration, because they deeply desire the pure Dharma;
they share the same purity, because they adorn their body, speech, and mind by accumulating the merits of a Buddha;
they share the same sublime intention, because their wisdom is clear and lucid regarding all phenomena.
They share the same diligence, because they universally gather all roots of goodness;
they share the same pure conduct, because they bring all bodhisattva practices to fulfillment;
they share the same non-obstruction, because they understand that all phenomena are signless.
They are identical in skillfulness, for they possess mastery of wisdom regarding all phenomena;
they are identical in accordance with aspiration, for they manifest realms in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
they are identical in skillful means, for they have well practiced everything that ought to be practiced.
They share the same protective mindfulness, because they have attained the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas;
they share the same entry into the stages, because they have attained entry into all bodhisattva stages;
they share the same dwelling, because they dwell securely in all bodhisattva positions.
They are identical in their prediction, for all Buddhas bestow predictions upon them;
they are identical in their samādhis, for in a single kṣaṇa they universally enter all gates of samādhi;
they are identical in their establishment, for they manifest the various deeds of all Buddhas.
They share the same right mindfulness, because they maintain right mindfulness toward all gateways of objective realms;
they share the same practice, because they cultivate all bodhisattva practices throughout all kalpas of the future;
they share the same pure faith, because they take supreme delight in the immeasurable wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
They are identical in renunciation, because they eliminate all obstacles;
identical in non-retrogressive wisdom, because their wisdom is equal to that of all Tathāgatas;
and identical in taking birth, because they manifest in response to bring sentient beings to maturity.
They share the same dwelling, because they abide in the gateway of skillful means for omniscience;
they share the same sphere of experience, because they have attained mastery over the realm of the dharma-dhātu;
they share the same lack of dependence, because they have forever severed all minds that rely on anything.
They are identical in their teaching of the Dharma, for they have already entered the wisdom of the equality of all phenomena;
they are identical in their diligent cultivation, for they are constantly sustained by the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas;
they are identical in their supernormal powers, for they awaken sentient beings and cause them to cultivate all bodhisattva practices.
They share the same spiritual powers, for they are able to enter the oceans of worlds in the ten directions;
they share the same dhāraṇīs, for they universally illumine the ocean of all total-retentions;
they share the same secret dharma, for they thoroughly understand the wondrous dharma-gates within all sūtras.
They are identical in profound Dharma, for they understand all phenomena to be like space;
they are identical in radiance, for they universally illumine all worlds;
they are identical in joyful delight, for they reveal the teachings according to the minds of sentient beings to bring them joy.
They are identical in their vibration, for they manifest supernatural powers for all sentient beings to universally shake all lands throughout the ten directions;
they are identical in their non-futility, for seeing, hearing, or remembering them causes the minds of all to become tamed;
and they are identical in their transcendence, for they fulfill the ocean of all great vows and accomplish the wisdom of the Tathāgata’s ten powers.

At that time, the youth Sudhana contemplated the night goddess Mahāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhāsa-sarvasattvatrāṇa and gave rise to ten kinds of pure minds, attaining as many qualities as there are atoms in a buddha-field that are identical to the conduct of bodhisattvas.
Having attained these, his mind became even more purified; he bared his right shoulder, prostrated at her feet, and with palms joined in single-minded devotion, praised her in verse:
"I have resolved upon a firm intention, Vowing to seek supreme enlightenment;”
Now, regarding the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one should give rise to the thought that they are oneself.
By beholding the spiritual friend, one accumulates inexhaustible pure dharmas (śukladharma),
eliminates all defilements of sin, and accomplishes the fruit of Bodhi.
I behold the spiritual friend, whose mind is adorned with merit;
throughout all lands and kalpas until the end of the future, I shall diligently cultivate the path they practice.
I am mindful of the spiritual friend, who has gathered me in and benefited me.
Reveal all of this to me: the true Dharma of the authentic teaching that closes off the evil destinies and reveals the path to humans and devas;
and likewise show the way for all Tathāgatas to achieve omniscience.
I call to mind the spiritual friend, who is a treasury of the Buddha’s merits;
in every thought-moment, they can give rise to an ocean of merit as vast as space.
They grant me the *pāramitās* and increase my inconceivable blessings.
May my pure merit increase, and may I be crowned with the Buddha’s silk ribbon.
I call to mind the spiritual friend who can fulfill the path of Buddha-wisdom;
I vow to rely upon them constantly, so that the pure, white Dharma may be perfected.
Because of these things, I am fully endowed with merit;
for the sake of all sentient beings, I shall proclaim the path to omniscience.
The Noble One is my teacher, who has bestowed upon me the unsurpassed Dharma.
"Even through immeasurable and incalculable kalpas, one could not repay their kindness.
At that time, having spoken this verse, Sudhana said:
"O Great Sage!"
I pray that you will explain this for me: what is the name of this gate of liberation?
How long has it been since you first resolved to attain enlightenment?
And after how much time shall you realize unexcelled, complete, and perfect awakening?
The night goddess said:
"Good son! This door of liberation is named: "
I teach and transform sentient beings, causing them to give rise to roots of goodness.

Because I have accomplished this liberation, I have awakened to the equality of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena; I have entered into the true nature of all dharmas and realized the dharma that is free from dependence. Having abandoned the world, I fully know the distinctions among the characteristics of all phenomena, and I am also able to penetrate the fact that blue, yellow, red, and white are all unreal by nature and without distinction, yet I constantly manifest immeasurable physical bodies.
That is to say: various physical bodies, non-unitary physical bodies, boundless physical bodies, pure physical bodies,
physically adorned with all ornaments, universally visible physical bodies, and physical bodies equal to those of all sentient beings.
The physical body that manifests before all sentient beings; the physical body whose radiance shines everywhere; the physical body that one never tires of beholding;
the physical body with pure marks and signs; the physical body with light free from all evils; the physical body that displays great valor;
the physical body that is extremely difficult to encounter; the physical body that no one in any world can outshine.
The body that conceals form; the body universally praised by all worlds as inexhaustible; the body that constantly observes in every thought-moment;
the body that manifests various clouds of color; the body of various shapes and manifest hues;
the body that displays immeasurable sovereign power; the body of wondrous radiance; and the body of all pure and sublime adornments.

The majestic physical body; the physical body that accords with and brings all sentient beings to maturity; the physical body that appears before them to subdue them according to their mental inclinations;
the physical body of unobstructed universal radiance; the physical body that is pure and free from turbidity or defilement;
the indestructible physical body fully adorned with ornaments; and the light of inconceivable skillful means of the Dharma.
The body of radiant form; the body that cannot be robbed and which robs all other forms; the body that destroys all darkness and is free from all obscurity;
the body that gathers all pure and white dharmas; the body of the ocean of merit with great power;
the body produced from causes of past reverence; the body produced from a mind as pure as space.
The form-body; the most supreme and vast form-body; the form-body that is uninterrupted and inexhaustible; the form-body that is an ocean of light;
the form-body of equality that has no dependence upon any world; the form-body that is unimpeded throughout the ten directions;
the form-body that manifests oceans of various forms and marks in every thought-moment; and that which increases all things.
The physical body that gladdens the hearts of all sentient beings; the physical body that gathers in the ocean of all sentient beings;
the physical body that proclaims the ocean of merits of all Buddhas from every single pore; the physical body that purifies the ocean of desires and understandings of all sentient beings;
the physical body that decisively realizes the meaning of all dharmas; and the physical body that shines forth universally without obstruction.
The body that is pure like the expanse of space; the body of pure radiance emitting vast light;
the body of stainless dharmas manifesting illumination; the incomparable body; the body adorned with diverse ornaments;
the body universally illuminating the ten directions; the body appearing at appropriate times in accordance with sentient beings; the tranquil body.
The body that extinguishes all afflictions; the body that is a field of merit for all sentient beings;
the body whose sight by all sentient beings is never in vain; the body of great wisdom and heroic power;
the body that is unobstructed and universally pervasive; and the body of wondrous clouds that appear throughout the world so that all may receive benefit.
The body of the color of the ocean of great compassion; the body of the king of jewel mountains of great merit;
the body that emits light universally illuminating all realms of existence in the world; the body of pure great wisdom;
the body that gives rise to the mind of right mindfulness in sentient beings; the body of the radiance of all jewels; and the body of the treasury of universal light.
The physical body manifesting various pure marks and colors in the world; the physical body seeking the locus of all-knowledge;
the physical body manifesting a smile to cause sentient beings to give rise to pure faith; the physical body of radiant light adorned with all jewels;
the physical body that neither grasps nor abandons any sentient being; and the physical body that is neither determinate nor ultimate.
The body that manifests the power of sovereign empowerment; the body that manifests all supernatural transformations;
the body born into the family of the Tathāgatas; the body that is free from all evils and pervades the ocean of the Dharma-realm;
the body that universally appears before the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas; and the body endowed with an ocean of various multitudes of colors.
The physical body flowing from virtuous conduct; the physical body manifested according to those to be transformed;
the physical body that all worlds never tire of beholding; the physical body of various pure radiances;
the physical body manifesting the oceans of all three periods of time; the physical body emitting oceans of all radiances; and the manifestation of infinite distinctions.
The body of the color of the ocean of light; the body of the light of all fragrances that transcends all worlds;
the body manifesting unspeakable clouds of solar discs; the body manifesting vast clouds of lunar discs;
the body emitting immeasurable clouds of exquisite flowers from Mount Sumeru; the body producing various clouds of garlands; the body manifesting all...
The body of the color of clouds of precious lotuses; the body that raises clouds of all kinds of burning incense pervading the Dharma-realm;
the body that scatters clouds from the treasury of all powdered incenses; the body that manifests the great vows of all Tathāgatas;
the body that manifests the ocean of the Dharma through all languages and sounds; and the body that manifests the image of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
The Body:

"In every thought-moment, he manifests such physical forms filling the ten directions, causing all sentient beings—whether by seeing them, recollecting them, hearing him preach the Dharma, through proximity, attaining awakening, witnessing his spiritual powers, or beholding his transformations—to be tamed according to their inclinations at the appropriate time, thereby abandoning unwholesome karma and abiding in virtuous conduct."

"Good son! You should know that it is by the power of great vows, the power of the knowledge of all modes, the power of the bodhisattva’s liberation, the power of great compassion, and the power of great loving-kindness that such deeds are performed."

“Good son! Having entered this liberation, I thoroughly understand that the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is without differentiation, yet I am able to manifest immeasurable physical bodies (*rūpakāya*). Each body manifests an ocean of immeasurable physical marks; each mark emits clouds of immeasurable light; each ray of light reveals immeasurable Buddha-lands; in each land appear immeasurable Buddhas arising in the world; and each Buddha displays immeasurable supernormal powers (*ṛddhibala*), awakening the roots of goodness from past lives of sentient beings—causing those not yet planted to be planted, those already planted to grow, and those already grown to reach maturity.
In every thought-moment, I cause immeasurable sentient beings to attain non-retrogression in their progress toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“Good son! Regarding what you have asked:
‘From how long ago did you first resolve upon bodhicitta and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva?’”
"Regarding this meaning, I shall now explain it for you through the Buddha’s spiritual power. 'Good son!

The wheel of wisdom of a bodhisattva is far removed from all realms of conceptual discrimination; it cannot be displayed through the distinctions of long or short, defiled or pure, broad or narrow, many or few, nor through such eons within the cycle of birth and death.'"

Why is this? Because the wheel of wisdom of a bodhisattva is pure by nature; it is free from the net of all conceptual discrimination, transcends all mountains of obstacles, and shines universally upon those who are to be transformed according to their needs.
“Good son! It is like the solar orb, for which there is no distinction between day and night;
yet when it rises, it is designated as such:”
Day is called night at the time of its passing;
the wheel of a bodhisattva’s wisdom is likewise thus: it is without discrimination and without the three periods of time.
They merely manifest according to the minds [of beings] to teach and transform sentient beings, speaking of their dwelling in past kalpas or future kalpas. "Good son!

It is like the orb of the sun, which dwells in the sky over Jambudvīpa; its reflection appears in all precious objects as well as in the pure waters of rivers and seas. All sentient beings behold it with their own eyes, yet that pure sun does not come here."

The wisdom-wheel of the Bodhisattva is also like this: having emerged from the ocean of existence and abiding in the true Dharma of the Buddha, it rests in the tranquil void without any dependence; yet, for the sake of transforming and delivering all sentient beings, it takes birth according to their kind within the various realms of existence.
In reality, it does not undergo birth and death, is free from defilement or attachment, and is devoid of conceptual discriminations regarding long or short kalpas.
Why is this? Because the bodhisattva has ultimately abandoned the perception of mind and thought, seeing all perversions;
having attained true vision, he sees the true nature of phenomena.

Knowing that all worlds are like dreams and illusions, and that no sentient beings truly exist, one nevertheless manifests before sentient beings to teach and subdue them through the power of great compassion and great vows.
“O Son of the Buddha!

It is like a boatman who, with a great ship upon the river, neither relies on this shore, nor clings to the opposite shore, nor dwells in midstream, yet ferries sentient beings across without ceasing.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: by means of the ship of the pāramitās, within the stream of birth and death, they do not rely on this shore, do not cling to the other shore, and do not dwell in the middle of the current, yet they ferry across sentient beings without ceasing;
though they cultivate the bodhisattva practices for immeasurable kalpas, they never differentiate between the length or brevity of those kalpas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Just as the great void is such that all worlds within it undergo formation and destruction without discrimination—its intrinsic nature being pure, unstained, undisturbed, unobstructed, and insatiable; neither long nor short, it sustains all lands throughout all future eons.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: with a vast and profound mind as equal to the realm of empty space, they give rise to the wind-circle of great vows to gather in all sentient beings, causing them to leave the evil realms and be born in the various good destinies, leading them all to dwell securely on the ground of omniscience, extinguishing the bonds of afflictions and the suffering of birth and death, all the while without any heart of sorrow, joy, weariness, or fatigue.

“Good son! Just as a person created by illusion, though possessing all limbs, lacks the ten kinds of phenomena—namely, inhalation and exhalation, cold and heat, hunger and thirst, sorrow and joy, birth and death.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: by means of the wisdom that is like an illusion, they manifest various forms and appearances from their equal Dharma-body. They dwell for immeasurable kalpas within all realms of existence to transform and guide sentient beings; amidst all circumstances within birth and death, they feel neither joy nor weariness, neither craving nor anger, neither suffering nor pleasure, neither grasping nor abandoning, and neither security nor fear.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Although the wisdom of a bodhisattva is thus profoundly deep and difficult to fathom, I shall, by relying on the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, explain it for you, so that all bodhisattvas of future ages may fulfill their great vows and accomplish all powers.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds,
there was an eon named Good Light, and a world named:”
Ratnaprabha.
Within that eon, ten thousand buddhas appeared in the world.
The first of these buddhas was named:
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparāja, whose ten titles were fully perfected.
In that Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital named Ratnavyūha.
Not far to its east, there was a great forest named Wondrous Light;
within it was a site of enlightenment named:
Precious Flower:
Within that site of enlightenment, there was a lion throne of the Universal Radiance Maṇi Lotus Treasury.

At that time, the Tathāgata, upon this throne, attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). He remained seated at the site of enlightenment for a full hundred years, expounding the True Dharma for the sake of the bodhisattvas, the devas, the people of the world, and those among the inhabitants of Jambudvīpa who had previously planted roots of goodness and whose faculties were already matured.
"At that time, there was a king named Prabhāsa.

The lifespan of the people of that age was ten thousand years, yet among them there were many who committed killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, frivolous speech, double-tongued speech, harsh speech, greed, anger, and wrong views; they were unfilial toward their parents and lacked respect for śramaṇas and brahmins."
At that time, in order to subdue them, the king constructed a prison and confined them with shackles and fetters, where immeasurable sentient beings suffered within.
The king had a crown prince named Subduer (Suvīra),
who was exceptionally handsome and pleasing to all who saw him, and possessed twenty-eight of the marks of a great man.
Within the palace, he heard from afar the sounds of the prisoners’ agonizing cries and felt deep compassion in his heart.

He emerged from the palace and entered the prison, where he saw the various offenders bound together by shackles, fetters, and manacles. They were placed in a dark and gloomy place; some were scorched with fire, others were smoked with fumes, some were subjected to flogging and caning, and others suffered the amputation of kneecaps or castration. Naked and with disheveled hair, emaciated by hunger and thirst, their tendons severed and bones exposed, they wailed in extreme agony.
Having seen this, the Prince felt compassion in his heart and comforted him with a fearless voice, saying:
"Do not be distressed! Do not grieve or fear!"
"I shall cause you all to attain liberation.

He then went to the king's presence and addressed him, saying, "The prisoners in the jail endure bitter suffering that is difficult to bear; I pray that you will grant them clemency and bestow upon them fearlessness."
Then the king immediately assembled five hundred ministers and asked them,
"What is the matter with this? The ministers replied:
"Those criminals have privately stolen official property, plotted to usurp the royal throne, and illicitly entered the inner palace; their crimes deserve execution.
Anyone who shows pity and attempts to rescue them shall likewise face the death penalty."
At that time, the prince’s heart of compassion grew even more urgent, and he said to the minister:
"As you have said, release this man;
as for me, you may deal with me however you see fit."

For their sake, I am able to endure all manner of suffering; even if my body were ground to dust or my life were extinguished, I would have no regard for them, so that these offenders may all be freed from their suffering.
Why is this? If I do not rescue these sentient beings, how can I rescue those sentient beings within the prison of the triple world who suffer from its various afflictions?

All sentient beings within the triple world are bound by craving and obscured by ignorance; they are destitute and devoid of merit, fallen into the evil realms, their physical forms base and ugly, their faculties dissolute, and their minds deluded. They seek no way out, have lost the light of wisdom, and take pleasure in attachment to the three realms of existence. They sever all roots of virtue, extinguish all wisdom, and their minds are turbid and chaotic due to various afflictions. Dwelling in the prison of suffering, they enter the net of Māra, constantly oppressed by such miseries as birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, pain, and distress.
"How shall I bring them to liberation?
I must sacrifice my own body and life to rescue them!
At that time, the ministers went together to the king's presence and, raising their hands, cried out in a loud voice:
"Great King, you should know that if the Prince follows his own whims, he will destroy the royal law and bring calamity upon ten thousand people.
If Your Majesty cherishes him and fails to punish him, the King’s precious throne will likewise not endure for long."
Upon hearing these words, the king was filled with a towering rage and ordered that the crown prince and the criminals be executed.

When the queen heard this, she wailed in sorrow and grief; she disfigured her appearance and cast off her finery, then hurried to the king’s presence with a thousand court ladies. Prostrating herself on the ground, she bowed her head at the king’s feet and spoke thus together with them:
“We only pray, Great King, that you spare the life of the crown prince!”
The king immediately turned his gaze back and said to the prince:
"Do not save this criminal; if you save him, I shall surely kill you!"

At that time, because the Prince sought exclusively for all-knowledge, because he desired to benefit all sentient beings, and because he wished to universally rescue and gather them through great compassion, his mind was firm and without retreat or fear; he spoke again to the King, saying:
"I pray you, forgive their offense; let my body alone receive the execution!"
The king said, "As you wish! Then, the queen addressed him, saying:
"Great King! We pray that you will grant the Prince permission to practice giving for half a month and cultivate merit as he pleases, after which his offense shall be punished.
The King immediately granted his consent.
At that time, to the north of the capital city, there was a great park named Sunlight,
which had been a site for almsgiving in the past.
The Prince went there and established a great assembly for giving.

Food and drink, clothing, flower garlands, necklaces, ointments, powdered incense, banners, flags, precious parasols, and all manner of ornamental articles—whatever was sought, none were provided without being fully supplied.
After half a month had passed, on the final day, the king, ministers, elders, householders, the people of the city and towns, as well as all the non-Buddhist practitioners, all assembled together.

At that time, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparāja, knowing that the time had come to subdue all sentient beings, entered that assembly together with a great multitude, surrounded by celestial kings, honored by dragon kings, protected by yakṣa kings, praised by gandharva kings, prostrated to with bowed heads by asura kings, with garuḍa kings scattering various precious flowers with pure hearts, urged on with joyful entreaties by kinnara kings, and gazed upon with single-minded devotion by mahoraga kings.

At that time, the prince and the great assembly saw from afar the Buddha approaching, majestic and extraordinary, his faculties serene and composed like a well-trained elephant; his mind free from defilement like a pure pool. He manifested great supernormal powers, displayed great sovereignty, and revealed great majesty; his body was adorned with various marks and signs of excellence, emitting a great radiance that universally illuminated the world. From every pore issued clouds of fragrant flames, shaking immeasurable Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, while at every place he reached, a rain of all manner of ornaments fell.
By means of the Buddha’s dignified deportment and the Buddha’s merits, sentient beings who beheld him felt their minds purified and filled with joy, and their afflictions were extinguished.

At that time, the prince and the great assembly prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground at his feet; having offered him a seat and joined their palms, they addressed him, saying:
"Welcome, World-Honored One!"
"Welcome, Sugata!
We pray that you will compassionately accept us and take your seat upon this throne!
Through the Buddha's supernatural power, the devas of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens immediately transformed this seat into a throne of fragrant maṇi lotuses.
The Buddha sat upon it, and the assembly of bodhisattvas likewise took their seats, surrounding him on all sides.
At that time, all sentient beings in the gathering, by virtue of seeing the Tathāgata, had their suffering extinguished and their obstacles removed, becoming capable of receiving the sublime Dharma.
At that time, the Tathāgata, knowing they were ready to be transformed, spoke a sūtra with a perfect voice,
titled "The Universal Illumination Wheel of Causes," so that all sentient beings might each understand it according to their own kind.
At that time, within that assembly, there were eighty nayutas of sentient beings who, being distanced from dust and free from defilement, attained the pure Dharma-eye;
immeasurable nayutas of sentient beings attained the stage of no-more-learning;
and ten thousand sentient beings dwelt in the path of the Mahāyāna, entered into the conduct of Samantabhadra, and brought their great vows to fulfillment.
At that time, sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within a hundred Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions attained mental discipline within the Mahāyāna;
all sentient beings in immeasurable worlds were freed from the evil destinies and reborn in the heavens.
At that very moment, Prince Subāhu attained the bodhisattva liberation door of “teaching and transforming sentient beings to cause them to produce roots of goodness.
“Good son! Could it be that the prince at that time was anyone other than [yourself]?”
I am that very person.

Because in the past I gave rise to a heart of great compassion, sacrificing my body, life, and wealth to rescue suffering sentient beings, and opening my doors to practice great giving as an offering to the Buddhas, I attained this liberation.

"O Son of the Buddha, you should know that at that time, I acted solely for the benefit of all sentient beings; I was unattached to the triple world, sought no karmic reward, and did not crave fame. I had no desire to praise myself or disparage others, and regarding all sensory objects, I was neither stained by craving nor overcome by fear. I merely adorned the essential path of the Great Vehicle and constantly delighted in contemplating the gateways to omniscience. By practicing asceticism, I attained this liberation."
“O Son of the Buddha!
What do you think? As for those five hundred ministers who at that time sought to harm me—could they have been anyone else?
They are none other than the present-day Devadatta and his five hundred followers.”

These people, having received the Buddha’s transformation through his teaching, shall all attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. In a future age, after eons as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru have passed,
there will be an eon named *Sūryaprabhā* (Good Light) and a world named *Ratnaprabhā* (Jewel Light), wherein they shall become Buddhas.
These five hundred buddhas appeared in the world in succession; the first Tathāgata was named Mahākāruṇika (Great Compassion);
the second was named:
Benefiting the World;
the third was named Great Compassionate Lion;
The fourth is named "Rescuing and Protecting Sentient Beings";
and so on, until the very last, which is named:

O King of Physicians, although the great compassion of those Buddhas is equal, their lands, lineages, fathers and mothers, births, nativities, renunciations, practices of the path, journeys to the site of enlightenment, turnings of the wheel of the true Dharma, preaching of the sūtras, speech, voices, radiances, assemblies, lifespans, durations of the Dharma, and their names are each distinct.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Those sinful beings whom I have rescued are none other than the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, such as Krakucchanda, and ten million *asaṃkhyeya* great Bodhisattvas. Having resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the presence of the Tathāgata Anantavīryabalakīrtiguṇajñāna, they are now practicing the Bodhisattva path in the lands of the ten directions, cultivating and increasing this Bodhisattva liberation that teaches and transforms sentient beings so that they may give rise to roots of goodness.”
The King Prasenajit of that time was none other than the great master of debate, the Nirgrantha Saccaka, who is present here now.

The king’s court ladies and various attendants were those sixty thousand disciples of the Nirgrantha; having come together with their teacher to erect the banner of great debate and engage in discussion with the Buddha, they were all defeated and received the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. It was they who are these very people.
"All these people shall all become Buddhas; their lands' adornments, the duration of their kalpas, and their names shall each be distinct.
O Son of the Buddha!"

At that time, after I had saved those who were to be punished, my parents permitted me to renounce my kingdom, wife, children, wealth, and treasures, so that I might leave the household life and study the Path under the Buddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparāja.

During five hundred years, he purely cultivated the Brahma-faring and thereby achieved one million *dhāraṇīs*, one million supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), one million treasuries of Dharma (*dharmanidhāna*), and one million forms of courageous perseverance in seeking all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*). He purified one million gateways of forbearance (*kṣāntimukha*), increased one million minds of contemplation, accomplished one million powers of a bodhisattva, entered one million gateways of bodhisattva wisdom, and attained one million gateways of the *prajñāpāramitā*. He beheld one million Buddhas of the ten directions and gave rise to one million great bodhisattva vows.
In every thought-moment, he illuminated one million Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions;
in every thought-moment, he recollected one million Buddhas of the past and future eons throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
In every thought-moment, they know the ocean of transformations of ten million Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions;

in every thought-moment, they see all sentient beings within ten million worlds across the ten directions, in their various realms of existence, as they undergo birth and death according to their karma—whether in good or evil destinies, with beautiful or ugly forms—and they clearly comprehend all the various mental activities, various inclinations, various faculties, various karmic habits, and various accomplishments of those sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!

After my life ended at that time, I was reborn once again in that royal family as a wheel-turning monarch. Following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Dharmacakraghoṣagaganapradīpa, I next encountered the Tathāgata Dharmākāśarāja and served and made offerings to him;
subsequently, as Śakra, I encountered the Tathāgata Devendragarbha at this very site of enlightenment and drew near to him to serve and make offerings.”
Next, as the King of the Yāma Heaven, he encountered the Tathāgata Mountain of Great Earth Power in this very world, whom he approached and made offerings to;
next, as the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, he encountered the Tathāgata King of the Sound of the Wheel-Dharma Light in this very world, whom he approached and made offerings to;
next, as the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, he encountered the Tathāgata King of Space-Wisdom in this very world, whom he approached and made offerings to.
Next, he became the King of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Emanations; in this very world, he encountered the Tathāgata Invincible Banner, whom he approached and made offerings to.
Next, he became an Asura King; in this very world, he encountered the Tathāgata King of the Thunderous Sound of All Dharmas, whom he approached and made offerings to.
Next, he became a Brahma King; in this very world, he encountered the Tathāgata Universal Manifestation of the Proclamation of the Dharma-Sound, whom he approached and made offerings to.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Within this Good Light eon of the Jewel Light world, ten thousand Buddhas appeared in the world; I approached, served, and made offerings to them all.”
Next, there was another eon named Sunlight,
during which sixty billion Buddhas appeared in the world. The first Tathāgata was named Wondrous Appearance Mountain (*Suvarṇakūṭa*), and at that time, I was a king named:
Mahāmati, having served and made offerings to that Buddha,
there appeared next a Buddha named Paripūrṇaskandha;
at that time, I was a lay devotee (gṛhapati) and I drew near to him to serve and make offerings.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Vimalakumāra;
I was his minister and attended upon him with offerings.
Next, a Buddha appeared named...
Courageous Upholder, when I was the King of the Asuras, I approached and made offerings to a Buddha;
subsequently, another Buddha appeared named Sumeru-Aspect,
and as a tree spirit, I approached and made offerings to him.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Vimalabāhu;
I was then a merchant leader who approached and made offerings to him.
Next, a Buddha appeared named...
When the Buddha Siṃhavikrāmin appeared, I was a city deity and attended upon him with offerings;
next, when a Buddha appeared named Ratnaśikhin,
I was the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa and attended upon him with offerings.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Supreme Dharma Renown;
I was then a Gandharva king and personally attended upon and made offerings to him.
Next, a Buddha appeared named:
"O Prabhāketu, when I was a king of the kumbhāṇḍas, I drew near to and made offerings to them.
During that kalpa, sixty billion Tathāgatas appeared in the world in this successive order."
I have constantly received various bodies here, approaching and making offerings to each and every Buddha, teaching and bringing to maturity immeasurable sentient beings;

at the site of each and every Buddha, I attained various gates of samādhi, various gates of dhāraṇī, various gates of supernatural powers, various gates of eloquence, various gates of all-knowledge, various gates of the light of Dharma, and various gates of wisdom, illuminating various oceans of the ten directions, entering various oceans of Buddha-lands, and beholding various oceans of Buddhas, thereby achieving purification and increasing them to vastness.

Just as one has approached, made offerings to, and attended upon that many Buddhas during this eon, so too shall it be for all the Buddhas who appear in the world throughout eons as numerous as the atoms within all places and all oceans of worlds—approaching and making offerings to them, hearing their teachings, and faithfully accepting and upholding them.
"In this way, all Tathāgatas have cultivated this gate of liberation and further attained immeasurable skillful means for liberation.
At that time, the Night Goddess Sarvasattvatrāṇaśaraṇadā, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, spoke these verses to Sudhana:
"With a heart of joy, faith, and delight, You inquire about this inconceivable dharma of liberation;
Relying on the power of the Tathāgata’s protective mindfulness, I shall proclaim for you that which you should hear and accept.
In the past, across boundless and vast eons— more numerous than the atoms within oceans of lands—
there was a world named Jewel Light, and within it, an eon called Auspicious Light.
During this Great Kalpa of Auspicious Light, ten thousand Tathāgatas appeared in the world;
I drew near to and made offerings to them all, training under them in this liberation.
At that time there was a royal capital named Priyavyūha, vast, level, and exceedingly magnificent,
where beings of various karmas resided— some with pure minds and some who committed evil.
At that time there was a king named Prabhāsa, who always governed all living beings with the True Dharma;
his crown prince was named Sudānta, whose physical form was upright and endowed with all the marks of excellence.
At that time, there were immeasurable sinners, their bodies bound in prison and destined for execution;
having seen them, the Prince gave rise to compassion and addressed the King, entreating him for clemency.
At that time, the ministers addressed the king together, saying:
"Now this crown prince endangers the kingdom; such a criminal ought to be executed. How can you save them all and grant them exemption?"
Then King Prasenajit said to the crown prince:
"If you save him from that crime, you shall surely receive it yourself!
The prince’s compassionate concern grew even deeper; he vowed to save all sentient beings without ever retreating or fearing.
At that time, the king’s consorts and maidens all came to the king’s presence and said to him:
“We pray that you will release the crown prince for half a month, so that he may practice giving to sentient beings and cultivate merit.”
Upon hearing this, the king immediately granted his permission; he established a great assembly of almsgiving to relieve the poor and destitute.
There were no sentient beings who did not arrive, and whatever they requested was all provided to them.
Thus, as the fifteen days of the fortnight drew to a close and the time for the Prince’s execution was approaching,
a great multitude of hundreds of thousands of millions of people gazed upon him simultaneously, all wailing in lamentation.
That Buddha, knowing the faculties of the assembly were about to ripen, came to this gathering to transform all living beings;
manifesting great adornments of supernatural transformations, there was none who did not draw near and pay him homage.
The Buddha, through the skillful means of a single voice, Shines the lamp of Dharma throughout the sūtras;
The minds of immeasurable beings become supple, And all receive the prediction of their enlightenment.
Prince Śubhavyūha gave rise to joy, And generated the aspiration for unexcelled perfect enlightenment;
He vowed to serve the Tathāgata, Universally acting as a refuge for all sentient beings.
He immediately left the household life to dwell in reliance upon the Buddha, practicing the path to all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*).
At that time, he attained this liberation, whereby his great compassion extensively saves all living beings.
Abiding therein for oceans of kalpas, They contemplate the true nature of all phenomena;
Constantly rescuing sentient beings from the ocean of suffering, In this way they cultivate the path to enlightenment.
All the Buddhas who appear throughout the kalpas, I shall serve them all without exception;
With a mind of pure faith and understanding, I shall listen to, uphold, and protect the Dharma they teach.
Furthermore, throughout oceans of immeasurable and boundless eons, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field,
for every Buddha appearing in the world, I shall make offerings in this very same manner to each and every one.
I recall that in the past, when I was a crown prince, seeing sentient beings in prison, I vowed to sacrifice my body to rescue and protect them; by that means, I realized this gate of liberation.
Having practiced for oceans of vast eons, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields,
causing them to increase in every thought-moment, they further attain boundless skillful means.
All the Tathāgatas therein whom I have beheld and from whom I have received awakening,
have caused me to further clarify this liberation, as well as through their various powers of skillful means.
For immeasurable billions of kalpas, I have studied this inconceivable gate of liberation;
the ocean of all Buddhas' teachings is boundless, yet I am able to drink it all at once.
All lands throughout the ten directions, his body enters them all without obstruction;
the various names of realms across the three periods of time, he knows them all completely in every thought-moment.
The oceans of all Buddhas throughout the three periods of time, I clearly perceive each and every one without exception;
Furthermore, I can manifest my physical form And travel universally to the abodes of those Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, throughout all lands in the ten directions, before all Buddhas, the Teachers,
they cause clouds of every kind of adornment to rain down universally, making offerings to all Unsurpassed Enlightened Ones.
Furthermore, with an ocean of boundless great questions, they entreated all the World-Honored Ones;
the clouds of the sublime Dharma rained down by those Buddhas, they received and upheld them all without ever forgetting or losing them.
Furthermore, throughout immeasurable lands in the ten directions, before the assemblies of all Tathāgatas,
they sit upon seats adorned with myriad wonders and manifest various supernormal powers.
Furthermore, throughout the immeasurable lands of the ten directions, He manifests all manner of supernatural transformations:
Within a single body he manifests infinite bodies, And within infinite bodies he manifests a single body.
Furthermore, from each and every pore, they emit countless great rays of light;
through various skillful means, they extinguish the fires of affliction within sentient beings.
Furthermore, from within each and every pore, clouds of immeasurable transformation bodies appear,
filling all worlds throughout the ten directions, universally raining down the rain of Dharma to deliver all classes of beings.
All the sons of the Buddhas of the ten directions, Entering this inconceivable door of liberation,
Throughout all future kalpas until the very end, Abide securely and practice the bodhisattva deeds.
He preaches the Dharma according to their inclinations, causing them all to cast off the net of false views;
he reveals the heavenly realms and the two vehicles, up to the Tathāgata’s omniscience.
In all places where sentient beings are born, He manifests boundless and diverse bodies;
Appearing in forms identical to each class of being, He preaches the Dharma universally according to their minds.
If one attains this gate of liberation, One dwells in an ocean of boundless merit;
Like the number of atoms in oceans of lands, It is inconceivable and immeasurable.
“Good son! I know only this door of liberation for teaching and transforming sentient beings to cause them to produce roots of goodness.

As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, they transcend all worlds and manifest bodies within the various realms of existence; they do not dwell upon objects of perception and are free from obstruction. They thoroughly understand the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, skillfully observe all phenomena, attain the wisdom of non-self, and realize the dharma of non-self. They teach and transform all sentient beings with constant ceaselessness, their minds always dwelling peacefully in the dharma-gate of non-duality, universally entering the ocean of all speech and expression.”
How could I now possibly know or describe that ocean of merit, that courageous wisdom, that sphere of mental activity, that realm of samādhi, and that power of liberation?
"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa, there is a grove named Lumbinī;
That garden has a deity named Wondrous Virtue Perfection.
Go to him and ask:

"How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva practice, take birth in the family of the Tathāgatas, and become a light for the world, remaining without weariness throughout all kalpas until the end of the future?
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined in reverence, gazed up at him before taking his leave and departing.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Seventy-Third;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Seventy-Four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, by Imperial Command.
In the fifteenth part of the "Entering the Dharma Realm" chapter, the thirty-ninth, part fifteen:

At that time, having attained the bodhisattva liberation from the presence of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, the youth Sudhana recollected, cultivated, mastered, and increased it.

Traveling by stages, he arrived at the Lumbinī Grove and searched everywhere for the goddess Sudarśanā. He saw her within a pavilion adorned with all kinds of precious trees, seated upon a lion throne of precious lotuses, surrounded by twenty billion nayutas of devas who paid her respectful homage. She was expounding for them the Sūtra on the Ocean of the Bodhisattva’s Birth, causing them all to be born into the family of the Tathāgatas and to increase the great ocean of a bodhisattva’s merit.
Having seen him, Sudhana prostrated at his feet, stood before him with palms joined, and said:
"O Great Sage!

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva cultivates the bodhisattva practices, enters the family of the Tathāgatas, and becomes a great light for the world."

The deity replied: "Good son! There are ten kinds of treasuries of birth for bodhisattvas. If a bodhisattva accomplishes these dharmas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas; in every thought-moment they increase their bodhisattva roots of goodness, without weariness or indolence, without aversion or regression, without interruption or loss. They remain free from all delusions and do not give rise to thoughts of cowardice, inferiority, vexation, or regret. They advance toward omniscience, enter the gates of the Dharma-realm, and give rise to the vast mind. They increase the perfections (pāramitās) and accomplish the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Buddhas. They abandon the worldly realms and enter the stage of the Tathāgata, obtaining supreme supernatural powers. The teachings of all Buddhas are ever present before them, as they accord with the realm of the true meaning of omniscience."
“What are these ten? First, the treasury of birth through the vow to constantly make offerings to all Buddhas;
second, the treasury of birth through the arousal of the bodhicitta;”
Third is the treasury of birth through diligent cultivation by contemplating all dharma-gates;
fourth is the treasury of birth through universally illuminating the three periods of time with a profoundly pure mind;
fifth is the treasury of birth through the light of equanimity.
Sixth is the treasury of birth by being born into the family of the Tathāgatas;
seventh is the treasury of birth through the light of the Buddha’s power;
eighth is the treasury of birth by contemplating the gateway to universal wisdom.
Ninth is the treasury of manifesting birth through universal adornment;
tenth is the treasury of entering the stage of the Tathāgata through birth. "Good son!..."
What is called "the treasury of taking birth through the vow to constantly make offerings to all Buddhas"? Noble son!
When a bodhisattva first resolves their mind [on enlightenment], they make this vow:

"I shall respect, revere, and make offerings to all Buddhas; never weary of seeing the Buddhas, I shall always give rise to love and joy toward them, always arouse deep faith, and cultivate all merits without ever ceasing."
This is called the "Womb of Rebirth through the Initial Accumulation of Roots of Goodness for the Sake of All-Knowledge" of a bodhisattva.
What is called the "Womb of Rebirth through the Arising of the Bodhicitta"?
Good son! This bodhisattva gives rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
That is to say:
They give rise to the mind of great compassion, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings;
they give rise to the mind of making offerings to the Buddhas, for the sake of ultimate service;
they give rise to the mind of universally seeking the true Dharma, for the sake of being entirely without stinginess.
They give rise to a mind of vast aspiration for the sake of seeking all-knowledge;
they give rise to a mind of immeasurable loving-kindness for the sake of universally gathering in all sentient beings;
they give rise to a mind that never abandons any sentient being, having donned the firm armor of the vow to seek all-knowledge.
They give rise to a mind free from flattery and deception, because they attain knowledge of reality as it is;
they give rise to a mind that acts according to their words, because they cultivate the bodhisattva path;
they give rise to a mind that does not deceive the Buddhas, because they protect the great vows of all Buddhas.
They give rise to the mind of the vow for omniscience, because they transform sentient beings without ceasing until the end of the future.
By means of such merits of the bodhicitta, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields, Bodhisattvas attain birth in the family of the Tathāgata.
This is the second treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called "the treasury of birth through diligent cultivation by contemplating all dharma-gates"?

"Good son! This bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to the mind that contemplates the ocean of all dharma-gates; gives rise to the mind that dedicates [merit] toward the path of the perfection of all-knowledge; gives rise to the mind of right mindfulness free from error or negligence; gives rise to the pure mind of the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis; gives rise to the mind that cultivates and accomplishes all bodhisattva merits; gives rise to the mind that adorns all bodhisattva paths; gives rise to the mind of great vigorous practice seeking all-knowledge, cultivating all merits like the blazing of the kalpa-fire without rest; gives rise to the mind that cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra to teach and transform all sentient beings; and gives rise to the true mind that skillfully studies all dignified conduct, cultivates bodhisattva merits, relinquishes all possessions, and dwells in non-possession."
This is the third treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called "the treasury of birth through universally illuminating the three periods of time with a profoundly pure mind"?

"Good son! This bodhisattva possesses a pure and superior mind, attains the light of the Tathāgata’s enlightenment, and enters the ocean of a bodhisattva’s skillful means. His mind is as firm and solid as a diamond; he turns his back on all rebirths within the realms of existence and accomplishes all the sovereign powers of the Buddhas. He cultivates sublime practices, is endowed with the faculties of a bodhisattva, and his mind is clear and pure. His power of aspiration is unshakable, and he is constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas. He shatters all mountains of obstacles and serves as a place of refuge for all sentient beings."
This is the fourth treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called "the treasury of birth through the light of equanimity"?
"Good son! This bodhisattva is fully endowed with all practices and universally transforms sentient beings;
of all that exists, he is able to relinquish it all."
They abide in the realm of the Buddha’s ultimate pure precepts;
they are fully endowed with the dharma of patience and have accomplished the light of the Buddhas' patience regarding all dharmas;
and through great diligence, they advance toward all-knowledge and reach the further shore.
Cultivating all meditative concentrations, they attain the Samādhi of the Universal Door;
with pure wisdom perfected, they illuminate all phenomena with the sun of wisdom;
attaining the unimpeded eye, they behold the oceans of all Buddhas and awaken to and enter the true nature of all dharmas.
All those in the world who see him rejoice, for he is well able to cultivate the dharma-gate of suchness as it truly is.
This is the fifth treasury of birth of a bodhisattva. What is called:
What is the treasury of birth through being born into the family of the Tathāgatas?

Noble son, this Bodhisattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas and dwells together with all Buddhas; they accomplish all profound Dharma-gates, possess the pure great vows of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and attain the same roots of goodness as all Buddhas. They share the same essential nature as all Tathāgatas, possess supramundane practices and pure wholesome dharmas, and abide securely in the Dharma-gates of vast merit.
Entering various samādhis, they behold the Buddha’s spiritual power;
according to those who should be transformed, they purify all sentient beings;
answering as asked, their eloquence is inexhaustible.
This is the sixth treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called "the treasury of birth through the light of the Buddha's power"?

"Good son! This Bodhisattva enters deeply into the power of the Buddhas; he travels through all Buddha-fields with a mind free from regression; he makes offerings to and serves the assemblies of Bodhisattvas without weariness or fatigue; he understands that all phenomena arise like illusions; he knows that all worlds are like things seen in a dream; he perceives all forms and appearances as being like light and shadows; he knows that the workings of his supernormal powers are like transformations; he understands that all births are entirely like reflections; and he perceives the Dharma teachings of all Buddhas as being like echoes, revealing the Dharma-realm so that all may reach ultimate realization."
This is the seventh treasury of birth of a bodhisattva.
What is called "the treasury of birth through contemplating the gateway to universal wisdom"?

"Good son! This Bodhisattva, abiding in the stage of youthful innocence (*kumārabhūmi*), contemplates each and every gateway of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). Throughout immeasurable eons, he expounds all the practices of Bodhisattvas and attains mastery of mind within the profound samādhis of all Bodhisattvas. In every thought-moment, he appears before the Tathāgatas in the worlds of the ten directions. Regarding differentiated objects, he enters non-differentiated concentration; regarding non-differentiated dharmas, he manifests differentiated wisdom. Within immeasurable objects, he knows the absence of objective realms; within limited objects, he enters immeasurable realms. He penetrates the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) as vast and boundless, knowing that all worlds are merely provisional designations and that everything arises from the consciousness-mind."
This is the eighth treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called "the treasury of birth through the universal manifestation of adornments"?

"Good son! This bodhisattva is able to adorn immeasurable Buddha-fields in various ways; they can universally manifest the bodies of all sentient beings and all Buddhas, attain fearlessness, and expound the pure Dharma, circulating throughout the dharma-realm without obstruction.

According to the inclinations of their hearts, they cause all to know and see, manifesting various practices for attaining enlightenment and causing them to give rise to the unobstructed path of omniscience."
Thus, his actions never miss their proper time, and he constantly dwells within the treasury of Vairocana’s wisdom-samādhi.
This is the ninth birth-treasury of a bodhisattva.
"What is meant by 'the treasury of taking birth upon entering the stage of the Tathāgata'? Good son!
This Bodhisattva has received the dharma of empowerment from all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time and universally knows the sequence of all realms.

That is to say: they know the sequence of the deaths and births of all sentient beings throughout the past and future; the sequence of the practices of all Bodhisattvas; the sequence of the mental thoughts of all sentient beings; the sequence of the attainment of Buddhahood by all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; and the sequence of teaching the Dharma through skillful means. They also know the names and sequences of all kalpas—whether of formation or destruction—throughout the beginning, middle, and end of all time.

In accordance with the needs of sentient beings to be transformed and delivered, he manifests the adornment of merit from attaining the Way, employing supernatural powers and preaching the Dharma to subdue them through skillful means.
This is the tenth treasury of birth of a bodhisattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva cultivates, increases, perfects, and accomplishes these ten dharmas, they will be able to manifest various adornments within a single adornment;
thus adorning all lands, they guide, instruct, and awaken all sentient beings without ceasing throughout all future kalpas.”
They expound the various realms and various modes of maturation within the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas, transmitting immeasurable teachings through successive generations;
they manifest the inconceivable sovereign power of Buddhas, filling all space and the Dharma-realm;
they turn the wheel of Dharma within the ocean of the mental activities of all sentient beings, manifesting the attainment of Buddhahood in all worlds, constantly and without interruption.
They expound all dharmas through ineffable, pure speech and sounds, abiding in immeasurable places and attaining unimpeded penetration;

they adorn the site of enlightenment with all dharmas, manifesting the attainment of Buddhahood according to the diverse inclinations and understandings of sentient beings, revealing immeasurable and profound treasuries of Dharma, and teaching and transforming all worlds until their full accomplishment.
At that time, the forest deity of Lumbinī, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, surveyed the ten directions by the Buddha’s spiritual power and spoke in verse:
"With a most supreme, stainless, and pure mind, Never weary of beholding all Buddhas,
Vowing to constantly make offerings throughout the future— This is the treasury of birth for those of brilliant wisdom."
Within all lands throughout the three periods of time, may all sentient beings and all Buddhas be fully delivered and constantly venerated; this is the inconceivable treasury of taking birth.
Hearing the Dharma without weariness and delighting in contemplation, universally unimpeded throughout the three periods of time,
with body and mind as pure as space— this is the treasury of birth for those of renowned fame.
His mind dwells perpetually in the ocean of great compassion, as firm as a diamond or a mountain of jewels;
having fully realized the gateway to all modes of omniscience, this is the womb of birth for the Most Victorious One.
Great compassion universally covers all; wondrous conduct constantly increases the ocean of perfections.
With the light of the Dharma, he illuminates all classes of beings—this is the birth-treasury of the heroic and valiant one.
Thoroughly realizing the nature of phenomena with an unimpeded mind, Born into the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
Universally entering the ocean of the dharma-realm of the ten directions— This is the treasury of birth for the wise and enlightened.
The Dharma-body is pure and the mind is unimpeded; It reaches universally all lands throughout the ten directions.
There is no power of any Buddha that it does not accomplish— This is the inconceivable treasury of birth.

Having attained mastery by entering deep wisdom, And having reached the ultimate consummation in all samādhis, One contemplates the gateway of omniscience as it truly is; This is the treasury of birth for the True Body.
Purifying all Buddha-fields, Diligently practicing the methods for universally transforming sentient beings,
Manifesting the sovereign power of the Tathāgata— This is the treasury of birth for those of great renown.
Having long practiced for omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), they are swiftly able to enter the stage of the Tathāgata;
realizing that the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) is entirely unobstructed—this is the treasury of birth for these sons of the Buddha.
“Good son! When a bodhisattva is endowed with these ten dharmas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgata and become a pure light for all the worlds. Good son!”
"Since immeasurable eons past, I have attained this liberation-door of sovereign birth.
Sudhana said, "Noble One!"
"What is the scope of this gate of liberation? He replied, "Noble son!
I previously made this vow:
"May I be able to draw near whenever all Bodhisattvas manifest their births;
may I enter the infinite ocean of births of the Tathāgata Vairocana."
By the power of her former vows, she was born in this world, within the Lumbinī Grove of Jambudvīpa, constantly mindful of when the Bodhisattva would descend to be born;
after a hundred years had passed, the World-Honored One indeed came from Tuṣita Heaven to be born here.
"At that time, ten kinds of signs appeared within this grove. What are these ten?
First, the ground of this garden suddenly became level of its own accord; all pits, hollows, mounds, and elevations completely disappeared."
Second, the ground is made of diamond, adorned with various jewels, and free from tiles, rubble, thorns, stumps, or stumps.
Third, rows of precious tala trees stand in circumference, their roots firmly planted down to the water's edge.

Fourth, it produces sprouts of various fragrances and manifests treasuries of various fragrances; precious incense forms trees that spread their branches and leaves in dense shade, and all these fragrances surpass even the perfumes of the heavens.
Fifth, various exquisite flower garlands and precious ornaments were arranged in rows and distributed everywhere, filling all places.
Sixth, every single tree within the garden naturally blossomed with mani-jewel flowers.
Seventh, within all the ponds and pools, flowers spontaneously grew, emerging from the earth and spreading across the surface of the water.

Eighth, at that time, all the kings of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas dwelling in the desire and form realms of this Sahā world gathered in this grove without exception, standing with palms joined in reverence.

Ninth, all the celestial maidens in this world, even down to the daughters of the mahoragas, were filled with joy; each of them carried various articles of offering and stood respectfully before the pi-lo-cha tree.
Tenth, from the uṣṇīṣas of all Buddhas of the ten directions, there radiates light called the "Lamp of Sovereignty in the Rebirth of Bodhisattvas," which universally illumines this grove.

Within each ray of light, there appear all the miraculous manifestations of the Buddhas' births and their descent into the world, as well as the merits of the rebirths of all bodhisattvas; furthermore, these rays emit the various voices and sounds of all Buddhas.
These are the ten kinds of auspicious signs in the grove.
When these signs appear, the celestial kings and others immediately know that a Bodhisattva is about to descend to be born;
seeing these omens, my joy is immeasurable.

“Good son! When Lady Māyā departed from the city of Kapilavastu and entered this grove, ten kinds of auspicious signs of light further appeared, causing all sentient beings to attain the light of the Dharma.”

What are these ten? They are: the light of the treasury of all jewel flowers; the light of the treasury of precious incense; the light that emanates the true and wondrous sound from the blossoming of precious lotuses; the light of the initial resolve of Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions; the light of the spiritual transformations manifested by all Bodhisattvas upon entering the various stages (*bhūmi*); the light of the perfected wisdom of all Bodhisattvas practicing the *pāramitās*; the light of the wisdom of the great vows of all Bodhisattvas; the light of the wisdom of skillful means for teaching and transforming sentient beings of all Bodhisattvas; the light of the wisdom of the true realization of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) of all Bodhisattvas; and the light of all Bodhisattvas attaining the sovereign power of a Buddha, being born, leaving home, and attaining perfect enlightenment.
These ten radiances universally illumine the minds of immeasurable sentient beings. "Good son!
When Lady Māyā sat beneath the Pīlu tree, there further appeared ten kinds of divine transformations as the Bodhisattva was about to be born."
What are these ten?

"Good son! When the Bodhisattva was about to be born, the sons and daughters of the gods from the heavens of the desire realm, as well as all the gods of the form realm, along with the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and their retinues, all gathered like clouds for the sake of making offerings."

The majesty and virtue of Lady Māyā were exceptionally sublime; all the pores of her body emitted radiance that illuminated the trichiliocosm without obstruction, causing all other lights to vanish. She extinguished the afflictions of all sentient beings and the sufferings of the evil realms.
This was the first supernatural manifestation as the Bodhisattva was about to be born.

Furthermore, noble son, at that time, within the womb of Lady Māyā, all the forms and images of the three thousandfold world system appeared in their entirety. Within each of the ten billion Jambudvīpas, there were respective capitals and cities, and respective gardens and groves, each with different names; in every one of them, Lady Māyā was seen dwelling therein, surrounded by hosts of devas, all manifesting the inconceivable signs of the supernatural manifestations of the Bodhisattva’s impending birth.
This was the second miraculous manifestation as the Bodhisattva was about to be born. Furthermore, noble son,

from every pore of Lady Māyā appeared the sounds of all the Buddhas preaching the Dharma, as well as the sight of the Tathāgata reverently making offerings to all those Buddhas during his past cultivation of the bodhisattva path.
Just as a bright mirror or water can manifest the images of the sun, moon, stars, clouds, and thunder in the sky, so too are all the pores of Queen Māyā’s body;
they can likewise manifest the Tathāgata’s past causes and conditions.
This was the third supernatural manifestation as the Bodhisattva was about to be born. "Furthermore, noble son!

Within every single pore of Lady Māyā’s body, there appeared all the worlds where the Tathāgata had dwelt while practicing the bodhisattva path in the past—cities, towns, villages, mountain forests, rivers, and seas; the kalpas of sentient beings; the appearance of Buddhas in the world; entry into pure lands; the manner of taking birth according to circumstances; the length of lifespans; and the practice of wholesome dharmas in reliance upon spiritual friends. In every land and at every place of birth, Lady Māyā constantly served as their mother."
All such things appeared within the pores of his skin without exception.
This was the fourth supernatural manifestation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to be born.
"Furthermore, son of good family!"

Within every single pore of Lady Māyā, there were manifested all the circumstances of the Tathāgata’s past cultivation of the bodhisattva path—his place of birth, his physical appearance and features, his clothing and food, and his experiences of suffering and joy—all appearing clearly and distinctly in their entirety.
This was the fifth miraculous manifestation as the Bodhisattva was about to be born.

Furthermore, noble son, from every single pore of Queen Māyā’s body, there appeared all that the World-Honored One had relinquished when he practiced the perfection of giving in the past—those things most difficult to give: his head, eyes, ears, nose, lips, tongue, teeth, body, hands, and feet; his blood, flesh, sinews, and bones; his sons, daughters, wives, and concubines; his cities, towns, palaces, clothing, necklaces, gold, silver, and precious treasures.
"In this way, all internal and external things, as well as the appearance, voice, and location of the recipient, are seen.
This is the sixth supernatural manifestation of the Bodhisattva as he is about to be born."

"Furthermore, noble son, when Lady Māyā entered this grove, the forest universally manifested all the lands, groves, garments, flower garlands, ointments, powdered incense, banners, streamers, and canopies—every adornment made of various jewels—as well as the exquisite sounds of music and song from the past, when all Buddhas had entered their mothers' wombs; it caused all sentient beings to see and hear these things everywhere."
This was the seventh miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.

"Furthermore, noble son, when Lady Māyā entered this grove, there emerged from her body the Bodhisattva’s palace and pavilions made of the king of *maṇi* jewels, which surpassed all the dwellings of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and human kings. Covered with jeweled nets, permeated by exquisite fragrances, and adorned with various treasures, they were pure both inside and out; each was distinct and not intermingled, filling the Lumbinī Grove on every side."
This was the eighth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.

"Furthermore, noble son, when Lady Māyā entered this garden, there emerged from her body as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields. The physical forms, features, marks, radiance, deportment, spiritual powers, and retinues of these bodhisattvas were all identical to those of the Bodhisattva Vairocana, without any difference; they all simultaneously praised the Tathāgata."
This was the ninth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
Furthermore, noble son,
as Lady Māyā was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, suddenly before her, from the adamantine foundation, there emerged a great lotus flower named:

It was a treasury adorned with all kinds of jewels, with a stem of vajra and filaments of various gems, its pedestal made of the king of wish-fulfilling jewels. It had as many petals as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, all fashioned from mani-jewels, and it was covered above by nets and canopies of precious gems.
It was upheld by all the celestial kings;
all the dragon kings showered down fragrant rain;
and all the yakṣa kings surrounded it with reverence, scattering various celestial flowers.
All the gandharva kings produced sublime sounds, singing praises of the bodhisattva’s merit from his past offerings to the Buddhas;
all the asura kings abandoned their arrogant minds and prostrated in respectful salutation;
and all the garuḍa kings hung down precious silk banners that filled the entirety of space.
All the kinnara kings looked up with joy, singing and praising the bodhisattva’s merits;
all the mahoraga kings were filled with delight, singing and praising him, while they universally rained down clouds of all manner of jewel-adornments.
This was the tenth divine manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born. "Good son!
After the Lumbinī Grove had displayed these ten kinds of signs, the Bodhisattva’s body was then born."

Like a pure solar disk appearing in the void of space, like auspicious clouds emerging from the summit of a high mountain, like flashes of lightning shining amidst dense clouds, or like a great torch being lit in the darkness of night;
at that time, when the Bodhisattva was born from his mother’s side, the radiance of his physical marks was likewise so.

Good son! At that time, although the Bodhisattva manifests his initial birth, he has already fully realized that all phenomena are like dreams and illusions, like shadows and images, neither coming nor going, neither arising nor ceasing.

“Good son! When I saw the Buddha manifest various miraculous transformations at his birth in the Lumbinī Grove within Jambudvīpa among these four continents, I also saw the Tathāgata manifest various miraculous transformations at his birth in the Lumbinī Groves within the Jambudvīpas of ten billion sets of four continents across the trichiliocosm.

I also saw immeasurable Buddha-fields within every single atom of the trichiliocosm, and I saw immeasurable Buddha-fields within every single atom of hundreds of Buddha-worlds, thousands of Buddha-worlds, and even all worlds throughout the ten directions. Within all such Buddha-fields, there were likewise Tathāgatas manifesting various miraculous transformations at their births.”
"In this manner, moment after moment, it is always without interruption.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to that goddess:
"Great Goddess, how long has it been since you attained this liberation?"
He replied, "Good son!
In the distant past, more than as many eons ago as there are atoms in a billion buddha-fields, and even beyond that number."
At that time, there was a world named Universal Jewels,
and an eon named Joyful Delight, in which eighty nayutas of buddhas appeared.
The first Buddha was named Sovereign Banner of Merit (*Svairaguṇadhvaja*), endowed with the ten titles.
In that world, there were four continents named:
It was adorned with wondrous light;
within Jambudvīpa of that four-continent world system, there was a royal capital named Sumeru-Adorned Banner.
Among them was a king named Jewel Flame Eye; his queen was named:
"Joyful Light.
Good son! In this world, Lady Māyā is the mother of Vairocana Tathāgata;
In that world, Lady Joyful Light, who was the mother of the first Buddha, was likewise so.
"Good son! When Lady Joyful Light was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, she went with twenty billion nayutas of female attendants to the Golden Flower Garden."
In the garden there is a tower named Wondrous Jewel Peak;
beside it is a tree named:
Sarvadatta. Lady Priyakara grasped a branch of that tree and gave birth to the Bodhisattva; the hosts of heavenly kings each held scented water and together bathed him.
At that time, there was a wet nurse named Pure Light (Vimalaprabhā) standing by his side.
Once he had been bathed, the assembly of heavenly kings handed him over to the wet nurse.
The wet nurse respectfully accepted [the child] and gave rise to great joy; she immediately attained the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Universal Eye.
Having attained this samādhi, she saw throughout the ten directions immeasurable Buddhas, and further attained the Bodhisattva liberation of sovereign mastery in manifesting birth in all places.
Just as the consciousness at the moment of initial conception is swift and unimpeded, so too is it for one who has attained this liberation:
seeing all Buddhas and, by the power of their original vows, attaining mastery over taking birth is likewise so.
"Good son! What do you think?
Was that wet nurse anyone other than [myself]?"
I am that very person.

Since that time, in every thought-moment, I have constantly seen Vairocana Buddha manifesting the ocean of births of bodhisattvas and his sovereign spiritual powers for the sake of taming sentient beings.

Just as I see Vairocana Buddha, by the power of his original vows, manifesting in every thought-moment within this trichiliocosm, and even within the atoms of all worlds throughout the ten directions, the miraculous transformations of a Bodhisattva’s birth;
and seeing that all Buddhas do likewise—I pay them all respectful service and offerings, listen to the Dharma they preach, and practice according to those teachings.
At that time, the forest deity of Lumbinī, wishing to reiterate the meaning of this liberation, and empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
