and possessing a body that is neither mind nor form— like empty space, its activity is unimpeded, transcending the eyes of all worlds; only...
This is what is seen by the Pure Eyes of Samantabhadra.

How may I now draw near to such a person, serve and make offerings to them, dwell together with them, observe their appearance, listen to their voice, contemplate their speech, and receive their instructions?
Having formed this thought, a guardian deity of the city named Ratnanetra appeared in the sky, surrounded by her retinue.
Adorned with various exquisite ornaments and holding countless jeweled flowers of many colors in her hands, she scattered them over Sudhana and spoke these words: "Noble son!
One should guard the city of the mind, which means:
not being covetous of any realm of birth and death;
one should adorn the city of the mind, which means:
One should single-mindedly seek the ten powers of the Tathāgata;
one should purify the city of the mind, which means:
ultimately severing and eliminating stinginess, envy, flattery, and deceit.
One should purify the city of the mind, which means:
contemplating the true nature of all phenomena;
one should expand the city of the mind, which means:
One should accomplish all dharmas that aid the path;
one should adorn the city of the mind, that is,
by constructing the palaces of various dhyānas and liberations.
One should illuminate the city of the mind, which means:
universally entering the bodhimaṇḍas of all Buddhas to hear and receive the Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā;
one should augment the city of the mind, which means:
It universally encompasses all the skillful means of the Buddhas;
one should fortify the city of the mind by constantly and diligently practicing the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra.
One should guard the city of the mind, which means:
constantly and single-mindedly resisting and warding off evil friends and the armies of Māra;
one should clear and illuminate the city of the mind, which means:
One should open the way to draw forth the light of the wisdom of all Buddhas;
one should skillfully repair the city of the mind, namely,
by listening to and receiving all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas.
One should support the city of the mind, which means:
having deep faith in the ocean of all Buddhas' merits;
one should expand the city of the mind, which means:
Great compassion should be extended universally to all worlds;
one should skillfully shield the city of the mind, namely,
by gathering all wholesome dharmas to cover it from above.
One should broaden the city of the mind, which means:
to have great compassion and pity for all sentient beings;
one should open the gates of the city of the mind, which means:
One should relinquish all possessions and bestow them as gifts according to need;
one should guard the city of the mind in secrecy,
that is, by preventing various evil desires from entering.
One should fortify the city of the mind, which means:
expelling all unwholesome dharmas so that they do not remain;
one should resolve the city of the mind, which means:
One should never regress from gathering all the dharmas that assist the path to omniscience;
one should establish the citadel of the mind, which means:
maintaining right mindfulness of all the spheres of activity of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
One should clarify the city of the mind, which means:
to clearly comprehend all the various dependent originations of the Dharma-gates contained within the sūtras of all Buddhas' True Wheel of Dharma;
one should partition the city of the mind, which means:
Universally illuminating and instructing all sentient beings so that they may all perceive the path to *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge);
one should maintain the city of the mind, which means:
giving rise to the great ocean of vows of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
One should enrich the city of the mind, which means:
accumulating the great mass of merit that pervades the entire dharma-realm;
one should cause the city of the mind to be clear and lucid, which means:
One should universally know the dharmas of the faculties, desires, and so forth of all sentient beings;
one should cause the city of the mind to be sovereign, namely:
universally encompassing the entirety of the ten directions of the dharma-realm.
One should cause the city of the mind to be pure, namely:
by maintaining right mindfulness of all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas;
one should know the intrinsic nature of the city of the mind, namely:
One should know that all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature;
one should know that the city of the mind is like an illusion, namely:
realizing the nature of all phenomena through omniscience.
“O Son of the Buddha!
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva can thus purify and cultivate the city of the mind, they will be able to accumulate all wholesome dharmas. Why is this?
Because they eliminate all obstacles and difficulties, namely:

the obstacle to seeing the Buddha, the obstacle to hearing the Dharma, the obstacle to making offerings to the Tathāgata, the obstacle to gathering in all sentient beings, and the obstacle to purifying the Buddha-lands.

"Good son! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva is free from such obstacles and difficulties, if they give rise to the aspiration to seek a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), they will see one without effort; eventually, they shall certainly attain buddhahood."

At that time, a host of body-deities named Padmadharmaguṇa and Suvicitrapuṣpābhāsa, surrounded by immeasurable deities before and behind, emerged from the site of enlightenment and remained in mid-air. Before Sudhana, they praised Māyādevī with various sublime voices; from their ear-ornaments, they emitted nets of light of infinite colors and forms, universally illuminating the boundless worlds of all Buddhas, and caused Sudhana to see all the Buddhas in the lands of the ten directions.
That net of light circled the world to the right; having completed one circuit, it then returned and entered the crown of Sudhana’s head, eventually pervading all the pores of his body.
Sudhana immediately attained the eye of pure radiance, because he was forever free from the darkness of all ignorance;
he attained the unobscured eye, because he was able to comprehend the nature of all sentient beings;
he attained the stainless eye, because he was able to contemplate the gateways to the nature of all phenomena.
They attain the eye of pure wisdom, for they are able to contemplate the nature of all Buddha-lands;
they attain the Vairocana-eye, for they see the Dharma-body of the Buddhas;
they attain the eye of universal radiance, for they see the inconceivable and equal body of the Buddhas.
They attain the eye of unimpeded light, because they observe the formation and destruction of all oceans of lands;
they attain the eye of universal illumination, because they see the Buddhas of the ten directions arising great skillful means to turn the wheel of the true Dharma;
they attain the eye of universal realms, because they see immeasurable Buddhas using their power of mastery to discipline sentient beings.
He attained the eye of universal vision, for he beheld all Buddhas appearing in all lands.
At that time, there was a rākṣasa king named Suvilocana, the guardian of the Bodhisattva Dharma Hall, who,
together with his retinue of ten thousand rākṣasas, stood in the air and scattered various exquisite flowers over Sudhana, saying these words:
“Good son! If a bodhisattva accomplishes ten dharmas, he will be able to draw near to spiritual friends. What are these ten?
That is to say:
their minds are pure and free from all flattery and deception;
they embrace all sentient beings with impartial great compassion, yet know that no sentient beings possess any true reality.
They proceed toward omniscience with a mind that never regresses;
through the power of faith and understanding, they universally enter the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas;
and having attained the eye of pure wisdom, they perceive the nature of all phenomena.
Great compassion is impartial and universally covers all sentient beings;
with the radiance of wisdom, it clears away all delusive realms;
and with the rain of nectar, it washes away the fever of birth and death.
To penetrate all phenomena with the vast eye;
and for the mind to always accord with spiritual friends.
These are the ten.
"Furthermore, Sons of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva accomplishes ten gates of samādhi, they constantly see all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra). What are these ten?

They are: the samādhi of the pure wheel of the emptiness of phenomena; the samādhi of observing the ocean of the ten directions; the samādhi of never abandoning nor being deficient in any realm of experience; the samādhi of universally beholding the appearance of all Buddhas; the samādhi of gathering the treasury of all merits; the samādhi of never forsaking spiritual friends at any time; the samādhi of constantly seeing all spiritual friends give rise to the merits of all Buddhas; the samādhi of never being separated from all spiritual friends; the samādhi of constantly making offerings to all spiritual friends; and the samādhi of never committing any fault in the presence of all spiritual friends.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva accomplishes these thirteen samādhi-doors, they constantly draw near to all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra). Furthermore, they attain the samādhi of the spiritual friend who turns the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas.
Having attained this samādhi, they fully know that the essential nature (dharmatā) of all Buddhas is equal, and they encounter spiritual friends everywhere.
When these words were spoken, the youth Sudhana looked up into the sky and replied to him,
saying, "Excellent, excellent!
Out of compassion and to sustain me, you have skillfully instructed me so that I may see a spiritual friend."
I pray that you will explain for me:
how should one go to the presence of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)?
In which direction, in what city, town, or village should one seek a spiritual friend?
The rākṣasa replied,
"Good son! You should universally pay homage to the ten directions and seek out spiritual friends."
One seeks a spiritual friend by contemplating all objects of experience with right mindfulness;
one seeks a spiritual friend by traveling throughout the ten directions with courageous mastery;
one seeks a spiritual friend by observing the body and the mind as being like dreams and like shadows.

At that time, Sudhana, having received and practiced those instructions, immediately beheld a great jewel lotus springing forth from the earth: its stem was of diamond, its calyx of exquisite jewels, its petals of mani-gems, its pericarp of radiant jewel-kings, and its filaments of various precious colors and fragrances; it was completely covered by countless nets of jewels.
Upon that terrace was a multi-storied pavilion named "Treasury Universally Encompassing the Dharma Realms of the Ten Directions.

It was wondrously and exquisitely adorned, with a floor made of vajra and a thousand pillars standing in rows, all fashioned from mani jewels. Its walls were made of Jambūnada gold, with necklaces of various jewels hanging down on all four sides, while the steps and railings were magnificently decorated all around.

Within that tower-palace was a seat of wish-fulfilling jewel lotuses, adorned with various kinds of precious gems. There were exquisite jeweled railings, with precious garments interspersed among them; jeweled canopies and nets covered the top, while banners of many precious silks hung down all around. As a gentle breeze moved them, light flowed and sounds resonated. From within the jeweled flower-pennants, various wonderful flowers rained down;
from the jeweled bells and chimes, beautiful sounds issued forth; from between the jeweled doors and windows, various necklaces hung down;
from within the bodies of the *maṇi* jewels, fragrant water flowed out; and from the mouths of the jeweled elephants...
From the Lotus Net, precious lion mouths emit clouds of exquisite fragrance; from the Brahma-form jeweled wheels, sounds of music according to all desires emerge;
from the diamond jeweled bells, the sounds of the great vows of all Bodhisattvas arise; from within the precious moon banners, the transformation bodies of Buddhas appear;
and from the Pure Treasury Jewel King, the sequence of the births of the Buddhas of the three periods of time is manifested. From the Sun Treasury...
The maṇi jewel emits great radiance that universally illumines all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions;
the maṇi-jewel king emits the perfect radiance of all Buddhas; the Vairocana maṇi-jewel king raises clouds of offerings to make offerings to all Tathāgatas;
and the wish-fulfilling jewel king manifests the spiritual power of Samantabhadra in every thought-moment.

The transformations filled the Dharma-realm; from the Sumeru Jewel King, celestial palaces emerged, wherein divine maidens sang various exquisite melodies in praise of the Tathāgata’s inconceivable and subtle merits.
At that time, Sudhana saw such a seat, surrounded by immeasurable seats for the assembly; upon that seat sat Lady Māyā, manifesting a pure physical body before all the beings in the gathering.
That is to say:
a physical body that transcends the three realms, for it has already emerged from all states of existence;
a physical body that accords with the mind's inclinations, for it is without attachment to any world.
The universally pervasive form-body, because it is equal in number to all sentient beings;
the incomparable form-body, because it causes all sentient beings to extinguish their inverted views;
the form-body of immeasurable kinds, because it manifests in various ways according to the minds of sentient beings.
The body of infinite marks and forms, because it universally manifests all manner of appearances;
the body that universally appears in correspondence, because it manifests through great sovereign mastery;
the body that transforms all things, because it manifests before beings according to what is appropriate for them.
The color-body that is constantly manifested, for it is inexhaustible throughout the entire realm of sentient beings;
the color-body that has no departure, for it does not cease within any state of existence;
the color-body that has no arrival, for it does not emerge from any world.
The form-body is not produced, because it is without origination;
the form-body does not perish, because it is beyond verbal expression;
the form-body is not substantial, because it is attained as it truly is.
The non-illusory body, because it manifests in accordance with the world;
the immovable body, because it is forever free from arising and ceasing;
the indestructible body, because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is indestructible.
The form-body of signlessness, because it transcends the path of speech;
the form-body of the single mark, because taking signlessness as its mark;
the form-body like a reflected image, because it manifests in response to the mind.
The illusory body, because it is produced by illusory wisdom;
the mirage-like body, because it is sustained only by mental conception;
the shadow-like body, because it manifests in birth according to vows.
The body of form like a dream, because it manifests in accordance with the mind;
the body of form of the dharma-realm, because its nature is pure as space;
the body of form of great compassion, because it constantly protects sentient beings.
The unobstructed body of form, because it pervades the Dharma-realm in every thought-moment;
the boundless body of form, because it universally purifies all sentient beings;
the immeasurable body of form, because it transcends all speech and language;
The non-abiding form-body, because it vows to deliver all worlds;
the non-localized form-body, because its constant transformation of sentient beings is uninterrupted;
the unarisen form-body, because it is accomplished through illusory vows.
The unsurpassed form-body, because it transcends all worlds;
the form-body as it truly is, because it is manifested by a concentrated mind;
the unborn form-body, because it appears in accordance with the karma of sentient beings.
The wish-fulfilling jewel body, because it universally fulfills the aspirations of all sentient beings;
the non-discriminative body, because it arises solely in accordance with the discriminations of sentient beings;
the body free from discrimination, because no sentient beings can know it.
The inexhaustible body, because it reaches the limit of birth and death for all sentient beings;
the pure body, because it is identical to the Tathāgata’s non-discrimination.
Such a body is not form, for all its formal characteristics are like reflections.
It is not sensation, because worldly painful sensations have been utterly extinguished;
it is not perception, because it manifests only in accordance with the perceptions of sentient beings;
it is not volitional formations, because it is accomplished by means of karma that is like an illusion.

Bodhisattvas are free from consciousness because their vow-knowledge is empty and devoid of intrinsic nature, because the linguistic expressions of all sentient beings have been severed, and because they have already attained the accomplishment of the body of quiescent extinction.

At that time, the youth Sudhana again beheld Lady Māyā, who manifested a physical body surpassing all those in the world, appearing in accordance with the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings.
That is to say:

they may manifest forms surpassing those of the goddesses of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, even up to surpassing those of the goddesses of the Heaven of the Four Great Kings; or they may manifest forms surpassing those of nāga girls, even up to surpassing those of human women. By manifesting such immeasurable physical forms, they bring benefit to sentient beings.
Gathering all the dharmas that assist the path to omniscience, they practice the pāramitā of giving with equanimity, and their great compassion universally covers all worlds.
They give birth to the immeasurable merits of the Tathāgata, cultivate and increase the mind of omniscience, and observe and contemplate the true nature of all phenomena;

they attain the ocean of profound patience, possess the various gates of concentration, abide in the realm of the samādhi of equality, and obtain the perfect radiance of the Tathāgata’s concentration, thereby exhausting the vast ocean of sentient beings' afflictions.

Their minds are always in right concentration, never wavering or disturbed; they constantly turn the pure wheel of Dharma that never regresses, and are well able to understand all Buddha-dharmas. They constantly observe the true reality of phenomena with wisdom;

seeing all Tathāgatas, their minds are never satiated. They know the sequence in which the Buddhas of the three periods of time appear, and as the Buddha-samādhis are ever present before them, they thoroughly comprehend the immeasurable and innumerable paths of purity through which the Tathāgatas appear in the world, traversing the space-like realm of all Buddhas.
Universally gathering in sentient beings, they teach and bring them to fulfillment according to each one's own mind.

They enter the Buddha’s immeasurable, pure *dharmakāya*, fulfill great vows, purify all buddha-fields, and ultimately subdue all sentient beings; their minds constantly and universally enter the realms of all Buddhas.
They give rise to the sovereign spiritual powers of bodhisattvas; having already attained the pure and undefiled *dharmakāya*, they constantly manifest infinite *rūpakāyas*.

They crush all demonic forces, achieve the power of great roots of goodness, give rise to the power of the True Dharma, and are endowed with the powers of all Buddhas. They attain the sovereign powers of all bodhisattvas and swiftly increase the power of all-encompassing wisdom.

They attain the light of the Buddha’s wisdom, which universally illumines all things, fully knowing the various distinctions within the ocean-like minds, faculties, natures, and inclinations of immeasurable sentient beings.

Their bodies pervade the oceans of lands throughout the ten directions, fully knowing the characteristics of the formation and destruction of all those lands; with vast eyes they behold the oceans of the ten directions, and with all-pervading wisdom they know the oceans of the three periods of time.

Their bodies universally serve the oceans of all Buddhas, and their minds constantly receive and uphold the oceans of all Dharmas. They cultivate all the merits of the Tathāgatas and give birth to all the wisdom of Bodhisattvas; they always delight in observing the path traversed by all Bodhisattvas from their first aspiration until their final accomplishment; they constantly and diligently protect all sentient beings; and they always delight in praising the merits of all Buddhas, vowing to become the mother of all Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld Lady Māyā manifesting as many gates of skillful means as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa.

Having seen this, Sudhana manifested as many bodies as Lady Māyā had manifested; in every place before Lady Māyā, he paid respectful homage. Immediately, he realized immeasurable and innumerable gateways of samādhi, examining them with discernment, practicing them, and entering into them.
Rising from samādhi, he circumambulated Māyā and her retinue three times to the right, stood with palms joined, and said:
"O Great Sage!
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva has instructed me to resolve my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, to seek spiritual friends, and to draw near to and make offerings to them."
At each and every station of a spiritual friend, I have gone to serve them without ever passing by in vain;
having gradually arrived here, I pray that you will explain to me:
how should a bodhisattva study the bodhisattva conduct so as to achieve its fulfillment?
She replied, "O Son of the Buddha!
I have already accomplished the bodhisattva liberation door of the illusory wisdom of great vows; for this reason, I am constantly the mother of all bodhisattvas."
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as I was born from the right side of Queen Māyā in the house of King Śuddhodana in the city of Kapilavastu within this Jambudvīpa, manifesting inconceivable and sovereign miraculous transformations;
even so, throughout this entire ocean of worlds, all Vairocana Tathāgatas enter my body and manifest the sovereign miraculous transformation of birth.
"Furthermore, noble son!

When the Bodhisattva was about to descend to be born in the palace of King Śuddhodana, I saw that from every single pore of the Bodhisattva’s body there radiated light named 'The Wheel of Merit of the Birth of All Tathāgatas.
From each and every pore, there appeared as many manifestations of the adornments of the birth of Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields."
All those rays of light universally illumined all worlds;
having illumined the worlds, they entered the crown of my head and even into all my pores.

Furthermore, within that light, there were universally manifested the names of all bodhisattvas, their miraculous manifestations of birth, their palaces and retinues, and their self-entertainment with the five desires;

moreover, one saw them renounce the world, proceed to the site of enlightenment, attain equal and perfect awakening, sit upon the lion throne surrounded by bodhisattvas, receive offerings from various kings, and turn the wheel of the true Dharma for the great assemblies;

furthermore, one saw the Tathāgatas, when they were practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, reverently making offerings at the abodes of various Buddhas, generating the bodhi-mind, purifying buddha-lands, and manifesting immeasurable transformation bodies in every thought-moment, pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions, until finally entering parinirvāṇa.
All such matters as these were seen by me without exception.
"Furthermore, good son!
When that wondrous light entered my body, although the dimensions of my physical form did not exceed their original state, in reality I had already transcended all worlds."
Why is this so? Because at that time, my body was equal in measure to empty space, capable of fully containing the various palaces adorned for the births of the bodhisattvas of the ten directions.

At that time, when the Bodhisattva was about to descend from the Tuṣita Heaven, there were bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields who surrounded him before and behind. All these bodhisattvas shared the same vows, the same practices, the same roots of goodness, the same adornments, the same liberations, and the same wisdom; they were equal in all the stages, all the powers, the dharma-body, and the form-body, even unto the spiritual powers, conduct, and vows of Samantabhadra.
Furthermore, eighty thousand dragon kings and all the lords of the world arrived together, riding upon their palaces, to make offerings.
At that time, by means of his supernormal powers, the Bodhisattva universally manifested himself in all the Tuṣita palaces together with the other Bodhisattvas.

Within each palace, he manifested the images of his taking birth within the Jambudvīpa of every world throughout the ten directions, skillfully teaching and transforming immeasurable sentient beings, causing the Bodhisattvas to abandon all indolence and remain free from attachment.
Furthermore, by means of his supernormal powers, he emits a great radiance that universally illumines the world, shattering all darkness and extinguishing all suffering and affliction;
he causes all sentient beings to recognize all their karmic actions from past lives, so that they may forever emerge from the evil realms.
Furthermore, in order to rescue and protect all sentient beings, they appear before them everywhere, manifesting various supernatural transformations.
Displaying such extraordinary and marvelous feats, they come together with their retinues and enter my body.

Those bodhisattvas move about with sovereign ease within my womb; they may take a single step across a trichiliocosm, or they may take a single step across as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields.

Furthermore, in every moment of thought, all the Tathāgatas in unspeakably unspeakable numbers throughout the worlds of the ten directions, along with their assemblies of bodhisattvas, as well as the devas of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, and even the Brahmā kings up to the Form Realm—all those who wish to behold the miraculous transformation of the Bodhisattva dwelling in the womb, to pay respectful homage and offerings, and to hear and receive the True Dharma—enter into my body.
Although my belly can entirely contain such a multitude of assemblies, my body neither becomes vast nor is it constricted;
each of those bodhisattvas perceives themselves as being situated within their own assembly at a site of enlightenment, pure and magnificently adorned.
“Good son! Just as I was the mother for the Bodhisattva’s birth within the Jambudvīpa of this four-continent world system,
it is exactly the same for all the Jambudvīpas within the ten billion four-continent world systems of the trichiliocosm.”
However, this body of mine is fundamentally non-dual; it does not abide in a single place, nor does it abide in many places.
Why is this? It is because I have cultivated the liberation door of the adornment of the illusory wisdom of the great vows of a bodhisattva.
"Good son! Just as I am the mother of the World-Honored One of the present age,
so too was I the mother of all the immeasurable Buddhas of the past."

“Good son! In the past, I was once a deity of a lotus pond. At that time, a bodhisattva suddenly manifested by transformation within a lotus calyx; I immediately supported, attended, and nurtured him. All the worlds together called me by the name ‘Mother of the Bodhisattva.’”

Furthermore, in the past, when I was the deity of the Bodhimaṇḍa, a bodhisattva suddenly manifested through transformation within my womb; for this reason, the world also called me "The Mother of the Bodhisattva."
"Good son! There are immeasurable bodhisattvas in their final birth who, through various skillful means, manifest taking birth in this world; I have been the mother to them all."

“Good son! Within this world during the Bhadrakalpa, in past ages, when Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, Kāśyapa Buddha, and the present World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha manifested their births, I was their mother.”

In a future age, when the Bodhisattva Maitreya is about to descend from the Tuṣita Heaven, he will emit a great radiance that universally illumines the Dharma-realm, manifesting the supernatural transformations of all bodhisattvas taking birth; he shall then be born into a great clan among humans to subdue sentient beings, and at that time, I shall also be his mother.
In this sequence, there were the Buddhas Siṃha, Dharmadhvaja, Sunetra, Vimalapadma, Puṣpavasu, Tiṣya, Puṣya, Sumati, Vajra, Vimala, Candraprabha, Dīpadhara, Yaśas, and Vajra.
Dhvajāgra Buddha, Viśuddhārtha Buddha, Nīlāṅga Buddha, Pāragata Buddha, Ratnārciḥparvata Buddha, Daṇḍadhara Buddha, Padmaguṇa Buddha, Yaśas Buddha,
Amitaguṇa Buddha, Varapradīpa Buddha, Vyūhitakāya Buddha, Suvilokita Buddha, Maitrīguṇa Buddha.
Anabhiniveśa Buddha, Mahāteja Buddha, Anantaghoṣa Buddha, Jitāri Buddha, Vigatasaṃśaya Buddha,
Viśuddha Buddha, Mahāprabha Buddha, Śuddhacitta Buddha, Meghaguṇa Buddha, Vyūhacūḍa Buddha,
Drumarāja Buddha, Ratnakuṇḍala Buddha, Sāgaraprajña Buddha, and Ratnavicitra Buddha.
Buddha, Flower-Crown Buddha, Fulfiller-of-Vows Buddha, Great-Sovereign Buddha, Wondrous-Virtue-King Buddha,
Most-Honored-and-Victorious Buddha, Sandalwood-Cloud Buddha, Azure-Eye Buddha, Supreme-Wisdom Buddha, Observing-Wisdom Buddha,
Blazing-King Buddha, Firm-Wisdom Buddha, Sovereign-Named Buddha, and Lion [Buddha].
King Buddha, Sovereign Buddha, Supreme Peak Buddha, Vajra Wisdom Mountain Buddha,
Wondrous Virtue Treasury Buddha, Jewel Net Adorned Body Buddha, Good Wisdom Buddha, Sovereign Heaven Buddha,
Great Heavenly King Buddha, Independent Virtue Buddha, Good Bestower Buddha, Flame Wisdom Buddha, and Water Heaven Buddha.
The Buddha Supreme Flavor, the Buddha Born of Unsurpassed Merit, the Buddha Attended by Sages, the Buddha Who Follows Worldly Speech,
the Buddha Sovereign Banner of Merit, the Buddha Light Banner, the Buddha Contemplating the Body,
the Buddha Wondrous Body, the Buddha Fragrant Flame, the Buddha Adorned with Vajra Jewels, the Buddha Joyful Eye, and the Buddha Free from Desire.
Buddha, Mahādeha Buddha, Vasudeva Buddha, Anuttara Buddha, Anupama-nirvāṇa Buddha,
Jñānabodhi Buddha, Vītarāga Buddha, Mahājvālendra Buddha, Śāntabhava Buddha, Viśākha-deva Buddha,
Vajraparvata Buddha, Jñānajvālāguṇa Buddha, Kṣema Buddha, and Guru.
The Buddha Subhūti, the Buddha Pūrṇaviśuddha, the Buddha Viśuddhasatya, the Buddha Paramārtha, the Buddha Śataprabha,
the Buddha Uttamottara, the Buddha Gambhīravibhu, the Buddha Mahāpṛthivīrāja, the Buddha Vyūharāja, the Buddha Vimukti, the Buddha Svararāja, the Buddha Viśeṣa, and the Buddha Vibhu.
The Buddha, the Unsurpassed King of Physicians, the Buddha Moon of Merit, the Buddha Unobstructed Light, the Buddha Mass of Merit,
the Buddha Appearance of the Moon, the Buddha Sun Deity, the Buddha Emerging from All Existences,
the Buddha Valiant Renown, the Buddha Gate of Radiance, the Buddha King of Śāla Trees, the Buddha Most Victorious, and the Buddha Medicine King.
Ratnavijaya Buddha, Vajramati Buddha, Anabhibhūta Buddha, Anabhibhāsana Buddha, Gaṇarāja Buddha, Mahāyaśas Buddha, Kṣipradhara Buddha, Amitaprabha Buddha,
Mahāpraṇidhiprabha Buddha, Dharmeśvarāmoṣa Buddha, Avaivartikabhūmi Buddha, and Śuddhadeva Buddha.
Buddha Sudeva, Buddha Dṛḍhatapā, Buddha Sarvasuhṛt, Buddha Vimuktasvara, Buddha Vikrīḍitarāja, Buddha Mithyākuṭilavinivartana, Buddha Campakanirmalaprabha,
Buddha Guṇasaṃbhava, Buddha Varacandra, Buddha Dhṛtaprajñolkā, Buddha Viśiṣṭakāya, and Buddha Anabhilāpya.
Buddha, Most Pure Buddha, Friend Who Brings Peace to Sentient Beings Buddha, Immeasurable Light Buddha, Fearless Sound Buddha,
Water-Heaven Virtue Buddha, Immovable Wisdom Light Buddha, Flower Victorious Buddha, Moon Flame Buddha,
Non-Retrogressive Wisdom Buddha, Free from Attachment Buddha, and Accumulated Mass of Merit Buddha.
Buddha, Destroyer of Evil Realms Buddha, Buddha Who Scatters Flowers Universally, Lion’s Roar Buddha, Ultimate Truth Buddha,
Unobstructed Vision Buddha, Vanquisher of Enemy Armies Buddha, Non-Attachment to Marks Buddha, Buddha Who Has Transcended the Ocean of Discrimination,
Ocean of Majestic Beauty Buddha, Sumeru Mountain Buddha, Unattached Wisdom Buddha, Boundless [Virtue] Buddha.
The Buddha Seat, the Buddha Pure Abode, the Buddha Following the Teacher’s Conduct, the Buddha Supreme Giver, the Buddha Constant Moon,
the Buddha King of Benefit, the Buddha Immovable Multitude, the Buddha Universal Gathering, the Buddha Beneficial Wisdom,
the Buddha Sustainer of Life, the Buddha Unextinguished, the Buddha Endowed with Renown, and the Buddha Great Power.
...the Buddha of Various Colors and Marks, the Buddha of Formless Wisdom, the Buddha of Immovable Heaven, the Buddha of Inconceivable Wondrous Virtue,
the Buddha of the Full Moon, the Buddha of the Moon of Liberation, the Buddha of the Unsurpassed King, the Buddha of the Rarefied Body,
the Buddha Honored by Brahmā, the Buddha Without Blinking, the Buddha Following the Ancients, and the Buddha of Supreme Action.
...Anudharmajñāna Buddha, Anabhibhūdeva Buddha, Acintyaguṇaprabha Buddha, Anudharmacārin Buddha, Amitabhadra Buddha, Sarvānugata-vaśavartin Buddha, Uttamadeva Buddha— and so on,
up to Ruci Tathāgata— within this Bhadrakalpa, in this trichiliocosm...
In a thousandfold world system, those who are to attain Buddhahood all have me as their mother.

Just as it is in this trichiliocosm, so too throughout all eons and in all the infinite worlds of the ten directions within this ocean of worlds, for all those who practice the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra in order to transform all sentient beings, I see my own body serving as their mother.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to Lady Māyā:
"O Noble One, how much time has passed since you attained this liberation? She replied:
“Good son! In the distant past,
beyond an inconceivable number of kalpas— beyond what can be known by the supernatural powers, the divine eye, or the wisdom of Bodhisattvas in their final birth—
there was a kalpa named Pure Light, and a world named:”
Sumeru-guṇa, although there are various mountains where the five destinies dwell together, his land is composed of many jewels, pure and magnificent, free from all impurities and evils.
There are a thousand billion sets of four continents; among them is one set of four continents named Lion Banner (*Siṃhadhvaja*), within which there are eight billion royal cities.
There is one royal city named...
There was a wheel-turning king named Great Majestic Virtue.
To the north of that royal city, there was a site of enlightenment named Full Moon Radiance;
the deity of that site of enlightenment was named:
Maitreyaprabha.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Vimaladhvaja,
who sat at the site of enlightenment, about to achieve perfect awakening.
There was an evil māra named Golden Light who, together with his retinue of immeasurable hosts, came to where the bodhisattva was.

That wheel-turning sage king of great majesty and virtue had already attained the sovereign power of a bodhisattva’s supernormal faculties; he manifested an army many times larger in number, which surrounded the site of enlightenment.
All the māras were terrified and fled in all directions;
thus, that bodhisattva attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, having witnessed these events, the deity of the site of enlightenment was filled with immeasurable joy. She conceived the thought of him as her son toward that king, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and made this vow:
"Wherever this Wheel-Turning King may be born, until he attains Buddhahood, may I always be his mother.
Having made this vow, she further made offerings to ten nayutas of Buddhas at this very site of enlightenment.
“Good son, what do you think?
Is that deity of the site of enlightenment anyone other than myself? It is I who am he.”
The Wheel-Turning King was none other than the present World-Honored One, Vairocana.

Since I first made my vow before him, this Buddha, the World-Honored One, has been born in every realm throughout all lands in the ten directions; he has planted various roots of goodness, cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva, and taught and brought to maturity all sentient beings, even manifesting his final body. Moment by moment, throughout all worlds, he universally manifests the miraculous transformations of a bodhisattva’s birth, always being my son, while I have always been his mother.

"Good son! In the past and present, when the immeasurable Buddhas of the worlds of the ten directions were about to attain Buddhahood, they all emitted a great radiance from between their eyebrows to illuminate my body and the palaces, mansions, and dwellings where I resided;
during their final births, I served as the mother for them all."
“Good son! I know only this bodhisattva liberation door of the illusory wisdom of great vows.

As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the treasury of great compassion, they never grow weary of teaching and transforming sentient beings; by their power of mastery, they manifest the spiritual transformations of immeasurable Buddhas from each and every pore.”
"How could I now know or describe their meritorious conduct?
'Good son! In this world, in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, there is a king named:'"
In that land of Right Mindfulness, the king has a daughter named Celestial Lord Light.
Go to her and ask:
"How should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

At that time, the youth Sudhana respectfully received his instruction, prostrated himself with his head at [the elder's] feet, circumambulated him countless times, and, gazing up at him with longing and admiration, withdrew while walking backward.
He then proceeded to the celestial palace, where he beheld those goddesses; he prostrated at their feet, circumambulated them, and stood before them with palms joined, saying: "Noble Ladies!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva practices."
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Noble One is skilled at providing instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me!
The goddess replied:
"Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'Pure Adornment of Unimpeded Mindfulness. "
"Good son! By the power of this liberation, I recollect the past: there was a most excellent eon named Blue Lotus."
During that kalpa, I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.

From the time those Tathāgatas first left the household life until their passing, I attended upon them all, protecting, honoring, and making offerings to them; I constructed monasteries and provided all necessary articles.

Furthermore, regarding those Buddhas—from the time they dwelt in their mothers' wombs as bodhisattvas, to their birth, to their taking seven steps, to their uttering the Great Lion’s Roar, to their dwelling in the palace during their youth, to their proceeding toward the Bodhi tree and attaining perfect enlightenment, and to their turning the wheel of the True Dharma and manifesting the spiritual transformations of a Buddha to teach, transform, and subdue sentient beings—I clearly remember all such deeds performed from their first resolution until the end of the Dharma, without exception; they are ever present before me, held in mindfulness without being forgotten.
Furthermore, I recall a past kalpa named Good Ground (*Sudhara*),
in which I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in ten Ganges Rivers;
furthermore, a past kalpa named:
"O Wondrous Virtue, in that [eonic period] I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world;
furthermore, in an eon named 'Non-attainment,' I made offerings to eighty-four billion hundred thousand nayutas of Tathāgatas."
Furthermore, there was an eon named Good Light,
during which I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa;

Measuring their desires, they should increase the bodhisattva’s immeasurable skillful means;
they should give birth to the bodhisattva’s immeasurable superior faculties; they should clarify the bodhisattva’s immeasurable resolute understandings;
they should enter into the bodhisattva’s immeasurable equanimity; they should purify the bodhisattva’s immeasurable virtues; they should cultivate and refine the bodhisattva’s...
One should manifest the immeasurable practices of a bodhisattva; one should demonstrate the immeasurable conduct of a bodhisattva that accords with the world;
one should generate the power of immeasurable pure faith; one should abide in the power of immeasurable diligence; one should purify the power of immeasurable right mindfulness;
one should fulfill the power of immeasurable samādhi; and one should give rise to the power of immeasurable pure wisdom. One should...
One should strengthen the power of immeasurable resolve; one should accumulate the power of immeasurable merit;
one should increase the power of immeasurable wisdom; one should arouse the power of immeasurable bodhisattvas;
one should fulfill the power of immeasurable Tathāgatas; one should discern immeasurable dharma-gates; one should thoroughly understand immeasurable dharma-gates; and one should purify them.
Regarding the immeasurable Dharma gates, one should produce the light of immeasurable Dharmas, should effect the illumination of immeasurable Dharmas,
should illuminate the faculties of immeasurable categories of beings, should know the diseases of immeasurable afflictions, should collect the medicines of immeasurable sublime Dharmas,
should treat the illnesses of immeasurable sentient beings, and should prepare the immeasurable nectar of immortality.
One should travel to immeasurable Buddha-lands; one should make offerings to immeasurable Tathāgatas;
one should enter immeasurable assemblies of Bodhisattvas; one should receive the teachings of immeasurable Buddhas; one should endure the offenses of immeasurable sentient beings;
one should extinguish the hardships of immeasurable evil realms; and one should cause immeasurable sentient beings to give rise to goodness.
The Way requires that one gather immeasurable sentient beings through the four means of integration; one should cultivate immeasurable gates of dhāraṇī;
one should give rise to immeasurable gates of great vows; one should cultivate immeasurable great compassion and the power of great vows;
one should diligently seek immeasurable teachings without ever resting; and one should give rise to immeasurable power of contemplation. One should give rise to...
One should purify the light of immeasurable wisdom regarding immeasurable supernormal powers; one should go to the immeasurable realms of sentient beings;
one should undergo immeasurable births; one should manifest immeasurable distinct bodies; one should know immeasurable modes of speech;
one should enter into immeasurable diverse minds; and one should know the great sphere of the bodhisattva.
O Dhātu, you should dwell in the great palace of the bodhisattvas; you should contemplate the profound and wondrous Dharma of the bodhisattvas;
you should know the realm of the bodhisattvas that is difficult to know; you should practice the various deeds of the bodhisattvas that are difficult to perform;

you should possess the honored majesty and virtue of the bodhisattvas; you should tread upon the correct station of the bodhisattvas that is difficult to enter; and you should know the lineage of the bodhisattvas.
One should plant all manner of practices; manifest the universal spiritual powers of a Bodhisattva; receive the equal Dharma-cloud of a Bodhisattva;
extensively expand the boundless net of a Bodhisattva’s conduct; fulfill the boundless perfections of a Bodhisattva;
receive the immeasurable predictions of enlightenment of a Bodhisattva; enter the immeasurable gates of patience of a Bodhisattva; and cultivate purification.
Regarding the immeasurable stages of a bodhisattva, one should purify the immeasurable Dharma-gates of a bodhisattva;
one should dwell together with all bodhisattvas for boundless eons, making offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, adorning and purifying unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands,
and giving rise to unspeakable numbers of bodhisattva vows.

Good son! To state the essentials: one should universally cultivate all bodhisattva practices; one should universally transform all realms of sentient beings; one should universally enter all kalpas; one should universally be born in all places; one should universally know all worlds; one should universally practice all dharmas; one should universally purify all lands; one should universally fulfill all vows; one should universally make offerings to all Buddhas; one should universally accord with the vows of all bodhisattvas; and one should universally serve all spiritual friends.
“Good son! In seeking spiritual friends, you should not grow weary;
upon seeing a spiritual friend, do not give rise to complacency.”
I ask you, virtuous friend, do not shrink from toil and hardship;
draw near to the virtuous friend, do not harbor thoughts of regression;
make offerings to the virtuous friend, and never cease.
One should not misinterpret the instructions of a spiritual friend;
one should not harbor doubts while learning the conduct of a spiritual friend;
and one should not hesitate upon hearing a spiritual friend expound the gateway to liberation.
When you see a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) acting in accordance with the afflictions (kleśa), do not give rise to dislike or wonder;
maintain a mind of deep faith and reverence toward the spiritual friend, and do not allow it to change.
Why is this? Son of good family!
It is because through spiritual friends, Bodhisattvas hear about all the practices of Bodhisattvas and accomplish them all.
The merit of a bodhisattva gives birth to all the great vows of bodhisattvas, brings forth all the roots of goodness of bodhisattvas,
accumulates all the requisites for the path of bodhisattvas, develops all the light of the Dharma of bodhisattvas,
reveals all the gates of renunciation of bodhisattvas, and cultivates the purity of all bodhisattvas.
Precepts: abiding securely in all bodhisattva qualities and dharmas; purifying all the vast aspirations of bodhisattvas;
increasing all the firm resolve of bodhisattvas; being fully endowed with all the dharanis and doors of eloquence of bodhisattvas;
attaining the pure treasury of all bodhisattvas; and giving birth to all bodhisattva samādhis.
Radiant light, attaining the supreme vows of all bodhisattvas, sharing the same vow as all bodhisattvas, hearing the supreme teachings of all bodhisattvas,
attaining the secret places of all bodhisattvas, reaching the island of the Dharma-treasure of all bodhisattvas,
increasing the sprouts of the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas, and causing them all to grow...
The wisdom-body of the bodhisattva protects the profound and secret treasury of all bodhisattvas, sustains the mass of merit of all bodhisattvas,
purifies the path of rebirth for all bodhisattvas, receives the clouds of the true Dharma of all bodhisattvas,
enters the path of the great vows of all bodhisattvas, and proceeds toward the fruit of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
They embrace all the sublime practices of bodhisattvas, reveal all the merits of bodhisattvas,
travel to all directions to hear and receive the sublime Dharma, praise the vast majesty and virtue of all bodhisattvas,
give rise to the power of great compassion in all bodhisattvas, encompass the supreme sovereign power of all bodhisattvas, and bring forth all...
The bodhisattva’s factors of enlightenment perform all deeds that benefit bodhisattvas.
"Good son! By being sustained by spiritual friends, bodhisattvas do not fall into the evil destinies;..."
Through being sustained by spiritual friends, one does not regress from the Mahāyāna;
through being protected by spiritual friends, one does not violate the bodhisattva precepts;
through being guarded by spiritual friends, one does not follow after evil associates.
Through being nurtured by spiritual friends, one does not lack or diminish the bodhisattva-dharma;
through being gathered by spiritual friends, one transcends the stage of ordinary beings;
through being instructed by spiritual friends, one transcends the stages of the two vehicles.
Through the guidance of spiritual friends, one attains liberation from the world;
through being nurtured by spiritual friends, one remains unstained by worldly dharmas;
and through serving spiritual friends, one cultivates all the practices of a bodhisattva.
By making offerings to spiritual friends, one becomes endowed with all factors conducive to enlightenment;
by associating with spiritual friends, one is not overcome by karma or afflictions;
by relying upon spiritual friends, one’s power becomes firm and steadfast, such that one fears no demons.
By relying upon spiritual friends, all factors conducive to enlightenment are increased. Why is this?
O son of noble family!
A virtuous friend can purify all hindrances, extinguish all transgressions, eliminate all calamities, and cease all evils;
they can shatter the long night of darkness of ignorance, destroy the solid prison of false views,
enable one to leave the city of birth and death, cause one to abandon the worldly home, and sever the nets of all māras.
They are able to extract the arrows of manifold suffering; they are able to leave behind the perilous places of ignorance;

they are able to emerge from the great wilderness of false views; they are able to cross over the currents of existence; they are able to depart from all deviant paths; they are able to show the path to Bodhi;

they are able to teach the Dharma of the bodhisattvas; they are able to cause one to dwell securely in the practices of a bodhisattva; and they are able to cause one to advance toward the One Vehicle.
All-knowledge can purify the eye of wisdom, can increase the bodhicitta, can give rise to great compassion,
can manifest sublime conduct, can expound the pāramitās, can banish evil associates, can cause one to abide in the various stages (bhūmis),
can cause one to attain the various patiences (kṣāntis), can cause one to cultivate all roots of goodness, and can cause one to...

It accomplishes all requisites; it is able to bestow all great merits; it can lead one to the stage of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); it can cause one to joyfully accumulate merit; it can cause one to leap with vigor while practicing all deeds;
it can cause one to enter into the profound meaning; it can cause one to reveal the gateway to liberation; it can cause one to close off... [the gates of cyclic existence].
It cuts off all evil realms; it can cause illumination by the light of the Dharma; it can cause moistening by the rain of the Dharma;
it can cause the extinction of all delusions; it can cause the relinquishing of all views;
it can cause the increase of all Buddha-wisdom; and it can cause one to dwell securely in all Dharma-gates of the Buddhas.
“Good son! A spiritual friend is like a compassionate mother, for she gives birth to the seeds of Buddhahood;
she is like a compassionate father, for she brings about vast benefit.”
They are like a wet nurse, for they protect one from committing evil;
they are like a teacher, for they show one what a bodhisattva must study;
they are like a skilled guide, for they can point out the path of the perfections.
Like a skilled physician, because he can cure the various diseases of the afflictions;
like the Snowy Mountains, because he increases the medicinal herbs of all-knowledge;
like a brave general, because he utterly eliminates all fears.
They are like ferrymen, for they cause one to emerge from the violent torrent of birth and death;
they are like ship captains, for they cause one to reach the jewel island of wisdom. Good son!
"You should always maintain such right mindfulness and reflection regarding all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
Furthermore, son of good family,
when you serve all spiritual friends, you should develop a mind like the great earth, because you bear heavy burdens without weariness."
One should generate a mind like a vajra, for one's vows are firm and indestructible;
one should generate a mind like Mount Cakravāḍa, for no suffering can move it;
one should generate a mind like that of a servant, for one complies with all instructions.
One should develop a mind like that of a disciple, because one does not oppose any instruction;
one should develop a mind like that of a servant, because one does not tire of any tasks;
one should develop a mind like that of a foster mother, because one undergoes all hardships without complaining of fatigue.
One should generate a mind like that of a hired laborer, because one does not oppose whatever instructions are received;
one should generate a mind like that of a man clearing away filth, because one is free from arrogance;
one should generate a mind like ripened grain, because one is able to remain humble.
One should develop a mind like that of a fine horse, because it is free from a wicked nature;
one should develop a mind like that of a great carriage, because it can carry heavy burdens;
one should develop a mind like that of a well-trained elephant, because it is always submissive and compliant.
One should resolve upon a mind like Mount Sumeru, because it is unshakable;
one should resolve upon a mind like a good dog, because it does not harm its master;
one should resolve upon a mind like a caṇḍāla, because it is free from arrogance.
One should develop a mind like that of a castrated ox, for it is free from wrath;
one should develop a mind like that of a boat, for it does not grow weary of coming and going;
one should develop a mind like that of a bridge, for it carries others across without forgetting its toil.
One should develop a mind like that of a filial son, because one must respectfully comply with their countenance;
one should develop a mind like that of a prince, because one must obey their commands and instructions. "Furthermore, good son!

You should conceive of yourself as being afflicted by illness, of the spiritual friend as a king of physicians, of the Dharma taught as excellent medicine, and of the practice cultivated as the curing of disease;

furthermore, you should conceive of yourself as one embarking on a long journey, of the spiritual friend as a guide, of the Dharma taught as the correct path, and of the practice cultivated as reaching the distant destination;

furthermore, you should conceive of yourself as one seeking to cross over, of the spiritual friend as a boatman, of the Dharma taught as a vessel and oars, and of the practice cultivated as arriving at the shore.
Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a crop, of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) as a dragon king, of the Dharma taught as seasonal rain, and of the practice cultivated as ripening;
one should also conceive of oneself as a pauper, of the spiritual friend as King Vaiśravaṇa, of the Dharma taught as wealth and treasure, and of the practice cultivated as abundance;

furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a disciple, of the spiritual friend as a skilled craftsman, of the Dharma taught as a craft or art, and of the practice cultivated as thorough understanding.

Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as being in a state of fear, of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) as a valiant hero, of the Dharma taught as a weapon, and of the practice undertaken as the destruction of enemies;
furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a merchant, of the spiritual friend as a guide, of the Dharma taught as precious treasure, and of the practice undertaken as the gathering of goods;
furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a son, of the spiritual friend as parents, of the Dharma taught as family property, and of the practice undertaken as the inheritance thereof.

Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a prince, of the spiritual friend as a minister, of the Dharma being taught as the king’s decree, and of the practice being undertaken as donning the royal crown, wearing the royal robes, binding the royal fillet, and sitting upon the royal throne.
“Good son! You should give rise to such a mind and form such an intention as to draw near to spiritual friends. Why is this?
With such a mind, one draws near to spiritual friends, causing their aspirations to become eternally pure.
Furthermore, good son, spiritual friends cause all roots of goodness to grow, just as the Snowy Mountains cause all medicinal herbs to grow.
A spiritual friend is a vessel for the Buddha-dharma, just as the great ocean swallows all flowing streams;
a spiritual friend is the locus of merit, just as the great ocean produces all manner of jewels;
a spiritual friend purifies the bodhicitta, just as a fierce fire can refine true gold.
A spiritual friend transcends worldly dharmas, just as Mount Sumeru rises above the great ocean;
a spiritual friend is unstained by worldly dharmas, like a lotus flower that is not adhered to by water;
a spiritual friend does not accept any evils, just as the great ocean does not harbor a corpse.
A spiritual friend increases pure dharmas, just as the white moon’s radiance becomes full;
a spiritual friend illuminates the dharma-realm, just as the blazing sun shines upon the four continents;
a spiritual friend nurtures the body of a bodhisattva, just as parents raise their children.
“Good son! To speak briefly,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can comply with the instructions of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra),
they will attain ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of merits and purify ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands...”
With a profound mind spanning billions of nayutas, they lengthen the faculties of bodhisattvas by ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas;
they purify the powers of bodhisattvas by ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas;
they sever ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of asaṃkhyeyas of hindrances; and they transcend ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of asaṃkhyeyas.
Transcending the realm of Māra, they enter ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* Dharma-gates;
they fulfill ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* aids to the Path; they cultivate ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* sublime practices;
and they give rise to ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* great vows.

“Good son! I shall further briefly explain all bodhisattva practices, all bodhisattva perfections, all bodhisattva stages, all bodhisattva patiences, all bodhisattva dharani-doors, all bodhisattva samadhi-doors, all bodhisattva supernormal knowledges and wisdoms, all bodhisattva dedications, and all bodhisattva vows.”

All bodhisattvas who accomplish the Buddha-dharma do so entirely through the power of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); they take the spiritual friend as their root, are born from the spiritual friend, emerge from the spiritual friend, grow by means of the spiritual friend, and abide by means of the spiritual friend; the spiritual friend is the causal condition, and the spiritual friend is able to initiate [the path].

At that time, having heard of such merits of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), which can reveal the immeasurable sublime practices of bodhisattvas and bring to fulfillment the immeasurable, vast, and great Buddha-dharmas, the youth Sudhana leaped for joy with great delight. He prostrated at the feet of Śrīsaṃbhavā and Guṇavatī, circumambulated them countless times, gazed up at them with earnest reverence, and then took his leave and departed.

At that time, having heard the instructions of the spiritual friend, Sudhana’s heart was moistened with joy; reflecting with right mindfulness upon the practices of all bodhisattvas, he set out for the country of Sāgaratīra.
Recalling that in past lives he had not cultivated respectful salutation, he immediately resolved to practice it with diligent effort;
recalling that in past lives his body and mind had been impure, he immediately resolved to focus exclusively on purifying them;
recalling that in past lives he had committed various evil deeds, he immediately resolved to focus exclusively on preventing and severing them.
Furthermore, recollecting how in past lives they gave rise to various delusive thoughts, they immediately resolved to maintain constant and correct contemplation;
recollecting how the practices cultivated in past lives were solely for their own sake, they immediately resolved to expand their minds so that they might reach all sentient beings;

and recollecting how in past lives they pursued objects of desire, constantly wasting themselves away without finding any true flavor, they immediately resolved to practice the Buddha-dharma to nourish their faculties and bring themselves peace and stability.

Furthermore, recollecting how in past lives they gave rise to wrong thoughts associated with perversion, they immediately resolved their minds to give birth to the mind of right view and to arouse the vows of a bodhisattva;
recollecting how in past lives they toiled day and night performing various evil deeds, they immediately resolved their minds to arouse great vigor to accomplish the Buddha-dharma;

and recollecting how in past lives they underwent births in the five destinies which brought no benefit to themselves or others, they immediately resolved their minds to use those very bodies to benefit sentient beings, to accomplish the Buddha-dharma, and to serve all spiritual friends.
Reflecting thus, he gave rise to great joy.

He further contemplated that this body is a dwelling place for the manifold sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death; therefore, he vowed to exhaust the kalpas of the future to cultivate the path of the Bodhisattva and transform sentient beings, to behold all Tathāgatas and achieve the Buddha-dharma, to travel through all Buddha-fields, to serve all Dharma masters, to uphold all Buddha-teachings, to seek out all Dharma companions, to meet all spiritual friends, to gather all the dharmas of the Buddhas, and to act as the causal condition for the bodies of vows and wisdom of all Bodhisattvas.

When he formed this thought, his inconceivable and immeasurable roots of goodness grew long; he immediately conceived deep faith and reverence for all Bodhisattvas, giving rise to the perception of their rarity and the perception of them as Great Teachers.

His faculties became pure and wholesome dharmas increased; he gave rise to respectful offerings to all Bodhisattvas, performed prostrations with palms joined before all Bodhisattvas, produced the perception of all Bodhisattvas as the universal eye that beholds the world, and gave rise to the perception of all Bodhisattvas as those who universally mind all sentient beings.
He manifested the infinite emanation-bodies of the vows of all Bodhisattvas and produced the perception of the pure sounds of praise and discourse of all Bodhisattvas.

They have beheld all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past and present, manifesting the attainment of enlightenment and miraculous transformations in all places, such that there is not even a single hair-tip’s breadth where they do not pervade;
furthermore, they have attained the eye of the light of pure wisdom, seeing the spheres of activity of all Bodhisattvas;
their minds universally enter the net of lands throughout the ten directions, and their vows pervade the void and the Dharma-realm, equal across the three periods of time without ceasing.
All of this was brought about solely by his faithful acceptance of the instructions of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).

With such reverence, such offerings, such praise, such contemplation, such power of aspiration, such reflection, and such immeasurable sphere of wisdom, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself before the Great Tower of Vairocana’s Adorned Treasury, momentarily withdrawing his thoughts to contemplate and observe.

By virtue of profound faith and understanding and the power of great vows, they enter the gate of the equality of the wisdom-body that pervades all places, universally manifesting their bodies before all Tathāgatas, before all bodhisattvas, before all spiritual friends, before all stūpas and temples of the Tathāgatas, before all images of the Tathāgatas, before all dwellings of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas, before all treasures of the Dharma, before all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and their stūpas and temples, before all fields of merit consisting of the noble assembly, before all parents and elders, and before all sentient beings of the ten directions; in all these cases, as previously described, they honor, prostrate to, and praise them, without ceasing until the end of the future.
Equal to space, because it is immeasurable;
equal to the dharma-realm, because it is unobstructed;
equal to the limit of reality, because it pervades all.
They are equal to the Tathāgatas because they are free from discrimination;
they are like reflections because they appear in accordance with wisdom;
they are like dreams because they arise from thought.
It is like a reflection, because it manifests all things;
it is like an echo, because it arises from conditions;
it is without birth, because it undergoes successive emergence and cessation.
They lack inherent nature, for they revolve according to conditions. Furthermore, one definitively knows that all retributions arise from karma;

all fruits arise from causes; all karmas arise from habitual tendencies; the arising of all Buddhas arises from faith; all manifested acts of offering arise entirely from resolute understanding; all transformation Buddhas arise from a heart of reverence; all Buddha-dharmas arise from roots of goodness; all emanation bodies arise from skillful means; all Buddha-activities arise from great vows; all practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas arise from dedication; and the vast adornments of the entire Dharma-realm arise from the sphere of omniscience.
They are free from the view of annihilation because they understand dedication;
they are free from the view of permanence because they understand non-arising;
they are free from the view of causelessness because they understand the true cause.
They are free from the view of inversion because they know the principle of reality as it is;
they are free from the view of a sovereign creator because they know things do not arise through another;
they are free from the view of self and other because they know things arise from conditions.
They are free from the view of clinging to extremes, because they know that the dharma-realm is boundless;
they are free from the view of coming and going, because they know it is like a reflection;
they are free from the view of existence and non-existence, because they know it is neither arising nor ceasing.
They are free from all views of dharmas because they know emptiness and non-arising, because they know the lack of self-mastery, and because they know the production through the power of vows;
they are free from all marks because they see the entry into the limit of the markless.
One knows that all phenomena arise like sprouts from seeds and like impressions from seals;
one knows that substance is like a reflection, sound is like an echo, objects are like dreams, and karma is like an illusion.

Because they understand that the world is a manifestation of the mind; because they understand that effects arise from causes; because they understand the accumulation of retributive karma; and because they understand that all dharmas of merit flow forth from the skillful means of bodhisattvas.
The youth Sudhana entered such wisdom, his mind upright and his thoughts pure;
before the pavilion, he prostrated himself with his entire body, reverently paying homage.
Inconceivable roots of goodness flowed through his body and mind, bringing him refreshing coolness and joyful satisfaction.
Rising from the ground, they gazed up with single-minded devotion, their eyes never wavering for a moment; joining their palms, they circumambulated it for countless circuits, thinking to themselves:
"This great multi-storied pavilion is the dwelling place of those who have realized emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
it is the dwelling place of those who are non-discriminative regarding all phenomena."
This is the dwelling place of those who realize that the dharma-realm is without differentiation;
it is the dwelling place of those who know that all sentient beings are ungraspable;
it is the dwelling place of those who know that all phenomena are unborn.
This is the dwelling place of those who do not cling to anything in the world;
this is the dwelling place of those who do not cling to any cave-dwellings or abodes;
this is the dwelling place of those who take no pleasure in any villages.
This is the dwelling place of those who do not rely on any objective realm;
it is the dwelling place of those who are free from all conceptualization;
it is the dwelling place of those who know that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature.
This is the dwelling place of those who have severed all conceptual activities;
this is the dwelling place of those who are free from all perceptions of mind, intellect, and consciousness;
this is the dwelling place of those who neither enter nor emerge from any path.
This is the dwelling place of those who enter all profound *prajñāpāramitā*;
this is the dwelling place of those who, through skillful means, abide in the universal dharma-realm;
this is the dwelling place of those who extinguish the fires of all afflictions.
Therefore, it is the dwelling place of those who, through superior wisdom, have severed all views, cravings, and conceits;
it is the dwelling place of those who give birth to all meditative concentrations, liberations, samādhis, supernormal powers, and clarities, and sport therein;
it is the dwelling place of those who observe the spheres of all bodhisattva samādhis.
This is the dwelling place of those who abide in the presence of all Tathāgatas;
this is the dwelling place of those who enter a single eon into all eons and all eons into a single eon, yet do not destroy their characteristics;
this is the dwelling place of those who enter a single buddha-field into all buddha-fields and all buddha-fields into a single buddha-field, yet do not destroy their characteristics.

This is the dwelling place of those who, by means of a single dharma, enter into all dharmas, and by means of all dharmas, enter into a single dharma, yet do not destroy their respective characteristics;

this is the dwelling place of those who, by means of a single sentient being, enter into all sentient beings, and by means of all sentient beings, enter into a single sentient being, yet do not destroy their respective characteristics;

this is the dwelling place of those who, by means of a single Buddha, enter into all Buddhas, and by means of all Buddhas, enter into a single Buddha, yet do not destroy their respective characteristics.
This is the dwelling place of those who, in a single thought-moment, know all that exists throughout the three periods of time;
this is the dwelling place of those who, in a single thought-moment, travel to all lands;
this is the dwelling place of those who manifest their bodies before all sentient beings.
This mind is the dwelling place of those who constantly benefit all worlds;
it is the dwelling place of those who are able to reach all places;
it is the dwelling place of those who, though having already transcended all worlds, constantly manifest their bodies therein for the sake of transforming sentient beings.
This is the dwelling place of those who do not cling to any buddha-field, yet travel to all buddha-fields for the sake of making offerings to all Buddhas;
it is the dwelling place of those who remain unmoved from their original location, yet are able to go everywhere to adorn all buddha-fields;
it is the dwelling place of those who draw near to all Buddhas, yet do not give rise to the notion of "Buddha."
This is the dwelling place of those who rely upon all spiritual friends yet do not give rise to the notion of "spiritual friend";
it is the dwelling place of those who reside in all the palaces of Māra yet do not indulge in the realms of desire;
it is the dwelling place of those who have forever abandoned all mental conceptions.
This is the dwelling place of those who, though manifesting their bodies among all sentient beings, do not give rise to dualistic notions of self and other;
it is the dwelling place of those who can universally enter all worlds yet harbor no notion of differentiation within the dharma-realm;
it is the dwelling place of those who vow to abide through all future eons yet harbor no notion of length or brevity regarding those eons.
This is the dwelling place of those who, without departing from the tip of a single hair, universally manifest their bodies in all worlds;
it is the dwelling place of those who can expound the Dharma that is difficult to encounter;

it is the dwelling place of those who abide in the Dharma that is difficult to know, the profound Dharma, the non-dual Dharma, the signless Dharma, the Dharma without antidote, the Dharma without acquisition, and the Dharma without conceptual proliferation.
This is the dwelling place of those who abide in great loving-kindness and great compassion;

it is the dwelling place of those who have already transcended all wisdom of the two vehicles, who have already surpassed all realms of Māra, who are already unstained by worldly dharmas, who have already reached the shore attained by Bodhisattvas, and who have already dwelt in the place where Tathāgatas dwell;

it is the dwelling place of those who, though detached from all marks, do not enter the fixed stage of the Śrāvakas, and who, though they understand that all dharmas are unarisen, do not abide in the nature of non-arising dharmas.

This is the dwelling place of those who, though contemplating impurity, do not realize the state of freedom from greed yet are not accompanied by greed; who, though cultivating loving-kindness, do not realize the state of freedom from hatred yet are not accompanied by the defilement of hatred; who, though contemplating dependent origination, do not realize the state of freedom from delusion yet are not accompanied by the confusion of delusion;

who, though abiding in the four dhyānas, are not reborn according to those meditative states; who, though practicing the four immeasurables, are not born in the form realm for the sake of transforming sentient beings; who, though cultivating the four formless concentrations, do not dwell in the formless realm due to their great compassion;

and who, though diligently practicing tranquility and insight for the sake of transforming sentient beings, do not realize final liberation, and who, though practicing equanimity, do not abandon the work of transforming sentient beings.

This is the dwelling place of those who, though contemplating emptiness, do not give rise to the view of emptiness; who, though practicing signlessness, constantly transform sentient beings attached to signs; and who, though practicing wishlessness, do not abandon the vows and practices for enlightenment.

This is the dwelling place of those who, while attaining mastery amidst all karma and afflictions, manifest compliance with various karmas and afflictions for the sake of transforming sentient beings; who, though free from birth and death, manifest the acceptance of birth and death for the sake of transforming sentient beings; and who, though already detached from all realms of existence, manifest entry into all realms for the sake of transforming sentient beings.

This is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing loving-kindness, harbor no attachment toward sentient beings; who, though practicing compassion, harbor no grasping toward sentient beings; who, though practicing sympathetic joy, constantly regard suffering beings with a heart of pity; and who, though practicing equanimity, do not abandon the work of benefiting others.
This is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing the nine successive meditative attainments, do not weary of taking birth in the desire realm;
who, though knowing that all phenomena are without arising or cessation, do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); and who, though entering the three gates of liberation...
They do not grasp at the liberation of the śrāvakas; though they contemplate the Four Noble Truths, they do not abide in the fruits of the Lesser Vehicle;

though they contemplate profound dependent origination, they do not abide in ultimate quiescence; though they cultivate the Eightfold Noble Path, they do not seek permanent transcendence from the world;
and though they surpass the stage of ordinary beings, they do not fall into the level of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
In the Buddha-ground, although one contemplates the five aggregates of clinging, one does not eternally extinguish these aggregates;
although one transcends the four māras, one does not discriminate among them; although one is unattached to the six sense bases, one does not eternally extinguish them;
although one dwells in true suchness (*tathatā*), one does not fall into the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); and although one teaches all vehicles, one does not abandon the Great Vehicle.
"This great celestial palace is the dwelling place of those who abide in all such virtues as these.
At that time, the youth Sudhana spoke in verse:
"This is the Great Compassionate One of Pure Wisdom, the Honored Maitreya who benefits the world;
the eldest son of the Buddhas within the stage of consecration, he has entered the dwelling place of the Tathāgata’s domain."

All these sons of the Buddhas of universal renown, Having entered the gate of liberation of the Mahāyāna, Wander through the dharma-realm with minds free from attachment; This is the dwelling place of those who are peerless.
Generosity, morality, patience, diligence, meditation, and wisdom, Skillful means, vows, power, and supernormal faculties—
This is the dwelling place of those who are fully endowed with all such Mahāyāna perfections.
Your wisdom is as vast as space, universally knowing all phenomena of the three periods of time;
unimpeded, independent, and without grasping, you thoroughly understand the abodes of all beings.
Skillfully able to understand all phenomena— Devoid of intrinsic nature, devoid of arising, and without dependence;
