Like a bird flying through the sky with sovereign ease— This is the dwelling place of those of great wisdom.

Thoroughly knowing the true nature of the three poisons, And discerning that they arise falsely through causes and conditions, One does not seek liberation out of aversion toward them; This is the dwelling place of those who dwell in tranquility.
The three gates of liberation, the eightfold noble path, The aggregates, bases, elements, and dependent origination—
One who can contemplate all these without falling into quiescence Is the dwelling place of those skilled in means.
The lands and sentient beings of the ten directions, he observes them all with unimpeded wisdom;
realizing that their nature is entirely empty and free from discrimination—this is the dwelling place of the one who abides in quiescence.
Universally traversing the dharma-realm without any obstruction, yet the nature of such practice cannot be apprehended;
like wind moving through space with nowhere to go—this is the dwelling place of those who are without dependence.

Universally beholding the multitudes of beings in the evil realms, Who undergo various torments and have no place of refuge, He emits great rays of compassionate light to utterly extinguish them; This is the dwelling place of the one who feels such pity.
Seeing all sentient beings who have lost the right path, like those born blind treading a perilous road, he leads them into the city of liberation; this is the dwelling place of the Great Guide.

Seeing all sentient beings fallen into the net of Māra, constantly oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, and death, he causes them to attain liberation and find peace; this is the dwelling place of the courageous and steadfast one.
Seeing all sentient beings afflicted by the disease of delusion, he gives rise to a vast heart of compassion;
with the medicine of wisdom, he completely eliminates it—this is the dwelling place of the Great King of Physicians.
Seeing all beings drowning in the ocean of existence, sinking and oppressed by sorrow as they undergo manifold sufferings, he rescues them all with the ship of the Dharma;
this is the dwelling place of the one who brings others safely across.
Seeing all sentient beings within the ocean of delusions, They are able to give rise to the wondrous jewel-mind of bodhicitta;
Entering therein to rescue and deliver them all— This is the dwelling place of the skillful fisherman.
With eyes of great compassion and constant vows, He universally observes all sentient beings;
Drawing them out from the ocean of existence— This is the abode of the Golden-Winged King.
Just as the sun and moon in the sky illuminate the entire world, so too is the radiance of wisdom; this is the dwelling place of those who illumine the world.
For the sake of transforming a single sentient being, a bodhisattva remains throughout all future incalculable eons;
as it is for one person, so it is for all—this is the dwelling place of the Saviors of the World.
Transforming sentient beings within a single land, Without rest throughout all future kalpas;
In every single land it is thus— This is the dwelling place of the firm resolve.
The Dharma taught by all Buddhas of the ten directions, they receive in its entirety while seated upon a single throne;
this shall remain so throughout all future kalpas—this is the dwelling place of those who possess the ocean of wisdom.
Wandering through all oceans of worlds, Universally entering all oceans of sites of enlightenment,
Making offerings to all oceans of Tathāgatas— This is the dwelling place of the practitioner.
Practicing an ocean of all sublime conduct, Arousing an ocean of boundless great vows,
Thus passing through oceans of many eons— This is the dwelling place of those who possess such merit.
Within the tip of a single hair are immeasurable lands; Buddhas, sentient beings, and eons are beyond description.
To clearly perceive all such things without exception—this is the dwelling place of the unimpeded eye.
A single thought universally encompasses boundless eons, The lands, the Buddhas, and all sentient beings;
With unimpeded wisdom, they know all correctly— This is the dwelling place of those endowed with virtue.
If the lands of the ten directions were ground into dust, and all the great oceans were measured by drops from a hair-tip,
even if a bodhisattva made vows numbering as many as these, this would still be the dwelling place of those who are unimpeded.
Having accomplished the gates of dhāraṇī and samādhi, Great vows, all dhyānas, and liberations—
Abiding in each of these for boundless eons, This is the dwelling place of the true sons of the Buddha.
The immeasurable and boundless sons of the Buddhas, Teach various dharmas to deliver sentient beings, And also expound the myriad arts of the world; This is the dwelling place of these practitioners.
Having accomplished the wisdom of skillful means regarding supernormal powers, they practice the wondrous Dharma-gate that is like an illusion;
manifesting births throughout the five destinies of the ten directions—this is the dwelling place of those who are unimpeded.
From the first moment of generating the mind of enlightenment, the Bodhisattva fully practices all deeds;
manifesting countless transformation bodies throughout the Dharma-realm—this is the dwelling place of those possessed of such spiritual power.
In a single thought, they accomplish the path to enlightenment, universally performing boundless deeds of wisdom;
while worldly sentiments and deliberations go mad, this is the dwelling place of those whose measure is unfathomable.
Having accomplished unimpeded supernormal powers, they travel throughout the dharma-realm without exception;
their minds never harbor any notion of attainment—this is the dwelling place of those with pure wisdom.
The Bodhisattva practices unimpeded wisdom, entering all lands without attachment;
with non-dual knowledge he illuminates everywhere—this is the dwelling place of those who are selfless.
Knowing that all phenomena have no basis, Their intrinsic nature is quiescent, like space;
Constantly practicing within such a realm— This is the dwelling place of those free from defilement.
Universally beholding all sentient beings undergoing various sufferings, They give rise to a mind of great compassion, kindness, and wisdom;
Vowing to constantly benefit all worlds—this is the dwelling place of those who possess such pity and mercy.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here appear universally before all sentient beings;
like the orbs of the sun and moon, they everywhere dispel the darkness of birth and death.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here universally accord with the minds of sentient beings.
Manifesting immeasurable bodies, they fill the lands of the ten directions.
Abiding here, the sons of the Buddha travel throughout all worlds,
at the abodes of all Tathāgatas, for immeasurable and innumerable eons.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here contemplate all the Buddha-dharmas;
throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, their minds never grow weary.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here enter samādhi in every thought-moment.
Each and every door of samādhi elucidates the realm of all Buddhas.
Abiding herein, the sons of the Buddha fully know all lands,
immeasurable and innumerable eons, as well as the names of sentient beings and Buddhas.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here, in a single thought-moment, encompass all kalpas;
yet they act solely in accordance with the minds of sentient beings, free from any conceptual discrimination.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here cultivate and practice all samādhis.
Within each and every thought-moment, they thoroughly know the phenomena of the three periods of time.
Abiding here, O Son of the Buddha, with body unmoving in the full lotus posture,
they universally manifest in all lands and within all realms of existence.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here Drink from the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas;
They enter deeply into the ocean of wisdom And are fully endowed with the ocean of merit.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here Know the number of all lands in their entirety.
The number of worlds and the number of sentient beings, And likewise the number of Buddhas' names—
A Son of the Buddha dwelling herein Can comprehend them all in a single thought.
Within all three periods of time, He fully understands the formation and destruction Of all lands throughout the universe.
Buddha-sons dwelling here universally know the Buddha’s practices and vows,
the conduct practiced by Bodhisattvas, and the faculties, natures, and inclinations of all sentient beings.
Buddha-sons dwelling here see within a single mote of dust:
The sites of enlightenment in immeasurable lands, as well as sentient beings and all kalpas, are contained within a single minute atom; so it is with every atom.
All varieties are fully present therein, and everywhere there is no obstruction.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here universally contemplate all phenomena:
sentient beings, lands, and worlds—arisingless and non-existent.
They observe that sentient beings are equal, phenomena are equal, and Tathāgatas are equal.
Buddha-fields, vows, and so forth— All are equal throughout the three periods of time.
The Sons of the Buddha dwelling herein Transform and guide all living beings,
Make offerings to all Tathāgatas, And contemplate the nature of all phenomena.
Throughout immeasurable tens of millions of kalpas, the vows, wisdom, and practices they have cultivated are vast and unfathomable;
even if one were to praise them, one could never exhaust them. Those great heroes and sages act without any obstruction.
Abiding within this state, I join my palms in reverent salutation.
To the eldest son of all Buddhas, the Noble and Virtuous Lord Maitreya;
I now pay homage with devotion—may you deign to look upon me with compassion!

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having praised all the bodhisattvas within the Great Pavilion of Vairocana’s Adorned Treasury with such infinite dharmas of praise and eulogy for bodhisattvas, bowed his body, joined his palms, and prostrated with reverence; with a single-minded resolve, he wished to see Maitreya Bodhisattva and draw near to him to make offerings.

Then he saw Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva coming from another direction, surrounded before and behind by immeasurable kings of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas; by Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors; by immeasurable retinues from his own birthplace; by a multitude of brahmins; and by countless hundreds of thousands of other sentient beings, all approaching together toward the Great Tower of the Treasury of Adornments.
Upon seeing this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he prostrated himself, casting his body to the ground in fivefold homage.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva observed Sudhana and, pointing him out to the great assembly, praised his meritorious virtues and spoke these verses:
“Behold Sudhana, whose wisdom and mind are pure!”
To practice for the sake of seeking Bodhi, you have come to my presence.
Welcome, O you of perfect loving-kindness; welcome, O you of pure compassion;
welcome, O you with eyes of quiescence, who practice without weariness.
Welcome, O one of pure intent; welcome, O one of vast mind.
Welcome, O one with non-regressing faculties, who practices without weariness.
Welcome, O one of unshakable conduct, who ever seeks out virtuous friends.
Thoroughly comprehending all phenomena, you tame all sentient beings.
Welcome to those who practice the wondrous path; welcome to those who abide in merit;
welcome to those who advance toward the fruit of Buddhahood, never experiencing weariness.
Welcome, you whose essence is virtue; welcome, nourished by the Dharma;
welcome, with boundless conduct, difficult for the world to behold.
Welcome, free from delusion, whom worldly dharmas cannot defile.
Regarding gain and loss, defamation and praise, and all such things, they remain entirely without discrimination.
Welcome with the bestowing of peace and happiness; gentle and pliant, they are fit to receive transformation.
Deceit, guile, anger, and pride—their minds have entirely extinguished them all.
Welcome, true son of the Buddha! You travel everywhere throughout the ten directions, increasing all merits with a mind that is gentle, supple, and free from weariness.
Welcome, you who possess the wisdom of the three times, knowing all phenomena thoroughly.
Universally giving birth to a treasury of merit, practicing without weariness or fatigue—
Mañjuśrī, Guṇamegha, and all other sons of the Buddhas—
have brought you to my presence and shown you the realm of non-obstruction.
Fully cultivating the bodhisattva practices, universally gathering in all living beings—
such a person of vast capacity has now come to my presence.
Seeking the pure realm of all Tathāgatas, they have arrived.
I ask why you have come to my presence with such vast aspirations.
You have come to my presence because you wish to practice and learn all the deeds and activities accomplished by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
Since you have come to me, desiring the subtle and wondrous Dharma from a spiritual friend and wishing to receive the bodhisattva practices,
you should keep in mind that spiritual friends are praised by all Buddhas.
Causing you to attain enlightenment, you have come to my presence.
You remember your spiritual friend, who gave birth to me like a father or mother and nurtured me like a nurse, increasing my factors of enlightenment.
Like a physician who treats all ailments, like the heavens showering down nectar,
like the sun revealing the true path, like the moon turning its pure wheel,
like a mountain that does not waver, and like the ocean that neither increases nor decreases.
Like a ferryman who brings others across, he has come to where I am.
Behold the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra): they are like a great and valiant general, like a great caravan leader, and also like a great guide.
It can raise the banner of the True Dharma; It can manifest the virtues of the Buddhas;
It can extinguish all evil realms; It can open the gates to the happy destinies;
It can reveal the bodies of all Buddhas; It can preserve the treasuries of all Buddhas.
Able to uphold all the Buddha-dharmas, for this reason I pray that you will look upon and serve me.
Desiring to fulfill pure wisdom, desiring to possess a handsome body,
and desiring to be born into a noble family, you have come to my presence.
"You all should observe this person: having drawn near to a spiritual friend, you should practice everything in accordance with what they have cultivated and studied.
By the causal conditions of past merit, Mañjuśrī has caused him to resolve his mind [upon enlightenment]."
Following them without opposition, practicing with tireless diligence;
abandoning parents, relatives, palaces, and wealth— all of these—
and seeking out wise teachers with humility.
Having purified the mind in this way, forever leaving behind the worldly body,
one shall be born in the Buddha-lands and receive all supreme karmic fruits.
When Sudhana beholds sentient beings suffering from birth, old age, sickness, and death, he [sees them]...
To give rise to the mind of great compassion, he diligently cultivates the unsurpassed path.
Seeing sentient beings constantly transmigrating through the five realms,
Sudhana seeks adamantine wisdom to shatter the wheel of their various sufferings.
Sudhana beheld sentient beings whose mental fields were utterly overgrown and defiled;
to remove the thorns of the three poisons, he sought exclusively the plow of sharp wisdom.
Sentient beings dwell in the darkness of ignorance, blind and lost on the right path.
Sudhana acts as the guide, showing them the place of peace and security.
With the armor of patience and the vehicle of liberation, and with wisdom as his sharp sword,
he is able to destroy the thieves of affliction within the three realms of existence.
Sudhana, the Master of the Dharma-ship, universally rescues all sentient beings,
causing them to cross the ocean of ignorance and swiftly reach the Isle of Pure Jewels.
Sudhana, the Sun of Perfect Enlightenment, possesses the wheel of great vows and the light of wisdom.
Traversing the emptiness of the dharma-realm, he universally illuminates the abodes of the deluded masses.
The moon of Sudhana’s perfect enlightenment has its white dharmas fully perfected;
with the cool light of his compassionate concentration, it shines equally upon the minds of all sentient beings.
Sudhana’s ocean of supreme wisdom Abides in reliance upon the straightforward mind;
As his bodhisattva practices gradually deepen, He gives birth to the myriad jewels of the Dharma.
Sudhana, the great-hearted dragon, Ascends into the void of the Dharma-realm.
Raising clouds and pouring down sweet rain, it brings all fruits to fruition.
So too does Sudhana kindle the lamp of Dharma: faith is the wick, compassion the oil, mindfulness the vessel, and merit the light;
together they extinguish the darkness of the three poisons.
The awakening mind is the embryo, compassion the chorion, and loving-kindness the flesh;
the factors of enlightenment are the limbs and joints, growing within the Tathāgatagarbha.
It increases the treasury of merit and the treasury of pure wisdom.
Revealing the treasury of skillful means, Giving birth to the treasury of great vows;
Such magnificent adornments as these Rescue and protect all living beings;
Among all devas and humans, They are difficult to hear and difficult to see.
Such is the tree of wisdom, its roots so deep it cannot be shaken;
as all practices gradually increase, it provides universal shade for all living beings.
Desiring to give birth to all virtues, desiring to inquire into all dharmas—
Wishing to sever all doubts, one should single-mindedly seek a virtuous friend (kalyāṇamitra).
Wishing to shatter the demons of delusion, wishing to remove the stains of various views,
and wishing to untie the bonds of sentient beings, one should single-mindedly seek a virtuous friend.
One shall extinguish all evil realms, And show the path to humans and devas;
Causing them to cultivate meritorious deeds, They shall swiftly enter the city of Nirvāṇa.
One shall deliver others from the perils of views, And sever the net of all views.
One shall dry up the waters of craving and desire; one shall show the way of the three realms of existence.
One shall become a refuge for the world, one shall become the light of the world, and one shall become the teacher of the three worlds, pointing out the place of liberation.
I shall also cause the world to universally abandon all conceptual attachments,
universally awaken from the sleep of afflictions, and universally emerge from the mire of craving and desire.
I shall thoroughly understand all diverse phenomena and purify all diverse buddha-fields.
All shall reach ultimate perfection, and their hearts will be filled with great joy.
Your conduct is exceedingly gentle and supple; your mind is profoundly pure.
Whatever merits you wish to cultivate shall all be brought to fulfillment.
Before long they shall behold all Buddhas, Thoroughly comprehend all dharmas,
Adorn and purify the oceans of lands, And achieve great Bodhi.
They shall fulfill the ocean of all practices, And they shall know the ocean of all dharmas.
When crossing the ocean of sentient beings, one should thus cultivate all practices;
when reaching the shore of merit, one should give rise to all wholesome qualities;
being equal to the sons of the Buddha, one’s mind shall be thus resolved.
One shall sever all delusions, purify all karma,
and subdue all māras, fulfilling such vows as these.
One shall give rise to the path of wondrous wisdom and open the path of the True Dharma.
Before long you shall abandon the path of afflictions, karma, and all sufferings.
All sentient beings revolve upon the wheel of existence, mired and lost within the wheel of the realms of being;
you must turn the Wheel of Dharma so that they may sever the wheel of suffering.
You shall uphold the seed of the Buddha; you shall purify the seed of the Dharma;
you are able to gather the seed of the Saṅgha, pervading all throughout the three periods of time.
You shall sever the net of manifold cravings; you shall tear asunder the net of manifold views.
I shall rescue the net of all sufferings; I shall fulfill this net of vows.
I shall deliver the realm of sentient beings; I shall purify the realm of the land.
I shall gather the realm of wisdom; I shall perfect this realm of the mind.
One should cause sentient beings to rejoice, one should cause bodhisattvas to rejoice, and one should cause all buddhas to rejoice; thus shall this joy be accomplished.
One shall see all realms of existence, and one shall see all buddha-fields.
One should see all phenomena; one shall attain this vision of a Buddha.
One shall emit light that shatters darkness, light that extinguishes heat, and light that destroys evil, thereby washing away the suffering of the three realms of existence.
One shall open the gate to the heavenly realms; one shall open the gate to the Buddha-way;
one shall show the gate of liberation, so that all sentient beings may enter.
One shall demonstrate the true path and sever the paths of evil.
Practicing diligently in this way, one accomplishes the path to enlightenment.
One should cultivate an ocean of merit; one should cross the ocean of the three realms of existence;
and one should cause the ocean of all living beings to emerge from the ocean of manifold sufferings.
Within the ocean of sentient beings, you shall dry up the ocean of afflictions, cause them to cultivate the ocean of all practices, and swiftly enter the ocean of great wisdom.
You shall increase the ocean of wisdom; you shall cultivate the ocean of practice.
The ocean of great vows of all Buddhas, you shall fulfill them all.
You shall enter the ocean of lands; you shall contemplate the ocean of phenomena;
and by the power of your wisdom, you shall drink deeply from the ocean of all dharmas.
One shall behold clouds of Buddhas; one shall raise clouds of offerings;
one shall hear clouds of the sublime Dharma; one shall give rise to clouds of these vows.
One shall travel everywhere through the chambers of the three realms of existence; one shall universally destroy the chambers of all delusions.
Universally entering the chamber of the Tathāgata, one should practice this path.
Universally entering the gates of samādhi, universally roaming through the gates of liberation,
and universally abiding in the gates of supernormal powers, one travels throughout the entire dharma-realm.
Manifesting universally before all sentient beings, Facing all Buddhas everywhere,
Like the light of the sun and moon, May I accomplish such power.
My conduct shall be free from agitation, My conduct shall be free from attachment.
Like a bird traversing the void, you shall accomplish this wondrous function.
Like Indra’s net, the network of lands abides in such a manner;
you should go to them all, unimpeded like the wind.
You shall enter the Dharma-realm, Go everywhere throughout all worlds,
Universally behold the Buddhas of the three periods of time, And give rise to great joy in your heart.
Regarding all dharma-gates, Those you have already attained and those you shall attain—
You should give rise to great joy, neither greedy nor weary.
You are a vessel of merit, able to follow the teachings of all Buddhas;
being able to cultivate the bodhisattva practices, you have been able to behold this marvel.
Thus, these sons of the Buddhas are difficult to encounter even in hundreds of millions of eons;
how much more so to behold their merits and the sublime paths they have cultivated!
You were born among human beings and have greatly attained all manner of wholesome benefits.

Having beheld Mañjuśrī and others, And their immeasurable virtues, You have already left behind all evil realms, You have already emerged from all places of peril, And you have already transcended all suffering and affliction; Excellent! Do not be indolent.
Having already left the stage of ordinary beings, And having already dwelled in the stages of bodhisattvas, One shall fulfill the stage of wisdom And swiftly enter the stage of the Tathāgata.
The conduct of the bodhisattva is like the ocean; The Buddha’s wisdom is equal to space.
Your aspiration is likewise so; you should give rise to great joy and celebration.
With your faculties untiring and your resolve ever firm, by drawing near to virtuous friends, you will before long fulfill it all.
The various practices of Bodhisattvas are all for the sake of taming sentient beings;
they universally practice all Dharma-gates—be careful not to give rise to doubt or confusion.
You possess inconceivable merit as well as true faith.
Therefore, on this very day, you have been able to behold these sons of the Buddhas.
By beholding these sons of the Buddhas, you shall all obtain vast and great benefits;
every one of their great vows, you shall all believe and accept.
Since you are able to cultivate the bodhisattva practices within the three realms of existence,
all the sons of the Buddha have shown you the gate of liberation.
One who is not a vessel for the Dharma, even if dwelling together with the sons of the Buddha—
Even if one were to pass through immeasurable eons, One could never know its realm.
That you have seen these bodhisattvas And been able to hear such a Dharma— This is exceedingly rare in the world;
You should give rise to great joy and celebration.
The Buddhas protect and mind you; the Bodhisattvas embrace and sustain you.
Being able to practice in accordance with their teachings, well done, O one who abides in this life!
You have already been born into the family of Bodhisattvas; you have already perfected the virtues of a Bodhisattva.
Having already grown the seed of the Tathāgata, you shall soon ascend to the rank of consecration.
Before long, you shall become equal to the sons of the Buddhas;
seeing sentient beings in suffering, you shall place them all in a state of peace and security.
As the seed is sown, so shall the fruit be obtained;
I now congratulate and comfort you—you should be greatly rejoiced.
Immeasurable bodhisattvas have practiced the Way for immeasurable eons.
Unable to accomplish this practice, you have now attained it all.
Through the power of firm resolve and joyful faith, Sudhana has perfected this path;
if anyone possesses a heart of reverence and admiration, they too should train in this way.
All practices of merit and virtue arise from aspiration and desire;
Sudhana has already understood this, and he constantly delights in diligent cultivation.
Just as a dragon spreads dense clouds, it will surely pour down a great rain.
When a Bodhisattva gives rise to the wisdom of aspiration, they resolutely cultivate all practices.
If there is a spiritual friend who shows you the conduct of Samantabhadra,
you should serve them well and be careful not to give rise to doubt.
Throughout immeasurable eons, you have recklessly sacrificed your body out of desire;
now, seeking enlightenment, this sacrifice is truly virtuous.
Throughout immeasurable eons, you have fully endured the sufferings of birth and death.
Never having served the Buddhas, you have not yet heard of such a practice.
Now that you have obtained a human body and encountered a Buddha as a spiritual friend, you hear and receive these practices for awakening; how could you not rejoice?
Though one may encounter the appearance of a Buddha in the world and meet with virtuous friends,
if one’s mind is not pure, one shall not hear such a Dharma. But if one has faith, joy,
and a heart of reverence toward virtuous friends, [one shall hear it].
Free from doubt and without weariness, one then hears such a Dharma as this.
If there are those who hear this Dharma and give rise to the mind of aspiration,
you should know that such persons have already attained vast and great benefit.
With such purity of mind, one shall always draw near to all Buddhas and likewise to all Bodhisattvas, and will certainly attain enlightenment.
If one enters this Dharma-gate, one will be endowed with all meritorious virtues.
Forever free from all evil realms, one shall not undergo any suffering.
Before long, casting off this body, one will be reborn in a Buddha-land,
where one constantly beholds the Buddhas of the ten directions as well as all the Bodhisattvas.
Through past causes and present pure understanding, And by the power of associating with virtuous friends,
All merits increase, Like lotuses growing in the water.
Delighting in serving spiritual friends, One diligently makes offerings to all Buddhas.
Listen to the Dharma with single-minded focus, And always practice without weariness.
You are a true vessel for the Dharma; You shall possess all dharmas, You shall cultivate all paths, And you shall fulfill all vows.
With a mind of faith and resolve, you have come to pay homage to me;
before long, you shall universally enter the assemblies of all Buddhas.
Excellent, true son of the Buddha, you who revere all Buddhas!
Before long, you shall fulfill all practices And reach the shore of the Buddha’s merits.
You should go to the one of great wisdom, Mañjuśrī;
he shall cause you to attain The profound and wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, standing before the assembled multitude, extolled the great treasury of merit of Sudhana.
Upon hearing this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; the hairs on his body stood on end, and he wept with choked sobs.
Rising to his feet, he joined his palms, gazed up at him with reverence, and circumambulated him countless times.
By the power of Mañjuśrī’s mental resolve, various flowers, necklaces, and diverse wonderful jewels suddenly filled his hands without him even realizing it;
filled with joy, Sudhana immediately offered them, scattering them over the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya.
Then, Maitreya Bodhisattva placed his hand upon Sudhana’s head and spoke these verses for him:
“Excellent, excellent, true son of the Buddha!
You universally exert all your faculties without weariness; Before long you shall be endowed with all virtues, Just like Mañjuśrī and myself.”
Then, the youth Sudhana replied in verse:
“I contemplate spiritual friends, Whom it is difficult to encounter even in billions of eons;
Having now been able to draw near to them all, I have come to your presence, O Venerable One.”
"Because of Mañjuśrī, I have been able to see those who are difficult to behold;
may I soon behold that Honored One of Great Merit once again.
*The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha’s Great Extensive Teachings*, Fascicle Seventy-Seven.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Seventy-Eight,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree,
Part Nineteen of Chapter Thirty-Nine: Entering the Dharma Realm.
At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in reverence and addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva once more, saying:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practices."
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path? 'O Great Sage!
All Tathāgatas have bestowed upon the Venerable One the prediction that in one more life he shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.'"
If one is to attain unsurpassed bodhi in a single lifetime, then one has already transcended all the dwelling places of bodhisattvas;
one has already surpassed all bodhisattva stages of the state beyond birth; one has already fulfilled all the pāramitās;
one has already deeply entered all the gates of patience; and one has already perfected everything.
As for the Bodhisattva stage, one has already sported in all doors of liberation,
already accomplished all dharmas of samādhi, already attained mastery over all bodhisattva practices,
already realized all dhāraṇīs and eloquence, and already attained sovereignty within all the sovereignties of bodhisattvas.
Then they have already accumulated all the factors conducive to enlightenment of a bodhisattva; they have already sported in wisdom and skillful means;
they have already brought forth the knowledge of great supernormal powers; they have already accomplished all the precepts of training;
they have already perfected all sublime conduct; they have already fulfilled all great vows; and they have already...
Having received the predictions of all Buddhas, they have already fully understood the gateways of all vehicles;
they have already become worthy of being protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas; they have already been able to encompass the Bodhi of all Buddhas;
they have already been able to uphold the treasury of the Dharma of all Buddhas; and they have already been able to sustain all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
As for the Secret Treasury, you have already become the foremost among all the assemblies of bodhisattvas;

you have already become a great heroic general capable of destroying the army of the māra of afflictions; you have already become a great guide capable of leading others out of the wilderness of birth and death;
you have already become a great King of Physicians capable of treating the grave illnesses of all delusions; you have already...
Among all sentient beings, one is the most supreme; one has already attained mastery among all lords of the world;

one has already become the foremost among all noble ones; one has already become the most preeminent among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; and one has [already crossed] the ocean of birth and death.
As a master mariner, he has already been able to cast the net for taming all sentient beings;
he has already been able to observe the faculties of all sentient beings; he has already been able to encompass the realms of all sentient beings;
he has already been able to protect the assembly of all bodhisattvas; he has already been able to discourse upon all bodhisattva matters; he has already...
One who is able to go to the abodes of all Tathāgatas has already been able to dwell in the assemblies of all Tathāgatas;
has already been able to manifest their bodies before all sentient beings; has already been able to remain unstained by any worldly dharmas;
has already been able to transcend all realms of Māra; and has already been able to abide in the One.
Having reached the realm of all Buddhas, one has already attained the unimpeded state of all Bodhisattvas;
one has already been able to diligently make offerings to all Buddhas; one’s essential nature has become identical with that of all Buddha-dharmas;
one has already bound the silken ribbon of the sublime Dharma; one has already received the Buddha-consecration; one has already dwelt in omniscience; and one has already been able to...
They universally give birth to all Buddha-dharmas and are already able to swiftly tread upon the stage of omniscience.
"O Great Sage! How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct?"

How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path? By practicing and training accordingly, one swiftly attains the fulfillment of all Buddha-dharmas; one is able to deliver and liberate all sentient beings as they are contemplated; one is universally able to bring to completion all great vows that have been made; one is universally able to bring to ultimate perfection all practices that have been initiated; one is universally able to comfort all devas and humans; one does not fail oneself; one does not sever the Three Jewels; one does not render void the lineage of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; and one is able to uphold the Dharma-eye of all Buddhas.
"May you please explain all such matters as these!
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya surveyed the entire assembly at the site of enlightenment, pointed toward Sudhana, and spoke these words:
"O virtuous ones!
"Do you see this son of a householder, who is now inquiring of me regarding the various merits of the bodhisattva conduct?
O virtuous ones!
This son of a householder is courageous and diligent; his aspirations are unadulterated, his profound mind is firm, and he never regresses."
Possessing supreme aspiration, they act as if their heads were on fire, never feeling satiated;
they delight in spiritual friends, drawing near to and making offerings to them, seeking them out everywhere, serving them, and requesting the Dharma.
"O virtuous ones!

This son of a householder, having previously received the instructions of Mañjuśrī in the City of Blessings, traveled southward in succession to seek spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). After passing through one hundred and ten spiritual friends, he has finally come to my presence, never for a moment giving rise to a thought of weariness or indolence."

"O worthy ones! This son of a householder is truly rare to encounter; he has set out upon the Great Vehicle, mounted on great wisdom, and has aroused great valor. He has donned the armor of great compassion, protects sentient beings with a heart of great kindness, and initiates the practice of the perfection of great diligence. Acting as a great caravan leader, he protects all sentient beings; serving as a great Dharma-ship, he ferries others across the ocean of existence. Abiding in the Great Path, he gathers the great treasures of the Dharma and cultivates all vast dharmas that assist the path.
Such a person is difficult to hear of, difficult to see, and difficult to approach, dwell with, or travel alongside."

Why is this? Because this son of a householder has resolved to rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing them to be liberated from all sufferings, to transcend all evil destinies, to leave behind all perils and difficulties, to shatter the darkness of ignorance, to emerge from the wilderness of birth and death, to bring rest to the wheel of the various realms of existence, to cross beyond the realm of Māra, to remain unattached to worldly dharmas, to emerge from the mire of desire, to sever the yoke of greed, to untie the bonds of views, to demolish the house of conceptualization, to cut off the path of delusion, to topple the banner of pride, to extract the arrows of confusion, to dispel the cover of sleep, to tear the net of craving, to extinguish ignorance, to cross the stream of existence, to depart from flattery and illusion, to purify the stains of the mind, to sever delusive confusion, and to emerge from birth and death.
"O virtuous ones! This son of a householder has constructed a great Dharma-ship for those drifting upon the four currents;
he has established a great Dharma-bridge for those submerged in the mire of views."
For those who are stupefied and deluded by the darkness of ignorance, he kindles the great lamp of wisdom;
for those wandering through the wilderness of birth and death, he reveals the Noble Path;
and for those afflicted by the grave illness of the afflictions, he prepares the medicinal elixir of the Dharma.
For those who encounter the sufferings of birth, old age, and death, he gives them the nectar of immortality to bring them peace and security;
for those who have entered the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion, he pours upon them the water of meditative concentration to make them cool and refreshed;
and for those with much anxiety and affliction, he comforts and exhorts them to find tranquility.
For those bound in the prison of existence, they instruct and exhort them so that they may emerge;
for those caught in the net of views, they open it with the sword of wisdom;
for those dwelling in the city of the realms, they show them the gates of liberation.
For those in peril, he guides them to a place of peace;
for those who fear the thieves of the fetters, he bestows the Dharma of fearlessness;
for those fallen into evil destinies, he extends the hand of compassion.
To those afflicted by the aggregates, he shows the city of Nirvāṇa;
for those entwined by the serpents of the elements, he liberates them through the Noble Path;
and for those attached to the empty village of the six sense-bases, he draws them out with the light of wisdom.
For those dwelling in wrong deliverance, they cause them to enter right deliverance;
for those who associate with evil friends, they show them virtuous friends;
for those who delight in mundane dharmas, they instruct them in the noble Dharma.
For those attached to birth and death, he causes them to enter the city of omniscience.

"O noble ones! This son of a householder constantly protects sentient beings through such practices; he has never ceased in his resolve for bodhicitta, never grown weary in seeking the Mahāyāna path, and never feels satiated in drinking the water of all dharmas. He always diligently accumulates the practices that assist the path, constantly delights in purifying all dharma-gates, and cultivates the conduct of a bodhisattva without abandoning diligence. He fulfills all vows through skillful means and, upon seeing spiritual friends, never tires of doing so; in serving spiritual friends, his body never grows fatigued; and hearing all the instructions of spiritual friends, he always delights in practicing in accordance with them, never once contravening them."
"O worthy ones! If there are sentient beings who are able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, this is rare;
if, having resolved their minds, they are furthermore able to thus apply themselves with diligence and skillful means to gather all the Buddha-dharmas, it is doubly rare."

Furthermore, one who can thus seek the bodhisattva path; who can thus purify bodhisattva conduct; who can thus serve spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); who can thus act with the urgency of one whose hair is on fire; who can thus comply with the instructions of spiritual friends; who can thus practice with firm resolve; who can thus accumulate the factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*); who can thus not seek any fame or gain; who can thus not abandon the singular, pure mind of a bodhisattva; who can thus take no pleasure in home life, have no attachment to sensual desires, and feel no longing for parents, relatives, or acquaintances, but instead delights only in seeking companions for the bodhisattva path; and who can thus disregard body and life, wishing only to diligently cultivate the path to omniscience—such a person should be known as increasingly more difficult to find than the former.

"O virtuous ones! While other bodhisattvas must pass through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of eons before they can fulfill the vows and practices of a bodhisattva, and before they can draw near to the enlightenment of all Buddhas;

this son of a householder, within a single lifetime, is able to purify Buddha-fields, is able to transform sentient beings, is able to penetrate the Dharma-realm with wisdom, is able to accomplish all the pāramitās, is able to expand all practices, is able to fulfill all great vows, is able to transcend all demonic activities, is able to serve all spiritual friends, is able to purify all bodhisattva paths, and is able to be fully endowed with all the practices of Samantabhadra."

At that time, after Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva had thus praised the various merits of the youth Sudhana and caused immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to resolve upon Bodhicitta, he addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!

"Good son! It is for the benefit of all the world, for the protection and deliverance of all sentient beings, and for the diligent seeking of all Buddha-dharmas that you have resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

“Good son! You have gained a sublime benefit; you have well obtained a human body; you have well sustained your life-span; you have well encountered the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world; and you have well beheld Mañjuśrī, the great spiritual friend.”
Your body is a vessel of goodness, moistened by all roots of virtue.

You are sustained by the support of pure dharmas; your understanding and aspirations are entirely purified; you are protected and remembered by all Buddhas, and you are embraced by all spiritual friends.
Why is this? "Good son! The bodhicitta is like a seed, for it is able to give birth to all the dharmas of the Buddhas."
The bodhicitta is like a fertile field, for it can cause the pure and white dharmas of sentient beings to grow;
the bodhicitta is like the great earth, for it can support all worlds;
the bodhicitta is like pure water, for it can wash away the stains of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like a great wind, for it is unimpeded throughout the entire world;
the bodhicitta is like a blazing fire, for it can burn away the fuel of all views;
the bodhicitta is like the pure sun, for it universally illuminates all worlds.
The bodhicitta is like the full moon, for all pure and white dharmas are therein perfected;
the bodhicitta is like a bright lamp, for it can radiate the manifold light of the Dharma;
the bodhicitta is like a clear eye, for it universally perceives all places of safety and peril.
The bodhicitta is like a great highway, for it enables all to enter the city of great wisdom;
the bodhicitta is like a correct ferry, for it causes one to leave behind all erroneous dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a great vehicle, for it is universally able to transport all bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like a gateway, for it reveals all the practices of a bodhisattva;
the bodhicitta is like a palace, for it provides a dwelling place for the cultivation of samādhi;
the bodhicitta is like a garden, for within it one sports and experiences the joy of the Dharma.
The bodhicitta is like a dwelling, for it provides security for all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is a place of refuge, for it benefits all worlds;
the bodhicitta is a basis of reliance, for it is the foundation upon which all bodhisattva practices depend.
The bodhicitta is like a compassionate father, for it instructs and guides all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like a compassionate mother, for it gives birth to and nurtures all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like a wet nurse, for it nourishes and sustains all bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like a virtuous friend, for it brings benefit and fulfillment to all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like a sovereign, for it surpasses all those of the two vehicles;
the bodhicitta is like a universal monarch, for it attains mastery over all aspirations.
The bodhicitta is like the great ocean, for all merits enter into it;
the bodhicitta is like Mount Sumeru, for its mind is impartial toward all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like the Iron Ring Mountains, for it sustains all worlds.
The bodhicitta is like the Snowy Mountains, for it nurtures all medicinal herbs of wisdom;
the bodhicitta is like the Fragrant Mountain, for it gives birth to the fragrance of all meritorious virtues;
the bodhicitta is like space, for its various sublime virtues are vast and boundless.
The bodhicitta is like a lotus flower, for it is unstained by any worldly phenomena;
the bodhicitta is like a well-trained elephant, for its mind is gentle and compliant rather than wild or unruly;
the bodhicitta is like a noble steed, for it is far removed from all evil dispositions.
The bodhicitta is like a charioteer, for it protects all the teachings of the Mahāyāna;
the bodhicitta is like an efficacious medicine, for it can cure the disease of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a pitfall, for it causes all unwholesome dharmas to fall into ruin.
The bodhicitta is like a vajra, for it is able to pierce through all phenomena;
the bodhicitta is like a casket of incense, for it can store the fragrance of all merits;
the bodhicitta is like a wondrous flower, for it is joyfully beheld by all the world.
The bodhicitta is like white sandalwood, for it removes the heat of all desires and brings about coolness;
the bodhicitta is like black agarwood, for it can permeate the entire dharma-realm pervasively;
the bodhicitta is like the king of medicines, Sudarśana, for it can destroy the disease of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like the vigama medicine, for it can extract all arrows of affliction;
the bodhicitta is like Śakra, for it is the most honored among all lords;
the bodhicitta is like Vaiśravaṇa, for it can sever all suffering of poverty.
The bodhicitta is like the goddess Puṇyavatī, for it is adorned with all merits;
the bodhicitta is like an ornament, for it adorns all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like the fire at the end of an eon, for it can incinerate all conditioned phenomena.
The bodhicitta is like a rootless medicinal herb, for it nurtures and grows all the qualities of a Buddha;
the bodhicitta is like a dragon’s pearl, for it can neutralize the poison of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a water-purifying jewel, for it can clarify the turbidity of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like a wish-fulfilling gem, for it provides for all who are destitute;
the bodhicitta is like a vase of merit, for it satisfies the hearts of all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like a wish-fulfilling tree, for it can rain down all manner of ornaments.
The bodhicitta is like a garment of swan feathers, for it is not defiled by any of the impurities of birth and death;
the bodhicitta is like white cotton thread, for its nature has been pure from the very beginning;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp plow, for it can cultivate the fields of all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is like Nārāyaṇa, for it can crush all enemies that are views of self;
the bodhicitta is like a swift arrow, for it can pierce through all sufferings;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp spear, for it can penetrate the armor of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like sturdy armor, for it can protect all minds that accord with reality;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp blade, for it can sever the heads of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a keen sword, for it can cut through the armor of all pride.
The bodhicitta is like the banner of a valiant general, for it can subdue all the armies of Māra;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp saw, for it can cut down the tree of ignorance;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp axe, for it can fell the trees of all suffering.
The bodhicitta is like armor, for it can ward off all hardships and sufferings;
the bodhicitta is like skillful hands, for it protects and guards the body of all perfections (pāramitās);
the bodhicitta is like excellent feet, for it establishes all roots of merit.
The bodhicitta is like medicinal ointment for the eyes, for it eliminates all cataracts of ignorance;
the bodhicitta is like tweezers, for it can extract the thorns of the view of a self-identity;
the bodhicitta is like bedding, for it brings rest to and alleviates all the weariness and suffering of birth and death.
The bodhicitta is like a spiritual friend, for it can untie all the bonds of birth and death;
the bodhicitta is like excellent treasure, for it can eliminate all states of poverty;
the bodhicitta is like a great guide, for it well knows the path of transcendence for bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure, for it brings forth the wealth of merit without exhaustion;
the bodhicitta is like a gushing spring, for it produces the waters of wisdom without end;
the bodhicitta is like a clear mirror, for it universally manifests the images of all dharma-gates.
The bodhicitta is like a lotus flower, for it is unstained by any defilement of sin;
the bodhicitta is like a great river, for it flows to lead forth and encompass all dharmas of deliverance;
the bodhicitta is like a great dragon king, for it can rain down the rain of all sublime dharmas.
The bodhicitta is like the life-faculty, for it sustains the body of the Bodhisattva’s great compassion;
the bodhicitta is like nectar, for it enables one to abide in the realm of the deathless;
the bodhicitta is like a great net, for it universally gathers in all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is like a lasso, for it gathers in all those who are to be transformed;
the bodhicitta is like a hook and bait, for it draws forth those dwelling within the abyss of existence;
the bodhicitta is like the agada medicine, for it can bring about illness-free and eternal peace.
The bodhicitta is like an antidote that neutralizes poison, for it can completely eliminate the poison of craving;
the bodhicitta is like a well-uttered mantra, for it can remove the poison of all perversions;
the bodhicitta is like a swift wind, for it can sweep away the mists of all obstacles.
The bodhicitta is like a great island of jewels, for it gives birth to all the jewels of the factors of enlightenment;
the bodhicitta is like a noble lineage, for it gives birth to all pure and white dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a dwelling, for it is the locus upon which all qualities of merit depend.
The bodhicitta is like a marketplace, for it is the place where the Bodhisattva-merchants conduct their trade;
the bodhicitta is like an alchemical elixir, for it can purify the defilements of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like fine honey, for it perfects the flavor of all meritorious qualities.
The bodhicitta is like a correct path, for it causes all bodhisattvas to enter the city of wisdom;
the bodhicitta is like an excellent vessel, for it can hold all pure and white dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like seasonal rain, for it can extinguish the dust of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is a dwelling place, for it is the abode where all bodhisattvas reside;
the bodhicitta is the life-force, for it does not grasp at the fruit of liberation of the śrāvakas;
the bodhicitta is like pure lapis lazuli, for its intrinsic nature is luminously pure and free from all defilements.
The bodhicitta is like the sapphire (*indranīla*), for it transcends the worldly wisdom of the two vehicles;
the bodhicitta is like the drum that signals the night watch, for it awakens all sentient beings from the sleep of afflictions (*kleśa*);
the bodhicitta is like pure water, for its nature is fundamentally clear and stainless, free from turbidity.
The bodhicitta is like Jāmbūnada gold, for it outshines all conditioned virtues;
the bodhicitta is like the king of great mountains, for it rises above all worlds;
the bodhicitta is that which provides refuge, for it does not reject any who come to it.
The bodhicitta is beneficial, for it can eliminate all causes of decline and affliction;
the bodhicitta is a sublime jewel, for it can cause all minds to rejoice;
the bodhicitta is like a great assembly of giving, for it fills the hearts of all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is supreme and exalted, for no mind among sentient beings can equal it;
the bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure, for it can encompass all the teachings of the Buddhas;
the bodhicitta is like Indra’s net, for it can subdue the asuras of the afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like the wind of Varuṇa, for it can move all those who are to be transformed;
the bodhicitta is like the fire of Indra, for it can burn away all afflictions and habitual tendencies;
the bodhicitta is like a stūpa of the Buddha, for it should be venerated by all the world.
“Good son! The bodhicitta accomplishes such immeasurable merits;
to state it briefly, you should know that it is entirely equal to all the merits of the Buddha-dharmas.”
Why is this? Because all bodhisattva practices arise from the bodhicitta, and because the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time are born from the bodhicitta.
Therefore, good son! If there are those who resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they have already produced immeasurable merit and are universally able to embrace the path to all-knowledge.
“Good son! It is like a person who, having obtained the medicine of fearlessness, is freed from five terrors. What are these five?
That is to say:
fire cannot burn it, poison cannot strike it, a blade cannot wound it, water cannot sweep it away, and smoke cannot suffocate it.

It is the same for the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: having obtained the medicine of the bodhicitta of omniscience, the fire of greed does not burn them, the poison of hatred does not strike them, the blade of delusion does not wound them, the currents of existence do not sweep them away, and the smoke of discursive thoughts and mental constructions cannot suffocate or harm them.
“Good son! It is like a person who, having obtained the medicine of liberation, will never encounter untimely calamities.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: having obtained the medicinal wisdom of liberation that is the bodhicitta, they are forever free from all untimely calamities of birth and death.”
“Good son! It is like a person who carries the mahā-aṅga medicine; when a venomous snake smells its scent, it immediately flees far away.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: carrying the great mahā-aṅga medicine of the bodhicitta, all the venomous snakes of the various afflictions, upon smelling its scent, are entirely dispersed and extinguished.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who possesses the invincible medicine; no enemy whatsoever can overcome them.
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva likewise possesses the invincible medicine of the bodhicitta, and is able to completely subdue all the armies of Māra.”
“Good son! It is like a person who, by holding the *vighuṣma* medicine, causes poisoned arrows to fall away naturally.
So too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: by holding the *vighuṣma* medicine of the bodhicitta, they cause the arrows of greed, hatred, delusion, and all false views to fall away naturally.”
“Good son! It is like a person who possesses the *sudarśana* medicine, which can eliminate all manner of illnesses.
In the same way, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva possesses the *sudarśana* king of medicines that is the bodhicitta, and thereby completely eliminates all diseases of the afflictions (*kleśa*).”
“Good son! It is like a medicinal tree named Śatana;
if one takes its bark and applies it to a wound, the wound is immediately healed.
However, its bark grows back as soon as it is taken, and can never be exhausted.

In the same way, the tree of all-knowledge that arises from the bodhicitta of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: if there are those who see it and give rise to faith, their wounds of afflictions and karma are entirely eliminated, yet the tree of all-knowledge suffers no loss whatsoever.
“Good son! It is like a medicinal tree named ‘Rootless,’ by whose power all the trees of Jambudvīpa grow and flourish.”

The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s tree of bodhicitta is likewise; by its power, it causes all the wholesome dharmas of those in training (śaikṣa), those beyond training (aśaikṣa), and all bodhisattvas to grow. "Good son!..."
It is like a medicine named Ālambā;
if it is applied to the body, both body and mind become fully capable.
It is the same for the bodhisattva-mahāsattva who obtains the Ālambā medicine of the bodhicitta, which causes their body and mind to increase in wholesome dharmas.
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains the medicinal herb of mindfulness; whatever they hear, they remember and retain without forgetting.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva obtains the wondrous medicine of the power of mindfulness of the bodhicitta, and is thus able to hear and retain all Buddha-dharmas without any loss or forgetfulness.”
“Good son! It is like a medicine named Great Lotus; whoever consumes it will live for an eon.”
In the same way, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva takes the great lotus-herb of the bodhicitta, their lifespan becomes sovereign throughout incalculable kalpas. "Good son!
For example, suppose there is a person who holds a medicinal drug that renders one invisible; neither humans nor non-humans can see them.
In the same way, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva holds the wondrous medicinal drug of the bodhicitta, all Māras are unable to perceive them.
“Good son! It is as if there were a jewel in the ocean named ‘Universal Gathering of All Jewels.
If this jewel is present, even if the kalpa-fire were to burn the world, it would be impossible for even a single drop of this ocean to be diminished.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s jewel of the bodhicitta is also like this: dwelling within the great ocean of a bodhisattva’s vows, if one constantly maintains it without allowing it to decline or be lost, there is absolutely no possibility that it could destroy even a single root of goodness of a bodhisattva;
yet if that mind should regress, all wholesome dharmas will immediately disperse and perish.
“Good son! It is like a mani jewel named ‘Great Radiance.
If anyone adorns their body with a necklace made of this jewel, it outshines all other precious ornaments, such that none of their lights appear at all.”

The jewel of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise: when it adorns their body, it outshines all the jewel-like minds of the two vehicles, such that none of their various ornaments possess any luster.
“Good son! Just as the water-purifying jewel can clarify turbid water, so too is the bodhicitta-jewel of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; it can clarify all the defilements of affliction.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains the water-abiding jewel and fastens it upon their body; when they enter the great ocean, they are not harmed by the water.”
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, having attained the jewel that dwells in water—the bodhicitta—enters the ocean of all saṃsāra without ever sinking.
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a dragon-jewel; if they carry it into a dragon palace, no dragons or snakes can cause them harm.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: having obtained the great dragon-jewel of the bodhicitta, when entering the realm of desire, the dragons and snakes of the afflictions cannot cause them harm.”
“Good son! Just as Śakra, wearing his maṇi crown, outshines all other hosts of devas, so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva:
wearing the precious crown of the great vow of the bodhicitta, he transcends all sentient beings within the triple world.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi), which eliminates all suffering of poverty.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva obtains the wish-fulfilling jewel of the bodhicitta, thereby remaining far removed from all fear of wrong livelihood.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a sun-crystal gem; when held toward the sunlight, it produces fire.
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva obtains the sun-gem of the bodhicitta-mind; when held toward the light of wisdom, it produces the fire of wisdom.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a moon-essence jewel; when held toward the light of the moon, it produces water.

In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva obtains the moon-essence jewel of the bodhicitta; holding this heart-jewel and reflecting the light of dedication, they produce the water of all vows for roots of goodness.”
“Good son! For example, it is like a dragon king who wears a crown of wish-fulfilling *maṇi* jewels upon his head and is thereby far removed from all fear of enemies.
So too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: wearing the precious crown of the great compassion of the bodhicitta, he is far removed from all the hardships of the evil realms.”
“Good son! It is like a precious jewel named ‘Treasury of Adornments for All Worlds.
If anyone should obtain it, all their desires will be completely fulfilled, yet this jewel suffers no depletion whatsoever.”
The jewel of the bodhicitta is likewise; if anyone obtains it, all their aspirations will be completely fulfilled, yet the bodhicitta itself suffers no diminution.
“Good son! It is like a wheel-turning monarch who possesses a maṇi jewel; when placed within his palace, it radiates great light, destroying all darkness.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: dwelling in the desire realm with the great maṇi-jewel of the bodhicitta, they radiate the light of great wisdom, completely shattering the darkness of ignorance throughout all realms of existence.
“Good son! For example, if there is a great indranīla mani jewel, whatever is touched by its light immediately becomes the same color as it.

The bodhicitta jewel of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: when one observes all phenomena and dedicates the roots of goodness, there is nothing that does not immediately become the same color as the bodhicitta.”
“Good son! Just as a lapis lazuli gem, even after remaining amidst impurities for hundreds of thousands of years, is not defiled by foul odors because its nature is fundamentally pure.”

The jewel of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise: though it remains within the desire realm for hundreds of thousands of kalpas, it is not defiled by the faults and afflictions of the desire realm, because its nature is as pure as the dharmadhātu.
“Good son! It is like a jewel named Pure Radiance,
which is able to outshine the colors of all other jewels.”
The jewel of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this, for it can completely outshine all the merits of ordinary beings and those of the two vehicles. "Good son!
For example, there is a jewel named "Flame" that is capable of completely extinguishing all darkness.
In the same way, the jewel of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise able to extinguish all the darkness of ignorance.
“Good son! It is like a priceless jewel in the ocean that a merchant obtains and carries on board his ship into the city;
among all other kinds of mani-jewels numbering in the hundreds of thousands of myriads, none can equal it in radiance, color, or value.”

The jewel of the bodhicitta is likewise: dwelling within the great ocean of birth and death, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva boards the ship of great vows and, with a continuous profound resolve, carries it into the city of liberation; no merit of the two vehicles can equal this.

“Good son! Suppose there were a precious gem called ‘Sovereign King’ located on Jambudvīpa, forty thousand yojanas away from the orbs of the sun and moon; all the adornments within the palaces of the sun and moon would be perfectly reflected in the image of that gem.

In the same way, the jewel of the pure merit of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has resolved upon bodhicitta likewise abides within saṃsāra while illuminating the emptiness of the dharma-realm; therein, all the suns and moons of buddha-wisdom and all merits are fully manifested.
“Good son! It is like a precious jewel named Sovereign King (Vajrarāja).
Wherever the light of the sun and moon shines upon it, the value of all other treasures, clothing, and such items cannot possibly equal it.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s jewel-king of the sovereign mind of bodhicitta is likewise: wherever the light of omniscience shines, all the merits of the gods and humans of the three periods of time, as well as those of the two vehicles—whether with outflows or without outflows—cannot equal it.
"Good son! Within the ocean there is a treasure called Ocean Treasury,
which universally manifests all manner of adornments within the sea."
The jewel of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this, for it can universally manifest all the adornments of the ocean of omniscience. "Good son!
For example, among the Jāmbūnada gold of the heavens, there is nothing that can equal it except for the Great Maṇi Jewel of the Mind-King.
In the same way, the Jāmbūnada gold of the bodhicitta generated by a bodhisattva-mahāsattva has nothing that can equal it except for the Great Jewel of the Mind-King of omniscience (sarvajñatā).
“Good son! It is like a person who is skilled in the methods for taming dragons and thus attains mastery over all dragons.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the method for taming dragons through the bodhicitta and thereby attains mastery over all the dragons of the afflictions.”
“Good son! It is like a valiant warrior who, having donned armor and taken up weapons, cannot be subdued by any enemy.

In the same way, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, having donned the armor and taken up the weapons of the great mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta), cannot be defeated by any enemies consisting of karma, afflictions, or evils.”

“Good son! For example, it is like the black sandalwood incense of the heavens: if one *zhu* of it is burned, its fragrance pervades a small thousand-world system (*sāhasra-lokadhātu*), such that the total value of all the precious jewels filling a three-thousandfold world system cannot equal it.”

The incense of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is also like this: the merit of a single thought universally perfumes the entire dharma-realm, such that all the merits of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot equal it.
“Good son! Just as when white sandalwood is applied to the body, it can completely eliminate all feverish afflictions and cause both body and mind to attain universal coolness;

so too is the incense of the bodhicitta of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva. It can eliminate all delusions and feverish afflictions—such as false imaginings, discrimination, greed, anger, and ignorance—and cause them to be endowed with the coolness of wisdom.”

“Good son! Just as Mount Sumeru takes on the same color as anyone who approaches it, so too is the mountain of the bodhicitta of the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: anyone who approaches it will entirely come to share its color of omniscience.”
“Good son! For example, the fragrance of the bark of the Pārijātaka tree cannot be matched by any of the fragrances of flowers such as the vārṣika, campaka, or sumana found within Jambudvīpa.”

The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s tree of the bodhicitta is likewise: the fragrance of the merit of the great vows it produces cannot be matched by any of the fragrances of the untainted precepts, concentrations, wisdom, liberations, or the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to those of the two vehicles.
“Good son! For example, although the pārijātaka tree has not yet blossomed, you should know that it is the source from which immeasurable flowers will arise.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s tree of bodhicitta is likewise: although it has not yet blossomed with the flowers of omniscience, one should know that it is the place where the innumerable bodhi-flowers of gods and humans are born.

“Good son! For example, if one perfumes a garment with a *pārijātaka* flower for a single day, even if one were to perfume it with *campaka*, *vārṣika*, or *sumana* flowers for a thousand years, they could not equal its fragrance.”

The flower of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: the fragrance of the various merits perfumed throughout a single lifetime pervades all the abodes of the Buddhas in the ten directions, such that it cannot be matched by the untainted merits of all those of the two vehicles, even if they were perfumed for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.

“Good son! It is like the coconut trees growing on an island in the ocean; their roots, stems, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are constantly harvested and utilized by all sentient beings without a moment’s rest.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s tree of the bodhicitta is likewise thus: from its initial arousal of the mind of compassionate vows until the attainment of Buddhahood and the endurance of the True Dharma in the world, it constantly benefits all the worlds without interruption.
“Good son! It is like a medicinal juice called *harītaka*;
if someone obtains it, one *liang* of it can transform one thousand *liang* of copper, all of which becomes pure gold, yet those one thousand *liang* of copper cannot transform this medicine.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: by means of the medicinal wisdom of dedication through the bodhicitta, they universally transform all phenomena such as karma and afflictions, causing them all to become the marks of omniscience; yet karma and afflictions cannot transform their mind.

“Good son! Just as a small fire grows more intense in its flames as it burns whatever it encounters, so too is the fire of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva: as it takes up various objects of focus, the flames of wisdom increase.”
“Good son! For example, when one lamp ignites hundreds of thousands of lamps, that original single lamp neither diminishes nor is exhausted.

The lamp of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is also like this: it universally ignites the wisdom-lamps of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, yet its own mind-lamp neither diminishes nor is exhausted.”
“Good son! For example, when a single lamp enters a dark room, it can completely destroy all the darkness accumulated over hundreds of thousands of years.

The lamp of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: when it enters the inner chamber of a sentient being’s mind, it can entirely eliminate the various karmic afflictions and manifold obscurations of darkness spanning unspeakable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas.”
“Good son! It is like the wick of a lamp: it emits light according to its size;
if one adds more oil, the light will never cease.”
The lamp of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise: with great vows as its wick, it illuminates the dharma-realm;
by adding the oil of great compassion, it teaches and transforms sentient beings, adorns buddha-lands, and performs buddha-deeds without ceasing.
“Good son! It is like the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, who wears a celestial crown of Jambūnada gold; none of the ornaments of the devaputras of the desire realm can equal it.”
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise: wearing the celestial crown of the great vow of the bodhicitta, all the merits of ordinary beings and those of the two vehicles cannot equal it.
“Good son! When the lion king roars, the lion cubs who hear it all increase in courage and strength, while the other beasts, upon hearing it, immediately flee and hide.

It should be understood that the lion-king Buddha’s roar of the bodhicitta is likewise: when all bodhisattvas hear it, their merits increase, whereas those who hold to acquisitions all retreat and scatter upon hearing it.
“Good son! It is like a person who uses a lion’s sinew as a string for a musical instrument;
once its sound is played, all other strings snap.”
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise: taking the lion-like *pāramitā*-body of the Tathāgata and the sinew of the bodhicitta as the strings for the lute of Dharma-joy;
once that sound is struck, all the strings of the five desires and the various merits of the two vehicles are completely severed and extinguished.

“Good son! It is like a person who collects various kinds of milk, such as that of oxen and sheep, until they fill the great ocean; yet if a single drop of lion’s milk were cast into it, it would cause all of it to turn sour and spoil, passing through unimpeded.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise: by placing the milk of the Tathāgata’s lion-like bodhicitta into the great ocean of the milk of karmic afflictions from immeasurable eons, he causes it all to be destroyed and utterly vanishes through without obstruction, never remaining within the liberation of the two vehicles.
“Good son! For example, it is like the kalaviṅka bird, which possesses great power within its eggshell, such that no other birds can equal it.”

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: having generated the bodhicitta within the shell of birth and death, the power of all their great compassion and merit is such that no śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha can equal it.

“Good son! It is like the prince of the garuḍa birds: when he is first born, his eyes are clear and sharp, and his flight is powerful and swift; though all other birds have been grown for a long time, none can equal him.”

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: having resolved upon the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta), they become a prince of the Buddha; with pure wisdom and courageous great compassion, they cannot be equaled by any of those of the two vehicles, even if they have practiced the path for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
“Good son! It is like a strong man who, grasping a sharp spear in his hand, pierces through dense and solid armor, passing straight through without obstruction.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: grasping the sharp, keen, and swift spear of the bodhicitta, he pierces the dense armor of all latent tendencies of false views, being able to penetrate them all completely without any hindrance.”
“Good son! It is like a great nāga, a hero of mighty strength; if he rouses his fierce wrath, a boil will inevitably appear upon his forehead.
As long as that boil has not yet healed, no person within Jambudvīpa is able to subdue him.”
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: if they give rise to great compassion, they will certainly produce the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta);
as long as they have not abandoned that mind, no Māras or followers of Māra in all the worlds can cause them harm.

“Good son! It is, for example, like a master archer who has many disciples; although they have not yet become fully practiced in their teacher’s arts, their wisdom, skillful means, and ingenuity surpass those of all other people.

It is likewise with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva at the initial moment of generating the mind of enlightenment: although they have not yet become habituated to all the practices of omniscience, their vows, wisdom, understanding, and aspirations surpass those of all ordinary worldlings and followers of the two vehicles.
“Good son! Just as a person learning archery first steadies their feet and then practices the technique, so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
wishing to learn the path of the Tathāgata’s all-knowledge, they should first abide securely in the bodhicitta, and only thereafter practice all the Buddha-dharmas.”

“Good son! It is like a magician who, when about to perform a magical feat, must first give rise to the intention and recollect the magical arts; only then will all that he intends to do be successfully accomplished.”

It is the same for the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: when about to manifest all the supernatural illusions of the buddhas and bodhisattvas, they must first give rise to the intention and resolve for bodhicitta; only then will everything be fully accomplished.
“Good son! It is like the art of illusion, which manifests forms where there are no forms.

The characteristic of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: although it has no form and cannot be seen, it can universally manifest all manner of adornments of merit throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions.”
“Good son! It is like a wildcat:
as soon as it sees a mouse, the mouse immediately enters its hole and dares not emerge again.

So too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who has resolved upon Bodhicitta: when he momentarily observes all delusions and karmas with the eye of wisdom, they all immediately flee into hiding and no longer arise.”
“Good son! It is like a person who wears ornaments made of Jambu-river gold; they outshine everything else, making it all appear like a mass of ink.

So too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: wearing the ornaments of the bodhicitta, they outshine all the merit-ornaments of ordinary beings and those of the two vehicles, rendering them entirely lusterless.”
