“Good son! Just as a fine magnet, by the power of even a small portion of itself, can attract and break apart all iron hooks and chains, so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who has resolved upon Bodhicitta:
if they give rise to even a single thought, they are able to destroy and extinguish all the hooks and chains of views, desires, and ignorance.”
“Good son! It is like a magnet: if iron sees it, it immediately disperses and none remains.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s production of the bodhicitta is also like this: when all karmas, afflictions, and the liberation of the two vehicles briefly behold it, they are immediately dispersed and extinguished, and none remain.”
“Good son! It is like a person who has skillfully entered the great ocean;
no aquatic creatures are able to cause him harm, and even if he were to enter the mouth of a makara fish, he would not be swallowed by it.”
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having resolved upon bodhicitta and entered the ocean of birth and death, various karmas and afflictions cannot cause him harm;
even if he enters the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, he is not obstructed or hindered by them.
“Good son! It is like a person who drinks the nectar-juice of ambrosia; no other things can cause them harm.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having drunk the nectar-dharma juice of the bodhicitta, they do not fall into the stages of the Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha, because they are endowed with the power of vast compassion and vows.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains añjana ointment and applies it to their eyes; though they walk among people, they are not seen by others.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having obtained the *añjana* ointment of the mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*), he is able to enter the realm of Māra through skillful means, such that all Māras are unable to see him.
“Good son! It is like a person who, by relying upon a king, has no fear of others.
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, by relying on the great and powerful king that is the bodhicitta, has no fear of the difficulties of hindrances, obscurations, or the evil realms.”
“Good son! It is like a person who, standing in water, does not fear being burned by fire.
So it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: dwelling in the water of the roots of goodness of the bodhicitta, they do not fear the fire of the wisdom of liberation of the two vehicles.”
“Good son! It is like a person who, by relying upon a valiant general, has no fear of any enemies.
In the same way, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, by relying upon the courageous great general that is the bodhicitta, does not fear any enemies of unwholesome conduct.”
“Good son! Just as the Heavenly King Śakra wields the vajra-pestle to crush and subdue all the hosts of asuras,
so too does the bodhisattva-mahāsattva wield the vajra-pestle of the bodhicitta to crush and subdue all māras and heterodox teachers.”
"Good son! It is like a person who takes an elixir of longevity and remains perpetually robust, neither aging nor growing thin.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: taking the longevity elixir of the bodhicitta, they cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva for incalculable eons, their mind never weary or disheartened, and remaining free from all defiled attachments."
“Good son! It is like a person who, wishing to prepare medicinal decoctions, must first take pure, clear water.
In the same way, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva who wishes to cultivate all the practices and vows of a bodhisattva must first give rise to the bodhicitta.”
“Good son! Just as a person who protects their body first protects the life-faculty, so too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva:
in upholding and maintaining the Buddha-dharma, they must likewise first protect the bodhicitta.”
“Good son! For example, if a person’s life-faculty is severed, they can no longer benefit their parents, kinsmen, or relatives.
It is the same for a bodhisattva-mahāsattva: if they abandon the bodhicitta, they cannot benefit all sentient beings, nor can they accomplish the merits of all Buddhas.”
“Good son! For example, just as the great ocean cannot be destroyed by anything, so too is the ocean of the bodhicitta;
it cannot be destroyed by any karma, afflictions, or the minds of those of the two vehicles.”
“Good son! For example, just as the light of the sun cannot be eclipsed by the radiance of the stars, so too is the sun of the bodhicitta;
it cannot be obscured by the light of the untainted wisdom (*anāsrava-jñāna*) of all those of the two vehicles.
“Good son! Just as a prince, immediately upon birth, is respected by great ministers because of the sovereignty of his lineage, so too is it with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva:

having resolved upon bodhicitta within the Buddha-dharma, he is respected by the elder śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas who have long practiced the holy life, because of the sovereignty of his great compassion.”
“Good son! For example, although a prince may be of tender age, all the great ministers pay him homage.

It is the same for a bodhisattva-mahāsattva: although he has only recently resolved to attain enlightenment and is practicing the bodhisattva path, those of the two vehicles who are long-standing elders should likewise pay him homage.”

“Good son! It is like a prince who, although he has not yet attained sovereign power among all his ministers and officials, already possesses the marks of a king and is not equal to any of those ministers and officials because his birth is noble and superior.”

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: although they have not yet attained mastery over all karma and afflictions, they are already fully endowed with the marks of enlightenment and are not equal to any of the followers of the two vehicles, because their spiritual lineage is supreme.
“Good son! For example, it is like a pure and wondrous maṇi jewel which appears impure because of a cataract in the eye.
The maṇi jewel of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: those who lack wisdom and lack faith perceive it as impure.”
“Good son! It is like a medicine that is empowered by mantras; if there are sentient beings who see it, hear it, or dwell together with it, all their various illnesses will be completely eliminated.”

The medicinal herb of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise: sustained by all roots of goodness, wisdom, skillful means, and the bodhisattva’s vow-knowledge, if any sentient beings see it, hear it, dwell with it, or bring it to mind, all diseases of the afflictions shall be completely eradicated.
“Good son! It is like a person who constantly holds ambrosia; their body will ultimately remain unchanging and indestructible.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: if they constantly recollect and maintain the ambrosia of the bodhicitta, they will cause the body of their vows and wisdom to remain ultimately indestructible.”
“Good son! Just as a wooden mechanical figure will have its body fall apart and be unable to move if it lacks the wedge, so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
without the bodhicitta, their practice disperses and they cannot accomplish all the Buddha-dharmas.”
“Good son! It is like a wheel-turning monarch who possesses a precious sandalwood called ‘Elephant Treasury’;”
If this incense is burned, the King’s fourfold army will all ascend into the void.

It is the same with the incense of the bodhicitta of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: if this intention is aroused, it causes all the roots of goodness of the Bodhisattvas to forever emerge from the triple world and proceed through the unconditioned space of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.

“Good son! For example, just as a diamond is produced only from a diamond mine or a gold mine, and not from the mines of other jewels, so too is the diamond of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;

it is produced only from the diamond mine of great compassion that protects and saves sentient beings, and from the gold mine of the sublime realm of the knowledge of all-knowledge, and not from the roots of goodness of other sentient beings.”
“Good son! It is like a tree named ‘Rootless,’ which does not grow from roots,
yet its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are all lush and abundant.”
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s tree of the bodhicitta is likewise thus: though no root can be found, it is able to nurture the great vows, the supernormal powers, and the wisdom of omniscience;
its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits spread wide and cast deep shade, universally covering the world.
“Good son! For example, a vajra cannot be contained or supported by an inferior or broken vessel, but only by a complete and exquisite vessel of the highest quality.”

The vajra of the bodhicitta is likewise: it cannot be contained or sustained within the vessels of inferior beings characterized by stinginess, envy, broken precepts, laziness, distracted mindfulness, and lack of wisdom; nor can it be contained or sustained within the vessels of those who have fallen away from their sublime aspirations, who are distracted, or who harbor evil thoughts—except for the precious vessel of the Bodhisattva’s profound mind.
“Good son! For example, just as a diamond can pierce all manner of jewels, so too is the diamond of the bodhicitta; it can completely penetrate all the treasures of the Dharma.”
“Good son! Just as a vajra can shatter all mountains, so too is the vajra of the bodhicitta; it can utterly destroy all mountains of false views.”
"Good son! For example, although a diamond may be broken and incomplete, no other jewel can surpass it.
The diamond of the bodhicitta is also like this: even if one's resolve is weak and there is some deficiency, it still surpasses all the merits of the two vehicles."
“Good son! For example, just as a diamond, even if it has flaws or cracks, can still eliminate all poverty;
so too is the diamond of the bodhicitta. Even if it has flaws—meaning that one does not advance in various practices—it can still cause one to abandon all of saṃsāra.”
“Good son! Just as a small vajra is able to destroy all things, so too is the vajra of the bodhicitta;
entering even a slight object, it immediately shatters all ignorance and delusions.”
“Good son! For example, just as a diamond cannot be obtained by ordinary people, so too is the diamond of the bodhicitta; it cannot be attained by sentient beings of inferior intent.”
"Good son! For example, just as those who do not recognize jewels do not know the power of a diamond and cannot obtain its utility, so it is with the diamond of the bodhicitta:
those who do not know the Dharma do not understand its power and cannot obtain its utility."
“Good son! For example, just as a diamond cannot be destroyed, so too is the diamond of the bodhicitta; no phenomena whatsoever can destroy it.”
“Good son! Just as a vajra-pestle cannot be held by any person of great strength, except for one who possesses the power of Mahānārāyaṇa, so too is the bodhicitta:
it cannot be sustained by any of the followers of the two vehicles, except for those Bodhisattvas who possess the firm and wholesome power of vast causes and conditions.”
“Good son! It is like a vajra:
there is nothing among all things that can destroy it, yet it can universally destroy all things, while its essential nature remains undiminished.”

The bodhicitta is likewise: throughout the countless eons of the three periods of time, it universally teaches and transforms sentient beings and practices asceticism; it can accomplish all that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are unable to do, yet it remains ultimately free from weariness and suffers no impairment.
“Good son! For example, just as a diamond cannot be supported by anything else, but can only be supported by a diamond ground, so too is the bodhicitta:
it cannot be supported by śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, except for those who are heading toward sarvajñatā.”
“Good son! Just as a vajra vessel, being free from cracks or flaws, never leaks water when used to hold it so that it does not seep into the earth;
likewise, the vajra vessel of the bodhicitta holds the water of roots of goodness and never leaks them away to enter the various realms of existence.”
“Good son! Just as the vajra-limit can support the great earth, preventing it from falling and sinking, so too is the bodhicitta;
it can sustain all the practices and vows of a bodhisattva, preventing them from falling and sinking into the triple world.”
“Good son! For example, just as a diamond remains for a long time in water without rotting or becoming wet, so too is the bodhicitta;
throughout all kalpas, while remaining amidst the waters of the karma and delusions of birth and death, it is neither destroyed nor transformed.”
“Good son! For example, just as adamant cannot be burned or heated by any fire, so too is the bodhicitta:
it cannot be burned or heated by any of the fires of affliction within the cycle of birth and death.”

“Good son! For example, within the trichiliocosm, it is only upon a vajra seat that one can support the Buddhas as they sit at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), subdue all Māras, and realize equal and perfect awakening; no other seat is capable of supporting them.”

The seat of the bodhicitta is likewise: it can sustain all the vows and practices of a bodhisattva, the various pāramitās, the various patiences, the various stages (bhūmis), the dedication of merit, the reception of predictions, and the cultivation and accumulation of the factors conducive to enlightenment; as well as the making of offerings to all Buddhas, hearing the Dharma, and receiving and practicing it—none of these can be sustained by any other mind.
“Good son! The bodhicitta accomplishes such immeasurable, boundless, and even unspeakably unspeakable, supreme merits.”
If there are sentient beings who resolve their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they shall obtain such supreme dharmas of merit. Therefore, good son!
You have gained a great benefit!
Because you have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, sought the bodhisattva practices, and have already acquired such great merit.
“Good son! As to what you have asked:
‘How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?’”

"Good son! You may enter this Great Pavilion of the Adorned Treasury of Vairocana and observe it thoroughly; then you will be able to understand how to train in the bodhisattva practices, and having trained, you will accomplish immeasurable merit."
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume 78; The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume 79.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree.
In the twentieth part of the thirty-ninth chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm," at that time, the youth Sudhana,
having circumambulated Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva respectfully to the right, addressed him, saying:
"I only pray that the Great Sage will open the door of the pavilion, so that I may enter!"
Then, Maitreya Bodhisattva went before the pavilion and snapped his fingers; as soon as the sound was made, the door opened, and he commanded Sudhana to enter.
Sudhana’s heart was filled with joy, and once he had entered, the door closed behind him.
He saw that the towers and pavilions were vast and immeasurable, equal to empty space, with grounds made of incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels;
there were incalculable palaces, incalculable gates, incalculable windows, incalculable stairways, incalculable balustrades, and incalculable roads, all composed of the seven treasures;
and incalculable banners, incalculable standards, and incalculable parasols were arrayed all around.
Countless necklaces of various jewels, countless necklaces of pearls, countless necklaces of red pearls, and countless necklaces of lion-pearls hung down everywhere;
they were further adorned with countless half-moons, countless silk ribbons, and countless jeweled nets.

Countless jewel bells produced music when stirred by the wind; countless varieties of celestial flowers were scattered; countless celestial jewel garlands and ribbons were suspended; countless incense burners made of various jewels were arrayed; countless fine gold powders rained down; countless jewel mirrors were hung; countless jewel lamps were lit; countless jewel robes were spread out; countless jewel canopies were set in rows; countless jewel thrones were prepared, with countless precious silk fabrics spread upon them;
countless images of youths and maidens of Jambūnada gold, countless images of various forms made of diverse jewels, and countless images of Bodhisattvas made of exquisite jewels filled every place;
and countless flocks of birds emitted harmonious and elegant sounds.
It was adorned with incalculable precious *utpala* flowers, incalculable precious *padma* flowers, incalculable precious *kumuda* flowers, and incalculable precious *puṇḍarīka* flowers;
there were incalculable rows of precious trees arranged in succession, and incalculable *maṇi* jewels emitted great radiance.
Thus, it was adorned with such immeasurable and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) ornaments.
Furthermore, within it, one saw hundreds of thousands of exquisite pavilions, each individually decorated exactly as described above;
vast, magnificent, and beautiful, they were all equal to space, without mutual obstruction and without confusion.
Within a single location, the youth Sudhana saw all locations; he saw them all in this same way.

At that time, seeing such various inconceivable and sovereign realms within the Vairocana-Adorned Treasury Pavilion, Sudhana was filled with great joy and leaped for immeasurable delight. His body and mind became supple; he was freed from all conceptualizations, removed all obstructions, and extinguished all delusions. What he saw he did not forget; what he heard he could remember; what he contemplated was not confused, as he entered the gate of unimpeded liberation.

Universally directing his mind, he universally beheld all things and universally proffered respectful salutations. As soon as he had begun to bow his head, through the majestic spiritual power of Maitreya Bodhisattva, he saw his own body pervading all the pavilions, clearly perceiving various inconceivable states of sovereign mastery.
That is to say:

they may see the name and clan of Maitreya Bodhisattva when he first resolved upon supreme enlightenment; the kind of virtuous friend who awakened him, causing him to plant such roots of goodness; his lifespan, the eon in which he lived, the Buddhas he encountered, and the adorned lands where he dwelt; the practices he cultivated and the vows he made;
as well as the assemblies of those Tathāgatas, their lifespans, and how long he attended upon and made offerings to them.
—all these he clearly beheld.
He saw Maitreya first realize the *maitrī-samādhi*, from which time forth he was named Maitreya;
or he saw Maitreya cultivating various sublime practices and bringing all the *pāramitās* to full completion.

Some see them attaining patience (*kṣānti*), some see them dwelling on the stages (*bhūmi*), some see them accomplishing pure buddha-fields, and some see them upholding the True Teaching of the Tathāgata as great Dharma masters, attaining the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and receiving the prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) of unsurpassed bodhi at a certain time, in a certain place, from a certain Tathāgata.
In some instances, they see Maitreya as a Cakravartin King, exhorting all sentient beings to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action;
in others, he acts as a World Protector (Lokapāla) to bring benefit to sentient beings;
or he acts as Śakra Devendra to rebuke the five desires.
Sometimes he becomes the King of the Yama Heaven, praising non-negligence;
sometimes he becomes the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, extolling the merits of bodhisattvas in their final birth;
and sometimes he becomes the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, manifesting for the assembly of devas the various transformations and adornments of bodhisattvas.
Sometimes he becomes the King of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, expounding all the teachings of the Buddhas for the assembly of devas;
sometimes he acts as a Mara King, teaching that all phenomena are entirely impermanent;
or he becomes a Brahma King, preaching of the various dhyānas and samādhis and their immeasurable bliss.

Or he may become a king of the asuras, entering the great ocean of wisdom and realizing that all phenomena are like illusions; for the sake of his assemblies, he constantly expounds the Dharma, severing all forms of arrogance, intoxication, and haughtiness.
Or again, they may see him in the realm of Yama, emitting great radiance to rescue those suffering in the hells;
or see him in the abode of hungry ghosts, bestowing food and drink to relieve their hunger and thirst;
or see him in the path of animals, employing various skillful means to tame and transform sentient beings.
Or again, he may see [the Buddha] preaching the Dharma for the assembly of the World-Protecting Heavenly Kings;
or again, he may see him preaching the Dharma for the assembly of the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; or again, he may see him preaching the Dharma for the assembly of the King of the Yama Heaven;
or again, he may see him preaching the Dharma for the assembly of the King of the Tuṣita Heaven; or again, he may see him preaching the Dharma for the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven.
He was seen preaching the Dharma to an assembly, or again, seen preaching the Dharma to an assembly of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
or again, seen preaching the Dharma to an assembly of the Great Brahma King; or again, seen preaching the Dharma to an assembly of Dragon Kings;
or again, seen preaching the Dharma to an assembly of Yakṣa and Rākṣasa kings; or again—
He saw [the Buddha] preaching the Dharma to an assembly of Gandharva and Kinnara kings;
or again, he saw him preaching the Dharma to an assembly of Asura and Dānava kings;
or again, he saw him preaching the Dharma to an assembly of Garuḍa and Mahoraga kings; or again, he saw him preaching to all other humans...
He may see them preaching the Dharma for assemblies of non-humans; or he may see them preaching the Dharma for assemblies of śrāvakas;

or he may see them preaching the Dharma for assemblies of pratyekabuddhas; or he may see them expounding the Dharma for the assembly of bodhisattvas, from those who have first resolved upon enlightenment up to those bound by only one more birth and those who have received the consecration.

In some places he saw the praise and exposition of all the merits of the first through the tenth stages; in some places he saw the praise and exposition of the fulfillment of all the *pāramitās*; in some places he saw the praise and exposition of entering the various gates of patience (*kṣānti*); in some places he saw the praise and exposition of the various gates of great samādhis; in some places he saw the praise and exposition of the profound gates of liberation; in some places he saw the praise and exposition of the spheres of dhyāna, samādhi, and supernormal powers (*abhijñā*); in some places he saw the praise and exposition of the various practices of bodhisattvas; in some places he saw the praise and exposition of the various great vows; in some places he saw him praising and expounding for fellow-practicing bodhisattvas the various worldly means of livelihood, crafts, and skillful methods for benefiting sentient beings; and in some places he saw him praising and expounding for bodhisattvas in their final birth the gate of the empowerment (*abhiṣeka*) of all Buddhas.

In some instances, they see Maitreya for hundreds or thousands of years walking back and forth, reciting, and transcribing sutras; diligently seeking and investigating, he preaches the Dharma for the sake of the multitude. At other times, he enters various meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) and the four immeasurable minds (*apramāṇa*), or enters the spheres of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*) and the various liberations (*vimokṣa*), or enters samādhi and manifests various supernatural transformations through the power of skillful means.
In some instances, they see various bodhisattvas entering the Samādhi of Transformation, from each and every pore of their bodies emitting clouds of all manner of transformation-bodies;

or they see them emit clouds of celestial hosts, or clouds of nāga hosts, or clouds of yakṣas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, asuras, garuḍas, mahoragas, Śakras, Brahmās, world-protectors, universal monarchs, minor kings, princes, ministers, officials, elders, and householders; or they see them emit clouds of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and various bodhisattvas and Tathāgatas; or they see them emit clouds of the bodies of all sentient beings.
Or they may see him emit sublime sounds, praising the various Dharma-gates of all bodhisattvas.
That is to say:
he praises and expounds the gate of the merits of the bodhicitta;
He praised and expounded upon the gateway of merits from the *dānapāramitā* up to the *jñānapāramitā*;

he praised and expounded upon the various means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*), the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurable states of mind (*apramāṇacitta*), as well as the various samādhis, the attainments (*samāpatti*), the supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), the clear knowledges (*vidyā*), the dhāraṇīs, the eloquence (*pratibhāna*), the truths (*satya*), the wisdoms (*jñāna*), tranquility and insight (*śamatha-vipaśyanā*), the liberations (*vimokṣa*), the conditions (*pratyaya*), the supports (*niśraya*), and the gateways for preaching the Dharma;

he praised and expounded upon the foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), the right efforts (*samyakpradhāna*), the bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*), the faculties (*indriya*), the strengths (*bala*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*), the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, the stages (*bhūmi*), the patiences (*kṣānti*), the practices (*caryā*), and the vows (*praṇidhāna*)—indeed, all such gateways of merit.
Furthermore, within that [vision], he sees various Tathāgatas surrounded by great assemblies;

he also clearly perceives the birthplaces, lineages, physical forms, lifespans, lands, eons, names, the benefits of their preaching, and the duration for which their teachings remain—indeed, all the various differences in their sites of enlightenment and their congregations.
Furthermore, within those various pavilions inside the Treasury of Adornments, he saw one pavilion that was lofty, vast, and exquisitely decorated, unsurpassed and peerless;
therein he clearly beheld ten billion sets of four continents and ten billion Tuṣita heavens throughout the three thousandfold world system,
each of which featured Maitreya Bodhisattva descending to be born, with Śakra and Brahmā holding him up.
He was borne upon his head; he walked seven steps; he surveyed the ten directions; he uttered the Great Lion’s Roar;
he manifested as a youth; he dwelt in palaces; he sported in gardens and groves; for the sake of all-knowledge, he left the household life and practiced austerities;
he demonstrated the acceptance of milk-rice; he proceeded to the site of enlightenment; he subdued all Māras; and he attained Equal and Perfect Enlightenment.
The initial application and sustained observation [of the mind] at the Bodhi tree; the Brahma King’s exhortation to turn the wheel of the sublime Dharma;
ascending to the celestial palaces to expound the Dharma; the number of kalpas and the span of his lifespan; the adornments of the assemblies; the lands purified; the practices and vows cultivated;
the skillful means for teaching and maturing sentient beings; the distribution of relics; and his abiding.
The teachings they uphold are all entirely different.
At that time, Sudhana saw his own body present before all those Tathāgatas;
he also beheld all their assemblies and all their Buddha-activities, retaining them in memory without forgetting and penetrating them without obstruction.

Furthermore, he heard that within all the multi-storied pavilions, the jeweled nets, bells, and various musical instruments all resounded with the inconceivable, subtle, and wondrous sounds of the Dharma, expounding upon manifold teachings.

That is to say: some speak of bodhisattvas generating the mind of enlightenment; some speak of practicing the perfections (pāramitās); some speak of various vows; some speak of the stages (bhūmis); some speak of reverently making offerings to the Tathāgatas; some speak of adorning the buddha-fields; and some speak of the differences in the Buddhas' preaching of the Dharma.
One hears all the aforementioned Buddha-dharmas, hearing their sounds clearly and understanding them with thorough discernment.

Furthermore, one hears that in a certain place there is a certain Bodhisattva who, having heard a certain Dharma-gate and being exhorted by a certain spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), has resolved upon Bodhicitta; and in a certain eon, at a certain site, in the presence of a certain Tathāgata, and within a certain great assembly, they have heard of such merits of a certain Buddha, generated such a mind, raised such vows, and planted such vast roots of goodness;

that for a certain number of eons they have practiced the Bodhisattva path, and after such a duration of time they shall attain perfect enlightenment, with such a name, such a lifespan, and such a land fully adorned; fulfilling such vows, transforming such multitudes, and presiding over such assemblies of Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas.
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for as many eons as this, benefiting such immeasurable sentient beings.

Or, one may hear that in a certain place there is a certain bodhisattva who practices giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, cultivating these various pāramitās.

Or one may hear that in a certain place there is a certain bodhisattva who, for the sake of seeking the Dharma, has renounced his royal throne and all precious treasures, as well as his wife, children, retinue, hands, feet, head, and eyes—being utterly without stinginess regarding any part of his body.

Or they may hear that in a certain place there is a certain bodhisattva who protects the true Dharma spoken by the Tathāgata, acting as a great Dharma teacher, extensively practicing the gift of Dharma, erecting the banner of Dharma, blowing the conch of Dharma, beating the drum of Dharma, raining down the rain of Dharma, constructing Buddha-stūpas and temples, fashioning images of the Buddha, and bestowing all instruments of happiness upon all sentient beings.

Or one may hear that in a certain place, a certain Tathāgata, during a certain eon, attained equal and perfect enlightenment; that his land was such, his assembly such, his lifespan such, the Dharma he taught such, the vows he fulfilled such, and that he transformed and guided such immeasurable sentient beings.

Upon hearing such inconceivable and subtle sounds of the Dharma, the youth Sudhana’s body and mind were filled with joy; they became supple, radiant, and serene. He immediately attained immeasurable gateways of dhāraṇī, gateways of eloquence, as well as all the meditative concentrations, forbearances, vows, perfections, supernormal powers, clarities, liberations, and samādhi gateways.
Furthermore, one sees various forms and images within all the precious mirrors, namely:

In some instances, they see the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of various Buddhas; in others, the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of Bodhisattvas; or the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of Śrāvakas; or the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of Pratyekabuddhas. They may see pure worlds, or impure worlds, or worlds that are both pure and impure, or worlds that are both impure and pure. They may see worlds where a Buddha resides, or worlds where no Buddha resides; small worlds, medium worlds, or large worlds; worlds like Indra’s net, inverted worlds, or upright worlds; level worlds, or worlds inhabited by those in the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of hungry ghosts; or worlds filled with devas and humans.

Within such worlds as these, he saw countless assemblies of great bodhisattvas, some walking or sitting while engaged in various activities; some giving rise to great compassion and pitying sentient beings; some composing treatises to benefit the world; some receiving or upholding [the teachings], some writing or reciting them, some questioning or answering; and all performing repentance at the three periods of the day, dedicating their merit, and making vows.

Furthermore, I saw from within all the precious pillars the emission of great nets of light from mani-kings, which were blue, yellow, red, white, crystal-colored, quartz-colored, indranila-blue, rainbow-colored, or the color of Jambūnada gold; or they manifested as every possible color of light.

Furthermore, he saw those youths and maidens of Jāmbūnada gold, as well as various jeweled images, some holding clouds of flowers with their hands, some holding clouds of garments, some holding banners and streamers, some holding garlands and canopies, some bearing various kinds of ointments and powdered incense, some holding exquisite nets of mani-jewels, some hanging golden chains, some draping necklaces, some raising their arms to hold up ornaments, and some bowing their heads to let mani-crowns hang down; they all gazed upward with bodies bent, their eyes never for a moment departing from him.
Furthermore, he saw those pearl necklaces constantly emitting fragrant water endowed with the eight meritorious qualities;
the lapis lazuli necklaces emitted hundreds of thousands of rays of light, illuminating all at once;
and banners, pennants, nets, and canopies—all such objects as these were adorned with every kind of precious jewel.

Furthermore, he saw blue lotuses (utpala), red lotuses (padma), yellow lotuses (kumuda), and white lotuses (puṇḍarīka), each producing immeasurable flowers—some as large as a hand, some a cubit in length, and others as broad and wide as a chariot wheel—with every single flower manifesting various forms and colors as adornments.
That is to say:

the forms of men, the forms of women, the forms of boys, the forms of girls, Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all bodhisattvas.
All these sentient beings likewise joined their palms, bowed their bodies, and paid respectful homage.
They also saw the Tathāgata sitting cross-legged, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man.
Furthermore, he saw that upon the ground of pure lapis lazuli, within every single step, there appeared inconceivable varieties of forms and images.
Namely: the forms and images of worlds, the forms and images of bodhisattvas, the forms and images of Tathāgatas, as well as the forms and images of the adornments of various pavilions.
Furthermore, within each individual branch, leaf, flower, and fruit of the jewel trees, they saw all manner of half-body images.

These included half-body images of Buddhas, half-body images of Bodhisattvas, as well as those of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, up to the world-protectors, wheel-turning kings, minor kings, princes, ministers, and high officials, along with the half-body images of the fourfold assembly.
Their various forms and appearances were such that some held flower garlands, some held necklaces, and some bore all manner of ornaments;
some bowed their bodies with palms joined in reverence, gazing up with single-minded devotion without averting their eyes for a moment;
some offered praises, while others entered into samādhi.
Their bodies were entirely adorned with the primary and secondary marks, universally emitting various kinds of colored light, namely:

golden light, silver-colored light, coral-colored light, duṣara-colored light, indranīla-colored light, vairocana-jewel-colored light, light of the colors of all manner of jewels, and light of the color of the campaka flower.

Furthermore, within the crescent moon images of the various pavilions, he saw immeasurable (*asaṃkhyeya*) suns, moons, and stars emitting all kinds of radiance that universally illumined the ten directions.
He also saw that the four walls surrounding each of the pavilions were adorned, step by step, with every kind of precious jewel.

Within each and every jewel, there appeared Maitreya, during his cultivation of the bodhisattva path in past kalpas, whether giving away his head or eyes, or his hands, feet, lips, tongue, teeth, ears, nose, flesh, blood, skin, marrow, or even his nails and hair—able to relinquish all such things;
or giving away his wives, concubines, sons, daughters, cities, towns, villages, kingdoms, and royal thrones, bestowing them all entirely according to whatever was required.
For those in prison, he causes them to escape;
for those who are bound, he brings about their liberation;
for those with illnesses, he provides healing.
To those who have entered onto deviant paths, he shows the true path;
or he acts as a boatman to enable them to cross the great ocean;
or he becomes a horse-king to rescue and protect them from evil calamities.
Sometimes he becomes a great seer, skillfully expounding various treatises;
sometimes he becomes a wheel-turning monarch, exhorting others to cultivate the ten wholesome paths of action;
and sometimes he becomes a king of physicians, skillfully healing all manner of ailments.

Some were filial and obedient to their parents; some drew near to virtuous friends; some became śrāvakas, some pratyekabuddhas, some bodhisattvas, or some Tathāgatas, teaching and taming all sentient beings;

some became Dharma masters, upholding and practicing the Buddha’s teachings, receiving, maintaining, reading, and reciting them, reflecting upon them according to principle, establishing Buddhist stūpas, and creating images of the Buddha—whether making offerings themselves or encouraging others to do so by anointing with incense, scattering flowers, and reverently prostrating.
Such events continued in succession without interruption.

In some instances, he saw [the Buddha] seated upon a lion throne, extensively expounding the Dharma, exhorting all sentient beings to abide securely in the ten wholesome paths of action, to single-mindedly take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, to receive and uphold the five precepts and the eight fast-day precepts, to leave the household life to hear the Dharma, and to receive, uphold, recite, and practice according to the principle.
He even beheld the Bodhisattva Maitreya throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeya kalpas, manifesting the various forms of his cultivation of all the perfections;
he also saw all the spiritual friends whom Maitreya had previously served, all adorned with every merit;

and he further saw Maitreya at each and every one of those spiritual friends' abodes, drawing near to them and making offerings, receiving and practicing their instructions, until he reached the stage of consecration.
At that time, his spiritual friends said to Sudhana, "Welcome, young man!
Behold these inconceivable deeds of the Bodhisattva; do not give rise to weariness or fatigue."

At that time, because the youth Sudhana had attained the power of unforgetting mindfulness, the pure eye that beholds the ten directions, the unimpeded wisdom of skillful observation, the sovereign wisdom of all bodhisattvas, and the vast understanding of all bodhisattvas who have entered the stages of wisdom, he saw within every single object in all the towers such things as these, as well as other immeasurable and inconceivable manifestations of sovereign realms and adornments.
It is as if, for example, there were a person who, in the midst of sleep and dreaming, saw various things, namely:
cities, towns, villages, palaces, gardens, groves, mountains, forests, rivers, ponds, clothing, food and drink, and even all manner of articles for sustaining life;
or they might see themselves with their parents, brothers, and relatives, both internal and external.
Some see the great ocean, Sumeru the king of mountains, and even all the celestial palaces, as well as the affairs of the four continents such as Jambudvīpa;

some see their own bodies vast in measure, hundreds of thousands of yojanas in size, with houses and clothing all proportionate thereto, such that they experience various states of bliss without sleeping or reclining for immeasurable periods throughout the day.
Upon waking from sleep, one realizes it was a dream and can clearly remember the events seen therein.

Sudhana the youth was likewise so: sustained by the power of Maitreya Bodhisattva, because he knew that all phenomena of the triple world are like dreams, because he had extinguished the narrow and inferior conceptions of sentient beings, because he had attained unobstructed and vast understanding, because he dwelt in the supreme realms of the bodhisattvas, and because he had entered the inconceivable wisdom of skillful means, he was able to perceive such a realm of sovereign mastery.
For example, when a person is about to die, they see the signs of the retribution they will receive according to their karma:

those who have committed evil deeds see all the realms of suffering belonging to the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts; they may see hell-wardens holding weapons, either angry or abusive, seizing and leading them away; they also hear sounds of wailing and lamentation; or they see the River of Ashes, or boiling cauldrons, or mountains of knives, or trees of swords—various oppressions through which they undergo manifold sufferings.

Those who have performed wholesome deeds immediately see the palaces of all the devas, with immeasurable hosts of devas and celestial maidens, adorned with various garments; the palaces and gardens are all exquisitely beautiful.
Although his body was not yet dead, he saw such things through the power of karma.
In the same way, the youth Sudhana, by the inconceivable power of the karma of a bodhisattva, was able to see all these adorned realms.
For example, it is like a person possessed by a spirit who sees all manner of things and is able to answer whatever questions are asked.

So too was it with the youth Sudhana; because he was sustained by the wisdom of the Bodhisattvas, he saw all those various adornments, and there was no questioner whom he could not satisfy with an answer.

For example, suppose there is a person who, possessed by a nāga, comes to believe himself to be a nāga; he enters the nāga palace and, in a brief moment, believes that many days, months, years, and even ages have already passed.

The youth Sudhana was likewise; because he dwelt in the perception of bodhisattva wisdom and because of the empowerment of Maitreya Bodhisattva, what was but a short time appeared to him as immeasurable eons.
It was like the Brahma palace named "Treasury of Adornments," wherein all things within the three thousandfold world system could be seen simultaneously without any confusion.
In the same way, the youth Sudhana, within the tower, universally beheld all the various distinctions of the adorned realms without any confusion.

For example, it is like a bhikṣu who has entered a universal base concentration (*kṛtsnāyatana-samādhi*); whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, the object of that concentration manifests before him according to the state of absorption he has entered.
The youth Sudhana was likewise; upon entering the tower-palace, all its realms became perfectly clear to him.
It was as if a person were to see a city of the gandharvas in the midst of space, complete with all its adornments, perceiving them all distinctly without any obstruction;
or as if the palace of a yakṣa and the palace of a human were situated in the same place yet remained unmixed, each appearing differently according to their respective karma.
It is like the great ocean, within which all the forms and images of the trichiliocosm are fully seen;
it is like a master of illusions, who by the power of illusion manifests various illusory phenomena and diverse activities.

The youth Sudhana was likewise; by the majestic spiritual power of Maitreya Bodhisattva, by the power of his inconceivable wisdom of illusion, by his ability to know all phenomena through illusory wisdom, and by attaining the sovereign powers of all bodhisattvas, he beheld within the pavilion all the sovereign realms of adornment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya withdrew his supernatural powers and entered the pavilion; snapping his fingers to make a sound, he addressed Sudhana, saying: "Good son!
Arising is the nature of phenomena; this is the mark manifested by the gathering of causes and conditions through the bodhisattva’s wisdom that knows all dharmas.
Such is their intrinsic nature: like an illusion, like a dream, like a shadow, like a reflection—they are entirely unestablished.
At that time, upon hearing the sound of the finger-snap, Sudhana arose from his samādhi.
Maitreya said to him, “Noble son!

Abiding in the inconceivable sovereign liberation of a bodhisattva, you experience the joy and bliss of the bodhisattvas' samādhis; you are able to see the various sublime and wondrously adorned palaces sustained by the spiritual powers of bodhisattvas, flowing from their factors of enlightenment, and manifested through their vows and wisdom;
you behold the conduct of bodhisattvas, hear the Dharma of bodhisattvas, know the virtues of bodhisattvas, and comprehend the vows of the Tathāgatas.
Sudhana replied, "Indeed, Noble One!"
This is due to the power of the spiritual support, mindfulness, and majestic authority of the spiritual friend.
Noble One! What is the name of this gate of liberation?
Maitreya replied: "Good son! This gate of liberation is named: "
The Treasury of Adornments of Wisdom that Enters All Realms of the Three Times Without Forgetting. Good son!
Within this gate of liberation, there are unspeakably unspeakable gates of liberation that can be attained by a Bodhisattva in a single lifetime.
Sudhana asked, "Where has this array of adornments gone? Maitreya replied:
"Go to where you came from.
He asked, "From where did you come?"
He replied:

"I come from the wisdom and spiritual power of the Bodhisattva; I abide by the wisdom and spiritual power of the Bodhisattva. I have no place of departure, nor do I have a place of abiding. I am neither accumulated nor permanent, being far removed from all things."
"Good son! It is like when a dragon king sends down rain: it does not issue from his body, nor does it issue from his mind; it has no accumulation, yet it is not unseen.
It is solely through the power of the dragon king’s mental resolve that the rain pours down in torrents, pervading the entire world. Such a realm is inconceivable."
“Good son! These matters of adornment are likewise: they do not abide within, nor do they abide without, yet they are not unseen;
it is solely through the power of the Bodhisattva’s majestic spiritual authority and the power of your own roots of goodness that you see such things.”
Good son! It is like a magician performing various illusory feats; they come from nowhere and go nowhere.
Although there is no coming or going, through the power of illusion, they are clearly visible.
The matter of those adornments is likewise: they come from nowhere, nor do they go anywhere;

yet, although there is no coming or going, they manifest in this way due to the power of the inconceivable wisdom of illusory mastery resulting from habitual practice, and by virtue of the power of former great vows.
The youth Sudhana asked,
"Great Sage, from where have you come?
Maitreya replied:
“Good son! All bodhisattvas come without coming and go without going; they come in such a manner.
They act without acting and abide without abiding; they come in such a manner.”

Without location or attachment, neither sinking nor arising, neither abiding nor shifting, neither moving nor originating, without longing or clinging, without karma or retribution, without origination or cessation, neither annihilated nor eternal—it comes in this manner.
"Good son! Bodhisattvas come from the state of great compassion because they wish to subdue all sentient beings;
they come from the state of great loving-kindness because they wish to rescue and protect all sentient beings."
They come from the station of pure precepts, for they take birth according to their inclinations;
they come from the station of great vows, for they are sustained by the power of their former aspirations;
they come from the station of supernormal powers, for they manifest themselves at will in all places.
They come from the state of immovability, for they never abandon or depart from all Buddhas;
they come from the state of neither grasping nor rejecting, for they do not cause their body or mind to engage in coming and going;
they come from the state of wisdom and skillful means, for they accord with and follow all sentient beings.
"I come from the place where transformations are manifested, for I appear through emanation like a reflected image.
Nevertheless, noble son, you ask me from where I have come."
"Noble son! I have come here from my birthplace, the country of Mālava. Noble son!"
In that place there was a village named Abode;
there was a son of a householder named:
Kubjottarā, he dwells there in order to transform those people and lead them into the Buddha-dharma;

furthermore, he dwells there to preach the Dharma according to their individual needs for all the inhabitants of that birthplace, and also to expound the Mahāyāna for his parents, various kinsmen, and Brahmins, so as to cause them to enter it.
"And from where have you come? Sudhana said, "Noble One!"
"What is the birthplace of a bodhisattva? He replied, "Good son!..."
Bodhisattvas have ten places of birth. What are the ten? Good son!
The bodhicitta is the birthplace of a bodhisattva, for it gives birth to the family of bodhisattvas;
the profound mind is the birthplace of a bodhisattva, for it gives birth to the family of spiritual friends;
the stages are the birthplace of a bodhisattva, for they give birth to the family of the perfections.
The great vow is the birthplace of the bodhisattva, for it gives birth to the family of sublime conduct;
great compassion is the birthplace of the bodhisattva, for it gives birth to the family of the four means of attraction;
investigation according to reality is the birthplace of the bodhisattva, for it gives birth to the family of the perfection of wisdom.
The Mahāyāna is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for they are born into the family of skillful means;
teaching and transforming sentient beings is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for they are born into the family of the Buddhas;
wisdom and skillful means are the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for they are born into the family of the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena.
The cultivation of all dharmas is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for it gives birth to them within the family of all Tathāgatas of the past, present, and future. "Good son!
For the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, the perfection of wisdom is the mother;
skillful means is the father; the perfection of generosity is the wet-nurse; the perfection of ethical discipline is the foster-mother;
the perfection of patience is the ornament; the perfection of diligence is the nurturer; and the perfection of meditative concentration...
The act of washing and cleansing is for them; the spiritual friend is their teacher;
all factors of enlightenment are their companions; all wholesome dharmas are their kin; all bodhisattvas are their brothers; the bodhicitta is their home;
practice according to the truth is their family tradition; the stages (bhūmis) are their dwelling place; and the various patiences (kṣāntis) are...
The family is the Great Vow; the family precept is the fulfillment of all practices; exhorting others toward the Mahāyāna is the succession of the family heritage;
the Bodhisattva bound to one more birth, consecrated by the water of the Dharma, is the crown prince;
and the realization of Bodhi is that which can purify the family.

“Good son! In this way, the bodhisattva transcends the stage of ordinary beings, enters the rank of bodhisattvas, is born into the family of the Tathāgatas, and dwells within the lineage of the Buddhas. He is able to cultivate all practices, ensures that the Three Jewels are not interrupted, and is well able to protect the bodhisattva clan. He purifies the bodhisattva seed, is born into a noble and superior station, and is free from all faults and evils. Thus, he is revered and praised by all the worlds—devas, humans, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas.”

“Good son! Once a bodhisattva-mahāsattva has been born into such a noble and eminent family, because he knows that all phenomena are like reflections, he harbors no loathing or contempt for any worldly realm;
because he knows that all phenomena are like magical transformations, he is free from any defiled attachment to any state of existence.”
Because they know that all phenomena are without self, they teach and transform sentient beings with minds free from weariness;
because their essential nature is great compassion, they gather in sentient beings without perceiving any toil or hardship;
and because they thoroughly understand that birth and death are like a dream, they pass through all kalpas without fear.
Because they understand that all aggregates are like illusions, they manifest birth without weariness or aversion;
because they know that the elements and sense bases are identical to the dharma-realm, they do not undergo destruction or extinction amidst any sensory objects;
because they know all perceptions are like mirages, they enter the various realms of existence without giving rise to deluded confusion.
Because they realize that all phenomena are like illusions, they enter the realm of Māra without giving rise to defiled attachment;
because they know the Dharma-body, all afflictions cannot deceive them;
and because they have attained mastery, they penetrate all realms of existence without obstruction.

“Good son! My body is universally born throughout the entire Dharma-realm; it is equal to the diverse physical forms of all sentient beings, equal to the various distinct voices of all sentient beings, equal to the manifold names of all sentient beings, and equal to the preferred modes of conduct of all sentient beings, teaching and subduing them in accordance with the world.

It is equal to the manifestations of birth by all pure sentient beings, equal to the activities performed by all ordinary sentient beings, equal to the perceptions of all sentient beings, and equal to the vows of all Bodhisattvas, manifesting its body so as to fill the Dharma-realm.”
“Good son! I act thus in order to transform and deliver those who practiced the same deeds as I in the past but have now fallen away from the bodhicitta;
and also to teach and transform my parents and kinsmen.”
Furthermore, for the sake of teaching and transforming the various brahmins, so that they might abandon their pride regarding their lineage and be born into the family of the Tathāgata,
he was born here in this Jambudvīpa world, in the kingdom of Mālava, in the village of Koṭṭa, into a brahmin family.
"Good son! Abiding here within this great multi-storied pavilion, I employ various skillful means to teach, transform, and subdue sentient beings according to the inclinations of their minds."

"Good son! It is because I wish to accord with the minds of sentient beings; because I wish to bring to maturity those gods who share my practice in the Tuṣita Heaven; because I wish to manifest the adornments of the transformations of a Bodhisattva’s merit and wisdom;

because I wish to transcend all realms of desire; because I wish to cause them to renounce the pleasures of desire; because I wish to cause them to know that all conditioned things are impermanent; because I wish to cause them to know that the prosperity of the gods must inevitably decline; and because I wish to manifest the Dharma-gate of Great Wisdom at the time of my impending descent into birth."

Because he engaged in discourse with bodhisattvas of the same lifetime, because he wished to gather and transform those of like practice, and because he wished to teach and transform those sent by Śākyamuni Tathāgata so that they might all awaken like blossoming lotuses, he passed away from this life and was reborn in Tuṣita Heaven.
"Good son! When my vows are fulfilled, I have attained all-knowledge, and at the time I realize Bodhi, you and Mañjuśrī shall both behold me. Good son!"
"You should go to the place of the spiritual friend Mañjuśrī and ask him:
'How should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct?
How does one enter the gateway of Samantabhadra’s conduct?'"
How is it accomplished?
How is it vast? How is it conformable?
"How is it purified? How is it perfected? "Good son!
He shall explain it in detail for you. Why is this?
The great vows held by Mañjuśrī are not shared by any other bodhisattvas, even those numbering in the hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas.
“Good son! The conduct of the youth Mañjuśrī is vast, and his vows are boundless; he brings forth all the virtues of a bodhisattva without ceasing.”

"Good son! Mañjuśrī is constantly the mother of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas; he is constantly the teacher of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Bodhisattvas. He teaches and brings to maturity all sentient beings, and his fame is heard throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
He constantly serves as a Dharma-preacher within the assemblies of all Buddhas and is praised by all Tathāgatas."
Abiding in profound wisdom, they are able to see all phenomena as they truly are, penetrate the realm of all liberations, and bring to ultimate fulfillment all the practices of Samantabhadra.

“Good son! The youth Mañjuśrī is your spiritual friend; he has caused you to be born into the family of the Tathāgata, nurtured all roots of goodness, initiated all factors conducive to enlightenment, and enabled you to encounter true spiritual friends.
He has caused you to cultivate all merits, enter the net of all vows, and abide in all great aspirations.”
"I shall explain to you all the secret dharmas of the bodhisattvas and manifest to you the inconceivable practices of all bodhisattvas;
we were born together and practiced together in the past.
Therefore, son of good family!"
"You should go to the place where Mañjuśrī is; do not give rise to weariness or fatigue. Mañjuśrī will explain all merits for you. Why is this?"

All those spiritual friends whom you previously beheld—those who heard the bodhisattva practices, entered the gates of liberation, and fulfilled their great vows—all owe this to the majestic spiritual power of Mañjuśrī; Mañjuśrī has attained ultimate perfection in all places.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, took his leave, and departed.
*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 79; *The Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 80.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan by Imperial Decree, Part Twenty-one of the Thirty-ninth Chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, following the instructions of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, traveled by stages until he had passed through more than one hundred and ten cities. He then arrived at the city of Sumana in the country of Samantamukha and stood at its gate. There he contemplated Mañjuśrī, observing him with focused attention, searching all around in his longing to behold him.
At that time, Mañjuśrī extended his right hand from afar, across a distance of one hundred and ten yojanas, and placed it upon Sudhana’s head, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!

“Good son! If one is devoid of the root of faith, with a mind that is weak, regretful, and sorrowful; if one’s meritorious practices are incomplete and one falls away from diligent effort; if one becomes attached to even a single root of goodness and considers a mere trifle of merit to be sufficient; if one cannot skillfully initiate vows and practices; if one is not sustained by spiritual friends and is not remembered by the Tathāgatas; then one will be unable to understand such a nature of phenomena, such a principle, such a dharma-gate, such a course of conduct, or such a realm.

One will be utterly incapable of knowing them universally, knowing them in their variety, knowing them to their very source and bottom; nor will one be able to comprehend, enter into, explain, discern, realize, or attain them.”

At that time, Mañjuśrī proclaimed this Dharma, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening him, so as to cause the youth Sudhana to accomplish incalculable dharma-gates and become fully endowed with the light of immeasurable great wisdom. He caused him to attain the Bodhisattva’s boundless dhāraṇīs, boundless vows, boundless samādhis, boundless supernormal powers, and boundless knowledge; he caused him to enter the site of Samantabhadra’s practice and then returned him to his own dwelling place.
Thereupon, Mañjuśrī withdrew and became invisible.

Thereupon, Sudhana reflected and contemplated, single-mindedly aspiring to see Mañjuśrī and to meet all the spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) as numerous as the atoms within a trichiliocosm; he vowed to draw near to them all, to serve them with reverence, and to receive and practice their instructions without opposition.

He resolved to increase his pursuit of all-encompassing wisdom, to expand the ocean of great compassion, and to augment the clouds of great loving-kindness. Surveying all sentient beings, he gave rise to great joy and became firmly established in the bodhisattva’s dharma-gate of tranquility.

Universally taking all vast realms as his object, he studied the vast merits of all Buddhas, entered the definitive knowledge and vision of all Buddhas, increased the factors conducive to the path for all-knowledge, skillfully cultivated the profound resolve of all bodhisattvas, and came to know the sequence of the appearance of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

They enter the ocean of all dharmas, turn all wheels of Dharma, and manifest throughout all worlds; they enter the ocean of all bodhisattva vows, abide through all kalpas cultivating bodhisattva practices, illuminate the realms of all Tathāgatas, and nurture the faculties of all bodhisattvas;
they attain the pure radiance of omniscience that universally illumines the ten directions, removing all obscurations of darkness, with wisdom pervading the entire dharma-realm;
in all buddha-fields and all states of existence, they universally manifest their bodies, reaching everywhere without exception.
Having crushed all obstacles and entered the unimpeded Dharma, they abide on the ground of the equality of the Dharma-realm;

observing the realm of liberation of Samantabhadra, they hear the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, as well as his practices and vows, the auxiliary paths, the direct path, the various stages, the skillful means of the stages, the entry into the stages, the advancement through the stages, the abiding in the stages, the cultivation of the stages, the realms of the stages, the power of the stages, and the co-residence within the stages.

Longing with thirsting devotion to see Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, they then, right here at this Vajragarbha Bodhimanda, before the lion throne of Vairocana Tathāgata, upon a seat of a universal jewel lotus treasury, gave rise to a mind as vast as the realm of empty space; a mind free from all attachment that relinquishes all lands; a mind of unimpeded action regarding all unobstructed dharmas; a mind of unimpeded entry into the oceans of all ten directions; a pure mind universally entering the sphere of all-knowledge; a clear-sighted mind contemplating the adornments of the site of enlightenment; a vast mind entering the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas; a pervasive mind transforming all realms of sentient beings; an immeasurable mind purifying all lands; an inexhaustible mind abiding through all kalpas; and a mind reaching the ultimate realization of the ten powers of a Tathāgata.

When the youth Sudhana gave rise to such a thought, by the power of his own roots of goodness, the power of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, and the power of the shared roots of goodness with Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, he beheld ten kinds of auspicious signs.
What are the ten? They are:
seeing all Buddha-fields as pure, and seeing all Tathāgatas attain perfect enlightenment;
He saw all Buddha-fields as pure, with no evil realms;
he saw all Buddha-fields as pure, adorned with various wondrous lotus flowers;
he saw all Buddha-fields as pure, with the bodies and minds of all sentient beings being pure.
He saw all Buddha-lands as pure, adorned with various kinds of precious jewels;
he saw all Buddha-lands as pure, with all sentient beings adorning their bodies with various marks;
he saw all Buddha-lands as pure, covered above by clouds of various adornments.
He saw all Buddha-fields as pure, where all sentient beings gave rise to mutual compassion, benefiting one another and refraining from causing harm;
he saw all Buddha-fields as pure, with their bodhimaṇḍas magnificently adorned;
he saw all Buddha-fields as pure, where the minds of all sentient beings were constantly mindful of the Buddha.
These are the ten. Furthermore, one sees ten kinds of signs of light. What are these ten?
That is to say:
seeing all the atoms within all worlds, from each and every atom, there emerge clouds of Buddha-light webs as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, shining everywhere;
from each and every atom, there emerge clouds of Buddha-light wheels as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, with various colors and forms pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
From within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of jewel-like physical forms of Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm;
from within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of flaming wheels of Buddha-light, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm;

from within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of various exquisite fragrances, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the ten directions and praising the great ocean of merit of Samantabhadra’s universal vows and practices.

Within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of suns, moons, and stars as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, all radiating the light of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and universally illuminating the Dharma-realm;

within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of the bodily forms and colors of all sentient beings as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, emitting the light of the Buddhas and universally illuminating the Dharma-realm;
within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of mani-jewels in the form of the physical images of all Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.

From within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of the physical forms and images of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, filling the entire Dharma-realm, causing all sentient beings to attain liberation and have their aspirations fulfilled;

from within each and every atom, there emerge clouds of the physical forms and images of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, proclaiming the vast vows of all Buddhas throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
These are the ten.
At that time, having seen these ten kinds of radiant signs, the youth Sudhana thought to himself:
"I shall now certainly see the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, increase my roots of goodness, and behold all Buddhas."
"Regarding the vast realm of all Bodhisattvas, he gives rise to resolute understanding and attains omniscience.
At that time, Sudhana restrained all his faculties and, with single-minded intent, sought to see Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; he aroused great diligence, his mind never regressing.

Immediately, with the universal eye, they observe the spheres of perception of all Buddhas and the assemblies of Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions, conceiving the thought that they have attained the vision of Samantabhadra;

with the wisdom-eye, they contemplate the path of Samantabhadra, their minds as vast as space, their great compassion as firm as a diamond, vowing to follow the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra for all future time, conforming to him in every thought-moment, practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra, accomplishing wisdom, entering the realm of the Tathāgatas, and dwelling on the stage of Samantabhadra.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld Samantabhadra Bodhisattva before the Tathāgata in the midst of the great assembly, seated upon a lion throne of precious lotuses, surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas. He was most preeminent and peerless in the world;
his realm of wisdom was immeasurable and boundless, unfathomable and inconceivable, equal to the Buddhas of the three periods of time, such that no bodhisattva could fully perceive it.

He saw that from every single pore of Samantabhadra’s body issued forth clouds of light as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and all worlds, extinguishing the sufferings and afflictions of all sentient beings and causing all Bodhisattvas to give rise to great joy;

he saw that from every single pore issued forth clouds of various colored fragrant flames as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands, pervading the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas throughout the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, universally perfuming them;

he saw that from every single pore issued forth clouds of various flowers as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands, pervading the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas throughout the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, raining down myriad wonderful blossoms.

He saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of incense trees as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, pervading the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas’ assemblies, raining down various sublime fragrances;

he saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of exquisite garments as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, pervading the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas’ assemblies, raining down various exquisite garments;

he saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of jewel trees as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, pervading the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas’ assemblies, raining down mani-jewels.
I saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of bodies of devas of the form realm, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, filling the dharma-realm and praising the bodhicitta;
I saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of bodies of Brahmā devas, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, exhorting all Tathāgatas to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma;
I saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of bodies of lords of the desire realm, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, protecting and upholding the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of Buddha-lands from the three periods of time, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space. For the sake of all sentient beings, they provided a place of refuge for those without refuge, protection for those without protection, and a basis of reliance for those without reliance.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of pure Buddha-lands, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space; therein, all Buddhas appeared in the world, and the assemblies of Bodhisattvas completely filled them.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of pure and impure Buddha-lands, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, causing all defiled sentient beings to attain purity;

in every single pore, he saw clouds of impure and pure Buddha-lands, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, causing all defiled sentient beings to attain purity;

in every single pore, he saw clouds of impure Buddha-lands, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, causing those who are purely defiled to attain purity.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of bodies of sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space; according to what was appropriate for them, they taught and transformed sentient beings, causing them all to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of bodies of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, extolling the various names of all Buddhas and causing all sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness.

I saw from each and every pore, in every thought-moment, clouds of bodhisattva bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields emerging and pervading all buddha-fields throughout the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, proclaiming the roots of goodness produced by all Buddhas and bodhisattvas from their first aspiration;

I saw from each and every pore, in every thought-moment, clouds of bodhisattva bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields emerging and pervading the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, and within each and every field of all those buddha-fields, proclaiming the ocean of vows of all bodhisattvas and the pure, wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;

I saw from each and every pore, in every thought-moment, clouds of the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva emerging, causing the minds of all sentient beings to attain fulfillment and enabling them to fully cultivate and accumulate the path to omniscience.

He saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of bodies of perfectly enlightened ones, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment in all Buddha-fields, causing all bodhisattvas to increase in the Great Dharma and achieve omniscience.

At that time, seeing such a realm of sovereign spiritual powers as this of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the youth Sudhana was filled with joy throughout his body and mind, leaping for joy beyond measure;
he gazed again upon each and every limb and each and every pore of Samantabhadra, and saw within them all three-thousandfold world systems.

The wind-wheel, water-wheel, earth-wheel, and fire-wheel; the great oceans, rivers, and various jewel mountains; Mount Sumeru and the Iron Encircling Mountains; villages, camps, cities, towns, palaces, and gardens; all the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, and the realm of King Yama; the eight classes of devas and nāgas, humans and non-humans; the abodes of the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm; the sun, moon, stars, and constellations; wind, clouds, thunder, and lightning; days, nights, months, seasons, years, and kalpas; the appearance of Buddhas in the world, the assemblies of Bodhisattvas, and the adornments of the sites of enlightenment—all such things as these were clearly seen.
Just as one sees this world, so too does one see all worlds throughout the ten directions;
just as one sees the present worlds of the ten directions, so too does one see all worlds of the past and future, each distinct and without confusion.
Just as he manifested such supernatural powers in the presence of this Vairocana Tathāgata,
so too did he manifest supernatural powers in the presence of the Buddha Bhadramukha in the world Padmaśrī in the eastern direction.
As it was in the presence of the Buddha Bhadramukha,
so it was in all worlds in the eastern direction; as it was in the eastern direction,
so it was [in all directions].

In the south, west, and north, in the four intermediate directions, and above and below—in all worlds where the Tathāgatas reside—one should know that they likewise manifest their supernormal powers in exactly this manner.

Just as it is in all worlds throughout the ten directions, so too in every single atom within all Buddha-fields of the ten directions, there are assemblies of Buddhas of the Dharma-realm; and at each and every Buddha’s location, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra sits upon a lion throne of precious lotuses, manifesting spiritual powers in exactly this same manner.

Within each and every body of Samantabhadra, there are manifested all realms of the three periods of time, all Buddha-lands, all sentient beings, the appearance of all Buddhas, and the assemblies of all Bodhisattvas; furthermore, one hears the voices of all sentient beings, the voices of all Buddhas, the wheels of Dharma turned by all Tathāgatas, the various practices accomplished by all Bodhisattvas, and the playful supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas.
Upon seeing such immeasurable and inconceivable great supernormal powers of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the youth Sudhana immediately attained ten kinds of wisdom-pāramitās.
What are these ten? They are:
the perfection of wisdom that, in every thought-moment, is able to pervade all buddha-fields;
The perfection of wisdom that, in every thought-moment, is able to go to the abodes of all Buddhas;
the perfection of wisdom that, in every thought-moment, is able to make offerings to all Tathāgatas;
the perfection of wisdom that, in every thought-moment, universally hears, receives, and upholds the Dharma from the presence of all Tathāgatas.
In every thought-moment, they contemplate the wisdom-pāramitā of the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
in every thought-moment, they know the wisdom-pāramitā of the inconceivable great supernormal powers of all Buddhas;
in every thought-moment, they possess the wisdom-pāramitā of inexhaustible eloquence in expounding a single phrase of the Dharma until the end of the future.
In every thought-moment, there is the perfection of wisdom that observes all phenomena with profound prajñā;
in every thought-moment, there is the perfection of wisdom that enters the ocean of the true mark of all dharma-realms;
in every thought-moment, there is the perfection of wisdom that knows the minds of all sentient beings.
In every thought-moment, the wisdom-paramita through which the practices of Samantabhadra’s wisdom universally manifest before him was attained by the youth Sudhana;
